Title: What is a central bank for?
text: What is a central bank for? Words from Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the Seminar On Citizenship The Witherspoon Institute Universidad Panamericana Mexico, Mexico City June 12, 2014 I am pleased to go to the Universidad Panamericana to participate in this magnificent seminar On Citizenship Organized by the Witherspoon Institute, and to have the opportunity to talk with you. After developing my career in the private sector, for me it has been an honor and a stimulus to venture into public service within a space of excellence such as the Bank of Mexico. The nature and importance of the functions performed by a central bank is not always evident, hence the relevance of talking with distinguished professionals from various areas about the features that define this type of institution. I do not intend to make an academic presentation but, rather, to transport them to the offices of a central bank, to expose them to the daily work and, above all, to share with them the sense of responsibility and intellectual motivation that involves participating in decision-making in that area. What are central banks At present, central banks are the entities that have the exclusive power to issue the currency of a country. Since, in addition to being a store of value and a unit of measure, currency is the main medium of exchange for companies, it must enjoy the public's trust.1 1 For a pioneering description of the functions of central banking as an art see Hawtrey, R.G. (1933), The art of central banking. London: Longmans, Green and Co. 1 Therefore, a central bank has as its primary purpose to preserve the purchasing power of the currency and defend it against what erodes it the most: inflation. This phenomenon, which consists of the continuous and generalized increase in prices, is harmful to the economy and affects both families and companies. With high inflation, the price system does not effectively fulfil its function of sending clear signals to consumers or producers. It is possible, then, that savings and investment decisions are distorted, wrong economic decisions are made, and speculation is encouraged, generating net losses for the whole society. In addition, when inflation rises, interest rates rise, as they must compensate for the loss of value of money and uncertainty. Long-term high rates make financing more expensive and distract it from speculative activities, preventing the realization of numerous potential projects and affecting economic growth and employment. Inflation hurts even more severely those who have the least: those who live up to date on their wages and have no way to protect their few assets from loss of value. Thus, inflation reduces the purchasing power of wages and worsens the distribution of income, to the extent that it has been called the most unfair and arbitrary tax. As is evident, the objective of controlling inflation is not opposed to economic growth, on the contrary, it is a prerequisite for growth. 2 sustainable in the long term. Empirical evidence reveals that the most successful experiences of economic expansion have been accompanied by price stability.2 Generally inflation is created by an increase in the growth of the money supply that exceeds its demand. It may also respond to temporary shocks in costs or prices, in which case the inflationary effect tends to be transitory. To control inflation, a central bank has monetary policy that, among other instruments, is typically integrated by a reference interest rate that guides the rest of the market rates, and by a communication strategy. In general, a monetary policy adjusts to the business cycle and tends to relax when there is a recession and to restrict when there is economic expansion. In addition to their primary purpose, central banks typically exercise some additional functions and most participate in the regulation and promotion of the financial system, serve as lenders of last resort, and foster the effectiveness of electronic payment systems.3 In the wake of the recent crisis, central banks have taken on greater responsibilities, including the preservation of financial stability, That which 2 Even the US Federal Reserve, which with a dual objective simultaneously seeks price stability and employment, seems to recognize in practice that controlling inflation is a prerequisite for reducing unemployment. 3 Bagehot's classic requirement for the lender of last resort is to lend only to solvent banks, against good collateral and at a punitive interest rate. See Bagehot, W. (1873), Lombard Street: A Description of the Money Market, London: H.S. King. 3 generates new challenges and questions.4 For some decades, the international consensus has been strengthened that a central bank, when autonomous, better fulfills both the fight against inflation and its other assigned functions. The disadvantages of not having independence may include, inter alia, forcing the central bank to cover fiscal deficits; that monetary policies are inconsistent over time and that short-term, inflation-generating approaches are adopted. Today, a large part of the central banks enjoy legal and, above all, effective autonomy, that is, a wider margin of maneuver to design and implement their strategies.5 While an autonomous monetary policy is essential to maintaining price stability and laying the foundations for development, it cannot replace the real sources of growth, which are investment, productivity and employment. That is why monetary policy must be accompanied by responsible fiscal policy as well as structural reforms. The role of the Bank of Mexico The Bank of Mexico is a public body with the priority objective of preserving the purchasing power of the national currency. Without pretending to be exhaustive, I would like 4 There is a debate about whether central banks are being overburdened with responsibilities, generating conflicts between objectives and jeopardizing their priority role. See, for example, Orphanides, A. (2013), "Is monetary policy overburdened?" Federal Reserve Bank of Boston Public Policy Discussion Papers, No. 13-8. 5 For the implications of the difference between de jure and de facto autonomy see Taylor, J.B. (2013), "The Effectiveness of Central Bank Independence vs. Policy Rules," Business Economics, 48(3). 4 to tell you about five highly representative aspects of the nature and work of our central bank. First, as of April 1, 1994, the Bank of Mexico became an autonomous institution. The essence of its autonomy lies in the fact that the Constitution expressly states that no other authority may oblige it to grant financing. This shields the institution against pressures of any kind and allows it to concentrate on controlling inflation in the long term. The ability to act autonomously is also guaranteed by budgetary and administrative independence; and by the mechanisms for the appointment of the five members of the Governing Board, which are the Governor and the four Deputy Governors, in charge of the management of the Bank and each with the same voting power. The members of that Board must meet strict requirements for professional training and experience in the monetary and financial field; they are proposed by the President and have to be ratified by the Senate, which guarantees the consensus of two powers; they are staggered appointees and have permanence and job security. All this promotes the independent attitude of each of them. Secondly, the decision-making of this collegiate body is a very dynamic process. The Board meets daily to deliberate on internal administration 5 or on the other legal tasks, such as issuing the working capital, participating in the regulation of the financial system and promoting the payment system. Of course, one of the essential tasks of the Governing Board is to determine monetary policy generally on dates that are announced since the end of the previous year. The periodic decision matures in meetings over almost a whole week, where the national and international economic situation, as well as the evolution of inflation and its expectations, are analyzed, based on a wide collection of information previously distributed. Subsequently, the members of the Board express their position, their arguments and their vote and draft the communication to the public. In these meetings it is possible to observe an informed, rigorous and open discussion, which is undoubtedly enriching and exemplary as a collegiate debate. Thirdly, it is worth elaborating on the monetary policy framework adopted by the Bank. This method, called inflation targeting, is characterized by having explicit targets, in our case three percent as a permanent objective, and because it maintains clear and constant communication about the application of monetary policy and its progress.6 A scheme such as the one described has the advantage that since there are multi-year objectives, in case inflation deviates temporarily, the medium-term targets become the anchor that limits the deterioration of expectations. 6 For a discussion of international experience with inflation targeting technique, see Bernanke, B.S., and M. Woodford (2005), The Inflation-Targeting Debate, National Bureau of Economic Research in NBER Book Series Studies in Business Cycles. 6 Monetary policy has operated with a flexible exchange rate regime. As you know, since 1995 the peso is no longer subject to a fixed parity and the exchange rate is free-floating, which implies that the value of the peso against other currencies is determined by the supply and demand between the national currency and other currencies. Only on rare occasions, in times of extreme volatility, and generally in accordance with pre-announced rules, has the Bank of Mexico intervened to restore order to the markets. The free floating of the exchange rate has given greater flexibility to the Mexican economy to adapt to external shocks, through the response of market interest rates and the exchange rate. To meet its objectives and like other central banks, the Bank of Mexico has accumulated international reserves, which are made up of highly liquid assets denominated in foreign currency. These come mostly from the currencies acquired from PEMEX by legal provision and, in general, function as an indicator that an economy has liquidity, which contributes to financial stability and contributes to the country having access to external resources in better conditions. Regarding international reserves, there is a persistent confusion: it lies in thinking that they are resources that could be invested in other areas. Specifically, they cannot be used to finance productive activity, since this would have to take the form of a loan to the Government, which in addition to being potentially inflationary if not counteracted, has legal impediments. 7 Fourth, and closely related to the success of the Bank's policies, is the communication strategy. Until a few decades ago, central banks were opaque institutions, governed by esoteric statements and oracular gestures. However, since an autonomous institution must legitimize its status through strict accountability, this situation has changed. The Bank of Mexico has followed this process of dissemination and transparency. It currently sends periodic reports to Congress and the Executive in which it details the application of monetary policy, as well as the exercise of its budget and other functions. Weekly statements and detailed quarterly financial statements, inflation releases and reports, reports on the financial system, among many other publications and indicators, are available on our website. In particular, since 2011 the detailed minutes of the monetary policy meetings of the Governing Board have been published. Fifth, many wonder if the Bank of Mexico can make gains or losses throughout its fiscal year and what it does with them. Indeed, this institution, like any other central bank, can record profits or losses. As it has no profit purpose, when there are profits, the Bank delivers to the Federal Government the amount of its remaining operation, once its capital reserves have been covered. Either way, since a central bank has a public function, while a commercial bank has profitability as its function, a central bank's balance sheets do not 8 they must be judged by the mere criterion of profit and loss, nor by their level of capital, but by progress towards their institutional objective. Achievements and challenges of the Bank of Mexico To date, the balance of the fight against inflation and its effects on economic stability can be considered adequate. We have gone from double-digit inflation to inflation getting closer to the three percent target, which has meant lower interest rates. Today, the government, the private sector and families are financed in better conditions and terms and, to mention an example, a young professional can acquire a mortgage loan with fixed payments to twenty years, something that would have seemed a fantasy in inflationary times. Similarly, efforts to improve the legal framework and financial regulation and supervisory processes in which the Bank is involved have enabled modern payment systems, sound and well-capitalized financial intermediaries, and deep financial markets that have been able to withstand recent financial turbulence. Despite these advances, it is very important that the institution's policies consolidate the convergence of inflation to the three percent target. This achievement does not mean that inflation should be matched to the target at all times, which would be impossible, but that it should remain fluctuating around it as closely as possible. 9 The Bank should also continue to participate in the constant updating of a financial regulatory framework that allows all participants to respond flexibly to changes in the sector, that competition between intermediaries is increased, that credit flows without incurring systemic risks, and that markets become deeper and more effective. Another important challenge, closely related to the previous one, is to promote the financial inclusion of those who have been marginalized from the formal banking sector. As is known, access to banking services allows individuals, families and companies to safeguard their assets and make more efficient economic decisions. However, inclusion in Mexico is modest not only with respect to advanced countries but with those of similar degree of development. Hence the importance of harmonizing ancestral forms of financial organization with the formal offer of the sector. With regard to the international environment, the Bank of Mexico must remain alert to the challenges to global financial stability arising from the expansionary monetary policy of the advanced countries. In particular, copious portfolio capital flows channelled to emerging markets can create imbalances and be quickly reversed. In addition, the exit strategies of these expansionary policies are beginning to pose unprecedented risks. 10 Conclusions If we understand citizenship as a set of political and economic rights and duties that include freedom of choice and equal opportunities, it is clear that price stability allows better decisions to be made for the whole society and contributes to preserving the purchasing power of the patrimony and income of the most disadvantaged, avoiding catastrophic swings for their future and providing them with means to overcome their condition. Of course, price stability is not the only condition for improving well-being, however, without it there is no possible improvement. No wonder the notion has been strengthened around the world that, in order to promote sustained economic growth, and I would say to broaden the concept of citizenship, the best contribution a central bank can make is to seek price stability. For the Bank of Mexico, it is very important that there is a thorough understanding of its objectives and a broad consensus on their importance, as this facilitates the social assimilation of its policies and reduces the cost of combating inflation. 11
text_original: Para qu sirve un banco central? Palabras de Manuel Snchez Gonzlez Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico en el Seminario mbitos de Ciudadana The Witherspoon Institute Universidad Panamericana Mxico, Ciudad de Mxico 12 de junio de 2014 Me da gusto acudir a la Universidad Panamericana para participar en este magnfico seminario mbitos de ciudadana organizado por el Instituto Witherspoon, y tener la oportunidad de platicar con ustedes. Despus de desarrollar mi carrera en el sector privado, para m ha constituido un honor y un estmulo incursionar en el servicio pblico dentro de un espacio de excelencia como el Banco de Mxico. No siempre resulta evidente la naturaleza e importancia de las funciones que realiza un banco central, de ah la pertinencia de conversar con distinguidos profesionistas de diversas reas sobre los rasgos que definen a este tipo de instituciones. No pretendo hacer una exposicin acadmica sino, ms bien, transportarlos a las oficinas de un banco central, exponerles el trabajo cotidiano y, sobre todo, compartirles el sentido de responsabilidad y motivacin intelectual que implica participar en la toma de decisiones en ese mbito. Qu son los bancos centrales En la actualidad, los bancos centrales son las entidades que poseen la facultad exclusiva de emitir la moneda de un pas. Dado que, adems de almacn de valor y unidad de medida, la moneda es el principal medio de cambio de las sociedades, sta debe gozar de la confianza del pblico.1 1 Para una descripcin pionera de las funciones de la banca central como un arte vase Hawtrey, R.G. (1933), The art of central banking. London: Longmans, Green and Co. 1 Por eso, un banco central tiene como su finalidad primordial preservar el poder adquisitivo de la moneda y defenderlo contra lo que ms lo erosiona: la inflacin. Este fenmeno, que consiste en el aumento continuo y generalizado de los precios, es nocivo para la economa y afecta tanto a las familias como a las empresas. Con una inflacin elevada, el sistema de precios no cumple eficazmente su funcin de enviar seales claras a los consumidores o productores. Es posible, entonces, que se distorsionen las decisiones de ahorro e inversin, se tomen decisiones econmicas errneas, y se incentive la especulacin, generando prdidas netas para toda la sociedad. Adems, cuando la inflacin aumenta se elevan las tasas de inters, pues stas deben compensar la prdida de valor del dinero y la incertidumbre. Las altas tasas por tiempo prolongado encarecen el financiamiento, y lo distraen hacia actividades especulativas, lo que impide la realizacin de numerosos proyectos potenciales e incide sobre el crecimiento econmico y el empleo. La inflacin daa todava ms severamente a quienes menos tienen: a quienes viven al da con sus sueldos y no cuentan con formas de proteger sus pocos activos de la prdida de valor. As, la inflacin reduce el poder de compra de los salarios y empeora la distribucin del ingreso, al grado de que se la ha llamado el impuesto ms injusto y arbitrario. Como resulta evidente, el objetivo de controlar la inflacin no es opuesto al crecimiento econmico, al contrario, es un requisito indispensable para propiciar un crecimiento 2 sostenible en el largo plazo. La evidencia emprica revela que las experiencias ms exitosas de expansin econmica han estado acompaadas de la estabilidad de precios.2 Generalmente la inflacin se crea por un aumento en el crecimiento de la oferta de dinero que excede su demanda. Tambin puede responder a choques temporales en los costos o en los precios, en cuyo caso el efecto inflacionario tiende a ser transitorio. Para controlar la inflacin, un banco central dispone de la poltica monetaria que, entre otros instrumentos, se integra tpicamente por una tasa de inters de referencia que orienta el resto de las tasas del mercado, y por una estrategia de comunicacin. En general, una poltica monetaria se ajusta al ciclo econmico y tiende a relajarse cuando hay recesin y a restringirse cuando hay expansin econmica. Adems de su objetivo primordial, los bancos centrales suelen ejercer algunas funciones adicionales y la mayora participa en la regulacin y promocin del sistema financiero, funge como prestamista de ltima instancia y fomenta la eficacia de los sistemas electrnicos de pagos.3 A raz de la crisis reciente, los bancos centrales han adquirido mayores responsabilidades, incluyendo la preservacin de la estabilidad financiera, lo que 2 Inclusive la Reserva Federal de los Estados Unidos, que con un objetivo dual busca simultneamente la estabilidad de precios y el empleo, parece reconocer en la prctica que el control de la inflacin es requisito previo para reducir el desempleo. 3 La prescripcin clsica de Bagehot respecto al prestamista de ltima instancia es prestar solamente a bancos solventes, contra una buena garanta y con una tasa de inters de castigo. Vase Bagehot, W. (1873), Lombard Street: A Description of the Money Market, London: H.S. King. 3 genera nuevos retos y cuestionamientos.4 Desde hace algunas dcadas, se ha fortalecido el consenso internacional de que un banco central, cuando es autnomo, cumple de mejor manera tanto el combate a la inflacin como sus otras funciones asignadas. Las desventajas de no tener independencia pueden ser, entre otras, que se obligue al banco central a sufragar los dficits fiscales; que las polticas monetarias sean incongruentes en el tiempo y que se adopten enfoques de corto plazo, generadores de inflacin. Hoy, gran parte de los bancos centrales gozan de autonoma legal y, sobre todo, efectiva, es decir, de un ms amplio margen de maniobra para disear e implementar sus estrategias.5 Si bien una poltica monetaria autnoma es fundamental para mantener la estabilidad de precios y sentar las bases del desarrollo, sta no puede sustituir las fuentes reales del crecimiento, que son la inversin, la productividad y el empleo. Por eso, la poltica monetaria debe ser acompaada de una poltica fiscal responsable, as como de reformas estructurales. La funcin del Banco de Mxico El Banco de Mxico es un organismo pblico con el objetivo prioritario de preservar el poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. Sin pretender ser exhaustivo, me gustara 4 Existe un debate sobre si se est sobrecargando de responsabilidades a los bancos centrales, generando conflictos entre objetivos y poniendo en peligro su funcin prioritaria. Vase, por ejemplo, Orphanides, A. (2013), Is monetary policy overburdened? Federal Reserve Bank of Boston Public Policy Discussion Papers, No. 13-8. 5 Para las implicaciones de la diferencia entre autonoma de jure y de facto vase Taylor, J.B. (2013), The Effectiveness of Central Bank Independence vs. Policy Rules, Business Economics, 48(3). 4 hablarles de cinco aspectos altamente representativos de la naturaleza y labor de nuestro banco central. En primer lugar, a partir del 1 de abril de 1994, el Banco de Mxico se convirti en una institucin autnoma. La esencia de su autonoma radica en que la Constitucin seala expresamente que ninguna otra autoridad podr obligarlo a conceder financiamiento. Ello blinda a la institucin contra presiones de cualquier ndole y le permite concentrarse en controlar la inflacin a largo plazo. La capacidad de actuar autnomamente se encuentra, adems, garantizada por la independencia presupuestal y administrativa; y por los mecanismos para el nombramiento de los cinco miembros de la Junta de Gobierno, que son el Gobernador y los cuatro Subgobernadores, encargados de la conduccin del Banco y cada uno con el mismo poder de voto. Los miembros de esa Junta deben cumplir estrictos requisitos de formacin profesional y experiencia en el mbito monetario y financiero; son propuestos por el Presidente y tienen que ser ratificados por el Senado, lo que garantiza el consenso de dos poderes; son designados escalonadamente y tienen permanencia y seguridad laboral. Todo ello promueve la actitud independiente de cada uno de ellos. En segundo lugar, la toma de decisiones de este rgano colegiado es un proceso muy dinmico. La Junta se rene cotidianamente para deliberar sobre la administracin interna 5 o sobre las otras encomiendas legales, como emitir el circulante, participar en la regulacin del sistema financiero y promover el sistema de pagos. Por supuesto, una de las labores esenciales de la Junta de Gobierno es determinar la poltica monetaria generalmente en fechas que se anuncian desde finales del ao anterior. La decisin peridica se madura en reuniones a lo largo de casi toda una semana, donde se analizan, con base en un amplio acervo de informacin previamente distribuida, la situacin econmica nacional e internacional, as como la evolucin de la inflacin y sus expectativas. Posteriormente, los miembros de la Junta expresan su postura, sus argumentos y su voto y redactan la comunicacin al pblico. En estas reuniones es posible observar una discusin informada, rigurosa y abierta, que sin duda es enriquecedora y ejemplar como debate colegiado. En tercer lugar, conviene abundar sobre el marco de poltica monetaria que ha adoptado el Banco. Este mtodo, denominado de objetivos de inflacin, se caracteriza por tener metas explcitas, en nuestro caso de tres por ciento como objetivo permanente, y porque mantiene una comunicacin clara y constante sobre la aplicacin de la poltica monetaria y sus avances.6 Un esquema como el descrito tiene la ventaja de que al existir objetivos multianuales, en caso de que la inflacin se desve temporalmente, las metas de mediano plazo se convierten en el ancla que limita el deterioro de las expectativas. 6 Para una discusin de la experiencia internacional con la tcnica de objetivos de inflacin, vase Bernanke, B.S, y M. Woodford (2005), The Inflation-Targeting Debate, National Bureau of Economic Research en NBER Book Series Studies in Business Cycles. 6 La poltica monetaria ha operado con un rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible. Como ustedes saben, desde 1995 el peso ya no est sujeto a una paridad fija y el tipo de cambio es de libre flotacin, lo que implica que el valor del peso frente a otras divisas se determina por la oferta y demanda entre la moneda nacional y otras monedas. nicamente en contadas ocasiones, en momentos de extrema volatilidad, y generalmente de acuerdo con reglas preanunciadas, el Banco de Mxico ha intervenido para restaurar el orden de los mercados. La libre flotacin del tipo de cambio le ha dado mayor flexibilidad a la economa mexicana para adaptarse a choques externos, mediante la respuesta de las tasas de inters de mercado y del tipo de cambio. Para cumplir con sus objetivos y como otros bancos centrales, el Banco de Mxico ha acumulado reservas internacionales, que se integran de activos altamente lquidos denominados en moneda extranjera. Estos provienen en su mayora de las divisas adquiridas de PEMEX por disposicin legal y, en general, funcionan como un indicador de que una economa tiene liquidez, lo que abona a la estabilidad financiera y contribuye a que el pas tenga acceso a recursos externos en mejores condiciones. Respecto a las reservas internacionales hay una confusin persistente: radica en pensar que son recursos que se podran invertir en otros rubros. Especficamente, no pueden utilizarse para financiar la actividad productiva, ya que ello tendra que adoptar la forma de un prstamo al Gobierno, lo que adems de ser potencialmente inflacionario si no se contrarresta, tiene impedimentos legales. 7 En cuarto lugar, y estrechamente relacionado con el xito de las polticas del Banco, se encuentra la estrategia de comunicacin. Hasta hace pocos lustros, los bancos centrales eran instituciones opacas, que se regan por declaraciones esotricas y gestos oraculares. Sin embargo, dado que una institucin autnoma debe legitimar su estatuto mediante una estricta rendicin de cuentas, esta situacin ha cambiado. El Banco de Mxico se ha acompasado a este proceso de difusin y transparencia. Actualmente enva informes peridicos al Congreso y al Ejecutivo en los que detalla la aplicacin de la poltica monetaria, as como el ejercicio de su presupuesto y otras funciones. Los estados de cuenta semanales y los estados financieros trimestrales detallados, los comunicados e informes sobre la inflacin, los reportes sobre el sistema financiero, entre otras muchas publicaciones e indicadores, estn disponibles en nuestra pgina web. En particular, desde 2011 se publican las minutas detalladas de las reuniones de poltica monetaria de la Junta de Gobierno. En quinto lugar, muchos se preguntan si el Banco de Mxico puede tener ganancias o prdidas a lo largo de su ejercicio y qu hace con ellas. En efecto, esta institucin, como cualquier otro banco central, puede registrar ganancias o prdidas. Al no tener propsito de lucro, cuando hay ganancias, el Banco entrega al Gobierno Federal el importe de su remanente de operacin, una vez cubiertas sus reservas de capital. De cualquier manera, dado que un banco central tiene una funcin pblica, mientras que un banco comercial tiene como funcin la rentabilidad, los balances de un banco central no 8 deben juzgarse por el mero criterio de ganancias y prdidas, ni por su nivel de capital, sino por los avances hacia su objetivo institucional. Logros y desafos del Banco de Mxico Hasta la fecha, el saldo del combate a la inflacin y sus efectos sobre la estabilidad econmica pueden considerarse adecuados. Hemos pasado de inflaciones de dos dgitos a una inflacin cada vez ms cercana a la meta de tres por ciento, lo que ha implicado bajas en las tasas de inters. Hoy, el gobierno, el sector privado y las familias se financian en mejores condiciones y plazos y, por mencionar un ejemplo, un joven profesionista puede adquirir un crdito hipotecario con pagos fijos a veinte aos, algo que hubiera parecido una fantasa en las pocas inflacionarias. Igualmente, los esfuerzos realizados para mejorar el marco legal y los procesos de regulacin y supervisin financiera, en los que el Banco interviene, han permitido contar con sistemas de pagos modernos, con intermediarios financieros slidos y bien capitalizados, y con mercados financieros profundos que han podido resistir las turbulencias financieras recientes. No obstante estos avances, es muy importante que las polticas de la institucin consoliden la convergencia de la inflacin al objetivo de tres por ciento. Este logro no significa que la inflacin deba ser coincidir con la meta en todo momento, lo que sera imposible, sino que permanezca fluctuando alrededor de ella lo ms cerca posible. 9 Igualmente, el Banco debe continuar participando en la actualizacin constante de un marco normativo en materia financiera que permita que todos los participantes respondan con flexibilidad a los cambios en el sector, que se eleve la competencia entre intermediarios, que el crdito fluya sin incurrir en riesgos sistmicos y que los mercados se vuelvan ms profundos y eficaces. Otro reto importante, muy relacionado con el anterior, consiste en fomentar la inclusin financiera de quienes han estado marginados del sector bancario formal. Como es sabido, el acceso a los servicios bancarios permite a los individuos, familias y empresas resguardar su patrimonio y tomar decisiones econmicas ms eficientes. Sin embargo, la inclusin en Mxico es modesta no solo con respecto a los pases avanzados sino con aquellos de similar grado de desarrollo. De ah la importancia de armonizar formas ancestrales de organizacin financiera con la oferta formal del sector. En lo que atae al entorno internacional, el Banco de Mxico debe mantenerse alerta a los desafos a la estabilidad financiera global derivados de la poltica monetaria expansiva de los pases avanzados. En particular, los copiosos flujos de capital de cartera canalizados a los mercados emergentes pueden generar desequilibrios y revertirse con rapidez. Adicionalmente, las estrategias de salida de estas polticas expansivas comienzan a plantear riesgos inditos. 10 Conclusiones Si entendemos la ciudadana como un conjunto de derechos y deberes polticos y econmicos que incluyen la libertad de eleccin y la igualdad de oportunidades, es evidente que la estabilidad de precios permite tomar mejores decisiones a toda la sociedad y contribuye a preservar el poder adquisitivo del patrimonio y los ingresos de los ms desfavorecidos, evitando vaivenes catastrficos para su futuro y brindndoles medios para superar su condicin. Por supuesto, la estabilidad de precios no es la nica condicin para mejorar el bienestar, sin embargo, sin ella no hay mejoramiento posible. No es extrao que se haya fortalecido en todo el mundo la nocin de que, para promover el crecimiento econmico sostenido, y yo dira para ensanchar el concepto de ciudadana, la mejor contribucin que un banco central puede hacer es buscar la estabilidad de los precios. Para el Banco de Mxico es muy importante que haya una comprensin cabal de sus objetivos y un consenso amplio en torno a su importancia, pues eso facilita la asimilacin social de sus polticas y disminuye el costo de combatir la inflacin. 11

Title: Formal act of the delivery-reception of the collection of Porfirian banknotes of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the formal ceremony of the delivery - reception of the collection of banknotes Porfirianos from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to the Bank of Mexico. June 1, 2015 ? Doctor Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena, Secretary of Foreign Affairs ? Dr. Maria Teresa Franco Gonzalez Salas, General Director of the National Institute of Anthropology and History ? Officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and fellow officials of the Bank of Mexico ? Ladies and gentlemen, One of the first calls I received from Foreign Minister Meade - already in his duties at the head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs - filled me with enthusiasm and enthusiasm. On that occasion, the foreign minister told me about the existence of a large collection of more than 60,000 Porfirian banknotes and his idea that it would be the Bank of Mexico that would guard that treasure. 1 historical. Today this brilliant idea of Dr. Meade has come true. Thank you very much, Chancellor. Today, in fact, concludes a long journey for more than 60 thousand Porfirian banknotes and it is for the Bank of Mexico a source of pride and gratitude that this "return home", of pieces of incalculable numismatic and historical value, culminates precisely in the Numismatic Collection of our Central Institute. As some of you may already know, these valuable numismatic pieces left Mexico, specifically the Customs of the port of Veracruz, in April 1914 and remained for decades sheltered in the United States Department of the Treasury. Today this historical treasure is not only back in Mexico, but thanks to the responsibility and generosity of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs that chose to deliver it on loan. 2 the Bank of Mexico will be part of the numismatic heritage of our Central Institute. This decision represents for us an honor and a recognition of the numismatic work developed by the Central Bank, and at the same time, it means a commitment to safeguard, preserve and disseminate this collection of banknotes. All of you can be absolutely sure that we will put our knowledge, experience and best effort into meritoriously fulfilling the task. "Centennial trip, from Veracruz to Chapultepec", name that we have given to the exhibition that accompanies this event, summarizes the history of the collection of Porfirian banknotes that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs formally gives us today. Let's make a little history: on April 21, 1914, the Navy of the United States of America invaded the port of Veracruz, but not before facing the heroic resistance of 3 residents and cadets of the Naval School, a feat that we commemorated last year with the minting and circulation of a 20-peso coin. One of the main objectives of the invading forces was to take the Customs of the port supposedly to prevent the entry of weapons destined for the illegitimate regime of Victoriano Huerta. With this to the infamous grievance that was the fact of the invasion, the US troops added the flagrant illegality of administering and operating customs, charging duties on imports and exports that were made during the months that the occupation lasted. Worse, the invading forces took with them, when they left the port in November of that year, a significant amount of the cash proceeds from customs collections, which they later deposited with the United States Department of the Treasury. 4 Although it is not for me to talk about the efforts made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to recover this historical and numismatic treasure, we must recognize the good result obtained and the meaning of it, since the collection of more than 60 thousand banknotes issued between 1888 and 1914, is a valuable testimony of the monetary circulation of the time and unique for its dimensions and characteristics. To its credit, this collection includes banknotes of twenty-eight Porfirian issuing banks, that is, of almost all those existing at that time, including numerous pieces of 500 and 1000 pesos, denominations little used at that time for their high facial value, among which several stand out previously unknown even to prestigious scholars of the period, such as the thousand-peso bills of the banks of Coahuila, Jalisco, Queretaro and San Luis Potosi, or those of 500 pesos of the 5 banks of the State of Mexico, Morelos, Nuevo Leon, Mercantil de Monterrey and Occidental de Mexico. I reiterate to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs our gratitude for the delivery of this acquis and for the trust placed in the Bank of Mexico. Likewise, I thank the National Institute of Anthropology and History and the National Museum of History - Chapultepec Castle for their hospitality to celebrate this event and present the exhibition "Centennial Trip, from Veracruz to Chapultepec" that accompanies it and, of course, for their support for the museographic development of it. I also congratulate the public servants of the General Directorates of Issuance of the Bank of Mexico and the General Directorate of the Historical and Diplomatic Heritage of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for the commitment and interest placed in the long process of registration, counting, photography and cataloguing of the collection, as well as the Legal Directorates of both 6 institutions in the preparation of the contract that makes possible the conclusion of this loan and the presentation of the exhibition that accompanies it. To conclude I want to invite you and from here to all Mexicans and many tourists who tour the Museum to visit the exhibition, which will be presented in this beautiful and historic enclosure for three months, as well as to know in its entirety the Porfirian banknotes that we receive today through the "Online Catalog of the Numismatic Collection of the Bank of Mexico" that you can find on our website. Thanks a lot. 7
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante el acto protocolario de la entrega recepcin de la coleccin de billetes porfirianos de la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores al Banco de Mxico. 1 de junio de 2015  Doctor Jos Antonio Meade Kuribrea, Secretario de Relaciones Exteriores  Doctora Mara Teresa Franco Gonzlez Salas, Directora General del Instituto Nacional de Antropologa e Historia  Funcionarios de la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores y compaeros funcionarios del Banco de Mxico  Seoras y seores: Una de las primeras llamadas que recib del seor canciller Meade  ya en sus funciones al frente de la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores- me llen de entusiasmo e ilusin. En esa ocasin, el canciller me habl de la existencia de un gran acervo de ms de 60 mil billetes porfirianos y de su idea de que fuese el Banco de Mxico quien custodiase ese tesoro 1 histrico. El da de hoy esta brillante idea del doctor Meade se ha hecho realidad. Muchas gracias, canciller. Hoy, en efecto, concluye un prolongado periplo para ms de 60 mil billetes porfirianos y es para el Banco de Mxico motivo de orgullo y agradecimiento que este regreso a casa, de unas piezas de incalculable valor numismtico e histrico, culmine precisamente en la Coleccin Numismtica de nuestro Instituto Central. Como tal vez algunos de ustedes ya saben, estas valiosas piezas numismticas salieron de Mxico, especficamente de la Aduana del puerto de Veracruz, en abril de 1914 y permanecieron por dcadas resguardadas en el Departamento del Tesoro de los Estados Unidos. Hoy este tesoro histrico no slo est de nuevo en Mxico, sino que gracias a la responsabilidad y generosidad de la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores que opt por entregarlo en comodato 2 al Banco de Mxico formarn parte del acervo numismtico de nuestro Instituto Central. Tal decisin representa para nosotros un honor y un reconocimiento al quehacer numismtico desarrollado por el Banco Central, y al mismo tiempo, significa un compromiso de resguardar, preservar y divulgar esta coleccin de billetes. Todos ustedes pueden estar absolutamente seguros que pondremos nuestro conocimiento, experiencia y mejor empeo en cumplir meritoriamente con la encomienda. Viaje centenario, de Veracruz a Chapultepec, nombre que hemos dado a la exposicin que acompaa este evento, resume la historia de la coleccin de billetes porfirianos que la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores nos entrega formalmente el da de hoy. Hagamos un poco de historia: el 21 de abril de 1914 la Marina de los Estados Unidos de Amrica invadi el puerto de Veracruz, no sin antes enfrentar la heroica resistencia de 3 pobladores y cadetes de la Escuela Naval, gesta que conmemoramos el ao pasado con la acuacin y puesta en circulacin de una moneda de 20 pesos. Uno de los principales objetivos de las fuerzas invasoras fue tomar la Aduana del puerto supuestamente para evitar la entrada de armamento destinado al rgimen ilegtimo de Victoriano Huerta. Con ello al infamante agravio que fue el hecho de la invasin, las tropas estadounidenses aadieron la flagrante ilegalidad de administrar y operar la Aduana, cobrando derechos sobre las importaciones y exportaciones que se realizaron durante los meses que dur la ocupacin. Peor an, las fuerzas invasoras se llevaron consigo, al abandonar el puerto en noviembre de ese ao, una importante cantidad del efectivo producto de los cobros en la Aduana, que ms tarde depositaron en el Departamento del Tesoro de los Estados Unidos. 4 Aunque no me corresponde hablar sobre las gestiones realizadas por la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores para recuperar este tesoro histrico y numismtico, debemos reconocer el buen resultado obtenido y el significado del mismo, ya que el acervo de ms de 60 mil billetes emitidos entre 1888 y 1914, es un valioso testimonio de la circulacin monetaria de la poca y nico por sus dimensiones y caractersticas. En su haber, esta coleccin incluye billetes de veintiocho bancos emisores porfirianos, es decir, de casi todos los existentes en esa poca, entre ellos numerosas piezas de 500 y 1000 pesos, denominaciones poco utilizadas en aquel tiempo por su alto valor facial, entre las que destacan varias antes desconocidas incluso para prestigiados estudiosos del periodo, como son los billetes de mil pesos de los bancos de Coahuila, Jalisco, Quertaro y San Luis Potos, o los de 500 pesos de los 5 bancos del Estado de Mxico, Morelos, Nuevo Len, Mercantil de Monterrey y Occidental de Mxico. Reitero a la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores nuestro agradecimiento por la entrega de este acervo y por la confianza depositada en el Banco de Mxico. Asimismo, agradezco al Instituto Nacional de Antropologa e Historia y al Museo Nacional de Historia  Castillo de Chapultepec su hospitalidad para celebrar este acto y presentar la muestra Viaje centenario, de Veracruz a Chapultepec que lo acompaa y, desde luego, por su apoyo para el desarrollo museogrfico de la misma. Tambin felicito a los servidores pblicos de las direcciones generales de Emisin del Banco de Mxico y de la Direccin General del Acervo Histrico y Diplomtico de la Secretara de Relaciones Exteriores por el empeo e inters puestos en el largo proceso de registro, recuento, fotografa y catalogacin del acervo, as como a las Direcciones Jurdicas de ambas 6 instituciones en la elaboracin del contrato que hace posible la celebracin de este comodato y la presentacin de la exposicin que le acompaa. Para concluir quiero invitarlos y desde aqu a todos los mexicanos y muchos turistas que recorren el Museo a visitar la muestra, que se presentar en este hermoso e histrico recinto durante tres meses, as como a conocer en su totalidad los billetes porfirianos que hoy recibimos a travs del Catlogo en lnea de la Coleccin Numismtica del Banco de Mxico que pueden encontrar en nuestra pgina de Internet. Muchas gracias. 7

Title: Putting into circulation the ten-peso coin commemorating the Battle of Puebla
text: Dr. Rafael Moreno Valle Rosas, Constitutional Governor of the State of Puebla; Major General, Diploma of the General Staff, Guillermo Galvan Galvan, Secretary of National Defense; Lic. Obdulio avila, Undersecretary of Government of the Ministry of the Interior, representative of the President of the Republic, Felipe Calderon; Distinguished Members of the Presidium; Senators and Deputies; Representatives of the Government of the State of Puebla; Ladies and gentlemen: It is an honor to participate, with the representation of the Bank of Mexico, in the national circulation of the ten-peso coin commemorating the Battle of Puebla, which takes place within the framework of the 150th anniversary of the Death of General Ignacio Zaragoza. The minting of the commemorative coin is due, in the first place, to the commitment of the Government and the representatives of the state of Puebla in the Federal Congress, who promoted a Special Commission in Charge of the Celebrations of the 150th Anniversary of the Battle of Puebla of May 5, 1862. The initiative to mint the coin was presented in the Senate of the Republic by members of the aforementioned commission, received majority support and the decree, with the characteristics of the coin, was published on May 4, 2012. Once the decree was published, the Bank of Mexico and the Mint made an exceptional effort to manufacture it as quickly as possible. The minting of a coin involves a series of complex and extensive processes that include the acquisition of materials, the design, the elaboration of the stamp and the manufacture itself. However, thanks to the enthusiasm and professionalism of everyone involved, from artists and designers to technicians and operators, it was possible to mint this splendid piece in a couple of months. In addition to its function as a means of payment, the currency, due to its wide circulation, has traditionally been an ideal vehicle for a country to evoke its 1 most relevant historical episodes, celebrate its cultural heritage and commemorate the legacy of its most significant heroes and personalities. Since ancient times, the coin displayed founding myths, revived paradigmatic figures or evoked famous events for a social conglomerate. It is not surprising that, today, numismatics, with the symbols, characters and events it commemorates, is a reflection of the collective memory and fundamental values of a nation. In Mexico we have a rich numismatic tradition and the collection of Mexican currency, in addition to an artisanal treasure, constitutes a panoramic record of historical events. Although in pre-Hispanic societies there were several means of payment, the history of metallic currency in Mexico begins with the Conquest. Due to the commercial exchange needs of the prosperous Spanish empire and its colonies, since 1535 the Mexican Mint was founded, the first in the American continent. Thanks to the mining wealth of the country, throughout the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, it was possible to mint millions and millions of coins with high precious metal content. In fact, since in other countries there was a lack of both mints and precious metal, the coin manufactured in Mexico went around the world, informally became an international currency and some pieces, highlighted with local characters, were used as a means of exchange in places as unsuspected as China, the Philippines, Japan, India or African territories. From independence, and throughout much of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, the issuance of currency suffered successive alterations due to political instability and economic turbulence that affected the country. In addition, the characteristics and iconography were closely linked to the changing hegemonies of the time. Thus, the coins of the Iturbide Empire, those of the First Republic, those of the Second Empire and those of the Porfirista period have very different features from each other. Even more picturesque are the coins that, after the outbreak of the Revolution, were issued by the different sides. The truth is that, until the foundation of the Bank of Mexico in 1925, it is possible to find again a regularization in the technical characteristics of the issuance of currency and, above all, a more consistent numismatic iconography that seeks to reflect a plural and panoramic vision of the various stages of Mexican history. 2 With this purpose of vindicating the broader vision of Mexican history and culture, coins and banknotes of current use have been designed, which include from pre-Hispanic motifs to figures of contemporary art. Likewise, when there is an ephemeris of great relevance, commemorative coins or banknotes with legal tender have been issued. This means that these coins can be used for any transaction and coexist with current currencies of the same denomination, although fewer copies are issued and tend to be collected. A commemorative coin has a challenge because, in addition to its utilitarian function, it must be deeply representative of the figure or historical fact evoked and establish an emotional link with the user, which compels him to stay with it. Although the battle of Puebla, and the role of its leader and strategist, General Zaragoza, had already been vindicated in the Mexican banknote of current course, it was very opportune to evoke the ephemeris, both of the battle of Puebla and of the premature death of General Zaragoza, with a commemorative coin. The fight against the French army, on May 5, 1862 in the fortifications of the hills of Loreto and Guadalupe, represents the most significant victory of the Mexican armies in defense of sovereignty. This victory constituted a brake on the expansionism of foreign powers in Mexico and became an emblematic episode of the integrity and dignity of a nation in defense of its integrity. This episode has been consolidated in the collective memory as a benchmark of national pride and Mexican identity, inside and outside our territory. Thus, May 5 usually becomes a feast of communion and empathy for Mexicans living in other countries, particularly in the United States of America. Therefore, for me it is a double satisfaction to participate in these celebrations. On the one hand, as a Poblano, I am very proud to evoke, with the presence of the General Secretary of Defense, the Governor and many countrymen, this moment and this figure so important in national and regional history; on the other hand, as a member of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, I am honored to fulfill our institutional duty and to put into circulation, on such a significant date, this beautiful numismatic specimen. As you will see, the commemorative coin is bimetallic and consists of two alloys: one of silver alpaca, in the center, and another of aluminum bronze, which is the 3 perimeter ring. As usual, on the obverse it bears the national coat of arms, with the legend "United Mexican States" around it. On the reverse we see in the foreground the portrait of General Ignacio Zaragoza; and behind, a scene of the battle, with the forts of Loreto and Guadalupe in the background. The effigies we commemorate on coins are exemplary symbols, but they also tend to become close, warm, and familiar figures. With the circulation of the ten-peso coin commemorating the Battle of Puebla, all Mexicans will be able to treasure, not only a means of payment or a particularly beautiful numismatic piece, but one of the closest and most endearing symbols of our nationality. Thank you very much and let me begin to share it with you. 4
text_original: Dr. Rafael Moreno Valle Rosas, Gobernador Constitucional del Estado de Puebla; General de Divisin, Diplomado del Estado Mayor, Guillermo Galvn Galvn, Secretario de la Defensa Nacional; Lic. Obdulio vila, Subsecretario de Gobierno de la Secretara de Gobernacin, representante del Presidente de la Repblica, Felipe Caldern; Distinguidos Miembros del Presdium; Senadores y Diputados; Representantes del Gobierno del Estado de Puebla; Seoras y Seores: Es un honor participar, con la representacin del Banco de Mxico, en la puesta en circulacin a nivel nacional de la moneda de diez pesos conmemorativa de la Batalla de Puebla, que se realiza en el marco del 150 aniversario Luctuoso del General Ignacio Zaragoza. La acuacin de la moneda conmemorativa se debe, en primer trmino, al empeo del Gobierno y los representantes del estado de Puebla en el Congreso Federal, quienes impulsaron una Comisin Especial Encargada de los Festejos del 150 Aniversario de la Batalla de Puebla del 5 de Mayo de 1862. Una vez publicado el decreto, el Banco de Mxico y la Casa de Moneda hicieron un esfuerzo excepcional para fabricarla con la mayor celeridad. La acuacin de una moneda implica una serie de procesos complejos y dilatados que incluyen la adquisicin de materiales, el diseo, la elaboracin del cuo y la propia fabricacin. Sin embargo, gracias al entusiasmo y profesionalismo de todos los involucrados, desde los artistas y diseadores hasta los tcnicos y operadores, fue posible acuar en un par meses esta esplndida pieza. Adems de su funcin como medio de pago, la moneda, por su amplia circulacin, tradicionalmente ha sido un vehculo idneo para que un pas evoque sus 1 episodios histricos ms relevantes, celebre su patrimonio cultural y conmemore el legado de sus prceres y personalidades ms significativas. Desde la antigedad, la moneda desplegaba mitos fundadores, reviva figuras paradigmticas o evocaba sucesos clebres para un conglomerado social. No es extrao que, hoy, la numismtica, con los smbolos, personajes y acontecimientos que conmemora, sea un reflejo de la memoria colectiva y los valores fundamentales de una nacin. En Mxico tenemos una rica tradicin numismtica y el acervo de la moneda mexicana, adems de un tesoro artesanal, constituye un registro panormico del acontecer histrico. Aunque en las sociedades prehispnicas existan varios medios de pago, la historia de la moneda metlica en Mxico inicia con la Conquista. Debido a las necesidades de intercambio comercial del prspero imperio espaol y sus colonias, desde 1535 se fund la Casa de Moneda de Mxico, la primera del continente Americano. Gracias a la riqueza minera del pas, a lo largo del siglo XVI y XVII, fue posible acuar millones y millones de monedas con alto contenido en metal precioso. A partir de la Independencia, y a lo largo de buena parte del siglo XIX y principios del siglo XX, la emisin de moneda sufri sucesivas alteraciones debido a la inestabilidad poltica y turbulencias econmicas que afectaron al pas. Adems, las caractersticas e iconografa se encontraban muy ligadas a las cambiantes hegemonas de la poca. As, las monedas del Imperio de Iturbide, las de la Primera Repblica, las del Segundo Imperio y las de la etapa porfirista tienen rasgos muy distintos entre s. Todava ms pintorescas resultan las monedas que, tras el estallido de la Revolucin, emitieron los distintos bandos. Lo cierto es que, hasta la fundacin del Banco de Mxico en 1925, es posible encontrar nuevamente una regularizacin en las caractersticas tcnicas de la emisin de moneda y, sobre todo, una iconografa numismtica ms consistente que busca reflejar una visin plural y panormica de las diversas etapas de la historia mexicana. 2 Con ese propsito de reivindicar la visin ms amplia de la historia y la cultura mexicana se han diseado las monedas y billetes de uso corriente, las cuales incluyen desde motivos prehispnicos hasta figuras del arte contemporneo. Igualmente, cuando existe una efemride de gran relevancia, se han emitido monedas o billetes conmemorativos con curso legal. Esto quiere decir que esas monedas pueden servir para cualquier transaccin y conviven con las monedas de curso corriente de la misma denominacin, aunque se emiten menos ejemplares y tienden a ser coleccionadas. Una moneda conmemorativa tiene un reto pues, adems de su funcin utilitaria, debe ser profundamente representativa de la figura o hecho histrico evocado y establecer un vnculo emotivo con el usuario, que lo conmine a quedarse con ella. Aunque la batalla de Puebla, y el papel de su lder y estratega, el general Zaragoza, ya haban sido reivindicados en el billete mexicano de curso corriente, resultaba muy oportuno evocar la efemride, tanto de la batalla de Puebla como de la prematura muerte del general Zaragoza, con una moneda conmemorativa. La lucha contra el ejrcito francs, el 5 de mayo de 1862 en las fortificaciones de los cerros de Loreto y Guadalupe, representa la victoria ms significativa de los ejrcitos mexicanos en defensa de la soberana. Esta victoria constituy un freno para el expansionismo de las potencias extranjeras en Mxico y se convirti en un episodio emblemtico de la entereza y dignidad de una nacin en defensa de su integridad. Este episodio se ha consolidado en la memoria colectiva como un referente del orgullo nacional y la identidad mexicana, dentro y fuera de nuestro territorio. As, el 5 de mayo suele convertirse en una fiesta de comunin y empata para los mexicanos que viven en otros pases, particularmente en Estados Unidos de Amrica. Por lo anterior, para mi es una doble satisfaccin participar en estos festejos. Como ustedes vern, la moneda conmemorativa es bimetlica y est constituida por dos aleaciones: una de alpaca plateada, al centro, y otra de bronce aluminio, que es el 3 anillo perimtrico. Como es habitual, en el anverso lleva el escudo nacional, con la leyenda Estados Unidos Mexicanos a su alrededor. En el reverso observamos en primer plano el retrato del general Ignacio Zaragoza; y detrs, una escena de la batalla, con los fuertes de Loreto y Guadalupe al fondo. Las efigies que conmemoramos en las monedas son smbolos ejemplares, pero tambin tienden a volverse figuras cercanas, clidas y familiares. Con la puesta en circulacin de la moneda de diez pesos conmemorativa de la Batalla de Puebla todos los mexicanos podremos atesorar, no slo un medio de pago o una pieza numismtica particularmente bella, sino uno de los smbolos ms prximos y entraables de nuestra nacionalidad. Muchas gracias y permtanme comenzar a compartirla con ustedes. 4

Title: Presentation of actions to boost the financial system
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of actions to boost the financial system. Mexico City, January 8, 2019 Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, Constitutional President of the United Mexican States; Dr. Carlos Urzua Macias, Secretary of Finance and Public Credit; Dr. Arturo Herrera Gutierrez, Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit; Mr. Marcos Martinez Gavica, President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen: It is an honor to participate in this forum and present some actions that have been approved by the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, which are added to the set of measures aimed at promoting the inclusion and depth of the financial sector, which are announced today. The purpose of the Bank of Mexico is to provide the country's economy with a national currency, with the priority objective of maintaining the stability of its purchasing power. In addition, it has two additional purposes: i) to promote the healthy development of the financial system, and ii) to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. These objectives are intertwined, since the issuance and circulation of fiat money fulfills its purpose when the population trusts that the issuing authority will take care of its function as a store of value and means of payment. Thus, a central bank must seek that the currency retains its purchasing power and that it functions broadly as a medium of exchange and base for all types of financial operations. 2 In a healthy financial system, intermediaries provide quality financial services, on appropriate terms and prices and in a sustainable manner. Likewise, a healthy financial system must be accessible and able to serve the entire population. Even the stability of the financial system itself must be understood as an imperative for citizens to permanently have the financial services they require. Thus, the ultimate goal of the Bank of Mexico's regulation revolves around consumers of financial services. In this strategy there are three axes of action. The first is to promote greater efficiency and competition in the provision of services, reducing the mobility costs of users, eliminating barriers to entry to new participants and forming an open architecture in information and payment networks. The second is to provide better information, since a higher quality and clarity of public information about products and 3 services offered by intermediaries allow users to compare and make better decisions. Transparency directly benefits the consumer and encourages greater competition between intermediaries. The third axis of action lies in the protection of the interests of consumers, preventing and punishing regulatory breaches and any abuse. Currently, thanks to the revolution of information technologies, as never before we have tools that allow significant progress in these three axes of action. New technologies offer a unique opportunity to address the lags in financial inclusion, foster competition and develop markets, reducing costs and saving time in ways unthinkable until recently. For example, consider the benefits that would be had if a smartphone can become a kind of bank branch. Thus, new technologies open the possibility of widely extending the benefits of the 4 banking, economic integration of vulnerable groups and greater equality of opportunities. Today I would like to refer to some measures that the Bank of Mexico has been working on and that will result in important benefits for society. The first relates to the institutional objective of promoting the smooth functioning of payment systems. It consists of developing a platform to make free electronic transfers through smartphones, that is, to be able to make mobile payments every day of the year and at any time. This has a clear favorable impact. On the one hand, the user who makes electronic payments with his phone, not only streamlines and makes his operations more secure, but also gets involved in the financial system and takes the first step to access other services. On the other hand, this type of transaction reduces the security risks of the use of cash, as well as others linked to possibilities of corruption or financing of illicit activities. 5 The new platform that we are announcing today, called CoDi or digital collection, will allow secure, expeditious and free payments in both face-to-face and remote purchases. This platform is being realized as an extension of the Interbank Electronic Payment System (SPEI) that, unlike other countries, works 24 hours a day every day of the year, makes payments immediately, is open to all customers of SPEI participants and covers high and low value payments. If we consider that in 2017 there were more than 64 million people with smartphones and only 34 million bank accounts, it is clear that the development of coDi will have a great impact on financial inclusion and the increased use of electronic payments. To develop the CoDi, with high standards of security, efficiency and speed, it requires both the payment infrastructure provided by the Bank of Mexico, as well as the close collaboration of the financial institutions participating in the SPEI, especially banking. 6 This platform will undoubtedly benefit a wide population, from young people who are natural users of these devices, to those segments that have historically been excluded from the formal financial system and, also, can be very useful in the distribution of social programs. The second measure to highlight is associated with the objective of promoting the development of the financial system and contemplates that workers can use their payroll bank accounts as a source of payment for all types of credits and with any bank, under an open architecture. Thus, the Credits Associated with Payroll can be contracted with any intermediary and not only with the one who keeps the payroll account. This measure pays, at the same time, to justice and efficiency, since, on the one hand, it makes effective the freedom of the user to choose between any bank and, on the other, increases the effectiveness of the sources of payment of credits, which reduces risks and costs in the financial system. This promotes competition and mobility of users. 7 The third measure corresponds to a series of actions to boost the financial markets of fixed income and capital. These include: (i) opening up the possibility for a greater number of financial institutions to carry out reporting operations; ii) allow the securities, subject to loan, to be shares of lower liquidity, and iii) expand the range of securities subject to reporting and lending to consider from those of BBB-quality. These measures relax criteria in order to make the fixed income and capital market deeper and more liquid, while maintaining strict control over risks at all times. Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, All the actions promoted by the Bank of Mexico, both in the monetary aspect, as well as in those of regulation of the financial system and payments, have as their central axis the citizen. Thus, we seek to promote actions that contribute to the financial system offering services on the best terms and conditions, and that empower users. The challenge is to find those strategies that give rise to the greatest benefits for society in a sustainable way over time. 8 Thus, the regulatory framework and the strategy adopted must have a twofold impact: on the one hand, on the quality of financial services by offering citizens better options for savings, investment or financing and, on the other, on making the financial system more competitive, resilient and profound and thus strengthening a fundamental lever of development. The Bank of Mexico reaffirms its readiness to, within the scope of its powers, collaborate constructively with the Federal Government in the construction of a financial system increasingly conducive to economic growth and social welfare. The actions we announce have been designed evaluating their costs and benefits, taking care of their viability and sustainability; and having as its central axis the consumer of financial services. Therefore, it is a pleasure to expose them and add them to the set of actions that will have to be presented in this forum, and that tend to create a more solid financial base for growth in the coming years. Thanks a lot 9
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la presentacin de acciones para impulsar el sistema financiero. Ciudad de Mxico, 8 de enero de 2019 Lic. Andrs Manuel Lpez Obrador, Presidente Constitucional de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos; Dr. Carlos Urza Macas, Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico; Dr. Arturo Herrera Gutirrez, Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico; Ing. Marcos Martnez Gavica, Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Seoras y seores: Es un honor participar en este foro y exponer algunas acciones que ha aprobado la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico, las cuales se suman al conjunto de medidas orientadas a impulsar la inclusin y profundidad del sector financiero, que hoy se anuncian. El Banco de Mxico tiene por finalidad proveer a la economa del pas de moneda nacional, con el objetivo prioritario de mantener la estabilidad de su poder adquisitivo. Adems, tiene dos finalidades adicionales: i) promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero, y ii) propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Estos objetivos se encuentran entrelazados, pues la emisin y circulacin de dinero fiduciario cumple con su propsito cuando la poblacin confa en que la autoridad emisora cuidar su funcin como depsito de valor y medio de pago. As, un banco central debe buscar que la moneda conserve su poder adquisitivo y que funcione ampliamente como medio de intercambio y base de todo tipo de operaciones financieras. 2 En un sistema financiero sano, los intermediarios proveen servicios financieros de calidad, en trminos y precios adecuados y de manera sostenible. Asimismo, un sistema financiero sano debe ser accesible y poder atender a toda la poblacin. Inclusive, la propia estabilidad del sistema financiero debe ser entendida como un imperativo para que la ciudadana cuente de manera permanente con los servicios financieros que requiere. As, el fin ltimo de la regulacin del Banco de Mxico gira alrededor de los consumidores de servicios financieros. En esta estrategia se tienen tres ejes de accin. El primero, es promover la mayor eficiencia y competencia en la provisin de servicios, reduciendo los costos de movilidad de los usuarios, eliminando barreras de entrada a nuevos participantes y conformando una arquitectura abierta en las redes de informacin y de pagos. El segundo, consiste en proveer mejor informacin, ya que una mayor calidad y claridad de la informacin pblica sobre los productos y 3 servicios que ofrecen los intermediarios permite que los usuarios puedan comparar y tomar mejores decisiones. La transparencia beneficia directamente al consumidor e incentiva una mayor competencia entre los intermediarios. El tercer eje de accin, radica en la proteccin de los intereses de los consumidores, previniendo y castigando los incumplimientos normativos y cualquier abuso. Actualmente, gracias a la revolucin de las tecnologas de informacin, como nunca antes contamos con herramientas que permiten avanzar significativamente en estos tres ejes de accin. Las nuevas tecnologas ofrecen una oportunidad nica para atender los rezagos en materia de inclusin financiera, fomentar la competencia y desarrollar los mercados, pues reducen costos y ahorran tiempo de manera impensable hasta hace poco. Por ejemplo, considrense los beneficios que se tendran si un telfono inteligente puede convertirse en una suerte de sucursal bancaria. As, las nuevas tecnologas abren la posibilidad de extender ampliamente los beneficios de la 4 bancarizacin, integrar econmicamente a grupos vulnerables y generar mayor igualdad de oportunidades. El da de hoy quiero referirme a algunas medidas en las que el Banco de Mxico ha venido trabajando y que redundarn en importantes beneficios para la sociedad. La primera est relacionada con el objetivo institucional de promover el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Consiste en desarrollar una plataforma para hacer transferencias electrnicas gratuitas a travs de telfonos inteligentes, es decir, poder hacer pagos mviles todos los das del ao y a cualquier hora. Esto tiene un claro impacto favorable. Por un lado, el usuario que hace pagos electrnicos con su telfono, no slo agiliza y hace ms seguras sus operaciones, sino que se involucra en el sistema financiero y da el primer paso para acceder a otros servicios. Por otro lado, esta modalidad de transaccin reduce los riesgos de seguridad del uso de efectivo, as como otros ligados a posibilidades de corrupcin o de financiamiento de actividades ilcitas. 5 La nueva plataforma que hoy anunciamos, denominada CoDi o cobro digital, permitir pagos seguros, expeditos y gratuitos tanto en compras presenciales como remotas. Esta plataforma se est concretando como una extensin del Sistema de Pagos Electrnicos Interbancarios (SPEI) que, a diferencia de otros pases, funciona las 24 horas de todos los das del ao, realiza los pagos de manera inmediata, est abierto a todos los clientes de los participantes del SPEI y abarca pagos de alto y bajo valor. Si consideramos que en 2017 existan ms de 64 millones de personas con telfonos inteligentes y slo 34 millones de cuentas bancarias, es claro que el desarrollo del CoDi tendr un gran impacto sobre la inclusin financiera y el mayor uso de pagos electrnicos.
