En la actualidad, la llamada curva de Phillips, que establece los cambios en la tasa de crecimiento de los precios o los salarios que podran ser esperados como consecuencia de reducciones en los niveles de desempleo o, ms generalmente, de una mayor utilizacin de recursos en la economa, representa una pieza fundamental en la implementacin de la poltica monetaria de numerosos bancos centrales. Sin embargo, esta relacin parece haberse debilitado en el transcurso de las ltimas dcadas como resultado de una combinacin de factores. Entre estos, se ha sealado el papel de la globalizacin, al permitir que la holgura en el mercado laboral global cobre mayor relevancia que aquella en el interno, especialmente en un contexto en el que el progreso tecnolgico facilita el traslado de la produccin de bienes y servicios a lugares con amplios recursos 7 Ver International Monetary Fund (2015): Monetary Policy and Financial Stability, IMF Policy Paper, September; y Haldane, Andrew, David Aikman, Sujit Kapadia y Marc Hinterschweiger (2017): Rethinking Financial Stability, documento presentado en la conferencia Rethinking Macroeconomic Policy del Peterson Institute for International Economics, October. 9 disponibles y a un costo inferior.8 Esto se refleja en la reducida capacidad de productores y trabajadores (o sindicatos) para incrementar precios y salarios, respectivamente, ante la latente competencia proveniente del exterior. Tambin se ha destacado el efecto de la exitosa implementacin de estrategias antiinflacionarias en numerosas economas, que ha diluido el impacto sobre los precios de episodios de menor holgura en la economa. Adems, algunos autores han subrayado que la reactivacin en el empleo que se ha observado en los ltimos aos parece haberse concentrado en sectores de ms baja remuneracin, conteniendo as el incremento promedio en los salarios, en tanto que otros no descartan la posibilidad de reducciones en la tasa natural de desempleo como resultado, por ejemplo, de reformas en el mercado laboral o de cambios demogrficos.9 Como es obvio, las dificultades para precisar los determinantes de la inflacin acentan los mrgenes de error en la implementacin de la poltica monetaria e incrementan la posibilidad de ajustes sorpresivos. Asimismo, el aparente debilitamiento de la relacin entre inflacin y desempleo de la curva de Phillips ha dado lugar a una discusin respecto de los mritos de mantener tasas de inters muy bajas, ante circunstancias en las que la holgura en el mercado laboral parece tener poco impacto sobre la inflacin, y el mantenimiento de polticas monetarias muy relajadas puede dar lugar a riesgos para la 8 Sin embargo, se ha sealado que el sustento emprico para esta hiptesis parece ser dbil en el caso de Estados Unidos y otras economas avanzadas. Ver Yellen, Janet (2017): Inflation, Uncertainty, and Monetary Policy, Remarks at the 59th Annual Meeting of the National Association for Business Economics, September. 9 Ver, por ejemplo, Leduc, Sylvain y Daniel Wilson (2017): Has the Wage Phillips Curve Gone Dormant?, Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco Economic Letter No. 2017-30, October; y Aaronson, Daniel, Luojia Hu Arian Seifoddini y Daniel Sullivan (2015): Changing Labor Force Composition and the Natural Rate of Unemployment, Chicago Fed Letter No. 338. 10 estabilidad financiera.10 La situacin se complica todava ms por la posibilidad de que la tasa neutral de inters (es decir, aquella que permite que la economa opere a plena capacidad sin presiones inflacionarias) en las economas avanzadas haya disminuido considerablemente en los ltimos aos, elevando an ms la complejidad tcnica inherente a la estimacin de esta variable. En quinto lugar, el entorno de tasas de inflacin persistentemente bajas, particularmente en las economas avanzadas, ha propiciado el surgimiento de dudas sobre los mritos de la independencia de los bancos centrales en estos pases. Esto, principalmente con el argumento de que la motivacin fundamental para dotar a las instituciones responsables de la poltica monetaria de independencia, a saber, la eliminacin de los incentivos para estimular el empleo y la actividad econmica a costa de la estabilidad de precios, podra haber perdido validez bajo las circunstancias actuales.11 La independencia de los bancos centrales tambin ha sido cuestionada ante la desfavorable evolucin de la actividad econmica en las economas avanzadas despus de la crisis financiera global, as como por el planteamiento de que, bajo los esquemas de relajamiento cuantitativo, la distincin entre la poltica monetaria y la fiscal se ha vuelto ms tenue, sin que la primera cuente con la legitimidad derivada de la aprobacin por parte de rganos sujetos a un proceso electoral. 10 Ver Borio, Claudio (2017): Through the Looking Glass, OMFIF City Lecture, September. 11 Ver Eggertsson, Gauti (2013): Fiscal Multipliers and Policy Coordination, en Cspedes, Luis y Jordi Gal (eds.), Fiscal Policy and Macroeconomic Performance, pp. 175-234. 11 Al respecto, diversos autores han sealado lo siguiente:12 a) las decisiones de poltica monetaria deben ser tomadas de manera oportuna en un ambiente de condiciones, tanto econmicas como financieras, continua y rpidamente cambiantes. Someter la poltica monetaria a un proceso de escrutinio y discusin poltica como el que tpicamente acompaa a otras decisiones de poltica econmica le restara efectividad; b) un banco central independiente cuenta con la visin de largo plazo y ajena al ciclo poltico, indispensable a la luz de los rezagos con los que la poltica monetaria opera en la economa; c) el logro de la credibilidad institucional del banco central necesaria para una implementacin eficiente de la poltica monetaria es ms difcil en ausencia de dicha independencia; d) es precisamente la independencia de los bancos centrales lo que ha permitido poner en marcha las medidas requeridas para atenuar los costos de la crisis financiera global; e) la experiencia de aos recientes demuestra que la coordinacin de las polticas fiscal y monetaria, cuando es necesaria y justificada, no se ve impedida por el hecho de que el banco central opere de manera independiente. En suma, a pesar de la mejora reciente de la economa mundial y un panorama en general ms alentador, los retos a los que hace frente la poltica monetaria en las economas avanzadas dan lugar a interrogantes sobre la capacidad de sus bancos centrales para sortear choques de distinta naturaleza, as como sobre la posibilidad de que sus mismas respuestas de poltica monetaria se conviertan en un factor de desestabilizacin a nivel global. No obstante, considero que es posible identificar algunas acciones concretas que podran 12 Ver, por ejemplo, Bernanke, Ben (2017): Monetary Policy in a New Era, documento presentado en la conferencia Rethinking Macroeconomic Policy del Peterson Institute for International Economics, October; y Walsh, Carl (2011): Central Bank Independence Revisited, Economic Papers 30(1):18-22, March. 12 adoptarse en estos pases con miras a favorecer un comportamiento ms ordenado tanto de sus economas, como de la mundial:  La implementacin de estrategias de comunicacin claras y efectivas sobre las acciones de poltica monetaria. Como se ha sealado, una de las principales fuentes de ansiedad en los mercados se deriva de las potenciales implicaciones del proceso de ajuste de tasas de inters y la salida de las medidas de estmulo cuantitativo puestas en marcha por los principales bancos centrales de este grupo. En la medida en que los cambios en sus respectivas posturas sean adecuadamente comunicados al pblico, el riesgo de episodios de alta volatilidad y ajuste desordenado en los mercados se vera atenuado.  La adopcin de enfoques de poltica ms balanceados. Las complejidades que caracterizan el entorno que actualmente enfrentamos obedecen en buena medida a una dependencia excesiva en la poltica monetaria para procurar la recuperacin de la actividad econmica y combatir las presiones deflacionarias. De hecho, de haberse recurrido a una distribucin ms equilibrada de la carga del ajuste entre los distintos instrumentos de poltica, tanto la disminucin requerida de las tasas de inters como los efectos no deseados sobre la economa mundial habran sido menores. Es cierto que muchas economas avanzadas no cuentan con espacio fiscal. Sin embargo, lo anterior no es aplicable a todas ellas, particularmente bajo las condiciones actuales de bajas tasas de inters.13 El margen de accin es 13 Ver Auerbach, Alan y Yuriy Gorodnichenko (2017): Fiscal Stimulus and Fiscal Sustainability, NBER Working Paper No. 23789, September. 13 mucho ms alto en el mbito del cambio estructural, ya que los esfuerzos al respecto en este grupo de pases dejan mucho que desear.  Una mayor conciencia de las repercusiones, a nivel global, de sus acciones de poltica. Lo anterior, no solo en virtud de los ya mencionados efectos indirectos que estas pueden generar, particularmente en las economas emergentes y en desarrollo, sino tambin en el propio inters de las economas avanzadas, tomando en consideracin la posibilidad de efectos bmeran. Lo anterior implica, naturalmente, impulsar mayores esfuerzos de investigacin que permitan obtener conclusiones robustas y de aplicabilidad directa para la poltica econmica. Para concluir, solo quisiera sealar que los retos que estn enfrentando los bancos centrales de los pases avanzados pueden dejar lecciones de gran relevancia para las economas emergentes y en desarrollo. Si bien la problemtica que enfrentan las autoridades monetarias de estos dos grupos de pases difiere en mltiples esferas, en otras su naturaleza es similar. Tal es el caso, por ejemplo, de las dudas existentes sobre las polticas idneas para preservar la estabilidad financiera, o la ms tenue relacin entre inflacin y desempleo, que parece tambin estar presente en algunas economas emergentes. Considero que es necesario, adems, tomar nota de los desafos que pueden surgir para la independencia de los bancos centrales en nuestros pases, ya sea por cuestionamientos sobre el manejo de la poltica monetaria como en las economas avanzadas o simplemente como un reflejo de presiones de esta ndole en esas naciones. Adicionalmente, las economas emergentes y en desarrollo deben participar en los esfuerzos por contar con 14 un fundamento analtico ms slido sobre las repercusiones de medidas de poltica econmica en las economas avanzadas sobre el resto del mundo. Y lo que resulta aun ms urgente. Ante los desafos sealados y otros bien conocidos factores de riesgo, tanto de naturaleza econmica como poltica, para el desempeo econmico mundial a corto y largo plazo, es indispensable que las economas emergentes y en desarrollo aprovechen el espacio brindado por las circunstancias actuales en la economa mundial para fortalecer sus fundamentos econmicos. Indudablemente, los esfuerzos realizados en aos recientes han mejorado las bases de crecimiento y la capacidad de muchas de estas economas para hacer frente a choques. Sin embargo, tambin es cierto que la tarea est incompleta, y que todava son demasiados los casos en los que se observan desequilibrios macroeconmicos importantes y un rezago considerable en materia de ajuste estructural. 15

Title: 81st National Banking Convention
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the Eighty-First National Banking Convention. Acapulco, Guerrero, March 8, 2018 Mr. President of the United Mexican States, Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto; Constitutional Governor of the State of Guerrero, Mr. Hector Astudillo Flores; Deputy Edgar Romo Garcia, President of the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Deputies; Senator Ernesto Cordero Arroyo, President of the Board of Directors of the Senate of the Republic; Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Jose Antonio Gonzalez Anaya; President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, engineer Marcos Martinez Gavica; Legislators, Secretaries, Undersecretaries, Local Authorities, Representatives of Business Organizations and distinguished members of the Presidium; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 It is a pleasure to participate in this Eighty-First National Banking Convention. This meeting takes place in an environment of profound changes and questions around the world economy and important challenges for The Mexican economy. In my speech I will address: (i) first, the logic and historical support that support the mandate and institutional design of the Bank of Mexico; ii) then, how the actions of the monetary authority constitute a factor of certainty in the face of the scenarios we face, and iii) finally, I will highlight some of the challenges and opportunities of the financial sector. One of the main purposes of central banks is to provide national currency to a country or region. This power, that of issuing and placing banknotes and coins, must be used with enormous responsibility and prudence. This has not always been the case, in several countries, including ours, it was intended, without success, to stimulate economic activity through the abuse of the issuance of primary money. This led to rising inflation, economic and financial instability and even crises of great magnitude. Inflation is one of the most harmful phenomena for people's well-being and economic growth. On the one hand, it redistributes income and purchasing power regressively, eroding wages and affecting lower-income families to a greater extent. On the other hand, it adversely affects the allocation of resources in the economy, and the financing of all kinds of productive projects, especially hindering the execution of investments with high social returns, to the clear detriment of growth in the economy. The traumatic inflationary experience of many nations, and the evidence of the limits of monetary policy, gave rise to a consensus regarding the 2 It is advisable for central banks, as State institutions, to concentrate permanently on maintaining low inflation, fostering an environment of stability, indispensable for economic growth. In this sense, stability can be conceptualized as a public good, which must be provided by the State. Thus, since the last decades of the last century, many countries have granted autonomy to their central banks, guaranteeing them a healthy independence from the fiscal needs of governments and the political cycle. With the autonomy of the central bank, the objective of reducing inflation is based on a clear and precise institutional mandate, rather than on the eventual coincidence between the monetary and fiscal authorities in turn. The decision to grant autonomy to the Bank of Mexico does not only stem from international experience. Our country has also experienced at various stages, and with terrible consequences, the scourge of inflation. In particular, in the seventies and eighties of the last century excessively expansionary public spending policies were applied and the Central Bank was obliged to extend credit to finance the consequent fiscal deficits. This led to acute, prolonged, and profoundly harmful inflations to society. After these experiences, in 1993 the reform of Article 28 of the Constitution was proposed, which granted the Bank of Mexico autonomy in its administration and functions, assigning it the priority objective of maintaining the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency and indicating, explicitly, that no authority can order it to grant financing. 3 Let me now turn to the fulfillment of the functions of the Bank of Mexico in an environment, external and internal, complex and uncertain, such as the current one. To fulfill its mandate, which is price stability, the Bank of Mexico has adopted, for the conduct of its monetary policy, an inflation targeting scheme. In our case, this is based on a specific target for general inflation of 3 percent, with a framework of transparency and a communication strategy that gives certainty and coordinates the expectations of economic agents. When the public is confident that the central bank will react to shocks that could steadily divert inflation from its target, its expectations tend to be aligned with that target. To strengthen this communication channel, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico has decided to make public, quarterly, the inflation forecasts for the following 8 quarters, these were published for the first time last week in the last Quarterly Report. In this way, the Bank of Mexico will evaluate, among other factors, whether the possible deviations of inflation from its forecasts, in the horizon in which monetary policy operates, give rise to any adjustment in the target interest rate. It should be noted that the efforts of the Bank of Mexico to achieve low and stable inflation have led to a lower persistence of inflation, an anchoring of medium- and long-term expectations at levels close to the target, and a lower transfer to inflation of the change in relative prices, especially exchange rate fluctuations. Thus, with its actions, the Bank of Mexico has sought to prevent the movements of the real exchange rate, which are natural adjustments in the face of different shocks, from giving rise to second-hand effects. 4 order in price formation or affect medium- and long-term inflation expectations. Undoubtedly, having a flexible exchange rate and a monetary policy that is conducted with an inflation targeting scheme has contributed to a better functioning of the price formation process in the economy. This entails important benefits for society, as it has allowed to face various shocks with less impact on economic activity. In recent years, Mexico, like other emerging economies, has faced a complex landscape, due to the confluence of various shocks and sources of uncertainty. The first concerns lower commodity prices that have prevailed for several years now, and which have implied a significant deterioration in the terms of trade in several emerging economies, lower tax revenues and even reductions in cyclical output and potential. In the case of Mexico, both the drop in oil prices and the contraction of its production platform significantly reduced oil revenues. The second factor corresponds to the increase in external interest rates, associated with the process of normalization of monetary policies in the main advanced economies, especially in the United States, which constitutes a risk for international financial markets, and could lead to adjustments in investment portfolios with positions in emerging economies. This factor has become more relevant, considering the cyclical position of the US economy and the effects of the recently approved fiscal stimulus. 5 The third factor is the growing risk of protectionist measures and the revision that some advanced economies have fostered with respect to regional and global integration models. Some examples of this are the case of Brexit and the renegotiation of the North American Free Trade Agreement. The latter will define the framework for trade and investment in the region. Therefore, throughout the negotiation, the changing perceptions about its result have generated uncertainty and volatility in our financial markets, especially the exchange rate. The effects of this complex external environment, and other internal shocks, significantly affected inflation in Mexico. At the beginning of 2017, this was pressured, both by a sharp depreciation of the peso, and by increases in the prices of several energy companies in the domestic market. Additionally, at the end of 2017 there were additional unforeseen shocks, such as the increase in the prices of natural gas and some vegetables due to transitory factors. All of the above led to a rebound in inflation, which reached 6.77% at the end of 2017 and the core 4.87%. In February of this year, inflation decreased to 5.34%, the result of a significant reduction in non-core inflation, and a smaller reduction in core inflation, which reached 4.27%. It should be noted that in recent years the Mexican economy has been going through an atypical economic cycle, both due to unprecedented external conditions and the type of shocks that have afflicted it. This has complicated the assessment of the slack conditions of the economy, and its role in price formation, which has been narrowing and could affect the assimilation of such shocks. 6 Given the complexity of this environment, and in order to avoid second-order effects on price formation and reinforce the downward trend in inflation, the Governing Board restricted the monetary policy stance, reaching the target interest rate of 7.5% in February of this year. Taking into account the current behavior of inflation, the evolution of its determinants, the current monetary policy stance and the time horizon in which it has an effect, it is expected that, in the absence of new shocks and unanticipated pressures, the downward inflection of general inflation will be consolidated, approaching throughout the year towards the 3% target, and reaching it in the first quarter of 2019. The Bank of Mexico will be attentive to all the determinants of inflation and its balance of risks, in order to maintain the convergence of inflation to its target. Finally, let me make a few thoughts related to the financial system. Experience shows that, in order to achieve sustained economic growth, it is essential to have a well-capitalized financial system with an adequate regulatory framework, which provides the right incentives for financial institutions to safely and efficiently mediate public savings in profitable projects with social impact. The Bank of Mexico seeks that the financial system offers services and development opportunities for all citizens in a sustained manner. To do this, it works on two main aspects. 7 The first concerns its powers as regulator and supervisor to promote the stability of the system and mitigate its risks. In this regard, it highlights that the financing of commercial banks to the private sector has been recovering steadily. This process of greater leverage, both of households and companies, has occurred on the basis of a healthy financial system. This, in part, is due to our country's timely adoption of the best international standards of regulation and supervision, which seek to strengthen the resilience of the system and align incentives between intermediaries and users of the financial system. With this, the Mexican financial sector is in a solid situation, capable of resisting various risks. The second aspect of responsibility of the Bank of Mexico with respect to the financial system is aimed at promoting greater coverage of financial services, prioritizing security and the protection of consumer interests. To this end, efforts will be redoubled to achieve greater efficiency in financial intermediation, strengthen competition, and that this is reflected in benefits for all users. As part of these efforts, the Governing Board approved a few days ago the "Policies for the Public Consultation of the General Provisions issued by the Bank of Mexico." With this, international standards were adopted in regulatory improvement, with open and transparent processes, which will allow for more effective regulation. On the other hand, as never before, we have new technological tools that allow us to reduce coverage costs, provide access to financial services to various sectors of the population and address the lags in terms of financial inclusion. 8 In order to fully exploit the potential of this sector, called Fintech, the Executive Branch presented a Bill to Regulate Financial Technology Institutions, which was approved by the Congress of the Union on March 1 of this year. With this new legal framework, order and transparency are provided in a sector of ascending importance and a powerful instrument is generated to take advantage of new financial technologies for the benefit of users. Ladies and gentlemen: The strength of Mexico's macroeconomic fundamentals has allowed that, despite the severity of the shocks that have been faced in recent years, the economy has maintained an environment of stability with growth. Monetary, fiscal, exchange rate and financial system soundness converge in this strategy. An environment of stability is indispensable for growth and development, and should be understood as a permanent obligation of the State. With regard to monetary policy, the Constitution provides for the State to have a central bank, autonomous in the exercise of its functions and in its administration, with the priority objective of ensuring the purchasing power of the national currency. The Bank of Mexico maintains this clear and precise mandate as the beacon and guide of all its activities. Thanks a lot 9
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la Octogsima Primera Convencin Nacional Bancaria. Acapulco, Guerrero, 8 de marzo de 2018 Seor Presidente de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto; Gobernador Constitucional del Estado de Guerrero, licenciado Hctor Astudillo Flores; Diputado Edgar Romo Garca, Presidente de la Mesa Directiva de la Cmara de Diputados; Senador Ernesto Cordero Arroyo, Presidente de la Mesa Directiva del Senado de la Repblica; Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Jos Antonio Gonzlez Anaya; Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, ingeniero Marcos Martnez Gavica; Legisladores, Secretarios, Subsecretarios, Autoridades Locales, Representantes de Organismos Empresariales y distinguidos miembros del Presdium; Seoras y seores: 1 Es un gusto participar en esta Octogsima Primera Convencin Nacional Bancaria. Este encuentro se realiza en un ambiente de profundos cambios e interrogantes en torno a la economa mundial y de importantes desafos para la mexicana. En mi intervencin abordar: i) primero, la lgica y el sustento histrico que soportan el mandato y el diseo institucional del Banco de Mxico; ii) despus, cmo las acciones de la autoridad monetaria constituyen un factor de certidumbre ante los escenarios que enfrentamos, y iii) finalmente, destacar algunos de los retos y oportunidades del sector financiero. Una de las principales finalidades de los bancos centrales, es proveer de moneda nacional a un pas o regin. Esta facultad, la de emitir y colocar billetes y monedas, debe usarse con una enorme responsabilidad y prudencia. Esto no siempre ha sido as, en diversos pases, incluido el nuestro, se pretendi, sin xito, estimular la actividad econmica mediante el abuso de la emisin de dinero primario. Esto provoc inflacin creciente, inestabilidad econmica y financiera e, incluso, crisis de gran magnitud. La inflacin es uno de los fenmenos ms lesivos para el bienestar de las personas y el crecimiento econmico. Por un lado, redistribuye el ingreso y el poder adquisitivo de manera regresiva, erosionando los salarios y afectando en mayor medida a las familias de menores ingresos. Por otro, afecta adversamente la asignacin de recursos en la economa, y el financiamiento de todo tipo de proyectos productivos, obstaculizando especialmente la ejecucin de inversiones con alto rendimiento social, en claro detrimento del crecimiento en la economa. La traumtica experiencia inflacionaria de muchas naciones, y la evidencia de los lmites de la poltica monetaria, dio lugar a un consenso respecto a la 2 conveniencia de que los bancos centrales, como instituciones del Estado, se concentren permanentemente en mantener una inflacin baja, propiciando un entorno de estabilidad, indispensable para el crecimiento econmico. En este sentido, la estabilidad puede conceptualizarse como un bien pblico, que debe ser provisto por el Estado. As, desde las ltimas dcadas del siglo pasado, numerosos pases otorgaron autonoma a sus bancos centrales, garantizndoles una sana independencia de las necesidades fiscales de los gobiernos y del ciclo poltico. Con la autonoma de la banca central, el objetivo de abatir la inflacin queda cimentado en un mandato institucional claro y preciso, ms que en la eventual coincidencia entre las autoridades monetarias y fiscales en turno. La decisin de otorgar autonoma al Banco de Mxico no slo se deriva de la experiencia internacional. Nuestro pas tambin ha experimentado en diversas etapas, y con terribles consecuencias, el flagelo de la inflacin. En particular, en los aos setenta y ochenta del siglo pasado se aplicaron polticas de gasto pblico excesivamente expansivas y se impuso al Banco Central la obligacin de extender crdito para financiar los consecuentes dficits fiscales. Esto propici inflaciones agudas, prolongadas, y profundamente dainas para la sociedad. Tras estas experiencias, en 1993 se plante la reforma al Artculo 28 de la Constitucin, que concedi al Banco de Mxico autonoma en su administracin y funciones, asignndole el objetivo prioritario de mantener la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional y sealando, explcitamente, que ninguna autoridad puede ordenarle conceder financiamiento. 3 Permtanme ahora, referirme al cumplimiento de las funciones del Banco de Mxico en un entorno, externo e interno, complejo e incierto, como el actual. Para cumplir con su mandato, que es la estabilidad de precios, el Banco de Mxico ha adoptado, para la conduccin de su poltica monetaria, un esquema de objetivos de inflacin. En nuestro caso, ste se basa en una meta especfica para la inflacin general de 3 por ciento, con un marco de transparencia y con una estrategia de comunicacin que d certeza y coordine las expectativas de los agentes econmicos. Cuando el pblico tiene confianza en que el banco central reaccionar ante los choques que pudieran desviar de manera sostenida a la inflacin de su objetivo, sus expectativas tienden a estar alineadas a dicho objetivo. Para reforzar este canal de comunicacin, la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico ha decidido hacer pblicos, trimestralmente, los pronsticos de inflacin para los siguientes 8 trimestres, estos se publicaron por primera vez la semana pasada en el ltimo Informe Trimestral. De esta manera, el Banco de Mxico evaluar, entre otros factores, si las eventuales desviaciones de la inflacin respecto a sus pronsticos, en el horizonte en el que opera la poltica monetaria, dan lugar a alguna adecuacin en la tasa de inters objetivo. Cabe destacar, que los esfuerzos del Banco de Mxico para alcanzar una inflacin baja y estable han propiciado una menor persistencia de la inflacin, un anclaje de las expectativas de mediano y largo plazo en niveles prximos a la meta, y un menor traspaso a la inflacin del cambio de precios relativos, en especial de fluctuaciones cambiarias. As, con sus acciones el Banco de Mxico ha buscado evitar que los movimientos del tipo de cambio real, que son ajustes naturales ante distintos choques, den lugar a efectos de segundo 4 orden en la formacin de precios o afecten las expectativas de inflacin de mediano y largo plazo. Sin duda, tener un tipo de cambio flexible y una poltica monetaria que se conduce con un esquema de objetivos de inflacin, ha contribuido a un mejor funcionamiento del proceso de formacin de precios en la economa. Esto conlleva importantes beneficios para la sociedad, pues ha permitido enfrentar diversos choques con menores afectaciones a la actividad econmica. En los ltimos aos, Mxico, al igual que otras economas emergentes, ha enfrentado un panorama complejo, debido a la confluencia de diversos choques y fuentes de incertidumbre. El primero se refiere a los menores precios de las materias primas que han prevalecido ya por varios aos, y que han implicado un importante deterioro en los trminos de intercambio en diversas economas emergentes, menores ingresos fiscales e, incluso, reducciones en el producto cclico y potencial. En el caso de Mxico, tanto la baja en los precios del petrleo, como la contraccin de su plataforma de produccin, redujeron significativamente los ingresos petroleros. El segundo factor corresponde al aumento en las tasas de inters externas, asociado al proceso de normalizacin de las polticas monetarias en las principales economas avanzadas, especialmente en Estados Unidos, el cual constituye un riesgo para los mercados financieros internacionales, y podra propiciar ajustes en los portafolios de inversin con posiciones en las economas emergentes. Este factor ha cobrado mayor relevancia, considerando la posicin cclica de la economa estadounidense y los efectos del estmulo fiscal recientemente aprobado. 5 El tercer factor, es el riesgo creciente de adopcin de medidas proteccionistas y la revisin que algunas economas avanzadas han propiciado respecto a los modelos de integracin regional y global. Algunos ejemplos de ello son el caso del Brexit y la renegociacin del Tratado de Libre Comercio de Amrica del Norte. Este ltimo definir el marco para el comercio y la inversin de la regin. Por ello, a lo largo de la negociacin, las percepciones cambiantes sobre su resultado, han generado incertidumbre y volatilidad en nuestros mercados financieros, especialmente el cambiario. Los efectos de este complejo entorno externo, y de otros choques internos, afectaron significativamente la inflacin en Mxico. A principios de 2017, esta se vio presionada, tanto por una fuerte depreciacin del peso, como por aumentos en los precios de varios energticos en el mercado interno. Adicionalmente, a finales de 2017 se registraron choques adicionales no previstos, como el aumento de precios del gas natural y algunas verduras por factores transitorios. Todo lo anterior, propici un repunte de la inflacin, que alcanz 6.77% al cierre del 2017 y la subyacente 4.87%. En febrero de este ao, la inflacin disminuy a 5.34%, resultado de una importante reduccin de la inflacin no subyacente, y una de menor magnitud en la subyacente, que alcanz 4.27%. Cabe sealar que en los ltimos aos la economa mexicana ha venido transitando por un ciclo econmico atpico, tanto por las condiciones externas inditas, como por el tipo de choques que la han aquejado. Esto ha complicado la evaluacin de las condiciones de holgura de la economa, y su papel en la formacin de precios, la cual se ha venido estrechando y podra afectar la asimilacin de dichos choques. 6 Ante la complejidad de este entorno, y a fin de evitar efectos de segundo orden en la formacin de precios y reforzar la tendencia decreciente de la inflacin, la Junta de Gobierno restringi la postura de poltica monetaria, alcanzando la tasa de inters objetivo 7.5% en febrero de este ao. Tomando en consideracin el comportamiento actual de la inflacin, la evolucin de sus determinantes, la postura vigente de poltica monetaria y el horizonte temporal en el que sta surte efectos, se espera que, en ausencia de nuevos choques y presiones no anticipadas, se consolide la inflexin a la baja de la inflacin general, aproximndose a lo largo del ao hacia el objetivo de 3%, y alcanzndolo en el primer trimestre de 2019. El Banco de Mxico, estar atento a todos los factores determinantes de la inflacin y su balance de riesgos, a fin de mantener la convergencia de la inflacin a su meta. Por ltimo, permtanme hacer algunas reflexiones relacionadas con el sistema financiero. La experiencia demuestra que, para alcanzar un crecimiento econmico sostenido, es indispensable contar con un sistema financiero bien capitalizado y con un marco normativo adecuado, que ofrezca los incentivos correctos para que las instituciones financieras intermedien de manera segura y eficiente el ahorro del pblico en proyectos rentables y con derrama social. El Banco de Mxico busca que el sistema financiero, ofrezca servicios y oportunidades de desarrollo para todos los ciudadanos de manera sostenida. Para ello, trabaja en dos grandes vertientes. 7 La primera, atae a sus facultades como regulador y supervisor para promover la estabilidad del sistema y mitigar sus riesgos. Al respecto, destaca que el financiamiento de la banca comercial al sector privado se ha venido recuperando de manera sostenida. Este proceso de mayor apalancamiento, tanto de hogares como de empresas, se ha dado sobre las bases de un sistema financiero sano. Ello, en parte, por la adopcin oportuna de nuestro pas de los mejores estndares internacionales de regulacin y supervisin, que buscan reforzar la resiliencia del sistema y alinear los incentivos entre los intermediarios y los usuarios del sistema financiero. Con ello, el sector financiero mexicano se encuentra en una situacin slida, capaz de resistir riesgos diversos. La segunda vertiente de responsabilidad del Banco de Mxico respecto al sistema financiero, est orientada a promover una mayor cobertura de los servicios financieros, priorizando la seguridad y la proteccin de los intereses del consumidor. Para ello, se redoblarn los esfuerzos para alcanzar una mayor eficiencia en la intermediacin financiera, reforzar la competencia, y que ello se refleje en beneficios para todos los usuarios. Como parte de estos esfuerzos, la Junta de Gobierno aprob hace unos das las Polticas para la Consulta Pblica de las Disposiciones de Carcter General que emita el Banco de Mxico. Con ello, se adoptaron estndares internacionales en mejora regulatoria, con procesos abiertos y transparentes, que permitirn contar con regulacin ms eficaz. Por otro lado, como nunca antes, contamos con nuevas herramientas tecnolgicas que permiten abatir costos de cobertura, brindar acceso a los servicios financieros a diversos sectores de la poblacin y atender los rezagos en materia de inclusin financiera. 8 A fin de aprovechar cabalmente el potencial de este sector, denominado Fintech, el Poder Ejecutivo present un Proyecto de Ley para Regular a las Instituciones de Tecnologa Financiera, que fue aprobado por el Congreso de la Unin el 1 de marzo del presente ao. Con este nuevo marco legal, se brinda orden y transparencia en un sector de importancia ascendente y se genera un poderoso instrumento para aprovechar las nuevas tecnologas financieras en beneficio de los usuarios. Seoras y seores: La solidez de los fundamentos macroeconmicos de Mxico ha permitido que, pese a la severidad de los choques que se han enfrentado en los ltimos aos, la economa haya mantenido un entorno de estabilidad con crecimiento. En esta estrategia convergen la poltica monetaria, la fiscal, la cambiaria y la solidez del sistema financiero. Contar con un entorno de estabilidad es indispensable para el crecimiento y el desarrollo, y debe ser entendida como una obligacin permanente del Estado. Por lo que toca a la poltica monetaria, la Constitucin contempla que el Estado tenga un banco central, autnomo en el ejercicio de sus funciones y en su administracin, con el objetivo prioritario de procurar el poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. El Banco de Mxico mantiene este claro y preciso mandato como el faro y gua de todas sus actividades. Muchas gracias 9

Title: The great experimentation with unconventional monetary and financial policy
text: REMARKS BY MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR AT THE BANCO DE MeXICO, AT THE PANEL POTENTIAL OUTCOME OF THE GREAT EXPERIMENTATION AND IMPLICATIONS FOR THE GLOBAL FINANCIAL ARCHITECTURE. CONFERENCE THE GREAT EXPERIMENTATION WITH UNCONVENTIONAL MONETARY AND FINANCIAL POLICY, ORGANIZED BY THE BANCO CENTRAL DE RESERVA DEL PERu AND THE REINVENTING BRETTON WOODS COMMITTEE. Cusco, Peru, July 3-4, 2013.1 First of all let me thank Governor Velarde for his kind invitation to participate in this interesting conference. I will concentrate my remarks on a few issues that in my view are important to increase the possibility of a successful outcome from UMPs, including some related to the international financial architecture, as requested by the organizers. UMPs have had thus far important beneficial effects both on the implementing countries and the overall world economy. They have contributed substantially to strengthen confidence, restore the functioning of interbank markets, support financial intermediation, lessen vulnerabilities in the banking system, and reduce long term yields and tail risks. Most importantly, UMPs have allowed to prevent a collapse of the world financial system, which would have most probably implied a cost in terms of output and employment well above what we have seen up to date. Nevertheless, these policies have also given rise to a number of risks. The latter include the effects of UMPs on capital flows to and outflows from emerging market economies and the related macroeconomic and financial stability challenges; the implications for financial stability of prolonged periods of low interest rates; the potential impact on inflation of exceptionally easy monetary policies; the challenges for central banks resulting from the fundamental change in the size and composition of their balance sheets deriving from UMPs; a possible reputational cost if expectations on the benefits of UMPs are too high and run beyond what central banks can reasonable achieve; and of course, as evidenced by recent events, the difficulties related to exit from UMPs. Let me note in this last respect, that a withdrawal of monetary stimulus resulting from the prospect of a sustained economic recovery should have beneficial medium and long term effects. However, one of the main problems here is timing of the exit itself, since central banks may move prematurely to a policy setting that might not prove sufficiently accommodative to ensure a sustainable recovery. As shown by the events of recent weeks, volatility in the financial markets and a more rapid than expected increase in long term interest rates is another possible result of an unwinding of UMPs. 1 The views expressed herein are strictly personal and do not necessarily coincide with those of the Banco de Mexico. 1 It is clear, then, that ensuring a successful outcome of UMPs requires simultaneous action in a number of fronts. I would like to refer briefly to three of them which in my view are particularly important: a. As I mentioned before, the potential impact of UMPs on financial stability is a source of concern. Both low interest rates resulting from UMPs, and alternatively a sharp increase in long term rates linked to the withdrawal of monetary stimulus, give rise to financial stability risks. The standard recommendation nowadays is to use macroprudential tools as one of the main lines of defense. I fully share the view that under current circumstances the attainment of financial stability requires a new policy focus in which macroprudential measures have a more prominent role than in the past. However, we must also be aware of the limitations that we face. In particular, further research is needed to provide the theoretical backing required for the design and setting in motion of integrated policy frameworks in this area. In addition, the authorities must make sure that they have in place the institutional framework required for a proper use of these instruments. Furthermore, the coordination of macroprudential policies with monetary, fiscal and microprudential policies in the pursuit of financial stability must be carefully assessed. Therefore, expectations on the potential contribution of macroprudential policy to financial stability should remain within realistic boundaries. b. Over a relatively short time span, communication policy at central banks has undergone a radical transformation. To put it simply, after a long period of opacity, around two decades ago a move towards more transparency among central banks gained strength. Thus, by the early years of this century some central banks began to use communication as a primary policy tool, i.e. as an independent tool for influencing the economy. Communication has become even more important after the onset of the financial crisis. With interest rates near zero and the introduction of UMPs, extensive new communication has been needed to establish a link between these policy instruments and macroeconomic objectives. Naturally, communication should also play a key role when the time comes for a withdrawal of the extraordinary monetary accommodation provided by UMPs. The problem is that although communication has changed, demands from financial markets and from the public in general have also rapidly evolved. As the events of the past few weeks suggest, we are shooting at a moving target. This underlines the importance of an extremely careful communication policy. Moreover, additional efforts are needed to ensure that we have an adequate understanding of how communication can influence the effectiveness of monetary policy. c. Although UMPs have been fundamental to overcome the challenges that have emerged as a result of the global financial crisis, monetary policy cannot solve its ultimate causes. Ensuring debt sustainability, strengthening the private sectors balance sheet, enhancing the economys competitiveness, and undertaking other structural reforms are well beyond the reach of monetary policy. Therefore, one of the most important actions that advanced economies can do to contribute to a successful outcome of UMPs, is precisely to set in 2 motion, the sooner the better, the actions needed to tackle the root causes of the current difficulties. Is reform of the international financial architecture relevant for a successful outcome of UMPs? The answer is clearly positive. The potential of financial volatility and instability in the world economy is likely to persist, and strengthening the international financial architecture can contribute a lot to counter some of the resulting risks. In this connection, I would like to make a few remarks on the role of the IMF first and then on the global financial reform agenda. With respect to the Fund, it is evident that in a situation like the one we are facing, it is more important than ever to endow the IMF with an adequate financial capacity. During the past few years, the Funds financial resources have been strengthened through quota increases, supplemented by an enlargement of the NAB, and more recently by the bilateral borrowing agreement framework implemented during the Mexican presidency of the G20. The last two initiatives have been extremely useful to allow the Fund to respond to member countries needs in the aftermath of the crisis. However, they are unlikely to represent permanent sources of financing for the Fund. In addition, contributions through these channels are not reflected in decision making at the institution. Therefore, they must not be considered as a substitute for quota increases. Moreover, present Fund financial capacity may fall short of the amounts needed in the current circumstances. a. The growth of IMF available resources has been below that of the global economy in the last decades, and too small in comparison with the growth of the global financial system. b. The situation is even more worrisome when the actual and potential demand for Fund resources by some advanced economies is taken into consideration. c. The globalization of financial markets makes it more likely than before that the IMF will have to address financial crises that affect more than one country at a time. The risks stemming from this situation are clearly large. Therefore, the international community should be open minded when assessing the adequacy of Fund resources in the context of the 15th General Review of Quotas (scheduled to be concluded by January 2014). Naturally, an important prerequisite here is to ratify, as soon as possible, the 2010 quota and governance reform. On the other hand, cooperation between the Fund and regional financing arrangements (another important player of the existing international financial safety net) should be further enhanced, among other means through closer communication and joint work in crisis prevention and resolution. Besides financing capacity, the Fund needs to have in place adequate financial facilities. Indeed, the IMF has done a good in job in overhauling its lending toolkit. Systemic costs and spillover effects are much higher in cases of crisis resolution. Therefore, I welcome in particular the efforts made to provide more and better crisis prevention instruments. 3 The Precautionary and Liquidity Line (PLL) and the Flexible Credit Line (FCL) have been a major achievement in the efforts made by the Fund to improve its preventive capacity and strengthen the international safety net. These facilities have the great advantage of stimulating sound policy frameworks, while supporting confidence and diminishing the need to accumulate international reserves. Furthermore, they are fully driven by member countries policy commitments and therefore alleviate the stigma traditionally associated with Fund programs. The Board of the Fund will be discussing later this year the effectiveness of the FCL and the PLL. On the basis of Mexicos successful experience with the FCL, I am convinced that they are an essential component of the international financial architecture. Moreover, in my view the Fund should explore possible means to stimulate a wider use of the available instruments, as well as the feasibility of putting in place other facilities of a preventive nature. My final comment on the IMF relates to its surveillance function. First of all let me stress that the recent strengthening of the Funds surveillance framework is a step in the right direction. I am very glad to see the deepening of multilateral surveillance activities, the inclusion of assessments regarding financial stability and spillover effects in Article IV Consultation reports, and the evaluation of risks originating in the main systemic countries. The series of papers that have been prepared on different aspects of unconventional monetary policies is also welcome. Although a lot has been achieved, there is still substantial room for improvement: a. Many Fund member countries find little value added in the institutions advise, especially that provided in the context of bilateral surveillance. It is often argued that this advise is too generic or based on a one-size-fits-all-approach. b. There is a clear need to deepen the understanding of macrofinancial linkages, and to reflect this knowledge in the analytical frameworks used and in the implementation of the surveillance work, both at the bilateral and multilateral levels. c. The perception that Fund recommendations are not evenhanded continue to be a barrier to effective surveillance. In a recent survey carried out by the Funds Internal Evaluation Office (IEO), about a third of country authorities and half of the mission chiefs interviewed did not believe that the IMF has become more evenhanded since the onset of the global financial crisis.2 Recent Fund programs in the advanced economies of the European Union was mentioned as an example of lack of evenhandedness. d. The Spillover Reports fill an important gap and are likely to improve a lot our understanding of interconnections in the world economy. However, as the Fund itself recognizes, much further effort is needed, since this work is only in its initial stages and its value as a surveillance tool is yet to be established. 2 Also, half of the surveyed mission chiefs of systemically important advanced economies admitted that the systemic importance had influenced the degree of candor of the dialogue. See IEO, The Role of the IMF as Trusted Advisor, January 17, 2013. 4 e. The old problem related to Fund surveillance remains: it lacks teeth. I am aware that this is an extremely complicated issue, but we must not surrender and keep on trying to find ways to enhance the practical impact of this crucial Fund activity. Let me turn now to global financial reform. A positive aspect of the global financial crisis is that it has elicited an unprecedented effort to reform the international financial sector. Contrary to previous episodes, on this occasion the response has been faster and it has involved a greater number of countries and international institutions. In general terms, the main objectives of the reform have been to strengthen the international financial system and the capacity to respond to crises. Some of the measures considered have a preventive nature (e.g. increasing the quality and quantity of banks capital, reducing leverage and enhancing supervision). Others are aimed at limiting the impact of financial institutions failures (e.g. cross border cooperation on crisis management and developing effective resolution regimes for banks), and the rest focus on strengthening the financial infrastructure and limiting the risk of contagion (e.g. standardization and central clearing of OTC derivatives). In my view, these efforts take into account all the major elements needed for a fundamental overhaul of the international financial architecture. In fact, their effects are already evident in a number of areas. Naturally, the road ahead is not free of challenges. In this respect, let me note the following: a. One of the most difficult issues for regulators is to find an appropriate balance between a weak worldwide economic outlook and stricter regulatory policies. We do not know with certainty what will be the impact and effect of stronger regulatory requirements on the world economy. There is consensus that global financial stability facilitates strong economic growth in the long run. However, there is also a possibility of increased funding costs for global banks, banks deleveraging to meet tighter capital requirements, and a reduction in the volume of credit, in the short term. b. Progress is uneven regarding implementation of the recommended measures. This is the case for instance of Basel III capital requirements. In addition to the implications for the strength of the financial system, this may lead to regulatory arbitrage opportunities, as institutions will try to do business in countries characterized by more lax regulatory frameworks. c. Significant progress in some areas, such as shadow banking, is yet to be seen. The situation is particularly important in this case, since a substantial amount of funds may be migrating to new unregulated activities. d. Since the crisis began in advanced economies, the reforms were designed to meet the needs of these countries. As a result, some of the recommended measures may have undesirable side effects on emerging market economies. To conclude, let me say a word about emerging market economies. On several previous occasions, major crises in these countries have been preceded by significant increases in international 5 interest rates after a prolonged period of abundant liquidity. I fully agree that there are many elements that suggest that it may be different this time. In particular, a radical improvement of economic fundamentals has been observed vis-a-vis the situation prevailing during those previous episodes. Perhaps the most compelling evidence in this regard lies in the fact that according to IMF figures, these economies have accounted for around three quarters of world economic growth during the last five years. Nevertheless, a complacent attitude would be a mistake. To start with, as shown by the recent turbulence in international financial markets the road ahead is likely to be bumpy. Furthermore, major differences from one country to another prevail, and even among many of those that have made most progress, a number of macroeconomic and/or structural challenges need to be tackled. To sum up, homework is far from finished and the strengthening of economic fundamentals needs to continue in this group. 6

Title: XX Annual Convention of Insurers
text: 1 Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, during the XX Annual Convention of Insurers (Mexican Association of Insurance Institutions). Monday, May 24, 2010, Mexico City.  Mr. President of the Mexican Association of Insurance Institutions, Mr. Ignacio Gil Anton  Mr. President of the National Insurance and Bonding Commission, Mr. Manuel Aguilera Verduzco  Ladies and gentlemen It gives me great pleasure to accompany you in this first plenary session of the Twentieth National Convention of Insurers. Thank you very much for your kind invitation. Today I would like to focus my remarks on one of the main lessons from the global financial crisis that has afflicted us since 2008. I am referring to the need for greater coordination between the financial authorities, in order to 1 2 anticipate and prevent risks of a systemic nature that may arise in virtually any sector or instrument of the financial system. A systemic risk is one that endangers the stability of an entire financial system as a whole. Now, when does a financial system lose its stability? When one or more events prevent it from fulfilling in an effective, efficient and timely manner its functions of channeling resources between different economic agents. It is clear, for example, that in the early autumn of 2008 much of the global financial system entered a period of acute instability. It is enough to recall the so-called "credit squeeze" that abruptly dried up financing not only for thousands of companies and millions of families, but for entire countries. The chain of events that provoked in 2008 and in subsequent months this sudden fracture in the channels of the global financial system had its origin, in turn, in a regulation and 2 3 Atomized supervision in the main advanced countries, which failed to detect and prevent undesirable risks from being assumed in the markets. Risks that, as would be seen later, ended up violating the stability of the main national and regional financial systems and, therefore, of the global system. Why did this happen? Allow me a schematic explanation of one of the most important causes: While modern financial systems naturally allow for an extensive network of transactions that interconnect different markets, the activity of national regulators and supervisors has tended to remain in more or less isolated institutional compartments. This causes a dangerous gap between what regulators and supervisors perceive, from a traditional perspective specialized in branches of activity, and what is actually happening day by day in the dynamics of the markets. Such disparity 3 4 of visions - as experienced in 2008 and 2009 - seriously jeopardizes the stability of the financial system. Thus, while the authorities regulate their supervisory and regulatory tasks according to borders of specialization that seem insurmountable and rigid, those who operate in the markets, as well as their clients, not only do not stop at these pre-established borders but even manage to erase them, in practice, through innovation and arbitration. I illustrate this by resorting to a dramatic case that you surely know well: AIG. The root of the terrible financial debacle of that large insurer was not, in any way, in its activity as an insurer, but in its reckless incursion into the assumption of large risks outside its traditional lines of business, in particular credit risks. But that irresponsible incursion was possible simply because regulators and supervisors did not. 4 5 they were looking at the global picture of the financial system as a whole, but only, and each of them, the isolated compartment that theoretically corresponded to them. This atomization of supervision and regulation - which we could colloquially describe as myopia of specialists or workshop blindness - contrasts dramatically with the more than panoramic view that many operators in the financial markets showed. It is clear that it is not a smart response to this problem to try to impose on financial markets, and the economic agents operating in them, the same workshop blindness that seems to deprive regulators and supervisors. Of course, it is not a viable answer either; it would be as candid and useless as wanting to put doors to the field. On the contrary, what is rationally imposed is to give regulatory and supervisory authorities the same vision. 5 6 panorama enjoyed by those who operate in the financial markets. And the way to do that is to establish the formal functional mechanisms for effective and timely coordination and collaboration between the various financial authorities, both at the national and global levels. That way it will ensure that the authorities as a whole have the desired panoramic view, without losing the advantage of specialization. In this line of coordination and cooperation have been the proposals that have been generated both in the G-20, where the Mexican financial authorities actively participate, and in various forums. For example, last Thursday the U.S. Senate approved the creation of the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC), while a House bill also creates a new council of federal regulators with broad authority to protect the 6 7 financial system of the kind of systemic risks that can spread rapidly, as happened in 2008. Both laws are part of an extensive package that strengthens financial supervision and regulation; the differences between the two laws, which are minor, will soon be reconciled by the two chambers to enact final legislation from which the Financial Stability Supervisory Board will begin to function. In Canada, the securities managers' organization has already created a Systemic Risk Committee; in the European Union, it has been proposed to establish a Systemic Risk Council under the auspices of the European Central Bank; in Germany, the Central Bank and the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority established a Joint Risk Committee to link macroeconomic prudential supervision with microeconomic supervision; in France, the National Council for Systemic Risk and Supervision has been proposed 7 8 Financial. There are similar experiences and proposals in Turkey and India, among other countries. In Mexico, too, we must address these lessons arising from the global crisis in a timely manner, and it would be desirable for the financial authorities to take similar cooperation and coordination initiatives in the shortest possible time to anticipate and avoid systemic risks. The right spirit for the prevention of systemic risks in financial markets lies precisely in having a panoramic view of the markets that allows regulators and supervisors to detect connections and arbitrages between instruments, as well as between risks. This, even if these linkages seemed unthinkable in a traditional perspective of isolated markets. In fact, when expressed in monetary terms, any financial asset also has, like money, a fungible character that allows it to arbitrate in practically any 8 9 market and have as collateral any other financial instrument. For this reason, it is also necessary that the financial authorities through close national and global coordination can detect and prevent in a timely manner the formation of speculative bubbles in the prices of any financial asset: real estate, commodity futures, hedges related to a possible default of sovereign debts, promises of payment, liabilities, etc. We have already seen, during the global crisis, that just as there is practically no niche or space in the financial markets that is not capable of generating innovative business opportunities, linking with other financial markets through arbitrage, there is also no privileged corner in these markets that escapes the dangers of being overwhelmed in case of systemic risk. 9 10 It is true, for example, that the insurance industry by its very nature tends to be a stabilizing factor of the system as a whole, but this happens as long as we confine it to the traditional lines of the insurance business. This stabilizing virtue of the insurance industry ceases to be true, and I return to the case of AIG, when the search for greater profitability - which is the legitimate and desirable engine of any lucrative company - coupled with a lag in regulation, which tacitly allows unregulated and unsupervised arbitration between assets of a very diverse nature, it drives her to take reckless risks. In this sense, the unfortunate episode of AIG reminds us that the insurance industry is not an exceptional case within the financial system, a separate entity that is always safe from risks and unpleasant surprises. Fortunately, and in contrast, we can say that during this crisis the insurance sector in Mexico has had a performance 10 11 practically impeccable and very satisfying. But precisely for this reason, because the insurance industry in Mexico also has valuable lessons to contribute to the rest of the financial system, I have no doubt that it is crucial that it joins the effort of cooperation and coordination to guarantee the stability of our system. Thanks a lot. 11
text_original: 1 Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, durante la XX Convencin Anual de Aseguradores (Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones de Seguros). Lunes 24 de mayo de 2010, ciudad de Mxico.  Seor presidente de la Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones de Seguros, licenciado Ignacio Gil Antn  Seor presidente de la Comisin Nacional de Seguros y Fianzas, licenciado Manuel Aguilera Verduzco  Seoras y seores Me da un gran gusto acompaarles en esta primera sesin plenaria de la Vigsima Convencin Nacional de Aseguradores. Muchas gracias por su amable invitacin. El da de hoy quisiera centrar mis comentarios en una de las principales lecciones que nos ha dejado la crisis financiera mundial que nos aqueja desde 2008. Me refiero a la necesidad de una mayor coordinacin entre las autoridades financieras, para 1 2 anticipar y prevenir oportunamente riesgos de carcter sistmico que pueden surgir prcticamente en cualquier sector o instrumento del sistema financiero. Un riesgo sistmico es aqul que pone en peligro la estabilidad de todo un sistema financiero en su conjunto. Ahora bien, cundo pierde su estabilidad un sistema financiero? Cuando uno o varios eventos le impiden cumplir de manera efectiva, eficiente y oportuna sus funciones de canalizar los recursos entre diferentes agentes econmicos. Es claro, por ejemplo, que a inicios del otoo de 2008 gran parte del sistema financiero mundial entr en un periodo de aguda inestabilidad. Basta recordar el llamado apretn crediticio que sec, abruptamente, el financiamiento no slo para miles de empresas y millones de familias, sino para pases enteros. La cadena de eventos que provocaron en 2008 y en meses subsecuentes esa fractura sbita en los canales del sistema financiero mundial tuvo su origen, a su vez, en una regulacin y 2 3 supervisin atomizadas en los principales pases avanzados, que fallaron para detectar y evitar que en los mercados se asumieran riesgos indeseables. Riesgos que, como se vera ms tarde, acabaron por vulnerar la estabilidad de los principales sistemas financieros nacionales y regionales y, por lo tanto, del sistema global. Por qu sucedi esto? Permtanme una explicacin esquemtica de una de las causas ms importantes: Mientras que naturalmente los sistemas financieros modernos permiten que se genere una extensa red de transacciones que interconectan diferentes mercados, la actividad de los reguladores y supervisores nacionales ha tendido a mantenerse en compartimentos institucionales ms o menos aislados. Esto provoca un peligroso desfase entre lo que perciben reguladores y supervisores, desde una ptica tradicional especializada en ramas de actividad, y lo que en realidad est sucediendo da a da en la dinmica de los mercados. Tal disparidad 3 4 de visiones  como se experiment en 2008 y en 2009- pone en serio peligro la estabilidad del sistema financiero. De esta forma, mientras las autoridades norman sus tareas de supervisin y regulacin de acuerdo con fronteras de especializacin que parecen infranqueables y rgidas, quienes operan en los mercados, as como sus clientes, no solamente no se detienen ante dichas fronteras preestablecidas sino que incluso logran borrarlas, en la prctica, mediante la innovacin y el arbitraje. Ilustro esto recurriendo a un caso dramtico que seguramente conocen bien: AIG. La raz de la terrible debacle financiera de esa gran aseguradora no estuvo, en modo alguno, en su actividad como aseguradora, sino en su temeraria incursin en la asuncin de cuantiosos riesgos ajenos a sus lneas tradicionales de negocio, en particular riegos crediticios. Pero esa incursin irresponsable fue posible sencillamente porque los reguladores y supervisores no 4 5 estaban viendo el panorama global del sistema financiero en su conjunto, sino solamente, y cada uno de ellos, el compartimento aislado que tericamente les corresponda. Esta atomizacin de la supervisin y de la regulacin  que coloquialmente podramos calificar de miopa de los especialistas o de ceguera de taller- contrasta dramticamente con la visin ms que panormica de la que hicieron gala muchos operadores en los mercados financieros. Resulta claro que no es una respuesta inteligente a este problema tratar de imponer a los mercados financieros, y a los agentes econmicos que operan en ellos, la misma ceguera de taller que parece privar entre reguladores y supervisores. Desde luego, tampoco es una respuesta viable; sera tan candorosa e intil como querer ponerle puertas al campo. Por el contrario, lo que racionalmente se impone es dotar a las autoridades reguladoras y supervisoras de la misma visin 5 6 panormica de la que disfrutan quienes operan en los mercados financieros. Y la forma de hacerlo es establecer los mecanismos funcionales formales para una eficaz y oportuna coordinacin y colaboracin entre las diversas autoridades financieras, tanto en el mbito nacional como en el global. De esa manera se asegurar que las autoridades en su conjunto tengan la deseada visin panormica, sin perder la ventaja de la especializacin. En esta lnea de coordinacin y cooperacin han ido las propuestas que se han generado tanto en el G-20, donde las autoridades financieras mexicanas participamos activamente, como en diversos foros. Por ejemplo, el jueves pasado el Senado de Estados Unidos aprob la creacin del Consejo Supervisor de la Estabilidad Financiera (Financial Stability Oversight Council o FSOC), en tanto que una ley de la Cmara de Representantes tambin crea un nuevo consejo de reguladores federales con amplia autoridad para proteger al 6 7 sistema financiero del tipo de riesgos sistmicos que pueden propagarse rpidamente, como sucedi en 2008. Ambas leyes forman parte de un extenso paquete que refuerza la supervisin y la regulacin financieras; las diferencias entre una y otra ley, que son menores, sern conciliadas en breve por las dos cmaras para promulgar una legislacin definitiva a partir de la cual empezar a funcionar el Consejo de Supervisin de la Estabilidad Financiera. En Canad, la organizacin de administradores de valores ya cre un Comit de Riesgos Sistmicos; en la Unin Europea se ha planteado establecer un Consejo de Riesgos Sistmicos bajo los auspicios del Banco Central Europeo; en Alemania, el Banco Central y la Autoridad de Supervisin Financiera Federal establecieron un Comit Conjunto de Riesgos, para vincular la supervisin prudencial macroeconmica con la supervisin microeconmica; en Francia se ha propuesto el Consejo Nacional de Riesgo Sistmico y Supervisin 7 8 Financiera. Hay experiencias y propuestas similares en Turqua y en la India, entre otros pases. Tambin en Mxico debemos atender oportunamente estas lecciones derivadas de la crisis global y sera deseable que en el plazo ms breve las autoridades financieras concretsemos iniciativas de cooperacin y coordinacin semejantes, que permitan prever y evitar riesgos sistmicos. El espritu adecuado para la prevencin de riesgos sistmicos en los mercados financieros radica, precisamente, en contar con una visin panormica de los mercados que permita a los reguladores y supervisores, detectar conexiones y arbitrajes entre instrumentos, as como entre riesgos. Esto, aun cuando esas vinculaciones pareciesen impensables en una ptica tradicional de mercados aislados. De hecho, al expresarse en trminos monetarios cualquier activo financiero tiene tambin, como el dinero, un carcter fungible que le permite arbitrarse prcticamente en cualquier 8 9 mercado y tener como colateral cualquier otro instrumento financiero. Por esta razn, tambin es preciso que las autoridades financieras mediante una estrecha coordinacin nacional y global puedan detectar y prevenir oportunamente la formacin de burbujas especulativas en los precios de cualquier activo financiero: bienes races, futuros de materias primas, coberturas relacionadas a un eventual incumplimiento de deudas soberanas, promesas de pago, pasivos, etctera. Ya hemos visto, durante la crisis global, que as como no hay prcticamente ningn nicho o espacio en los mercados financieros que no sea susceptible de generar oportunidades innovadoras de negocio, vinculndose con otros mercados financieros mediante el arbitraje, tampoco hay ningn rincn privilegiado en dichos mercados que escape a los peligros de ser avasallado en caso de suscitarse un riesgo sistmico. 9 10 Es cierto, por ejemplo, que la industria de los seguros por su misma naturaleza tiende a ser un factor estabilizador del sistema en su conjunto, pero ello sucede siempre y cuando la circunscribamos a las lneas tradicionales del negocio de los seguros. Deja de ser cierta esta virtud estabilizadora de la industria de los seguros, y vuelvo al caso de AIG, cuando la bsqueda de una mayor rentabilidad  que es el motor legtimo y deseable de toda empresa lucrativa- aunada a un rezago en la regulacin, que permite tcitamente un arbitraje no regulado ni supervisado entre activos de naturaleza muy diversa, la impulsa a tomar riesgos temerarios. En este sentido, el lamentable episodio de AIG nos recuerda que la industria aseguradora no es un caso excepcional dentro del sistema financiero, un ente aparte que est siempre a salvo de riesgos y de sorpresas desagradables. Por fortuna, y en contraste, podemos decir que durante esta crisis el sector asegurador en Mxico ha tenido un desempeo 10 11 prcticamente impecable y muy satisfactorio. Pero justamente por ello, porque tambin la industria aseguradora en Mxico tiene valiosas enseanzas que aportar al resto del sistema financiero, no me cabe duda que es crucial que se sume al esfuerzo de cooperacin y coordinacin para garantizar la estabilidad de nuestro sistema. Muchas gracias. 11

Title: Presentation of the coin commemorating the Fiftieth Anniversary of Plan DN-III E of the Ministry of National Defense for the aid of the civilian population in cases of disaster
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, on the occasion of the circulation of the coin commemorating the Fiftieth Anniversary of Plan DN-III E of the Ministry of National Defense for the aid of the civilian population in cases of disaster. July 2017 Mexico is a great country endowed with a variety of natural resources and a unique human wealth in the world, but it is also a country prone to natural disasters, among others: hurricanes with devastating effects, relentless overflows of mighty rivers due to torrential rains, frightening and destructive earthquakes. There is nothing that can concern a human being more than preserving life, one's own as well as the life and health of our loved ones. For this reason, we will always be grateful and proud to have an armed forces that, always, without fail, whatever the misfortune of whatever magnitude, are present there - in the dark moments as an invaluable balm. The Mexican Army and Navy are always, when we most need support and protection, providing effective help to the population: food, health care, shelter, guidance, shelter, physical security. No one can fail to recognize the diligence, professionalism, human warmth and skill that our Armed Forces deploy to mitigate, to the extent of what is humanly possible, the shortcomings and sufferings that follow a calamity. 1 For all the above I am very honored to be here among you to put into circulation the 20 peso coin commemorating the Fiftieth Anniversary of the implementation of Plan DN-III-E, whose obverse bears the national shield and on the reverse, according to a design proposed by the Ministry of National Defense, bears as its main motif the distinctive bracelet of Plan DN-III-E and two images alluding to the Army and the Force. Mexican Area. I want to take advantage of this event to thank and recognize the support that the armed forces have provided for years for the security of the strategic facilities of the Bank of Mexico and in particular to guard and distribute banknotes throughout the country. Thank you very much General Secretary Cienfuegos. The event is also conducive to informing that an action protocol is ready for the supply of banknotes in disaster areas, when the banking infrastructure is collapsed and it is practically impossible for users of banking services to dispose of their money when they need it most. Also in those moments of greatest urgency is when our armed forces will be present to activate the protocol, together with the Association of Banks of Mexico, the National Bank of the Army, Air Force and Navy (Banjercito), the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Bank of Mexico, to send point of sale terminals to the affected area that will allow people who have a debit or credit card to withdraw cash, until bank branches and ATMs can provide service normally. 2 May this coin, which is being put into circulation today, serve as recognition of the sacrificial and extremely effective work of all those who make up our National Army. I remind you that it can be used to make any type of payment in your daily transactions, although I hope that many Mexicans keep it to proudly remember those who safeguard us. Finally, I thank all of you for your attention, as well as the public servants of the Mexican Mint and the Bank of Mexico, for their contribution to minting and issuing this new commemorative coin. I especially congratulate the Ministry of National Defense on the Fiftieth Anniversary of the noble and successful implementation of Plan DN-III-E in our country. Thanks a lot. 3
