Title: Presentation of the Banxico Contact Award 2020
text: 1 Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of the 2020 Banxico Contact Award. Mexico City, December 3, 2020 It gives me great pleasure to greet you at the presentation of the Contacto Banxico Award 2020, I hope that all of you and yours are in good health and good spirits. We have lived an atypical year, full of challenges and, therefore, I especially value the effort and discipline of the students who participated in the 2020 edition of this contest. The Contacto Banxico Award was created 12 years ago to bring the Bank of Mexico closer to the upper secondary education segment and encourage teachers and students of that level to know the purposes and operation of the central bank, as well as the benefits that its work generates to society. This contest is one of the oldest and most successful tools of the financial education program of Banco de Mexico and, during its validity, more than 50 thousand people from all the states of the Republic have registered and we have reviewed more than 6 thousand 500 works. 2 Until last year, the participants formed teams of three or four students and a teacher from the same institution for the elaboration of a written work or a video, on the subject of economics that is proposed in each edition. In the 2020 edition, derived from the contingency, the call was made individually. The written work and video categories were maintained, although the teacher's advisory participation was eliminated. Despite the difficult environment, this year 926 people (51% women and 49% men) from 31 states registered, answered a questionnaire 730 and received 473 works (359 written and 114 videos). The students registered from the Prize platform, answered a questionnaire on economic issues and attached their text or video, which in the rules of the contest are called entries. The entries of the participants were evaluated by 15 outstanding juries of the economic-financial environment, whom I thank very much for their collaboration. After this stage, the jurors interviewed by videoconference the best averages to select the 6 best in each category and, among them, a winner in the category of written work and another in the category of video. 3 In 2020, the theme of the contest was "The Bank of Mexico and your money" to address the way in which the central bank intervenes in the most varied forms of issuance and circulation of money. Money is a reference of value that facilitates its transfer, acceptance and registration. In our days, money acquires the most diverse modalities, from paper money to a bank deposit or an electronic transfer made from a mobile phone. Confidence in the stability of the purchasing power of money allows it to be an effective reference over time and to adequately fulfill its functions as a means of payment, unit of account and store of value. Thus, when there is confidence in the stability of the purchasing power of money, it is possible to facilitate trade, make economic and financial planning with a wider time horizon, direct resources more effectively, undertake long-term projects with greater 4 it spills over and better protects citizens' incomes and assets. On the other hand, when the public perceives that money can suffer losses in its purchasing power, an environment of uncertainty and instability is propitiated that considerably affects economic activity and social welfare. Central banks play a central role in ensuring that money effectively fulfils its functions. In effect, central banks are responsible for issuing and distributing fiat money and have as their primary objective to ensure the stability of their purchasing power. Most central banks, too, participate in the regulation of the financial system to ensure that money is protected and manage payment systems so that individuals can carry out all their transactions with agility, security and certainty. In doing so, central banks contribute to creating an environment of trust, which is indispensable for any process of sustainable economic growth. 5 Allow me to detail the progress that we at the Bank of Mexico have recently made in each of these functions. On the one hand, the Bank of Mexico has the obligation to provide the economy with national currency. In our country, the quarterly surveys of the central bank reveal that, regardless of whether you use other means of payment, 96% of the population usually uses cash. In this sense, it is important to provide the public with the means of payment used and, therefore, the Bank of Mexico has sought to offer the population both the best banknotes and coins and the most agile and efficient means of payment, so that users can choose those that most adequately meet their specific requirements. In this regard, last month, on November 12 and 19, the denominations corresponding to 100 and 1000 pesos of the new family of banknotes were presented, which contain elements that guarantee their greater security and durability, as well as a renewed design that alludes to our historical identity and natural heritage. It is worth mentioning the institutional effort involved, in a context of pandemic, to make these two denominations available to the population. 6 In addition to meeting the demand for cash, the Bank of Mexico promotes the healthy development of the financial system and the access of more and more segments of the population to the benefits of this system. This greater inclusion is now becoming more viable, thanks to the technological revolution, which has allowed financial activities to continue operating remotely, efficiently and safely during the pandemic. Therefore, it is appropriate to observe this situation, as a call to consolidate the use of new technologies to provide a greater range of services and, above all, to include the majority in this area. In addition, in the face of the pandemic, the Bank of Mexico has taken specific measures to promote the stability and orderly functioning of financial markets, as well as to protect the interests and well-being of users. With regard to the aim of promoting the proper functioning of the payment system, the Bank of Mexico, taking advantage of technological advances, has promoted an efficient, expeditious and expeditious payment scheme. 7 low cost, which is the CoDi. This scheme allows anyone who owns a smartphone and opens a bank account to make electronic payments 24 hours a day safely and free of charge. Apart from its impact on efficiency and cost reduction, the CoDi is an instrument of inclusion and contributes to familiarize the user with digital services in the financial system. Dear contestants and friends: The finalist works approached the theme established this year "The Bank of Mexico and your money" with a sharp capacity for analysis, with an accessible and pedagogical style and, sometimes, with inventiveness and sense of humor. Everyone agrees that money is a complex and delicate ecosystem and that the central bank is at the center of it. Therefore, they agree on the importance of the central bank providing national currency, protecting its purchasing power, and promoting the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of payment systems. For the Bank of Mexico it is very significant to share this space for reflection with the new generations of students who, in the future, 8 very close, they will have to unfold their vocation and exert their influence and talent on society. Therefore, I thank you again for your participation and initiative and I congratulate you for the excellence of your work that, as usual, posed a difficult dilemma for our juries. Congratulations.
text_original: 1 Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la presentacin del Premio Contacto Banxico 2020. Ciudad de Mxico, 3 de diciembre de 2020 Me da mucho gusto saludarlos en la presentacin del Premio Contacto Banxico 2020, espero que todos ustedes y los suyos se encuentren con salud y buen nimo. Hemos vivido un ao atpico, lleno de desafos y, por eso, valoro especialmente el esfuerzo y la disciplina de los estudiantes que participaron en la edicin 2020 de este certamen. *** El Premio Contacto Banxico fue creado hace 12 aos para acercar al Banco de Mxico al segmento de educacin media superior e incentivar a profesores y estudiantes de ese nivel a conocer las finalidades y operacin del banco central, as como los beneficios que su labor genera a la sociedad. Este concurso es una de las herramientas ms antiguas y exitosas del programa de educacin financiera de Banco de Mxico y, durante su vigencia, se han inscrito ms de 50 mil personas de todos los estados de la Repblica y hemos revisado ms de 6 mil 500 trabajos. 2 Hasta el ao pasado, los participantes formaban equipos de tres o cuatro alumnos y un profesor de su misma institucin para la elaboracin de un trabajo escrito o un video, sobre el tema de economa que se propone en cada edicin. El dinero es una referencia de valor que facilita su traslado, aceptacin y registro. En nuestros das, el dinero adquiere las ms diversas modalidades, desde el papel moneda hasta un depsito bancario o una transferencia electrnica realizada desde un telfono mvil. La confianza en la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo del dinero permite que ste sea una referencia eficaz a lo largo del tiempo y que cumpla adecuadamente sus funciones como medio de pago, unidad de cuenta y almacn de valor. As, cuando existe confianza en la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo del dinero es posible facilitar el comercio, hacer una planeacin econmica y financiera con un horizonte temporal ms amplio, dirigir los recursos de manera ms eficaz, emprender proyectos de largo plazo con mayor 4 derrama social y proteger de mejor modo los ingresos y el patrimonio de los ciudadanos. En cambio, cuando el pblico percibe que el dinero puede sufrir mermas en su poder adquisitivo, se propicia un ambiente de incertidumbre e inestabilidad que afecta considerablemente la actividad econmica y el bienestar social. Los bancos centrales desempean un papel medular para que el dinero cumpla eficazmente sus funciones. En efecto, los bancos centrales son los encargados de emitir y distribuir el dinero fiduciario y tienen como objetivo primordial procurar la estabilidad de su poder adquisitivo. La mayora de los bancos centrales, tambin, participan en la regulacin del sistema financiero para garantizar que el dinero se encuentre protegido y administran los sistemas de pagos para que los individuos puedan realizar con agilidad, seguridad y certeza todas sus transacciones. Con ello, los bancos centrales contribuyen a crear un ambiente de confianza, indispensable para cualquier proceso de crecimiento econmico sostenible. 5 Permtanme, detallar el avance que, en el Banco de Mxico, hemos logrado recientemente en cada una de estas funciones. *** Por un lado, el Banco de Mxico tiene la obligacin de proveer a la economa de moneda nacional. En nuestro pas, las encuestas trimestrales del banco central revelan que, independientemente de que utilice otros medios de pago, el 96% de la poblacin acostumbra usar efectivo. En este sentido, es importante proveer al pblico los medios de pago que utiliza y, por ello, el Banco de Mxico ha buscado ofrecer a la poblacin tanto los mejores billetes y monedas como los medios de pago ms giles y eficaces, a fin de que los usuarios elijan los que ms adecuadamente satisfacen sus requerimientos especficos. Cabe destacar el esfuerzo institucional que implic, en un contexto de pandemia, poner a disposicin de la poblacin estas dos denominaciones. 6 *** En adicin a la satisfaccin de la demanda de efectivo, el Banco de Mxico promueve el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el acceso de cada vez ms segmentos de la poblacin a los beneficios de dicho sistema. Esta mayor inclusin se hace ms viable ahora, gracias a la revolucin tecnolgica, la cual ha permitido que, durante la pandemia, las actividades financieras sigan funcionando de manera remota, eficiente y segura. Por eso, conviene observar esta coyuntura, como un llamado a consolidar el uso de las nuevas tecnologas para proveer una mayor gama de servicios y, sobre todo, para incluir a las mayoras en este mbito. Adems, ante la pandemia, el Banco de Mxico ha tomado medidas especficas para promover la estabilidad y el funcionamiento ordenado de los mercados financieros, as como para proteger los intereses y el bienestar de los usuarios. *** En lo que atae a la finalidad de propiciar el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos, el Banco de Mxico, aprovechando los avances tecnolgicos, ha impulsado un esquema de pagos eficiente, expedito y 7 de bajo costo, que es el CoDi. Este esquema permite a cualquiera que tenga un telfono inteligente y abra una cuenta bancaria realizar pagos electrnicos las 24 horas del da de manera segura y gratuita. Estimados concursantes y amigos: Los trabajos finalistas abordaron el tema establecido este ao El Banco de Mxico y tu dinero con una aguda capacidad de anlisis, con un estilo accesible y pedaggico y, en ocasiones, con inventiva y sentido del humor. Todos concuerdan en que el dinero constituye un complejo y delicado ecosistema y en que el banco central se encuentra en el centro de ste. Por eso, coinciden en la importancia de que el banco central provea moneda nacional, protegiendo su poder adquisitivo, y promueva el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Para el Banco de Mxico es muy significativo compartir este espacio de reflexin con las nuevas generaciones de estudiantes que, en un futuro 8 muy prximo, habrn de desplegar su vocacin y ejercer su influencia y talento sobre la sociedad. Por eso, les agradezco nuevamente su participacin e iniciativa y los felicito por la excelencia de sus trabajos que, como es habitual, plantearon un difcil dilema para nuestros jurados. Enhorabuena.

Title: 480th anniversary of the Mexican Mint and the opening of the exhibition: Paper stories: the banknote in Mexico
text: 1 REMARKS BY MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, DURING THE 480TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE MEXICAN MINT AND THE INAUGURATION OF THE EXHIBITION "PAPER STORIES: THE BANKNOTE IN MEXICO" AT THE NATIONAL NUMISMATIC MUSEUM. Mexico City, May 11, 2015 Mr. Guillermo Hopkins Gamez General Director of the Mexican Mint Dr. Luis Madrazo Lajous Head of the Economic Planning Unit of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit Dr. Alejandra Moreno Toscano General Coordinator of the Historic Center Authority Ladies and gentlemen It is an honor for me to participate in the celebration of the 480th anniversary of the Mexican Mint in these historic facilities of the old Mint, which today guard the National Numismatic Museum. In this beautiful property, dating from 2 At the beginning of the seventeenth century, the so-called "apartado" was carried out, a process by which gold was separated from the silver extracted from the mines. Now we can see that this building, listed in 1931 as a historical monument, has been transformed into a modern and dynamic museum. I would like to express a very particular thanks to the General Director of the Mint of Mexico, Mr. Guillermo Hopkins, for his attentive invitation both to participate in this event, and to have a space in this enclosure so that the Bank of Mexico can share with all of you and the general public, a part of its Numismatic Collection. It is worth mentioning that this Collection historically documents the issuance of banknotes and coins in Mexico from their appearance to the present day. At present, the Collection has about 60 thousand pieces, including coins, medals, banknotes and specimens, both national and foreign. That is why it has been recognized as the most important in the country, not only for the number of pieces that make it up, but for the quality and rarity of many of them. 3 The exhibition "Paper Stories" that the Bank of Mexico presents, is an ideal complement to the collections of this Museum. The metallic coin is a very old means of payment. However, the widespread use of paper money dates back to the modern era, and in general its process of evolution and social acceptance has been more complex. Mexico has been no exception. Thus, unlike the silver, viceregal and republican coins, which circulated throughout the world and had great roots, the paper money that began to be used in our country during the nineteenth century faced, at first, reluctance among the population. In fact, it was not until 1925, with the founding of the Bank of Mexico and the determination that it was the sole issuer of currency, when the foundations were laid to give credibility to the banknote as a means of payment in our country. With the presentation of a sample of banknotes from the collection of the Numismatic Collection of the Bank of Mexico in this Museum, the viewer will be able to make an interesting tour that begins with the emergence of paper money in Mexico, that is, with the so-called 4 cartons of San Miguel el Grande of 1813, the Iturbidista paper money and the Republican banknote of 1823, just reached the National Independence. You can also admire the variety and beauty of the first banknotes put into circulation during the second half of the nineteenth century and the first years of the twentieth; as well as the maelstrom of revolutionary issues, until concluding with the different families of banknotes of the Bank of Mexico, both those printed by the American Bank Note Company of New York, and those produced in Mexico, by the Banknote Factory of the Central Institute itself, inaugurated in 1969. With this exhibition, the public will be able to learn more about Mexico's banknotes, and will be able to approach our past and present from new perspectives. Likewise, I am sure that the Mint of Mexico and the Bank of Mexico will continue to work on joint projects for cultural and scientific promotion, which generate debate and reflection around our coins and banknotes of yesterday and today, and thus contribute to expand and diversify the numismatic horizon of Mexico. 5 In closing, I just want to reiterate my sincere thanks to the directors and staff of the Mexican Mint for their hospitality, and express my sincere congratulations on this 480th anniversary of the institution. Thanks a lot.

Title: Presentation of the book: Corporate social responsibility of Dr. Alejandra Olay Cheu
text: Presentation of the book "Corporate Social Responsibility" by Dr. Alejandra Olay Cheu By Jonathan Heath Intervention held at the Escuela Libre de Derecho January 16, 2020 I would like to thank Dr. Alejandra Olay Cheu for her invitation to participate in the presentation of her book, "Corporate Social Responsibility". This issue is of vital importance for the sustainable development of any society where free enterprise is a basic element of its organization. In the first part of my speech I will talk about the book's contributions to this topic. In addition, this presentation is an opportunity for me to comment in the second part of my speech on the achievements that the Bank of Mexico has had as a socially responsible institution and the benefits that this has brought to Mexican society. Reflections on the book Corporate Social Responsibility Reading it and having talked with Alejandra about the reasons that led her to write it and what her contributions are to the subject, I realized that the book offers a very useful vision, not only for professionals in the business world but also for public policy makers. It addresses essential elements for the implementation of these principles in the organizational scheme of the company, as well as in its incentives. First of all, professionals in the financial world, and I would say anyone else involved in a company, should read this book, as it gives a clear vision on the subject of corporate social responsibility, which is subject to many prejudices and misconceptions. For example, corporate social responsibility seems to encompass two concepts that in principle are alien but in reality are not. Originally, social responsibility was thought to be a concept whose implications were alien to the company. It is thought that companies seek to maximize their profits and avoid any loss of value. In this sense, what are the incentives of the company to implement socially responsible actions that are not profitable? In my perspective, the 1 The most important contribution of the book is that it shows that social responsibility has a positive and direct impact on the operational efficiency of companies and their governance. Alejandra shows us that social responsibility is profitable for the company because its benefits are greater than its costs, so there are positive incentives for its adoption. The benefits of corporate social responsibility go beyond an improvement in image and a revaluation of the brand, although this in itself would already be an additional advantage for the business sector in our country. There are benefits in the efficiency of operation and reduction of future costs by adopting the principles of social responsibility, as the company anticipates a regulation that sooner or later will be imposed, which could be more expensive later. For example, adopting pro-environmental practices prevents future payment of environmental damage mitigation measures that prove to be very costly. In the same way, the adoption of these principles increases its competitiveness since they are a distinctive to comply with rules that could not only be imperative in the national context, but also in the scope of other markets where the company wishes to expand. Finally, social responsibility helps to reduce negative externalities caused by companies and contribute to a more just, equitable and responsible society. Corporate social responsibility has been gradually adopted resulting in a combination of norms where some have been self-imposed and others come from the State. In many situations custom becomes law. In the case of social responsibility, its adoption has begun as a practice within companies, which results in principles and norms that are adopted as standards in the industry and that in some cases become law. In the end, the regulatory framework turns out to be a hybrid between what companies impose themselves on themselves and what regulatory bodies demand. A good example is the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, which are standards for companies issued by the Mexican Institute of Public Accountants, a private association, which the country's legal framework adopts to make them mandatory for companies. 2 Considering these lessons from the book, how can companies and financial institutions contribute significantly to the spread of social responsibility? A first contribution is through the implementation of mechanisms where the company faces costs by not aligning with most of these principles. For this, the financial markets have a very powerful tool: the market value of the company. For this mechanism to be effective, transparency and accountability must be strengthened, as well as the design of corporate governance to avoid excessive risk-taking. An example of this was Enron, a company recognized between 1996 and 2001 as the most innovative to market contracts for the purchase and sale of electrical services through the futures market. However, Enron opted for an accounting scheme with the flexibility to under-represent losses in its investment projects, magnify the value of other businesses through a network of satellite companies and remove from its balance sheet elements that would deteriorate its financial position. Despite having corporate governance, its managers acted with discretion. This situation became known at the end of 2001, which led to the bankruptcy of the company after the price per share plummeted to a level of 0.26 US cents, after having reached a maximum above 90 dollars in 2000.1 Not only was there a market punishment when the value of the company was practically reduced to zero, but it also had fundamental ramifications when Arthur Anderson, one of the five most important auditing and accounting firms in the world, disappeared. This was a key lesson to begin to understand that greater transparency, accountability and governance will allow the market to more effectively sanction companies that do not adhere to its principles. A second contribution is the dissemination of investment principles for companies to invest in socially responsible projects. From the 1 Enron became a benchmark in the energy sector in 1999 when it launched an electronic platform to market contracts for the purchase and sale of electricity services through the futures market. Enron founded a network of intermediary companies to generate new capital inflow to manage risks associated with specific assets. Legally it had a corporate governance defined by a board of directors with external advisors and supported by an audit committee. In practice, however, the company's leadership lay primarily with the CEO and CFO, who engaged in unethical practices in Enron's financial records. 3 In the past decade, a group of international investors developed the Principles for Responsible Investment (PIR) so that adherent companies incorporated environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into their investment decisions. In environmental matters these principles consider: climate change, greenhouse gas emissions, waste and pollution. In social issues, working conditions (including slavery and child labor), health, safety, and employee relations are considered. Finally, corporate governance is considered executive compensation, bribery and corruption, diversity and structure of boards of directors and tax strategy. In 2005, the UN launched an effort to disseminate these principles and currently there are about 23,000 adherent institutions with more than 80 trillion dollars in management.2 Currently, Mexico only has 5 signatories: Ainda, Energia & Infraestructuras, Discovery Americas and Grupo Financiero Banorte, so the financial community must redouble efforts to disseminate these practices. In parallel, since 2015 the Association of Banks of Mexico has created a sustainability protocol to promote the financing of environmentally sustainable projects.3 A third contribution is the creation of special financing vehicles for socially responsible projects and for the companies that implement them. For example, green bonds are a financing vehicle for sustainable projects. In 2016, the first issuance of these instruments was carried out by Nacional Financiera for the financing of wind farms in Oaxaca.4 Additionally, in 2018 the principles of Green Bonds MX of the Green Finance Advisory Council (CCFV)5 were developed, where the adherents commit that a 2 For more information see 3 The protocol has 5 principles: 1) Establish an internal policy, with the support of the Board of Directors and a sustainability committee should be formed. 2) Management of environmental and social risks in investment or credit processes. 3) Promote the financing of projects that promote environmental and social sustainability. 4) A corporate policy that integrates the principles of sustainability in internal operations and 5) Monitoring and dissemination of the union's sustainability practices and policies. Include a sustainability section in the annual report. 4 The issuance of this bond was for 500 million for a five-year term. 5 The Advisory Board represents more than 300 organizations and was created in 2016 in response to the growing need to develop a sustainable financial market in Mexico with a true long-term vision. The CCFV is especially focused on raising awareness regarding national vulnerability to the impacts of climate change; since it is located between two oceans, it is exposed to climate disasters and sea level rise. 4 Green bond has an opinion from a third party on the environmental impact of the projects for which the resources are allocated. Similarly, principles have also been developed for green credits for projects that have a favourable impact on the environment. Actions of the Bank of Mexico as a socially responsible institution Finally, when reading the book, I thought about the state-business synergy that Alejandra highlights in her book. While the Bank of Mexico is not a private entity, I would like to take the opportunity to share the Bank's experience in this regard to point out how a financial institution, even in the public sphere, can contribute to social responsibility. Although the Bank of Mexico does not have the "Socially Responsible Company" (ESR) distinction6 since its focus is mainly on private sector companies, institutional efforts have been made in labor, accountability and environmental matters, so the Bank's main contribution in this area has been to lead by example. The Governing Board of the Bank has worked hard to maintain an environment of labor equality and non-discrimination within the institution, which has led it to be a reference in this area. In 2017, the Bank of Mexico was the first central bank in the world to obtain the "Economic Dividends for Gender Equality" certification, known as EDGE.7 Similarly, last year the Bank obtained the certification of the "Mexican Standard on Labor Equality and Non-Discrimination" (NMX).8 These certifications are the product of endless efforts such as the creation of the Labor Equality and Non-Discrimination Committee, 9 which is a consultative and advisory body of the Governing Board, in charge of monitoring the implementation of policies and practices for labor equality and non-discrimination in the Bank of Mexico and is composed of employees in a representative manner in terms of gender, areas and hierarchical levels.10 Between 6 This distinction is awarded by the Mexican Center for Philanthropy, A.C. (Cemefi) and the Alliance for Corporate Social Responsibility (AliarSE). To see a list of the companies that have this badge consult 7 This certification that was renewed in November of last year with effect until 2021. 8 On 16 July 2019, the Bank obtained certification for 4 years. 9 On 25 July 2018, the Governing Board of banco de Mexico adopted the "Agreement on the creation, integration and functioning of the Banco de Mexico's Committee on Labour Equality and Non-Discrimination". The Committee was created on August 28, 2018. 10 Within its powers, the Committee has the functions of: 1) Proposing standards and Policy on Labor Equality and Non-Discrimination, 2) Integrating the institutional communication strategy on labor equality and 3) following up on the commitments to achieve, among others. 5 I would like to highlight the research agenda on women's economic empowerment, the implementation of measures that allow a life-work balance and systematic analysis to ensure equal pay between men and women. We also have strong advances in areas of non-discrimination such as the recognition and acceptance of the LGBT community and hiring policies free of bias as well as the inclusion of people with different abilities in our workforce. Banco de Mexico also maintains a strong commitment to transparency and accountability. We think this is essential to gain the trust of society. The Open Government metric carried out by CIDE in 2018 distinguished us as the best autonomous body in terms of transparency. Since 2017, the Bank has been recognized by the National Institute for Access to Information (INAI) as a one hundred percent institution trained in transparency and personal data. Since 2018, the Bank has obtained the rating of 100% in compliance with the transparency obligations on the internet portal as well as the first places in the awards for innovation in transparency and good practices in the handling of personal data.11 In addition, the Bank has also imposed stricter rules than those established by law. An example of this is that in 2019 the Bank responded to requests for information at a time well below the deadline set by law. For these and other actions, the Bank of Mexico has been a benchmark in terms of transparency, even at the international level, since other central banks have approached them to share their experience. In environmental matters, the Bank of Mexico has also maintained a deep sense of social responsibility by obtaining clean industry certifications, by extending the life cycle of some banknotes, by carrying out environmental impact studies, as well as by maintaining actions aimed at recycling part of the material used in the manufacture of banknotes. Since 2012, the banknote factory in the Legaria Complex is certified as 11 In 2018, the Bank of Mexico received, from INAI, the 2nd. place in the "Award for Innovation and Good Practices in the Protection of Personal Data 2018". In 2019 Banco de Mexico obtained the 3rd place in the "Innovation in Transparency Award in 2019", by the INAI. 6 Clean Industry at the highest level granted by the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection (PROFEPA) to organizations that demonstrate compliance with current environmental legislation.12 In the manufacture of banknotes, for almost 20 years, the Bank began the replacement of cotton substrate by polymer in banknotes of 20 and 50 pesos which doubles its average life in circulation, in order to require the manufacture and distribution of fewer banknotes, with the aim of reducing environmental impacts.13 The Bank has also carried out environmental impact assessments on the life cycle of banknotes, from their manufacture to their final disposal for the design of strategies that mitigate the environmental impact, evaluations that have only been carried out by four central banks in the world (Canada, United Kingdom, European Union and Switzerland). For this reason, in 2016, the Bank was invited to participate in the LCInitiative (Life Cycle Initiative) project, promoted by the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) and the Society of Toxicology and Environmental Chemistry (SETAC), being the only participating Central Bank. Finally, since 2015 the destroyed polymer banknotes are reused to manufacture items such as plastic canisters and cleaning supplies. This has reduced the pollution to the soil, water and air that the Bank generates in its manufacturing and distribution processes of national currency. In conclusion, I consider that this book is a significant contribution to the dissemination of the topic of social responsibility, not only for entrepreneurs and professionals in the financial world, but for all those directly or indirectly involved with the business world and its impact on social welfare. It is also a reminder of what each of us, from our respective trenches, can do. Congratulations Alejandra for this book and I leave you with my widest recommendation that you read it and we all join this new guideline of social responsibility. 12 This recognition is renewed every two years and is currently in force with Environmental Performance Level 2. 13 In 2002 the denomination of 20 pesos was issued in polymer and in 2006 that of 50 pesos. Similarly, the Bank has also sought to extend the useful life of banknotes made with cotton substrate using high durability materials that repel dirt. 7

Una primera contribucin es mediante la implementacin de mecanismos donde la empresa enfrenta costos al no alinearse a la mayora de estos principios. Pese a contar con un gobierno corporativo, sus directivos actuaron con discrecionalidad. Esta fue una leccin clave para empezar a entender que una mayor transparencia, rendicin de cuentas y gobernanza permitir que el mercado sancione de manera ms efectiva a las empresas que no se apeguen a sus principios. Una segunda contribucin, es la difusin de principios de inversin para que las empresas inviertan en proyectos socialmente responsables. Desde la 1 Enron, se convirti en un referente del sector energtico en 1999 cuando lanz una plataforma electrnica para comercializar contratos de compra y venta de servicios elctricos mediante el mercado de futuros. Sin embargo, en la prctica la conduccin de la empresa yaca principalmente en el CEO y CFO, quienes incurrieron en prcticas antiticas en los registros financieros de Enron. 3 dcada pasada un grupo de inversionistas internacionales elaboraron los Principios de Inversin Responsable (PIR) a fin de que las empresas adherentes incorporaran factores ambientales, sociales y de gobierno corporativo (ASG) en sus decisiones de inversin. Title: US-Mexico Chamber of Commerce Good Neighbor Awards
text: Remarks by Agustin Carstens, Governor of Banco de Mexico at the US-Mexico Chamber of Commerce Good Neighbor Awards Washington D.C., May 12, 2011 Mr. Al Zapanta, Chairman Ben Bernanke, Governor Enrique Pena Nieto It is an honor and a pleasure to be here tonight, at the US-Mexico Chamber of Commerce 2011 Good Neighbor Award event. At the outset, I would like to commend the US-Mexico Chamber of Commerce, and in particular its heart and soul, Al Zapanta, for its unrelenting effort to bring our two great nations together, promoting always cooperation and fair trade. Also, I would like to thank the Chamber for having chosen me as one of the recipients of this years Public Sector Award. It is particularly meaningful for me to receive it together with Chairman Bernanke, an 1 outstanding economist, exemplary public servant and Chairman of the Federal Reserve System (Fed). I have to say that Chairman Bernanke has done a phenomenal job during the last years in steering the US economy through extremely turbulent waters, fostering at the same the recovery of world economic growth and the return to stability in international financial markets. We all have been extremely fortunate to have Ben as Chairman of the Fed precisely at the time when the US has been bravely tackling its most severe economic challenge of the last 80 years. I tend to believe that the award that both Chairman Bernanke and I are receiving is meant more than anything to celebrate the very close cooperation and collaboration that has characterized the relationship between the Fed and Banco de Mexico for decades. This relationship between both central banks goes back to at least 85 years, pretty much since the foundation of Banco de Mexico in 1925. As a matter of fact, the original chapter of Banco de Mexico was drafted having as benchmark the Feds one. Banco de Mexico throughout the years has received many technical assistance missions from the Fed, and several of our officials have 2 been trained at the Fed. From a more substantive point of view, Mexico has benefited from multiple swap agreements that both central banks have subscribed since 1941. These arrangements have provided timely financial support to Mexico during different episodes we have faced balance-of-payments problems, and more recently when some discontinuities appeared in the international financial system, not related to specific problems attributable to Mexico. The financial support we received from the Fed through these means has been invaluable for the adoption of corrective macroeconomic policies and to regain access to capital markets. Let me illustrate the evolving nature of the cooperation between the Fed and Banco de Mexico, as the Mexican economy has become more resilient and less prone to crisis. As a result of the daunting financial crisis of 20082009, an unprecedented shortage of US-Dollar liquidity erupted that, if left unattended, was threatening the ongoing crisis to escalate. This evolution would have had disastrous consequences for the world economy and trade. Under such circumstances, the Fed offered several central banks of strategic importance, among them Banco de Mexico, temporary currency arrangements. The swap mechanism for 3 Mexico was set for up to US30 billion, of which Mexico only accessed US3.2 billion, resources that by early 2010 were already fully paid. This temporary facility offered by the Fed was essential to kick-start the world US-Dollar credit market, thereby eliminating a bottleneck that was choking world trade and economic growth. I do not want to leave you with the impression that cooperation between the Fed and Banco de Mexico has only flourished in times of crises. In October 2004, the Fed and Banco de Mexico connected the payments system of both countries. The end result of this cooperative action was that Mexicans living and working in the US can now send money to their families in a safer and timelier manner, at a noticeable lower cost that the one they had to pay before the direct connection between our payments systems was established. Ladies and gentlemen, Mexico is emerging from this period of hardship for the world economy with renewed strengths. I venture to say that Mexico is one of the few G20 member countries who: 4 1) Performed a fiscal adjustment in 2009, has kept its fiscal accounts pretty much in line, and has not seen a substantial increase in its debt/GDP ratio, as it has stayed close to 35% of GDP. 2) Did not face the need to implement unconventional monetary policy measures, and kept at the same time inflation under control. 3) Has preserved a strong and well-capitalized banking system, with the capacity to contribute importantly to economic growth. 4) Has a strong balance-of-payments situation, with exports growing more than 20%, attracting substantial amounts of foreign capital and with record-high levels of international reserves. This has been complemented by access to an unconditional Flexible Credit Line (FCL) of US73 billion with the International Monetary Fund (IMF). This credit line has the added benefit that represents a strong commitment by President Calderons Administration to preserve a solid macroeconomic framework for the coming 20 months. These conditions allowed 2010 to be a good year for the Mexican economy, as we experienced a much higher rate of economic growth than originally forecasted, 5.5% vs. 3.0%, and lower inflation. This combination, i.e. higher growth and less inflation, is likely to be 5 repeated in 2011. As a matter of fact, for the first time in several years the Mexican economy in 2011 will growth at a faster rate than Brazils. On the other hand, we also expect a continued recovery of the US economy, as private sector expenditure and net exports pick up steam. For all these reasons both of our economies will benefit, particularly if we take advantage of the actual situation to further deepen collaboration and cooperation between Mexico and the US at all levels, for the well-being of both the American and Mexican people. Thank you very much. 6

Title: Delivery of the Contact Banxico Award, 2021
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of the Banxico Contact Award, 2021.1 Mexico City, December 2, 2021 Introduction I am very pleased to participate in the delivery of the Thirteenth Edition of the Contacto Banxico Award. This is a national contest aimed at high school students, which was conceived to meet 3 primary objectives. First, as a vehicle to bring the Bank of Mexico closer to society, particularly the population of upper secondary education. This segment is very important, as they are at the stage of imminent choice of their professional career, as well as on the threshold of their civilian life. Second, to encourage teachers and students at the baccalaureate level to know the purposes, priority objective and operation of the Bank 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 of Mexico. The idea is to raise awareness of the social and economic importance of the central bank's objectives. Third, it is a natural channel for the dissemination of the material that the Bank of Mexico produces in the field of financial disclosure and education. Trajectory and change of format to virtual and individual. This contest is one of several financial education products that the Bank of Mexico has created for young people and, in its 13 years of existence, has obtained wide recognition and popularity in the academic and student population at the baccalaureate level. Since its creation in 2009, public and private schools from all the States of the Republic have participated, more than 11,000 teams have registered and more than 6,600 proposals (written works or videos) have been reviewed. Since last 2020, when participation was modified to become individual, we have had 1990 registered. The participants traditionally formed teams of three or four students and a teacher from the same institution for the elaboration of 2 a written work or a video, on some topic of economics that is proposed in each edition. Since the 2020 edition derived from the health contingency and to promote healthy distance, the call was launched individually and 100% online in all its stages. The categories written work and video were maintained, and the participation of teacher advice was eliminated to give opportunity to high school participants of the open system. Theme of the 2021 edition. The theme that was assigned for this thirteenth edition was "The Bank of Mexico and economic-financial decision-making in the face of unexpected circumstances". In particular, it was expected that, from this thematic line, the participants would identify how the work of the Bank of Mexico can contribute to maintaining the right economic and financial conditions and facilitate people, companies and government, decision-making, even in circumstances with unexpected challenges. 3 Indeed, the priority objective of maintaining price stability enables people to make better financial decisions about their future. Similarly, the Bank of Mexico seeks, together with other authorities, financial stability and the efficiency of financial and payment systems. This allows people to have stronger savings, credit and investment options and to be able to transact quickly, safely and at low cost, in real time and at any time. The COVID-19 pandemic has been one of the most important challenges the world has faced in this century. This health emergency changed the economy, forms of work, forms of socialization and all aspects of the daily lives of millions of people across the globe. In this environment, the work of a central bank as a driver and guarantor of price and financial stability is essential for society to have the certainty that its resources will retain its purchasing power and that it will be able to continue to carry out, remotely, its essential economic operations. 4 In the case of our country, the Bank of Mexico took the necessary measures to deal with the COVID-19 crisis and adjusted its monetary policy stance to promote an orderly adjustment of the markets and the economy and seek the convergence of inflation with its target. Thus, Mexicans maintained at all times the certainty that the money they used would fully maintain its functions as a generally accepted means of payment, as a safeguard of value and as a reliable reference to set the prices of the economy. This helped mitigate the effects they faced, giving greater confidence to decision-making. Similarly, even in the strictest stages of social distancing, the financial and payment systems maintained their operational continuity. One of the keys to be able to continue with this essential activity was technology. On the one hand, financial institutions have deepened their adoption of digitalization, which limits costs and expands their coverage possibilities. On the other hand, more and more people, particularly young people, are venturing into the digital world, but, in the face of the emergency, even older generations 5 began to conduct their operations online. For example, in 2020 the number of operations of the general public in the SPEI (excluding operations between financial institutions) amounted to 1,070 million operations of which 885 million were less than 8,000 pesos. For its part, between January and October 2021, 1,445 million operations have been carried out, of which 1,253 million were less than 8,000 pesos. As for the amount operated by the general public, in 2020 this figure reached 106.1 billion pesos, of which 1.4 billion pesos were from operations less than 8,000 pesos. Between January and October 2021, the amount operated was 97.5 billion pesos, of which 1.8 billion corresponded to operations of less than 8,000 pesos. Thus, more and more citizens are adopting digital instruments to carry out their daily operations. Hence the importance of bridging the gap between those who have access to and not to technology and the imperative to promote financial inclusion. 6 The activity of the Bank of Mexico to support the operational continuity of the institutions and support the population in the face of the damages of the crisis was also significant. On the one hand, the bank established various administrative and regulatory facilities so that financial institutions could continue their activity and, on the other, it made available liquidity options to strengthen credit channels, especially for medium and small companies. The set of approved actions contemplated support for up to 750 billion pesos (equivalent to 3.3% of GDP in 2019). In short, during the complex environment of the health emergency, the Bank of Mexico contributed significantly to generating a climate of stability and certainty, which contributed to mitigating the economic effects of the pandemic and made it possible for citizens to make better decisions. Results Responding to the call with the theme already indicated, this year 1064 people registered (15% more registered than the previous year) from 28 States of the Republic and we received 609 entries. Distribution 7 by gender was 55% women, 44% men and 1% people who preferred not to indicate their gender. The registration and selection process is important because it ratifies the transparency and impartiality that has given prestige and credibility to the award. Students register from the Prize platform, which protects their data and provides them with a folio to maintain anonymity before the Jury. On the same platform, they answer a questionnaire on economic issues and attach their work or video, which in the contest rules are called "entries". The members of the Jury review around 150 entries, selected. The 10 best averages of each category (semifinalists) have an interaction session with the Jury (10-minute interview), from which the 5 finalists are selected and, subsequently, the winner of each category. Fellow participants: It is a pleasure to meet young students who, from a very early age, commit their intelligence, prospective vision and dynamism in 8 the study of crucial issues so that in the future we have a better country. As always, the large quantity and quality of the works received put the jury in trouble, to whom we thank for their generosity and professionalism. Most of the works combine analytical seriousness and expository freshness and spread enthusiasm and optimism. Therefore, I welcome the great pool of talent we have in our most recent generations and congratulate all the participants and, of course, our finalists and winners. 9

Tema de la edicin 2021. El tema que se asign para esta treceava edicin fue El Banco de Mxico y la toma de decisiones econmico-financieras frente a circunstancias inesperadas. En particular, se esperaba que, a partir de esta lnea temtica, los participantes identificaran cmo el quehacer del Banco de Mxico puede contribuir a mantener las condiciones econmicas y financieras adecuadas y facilitar a las personas, empresas y gobierno, la toma de decisiones, incluso en circunstancias con retos inesperados. 3 En efecto, el objetivo prioritario de mantener la estabilidad de precios permite a las personas tomar mejores decisiones financieras sobre su futuro. De igual manera, el Banco de Mxico procura, junto con otras autoridades, la estabilidad financiera y la eficiencia de los sistemas financieros y de pagos. Ello permite que las personas cuenten con opciones de ahorro, crdito e inversin ms slidas y que puedan realizar transacciones de manera rpida, segura y a bajo costo, en tiempo real y a cualquier hora. La pandemia del COVID-19 ha sido uno de los retos ms importantes que ha enfrentado el mundo en este siglo. Esta emergencia sanitaria cambi la economa, las formas de trabajo, las modalidades de socializacin y todos los aspectos de la vida cotidiana de millones de personas a lo largo de todo el planeta. En este entorno, la labor de un banco central como impulsor y garante de la estabilidad de precios y financiera es fundamental para que la sociedad tenga la certidumbre de que sus recursos conservarn su poder adquisitivo y de que podr seguir realizando, de manera remota, sus operaciones econmicas esenciales. 4 En el caso de nuestro pas, el Banco de Mxico tom las medidas necesarias para hacer frente a la crisis del COVID-19 y ajust su postura de poltica monetaria para propiciar un ajuste ordenado de los mercados y la economa y procurar la convergencia de la inflacin con su meta. As, los mexicanos mantuvieron en todo momento la certeza de que el dinero que usaban mantendra plenamente sus funciones como medio de pago generalmente aceptado, como resguardo de valor y como referencia confiable para fijar los precios de la economa. Eso contribuy a mitigar las afectaciones que se enfrentaban, dando mayor confianza a la toma de decisiones. Igualmente, aun en las etapas ms estrictas del distanciamiento social, los sistemas financiero y de pagos mantuvieron su continuidad operativa. Una de las claves para poder proseguir con esta actividad esencial fue la tecnologa. Por un lado, las instituciones financieras han profundizado en su adopcin de la digitalizacin, lo que limita costos y ampla sus posibilidades de cobertura. Por otro lado, cada vez ms personas, particularmente los jvenes, incursionan en el mundo digital, pero, ante la emergencia, incluso las generaciones de mayor edad 5 comenzaron a realizar sus operaciones en lnea. Por ejemplo, en 2020 el nmero de operaciones del pblico en general en el SPEI (excluyendo operaciones entre entidades financieras) ascendi a 1,070 millones de operaciones de las cuales 885 millones fueron menores a 8,000 pesos. Por su parte, entre enero y octubre de 2021 se han realizado 1,445 millones de operaciones de las cuales 1,253 millones fueron menores a 8,000 pesos. En cuanto al monto operado por el pblico en general, en 2020 esta cifra alcanz 106.1 billones de pesos, de los cuales 1.4 billones de pesos fueron de operaciones menores a 8,000 pesos. Entre enero y octubre de 2021 el monto operado fue de 97.5 billones de pesos, de los cuales 1.8 billones correspondieron operaciones menores a 8,000 pesos. As, cada vez ms ciudadanos adoptan instrumentos digitales para realizar sus operaciones cotidianas. De ah la importancia de romper la brecha entre los que tienen acceso y no a la tecnologa y el imperativo de promover la inclusin financiera. 6 La actividad del Banco de Mxico para apoyar la continuidad operativa de las instituciones y respaldar a la poblacin ante los perjuicios de la crisis tambin fue significativa. Por un lado, el banco estableci diversas facilidades administrativas y regulatorias para que las instituciones financieras pudieran continuar su actividad y, por el otro, puso a disposicin opciones de liquidez para fortalecer los canales de crdito, especialmente para las medianas y pequeas empresas.
