Title: The operation of monetary policy
text: The operation of monetary policy Words of Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the opening of the First Seminar on Monetary Operations Bank of Mexico and FMI Mexico City October 24, 2016 On behalf of the Bank of Mexico, it is an honor for me to welcome the participants of the First Seminar on Monetary Operations, organized by this central institute with the support of the Regional Center for Technical Assistance for Central America, Panama and the Dominican Republic of the International Monetary Fund. Monetary policy is the core activity of central banks and its operation contributes to creating an environment conducive to economic growth. Therefore, the work of those who perform this task takes on a special relevance with high social impact. Given the complex circumstances facing the world economy, it is essential to discuss monetary policy at the international level. For this reason, the Bank of Mexico has sought to strengthen ties with other central banks, in order to share experiences and identify common challenges. Undoubtedly, this seminar will contribute to a better understanding of these relevant issues. Monetary policy has a high potential when it focuses on achievable objectives. In contrast, if employed in pursuit of other goals, the results can backfire. Some of its capabilities are well known, while others are still in the process of being tested. That's why, for 1 Those of us who are involved in the design and implementation of monetary policy, it is very important to assess modestly what it can and cannot do. Monetary policy is clearly effective in combating inflation. Since the end of the last century there has been a growing consensus on the harmful effect of price instability on the growth and well-being of the population, which has led to focusing the work of central banks to combat this phenomenon. As a result, global inflation has fallen considerably. Beginning in 2007, many advanced countries embarked on unprecedented monetary easing in order to mitigate some of the most pressing effects of the crisis. The provision of liquidity in the midst of the great turbulence was highly effective. However, the subsequent growing expansion aimed at boosting economic growth has had less clear results. On the other hand, prolonged and extraordinary monetary laxity in developed economies could be producing unintended effects, such as distorting asset prices, increasing risks of financial instability, and compromising future control of inflation. Some of these costs may take a certain period to manifest, thus allowing expansionary monetary policies to claim, for the time being, mainly benefits. An objective assessment of possible negative effects will necessarily take time. 2 Likewise, since the crisis, the possibility of central banks acquiring a leading role in safeguarding financial stability has been emphasized. While central institutes can contribute constructively to this objective by participating in the design of an appropriate framework for financial supervision and regulation, monetary policy is not the ideal vehicle for meeting this objective. Overloading monetary policy with goals and responsibilities could lead to eroding the effectiveness of its actions and damaging its credibility. Hence the importance that, those of us who participate in the concrete operation of the central bank, have a realistic vision of the potentials and restrictions of monetary measures. The mandate of the Bank of Mexico Without neglecting other purposes such as the development of the financial system and the proper functioning of payment systems, the Bank of Mexico is committed to its priority mandate, which is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency. Progress in combating inflation has been remarkable. Since last year, there has been a convergence of inflation with the 3 percent target, which is unprecedented in our institutional trajectory. 3 The qualified work of all members of the Bank of Mexico's Directorates-General for Operations and Economic Research has been crucial to this achievement. Of course, we have to be vigilant in safeguarding and consolidating convergence, because it took a long time to achieve it and it would be unfortunate to stop persevering. The seminar In this seminar some of the most distinguished members of the Banco de Mexico team will share with you their knowledge and experience. The program is very rich and comprehensive because it includes both the analysis of fundamental aspects, as well as the relationship between monetary policy and inflation, and the review of operational issues that include financial programming, open market operations and the administration of international reserves. Thus, the participants in this colloquium will be able to identify the analogies and differences between the monetary operation practices of the different countries. The didactic experience will be complemented by two guided tours. On the one hand, to the banknote factory of the Bank of Mexico, where you can observe the cutting-edge processes that are used to make the Mexican banknote a safe medium of exchange and, on the other hand, to the Interactive Museum of Economy (MIDE), which in its facilities and digital platforms, disseminates knowledge of the subject with attractive and innovative methods. 4 Again welcome, it is a pleasure and a privilege to have you here. I hope that this meeting will serve to fruitfully exchange experiences of monetary operations and to support more effectively the fulfillment of the legal mandate of each of the different central institutes represented here. 5
text_original: La operacin de la poltica monetaria Palabras de Manuel Snchez Gonzlez Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico en la apertura del Primer Seminario de Operaciones Monetarias Banco de Mxico y FMI Ciudad de Mxico 24 de octubre de 2016 A nombre del Banco de Mxico es para m un honor dar la bienvenida a los participantes del Primer Seminario de Operaciones Monetarias, organizado por este instituto central con apoyo del Centro Regional de Asistencia Tcnica para Centroamrica, Panam y Repblica Dominicana del Fondo Monetario Internacional. La poltica monetaria constituye la actividad fundamental de los bancos centrales y su operacin contribuye a generar un entorno propicio para el crecimiento econmico. Por eso, la labor de quienes realizan esta tarea cobra una especial relevancia con alto impacto social. Ante las complejas circunstancias que enfrenta la economa mundial resulta indispensable discutir la poltica monetaria a nivel internacional. Por ello, el Banco de Mxico ha buscado fortalecer los lazos con otros bancos centrales, a fin de compartir experiencias e identificar desafos comunes. Sin duda, este seminario contribuir a comprender mejor estos temas relevantes. Los alcances de la poltica monetaria La poltica monetaria tiene un alto potencial cuando se enfoca en objetivos alcanzables. En contraste, si se emplea en la persecucin de otras metas, los resultados pueden ser contraproducentes. Algunas de sus capacidades son bien conocidas, mientras que otras an estn en proceso de comprobacin. Por eso, para 1 quienes participamos en el diseo y la aplicacin de la poltica monetaria, resulta muy importante evaluar con modestia qu es lo que sta puede y no puede hacer. La poltica monetaria es claramente efectiva para combatir la inflacin. Desde finales del siglo pasado ha habido un creciente consenso en torno al efecto nocivo de la inestabilidad de precios sobre el crecimiento y el bienestar de la poblacin, lo que ha conducido a enfocar el quehacer de los bancos centrales a combatir este fenmeno. Gracias a ello, la inflacin mundial ha descendido considerablemente. A partir de 2007, muchos pases avanzados emprendieron un relajamiento monetario sin precedentes con el fin de paliar algunos de los efectos ms apremiantes de la crisis. La provisin de liquidez en medio de la gran turbulencia fue altamente efectiva. Sin embargo, la creciente expansin posterior orientada a impulsar el crecimiento econmico ha tenido resultados menos claros. Por otra parte, la prolongada y extraordinaria laxitud monetaria en las economas desarrolladas podra estar produciendo efectos no deseados, tales como distorsionar los precios de los activos, aumentar los riesgos de inestabilidad financiera, y comprometer el control futuro de la inflacin. Algunos de estos costos pueden llevar un determinado periodo para manifestarse, permitiendo as que las polticas monetarias expansivas puedan reclamar, por lo pronto, principalmente beneficios. Una evaluacin objetiva de posibles efectos negativos necesariamente tomar tiempo. 2 Asimismo, a partir de la crisis se ha enfatizado la posibilidad de que los bancos centrales adquieran un papel protagnico en la salvaguarda de la estabilidad financiera. Si bien los institutos centrales pueden contribuir constructivamente a este objetivo participando en el diseo de un marco adecuado de supervisin y regulacin financiera, la poltica monetaria no es el vehculo idneo para cumplir este objetivo. Sobrecargar de metas y responsabilidades a la poltica monetaria podra llevar a erosionar la efectividad de sus acciones y a daar su credibilidad. De ah la importancia de que, quienes participamos en la operacin concreta de la banca central, tengamos una visin realista de los potenciales y restricciones de las medidas monetarias. El mandato del Banco de Mxico Sin descuidar otras finalidades como el desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos, el Banco de Mxico est comprometido con su mandato prioritario, que es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda. El progreso en el combate de la inflacin ha sido notable. Desde el ao pasado, ha habido una convergencia de la inflacin con el objetivo de 3 por ciento, lo que no tiene precedente en nuestra trayectoria institucional. 3 El trabajo calificado de todos los miembros de las direcciones generales de operaciones y de investigacin econmica del Banco de Mxico ha sido crucial para este logro. Por supuesto, tenemos que estar vigilantes para salvaguardar y consolidar la convergencia, pues tom un largo tiempo alcanzarla y sera lamentable dejar de perseverar. El seminario En este seminario algunos de los ms distinguidos miembros del equipo del Banco de Mxico compartirn con ustedes sus conocimientos y experiencia. El programa es muy rico y completo pues contempla tanto el anlisis de aspectos fundamentales, como la relacin entre poltica monetaria e inflacin, y la revisin de temas operativos que incluyen la programacin financiera, las operaciones de mercado abierto y la administracin de las reservas internacionales. As, los participantes en este coloquio podrn identificar las analogas y las diferencias entre las prcticas de operacin monetaria de los diferentes pases. La experiencia didctica se complementar con dos visitas guiadas. Por un lado, a la fbrica de billetes del Banco de Mxico, donde podrn observar los procesos de punta que se utilizan para hacer el billete mexicano un medio de cambio seguro y, por otro lado, al Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE), que en sus instalaciones y plataformas digitales, difunde el conocimiento de la materia con mtodos atractivos e innovadores. 4 Nuevamente bienvenidos, es un gusto y un privilegio tenerlos aqu. Espero que este encuentro sirva para intercambiar fructferamente experiencias de las operaciones monetarias y apoyar ms eficazmente el cumplimiento del mandato legal de cada uno de los distintos institutos centrales aqu representados. 5

Title: Celebration of the 80th anniversary of El Trimestre Econmico
text: Remarks by the Governor of Banco de Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens during the celebration of the 80th Anniversary of the Economic Quarter. July 31, 2014. First of all, I would like to thank the kind invitation I received from the Fondo de Cultura Economica to participate in the celebration of the first 80 years of the magazine El Trimestre Economico, an academic publication of great prestige and that is the oldest in our country. As conceived by its founders, notably Don Daniel Cosio Villegas, "the quarter" has played a central role in the development of economic science in Mexico and Latin America, and has contributed to the training of several generations of economists. But above all it has been an example of the vitality of economic science, manifested in the diversity and plurality of research works and novel, provocative and stimulating reflections. It should be noted that most of the promoters and founders of El Trimestre Economico were also an important part of the Bank of Mexico in its first years of life, either as founders and members of the first Board of Directors of the Bank - as was the case of Manuel Gomez Morin -, or as directors of the Central Institute - which is the case of 1 Eduardo Villasenor and Gonzalo Robles- or as officials or investigators as happened with Daniel Cosio Villegas. In this way, El Trimestre Economico and the Bank of Mexico established a particular synergy in the promotion of economic research and in the formation of high-quality human capital dedicated to economic policy. In this regard, I would like to take this opportunity to warmly congratulate all those whose work and effort have made it possible for us to meet today celebrating one more anniversary of The Economic Quarter. On this occasion on the occasion of this anniversary, a lecture is given by Professor Kaushik Basu on his book "Beyond the Invisible Hand: Foundations for a New Economy". A book written in an intelligent way that undoubtedly arouses intellectual curiosity. Professor Basu's work is extremely critical while showing great intellectual rigor. It is a book that opens the door to very interesting topics that must be addressed by economists; what better than to do it through magazines like El Trimestre Economico. 2 Indeed, "The Economic Quarter" has always been a forum open to all currents of economic thought and the scene of a fruitful exchange of ideas. As the title of Professor Basu's work suggests, the time would seem to have come to question an approach that has been fundamental in the history of economic thought and that is an important piece of modern economic theory: the paradigm or model of the invisible hand. As we all know, it is a formulation proposed by Adam Smith in the eighteenth century that for his time represented a seminal idea that gave rise to a whole economic current. In short, the theory of the invisible hand postulates that the free competition in the market of a multitude of individuals interested in maximizing their own profit will ultimately yield an efficient and socially optimal result, without resorting to a central planner to make economic decisions. It should be noted, as Professor Basu does, that thanks to the development of economic techniques, primarily mathematical economics, this theory has been formalized giving rise to the so-called first welfare theorem. This formalization is important because it makes it possible to assess more clearly what the conditions are for, in fact, 3 the market system functions as an invisible hand that guides economic agents to an efficient and socially optimal result. This is fundamental, since we cannot pretend to apply the invisible hand theorem to the real world without taking into consideration those conditions that are essential for it to be fulfilled. From the critical tone of Professor Basu's book comes the impression that in undergraduate and graduate economics programs only the theorem and its mathematical derivation are taught, and that this model is then applied dogmatically. However, in my experience as a student and professor, although it is based on this theorem, I would say that in economics programs in practically all universities the vast majority of time is spent finding analytical methods to deal with the consequences that precisely those ideal conditions of the invisible hand are not usually present. It would be a caricature of reality to say that the dominant teaching in economics is restricted to postulating the invisible hand theorem without further critical adjustments or analysis. 4 In this context, I would like to emphasize three points that, personally, I consider fundamental in any analysis of the theorem in question: the role of competitive markets, considerations of fairness and, mainly, the importance of the institutional framework. First, the result of the invisible hand theorem corresponds to a competitive economy, in which each economic agent is small enough that its individual actions do not affect prices in the markets. That is, such agents are price-accepting. However, it is common that in reality we find ourselves with markets in which one participant or a small number of them are large enough to be able to influence prices. In these cases, the behaviour of these actors is strategic in nature and this often leads to inefficient results. Second, when we talk about the invisible hand theorem, we must also take into account the issue of justice or equity. That is, although the market system can lead us to an efficient result, or in technical terms, to a Pareto optimum, it is also true that depending on the initial conditions this result can be one in which 5 High inequality prevails. That is: a socially undesirable outcome. Third, in addition to all of the above, we must take into consideration that the invisible hand theorem does not occur in a vacuum. That is: economic agents interact with each other within the framework of a set of laws, social norms and values that regulate the behavior of the members of society. This is something that we sometimes ignore but that we must always keep in mind. Thus, the institutional framework is crucial for the good performance of economies. As we know, this has helped to explain why some economies have prospered and achieved high levels of well-being while others have lagged behind and have serious poverty problems. As Professor Basu points out, there are laws, social norms and values that facilitate economic growth, but there are also other institutional arrangements that, on the contrary, can hinder growth or make it inequitable. These three examples of deviations from the invisible hand theorem have been widely recognized in the economics profession and studied extensively. Thus, an important contribution that modern economics has made is precisely the analysis and design of mechanisms. 6 to align the incentives faced by economic agents. This is important because individual interests often do not coincide with the interest of society as a whole. In addition to the above and without denying the importance of economic incentives, Professor Basu reminds us that some human behaviors are not necessarily motivated by the personal or private interest of individuals, and that such behaviors can also be key to the good performance of economies. Indeed, values such as honesty and personal integrity, as well as certain social norms, can be decisive for the economic progress of societies. Something that caught my attention powerfully from the book is that its author, although he is critical of neoclassical economics, uses tools of this economic current to illustrate his ideas and hypotheses. For example, throughout the book he recurrently uses game theory to analyze topics such as altruism, trust and the role of law in the economy, among other topics that, indisputably, are relevant and to which we must pay even greater attention in research agendas. As Professor Basu mentions, 7 fortunately, that is what has been happening in recent years. In my opinion, the institutional framework prevailing in a country, including laws, social norms and values, depends on cultural, social and historical factors. Likewise, this framework does not remain immutable through time. On the contrary, societies are dynamic and constantly evolving. In this context, we must further deepen our knowledge of those institutions that are most favourable to economic growth and, above all, of how such institutions can be firmly created and established in a country's economy. This requires multidisciplinary work, in which economists collaborate with professionals from other branches of knowledge. Without a doubt, this is a fascinating topic, which raises many questions and must be taken into account within the research agendas. I hope that many projects will emerge that end up materializing in academic works and, most importantly, that they will be disseminated in prestigious journals such as El Trimestre Economico. As a practical and current conclusion of these considerations I would like to make a further reflection on the application of the 8 theory of the invisible hand. In my opinion, and as I have mentioned, policymakers cannot simply de-regulate markets and expect the economy to automatically perform well and grow at high rates and on a sustained basis. Public policies and economic reforms aimed at creating the institutional conditions are also necessary so that, in effect, the market system can promote an efficient allocation of scarce resources available to the economy. In this way, the role that the State can play in issues ranging from the design and implementation of an anti-monopoly policy that promotes conditions of competition in the markets is fundamental, to a social policy that focuses on addressing the problems of poverty and inequality, through which I consider the three most effective mechanisms of mobility and social promotion: education, health services and the availability of credit, within a framework of macroeconomic stability. The book questions results that emerge from the economic theory formulated from the invisible hand theorem, under the assumption that this theorem and its results are flawed. The main criticism I would make of the book, in this sense, 9 it is to suppose that policymakers faithfully, mechanically and dogmatically follow and apply the ideal postulates of an invisible hand, when precisely those of us who make public policies - and I include myself in the whole thanks to an experience of more than 30 years - do not follow at the foot of the letter this or that theoretical model or the recipe derived from the most recent research paper; on the contrary, the maker of public policies takes advantage of what serves him from the wide and diverse set of technical and theoretical tools learned, draws on his experience and common sense and what he applies surely, in the vast majority of cases, will not be based on the theoretical assumptions of a model or academic research, but in what is feasible and desirable in the face of a dynamic and changing reality. Despite this fact, the references that we find in the bibliography of the commented book are to works and theoretical articles, but references to public documents of the governments of the different countries are missing, which there are and are abundant, where the real considerations that the makers of public policies have taken into account to implement economic policies are addressed. And in my experience of more than 30 years as a maker of economic policies I must say that I have never had to see that theoretical postulates or academic recipes are applied automatically or on foot. 10 While economic models can be extremely useful in this process, the intuition, common sense and good judgment of all those involved in the development and implementation of public policies and economic reforms are of paramount importance. In addition to the above, it is also important the willingness to make changes, as well as the ability to reach agreements between all parties involved, so that such changes can materialize. In this context, I would like to make a final comment on the process of structural transformations that our country is currently experiencing. As we know, an additional incentive for the formulation of structural reforms is the particularly complex external environment facing emerging market economies today, such as Mexico. Reforms, by themselves and by the formidable boost they will give to productivity, are indispensable, but they become even more urgent when considering the need to promote domestic sources of growth that more than compensate for the weakness of external demand. The aim, of course, must be to improve the well-being of the entire population and overcome the many lags that still afflict 11 to millions of Mexicans, and the ideal means to achieve this is to increase total factor productivity. Undoubtedly, Mexico has taken important steps in this direction. Indeed, the package of reforms that has recently been approved by Congress in our country includes reforms in economic competition, telecommunications, labor market, financial sector, energy, public finances and education. These reforms have the potential to encourage resources to be allocated to their most productive uses, as well as to produce goods and services at more accessible prices to the population. Despite the above, it is important to be aware that it is not enough to approve an economic reform for it to bear fruit. A fundamental issue is that these reforms are well designed and, above all, that they are implemented properly. As Professor Basu rightly mentions in his book, it is not enough to change the Law to change people's behaviour. This is something that policymakers must take into consideration when designing and implementing public policies. In this sense, I welcome the publication of works such as Professor Basu's book and the existence of academic journals such as 12 The Economic Quarter, which contribute significantly to the dissemination of economic analysis and, consequently, to improving our understanding of the functioning of the economy. To the extent that this translates into better public policies and appropriate economic reforms, we can achieve higher economic growth, higher employment rates, a more equitable distribution of income, reduce poverty and, in short, achieve a better quality of life for the entire population. Thanks a lot. 13
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador de Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens durante la celebracin del 80 Aniversario de El Trimestre Econmico. 31 de julio de 2014. En primer trmino, me gustara agradecer la amable invitacin que recib del Fondo de Cultura Econmica para participar en la celebracin de los primeros 80 aos de la revista El Trimestre Econmico, una publicacin acadmica de mucho prestigio y que es la de mayor antigedad en nuestro pas. Tal como la concibieron sus fundadores, entre ellos de forma destacada don Daniel Coso Villegas, el trimestre ha tenido un papel central en el desarrollo de la ciencia econmica en Mxico y en Amrica Latina, y ha contribuido a la formacin de varias generaciones de economistas. Pero sobre todo ha sido un ejemplo de la vitalidad de la ciencia econmica, manifiesta en la diversidad y pluralidad de trabajos de investigacin y de reflexiones novedosas, provocadoras y estimulantes. Cabe sealar que la mayora de los impulsores y fundadores de El Trimestre Econmico fueron tambin parte importante del Banco de Mxico en sus primeros aos de vida, ya sea como fundadores y miembros del primer Consejo de Administracin del Banco  como fue el caso de Manuel Gmez Morn-, sea como directores del Instituto Central  que es el caso de 1 Eduardo Villaseor y Gonzalo Robles- o como funcionarios o investigadores como sucedi con Daniel Coso Villegas. De esa forma, El Trimestre Econmico y el Banco de Mxico establecieron una particular sinergia en la promocin de la investigacin econmica y en la formacin de capital humano de gran calidad dedicado a la poltica econmica. En este sentido, quiero aprovechar esta ocasin para felicitar de una manera afectuosa a todos aquellos cuyo trabajo y esfuerzo han hecho posible que hoy estemos reunidos celebrando un aniversario ms de El Trimestre Econmico. En esta ocasin con motivo de este aniversario se lleva a cabo una conferencia impartida por el profesor Kaushik Basu sobre su libro Ms all de la mano invisible: fundamentos para una nueva economa. Un libro escrito de una manera inteligente que sin duda, despierta la curiosidad intelectual. El trabajo del profesor Basu es sumamente crtico al tiempo que muestra un gran rigor intelectual. Es un libro que abre la puerta a temas muy interesantes que deben ser atendidos por los economistas; qu mejor que hacerlo a travs de revistas como El Trimestre Econmico. 2 En efecto, El Trimestre Econmico siempre ha sido un foro abierto a todas las corrientes del pensamiento econmico y escenario de un intercambio fructfero de ideas. Como el ttulo de la obra del profesor Basu sugiere parecera llegada la hora de cuestionar un planteamiento que ha sido fundamental en la historia del pensamiento econmico y que es pieza importante de la teora econmica moderna: el paradigma o modelo de la mano invisible. Como todos sabemos, se trata de una formulacin planteada por Adam Smith en el siglo XVIII que para su tiempo represent una idea seminal que dio origen a toda una corriente econmica. En breve, la teora de la mano invisible postula que la libre concurrencia en el mercado de una multitud de individuos interesados en maximizar su propio beneficio arrojar a la postre un resultado eficiente y socialmente ptimo, sin recurrir a un planificador central que tome las decisiones econmicas. Cabe advertir, como lo hace el profesor Basu, que gracias al desarrollo de las tcnicas econmicas, primordialmente de la economa matemtica, dicha teora se ha formalizado dando lugar al llamado primer teorema del bienestar. Dicha formalizacin es importante ya que permite apreciar con mayor claridad cules son las condiciones para que, en efecto, 3 el sistema de mercado funcione como una mano invisible que gue a los agentes econmicos a un resultado eficiente y socialmente ptimo. Ello es fundamental, ya que no podemos pretender aplicar el teorema de la mano invisible al mundo real sin tomar en consideracin aquellas condiciones que son esenciales para que ste se cumpla. Del tono crtico del libro del profesor Basu se desprende la impresin que en los programas de economa de licenciatura y de posgrado slo se ensea el teorema y su derivacin matemtica, y que este modelo despus se aplica de forma dogmtica. Sin embargo, en mi experiencia como alumno y profesor, si bien se parte de este teorema, yo dira que en los programas de economa en prcticamente todas las universidades se destina la gran mayora del tiempo a encontrar mtodos analticos para lidiar con las consecuencias de que precisamente esas condiciones ideales de la mano invisible no suelen estar presentes. Sera una caricatura de la realidad decir que la enseanza dominante en la economa se restringe a postular el teorema de la mano invisible sin ajustes ni anlisis crticos posteriores. 4 En este contexto, me gustara enfatizar tres puntos que, en lo personal, considero fundamentales en todo anlisis del teorema en cuestin: el papel de los mercados competitivos, las consideraciones de equidad y, principalmente, la importancia del marco institucional. Primero, el resultado del teorema de la mano invisible corresponde a una economa competitiva, en la que cada agente econmico es lo suficientemente pequeo para que sus acciones individuales no afecten los precios en los mercados. Es decir, dichos agentes son precio-aceptantes. No obstante, es comn que en la realidad nos encontremos con mercados en los que un participante o un nmero reducido de stos son lo suficientemente grandes para poder influir en los precios. En estos casos, el comportamiento de dichos agentes es de carcter estratgico y ello suele dar lugar a resultados ineficientes. Segundo, cuando hablamos del teorema de la mano invisible tambin hay que tomar en cuenta el tema de la justicia o equidad. Es decir, si bien el sistema de mercado nos puede llevar a un resultado eficiente, o dicho en trminos tcnicos, a un ptimo de Pareto, tambin es cierto que dependiendo de las condiciones iniciales dicho resultado puede ser uno en el que 5 prevalezca una elevada desigualdad. Esto es: un resultado indeseable socialmente. Tercero, en adicin a todo lo anterior, debemos tomar en consideracin que el teorema de la mano invisible no se da en el vaco. Es decir: los agentes econmicos interactan entre s en el marco de un conjunto de leyes, normas sociales y valores que regulan el comportamiento de los miembros de la sociedad. Ello es algo que a veces obviamos pero que siempre debemos tener presente. As, el marco institucional es crucial para el buen desempeo de las economas. Como sabemos, ello ha ayudado a explicar por qu algunas economas han prosperado y alcanzado niveles elevados de bienestar mientras que otras se han rezagado y tienen graves problemas de pobreza. Como seala el profesor Basu, hay leyes, normas sociales y valores que facilitan el crecimiento econmico, pero tambin hay otros arreglos institucionales que, por el contrario, pueden obstaculizar el crecimiento o hacerlo inequitativo. Estos tres ejemplos de desviaciones del teorema de la mano invisible han sido ampliamente reconocidos en la profesin econmica y estudiados exhaustivamente. As, una aportacin importante que ha hecho la economa moderna es precisamente el anlisis y diseo de mecanismos 6 para alinear los incentivos que enfrentan los agentes econmicos. Ello es importante ya que con frecuencia los intereses individuales no coinciden con el inters de la sociedad en su conjunto. En adicin a lo anterior y sin negar la importancia de los incentivos econmicos, el profesor Basu nos recuerda que algunos comportamientos humanos no necesariamente estn motivados por el inters personal o privado de los individuos, y que dichos comportamientos tambin pueden ser clave para el buen desempeo de las economas. En efecto, valores como la honestidad y la integridad personal, as como ciertas normas sociales, pueden ser decisivos para el progreso econmico de las sociedades. Algo que me llamo poderosamente la atencin del libro es que su autor, si bien es crtico de la economa neoclsica, utiliza herramientas de esta corriente econmica para ilustrar sus ideas e hiptesis. Por ejemplo, a lo largo del libro emplea de manera recurrente la teora de juegos para analizar temas como el altruismo, la confianza y el papel del derecho en la economa, entre otros temas que, indiscutiblemente, son relevantes y a los que debemos prestar una atencin todava mayor en las agendas de investigacin. Como menciona el profesor Basu, 7 afortunadamente eso es lo que ha venido ocurriendo en los ltimos aos. En mi opinin, el marco institucional prevaleciente en un pas, incluyendo leyes, normas sociales y valores, depende de factores culturales, sociales e histricos. Asimismo, dicho marco no permanece inmutable a travs del tiempo. Todo lo contrario, las sociedades son dinmicas y se encuentran en permanente evolucin. En este contexto, debemos profundizar todava ms nuestro conocimiento sobre aquellas instituciones que son ms favorables para el crecimiento econmico y, sobre todo, en la manera en que dichas instituciones pueden crearse y establecerse de manera firme en la economa de un pas. Lo anterior requiere de un trabajo multidisciplinario, en el que los economistas colaboren con profesionales de otras ramas del conocimiento. Sin duda este es un tema fascinante, que despierta muchas preguntas y que debe tomarse en cuenta dentro de las agendas de investigacin. Espero que surjan muchos proyectos que terminen materializndose en trabajos acadmicos y, lo ms importante, que sean difundidos en revistas de prestigio como El Trimestre Econmico. Como conclusin prctica y actual de estas consideraciones me gustara hacer una reflexin adicional sobre la aplicacin de la 8 teora de la mano invisible. En mi opinin, y como lo he mencionado, los hacedores de polticas pblicas no pueden simplemente des-regular los mercados y esperar que la economa automticamente tenga un buen desempeo y crezca a tasas elevadas y de manera sostenida. Tambin son necesarias polticas pblicas y reformas econmicas encaminadas a crear las condiciones institucionales para que, en efecto, el sistema de mercado pueda propiciar una asignacin eficiente de los recursos escasos con los que cuenta la economa. De esta manera, es fundamental el papel que el Estado puede desempear en temas que van desde el diseo y aplicacin de una poltica anti-monopolios que promueva condiciones de competencia en los mercados, hasta una poltica social que se enfoque en atender los problemas de pobreza y desigualdad, a travs de los que considero los tres ms eficaces mecanismos de movilidad y promocin social: la educacin, los servicios de salud y la disponibilidad de crdito, en un marco de estabilidad macroeconmica. El libro cuestiona resultados que se desprenden de la teora econmica formulada a partir del teorema de la mano invisible, bajo el supuesto de que este teorema y sus resultados son fallidos. La crtica principal que yo hara al libro, en este sentido, 9 es suponer que los hacedores de poltica siguen y aplican fiel, mecnica y dogmticamente los postulados ideales de una mano invisible, cuando precisamente quienes hacemos polticas pblicas  y me incluyo en el conjunto gracias a una experiencia de ms de 30 aos  no seguimos al pe de la letra tal o cual modelo terico o la receta derivada del ms reciente paper de investigacin; por el contrario, el hacedor de polticas pblicas aprovecha lo que le sirve del amplio y diverso conjunto de herramientas tcnicas y tericas aprendidas, echa mano de su experiencia y del sentido comn y lo que aplica seguramente, en la inmensa mayora de los casos, no se basar en los supuestos tericos de un modelo o de una investigacin acadmica, sino en lo que es factible y deseable ante una realidad dinmica y cambiante. A pesar de este hecho, las referencias que encontramos en la bibliografa del libro comentado son a trabajos y artculos tericos, pero se echan en falta referencias a documentos pblicos de los gobiernos de los distintos pases, que los hay y son abundantes, donde se abordan las consideraciones reales que los hacedores de polticas pblicas han tomado en cuenta para implementar polticas econmicas. Y en mi experiencia de ms de 30 aos como hacedor de polticas econmicas debo decir que nunca me ha tocado ver que los postulados tericos o las recetas acadmicas se apliquen de forma automtica o a pie juntillas. 10 Si bien los modelos econmicos pueden ser sumamente tiles en este proceso, son de primordial importancia la intuicin, el sentido comn y el buen juicio de todos aquellos involucrados en la elaboracin e implementacin de las polticas pblicas y de las reformas econmicas. Aunado a lo anterior, tambin es importante la voluntad para hacer cambios, as como la capacidad para llegar a acuerdos entre todas las partes involucradas, de tal manera que dichos cambios puedan materializarse. En este contexto, me gustara hacer un comentario final sobre el proceso de transformaciones estructurales que hoy da vive nuestro pas. Como sabemos, un acicate adicional para la formulacin de las reformas estructurales es el entorno externo particularmente complejo que enfrentan hoy da las economas de mercados emergentes, como es el caso de Mxico. Las reformas, por s mismas y por el formidable impulso que le darn a la productividad, son indispensables, pero se vuelven an ms urgentes al considerar la necesidad de promover fuentes internas de crecimiento que ms que compensen la debilidad de la demanda externa. La finalidad, desde luego, debe ser mejorar el bienestar de toda la poblacin y superar los numerosos rezagos que an aquejan 11 a millones de mexicanos, y el medio idneo para lograrlo es incrementar la productividad total de los factores. Sin duda, Mxico ha tomado pasos importantes en esta direccin. Efectivamente, el paquete de reformas que recientemente ha sido aprobado por el Congreso en nuestro pas incluye reformas en materia de competencia econmica, telecomunicaciones, mercado laboral, sector financiero, energa, finanzas pblicas y educacin. Estas reformas tienen el potencial para propiciar que los recursos se asignen a sus usos ms productivos, as como para que se produzcan bienes y servicios a precios ms accesibles para la poblacin. A pesar de lo anterior, es importante estar conscientes de que no es suficiente aprobar una reforma econmica para que sta rinda frutos. Un tema fundamental es que dichas reformas estn bien diseadas y, sobre todo, que se implementen de manera adecuada. Como menciona atinadamente el profesor Basu en su libro, no basta con cambiar la Ley para que se modifique el comportamiento de las personas. Lo anterior es algo que los hacedores de polticas debemos tomar en consideracin durante el diseo e instrumentacin de polticas pblicas. En este sentido, celebro la publicacin de trabajos como el libro del profesor Basu y la existencia de revistas acadmicas como 12 El Trimestre Econmico, que contribuyen significativamente a la difusin del anlisis econmico y, por consiguiente, a mejorar nuestro entendimiento sobre el funcionamiento de la economa. En la medida en que lo anterior se traduzca en mejores polticas pblicas y en reformas econmicas idneas, podremos alcanzar un mayor crecimiento econmico, tasas de empleo ms elevadas, una distribucin del ingreso ms equitativa, abatir la pobreza y, en pocas palabras, lograr una mejor calidad de vida para toda la poblacin. Muchas gracias. 13

Title: Presentation of the commemorative coin for the awarding of the Nobel Prize for Literature to the poet Octavio Paz
text: REMARKS BY DR. AGUSTIN CARSTENS, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, ON THE OCCASION OF THE PRESENTATION OF THE COMMEMORATIVE COIN FOR THE AWARDING OF THE NOBEL PRIZE FOR LITERATURE TO THE POET OCTAVIO PAZ. ? Mrs. Marie Jose Paz ? Ms. Consuelo Saizar Guerrero, President of the National Council for Culture and the Arts ? Public Accountant Marcelo de los Santos Fraga, Director General of The Mint ? Ladies and gentlemen, For the Bank of Mexico and for me personally, it is a great honor to be part of this ceremony in which, on the occasion of disseminating the coin that commemorates the delivery of the Nobel Prize for Literature to Octavio Paz, we are actually 1 remembering and celebrating that great writer, glory of Mexican letters and leading figure of Mexican culture. It has been 20 years since the most transcendent poet of contemporary Mexico was awarded the most prestigious recognition in the world of letters. Octavio Paz joined the gift of poetry with an extraordinary talent and acuity as an essayist; With an elegant and measured prose, Paz bequeathed us, among many other riches, one of the most suggestive mirrors of who we are as Mexicans, where we come from and where we are going. The proposal for the creation of this piece arose from the deputy Kenia Lopez Rabadan, of the parliamentary group of the National Action Party, but very soon it became a plural proposal, which transcended parties, philias and phobias. Thanks to all those who from the Legislative Branch promoted and supported such a happy initiative. A commendable mention also deserves the experts of the 2 Mint whose design of the piece was in charge and also the technical staff that has carried out the production of the coin. ------------------------------------------ the ------------------------------ That the figure of the poet Octavio Paz has been chosen to create a commemorative coin entails in my opinion a double success. On the one hand, this project enriches the tradition of commemorative coins, through the recognition of representatives of art and figures of the humanities. Second, special celebrations should be given to the only Mexican writer who has won the Nobel Prize in Literature. That award was granted to Paz when he was 76 years old and was strictly the only literary recognition he had yet to receive, after many others highly valued. 3 Paz won all these awards for a compelling reason: for his great quality as a poet and essayist and for his multifaceted character as a writer. Metaphorically there was not a single writer in Octavio Paz but many: the poet, the essayist, the artistic critic, the polemicist, the poetic analyst, the philosopher of Mexican anthropology, the political critic, the journalist and a long etcetera. In its great coverage and mastery of genres resided in a certain sense its greatness. Octavio Paz was of course a great professional of literature, a skillful and elegant handler of the language, backed by an encyclopedic culture of practically impeccable invoice. However, not only his skills as a writing professional allow us to understand his transcendence as a figure of letters, his time and his homeland. Enrique Krauze has rightly highlighted the constructive passion that moved Octavio Paz all his life: "passion 4 for freedom, literature, clarity, criticism, reason; but above all, passion for the truth." No one like Octavio Paz managed to put the name of Mexico on the horizon of world culture so high, so bright, so clear. The mystery of Mexicanity, "that invisible substance that is somewhere", motivated and went through all the work of the great writer starting of course with his poetry. If so much has been due to that poet the knowledge about Mexico and the international promotion of the image of the country, it is hardly fair that his memory is preserved in a commemorative coin, a tradition that has also earned much prestige to our homeland. Ladies and gentlemen: 5 Due to its meaning and its characteristics, the commemorative piece that we present today is called to receive the best reception imaginable. It is foreseeable that it will become a piece within the reach of anyone who wishes to admire it and, why not?, treasure it. In addition, it is worth highlighting the beauty of the design that was developed for the coin with a bimetallic format. The obverse of this coin will have the traditional image, with the national coat of arms and the legend United Mexican States. For its part, the reverse is dedicated to celebrating the figure of the writer Octavio Paz with his effigy and the motto "Nobel Prize for Literature 1990". I can only reiterate my congratulations to all the creators of this coin that will come to enrich in a very important way the Mexican numismatics. A special recognition deserves the Conaculta and some figures of the intellectual environment that supported the proposal. 6 The most important congratulations go to the legislators who pushed hard for the realization of this project. Generating goods of this nature, whose main value is to give honor and recognition to the great Mexicans who fill us all with pride, is a facet of legislative work that is rarely recognized and disseminated. It is deserved to do so on this occasion. Thanks a lot 7
text_original: PALABRAS DEL DOCTOR AGUSTIN CARSTENS, GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE MEXICO, EN OCASIN DE LA PRESENTACION DE LA MONEDA CONMEMORATIVA POR EL OTORGAMIENTO DEL PREMIO NOBEL DE LITERATURA AL POETA OCTAVIO PAZ.  Seora Marie Jos Paz  Licenciada Consuelo Sizar Guerrero, Presidenta del Consejo Nacional para la Cultura y las Artes  Contador Pblico Marcelo de los Santos Fraga, Director General de Casa de Moneda  Seoras y seores: Para el Banco de Mxico y para m en lo personal, es un gran honor ser parte de esta ceremonia en la que, con motivo de difundir la moneda que conmemora la entrega del Premio Nobel de Literatura a Octavio Paz, en realidad estamos 1 recordando y celebrando a ese gran escritor, gloria de las letras mexicanas y figura seera de la cultura mexicana. Hace 20 aos que al poeta ms trascendente del Mxico contemporneo se le concedi el reconocimiento de mayor prestigio en el mundo de las letras. Octavio Paz uni al don de la poesa un extraordinario talento y agudeza como ensayista; con una prosa elegante y medida, Paz nos leg, entre otras muchas riquezas, uno de los espejos ms sugerentes de quines somos como mexicanos, de dnde venimos y a dnde vamos. La propuesta para la creacin de esta pieza surgi de la diputada Kenia Lpez Rabadn, del grupo parlamentario del Partido Accin Nacional, pero muy pronto se convirti en una propuesta plural, que trascendi partidos, filias y fobias. Gracias a todos los que desde el Poder Legislativo impulsaron y apoyaron tan feliz iniciativa. Una mencin elogiosa merecen tambin los expertos de la 2 Casa de Moneda a cuyo cargo estuvo el diseo de la pieza y tambin el personal tcnico que ha llevado a cabo la produccin de la moneda. ------------------------------------------ o ------------------------------ Que se haya elegido a la figura del poeta Octavio Paz para crear una moneda conmemorativa conlleva a mi juicio un acierto doble. Por un lado, este proyecto enriquece la tradicin de las monedas conmemorativas, mediante el reconocimiento a representantes del arte y figuras de las humanidades. Segundo, cabe celebrar de manera especial al nico escritor mexicano que se ha hecho acreedor al Premio Nobel de Literatura. Ese galardn le fue concedido a Paz cuando contaba con 76 aos de edad y era en rigor el nico reconocimiento literario que le faltaba por recibir, tras muchos otros muy valorados. 3 Paz se hizo acreedor a todos esos galardones por una razn de peso: por su gran calidad como poeta y ensayista y por su carcter polifactico como literato. Metafricamente no hubo un solo escritor en Octavio Paz sino muchos: el poeta, el ensayista, el crtico artstico, el polemista, el analista potico, el filosofo de la antropologa mexicana, el crtico poltico, el periodista y un largo etctera. En su gran cobertura y dominio de gneros residi en cierto sentido su grandeza. Octavio Paz fue desde luego un gran profesional de la literatura, un manejador diestro y elegante del idioma, respaldado por una cultura enciclopdica de factura prcticamente impecable. Con todo, no slo sus destrezas como profesional de la escritura permiten comprender su trascendencia como figura de las letras, de su tiempo y de su patria. Enrique Krauze ha destacado, con razn, la pasin constructiva que movi toda su vida a Octavio Paz: pasin 4 por la libertad, la literatura, la claridad, la crtica, la razn; pero sobre todo, pasin por la verdad. Nadie como Octavio Paz logr poner el nombre de Mxico en el horizonte de la cultura mundial tan alto, tan brillante, tan claro. El misterio de la mexicanidad, esa invisible sustancia que est en alguna parte, motiv y recorri toda la obra del gran escritor empezando desde luego por su poesa. Si tanto le ha debido a ese poeta el conocimiento sobre Mxico y la promocin internacional de la imagen del pas, resulta apenas justo que su recuerdo quede preservado en una moneda conmemorativa, tradicin que tambin le ha granjeado mucho prestigio a nuestra patria. Seoras y seores: 5 Por su significado y por sus caractersticas, la pieza conmemorativa que hoy damos a conocer est llamada a recibir la mejor acogida imaginable. Es previsible que se convierta en una pieza al alcance de cualquiera que desee admirarla y, por qu no?, atesorarla. En adicin, cabe resaltar la belleza del diseo que se discurri para la moneda con un formato bimetlico. El anverso de esta moneda tendr la imagen tradicional, con el escudo nacional y la leyenda Estados Unidos Mexicanos. Por su parte, el reverso est dedicado a celebrar la figura del escritor Octavio Paz con su efigie y la divisa Premio Nobel de Literatura 1990. No me queda ms que reiterar mi felicitacin a todos los creadores de esta moneda que vendr a enriquecer de una manera muy importante la numismtica mexicana. Un reconocimiento especial merece el Conaculta y algunas figuras del ambiente intelectual que apoyaron la propuesta. 6 La felicitacin ms importante corresponde a los legisladores que impulsaron con ahnco la realizacin de este proyecto. Generar bienes de esta naturaleza, cuyo principal valor consiste en dar honor y reconocimiento a los grandes mexicanos que nos llenan de orgullo a todos, se trata de una faceta del trabajo legislativo que pocas veces se reconoce y difunde. Es merecido hacerlo en esta ocasin. Muchas gracias 7

Title: Ceremony of delivery of the first degree Doctorate Honoris Causa of the Banking and Commercial School to Don Manuel Gmez Morn (posthumously)
text: "Our strength lies in our institutions" Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, during the ceremony of delivery of the first degree Doctorate Honoris Causa of the Banking and Commercial School to Don Manuel Gomez Morin (posthumously), in the Banking Room of the main building of the Bank of Mexico. November 21, 2014 - Good morning ? Mr. Rector of the Banking and Commercial School, doctor Carlos Prieto Sierra, ? Very dear Mr. Antonio del Valle Ruiz, representative of the Jury of Honor that defined the name of who would receive this first Doctorate Honoris Causa of the prestigious Banking and Commercial School, ? Mr. Professor Dean of the Banking and Commercial School, Public Accountant Vicente Romero Said, ? Mr. Juan Pablo Gomez Morin Rivera, in honorable representation of the relatives and descendants of Don Manuel Gomez Morin, ? Professors, distinguished alumni and members of the vigorous academic community of the Banking and Commercial School, ? Colleagues of the Bank of Mexico, ? Ladies and gentlemen, 1 Welcome to this historic and emblematic Banking Room of our Central Institute. For the Bank of Mexico, and for me personally, it is a great honor to host and witness this important ceremony in which an illustrious Mexican founder of Institutions is distinguished at the same time, as was Mr. Manuel Gomez Morin and one of the institutions of excellence that he forged and promoted from his first steps, in a visionary way: the Banking and Commercial School. It is particularly fortunate that this ceremony is held here in the Banking Room of the main building of the Bank of Mexico, which is another of the great institutions that Don Manuel contributed to create with care, talent and with that seal of humanist excellence at the service of the Homeland, which was characteristic of the most varied ventures carried out by Gomez Morin. We have had the opportunity to hear how today's Banking and Commercial School was created here, at the Bank of Mexico, 2 idea actively promoted by who was the first President of the Board of our Central Bank, precisely Mr. Manuel Gomez Morin, in the times of its first managing director, Mr. Alberto Mascarenas Navarro. Don Antonio del Valle also reminded us of the three attributes of excellence that the Banking and Commercial School, as an institution of higher education, has endeavored to imbue in all its graduates: "Solidity in knowledge, skill in doing and integrity in being". Well seen things, in everything that has been said here we find a constant, a common thread or "leitmotiv", which is the crucial importance of institutions to forge a strong country that is a space conducive to the development and well-being of all of us who are fortunate enough to live in it. In the case of the Bank of Mexico, this institutional character is based on the generation of trust on which depends, precisely, the good progress and healthy development of all the 3 banking system. For a Central Bank, the main asset, essential, is trust. And a Central Bank can only fulfill its mission - to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency it issues - if it radiates confidence. That is an Institution, not a material building, however beautiful, solid and endearing it may be, as is the case with this beautiful building in which we are. Institutions are social agreements that allow joint efforts to be harmonized, under known, invariable rules of the game, which are always and everywhere fulfilled. In this way, for example, the legal tender itself is an institution that gives strength and sustenance to the economy of a country. And some institutions need other institutions or even, as in the case of the Bank of Mexico and the Banking and Commercial School, contribute to creating new institutions. 4 For the good performance of the Central Bank, as Gomez Morin clearly saw, it was necessary that the professionalism and capacity of the staff of the Institution contribute to generate that invaluable asset that is trust. And there, precisely, arises the visionary idea put into practice of creating the "Banking School of the Bank of Mexico" that would later become the Banking and Commercial School. Seeking an increasingly better and greater formation of human capital has been, since its foundation, a commitment that has characterized the Bank of Mexico and that, obviously, explains the origins of what is now the Banking and Commercial School. Institution that has been, in turn and over the years, one of the main sources of training for professionals and personnel of excellence from which our Central Institute has been nourished. To this day, around fifty of our colleagues active in the 5 Banco de Mexico - not to mention several dozen more Banxico retirees - are graduates of bachelor's degrees, diplomas, master's degrees, courses from the Banking and Commercial School or, even, are currently students of the EBC. To conclude I would like to round off this idea about the great importance of institutions to give a country strength, both in flattering times and in difficult times, and to give it harmony the same when the winds blow in favor as when the skies become stormy and seem to conspire against the right course. Let us take up that life lesson that Gomez Morin and other great forgers of Institutions of Modern Mexico bequeathed to us: Institutions matter, let us always bet on Institutions, let us always take care of the Institutions and let us feel proud to contribute, each one from the place that corresponds to him, to enlarge our Institutions. Thanks a lot. 6

Title: Presentation of the commemorative coin of the 100th anniversary of the founding of the National Autonomous University of Mexico
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, at the presentation ceremony of the commemorative coin of the 100th anniversary of the founding of the National Autonomous University of Mexico. September 29, 2011  Rector of the National Autonomous University of Mexico, Dr. Jose Narro Robles.  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena  Senator of the Republic and distinguished friend, Rogelio Rueda  Mr. General Director of the Mint of Mexico, public accountant Jesus Marcelo de los Santos Fraga  Distinguished guests of the National Autonomous University of Mexico  Colleagues of the Bank of Mexico  Ladies and gentlemen, It is truly a great honor for the Bank of Mexico, and for me personally as Governor of the Institution, to preside over this ceremony with which the currency is put into circulation. 1 of silver that commemorates the first centenary of our National University. The minting of this commemorative coin is an event forced by history, forced by the most elementary sense of recognition and gratitude to all that the National University has contributed and contributes daily to Mexico, obliged, in short, by the reciprocity that the Nation as a whole owes to our house of studies par excellence and, in the particular case of the Central Bank, obliged because we feel twinned to the University by sharing the character of fundamental and foundational institutions of modern Mexico. Institutions that transcend people, while exalting them, and that give permanence to Mexico above conjunctures and vicissitudes. 2 But that this is, for multiple reasons, an obligatory event, does not take away one iota from its character as an endearing, exciting and festive event. On countless occasions the stories of UNAM and the Bank of Mexico have intersected. At such crossroads we find key characters in the history of Mexico during the last hundred years. For example, a few years after having actively participated in the founding of the Bank of Mexico we find Manuel Gomez Morin as Rector of the most emblematic house of studies in Mexico leading the decisive battle to make the National University a State Institution, yes, but autonomous. A battle that the founder of the National University, Don Justo Sierra, had already outlined clearly since the prolegomena of its foundation. Justo Sierra argued when defending the idea of the new National University in the early years of the twentieth century, and 3 I quote: "In order to achieve the lofty aims of the new institution, the relative bill establishes it as a State institution, but with such elements as to enable it to perform its functions by itself, endowing it with considerable autonomy" (the quote ends). Undoubtedly, the vague adjective of "considerable" was dictated to Sierra, at that particular moment in history and given the circumstances, by political prudence, but shortly after in 1929 the yearning for full autonomy would finally crystallize. In addition to the fact that numerous employees, officials and managers of the highest hierarchy in the Bank of Mexico, both active and retired, were trained in the classrooms of our National University, the collaboration between both institutions has been constant. I quote, among many others, four episodes in which the support of the UNAM to the Central Bank has been formidable and of excellence, all four are referred in this particular case to the manufacture of banknotes: 4  At the end of the decade of the 80s the Institute of Astronomy of the UNAM developed the programming and the ideal equipment for the design of the funds of the banknotes manufactured by the Bank, as well as for their engraving.  What strikes me is that it has been precisely the Institute of Astronomy, they are very versatile.  At the beginning of the 90s, the Engineering area of the UNAM supported the Bank of Mexico in the elaboration of prototypes of hydraulic, electromechanical and ergonomic tables that would allow the personnel who carry out the thorough examination of semi-printed paper money to be more efficient in their movements, while significantly reducing the physical risk for workers.  The Biochemistry area of the National University has advised the Bank of Mexico to develop a 5 protocol for the analysis and determination of biological contaminants in banknotes.  And, of course, in relation to the beautiful coin that we present today, made with the characteristic care of the Mint of Mexico, we must remember that in November 2010 through the National School of Plastic Arts of the UNAM the university community was summoned to the design contest that would hold the reverse of the coin, commemorating precisely the centenary of the founding of the UNAM. I mention some details of this design made by the university Nayeli Garcia Cansino, winner of the contest, and that today is embodied in the reverse of the commemorative coin: It is a contemporary composition that shows in a stylized way emblematic buildings of the University City, such as the main facade of the Torre de 6 Rectory, in which we appreciate the silhouette of the university emblem, the Central Library from which we observe the north wall and, in the background of the composition, the silhouette of the university Olympic stadium is distinguished. Below this architectural ensemble the coin shows elements of the sculptural-painting of the Rectory, "The people to the university and the university to the people", by David Alfaro Siqueiros. All this framed by the allusive legends: NATIONAL AUTONOMOUS UNIVERSITY OF MEXICO and "FOR MY RACE WILL SPEAK THE SPIRIT", accompanied by the mint (characteristic mark of the coinage), the commemorative year of 2010 and the denomination 10 (10 pesos). By the way, many of those present will remember and even some will carefully preserve as collectors the beautiful two thousand peso banknote manufactured by the Bank of Mexico in the 80s, which paid well-deserved tribute to the UNAM and its founder, Don Justo Sierra. On the back of the 7 banknote in shades of light green and sepia, the effigy of Sierra appears on the left and in the background, on the right, an image of the building of the Central Library of the UNAM, whose facade adorns the formidable mural by Juan O'Gorman: "Historical representation of culture". And I would precisely like to end my message by evoking a few words of Don Justo Sierra in his speech at the inauguration of the National University. These are words of great relevance because the UNAM, today as 101 years ago, perseveres in its vocation as a young, plural and tolerant university, open to the incessant search for the truth. Justo Sierra said in that speech on September 23, 1910: "The founders of the University of yesteryear said: 'the truth is defined, teach it'; we say to today's university students: 'the truth is being defined, seek it.'" Thanks a lot. 8 9
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, en la ceremonia de presentacin de la moneda conmemorativa de los 100 aos de la fundacin de la Universidad Nacional Autnoma de Mxico. 29 de septiembre de 2011  Seor Rector de la Universidad Nacional Autnoma de Mxico, doctor Jos Narro Robles. Sin duda, el vago adjetivo de considerable le fue dictado a Sierra, en ese momento particular de la historia y dadas las circunstancias, por la prudencia poltica, pero poco despus en 1929 el anhelo de autonoma plena cristalizara por fin. Adems de que numerossimos empleados, funcionarios y directivos de la ms alta jerarqua en el Banco de Mxico, tanto en activo como jubilados, fueron formados en las aulas de nuestra Universidad Nacional, la colaboracin entre ambas instituciones ha sido constante. Cito, entre otros muchos, cuatro episodios en los que el apoyo de la UNAM al Banco Central ha sido formidable y de excelencia, los cuatro son referidos en este caso particular a la fabricacin de billetes: 4  A fines de la dcada de los aos 80 el Instituto de Astronoma de la UNAM desarroll la programacin y el equipo idneo para el diseo de los fondos de los billetes que fabrica el Banco, as como para su grabado.  Lo que me llama la atencin es que haya sido precisamente el Instituto de Astronoma, son muy verstiles.  A principios de los aos 90 el rea de Ingeniera de la UNAM apoy al Banco de Mxico en la elaboracin de prototipos de mesas hidrulicas, electromecnicas y ergonmicas que permitiesen al personal que realiza el examen minucioso del papel moneda semi-impreso ser ms eficiente en sus movimientos, al tiempo que disminuy notablemente el riesgo fsico para los trabajadores.  El rea de Bioqumica de la Universidad Nacional ha asesorado al Banco de Mxico para desarrollar un 5 protocolo de anlisis y determinacin de contaminantes biolgicos en los billetes.  Y, por supuesto, en relacin a la hermosa moneda que hoy presentamos, realizada con el caracterstico esmero de la Casa de Moneda de Mxico, hay que recordar que en noviembre de 2010 a travs de la Escuela Nacional de Artes Plsticas de la UNAM se convoc a la comunidad universitaria al concurso del diseo que ostentara el reverso de la moneda, conmemorando justamente el centenario de la fundacin de la UNAM. Menciono algunos detalles de este diseo realizado por la universitaria Nayeli Garca Cansino, ganadora del concurso, y que hoy est plasmado en el reverso de la moneda conmemorativa: Se trata de una composicin contempornea que muestra de forma estilizada edificios emblemticos de la Ciudad Universitaria, tales como la fachada principal de la Torre de 6 Rectora, en la que apreciamos la silueta del emblema universitario, la Biblioteca Central de la cual observamos el muro norte y, al fondo de la composicin, se distingue la silueta del estadio olmpico universitario. Debajo de este conjunto arquitectnico la moneda muestra elementos de la esculto-pintura de la Rectora, El pueblo a la universidad y la universidad al pueblo, de David Alfaro Siqueiros. Todo ello enmarcado por las leyendas alusivas: UNIVERSIDAD NACIONAL AUTNOMA DE MXICO y POR MI RAZA HABLAR EL ESPRITU, acompaadas de la ceca (marca caracterstica de la acuacin), el ao conmemorativo de 2010 y la denominacin $10 (10 pesos). Por cierto, muchos de los presentes recordarn e incluso algunos conservarn cuidadosamente como coleccionistas el hermoso billete de dos mil pesos fabricado por el Banco de Mxico en los aos 80, que renda homenaje merecidsimo a la UNAM y a su fundador, don Justo Sierra. En el reverso del 7 billete en tonalidades de verde claro y sepia, aparece la efigie de Sierra a la izquierda y al fondo, a la derecha, una imagen del edificio de la Biblioteca Central de la UNAM, cuya fachada engalana el formidable mural de Juan OGorman: Representacin histrica de la cultura. Y precisamente deseo terminar mi mensaje evocando unas palabras de don Justo Sierra en su discurso de inauguracin de la Universidad Nacional. Son palabras de gran actualidad porque la UNAM, hoy como hace 101 aos, persevera en su vocacin de universidad joven, plural y tolerante, abierta a la bsqueda incesante de la verdad. Deca Justo Sierra en ese discurso el 23 de septiembre de 1910: Los fundadores de la Universidad de antao decan: la verdad est definida, enseadla; nosotros decimos a los universitarios de hoy: la verdad se va definiendo, buscadla. Title: Business innovation and financial stability
text: Business Innovation and Financial Stability Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, on the occasion of the inauguration of the exhibition "Being an entrepreneur: a personal story", at the Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE), in Mexico City, on October 26, 2011. It is an honor for me to have the opportunity to address a few words to you when the exhibition "Being an entrepreneur: a personal story" opens today at MIDE. Just as the first obligation of a speaker is to be brief so as not to annoy the audience, an obligation that I will try to fulfill, the first requirement to be an entrepreneur is to innovate. History shows us, time and again, that sustained economic progress is rooted in innovation. Someone finds a new way to do something, or improves a process, a product or a service and, thanks to that innovation, you can do the same as before, but in less time, or with higher quality or with fewer resources. That, and nothing else, is what we call productivity. And it is only through these sometimes memorable changes that are truly giant leaps in harnessing scarce resources that nations, families and individuals at all levels of society prosper and live better and better. That is why the presence of the entrepreneur, the innovator who manages to do more with less, and who makes our life more and more bearable, is decisive for the progress of humanity. That is why the untimely death of an exceptional entrepreneur, such as Steve Jobs, produced such an instant shock in millions of people who never knew him personally, but for whom Jobs' contributions made life easier and less limited. A measure of the magnitude of the contributions of an extraordinary entrepreneur such as Jobs, is that the vast majority of millions of 1 people who knew all over the planet the news of his death in a few minutes, found out thanks to some invention in whose gestation Jobs himself participated. This museum, the MIDE, is also an example of particularly fortunate entrepreneurial innovation. In 2002, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico approved its establishment and ordered the constitution of a trust to operate a cultural and educational space dedicated to monetary, financial and economic matters. An innovation process was then unleashed that, in a first stage, required the Bank of Mexico to restore this building, known as the Old Convent of the Betlemitas, and carried out various conditioning works that allowed to have an ideal space for the Museum. In a second stage, starting in 2005, the main banks and financial intermediaries of the country participated with monetary and in-kind contributions for the creation of the Museum, for which they had the technical advice of specialists from the Bank of Mexico. Finally, the efforts were crystallized in July 2006, when MIDE opened its doors to the public, with an innovative and modern educational offer, which has allowed it to remain a high-quality cultural venue, oriented to the teaching and dissemination of current economic and financial issues. All this would not have been possible without the seed of an innovative idea, which was to make the dissemination of financial and economic issues among the general public, something exciting, fun, memorable. And do it very well, with care, adding value to what already exists. Being an entrepreneur: a personal story For all this, it is a reason for congratulations that MIDE, faithful to its commitment of origin and with the collaboration of the Financial Education Program of Banamex, "Saber Cuenta", presents today this new exhibition "Being an Entrepreneur: a personal story". 2 The figure of the entrepreneur as an agent of change has been known in economic science since at least the late eighteenth century.1 Since then various economists have studied the importance of the entrepreneur and the creation of innovative businesses and products in economic growth. A key element of entrepreneurs has to do with innovation; in fact, for the Austrian economist, Joseph A. Schumpeter, an entrepreneur ceases to be one simply and simply when he stops innovating; when it no longer creates new products, production methods, distribution systems, new ways of approaching markets, or forms of organization. I must warn that by innovating, inevitably other products, other ways of doing things, other processes immediately become obsolete and unnecessary. The innovative process that displaces the current model to adopt a better one is therefore known as "creative destruction".2 In fact, the first symptom of vitality of a dynamic economy is the constant disappearance of businesses that are replaced by better ones. It is impressive to see in this type of economy that, despite the high probabilities of failure faced by businesses, every day there are countless entrepreneurs willing to innovate and develop new projects. Undoubtedly, all this happens in an environment of free competition, which allows the entry of new participants which, in the end, benefits the consumer with better products at lower prices. In short, innovation is the fundamental piece to be an entrepreneur and its relationship with economic development is confirmed by seeing that those countries with more generation of patents, as an indicator of innovation, have a higher GDP per capita. Of course, the determinants of economic development are manifold; however, it is not difficult to imagine that a country with more and better innovations will be more prepared to produce goods and services efficiently and with quality. 1 Vease Cantillon, R., (1755), Essai Sur la Nature du Commerce en General, Kessinger Publishing. 2 Vease Schumpeter, J.A., (1934), The Theory of Economic Development, Cambridge, Mass: Harvard University Press; y Schumpeter, J.A., (1943), Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy, London: George Allen and Unwin. 3 Stability and innovation However, innovation is a complex process that requires an environment conducive to flourishing. In particular, a country must offer a stable economic environment that allows any individual to plan and organize their efforts, as well as the appropriate incentives to become, if they wish, an entrepreneur, and assure them that they will receive the benefits of their creation. Among these incentives is the existence of solid institutions that guarantee respect for property rights and a developed, deep and stable financial system that allows channeling the resources of the economy to their most productive uses. Unfortunately, the economic environment does not always favor the emergence of entrepreneurs. History is full of recurrent economic crises that inhibit the creative process and, for this reason, slow down economic growth. Precisely, at present, the world economy faces the consequences of one of the most severe and widespread crises in memory, which has resulted in expectations of slow growth for several years. In this environment, Mexico has stood out for the strength of its economic fundamentals, which has allowed it to differentiate itself from the advanced economies in trouble and from other emerging economies. Indeed, our economy enjoys sound public finances and low inflation converging to the three percent annual target. In addition, unlike other times, today the national economy shows a balance in its external accounts, based on both a moderate trade deficit and capital inflows largely in the medium term, with a flexible exchange rate regime. Likewise, the Mexican financial system is made up of well-capitalized intermediaries with adequate reserves and liquidity, as well as developed and deep financial markets compared to other emerging economies. 4 According to its constitutional mandate, the Bank of Mexico, in addition to fulfilling its priority objective of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, seeks to promote the healthy development of the financial system and promote the proper functioning of payment systems. To achieve these aims, it must promote and maintain a financial system capable of performing its intermediation function normally, even in adverse circumstances. This is done by conducting a monetary policy consistent with its objective of price stability. In addition, together with other authorities, it contributes to the strengthening of the regulatory and supervisory framework of the financial system. It also seeks to continuously monitor the risks of the financial system in order to anticipate threats to stability with opportunity and take measures to mitigate them. All these tasks are essential for the innovation of entrepreneurs to flourish, for the benefit of society as a whole. Final comments I conclude by congratulating again the organizers of this important avant-garde project that will surely provide the basic tools for those who seek to create and innovate, for our future entrepreneurs. I am certain that Mexico will continue to benefit from financial stability, which is the fertile ground for the emergence of more and more innovative entrepreneurs. 5
text_original: Innovacin Empresarial y Estabilidad Financiera Palabras del Dr. Manuel Snchez Gonzlez, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, con motivo de la inauguracin de la exposicin Ser emprendedor: una historia personal, en el Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE), en la Ciudad de Mxico, el 26 de octubre de 2011. Es para m un honor tener la oportunidad de dirigirles unas palabras al inaugurarse hoy en el MIDE, la exposicin Ser emprendedor: una historia personal. As como la primera obligacin de un orador es la de ser breve para no fastidiar al auditorio, obligacin que tratar de cumplir, el primer requisito para ser un emprendedor es innovar. La historia nos demuestra, una y otra vez, que el avance econmico sostenido tiene como raz la innovacin. Alguien encuentra una nueva forma de hacer algo, o mejora un proceso, un producto o un servicio y, gracias a esa innovacin, se puede lograr hacer lo mismo que antes, pero en menos tiempo, o con mayor calidad o con menos recursos. Eso, y no otra cosa, es lo que llamamos productividad. Y slo mediante esos cambios, que en ocasiones memorables, son verdaderos saltos gigantescos en el aprovechamiento de los recursos escasos, las naciones, las familias y las personas de todos los niveles sociales prosperan y viven cada vez mejor.
