Por eso la presencia del emprendedor, del innovador que consigue hacer ms con menos, y que hace nuestra vida cada vez ms llevadera, es decisiva para el progreso de la humanidad. Por eso, el prematuro fallecimiento de un emprendedor excepcional, como fue Steve Jobs, produjo tal conmocin instantnea en millones de personas que jams lo conocieron personalmente, pero para quienes las aportaciones de Jobs hicieron la vida ms fcil y menos limitada. Una medida de la magnitud de las aportaciones de un emprendedor extraordinario como lo fue Jobs, es que la inmensa mayora de los millones de 1 personas que conocieron en todo el planeta la noticia de su fallecimiento en unos cuantos minutos, se enteraron gracias a algn invento en cuya gestacin particip el propio Jobs. Este museo, el MIDE, es tambin un ejemplo de innovacin emprendedora particularmente afortunada. En 2002 la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico aprob su establecimiento y dispuso la constitucin de un fideicomiso para operar un espacio cultural y educativo dedicado a la materia monetaria, financiera y econmica. Se desat entonces un proceso de innovacin que, en una primera etapa, requiri que el Banco de Mxico restaurase este edificio, conocido como Antiguo Convento de los Betlemitas, y llev a cabo diversos trabajos de acondicionamiento que permitieron contar con un espacio idneo para el Museo. En una segunda etapa, a partir del 2005, los principales bancos e intermediarios financieros del pas participaron con aportaciones monetarias y en especie para la creacin del Museo, para lo cual se cont con la asesora tcnica de especialistas del Banco de Mxico. Por ltimo, los esfuerzos se vieron cristalizados en julio de 2006, cuando el MIDE abri sus puertas al pblico, con una oferta educativa innovadora y moderna, que le ha permitido mantenerse como un recinto cultural de alta calidad, orientado a la enseanza y divulgacin de temas econmicos y financieros de actualidad. Todo esto no habra sido posible sin la semilla de una idea innovadora, que fue la de hacer de la difusin de los asuntos financieros y econmicos entre el gran pblico, algo apasionante, divertido, memorable. Y hacerlo muy bien, con esmero, aadiendo valor a lo ya existente. Ser emprendedor: una historia personal Por todo esto, es motivo de congratulacin que el MIDE, fiel a su compromiso de origen y con la colaboracin del Programa Educacin Financiera de Banamex, Saber Cuenta, presente hoy esta nueva exposicin Ser Emprendedor: una historia personal. 2 La figura del emprendedor como agente de cambio es conocida en la ciencia econmica por lo menos desde fines del siglo XVIII.1 Desde entonces diversos economistas han estudiado la importancia del emprendedor y de la creacin de negocios y productos innovadores en el crecimiento econmico. Un elemento clave de los emprendedores tiene que ver con la innovacin; de hecho, para el economista austriaco, Joseph A. Schumpeter, un emprendedor deja de serlo simple y sencillamente cuando deja de innovar; cuando ya no crea nuevos productos, mtodos de produccin, sistemas de distribucin, nuevas formas de abordar los mercados, ni formas de organizacin. Debo advertir que al innovar, irremediablemente otros productos, otras formas de hacer las cosas, otros procesos se vuelven de inmediato obsoletos e innecesarios. Al proceso innovador que desplaza al modelo vigente para adoptar uno mejor se le conoce, por eso, como destruccin creativa.2 De hecho, el primer sntoma de vitalidad de una economa dinmica es la constante desaparicin de negocios que son reemplazados por otros mejores. Es impresionante ver en este tipo de economas que, a pesar de las altas probabilidades de fracaso que enfrentan los negocios, todos los das surge un sinnmero de emprendedores dispuestos a innovar y a desarrollar nuevos proyectos. Indudablemente, todo ello ocurre en un ambiente de libre competencia, que permite la entrada de nuevos participantes lo que, a fin de cuentas, beneficia al consumidor con mejores productos a menores precios. En suma, la innovacin es la pieza fundamental para ser empresario y su relacin con el desarrollo econmico se constata al ver que aquellos pases con ms generacin de patentes, como un indicador de innovacin, tienen un PIB per cpita ms elevado. Por supuesto, los determinantes del desarrollo econmico son mltiples; sin embargo, no es difcil imaginar que un pas con ms y mejores innovaciones estar ms preparado para producir bienes y servicios de manera eficiente y con calidad. 1 Vase Cantillon, R., (1755), Essai Sur la Nature du Commerce en General, Kessinger Publishing. 2 Vase Schumpeter, J.A., (1934), The Theory of Economic Development, Cambridge, Mass: Harvard University Press; y Schumpeter, J.A., (1943), Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy, London: George Allen and Unwin. 3 Estabilidad e innovacin Ahora bien, la innovacin es un proceso complejo que requiere de un ambiente propicio para florecer. En particular, un pas debe ofrecer un entorno econmico estable que permita a cualquier individuo planear y organizar sus esfuerzos, as como los incentivos adecuados para convertirse, si lo desea, en emprendedor, y asegurarle que recibir los beneficios de su creacin. Entre esos incentivos se encuentra la existencia de instituciones slidas que garanticen el respeto a los derechos de propiedad y de un sistema financiero desarrollado, profundo y estable, que permita canalizar los recursos de la economa a sus usos ms productivos. Desafortunadamente, el entorno econmico no siempre favorece el surgimiento de los emprendedores. La historia est llena de crisis econmicas recurrentes que inhiben el proceso creativo y, por tal motivo, frenan el crecimiento econmico. Precisamente, en la actualidad, la economa mundial enfrenta las consecuencias de una de las crisis ms severas y extendidas de las que se tenga memoria, la cual se ha traducido en expectativas de crecimiento lento para varios aos. En este entorno, Mxico se ha destacado por la fortaleza de sus fundamentos econmicos, lo cual le ha permitido diferenciarse de las economas avanzadas en problemas y de otras economas emergentes. En efecto, nuestra economa goza de finanzas pblicas sanas y de una inflacin baja convergiendo a la meta del tres por ciento anual. Adems, a diferencia de otras pocas, hoy la economa nacional muestra un equilibrio en sus cuentas externas, basado tanto en un moderado dficit comercial como en un ingreso de capitales en buena medida de mediano plazo, con un rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible. Asimismo, el sistema financiero mexicano est integrado por intermediarios bien capitalizados y con reservas y liquidez adecuadas, as como de mercados financieros desarrollados y profundos en comparacin con otras economas emergentes. 4 De acuerdo a su mandato constitucional, el Banco de Mxico adems de cumplir con su objetivo prioritario de procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional, busca promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Para la consecucin de estas finalidades debe fomentar y mantener un un sistema financiero capaz de realizar su funcin de intermediacin con normalidad, incluso en circunstancias adversas. Lo anterior lo realiza conduciendo una poltica monetaria congruente con su objetivo de estabilidad de los precios. Adems, junto con otras autoridades, contribuye al fortalecimiento del marco de regulacin y supervisin del sistema financiero. Asimismo, procura dar un seguimiento continuo a los riesgos del sistema financiero para anticipar con oportunidad amenazas a la estabilidad y tomar medidas para mitigarlas. Todas estas tareas son esenciales para que la innovacin de los emprendedores florezca, en beneficio de toda la sociedad. Comentarios finales Concluyo felicitando nuevamente a los organizadores de este importante proyecto vanguardista que seguramente brindar las herramientas bsicas para quienes buscan crear e innovar, para nuestros futuros emprendedores. Tengo la certeza de que Mxico continuar beneficindose de la estabilidad financiera, la cual es el terreno propicio, abonado, para el surgimiento de cada vez ms empresarios innovadores. 5

Title: Presentacin del billete de 50 pesos
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of the 50 peso banknote.1 October 28, 2021 Dear Deputy Governors and Esteemed Deputy Governors of the Bank of Mexico; Alejandro Alegre, General Director of Issuance of the Bank; Representatives of the media; Companions; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 On behalf of the Governing Board, I am pleased to welcome you to the ceremony of putting into circulation the new 50 peso note, which is the sixth denomination of the G family. Like most central banks in the world, the Bank of Mexico has the priority objective of providing national currency to the country's economy and preserving the stability of its purchasing power. To achieve its primary objective, it is important for a central bank to have clear legal mandates and institutional mandates that prevent its exclusive power to issue money from being misused, which would lead to serious economic and social consequences. That is why, since the end of the twentieth century, a broad consensus was generated that autonomy was the ideal statute for a central bank to concentrate its instruments and efforts on promoting price stability with a consistent and far-reaching vision. Under this institutional arrangement it is possible to generate in the public the certainty that, when issuing and placing money, the central bank will act following 2 rules that honor your commitment to society to maintain low and stable inflation. This, in turn, contributes to the efficient fulfillment of money's three essential functions: (i) being a generally accepted means of payment; (ii) function as a reliable store of value over time and (iii) serve as a unit of account for all transactions in the economy. Since 1994, the Bank of Mexico has had the autonomy to better fulfill its priority mandate to maintain the purchasing power of the currency. With this scheme, our country has achieved one of the longest stages of price stability in its history, which reinforces the confidence of the population in the use of their banknotes and coins. In fulfillment of its constitutional mandate, since its foundation in 1925, this Central Institute has been responsible for issuing banknotes. From 1969, Mexican banknotes began to be printed in national territory with the start of operations of the first banknote factory in the country, located in Mexico City. Now, since 2018, this function is also performed in the Jalisco factory, which reinforces the capacity 3 of production of national currency for the full fulfillment of the constitutional mandate. The Bank of Mexico had put into circulation 6 families of banknotes, from the "AA" to the "F". In 2013, after an in-depth prospective analysis of the situation of banknotes in our country, the Institution made the decision to issue the seventh family, known as "G", according to different reasons: 1) Provide the population with a secure and reliable means of payment, with new and reinforced security elements that will hinder the illegal reproduction of banknotes. This is taking into account the advances and diffusion of digital graphic printing technologies. 2) Provide tickets, whose use is simple, and which can be easily identified by all types of users or devices, whether blind and visually impaired or automated equipment. 3) Preserve the security and functionality features of banknotes for longer, by increasing their useful life in circulation. 4 4) Reinforce, through banknotes, elements of national identity that link us with the natural and cultural wealth of Mexico and with fundamental aspects of our history. With the issuance of the new 50 peso note, the Bank of Mexico completes the issuance of the G family and closes a cycle that began 8 years ago. The new 50 peso banknote has purple as its predominant color, its format is vertical, it is printed in polymer substrate and its obverse alludes to the Tenochtitlan Foundation, representing the historical period of Ancient Mexico, while its reverse is dedicated to the ecosystem of rivers and lakes, with the axolotl and corn, in Xochimilco in Mexico City, cultural heritage of humanity. The main motif of the banknote on its obverse consists of a fragment of the back of the monolith known as "Teocalli of the Sacred War" that was carved during the Mexica empire by orders of Emperor Moctezuma II. This monolith consists of an eagle perched on a nopal with the "Atl-tlachinolli" in the beak, symbol that means water- 5 bonfire, opposite and complementary elements, whose union is a metaphor for sacred war. The "Teocalli" was rescued in the twenties of the last century from the foundations of the National Palace, where the palace of Moctezuma II was located. In the first of the studies on this monolith, in 1927, the anthropologist Alfonso Caso highlighted the richness of its symbols and concluded that it celebrates the triumph of the sun and the military power of the Mexica after the foundation of their city. The back of the "Teocalli" refers to the founding sign of the city of the Aztec people, after a long pilgrimage of more than 200 years. The account of the pilgrimage explains that the Aztecs left Aztlan, attending to the indication of Huitzilopochtli to go to new lands and found their city where an eagle perched on a nopal was. The Aztecs wandered around various places and finally, in the year "dos casa" (1325), which is depicted on the note under the vignette, they established the city of Tenochtitlan. This is the origin of the current national coat of arms, in which an eagle devouring a 6 snake, making it the symbol and national reference of greater importance in our history. It is very significant to have, in this ceremony, a replica of this impressive monolith and we thank Antonio Saborit, director of the National Museum of Anthropology, for the loan of this piece. The representation of the monolith is accompanied by a fragment of Diego Rivera's mural "La gran Tenochtitlan (seen from the Tlatelolco market)", in which the Tlacopan road, today the Tacuba road, is observed, which leads to the Templo Mayor, a space that was the center of the political and religious life of Mexica society and, in the background, Lake Texcoco and the Popocatepetl and Iztaccihuatl volcanoes. This mural shows in full swing the city of Tenochtitlan, the most populated and richest in Mesoamerica and one of the largest in the world at the time. The composition of the obverse is framed by the lunar glyph, in allusion to the name of Mexico. We owe to Alfonso Caso the explanation of the etymology of this name, which derives from the words metztli (moon), xictli (navel, 7 center), and co (place), giving in its composition the word Mexi-co, whose meaning is "in the center of the Moon".2 The transparent window is surrounded by a very significant element in the pre-Hispanic tradition, the "Ollin", which is formed by two intertwined bands, whose meaning is "movement".3 As Don Miguel Leon Portilla indicated, "oneself is the origin of the Nahua words movement, heart and soul. Which proves that for the ancient Mexicans life without movement was inconceivable."4 The back of the banknote is dedicated to the ecosystem of rivers and lakes, with axolotl and corn, in Xochimilco in Mexico City, cultural heritage of humanity; the latter is a space of great ecological and cultural importance. This site was declared a cultural heritage site by UNESCO in 1987 for being a living testimony of the lake culture of the Valley 2 Alfonso Caso, "El aguila y el nopal", in Estudios de cultura nahuatl, no. 50, Mexico, UNAM, Instituto de Investigaciones Historicas, July-December 2015, pp. 355-369, p. 360. 3 Yolotl Gonzalez Torres, Diccionario de mitologia y religion de Mesoamerica, Mexico, Ediciones Larousse, 1995, p. 130. 4 Miguel Leon Portilla, La filosofia nahuatl estudiada en sus fuentes, 11a ed., Mexico, UNAM, Instituto de Investigaciones Historicas, 2017, p. 167. 8 of Mexico, as well as for having a unique traditional agricultural system in the world, the chinampas. The banknote also reflects the cultivation of corn, of great economic and social importance in Mexico and whose presence, in pre-Hispanic cultures, marked their ritual life and the development of all their daily activities. Framed the back of the bill the tree of ahuejote or water willow that forms riparian forests and that; for the Mexicas, it was a sacred tree, vital to maintain the structure of the chinampas. Among the species that house the lake region of Xochimilco is the Mexican axolotl, represented prominently on the ticket. This amphibian, from the group of salamanders, is the subject of multiple studies for its rarity, beauty and great biological richness. In addition, the axolotl was relevant in pre-Hispanic cultures since it represented Xolotl, god of sunset, protector of fire and one of the lords of the underworld, brother of Quetzalcoatl. These are, in short, the characteristics of the new 50 peso bill, which today is presented to Mexicans. I want to emphasize that the route 9 to put into circulation this banknote, and the entire G family, has entailed important learnings and challenges, and has included, among other aspects: the detailed study of the ideal characteristics to be incorporated into the banknotes; the development of several sketch proposals; the care of each line that makes up the design, the integration of raw materials and inputs with the banknote production machines and, of course, their distribution in all corners of the country. They have been years of constant work, in which the needs, habits and preferences of Mexican society were studied, in order to verify the usefulness and potential acceptance of the ticket and strategically place each security, thematic and word component that makes it up. Of course, the Bank of Mexico did not travel this path alone and worked closely with industry suppliers and other specialists. In particular, with regard to the subject of banknotes, the Bank of Mexico owes an enormous debt of gratitude to a large group of experts in the field of history, 10 biodiversity, art and culture of our country. These experts come from the most recognized academic institutions and research centers nationwide, and collaborated with us in the selection of the motives that would best represent our nation and that would strengthen the feeling of belonging and unity. Therefore, our greatest thanks to:  The Mexican Academy of History;  The Mexican Academy of Language;  The Old College of San Ildefonso;  The Center for Research and Higher Studies in Social Anthropology of the National Council of Science and Technology;  The College of Mexico;  The National College;  The National Commission of Natural Protected Areas;  The National Commission for the Knowledge and Use of Biodiversity;  The National Council for Culture and the Arts, now the Ministry of Culture; 11  The Fomento Cultural Banamex A.C.;  The National Institute of Anthropology and History;  The National Institute of Statistics and Geography;  The National Institute of Historical Studies of Revolutions from Mexico;  The Regional Museum of the Mexican Revolution, Casa de los Serdan Brothers;  The University of the Cloister of Sor Juana;  and the National Autonomous University of Mexico, through its various institutes. Of course, I deeply thank the comrades of the Bank of Mexico, particularly all the members of the General Directorate of Issuance, for their great commitment, dedication and professionalism to fulfill the presentation of the entire G family. In very complex circumstances, due to the challenges posed by the pandemic. For everyone at the Bank of Mexico, the task of designing, manufacturing and distributing the banknotes of this family has represented a yearning, a continuous motivation and, today, a reality. 12 As on every occasion that one of the G family banknotes has been presented, I am sure that this monetary sign will not only be an efficient, safe and durable means of payment, but will also be a reason to evoke and take pride in what unites us powerfully as Mexicans: the richness of our history and cultural identity, as well as the abundance and variety of our natural heritage. Thanks a lot. 13
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la presentacin del billete de 50 pesos.1 28 de octubre de 2021 Estimadas subgobernadoras y estimados subgobernadores del Banco de Mxico; Alejandro Alegre, director general de Emisin del Banco; Representantes de los medios de comunicacin; Compaeras y compaeros; Seoras y seores: 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad del autor y no necesariamente representan la posicin institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno. 1 A nombre de la Junta de Gobierno, me complace darles la bienvenida a la ceremonia de puesta en circulacin del nuevo billete de 50 pesos, que es la sexta denominacin de la familia G. *** Como gran parte de los bancos centrales en el mundo, el Banco de Mxico tiene el objetivo prioritario de proveer de moneda nacional a la economa del pas y preservar la estabilidad de su poder adquisitivo. Para alcanzar su objetivo primordial, es importante que un banco central cuente con mandatos legales y encomiendas institucionales claras que eviten que su facultad exclusiva de emitir dinero sea utilizada inadecuadamente, lo que ocasionara graves consecuencias econmicas y sociales. Por eso, desde finales del siglo XX, se gener un amplio consenso de que la autonoma era el estatuto idneo para que un banco central concentrara sus instrumentos y esfuerzos en promover la estabilidad de precios con una visin consistente y de largo alcance. Bajo este arreglo institucional es posible generar en el pblico la certeza de que, al emitir y colocar dinero, el banco central actuar siguiendo 2 reglas que honren su compromiso con la sociedad de mantener una inflacin baja y estable. Ello, a su vez, contribuye a que el dinero cumpla eficientemente sus tres funciones esenciales: i) ser un medio de pago generalmente aceptado; ii) funcionar como un depsito de valor confiable en el tiempo y iii) fungir como unidad de cuenta para todas las transacciones de la economa. Desde 1994, el Banco de Mxico cuenta con autonoma para cumplir de mejor manera su mandato prioritario de mantener el poder adquisitivo de la moneda. Con este esquema, nuestro pas ha logrado una de las etapas ms prolongadas de estabilidad de precios en su historia, lo cual refuerza la confianza de la poblacin en el uso de sus billetes y monedas. *** En cumplimiento de su mandato constitucional, desde su fundacin en 1925, este Instituto Central se ha encargado de emitir billetes. A partir de 1969, los billetes mexicanos se comenzaron a imprimir en territorio nacional con el inicio de operaciones de la primera fbrica de billetes del pas, ubicada en la Ciudad de Mxico. Ahora, desde 2018, esta funcin tambin se realiza en la fbrica de Jalisco, lo que refuerza la capacidad 3 de produccin de moneda nacional para el cabal cumplimiento del mandato constitucional. El Banco de Mxico haba puesto en circulacin 6 familias de billetes, desde la AA hasta la F. En 2013, tras un profundo anlisis prospectivo de la situacin de los billetes en nuestro pas, la Institucin tom la determinacin de emitir la sptima familia, conocida como G, atendiendo a distintas razones: 1) Brindar a la poblacin un medio de pago seguro y confiable, con nuevos y reforzados elementos de seguridad que dificultaran la reproduccin ilegal de los billetes. Ello considerando los avances y difusin de las tecnologas de impresin grfica digital. 2) Suministrar billetes, cuyo uso resulte sencillo, y que puedan ser fcilmente identificados por todo tipo de usuarios o dispositivos, ya sea personas ciegas y dbiles visuales o equipos automatizados. 3) Preservar las caractersticas de seguridad y funcionalidad de los billetes por ms tiempo, al incrementar su vida til en circulacin. 4 4) Reforzar, por medio de los billetes, elementos de identidad nacional que nos vinculen con la riqueza natural y cultural de Mxico y con aspectos fundamentales de nuestra historia. Con la emisin del nuevo billete de 50 pesos, el Banco de Mxico culmina la emisin de la familia G y cierra un ciclo que comenz hace 8 aos. *** El nuevo billete de 50 pesos tiene como color predominante el morado, su formato es vertical, est impreso en sustrato de polmero y su anverso hace alusin a la Fundacin de Tenochtitlan, representando el periodo histrico del Mxico Antiguo, mientras que su reverso est dedicado al ecosistema de ros y lagos, con el ajolote y el maz, en Xochimilco en la Ciudad de Mxico, patrimonio cultural de la humanidad. El motivo principal del billete en su anverso consiste en un fragmento del dorso del monolito conocido como Teocalli de la Guerra Sagrada que fue labrado durante el imperio mexica por rdenes del emperador Moctezuma II. Este monolito consiste en un guila posada sobre un nopal con el Atl-tlachinolli en el pico, smbolo que significa agua- 5 hoguera, elementos opuestos y complementarios, cuya unin es metfora de la guerra sagrada. El Teocalli fue rescatado en los aos veinte del siglo pasado de los cimientos del Palacio Nacional, donde estaba situado el palacio de Moctezuma II. En el primero de los estudios sobre este monolito, en 1927, el antroplogo Alfonso Caso destac la riqueza de sus smbolos y concluy que celebra el triunfo del sol y el poder militar de los mexicas tras la fundacin de su ciudad. El dorso del Teocalli remite a la seal fundacional de la ciudad del pueblo azteca, despus de un largo peregrinar de ms de 200 aos. El relato de la peregrinacin explica que los aztecas salieron de Aztln, atendiendo la indicacin de Huitzilopochtli para que fueran hacia nuevas tierras y fundaran su ciudad donde estuviera un guila posada sobre un nopal. Los aztecas deambularon por varios lugares y finalmente, en el ao dos casa (1325), que se representa en el billete debajo de la vieta, establecieron la ciudad de Tenochtitlan. Este es el origen del actual escudo nacional, en el que destaca un guila devorando una 6 serpiente, convirtindolo en el smbolo y referente nacional de mayor importancia en nuestra historia. Resulta muy significativo contar, en esta ceremonia, con una rplica de este impresionante monolito y agradecemos a Antonio Saborit, director del Museo Nacional de Antropologa, por el prstamo de esta pieza. La representacin del monolito se acompaa por un fragmento del mural de Diego Rivera La gran Tenochtitlan (vista desde el mercado de Tlatelolco), en el que se observa la calzada de Tlacopan, hoy calzada de Tacuba, la cual dirige al Templo Mayor, espacio que fue el centro de la vida poltica y religiosa de la sociedad mexica y, de fondo, el lago de Texcoco y los volcanes Popocatpetl e Iztacchuatl. Este mural muestra en pleno apogeo la ciudad de Tenochtitlan, la ms poblada y rica de Mesoamrica y una de las ms grandes del mundo en la poca. Enmarca la composicin del anverso el glifo lunar, en alusin al nombre de Mxico. Debemos a Alfonso Caso la explicacin de la etimologa de este nombre, que deriva de los vocablos metztli (luna), xictli (ombligo, 7 centro), y co (lugar), dando en su composicin la palabra Mexi-co, cuyo significado es en el centro de la Luna.2 Rodea la ventana transparente un elemento muy significativo en la tradicin prehispnica, el Ollin, el cual est formado por dos bandas entrelazadas, cuyo significado es movimiento.3 Como indic don Miguel Len Portilla, uno mismo es el origen de las palabras nahuas movimiento, corazn y alma. Lo cual prueba que para los antiguos mexicanos era inconcebible la vida sin el movimiento.4 El reverso del billete est dedicado al ecosistema de ros y lagos, con el ajolote y el maz, en Xochimilco en la Ciudad de Mxico, patrimonio cultural de la humanidad; este ltimo es un espacio de gran importancia ecolgica y cultural. Este sitio fue declarado patrimonio cultural por la UNESCO en 1987 por ser testimonio vivo de la cultura lacustre del Valle 2 Alfonso Caso, El guila y el nopal, en Estudios de cultura nhuatl, nm. 50, Mxico, UNAM, Instituto de Investigaciones Histricas, julio-diciembre de 2015, pp. 355-369, p. 360. 3 Yolotl Gonzlez Torres, Diccionario de mitologa y religin de Mesoamrica, Mxico, Ediciones Larousse, 1995, p. 130. 4 Miguel Len Portilla, La filosofa nhuatl estudiada en sus fuentes, 11a ed., Mxico, UNAM, Instituto de Investigaciones Histricas, 2017, p. 167. 8 de Mxico, as como por contar con un sistema agrcola tradicional nico en el mundo, las chinampas. En el billete tambin se plasma el cultivo de maz, de gran importancia econmica y social en Mxico y cuya presencia, en las culturas prehispnicas, marcaba su vida ritual y el desarrollo de todas sus actividades cotidianas. Enmarca el reverso del billete el rbol de ahuejote o sauce de agua que forma bosques ribereos y que; para los mexicas, era un rbol sagrado, vital para mantener la estructura de las chinampas. Entre las especies que aloja la regin lacustre de Xochimilco se encuentra el ajolote mexicano, representado destacadamente en el billete. Este anfibio, del grupo de las salamandras, es motivo de mltiples estudios por su rareza, belleza y gran riqueza biolgica. Adems, el ajolote fue relevante en las culturas prehispnicas ya que representaba a Xlotl, dios del ocaso, protector del fuego y uno de los seores del inframundo, hermano de Quetzalcatl. *** Estas son, en breve, las caractersticas del nuevo billete de 50 pesos, que hoy se presenta a los mexicanos. Quiero destacar que el recorrido 9 para poner en circulacin este billete, y toda la familia G, ha conllevado importantes aprendizajes y retos, y ha comprendido, entre otros aspectos: el estudio detallado de las caractersticas idneas a incorporar en los billetes; el desarrollo de varias propuestas de bocetos; el cuidado de cada lnea que conforma el diseo, la integracin de las materias primas e insumos con las mquinas de produccin de billetes y, por supuesto, su distribucin en todos los rincones del pas. Han sido aos de trabajo constante, en los que se estudiaron las necesidades, hbitos y preferencias de la sociedad mexicana, a fin de verificar la utilidad y potencial aceptacin del billete y situar estratgicamente cada componente de seguridad, temtico y denominativo que lo conforma. Desde luego, el Banco de Mxico no recorri este camino solo y colabor estrechamente con los proveedores de la industria y con otros especialistas. En particular, en lo que respecta a la temtica de los billetes, el Banco de Mxico tiene una enorme deuda de gratitud con un amplio grupo de expertas y expertos en materia de historia, 10 biodiversidad, arte y cultura de nuestro pas. Dichas expertas y expertos provienen de las ms reconocidas instituciones acadmicas y centros de investigacin a nivel nacional, y colaboraron con nosotros en la seleccin de los motivos que mejor representaran a nuestra nacin y que fortaleceran el sentimiento de pertenencia y unidad. Por ello, nuestro mayor agradecimiento a:  La Academia Mexicana de la Historia;  La Academia Mexicana de la Lengua;  El Antiguo Colegio de San Ildefonso;  El Centro de Investigaciones y Estudios Superiores en Antropologa Social del Consejo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnologa;  El Colegio de Mxico;  El Colegio Nacional;  La Comisin Nacional de reas Naturales Protegidas;  La Comisin Nacional para el Conocimiento y Uso de la Biodiversidad;  El Consejo Nacional para la Cultura y las Artes, hoy Secretara de Cultura; 11  El Fomento Cultural Banamex A.C.;  El Instituto Nacional de Antropologa e Historia;  El Instituto Nacional de Estadstica y Geografa;  El Instituto Nacional de Estudios Histricos de las Revoluciones de Mxico;  El Museo Regional de la Revolucin Mexicana, Casa de los Hermanos Serdn;  La Universidad del Claustro de Sor Juana;  y la Universidad Nacional Autnoma de Mxico, a travs de sus diversos institutos. Por supuesto, agradezco profundamente a las compaeras y compaeros del Banco de Mxico, particularmente a todos los integrantes de la Direccin General de Emisin, por su gran compromiso, entrega y profesionalismo para cumplir con la presentacin de toda la familia G. En circunstancias muy complejas, por los retos que ha entraado la pandemia. Para todos en el Banco de Mxico la tarea de disear, fabricar y distribuir los billetes de esta familia, ha representado un anhelo, una motivacin continua y, hoy, una realidad. 12 Como en cada ocasin que se ha presentado uno de los billetes de la familia G, estoy seguro que este signo monetario no slo ser un medio de pago eficiente, seguro y durable, sino que tambin ser un motivo para evocar y enorgullecernos de lo que nos une poderosamente como mexicanos: la riqueza de nuestra historia e identidad cultural, as como la abundancia y variedad de nuestro patrimonio natural. Muchas gracias. 13

Title: Financial Systemic Risk
text: G20 Conference on Financial Systemic Risk September 27-28, Istanbul, Turkey Opening Remarks by Deputy Governor Manuel Ramos-Francia Governor Bac, Deputy Prime Minister Babacan, Distinguished Guests, First of all, allow me to thank the Central Bank of Turkey for organizing this very relevant seminar in such a wonderful city. I am certain that the discussions we will hold in these couple of days will be fruitful and enlightening. This Seminar is part of the work of the G20 for 2012 and I am looking forward to listening to the presentations of the distinguished guests. The past few years have put the word systemic in the minds and lips of most policymakers, analysts, and the media. Indeed, the financial crisis that started since 2007 evidenced the deep interconnections between financial systems, and between financial systems and economies across the world. The complexity of the financial instruments multiplied the links between various holders of these securities far and beyond national boundaries. Even countries whose financial systems did not incur in the excesses that were evident in some other countries became vulnerable to sudden stops and liquidity squeezes. No matter how sound the practices were in some domestic financial systems, and how prudent the regulation, the magnitude of the crisis affected everyone (though, it must be said, in different degrees). In this environment, authorities around the world and in the G20 in particular, began to think much harder about the origins of risk, the channels through which it spreads, the consequences of tail events, and ways to minimize the losses that could arise when these risks actually materialize. In this sense, financial systemic risk is at the core of current discussions at the G20. Indeed, many of our efforts like enhancing surveillance, engaging in spillover reports, mutual assessment of economic policies, and the identification of areas of opportunity, all aim at identifying risks, including financial systemic risk. Financial stability is a strategic front because of its important role in the recovery of the economy and therefore, it is not surprising that we have had a multidimensional approach to this issue. In fact, the structure of this Conference is a very 1 appropriate illustration of the many fronts we have to delve into in order to tackle this complex issue. Indeed, the outline of the conference has a correspondence to many of the topics and preoccupations we have been dealing with at the G20. In this regard, one of the main aspects of the G20 process is that of the Framework for a Strong, Sustainable and Balanced Growth. This framework, in turn, has several components, including a regular practice of a mutual assessment of policies and the evaluation by international financial institutions. In this last aspect, we have made significant progress in making this analysis more efficient and timely and in addressing not only the internal consistency of policies, but also the mutual consistency of policies across countries with the purpose of identifying risks to growth. The current crisis in Europe illustrates painfully well how the adverse feedback loop between financial vulnerabilities has reduced economic activity and sovereign debt sustainability remains one of the key risks to the global economic outlook. As I said before, under the present context of a fragile global economy, the analysis of financial systemic risk has a strategic relevance. For instance, the potential impacts of the current process of banks deleveraging on financial systemic risk are uncertain. Another important aspect of our work has been the strengthening of the international financial architecture. In this area, we have looked at the characteristics of the International Monetary System and how, under certain circumstances, shocks can spread around the world, for instance through volatile capital flows and droughts in global liquidity. We have recognized the importance of global financial safety nets that function as a backstop to prevent or reduce contagion. During the Mexican Presidency of the G20 we have been able to reinforce these global financial safety nets through a significant collaborative effort of several countries, both G20 and non-G20. At the end of the day, both the strengthening of surveillance and of the global financial firewalls aim at dealing with systemic risks in a preemptive way. The challenge for the future lies in setting up the architecture that will allow us to focus on crises prevention rather than on crises resolution. One other issue at the core of the work of the G20, in particular under the G20 Mexican Presidency, is financial regulation. This subject is, obviously, the most direct way of approaching the issue of financial systemic risk and we have been looking at it from several directions. The big leap in modern science was launched by measurement. Economics is not the exception, and successful efforts, such as the Cowles Foundation, embraced its importance with the motto Science is measurement, and later Theory and measurement. 2 One aspect that corresponds to Session 1 of this Conference is related to the efforts to bridge data gaps. Let me say something, in more detail, about the issue of the measurement of systemic risk. There is no doubt that in order to have useful indicators we need sufficient and reliable data. In this respect, the G20 made an early start soon after the crisis by creating the DATA GAPS initiative. During the crisis it was clear that the lack of accurate and consistent information proved to have a very high cost. Also, for our efforts to result in a more efficient supervisory framework we need better information than we had prior to the crisis. This would allow for the timely identification of the build-up of systemic risk. In particular, the G20 Data Gaps Initiative aims at improving the early identification of risks and vulnerabilities in the financial sector, gathering information in a structured manner to better understand the interconnections in a bottom up approach. This means looking at a wide array of domestic indicators trying to find weak spots and potential sources of vulnerabilities. By taking a comprehensive look at these indicators at the international level, we could also identify potential transmission channels of shocks. The objective is to create the infrastructure to be able to monitor global flows and positions in a timely and active manner. We have to remember that in todays international financial system, the resilience of the whole system is as strong as its weakest link. Therefore, the goal is to strengthen each and every one of its components. We cannot minimize the importance of macroprudential policies and the regulatory agenda as key elements for mitigating financial systemic risks. As expressed by G20 leaders, our objective is to develop macroprudential policy frameworks and tools to limit the build-up of risks in the financial sector, building on the ongoing work of the FSB-BIS-IMF on this subject. In particular, the G20 has been calling for international bodies to take into account emerging market and developing economies specific circumstances and concerns in designing new international financial standards and policies. And here, let me emphasize that we need to maintain momentum on the financial sector institutional reforms in order to safeguard the financial systems over the medium term, while taking appropriate actions in the short term to protect credit channels and the integrity of global payments and settlements systems. Notwithstanding all the work that has been done, it is evident that there still is significant value added to be obtained from including a more thorough assessment of financial systemic risk in our policy discussions. In fact, a first step in this regard can be to explicitly connect our technical discussions regarding financial regulation and measurement of systemic risk to the global outlook assessment. Strong macroprudential policies are one way to avoid systemic risks, but we are far from having a clear analysis of how these policies can work in the most effective manner alongside with monetary policy. We still have a lot of work to do in order to 3 understand how monetary policy interacts with banks risk-taking under the new regulatory framework. This is, clearly, a very important consideration for the way in which we should assess risks going forward. In addition, we have to be careful not to put under the umbrella of the macroprudential framework every possible policy measure; including protectionist ones. At the end of the day, we should strive to have a thorough analysis of these policies to evaluate their effectiveness with respect to the understanding and identification of the accumulation of systemic risk. Let me finish with the following thoughts and a word of caution: Back in 2003, one of the most renowned macroeconomists stated, and I quote: Macroeconomics was born as a distinct field in the 1940s, as a part of the intellectual response to the Great Depression. The term then referred to the body of knowledge and expertise that we hoped would prevent the recurrence of that economic disaster. My thesis in this lecture is that macroeconomics in this original sense has succeeded: Its central problem of depression-prevention has been solved, for all practical purposes, and has in fact been solved for many decades. [] End of quote. (That was Lucas in 2003). Clearly, this reflected the state of overconfidence at the time and, perhaps, gave a false sense of security to the profession and the general public. Very few were the dissenting voices that warned us of the incoming peril. It took, since then, less than a lustrum for another economic disaster to ensue. As I have commented, and all of you have seen, the policy response to the crisis has been unprecedented, both at the domestic and the international levels. Accordingly, after the crisis, research done in policy institutions, think tanks, and universities on financial systemic risk has been commensurate. Nonetheless hitherto, as I have also mentioned, we are far from a consensus on financial systemic risk and, albeit some common themes are emerging, much remains to be done. Having said that, it is useful to remember the following: First, as emphasized by Reinhart and Rogoff (2009), financial crises have been part of history, or more generally, risk is a fact of life. In effect, there is a given level of risk in the economy that is impossible to eliminate, it is essentially nondiversifiable, call it macroeconomic or systematic risk. In this context, while there is an unavoidable level of risk, above and beyond this level, there can easily be more risk. Evidently, broadly speaking, we should procure to be at the lowest level of risk possible, subject to the restrictions we face (prevention). 4 In addition, given that some level of risk is inevitable, we need contingency plans in case a crisis follows. In particular, we need ex-ante risk-sharing mechanisms (mitigation).1 Second, there is a trade-off between economic growth and risk. There is a point in which ensuring less risk necessarily entails less economic growth. It seems that we are nowadays unconditionally embracing risk regulation without carefully considering what it could imply for economic growth or other potential consequences in the long run. Indeed, there could be pernicious incentives to overregulate. In this context, we need to do at least two things: To quantify this growth-risk trade-off (which is a technological issue); and, Decide, to the extent possible, upon its magnitude (which is a preferences issue). Needless to say, these basic finance principles, apply also to systemic risk. Of course, this seminar is directed towards making progress on all of this. Once again, I thank the Central Bank of Turkey, Governor Bac, and the Turkish financial authorities, Minister Babacan, for welcoming us in Istanbul and I look forward to the fruitful discussions that lie ahead. Thank you very much. 1 Ex post adjustment mechanisms, although sometimes used, are negotiated or imposed and thus are typically not conducive to a swift recovery. 5 References Lucas, R.E. (2003). "Macroeconomic Priorities." American Economic Review. Volume 93(1), pages 1-14, March. Reinhart, C. and K.S. Rogoff (2009). This Time is Different: Eight Centuries of Financial Folly. Princeton University Press. 6

Title: FIRA: a success story of development banking
text: FIRA: A development banking success story Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico during the inauguration of the seminar on the occasion of the 60th Anniversary of FIRA (Trusts Instituted in Relation to Agriculture), of which the Bank of Mexico is its trustee. Morelia, Michoacan, December 11, 2014 ? Mr. Salvador Jara Guerrero, Governor of the State of Michoacan, ? Mr. Enrique Martinez y Martinez, Secretary of Agriculture, Livestock, Rural Development, Fisheries and Food, ? Mr. Alfredo Castillo Cervantes, Commissioner for Safety and Security Integral Development of Michoacan, ? Senator Manuel Cota Jimenez, President of the National Confederation Peasant and President of the Agriculture and Livestock Commission of the Senate of the Republic, ? Senator Gerardo Sanchez Garcia, Former President of the National Peasant Confederation ? Deputy Silvano Aureoles Conejo, President of the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Deputies, ? Deputy Salvador Barajas, President of the Livestock Commission of the Chamber of Deputies, ? Mr. Luis Robles Miaja, President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, ? Mr. Luis Gomez Garay, Coordinator of the Permanent Agrarian Congress (CAP), ? Lic. Maria Esther Teran Velazquez, President of the National Confederation of Rural Owners (CNPR), 1 ? Eng. Hector Padilla Gutierrez, Secretary of Rural Development of Jalisco and President of the Mexican Association of Secretaries of Agricultural Development, A.C. (AMSDA) ? Officials and employees of FIRA, ? Ladies and gentlemen: Good morning. 60 years away, and in view of what FIRA means today within development banking and for the agricultural sector in Mexico, I have no doubt about the accurate vision that Don Rodrigo Gomez, then director of the Bank of Mexico, who conceived and promoted the creation of this second-floor bank, had. FIRA throughout six decades of history has established itself as an indispensable reference for development projects in the Mexican countryside and has been guided by the three main objectives that inspired its creation: ? Improve the standard of living of agricultural producers through productive and profitable projects, 2 ? Increase capital formation in the agricultural sector, where human capital formation through technical advice clearly stands out, and ? Generate a greater participation of private banks in the country's agricultural financing. Undoubtedly, FIRA has reason to be proud of these six decades of achievements, but there is still ample room to enhance the singularities of FIRA within development banking and there are new and transcendental challenges that FIRA will have to undertake in the immediate future, as I will mention later. For now, trying to identify the factors that have made FIRA a unique financial institution I can highlight four that are: 1. The credibility and vision of stability and long term granted by its trustee, the Bank of Mexico. Indeed, the trustee represents advantages for the financial operation of FIRA, having facilitated the maintenance of rigorous standards of financial and operational planning, since, like the Bank of Mexico, FIRA has privileged the values of permanence and stability. 3 In this same aspect, a career civil service has been developed that has led to the accumulation and continuous improvement of the human capital of the Institution, which manifests great pride in belonging to an entity recognized for its professional performance and for its high work ethic. 2. A business model with comprehensive financing, with guarantees and funding, adapted to the permanent need to mitigate risks - both for producers and financial intermediaries - that characterizes the agricultural sector throughout history and throughout the world. It is a model that to date remains innovative. In fact, FIRA's guarantee fund, the FEGA, is recognized as the oldest guarantee fund of continuous operation in Latin America. 3. Another unique asset of FIRA is the capacities it has developed throughout its history in the evaluation and monitoring of agricultural projects. On the one hand, FIRA's 108 offices throughout all the entities of the country allow it to closely monitor those accredited and the development of the financed projects. 4 On the other hand, this same regional coverage, in addition to promoting direct contact with producers, has facilitated the creation of a unique local information infrastructure that is key in the evaluation of new projects. In addition, practically since its inception FIRA has given special emphasis to the granting of advice, training and technology transfer in order to raise the productivity and profitability of projects, which also allows companies to expand and deepen the coverage of complete services in rural areas. The FIRA method consists of supporting the organization of producers, formulating business plans, detecting investment opportunities and structuring, based on these foundations, new projects that can be financed. In this way, FIRA acts to stimulate both the supply and demand of credit. FIRA has five technological development centers that provide technical advice and training as well as the most extensive and consolidated network of agribusiness consultants, with 1,463 certified technicians and 219 offices, whose promotion work multiplies the impact of this development bank, and 5 4. Thanks to a prudent operation FIRA is characterized by the strength of its heritage. At no time throughout its history, not even as a result of the severe crises suffered by the national economy in the final decades of the last century, FIRA has required bailouts to reconstitute its heritage. It should be noted that FIRA operates with its own assets and has no guarantee from the federal government. Thus, at the end of October 2014, FIRA's assets ranked first among development banks and fifth place compared to the country's commercial banks. It would be a mistake, however, for this magnificent record of FIRA to lead us to complacency. FIRA has forward not only the challenge of endorsing and consolidating the good financial practices that have allowed it to occupy this prominent place, it also has in the immediate two new challenges of great importance. The first of these challenges is to help efficiently reduce the volatility that has characterized the prices of many of the main agricultural products, since this volatility affects the same to the 6 producers than consumers, and may even disturb the anchoring of expectations of low and stable inflation. On the one hand, the persistence of notable variations, up and down, in agricultural prices prevents producers from making better investment decisions, since it increases uncertainty about the profitability of future harvests. In turn, this greater margin of uncertainty inhibits the supply of credit to producers because financial intermediaries perceive, not without reason, a greater risk. On the other hand, the constant variations in the prices of agricultural products damage the budget of consumers and affect more those who have less, because it is precisely households with lower incomes that allocate more spending to the food and beverage sector. Indeed, while households in the highest income decile spend only about 16% of their total spending on food and beverages, households at the other end of the income distribution, that is, those in the lowest income decile, spend on average more than 47% of their total income on food and beverages. 7 FIRA, with the collaboration and advice of the Bank of Mexico, has made a diagnosis of the four areas in which specific actions must be carried out to mitigate the volatility of agricultural prices: 1. Geographical diversification, 2. Increase in productivity, 3. Storage and 4. Information systems. It is clear that focusing on the four aspects that I have just mentioned, FIRA has an impact on the generation of greater certainty for producers and financial intermediaries, which in turn translates into greater stability of supply over time and, therefore, contributes to mitigating the volatility of agricultural prices. Likewise, they are actions that promote better and greater access to credit for producers as well as the increase in the profitability of agricultural activities. The second immediate challenge that FIRA has, and in which it is already working, is the one that refers to contributing to the development of the special economic zones in the south of the country, which a few days ago the President of the Republic instructed. 8 As is known, the presidential proposal for these special zones contemplates providing them with a modern infrastructure, strengthening security and the rule of law and making them recipients of preferential financing by development banks. The President's proposal contemplates a differentiated fiscal treatment for producers in Chiapas, Guerrero, Oaxaca, as well as around Lazaro Cardenas Michoacan, and promote, in these entities, the establishment and growth of agro-industrial companies. All this, together with emerging programs to boost the countryside with an investment of 4 billion additional pesos in credit and a program of renovation and repopulation of coffee plantations. To contribute to this promising program of development of special economic zones FIRA has different instruments and strategic programs, for which it has resources from the Budget of Expenditures of the Federation directly, for which I thank the legislators several of them present here who support the field. Likewise, FIRA counts to support many productive projects with the operation of programs of the 9 SAGARPA, for which I thank Secretary Martinez y Martinez for the support he has given to FIRA to make successful synergies feasible. I briefly describe the tasks of FIRA to collaborate in this ambitious effort to develop special economic zones: 1. To improve and promote access to credit in the areas determined by the Presidential Plan, FIRA will support the reduction of 200 basis points in the cost of the interest rate in financing granted up to 800 thousand pesos; in the same vein, it will guarantee financial intermediaries up to 80% of the financing they grant and will provide support equivalent to 70% of the cost of the service of this guarantee and will channel technical assistance and training resources to support the organization of producers, the creation of legal figures appropriate to economies of scale and integration into value networks. It will also launch the family farming program through which financing will be channeled to productive projects that generate value and permanence of the family business, through institutions of 10 Social Banking. To achieve this, the risk premium and support for the reduction of transaction costs will be subsidized. 2. FIRA has developed targeted programs to strengthen the main prevailing value chains. In particular, the renovation of coffee plantations and the establishment of fruit trees will be supported through a specific guarantee fund; this means providing financing that is complemented by a guarantee of first losses to financial intermediaries and supporting producers with the payment of interest during the pre-productive period of the plantation. Likewise, in the southern states, strategic projects will be developed with a mixture of resources from the south-southeast development program that includes support of up to 50% of the investment. It should be noted that at the President's call to promote economic activity in Michoacan, FIRA launched a special strategy of which we highlight: 1. The committed amount of operation was 8,000 MDP, having an estimate to close the year with at least 8,700 MDP in 11 credit flow (8.75% additional to the program), reaching the fifth statement of greater credit flow in the FIRA portfolio. The expected credit balance is 5,500 million pesos, 12% more real than at the end of 2013. 2. The above, added to the contribution of producers to investment projects, represents at least 10,700 MDP that have been injected into the agri-food sector of Michoacan during 2014. 2. This financing has been given to 65,234 beneficiaries with the possibility of incorporating an additional 3,000. 3. The area served is 133 thousand ha, 290 tractors financed, for the benefit of 1,667 companies. To efficiently address these immediate challenges, FIRA is backed by its own success story over these six decades. In this way, guided by the good financial practices that have characterized it, supported its business model and the quality of its human capital, I have no doubt that FIRA will continue to endorse its well-deserved prestige within development banking in our country. 12 I can only congratulate all the staff of FIRA for the first 60 years of the successful existence of this financial institution. Thanks a lot. 13
text_original: FIRA: Una historia de xito de la banca de desarrollo Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico durante la inauguracin del seminario con motivo del 60 Aniversario de FIRA (Fideicomisos Instituidos en Relacin con la Agricultura), del cual el Banco de Mxico es su fiduciario. Morelia, Michoacn, 11 de diciembre de 2014  Lic. Salvador Jara Guerrero, Gobernador del Estado de Michoacn,  Lic. Enrique Martnez y Martnez, Secretario de Agricultura, Ganadera, Desarrollo Rural, Pesca y Alimentacin,  Lic. Alfredo Castillo Cervantes, Comisionado para la Seguridad y el Desarrollo Integral de Michoacn,  Senador Manuel Cota Jimnez, Presidente de Confederacin Nacional Campesina y Presidente de la Comisin de Agricultura y Ganadera del Senado de la Repblica,  Senador Gerardo Snchez Garca, Ex Presidente de la Confederacin Nacional Campesina  Diputado Silvano Aureoles Conejo, Presidente de la Mesa Directiva de la Cmara de Diputados,  Diputado Salvador Barajas, Presidente de la Comisin de Ganadera de la Cmara de Diputados,  Lic. Luis Robles Miaja, Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico,  Lic. Luis Gmez Garay, Coordinador del Congreso Agrario Permanente (CAP),  Lic. Mara Esther Tern Velzquez, Presidenta de la Confederacin Nacional de Propietarios Rurales (CNPR), 1  Ing. Hctor Padilla Gutirrez, Secretario de Desarrollo Rural de Jalisco y Presidente de la Asociacin Mexicana de Secretarios de Desarrollo Agropecuario, A.C. (AMSDA)  Funcionarios y empleados de FIRA,  Seoras y seores: Muy buenos das. A 60 aos de distancia, y a la vista de lo que hoy significa FIRA dentro de la banca de desarrollo y para el sector agropecuario en Mxico, no me cabe duda de la certera visin que tuvo don Rodrigo Gmez, director entonces del Banco de Mxico, quien concibi e impuls la creacin de este banco de segundo piso. FIRA a lo largo de seis dcadas de historia se ha consolidado como una referencia indispensable para los proyectos de desarrollo en el campo mexicano y se ha guiado por los tres grandes objetivos que inspiraron su creacin:  Mejorar el nivel de vida de los productores agropecuarios a travs de proyectos productivos y rentables, 2  Aumentar la formacin de capital del sector agrcola, donde destaca claramente la formacin de capital humano mediante la asesora tcnica, y  Generar una mayor participacin de la banca privada en el financiamiento agropecuario del pas. Indudablemente, FIRA tiene motivos para enorgullecerse por estas seis dcadas de logros, pero an hay amplio margen para potenciar las singularidades de FIRA dentro de la banca de desarrollo y hay nuevos y trascendentales desafos que FIRA deber emprender en el futuro inmediato, como mencionar ms adelante. Por lo pronto, tratando de identificar los factores que han hecho de FIRA una institucin financiera nica puedo destacar cuatro que son: 1. La credibilidad y visin de estabilidad y largo plazo que le otorga su fiduciario, el Banco de Mxico. En efecto, el fiduciario representa ventajas en para la operacin financiera de FIRA, al haber facilitado que se mantengan rigurosos estndares de planeacin financiera y operativa, ya que, a semejanza del Banco de Mxico, FIRA ha privilegiado los valores de la permanencia y la estabilidad. 3 En esta misma vertiente, se ha desarrollado un servicio civil de carrera que ha propiciado la acumulacin y mejora continua del capital humano de la Institucin, que manifiesta un gran orgullo por pertenecer a una entidad reconocida por su desempeo profesional y por su elevada tica laboral. 2. Un modelo de negocio con financiamiento integral, con garantas y fondeo, adaptado a la permanente necesidad de mitigar riesgos  tanto para los productores como para los intermediarios financieros- que caracteriza al sector agropecuario a lo largo de la historia y en todo el mundo. Es un modelo que a la fecha sigue siendo innovador. De hecho, el fondo de garanta de FIRA, el FEGA, es reconocido como el fondo de garantas con mayor antigedad de operacin continua en Iberoamrica. 3. Otro activo nico de FIRA es el que constituyen las capacidades que ha desarrollado a lo largo de su historia en la evaluacin y el monitoreo de proyectos agropecuarios. Por una parte, las 108 oficinas de FIRA a lo largo de todas las entidades del pas le permiten dar un seguimiento cercano a los acreditados y al desenvolvimiento de los proyectos financiados. 4 Por otra, esta misma cobertura regional adems de propiciar el contacto directo con los productores ha facilitado la creacin de una infraestructura nica de informacin local que resulta clave en la evaluacin de nuevos proyectos. Adems, prcticamente desde su origen FIRA ha dado especial nfasis al otorgamiento de asesora, capacitacin y transferencia tecnolgica con el objeto de elevar la productividad y la rentabilidad de los proyectos, lo que, asimismo, permite que las empresas amplen y profundicen la cobertura de servicios completos en el medio rural. El mtodo de FIRA consiste en apoyar la organizacin de los productores, formular planes de negocios, detectar oportunidades de inversin y estructurar, a partir de esos fundamentos, nuevos proyectos susceptibles de ser financiados. De esta forma, FIRA acta para estimular tanto la oferta como la demanda de crdito. FIRA cuenta con cinco centros de desarrollo tecnolgico que brindan asesora tcnica y capacitacin as como con la ms extensa y consolidada red de consultores en Agronegocios, con 1,463 tcnicos certificados y 219 despachos, cuya labor de promocin multiplica el impacto de esta banca de desarrollo, y 5 4. Gracias a una prudente operacin FIRA se caracteriza por la fortaleza de su patrimonio. En ningn momento a lo largo de su historia, ni siquiera como consecuencia de las severas crisis que padeci la economa nacional en las dcadas finales del siglo pasado, FIRA ha requerido de rescates para reconstituir su patrimonio. Debe notarse que FIRA opera con patrimonio propio y no dispone de garanta del gobierno federal. De esta forma, al cierre de octubre de 2014 el patrimonio de FIRA ocupa el primer lugar entre la banca de desarrollo y el quinto lugar si le compara con los bancos comerciales del pas. Sera un error, sin embargo, que este magnfico historial de FIRA nos llevara a la autocomplacencia. FIRA tiene hacia adelante no slo el desafo de refrendar y consolidar las buenas prcticas financieras que le han permitido ocupar este lugar destacado, tambin tiene en lo inmediato dos nuevos retos de gran importancia. El primero de estos retos es coadyuvar eficientemente a disminuir la volatilidad que ha caracterizado a los precios de muchos de los principales productos agropecuarios, ya que dicha volatilidad afecta lo mismo a los 6 productores que a los consumidores, e incluso puede perturbar el anclaje de las expectativas de una inflacin baja y estable. Por una parte, la persistencia de variaciones notables, al alza y a la baja, en los precios agropecuarios impide que los productores tomen mejores decisiones de inversin, dado que incrementa la incertidumbre acerca de la rentabilidad de las futuras cosechas. A su vez, este mayor margen de incertidumbre inhibe la oferta de crdito a los productores porque los intermediarios financieros perciben, no sin razn, un riesgo mayor. Por otra parte, las constantes variaciones en los precios de los productos agropecuarios lesionan el presupuesto de los consumidores y afectan ms a quienes menos tienen, porque son precisamente los hogares con ingresos ms bajos los que destinan ms gasto al rubro de alimentos y bebidas. En efecto, mientras los hogares ubicados en el decil de ingresos ms alto destinan slo alrededor del 16% de su gasto total a alimentos y bebidas, los hogares situados en el otro extremo de la distribucin del ingreso, esto es: los del decil de ingresos ms bajo, gastan en promedio ms del 47% de sus ingresos totales en alimentos y bebidas. 7 FIRA, con la colaboracin y asesora del Banco de Mxico, ha realizado un diagnstico de cules son las cuatro reas en las que se deben realizar acciones especficas para mitigar la volatilidad de los precios agropecuarios: 1. Diversificacin geogrfica, 2. Incremento de la productividad, 3. Almacenamiento y 4. Sistemas de informacin. Es claro que al enfocarse en las cuatro vertientes que acabo de mencionar FIRA incide en la generacin de una mayor certidumbre para los productores y para los intermediarios financieros, lo que a su vez se traduce en una mayor estabilidad de la oferta a lo largo del tiempo y, por ende, contribuye a mitigar la volatilidad de los precios de productos agropecuarios. Asimismo, son acciones que propician un mejor y mayor acceso al crdito para los productores as como el incremento de la rentabilidad de las actividades agropecuarias. El segundo desafo inmediato que tiene FIRA, y en el cual ya est trabajando, es el que se refiere a contribuir al desarrollo de las zonas econmicas especiales en el sur del pas, que hace unos das instruy el Presidente de la Repblica. 8 Como se sabe, la propuesta presidencial para estas zonas especiales contempla dotarlas de una infraestructura moderna, reforzar en ellas la seguridad y el estado de derecho y hacerlas receptoras de financiamiento preferencial por parte de la banca de desarrollo. En la propuesta del Presidente se contempla un trato fiscal diferenciado para los productores de Chiapas, Guerrero, Oaxaca, as como entorno a Lzaro Crdenas Michoacn, e impulsar, en esas las entidades, el establecimiento y crecimiento de empresas agroindustriales. Todo esto, junto con programas emergentes de impulso al campo con una inversin de 4 mil millones de pesos adicionales en crdito y un programa de renovacin y repoblamiento de cafetales. Para contribuir a este promisorio programa de desarrollo de zonas econmicas especiales FIRA cuenta con distintos instrumentos y programas estratgicos, para lo que cuenta con recursos provenientes del Presupuesto de Egresos de la Federacin directamente, por lo cual agradezco a los legisladores varios de ellos aqu presentes que apoyan al campo. Asimismo, FIRA cuenta para sustentar muchos proyectos productivos con la operacin de programas de la 9 SAGARPA, por lo que agradezco al Secretario Martnez y Martnez el apoyo que ha brindado a FIRA para hacer factibles sinergias exitosas. Describo brevemente las tareas de FIRA para colaborar en este ambicioso esfuerzo de desarrollo de zonas econmicas especiales: 1. Para mejorar y promover el acceso al crdito en las zonas determinadas por el Plan Presidencial, FIRA apoyar la reduccin de 200 puntos base en el costo de la tasa de inters en financiamientos que se otorguen hasta por 800 mil pesos; en la misma lnea garantizar a los intermediarios financieros hasta el 80% de los financiamientos que stos otorguen y dar un apoyo equivalente al 70% del costo del servicio de esta garanta y canalizar recursos de asistencia tcnica y capacitacin para apoyar la organizacin de productores, la creacin de figuras legales adecuadas a economas de escala y la integracin a las redes de valor. Adems pondr en marcha el programa de agricultura familiar mediante el cual se canalizar financiamiento a proyectos productivos que generen valor y permanencia de la empresa familiar, a travs de instituciones de 10 Banca Social. Para lograr esto se subsidiar la prima de riesgo y el apoyo a la reduccin de los costos de transaccin. 2. FIRA ha desarrollado programas focalizados para fortalecer a las principales cadenas de valor prevalecientes. En particular, se apoyar la renovacin de cafetales y el establecimiento de frutales a travs de un fondo de garanta especfico; esto significa otorgar financiamiento que se complementa con una garanta de primeras prdidas a los intermediarios financieros y dar apoyo a los productores con el pago de intereses durante el perodo preproductivo de la plantacin. Asimismo, en los estados del sur se desarrollarn proyectos estratgicos con mezcla de recursos del programa de desarrollo sur-sureste que contempla apoyos de hasta 50% de la inversin. Cabe destacar que al llamado del Presidente para promover la actividad econmica en Michoacn, FIRA puso en marcha una estrategia especial de la que destacamos: 1. El monto comprometido de operacin fue de 8,000 MDP, tenindose una estimacin de cerrar el ao con cuando menos 8,700 MDP en 11 flujo de crdito (8.75% adicional al programa), alcanzando el quinto estado de mayor flujo de crdito en la cartera de FIRA. El saldo de crdito esperado es de 5,500 millones de pesos, 12% real ms que al cierre de 2013. 2. Lo anterior sumado a la aportacin de los productores a los proyectos de inversin, representa cuando menos 10,700 MDP que se han inyectado al sector agroalimentario de Michoacn durante el 2014. 2. Este financiamiento se ha dado para 65,234 beneficiarios con posibilidad de incorporar unos 3,000 adicionales. 3. La superficie atendida son 133 mil ha, 290 tractores financiados, en beneficio de 1,667 empresas. Para hacer frente con eficiencia a estos desafos inmediatos FIRA cuenta con el respaldo ejemplar de su propia historia xito durante estas seis dcadas. De esta forma, guiado por las buenas prcticas financieras que le han caracterizado, apoyado en su modelo de negocios y en la calidad de su capital humano, no me cabe duda que FIRA seguir refrendando su merecido prestigio dentro de la banca de desarrollo en nuestro pas. 12 No me resta sino felicitar a todo el personal de FIRA por los primeros 60 aos de venturosa existencia de esta institucin financiera. Muchas gracias. 13

Title: Inauguration of National Financial Education Week
text: Speaker of Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the inauguration of the National Week of Financial Education. November 4, 2020 I very much appreciate the invitation to participate in the opening of this National Week of Financial Education, many thanks to Secretary Herrera, oscar Rosado, the Ministry of Public Education, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Association of Banks of Mexico, the Mexican Association of Insurance Institutions, the Mexican Association of Retirement Fund Administrators, and to all the authorities, intermediaries and experts who make this extraordinary forum possible. This year, the world has faced an unprecedented scenario: the pandemic, and the measures of confinement and social distancing have profoundly affected the daily life and economic activities of individuals. In this context, technology has been a key tool to mitigate the effects of this pandemic and avoid a major paralysis in many activities. 1 In the field of financial services, the technological revolution underway has allowed continuity to the activity in this sector and has made it possible for many people to continue to have access to these essential services, remotely, efficiently and safely. Therefore, in the face of the challenges imposed by this global health contingency, we must strengthen the use of new technologies and consolidate them as a method for the provision of a wide range of financial services and in the promotion of greater inclusion in this area. In this difficult circumstance, financial services must better and flexibly accompany the needs of their users and approach the entire population. The inclusion and expansion of the range of financial instruments and services that can be provided remotely also requires a strengthening of education in the field. Thus, education and financial inclusion are reinforced as a fundamental binomial to mitigate, in the short term, the effects of the pandemic and to, towards the future, promote a more sustained development with better opportunities for all. 2 Indeed, it is clear that simultaneous access to education and financial services allows individuals to improve their consumption opportunities, better protect their assets and fully deploy their productive projects. Greater inclusion and financial education not only transform the opportunities of individuals, they also have a proven collective benefit, since the deeper and more inclusive a financial system is, the more vigorous growth you have and you can reduce poverty quickly. For this reason, the Bank of Mexico has been promoting a financial education strategy for many years and, in addition, participates in inter-institutional efforts to promote this activity, such as this great educational day. In its 2020 edition, which will be completely virtual, this meeting adopted the theme "I take care of my money, I protect my health". It is a very pertinent issue because, in the pandemic environment, we must multiply the 3 tools available to perform a wide range of transactions, reducing personal contact. A significant example of these tools is the platform called Cobro Digital (CoDi), which came into operation in the fourth quarter of 2019. Using the infrastructure of the Interbank Electronic Payments System (SPEI) operated by the Bank of Mexico, the CoDi allows anyone who has a smartphone and a bank account to make electronic payments, 24 hours a day, free of charge and with the highest security standards. The CoDi is very flexible and includes various modalities of use both face-to-face and remote. In some establishments, just by providing the telephone number, the payment request is received immediately. In addition, the request for collection through the QR code can be sent by phone as any message so that remotely and remotely another person receives the payment request. To date, around 5 million 800 thousand people have joined the scheme and about 140 large businesses and developers 4 work so that more establishments adopt CoDi as a means of payment. Apart from its impact on efficiency and cost reduction, this scheme is an instrument of inclusion and contributes to familiarize the user with digital services in the financial system and with the possibility of accessing other more complex services. Undoubtedly, throughout the workshops, conferences, colloquiums and other activities contemplated by this meeting, the public will be shown the multiple modalities through which technology and financial education contribute to greater economic efficiency and greater well-being for all Mexicans. Congratulations and much success. 5
