Title: Signing of the collaboration agreement between the National Institute of Transparency, Access to Information and Protection of Personal Data and the Bank of Mexico
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the signing of the collaboration agreement between the National Institute of Transparency, Access to Information and Protection of Personal Data and the Bank of Mexico January 26, 2016  Dr. Ximena Puente de la Mora, Commissioner President of the National Institute of Transparency, Access to Information and Protection of Personal Data,  Ladies and gentlemen Commissioners of the National Institute of Transparency, Access to Information and Protection of Personal Data,  Ladies and gentlemen officials of the National Institute of Transparency, Access to Information and Protection of Personal Data,  Fellow members of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, 1  Officials of the Bank of Mexico,  Representatives of the media,  Ladies and gentlemen. Good morning. On behalf of myself, and of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, I thank the Presiding Commissioner and the Commissioners of INAI for the cordial invitation to formalize publicly, with this ceremony, the signing of the Collaboration Agreement between the Bank of Mexico and the Institute. This agreement endorses the great interest we have in the Central Bank to continue building, with the support and collaboration of INAI, an extensive and deep culture of transparency and accountability in Mexico. In fact, the agreement that we will sign today will serve as a channel to continue channeling the invaluable support that, in terms of 2 of training and advice, the Bank of Mexico has been receiving from the INAI during the recent months; Likewise, the agreement extends the collaboration between both autonomous institutions of the Mexican State and should be the ideal instrument to work very closely with the INAI, in everything related to transparency, as well as in the next stages that are close to being defined by the Legislative Power, which refer to the protection of personal data and the optimal management of public archives. Undoubtedly, continuing to advance in Mexico without pause in the construction of a culture of transparency and accountability will result in an increasingly solid democratic life and in a higher quality of public work in our country. It is clear that this is a topic of great breadth and with multiple angles that deserve to be addressed. On this occasion I would like to share with all of you some reflections on the decisive role that the 3 Transparency and accountability play - as essential elements - in the design and execution of a good monetary policy. As you all know, monetary policy is the daily and permanent task of a central bank. In the case of the Bank of Mexico, constitutionally autonomous since 1993, and whose objective and priority mandate is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency, I can assure you that the monetary policy that we exercise from the Governing Board would lack efficiency and effectiveness if it were not impregnated with transparency in all its stages, from the initial approaches to its execution, going through the collection of all the pertinent information for decision-making, by the exhaustive discussion, characteristic of the collegiate governing bodies, and of course by the same decision of what we call a monetary policy stance, which is expressed, in the case of the Bank of Mexico 4 as in most central banks of the world, in setting a one-off target for a benchmark interest rate. The exercise of a modern monetary policy, which achieves a tangible objective in terms of low and stable inflation, can only be achieved by creating credible and well-anchored expectations in the first instance in the financial markets, but also, and increasingly, in the whole society. It is well known that public credibility is only achieved in an environment of full transparency, in which society is widely and timely informed. That is why the history of the Bank of Mexico, especially since its quality as an autonomous entity of the State was reflected in the Constitution, has been characterized by a continuous and sustained process of progress in terms of transparency. The more and better society is informed of everything that affects monetary policy and specific goals. 5 that the Bank of Mexico pursues with the formulation of the same, the better results we will obtain and the more anchored will be the expectations of a low and stable inflation. As I have already pointed out on other occasions, and I will continue to do so because this is a key issue for the Bank of Mexico, autonomy is not so much a prerogative of the central bank as a guarantee for society, and for each individual within it, that legal tender will not be subject to advantageous manipulations by the government, to the detriment of citizens' heritage. Therefore, autonomy brings with it the natural requirement of greater transparency and ever better accountability. In the case of the Bank of Mexico, the constitutional mandate to maintain low and stable inflation makes accountability simple and expeditious for the fulfillment of this priority objective. 6 Precisely, our central bank is accountable to society on a daily basis through the results in terms of inflation and exercising its functions with the greatest transparency. In particular, I am referring to the transparency that must prevail over the information, analyses, reasons and deliberations that underpin your monetary policy decisions. I dare say that there are few public policies that, by their very nature, are as clearly exposed to public scrutiny as the monetary policies of those central banks that disseminate the minutes of their monetary policy meetings, as is the case with the Bank of Mexico since February 2011. That is why at the Bank of Mexico we celebrate and receive with enthusiasm all the advances that the country is making in terms of transparency. 7 Because in addition, in terms of transparency and accountability, progress has the characteristic of being practically irreversible. Historical experience and in the most diverse latitudes suggests that once a public entity has opened a door to greater transparency, through deliveries of timely information, that door cannot be closed again, fortunately. It would be inconceivable, for example, that once the Bank of Mexico has offered society on a weekly basis the information of its account statement - as we have done for eleven years - we would even think about stopping doing so just because in a certain circumstance the data of that information seemed unfavorable or could cause concern. On the contrary, in terms of transparency, once a door is opened, it remains only to continue opening more and more doors. 8 Opening more doors means enriching information, making it more and more accurate and increasingly timely, taking advantage of the immense advantages of advances in information technologies so that it, the information, reaches more and more quickly, with more precision and to more and more members of society. Along the same lines, the Bank of Mexico informs Congress and the Executive of its budget plan; likewise, at the beginning of each year we send the Legislative Branch our Monetary Program and every day we inform society of numerous economic indicators, from the exchange rate to interest rates in their various terms and modalities, as well as the conditions of the financial system and banking, credit instruments, savings and investment. All this information is available to the public on our website, in addition to disseminating it through social networks. 9 The conclusion of this Agreement reaffirms the commitment and vocation of the Bank of Mexico in terms of transparency. The most valuable asset of a Central Bank is its credibility and we are certain that credibility is only consolidated and sustained over time in an environment of full transparency and we are pleased to have the invaluable support of INAI in the construction of that environment. Thanks a lot. 10
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la firma del convenio de colaboracin entre el Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Informacin y Proteccin de Datos Personales y el Banco de Mxico 26 de enero de 2016  Doctora Ximena Puente de la Mora, Comisionada Presidente del Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Informacin y Proteccin de Datos Personales,  Seoras y seores Comisionados del Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Informacin y Proteccin de Datos Personales,  Seoras y seores funcionarios del Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Informacin y Proteccin de Datos Personales,  Compaeros integrantes de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico, 1  Funcionarios del Banco de Mxico,  Representantes de los medios de comunicacin,  Seoras y seores. Muy buenos das. A nombre propio, y de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico, agradezco a la Comisionada Presidenta y a los Comisionados del INAI la cordial invitacin a formalizar de manera pblica, con esta ceremonia, la firma del Convenio de Colaboracin entre el Banco de Mxico y el Instituto. Este convenio refrenda el gran inters que tenemos en el Banco Central por seguir construyendo, con el apoyo y la colaboracin del INAI, una extensa y profunda cultura de transparencia y rendicin de cuentas en Mxico. De hecho, el convenio que hoy firmaremos servir como cauce para continuar canalizando el invaluable apoyo que, en materia 2 de capacitacin y asesora, ha estado recibiendo el Banco de Mxico de parte del INAI durante los meses recientes; asimismo, el convenio extiende la colaboracin entre ambas instituciones autnomas del Estado mexicano y deber ser el instrumento idneo para trabajar muy de cerca con el INAI, en todo lo relativo a la transparencia, as como en las prximas etapas que estn prximas a definirse por el Poder Legislativo, que se refieren a la proteccin de datos personales y al ptimo manejo de los archivos pblicos. Sin duda, seguir avanzando en Mxico sin pausa en la construccin de una cultura de transparencia y rendicin de cuentas se traducir en una vida democrtica cada da ms slida y en una mayor calidad del quehacer pblico en nuestro pas. Es claro que se trata de un tema de gran amplitud y con mltiples ngulos que merecen abordarse. En esta ocasin me gustara compartir con todos ustedes algunas reflexiones acerca del papel decisivo que la 3 transparencia y la rendicin de cuentas juegan como elementos esenciales- en el diseo y en la ejecucin de una buena poltica monetaria. Como todos ustedes saben, la poltica monetaria es el quehacer cotidiano y permanente de un banco central. En el caso del Banco de Mxico, constitucionalmente autnomo desde 1993, y cuyo objetivo y mandato prioritario es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda, puedo asegurarles que la poltica monetaria que ejercemos desde la Junta de Gobierno carecera de eficacia y efectividad si no estuviese impregnada de transparencia en todas sus etapas, desde los planteamientos iniciales hasta su ejecucin, pasando por el acopio de toda la informacin pertinente para la toma decisiones, por la discusin exhaustiva, caracterstica de los rganos colegiados de gobierno, y desde luego por la misma decisin de lo que llamamos una postura de poltica monetaria, que se expresa, en el caso del Banco de Mxico 4 como en la mayora de los bancos centrales del mundo, en el establecimiento de un objetivo puntual para una tasa de inters de referencia. El ejercicio de una poltica monetaria moderna, que alcance un objetivo tangible en trminos de inflacin baja y estable, slo puede lograrse creando expectativas crebles y bien ancladas en una primera instancia en los mercados financieros, pero tambin, y cada vez ms, en toda la sociedad. Es sabido que la credibilidad pblica slo se logra en un entorno de total transparencia, en el cual la sociedad est amplia y oportunamente informada. Es por ello que la historia del Banco de Mxico, en especial a partir de que se plasm su calidad de ente autnomo del Estado en la Constitucin, se ha caracterizado por un proceso continuo y sostenido de avances en materia de transparencia. Mientras ms y mejor informada est la sociedad de todo lo que incide en la poltica monetaria y de las metas especficas 5 que persigue el Banco de Mxico con la formulacin de la misma, mejores resultados obtendremos y ms ancladas estarn las expectativas de una inflacin baja y estable. Como ya he sealado en otras ocasiones, y lo seguir haciendo porque se trata de un tema clave para el Banco de Mxico, la autonoma no es tanto una prerrogativa del banco central sino una garanta para la sociedad, y para cada individuo dentro de ella, de que la moneda de curso legal no ser objeto de manipulaciones ventajosas por parte del gobierno, en detrimento del patrimonio de los ciudadanos. Por eso, la autonoma trae consigo el requerimiento natural de una mayor transparencia y de una cada vez mejor rendicin de cuentas. En el caso del Banco de Mxico el mandato constitucional de mantener una inflacin baja y estable hace sencilla y expedita la rendicin de cuentas en cuanto al cumplimiento de dicho objetivo prioritario. 6 Precisamente, nuestro banco central rinde cuentas ante la sociedad cotidianamente a travs de los resultados en materia de inflacin y ejerciendo con la mayor transparencia sus funciones. Muy en especial, me refiero a la transparencia que debe prevalecer acerca de la informacin, los anlisis, las razones y las deliberaciones que fundamentan sus decisiones de poltica monetaria. Me atrevo a decir que hay pocas polticas pblicas que, por su propia naturaleza, estn tan claramente expuestas al examen pblico, como las polticas monetarias de aquellos bancos centrales que difunden las minutas de sus reuniones de poltica monetaria, como es el caso del Banco de Mxico desde febrero de 2011. Es por ello que en el Banco de Mxico celebramos y recibimos con entusiasmo todos los avances que el pas est haciendo en materia de transparencia. 7 Porque adems, en lo que se refiere a transparencia y rendicin de cuentas, los avances tienen la caracterstica de ser prcticamente irreversibles. La experiencia histrica y en las ms diversas latitudes apunta a que una vez que un ente pblico ha abierto una puerta a una mayor transparencia, mediante entregas de informacin puntual, esa puerta no puede volver a cerrarse, afortunadamente. Sera inconcebible, por ejemplo, que una vez que el Banco de Mxico ha ofrecido a la sociedad de manera semanal la informacin de su estado de cuenta  como lo hacemos desde hace once aos- penssemos siquiera en dejar de hacerlo slo porque en determinada circunstancia los datos de esa informacin pareciesen desfavorables o pudiesen causar inquietud. Por el contrario, en materia de transparencia una vez que se abre una puerta, slo queda seguir abriendo ms y ms puertas. 8 Abrir ms puertas significa enriquecer la informacin, hacerla cada vez ms precisa y cada vez ms oportuna, aprovechar las inmensas ventajas de los avances en las tecnologas de la informacin para que sta, la informacin, llegue cada vez ms rpido, con ms precisin y a cada vez ms miembros de la sociedad. En esta misma lnea, el Banco de Mxico informa al Congreso y al Ejecutivo de su plan de presupuesto; asimismo, al principio de cada ao enviamos al Poder Legislativo nuestro Programa Monetario y todos los das informamos a la sociedad de numerosos indicadores econmicos, desde el tipo de cambio hasta las tasas de inters en sus diversos plazos y modalidades, as como de las condiciones del sistema financiero y de la banca, de los instrumentos de crdito, ahorro e inversin. Toda esta informacin est disponible para todo el pblico en nuestra pgina de Internet, adems de difundirla por redes sociales. 9 Con la celebracin de este Convenio se reafirma el compromiso y la vocacin del Banco de Mxico en materia de transparencia. El activo ms valioso de un Banco Central es su credibilidad y estamos ciertos de que la credibilidad slo se consolida y se sostiene a lo largo del tiempo en un entorno de plena transparencia y nos congratulamos de contar con el invaluable apoyo del INAI en la construccin de ese entorno. Muchas gracias. 10

Title: Presentation of the Cont@cto Banxico Award 2014
text: REMARKS BY MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, ON THE OCCASION OF THE PRESENTATION OF THE CONT@CTO BANXICO AWARD 2014. Mexico City, November 19, 2014. Good night. It is an honor for me to address a few words to you on the occasion of the delivery of the "banxico Cont@cto Award", which this year celebrates its sixth edition, now around the theme "The challenges of the issuance of banknotes and coins". On behalf of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, I thank all of you for your presence and I give you the warmest welcome. By constitutional mandate, the Bank of Mexico has as a priority objective to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency. In addition, its Law establishes the purpose of providing the country's economy with national currency, promoting the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of the payment system. In order to promote a better social understanding of its mandate and purposes, the Bank of Mexico has sought to consolidate a direct relationship with the population through financial education activities. This is a task of enormous relevance, as it helps citizens to better understand the importance of planning in consumption, savings and investment decisions; it allows a better understanding of the benefits and risks of available financial products and, in general, improves the efficiency of families' economic decisions. In addition, a better population 1 Informed has a greater capacity to understand the actions and objectives of economic policy, which facilitates the scope of the latter. Thus, our Central Institute has joined a national strategy of financial education, which includes the effort of various public entities and financial and educational institutions, which seek to act in a coordinated manner in the development of programs, materials and projects, which help prepare the population for a better understanding and use of financial products and services. It should be noted that the financial education strategy of the Bank of Mexico is aimed at very diverse audiences and age ranges. In this context, the Bank of Mexico has launched various actions to make society more clear what the Bank is, what its priority objective and purposes are, and why compliance with these powers is important for the economy and the well-being of families. As part of these efforts, the "Banxico Cont@cto Award" stands out. This event, which began in 2009, seeks to be a vehicle to bring the Central Bank closer to young people in upper secondary education, and to promote in students, teachers and educational institutions, a greater interest and knowledge regarding the work of the Institution and how it affects the economic development of the country. The "Cont@cto Banxico Award" has provoked a wide student participation in practically all the federative entities of the Republic. 2 Throughout its six editions, essays have been received from more than 3000 work teams. As I pointed out earlier, for this year "The challenges of the issuance of banknotes and coins" was chosen as the theme of analysis. Banknotes and coins have been the most common means of payment throughout the evolution of modern economies, so their functionality, credibility and stability is crucial for nations. In Mexico, the history of issuing coins and banknotes is ancient. However, these means of payment have not always enjoyed the great acceptance and trust they enjoy today. The issuance of metallic currency began during the Colony. Given the abundance of fine metals in the country, it was possible to forge a rich numismatic tradition and coins made in Mexico came to have an important international circulation. Still in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, an important part of the circulation in Mexico were coins made of precious metals, with a high intrinsic and nominal value. For its part, the banknote began to be used since the early nineteenth century, although its acceptance was complex. Given the chronic economic and political instability, banknotes issued during the early part of the nineteenth century never managed to gain the credibility of the population. During the Porfiriato, the banknote began to take hold as a means of payment. However, the outbreak of the Mexican Revolution led to a profusion of banknote issuances by the various factions, which again eroded certainty in this means of payment. 3 To restore trust, the Constitution of 1917 reserved for the State exclusively the minting of currency and the issuance of banknotes. Thus, in addition to putting into circulation the banknotes and coins, in the Bank of Mexico all the banknotes that we Mexicans use are manufactured, while the coins are minted by the Mint of Mexico, based on instructions from our Central Institute. The issuance of banknotes and coins has also increased the numismatic prestige of the country. In fact, a significant number of these pieces have been recognized and awarded internationally. This is due to its high technical and aesthetic quality, which incorporates elements deeply representative of our culture and identity. In view of the importance of banknotes and coins as a means of exchange for society, it is essential to consolidate public confidence in them. This trust is safeguarded by two fundamental aspects: the preservation of its purchasing power and the certainty of its authenticity. The preservation of the purchasing power of the currency implies avoiding the occurrence of continuous and generalized price increases, which cause individuals to acquire fewer and fewer goods and services with the same amount of money. In other words, fight inflation. The achievements in this area, fundamentally supported by the constitutional reform that granted autonomy to the Bank of Mexico since 1994, are evident. Suffice it to point out the contrast between the situation. 4 that prevails today in our country, characterized by low and stable inflation, and the years in which inflation rates of two and up to three digits were recorded. Progress in the fight against inflation has resulted in an environment of greater stability and certainty; lower financing costs for families, businesses and government; and, in general, on firmer foundations for economic growth, with benefits of particular relevance for the most unprotected sectors of the population. It is also very important that the authorities guarantee the authenticity of banknotes and coins, thoroughly combating the phenomenon of counterfeiting. In this regard, the Bank of Mexico has sought to determine the security elements of its banknotes with the highest quality standards and the most advanced technology. In addition, it has undertaken mass dissemination strategies, so that these security elements are properly identified by the general public. This contributes to strengthening the security of monetary circulation and promoting financial and economic culture in our country. In addition to the above, the proper fulfillment of the issuing function of a central bank implies planning and logistical challenges of great complexity. By this I mean, first of all, the accurate and timely estimation of the demand for banknotes and coins by the public. Thus, it is important to determine in advance not only the total amount that the public will demand from banknotes and coins, but also the time, place and denominations in which it will do so. Secondly, and once these estimates are available, the logistical challenge is to physically deliver them. 5 banknotes and coins to those who require them, a task that, it is worth mentioning, is not trivial. Similarly, it is important to preserve the quality of the banknotes in use. Of the amount of banknotes that are put into circulation annually in Mexico, about 80 percent goes to the replacement of deteriorated banknotes. Likewise, the Central Institute campaigns for the population to contribute to keeping their banknotes in good condition, for example, by not scratching or folding them. With regard to coins, a significant amount of resources are allocated to mint and distribute them, but it is common that low-denomination coins do not circulate optimally, as they end up being stored in homes. This is another challenge for the Central Bank. Paper money remains the most accepted and ingrained means of payment among the population. However, the accelerated development of other means of payment raises doubts about the possibility that the demand for working capital will decrease in the coming years. Electronic media, the product of the development of information technology, have established unprecedented ways of processing information and circulating wealth. The intangible is a fundamental part of that environment where the physical element ceases to be essential. Thus, money has been able to take the identity of electronic data that circulates through computer networks. Notwithstanding the above, it should be noted that the amount of cash has continued to show sustained growth. On the other hand, banknotes and coins continue to play a predominant role. 6 as a means of payment among a good part of the population, either by custom, cultural factors or practical advantages. In addition, we must not forget the still limited scope and infrastructure of information and communication technologies, as well as the still low levels of financial penetration, which are essential for the operation of electronic means of payment. The challenges in this regard are particularly important in emerging and developing countries. These and other challenges of the issuance of banknotes and coins, are what served as the basis for the development of the essays prepared for this edition of the contest. The result of the call for this Award has been very satisfactory both in the quantitative aspect of the participation, and in relation to the quality of the analyses carried out. For the 2014 edition, 978 teams participated initially, from both public and private schools in 31 states of the Mexican Republic. This is proof of the active interest in the work of our Central Institute. Today, we are honored with their presence by those teams that after a careful and difficult evaluation process, were considered by the jury as the five best. I would like to congratulate very warmly the members of these five teams, both for the effort made and for the level of their work. Having reached this final stage is undoubtedly a great achievement for you. 7 I also thank all the teams registered in the contest for their important contributions, the members of the Jury for the careful reading and evaluation of the works presented, and the Banco de Mexico team that made possible the organization of this contest. I hope that the banxico C@ntacto Award will continue to be an incentive for the creativity, talent and commitment of our students for many years to come. Thanks a lot. 8
text_original: PALABRAS DEL LIC. JAVIER GUZMN CALAFELL, SUBGOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE MXICO, CON MOTIVO DE LA ENTREGA DEL PREMIO CONT@CTO BANXICO 2014. Mxico, D.F., 19 de noviembre de 2014. Buenas noches. Es un honor para m dirigirles unas palabras con motivo de la entrega del Premio Cont@cto Banxico, que este ao celebra su sexta edicin, ahora en torno al tema Los desafos de la emisin de billetes y monedas. A nombre de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico, agradezco a todos ustedes su presencia y les doy la ms cordial bienvenida. Por mandato constitucional, el Banco de Mxico tiene como objetivo prioritario procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda. Adems, su Ley establece como finalidades proveer a la economa del pas de moneda nacional, promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. Con el fin de fomentar una mejor comprensin social de su mandato y finalidades, el Banco de Mxico ha buscado consolidar una relacin directa con la poblacin mediante actividades de educacin financiera. Esta es una tarea de enorme relevancia, pues ayuda a la ciudadana a entender mejor la importancia de la planeacin en las decisiones de consumo, ahorro e inversin; permite comprender mejor los beneficios y riesgos de los productos financieros disponibles y, en general, mejora la eficiencia de las decisiones econmicas de las familias. Adems, una poblacin mejor 1 informada tiene una mayor capacidad para entender las acciones y objetivos de la poltica econmica, lo que facilita el alcance de estos ltimos. As, nuestro Instituto Central se ha sumado a una estrategia nacional de educacin financiera, que comprende el esfuerzo de diversas entidades pblicas e instituciones financieras y educativas, que buscan actuar de forma coordinada en el desarrollo de programas, materiales y proyectos, que ayuden a preparar a la poblacin para una mejor comprensin y uso de productos y servicios financieros. Cabe sealar que la estrategia de educacin financiera del Banco de Mxico va dirigida a muy diversas audiencias y rangos de edades. En este contexto, el Banco de Mxico ha puesto en marcha diversas acciones para que la sociedad comprenda con mayor claridad qu es el Banco, cul es su objetivo prioritario y sus finalidades, y por qu el cumplimiento de dichas facultades es importante para la economa y el bienestar de las familias. Como parte de estos esfuerzos, destaca precisamente el Premio Cont@cto Banxico. Este certamen, que inici en 2009, busca ser un vehculo para acercar al Banco Central a los jvenes de educacin media superior, y promover en los estudiantes, profesores e instituciones educativas, un mayor inters y conocimiento respecto de la labor de la Institucin y como sta incide en el desarrollo econmico del pas. El Premio Cont@cto Banxico ha suscitado una amplia participacin estudiantil en prcticamente todas las entidades federativas de la Repblica. 2 A lo largo de sus seis ediciones, se han recibido ensayos de ms de 3000 equipos de trabajo. Como seal con anterioridad, para este ao se eligi como tema de anlisis Los desafos de la emisin de billetes y monedas. Los billetes y monedas han sido los medios de pago ms habituales a lo largo de la evolucin de las economas modernas, por lo que su funcionalidad, credibilidad y estabilidad resulta crucial para las naciones. En Mxico, la historia de la emisin de monedas y billetes es antigua. Sin embargo, estos medios de pago no siempre han gozado de la gran aceptacin y confianza de la que disfrutan hoy en da. La emisin de moneda metlica comenz durante la Colonia. Dada la abundancia de metales finos en el pas, se logr forjar una rica tradicin numismtica y las monedas fabricadas en Mxico llegaron a tener una importante circulacin internacional. Todava en el siglo XIX y a principios del XX, una parte importante del circulante en Mxico eran monedas hechas en metales preciosos, con un alto valor intrnseco y nominal. Por su parte, el billete comenz a utilizarse desde principios del siglo XIX, aunque su aceptacin fue compleja. Dada la crnica inestabilidad econmica y poltica, los billetes emitidos durante la primera parte del siglo XIX nunca lograron obtener la credibilidad de la poblacin. Durante el Porfiriato, el billete comenz a afianzarse como medio de pago. Sin embargo, el estallido de la Revolucin mexicana condujo a una profusin de emisiones de billetes por las diversas facciones, lo que nuevamente erosion la certidumbre en este medio de pago. 3 Para reestablecer la confianza, la Constitucin de 1917 reserv al Estado de manera exclusiva la acuacin de moneda y la emisin de billetes. As, adems de poner en circulacin los billetes y monedas, en el Banco de Mxico se fabrican todos los billetes que usamos los mexicanos, mientras que las monedas son acuadas por la Casa de Moneda de Mxico, sobre la base de instrucciones de nuestro Instituto Central. La emisin de billetes y monedas tambin ha acrecentado el prestigio numismtico del pas. De hecho, un nmero importante de estas piezas han sido reconocidas y galardonadas a nivel internacional. Ello debido a su alta calidad tcnica y esttica, que incorpora elementos profundamente representativos de nuestra cultura e identidad. En vista de la importancia de los billetes y monedas como medio de cambio de la sociedad, es indispensable consolidar la confianza del pblico en ellos. Esta confianza se resguarda mediante dos aspectos fundamentales: la preservacin de su poder adquisitivo y la certeza de su autenticidad. La preservacin del poder adquisitivo de la moneda implica evitar la ocurrencia de aumentos continuos y generalizados de precios, que provoquen que los individuos puedan adquirir cada vez menos bienes y servicios con la misma cantidad de dinero. En otras palabras, combatir la inflacin. Los logros en este mbito, apoyados de manera fundamental por la reforma constitucional que otorg autonoma al Banco de Mxico a partir de 1994, son evidentes. Baste sealar al respecto el contraste entre la situacin 4 que prevalece en la actualidad en nuestro pas, caracterizada por una inflacin baja y estable, y los aos en los que se registraban tasas de inflacin de dos y hasta tres dgitos. Los avances en la lucha contra la inflacin se han traducido en un entorno de mayor estabilidad y certidumbre; en menores costos de financiamiento para familias, empresas y gobierno; y, en general, en bases ms firmes para el crecimiento econmico, con beneficios de particular relevancia para los sectores ms desprotegidos de la poblacin. Es muy importante tambin que las autoridades garanticen la autenticidad de los billetes y monedas, combatiendo a fondo el fenmeno de la falsificacin. Al respecto, el Banco de Mxico ha buscado determinar los elementos de seguridad de sus billetes con los ms altos estndares de calidad y la ms avanzada tecnologa. Adems, ha emprendido estrategias de difusin masiva, a fin de que estos elementos de seguridad sean debidamente identificados por el pblico en general. Con ello, se contribuye a fortalecer la seguridad de la circulacin monetaria y a fomentar la cultura financiera y econmica en nuestro pas. En adicin a lo anterior, el adecuado cumplimiento de la funcin emisora de un banco central implica retos de planificacin y logsticos de una gran complejidad. Con esto me refiero, en primer lugar, a la estimacin precisa y oportuna de la demanda de billetes y monedas por parte del pblico. As, es importante determinar con anticipacin no solo el monto total que el pblico demandar de billetes y monedas, sino tambin el momento, el lugar y las denominaciones en que lo har. En segundo lugar, y una vez que se cuenta con estas estimaciones, el reto logstico consiste en hacer llegar fsicamente 5 los billetes y monedas a quienes los requieren, tarea que, cabe mencionar, no es trivial. De igual forma, es importante preservar la calidad de los billetes en uso. Del monto de billetes que anualmente se pone en circulacin en Mxico, alrededor del 80 por ciento se destina al reemplazo de billetes deteriorados. Asimismo, el Instituto Central hace campaas para que la poblacin contribuya a conservar sus billetes en buen estado, por ejemplo, no rayndolos o doblndolos. Respecto de las monedas, se destina un monto importante de recursos para acuarlas y distribuirlas, pero es frecuente que las monedas de baja denominacin no circulen de forma ptima, pues terminan siendo almacenadas en los hogares. He ah otro reto para el Banco Central. El papel moneda sigue siendo el medio de pago ms aceptado y arraigado entre la poblacin. Sin embargo, el acelerado desarrollo de otros medios de pago hace surgir dudas sobre la posibilidad de que la demanda de circulante disminuya en los prximos aos. Los medios electrnicos, producto del desarrollo de la tecnologa de la informacin, han instaurado formas inditas de procesar informacin y hacer circular la riqueza. Lo intangible es parte fundamental de ese entorno en donde el elemento fsico deja de ser imprescindible. As, el dinero ha podido tomar la identidad de datos electrnicos que circulan por conducto de redes computarizadas. No obstante lo anterior, cabe destacar que la cantidad de dinero en efectivo ha continuado mostrando un crecimiento sostenido. Por otra parte, los billetes y monedas siguen teniendo un papel predominante 6 como medio de pago entre una buena parte de la poblacin, ya sea por costumbre, factores culturales o ventajas prcticas. Adems, no debemos olvidar los todava limitados alcance e infraestructura de las tecnologas de informacin y comunicacin, as como los an bajos niveles de penetracin financiera, indispensables para el funcionamiento de los medios electrnicos de pago. Los retos a este respecto son especialmente importantes en los pases emergentes y en desarrollo. Estos y otros desafos de la emisin de billetes y monedas, son los que sirvieron de base para el desarrollo de los ensayos elaborados para esta edicin del certamen. El resultado de la convocatoria a este Premio ha sido muy satisfactorio tanto en el aspecto cuantitativo de la participacin, como en lo referente a la calidad de los anlisis realizados. Para la edicin 2014 se cont con la participacin inicial de 978 equipos, provenientes tanto de escuelas pblicas como privadas de 31 entidades federativas de la Repblica Mexicana. Esto es una prueba del inters activo en el trabajo de nuestro Instituto Central. El da de hoy, nos honran con su presencia aquellos equipos que despus de un cuidadoso y difcil proceso de evaluacin, fueron considerados por el jurado como los cinco mejores. Deseo felicitar de manera muy calurosa a los integrantes de estos cinco equipos, tanto por el esfuerzo realizado como por el nivel de sus trabajos. El haber llegado a esta etapa final representa sin duda un gran logro para ustedes. 7 Agradezco tambin a todos los equipos inscritos en el concurso por sus importantes contribuciones, a los miembros del Jurado por la cuidadosa lectura y evaluacin de los trabajos presentados, y al equipo del Banco de Mxico que hizo posible la organizacin de este certamen. Hago votos para que el Premio C@ntacto Banxico contine siendo por muchos aos un incentivo para la creatividad, el talento y el compromiso de nuestros estudiantes. Muchas gracias. 8

Title: Signing of the contract to establish the Trust of the Mexican Petroleum Fund for Stabilization and Development
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the signing of the contract to constitute the Trust of the Mexican Petroleum Fund for Stabilization and Development September 30, 2014  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso  Mr. Secretary of Energy, Mr. Pedro Joaquin Coldwell  Mr. Secretary of Economy, Mr. Ildefonso Guajardo Villareal  Mr. General Director of Nacional Financiera, Dr. Jacques Rogozinski  Mr. General Director of Banobras, Mr. Alfredo del Mazo Maza  Ladies and gentlemen, Good morning. 1 For the Bank of Mexico it is a great honor, as a stimulating challenge, to be the trustee of the Mexican Petroleum Fund for Stabilization and Development, in fulfillment of a constitutional mandate. Since the first discussions in the Congress of the Union regarding constitutional reforms in energy matters, the Bank of Mexico has followed with great interest the corresponding legislative work. We pay special attention to how the task that would correspond to the Central Institute was outlined, throughout the legislative process, and that today is reflected in the contract that the Bank itself has just signed with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit. Of course, with the signing of this contract, the Bank of Mexico will focus on fully complying with the actions that it is responsible for taking so that this Fund operates with full transparency and in accordance with the objectives that it is 2 have assigned. It is clear that it must be a Fund that allows society to know in a timely, precise and clear manner everything related to the reception, administration and destination of the resources derived from the production of oil and other hydrocarbons. The experience that the Bank of Mexico has acquired over decades in the management of central bank operations, as a financial agent of the Federal Government and in the administration of international reserves, makes it possible to ensure that the Central Institute has the technical knowledge and operational capacity to fulfill the mandate that the Constitution has conferred on it, that is: to receive, administer and distribute the state's oil revenues for the benefit of all Mexicans, promptly following the decisions of the Fund's Technical Committee. The Mexican Petroleum Fund for Stabilization and Development is one of the pillars of the energy reform that 3 approved the Permanent Constituent Assembly and stands out because it will play a strategic role in maintaining the stability of the national economy. As the destination to be given to oil revenues derived from the energy reform has been reflected in the constitutional order, the reference framework from which public finances are managed in an intertemporal environment has been strengthened and modernized. The same Constitution directs the Fund to invest in long-term savings instruments with the aim that Mexico takes advantage of the additional returns produced by having a broader horizon in the allocation of resources, while seeking greater intergenerational justice - similar to those that in other nations have already proven their effectiveness and their social benefits over time. This facet of the Fund will ensure that the income obtained from the extraction of hydrocarbons, owned by the Nation, 4 they will produce benefits both for present generations and benefits for future generations. For all these reasons, the Bank of Mexico is honored with the very high responsibility of being the trustee of the Fund and is committed to society to fulfill this task with care, efficiency and transparency. Thanks a lot. 5

Title: Special session of the international conference to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico ("Independence of the Central Banks. Progress and challenges")
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the Special Session of the International Conference to commemorate the 20th Anniversary of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico ("Independence of Central Banks. Progress and challenges") October 14, 2013 ? Mr. President of the Republic, Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto ? Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso ? Distinguished Central Bank Governors, Legislators and Exhibitors, ? Representatives of the Media, ? Ladies and gentlemen, Today Mexico is immersed in a deep and ambitious effort of institutional transformation. The same is true of reforms already enacted, such as education, as well as major reforms that are the subject of intense debates, such as the one that refers to the promising energy sector, the will to 1 change is obvious. We all know that the Administration headed by President Enrique Pena Nieto has been characterized both by its modernizing spirit and by its eager search for consensus. No one could doubt that this long-awaited "sense of urgency", indispensable for the achievement of profound and profitable transformations, is present today. As I have mentioned on other occasions, the macroeconomic stability achieved by Mexico, underpinned by many years of responsible fiscal, financial and monetary policies, is the ideal platform to promote structural reforms that raise Mexico's potential growth to much higher rates than the current ones and in a sustained manner. Only in this way will the country be able to overcome multiple lags. This environment of institutional transformation that we are experiencing is particularly fortunate to commemorate. 2 the twentieth anniversary of one of the most solid and profitable structural reforms that has been carried out in the modern history of Mexico: the granting of autonomy at the constitutional level to the Bank of Mexico. History, not only of Mexico, but of multiple nations, shows us that the lasting reforms that transform a country are those that translate into tangible and forceful results over time. I have no doubt that the reform that 20 years ago granted autonomy to the Bank of Mexico can now show, with conclusive results, that it was a profoundly successful and profitable institutional change for all Mexicans. In 1993, when the Congress of the Union received the presidential initiative to modify three constitutional articles in order to grant autonomy to the Bank of Mexico, practically all Mexicans had very fresh in the 3 I remember the devastating damage that had caused them acute and prolonged episodes of high inflation: widespread poverty, cancellation of investment projects, employment, daily hardships to meet basic needs, assets lost in a few months after many years of constant effort to build them. For the younger population of Mexico it can be difficult to understand the damage caused by an environment of high inflation, especially if we take into account that next April will be 14 uninterrupted years of registering, month by month, annual inflations of a single digit. To establish the contrast with the situation prior to the autonomy of our Issuing Institute, it is enough to remember that in 1993 almost half of Mexicans at that time, 45 million compatriots, had only known in their lives inflations of two or more digits. 4 Today, more than 32 million Mexicans (those 14 years of age or younger) have never suffered annual inflations of more than one digit. Today, thousands of Mexicans have access to mortgage loans to acquire a home at fixed rates, in pesos, with terms that can be up to 30 years. That was simply unthinkable in 1993, when the Bank of Mexico gained its autonomy. Thanks also to lower inflation, the Mexican government can today place its Federation Treasury Certificates (Cetes) at the lowest interest rates in history: just 3.40 percent within 28 days, as happened in last week's auction of government securities. Also, thanks to well-anchored inflation expectations, the Mexican government has progressively decreased the cost of its internal and external public debt, and has increased its maturities: 5 In 1994, the weighted average term of government debt in pesos in Mexico was 0.63 years (230 days), while that of government debt in the United States was 5.08 years (about 1,854 days). Today, in Mexico, the weighted average term of government debt in pesos is 7.9 years (2,829 days) while that of U.S. government debt is 5.4 years (1,935 days). This means not only that in these 20 years the maturity of government debt in pesos has been extended by more than twelve times, but that, in terms of maturity, our government debt exceeds by more than two years that corresponding to the United States. Of course, this genuine transformation of the economic scenario in which Mexico's life takes place would have been unthinkable without an autonomous Central Bank. 6 In fact, independence is not so much a prerogative of the Central Bank as a guarantee for society as a whole and for each individual within it: the guarantee that the purchasing power of legal tender will not be subject to advantageous manipulations by governments to the detriment of citizens' assets. Undoubtedly, autonomy brings with it the natural requirement of better accountability. In the case of the Bank of Mexico, the priority constitutional mandate to maintain low and stable inflation makes this accountability simple and expeditious. Precisely the Bank of Mexico is accountable to society through the periodic results in terms of inflation and exercising its functions with the greatest transparency. I am referring to the full transparency that must prevail over the information, analyses, reasons and deliberations that underpin monetary policy decisions. Few public policies are so 7 clearly exposed to public scrutiny, such as the monetary policies of those central banks that disseminate the minutes of their monetary policy meetings, as is the case of the Bank of Mexico. This goes beyond even the usual and adequate accountability to which autonomous institutions must be subject in a democratic society, because not only is the very content of the decision visible to all, but its gestation process within a collegiate governing body. This is so, because it has been shown that this full transparency in communication is decisive for anchoring the inflation expectations of economic agents. The essence of autonomy is to prevent the Central Bank from providing direct financing to the government. In other words, autonomy closes the possibility for fiscal deficits to be financed with credit from the Central Bank. This 8 Prohibition becomes easy to enforce when there is a harmonious relationship between fiscal and monetary policies, which are the two main pillars of macroeconomic stability. In this sense, the work of the Bank of Mexico to maintain the purchasing power of the national currency has been facilitated by the healthy management of public finances that Mexico has already shown for many years. The recent initiative proposed by President Pena Nieto to strengthen the Federal Law on Budget and Financial Responsibility constitutes an important additional step to ensure fiscal stability and the sustainability of public debt in the medium and long term. Therefore, this initiative will also be, if approved, a fundamental element to guarantee low and stable inflation rates in the years to come in our country, and thus recreate 9 fertile ground for further sustainable economic growth. In another order of ideas, it is pertinent to mention that the Constitution also grants budgetary autonomy to the Bank of Mexico, which has allowed it to forge and increase the main asset it has: I refer to its highly qualified personnel and fully committed to the responsibilities that the Constitution assigns to the Central Institute. *** Mr. President, Mr. Secretary, Governors of Central Banks, friends: The global crisis unleashed in 2008 has pushed several central banks, many of them represented here by their governors, to the limit of their capacities. The aforementioned institutions have shown a great mastery to innovate in the 10 execution of their monetary policy, in such a way that they have facilitated the stability of financial systems and have led to the recovery of their economies. But they have always done so without neglecting the objective of keeping inflation low and stable. The actions implemented in monetary matters by the central banks of several advanced economies have opened a window for their respective governments to implement another series of reforms, in fiscal, financial and regulatory matters, to stabilize their economies definitively and to resume the path of economic growth. It would not be presumptuous to say that the central banks of the advanced countries, by opening that window of time, have been the main catalyst to overcome the crisis that still afflicts us. 11 But it is urgent that the countries most affected by the crisis make effective use of that window of time offered by central banks, since monetary policy alone cannot solve the problems suffered by economies that represent more than 40 percent of world GDP, if we consider the United States. Japan, the United Kingdom and the European Monetary Union. In this sense, this meeting is very fortunate because we will be able to discuss the value of the autonomy of central banks in times of crisis and how this autonomy can be exercised responsibly in difficult times. Last but not least, I would like to acknowledge and thank president Pena Nieto and his government for their deep respect for the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. In addition, the Bank of 12 Mexico, in its sphere of competence and action, will always be willing to collaborate so that this transformative impulse led by you, Mr. President, comes to fruition and produces its best fruits for the benefit of all Mexicans. Thanks a lot. 13

Avances y retos) 14 de octubre de 2013  Seor Presidente de la Repblica, licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Luis Videgaray Caso  Distinguidos Gobernadores de Bancos Centrales, Legisladores y Expositores,  Representantes de los Medios de Comunicacin,  Seoras y seores, Hoy Mxico est inmerso en un profundo y ambicioso esfuerzo de transformacin institucional. Lo mismo se trate de reformas ya promulgadas, como la educativa, que de grandes reformas que son motivo de intensos debates, como la que se refiere al promisorio sector de la energa, la voluntad de 1 cambio salta a la vista. Todos sabemos que la Administracin que encabeza el Presidente Enrique Pea Nieto se ha caracterizado tanto por su talante modernizador como por su bsqueda afanosa de consensos. Nadie podra poner en duda que ese anhelado sentido de urgencia, indispensable para la consecucin de transformaciones profundas y provechosas, hoy est presente. Como he mencionado en otras ocasiones, la estabilidad macroeconmica alcanzada por Mxico, sustentada en muchos aos de polticas fiscales, financieras y monetarias responsables, es la plataforma ideal para impulsar reformas estructurales que eleven el crecimiento potencial de Mxico a tasas mucho ms altas que las actuales y de forma sostenida. Slo as el pas lograr superar mltiples rezagos. Este entorno de transformacin institucional que estamos viviendo resulta particularmente afortunado para conmemorar 2 el vigsimo aniversario de una de las reformas estructurales ms slidas y provechosas que se ha realizado en la historia moderna de Mxico: el otorgamiento de autonoma a nivel constitucional al Banco de Mxico. La historia, no slo de Mxico, sino de mltiples naciones, nos demuestra que las reformas duraderas que transforman a un pas son aquellas que se traducen en resultados palpables y contundentes a lo largo del tiempo. No me cabe duda que la reforma que hace 20 aos otorg autonoma al Banco de Mxico hoy puede mostrar, con resultados contundentes, que se trat de un cambio institucional profundamente acertado y provechoso para todos los mexicanos. En 1993, cuando el Congreso de la Unin recibi la iniciativa presidencial para modificar tres artculos constitucionales con el objeto de otorgar autonoma al Banco de Mxico, prcticamente todos los mexicanos tenan muy frescos en la 3 memoria los daos devastadores que les haban causado episodios agudos y prolongados de alta inflacin: pobreza extendida, cancelacin de proyectos de inversin, de empleo, penurias diarias para satisfacer necesidades bsicas, patrimonios perdidos en unos cuantos meses tras muchos aos de esfuerzo constante por construirlos. Para la poblacin ms joven de Mxico puede ser difcil comprender los daos que causa un entorno de alta inflacin, sobre todo si tomamos en cuenta que el prximo mes de abril se cumplirn en nuestro pas 14 aos ininterrumpidos de registrar, mes a mes, inflaciones anuales de un solo dgito. Para establecer el contraste con la situacin previa a la autonoma de nuestro Instituto Emisor, basta recordar que en 1993 casi la mitad de los mexicanos en ese entonces, 45 millones de compatriotas, slo haban conocido en su vida inflaciones de dos o ms dgitos. 4 Hoy, ms de 32 millones de mexicanos (los de 14 aos de edad o menos) jams han padecido inflaciones anuales de ms de un dgito. Hoy, miles de mexicanos tienen acceso a crditos hipotecarios para adquirir una vivienda a tasas fijas, en pesos, a plazos que pueden llegar a ser hasta de 30 aos. Eso era simplemente impensable en 1993, cuando el Banco de Mxico obtuvo su autonoma. Gracias tambin a la menor inflacin, el gobierno mexicano puede colocar hoy sus Certificados de la Tesorera de la Federacin (Cetes) a las tasas de inters ms bajas de la historia: tan slo 3.40 por ciento en el plazo de 28 das, como sucedi en la subasta de valores gubernamentales de la semana pasada. Asimismo, gracias a expectativas de inflacin bien ancladas, el gobierno mexicano ha disminuido progresivamente el costo de su deuda pblica interna y externa, y ha incrementado sus plazos de vencimiento: 5 En 1994, el plazo promedio ponderado de la deuda gubernamental en pesos en Mxico era de 0.63 aos (230 das), mientras que el de la deuda gubernamental en Estados Unidos era de 5.08 aos (alrededor de 1,854 das). Hoy, en Mxico, el plazo promedio ponderado de la deuda gubernamental en pesos es de 7.9 aos (2,829 das) en tanto que el de la deuda del gobierno de Estados Unidos es de 5.4 aos (1,935 das). Esto significa no slo que en estos 20 aos se ha ampliado ms de doce veces el plazo de vencimiento de la deuda gubernamental en pesos, sino que, en trminos de plazo de vencimiento, nuestra deuda gubernamental supera por ms de dos aos a la correspondiente a los Estados Unidos. Por supuesto, esta genuina transformacin del escenario econmico en el cual transcurre la vida de Mxico habra sido impensable sin un Banco Central autnomo. 6 De hecho, la independencia no es tanto una prerrogativa del Banco Central como una garanta para la sociedad en su conjunto y para cada individuo dentro de ella: la garanta de que el poder adquisitivo de la moneda de curso legal no ser objeto de manipulaciones ventajosas por parte de los gobiernos en detrimento del patrimonio de los ciudadanos. Sin duda, la autonoma trae consigo el natural requerimiento de una mejor rendicin de cuentas. En el caso del Banco de Mxico, el mandato constitucional prioritario de mantener una inflacin baja y estable hace sencilla y expedita esta rendicin de cuentas. Precisamente el Banco de Mxico rinde cuentas ante la sociedad a travs de los peridicos resultados en materia de inflacin y ejerciendo con la mayor transparencia sus funciones. Me refiero a la total transparencia que debe prevalecer acerca de la informacin, los anlisis, las razones y las deliberaciones que fundamentan las decisiones de poltica monetaria. Pocas polticas pblicas estn tan 7 claramente expuestas al examen del pblico, como las polticas monetarias de aquellos bancos centrales que difunden las minutas de sus reuniones de poltica monetaria, como es el caso del Banco de Mxico. Esto va ms all, incluso, de la habitual y adecuada rendicin de cuentas a la que instituciones autnomas deben estar sujetas en una sociedad democrtica, porque no slo est a la vista de todos el contenido mismo de la decisin, sino su proceso de gestacin al interior de un rgano colegiado de gobierno. Esto es as, porque se ha demostrado que esa plena transparencia en la comunicacin resulta decisiva para el anclaje de las expectativas de inflacin de los agentes econmicos. La esencia de la autonoma es impedir que el Banco Central otorgue financiamiento directo al gobierno. Dicho de otra forma, la autonoma cierra la posibilidad de que los dficit fiscales se financien con crdito del Banco Central. Esta 8 prohibicin se vuelve fcil de cumplir cuando existe una relacin armnica entre las polticas fiscal y monetaria, que son los dos grandes pilares de la estabilidad macroeconmica. En este sentido, la labor del Banco de Mxico de mantener el poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional ha sido facilitada por el sano manejo de las finanzas pblicas que Mxico ha mostrado ya por muchos aos. La reciente iniciativa propuesta por el Presidente Pea Nieto para reforzar la Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria constituye un importante paso adicional para asegurar la estabilidad fiscal y la sostenibilidad de la deuda pblica en el mediano y largo plazos. Por consiguiente, esta iniciativa tambin ser, de aprobarse, un elemento fundamental para garantizar tasas de inflacin bajas y estables en los aos por venir en nuestro pas, y as recrear 9 un terreno frtil para un mayor crecimiento econmico sostenible. En otro orden de ideas, es pertinente mencionar que la Constitucin tambin le otorga autonoma presupuestal al Banco de Mxico, lo que le ha permitido forjar e incrementar el principal activo que tiene: me refiero a su personal altamente calificado y plenamente comprometido con las responsabilidades que la Constitucin le asigna al Instituto Central. *** Seor Presidente, seor Secretario, seores Gobernadores de Bancos Centrales, amigas y amigos: La crisis global desatada en 2008 ha llevado a varios bancos centrales, muchos de ellos aqu representados por sus gobernadores, al lmite de sus capacidades. Las instituciones referidas han mostrado una gran maestra para innovar en la 10 ejecucin de su poltica monetaria, de forma tal que han facilitado la estabilidad de los sistemas financieros y han propiciado la recuperacin de sus economas. Pero siempre lo han hecho sin desatender el objetivo de mantener una inflacin baja y estable. Las acciones implementadas en materia monetaria por los bancos centrales de varias economas avanzadas han abierto una ventana para que sus respectivos gobiernos pongan en marcha otra serie de reformas, en materia fiscal, financiera y regulatorias, para estabilizar sus economas de manera definitiva y puedan retomar la senda del crecimiento econmico. No sera presuntuoso decir que los bancos centrales de los pases avanzados, al abrir esa ventana de tiempo, han sido el principal catalizador para superar la crisis que an nos aqueja. 11 Pero es urgente que los pases ms afectados por la crisis hagan uso efectivo de esa ventana de tiempo que han ofrecido los bancos centrales, pues la poltica monetaria no puede resolver por s sola los problemas que padecen las economas que representan ms del 40 por ciento del PIB mundial, si consideramos a Estados Unidos, Japn, al Reino Unido y a la Unin Monetaria Europea. En este sentido, es muy afortunada esta reunin porque podremos dialogar sobre el valor que tiene la autonoma de los bancos centrales en tiempos de crisis y acerca de cmo se puede ejercer dicha autonoma de manera responsable en momentos difciles. Por ltimo, y no por ello menos importante, quisiera reconocer y agradecer el profundo respeto hacia la autonoma del Banco de Mxico que repetidamente han manifestado el Presidente Pea Nieto y su gobierno. Asimismo, el Banco de 12 Mxico, en su mbito de competencia y accin, siempre estar dispuesto a colaborar para que este impulso transformador encabezado por Usted, Seor Presidente, llegue a buen puerto y produzca sus mejores frutos en beneficio de todos los mexicanos. Muchas gracias. 13

Title: The challenges in a digital age
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the Thirteenth Symposium on Risk Management. "The Challenges in a Digital Age". Mexico City, October 18, 2018 Maestro Bernardo Gonzalez Rosas, President of the National Banking and Securities Commission; Engineer Marcos Martinez Gavica, President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Engineer Heleodoro Ruiz Santos, President of the Risk Management Committee of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Mr. Juan Carlos Jimenez Rojas, General Director of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 It is a pleasure to participate in the Thirteenth edition of the Risk Management Symposium, "The challenges in a digital age", organized by the Association of Banks of Mexico. In the current context, both the institutions that are part of the financial system and the regulatory entities face diverse challenges, specifically those associated with both globalization and accelerated technological change. In this context, it should be noted that in addition to the risks traditionally occupied by the financial system, new challenges are added. In particular, the management of non-financial risks has become more relevant, especially the so-called operational risks. Responding to these challenges requires changes in the organizational structure of regulatory bodies and financial institutions, as well as greater harmonization and integration of risk control and management processes. 2 In this digital age, access to new technologies provides a unique opportunity to streamline operations, design new products and expand the coverage of financial services to more and more sectors of the population. This not only promotes the strengthening and deepening of financial systems, but also unleashes the potential of individuals and generates greater equity of opportunity and better development conditions for millions of people. However, the opportunities of the digital age are not without significant challenges, ranging from cybercrime to unforeseen consequences arising from new technological developments, platforms or business models applied to the provision of financial services. In this regard, by fully addressing the risks of the digital age, not only does it make the financial system more resilient and reduce the possibility of facing cyber attacks, but it is also in a better position to take advantage of it. 3 fully the opportunities that the technological revolution allows in financial services. To highlight how important it is to have a full understanding of the risks present in the financial system, it is worth remembering that 10 years ago we witnessed the outbreak of the most important financial crisis of this century, whose effects strongly impacted financial systems at a global level. There is no doubt that an inadequate understanding of the financial risks associated with various instruments supported directly and indirectly by mortgage payments and their effects on the balance sheets of various financial intermediaries was one of the main factors that led to the crisis. To deal with this crisis, multiple actions were triggered by the authorities around the world, in order to restore the required confidence in the international financial system. In turn, they initiated a series of important modifications to the regulation. 4 These modifications have sought to significantly improve: (i) the identification and measurement of risks; (ii) the valuation of assets; (ii) portfolio granting practices, (iv) portfolio management; (v) aligning incentives in the origination and financing of credits; and (vi) transparency and accountability for operations in the financial system. There is no doubt that much progress has been made in having a more resilient financial system, and in this, having better methods to quantify and mitigate all kinds of risks has been fundamental. Today, risk managers face a wide variety of challenges. In this intervention I will emphasize those associated with cybersecurity and the need to incorporate criteria of environmental sustainability and social impact in investment decisions, which will be addressed in this Symposium. 5 Cybercrime and attacks on the technological infrastructures of the financial system have become widespread, occurring in a wide range of countries and financial intermediaries. These crimes and attacks, with their increasing sophistication and frequency, can cause everything from affectations in the provision of services, to possible losses of information and assets, both for users and intermediaries. The Bank of Mexico believes that in order to maintain the confidence of users in the financial system, it is crucial to guarantee the security of its systems, with an active and coordinated participation of the authorities and financial institutions, with a comprehensive strategy that strengthens the capacity to detect, contain and mitigate cyberattacks. In terms of cybersecurity, all participants are important. Our country has been no stranger to these cybersecurity challenges. In April of this year there were incidents in the operation of some participants of the 6 interbank electronic payment system (SPEI). These incidents occurred in the infrastructure of some participants in the SPEI. To deal with this situation, the Bank of Mexico migrated to contingency schemes to the institutions that could have risks which, although it made the operations of these institutions somewhat slower, allowed to guarantee the security and operation of the system as a whole. Likewise, actions were taken such as extending the Bank's support to the participants, establishing additional control measures to verify the integrity of the funds transfer operations and, above all, maintaining a fluid communication with the public through a micro-site that reports daily on the evolution of the SPEI. To deal with this type of risk, on May 24, the "Bases of coordination in the field of information security" were signed between the different financial authorities of the country, the associations that represent the guilds of the financial system and the Attorney General's Office of the Republic. 7 This document established the basis for information security events to be treated in a comprehensive manner, which includes promoting response protocols and timely communication among all participants. This includes establishing the minimum necessary to guarantee an adequate level of security for the entire network, since information security often tends to be breached from the weakest link in the chain. In addition, the Financial System Stability Council is promoting the strengthening of computer security in the financial system, based on 10 principles that cover the corporate governance of computer security, data protection schemes, risk management, device access controls, incident response protocols, service providers, infrastructure protection policies and training systems and programmes and the promotion of a culture of it security for both staff and customers of financial institutions. Strengthening security and intensifying oversight stand as pieces 8 fundamental to preserving financial stability and confidence in its institutions. Sustainable investments Another of the great paradigm shifts regarding risk management and the investment process is to have a broad framework for the evaluation of all types of risks, which can directly or indirectly affect the performance of the credit portfolio or an investment portfolio. In this regard, environmental risks imply a financial risk. To do this, just consider how the ability to pay of an accredited person facing a significant environmental risk that could jeopardize their operation would be affected. Thus, if the credit allocation does not take into account all the associated risks, the capital allocation will not be adequate and could be subject to significant exposures. 9 In this regard, financial authorities must consider the possible effects of various environmental contingencies and their impact on the credit risk of the financial system. It should be noted that the Bank of Mexico is a member, since its foundation, of the Network of Central Banks and Supervisory Authorities to Green the Financial System, which began with 8 members and currently has 19 members and 5 observers. In this network, it is considered that authorities and financial institutions should promote greater generation of information on environmental risks and develop new analytical, risk measurement, and supervisory approaches that consider prospective scenarios and stress tests. These considerations also help prevent and mitigate significant losses in the financial sector in the face of catastrophic natural events. Additionally, there is an increasing relevance of sustainable investments, such as bonds that meet certain criteria related to the environment, positive social impact or forms of corporate governance. In fact, some information providers have incorporated, 10 in the analysis of some of the issuers they track, additional sustainability criteria.1 Undoubtedly, sustainable emissions represent one of the segments with the greatest growth potential, by virtue of their ability to generate value in investments and that they offer an investment alternative that allows building portfolios with a specific profile that combines profitability with social and environmental responsibility. Of course, as this segment develops, some important challenges will appear, among which would be the design and implementation of the processes of verification of compliance with the sustainability criteria. Ladies and gentlemen, the scope for risk managers is increasingly broad and requires, at the same time, greater specialization and greater flexibility. To the already traditional market, credit and liquidity risks, 1 As an example, the S&P Green Bond Index published by S&P Dow Jones Indices. All this motivates a new, broader, deeper and strategic approach to risk management. I am sure that this forum, which brings together renowned national and international experts, will be a propitious space to share ideas, compare experiences and improve risk management both in the field of public policies and in the one that corresponds to each institution. For all of the above, I congratulate the Association of Banks of Mexico and I am pleased to declare the Thirteenth Symposium on Risk Management inaugurated. "The Challenges in a Digital Age". text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante el Dcimo Tercer Simposio de Administracin de Riesgos. Los Desafos en una Era Digital. Ciudad de Mxico, 18 de octubre de 2018 Maestro Bernardo Gonzlez Rosas, Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores; Ingeniero Marcos Martnez Gavica, Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Ingeniero Heleodoro Ruiz Santos, Presidente de la Comisin de Administracin de Riesgos de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Licenciado Juan Carlos Jimnez Rojas, Director General de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Seoras y seores: 1 Es un gusto participar en la Dcimo Tercera edicin del Simposio de Administracin de Riesgos, Los desafos en una era digital, que organiza la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico. En el contexto actual, tanto las instituciones que forman parte del sistema financiero como los entes reguladores enfrentamos retos diversos, especficamente los asociados tanto a la globalizacin, como al acelerado cambio tecnolgico. En este contexto, cabe destacar que en adicin a los riesgos que tradicionalmente ocupan al sistema financiero, se agregan nuevos desafos. En particular, la gestin de riesgos no financieros ha cobrado mayor relevancia, especialmente los denominados riesgos operacionales. Para responder a estos retos se requieren cambios tanto en la estructura organizacional de los rganos regulatorios e instituciones financieras, como una mayor armonizacin e integracin de los procesos de control y administracin de riesgos. 2 En esta era digital, el acceso a las nuevas tecnologas brinda una oportunidad nica para agilizar las operaciones, disear nuevos productos y ampliar la cobertura de los servicios financieros a cada vez ms sectores de la poblacin. Ello no slo promueve el fortalecimiento y profundizacin de los sistemas financieros, sino que permite liberar el potencial de los individuos y generar mayor equidad de oportunidades y mejores condiciones de desarrollo para millones de personas. Sin embargo, las oportunidades de la era digital no estn exentas de retos de consideracin, los cuales van desde los delitos cibernticos, hasta consecuencias no previstas derivadas de nuevos desarrollos tecnolgicos, plataformas o modelos de negocios aplicados a la provisin de servicios financieros. Al respecto, al atender plenamente los riesgos de la era digital, no slo se hace ms resiliente al sistema financiero y se reduce la posibilidad de enfrentar ataques cibernticos, sino tambin se est en mejor posicin para aprovechar 3 cabalmente las oportunidades que la revolucin tecnolgica permite en los servicios financieros. Para destacar lo importante que resulta un cabal entendimiento de los riesgos presentes en el sistema financiero, conviene recordar que hace 10 aos presenciamos el estallido de la crisis financiera ms importante de este siglo, cuyos efectos impactaron fuertemente los sistemas financieros a nivel global. No hay duda que una inadecuada comprensin de los riesgos financieros asociados a diversos instrumentos respaldados directa e indirectamente por los pagos de hipotecas y sus efectos en los balances de diversos intermediarios financieros fue uno de los principales factores que propici la crisis. Para hacer frente a dicha crisis, se detonaron mltiples acciones por parte de las autoridades alrededor del mundo, a fin de reestablecer la confianza requerida en el sistema financiero internacional. A su vez, iniciaron una serie de importantes modificaciones a la regulacin. 4 Estas modificaciones han buscado mejorar significativamente: i) la identificacin y la medicin de riesgos; ii) la valuacin de activos; ii) las prcticas de otorgamiento de cartera, iv) el manejo de portafolios; v) alinear los incentivos en la originacin y el financiamiento de crditos; y, vi) la transparencia y rendicin de cuentas respecto de las operaciones que se desarrollan en el sistema financiero. No hay duda que se ha avanzado mucho en contar con un sistema financiero ms resistente, y en ello, el contar con mejores mtodos para cuantificar y mitigar todo tipo de riesgos ha sido fundamental. En la actualidad, los administradores de riesgos enfrentan una gran variedad de desafos. En esta intervencin har nfasis en los asociados a la ciberseguridad y la necesidad de incorporar criterios de sustentabilidad ambiental e impacto social en las decisiones de inversin, que sern abordadas en este Simposio. 5 Ciberseguridad Los delitos cibernticos y los ataques a las infraestructuras tecnolgicas del sistema financiero se han generalizado, presentndose en una amplia gama de pases y de intermediarios financieros. Estos delitos y ataques, con su creciente sofisticacin y frecuencia, pueden provocar desde afectaciones en la provisin de los servicios, hasta posibles prdidas de informacin y patrimoniales, tanto para los usuarios como para los intermediarios. El Banco de Mxico considera que para mantener la confianza de los usuarios en el sistema financiero, es crucial garantizar la seguridad de sus sistemas, con una participacin activa y coordinada de las autoridades e instituciones financieras, con una estrategia integral que fortalezca la capacidad para detectar, contener y mitigar los ciberataques. En materia de ciberseguridad todos los participantes son importantes. Nuestro pas no ha sido ajeno a estos desafos de ciberseguridad. En abril de este ao se registraron incidentes en la operacin de algunos participantes del 6 sistema de pagos electrnicos interbancarios (SPEI). Estos incidentes se presentaron en la infraestructura de algunos participantes en el SPEI. Para hacer frente a esta situacin, el Banco de Mxico migr a esquemas de contingencia a las instituciones que podan tener riesgos lo que, si bien hizo un tanto ms lenta las operaciones de dichas instituciones, permiti garantizar la seguridad y la operacin del sistema en su conjunto. Igualmente, se tomaron acciones como extender el soporte del Banco a los participantes, establecer medidas adicionales de control para verificar la integridad de las operaciones de transferencia de fondos y, sobre todo, mantener una comunicacin fluida con el pblico a travs de un micro-sitio que informa cotidianamente de la evolucin del SPEI.
