La informacin solicitada a los intermediarios, que identifica las caractersticas de cada operacin, as como sus diferentes componentes, ha sido utilizada para generar modelos de contagio financiero basados en redes de interconexin, lo que ha permitido en diversos 3 episodios recientes de turbulencia financiera internacional, dar seguimiento cuidadoso al riesgo de exposiciones entre contrapartes. El elevado nivel de detalle de estas estadsticas ha sido tambin utilizado en los ltimos aos para mejorar la informacin sobre la solvencia y liquidez de las instituciones bancarias de acuerdo con los estndares establecidos en Basilea III. Este conjunto de esfuerzos representa un avance de enorme vala para contar con sistemas de informacin financiera acordes con los retos actuales. Indudablemente, las iniciativas internacionales a las que antes hice referencia han desempeado un papel fundamental en la homologacin de los modelos de informacin entre pases y en la identificacin de los mecanismos de transmisin de riesgos entre sistemas financieros. Es de esperarse que esto permita un anlisis de los fenmenos financieros de una manera global e integral, contribuyendo a evitar el riesgo de contagio. Por otra parte, estoy seguro de que, como en el caso de Mxico, los esfuerzos en muchos otros bancos centrales han contribuido a un manejo ms adecuado de los riesgos y a una toma de decisiones mejor fundamentada. Sin embargo, tambin estoy convencido de que existe un amplio margen de accin para que los pases de Amrica Latina y el Caribe se beneficien en mayor medida de estos avances. En este sentido, quisiera sealar, por una parte, que las iniciativas de informacin recientes a nivel global han estado enfocadas principalmente en las preocupaciones y necesidades de los pases directamente afectados por la crisis, en su mayora pases avanzados. Adems, la participacin en muchos de los foros en los que se discuten estas iniciativas es restringida. Por otra parte, el dilogo entre nuestros bancos centrales respecto a los esfuerzos que se han realizado a nivel nacional ha sido insuficiente. 4 Por lo tanto, me parece que para los pases de nuestra regin se vuelve necesario un proceso de reflexin sobre las iniciativas internacionales antes sealadas, a fin de incorporar adecuadamente sus recomendaciones en nuestros sistemas informativos y, en la medida en que ello sea conveniente, adaptarlas a nuestras propias necesidades y realidades. Considero que tambin es importante abrir espacios para compartir los avances y experiencias derivados de los esfuerzos realizados a nivel nacional, y explorar posibles vas de cooperacin. Desde mi punto de vista, esta reunin constituye un primer paso de gran trascendencia en esta direccin. Considerando la diversidad de experiencias y la calidad de los expositores, no tengo duda de que sus discusiones de los prximos dos das sobre el uso de la informacin financiera en la toma de decisiones tanto de poltica monetaria como macroprudencial, las iniciativas internacionales en materia de informacin financiera como un detonador para el enriquecimiento de los modelos de informacin y los aspectos relacionados con la gestin de la informacin, sern de mucho inters y utilidad. Si me lo permiten, quisiera subrayar la importancia del ltimo tema de su agenda de trabajo, es decir, la colaboracin entre nuestros bancos centrales a travs de la creacin de un foro en el que puedan interactuar para compartir experiencias y buscar esquemas de colaboracin. Me gustara sealar en primer lugar que la experiencia del CEMLA con este tipo de foros habla por s sola, ya que ha sido muy exitosa. En segundo lugar, me parece que la ausencia de un espacio para que los bancos centrales miembros del Centro puedan interactuar en temas relacionados con la informacin financiera es una omisin obvia, que debera subsanarse. En tercer lugar, considero importante enfatizar que el alcance que se le quiera dar a una iniciativa de esta naturaleza, depende bsicamente de los intereses y necesidades de ustedes. La creacin del foro les permitira, adems de intercambiar experiencias y establecer una red de 5 contactos a nivel internacional, plantear al CEMLA sus requerimientos de capacitacin en la materia; solicitar, a travs del CEMLA o de manera bilateral, asistencia tcnica; crear grupos de trabajo para colaborar de manera conjunta en proyectos que sean de su inters; e inclusive proponer iniciativas que puedan obtener el respaldo de otras instituciones o grupos internacionales. Para terminar, quisiera dar las gracias al equipo organizador, y especialmente a Alejandro Gaytn del Banco de Mxico y a Ral Morales del CEMLA, por su eficiente trabajo para hacer posible esta excelente reunin. Aprecio mucho tambin el apoyo que le ha dado Fernando Tenjo a este proyecto, y su decisin de incluirlo en el Plan Estratgico del CEMLA para los prximos aos. Tambin agradezco a todos ustedes su valiosa participacin. Espero sinceramente que esta importante iniciativa se vea replicada en el futuro y que, con el apoyo del CEMLA, sus esfuerzos contribuyan a que nuestros bancos centrales cuenten con una base ms slida de informacin financiera que nos ayude a superar los retos a los que deberemos hacer frente en los prximos aos. Muchas gracias 6

Title: The challenges of financial education and inclusion, the central bank's perspective
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the inauguration of the 5th Banamex Financial Education Meeting ("Towards a responsible and weighty financial inclusion"), on June 5, 2012, in Mexico City. Good morning  Highly esteemed graduate Margarita Zavala Gomez del Campo, President of the Citizen Advisory Council of the National System for the Integral Development of the Family  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena  Mr. President of the Executive Committee of Grupo Financiero Banamex and the National Bank of Mexico, Mr. Manuel Medina Mora Escalante  Mr. General Director of Grupo Financiero Banamex, Javier Arrigunaga Gomez del Campo  Dear Luisa Daniel Perez, Banamex National Award for Microenterprise 2010,  Loreto Garcia Muriel, Director of Organizational Culture and Financial Education at Banamex  Ladies and gentlemen The challenges of financial education and inclusion, the central bank's perspective As Governor of the Bank of Mexico, it is an honor to participate in this inauguration of the Fifth Meeting of Financial Education organized by Banamex. In my speech I will try to show how economic stability, through responsible and sustained fiscal and monetary policies throughout 1 Over time, it is crucial to cement financial education and is a prerequisite for promoting greater financial inclusion, both in terms of the infrastructure needed to provide greater access to financial services for more and more people, and the increasingly widespread and intensive use of such services. Mexico is currently in a privileged position to undertake these great challenges. It would be unfortunate if we were to miss this opportunity. Our country has an enviable economic stability based on a disciplined and responsible fiscal policy, as well as on a prudent and firm monetary policy in the fulfillment of its priority objective, which is price stability. This position contrasts with that prevailing in many of the world's most advanced economies, immersed in a fight against serious fiscal imbalances, threats of financial breakdowns and not so simple dilemmas between the indispensable fiscal responsibility and the desired greater economic growth. The global financial crisis that erupted in 2008, and which is still far from over, has so shaken our world that various paradigms and beliefs about economics and finance are subject to review and examination. It has rightly been said that poor financial education is among the main root causes of this global crisis. Governments, regulatory authorities and financial institutions in the world - among others - are co-responsible for this precarious financial knowledge and we have a pressing duty not only to offer realistic and viable responses to the current crisis, but to intensify efforts to propagate financial education that is efficient, that promotes sustainable well-being, that fosters accountability and preserves, with appropriate legal and regulatory frameworks, the basic ingredient of any healthy financial activity: trust. 2 Trust is precisely the most precious commodity and the product par excellence that central banks must offer in the world. We issue legal tender and our priority objective, set out without restrictions in the Constitution, is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of that currency. Without generating and increasing confidence in the currency, and in everything that derives from it, especially in the financial field, the Central Bank would not be fully fulfilling its mission. Today, like various central banks in the world, the Bank of Mexico is increasingly involved in activities aimed at financial education. We do so because greater and better financial education, as well as all the advances in financial inclusion translate, without a doubt, into greater well-being for the population. At the same time, the Central Bank's priority objective, price stability, and its main functions show not only great compatibility with the aims pursued by financial education and inclusion, but also feed back profitably. The greater the financial education and inclusion, the Issuing Institute better fulfills its mandate and functions and, conversely, to the extent that the Central Bank honors its mission to preserve price stability and efficiently performs its functions, relating to the financial system and payment systems, financial education and inclusion will be strengthened. In Mexico, the challenges of education and financial inclusion are immense and the tasks we must undertake to address them are enormous. I do not intend to encompass them in this brief speech, but to show, with examples of what we are doing at the Bank of Mexico in this regard, the multifaceted nature of these challenges and to show, perhaps, a persuasive picture of the magnitude of the task ahead to face such challenges effectively and efficiently. The ideal of financial education is to have consumers of financial services who, in the first place, do not feel intimidated by 3 they, and once they have overcome this fear through basic knowledge, are enlightened users not only about financial principles and their modalities, but also responsible, beneficiaries of an intelligent and intensive use of new technologies, who know how to decipher and assume the risks implicit in financial products and services in order to neutralize or minimize them, that they know their rights and the mechanisms to enforce them and that they appreciate the value of timely information to take advantage of it for their benefit. It is up to the financial authorities to create the conditions so that more and more of the general public has the tools to become that ideal consumer of financial products and services. First of all, we must give certainty and confidence. A responsible fiscal policy and a prudent monetary policy, together with an appropriate legal and regulatory framework, are the inputs to generate certainty and confidence. Of course, laws and regulations must be not only known but applied in a timely manner and without discretion. In this sense, transparency and timeliness in information is indispensable. For example, today the Bank of Mexico makes every effort to communicate its decisions with clarity, timeliness and transparency. We have set out to break the tradition of secrecy that used to characterize central banks in practically the whole world. In this way, we seek to overcome the paradigm that central banks should only have an indirect relationship - through financial intermediaries and markets - with the general public. To establish a new direct relationship with the population, the Bank of Mexico has taken advantage of the immense advantages offered by new information technologies, with the slogan of giving priority to transparency in all our actions and decisions. 4 And this starts from the core of what affects the financial system in any country, which is monetary policy decisions. Today, for example, we are one of the few central banks in the world that disclose the content of the minutes of the Governing Board relating to monetary policy decisions, making public the arguments, the reasons, the divergences of opinion within the Board itself, which precede each decision and give it support. In the same way, we broadcast live, through the Internet, the quarterly inflation reports presented by the Governor accompanied by the Governing Board, as well as the press conference that complements that information. All this material is, of course, available to the public on the Bank's website. The transparent and timely dissemination of monetary policy facilitates the anchoring of expectations of price stability among the population, which in turn must generate confidence, that product par excellence, as I said, of the central bank that fulfills its mission. But it is not just a question of reporting on monetary policy in a timely manner. New technologies give us the opportunity to also have a very effective impact on a better functioning of the financial system and the markets themselves, through the disclosure of timely information on fees, commissions and costs in the financial system; through timely information we try to make consumers know and evaluate the best options. This information fosters greater competition and encourages financial inclusion to go beyond promoting a more extensive infrastructure - that is, greater potential access to financial products and services, but also generate greater penetration, a more intensive and constant use of them for the benefit of consumers. Note that all this is building a virtuous circle that is the fertile ground for greater financial inclusion to flourish, since there will be no 5 It spurs more effectively so that the benefits of the financial system reach more and more people every day, than the same demand exerted by consumers better informed and gradually accustomed to compare, quote and demand the financial products and services they require and want. Along with the information we must be attentive to collaborate with financial institutions in the design of products more appropriate to the needs and habits of the population. A good example of this has been the creation of basic accounts, simple products without charging commissions that all banks that take deposits from the public must offer. Here it seems to me that we have all learned that simple-to-understand, transparent, uncomplicated products and services have been particularly effective in overcoming some of the atavisms and cultural barriers with which banks and financial institutions are often viewed among large segments of the population. In the same vein, in August 2011 the Bank of Mexico regulation came into force that allows banks to offer new types of deposit accounts, known as simplified file accounts, which promote the offer of payment services to sectors of the population with fewer resources. They are accounts that can be opened by phone and through offices of attention and sale of correspondents of the banks, for example in Telecomm Telegrafos or in convenience stores, and that do not require the physical presence or the transfer to a bank branch. Another objective of the Bank of Mexico is to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. In this area, the Interbank Electronic Payments System, the SPEI, developed by the Bank of Mexico and which began operations in 2004, has had an undoubted impact on promoting greater financial inclusion. Today the SPEI processes more than three million payments daily. And we are talking about a large percentage of payments for relatively low amounts which indicates the acceptance of the system by broad sectors of the population. In fact, 47 percent of the payments processed by the SPEI are for amounts less than five thousand pesos. 6 Of course, the Bank of Mexico carries out constant campaigns to disseminate the benefits of the SPEI that, recently, in accordance with the communication strategy approved by the Bank's Governing Board, have focused especially on non-conventional media, precisely through the Internet. Payers and beneficiaries of payments processed in the SPEI can obtain on the website of the Bank of Mexico, at no cost, information about the status of their payments. In addition, since April 2012 both payers and beneficiaries can obtain, on the Central Bank's website, a signed proof that the payment was paid into the beneficiary's account, which increases the security and confidence of users. As I pointed out, these are just some examples of that vast universe of tasks to be developed that involve financial education and inclusion in our country. Ladies and gentlemen: It is a fact that Mexico enjoys a healthy financial system, well capitalized, with advanced regulation (to the extent that we will be one of the first countries to comply with the new requirements of global banking regulation known as Basel III), well supervised and with a high capitalization, so that today we are one of the few countries in the world whose banks are able to expand the granting of credit quickly and sustainably. at affordable rates and in conditions of great security for the institutions and for the potential accredited. 7 The low penetration of the financial system in Mexico means that we have a large window of opportunity to expand financing and savings services, well above those currently being offered. This is the necessary correlate for financial education. If this expansion of financial services materializes, for which all the conditions are given, the Gross Domestic Product could increase, with that contribution alone, at least one percentage point more than what we observe today. A fundamental element in achieving this goal is financial education as well as a firm commitment to financial inclusion, all of which, in the end, will translate into greater well-being for the entire population and invaluable support in the fight against poverty. The challenges and the tasks involved are very great, but our commitment and coordination to face them cannot be minor. Thanks a lot. 8
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la inauguracin del 5 Encuentro de Educacin Financiera Banamex (Hacia una inclusin financiera responsable y de peso), el 5 de junio de 2012, en la ciudad de Mxico. Buenos das  Muy estimada licenciada Margarita Zavala Gmez del Campo, Presidenta del Consejo Ciudadano Consultivo del Sistema Nacional para el Desarrollo Integral de la Familia  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Jos Antonio Meade Kuribrea  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Ejecutiva de Grupo Financiero Banamex y del Banco Nacional de Mxico, licenciado Manuel Medina Mora Escalante  Seor Director General de Grupo Financiero Banamex, licenciado Javier Arrigunaga Gmez del Campo  Estimada Luisa Daniel Prez, Premio Nacional Banamex a la Microempresa 2010,  Licenciada Loreto Garca Muriel, Directora de Cultura Organizacional y Educacin Financiera de Banamex  Seoras y seores Los desafos de la educacin y la inclusin financieras, la perspectiva del Banco Central Como Gobernador del Banco de Mxico es un honor participar en esta inauguracin del Quinto Encuentro de Educacin Financiera que organiza Banamex. En mi intervencin tratar de mostrar cmo la estabilidad econmica, a travs de polticas fiscales y monetarias responsables y sostenidas a lo largo 1 del tiempo, es crucial para cimentar la educacin financiera y es requisito indispensable para promover una mayor inclusin financiera, tanto en lo que se refiere a la infraestructura necesaria para ofrecer un mayor acceso a cada vez ms personas a los servicios financieros, como al uso cada vez ms extendido e intensivo de dichos servicios. Mxico est en estos momentos en una posicin privilegiada para emprender estos grandes desafos. Sera lamentable que dejsemos pasar de largo esta oportunidad. Nuestro pas cuenta con una envidiable estabilidad econmica fundamentada en una poltica fiscal disciplinada y responsable, as como en una poltica monetaria prudente y firme en el cumplimiento de su objetivo prioritario, que es la estabilidad de precios. Esta posicin contrasta con la que prevalece en muchas de las economas ms avanzadas del mundo, inmersas en una lucha contra graves desequilibrios fiscales, amenazas de quebrantos financieros y dilemas nada sencillos entre la indispensable responsabilidad fiscal y el anhelado mayor crecimiento econmico. La crisis financiera global que estall en 2008, y que an est lejos de haber sido superada, ha conmovido de tal forma nuestro mundo que diversos paradigmas y creencias acerca de la economa y de las finanzas estn sujetos a revisin y a examen. Se ha dicho con razn que la deficiente educacin financiera est entre las principales causas de origen de esta crisis global. Los gobiernos, las autoridades encargadas de la regulacin y las instituciones financieras en el mundo  entre otros- somos corresponsables de este precario conocimiento financiero y tenemos el deber acuciante no slo de ofrecer respuestas realistas y viables a la crisis actual, sino de intensificar los esfuerzos para propagar una educacin financiera que sea eficiente, que promueva un bienestar sostenible, que propicie la responsabilidad y preserve, con marcos jurdicos y de regulacin adecuados, el ingrediente bsico de toda actividad financiera saludable: la confianza. 2 Justamente la confianza es el bien ms preciado y el producto por excelencia que debemos ofrecer los bancos centrales en el mundo. Emitimos la moneda de curso legal y nuestro objetivo prioritario, plasmado sin cortapisas en la Constitucin, es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de dicha moneda. Sin generar y acrecentar la confianza en la moneda, y en todo lo que de ella se deriva, especialmente en el terreno financiero, el Banco Central no estara cumpliendo cabalmente su misin. Hoy da, al igual que diversos bancos centrales en el mundo, el Banco de Mxico est involucrado cada vez con mayor intensidad en actividades orientadas a la educacin financiera. Lo hacemos porque una mayor y mejor educacin financiera, as como todos los avances en materia de inclusin financiera se traducen, sin lugar a dudas, en un mayor bienestar para la poblacin. A la vez, el objetivo prioritario del Banco Central, la estabilidad de precios, y sus funciones principales muestran no slo una gran compatibilidad con los fines que persiguen la educacin y la inclusin financieras, sino que tambin se retroalimentan provechosamente. A mayor educacin e inclusin financieras, el Instituto Emisor cumple mejor su mandato y sus funciones y, a la inversa, en la medida que el Banco Central honra su misin de preservar la estabilidad de precios y realiza eficientemente sus funciones, relativas al sistema financiero y a los sistemas de pagos, la educacin y la inclusin financieras se vern fortalecidas. En Mxico, los desafos de la educacin y de la inclusin financiera son inmensos y las tareas que debemos acometer, para abordarlos, son ingentes. No pretendo abarcarlos en este breve discurso, sino mostrar, con ejemplos de lo que estamos haciendo en el Banco de Mxico al respecto, la naturaleza multifactica de estos desafos y mostrar, tal vez, una imagen persuasiva de la magnitud de la tarea que tenemos por delante para enfrentar tales desafos con eficacia y con eficiencia. El ideal de la educacin financiera es contar con consumidores de los servicios financieros que, en primer lugar, no se sientan intimidados por 3 ellos, y una vez que han superado ese temor mediante los conocimientos bsicos, sean usuarios ilustrados no slo acerca de los principios financieros y sus modalidades, sino responsables, beneficiarios de un uso inteligente e intensivo de las nuevas tecnologas, que sepan descifrar y asumir los riesgos implcitos en los productos y servicios financieros para neutralizarlos o minimizarlos, que conozcan sus derechos y los mecanismos para hacer que se cumplan y que aprecien el valor de la informacin oportuna para aprovecharla en su beneficio. A las autoridades financieras nos corresponde crear las condiciones para que cada vez ms el pblico en general tenga las herramientas para convertirse en ese consumidor ideal de los productos y servicios financieros. Antes que nada, debemos dar certidumbre y confianza. Una poltica fiscal responsable y una poltica monetaria prudente, junto con un marco jurdico y de regulacin apropiado, son los insumos para generar certidumbre y confianza. Por supuesto, leyes y normas deben ser no slo conocidas sino aplicadas oportunamente y sin discrecionalidad. En este sentido, la trasparencia y oportunidad en la informacin es indispensable. Por ejemplo, hoy da el Banco de Mxico hace el mayor de los esfuerzos para comunicar con claridad, oportunidad y transparencia sus decisiones. Nos hemos propuesto romper la tradicin de hermetismo que sola caracterizar en prcticamente todo el mundo a los bancos centrales. De esta forma, buscamos superar el paradigma de que los bancos centrales slo deben tener una relacin indirecta  a travs de los intermediarios financieros y de los mercados  con el pblico en general. Para establecer una nueva relacin directa con la poblacin, el Banco de Mxico ha aprovechado las inmensas ventajas que ofrece las nuevas tecnologas de la informacin, con la consigna de darle prioridad a la transparencia en todas nuestras acciones y decisiones. 4 Y esto empieza desde el ncleo de lo que afecta al sistema financiero en cualquier pas, que son las decisiones de poltica monetaria. Hoy, por ejemplo, somos uno de los pocos bancos centrales en el mundo que divulgamos el contenido de las minutas de la Junta de Gobierno relativas a las decisiones de poltica monetaria, haciendo pblicos los argumentos, las razones, las divergencias de opinin al interior de la propia Junta, que preceden a cada decisin y le dan sustento. Del mismo modo, transmitimos en vivo, a travs de Internet, los informes trimestrales de inflacin que presenta el Gobernador acompaado de la Junta de Gobierno, as como la conferencia de prensa que complementa esa informacin. Todo ese material queda, por supuesto, disponible para el pblico en la pgina de Internet del Banco. La difusin transparente y oportuna de la poltica monetaria facilita el anclaje de las expectativas de estabilidad de precios entre la poblacin, lo que a su vez debe generar confianza, ese producto por excelencia, como he dicho, de la banca central que cumple su misin. Pero no slo se trata de informar oportunamente sobre la poltica monetaria. Las nuevas tecnologas nos dan oportunidad de incidir tambin con gran eficacia en un mejor funcionamiento del sistema financiero y de los mercados mismos, mediante la divulgacin de informacin oportuna sobre tasas, comisiones y costos en el sistema financiero; mediante informacin puntual tratamos de que los consumidores conozcan y evalan las mejores opciones. Esta informacin propicia una mayor competencia e incentiva que la inclusin financiera vaya ms all de promover una infraestructura ms extensa  esto es, mayor acceso potencial a productos y servicios financierossino que adems genere una mayor penetracin, un uso ms intensivo y constante de los mismos en beneficio de los consumidores. Ntese que todo esto va construyendo un crculo virtuoso que es el terreno abonado para que florezca una mayor inclusin financiera, ya que no habr 5 acicate ms eficaz para que los beneficios del sistema financiero lleguen a cada da ms personas, que la misma demanda ejercida por consumidores mejor informados y gradualmente habituados a comparar, cotizar y exigir los productos y servicios financieros que requieren y desean. Junto con la informacin debemos estar atentos para colaborar con las instituciones financieras en el diseo de productos ms adecuados a las necesidades y hbitos de la poblacin. Un buen ejemplo de esto ha sido la creacin de las cuentas bsicas, productos sencillos sin cobro de comisiones que todos los bancos que toman depsitos del pblico deben ofrecer. Aqu me parece que todos hemos aprendido que los productos y servicios sencillos de entender, transparentes, sin complejidades, han sido particularmente eficaces para vencer algunos de los atavismos y barreras culturales con que frecuentemente son vistos los bancos y las instituciones financieras entre grandes segmentos de la poblacin. En la misma lnea, en agosto de 2011 entr en vigor la regulacin del Banco de Mxico que permite a los bancos ofrecer nuevos tipos de cuentas de depsito, conocidas como cuentas de expediente simplificado, que promueven la oferta de servicios de pago a sectores de la poblacin con menos recursos. Son cuentas que se pueden abrir por telfono y a travs de oficinas de atencin y venta de corresponsales de los bancos, por ejemplo en Telecomm Telgrafos o en tiendas de conveniencia, y que no requieren la presencia fsica o el traslado a una sucursal bancaria. Otro de los objetivos del Banco de Mxico es propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. En este terreno el Sistema de Pagos Electrnicos Interbancarios, el SPEI, desarrollado por el Banco de Mxico y que inici operaciones en 2004, ha tenido un impacto indudable en promover una mayor inclusin financiera. Hoy el SPEI procesa diariamente ms de tres millones de pagos. Y estamos hablando en un gran porcentaje de pagos por montos relativamente bajos lo que indica la aceptacin del sistema por sectores amplios de la poblacin. En efecto, el 47 por ciento de los pagos que procesa el SPEI son por montos menores a los cinco mil pesos. 6 Por supuesto, el Banco de Mxico realiza constantes campaas de difusin de los beneficios del SPEI que, recientemente, de acuerdo con la estrategia de comunicacin aprobada por la Junta de Gobierno del Banco, se han focalizado de forma especial en medios de comunicacin no convencionales, precisamente a travs de Internet. Los ordenantes y beneficiarios de pagos procesados en el SPEI pueden obtener en el sitio de Internet del Banco de Mxico, sin costo, informacin sobre el estado en que se encuentran sus pagos. Adems, desde abril de 2012 tanto los ordenantes como los beneficiarios pueden obtener, en el sitio Web del Banco Central, un comprobante firmado de que el pago fue abonado en la cuenta del beneficiario, lo cual incrementa la seguridad y la confianza de los usuarios. Como seal estos son slo algunos ejemplos de ese vasto universo de tareas a desarrollar que implican la educacin y la inclusin financieras en nuestro pas. Seoras y seores: Es un hecho que Mxico disfruta de un sistema financiero sano, bien capitalizado, con una regulacin avanzada (al grado de que seremos de los primeros pases en cumplir con los nuevos requerimientos de regulacin global bancaria conocidos como Basilea III), bien supervisado y con una capitalizacin elevada, de tal suerte que hoy somos uno de los pocos pases en el mundo cuya banca est en capacidad de ampliar acelerada y sostenidamente el otorgamiento de crdito a tasas accesibles y en condiciones de gran seguridad para las instituciones y para los potenciales acreditados. 7 La baja penetracin del sistema financiero en Mxico significa que tenemos una gran ventana de oportunidad para expandir el financiamiento y los servicios de ahorro, muy por encima de los que actualmente se estn ofreciendo. Este es el correlato necesario para la educacin financiera. De concretarse esta expansin de los servicios financieros, para la cual todas las condiciones estn dadas, el Producto Interno Bruto podra incrementarse, con ese solo aporte, al menos un punto porcentual ms de lo que hoy observamos. Un elemento fundamental para lograr esta meta es la educacin financiera as como un compromiso decidido con la inclusin financiera, todo lo cual, a la postre, se traducir en un mayor bienestar para toda la poblacin y en un apoyo invaluable en la lucha contra la pobreza. Los desafos y las tareas que implican son muy grandes, pero nuestro empeo y coordinacin para afrontarlos no pueden ser menores. Muchas gracias. 8

Title: Opening of National Financial Education Week 2011
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, at the opening of the National Financial Education Week 2011. September 30, 2011  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena  Mr. President of the National Commission for the Protection and Defense of Users of Financial Services (CONDUSEF), Dr. Luis Pazos de la Torre  Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, Mr. Jaime Ruiz Sacristan  Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, I would like to greet with the greatest enthusiasm the realization of this National Week of Financial Education and congratulate the Ministry of Finance, the Condusef and the numerous institutions and associations that have joined this effort. Increasingly and with increasing intensity, various central banks in the world have been involved in activities aimed at financial education. The Bank of Mexico is no exception, even though financial education itself is not among the purposes set by law, nor is it part of its substantive functions. The Bank of Mexico does so, like many other central banks, because greater and better financial education has a decisive impact, and certainly for the better, on the fulfillment of its constitutional mandates and functions. First, better and increasingly widespread financial education helps the population to understand more clearly the benefits of price stability, which is the Central Bank's priority objective. And that better understanding of the evils that inflation brings makes it easier for the 1 monetary policy decisions taken by the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico achieve their objectives more effectively. On the other hand, the Central Bank must make every effort to communicate with clarity, timeliness and transparency these decisions and the arguments on which they are based. For this reason, the Bank of Mexico has proposed in recent years to break the tradition of secrecy that used to characterize, in practically the whole world, central banks. Today, for example, we are one of the few central banks in the world that disclose the content of the minutes of the Governing Board relating to monetary policy decisions, making public the reasons, arguments, data and differences of opinion, within the Board itself, which precede the decision and give it support. This constant communication effort undoubtedly contributes to and reinforces financial education. Financial education also helps the Central Bank to fulfil its task of promoting the proper functioning of a healthy and competitive financial system, while reinforcing the tasks entrusted to it by law in terms of regulation and supervision of the financial system, such as verifying that consumers of financial products and services have complete information, truthful and timely or that financial institutions comply with the legal provisions on the collection of commissions. The same can be said of the proper functioning of payment systems and their relationship with financial education. To the extent that all payment options and their costs, benefits and characteristics are better known, the Bank of Mexico fulfills its functions better. For example, by disseminating and explaining the advantages of the Interbank Electronic Payment System, the SPEI, in terms of costs and security or the existence of the Direct to Mexico program, which significantly lowers the costs of sending remittances for Mexicans working abroad and for their families in Mexico. As a core part of all this effort of the Bank of Mexico to promote financial education we recently renewed our website, 2 so that it would be a site much more consulted not only by specialists and market trainers, but by the general public. In an effort that involved all the operational areas of the Bank of Mexico, we created, on the Bank's new website, a new disclosure portal that explains, step by step and in accessible and simple language, the four tasks and functions of the Central Bank, that is: the preservation of price stability or the fight against inflation through monetary policy; what a financial system is and how it works, starting with clear definitions of savings, investment, credit, the various financial intermediation institutions; what is a payment system, what payment systems work in our country and what are its advantages and, finally, everything related to the issuance of banknotes and coins, its characteristics and its history. In parallel to this new website, which came to light on July 11, the Bank has ventured with great success into social networks, mainly through Twitter. As of last Thursday, more than 28,800 people followed the daily punctual messages of the Bank of Mexico through the institutional Twitter account @Banxico, which is growing at a rate of about one hundred new followers every day. Along with this institutional account, the account @DivulgaBanxico has been created in the last month, which every day, in synthetic phrases, of no more than 140 characters, disseminates around ten financial education messages, referenced precisely to the dissemination portal of our Website. Other outreach efforts using the potential of the Internet and social networks will be added soon for specific products and services that are the responsibility of the Bank of Mexico, such as SPEI and Directo a Mexico. For the third consecutive year, the Bank of Mexico has announced the Contacto Banxico award for high school students, which awards the three best essays on financial education issues, such as the benefits of price stability (theme of the year 2010) and this year the benefits of having a healthy financial system. 3 Of course, I cannot fail to mention the important work of disseminating financial education carried out by the Interactive Museum of Economics, MIDE. As everyone knows, this new concept of educational museography around the dissemination of basic concepts of economics and finance arose at the initiative of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico five years ago and the conceptual design of its contents was in charge of the economists of the Bank of Mexico, especially the General Directorate of Economic Studies. The MIDE daily makes available to all, in a pleasant and didactic way, the foundations of a good economic and financial culture. Additionally, Congress has given the Bank of Mexico powers to protect consumer rights. Thus, basic accounts have been regulated, financial practices contrary to or inconsistent with free competition have been prohibited. It is clear that for users of financial services to take full advantage of all the benefits of these legal and regulatory provisions, financial education is crucial. Of course, much remains to be done, but the encouraging results are the best stimulus to continue with this task of financial education, through greater communication and specific outreach tasks. We all have a lot to contribute to this effort and we all have a lot to gain from it. Congratulations and the best of successes for this National Financial Education Week. Thanks a lot. 4
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, en la inauguracin de la Semana Nacional de la Educacin Financiera 2011. 30 de septiembre de 2011  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Jos Antonio Meade Kuribrea  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional para la Proteccin y Defensa de los Usuarios de Servicios Financieros (CONDUSEF), doctor Luis Pazos de la Torre  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, licenciado Jaime Ruz Sacristn  Seoras y seores: En primer trmino deseo saludar con el mayor entusiasmo la realizacin de esta Semana Nacional de la Educacin Financiera y felicitar a la Secretara de Hacienda, a la Condusef y las numerosas instituciones y asociaciones que se han sumado a este esfuerzo. En la medida que se conozcan mejor todas las opciones de pago y sus costos, sus beneficios y sus caractersticas, el Banco de Mxico cumple mejor con sus funciones. Por ejemplo, al difundir y explicar las ventajas del Sistema de Pagos Electrnicos Interbancarios, el SPEI, en trminos de costos y seguridad o la existencia del programa Directo a Mxico, que abarata notablemente los costos de envo de remesas para los mexicanos que trabajan en el extranjero y para sus familias en Mxico. Como parte toral de todo este esfuerzo del Banco de Mxico por impulsar la educacin financiera recientemente renovamos nuestra pgina de Internet, 2 para que fuese un sitio mucho ms consultado no slo por los especialistas y formadores de mercados, sino por el pblico en general. En un esfuerzo que involucr a todas las reas operativas del Banco de Mxico creamos, en el nuevo sitio de Internet del Banco, un nuevo portal de divulgacin que explica, paso a paso y en un lenguaje accesible y sencillo, las cuatro tareas y funciones del Banco Central, esto es: la preservacin de la estabilidad de precios o el combate a la inflacin a travs de la poltica monetaria; lo que es y cmo funciona un sistema financiero, empezando por definiciones claras de ahorro, inversin, crdito, las diversas instituciones de intermediacin financiera; qu es un sistema de pagos, cules sistemas de pagos funcionan en nuestro pas y cules son sus ventajas y, por ltimo, todo lo relativo a la emisin de billetes y monedas, sus caractersticas y su historia. En paralelo a esta nueva pgina de Internet, que sali a la luz el pasado 11 de julio, el Banco ha incursionado con gran xito en las redes sociales, principalmente a travs de Twitter. Al jueves pasado seguan cotidianamente los mensajes puntuales del Banco de Mxico ms de 28 mil 800 personas a travs de la cuenta institucional en Twitter @Banxico, que est creciendo a un ritmo de unos cien nuevos seguidores cada da. Junto con esa cuenta institucional se ha creado en el ltimo mes la cuenta @DivulgaBanxico que todos los das, en frases sintticas, de no ms de 140 caracteres, difunde alrededor de diez mensajes de educacin financiera, referenciados precisamente al portal de divulgacin de nuestra pgina de Internet. Prximamente se sumarn otros esfuerzos de divulgacin utilizando el potencial de Internet y de las redes sociales, para productos y servicios especficos que son responsabilidad del Banco de Mxico, como el SPEI y Directo a Mxico. Por tercer ao consecutivo, el Banco de Mxico ha convocado al premio Contacto Banxico a estudiantes de bachillerato, en el que se premia a los tres mejores ensayos sobre asuntos de educacin financiera, tales como los beneficios de la estabilidad de precios (tema del ao 2010) y en este ao los beneficios de contar con un sistema financiero sano. 3 Por supuesto, no puedo dejar de mencionar la importante labor de divulgacin de la educacin financiera que realiza el Museo Interactivo de Economa, MIDE. Como todos saben este novedoso concepto de museografa educativa alrededor de la difusin de conceptos bsicos de la economa y de las finanzas surgi a iniciativa de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico hace cinco aos y el diseo conceptual de sus contenidos estuvo a cargo de los economistas del Banco de Mxico, especialmente de la Direccin General de Estudios Econmicos. El MIDE cotidianamente pone al alcance de todos, de forma amena y didctica, los fundamentos de una buena cultura econmica y financiera. Adicionalmente, el Congreso le ha dado facultades al Banco de Mxico que tienen que ver con la proteccin de los derechos de los consumidores. As, se han regulado las cuentas bsicas, se han prohibido prcticas financieras contrarias o inconsistentes con una libre competencia. Es evidente que para que los usuarios de los servicios financieros aprovechen plenamente todos los beneficios de estas disposiciones legales y de regulacin, la educacin financiera resulta decisiva. Por supuesto, queda mucho por hacer, pero los resultados alentadores son el mejor estmulo para seguir con esta tarea de educacin financiera, a travs de una mayor comunicacin y de tareas especficas de divulgacin. Todos tenemos mucho que aportar a este esfuerzo y todos tenemos mucho que ganar con l. Felicidades y el mejor de los xitos para esta Semana Nacional de la Educacin Financiera. Muchas gracias. 4

Title: Trust in legal tender
text: "Trust in legal tender" Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the signing ceremony of the collaboration agreement between the Bank of Mexico and the Ministry of the Interior to prevent and combat crimes that threaten security in monetary circulation. 21 July 2014  Mr. Secretary of the Interior, Mr. Miguel angel Osorio Chong,  Mr. National Commissioner of Security, Mr. Monte Alejandro Rubido Garcia,  Commissioner General of the Federal Police, Enrique Francisco Galindo Ceballos,  Distinguished representatives of the media,  Ladies and gentlemen, Good afternoon. 1 For the Bank of Mexico and for me personally, it has a high significance to sign this agreement with the Ministry of the Interior, aimed at preventing and combating crimes that threaten the security of our banknotes and coins. I am truly grateful for the commitment and willingness of Secretary Osorio Chong and his collaborators to assist the Bank of Mexico in this important role. The Bank of Mexico is assigned the task of issuing the legal tender in the country. For the currency to fulfill its key function in the life of a Nation, which is to facilitate millions of transactions throughout the territory, as well as to allow millions of economic decisions, savings, credit, investment, this currency has to be a sign that generates trust among all its users. The priority objective of the Bank of Mexico, which is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency, is a direct consequence of its function as a single bank of issue. And to comply 2 In addition to this priority objective - which is the fight against inflation - the Bank of Mexico uses all the tools of monetary policy at its disposal in order to underpin confidence in the national currency. But not only high inflation can damage confidence in the currency, but also the episodes of counterfeiting of banknotes and coins hurt that confidence. This is even though, as in Mexico, these are isolated episodes that the State fights effectively and with the severity that the gravity of said crime deserves. To comply with the reliable provision of the national currency it is necessary to inhibit counterfeiting, which implies three tasks that must be articulated as a gear. In the first place, banknotes must have security features that, on the one hand, are difficult to imitate by those who intend to counterfeit them but, on the other hand, are easy to identify for the entire user public. To achieve this, the Bank of 3 Mexico, through its Banknote Factory, permanently seeks to incorporate the latest advances in security into banknotes. Thus, for example, Mexico is the first country in the world to print a security element that changes color in a transparent window, as is the case of the butterfly that we all know in the new 50 peso bill. The second task in inhibiting counterfeiting is to provide the public with a broad understanding of how to identify these security features. That is why the Bank of Mexico permanently disseminates information on radio and television, in brochures, on its website and through social networks, to explain to the population in a simple way how to identify an authentic banknote. The massive dissemination of this information is thanks to the fact that the Bank of Mexico has the support of the State through the so-called "official times" in radio and television administered by the Ministry of the Interior, through the General Directorate of 4 Radio, Television and Cinematography, for which I am very grateful to Secretary Osorio and his collaborators for their determined support in this communication task. Thirdly, there is the prevention and prosecution of crime and the application of the law. At the moment we can say that in general the level of imitation is unprofessional and of low quality, so in most cases its detection is simple among the user public. However, more technically elaborated forgeries appear with some frequency. Faced with this reality, it has been very important to have the full support and strength of the Mexican State to effectively combat counterfeiting and, in this way, maintain the high degree of confidence that our monetary signs arouse. That is why in the Central Bank we are committed to strengthening our coordination with the Federal Government and now in particular with the Ministry of the Interior, through the National Security Commission and the Federal Police, agencies, by 5 True, from which we already receive effective support in other tasks. I mention as an example the ground escort that they provide to the security paper that is imported for the manufacture of banknotes and the monitoring of our facilities within the framework of the Coordination Group of Strategic Facilities of the Mexican State. Also noteworthy is the integration of a Coordination Group in which the Bank of Mexico, the Federal Police and the Attorney General's Office participate. It should be noted that with the signing of this agreement, the Federal Police will permanently establish a group of police officers from the Investigation Division specialized in the prevention, investigation and fight against counterfeiting. I take this opportunity to invite society to join these efforts to combat counterfeiting in a simple and effective way: it is enough to know the security elements of banknotes and literally spend a few seconds verifying the 6 same with touch and with sight. To the extent that we all make such verification a habit, attempts to put counterfeit banknotes into circulation will be unsuccessful. In case we arrive to receive a banknote whose authenticity we doubt, we must not circulate it, we must take it to any bank branch to request that it be sent to Banco de Mexico for analysis. In the Bank of Mexico we will determine if it is authentic or false, we will give an answer to the user and we will share the information with the Attorney General's Office and with the Federal Police to support the work of prosecuting the crime. This culture of legality also implies that any citizen reports to the Federal Police anyone who they suspect is committing the crime of counterfeiting. I conclude by reiterating our deep gratitude to Secretary Osorio Chong and all his collaborators in the National Commission. 7 of Security and in the Federal Police, just as we recognize and value the efforts and work they have deployed in this specific matter, despite the accumulation of other important tasks that they carry out permanently to provide security to all Mexicans. Thanks a lot. 8
text_original: La confianza en la moneda de curso legal Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la ceremonia de firma del convenio de colaboracin entre el Banco de Mxico y la Secretara de Gobernacin para prevenir y combatir los delitos que atenten contra la seguridad en la circulacin monetaria. 21 Julio 2014  Seor Secretario de Gobernacin, licenciado Miguel ngel Osorio Chong,  Seor Comisionado Nacional de Seguridad, licenciado Monte Alejandro Rubido Garca,  Seor Comisionado General de la Polica Federal, Enrique Francisco Galindo Ceballos,  Distinguidos representantes de los medios de comunicacin,  Seoras y seores: Buenas tardes. 1 Para el Banco de Mxico y para m en lo personal tiene un alto significado suscribir este convenio con la Secretara de Gobernacin, destinado a prevenir y combatir los delitos que atentan contra la seguridad de nuestros billetes y monedas. Agradezco de verdad el compromiso y la buena disposicin del secretario Osorio Chong y de sus colaboradores, en coadyuvar con el Banco de Mxico en esta importante funcin. El Banco de Mxico tiene asignada la tarea de emitir la moneda de curso legal en el pas. Para que la moneda cumpla su funcin clave en la vida de una Nacin, que es la de facilitar millones de transacciones en todo el territorio, as como tambin permitir millones de decisiones econmicas, de ahorro, de crdito, de inversin, dicha moneda tiene que ser un signo que genere confianza entre todos sus usuarios. El objetivo prioritario del Banco de Mxico, que es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda, es consecuencia directa de su funcin como Banco nico de emisin. Y para cumplir 2 cabalmente ese objetivo prioritario  que es el combate a la inflacin-, el Banco de Mxico utiliza todas las herramientas de la poltica monetaria de las que dispone con el objeto de apuntalar la confianza en la moneda nacional. Pero no slo una inflacin elevada puede lesionar la confianza en la moneda, tambin lastiman esa confianza los episodios de falsificacin de billetes y monedas. Esto aun cuando, como sucede en Mxico, se trate de episodios aislados que el Estado combate con eficacia y con la severidad que amerita la gravedad de dicho delito. Para cumplir con la provisin confiable de la moneda nacional es necesario inhibir la falsificacin, lo que implica tres tareas que deben articularse como un engranaje. En primer lugar, los billetes deben contar con elementos de seguridad que, por un lado, sean difciles de imitar por quienes pretenden falsificarlos pero que, por otro lado, sean fciles de identificar para todo el pblico usuario. Para lograrlo el Banco de 3 Mxico, a travs de su Fbrica de Billetes, busca permanentemente incorporar en los billetes los ltimos avances en materia de seguridad. As, por ejemplo, Mxico es el primer pas del mundo en imprimir un elemento de seguridad que cambia de color en una ventana transparente, como es el caso de la mariposa que todos conocemos en el nuevo billete de $50 pesos. La segunda tarea para inhibir la falsificacin de billetes es propiciar entre el pblico un amplio conocimiento acerca de cmo identificar esos elementos de seguridad. Por eso el Banco de Mxico difunde permanentemente informacin en radio y televisin, en folletos, en su pgina en internet y a travs de las redes sociales, para explicar a la poblacin de manera sencilla cmo identificar un billete autntico. La difusin masiva de esta informacin se da gracias a que el Banco de Mxico cuenta con el apoyo del Estado mediante los llamados tiempos oficiales en radio y televisin que administra la Secretara de Gobernacin, a travs de la Direccin General de 4 Radio, Televisin y Cinematografa, por lo que mucho agradezco al secretario Osorio y a sus colaboradores su decidido respaldo en esta tarea de comunicacin. En tercer lugar se tiene la prevencin y persecucin del delito y la aplicacin de la ley. Por el momento podemos afirmar que en general el nivel de imitacin es poco profesional y de baja calidad, por lo que en la mayora de los casos su deteccin es sencilla entre el pblico usuario. No obstante, con cierta frecuencia aparecen falsificaciones de mayor elaboracin tcnica. Ante esta realidad ha sido muy importante contar con todo el apoyo y la fuerza del Estado mexicano para combatir eficazmente la falsificacin y, de esa forma, mantener el alto grado de confianza que suscitan nuestros signos monetarios. Es por eso que en el Banco Central estamos empeados en estrechar nuestra coordinacin con el Gobierno Federal y ahora en particular con la Secretaria de Gobernacin, a travs de la Comisin Nacional de Seguridad y de la Polica Federal, organismos, por 5 cierto, de los que ya recibimos un apoyo efectivo en otras tareas. Menciono como ejemplo la escolta terrestre que brindan al papel seguridad que se importa para la fabricacin de los billetes y el monitoreo de nuestras instalaciones en el marco del Grupo de Coordinacin de Instalaciones Estratgicas del Estado mexicano. Sobresale, tambin, la integracin de un Grupo de Coordinacin en el que participamos el Banco de Mxico, la Polica Federal y la Procuradura General de la Repblica. Cabe advertir que con la firma de este convenio la Polica Federal establecer con carcter permanente un grupo de policas de la Divisin de Investigacin especializado en la prevencin, investigacin y combate a la falsificacin. Aprovecho esta oportunidad para invitar a la sociedad a sumarse a estos esfuerzos de combatir la falsificacin de una manera sencilla y eficaz: basta con conocer los elementos de seguridad de los billetes y dedicar literalmente unos segundos a la verificacin de los 6 mismos con el tacto y con la vista. En la medida que todos hagamos de dicha verificacin un hbito, los intentos de introducir a la circulacin billetes falsos sern infructuosos. En caso de que llegsemos a recibir un billete de cuya autenticidad dudemos, no hay que circularlo, hay que llevarlo a cualquier sucursal bancaria para solicitar que sea enviado a Banco de Mxico para su anlisis. En el Banco de Mxico determinaremos si es autntico o falso, le daremos una respuesta al usuario y compartiremos la informacin con la Procuradura General de la Repblica y con la Polica Federal para apoyar las labores de persecucin del delito. Esta cultura de legalidad tambin implica que cualquier ciudadano denuncie ante la Polica Federal a quien sospeche que est cometiendo el delito de falsificacin. Termino reiterando nuestro profundo agradecimiento al Secretario Osorio Chong y a todos sus colaboradores en la Comisin Nacional 7 de Seguridad y en la Polica Federal, al igual que reconocemos y valoramos los esfuerzos y la labor que han desplegado en esta materia especfica, no obstante el cmulo de otras importantes tareas que llevan a cabo de manera permanente para brindar seguridad a todos los mexicanos. Muchas gracias. 8

Title: Monetary policy and economic outlook
text: Monetary Policy and Economic Outlook Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, at the College of Economists of Nuevo Leon, Monterrey, N.L., on June 3, 2011 I am very grateful to the College of Economists of Nuevo Leon for the invitation to participate in its monthly meeting. It is a great pleasure to return to my hometown where I did my studies and worked as an economist in the early years of my professional career. But it is especially an honor to be able to address, once again, the professional friends and colleagues of this state to talk about the monetary policy and the economic outlook of our country. On monetary policy, I would like to share with you the following message. The benefits of price stability have been so clear that, in recent years, the world and our country have moved towards low inflations. In this transition, it has been confirmed that there is no real dilemma between inflation and economic growth and that it is counterproductive to subordinate the objective of price stability to ephemeral alternative targets. That is why our country must continue its efforts to consolidate price stability. In the last part, I will analyze, succinctly, the economic prospects of Mexico. Benefits of low inflation In any nation, inflation is an evil that generates inefficiencies and inequality with severe damage to well-being. Even when perfectly anticipated, inflation causes society to waste time and other resources to adapt to it. However, as we know, inflation 1 it can hardly be predicted exactly. When it is not forecast or detected with opportunity, entrepreneurs can make the wrong production and investment decisions. In addition, unexpected inflation generates unagreed income redistributions in transactions, which depend on errors or differences in bargaining power of the parties involved. In any case, the most dramatic effect of inflation falls on the poorest people, who keep most of their savings monetarily and can scarcely protect themselves against this evil. The empirical evidence on the harms of inflation is ample. Perhaps the clearest proof is the repeated negative association observed between economic growth and inflation, using national and international data and different periods. Many statistical studies have confirmed that the inverse relationship described goes beyond a simple correlation, confirming an adverse effect of inflation on per capita income growth, once other factors that may contribute to economic development are taken into account.1 The widespread recognition that more inflation produces only harm to society has led most countries to pursue monetary policies consistent with price stability. In this way, the average annual growth of prices in the world fell from just under eleven percent in the seventies of the last century, to less than four percent in the first decade of this century. By the way, it should be noted that this progress has not been uniform among nations. For example, in the period in question, the average annual inflation of advanced economies fell from almost nine to about two percent. In contrast, in emerging economies, although the fall in inflation was notable for having started from an average rate almost double that of developed countries, and having worsened along the way, the data 1 Vease, por ejemplo, Barro, R. J. (1997), Determinants of Economic Growth: A Cross Country Empirical Study, Cambridge, The MIT Press; y, Guerrero, F. (2006), "Does Inflation Cause Poor Long-Term Growth Performance?," Japan and the World Economy 18: 72-89. 2 It is still more than triple the benchmark for advanced countries, or nearly seven percent.2 The decline in inflation in developing regions remains a major challenge. Mexico has gained considerable ground in combating this evil that has so affected its economic performance in the past. As in other emerging economies, the most profound and lasting improvement has been recorded in this century. This effort has generated tangible benefits for the Mexican economy. For example, lower inflation has allowed for a significant drop in interest rates and greater financial development, by reducing uncertainty about the real return on investments, which has made it possible for the Federal Government and companies to finance themselves at fixed nominal rates at increasingly longer terms. Additionally, although greater banking penetration in the economy is still required, credit granted by financial institutions to the private sector has expanded and long-term mortgage credit and fixed nominal rates have flourished. There is no dilemma between inflation and economic growth The increase in world inflation in the seventies was due, to a large extent, to a misconception of the time, that there was a dilemma between economic growth and inflation. As you know, this view was based on an apparent inverse statistical relationship between inflation and the unemployment rate, known as the Phillips Curve after the name of the professional who first identified it, which led to economic policy recommendations aimed at accepting a little more inflation in exchange for less unemployment.3 2 See International Monetary Fund, International Financial Statistics, Washington, D.C. 3 The pioneering statistical work was based on the relationship between unemployment and changes in nominal wages. See Phillips, A. W. (1958), "The Relationship Between Unemployment and the Rate of Change of Money Wage Rates in the United Kingdom, 1861-1957," Economica 25 (100): 283-299. 3 The high rates of inflation, combined with the episodes of recession in the seventies of the last century, blurred this relationship and called into question the supposed dilemma. From then on, most economists abandoned the wrong paradigm and recognized that there is no real trade-off between inflation and economic growth. As Friedman and Phelps had predicted years ago, the alleged tension between these variables was unfounded. In summary, these authors recognized that at any time there is a "natural rate of unemployment" that is due to non-monetary factors. If the central bank tries to reduce unemployment below that rate and the public knows it, the result is more inflation. If, on the other hand, there are imperfections of information, a temporary reduction in unemployment can be achieved, which disappears when inflation resurfaces. The problem is that this opportunity to reduce unemployment cannot be used systematically since economic agents will anticipate the increase in inflation, which eliminates the effect of surprise and generates an inflationary bias.4 This highlights the role of monetary policy, which it can and cannot do. Monetary policy cannot be used to arbitrarily boost economic growth. If you try, it only produces inflation. That is, the relevant Phillips curve is vertical. What monetary policy can do is focus on creating an environment of price stability. This protects the purchasing power of household income and savings and allows the efficiency of the economy and the proper use of productive opportunities. In preserving price stability, monetary policy must certainly take into account the phase of the cycle in which the economy finds itself. Thus, interest rate movements, which are the primary tool of central banks to preserve price stability, must 4 Vease Friedman, M. (1968), "The Role of Monetary Policy," The American Economic Review 58 (1): 1-17; y Phelps, E.S. (1968), "Money-Wage Dynamics and Labor-Market Equilibrium," The Journal of Political Economy 76 (4): 678-711. 4 interpreted as adjustments towards new levels of equilibrium consistent with the economic situation. For example, in the face of an adverse shock to productivity, the equilibrium interest rate is likely to fall as the marginal productivity of capital has declined. However, this monetary policy action should not, in my view, be interpreted as a stimulus that calls into question the commitment to stability. However, I would like to comment on two recurring themes in the public debate on the role of monetary policy. The first is the common warning not to pursue the stability objective because of the cost that could be incurred during the transition from high to low inflation. To be sure, this cost could appear to the extent that stabilization lacks credibility and society does not have enough time to prepare for lower inflation. At the outset, it should be noted that, even if recorded, such slaughter would be transitory and certainly less than the lasting benefits of stability. Either way, in Mexico there is no evidence of a social cost related to recent stabilization, as the approach has been gradual and has been accompanied by reductions in expected inflation. A second issue has to do with the recommendation to relax monetary policy in order to encourage a depreciation of the currency against the dollar and thus promote exports. However, it should be noted that for exports the relevant price is the real exchange rate which, in equilibrium, is determined by real fundamental factors such as movements in the "terms of trade", productivity and profitability of investments.5 If, for example, the terms of trade improve due to increases in the relative prices of several of the exportable products, it is natural that the currency tends to appreciate. A monetary policy that sought to combat appreciation could risk a commitment to price stability, as well as depress real wages with an adverse impact on domestic spending in the economy. 5 Terms of trade are defined as the price of an average exportable good in terms of an average importable good. 5 Monetary policy and recent inflation in Mexico Since 2000, the Bank of Mexico has followed a formal inflation targeting strategy, in which monetary policy is guided by explicitly announced inflation targets. The Central Bank's commitment to achieving these objectives serves as an "anchor" for price formation and inflation expectations in the economy. As you know, since the end of 2003 the permanent inflation target has been three per cent per annum. This target is accompanied by a range of variability of plus minus one percent, which does not represent an objective or a range of indifference but the limited possibility of inflation variations around the target due to changes in highly volatile prices. The process of disinflation based on the inflation targeting strategy has been remarkable. Average annual inflation fell from more than 16% in 1999 to just over 4% since the end of 2003. The convergence of inflation towards the permanent target of three per cent represents a completely achievable task. The Governing Board has reiterated its commitment to ensure that this process is completed. Recent developments in annual price growth go in that direction. After a considerable rise in annual inflation in 2008, driven, among other factors, by extraordinary increases in commodity prices and the depreciation of the peso against the dollar in the context of the global crisis, price growth has been declining since 2009. Recent developments have been helped by the shift from a positive "output gap" during 2007 and 2008 to a negative one since 2009, currency appreciation, as well as a less adverse behavior in the non-core price index.6 6 Generally speaking, the output gap is defined as the difference between the observed output and the potential output of the economy. For a technical description, see Banco de Mexico, April-June 2009 Inflation Report, page 74. 6 In this context, monetary policy has sought to be preventive taking into account the foreseeable evolution of inflation and the nature of the shocks that affect it. Hence, after increasing the target interest rate by 75 basis points in the middle of the previous year to cope with unusual price pressures, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico has adjusted this variable downwards by 375 points during 2009. In the first five months of 2011, annual headline inflation has continued to decline. Repeated falls in the agricultural price component have contributed to this, especially in May. However, some of the factors that have favored the recent drop in inflation to rates close to three percent may not be repeated in the future. Therefore, the Governing Board has reiterated in its monetary policy statements that it will remain attentive to the different risk factors that could warn about generalized pressures on prices to, if they materialize, adjust the monetary stance in a timely manner to achieve the convergence of inflation towards the permanent objective of three percent. Economic Outlook As a result of the gradual correction of the imbalances that triggered the financial debacle, since mid-2009 the world economy has been on a trend towards recovery. This development has been more vigorous in emerging economies than in advanced ones. Thus, while the industrial production of the first group exceeded pre-crisis levels towards the end of 2009, that of the second group is still below its corresponding reference in 2011. It should be noted that the U.S. economy is in the eighth consecutive quarter of expansion. Since mid-2009, this country has recorded an average annualized quarterly growth of almost three percent. Such dynamism has been underpinned by consumption and investment. 7 private, suggesting a certain degree of self-sustainability. However, the housing sector, whose price adjustment seems far from over, as well as employment, remain lagging behind. Moreover, recently different indicators have pointed towards a certain moderation in the growth of the world economy. One of them is the economic dynamism of the United States in the first quarter, lower than expected. Another is the deterioration of financial problems in some economies of the European Monetary Union. A third factor concerns the impact related to the natural disasters that occurred last March in Japan. Perhaps the biggest challenge in the medium term is the implications for economic growth of the abandonment of the extraordinary monetary and fiscal stimuli that advanced economies will sooner or later have to carry out. Therefore, the consensus of analysts has moderately adjusted downwards the global economic outlook and those of the United States. Despite this, it should be noted that a prospect of recovery remains. In particular, for the United States, the consensus of analysts expects GDP to expand 2.7 and 3.2 percent and industrial production 5.0 and 4.2 percent, during 2011 and 2012, respectively.7 In line with the global economic recovery, Mexico's economy has maintained an improving trend since the second half of 2009. Thus, after having fallen 6.1 percent in 2009, GDP increased 5.5 percent in 2010. The initial impetus came from external demand for Mexican manufacturing products, as U.S. industrial production revived, with which they are closely related. Subsequently, consumption and, to a lesser extent, private investment have recovered. During the first quarter, Mexico's GDP grew 4.7 percent, faster than that observed in the first and last quarters of 2010. A similar comment can be made regarding the dynamism of both the industrial sector and 7 Bluechip Economic Indicators 36(5), 10 mayo 2011. 8 that of services. Seasonally adjusted monthly IGAE data reveal that production registered a slight contraction in March, which included a fall in tertiary activities. These data, however, are not enough to identify a trend of slowdown in the Mexican economy. In any case, a certain moderation of the economic dynamism of our country cannot be excluded as a result of adverse effects from abroad, such as the manufacturing contraction in Japan with a possible impact on supplies to companies in Mexico. The Mexican economy is expected to continue its growth trajectory during this and next year, supported by the increased US industrial production, the revival of bank credit as well as the strengthening of employment and real wages in the country. Thus, the Bank of Mexico forecasts that GDP growth will be between 4 and 5 percent during 2011 and between 3.8 and 4.8 percent in 2012. The risks of this forecast largely coincide with those described for the world stage. Conclusion The reduction in global inflation in recent decades reflects a change of vision and the absence of dilemmas between this evil and economic growth. Central banks have found that their greatest contribution to social welfare is to contribute to price stability. During the present century, Mexico has made significant progress in the process of convergence towards the permanent inflation target of three percent. This goal is perfectly achievable as evidenced by Mexico's own experience and that of many other countries. Finally, although they have moderated recently, the prospects for economic growth remain positive for the world and for our country. 9
text_original: Poltica Monetaria y Perspectivas Econmicas Palabras del Dr. Manuel Snchez Gonzlez, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, en el Colegio de Economistas de Nuevo Len, Monterrey, N.L., el 3 de junio de 2011 Agradezco mucho al Colegio de Economistas de Nuevo Len la invitacin para participar en su reunin mensual. Es un enorme gusto regresar a mi ciudad natal en donde realic mis estudios y me desempe como economista en los primeros aos de mi carrera profesional. Pero, en especial, es un honor poder dirigirme, una vez ms, a los amigos y colegas profesionistas de este estado para hablar sobre la poltica monetaria y el panorama econmico de nuestro pas. En materia de poltica monetaria me gustara compartir con ustedes el siguiente mensaje. Los beneficios de la estabilidad de precios han sido tan claros que, en aos recientes, el mundo y nuestro pas se han movido hacia inflaciones bajas. En esta transicin, se ha confirmado que no existe un dilema real entre inflacin y crecimiento econmico y que es contraproducente subordinar el objetivo de estabilidad de precios a metas alternativas efmeras. De ah que nuestro pas deba continuar con sus esfuerzos por consolidar la estabilidad de los precios. En la ltima parte, analizar, de forma sucinta, las perspectivas econmicas de Mxico. Beneficios de una inflacin baja En cualquier nacin, la inflacin es un mal que genera ineficiencias e inequidad con severos daos sobre el bienestar. An cuando se anticipe perfectamente, la inflacin propicia que la sociedad desperdicie tiempo y otros recursos para adaptarse a ella. Sin embargo, como sabemos, la inflacin 1 difcilmente puede predecirse con exactitud. Cuando no se pronostica ni se detecta con oportunidad, los empresarios pueden tomar decisiones de produccin e inversin equivocadas. Adems, la inflacin inesperada genera redistribuciones de ingreso no pactadas en las transacciones, que dependen de los errores o de las diferencias de poder de negociacin de las partes involucradas. En todo caso, el efecto ms dramtico de la inflacin recae sobre la gente ms pobre, la cual mantiene la mayor parte de sus ahorros de forma monetaria y escasamente puede protegerse contra este mal. La evidencia emprica sobre los daos de la inflacin es amplia. Tal vez la prueba ms clara sea la repetida asociacin negativa que se observa entre el crecimiento econmico y la inflacin, usando datos nacionales e internacionales y diferentes perodos. Muchos estudios estadsticos han confirmado que la relacin inversa descrita va ms all de una simple correlacin, al confirmar un efecto adverso de la inflacin sobre el crecimiento del ingreso por habitante, una vez que se toman en cuenta otros factores que pueden contribuir al desarrollo econmico.1 El reconocimiento generalizado de que ms inflacin produce slo perjuicios para la sociedad ha llevado a la mayora de los pases a aplicar polticas monetarias congruentes con la estabilidad de precios. De esta manera, el crecimiento promedio anual de los precios en el mundo se redujo de poco menos de once por ciento en los aos setenta del siglo pasado, a menos de cuatro por ciento en la primera dcada del presente siglo. Por cierto, debe sealarse que este avance no ha sido uniforme entre naciones. Por ejemplo, en el lapso referido, la inflacin promedio anual de las economas avanzadas descendi de casi nueve a aproximadamente dos por ciento. En contraste, en las economas emergentes, si bien la cada de la inflacin fue notable por haber partido de una tasa promedio casi del doble de la de los pases desarrollados, y haberse agravado en el camino, el dato 1 Vase, por ejemplo, Barro, R. J. (1997), Determinants of Economic Growth: A Cross Country Empirical Study, Cambridge, The MIT Press; y, Guerrero, F. (2006), Does Inflation Cause Poor LongTerm Growth Performance?, Japan and the World Economy 18: 7289. 2 reciente se ubica todava en ms del triple de la referencia de los avanzados, es decir, casi siete por ciento.2 El abatimiento de la inflacin en las regiones en desarrollo contina siendo un importante desafo. Mxico ha ganado considerable terreno en el combate de este mal que tanto afect su desempeo econmico en el pasado. Como en otras economas emergentes, el mejoramiento ms profundo y duradero se ha registrado en este siglo. Este esfuerzo ha generado beneficios tangibles para la economa mexicana. Por ejemplo, la menor inflacin ha permitido una baja significativa de las tasas de inters y un mayor desarrollo financiero, al reducir la incertidumbre sobre el rendimiento real de las inversiones, lo que ha posibilitado que el Gobierno Federal y las empresas se financien a tasas nominales fijas a plazos cada vez ms largos. Adicionalmente, aunque an se requiere una mayor penetracin bancaria en la economa, se ha expandido el crdito otorgado por las instituciones financieras al sector privado y ha florecido el crdito hipotecario a plazos largos y tasas nominales fijas.
