Title: The exchange rate and the Mexican economy
text: The exchange rate and the Mexican economy * Agustin Carstens, Governor of the Bank of Mexico Given the depreciation of the Mexican peso against the US dollar, multiple questions have arisen among the public: Why has the peso depreciated?, how is it possible that Mexico today has the lowest inflation in the last 40 years, at the same time that its currency depreciates?, what are the country's financial authorities doing in the face of this? The main causes of this depreciation are external to Mexico. It is a global phenomenon consisting of a remarkable strengthening of the dollar against practically all currencies, both advanced and emerging countries. It is a phenomenon accompanied by other important elements, which interact with each other and which are: A sharp fall in international prices of most basic goods and raw materials, such as oil and many more; the weakening of the economy in emerging countries, and a recovery in economic activity in the United States that makes higher interest rates imminent in that country. Therefore, there is a global phenomenon of appreciation of the US dollar; it is not something that only affects Mexico, and in fact our country is not among the group of countries most affected by this phenomenon. Sample of the latter is represented by the Mexican peso, in the last twelve 1 months, it has depreciated against a basket of currencies weighted by the issuing country's share of our international trade, only half of what it has against the US dollar. The "boom" in the prices of basic goods and raw materials has ended. This implies that there are prices, such as oil, that will take many years to recover. In this sense, a part of the depreciation of the peso reflects this new paradigm, among other factors, given the importance of oil revenues in public finances in Mexico. Indeed, this enduring environment of low oil prices represents a structural weakness of our fiscal framework, so we must confront it with a determined strengthening of public finances. The high historical correlation between inflation and exchange rate depreciation was broken more than a decade ago thanks to the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico, which means the existence of an entity within the State with the priority mandate to maintain low and stable inflation. The latter has been achieved, judging by the fact that today we enjoy the lowest inflation in four decades. Hence, inflation expectations in the future have remained low and well anchored. In addition, this has allowed interest rates to also be at historically low levels and that real wages have been growing fundamentally at the same rate as productivity, which has resulted in the costs of 2 companies due to these factors have not been affected by depreciation. There have also been significant reductions in domestic prices for inputs that are transversal to the economy, such as the prices of some fuels, electricity and telecommunications (partly reflected in structural reforms), along with the fall in the prices of basic commodities, which are also inputs, such as those of metals and grains. All of the above, in a context of weak aggregate demand, has offset some higher costs in imported inputs caused by the depreciation of the domestic currency. Thus, in the light of the above factors, it should not be surprising that exchange rate depreciation has so far had a limited impact on the inflation rate. The financial authorities have responded actively, consistent with the flexible exchange rate regime in place in Mexico. The measures taken by the Foreign Exchange Commission have been effective so that movements in the exchange market take place in an orderly manner, avoiding an artificial shortage of foreign exchange. At the Bank of Mexico, we are vigilant to prevent turbulence in the foreign exchange market from leading to a rise in inflation expectations, and we will not hesitate to act by increasing the benchmark interest rate to stem any inflationary pressure. Mexicans are facing a new world economic scenario that is undoubtedly challenging. Successful countries 3 they will be the ones who manage to offer financial stability with sustained economic growth. It is up to us to achieve that virtuous combination. ? (Article originally published in the newspaper "Reforma" on Sunday, August 16, 2015) 4
text_original: El tipo de cambio y la economa mexicana * Agustn Carstens, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico Ante la depreciacin del peso mexicano frente al dlar estadounidense, han surgido entre el pblico mltiples preguntas: Por qu se ha depreciado el peso?, cmo es posible que Mxico tenga hoy la inflacin ms baja en los ltimos 40 aos, al mismo tiempo que su moneda se deprecia?, qu estn haciendo las autoridades financieras del pas ante esto? Las principales causas de esta depreciacin son externas a Mxico. Se trata de un fenmeno mundial consistente en un fortalecimiento notable del dlar frente a prcticamente todas las divisas, tanto de pases avanzados como emergentes. Es un fenmeno acompaado de otros elementos importantes, que interactan entre s y que son: Una fuerte cada de los precios internacionales de la mayora de los bienes bsicos y materias primas, como el petrleo y muchos ms; el debilitamiento de la economa en pases emergentes, y una recuperacin de la actividad econmica en los Estados Unidos que hace inminente mayores tasas de inters en ese pas. Por tanto, hay un fenmeno global de apreciacin del dlar estadounidense; no es algo que slo afecte a Mxico, y de hecho nuestro pas no est entre el grupo de pases ms golpeados por este fenmeno. Muestra de esto ltimo lo representa el que el peso mexicano, en los ltimos doce 1 meses, se ha depreciado contra una canasta de divisas ponderadas por la participacin del pas emisor en nuestro comercio internacional, slo la mitad de lo que lo ha hecho contra el dlar estadounidense. Ha concluido el boom de los precios de los bienes bsicos y de las materias primas. Ello implica que hay precios, como el del petrleo, que tardarn muchos aos en recuperarse. En este sentido, una parte de la depreciacin del peso refleja este nuevo paradigma, entre otros factores, dada la importancia que tienen los ingresos petroleros en las finanzas pblicas en Mxico. De hecho, este entorno perdurable de bajos precios del petrleo representa una debilidad estructural de nuestro marco fiscal, por lo que debemos enfrentarlo con un decidido fortalecimiento de las finanzas pblicas. La alta correlacin histrica entre la inflacin y la depreciacin cambiaria se rompi hace ms de una dcada gracias a la autonoma del Banco de Mxico, la cual significa la existencia de una entidad dentro del Estado con el mandato prioritario de mantener una inflacin baja y estable. Esto ltimo se ha logrado, a juzgar por el hecho de que al da de hoy gozamos de la inflacin ms baja en cuatro dcadas. De ah que las expectativas de inflacin en el futuro se han mantenido bajas y bien ancladas. Adems, lo anterior ha permitido que las tasas de inters tambin se encuentren a niveles histricamente bajos y que los salarios reales vengan creciendo fundamentalmente al mismo ritmo que la productividad, lo que ha redundado en que los costos de las 2 empresas por estos factores no se hayan vistos afectados por la depreciacin. Tambin se han registrado reducciones significativas en los precios internos de insumos que son transversales a la economa, como los precios de algunos combustibles, electricidad y telecomunicaciones (reflejo en parte de las reformas estructurales), junto con la cada de los precios de mercancas bsicas, que tambin son insumos, como los de los metales y granos. Todo lo anterior, en un contexto de una demanda agregada dbil, ha contrarrestado algunos costos mayores en insumos importados causados por la depreciacin de la moneda nacional. As pues, a la luz de los factores mencionados, no debera ser sorprendente que la depreciacin cambiaria haya tenido hasta la fecha un impacto limitado sobre la tasa de inflacin. Las autoridades financieras hemos respondido de forma activa, en congruencia con el rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible vigente en Mxico. Las medidas tomadas por la Comisin de Cambios han sido efectivas para que los movimientos en el mercado cambiario se den de manera ordenada, evitando una escasez artificial de divisas. En el Banco de Mxico estamos vigilantes para evitar que las turbulencias en el mercado de divisas propicien un alza en las expectativas de inflacin, y no dudaremos en actuar mediante aumentos de la tasa de inters de referencia para atajar cualquier presin inflacionaria. Los mexicanos estamos ante un nuevo escenario econmico mundial que es sin duda desafiante. Los pases exitosos 3 sern los que consigan ofrecer estabilidad financiera con crecimiento econmico sostenido. De nosotros depende conseguir esa combinacin virtuosa.  (Artculo publicado originalmente en el diario Reforma el domingo 16 de agosto de 2015) 4

Title: Economic and financial education: implications for the economy and the role of the central bank
text: "ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL EDUCATION: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE ECONOMY AND THE ROLE OF THE CENTRAL BANK". INTERVENTION OF MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, AT THE BENITO JUaREZ AUTONOMOUS UNIVERSITY OF OAXACA. Oaxaca, March 16, 2018.1 I am very honored to participate in this inaugural event of the "We Are UABJO" campaign. This prestigious school has played since its creation in the early nineteenth century as an Institute of Sciences and Arts, a fundamental role, not only in the education of the state population, but in practically all areas of Oaxacan life. As a graduate of the Preparatory School of this University, I am very pleased to be able to contribute to this important effort to reaffirm the ties with society and return to this one something of the much that has contributed to us. My sincere thanks to the Rector, Dr. Eduardo Bautista Martinez, for the invitation to accompany you as a lecturer on this special occasion. I would like to take this opportunity to concentrate my presentation on a topic in which the functions of the UABJO and the Bank of Mexico overlap, that is, education, and in particular that oriented to the economic and financial areas. The study of economic growth and development is one of the topics that have most captured the attention of academics and public officials for several centuries. Although the analysis of its determinants is constantly evolving, it is clear that education plays a summative role. 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board as a whole. 1 importance in this regard, by affecting the productive capacity of an economy through a wide variety of channels. On the one hand, the greater human capital of a more prepared workforce allows it to increase its productivity and, therefore, the income levels associated with the labor factor. On the other hand, innovation and technological change, in turn determining factors of the growth potential of an economy, are stimulated in the presence of adequate educational levels. In the first instance, this occurs through the establishment of the necessary conditions for the adoption of technologies already existing elsewhere. At the same time, at a stage of greater scope, education promotes the generation of knowledge, ideas and creativity indispensable for innovation and the expansion of the technological frontier within an economy. Clearly, the amount of resources allocated to education represents a key aspect for the formation of a society's human capital. However, experience shows that a strategy based on an approach that privileges the expansion of access to and quantity of education is limited in scope. Indeed, the benefits of greater education on economic growth and development are given through the ability to translate the investment made in it, in the transmission of knowledge and skills to students, which provide them with the necessary tools to perform successfully in a changing and increasingly competitive economic and work environment. These results are derived more directly from the quality of the education provided. In other words, 2 when considering the impact of education on the performance of an economy, quality is even more relevant than quantity. Indeed, multiple empirical analyses at the international level suggest that, while there is a close relationship between various measures associated with the quantity of education (e.g., levels of schooling and student enrollment) and economic performance,2 this relationship tends to weaken once other variables that reflect the quality of education are taken into account. the latter acquiring a substantially greater relative importance.3 If we add to the above the effect of improvements in educational quality on the incentives for families and individuals to remain in the classroom, it is evident that due attention to this dimension of education is fundamental for the materialization of its transformative potential on our societies. In view of the beneficial effect of improvements in the quantity and, particularly, in the quality of education on the performance of an economy and the well-being of its population, the lag in this regard in emerging and developing countries is worrying. Despite important differences between the different regions of the world, the generally low levels of schooling registered in these countries stand out, largely explained by the high rates of student dropout and even by the high percentage of 2 Ver, por ejemplo, Temple, Jonathan (2001): "Growth Effects of Education and Social Capital in the OECD Countries", OECD Economic Studies 33:57-101; Krueger, Alan B. y Mikael Lindahl (2001): "Education for Growth: Why and for Whom?", Journal of Economic Literature 39(4):1101-1136; y Sianesi, Barbara y John van Reenen (2003): "The Returns to Education: Macroeconomics", Journal of Economic Surveys 17(2):157-200. 3 Ver, por ejemplo, Hanushek, Eric A. y Dennis D. Kimko (2000): "Schooling, Labor Force Quality, and the Growth of Nations", American Economic Review 90(5):1184-1208; Barro, Robert J. (2001): "Human Capital and Growth", American Economic Review 91(2):12-17; y Hanushek, Eric A. y Ludger Wobmann (2007): "The Role of Education Quality in Economic Growth", World Bank Policy Research Working Paper No. 4122. 3 people who never started a formal education. Likewise, and in turn magnifying the challenges, the results obtained in various tests of international application reveal a high concentration in these countries of students with low academic performance, registering in most cases scores lower than those that would correspond to knowledge and cognitive skills of levels that are considered basic. Unfortunately, the case of Mexico is far from the exception. Although the coverage rates for basic education (i.e. primary and secondary) point to a situation close to universality in our country, the results obtained by our students in international tests are less encouraging. For example, the most recent PISA test applied by the OECD in 2015 to 15-year-old students in about 70 countries reveals that Mexico is well below the international average in science, mathematics and reading. Likewise, there is a generalization of poor results among our students, since about half showed a performance that is considered deficient in these same subject areas (56.6 percent in mathematics, 47.8 percent in science and 41.7 percent in reading), while less than one percent reached levels of excellence. Additionally, this deficit of knowledge and cognitive skills can contribute to explain the dramatic falls in school enrolment rates in upper secondary education (54 percent) and higher education (16 percent), both metrics in which Mexico ranks last among OECD member countries (which, on average, register figures of 84 percent and 36 percent, respectively). 4 This highlights the importance of correcting flaws in our educational system that may be preventing or, at least, hindering the transformation of the resources allocated to this activity, into knowledge and skills of economic and social value for our young people. Given the nature of the areas of responsibility of the Bank of Mexico, for this Central Institute it is of particular relevance that the population of our country has an adequate understanding of economic and financial issues. In fact, the importance of education in these areas has been positioned increasingly prominently on the policy agenda on a global scale in recent years, currently positioning itself as a topic of active discussion and debate in forums aimed at international consultation and cooperation, such as the so-called Group of 20 (G20), that brings together the main economies of the world and of which Mexico is a member. Naturally, the above rests on the multiplicity of benefits, closely related to each other, that a more widespread and in-depth economic and financial education represents for all parties involved, including individuals and households in their role as consumers of financial products and services; private financial intermediaries who, through greater participation and inclusion of the population in these activities, may see increases both in demand for the products and services they offer and in the availability of resources to be channeled for financing from other sectors; and central banks, both in achieving their price stability objectives and 5 financial, as in the performance of their duties as supervisors and regulators of activities in these markets. Undoubtedly, the allocation of resources of individuals and households to consumption, savings and investment will be more efficient and, therefore, will bring them greater well-being, to the extent that they have more and better tools to understand the different financial instruments to which they have access, and can thus select from among them the most convenient for such purposes. This is particularly true in a context in which, in the face of the increasing sophistication of financial markets, the options for borrowing and savings for society have multiplied, increasing both opportunities and risks. Also, with the increase in life expectancy and the pressures on public finances observed in many countries, it is expected that families will have to assume greater responsibility in the management of their finances in the coming years. At perhaps a more basic level, a better understanding of economic and financial concepts allows households to protect themselves from abusive and potentially fraudulent practices employed by some intermediaries, particularly in the informal financial sector, which still maintains a relatively large presence in many emerging and developing economies. On the other hand, and in a clear feedback loop, the greater sense of empowerment of families about their own economic and financial situation, works as a strong motivation to seek the deepening of their understanding and competence in the matter. 6 From the perspective of a central bank, a better level of economic and financial knowledge among the population brings important benefits that facilitate the fulfillment of its functions. First, it highlights the possibility of monetary policy operating more efficiently towards the achievement of price stability, since the communication of these central institutes regarding their actions, strategies and objectives has a greater impact when it is addressed to an audience capable of understanding the messages that are sought to be transmitted, increasing the effectiveness of transparency and accountability efforts. Likewise, the objective of financial stability is favored in the presence of participants who are better informed and better able to make decisions that reduce the risk of imbalances and vulnerabilities in the financial system, while through greater knowledge and demand they promote discipline and competition in these markets. Finally, a better public empowered to understand the interactions between the different tools of economic and strictly monetary policy increases the likelihood of greater congruence between them and this.4 Despite these and other important benefits that both individually and collectively represent having an adequate level of economic and financial education, the situation in Mexico and in many other countries presents important lags. Indeed, a recent OECD study5 on financial capacities shows, on the basis of information gathered, 4 Ver Gnan, Ernest, Maria Antoinette Silgoner y Beat Weber (2007): "Economic and Financial Education: Concepts, Goals and Measurement", Monetary Policy & the Economy, Oesterreichische Nationalbank (Austrian Central Bank), No. 3:28-49. 5 Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (2017): "G20/OECD INFE Report on Adult Financial Literacy in G20 countries". 7 through surveys of adults between 18 and 79 years of age in 21 countries, the average score of respondents reaches only 60.5 percent of the maximum score, while the corresponding figure for Mexico is even lower (57.6 percent). In addition to the poor performance in terms of financial knowledge, a series of attitudes and behaviors are observed that could be considered in frank conflict with a healthy and responsible financial management. For example, despite the recognized importance of having a monetary budget, only 60 percent of households in the countries considered make use of this tool, while more than 70 percent of the individuals surveyed report agreeing with the statement "money is to be spent", in clear disdain for savings and long-term financial planning. In fact, only about half of the respondents reported following attitudes and behaviors at least comparable to the minimum desired level. While a higher level of economic and financial knowledge would be expected to go hand in hand with attitudes and behaviours that are reflected in better decisions at the individual level, results such as the above highlight the importance of a holistic approach in the design and implementation of national education strategies in these areas, that considers not only the technical aspects of managing finances 8 but also the multiple psychological, cultural, and social factors that can play a role in making these important decisions.6 Obviously, trying to determine a single model of economic and financial education whose application works properly in all cases is an unattainable goal. However, in the light of the available evidence, it is appropriate to concentrate efforts on identifying a series of principles of a general nature and flexible application, which can be adapted to the needs, context and idiosyncrasies of each society. These include: 1. The importance of these strategies seeking to reach the target population at a timely stage of their training, including from childhood, and that they take into account that it is not possible to rest on actions that simultaneously cover all segments of the population, since the skills required vary according to the needs of consumers throughout their lives. 2. Such training should be accompanied by actions promoting free and transparent access to, as well as the efficient use of, relevant information on the increasingly complex and sophisticated financial products, instruments and services available to the public. Achieving this goal could be aided by more intensive use and 6 Examples of the above include: the perception that consumption expenditure on some goods or services is a sign of "status"; the impact of the behavior of other members of the group to which an individual belongs on one's own; financial decision-making motivated by pressure from agents with interests opposed to that of the individual; and herd behaviors or fear of missing investment opportunities in highly risky assets or instruments with price dynamics far from their fundamentals, among others. 9 widespread digital platforms and media, which have the potential to reach broad sectors of the population at a low cost. 3. It is essential to carry out a frequent measurement of the results obtained by the different measures implemented, in order to have a guide that allows to make the necessary adjustments in a timely manner and identify new challenges as they emerge. 4. While it is necessary to recognize that a successful strategy of economic and financial education will require the participation and coordinated collaboration of multiple actors, including authorities in a variety of fields, from education and public finance to central banking, as well as private financial intermediaries, it is also important to have sufficient clarity as to the specific roles and functions that each will have to fulfill. 5. It should be borne in mind that economic and financial education is only one component of a set of actions that should be implemented to ensure that families benefit from the development of financial markets, including appropriate financial inclusion and consumer protection policies. Turning to the specific case of Mexico, the available information allows us to make a only partial diagnosis of the situation of our country in terms of economic and financial education, especially by virtue of the lack of statistical information for the segment of the population of children and young people. However, the picture is not encouraging. In addition to comparing unfavorably with the average of the G20 member countries in a variety of indicators that seek to measure knowledge, attitudes and 10 Mexico presents a significant lag in other areas. Thus, it highlights a notable lack of familiarity with our financial system and the products and services that can be found in it, including some of low cost or that have expressly regulated guarantees.7 Likewise, there is insufficient confidence in the institutions that make up the Mexican financial system, which could be having a negative effect on the rates of use of formal means for savings, particularly for retirement.8 Finally, it is worth mentioning the existence of financial decisions that are clearly wrong from a rational point of view, the motivation of which is difficult to understand.9 Against this background, the authorities have designed a National Financial Education Strategy focused on comprehensively addressing the challenges facing Mexico in this regard, although it still faces implementation challenges. This strategy contemplates a multidimensional action plan for the achievement of its objectives, but there are some key aspects that are important to highlight. First, the identification and exploitation of synergies between the different actors and the diverse 7 For example, according to the results of the 2015 National Financial Inclusion Survey (ENIF), less than half of respondents were aware of basic bank accounts that do not charge commissions, while only a quarter knew that bank deposits are insured. 8 Although there has been some progress in this regard in recent years, the statistics derived from the ENIF 2015 indicate that around 1.7 million workers do not make voluntary contributions to their individual retirement savings account, because they do not trust the Afores. 9 Examples of this include: the contracting of credits with a Total Annual Cost (CAT) higher than the alternatives; the transfer of retirement savings accounts to Afores with a lower yield; and the increased use of credit cards that charge higher interest rates, while prioritizing debt repayment on cards with lower rates. 11 existing mechanisms and structures.10 Secondly, the focus of the different public policy measures not only in terms of the relevant population, but also taking into account the moment, context or specific circumstances in which they may have the greatest impact.11 Third, the forecast of actions and mechanisms that allow timely monitoring and evaluation, both the situation at the time and the results obtained.12 The Bank of Mexico has been contributing for many years and through a variety of channels to the strengthening of economic and financial education in our country. In addition to its contributions to the National Financial Education Strategy in its role as a permanent member of both the Financial Education Committee and the Monitoring, Development and Research Group and the National Council for Financial Inclusion, our Central Institute carries out, on its own, a significant number of initiatives and actions aimed at this same purpose under a wide range of modalities. 10 Thus, it is proposed, for example, to incorporate instruction in the field into the national education system, to accompany actions to protect users of financial products and services with measures that promote a culture of responsible and informed consumption of them, and to make use of technological innovations, including those developed in the financial sector based on an intensive use of information and communication technologies (fintech), to magnify the scope of these efforts, without ruling out the collaboration of private initiative and non-governmental and international organizations. 11 In this regard, the Strategy proposes specific actions aimed at children and young people in stages of school training, adults of both working age and older, beneficiaries of social programmes, the rural population, workers who have emigrated outside the country, entrepreneurs and companies (especially smaller ones), as well as women. 12 In addition to internal measures in that direction, such as the formation of a Monitoring, Development and Research Group composed of representatives of the various entities involved, Mexico is proposed to participate more actively in similar international initiatives, such as the OECD PISA test specializing in financial education. 12 Among these, it is worth mentioning the various courses, seminars, workshops and other educational programs that the Bank of Mexico teaches to children, youth and adults, to students and teachers, to employees both their own and those of other public entities, and in general to all the interested public, either in person or through digital media, covering various topics on economics, finance and the Bank itself. Likewise, it seeks to awaken and promote interest and study at deeper levels of economic and financial issues among high school graduates and university students in the country, through contests and contests that have attracted the attention of about 50,000 participants since 2009. Complementing the above, the Bank of Mexico is in continuous search of means to strengthen its ties with Mexican society and thus enhance the scope of its educational work, making use of innovative didactic tools. In this regard, the most prominent example is the Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE, the first of its kind in the world), created in 2006 by the Bank in collaboration with private financial institutions in the country, with the aim of disseminating economic science and promoting financial education, with accessible and attractive content for visitors of all ages. Although the widespread dissemination of economic and financial skills and knowledge at a minimum level is of paramount importance for the development of the country, the Bank of Mexico has also been concerned with promoting the training of professionals in the field of the highest technical capacity. Thus, it is noteworthy the use of schemes for the financing of advanced studies in these and other disciplines, available both to employees of the Institution (through our General Scholarship Program) 13 and for people outside it (through the Human Resources Development Fund, or FIDERH, a federal trust that has been administered by the Bank of Mexico for more than 40 years). Beyond the above, the high number of cadres trained in the Bank who have held prominent positions in both the public and private sectors only confirms the commitment of our Central Institute to the training of high-level personnel in the country. In conclusion, I would just like to emphasize that, despite the efforts made over many years, our country continues to face considerable lags in education in general, and in the field of economic and financial education in particular. This situation is worrying, since education is a crucial element for self-improvement, for the reduction of poverty, for combating the unequal distribution of income and, in general, for economic development. I believe that the National Financial Education Strategy will be a very important step to address the challenges we face in this area. At the Bank of Mexico, we will continue to contribute enthusiastically to the success of this initiative, bearing in mind the need to address with all objectivity and open-mindedness the actions we need to implement to achieve the objectives sought. 14

Debe tenerse presente que la educacin econmica y financiera es solo un componente de un conjunto de acciones que deben implementarse para asegurar que las familias se beneficien del desarrollo de los mercados financieros, entre ellas polticas adecuadas de inclusin financiera y proteccin al consumidor. Pasando al caso especfico de Mxico, la informacin disponible permite hacer un diagnstico solo parcial de la situacin de nuestro pas en materia de educacin econmica y financiera, especialmente en virtud de la falta de informacin estadstica para el segmento de la poblacin de nios y jvenes. No obstante, el panorama es poco alentador. Adems de compararse desfavorablemente con el promedio de los pases miembros del G20 en una diversidad de indicadores que buscan medir conocimientos, actitudes y 10 comportamientos financieros de sus adultos, Mxico presenta un rezago importante en otras reas. As, destaca una notable falta de familiaridad con nuestro sistema financiero y los productos y servicios que en l se pueden encontrar, incluyendo algunos de bajo costo o que cuentan con garantas expresamente reguladas.7 Asimismo, existe una insuficiente confianza en las instituciones que conforman el sistema financiero mexicano, misma que podra estar teniendo un efecto negativo sobre las tasas de utilizacin de medios formales para el ahorro, particularmente para el retiro.8 Finalmente, cabe mencionar la existencia de decisiones financieras claramente errneas desde un punto de vista racional, cuya motivacin es difcil de entender.9 Ante este panorama, las autoridades han diseado una Estrategia Nacional de Educacin Financiera enfocada a atender, de manera integral, los retos que enfrenta Mxico a este respecto, aunque todava enfrenta retos de implementacin. Dicha estrategia contempla un plan de accin multidimensional para el logro de sus objetivos, pero hay algunos aspectos clave que es importante destacar. En primer lugar, la identificacin y aprovechamiento de sinergias entre los distintos actores y los diversos 7 Por ejemplo, de acuerdo con los resultados de la Encuesta Nacional de Inclusin Financiera (ENIF) 2015, menos de la mitad de los encuestados conoca la existencia de cuentas bancarias bsicas que no cobran comisiones, mientras que tan solo una cuarta parte saba que los depsitos bancarios cuentan con un seguro. 8 En efecto, si bien ha habido algunos avances a este respecto en aos recientes, la estadstica derivada de la ENIF 2015 indica que alrededor de 1.7 millones de trabajadores no realizan aportaciones voluntarias a su cuenta individual de ahorro para el retiro, porque no confan en las Afores. 9 Como ejemplos de esto, se encuentran: la contratacin de crditos con un Costo Anual Total (CAT) mayor que las alternativas; el traspaso de cuentas de ahorro para el retiro a Afores con un menor rendimiento; y el mayor uso de tarjetas de crdito que cobran tasas de inters ms altas, al tiempo que se le da prioridad al pago de deudas en tarjetas con tasas ms bajas. 11 mecanismos y estructuras ya existentes.10 En segundo lugar, la focalizacin de las distintas medidas de poltica pblica no solo en trminos de la poblacin relevante, sino tambin tomando en cuenta el momento, contexto o circunstancias especficos en los que estas pueden tener el mayor impacto.11 Tercero, la previsin de acciones y mecanismos que permitan llevar a cabo un monitoreo y evaluacin oportunos, tanto de la situacin en el momento como de los resultados obtenidos.12 El Banco de Mxico ha venido contribuyendo desde hace muchos aos y a travs de una diversidad de canales al fortalecimiento de la educacin econmica y financiera en nuestro pas. Adems de sus aportaciones a la Estrategia Nacional de Educacin Financiera en su rol como miembro permanente tanto del Comit de Educacin Financiera como del Grupo de Seguimiento, Desarrollo e Investigacin y del Consejo Nacional de Inclusin Financiera, nuestro Instituto Central lleva a cabo, por cuenta propia, un nmero importante de iniciativas y acciones orientadas a este mismo propsito bajo una amplia gama de modalidades. 10 As, se propone por ejemplo incorporar la instruccin en la materia en el sistema educativo nacional, acompaar las acciones de proteccin a los usuarios de productos y servicios financieros de medidas que promuevan una cultura de consumo responsable e informado de los mismos, y hacer uso de las innovaciones tecnolgicas, incluyendo las que se desarrollen en el sector financiero basado en un uso intensivo de tecnologas de la informacin y la comunicacin (fintech), para magnificar el alcance de estos esfuerzos, sin descartar la colaboracin de la iniciativa privada y los organismos no gubernamentales e internacionales. 11 En este sentido, la Estrategia plantea acciones concretas destinadas a nios y jvenes en etapas de formacin escolar, a adultos tanto en edad de trabajar como mayores, a beneficiarios de programas sociales, a la poblacin rural, a trabajadores que han emigrado al exterior del pas, a emprendedores y empresas (especialmente las de menor tamao), as como a las mujeres. 12 Adems de medidas de carcter interno en esta direccin, como la formacin de un Grupo de Seguimiento, Desarrollo e Investigacin compuesto por representantes de las distintas entidades involucradas, se propone una participacin ms activa de Mxico en iniciativas similares de corte internacional, tales como la prueba PISA de la OCDE especializada en educacin financiera. 12 Entre estas, cabe mencionar los varios cursos, seminarios, talleres y otros programas educativos que el Banco de Mxico imparte a nios, jvenes y adultos, a estudiantes y profesores, a empleados tanto propios como de otras entidades pblicas, y en general a todo el pblico interesado, de manera ya sea presencial o a travs de medios digitales, que cubren diversos temas sobre economa, finanzas y el propio Banco. Asimismo, se busca despertar y promover el inters y el estudio a niveles ms profundos de temas econmicos y financieros entre bachilleres y estudiantes universitarios del pas, mediante concursos y certmenes que han atrado la atencin de cerca de 50,000 participantes desde 2009. Complementando lo anterior, el Banco de Mxico est en continua bsqueda de medios para estrechar sus vnculos con la sociedad mexicana y potenciar as el alcance de su labor educativa, haciendo uso adems de herramientas didcticas innovadoras. A este respecto, el ejemplo ms destacado es el Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE, el primero en su tipo en el mundo), creado en 2006 por el Banco en colaboracin con instituciones financieras privadas del pas, con el objetivo de divulgar la ciencia econmica y promover la educacin financiera, con contenidos accesibles y atractivos para visitantes de todas las edades. Si bien la difusin generalizada de habilidades y conocimientos econmicos y financieros a un nivel al menos bsico es de suma importancia para el desarrollo del pas, el Banco de Mxico tambin se ha preocupado por impulsar la formacin de profesionales en la materia de la ms alta capacidad tcnica. As, es de destacar el uso de esquemas para el financiamiento de estudios avanzados en estas y otras disciplinas, disponibles tanto para empleados de la Institucin (a travs de nuestro Programa General de Becas) 13 como para personas externas a la misma (a travs del Fondo para el Desarrollo de Recursos Humanos, o FIDERH, un fideicomiso federal que ha sido administrado por el Banco de Mxico por ms de 40 aos). Ms all de lo anterior, el alto nmero de cuadros formados en el Banco que han ocupado posiciones prominentes tanto en el sector pblico como en el privado no hace sino constatar el compromiso de nuestro Instituto Central con la capacitacin de personal de alto nivel en el pas. Para terminar, solo quisiera enfatizar que, no obstante los esfuerzos realizados a lo largo de muchos aos, nuestro pas sigue enfrentando rezagos considerables en materia educativa en general, y en el mbito de la educacin econmica y financiera en particular. Esta situacin es preocupante, ya que la educacin es un elemento crucial para la superacin personal, para la disminucin de la pobreza, para combatir la distribucin desigual del ingreso y, en general, para el desarrollo econmico. Considero que la Estrategia Nacional de Educacin Financiera ser un paso de gran importancia para atender los retos que enfrentamos en esta materia. En el Banco de Mxico continuaremos contribuyendo con entusiasmo al xito de esta iniciativa, teniendo en mente la necesidad de abordar con toda objetividad y apertura de miras las acciones que necesitamos poner en marcha para lograr los objetivos buscados. 14

Title: Conference on central bank independence, mandates and policies, Faculty of Economics of Universidad de Chile: institutional mandates, policy tools and policy coordination
text: Remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of Banco de Mexico, at the Conference on Central Bank Independence, Mandates and Policies, Institutional mandates, policy tools and policy coordination, organized by the Faculty of Economics of Universidad de Chile.1 October 21, 2021 Central banks are unique institutions. They all share the responsibility of providing our countries with national currency. Money is an essential public good that needs to be an effective medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account. Societies have found that the best form of money is not that which provides intrinsic value, but that which, although immaterial fiat Money, given the rules and strategies followed by its issuer, ensures the issuers commitment to pursue societies long-term goals. The mandate, goals and objectives defined by society for central banks determine the strategies and terms and conditions by which they provide money to their national economies. This clearly represents an issue of 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the sole responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Banco de Mexico or of its Governing Board. 1 sovereignty and social contract of utmost importance. Countries may set different priorities or take specific elements into consideration. To a certain extent, central banks mandates are usually influenced by the most adverse monetary episodes previously experienced by each country. For example, Germanys 1920s hyperinflation must have influenced their societys search for price stability, as the Great Depression may have raised employment considerations in the US Federal Reserves dual mandate. In the case of many central banks in Latin America, between the late 70s and early 90s many economies in the region experienced periods of high inflation. Since that time, concerns have been that central banks under political influence, tend to set expansionary policies to finance governments and stimulate short-term economic growth, regardless of the medium- and long-run consequences. This was the main reason why it was necessary to isolate monetary policy-making from direct political influence. Many central banks in Latin America and in other regions were thus granted independence, with mandates set mainly on pursuing price 2 stability. In this context, Chile was one of the first economies to modernize its monetary policy framework with this objective. Central bank independence requires an institutional set-up that sometimes involves making politically unpopular decisions, but which are intended for the long-run benefit of the country. Its key features are: 1. A clear legal mandate and specific objectives. 2. Limiting the governments discretionary power of appointing central bank governing board members. 3. Limiting the ability of any government authority to use the central bank as a source of financing. 4. Consolidate collegiate decision-making bodies, with proven technical capacity and the guarantee to act independently. 5. Allowing the central bank to choose the best means to achieve the objectives set by law. The paradigm of autonomous, flexible inflation-targeting central banks, was the result of societys recognition that central banks best contribution to long-term growth was to maintain sustained price stability. And that monetary policy should deliver long-run inflation around a 3 specifically defined target, with non-persistent fluctuations in inflation. This clearly recognizes the notion that there is no exploitable trade-off between inflation and real variables. Even though most central banks have price stability mandates, the sharp contractions in economic activity experienced during the global financial crisis of 2008 and the current Covid-19 pandemic have led to the revision of the adequate monetary policy mandate and frameworks. Theoretically, economic models point towards optimal monetary policy strategies that minimize fluctuations around the inflation target and potential output. The key question is which central bank legal and institutional framework, mindful of political economy considerations and domestic conditions, delivers such outcome. In this regard, when an economy faces inflationary pressures from aggregate demand, monetary authorities with a single or dual mandate operate to stabilize inflation and output gaps. However, more challenging scenarios in which these gaps move in opposite directions may take place. In this context, central banks would face a complex 4 trade-off, regardless of their mandates. Under a dual mandate, these institutions are likely to face strong pressure to prioritize economic activity concerns, in spite of the presence of a positive inflation gap. In this regard, the ECB, whose primary objective is to maintain price stability in the euro area, when facing supply-related disturbances, conducts monetary policy aimed at achieving a gradual and orderly convergence of inflation to its target, while avoiding a sharp fall in economic activity and employment. In advanced economies, inflation dynamics are strongly anchored around their targets and they are mainly driven by aggregate demand dynamics. This may reduce the circumstances when the central bank faces more complex policy tradeoffs. Emerging economies face a more challenging environment: 1) While they have strengthened their macroeconomic policy frameworks and improved their economic fundamentals over the last decades, and despite their great advances in controlling inflation, many of them have not fully consolidated an environment 5 of low and stable inflation and medium and long-term inflation expectations are not fully anchored at the target. Monetary policy is still in the process of attaining this goals. 2) Emerging economies face larger and more frequent inflationary shocks and thus have historically registered higher levels of both inflation and its expectations. 3) They are predominantly small open economies, whose terms of trade are strongly influenced by commodity prices. They are also open to capital flows, and thus subject to variation in investor sentiment and global risk aversion. For these reasons, they are highly exposed to fluctuations in global economic and financial conditions which, in turn, is reflected in a large exchange rate volatility and in frequent inflationary shocks. Moreover, consumer price indices in these economies have larger weights on the prices of volatile items such as food and energy. As a result, inflation is, on average, more volatile and more difficult to forecast than in advanced economies. 6 To illustrate this point, let me highlight the recent research at Banco de Mexico suggests that, on average, shocks to the output gap have explained only about 10.2 % of the variation of core inflation across Latin American countries since the early 2000s. On the other hand, exchange rate shocks account for 23.7% of the variation, idiosyncratic inflationary shocks, originating from government-authorized prices, weather factors and so on, account for 61.2%, and commodity price shocks account for the remaining variation. When there are insufficiently credible inflation targets and inflation dynamics are dominated by foreign exchange and supply-related shocks, a well-defined and broadly understood and communicated single mandate can better contribute to reduce uncertainty about the central banks reaction-function and reduce term premium. In this case, the central bank can commit to a low and stable inflation around its target, while avoiding spillovers on economic activity and employment. For emerging economies facing these conditions, adopting a dual mandate could require a tighter monetary policy stance to compensate for the added uncertainty in the reaction-function and its effect on both inflation and the term premium. 7 When central banks in emerging economies face a complex policy tradeoff because inflation and output gaps move in opposite directions, they have to ensure that monetary policy does not lead to increases in risk premia and induce a steeper yield curve. In this circumstance, a dual mandate could add uncertainty to the policy response and put pressure on inflation risk premium. Under these circumstances, emerging economies could be better served by a well-defined single mandate centered on price stability, to directly contain inflation expectations and risk premia. There is an additional challenge faced by emerging economies, especially in Latin America, where there is a significant economic growth deficit that over the last decades has resulted in a lower per-capita GDP relative to other emerging and advanced economies. In the case of Mexico, we have even seen a reduction of potential GDP over the last years. In this environment, political pressures seeking stimulus and higher growth will not be put to rest by the reasons behind the update of potential GDP, a non-observable variable. Thus, in these economies, 8 central banks are bound to face greater pressures to put aside long-term price stability concerns and provide a short-term stimulus to the economy. Summing up, under the current setting, an institutional mandate that is attainable, time consistent, and allows society to make policymakers accountable for their actions by having them build credibility in their commitment to their goals is fundamental. In the specific case of Mexico, monetary policy has been conducted to achieve a primary price stability mandate. This approach has led to direct benefits, such as lower inflation, a lower exchange rate passthrough, stable inflation expectations, and lower term premia and indirectly to other beneficial changes in the economy, such as the development of long-term financial instruments. It is important to underline that a central bank by itself cannot achieve macroeconomic stability. Coordination and communication between both monetary and fiscal policies is crucial to achieve success. Mexico has had a successful experience of cooperation between Banco de 9 Mexico and the Treasury while at the same time maintaining central bank independence. Of utmost importance is that this approach has allowed Banco de Mexico to remain a strong public institution and sustain its independence with legitimacy in the eyes of the public. In this regard, central banks, especially in emerging economies, must also play the role of an anchor, both economically and institutionally, and a clear, attainable mandate contributes to strengthen institutions. Overall, while the ultimate goal of any central bank is and must be to contribute to the welfare of society, there is no unique institutional design that fits all economies at all times. Authorities and legislators have to consider multiple elements based on the historical experience of each country, the nature of the shocks faced by their economies, and any other likely pressures that institutions may face under diverse circumstances. In sum, long-term-oriented institutions, including central banks, now more than ever, need to be designed thoughtfully and, particularly, must have a clear time-consistent mandate that allows for good decision-making for the benefit of our societies. 10

Title: 82nd National Banking Convention
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the Eighty-Second Banking Convention. Acapulco, Guerrero, March 21, 2019 Dr. Carlos Urzua Macias, Secretary of Finance and Public Credit; Dr. Arturo Herrera Gutierrez, Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit; Eng. Adalberto Palma, President of the National Banking and Securities Commission; Mr. Marcos Martinez, outgoing President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Mr. Luis Nino de Rivera, incoming President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen: It gives me great pleasure to participate in this Eighty-Second Banking Convention. This meeting is a great opportunity to refine an agenda for collaboration between regulators and financial sector participants. I want to focus my speech on three aspects: one, the logic and purpose of the mandate of the Bank of Mexico and the importance of its autonomy, of which 2019 marks twenty-five years; two, the context and recent behavior of inflation and, three, some of the main opportunities and challenges facing the financial system. The mandate and autonomy of the Bank of Mexico Central banks have the main mission of providing fiat money to their economies. Having the exclusive power to issue banknotes and coins, the tasks of the central bank must be carried out with extreme responsibility and prudence, since the functionality of fiat money lies in the confidence that the population has in its effectiveness as a means of payment, safeguard of value and unit of account. 2 When the public perceives that money can suffer significant losses in its purchasing power, this leads to an environment of instability and considerably affects economic activity and social welfare. Hence the importance of an environment of price stability that generates certainty for the planning of all participants in the economy, that allows resources to be directed more efficiently, that promotes investment in long-term productive projects with broad social benefits and that protects the purchasing power of wages. These conditions are a prerequisite for any process of sustainable economic growth. Therefore, central banks must be guarantors of price stability and promote public confidence in fiat money, which is achieved when they have clear, verifiable objectives linked to their possibilities. At the end of the last century, multiple nations that did not have the right framework for central bank activity tried to use 3 monetary policy as a direct instrument to promote growth, unleashing costly inflationary episodes and economic decline. Therefore, a clear conclusion was reached on the possibilities and limits of monetary policy. Both historical experience and empirical evidence reliably demonstrate that monetary policy influences the trajectory of long-term inflation, while being clearly ineffective in influencing growth and employment in the long run. Due to the above, since the last two decades of the twentieth century, the consensus spread around the importance of maintaining, within the State, an institution fundamentally oriented to seek price stability with a long-term mandate and, therefore, many nations granted autonomy to their central banks. In Mexico, persistently high inflation rates that were closely associated with public deficits financed by central bank credit and that significantly affected economic growth and the well-being of the population, also led to the separation, on a firm constitutional and legal basis, of money creation from others. 4 government functions facing permanent demands to increase spending. Thus, in 1993 a constitutional reform was approved that, from 1994, provided autonomy in its administration and functions to the Bank of Mexico and established as its main objective to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. The law also identifies two additional functions, closely related to its priority objective, which are to promote the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of the payment system. Since the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico came into force, a clear awareness has been consolidated that transparency and accountability are practices that go hand in hand with the greatest independence and that are essential to consolidate credibility and improve the effectiveness of the institution's policies. In parallel, in line with robust academic evidence, in the nineties a new international paradigm in driving emerged. 5 of monetary policy: called inflation targeting, which is based on: i. the establishment of an explicit inflation target, ii. disclosure of methods and procedures for achieving it and iii. strict accountability for results. The Bank of Mexico formally adopted this scheme starting in 2001, and it is based on a permanent target for headline inflation of 3 percent, with a range of variability of plus or minus one percentage point. This goal is accompanied by a communication strategy that seeks to provide certainty and consolidate itself as a guide to the inflation expectations of economic agents. When the public knows the central bank's goals and strategies and has a clear idea that it will react to shocks that could steadily divert inflation from its target, their expectations tend to be aligned with that target. Therefore, it is essential to disseminate with breadth and opportunity the economic data and analyses, on which the Bank of Mexico bases its decision-making. This allows the public a better understanding, 6 monitoring and evaluation of the central bank's actions, which, in turn, generates confidence regarding the fulfillment of the goal. Over the past year, the Bank of Mexico has adopted new transparency measures. In particular: i. Since February 2018, forecasts have been published in each report punctual for the quarterly average inflation of the next eight quarters. With them, the public has an explicit reference to the guide to monetary policy actions. ii. Since May last year, the minutes of monetary policy decisions include the identity of the voters and, in case there is any dissent, add an explanation of it. iii. The full minutes of the meetings of the Governing Board at which the monetary policy decision is adopted shall be disclosed three years after the corresponding meeting, a period shorter than that used by most central banks. Additionally, to promote a broader discussion on the financial regulations issued by the Bank of Mexico, a mechanism of public, open, homogeneous and transparent consultations was adopted, in which all agents know, with the same opportunity, the draft provisions and can comment on them, under a public process. This encourages participation and enriches the 7 criterion of the authority in the generation of norms, under a principle of "even floor". Context of monetary policy In recent years, monetary policy has operated in a complex environment, since 2014 the Mexican economy has faced a series of adverse shocks and uncertainty, which have implied a reduction in the sources of external financing. The shocks have been of such magnitude that the flows of financial resources from abroad went from representing 4.1% of GDP on average between 2013 and 2014 to only 1.3% on average between 2015 and 2018. On the one hand, there has been a drastic drop in oil prices since mid-2014. Additionally, the production platform of this energy has been reduced considerably. This led to a radical change in the oil trade balance that, since it was recorded in 1993, had been surplus and that, as of 2015, became a deficit, reaching at the end of 2018 a deficit of more than 23 billion dollars. 8 On the other hand, after advanced economies adopted the most significant and prolonged monetary stimulus cycle in history, the normalization process has had an impact on international financial markets and the availability of resources for emerging economies has diminished. Additionally, doubts about the future of Mexico's trade scheme with the United States and Canada considerably affected expectations about the sustainability of our country's external accounts. The adjustment of the economy to this environment has required a smaller current account deficit, consistent with the lower availability of external resources. However, considering the significant deterioration in the oil trade balance, a much greater adjustment in the non-oil balance was required. In fact, since it has been recorded, in 2017 and 2018 it is the first time that the non-oil trade balance registers a surplus consecutively in two years. 9 In order for the external accounts to have this adjustment, a considerable depreciation of the bilateral real exchange rate against the US dollar was necessary, which between November 2014 and its highest point in January 2017, was 50% and which at the end of 2018 was 33%. To assess the magnitude of the real exchange rate adjustment that has been made in recent years, similar adjustments have only been made in 1982, 1987 and 1995. This makes clear the dimension of the challenge involved in ensuring that the economy had an orderly adjustment, which would facilitate a significant change in relative prices, avoiding second-order effects in the process of price formation and in which growth conditions were preserved. The macroeconomic response required an adjustment in the monetary policy stance and an improvement in the public finance stance. In particular, monetary policy measures contributed to anchoring medium- and long-term inflation expectations, as well as encouraging greater domestic savings. In the last quarter of 2018, to the external shocks already mentioned, elements of internal uncertainty were added, related to the 10 announcement of cancellation of the New Mexico International Airport project and the challenges facing PEMEX. This produced volatility in the markets, an adjustment of the exchange rate, an increase in risk premiums and even a change of outlook, from stable to negative, of Mexican sovereign debt by several rating agencies. However, volatility in domestic financial markets has decreased since the end of last year and in 2019. This is in response to external factors, such as the expectation of smaller increases in interest rates in the United States and the weakening of the dollar, and to internal factors, such as the approval of the Economic Package with a primary surplus target of 1% of GDP for this year. With regard to inflation, although it reached 6.77% at the end of 2017, its highest level since May 2001, the monetary policy stance has led to inflation falling to 3.94% and core inflation to 3.54% by February 2019. These levels are similar to the trajectory predicted by the Bank of Mexico, both in 11 November 2018 as in February of this year, which considers that inflation converges with its target in the first half of 2020. The environment described shows that the Mexican economy has been subject to significant shocks and structural changes, which make it necessary to incorporate in the evaluation of inflationary pressures, not only those associated with the cyclical position of the economy, but also those derived from the adverse factors, external and internal, that we have faced. Measures to promote the development of the financial system Let me now turn to the other functions entrusted to the Bank of Mexico that are crucial for the economy: to promote the healthy development of the financial system and to encourage the proper functioning of the payment system. On this occasion, the Banking Convention has adopted the very successful title of "A vision of the future". I believe that in no economic activity, such as in financial activity, is there such a pressing need to deploy a vision of the future, a prospective analysis, 12 that allows us to take advantage of opportunities and face the challenges of technological change. Access to new technologies provides a unique opportunity to transform financial systems and payment systems, streamlining operations, designing new products according to the needs of users and expanding the coverage of financial services to more and more sectors of the population. This can help unlock the potential of individuals, generate greater equality of opportunity and improve development conditions for millions of people. However, these great opportunities are not without significant challenges, ranging from increasingly complex cybercrimes, to unintended consequences and risks associated with the application of new technologies. In this environment of unprecedented opportunities and challenges, the Bank of Mexico has the user at the center of its efforts. 13 In this regard, the financial authorities, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Bank of Mexico, and the intermediaries have a shared agenda, as was stated on January 8, when announcing several measures to promote the development of the financial system and greater inclusion, as well as the better performance of the payment system. On the one hand, in order to improve the functioning of the payment system and benefit millions of users who currently do not have access to the financial sector, the development of the platform called Digital Collection (CoDi) was announced. This platform, through the use of QR codes, will allow users to make electronic transfers through smartphones, every day of the year and at any time, from a bank account. This platform is being concretized as an extension of the Interbank Electronic Payment System (SPEI), which constitutes the most important transactional mechanism in the country and which, unlike other nations, works 24 hours a day, every day of the year and makes payments immediately. 14 The CoDi is progressing as scheduled, there are already 6 institutions in the pilot of technical tests and, by the last day of September, it will be mandatory for all banks with more than 3 thousand accounts. The entry into force of the CoDi will have a positive effect on the user and on the financial system. On the one hand, the user, while being able to streamline payments, reduce costs and maximize the security of their operations, will also be able to familiarize themselves with the financial system and take a first step to access other services that improve their well-being. On the other hand, if we consider that the number of people with smartphones almost doubles the number of those who own bank accounts, it is clear that the development of CoDi can have a great impact on inclusion and incorporate a new universe of potential customers into the financial sector. Additionally, the use of the CoDi can support objectives of great social importance, by limiting the security risks or the possibilities of corruption or illicit activities that may involve the use of the 15 effective, or, by being a useful vehicle for the dispersion of social programs in places with little financial penetration. For new technologies and business models in the financial field to effectively benefit the user, careful and prudent work of regulatory design is required. In this regard, the Bank of Mexico published various provisions relating to the Law to Regulate Financial Technology Institutions. On the one hand, and in line with what is established in other economies, the Bank of Mexico considers it convenient to maintain a healthy distance between virtual assets and the financial system, given the risks they entail for the user, the institutions and the system as a whole. However, it is also in our interest to allow the use of new technologies aimed at greater efficiency. Therefore, provisions were issued that regulate the operation of virtual assets within the financial system, which are associated with the internal operations carried out by institutions, without implying direct exposure to customers. Likewise, the requirements that must be met by the 16 legal entities that, under the scheme of novel models, obtain authorizations to offer various services. In the "vision of the future" to which the title of this Convention summons us, another great challenge is to better assess the financial risks related to the environment. Environmental risks are not only a phenomenon that damages the growth potential and well-being of countries, but also pose specific challenges for financial intermediaries. Indeed, a poor assessment of those risks can result in credit risks, capable of affecting the assets and stability of the institutions and the system. At the Bank of Mexico, we are aware of these challenges and the need to have more uniform methodologies and criteria to assess environmental risk, as well as to promote sustainable investment instruments that contribute to a better allocation of resources in the economy. In short, intermediaries and authorities must work, with continuous communication and coordination, to: i. take advantage of technology in favor of greater financial inclusion; 17 ii. strengthen cybersecurity schemes; iii. to match the regulation with the evolution of the products financial and business models, and iv. promote the incorporation of environmental risks in the financing and investment decisions. In this regard, the Association of Banks of Mexico has historically established itself as a solid and professional interlocutor, with which long-term agreements and commitments have been reached. I take this opportunity to thank deeply the collaboration of outgoing President Marcos Martinez and wish the incoming President, Luis Nino de Rivera, every success. I am sure that we will maintain broad and effective cooperation. Ladies and gentlemen, in a global environment marked by profound changes and uncertain prospects, it is imperative for central banks to persevere in maintaining low and stable inflation, as a basis for the success of any economic strategy. In our country, the achievements in this area go hand in hand with the statute of constitutional autonomy that the Bank of Mexico has. This condition, which so long and 18 Effort has cost consolidation, is a fundamental requirement for growth and should be considered a precious public good. In addition, it is necessary to adopt, with prudence, graduality and responsibility, new tools and technologies that allow achieving pending goals, which in our case implies including, in a safe, sustainable and sustainable way, more and more sectors of the population in the benefits of the financial system. Thanks a lot 19
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la Octogsima Segunda Convencin Bancaria. Acapulco, Guerrero, 21 de marzo de 2019 Dr. Carlos Urza Macas, Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico; Dr. Arturo Herrera Gutirrez, Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico; Ing. Adalberto Palma, Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores; Ing. Marcos Martnez, Presidente saliente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Lic. Luis Nio de Rivera, Presidente entrante de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Seoras y seores: Me da mucho gusto participar en esta Octogsima Segunda Convencin Bancaria. Este encuentro constituye una magnfica oportunidad para afinar una agenda de colaboracin entre las autoridades reguladoras y los participantes del sector financiero. Quiero centrar mi intervencin en tres aspectos: uno, la lgica y el propsito del mandato del Banco de Mxico y la importancia de su autonoma, de la cual en este 2019 se cumplen veinticinco aos; dos, el contexto y el comportamiento reciente de la inflacin y, tres, algunas de las principales oportunidades y retos que enfrenta el sistema financiero. El mandato y autonoma del Banco de Mxico Los bancos centrales tienen la misin principal de dotar de dinero fiduciario a sus economas. Al contar con la facultad exclusiva de emitir billetes y monedas, las tareas del banco central deben realizarse con extremada responsabilidad y prudencia, pues la funcionalidad del dinero fiduciario radica en la confianza que la poblacin tiene en su efectividad como medio de pago, resguardo de valor y unidad de cuenta. 2 Cuando el pblico percibe que el dinero puede sufrir mermas significativas en su poder adquisitivo, ello propicia un ambiente de inestabilidad y afecta considerablemente la actividad econmica y el bienestar social. De ah la importancia de un entorno de estabilidad de precios que genere certidumbre para la planeacin de todos los participantes de la economa, que permita dirigir los recursos de manera ms eficiente, que promueva la inversin en proyectos productivos de largo plazo con amplios beneficios sociales y que proteja el poder adquisitivo de los salarios. Estas condiciones son un requisito indispensable para cualquier proceso de crecimiento econmico sostenible. Por ello, los bancos centrales deben ser garantes de la estabilidad de precios y propiciar la confianza del pblico en el dinero fiduciario, lo cual, se logra cuando estos cuentan con objetivos claros, verificables y ligados a sus posibilidades. A finales del siglo pasado, mltiples naciones que no contaban con el marco adecuado para la actividad del banco central, intentaron utilizar 3 la poltica monetaria como instrumento directo de promocin del crecimiento, desatando costosos episodios inflacionarios y de retroceso econmico. Por ello, se lleg a una conclusin clara sobre las posibilidades y lmites de la poltica monetaria. Tanto la experiencia histrica como la evidencia emprica demuestran de manera fehaciente que la poltica monetaria influye en la trayectoria de la inflacin de largo plazo, mientras que es claramente ineficaz para influir en el crecimiento y el empleo en el largo plazo. Debido a lo anterior, desde las dos ltimas dcadas del siglo XX, se extendi el consenso en torno a la importancia de mantener, dentro del Estado, una institucin orientada fundamentalmente a procurar la estabilidad de precios con un mandato de largo plazo y, por ello, numerosas naciones otorgaron autonoma a sus bancos centrales. En Mxico, las altas y persistentes tasas de inflacin que estuvieron estrechamente asociadas a los dficits pblicos financiados con crdito del banco central y que afectaron significativamente el crecimiento econmico y el bienestar de la poblacin, tambin llevaron a separar, con una base constitucional y legal firme, la creacin de dinero de otras 4 funciones del gobierno que enfrentan demandas permanentes para aumentar el gasto. As, en 1993 se aprob una reforma constitucional que, a partir de 1994, brind autonoma en su administracin y funciones al Banco de Mxico y estableci como su principal objetivo procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. La ley tambin seala dos funciones adicionales, estrechamente relacionadas con su objetivo prioritario, que son promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. Desde que entr en vigor la autonoma del Banco de Mxico, se ha consolidado una clara conciencia de que la transparencia y la rendicin de cuentas son prcticas que van de la mano con la mayor independencia y que son indispensables para consolidar la credibilidad y mejorar la eficacia de las polticas de la institucin. Paralelamente, en lnea con una robusta evidencia acadmica, en los aos noventa surgi un nuevo paradigma internacional en la conduccin 5 de la poltica monetaria: denominado de objetivos de inflacin, el cual se basa en: i. el establecimiento de una meta explcita de inflacin, ii. la divulgacin de los mtodos y procedimientos para alcanzarla y iii. la estricta rendicin de cuentas sobre los resultados. El Banco de Mxico adopt formalmente este esquema a partir de 2001, y se basa en una meta permanente para la inflacin general de 3 por ciento, con un intervalo de variabilidad de ms o menos un punto porcentual. Esta meta va acompaada de una estrategia de comunicacin que busca dar certeza y consolidarse como una gua de las expectativas de inflacin de los agentes econmicos. Cuando el pblico conoce las metas y estrategias del banco central y tiene una idea clara de que reaccionar ante los choques que pudieran desviar de manera sostenida a la inflacin de su objetivo, sus expectativas tienden a estar alineadas a dicho objetivo. Por eso, es fundamental divulgar con amplitud y oportunidad los datos econmicos y los anlisis, en los que el Banco de Mxico basa su toma de decisiones. Ello permite al pblico una mejor comprensin, 6 seguimiento y evaluacin de las acciones del banco central, lo que, a su vez, genera confianza respecto al cumplimiento de la meta. A lo largo del ao pasado el Banco de Mxico adopt nuevas medidas de transparencia. En particular: i. Desde febrero del 2018 se publican en cada informe los pronsticos puntuales para la inflacin promedio trimestral de los prximos ocho trimestres. Con ellos, el pblico cuenta con una referencia explcita de la gua de las acciones de poltica monetaria. ii. Desde mayo del ao pasado, las minutas de las decisiones de poltica monetaria incluyen la identidad de los votantes y, en caso de que exista algn disentimiento, aaden una explicacin del mismo. iii. Las minutas ntegras de las reuniones de la Junta de Gobierno en las que se adopta la decisin de poltica monetaria se divulgarn tres aos despus de la reunin correspondiente, plazo menor al utilizado por la mayora de bancos centrales. Adicionalmente, para propiciar una discusin ms amplia sobre la normatividad en materia financiera que emite el Banco de Mxico, se adopt un mecanismo de consultas pblicas, abiertas, homogneas y transparentes, en la que todos los agentes conocen, con la misma oportunidad, los borradores de disposiciones y pueden comentarlos, bajo un proceso pblico. Ello favorece la participacin y enriquece el 7 criterio de la autoridad en la generacin de normas, bajo un principio de piso parejo. Contexto de la poltica monetaria En los ltimos aos, la poltica monetaria ha operado en un ambiente complejo, desde 2014 la economa mexicana ha enfrentado una serie de choques adversos e incertidumbre, que han implicado una reduccin de las fuentes de financiamiento externo. Los choques han sido de tal magnitud que los flujos de recursos financieros provenientes del exterior pasaron de representar 4.1% del PIB en promedio entre 2013 y 2014 a slo 1.3% en promedio entre 2015 y 2018. Por un lado, se ha experimentado una cada drstica en los precios del petrleo desde mediados de 2014. Adicionalmente, la plataforma de produccin de este energtico se ha venido reduciendo considerablemente.
