Title: Putting into circulation the commemorative coin of the Taking of Zacatecas
text: REMARKS BY MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, DURING THE EVENT OF PUTTING INTO CIRCULATION THE COMMEMORATIVE COIN OF THE CAPTURE OF ZACATECAS. Zacatecas, Zacatecas. September 5, 2014. Miguel Alejandro Alonso Reyes, Constitutional Governor of the State of Zacatecas, Mr. Juan Antonio Castaneda Ruiz, President Magistrate of the Superior Court of Justice Deputy Claudia Anaya, President of the Board of Directors of the State Congress Senators and Federal Deputies of Zacatecas Brigadier General, Diploma of General Staff, Antelmo Rojas Yanez, Commander of the Eleventh Military Zone Carlos Pena Badillo, Municipal President of Zacatecas Miguel angel Moreno Tello, Representative of the Mint of Mexico Ladies and gentlemen 1 It is an honor for me to represent the Bank of Mexico in this significant event of putting into circulation the 20 peso coin, commemorating the centenary of the Taking of Zacatecas. What better scenario for this than the beautiful city of Zacatecas, and with the presence of members of the three branches of government and representatives of Zacatecan society. Since Roman antiquity, the coin has been used as a commemorative instrument. Engraving in gold, silver or copper images alluding to the great works and events of men with the purpose that they endure in the collective memory, has been a common practice throughout the centuries. For this reason, in Antiquity commemorative coins were minted. During the Renaissance and the Modern era medals were preferred (also metal pieces although without legal tender), but in the contemporary world, the coin has once again been the preferred means to commemorate the great historical and cultural facts of nations, thanks to the enormous amounts of monetary pieces that are minted, its ubiquitous presence and its widespread use, which allows large sectors of the population to participate in the commemoration. In Mexico, since the late eighteenth century medals of proclamation and oath of the Spanish monarchs were minted, from Ferdinand VI to Ferdinand VII. In 1823 the ascent of Guadalupe Victoria to the presidency of the Republic was commemorated through the coinage of medals. However, it was not until 1910 when the first commemorative coins were minted in our country. With the so-called "horse weights" the centenary of the 2 the beginning of the struggle for national independence and, in 1921, the stamping of the "centenarians" of gold and the "victories" of silver, allowed to honor the consummation of it. The twenty-first century has been particularly prolific in this area. It began with the commemorative pieces of the turn of the millennium, which were followed by those alluding to the union of the States in a Federation, which as some of you will remember began their national circulation right here in Zacatecas in 2003, and the very successful commemorative pieces of the bicentennial of our Independence and the centenary of the Revolution. To these have been added those that refer us to the publication of Don Quixote de la Mancha, the delivery of the Nobel Prize to Octavio Paz, the foundation of the National University, the Battle of May 5, the Centennial of the Mexican Army and the heroic defense of the port of Veracruz in 1914, among others. The piece alluding to the centenary of the Toma de Zacatecas, whose circulation brings us together today, adds to our commemorative coinage. Without intending to enter into the historical account of that transcendental battle, let me briefly highlight some of its aspects of greatest relevance. To refer to the Taking of Zacatecas, is to turn our gaze to a milestone of the Mexican Revolution; to a battle that marked destiny and opened the doors to the definitive triumph of Constitutionalism and a new country project. 3 The battle took place on June 23, 1914 in this city. By then, the federal forces, with the best of their troops, had fortified their positions in and around Zacatecas. The square seemed impregnable. Up to that point, the Federals had stopped the constant and unsuccessful attacks by the Center Division, which operated under the command of General Panfilo Natera and the Arrieta brothers. However, the arrival and help of the powerful Northern Division and its efficient artillery changed the course of the battle. The unquestionable military genius of Generals Francisco Villa and Felipe angeles, as well as the dedication and experience of their subordinates and troops, contributed to the early victory over the federal army. Thus the way was clear for the revolutionaries to continue their advance towards the center of the Republic and the capital of the country. In this way, the constitutionalists achieved their most important military victory and the definitive defeat of the usurper government of Victoriano Huerta. Therefore, it is a source of great pride for the Bank of Mexico and for me personally the circulation of the commemorative coin of the Taking of Zacatecas. The main characteristics of the currency, as established in the decree published in the Official Gazette of the Federation of May 22 of this year, are the following: As I mentioned, its denomination is 20 pesos. It is a bimetallic piece, with the cupronickel core and the bronze-aluminum ring. Its diameter is 32 mm and its total weight is 15,945 4 grams, characteristics identical to those of other commemorative pieces of this same denomination coined previously. As with all our coins, its obverse is occupied by the national shield in sculptural relief, surrounded by the legend "UNITED MEXICAN STATES" in a semicircle. The reverse, whose design was proposed by the Government of the State of Zacatecas, bears as main motifs the equestrian figure of Francisco Villa, flanked by the portraits of generals Felipe angeles and Panfilo Natera, with their respective names, surrounded by the inscription "CENTENARY OF THE TAKING OF ZACATECAS". In the lower part of the field you can see the crest of the hill of La Bufa with the years "1914-2014", and in the exergo the denomination "20" and the "M", mint of the Mint of Mexico. I want to emphasize that this coin is legal tender, so the public can use them to carry out any monetary transaction, although I am aware that many of them will be jealously kept and treasured by their holders, precisely because of their commemorative character. I congratulate the wise Zacatecan initiative to promote the minting of this piece, as well as the extraordinary work done to this end by the Mexican Mint. In addition, I want to share with all of you my certainty that this coin will enjoy the full acceptance of the user public, and that it will enrich the almost five times centennial numismatic tradition of Mexico. 5 Additionally, I would like to point out that the Bank of Mexico is also participating in the commemorations of the Centenary of the Taking of Zacatecas with the numismatic exhibition "Currency and History. A hundred years after the Taking of Zacatecas", which is presented at the Government Palace-Cultural Center, which refers to the history of Zacatecan currency during the War of Independence and the nineteenth century, and the villista issues of the Revolution, through 132 pieces of the Numismatic Collection of the Bank of Mexico, that we wish to share with the Zacatecans and their many visitors. My sincere thanks to Governor Alonso Reyes, for having had the initiative to show this collection in Zacatecas and lead its inauguration. I would also like to inform you that as of today the currency that we are putting into circulation, is incorporated into a mobile application for the IOS and Android platforms, which for free makes the Bank of Mexico available to the public. In it you can consult the characteristics and images of the Mexican coins currently in progress, which adds to the information available on the characteristics and security elements of our banknotes. I would not like to end my speech without recalling that next September 8 marks one more year since the founding of Zacatecas, which is why I extend my warmest congratulations to the authorities and the people of this beautiful and historic city. Thanks a lot. 6
text_original: PALABRAS DEL LIC. JAVIER GUZMN CALAFELL, SUBGOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE MXICO, DURANTE EL EVENTO DE PUESTA EN CIRCULACIN DE LA MONEDA CONMEMORATIVA DE LA TOMA DE ZACATECAS. Zacatecas, Zacatecas. 5 de septiembre de 2014. Licenciado Miguel Alejandro Alonso Reyes, Gobernador Constitucional del Estado de Zacatecas, Licenciado Juan Antonio Castaeda Ruiz, Presidente Magistrado del Tribunal Superior de Justicia Diputada Claudia Anaya, Presidenta de la Mesa Directiva del Congreso del Estado Senadores y Diputados Federales de Zacatecas General de Brigada, Diplomado de Estado Mayor, Antelmo Rojas Yez, Comandante de la Dcimo Primera Zona Militar Licenciado Carlos Pea Badillo, Presidente Municipal de Zacatecas Licenciado Miguel ngel Moreno Tello, Representante de la Casa de Moneda de Mxico Seoras y seores 1 Es para m un honor representar al Banco de Mxico en este significativo evento de puesta en circulacin de la moneda de $20 pesos, conmemorativa del centenario de la Toma de Zacatecas. Qu mejor escenario para ello que la hermosa ciudad de Zacatecas, y con la presencia de integrantes de los tres poderes del estado y representantes de la sociedad zacatecana. Desde la Antigedad romana, la moneda ha sido utilizada como instrumento conmemorativo. Grabar en oro, plata o cobre imgenes alusivas a las grandes obras y acontecimientos de los hombres con el propsito de que stos perduren en la memoria colectiva, ha sido una prctica comn a lo largo de los siglos. Por ello, en la Antigedad se acuaron monedas conmemorativas. Durante el Renacimiento y la poca Moderna se prefirieron las medallas (tambin piezas metlicas aunque sin curso legal), pero en el mundo contemporneo, la moneda ha vuelto a ser el medio predilecto para conmemorar los grandes hechos histricos y culturales de las naciones, gracias a las enormes cantidades de piezas monetarias que se acuan, a su ubicua presencia y a su uso generalizado, lo que permite hacer partcipes de la conmemoracin a amplios sectores de la poblacin. En Mxico, desde finales del siglo XVIII se acuaron medallas de proclamacin y jura de los monarcas espaoles, de Fernando VI a Fernando VII. En 1823 se conmemor el ascenso de Guadalupe Victoria a la presidencia de la Repblica mediante la acuacin de medallas. Sin embargo, no fue sino hasta 1910 cuando se acuaron las primeras monedas conmemorativas en nuestro pas. Con los llamados pesos de caballito se conmemor el centenario del 2 inicio de la lucha por la independencia nacional y, en 1921, la troquelacin de los centenarios de oro y de las victorias de plata, permiti honrar la consumacin de la misma. El siglo XXI ha sido particularmente prolfico en la materia. Inici con las piezas conmemorativas del cambio de milenio, a las que siguieron las alusivas a la unin de los Estados en una Federacin, que como algunos de ustedes recordarn iniciaron su puesta en circulacin nacional justo aqu en Zacatecas en el ao 2003, y las muy exitosas piezas conmemorativas del bicentenario de nuestra Independencia y del centenario de la Revolucin. A estas se han sumado las que nos remiten a la publicacin del Quijote de la Mancha, a la entrega del Premio Nobel a Octavio Paz, a la fundacin de la Universidad Nacional, a la Batalla del 5 de mayo, al Centenario del Ejrcito Mexicano y a la heroica defensa del puerto de Veracruz en 1914, entre otras. La pieza alusiva al centenario de la Toma de Zacatecas, cuya puesta en circulacin nos rene el da de hoy, se suma a nuestras acuaciones conmemorativas. Sin pretender entrar en la relatora histrica de esa trascendental batalla, permtanme destacar brevemente algunos de sus aspectos de mayor relevancia. Referirnos a la Toma de Zacatecas, es volver la mirada hacia un hito de la Revolucin Mexicana; a una batalla que marc el destino y abri las puertas al triunfo definitivo del Constitucionalismo y a un nuevo proyecto de pas. 3 La batalla tuvo lugar el 23 de junio de 1914 en esta ciudad. Para entonces, las fuerzas federales, con lo ms granado de sus tropas, haban fortificado sus posiciones en Zacatecas y sus alrededores. La plaza pareca inexpugnable. Hasta ese momento, los federales haban detenido los constantes e infructuosos ataques de la Divisin del Centro, que operaba bajo el mando del general Pnfilo Natera y de los hermanos Arrieta. Sin embargo, la llegada y auxilio de la poderosa Divisin del Norte y de su eficiente artillera cambiaron el derrotero de la batalla. El incuestionable genio militar de los generales Francisco Villa y Felipe ngeles, as como la entrega y experiencia de sus subalternos y tropas, contribuyeron a la pronta victoria sobre el ejrcito federal. As qued franco el camino para que los revolucionarios continuaran su avance hacia el centro de la Repblica y la capital del pas. De esta forma, los constitucionalistas lograron su ms importante victoria militar y la derrota definitiva del gobierno usurpador de Victoriano Huerta. Por lo anterior, es motivo de gran orgullo para el Banco de Mxico y para m en lo personal la puesta en circulacin de la moneda conmemorativa de la Toma de Zacatecas. Las principales caractersticas de la moneda, segn lo establecido en el decreto publicado en el Diario Oficial de la Federacin del 22 de mayo de este ao, son las siguientes: Como ya mencion, su denominacin es de 20 pesos. Es una pieza bimetlica, con el ncleo de cupronquel y el arillo de bronce aluminio. Su dimetro es de 32 mm y su peso total de 15.945 4 gramos, caractersticas idnticas a las de otras piezas conmemorativas de esta misma denominacin acuadas anteriormente. Como sucede con todas nuestras monedas, su anverso lo ocupa el escudo nacional en relieve escultrico, rodeado por la leyenda ESTADOS UNIDOS MEXICANOS en semicrculo. El reverso, cuyo diseo fue propuesto por el Gobierno del Estado de Zacatecas, lleva como motivos principales la figura ecuestre de Francisco Villa, flanqueada por los retratos de los generales Felipe ngeles y Pnfilo Natera, con sus respectivos nombres, rodeados por la inscripcin CENTENARIO DE LA TOMA DE ZACATECAS. En la parte inferior del campo se observa el crestn del cerro de La Bufa con los aos 19142014, y en el exergo la denominacin $20 y la M, ceca de la Casa de Moneda de Mxico. Quiero enfatizar que esta moneda es de curso legal, por lo que el pblico puede utilizarlas para realizar cualquier transaccin monetaria, aunque estoy consciente de que muchas de ellas sern celosamente guardadas y atesoradas por sus tenedores, precisamente por su carcter conmemorativo. Felicito la atinada iniciativa zacatecana de promover la acuacin de esta pieza, as como el extraordinario trabajo realizado con este fin por la Casa de Moneda de Mxico. Adems, quiero compartir con todos ustedes mi certeza de que esta moneda gozar de la plena aceptacin del pblico usuario, y de que enriquecer la casi cinco veces centenaria tradicin numismtica de Mxico. 5 De forma adicional, me gustara sealar que el Banco de Mxico tambin est participando en las conmemoraciones del Centenario de la Toma de Zacatecas con la exposicin numismtica Moneda e Historia. A cien aos de la Toma de Zacatecas, que se presenta en el Palacio de GobiernoCentro Cultural, la cual refiere la historia de la moneda zacatecana durante la Guerra de Independencia y el siglo XIX, y de las emisiones villistas de la Revolucin, a travs de 132 piezas de la Coleccin Numismtica del Banco de Mxico, que deseamos compartir con los zacatecanos y sus numerosos visitantes. Mi ms sincero agradecimiento al Gobernador Alonso Reyes, por haber tenido la iniciativa de mostrar en Zacatecas dicha coleccin y encabezar su inauguracin. Me permito tambin informarles que a partir de hoy la moneda que estamos poniendo en circulacin, se incorpora a una aplicacin mvil para las plataformas IOS y Android, que de forma gratuita pone el Banco de Mxico a disposicin de todo el pblico. En ella se pueden consultar las caractersticas e imgenes de las monedas mexicanas en curso actualmente, lo que se suma a la informacin disponible sobre las caractersticas y elementos de seguridad de nuestros billetes. No quisiera terminar mi intervencin sin recordar que el prximo 8 de septiembre se cumple un ao ms de la fundacin de Zacatecas, motivo por el cual extiendo mi ms calurosa felicitacin a las autoridades y al pueblo de esta bellsima e histrica ciudad. Muchas gracias. 6

Title: Presentation of the book: Constant and sound memory: coins, banknotes and medals of Independence and revolution
text: REMARKS BY DR. AGUSTIN CARSTENS, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, ON THE OCCASION OF THE PRESENTATION OF THE BOOK "MEMORIA CONTANTE Y SONANTE: MONEDAS, BILLETES Y MEDALLAS DE LA INDEPENDENCIA Y LA REVOLUCIoN" ? Senator Carlos Navarrete Ruiz - President of the Board of Directors of the Senate ? Senator Melquiades Morales Flores - President of the Committee of the Bicentennial and Centennial ? Senator Rogelio Rueda Sanchez - Secretary of the Development Committee Social and Secretary of the Finance and Public Credit Commission ? Public Accountant- Marcelo de los Santos- Director of Casa de Moneda Once again it is an honor to be present in this chamber of the Senate of the Republic and to offer a respectful greeting to its honorable members. This fact makes it even more satisfying for me to be able to participate as Governor of the Bank of Mexico in this ceremony that has been organized to present the beautiful book entitled "Memoria Contante y Sonante. Coins, banknotes and medals of Independence and Revolution." The great variety of species presented in this and other treatises on 1 Numismatic is, however, a reflection of the intense monetary instability that Mexico has suffered during some periods. The Bank of Mexico gladly agreed to collaborate in the co-edition of this work and from the beginning in the cultural project that gave rise to it promoted by Senator Melquiades Morales. He did so out of solidarity and recognition with the Senate of the Republic and also for reasons of institutional specialization. The Mint and the Bank of Mexico are the only institutions empowered to make money. In the case of our central institute, this faculty combines the functions of monetary administration assigned to it by law and the objectives that it must pursue for the benefit of the national economy. The opportunity is therefore propitious to share with such a distinguished audience some reflections on the importance of having a healthy and well-managed currency, taking 2 as a historical perspective what happened in this matter during the Independence and the Revolution. ------------------------------- the ------------------------------- Although it is possible to identify parallels between what happened in terms of currency during Independence and the Revolution, there was a very important difference in both experiences. That great difference was marked by the excessive way in which the issuance of paper money was resorted to during the revolutionary period. Those bills that depreciated vertiginously the public baptized them with the generic and derogatory term of "bilimbiques". Apart from the destruction that inexorably occurred during the War of Independence, I would like to highlight the damage suffered by the monetary system. The main problems stemmed from the scarcity of currency and the great difficulties faced by its distribution along and 3 width of the national territory. Likewise, the panorama of monetary difficulties was complicated by the plague of counterfeiting that plagued both realistic and insurgent emissions and the problems that arose with the dubious authenticity of many of the pieces that circulated. The scarcity of currency in the period is explained by several causes. A first, for the damage suffered by the production of metals whose coining originated the increase in the money supply. The second factor, already mentioned, came from the transport difficulties that were suffered at the time. On the one hand, the roads suffered destruction and to this we must add the dangers that hung over the transport due to the threat of groups of insurgents or sheaves of assailants. This historical fact allows me to highlight a function that modern central banking performs in Mexico with efficiency and security and about which the public does not always have the due conscience. I am referring to the system of 4 distribution of currency that the Bank of Mexico has and which allows there to be sufficient circulation in all the populations of the country, with pieces in good physical condition and in the appropriate combinations of banknotes and coins. Other monetary difficulties suffered by the population during Independence and announced by those that would arise in the Revolution had to do with three factors: with the promising currency issued by an insurgent faction, with the hoarding of currency and with the stamps and countermarks that were lavished in the period. The hoarding of currency is explained by the fact that there were circulating species of different quality in the period. Thus, the public kept the pieces with the highest value and left in circulation those that had it to a lesser extent. In particular, this was the case of the promising copper coin created in 1811 by Ignacio Lopez Rayon and which constituted the first example in Mexico of currency with an intrinsic value lower than the face value. The 5 The term "promising" comes from the fact that these were promises of payment that would be settled once the insurgency triumphed. ------------------------------- the ------------------------------- Also the monetary issues that were made during the Revolution suffered the problems derived from their plurality, their dubious legality and vulnerability to the danger of their apocryphal reproduction. But in the case of the revolutionary species to these three evils was added a much more serious one relative to their quantity. The two main revolutionary sides - the "constitutionalist" headed by Carranza and the villismo - resorted very widely to the issuance of paper money and these issues were the cause of the very intense inflationary process that was experienced in Mexico in the period. As an example, from August 1914 when Carranza took the capital to December 1915 the 6 New York's price of the constitutionalist note plummeted by more than 400 percent. Carranza explained that the only affordable financing options for the constitutionalist movement had been the issuance of paper money, forced loans or discretionary seizures. The so-called First Chief then pointed out that the issuance of a banknote had been resorted to in the knowledge of the harmful effects that this entailed. And Carranza wasn't wrong. Very serious harmful effects are caused when currency is issued in excessive amounts. In the Revolution prices rose at such a speed that as soon as money fell into the hands of the citizens, they rushed to spend it further exacerbating the acute upward process. After militarily defeating villismo, the Carrancista government tried unsuccessfully to solve the problem of 7 constitutionalist paper money through the project of the so-called unfalsifiable banknote. The failure of this project can be attributed to the fact that of the four problems suffered by the constitutionalist banknote, it only offered a solution for the first three - the diversity of emissions, the legality of the pieces and the counterfeiting - but left untouched what was perhaps the most serious of them: that of its excessive quantity. Ladies and gentlemen: After the First World War there were other cases of hyperinflation in countries such as Germany, Poland or Hungary. All those experiences were very traumatic. The damage suffered by the peoples with inflation is exacerbated by the intensity of the upward process. In the inflationary phases, those who suffer the most are the popular strata and the least favored people on the social scale. 8 But the history of inflation in the twentieth century did not end with those extreme experiences. In Latin America an important chapter was written and also painful for the inflations that were unleashed mainly during the third quarter of that century. Unfortunately, Mexico was not spared from these destabilizing experiences. Remembering them offers us perspective to understand the reformist reactions that arose in order to avoid new outbreaks of inflation. Mexico, as is well known, was an important case in that reform movement. The autonomy granted to the Bank of Mexico in 1994 responds to the motivation of ensuring that our country has a stable and solid currency. This aspiration should not be seen, because it is not, as an end in itself but as a means to a more prosperous and inclusive economy. Stability is an indispensable precondition for sustained growth with continuously rising employment and real wages. 9 Seeking a healthy currency is the best contribution that the Bank of Mexico can make to the economic development of our country. 10
text_original: PALABRAS DEL DR. AGUSTIN CARSTENS, GOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE MXICO, EN OCASIN DE LA PRESENTACIN DEL LIBRO MEMORIA CONTANTE Y SONANTE: MONEDAS, BILLETES Y MEDALLAS DE LA INDEPENDENCIA Y LA REVOLUCIN  Senador Carlos Navarrete Ruz  Presidente de la Mesa Directiva del Senado  Senador Melquiades Morales Flores  Presidente de la Comisin del Bicentenario y Centenario  Senador Rogelio Rueda Sanchez Secretario de la Comisin de Desarrollo Social y Secretario de la Comisin de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico  Contador Pblico- Marcelo de los Santos- Director de Casa de Moneda Una vez ms es un honor estar presente en este recinto del Senado de la Repblica y ofrecer un saludo respetuoso a sus honorables integrantes. Este hecho hace an ms satisfactorio para mi poder participar en calidad de Gobernador del Banco de Mxico en esta ceremonia que se ha organizado para presentar el bello libro intitulado Memoria Contante y Sonante. Monedas, billetes y medallas de la Independencia y la Revolucin. La gran variedad de especies que se presentan en este y otros tratados sobre 1 numismtica es, sin embargo, un reflejo de la intensa inestabilidad monetaria que ha sufrido Mxico durante algunas pocas. El Banco de Mxico acept con gusto colaborar en la coedicin de esta obra y desde un principio en el proyecto cultural que le dio origen impulsado por el senador Melquiades Morales. Lo hizo por solidaridad y reconocimiento con el Senado de la Repblica y adems por razones de especializacin institucional. La Casa de Moneda y el Banco de Mxico son las nicas instituciones facultadas para fabricar dinero. En el caso de nuestro instituto central a esa facultad se anan las funciones de administracin monetaria que tiene asignadas por ley y los objetivos que debe procurar en beneficio de la economa nacional. La oportunidad es por tanto propicia para compartir con tan distinguido auditorio algunas reflexiones sobre la importancia de tener una moneda sana y bien administrada, tomando 2 como perspectiva histrica lo ocurrido en esta materia durante la Independencia y la Revolucin. ------------------------------- o ------------------------------- Aunque es posible identificar paralelismos entre lo ocurrido en materia de moneda durante la Independencia y la Revolucin existi una diferencia muy importante en ambas experiencias. Esa gran diferencia estuvo marcada por la forma excesiva en que se recurri durante el periodo revolucionario a la emisin de papel moneda. A esos billetes que se depreciaron vertiginosamente el pblico los bautiz con el trmino genrico y despectivo de bilimbiques. Aparte de la destruccin que inexorablemente se produjo durante la guerra de Independencia, me permito destacar los perjuicios que sufri el sistema monetario. Los principales problemas se derivaron de la escasez de moneda y de las grandes dificultades que enfrent su distribucin a lo largo y 3 ancho del territorio nacional. Asimismo, el panorama de dificultades monetarias se complic con la plaga de la falsificacin que asol tanto a las emisiones realistas como insurgentes y los problemas que surgieron con la autenticidad dudosa de muchas de las piezas que circularon. La escasez de moneda en el periodo se explica por varias causas. Una primera, por los daos que sufri la produccin de metales de cuya amonedacin se originaba el aumento de la oferta de dinero. El segundo factor, ya mencionado, provino de las dificultades de transporte que se padecieron en la poca. Por un lado, los caminos sufrieron destruccin y a ello cabe agregar los peligros que pendan sobre el transporte por la amenaza de los grupos de insurrectos o de gavillas de asaltantes. Este hecho histrico me permite destacar una funcin que la banca central moderna realiza en Mxico con eficiencia y seguridad y sobre la cual no siempre tiene el pblico la conciencia debida. Me refiero al sistema de 4 distribucin de moneda con que cuenta el Banco de Mxico y el cual permite que haya circulante suficiente en todas las poblaciones del pas, con piezas en buen estado fsico y en las combinaciones adecuadas de billetes y monedas. Otras dificultades monetarias que sufri la poblacin durante la Independencia y que anunciaban las que surgiran en la Revolucin tuvieron que ver con tres factores: con la moneda promisoria que expidi una faccin insurgente, con el atesoramiento de moneda y con los resellos y contramarcas que se prodigaron en el periodo. El atesoramiento de moneda se explica porque existieron en el periodo especies circulantes de distinta calidad. As, el pblico guardaba las piezas con mayor valor y dejaba en la circulacin las que lo tuvieran en menor medida. En particular, este fue el caso de la moneda promisoria en cobre que cre en 1811 Ignacio Lpez Rayn y que constituy el primer ejemplo en Mxico de moneda con valor intrnseco inferior al valor facial. El 5 calificativo de promisoria proviene de que se trat de promesas de pago que se saldaran una vez que triunfara la insurgencia. ------------------------------- o ------------------------------- Tambin las emisiones monetarias que se realizaron durante la Revolucin padecieron los problemas derivados de su pluralidad, de su dudosa legalidad y de la vulnerabilidad ante el peligro de su reproduccin apcrifa. Pero en el caso de las especies revolucionarias a esos tres males se sum uno mucho ms grave relativo a su cantidad. Los dos principales bandos revolucionarios el constitucionalista encabezado por Carranza y el villismo recurrieron en forma amplsima a la emisin de papel moneda y esas emisiones fueron la causa del muy intenso proceso inflacionario que se experiment en Mxico en el periodo. A guisa de ejemplo, de agosto de 1914 en que Carranza tom la capital a diciembre de 1915 la 6 cotizacin en Nueva York del billete constitucionalista se desplom en ms de 400 por ciento. Carranza explic que las nicas opciones de financiamiento asequibles para el movimiento constitucionalista haban sido la emisin de papel moneda, los prstamos forzosos o las incautaciones discrecionales. Acto seguido, el llamado Primer Jefe seal que se haba recurrido a la emisin de billete a sabiendas de los efectos perniciosos que ello implicaba. Y Carranza no se equivocaba. Efectos perjudiciales muy graves se causan cuando se expide moneda en cantidades excesivas. En la Revolucin los precios suban a tal velocidad que tan pronto caa dinero en manos de los ciudadanos, stos se apresuraban a gastarlo exacerbando an ms el agudo proceso alcista. Despus de derrotar militarmente al villismo, el gobierno carrancista trat infructuosamente de resolver el problema del 7 papel moneda constitucionalista mediante el proyecto del llamado billete infalsificable. Cabe atribuir el fracaso de ese proyecto a que de los cuatro problemas que padeca el billete constitucionalista solamente ofreci solucin para los tres primeros la diversidad de emisiones, la legalidad de las piezas y la falsificacin pero dej insoluto el que era quiz el ms grave de ellos: el de su excesiva cantidad. Seoras y seores: Despus de la Primera Guerra Mundial hubo otros casos de hiperinflacin en pases como Alemania, Polonia o Hungra. Todas esas experiencias fueron muy traumticas. Los daos que sufren los pueblos con las inflaciones se agudizan en razn directa a la intensidad del proceso alcista. En las fases inflacionarias quienes ms sufren son los estratos populares y las personas menos favorecidas en la escala social. 8 Pero la historia de la inflacin en el siglo XX no se termin con esas experiencias extremas. En Amrica Latina se escribi un captulo importante y tambin doloroso por las inflaciones que se desataron principalmente durante el tercer cuarto de ese siglo. Por desgracia, Mxico no se salv de esas vivencias desestabilizadoras. Recordarlas nos ofrece perspectiva para entender las reacciones reformistas que surgieron a fin de evitar nuevos brotes de inflacin. Mxico, como es bien sabido, fue un caso importante en ese movimiento reformista. La autonoma que se le otorg al Banco de Mxico en 1994 responde a la motivacin de procurar que nuestro pas cuente con una moneda estable y slida. Esta aspiracin no debe verse, porque no lo es, como un fin en s mismo sino como un medio para tener una economa ms prspera e incluyente. La estabilidad es una precondicin indispensable para crecer de manera sostenida con elevacin continua del empleo y de los salarios reales. 9 Procurar una moneda sana es la mejor contribucin que puede hacer el Banco de Mxico al desarrollo econmico de nuestro pas. 10

Title: El Trimestre, a project in transformation
text: El Trimestre, a project in transformation Words of Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the presentation of the book Own Answers 80 years of El Trimestre Mexico City, March 10, 2015 It is a privilege to moderate the presentation of the anthology Respuestas propias 80 anos de El Trimestre by Graciela Marquez and Gustavo Del angel, neatly edited by the Fondo de Cultura Economica. I am pleased to share the table with the compilers, whom I congratulate on their wise selection and introduction, as well as with my colleagues Carlos Bazdresch, Rodolfo de la Torre and Fausto Hernandez, who in recent times have directed the magazine and have marked it with a more modern and rigorous profile. El Trimestre Economico was founded in 1934 and, although it is one of the longest-running scientific journals in Spanish, it maintains a great validity. The magazine was conceived to disseminate the novelties of economic knowledge and discuss the main topics of the world and Mexican economy. This commemorative anthology brings together ten texts representative of the history of the magazine. From my reading, I would group the articles into four dimensions or stages, which I will use to organize my comments. The Economic Quarter Without Economists Let me refer to the first period as The Economic Quarter without economists, since at that time few Latin American authors had an academic background in economics. In fact, the founders of the magazine were a lawyer, Daniel Cosio Villegas, and an engineer, Eduardo Villasenor. I must say, however, that this absence of formal economic knowledge does not 1 it necessarily constituted a disadvantage, since the authors made up for their lack of technical tools with intuition and common sense. For example, cosio Villegas' essay that seeks to demystify the idea that Mexico is an opulent country in natural resources is fascinating. Although his notion of wealth does not correspond to that postulated almost two centuries ago by Adam Smith and mixes dissimilar and somewhat anachronistic concepts even for his time, the author succeeds in questioning a widespread stereotype. In addition, with polemical grace, he presumes not to be an economist and jokes about some attitudes and explanations of the guild. Another very constructive article is by Eduardo Villasenor, who talks about the role of banking in economic expansion, its complementary functions with the State and the evolution of this activity in Mexico until the middle of the last century. In accordance with the climate of the ideas of his time, Villasenor gave a fundamental role to the State, defended the public works program and called for the coordination of public and private investment. However, it recognized that the fundamental condition of development was monetary stability and warned of the dangers and, in the end, the unviability of inflationary growth. Villasenor's common sense is prescient and his claims about stability have been corroborated in practice, and are part of the fundamental tenets of modern central banking. 2 In both articles, there is no complex theory, nor a specialized apparatus. However, one can appreciate a prudent and pragmatic eclecticism, characteristic of those generations of authors who were trained in economics, rather than studying it, intuiting it and exercising it in practical situations. The second class of texts in the anthology is what I identify as the totalizing visions from underdevelopment, which began to proliferate towards the fifties. Raul Prebisch's article is an example of this trend and constitutes a germinal piece of ECLAC's economic paradigm. This model was based on a simple premise: the terms of trade between the primary products exported by developing countries and the industrialized goods they received from advanced countries were invariably unfair, so the remedy was to promote substitute industrialization. Prebisch considered that one of the failures of general economic theory was its "false sense of universality" and advocated making a theory for the countries of the periphery, different from that applicable for those of the center. In a static view of income distribution, he pointed out that, given the asymmetric terms of exchange, large industrial centers were the permanent winners in 3 to the detriment of the underdeveloped, in what could now be called a zero-sum game. These premises became extremely influential in the public policies of the time in several countries, which incorporated preferential treatments for certain segments of the population. While these measures can be said to have stimulated industrialization heavily dependent on protection and subsidies, in return, they introduced distortions and inhibited the exploitation of international trade, limiting productivity and harming consumers. Another influential economist within this trend was W. Arthur Lewis who proposed a theory of economic development based on the unlimited supply of labor. He believed that in developing countries the marginal productivity of labour was negligible, zero or even negative. He postulated that the markets would improve with the disappearance of stalls or tendajones since, according to him, consumers would gain by disappearing the margins of this type of sales. This author thought that the "imperialist" countries invested capital, but managed to keep wages low, thanks to the fact that the surplus population allowed labor with a subsistence income. In his attempt to formalize his assumption, Lewis went so far as to incur reductionisms by thinking that intrinsically the rich have different incentives than the poor, or by prescribing as 4 recipe for development, the mere investment in physical capital, ignoring other fundamental sources of growth, such as the creation of human capital and the institutional framework. In keeping with the prestige at the time of planning and state intervention, these models conceived of economics as a kind of social engineering by which a clairvoyant planner could make the decisions that correspond to the individual. Already with the advantage of hindsight, it is possible to affirm that these maximalist models, with a notion of exceptionality and with a strong interventionist component, led to errors in economic diagnosis and policy design. The historian's glasses A third dimension of the texts selected by Graciela and Gustavo I call the glasses of the historian. Fernando Rosenzweig documents the economic growth during the Porfiriato, whose annual average, although clearly higher than that of previous decades, does not seem so high, nor so miraculous, since it barely exceeds one percent per inhabitant. The author points out that, thanks to a climate conducive to investment, foreign capital and exports made it possible to acquire capital goods from abroad, while the development of railways allowed a progressive extension of the market economy. This study, in addition to illuminating a stage as important as controversial in the 5 The national imaginary makes it possible to infer some general conditions aimed at development. For his part, Clark W. Reynolds, in a conjuncture document for the United States Congress, makes a historical account of the "stabilizing development", which he describes as destabilizing. Reynolds classifies the economic policies of that stage as conservative because, in his opinion, they favored mainly certain segments of the private sector. While acknowledging that during that stage social security benefits were extended and savings were promoted through high real interest rates, he complained that the country lacked a long-term planning framework and that the tripling of per capita income had not been better distributed. In addition, it suggests that at that stage the imbalances that precipitated the crisis of the seventies began to incubate, as fundamental reforms such as fiscal reforms had been deferred and a fixed exchange rate maintained. Reconciliation with global flows The fourth and final dimension, which I call reconciliation with global currents, begins in the mid-eighties, with the arrival of Carlos Bazdresch as director, who promotes a change towards professional updating and greater academic rigor. This laudable momentum has been continued by Rodolfo de la Torre and Fausto Hernandez. 6 To this stage belongs the article by Santiago Levy, which addresses a topic very much in vogue in the eighties, when Latin American economies faced a peremptory and onerous external debt. Rejecting devaluation as a remedy, Levy wonders if export subsidies increase the trade balance at a lower cost to the country and concludes that it does, although he recognizes that they must be paid with the reduction of public spending or the increase in taxes, aspects in which he does not delve. The remaining three items in the collection most clearly represent the shift to reconciliation with global currents and are probably those of the highest technical level and practical utility. Alvin Roth's discussion of market design is extremely interesting. The author shares certain lessons about special transactions in which there may not be enough density or suffer from the problem of congestion. In particular, he discusses some U.S. case studies on the markets of newly graduated physicians, kidney donor exchange, school choice, the gastroenterologist market, and that of recently graduated economists. It is a proactive and novel approach to how to strengthen certain markets that operate under special conditions. For their part, Aaron Tornell and Andres Velasco are concerned with interpreting, from game theory, an apparent paradox: the outflow of capital from poor countries to 7 rich countries. The model they use to explain capital flight is simple and rigorous and rationalizes an empirical observation. In his model, the private return on investment in a poor country can be reduced by the expropriation of those investments by interest groups. It is an example of what they are for and how theoretical models are applied. Finally, in the empirical work on regional convergence in Mexico, Gerardo Esquivel applies an economic and statistical approach used in other countries. The author finds that, for more than half a century, regional disparities narrowed at a low rate in the international comparison. For Esquivel, one of the main causes of this phenomenon, which slows down development and exacerbates income inequality, could be the enormous regional divergence in the formation of human capital, which, by the way, fills the gap left by Lewis's assumptions. This is a fundamental reference text on the subject of more balanced and equitable regional development. The future of one's own answers Let me conclude by pointing out that reading this anthology is not only instructive, but entertaining and picturesque. Indeed, given that El Trimestre was created at the dawn of economic science in Mexico, in its trajectory we can trace the gradual evolution of this discipline in our country, as well as the validity of this discipline. 8 obsolescence of various technical tools, theoretical approaches and institutional visions. In particular, the title seems very suggestive, because the search for their own answers has been one of the motivations that led many authors to collaborate in this space. Certainly, when this search has led to notions of exceptionalism and isolation, the resulting models have been abstracted from the real dynamics of the economy and have been unhelpful and even counterproductive. Therefore, the investigation of one's own answers must be framed in a global environment and in the normal parameters of the evolution of a science. It only remains for me to congratulate Graciela and Gustavo again for their exhaustive work, which sums up eight decades of production and economic debate, and to hope that El Trimestre will remain, for a long time, a fruitful space for training and discussion for economists and non-economists. 9

Desde mi lectura, yo agrupara los artculos en cuatro dimensiones o etapas, que utilizar para organizar mis comentarios. Acorde con el clima de las ideas de su poca, Villaseor otorgaba un protagonismo fundamental al Estado, defenda el programa de obras pblicas y llamaba a coordinar la inversin pblica y privada. Sin embargo, reconoca que la condicin fundamental del desarrollo era la estabilidad monetaria y adverta sobre los peligros y, al final, la inviabilidad de un crecimiento inflacionario. El sentido comn de Villaseor es premonitorio y sus afirmaciones sobre la estabilidad han sido corroboradas en la prctica, y son parte de los postulados fundamentales de la banca central moderna. 2 En ambos artculos, no hay una teora compleja, ni un aparato especializado. Sin embargo, puede apreciarse un prudente y pragmtico eclecticismo, caracterstico de aquellas generaciones de autores que se formaron en la economa, ms que estudindola, intuyndola y ejercindola en situaciones prcticas. Las visiones totalizadoras desde el subdesarrollo La segunda clase de textos de la antologa es la que yo identifico como las visiones totalizadoras desde el subdesarrollo, las cuales comenzaron a proliferar hacia la dcada de los cincuenta. El artculo de Ral Prebisch es un ejemplo de esta tendencia y constituye una pieza germinal del paradigma econmico de la CEPAL. Dicho modelo parta de una premisa sencilla: los trminos de intercambio entre los productos primarios que exportaban los pases en desarrollo y los bienes industrializados que reciban de los pases avanzados eran invariablemente injustos, por lo que el remedio consista en promover una industrializacin sustitutiva. Si bien puede decirse que estas medidas estimularon una industrializacin muy dependiente de la proteccin y los subsidios, a cambio, introdujeron distorsiones e inhibieron el aprovechamiento del comercio internacional, limitando la productividad y perjudicando a los consumidores. Otro economista influyente dentro de esta tendencia fue W. Arthur Lewis que propuso una teora del desarrollo econmico basado en la oferta ilimitada de la mano de obra. Acorde con el prestigio en ese entonces de la planificacin y la intervencin estatal, estos modelos conceban la economa como una suerte de ingeniera social mediante la cual un planificador clarividente podra tomar las decisiones que corresponden al individuo. Los anteojos del historiador Una tercera dimensin de los textos seleccionados por Graciela y Gustavo la llamo los anteojos del historiador. Fernando Rosenzweig documenta el crecimiento econmico durante el Porfiriato, cuyo promedio anual, si bien claramente superior al de las dcadas anteriores, no se antoja tan alto, ni tan milagroso, pues apenas supera el uno por ciento por habitante. Este estudio, adems de iluminar una etapa tan importante como controvertida en el 5 imaginario nacional, permite inferir algunas condiciones generales tendientes al desarrollo. Por su parte, Clark W. Reynolds, en un documento de coyuntura para el Congreso de los Estados Unidos, hace un recuento histrico del desarrollo estabilizador, que l califica como desestabilizador. Reynolds clasifica las polticas econmicas de esa etapa como conservadoras porque, en su opinin, favorecan principalmente a ciertos segmentos del sector privado. Si bien reconoce que durante esa etapa se extendieron los beneficios de la seguridad social y se promocion el ahorro mediante tasa de inters reales elevadas, se queja de que el pas careciera de un marco de planeacin de largo plazo y de que la triplicacin del ingreso per cpita no se haya distribuido mejor. Los tres artculos restantes de la coleccin representan ms ntidamente el viraje a la reconciliacin con las corrientes globales y son, probablemente, los de mayor nivel tcnico y utilidad prctica. La discusin sobre el perfeccionamiento en el diseo de los mercados de Alvin Roth es sumamente interesante. El autor comparte ciertas lecciones sobre transacciones especiales en las cuales puede no haber suficiente densidad o se sufre del problema de congestin. En particular, analiza algunos estudios de caso en Estados Unidos sobre los mercados de los mdicos recin egresados, el intercambio de donantes de rin, la eleccin de escuela, el mercado de gastroenterlogos, y el de los economistas recin egresados. En su modelo el rendimiento privado de la inversin en un pas pobre puede reducirse con la expropiacin que logran de esas inversiones los grupos de inters. Es un ejemplo de para qu sirven y cmo se aplican los modelos tericos. Finalmente, en el trabajo emprico sobre la convergencia regional en Mxico, Gerardo Esquivel aplica un enfoque econmico y estadstico utilizado en otros pases. El autor encuentra que, durante ms de medio siglo, las disparidades regionales se redujeron a un ritmo bajo en el comparativo internacional. Para Esquivel una de las principales causas de este fenmeno, que frena el desarrollo y agudiza la desigualdad del ingreso, podra ser la enorme divergencia regional en la formacin de capital humano, lo que, por cierto, llena el vaco que dejaban los supuestos de Lewis. Este es un texto de referencia fundamental en el tema de un desarrollo regional ms equilibrado y equitativo. El porvenir de las respuestas propias Permtanme concluir sealando que la lectura de esta antologa no slo es instructiva, sino amena y pintoresca. En efecto, dado que El Trimestre se cre en los albores de la ciencia econmica en Mxico, en su trayectoria se puede rastrear la evolucin gradual de esta disciplina en nuestro pas, as como la validez u 8 obsolescencia de diversas herramientas tcnicas, enfoques tericos y visiones institucionales. En particular, el titulo me parece muy sugerente, porque la bsqueda de respuestas propias ha sido una de las motivaciones que llev a muchos autores a colaborar en este espacio. Ciertamente, cuando esta bsqueda ha conducido a las nociones de excepcionalidad y al aislamiento, los modelos resultantes se han abstrado de las dinmicas reales de la economa y han sido poco tiles y hasta contraproducentes. Por eso, la indagacin de respuestas propias debe enmarcarse en un entorno global y en los parmetros normales de la evolucin de una ciencia. Slo me resta felicitar nuevamente a Graciela y a Gustavo por su exhaustiva tarea, que nos resume ocho dcadas de produccin y debate econmico, y desear que El Trimestre siga siendo, por mucho tiempo, un espacio fecundo de formacin y discusin para economistas y no economistas. 9

Title: Future issues for central banking
text: FUTURE TOPICS FOR CENTRAL BANKING VIRTUAL CONFERENCE GIVEN AT THE CLOSING EVENT OF THE SUBJECT OF THE BANK OF MEXICO 2020-2021 BY MTRA. IRENE ESPINOSA CANTELLANO1 JANUARY 21, 2021 1. Introduction It is a great pleasure for me to participate in the closing event of the Subject of the Bank of Mexico 2020-2021. During the past months you learned about the daily work of the central bank of our country, from the voices of the same public servants in charge of carrying out the tasks required for this institution to fully and opportunely fulfill its functions. I trust that this experience has contributed to a deeper understanding of what the Bank of Mexico does in the service of society. We live in a changing economy and, in particular, its financial system is constantly evolving. Central banking is currently facing unprecedented challenges around the world. Therefore, I would like to take this opportunity to reflect on what we could expect for the coming years in its operation and to talk about issues that are becoming more relevant in its sphere of influence. To form an idea about the future of central banking, it is convenient to start from the review of the main transformations that it has had during the last decades and the challenges we face today. Therefore, I have ordered my presentation in three parts. In the first, I will tell you about the structural changes that central banking experienced in order to 1 The views and opinions presented in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 to improve their performance, especially on price stability, through greater independence, transparency and accountability. I will then mention how the emergence of the information economy influenced the way monetary policy was conducted and propelled the growing role of effective central bank communication. Third, I will refer to how the international financial crisis led central banks to implement unconventional monetary policy measures to address critical situations and to focus more on financial stability. The second part will be devoted to dealing with a core issue, directly related to two inherent functions of central banks: the provision of currency and the promotion of the proper functioning of payment systems. In particular, I will focus on the opportunities, risks and challenges that innovation in payment methods represents for monetary authorities, especially electronic payments and digital currencies. Finally, in the third section I will comment on the importance of incorporating environmental risks in financial institutions and the role of central banks, together with other financial authorities. I will also tell you about the steps we have taken in Mexico in that direction and we will see that although there have been crucial advances at the global level, there is still a lot of work to be done. 2 2. Evolution towards modern central banking In the late sixties began an upward trend of inflation around the world that lasted for more than two decades. This phenomenon was due, in part, to the lack of knowledge on the part of policymakers about the functioning of monetary policy and the process of forming inflation expectations. This lack of knowledge contributed to inflationary processes due to both demand shocks (expansionary monetary policies) and supply shocks (oil shocks). In advanced economies, average inflation rose to double digits and remained so for most of the period. In emerging economies, the problem was much more severe and prolonged, even hyperinflationary processes were promoted in several Latin American economies.2 In many emerging and developing economies, where the central bank lacked effective independence, the government used monetary policy to finance its deficits. The subordination of monetary policy to fiscal policy led to the phenomenon known as "fiscal dominance", where the central bank loses control over the monetary base, since it is forced to acquire government-issued debt. At that time, central banks used monetary aggregates as the main instrument of monetary policy and used the latter as a nominal anchor in their economies. However, the episodes of price instability that took place during the decades of the seventies and eighties sowed the 2 Para un analisis de la naturaleza de las hiperinflaciones modernas vease Carmen M. Reinhart and Miguel A. Savastano, "The Realities of Modern Hyperinflation", IMF Finance & Development June (2003). 3 seed of the reforms that were implemented to shape modern central banking. It can be said that from the 1980s the great reforms to central banking in the world begin, which can be summarized in three elements: the granting of greater independence to central banks, the definition of objectives or rules to guide their monetary policy and a fundamental change in their communication paradigm towards transparency and accountability, in order to better guide inflation expectations. Undoubtedly, during that period, substantial progress was made in global macroeconomic stability, as it was possible to reduce average inflation to one-digit levels (first in advanced economies and then in emerging economies) and maintain global economic growth. In the United States, this period has been called "The Great Moderation." However, during the nineties the new "information economy" and the acceleration of financial innovation began to generate new challenges and opportunities for central banking in the face of the new millennium. In terms of the conduct of monetary policy, the main international changes during that period consisted of the increasing adoption of flexible exchange rates and the use of inflation targets as a nominal anchor. Likewise, the use of monetary aggregates in favor of the determination of a nominal interest rate as an instrument of monetary policy was abandoned. It is no exaggeration to say that the international financial crisis of 2008-2009 set a watershed in the transformation of central banking. As former U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Ben S. Bernanke points out, in 4 That country and other advanced economies, the critical turning point for monetary policy was the global financial crisis of 2007-2009.3 Fears of the worst global recession and the risk of deflation pushed benchmark rates in the major advanced economies to levels close to zero, and even in some of them, to negative territory in the following years. It also became clear that central banks should better integrate the objective of financial stability with that of price stability, especially in advanced economies. For several years, the latter saw the need to implement unconventional monetary policy measures that were considered transitory. As deflationary risks eased and economies consolidated their recovery, a period of monetary policy normalization began, in which monetary authorities began to raise their benchmark rates and gradually reverse extraordinary stimulus. However, this process was abruptly interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic and lockdown measures. During 2020, in the face of the deepest global recession since the Great Depression of the thirties of the last century, the central banks of the advanced economies not only fully and immediately reversed monetary normalization, but also implemented additional stimulus measures. For their part, the central banks of emerging economies relaxed their monetary policies and even some dabbled in unconventional measures. All this was possible since the perception of inflationary risk decreased in an overall way. Based on the above, we can anticipate that one of the first legacies of the pandemic crisis to monetary policy is permanence. 3 Ben S. Bernanke, "The New Tools of Monetary Policy", American Economic Review 110 n.4 (2020): 994, . 5 indefinite of unconventional policies, which before the health crisis were in a process of withdrawal. Likewise, the review of the Fed's long-term monetary policy strategy in August last year has laid the foundations for greater flexibility in the conduct of monetary policy in that country. What can we expect for the future of monetary policy? We will see it later, but for this we need to detail several aspects of the synthesis that I have just presented to you. 2.1. Causes of poor results and reforms Why were the central bank's performance in controlling inflation so poor during the seventies and eighties in almost the whole world? Based on this experience, three reasons can be cited why central banking may fail to preserve price stability according to the economic literature:4 (a) Due to short-term political pressures. There is evidence that central banks may be exposed to strong political pressures. This situation derives from the fact that the planning horizon of central banks is longer than that of the governments in turn. Another cause of the poor performance of central banks derives from trying to resolve economic distortions whose nature is not monetary with monetary policy. For example, uncompetitive market structures can lead to growth and job creation in the economy being at low levels in relation to social needs. In this context, using monetary policy to correct the problem would only lead to higher inflation, as happened in the United States at the beginning of the period known as The Great Inflation.5 (c) Lack of credible future commitment. This is a more subtle, but fundamental problem that has greatly influenced the architecture of modern central banking. When there is broad discretion in the conduct of monetary policy, monetary decision-makers may have incentives to deviate from the path that leads to price stability. This in order to produce short-term benefits in terms of production and employment. Faced with this situation, credibility in the commitment to maintain policies consistent with price stability may be lost and lead to equilibriums with higher levels of inflation than there would be if such credibility existed. In such circumstances, reducing discretion through a monetary policy framework that establishes a credible commitment to the future conduct of monetary policy contributes to reducing the problem. 5 Great Inflation, which stretched from 1965 to 1982, was a crucial period that led economists to rethink the policies of the Fed and other central banks. Likewise, the institutional arrangement that supports monetary policy is crucial in this process. Greater independence of the monetary authority in its administration and operation facilitates the consolidation of price stability, by mitigating the three problems described. The results of the reforms to the central banks were favorable since inflation was reduced and stabilized, first in the advanced economies and then in the emerging economies. However, new challenges and opportunities emerged from the "information economy", that is, one where services based on the use of knowledge and information become more relevant than manufacturing. In this context, central banking communication began to take on the core role it plays today. 2.2. The 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic From the mid-1980s to 2007 there was a period of relative calm following the Great Inflation of the seventies and early eighties. Inflation was low and relatively stable and a very prolonged economic expansion materialized. However, this period was interrupted by the outbreak of the subprime mortgage crisis in the United States, which gave rise to the international financial crisis of 2008-2009. The main problem faced by central banks was that the financial system ceased to fulfill its intermediation function and benchmark interest rates soon reached their effective lower bound. In response, these 10 Woodford, "Monetary policy in the information economy", 22. 10 institutions had to resort to unconventional monetary policy measures, i.e. tools without interest rates; these include the provision of liquidity, the purchase of assets and the commitment to future monetary policy actions. This is in order to influence the long part of the yield curve and reactivate credit markets to boost aggregate demand. Initially, it was envisaged that such extraordinary measures would be temporary. However, their presence has dragged on for more than a decade. Moreover, in response to the unprecedented real shock represented by the COVID19 pandemic, central banks again resorted to such measures. At present, benchmark rates are at historic lows and are not expected to rise in the near future, as is clear from communications from major central banks. Of particular note is the fact that the Federal Reserve System of the United States (the Fed), in August 2020, revised its long-term monetary policy strategy, in order to have greater flexibility. Some experts have even suggested that this move could lead to a more discretionary and less predictable and systematic approach to the conduct of monetary policy.11 The "quantitative stimulus" applied by the Fed due to the COVID-19 pandemic has raised the size of its balance sheet to historic levels. To visualize the scale of the intervention, it is enough to observe that before the US mortgage crisis the Fed's assets amounted to about one trillion dollars. By 2015, when the peak was reached before the sale began 11 Mickey D. Levy and Charles Plosser, "The Murky Future of Monetary Policy", Hoover Institution Economics Working Paper No. 20119, 1 de octubre de 2020, 8, . 11 of assets, their value exceeded four trillion dollars. And during 2020, the Fed's asset purchases increased rapidly to reach more than seven trillion dollars in less than a year. Finally, another fundamental change for central banking bequeathed by the international financial crisis was the integration of the objective of price stability with that of financial stability. The financial crisis of 2008-2009 showed that financial authorities did not adequately weigh systemic risk and that price stability did not guarantee financial stability. In response, advanced and emerging economies implemented financial reforms to improve the regulation and supervision of financial institutions and markets in order to limit systemic risk through the implementation of macroprudential policies. Explicitly or implicitly, central banks reinforced the goal of financial stability on their agenda. 2.3. The future of monetary policy To conclude this section, I would like to propose some considerations on the possible future of monetary policy. In advanced economies, a permanent integration of unconventional policy instruments into the central bank toolbox is to be expected, and it will take many years to complete the withdrawal of stimulus. In addition, in some of them, there is already an increase in discretion in the conduct of monetary policy, due to a more flexible monetary policy framework in terms of inflation targeting. Likewise, the effectiveness of communication in driving public expectations will be more important. 12 On the other hand, in emerging economies the situation is substantially different, since they are far from a problem of too low inflation and the role of their assets in international financial markets is different. Thus, it is to be expected that the use of conventional monetary policy instruments will prevail over unconventional ones and that limits on discretion will remain central to the effectiveness of monetary policy, in order to consolidate the credibility of its central banks. Capital flows will also remain a crucial factor in the conduct of monetary policy, as well as the consistency between communication and the use of its monetary policy instruments to contribute to the consolidation of price stability. 3. Innovation in the means of payment allows us to interact more easily, quickly and cheaply. But this innovation also presents new risks and challenges for monetary authorities. Central banks have a crucial role to play in this transformation because of our responsibility to preserve the smooth functioning of payment systems and contribute to greater financial inclusion, an effort that has been strengthened in recent years. In this sense, the promotion of electronic payments, as well as the promotion of greater interoperability and standardization in the systems and platforms that facilitate the clearing and settlement of electronic payments, are actions that 13 have helped to reduce the costs and timing of transactions between economic agents.12 We also have a duty to maintain a balance between risks and benefits in payment innovation, to ensure that money continues to serve its purpose properly. For example, payment systems are subject to strong scale or network effects, as the more users a system has, the more attractive it becomes to new users. Final considerations Central banking in the world faces formidable challenges that lead us to reflect on the best way to face them. By way of conclusion, I leave four reflections of the topics exposed on the future of central banking. First, we must recognize that central banks have been transforming according to the challenges they have faced in the economic and social context in order to meet their objective of price stability. In this sense, central banking, like the economy, is constantly evolving. Second, over the past decade the instruments at the central bank's disposal to conduct monetary policy have increased and transmission mechanisms over the economy have become more complex. Faced with this reality, it is increasingly important to consolidate the progress made over decades through reforms aimed at building confidence in the commitment of these institutions to long-term stability. It is also critical to recognize both the potential and limits of monetary policy to help the economy assimilate the short-term effects of shocks of various kinds. Third, together with various structural changes, technological innovation represents new challenges in crucial aspects for society. In particular, the 31 The digitalization of the financial system is directly related to three pillars of central banking: the implementation of monetary policy, the pursuit of financial stability and the proper functioning of payment systems. In this regard, central banks should explore and take advantage of the efficiency gains of digitalization, but they should not forget to assess the risks involved. In Mexico, where a large part of the population uses cash to make payments and is unbanked, the digitization of means of payment and the use of an electronic currency offer great opportunities in terms of efficiency and inclusion, but their design and implementation requires careful evaluation and planning. Finally, the incorporation at the international level of new issues for central banking responds to the need to build a more sustainable and inclusive economy. The role of central banks is crucial since these institutions are responsible for monitoring the sound development of the financial system, which is the main intermediary in an economy, and cannot be left out of such efforts. The implementation of environmental, social and governance criteria in the financial system contributes to the pursuit of financial stability that, explicitly or implicitly, is inherent in the mandates of modern central banks. Significant progress has been made in recent years at the international level, of which the Bank of Mexico is a part, but much remains to be done. Thanks a lot! 32

A manera de conclusin, dejo cuatro reflexiones de los temas expuestos sobre el futuro de la banca central. En tercero, junto con diversos cambios estructurales, la innovacin tecnolgica representa nuevos retos en aspectos cruciales para la sociedad. En particular, la 31 digitalizacin del sistema financiero se relaciona directamente con tres pilares de la banca central: la implementacin de la poltica monetaria, la procuracin de la estabilidad financiera y el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Al respecto, los bancos centrales deben explorar y aprovechar las ganancias en eficiencia de la digitalizacin, pero no deben olvidarse de evaluar los riesgos que conlleva. En Mxico, donde un gran parte de la poblacin usa el efectivo para realizar pagos y no est bancarizada, la digitalizacin de los medios de pago y el uso de una moneda electrnica ofrecen grandes oportunidades en trminos de eficiencia e inclusin, pero su diseo e instrumentacin requiere una evaluacin y planeacin cuidadosa. Por ltimo, la incorporacin a nivel internacional de nuevos temas para la banca central responde a la necesidad de construir una economa ms sostenible e inclusiva. El papel de los bancos centrales resulta crucial puesto que estas instituciones se encargan de vigilar el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero, que es el principal intermediario en una economa, y no pueden quedarse al margen de dichos esfuerzos. La implementacin de criterios ambientales, sociales y de gobernanza en el sistema financiero contribuye a la procuracin de la estabilidad financiera que, de manera explcita o implcita, es inherente a los mandatos de los bancos centrales modernos. Se ha logrado un avance importante en los ltimos aos a nivel internacional, del cual el Banco de Mxico es parte, pero queda mucho por hacer. Muchas gracias! 32

Title: 73 Banking Convention
text: 1 Remarks by the Governor of Banco de Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, on the occasion of the 73rd Banking Convention, Acapulco, Guerrero. April 22, 2010.  Governor of the State of Guerrero, accountant Carlos Zeferino Torreblanca Galindo  Mr. Municipal President of Acapulco, Dr. Manuel Anorve Banos  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Teacher Ernesto Cordero Arroyo  Mr. President of the National Banking and Securities Commission, doctor Guillermo Babatz Torres  Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, engineer Ignacio Deschamps Gonzalez  Dear Vice-Presidents of the Association of Banks of Mexico  Distinguished Special Guests  Ladies and Gentlemen It is a great honor for me to attend this 73rd Banking Convention now as Governor of the Bank of Mexico. I wish to thank the Association of Banks of Mexico and all its members for the fruitful interaction I was able to have with them during three years in my role as Secretary of Finance and Public Credit. I am sure that now, from the Central Institute, we will continue to collaborate in an equally fruitful way to consolidate a 1 2 National financial system increasingly stronger and more suitable to serve the ambitious expectations of growth and sustainable development that Mexico has. I. It is pertinent to remember that a year ago this annual banking convention was held when the Mexican economy was experiencing the most severe effects of the global crisis, aggravated in those days, in addition, by the economic repercussions, in terms of production and employment, that the influenza A(H1-N1) epidemic had. Today we are facing a moderately encouraging international environment with strong contrasts. It is a fact that the recovery of the world economy has continued during the first quarter of this year, even at a faster pace than anticipated, but it is also a fact that there are notable differences between countries. On the one hand, the progress of developed economies is modest and depends to a large extent on the maintenance of accommodative macroeconomic policies, which in turn represents a high fiscal vulnerability for these nations. On the other hand, most emerging economies have shown, both during the crisis and now, solid economic fundamentals and their growth has been encouraged by strong global demand for raw materials as well as a rebound in world trade. It is, therefore, a panorama that invites us to qualify optimism with caution. 2 3 For Mexico, the picture is also one of contrasts. While the signs of recovery in industry, especially those linked to the export of manufactures, are clear, the indicators of domestic demand are weak. In particular, private investment remains lethargic. This means that economic activity continues to fall short of its production potential. The recovery and consolidation of the international financial system has generally proceeded expeditiously. The main achievement to highlight is that the imminence of a systemic crisis at the global level has vanished, even though in many countries bank credit has not yet been reactivated. It is also worth mentioning the speed with which most emerging economies have regained their access to international financial markets, as well as the speed with which the different country risk measures of several emerging nations have improved. This is attributable to the strength of its macroeconomic fundamentals and has been noticeable in the case of Mexico. As a sample we have the country risk indicators related to the hedges for risks in sovereign bonds or CDS (Credit Default Swaps): a year ago the country risk of Spain and Brazil was lower than that of Mexico, today the situation is the reverse. This shows something that has been crucial in the evolution of several emerging economies: maintaining solid economic fundamentals pays well. Indeed, most emerging economies, such as Mexico, have worked for more than ten years to have fiscal discipline, a policy 3 4 Responsible monetary, a low level of indebtedness and in preserving the strength of its financial intermediation systems. Let's remember. The eruption of the financial crisis, among other consequences, generated an abrupt depreciation of the national currency. Over the course of four months alone, from September 2008 to January 2009, the peso price fell by more than 33 percent. This represented a great challenge for the Bank of Mexico, since it is well known that in the past significant depreciations of the nominal exchange rate were immediately transferred to prices, that is: they became inflation. However, the credibility of the Central Bank as the institution in charge of combating and anchoring inflation contributed to the fact that, despite the magnitude of the depreciation of the peso, it did not translate to all the prices of goods and services in the economy. Although it is also pertinent to remember that the sharp fall in economic activity, the increase in unemployment and the freezing of several public prices contributed to obtain this result. The truth is that the control of inflation that took place during 2009 allowed the real exchange rate to register a depreciation that has been a factor that today plays in favor of the recovery of economic activity. In fact, that depreciation of the real exchange rate was the foreseeable result for our country of the aftermath of a global financial crisis like the one that happened. The first sequel was the sudden and sharp collapse of our exports, in particular those directed to our main trading partner, a country where, incidentally, the epicenter of the 4 5 crisis. The second was that the availability of financial resources for emerging economies also dried up suddenly. The point to note is that the depreciation of the real exchange rate as an effective adjustment mechanism in the face of external shocks of this nature, only operates in economies with congruent macroeconomic frameworks, which has been precisely the case in Mexico. On the other hand, it should be noted that in the most acute phase of the crisis several prices did not plummet in our country as happened in others.
