It is plausible to attribute this phenomenon, at least in part, to the existence in Mexico of several strategic markets in which precarious or scarce competition allows bidders to maintain high prices in spite of weak demand. Hence the sense of urgency for Mexico that the H. Congress of the Union approves the Initiative sent by the Federal Executive to reform the Federal Law on Economic Competition. The benefits of increased competition are not, of course, limited to such competition generating lower rates of inflation. There are other very powerful arguments that underpin this urgency. I mention only two of them: first, greater competition in the markets would increase the potential growth rate of the Mexican economy, since resources would be allocated more efficiently, sectors of productive activity currently closed would be opened to investment with cutting-edge technologies and the cost of inputs would be reduced. Second, more competition would certainly have a direct impact on a huge redistribution of income, since more than 40 percent of the goods consumed by Mexican families who 5 6 they are in the lowest income deciles correspond to markets in which there is currently little competition. It is foreseeable, therefore, that in an environment of greater competition the prices of these goods tended to be lower with the consequent benefit for Mexicans with lower incomes. During 2010 the challenge facing the monetary policy of the Bank of Mexico has been different from that of the previous two years. As a result of tax measures and adjustments in public prices, as well as the erratic behavior of the prices of some fruits and vegetables, a significant increase in inflation was observed during the first three months of the year. It is worth mentioning that the Central Institute itself reported in a timely manner, since the end of 2009, about the possible impact on inflation of fiscal measures and has explained that since this impact is largely transitory, it will surely tend to dissipate from the beginning of 2011. Precisely for this reason, as the Bank has repeatedly said, it was not appropriate to take restrictive monetary policy measures immediately, unless the tax and adjustment measures in public prices already mentioned began to pollute the prices of goods and services that were not directly related to those adjustments. So far, indeed, that has not happened and, therefore, the monetary policy stance has not needed to be adjusted. To be more precise, the Governing Board has based this decision on the following factors: 6 7 First, changes in taxes and public prices have generated an increase in headline inflation that remained in line with the Bank of Mexico's forecast, which means that the price formation process in the rest of the economy has not been contaminated. Second, although the country's economic growth has been revived, it remains below its potential. Third, while still above the 3 percent target, inflation expectations for the medium and long term remain relatively stable. Fourth, wage increases have not generated inflationary pressures, and Fifth, exchange rate appreciation has mitigated potential pressures on the prices of tradable goods and on the production costs of those goods and services that use imported inputs. In any case, the Governing Board has said that "it will carefully monitor the trajectory of medium- and long-term inflation expectations, as well as other determinants of inflation that could warn about unexpected and widespread pressures on prices. In particular, attention will be paid to the speed with which the product gap will be closed." The anchoring of long-term inflation expectations, framed in an environment of strengthening public finances, has been reflected in the evolution of the yield curve in recent months. While the 7 8 The short part of the curve has remained stable, the long part of it shows a noticeable decrease so far this year. But this relative flattening of the yield curve also reflects the effect of the substantial capital inflows that have been observed in recent months. These capital inflows have resulted in a considerable appreciation of the national currency, which, as already mentioned, has helped to ease price pressures and led to less accommodative monetary conditions. The phenomenon described is not without risks because although part of the increase in capital inflows is explained by the perception of better prospects and fundamentals of the Mexican economy, another part is due to the expansionary monetary policy in the United States, which will inevitably have to end one day. When that happens, a sudden reversal of much of these capital flows could be generated. This forecast explains the decision of the Exchange Commission - in which both the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Mexico participate - to accumulate international reserves that allow the country to equip itself in the face of sudden changes in these flows, as these could seriously disrupt productive activity and employment. II. One of the first lessons from the global crisis was the undeniable relevance of the mandate by which central banks are obliged to pursue price stability. Indeed, virtually all central banks have as their priority, and unique in many cases, the objective of 8 9 ensure low and stable inflation. Such a mandate proved to be adequate also to overcome an unusual and profound fall in economic activity, in which even several countries were exposed to the risk of deflation. This shows, empirically, that such a mandate for price stability is in no way a mandate contrary to economic growth or job creation. Let me explain. A good part of the central banks of the industrialized economies adopted an openly expansionary policy in the face of the crisis, especially bearing in mind the lessons left by the Great Depression of the world of the 30s of the last century. This expansionary policy served to stabilize financial markets, restore their flows and prevent their collapse; it also helped stimulate economic growth. But all this could be done because the central banks of the most developed economies enjoy great credibility, built with many years of persistent, determined and effective fight against inflation. By contrast, during this crisis most emerging economies have not been able to go beyond certain narrow limits in the adoption of monetary stimulus. This is because its central banks have not yet fully consolidated decades of credibility based on a constant and determined fight against inflation. In the case of Mexico, the central bank responded to the recent crisis by adopting a loose monetary stance, which is evident if one looks at any index of monetary conditions and is even more obvious if one looks at any monetary conditions. 9 10 considers that we have negative real interest rates, given that the Overnight Interbank Interest Rate (which is the reference rate of monetary policy) is below the expected inflation rate for the year. The possibility that the Bank of Mexico has carried out this monetary easing effort is due to the fact that in the last 15 years there has been constant work to consolidate a reputation for monetary responsibility and credibility, which has been accompanied, it must also be said, by a sound fiscal policy. Now, perhaps in the future the Bank of Mexico will be able to expand its degrees of freedom in the administration of its monetary policy, and it is desirable that this happens. But it will only be able to do so by persevering in fulfilling its priority mandate to combat inflation and thus consolidate its credibility. In that context, it seems foolish to question the relevance of that mandate and to propose alternative experiments that would collapse what has been achieved in the field of credibility. It is worth reiterating: The mandate for price stability is by no means a mandate contrary to economic growth, but a necessary condition for sustained growth. III. Another lesson that, in a very dramatic way, the crisis has left us is that central banks, in coordination with other authorities, must 10 11 pay greater attention to the task of consolidating the financial stability of their respective countries. An apparent peculiarity of this global crisis was the sudden appearance of severe discontinuities in the functioning of global financial flows. These ruptures, unlike other crises, were not preceded by severe alterations in price indices or by inflationary triggers. They occurred in the midst of a more or less generalized stability in the variations of the price indices, they arose without significant deviations from the inflation targets in the main industrial economies. However, such shocks were clearly the result of an unhealthy expansion of credit; expansion that the central banks of those countries could not neutralize or combat in a timely manner, largely because it did not have a clear reflection or correlation in the price indices they use to detect inflationary pressures. "Ex post facto", after the fact, it is clear that this vertiginous growth of financial assets and liabilities was unsustainable, but it should also be clear to us that the global prudential framework in force until before the crisis did not serve to detect that risk in a timely manner and prevent it. The great global task now, in which central banks must play a decisive role, is to strengthen that prudential framework and timely warnings, which also means reinforcing their implicit responsibility to preserve financial stability. 11 12 Thus, the real great challenge that the global crisis has left central banks is not to alter their mandates so that they directly promote economic growth, but to broaden their perspective so that it also includes the preservation of the country's financial stability understood in a broad sense. This mission is closely linked to the role of central banks as lenders of last resort. Preserving financial stability is not an objective unrelated to that of combating inflation, but closely related to it. Both responsibilities support each other. Just as inflation has a clear corrosive effect on the wealth of families and nations, so financial instability cancels out sources of wealth creation. In both cases, instability - be it price or financial - is an insurmountable obstacle to achieving sustained economic growth. Even financial instability sooner or later can lead to a problem of higher inflation. And, to be clear, the pursuit of financial stability cannot and should not be the exclusive function of the central bank, but also of the tax authorities and regulatory commissions. Precisely, meeting the challenge of ensuring financial stability requires a great deal of collaboration and cooperation between different authorities and regulators. In this regard, I welcome the fact that there is a great willingness to collaborate and cooperate between the Bank of Mexico, the Ministry of Finance, the National Banking and Securities Commission and the Institute for the Protection of Bank Savings, so that we can further strengthen the 12 13 financial stability and minimize the chances of a systemic crisis in our country. In fact, the objective of financial stability goes beyond national borders. Hence, the Mexican financial authorities are also participating in a coordinated manner in the international forums that have recently emerged to discuss these issues. IV. It is a fact that the banks in Mexico not only endured the onslaught of the crisis without major shocks but are, at least from the point of view of their capital index, of 17.25 percent on average, in splendid conditions to fully support the growth of the country. In this regard, I reiterate the invitation I made to the Association of Banks of Mexico at the end of last year, when I was still Secretary of Finance. It was an invitation to work shoulder to shoulder to achieve conditions that would stimulate credit growth in our country. I widely acknowledge the effort made in this line by the Association and its member banks, but it has not been enough. The figures as of March for total financing to the private sector continue to fall. I understand that the global crisis has exacerbated the perception of risk and that this explains a certain reluctance to undertake and support new projects. However, I firmly believe that with the capabilities of credit institutions, coupled with the collaboration of development banks and the best 13 14 In the economic perspective, this desirable credit expansion may be carried out carefully and will not put intermediaries at risk. If in Mexico we manage to get financing to the private sector at least to levels similar to that reached in economies equivalent in size, the country's potential Gross Domestic Product could grow substantially. This consideration should be another incentive for us to join forces and once again the national banking system becomes an effective promoter of Mexico's economic growth. Thanks a lot. 14
text_original: 1 Palabras del Gobernador de Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, con motivo de la 73 Convencin Bancaria, Acapulco, Guerrero. 22 de abril de 2010.  Seor Gobernador del Estado de Guerrero, contador Carlos Zeferino Torreblanca Galindo  Seor Presidente Municipal de Acapulco, doctor Manuel Aorve Baos  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, maestro Ernesto Cordero Arroyo  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, doctor Guillermo Babatz Torres  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, ingeniero Ignacio Deschamps Gonzlez  Estimados Vicepresidentes de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico  Distinguidos invitados especiales  Seoras y seores Es para m un gran honor acudir a esta 73 Convencin Bancaria ahora como Gobernador del Banco de Mxico. Deseo agradecer a la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico y a todos sus miembros la fructfera interaccin que pude tener con ellos durante tres aos en mi papel como Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico. Estoy seguro de que ahora, desde el Instituto Central, seguiremos colaborando de manera igualmente fecunda para consolidar un 1 2 sistema financiero nacional cada da ms fuerte e idneo para servir a las ambiciosas expectativas de crecimiento y desarrollo sostenible que tiene Mxico. I. Es pertinente recordar que hace un ao esta convencin anual de la banca se realiz cuando la economa mexicana experimentaba los efectos ms severos de la crisis global, agravados en esos das, adems, por las repercusiones econmicas, en trminos de produccin y empleo, que tuvo la epidemia de influenza A(H1N1). Hoy estamos ante un entorno internacional moderadamente alentador y de fuertes contrastes. Es un hecho que la recuperacin de la economa mundial ha seguido durante el primer trimestre de este ao, incluso a un ritmo mayor del anticipado, pero tambin es un hecho que hay notables diferencias entre pases. Por una parte, el avance de las economas desarrolladas es modesto y depende en gran medida del sostenimiento de polticas macroeconmicas acomodaticias, lo que a su vez representa para esas naciones una elevada vulnerabilidad fiscal. Por la otra, la mayora de las economas emergentes han mostrado, tanto durante la crisis como ahora, slidos fundamentos econmicos y su crecimiento se ha visto alentado por la fuerte demanda global de materias primas as como por un repunte del comercio mundial. Es, pues, un panorama que invita a matizar el optimismo con la cautela. 2 3 Para Mxico el panorama tambin es de contrastes. Mientras que las seales de recuperacin en la industria, especialmente en la vinculada a la exportacin de manufacturas, son claras, los indicadores de la demanda interna son dbiles. En concreto, la inversin privada permanece en el letargo. Esto significa que la actividad econmica contina por debajo de su potencial de produccin. La recuperacin y consolidacin del sistema financiero internacional ha procedido, en trminos generales, de forma expedita. El principal logro a destacar es que la inminencia de una crisis sistmica a nivel global se ha desvanecido, aun cuando en muchos pases el crdito bancario an no se ha reactivado. Tambin merece mencionarse la rapidez con la que la mayor parte de las economas emergentes han recobrado su acceso a los mercados financieros internacionales, as como la velocidad con la que las diferentes medidas de riesgopas de varias naciones emergentes han mejorado. Esto es atribuible a la solidez de sus fundamentos macroeconmicos y ha sido notorio en el caso de Mxico. Como una muestra tenemos los indicadores de riesgo pas relativos a las coberturas para riesgos en bonos soberanos o CDS (Credit Default Swaps): hace un ao el riesgopas de Espaa y de Brasil era menor que el de Mxico, hoy la situacin es la inversa. Esto evidencia algo que ha sido crucial en la evolucin de varias economas emergentes: mantener fundamentos econmicos slidos paga bien. En efecto, la mayora de las economas emergentes, como Mxico, han trabajado desde hace ms de diez aos en tener disciplina fiscal, una poltica 3 4 monetaria responsable, un bajo nivel de endeudamiento y en preservar la fortaleza de sus sistemas de intermediacin financiera. Hagamos memoria. La erupcin de la crisis financiera, entre otras consecuencias, gener una depreciacin abrupta de la moneda nacional. Tan slo en el transcurso de cuatro meses, de septiembre de 2008 a enero de 2009, la cotizacin del peso descendi ms del 33 por ciento. Esto represent un gran desafo para el Banco de Mxico, pues es bien sabido que en el pasado depreciaciones significativas del tipo de cambio nominal se trasladaron inmediatamente a los precios, esto es: se volvieron inflacin. Empero, la credibilidad del Banco Central como la Institucin encargada de combatir y anclar la inflacin contribuy a que, pese a la magnitud de la depreciacin del peso, sta no se trasladara a todos los precios de bienes y servicios en la economa. Aunque tambin es pertinente recordar que la fuerte cada en la actividad econmica, el aumento en el desempleo y la congelacin de varios precios pblicos coadyuvaron para obtener este resultado. Lo cierto es que el control de la inflacin que tuvo lugar durante 2009 permiti que el tipo de cambio real registrara una depreciacin que ha sido un factor que hoy juega a favor de la recuperacin de la actividad econmica. De hecho, esa depreciacin del tipo de cambio real fue el resultado previsible para nuestro pas de las secuelas de una crisis financiera mundial como la que sucedi. La primera secuela fue el fuerte y sbito desplome de nuestras exportaciones, en particular aquellas dirigidas a nuestro principal socio comercial, pas en donde, dicho sea de paso, se registr el epicentro de la 4 5 crisis. La segunda fue que la disponibilidad de recursos financieros para las economas emergentes se sec tambin de manera repentina. El punto a destacar es que la depreciacin del tipo de cambio real como mecanismo eficaz de ajuste ante choques externos de esta naturaleza, slo opera en economas con marcos macroeconmicos congruentes, lo cual ha sido justamente el caso de Mxico. Por otro lado, debe advertirse que en la fase ms aguda de la crisis varios precios no se desplomaron en nuestro pas como sucedi en otros. Es plausible atribuir este fenmeno, cuando menos en parte, a la existencia en Mxico de varios mercados estratgicos en los que una precaria o escasa competencia permite a los oferentes mantener precios altos a despecho de la debilidad de la demanda. De ah el sentido de urgencia que tiene para Mxico el que el H. Congreso de la Unin apruebe la Iniciativa enviada por el Ejecutivo Federal para reformar la Ley Federal de Competencia Econmica. Los beneficios de una mayor competencia no se limitan, desde luego, a que tal competencia genere menores tasas de inflacin. Hay otros argumentos muy poderosos que sustentan esta urgencia. Menciono slo dos de ellos: primero, con una mayor competencia en los mercados aumentara la tasa potencial de crecimiento de la economa mexicana, ya que se asignaran ms eficientemente los recursos, se abriran a la inversin con tecnologas de punta sectores de actividad productiva actualmente cerrados y se abatira el costo de los insumos. Segundo, con toda seguridad, una mayor competencia incidira directamente en una enorme redistribucin del ingreso, ya que ms del 40 por ciento de las mercancas que consumen las familias mexicanas que 5 6 se encuentran en los deciles ms bajos de ingresos corresponden a mercados en los que hoy da hay escasa competencia. Es previsible, por tanto, que en un entorno de mayor competencia los precios de esos bienes tendieran a ser menores con el consecuente beneficio para los mexicanos de menores ingresos. Durante 2010 el desafo que enfrenta la poltica monetaria del Banco de Mxico ha sido diferente al de los dos aos anteriores. Como resultado de las medidas tributarias y de ajustes en los precios pblicos, as como del comportamiento errtico de los precios de algunas frutas y verduras, se observ un aumento significativo de la inflacin durante los tres primeros meses del ao. Cabe mencionar que el propio Instituto Central inform oportunamente, desde fines de 2009, acerca del posible impacto sobre la inflacin de las medidas fiscales y ha explicado que dado que dicho impacto en gran medida es transitorio, seguramente tender a disiparse a partir del inicio de 2011. Precisamente por esta razn, como ha dicho reiteradamente el Banco, no era oportuno tomar medidas restrictivas de poltica monetaria de forma inmediata, salvo que las medidas tributarias y de ajuste en los precios pblicos ya referidas comenzasen a contaminar los precios de bienes y servicios que no estuvieran directamente relacionados con esos ajustes. Hasta el momento, efectivamente, eso no ha sucedido y, por tanto, no ha sido preciso ajustar la postura de poltica monetaria. Para ser ms precisos, la Junta de Gobierno ha basado esta decisin en los siguientes factores: 6 7 Primero, los cambios en impuestos y en precios pblicos han generado un incremento en la inflacin general que se mantuvo en lnea con la previsin del Banco de Mxico, lo que significa que no se ha contaminado el proceso de formacin de precios en el resto de la economa. Segundo, a pesar de que se ha reactivado el crecimiento econmico del pas, ste contina por debajo de su potencial. Tercero, aunque siguen por arriba de la meta de 3 por ciento, las expectativas de inflacin para el mediano y largo plazos permanecen relativamente estables. Cuarto, los aumentos salariales no han generado presiones inflacionarias, y Quinto, la apreciacin del tipo de cambio ha mitigado posibles presiones sobre precios de bienes comerciables y sobre los costos de produccin de aquellos bienes y servicios que utilizan insumos importados. En todo caso, la Junta de Gobierno ha dicho que vigilar cuidadosamente la trayectoria de las expectativas de inflacin de mediano y de largo plazo, as como otros determinantes de la inflacin que pudieran alertar acerca de presiones inesperadas y de carcter generalizado sobre los precios. En particular se pondr atencin a la velocidad con la cual se cerrar la brecha del producto. El anclaje de las expectativas de inflacin de largo plazo, enmarcado en un entorno de fortalecimiento de las finanzas pblicas, se ha reflejado en la evolucin de la curva de rendimientos en los ltimos meses. Mientras que la 7 8 parte corta de la curva se ha mantenido estable, la parte larga de la misma muestra una notoria disminucin en lo que va del ao. Pero este relativo aplanamiento de la curva de rendimientos tambin refleja el efecto de las sustanciales entradas de capital que se han observado en los ltimos meses. Estas entradas de capital se han traducido en una apreciacin considerable de la moneda nacional, la cual, como ya se dijo, ha contribuido a atenuar las presiones sobre los precios y ha conducido a condiciones monetarias menos laxas. El fenmeno descrito no est exento de riesgos pues si bien una parte del incremento en las entradas de capital se explica por la percepcin de mejores perspectivas y fundamentos de la economa mexicana, otra parte obedece a la poltica monetaria expansiva en Estados Unidos, que inevitablemente tendr que concluir algn da. Cuando eso ocurra se podra generar una reversin repentina de buena parte de esos flujos de capitales. Esta previsin explica la decisin de la Comisin de Cambios  en la que participan tanto la Secretara de Hacienda como el Banco de Mxico  de acumular reservas internacionales que permitan al pas pertrecharse ante sbitos cambios en dichos flujos, pues estos podran trastornar seriamente la actividad productiva y el empleo. II. Una de las primeras enseanzas que arroj la crisis mundial fue la innegable pertinencia del mandato por el cual los bancos centrales estn obligados a procurar la estabilidad de precios. En efecto, prcticamente todos los bancos centrales tienen como objetivo prioritario, y nico en muchos casos, de 8 9 procurar una inflacin baja y estable. Tal mandato mostr ser adecuado tambin para sortear una cada inslita y profunda de la actividad econmica, en la que incluso varios pases quedaron expuestos al riesgo de una deflacin. Eso demuestra, de forma emprica, que tal mandato a favor de la estabilidad de precios no es, en modo alguno, un mandato contrario al crecimiento econmico o a la generacin de empleos. Me explico. Buena parte de los bancos centrales de las economas industrializadas adoptaron ante la crisis una poltica abiertamente expansiva, sobre todo teniendo en mente las lecciones que dejara la Gran Depresin mundial de los aos 30 del siglo pasado. Esa poltica expansiva sirvi para estabilizar los mercados financieros, restablecer sus flujos y evitar su colapso; tambin auxili a estimular el crecimiento econmico. Pero todo ello se pudo hacer porque los bancos centrales de las economas ms desarrolladas gozan de una gran credibilidad, construida con muchos aos de persistente, decidido y efectivo combate a la inflacin. Por contraste, durante esta crisis la mayora de las economas emergentes no han podido ir ms all de ciertos lmites estrechos en la adopcin de estmulos monetarios. Esto debido a que sus bancos centrales an no han consolidado plenamente dcadas de credibilidad fundada en un constante y decidido combate a la inflacin. En el caso de Mxico el banco central respondi a la reciente crisis adoptando una postura monetaria laxa, lo que es evidente si uno observa cualquier ndice de condiciones monetarias y es an ms obvio si se 9 10 considera que tenemos tasas de inters reales negativas, dado que la Tasa de Inters Interbancaria a un da (que es la tasa de referencia de la poltica monetaria) est por debajo de la tasa de inflacin esperada para el ao. La posibilidad de que el Banco de Mxico haya llevado a cabo este esfuerzo de relajacin monetaria se debe a que en los ltimos 15 aos ha habido un trabajo constante para consolidar una reputacin de responsabilidad monetaria y credibilidad, que ha estado acompaada, tambin hay que decirlo, de una slida poltica fiscal. Ahora bien, quiz en el futuro el Banco de Mxico podr ampliar sus grados de libertad en la administracin de su poltica monetaria, y es deseable que eso suceda. Pero slo podr hacerlo de perseverar en el cumplimiento de su mandato prioritario de combatir la inflacin y consolidar as su credibilidad. En ese contexto se antoja insensato poner en entredicho la pertinencia de ese mandato y proponer experimentos alternativos que derrumbaran lo alcanzado en el terreno de la credibilidad. Vale la pena reiterarlo: El mandato por la estabilidad de precios no es, en modo alguno, un mandato contrario al crecimiento econmico, sino una condicin necesaria para el crecimiento sostenido. III. Otra leccin que, en forma por dems dramtica, nos ha dejado la crisis es que los bancos centrales, en coordinacin con otras autoridades, deben 10 11 prestar mayor atencin a la tarea de consolidar la estabilidad financiera de sus respectivos pases. Una aparente peculiaridad de esta crisis global fue la aparicin repentina de discontinuidades graves en el funcionamiento de los flujos financieros globales. Estas rupturas, a diferencia de otras crisis, no fueron antecedidas por alteraciones severas en los ndices de precios o por disparos inflacionarios. Se dieron en medio de una estabilidad ms o menos generalizada en las variaciones de los ndices de precios, surgieron sin que se registrasen desviaciones significativas respecto de las metas inflacionarias en las principales economas industriales. Sin embargo, tales perturbaciones fueron claramente resultado de una expansin insana del crdito; expansin que los bancos centrales de esos pases no pudieron neutralizar o combatir oportunamente, en gran medida porque no tuvo un reflejo o un correlato claro en los ndices de precios que usan para detectar las presiones inflacionarias. Ex post facto, despus de los hechos, queda claro que este vertiginoso crecimiento de activos y pasivos financieros era insostenible, pero tambin debera quedarnos claro que el marco prudencial global vigente hasta antes de la crisis no sirvi para detectar oportunamente ese riesgo y prevenirlo. Ahora la gran tarea mundial, en la que los bancos centrales deben desempear un papel decisivo, es reforzar ese marco prudencial y de alertas oportunas, lo que significa tambin reforzar la responsabilidad implcita que tienen de preservar la estabilidad financiera. 11 12 As, el verdadero gran desafo que la crisis global les ha dejado a los bancos centrales no es el de alterar sus mandatos para que promuevan directamente el crecimiento econmico, sino ampliar su perspectiva para que abarque tambin la preservacin de la estabilidad financiera del pas entendida en un sentido amplio. Esta misin est estrechamente vinculada a la funcin de los bancos centrales como prestamistas de ltima instancia. Preservar la estabilidad financiera no es un objetivo ajeno al de combatir la inflacin, sino estrechamente emparentado con l. Una y otra responsabilidades se apoyan entre s. As como la inflacin tiene un claro efecto corrosivo sobre la riqueza de las familias y de las naciones, del mismo modo la inestabilidad financiera cancela las fuentes de creacin de riqueza. En ambos casos, la inestabilidad  sea de precios, sea financiera es un obstculo infranqueable para lograr el crecimiento econmico sostenido. Incluso la inestabilidad financiera tarde o temprano puede conducir a un problema de mayor inflacin. Y, siendo claros, la procuracin de la estabilidad financiera no puede ni debe ser exclusivamente funcin del banco central, sino tambin de las autoridades hacendarias y de las comisiones reguladoras. De manera precisa, hacer frente al desafo de garantizar la estabilidad financiera requiere de una gran colaboracin y cooperacin entre las distintas autoridades y reguladores. En este sentido celebro que exista una gran disposicin de colaboracin y cooperacin entre el Banco de Mxico, la Secretara de Hacienda, la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores y el Instituto para la Proteccin del Ahorro Bancario, para que podamos fortalecer an ms la 12 13 estabilidad financiera y minimizar las probabilidades de una crisis sistmica en nuestro pas. De hecho, el objetivo de estabilidad financiera rebasa las fronteras nacionales. De ah que las autoridades financieras mexicanas tambin estemos participando de manera coordinada en los foros internacionales que han surgido recientemente para discutir estos temas. IV. Es un hecho que la banca en Mxico no slo soport sin mayores sobresaltos el embate de la crisis sino que se encuentra, al menos desde el punto de vista de su ndice de capital, de 17.25 por ciento en promedio, en esplndidas condiciones para apoyar de lleno el crecimiento del pas. En este sentido, reitero la invitacin que hice a la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico a fines del ao pasado, cuando an era secretario de Hacienda. Fue una invitacin a trabajar hombro con hombro para lograr condiciones que permitan estimular el crecimiento del crdito en nuestro pas. Reconozco ampliamente el esfuerzo que han hecho en esta lnea la Asociacin y sus bancos miembros, pero no ha sido suficiente. Las cifras a marzo del financiamiento total al sector privado siguen cayendo. Entiendo que la crisis global ha exacerbado la percepcin de riesgo y que ello explica cierta reticencia para emprender y apoyar nuevos proyectos. Sin embargo, creo firmemente que con las capacidades de las instituciones de crdito, aunadas a la colaboracin de la banca de desarrollo y a las mejores 13 14 perspectivas econmicas, es posible que esa deseable expansin del crdito se realice de forma cuidadosa y no ponga en riesgo a los intermediarios. Si en Mxico logrsemos que el financiamiento al sector privado llegase al menos a niveles similares al que alcanza en economas equivalentes en tamao, el Producto Interno Bruto potencial del pas podra llegar a crecer sustancialmente. Esta consideracin debe ser otro incentivo para que unamos fuerzas y nuevamente el sistema bancario nacional se convierta en un efectivo promotor del crecimiento econmico de Mxico. Muchas gracias. 14

Title: Lessons from the financial crisis in Mexico
text: Lessons from the Financial Crisis in Mexico Remarks by Manuel Sanchez Deputy Governor The Bank of Mexico at the Seventh China International Finance Forum Pudong, Shanghai October 17, 2010 I would like to thank the organizers of the China International Finance Forum for the opportunity to participate, for a second time, in this important annual conference. It is a privilege to be back in this beautiful country and to take part in this forum in the opening session, which is devoted to the financial industry and financial cooperation. On this occasion, I would like to share some lessons with you from the recent global crisis as it affected Mexico. My central argument will be that the factors that led to the crisis in the United States and other advanced countries were not present in many emerging economies, including Mexico. Although several explanations can be postulated for this observation, the regulatory and supervisory framework in many emerging economies seems to have played a crucially positive role. Also, the implementation of sound macroeconomic and financial policies likely exerted a favorable influence. Causes and effects of the global meltdown There is a consensus that a combination of factors contributed to the gestation of the recent global crisis. The various underlying elements that triggered the boom had at least one element in common: they all encouraged unsustainable risk taking by market participants. Highly leveraged positions were widespread, and they were based on the assumption that past gains from increasing housing prices would continue into the indefinite future. 2 As we now know, this enthusiasm created a bubble in the credit and housing markets that, as is always the case, ended in a bust. This collapse confirmed, once again, that asset prices cannot go up for too long, unless they are backed by fundamentals which are not always clear. In searching for the causes of the crisis, one would like to identify the environment that encouraged the generalized underestimation of risks. By environment, I mean a set of institutions and economic policies that likely led to this untenable behavior. Even though some empirical research in this area has been undertaken, the relative importance of the causes is still being debated. Let me start by arguing that financial innovation cannot be a cause of the crisis. It is, rather, a means to an end, like risk diversification and hedging. Loan securitization and operations with derivatives, such as credit default swaps, which were used intensively during the years prior to the crisis, certainly served as vehicles for credit expansion. Their utilization allowed many market participants to increase their leverage in a highly interconnected and complicated way. Those products, however, were only instruments but not the cause of the turmoil. For expedience, I would like to classify the most commonly identified conditions for the crisis, as cyclical and structural. Regarding the former, two types of factors stand out. One refers to the unusually low interest rates that prevailed before the crisis, making borrowing cheap and causing asset prices to 3 rise. Authors diverge in their views regarding the source and relevance of this factor. While some economists argue that low interest rates mainly reflected the expansionary monetary policy prevailing in the United States and other developed economies, others interpret those rates as a result of excess global savings over intended investment. Indeed, there is an ongoing discussion about the importance of the possible deviation of U.S. monetary policy from the correct Taylor rule in nurturing the crisis. Although various empirical studies attribute different weights to monetary policy in the generation of the crisis, most of them recognize that it did play a certain role.1 The other type of cyclical conditions encompasses policies that were aimed at promoting the expansion of mortgage lending. Stimulus measures included fiscal subsidies for borrowers, as well as credit targets for financial intermediaries. For example, policies to make housing affordable for lowincome people and the promotion of securitization by government-sponsored enterprises likely contributed to the boom of mortgage credit in the United States. As for the structural factors, at the time, financial institutions had a poor regulatory and supervisory framework that facilitated excessive risk taking. Deficiencies included weak capitalization and liquidity standards for 1 For more on this controversy see, for example, Bernanke, Ben S., Monetary Policy and the Housing Bubble, presented at the Annual Meeting of American Economic Association, Atlanta, Georgia, January 3, 2010 and Taylor, John B., The Fed and the Crisis: A replay to Ben Bernanke, WSJ, January 11, 2010. 4 intermediaries and government guarantees for investors and institutions, partly as a consequence of a too big to fail policy. Some examples of the resulting arrangements that reflected inadequate incentives were: (a) compensation schemes in banks that privileged short-term gains in structuring financial products at the expense of adequate due diligence; (b) deficient risk evaluation of complex credit securities by rating agencies; (c) propagation of quasi-bank intermediaries that were not properly regulated; and (d) a high degree of leveraging by financial institutions, which probably expected government support in the event of problems. Provided that the list of causes is reasonably complete, preventing future crises would seem to require only substituting such causes with the opposite conditions. Unfortunately, this prescription is too blunt to be useful. Any list of factors is bound to be incomplete, not only to explain the recent crisis but to anticipate future ones. More research is needed to confirm a set of sufficient conditions for crises. In any event, the identified factors would have to be general, so no mechanical application could be feasible or even desirable. Let me turn now to the effects of the crisis. As I said, although the epicenter of the turmoil was the United States, many other economies were severely affected. Contagion to the rest of the world occurred first through well-known financial channels, depressing stock, currency and debt prices. The widespread financial instability came in the form of a global flight to safety, i.e., flight to 5 risk-free assets such as U.S. Treasury bills, in which country-specific factors performed, in general, a secondary function. The stress on financial markets was accompanied by intense real effects, which were disseminated by a plunge in international trade and commodity prices. As a result, world GDP contracted by 0.6% in 2009 after having grown 3.0% in 2008 and 5.2% in 2007.2 In Mexico, the crisis had severe repercussions for the financial markets, especially in the form of a sharp depreciation of the peso against the U. S. dollar. Additionally, a fall in manufacturing exports, the reduction of international oil prices and a contraction in workers remittances from abroad constrained Mexicos economic activity. To partly offset these factors, the Mexican authorities implemented several measures. In the foreign exchange market, actions included interventions and U.S. dollar auctions with and without a minimum price for financial institutions; the agreement of a dollar liquidity swap line with the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank for US30 billion; and the acquisition of a precautionary Flexible Credit Line (FCL) for around US47 billion from the International Monetary Fund. With the exception of the FCL, which has been renewed because of its low funding cost, all these measures have been suspended. 2 IMF World Economic Outlook April 2010. 6 In the domestic market, the Bank of Mexico auctioned purchases of long-term bonds and interest rate swaps with financial intermediaries. This did not noticeably affect the size of the central banks balance sheet. Additionally, the Bank of Mexico reduced its policy interest rate by 375 basis points during the first seven months of 2009 and since then has left it unchanged at 4.5 percent. During 2008 and 2009, various fiscal measures were also implemented which included some tax incentives for employment, the freezing of public-sector fees and fares, and increased government expenditures in infrastructure. Government-owned development banks also launched temporary guarantee programs to facilitate the refinancing of commercial paper issued by businesses and non-bank financial firms. In spite of these measures, in 2009 Mexicos GDP fell by 6.5 percent. This profound effect from the crisis mainly reflects the economic integration of Mexico with the United States, as illustrated by the fact that more than 80% of Mexicos manufacturing exports are sent to its northern neighbor. Fortunately, since the second half of 2009 the Mexican economy has exhibited an upturn. The Bank of Mexico estimates that GDP will grow between 4% and 5% in 2010 and between 3.2% and 4.2% in 2011. The lack of an autonomous crisis in Latin America Notwithstanding the negative effects of the global crisis, many countries did not experience an autonomous crisis of the type observed in the United States and 7 other developed economies. To different degrees and features, this group of countries encompasses many emerging economies, such as major Latin American countries.3 One common characteristic of these non-crisis countries during the years prior to the global crisis was the absence of an explosive growth of mortgage lending and housing prices. Even though in several countries loan expansion was relatively high, this dynamism reverted and corrective measures were implemented once signs of portfolio deterioration started to appear. In particular, as a reflection of the business cycle, credit in Latin America slowed and even contracted during this period. Negative conditions affected the ability of borrowers to repay their debts, making non-performing loan ratios rise beginning in 2008. However, loan portfolio deteriorated moderately and did not reach unmanageable levels. Thanks to their high loan-loss reserves, banks continued to function normally, without having any significant pressures of liquidity and even exhibiting profitability during the crisis. Capital adequacy remained stable at levels higher than 10% during the crisis, above the international 8% standard.4 What might explain this performance? The absence of or weaker presence of the aforementioned causes of the crisis seems to have set non-crisis countries 3 In what follows and to different degrees, we include in the Latin America group Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru and Venezuela. 4 For more information, see Gallego, Sonsoles et al. The Impact of the Global Economic and Financial Crisis on Central Eastern and Southeastern Europe and Latin America, Documentos Ocasionales 1002, Banco de Espana, 2010. 8 apart. While each economy has its own peculiarities, especially related to the state of development of its financial system, certain factors appear to be common. First, most Latin American countries had implemented prudent monetary policies. These economies tended to have relatively conservative monetary stances because their average inflation has historically been higher than that of developed countries and, often, the process of convergence to price stability had not yet been completed. Second, most countries in Latin America had not implemented particularly aggressive financial policies to encourage mortgage credit expansion. Although many countries have active housing public institutions and do give tax incentives to mortgage borrowers, their government-backed securitization was relatively confined due to the low stage of development of this market. Third, the regulatory and supervisory frameworks in many non-crisis countries appear, in certain ways, to be stricter than that of developed countries. It is in this area where most Latin American countries have taken important steps in strengthening their financial systems. In particular, bank capital and liquidity standards, including those related to foreign currency positions, have been raised, supervision has improved, and risk controls have been tightened. Additionally, during the previous decade, most Latin American countries had adopted a flexible-exchange rate regime and developed their domestic debt 9 markets. These measures, together with the regulations on banks foreign currency positions, led to a reduction of foreign-currency mismatches that contributed to the macroeconomic resilience during the global financial shock.5 Lessons from the Mexican experience Like other Latin American countries, Mexico did not experience a banking collapse during the recent financial turmoil. The domestic recession made delinquency rates rise, especially of consumer lending, which had expanded significantly during the preceding years, mainly due to laxer origination standards. The rest of the loan portfolio revealed a smaller deterioration and, in particular, the quality of the mortgage portfolio declined slightly. During the economic slump, the banking system maintained strong solvency and profitability indicators. This performance resulted from generally prudent banking practices, which were shaped by lessons from the Mexican crisis of the mid 1990s. That catastrophe underlined the need for sound macroeconomic policies. The reforms that were implemented in the aftermath of the crisis included the adoption of a flexible exchange-rate regime, the strengthening of the fiscal position, extending the domestic-debt yield curve to 30 years, and the implementation of independent monetary policy committed to price stability. 5 See Caruana, Jaime, Financial Globalization, the Crisis and Latin America speech at the XLVI Meeting of Central Bank Governors of the American Continent and LXXXVII Meeting of Central Bank Governors of Latin America and Spain, 14 May 2009. 10 These policies provided the banking system and the economy with a stable environment in which to operate. The crisis of the mid 1990s also evidenced that the regulation and supervision of banks were inadequate. The capital of the banks had been depleted as a consequence of risk mismanagement. To overcome structural limitations, Mexico implemented profound measures to enhance the capital and liquidity of banks and to improve their appraisal of risks. Some of these actions have made Mexican regulations tougher than that of other countries.6 One important measure was the removal of all restrictions on foreign investment in banks, something which helped to capitalize and modernize the financial system. Foreign banks in Mexico have promoted efficiency through competition and transfer of expertise. Since foreign banks can only operate through subsidiaries, not branches, they are subject to the same regulation and supervision as domestic banks. A significant regulatory improvement was the definition of banks capital composition. Among other requirements, investments in financial institutions must be fully deducted from core capital; deferred taxes cannot exceed 10% of core capital; and in order to be computed as part of core capital, subordinated debt must be allowed to absorb loses. At the beginning of the recent global 6 See Porzecanski, Arturo C., Latin America: the Missing Financial Crisis, Studies and Perspectives Series, ECLAC, United Nations, October 2009. 11 crisis, the capital adequacy ratio of the Mexican banking system was 16%, twice as high as that recommended under the Basel Accords. Additionally, Mexicos central bank issued prudential regulations for banks foreign currency operations. These intermediaries are required to maintain liquid foreign currency assets on a daily basis sufficient to face short-term foreign currency liabilities. Banks medium-term liabilities denominated in foreign exchange cannot exceed 1.83 times their capital. Their net position in a foreign currency cannot surpass 15% of their core capital. To improve risk management, the Bank of Mexico and the National Banking and Securities Commission established requirements for banks that undertake derivatives operations, which included the compulsory creation of risk management units and upper bounds on the types of structured notes that can be issued. Financial and credit derivatives were adopted gradually by the banking system, under control and supervision. The painful experience of the crisis of the 1990s seems to have also made banks and the public more risk-averse in granting and taking on credit. Intermediaries strengthened their own screening of customers, risk evaluation procedures, and product characteristics in order to develop resilience to possible stress situations, such as spikes in interest rates and unemployment. This was particularly the case in the design of mortgage products, which in Mexico, do not allow for negative amortization. In addition, most mortgage products are based on fixed nominal interest rates and monthly payments. 12 Finally, although the Mexican banking system was in a strong position to face the international crisis, additional strengthening of the regulatory and supervisory framework is required in order to reduce the likelihood of a domestic systemic crisis. This includes the improvement of capital, liquidity and provisioning requirements, as well as expedient resolution mechanisms for insolvent banks. Concluding Remarks The global financial crisis unveiled a combination of causal factors, including low interest rates, excessive credit promotion policies, and inadequate financial regulation and supervision in advanced economies. In contrast, many emerging economies had already learned significant lessons from previous crises. The implementation of sound macroeconomic policies, the aversion of households to excessive debt, banks more prudent approach to lending and stricter financial regulations prevented the emergence of problems. In Mexico, major macroeconomic and financial reforms have certainly paid off. The deepening of this process, especially in macro prudential supervision and the strengthening of the regulatory and supervisory framework for financial institutions, promises to be a challenging and rewarding endeavor. 13

Title: 60th anniversary of the Center for Economic Research of the Faculty of Economics of the UANL
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, during the 60th Anniversary of the Center for Economic Research of the Faculty of Economics of the UANL. September 10, 2020 I am very honored to participate in this celebration for the sixtieth anniversary of the Center for Economic Research of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon. It is a pleasure to share this virtual space with the rector of the University, the teacher Rogelio Garza Rivera; with the director of the Faculty of Economics, Professor Jose Raymundo Galan; with the director of the Center for Economic Research, Dr. Joana Cecilia Chapa; with the former director of the Faculty and the Center, Dr. Daniel Flores Curiel and, of course, with the admired economist and friend, Mr. Everardo Elizondo. Thank you very much for the invitation, because, as you will see, this celebration is also very significant for the Bank of Mexico. I. The relevance of economic research For our central bank, it is essential that there are economic research spaces that generate rigorous, timely and reliable information and reflection that support decision-making. Since its founding 95 years ago, the Bank of Mexico has been a constant source of information and research. The Bank collects and disseminates a comprehensive set of economic, financial and payment system statistics, conducts surveys and publishes reports. This information, apart from the fact that it allows to evaluate the performance of the Bank, is a reference for the decisions and operations of economic agents. Likewise, this enormous body of information is extremely useful for academic work, research and scientific development. In this sense, the economic information disseminated by the Bank of Mexico constitutes a public good, with clear benefits for the whole society. 1 Likewise, since its inception, the bank has promoted the internal production of research and has sought to attract to its ranks technical cadres of excellence in the field. From its areas of economic research, the Bank of Mexico has not only addressed central banking issues, such as inflation, monetary policy, financial stability or payment systems, but also seeks to make contributions to other core issues of the economy. In this sense, for many decades, the Central Institute has played an important role in the generation and debate of economic information and ideas. For this reason, the Bank of Mexico has always sought to link with the student and academic communities and maintain feedback with the different spaces and research institutions. Currently, the Bank has several programs of dissemination and university linkage and promotes two well-known reflection contests on economic issues for students of secondary and higher education. In particular, the Bank played a significant role in the establishment of the Center for Economic Research of the Faculty of Economics of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon. Don Rodrigo Gomez, who served as director of the Bank of Mexico between 1952 and 1970, was not only one of the architects of the so-called stabilizing development, but was also one of the great promoters of the promotion of economic studies in the country, including the Faculty of Economics of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon. Certainly, after the peak period of the Mexican Revolution, during the decades of economic reconstruction and institution-building, Mexico faced a great demand for qualified human resources and a shortage of specialized economic cadres. In fact, some of the characters who had positions of greater responsibility in the economic areas, were not specialists. 2 trained in the field, but lawyers, engineers or accountants who, with admirable versatility and pragmatism, knew how to adapt their profile to their functions. Rodrigo Gomez himself, who did not have the opportunity to have higher education, became, thanks to his extraordinary capacity for self-taught learning and his experience, one of the most respected specialists in the world on issues of change, monetary policy and central banking. For Mr. Rodrigo Gomez, the training of specialized cadres was essential to strengthen the structure of the public administration and make more effective the planning and execution of an economic policy oriented to development. Therefore, the Bank of Mexico stimulated training programs and scholarships that allowed bank employees, and then talented professionals, to specialize in urgent issues for the national economy. As Mr. Miguel Mancera pointed out in a tribute to his predecessor: "Don Rodrigo Gomez was fully aware that institutions are not their buildings and other facilities, not even their statutes, but above all, the people who make it up. It is the individuals who give it a political and economic dimension, its historical significance. For this reason, Mr. Rodrigo Gomez paid so much attention at the Bank of Mexico to the training of professional cadres. During his time as director, training formulas at all levels advanced."1 In addition to the training of cadres abroad, Don Rodrigo Gomez thought about the establishment, in Mexico, of centers of excellence in the training of economists that would make training more accessible and form a tradition of rigor in teaching and research. Among others, this is the case of the Faculty of Economics of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon. 1 Mancera, Miguel, "Homenaje a don Rodrigo Gomez en el XX aniversario de su muerte", El Trimestre Economico, vol. 57 (4), no. 228, October-December, 1990. 3 As the economic historian Maria Eugenia Romero Sotelo suggests, regarding the Bank's support for the Faculty of Economics of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon: "Rodrigo Gomez's support for the company was very important since the Central Bank granted the new program financial resources for its development. This program of study has been recognized as one of the most rigorous economic programs in Mexico and became an important source of training for Central Bank officials in the sixties and seventies."2 In fact, Don Rodrigo Gomez was especially interested in the development of the studies and economic cadres of Nuevo Leon. This was influenced not only by the fact that he was a native of this entity, but also by the clear awareness that this state, and in general the northeast region, were called to consolidate itself as an axis of the industrial and financial development of the country. Therefore, he had a significant participation in the consolidation of a Faculty of Economics and, later, in the creation of a Center for Economic Research. As is known, the school of economics of the University of Nuevo Leon was founded in 1957; however, as Romero Sotelo points out, "the absence of economic professionals in the teaching staff was one of the reasons that led the rector, at the request of the director of the school, the accountant Ramon Cardenas, to request help from the director of the Bank of Mexico so that the services of one or two economists who would take charge of the teaching of economics subjects were provided."3 2 Romero Sotelo Maria Eugenia, "Rodrigo Gomez: economic development and stability, two sides of the same coin" in Ludlow, Leonor and Maria Eugenia Sotelo, El Banco de Mexico a traves de sus constructores 1917-2017, Mexico, UNAM, 2019. p. 427. 3 Ibid. 4 Don Rodrigo Gomez recommended Consuelo Meyer, an employee of the Bank of Mexico, to review and contribute to the institution's study program. Consuelo Meyer was an economist by training, who had also taken courses in the schools of jurisprudence, philosophy and anthropology and had completed a postgraduate degree in England. Her solid and varied training, her practical sense and her strict character made her the ideal profile to rethink the direction of the faculty. In his reorganization proposal Meyer proposed to have a solid curriculum in its empirical foundations, a full-time faculty plant, a good selection of students, a functional library and, above all, discipline. Shortly after, Consuelo Meyer herself became director of the Faculty of Economics of this University. She, in turn, sheltered the project of, in addition to consolidating the faculty as a training space, establishing a space for the generation of ideas and analysis, the Center for Economic Research, whose first director was Manuel Rodriguez Cisneros, also an economist trained at the Bank of Mexico. It should be noted that all the evocations of Consuelo Meyer show a legendary figure with extraordinary capacity for work and, at the same time, great human quality. That is why I am pleased to learn that a research award has been established that bears his name, as it is a very fruitful way to honour his memory and reproduce his legacy. In short, the Bank of Mexico, the Faculty of Economics of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon and this Center for Economic Research have an endearing bond. In fact, several graduates of this faculty have joined the Central Institute and two of them, Everardo Elizondo Almaguer and Jesus Marcos Yacaman, have been prominent members of its Governing Board. I had the pleasure of learning from them for many years, when they were part of the Governing Board. 5 Throughout its sixty years, the Center for Economic Research has put research at the service of the public and private sectors of the northeast region, and has gained a wide and deserved prestige. This Center has paraded leading professionals and, from here, research has been generated on topics ranging from demography and economic geography of the region to labor studies, poverty and income distribution. Likewise, the Center participates with various levels of government and private sector agents in various consulting tasks that serve as input for decision-making regarding specific economic projects. In addition to its research and consulting tasks, the Centre carries out an important dissemination task. The Center, for example, promotes the prestigious publication Ensayos, a journal of economics, which analyzes the main topics of economics from a rigorous academic perspective. Likewise, the Center offers public information, such as indexes, series, surveys and other reliable and timely data of great utility for economic agents, especially those in the region. Today more than ever, theoretical and applied research is essential to be able to respond better to the challenges posed by development and economic growth in our time, whose constant is change. Certainly, change, in its various forms, is one of the most relevant characteristics of our times. On the one hand, there are great historical, social or demographic transformations, which take place gradually and, on the other, there are usually profound and revolutionary technological changes, financial crises or contingencies, such as the current pandemic, which manifest themselves unexpectedly and that from one moment to another radically modify economic scenarios. To face these changes, whether gradual or sudden, it is essential to have adequate theoretical models and 6 robust, empirical research, comparative economic history, and timely and reliable information that provides guidance in the most diverse circumstances. II. The pandemic and the associated challenges Precisely, in this speech I would like to refer to some of the effects of the current pandemic on the Mexican economy and the responses that the monetary authority has provided in the face of this unexpected situation. The social and economic landscape we are experiencing today was hardly conceivable at the beginning of this year. The current circumstance is the product of a health problem, external to the economic and financial cycle that, however, has had immediate and intense repercussions on the global and national economy. In relation to the external environment, it highlights the profound impact that the pandemic and the measures adopted to prevent its spread have had on global economic activity and international financial markets. In response to these impacts, central banks in advanced economies have significantly reduced their interest rates and used their balance sheets to promote the orderly functioning of financial markets. In turn, in emerging economies, several institutions have cut their policy rates and implemented various measures in support of a better functioning of their financial systems. A number of countries have also announced major fiscal stimulus measures to mitigate adverse effects on employment and household and business incomes. Considering the fiscal, financial and monetary stimuli implemented in systemically important economies, global risk aversion was contained and international financial markets began to recover since the end of March. This, together with the gradual lifting of some confinement measures in several economies, contributed to the presentation of a certain 7 recovery from the historically low levels recorded in March and April. However, the balance of risks to global growth remains negative, especially given the possibility of a reimposition of certain lockdown measures in some economies that had already relaxed them. Therefore, new episodes of volatility in global financial markets cannot be ruled out, which would hinder economic recovery and generate greater risks for the financial system. In addition to the risks inherent in the evolution of the pandemic, other risk factors persist such as the high levels of indebtedness of the private sector, the solvency problems of companies in the most affected sectors, a new escalation in trade tensions and geopolitical and social conflicts in various regions of the world, among others. In this context, the Mexican economy faced three simultaneous shocks derived from the pandemic, which impacted economic activity, inflation and financial conditions in the country:  First, in the face of a considerable increase in risk aversion. between global investors and the fall in oil prices, the Mexican economy faced a financial shock that led, in a very short period, to significant increases in risk premiums and medium- and long-term interest rates, as well as a significant depreciation of the peso and capital outflows. While this shock has moderated, risks remain that could intensify it again.  Second, the economy has faced a supply shock. In particular, measures to contain the spread of the virus have involved the suspension of the production of various goods and services and have affected global value chains, and, consequently, the provision and distribution of various inputs required by domestic production. 8  Finally, the economy has also suffered a demand shock, as the social distancing measures implemented, the fear of contagion of the population and the lower incomes of companies and households, both internationally and nationally, have led to a significant decrease in domestic and external demand, although the latter has recently shown some recovery. It is important to mention that these shocks operate on different horizons. The financial shock had an immediate impact on domestic financial markets. On the other hand, the effects derived from the supply and demand shocks on the national economy operate in a longer horizon. In this complex environment, the Bank of Mexico has sought to conduct monetary policy in a timely and prudent manner, promoting an orderly adjustment both in the financial markets and in the economy as a whole. In all this effort, conditions are sought that preserve the purchasing power of the national currency over time. The Bank has also taken a number of measures commensurate with its aims to promote the sound development of the financial system and the smooth functioning of payment systems. In this way, within the scope of its possibilities and purposes, it has contributed to mitigating the adverse effects of the pandemic on Mexican families. In particular, the Bank announced a series of measures to promote the orderly functioning of financial markets, strengthen credit channels, and provide liquidity for the healthy development of financial and payment systems. By their function, these measures are located in four groups: 1) those focused on providing liquidity and restoring operating conditions in the money market; 9 2) those that seek to promote orderly behavior in the government securities and corporate securities markets; 3) those aimed at strengthening credit channels in the economy; and (4) decisions to ensure orderly market behaviour exchange rate, in accordance with the guidelines of the Exchange Commission. It is important to emphasize that these measures include operations that the Bank of Mexico Law empowers it to carry out. Taken together, the measures in national currency in support of the financial system represent a cumulative amount of up to 800 m.m.p. equivalent to 3.3% of GDP in 2019. It should be noted that the liquidity granted with these facilities to banks and market participants has adequate and sufficient collateral. After the significant effects on the national financial markets registered in March, during the course of the second quarter of the year the prices of financial assets in Mexico began to recover in line with the positive behavior of international financial markets and with the effects of the measures adopted by the monetary authority in Mexico to promote an orderly functioning of financial markets, strengthen credit channels and provide liquidity for the healthy development of the financial system. In particular, interest rates on government securities and risk premiums have declined, while the Mexican peso has appreciated from the levels it reached in March and April. However, financial markets have not reached the conditions prior to the pandemic and there have been some episodes of volatility. Likewise, various external and idiosyncratic risk factors persist that, if materialized, could lead to the financial shock intensifying again. 10 Abounding in what have been the effects on the real sector. In the second quarter, the effects on economic activity caused by the pandemic and the actions implemented to contain it were accentuated. In particular, April saw sharp declines in the main components of aggregate demand, as well as in the production of goods and services. In May, economic activity continued to contract, albeit at a more moderate rate, while in June there was some recovery. However, this recovery is moderate and part of the extremely low levels of activity presented in April and May, while maintaining an environment of uncertainty. Due to the pandemic, labor market conditions showed a significant deterioration, as there was a sharp fall in employment, as well as a sharp reduction in hours worked and an increase in underemployment. Given that the evolution of the pandemic is still in process, it is difficult to determine the times and pace at which a full normalization of national economic activity could be expected, so it is likely that ups and downs and intermittencies will be observed in the recovery and that the dynamics between sectors of activity and regions will not be uniform. The effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on demand and consumption patterns, as well as the supply shocks to which this pandemic has resulted, and the exchange rate adjustment that has occurred, have significantly influenced the evolution of inflation. In April, annual headline inflation recorded its second-lowest level historically, standing at 2.15%. This is largely the result of the significant decreases in energy prices, given the abrupt reductions in their international references. Thus, in April the pressures 11 the decline due to these factors exceeded those that were presented to the rise in the prices of some goods, such as certain foods, medicines and household products, which presented a greater relative demand as a result of the confinement. Since May, annual headline inflation has increased due, firstly, to the fact that international energy benchmarks have increased and, with them, domestic prices, putting upward pressure on non-core inflation; and, secondly, that core inflation has picked up. As for the latter, the evolution of the pandemic has led to relative price adjustments, with a recomposition within core inflation, since there have been downward pressures on the prices of services and upward pressures on those of goods, especially food. Being of greater magnitude those registered in the goods. With this, in August headline inflation increased to 4.05% and core inflation to 3.97%. Regarding the forecasts for general and core inflation, although their recent increases led to a slight upward revision in the trajectory anticipated by the Bank of Mexico for the short term, the forecasts in the forecast horizon of 12 to 24 months are around the target of 3%. Regarding the monetary policy decisions adopted, from March 2020 to date, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico reduced the target for the Overnight Interbank Interest Rate by 250 basis points. In particular, at its early meeting in March and its extraordinary meeting in April, as well as at its scheduled meetings in May, June and August, it decided to reduce the benchmark rate in each by 50 basis points, to currently place it at 4.5%. Going forward, the available space will depend on the evolution of the factors that affect the inflation outlook and its expectations, including the effects that the pandemic could have on both. 12 He also announced additional measures to promote an orderly behavior of the financial markets, strengthen the channels of granting credit and provide liquidity for the healthy development of the financial system, measures to which I already referred a moment ago. Given the challenges posed by the pandemic, persevering in strengthening macroeconomic fundamentals and taking the necessary actions, both in the monetary and fiscal spheres, will contribute to a better adjustment of national financial markets and the economy as a whole. Ladies and gentlemen: The celebration of the anniversary of this Center also coincides with a reason for celebration of the Bank of Mexico, since just a few days ago the 95th anniversary of the entry into operations of our Central Institute was commemorated. On August 25, 1925, the law establishing the Bank of Mexico was promulgated, which was inaugurated on September 1 of the same year. Its creation, provided for in the Constitution of 1917, materialized an old aspiration, which can be traced back to the beginnings of Mexico as an independent nation, to have a single instance that gave support and certainty to the issuance and circulation of money. The Bank of Mexico faced the enormous challenge of restoring the population's confidence in fiat money through an issue of national currency that would ensure the stability of its value. Likewise, the Bank of Mexico contributed significantly to laying the foundations for the consolidation of a modern financial system and for an efficient payment system. 95 years after its foundation, the Bank of Mexico ratifies its mission to provide the country with a national currency seeking the stability of its value, as well as to promote the 13 healthy development of the financial and payment systems, in order to contribute to facilitating economic activities, stimulating growth and improving the standard of living of all Mexicans. To achieve this mission, we are committed to continue serving the citizen by providing a stable and secure means of payment of value; protecting your rights as a user of financial and payment services and providing you with relevant and timely information to support your decision-making. The proximity of these two institutions to the dates of celebration is very fortunate. Therefore, I want to extend my most sincere congratulations to the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon, its economics faculty and all those who have given life to this space of intellectual excellence that is the Center for Economic Research. Thank you very much and congratulations. 14

La relevancia de la investigacin econmica Para nuestro banco central es indispensable que existan espacios de investigacin econmica que generen informacin y reflexin rigurosa, oportuna y confiable, que apoye la toma de decisiones. En particular, el Banco desempe un papel significativo en el establecimiento del Centro de Investigaciones Econmicas de la Facultad de Economa de la Universidad Autnoma de Nuevo Len. Don Rodrigo Gmez, quien se desempe como director del Banco de Mxico entre 1952 y 1970, no slo fue uno de los artfices del llamado desarrollo estabilizador, sino que tambin fue uno de los grandes impulsores de la promocin de los estudios econmicos en el pas, incluida la Facultad de Economa de la Universidad Autnoma de Nuevo Len. Ciertamente, tras el periodo ms lgido de la Revolucin Mexicana, durante las dcadas de reconstruccin econmica y creacin de instituciones, Mxico enfrent una gran demanda de recursos humanos calificados y una escasez de cuadros econmicos especializados. De hecho, algunos de los personajes que tuvieron puestos de mayor responsabilidad en las reas econmicas, no eran especialistas 2 formados en la materia, sino abogados, ingenieros o contadores que, con admirable versatilidad y pragmatismo, supieron adaptar su perfil a sus funciones. El propio don Rodrigo Gmez, quien no tuvo la oportunidad de tener estudios superiores, se convirti, gracias a su extraordinaria capacidad de aprendizaje autodidacta y a su experiencia, en uno de los especialistas ms respetados del mundo en temas de cambios, poltica monetaria y banca central. Por ello, don Rodrigo Gmez prest tanta atencin en el Banco de Mxico a la formacin de cuadros profesionales. Durante su poca de director tuvieron gran avance las frmulas de capacitacin a todos los niveles.1 Adems de la formacin de cuadros en el extranjero, don Rodrigo Gmez pensaba en el establecimiento, en Mxico, de centros de excelencia en la formacin de economistas que hicieran ms accesible la capacitacin y formaran una tradicin propia de rigor en la docencia e investigacin. Entre otros, este es el caso de la Facultad de Economa de la Universidad Autnoma de Nuevo Len. 1 Mancera, Miguel, Homenaje a don Rodrigo Gmez en el XX aniversario de su fallecimiento, El Trimestre Econmico, vol. 57 (4), nm. 228, octubre-diciembre, 1990. 3 Como sugiere la historiadora econmica Mara Eugenia Romero Sotelo, respecto al respaldo del Banco a la facultad de Economa de la Universidad Autnoma de Nuevo Len: el apoyo de Rodrigo Gmez a la empresa fue muy importante ya que el Banco Central otorg al nuevo programa, recursos financieros para su desarrollo. En ello influan no slo el hecho de que era oriundo de esta entidad, sino la clara conciencia de que este estado, y en general la regin noreste, estaban llamados a consolidarse como un eje del desarrollo industrial y financiero del pas. Consuelo Meyer era una economista de formacin, que adems haba tomado cursos en las escuelas de jurisprudencia, filosofa y antropologa y haba realizado un posgrado en Inglaterra. Su slida y variada formacin, su sentido prctico y su carcter estricto la hacan el perfil ideal para replantear el rumbo de la facultad. En su propuesta de reorganizacin Meyer propuso tener un plan de estudios slido en sus fundamentos empricos, una planta de profesores de tiempo completo, una buena seleccin de alumnos, una biblioteca funcional y, sobre todo, disciplina. Poco despus la propia Consuelo Meyer se convirti en directora de la Facultad de Economa de esta Universidad. Ella, a su vez, abrig el proyecto de, adems de consolidar la facultad como espacio de formacin, establecer un espacio de generacin de ideas y anlisis, el Centro de Investigaciones Econmicas, cuyo primer director fue Manuel Rodrguez Cisneros, tambin economista formado en el Banco de Mxico. Cabe destacar que todas las evocaciones de Consuelo Meyer muestran una figura legendaria con extraordinaria capacidad de trabajo y, a la vez, gran calidad humana. Por eso, me complacer saber que se ha establecido un premio de investigacin que lleva su nombre, pues es una forma muy fecunda de honrar su memoria y reproducir su legado. En suma, el Banco de Mxico, la Facultad de Economa de la Universidad Autnoma de Nuevo Len y este Centro de Investigaciones Econmicas tienen un vnculo entraable.
