In addition, the risk of overvaluation also affects other markets, such as equity and corporate debt. 2 Third, trade tensions, particularly between China and the United States, can lead to distortions in resource allocation and adverse effects on global economic activity, as well as affect international financial markets. Indeed, as seen in recent weeks, uncertainty about the potential escalation of these stocks may result in disorderly adjustments in these markets, with consequent adverse effects on the global economy. In addition to the above, an environment of high volatility and tightening of global financial conditions such as that which could arise from these risks, and others of a domestic or geopolitical nature, could exacerbate some remaining vulnerabilities of consideration. In this regard, I think it is pertinent to underline the concern that has recently arisen about the high levels of indebtedness in many economies, both advanced and emerging. Naturally, the better performance of the world economy in recent months has had a favorable impact on the direction of the Mexican economy. However, the aforementioned risks have also given rise to uncertainty, which has been accentuated by factors, both internal and external, more directly linked to Mexico. During the first months of 2018, the Mexican economy has continued to recover from the contraction observed in the third quarter of 2017, although the figures continue to reflect in part the effect of the earthquakes registered last September. In particular, the growth in domestic demand has been driven, among other factors, by investment, the result in turn of the 3 reconstruction efforts in the wake of the aforementioned natural disasters, but also of the public infrastructure works underway and the expansion of spending on machinery and equipment. At the same time, there continues to be an expansion of private consumption, albeit with signs of slowing, and solid export growth, underpinned by strong external demand, especially from the United States, and by a competitive exchange rate. On the supply side, the growth of the economy is explained by the trajectory of the service sector and, to a lesser extent, the industrial sector, highlighting in the latter the strengthening of construction as a result of the factors described above. Slack conditions in the Mexican economy remain narrow, although the precise reading of its cyclical position is complex. This is illustrated by the situation in the labour market. The unemployment rate is clearly below both the estimates of its level in the long run and the lows observed before the global financial crisis. However, alternative estimates under broader definitions of this, such as those that also consider underemployed workers or those who are not employed but who sought work in the recent past, show figures similar to those recorded before that crisis. In addition, the decline in the unemployment rate has been accompanied by a decrease in labor participation. When considering the latter phenomenon in counterfactual estimates of the unemployment rate, results can be observed that are not significantly different from its 4 long-term level. Excessive wage pressures also remain unmet and the unit labour cost index for the economy as a whole continues to decline. It is also worth noting that the fall in the unemployment rate has slowed in recent months. In my opinion, a labour market situation such as that suggested by the traditional definition of the unemployment rate should result in wage increases greater than those currently observed, as well as demand pressures in other sectors, which to date are not evident. However, although the unemployment rate does not seem to accurately reflect the situation of the labour market, the set of available indicators suggests tight conditions in that market and the output gap is estimated at levels that are not statistically different from zero. This makes it essential to continue to carefully monitor the degree of slack in the economy, since there is a risk of the emergence of pressures on prices, both on the side of wages and demand. Economic activity is expected to continue expanding in the coming months, registering during 2018 and 2019 figures slightly higher than those observed in 2017. This would keep the output gap at levels close to zero. In my opinion, although the risks to this scenario remain skewed to the downside, some of these have eased in recent weeks, especially as a result of more favorable expectations regarding the renegotiation of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). In any case, the possibility of protracted negotiations or failure of such negotiations persists. To this must be added the potential adverse effect 5 in the economic activity of the greatest protectionist tendencies at the global level, of episodes of turbulence in the international financial markets, of the fiscal reform in the United States and of the electoral process in Mexico. Inflation has continued to decline in the first months of 2018, registering in its latest readings a more favorable behavior than anticipated until recently. The latter has been influenced by the behavior of both core and non-core inflation, although the impact of the latter has been greater. In this way, in the first half of April, general consumer inflation registered its lowest figure since the second half of January 2017 and the inflation indicators most linked to the economic cycle also registered a decrease. This behavior has been the result of the monetary policy actions implemented, the fading of the supply shocks observed in 2017, the appreciation of the exchange rate and a favorable evolution of the prices of various agricultural products. Survey-based inflation expectations, both short- and long-term, have remained relatively stable. However, expectations for the end of 2018 and 2019 exceed the projections of the Bank of Mexico, while those for the long term continue to be at levels above the target. The Bank of Mexico anticipates that inflation will converge to figures close to the 3 percent target in the first months of 2019, under the assumptions of a 6 relatively stable exchange rate, and the absence of new supply shocks on inflation and pressures from the labour market. I believe that the possible trajectory of the exchange rate continues to be the main risk for this scenario. The peso's exchange rate may be affected, among other factors, by the uncertainty derived from the renegotiation of NAFTA, by surprises in the normalization of monetary policy in the United States and by episodes of volatility linked to the elections that will take place at the beginning of July. On the other hand, the possibility of inflationary pressures arising from the normally volatile behaviour of non-core inflation or demand developments cannot be ruled out. In my opinion, the balance of risks to inflation maintains an upward bias, although, as in the case of economic activity, those derived from the renegotiation of NAFTA have been reduced. Fundamentally as a result of the monetary policy actions implemented and a more favorable outlook in relation to NAFTA, among other factors, the exchange rate of the peso against the dollar registered a significant strengthening in the first months of the year, reaching this parity levels not observed since September 2017, as well as an appreciation against the currencies of most emerging economies. However, the volatility of recent days has led to a partial reversal of these gains in the price of our currency, largely due to both the appreciation of the dollar and uncertainty around the current electoral process. It should be noted that, no 7 Despite these pressures, operating conditions in the foreign exchange market have remained stable. While long-term interest rates have picked up lately, financial markets have continued to perform in an orderly manner, with a significant narrowing of the long-term interest rate differential with the United States over the course of the past few months. However, for the reasons already mentioned, the possibility of more acute or widespread episodes of volatility that may lead to a deterioration in operating conditions in these markets remains latent. Although the risks facing the Mexican economy could affect our financial system, several elements mitigate its potential scope. Among these, it is worth mentioning the strength of the banking system that, in addition to being well capitalized and registering high rates of return, has liquidity levels significantly above the minimum required. In addition, the country's non-financial private sector is well protected against increases in the exchange rate or interest rates, thanks to long-term and fixed-rate foreign currency debt placements, as well as hedges, both natural and through derivative instruments, against exchange rate risks. On the other hand, although some companies face foreign exchange or refinancing risks, the exposure of Mexican financial institutions to these companies is small in relation to their capitalization levels or their positioning in assets. To date, monetary policy actions have made it possible to avoid second-order effects of the shocks that have had an impact on prices, and the 8 inflation is trending downward. However, given an adjustment of 450 basis points to the reference rate since December 2015, and the fact that it is slightly above the neutral interest rate estimate band, it is worth asking whether the monetary adjustment has been excessive. In my opinion, this argument can hardly be defended, in an environment in which the economy still faces the prospect of a near-zero output gap for this year and next, a balance of upside risks to inflation and expectations for it in the long term still above the target. Although some of the risks that may affect the behavior of inflation have been reduced, these have not disappeared and, in general, we continue to face very high levels of uncertainty. Under these circumstances, it is essential to maintain a prudent monetary policy and to bear in mind that the possibility of further increases in the reference interest rate persists. Naturally, an action of this nature will depend on a thorough analysis of the behavior of inflation, its outlook and the risks arising from both internal and external factors. It will also be necessary to continue to carefully assess the possible implications of monetary actions for economic activity. Finally, I would like to conclude by pointing out that, despite the environment of high uncertainty facing the Mexican economy, as well as the persistence of significant risks, it has fundamentals that provide a firm basis to face them. However, it is also true that there are important tasks still pending, particularly for the medium and long term. It is therefore essential to ensure preservation. 9 of our achievements, and to continue to build on the foundations of the progress achieved, with a view to taking the additional steps that may be required to overcome the remaining challenges. 10
text_original: LA POLTICA MONETARIA EN MXICO ANTE CONDICIONES DE ELEVADA INCERTIDUMBRE. INTERVENCIN DEL LIC. JAVIER GUZMN CALAFELL, SUBGOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE MXICO, EN EL CFO MEXICO CITY FORUM DEL COUNCIL OF THE AMERICAS. Ciudad de Mxico, 26 de abril de 2018.1 Agradezco a los organizadores la gentil invitacin para participar en este importante Foro. La economa mundial presenta en la actualidad condiciones en general favorables, que se espera se mantengan durante los prximos meses. En un entorno de posturas de poltica monetaria acomodaticias por parte de los principales bancos centrales y medidas de estmulo fiscal en Estados Unidos, la actividad econmica mundial contina mostrando una trayectoria de crecimiento que, si bien moderado, se espera registre un fortalecimiento adicional a lo largo de este ao y el siguiente. Para las economas avanzadas, se anticipa una expansin por encima de su potencial en este lapso. Cabe destacar, por su relevancia para Mxico, la importante mejora en las proyecciones del crecimiento del PIB y de la produccin industrial en Estados Unidos. Asimismo, es importante hacer notar que, en parte como resultado de este mejor desempeo de la economa mundial, los precios del petrleo y otras materias primas han mostrado una tendencia al alza. Desafortunadamente, no obstante esta mejora en las proyecciones econmicas para el corto plazo, existe la percepcin generalizada de que las 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad del autor y no necesariamente representan la postura institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno en conjunto. 1 perspectivas de la economa mundial para horizontes ms largos presentan un balance de riesgos con un sesgo negativo. Al respecto, cabe destacar en primer lugar el riesgo de una normalizacin monetaria en Estados Unidos ms rpida de lo previsto. Si bien el Comit Federal de Mercado Abierto ha reiterado que ajustar su postura de poltica monetaria de manera gradual, el riesgo de sorpresas se ha acentuado. Lo anterior especialmente en virtud de la implementacin de medidas de estmulo fiscal, bajo una situacin caracterizada por escasa o nula holgura en el mercado laboral, lo que puede redundar en el surgimiento de presiones adicionales sobre los salarios y los precios. Los retos se incrementan al considerar que sigue anticipndose que otras economas avanzadas tambin normalicen sus posturas de poltica monetaria, si bien a un ritmo ms gradual que en Estados Unidos. En segundo lugar, y muy vinculado al punto anterior, no obstante las correcciones registradas en meses recientes, algunos activos parecen seguir cotizndose en niveles excesivos. Por ejemplo, las primas por plazo en los mercados de bonos a nivel global son muy reducidas. Aunque la posibilidad de una desalineacin con respecto a los fundamentos econmicos est sujeta a debate, dichas primas son muy sensibles a revisiones del rumbo esperado para los principales agregados macroeconmicos y la poltica monetaria. Las implicaciones de una descompresin repentina de las primas por plazo podra tener consecuencias severas para la economa mundial, especialmente tomando en cuenta la elevada correlacin de estas entre pases. Adems, el riesgo de sobrevaluacin tambin afecta a otros mercados, como el accionario y el de deuda corporativa. 2 En tercer lugar, las tensiones en materia comercial, particularmente entre China y Estados Unidos, pueden dar lugar a distorsiones en la asignacin de recursos y efectos adversos en la actividad econmica global, adems de afectar los mercados financieros internacionales. En efecto, como se vio en semanas recientes, la incertidumbre en torno al potencial escalamiento de estas acciones puede redundar en ajustes desordenados en dichos mercados, con los consecuentes efectos adversos para la economa mundial. En adicin a lo anterior, un entorno de elevada volatilidad y de apretamiento de las condiciones financieras globales como el que podra derivarse de estos riesgos, y de otros de naturaleza interna o geopoltica, podra exacerbar algunas vulnerabilidades de consideracin todava presentes. Al respecto, me parece pertinente subrayar la preocupacin que ha surgido recientemente por los elevados niveles de endeudamiento en numerosas economas, tanto avanzadas como emergentes. Naturalmente, el mejor desempeo de la economa mundial en los ltimos meses ha incidido favorablemente en el rumbo de la economa mexicana. Sin embargo, los riesgos antes sealados tambin han dado lugar a incertidumbre, misma que ha sido acentuada por factores, tanto internos como externos, ms directamente vinculados a Mxico. Durante los primeros meses de 2018 la economa mexicana ha continuado recuperndose de la contraccin observada en el tercer trimestre de 2017, si bien las cifras siguen reflejando en parte el efecto de los sismos registrados en septiembre pasado. En particular, el crecimiento de la demanda interna ha sido impulsado entre otros factores por la inversin, resultado a su vez de los 3 esfuerzos de reconstruccin a raz de los citados desastres naturales, aunque tambin de las obras de infraestructura pblica en marcha y de la expansin del gasto en maquinaria y equipo. Al mismo tiempo, contina observndose una expansin del consumo privado, aunque con indicios de desaceleracin, y un slido crecimiento de las exportaciones, apuntaladas por la fortaleza de la demanda externa, especialmente de Estados Unidos, y por un tipo de cambio competitivo. Por el lado de la oferta, el crecimiento de la economa se explica por la trayectoria del sector de servicios y, en menor medida, del industrial, destacando en este ltimo el fortalecimiento de la construccin como resultado de los factores antes descritos. Las condiciones de holgura en la economa mexicana se mantienen estrechas, si bien la lectura precisa de su posicin cclica es compleja. Lo anterior se ilustra con la situacin en el mercado laboral. La tasa de desempleo se ubica claramente por debajo tanto de los clculos de su nivel en el largo plazo como de los mnimos observados antes de la crisis financiera global. Sin embargo, estimaciones alternativas bajo definiciones ms amplias de esta, como aquellas que consideran tambin a los trabajadores subocupados o a los que no estn empleados pero que buscaron trabajo en el pasado reciente, arrojan cifras similares a las registradas antes de dicha crisis. Adicionalmente, el descenso de la tasa de desempleo ha venido acompaado de una disminucin de la participacin laboral. Al considerar este ltimo fenmeno en estimaciones contrafactuales de la tasa de desocupacin, se pueden observar resultados que no son significativamente diferentes de su 4 nivel de largo plazo. Asimismo, siguen sin observarse presiones salariales excesivas y el ndice de costos laborales unitarios para la economa en su conjunto contina disminuyendo. Tambin vale la pena sealar que la cada de la tasa de desempleo se ha frenado en los ltimos meses. En mi opinin, una situacin del mercado laboral como el sugerido por la definicin tradicional de la tasa de desempleo debera traducirse en aumentos salariales mayores a los observados en la actualidad, as como en presiones de demanda en otros sectores, que a la fecha no son evidentes. Ahora bien, aunque la tasa de desocupacin no parece reflejar con precisin la situacin del mercado laboral, el conjunto de indicadores disponibles sugiere condiciones apretadas en dicho mercado y la brecha del producto se estima en niveles que no son estadsticamente diferentes de cero. Lo anterior hace indispensable continuar dando un seguimiento cuidadoso al grado de holgura en la economa, ya que existe el riesgo del surgimiento de presiones sobre los precios, tanto por el lado de los salarios como de la demanda. Se espera que la actividad econmica contine expandindose en los prximos meses, registrando durante 2018 y 2019 cifras ligeramente superiores a las observadas en 2017. Esto mantendra la brecha del producto en niveles cercanos a cero. A mi parecer, aunque los riesgos para este escenario continan sesgados a la baja, algunos de estos se han atenuado en las ltimas semanas, especialmente como resultado de expectativas ms favorables en relacin a la renegociacin del Tratado de Libre Comercio de Amrica del Norte (TLCAN). En todo caso, la posibilidad de negociaciones prolongadas o de un fracaso de estas persiste. A lo anterior cabe agregar el potencial efecto adverso 5 en la actividad econmica de las mayores tendencias proteccionistas a nivel global, de episodios de turbulencia en los mercados financieros internacionales, de la reforma fiscal en Estados Unidos y del proceso electoral en Mxico. La inflacin ha continuado disminuyendo en los primeros meses de 2018, registrando en sus ltimas lecturas un comportamiento ms favorable del anticipado hasta hace poco. Esto ltimo ha sido influido por el comportamiento tanto de la inflacin subyacente como de la no subyacente, si bien el impacto de esta ltima ha sido mayor. De esta forma, en la primera quincena de abril la inflacin general al consumidor registr su menor cifra desde la segunda quincena de enero de 2017 y los indicadores de inflacin ms vinculados al ciclo econmico tambin registran una disminucin. Este comportamiento ha sido resultado de las acciones de poltica monetaria implementadas, el desvanecimiento de los choques de oferta observados en 2017, la apreciacin del tipo de cambio y una evolucin favorable de los precios de diversos productos agrcolas. Las expectativas de inflacin basadas en encuestas, tanto de corto como de largo plazo, se han mantenido relativamente estables. Sin embargo, las expectativas para finales de 2018 y 2019 superan a las proyecciones del Banco de Mxico, en tanto que las de largo plazo continan ubicadas en niveles por encima de la meta. El Banco de Mxico anticipa que la inflacin converger a cifras cercanas a la meta de 3 por ciento en los primeros meses de 2019, bajo los supuestos de un 6 tipo de cambio relativamente estable, y la ausencia de nuevos choques de oferta sobre la inflacin y de presiones provenientes del mercado laboral. Considero que la posible trayectoria del tipo de cambio contina siendo el principal riesgo para este escenario. El tipo de cambio del peso puede ser afectado, entre otros factores, por la incertidumbre derivada de la renegociacin del TLCAN, por sorpresas en la normalizacin de la poltica monetaria en Estados Unidos y por episodios de volatilidad vinculados a las elecciones que tendrn lugar a principios de julio. Por otra parte, la posibilidad de presiones inflacionarias derivadas del normalmente voltil comportamiento de la inflacin no subyacente o de la evolucin de la demanda no puede descartarse. A mi juicio, el balance de riesgos para la inflacin mantiene un sesgo al alza, aunque, como en el caso de la actividad econmica, aquellos derivados de la renegociacin del TLCAN se han reducido. En lo fundamental como resultado de las acciones de poltica monetaria implementadas y de un panorama ms favorable en relacin al TLCAN, entre otros factores, el tipo de cambio del peso frente al dlar registr un fortalecimiento importante en los primeros meses del ao, alcanzando esta paridad niveles no observados desde septiembre de 2017, as como una apreciacin frente a las monedas de la mayora de las economas emergentes. Sin embargo, la volatilidad de das recientes ha derivado en una reversin parcial de dichas ganancias en la cotizacin de nuestra moneda, obedeciendo en buena medida tanto a la apreciacin que ha registrado el dlar como a incertidumbre en torno al actual proceso electoral. Cabe destacar que, no 7 obstante estas presiones, las condiciones de operacin en el mercado cambiario se han mantenido estables. Si bien las tasas de inters de largo plazo han repuntado ltimamente, los mercados financieros han continuado mostrando un funcionamiento ordenado, observndose una reduccin significativa del diferencial de tasas de inters de largo plazo con Estados Unidos en el transcurso de los ltimos meses. No obstante, por los motivos ya sealados, la posibilidad de episodios ms agudos o extendidos de volatilidad que puedan dar lugar a un deterioro de las condiciones de operacin en estos mercados se mantiene latente. Aun cuando los riesgos que enfrenta la economa mexicana podran incidir en nuestro sistema financiero, diversos elementos mitigan su potencial alcance. Entre estos, cabe destacar la fortaleza del sistema bancario que, adems de encontrarse bien capitalizado y registrar altas tasas de rentabilidad, cuenta con niveles de liquidez significativamente por encima de los mnimos requeridos. Adems, el sector privado no financiero del pas se encuentra bien protegido ante alzas del tipo de cambio o de las tasas de inters, gracias a colocaciones de deuda en moneda extranjera a largo plazo y a tasa fija, as como a coberturas, tanto naturales como a travs de instrumentos derivados, ante riesgos cambiarios. Por otra parte, aunque algunas empresas enfrentan riesgos cambiarios o de refinanciamiento, la exposicin de las entidades financieras mexicanas a estas empresas es pequea en relacin a sus niveles de capitalizacin o a su posicionamiento en activos. Hasta la fecha, las acciones de poltica monetaria han permitido evitar efectos de segundo orden de los choques que han incidido sobre los precios, y la 8 inflacin registra una tendencia descendente. Sin embargo, ante un ajuste de 450 puntos base a la tasa de referencia desde diciembre de 2015, y el hecho de que esta se ubica ligeramente por encima de la banda de estimacin de la tasa de inters neutral, cabe preguntarse si el ajuste monetario ha sido excesivo. En mi opinin, difcilmente puede defenderse este argumento, en un entorno en el cual la economa enfrenta todava la perspectiva de una brecha del producto cercana a cero para este ao y el siguiente, un balance de riesgos al alza para la inflacin y expectativas para esta en el largo plazo todava por encima de la meta. Aunque algunos de los riesgos que pueden incidir sobre el comportamiento de la inflacin se han aminorado, estos no han desaparecido y, en general, continuamos haciendo frente a niveles de incertidumbre muy elevados. Bajo estas circunstancias, es indispensable mantener una poltica monetaria prudente y tener presente que la posibilidad de nuevos aumentos de la tasa de inters de referencia persiste. Naturalmente, una accin de esta naturaleza depender de un anlisis exhaustivo del comportamiento de la inflacin, sus perspectivas y los riesgos derivados de factores tanto internos como externos. Tambin ser preciso continuar evaluando cuidadosamente las posibles implicaciones de las acciones monetarias para la actividad econmica. Finalmente, quisiera concluir sealando que, no obstante el entorno de elevada incertidumbre que enfrenta la economa mexicana, as como la persistencia de riesgos de consideracin, esta cuenta con fundamentos que proporcionan una base firme para enfrentarlos. Sin embargo, tambin es cierto que existen importantes tareas an pendientes, particularmente para el mediano y largo plazos. Por tanto, es indispensable asegurar la preservacin 9 de nuestros logros, y continuar edificando sobre los cimientos del progreso alcanzado, con miras a adoptar las medidas adicionales que sean requeridas para superar los desafos remanentes. 10

Title: Opening of the international seminar: Responsible and successful financial inclusion: international models
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the opening of the international seminar "Responsible and successful financial inclusion: international models". May 30, 2013  Mr. Heinrich Haasis, President of the World Box Institute of Savings and the German Foundation of Savings Banks for International Cooperation (Sparkassenstiftung) for International cooperation)  Mr. Niclaus Bergmann, Director General of the Foundation German Savings Banks for International Cooperation (Sparkassenstiftung fur Internationale Kooperation)  Mr. Gerd Weissbach, Director of the Office of Representation in Latin America (Sparkassenstiftung fur International cooperation)  Ladies and gentlemen, I am grateful for the kind invitation of the German Foundation of Savings Banks for International Cooperation to inaugurate this international seminar that has set out to address a topic as vast as it is important: inclusion 1 financial and successful ways in the world to promote and increase savings and credit, especially through savings banks as non-profit institutions so well known and widespread in Europe and, in particular, in Germany. There is no doubt that Mexico has generated a special interest in the Foundation and we are very grateful for it. Proof of this special interest are, among many other contributions that the German Foundation of Savings Banks for International Cooperation has made to Mexico in recent years, the different ventures of the foundation in conjunction with Bansefi to strengthen more than 150 solidarity funds, as well as the strengthening of 17 popular funds affiliated to the Social Strength Federation and three boxes of the Alliance Federation. And above all, within the framework of financial inclusion, the PATMIR phase II project promoted together with SAGARPA stands out, 2 an ongoing project to bring financial services closer to people living in marginal rural areas through partnerships, all with the goal of "financially including" 120,000 people in more than 22 states of the Republic. This is just one of the Foundation's many ongoing projects. And it seems to me elementary justice, at the beginning of my speech, to make a public recognition of how much the Foundation has served Mexico, especially those who need it most. There is ample theoretical and empirical evidence about the link between the development of a country's financial institutions and markets and that country's economic development; for example, if a broad cross-section is made, countries with a higher GDP per capita also have a higher credit ratio to the private sector (as a proportion of GDP); in parallel, in the 3 countries where a larger proportion of the population lives in poverty tend to have little credit to the private sector relative to national income. Financial inclusion is a central component of financial development as it allows for a greater amount of resources for investment and a more efficient allocation of resources. Recent economic literature has shown that access to basic financial services, such as deposit or savings accounts and small loans, allows individuals to save more and more safely, better manage negative shocks to their health or income. Greater financial inclusion has also been shown to increase small business activity and employment in the beneficiary communities. In this way, one can speak of a virtuous circle between inclusion and financial development and general economic growth. 4 Financial inclusion has been a permanent concern of the Mexican financial authorities; in recent years, and in response to such concern, a number of regulations and amendments to existing laws have been put in place to encourage it. One of the advances with the greatest inclusive potential is the introduction of mobile banking. In 2011, the Bank of Mexico issued regulations that allow the opening of different types of accounts according to the level of operability and ease of opening they have; low-level accounts can be opened without visiting a branch and fewer documents are required to do so. These accounts are part of the mobile banking scheme that has been successful in other countries to expand inclusion. In parallel, the National Banking and Securities Commission created the figure of banking commission agent; these are non-bank agents authorized to provide services in the name and on behalf of a bank. The 5 Commission agents are an efficient channel to serve remote locations as they take advantage of the infrastructure installed by another company to offer a range of banking services. With these changes, it is no longer necessary to go to a branch or a cashier to check the balance of the account or make any payment. This can be done from your cell phone or at a nearby store that acts as a commission agent. Thus, it is expected that more Mexicans, for whom it was not feasible to use banking services, will decide to access them. In 2012, the National Council for Financial Inclusion (CNIF) was established, whose task is, on the one hand, to coordinate the effort that many public and private institutions have made in terms of financial inclusion and, on the other, to set the direction that the country must follow to achieve higher levels of inclusion. 6 Although promoting financial inclusion is not its primary function, the Bank of Mexico has actively participated in the board (CNIF) and has adopted a series of measures that have an impact on financial inclusion, among which the regulation of basic accounts stands out. These are accounts that provide savings and payment services at no cost and that all banks that receive deposits are required to offer. However, the Bank of Mexico's main contribution to financial inclusion is the maintenance of price stability. Mexico has enjoyed low and stable inflation for more than a decade, getting closer to the 3 percent annual target. In financial markets and among the public, there are solidly anchored expectations of low inflation. All this is thanks to a responsible monetary policy framed in the autonomy obtained by the Bank of Mexico 20 years ago. 7 This is a key contribution to financial development as it would be unthinkable, for example, to promote long-term savings and credit without price stability. One of the regulations of particular interest for this conference is that of the Popular Savings and Credit sector; financial authorities have made an effort to make it more reliable and secure for users. Thus, a regulation was established that seeks to formalize the services provided by the Savings Banks and other institutions in the sector through effective supervision and a deposit guarantee program. Despite the positive impact that the aforementioned regulations have had and the favorable trend of inclusion indicators, there are still lags in this area in Mexico. The National Survey of Financial Inclusion carried out in Mexico last year by INEGI reveals that in terms of 8 25 million adults (36% of the total) claim to have at least one formal savings instrument. In contrast, the World Bank reports that 42% of Chilean adults and 56% of Brazilians have a bank account. Among formal savings instruments, payroll accounts and savings accounts have the largest number of users. Although payroll accounts are the predominant product of recruitment, only 16% of those who have them use them to save money. The Survey found that 44% of adult Mexicans (i.e. 31 million people) save in the informal market. Within this group, the favorite savings mechanisms are 28% "at home" and 14% through "batches". 73% of adults who do not save (which is 45 million) or who do so in an informal institution, mention as the main barrier or obstacle that their income is not enough to save or are too variable incomes. To 9 in turn, 16% mention that they do not save because they "are not interested" or "do not need it". . The lag is also notable as regards credit to enterprises, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises. According to a survey conducted by the World Bank in 2010, only 32% of formal companies in Mexico had a bank loan or line of credit, while in Chile it was 80% and in Brazil 66%. For SMEs the situation is even more serious since in Mexico only 18.75% of formal companies with less than 20 employees had a line of credit while in Chile this figure was 73% and in Brazil 43%. In this context, the financial reform that the President of the Republic and leaders of various political parties, within the framework of the Pact for Mexico, have recently proposed to the Legislative Branch will contribute decisively to increasing the 10 financial inclusion. I would like to highlight some aspects of the reform that point in this direction:  The improvement of consumer protection is one of the central objectives of the reform, which is achieved by proposing greater powers for CONDUSEF to regulate the content of contracts and informative documents to customers, in addition to empowering CONDUSEF itself to eliminate unfair clauses in contracts. These powers will provide greater protection to users and better information regarding financial services, which will foster the confidence of the population in the formal financial system;  In the same direction points the creation of the Bureau of Financial Institutions that will allow consumers to compare the quality of the services of the bidders, the registration and disclosure of the commissions charged by the 11 popular financial institutions and banks as well as the prohibition of tied sales;  The reform explicitly provides for development banks to perform social banking functions, with the aim of promoting savings, financing, financial inclusion, the promotion of innovation, the gender perspective and investment among members of the popular savings and credit sector.  Finally, the possibilities of access to the system are further expanded by allowing popular financial companies to offer services through commission agents, which will help these institutions reach isolated segments of the population and compete equitably in this aspect with the banking sector. I urge all those who in one way or another participate or will participate in the design and final elaboration of said 12 reform not to lose sight of the fact that it will be a valuable instrument so that more and more Mexicans have access to savings and credit instruments, in increasingly better conditions and with better elements of protection in their use. This seminar, as proposed by the Foundation itself, will seek to disseminate the principles and best practices for the provision of financial services, especially savings, as a strategy to combat poverty and reduce social marginalization. We must be attentive to the lessons that it will offer in this circumstance of change and institutional improvement in the aspects that will be addressed. Congratulations for the excellent work that the Foundation promotes in Mexico and again thank you very much for these first ten years of persevering work in our country to favor the integral development of the poorest population. 13 I wish you every success in the work of this international seminar that is now beginning. 14
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la inauguracin del seminario internacional Inclusin financiera responsable y exitosa: modelos internacionales. 30 de mayo de 2013  Seor Heinrich Haasis, Presidente del Instituto Mundial de Cajas de Ahorro y de la Fundacin Alemana de Cajas de Ahorro para la Cooperacin Internacional (Sparkassenstiftung fr Internationale Kooperation)  Seor Niclaus Bergmann, Director General de la Fundacin Alemana de Cajas de Ahorro para la Cooperacin Internacional (Sparkassenstiftung fr Internationale Kooperation)  Seor Gerd Weissbach, Director de la Oficina de Representacin en Amrica Latina (Sparkassenstiftung fr Internationale Kooperation)  Seoras y seores: Agradezco la amable invitacin de la Fundacin Alemana de Cajas de Ahorro para la Cooperacin Internacional a inaugurar este seminario internacional que se ha propuesto abordar un tema tan vasto como importante: la inclusin 1 financiera y las modalidades exitosas en el mundo para fomentar y acrecentar el ahorro y crdito, en especial mediante las cajas de ahorro como instituciones no lucrativas tan conocidas y difundidas en Europa y, en particular, en Alemania. No cabe duda que Mxico ha generado un especial inters en la Fundacin y estamos muy agradecidos por ello. Y sobre todo destaca, en el marco de la inclusin financiera, el proyecto PATMIR fase II impulsado junto con SAGARPA, 2 un proyecto vigente para acercar los servicios financieros a personas que habitan en zonas rurales marginales a travs de alianzas, todo ello con la meta de incluir financieramente a 120 mil personas en ms de 22 estados de la Repblica. Este es slo uno de los muchos proyectos vigentes de la Fundacin. Y me parece de elemental justicia, al inicio de mi intervencin, hacer un reconocimiento pblico de lo mucho que la Fundacin ha servido a Mxico, especialmente a quienes ms lo necesitan. Existe vasta evidencia terica y emprica acerca del vnculo entre el desarrollo de las instituciones y los mercados financieros de un pas y el desarrollo econmico que tiene dicho pas; por ejemplo, si se hace un amplio corte transversal, los pases que tienen un PIB per cpita ms elevado tienen tambin una mayor razn de crdito al sector privado (como proporcin del PIB); de manera paralela, en los 3 pases en los que una mayor proporcin de la poblacin vive en pobreza suele haber poco crdito al sector privado en relacin al ingreso nacional. La inclusin financiera es un componente central del desarrollo financiero ya que permite que exista una mayor cantidad de recursos para la inversin y que se haga una asignacin ms eficiente de los recursos. La literatura econmica reciente ha mostrado que el acceso a servicios financieros bsicos, como las cuentas de depsito o ahorro y pequeos prstamos, permite que los individuos ahorren ms y de manera ms segura, que manejen mejor choques negativos a su salud o a su ingreso. Tambin se ha demostrado que una mayor inclusin financiera aumenta la actividad de pequeos empresarios y el empleo en las comunidades beneficiadas. De este modo, se puede hablar de un crculo virtuoso entre inclusin y desarrollo financiero y crecimiento econmico general. 4 La inclusin financiera ha sido una preocupacin permanente de las autoridades financieras mexicanas; en aos recientes, y en respuesta a tal preocupacin, se han puesto en marcha una serie de regulaciones y modificaciones a las leyes existentes para fomentarla. Uno de los avances con mayor potencial inclusivo es la introduccin de la banca mvil. En 2011, el Banco de Mxico emiti regulacin que permite la apertura de diferentes tipos de cuentas de acuerdo al nivel de operatividad y facilidad de apertura que tienen; las cuentas de bajo nivel se pueden abrir sin necesidad de visitar una sucursal y se requieren menos documentos para hacerlo. Estas cuentas conforman parte del esquema de banca mvil que ha tenido xito en otros pases para expandir la inclusin. De manera paralela, la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores cre la figura de comisionista bancario; estos son agentes no bancarios autorizados para prestar servicios a nombre y por cuenta de un banco. Los 5 comisionistas constituyen un canal eficiente para servir a localidades remotas ya que aprovechan la infraestructura instalada por otra empresa para ofrecer una gama de servicios bancarios. Con estos cambios, ya no es necesario ir a una sucursal o un cajero para consultar el saldo de la cuenta o hacer algn pago. Esto se puede hacer desde el telfono celular o en alguna tienda cercana que acte como comisionista. As, se espera que ms mexicanos, para los que no era viable usar los servicios bancarios, decidan acceder a ellos. En 2012 se estableci el Consejo Nacional de Inclusin Financiera (CNIF) cuya labor es por un lado, coordinar el esfuerzo que muchas instituciones pblicas y privadas han hecho en materia de inclusin financiera y, por otra, fijar la direccin que debe seguir el pas para alcanzar mayores niveles de inclusin. 6 Aunque promover la inclusin financiera no es su funcin primordial, el Banco de Mxico ha participado activamente en el consejo (CNIF) y ha adoptado una serie de medidas que tienen un impacto en la inclusin financiera, entre las que destaca la regulacin de cuentas bsicas. Estas son cuentas que proveen servicios de ahorro y pagos sin costo alguno y que todos los bancos que reciben depsitos estn obligados a ofrecer. Sin embargo, la principal contribucin del Banco de Mxico a la inclusin financiera es el mantenimiento de la estabilidad de precios. Mxico ha disfrutado por ms de una dcada de una inflacin baja y estable, cada vez ms cerca del objetivo del 3 por ciento anual. En los mercados financieros y entre el pblico existen expectativas de baja inflacin slidamente ancladas. Todo ello es gracias a una poltica monetaria responsable enmarcada en la autonoma que obtuvo el Banco de Mxico hace 20 aos. 7 Esta es una contribucin clave al desarrollo financiero ya que sera impensable, por ejemplo, promover el ahorro y el crdito de largo plazo sin estabilidad de precios. A pesar del impacto positivo que han tenido las regulaciones mencionadas y de la tendencia favorable de los indicadores de inclusin, todava existen en Mxico rezagos en esta materia. La Encuesta Nacional de Inclusin Financiera realizada en Mxico el ao pasado por el INEGI revela que en materia de 8 ahorro, 25 millones de adultos (el 36% del total) afirman tener al menos un instrumento de ahorro formal. En contraste, el Banco Mundial reporta que 42% de los adultos chilenos y 56% de los brasileos tiene una cuenta de banco. Entre los instrumentos de ahorro formal, las cuentas de nmina y las cuentas de ahorro son las que tienen el mayor nmero de usuarios. Aun siendo las cuentas de nmina el producto predominante de captacin, slo el 16% de quienes las tienen las usan para ahorrar dinero. La Encuesta encontr que el 44% de los mexicanos adultos (esto es: 31 millones de personas) ahorran en el mercado informal. Dentro de este grupo los mecanismos favoritos de ahorro son 28% en la casa y 14% mediante tandas. El 73 % de los adultos que no ahorran (que son 45 millones) o que lo hacen en una institucin informal, mencionan como principal barrera u obstculo que sus ingresos no les alcanzan para ahorrar o son ingresos demasiado variables. A 9 su vez, un 16% menciona que no ahorra porque no le interesa o no lo necesita. . El rezago es tambin notable en lo que se refiere al crdito a empresas, en particular pequeas y medianas. Segn una encuesta realizada por el Banco Mundial en 2010, slo 32% de las empresas formales en Mxico tenan un prstamo bancario o lnea de crdito, mientras en Chile eran 80% y en Brasil 66%. Para las PyMEs la situacin es an ms grave ya que en Mxico slo el 18.75% de las empresas formales con menos de 20 empleados tenan lnea de crdito mientras que en Chile esta cifra era 73% y en Brasil 43%. En este contexto la reforma financiera que recientemente el Presidente de la Repblica y dirigentes de diversos partidos polticos, en el marco del Pacto por Mxico, han propuesto al Poder Legislativo contribuir decisivamente a incrementar la 10 inclusin financiera. Quisiera destacar algunos aspectos de la reforma que apuntan en esta direccin:  La mejora a la proteccin de los consumidores es uno de los objetivos centrales de la reforma, lo cual se logra planteando mayores facultades para CONDUSEF para normar el contenido de contratos y documentos informativos a la clientela, adems de facultar a la propia CONDUSEF a eliminar clusulas abusivas en los contratos. Estas facultades proveern de mayor proteccin a los usuarios y mejor informacin con respecto a los servicios financieros lo que fomentar la confianza de la poblacin en el sistema financiero formal;  En la misma direccin apunta la creacin del Bur de Entidades Financieras que permitir a los consumidores comparar la calidad de los servicios de los oferentes, el registro y revelacin de las comisiones que cobran las 11 financieras populares y los bancos as como la prohibicin de las ventas atadas;  La reforma prev explcitamente que la banca de desarrollo realice funciones de banca social, previndose como su objeto promover el ahorro, el financiamiento, la inclusin financiera, el fomento de la innovacin, la perspectiva de gnero y la inversin entre los integrantes del Sector de ahorro y crdito popular.  Por ltimo, se amplan an ms las posibilidades de acceso al sistema al permitir que las financieras populares ofrezcan servicios a travs de comisionistas lo cual ayudar a que ests instituciones alcancen a segmentos aislados de la poblacin y compitan de manera equitativa en este aspecto con el sector bancario. Exhorto a todos los que de una u otra forma participamos o participaremos en el diseo y elaboracin final de dicha 12 reforma a no perder de vista que la misma ser un instrumento valioso para que cada vez ms mexicanos tengan acceso a los instrumentos de ahorro y crdito, en cada vez mejores condiciones y con mejores elementos de proteccin en su uso. En este seminario, segn lo ha propuesto la misma Fundacin, se buscar difundir los principios y las mejores prcticas para la provisin de servicios financieros, especialmente de ahorro, como estrategia para combatir la pobreza y reducir la marginacin social. Title: The museum and economic science
text: The museum and economic science Words of Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the inauguration of the board of directors of the Mexican Association of Museums and Science and Technology Centers Interactive Museum of Economy Mexico, D.F. January 18, 2016 It gives me great pleasure to participate in this academic day organized by the Mexican Association of Museums and Science and Technology Centers. This occasion is special because the inauguration of the new board of directors of the Association for the period 2016-2018 is also taking place, which will honorably preside over the Interactive Museum of Economy (MIDE). The transformation of the notion of museums Museums were born as spaces to preserve and exhibit sets of artistic objects or collections of scientific, historical and any other information, which societies consider significant to protect. Through aesthetic or intellectual revelation, museums have enormous potential to change, in a very short time, the individual's perspective towards his environment. The visitor of a museum can leave it with a renewed vision around the world, as well as with new tools. Until a few decades ago, museums used to be conceived as elitist and solemn environments, to which the visitor came, somewhat inhibited and passively, to contemplate an unappealable testimony of human inventiveness. This conception has been changing. The mass dissemination strategies and interactive approaches being adopted by most of the world's leading museums 1 they contribute to eliminating the halo of grandiloquence of these places and to promote a more empathetic experience with the viewer. Scientific and technological museums have been pioneers in this new relationship with the public. By their nature, these enclosures require managing a strategy of interaction with their visitors that allows them, through an attractive and synthetic arrangement of information, to present the different branches and cultivate vocations. In the case of a museum dedicated exclusively to economics, such as MIDE, it is important that the scientific nature of the discipline is shown and its logic is disseminated in an accessible way to audiences of all kinds. Economics is a science, just like medicine, physics, or mathematics, because it uses the scientific method. The elaboration of formal theories based on basic principles and their methods of verification consolidate its character as a science. However, while almost no one would feel entitled to submit a mathematical theorem, a concept of physics or a corroborated medical procedure to discussion and public consultation, most people consider themselves fit to express their opinion and debate on economic matters. 2 Economics is not an exact science, as is not entirely any of the disciplines. Its predictive power in the short term is fallible and some of its conclusions may be provisional and reviewable. However, there are a number of principles and laws that are highly useful for interpreting countless phenomena. This includes aspects traditionally considered non-economic, such as patterns of delinquency, vocational guidance, or choosing a partner.1 It is worth asking: why, despite the status of economics as a science, do most insist on considering themselves capable of expressing an opinion on its management and of manipulating or reinventing its fundamental postulates? Of course, in the democratic sense, it is very understandable that many citizens are interested in the economy and seek to influence issues and policy actions that may affect them. In this search for influence, it is not surprising that proposals are often put forward that sound seductive, but are unfeasible from the point of view of economic logic. Sometimes those who lead these ideas are interest groups 1 For this topic see the seminal work of Gary Becker, Becker, G.S. and G.N. Becker (2002). The Everyday Economy, Mexico: Planet. 3 who seek dividends for their cause, at other times are people of good faith who ignore the repercussions of such initiatives. These proposals that appeal more to emotions than to the reasoning to be accredited, usually fall into the category of fallacies. To mention a simple example, a fallacy is established when the expectation is created that, in order to safeguard employment, it is essential to protect local companies from competition, mainly from abroad, ignoring the potential for growth and social welfare implied by the profusion of projects that flourish in an environment of openness.2 The role of MIDE From all the above derives the importance of an institution such as MIDE, which seeks to explain in simple terms the functioning of the economy. That is why, since its inception, the Bank of Mexico has strongly supported the project of this museum. With an extraordinary inventiveness, which incorporates the use of interactive equipment, computer games, multimedia resources, shows or workshops, the MIDE allows to introduce audiences of all ages in topics such as 2 For a review of the nature and role of economic fallacies, as well as their various varieties, see Sowell, T. (2011) Economic Facts and Fallacies, New York: Basic Books. 4 principles of growth, the functioning of markets and the rudiments of finance. I have visited this museum many times for pleasure and I am particularly pleased with this pedagogical approach that enables children and young people, through entertaining games, to acquire the responsibility of managing a budget and, in many ways, to emulate the dilemmas of an entrepreneur, a head of family, or an economic policy maker. These recreational exercises can be a permanent revelation for MIDE users. In particular, perceiving the trade-offs of opportunity costs, and understanding that resources are scarce and one choice involves the sacrifice of another, or learning to exercise ingenuity and discipline to maximize benefits within certain budgetary constraints, contributes to educating agency and helps an individual, a company or a country avoids costly and sometimes tragic mistakes. New challenges for scientific, technological and economic museums The dissemination of scientific and technological culture is fundamental for the country. The Mexican Association of Museums and Science and Technology Centers, which already has 35 members, plays a very important role in sharing experiences and coordinating the efforts of institutions with similar missions. 5 I am sure that, with collaboration and the exchange of information, it will be feasible to extend the coverage and impact of scientific and technological museums, as well as to make the most of modern platforms to attract new audiences. In particular, with regard to today's academic day, the presence of keynote speakers will undoubtedly contribute to enriching the discussion on crucial issues such as funding, media positioning or the digital transformation of museums and science centers. Regarding the change of board of directors of the Association, the Bank of Mexico is proud that MIDE has been elected to preside for the next two years. With the hard work of its great team, MIDE has exceeded the expectations placed at the time of its creation and, in its still brief history, has accumulated important recognitions and has positioned itself as a vanguard model in economic dissemination. Therefore, I congratulate each and every one of the participants in the academic day, and I wish the greatest success to the members of the new board of directors of the Mexican Association of Museums and Science and Technology Centers. 6
text_original: El museo y la ciencia econmica Palabras de Manuel Snchez Gonzlez Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico en la toma de posesin de la mesa directiva de la Asociacin Mexicana de Museos y Centros de Ciencia y Tecnologa Museo Interactivo de Economa Mxico, D.F. 18 de enero de 2016 Me da mucho gusto participar en esta jornada acadmica organizada por la Asociacin Mexicana de Museos y Centros de Ciencia y Tecnologa. Esta ocasin es especial porque tambin se lleva a cabo la toma de posesin de la nueva mesa directiva de la Asociacin para el periodo 2016-2018, la cual honrosamente presidir el Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE). La transformacin de la nocin de los museos Los museos nacieron como espacios para conservar y exhibir conjuntos de objetos artsticos o acervos de informacin cientfica, histrica y de cualquier otra ndole, que las sociedades consideran significativo resguardar. Mediante la revelacin esttica o intelectual, los museos tienen un enorme potencial para cambiar, en un lapso muy breve, la ptica del individuo hacia su entorno. El visitante de un museo puede salir de este con una visin renovada en torno al mundo, as como con nuevas herramientas. Hasta hace pocas dcadas, los museos solan concebirse como ambientes elitistas y solemnes, a los que el visitante acuda, un tanto inhibido y de forma pasiva, a contemplar un testimonio inapelable de la inventiva humana. Tal concepcin ha venido cambiando. Las estrategias de difusin masiva y los enfoques interactivos que est adoptando la mayora de los museos ms importantes del mundo 1 contribuyen a eliminar el halo de grandilocuencia de estos lugares y a propiciar una experiencia ms emptica con el espectador. Los museos cientficos y tecnolgicos han sido pioneros en esta nueva relacin con el pblico. Por su naturaleza, estos recintos requieren manejar una estrategia de interaccin con sus visitantes que les permita, mediante una disposicin atractiva y sinttica de la informacin, presentar las distintas ramas y cultivar vocaciones. En el caso de un museo dedicado exclusivamente a la economa, como el MIDE, es importante que se muestre la naturaleza cientfica de la disciplina y se difunda de manera accesible su lgica hacia audiencias de todo tipo. La naturaleza del conocimiento econmico La economa es una ciencia, al igual que la medicina, la fsica o las matemticas, porque utiliza el mtodo cientfico. La elaboracin de teoras formales a partir de principios bsicos y sus mtodos de comprobacin consolidan su carcter de ciencia. No obstante, mientras que casi nadie se sentira autorizado a someter a discusin y consulta pblica un teorema matemtico, un concepto de la fsica o un procedimiento mdico corroborado, la mayora de las personas se considera apta para opinar y debatir sobre asuntos econmicos. 2 La economa no es una ciencia exacta, como no lo es en su totalidad ninguna de las disciplinas. Su poder predictivo en el corto plazo es falible y algunas de sus conclusiones pueden ser provisionales y revisables. Sin embargo, existe una serie de principios y leyes que son altamente tiles para interpretar un sinnmero de fenmenos. Esto incluye aspectos tradicionalmente considerados no econmicos, como los patrones de la delincuencia, la orientacin vocacional o la eleccin de una pareja.1 Cabe preguntarse: por qu, pese al estatuto de la economa como ciencia, la mayora insiste en considerarse capacitada para opinar sobre su manejo y para manipular o reinventar sus postulados fundamentales? Por supuesto, en el sentido democrtico, es muy entendible que muchos ciudadanos se interesen por la economa y busquen influir en temas y acciones de poltica que los pueden afectar. En esta bsqueda de influencia no es extrao que, con frecuencia, se enarbolen propuestas que suenan seductoras, pero que son inviables desde el punto de vista de la lgica econmica. A veces quienes encabezan estas ideas son grupos de inters 1 Para este tema vase el trabajo seminal de Gary Becker, Becker, G.S. y G.N. Becker (2002). La Economa Cotidiana, Mxico: Planeta. 3 que persiguen dividendos para su causa, en otras ocasiones son personas de buena fe que ignoran las repercusiones de dichas iniciativas. Estas propuestas que apelan ms a las emociones que al razonamiento para acreditarse, suelen caer en la categora de falacias. Por mencionar un sencillo ejemplo, una falacia se establece cuando se crea la expectativa de que, para resguardar el empleo, es indispensable proteger a las empresas locales de la competencia, principalmente del exterior, ignorando el potencial de crecimiento y bienestar social que implica la profusin de proyectos que florecen en un ambiente de apertura.2 El papel del MIDE De todo lo anterior se deriva la importancia de una institucin como el MIDE, que busca explicar en trminos sencillos el funcionamiento de la economa. Por eso, desde su gestacin, el Banco de Mxico ha apoyado decididamente el proyecto de este museo. Con una extraordinaria inventiva, que incorpora la utilizacin de equipos interactivos, juegos de computadora, recursos multimedia, espectculos o talleres, el MIDE permite introducir a pblicos de todas las edades en temas como los 2 Para una revisin de la naturaleza y el papel de las falacias econmicas, as como de sus distintas variedades, vase Sowell, T. (2011) Economic Facts and Fallacies, Nueva York: Basic Books. 4 principios del crecimiento, el funcionamiento de los mercados y los rudimentos de las finanzas. He visitado muchas veces este museo por placer y me complace particularmente ese enfoque pedaggico que posibilita a nios y jvenes, mediante entretenidos juegos, adquirir la responsabilidad de administrar un presupuesto y, en muchos sentidos, emular los dilemas de un empresario, de un jefe de familia, o de un responsable de poltica econmica. Estos ejercicios recreativos pueden constituir una revelacin permanente para los usuarios del MIDE. En particular, el percibir las disyuntivas que implican los costos de oportunidad, y entender que los recursos son escasos y una eleccin implica el sacrificio de otra o, bien, el aprender a ejercer el ingenio y la disciplina para maximizar los beneficios dentro de determinadas restricciones presupuestales, contribuye a educar el albedro y ayuda a que un individuo, una empresa o un pas eviten errores costosos y en ocasiones trgicos. Nuevos retos de los museos cientficos, tecnolgicos y econmicos La difusin de la cultura cientfica y tecnolgica es fundamental para el pas. La Asociacin Mexicana de Museos y Centros de Ciencia y Tecnologa, que cuenta ya con 35 miembros, cumple un papel muy importante para compartir experiencias y coordinar esfuerzos de instituciones con misiones similares. 5 Estoy seguro que, con la colaboracin y el intercambio de informacin, ser factible extender la cobertura e impacto de los museos cientficos y tecnolgicos, as como aprovechar al mximo las modernas plataformas para captar nuevos pblicos. En particular, en lo que toca a la jornada acadmica de hoy, sin duda la presencia de ponentes de primer orden contribuir a enriquecer la discusin en torno a temas cruciales como el fondeo, el posicionamiento meditico o la transformacin digital de los museos y centros de ciencia. En lo que atae al cambio de mesa directiva de la Asociacin, para el Banco de Mxico es un orgullo que el MIDE haya sido elegido para presidir por los prximos dos aos. Con el trabajo denodado de su gran equipo, el MIDE ha superado las expectativas depositadas al momento de su creacin y, en su todava breve historia, ha acumulado importantes reconocimientos y se ha situado como un modelo de vanguardia en la divulgacin econmica. As pues, felicito a todos y cada uno de los participantes en la jornada acadmica, y deseo el mayor de los xitos a los integrantes de la nueva mesa directiva de la Asociacin Mexicana de Museos y Centros de Ciencia y Tecnologa. 6

Title: Biodiversity and environmental challenges for the financial system conference
Subtitle: Remarks by Alejandro Daz de Len, Governor of Banco de Mxico, at the Biodiversity and Environmental Challenges for the Financial System Conference
text: Remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of Banco de Mexico, at the Biodiversity and Environmental Challenges for the Financial System Conference.1 Mexico City, November 30, 2021 1. Mexico is a biodiverse country Good morning, good afternoon, good evening ladies and gentlemen. First let me thank our very distinguished speakers and participants for making this first Biodiversity and Environmental Challenges for the Financial System conference possible. The conference is only starting but from the very high interest all over the world I am confident to say that it will be very successful. Mexico is a biologically megadiverse country. It ranks fourth in the group of 17 megadiverse countries that have 70% of globally known species (Mittermeier et al., 1997, 2011a). Biodiversity provides a range of benefits and significant positive global and local externalities. Unfortunately, it is threatened by climate change, 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the sole responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Banco de Mexico or of its Governing Board. 1 deforestation originated in agricultural and livestock extension, as well as by air, water, ocean and soil pollution, unsustainable fisheries and the pressures of unplanned urbanization. These are particularly acute in emerging markets and low-income countries. 2. There is an unsustainable degradation of ecosystems and biodiversity At the origin of loss of biodiversity and ecosystem degradation is failure by markets to internalize and to properly price-in both the positive externalities from biodiversity and ecosystems services, and the negative externalities caused by activities that erode our biodiversity and natural capital. The high demands we are placing on ecosystems, given the current level of economic activity, are no longer sustainable. They compromise the health and living conditions of current and future generations and entail unknown economic and financial risks. Preserving and restoring natural capital is essential to mitigate these risks. Ecosystems provide a wide range of services such as urban cooling, coastal protection, energy production, carbon capture, food production, 2 supporting physical and mental health, and scenic beauty. For example, forests play a crucial role in water supply: storage and flows, drinking, irrigation, flood control protection of downstream communities and property and even have influence on the levels of precipitation. Mangroves are transitional ecosystems between terrestrial and marine ones, they develop in coastal lagoons and river mouths and act as a natural flood control system; they act as a barrier against hurricanes; they reduce erosion and protect coasts; they capture carbon and improve water quality by acting as a biological filter, and also serve as a refuge for numerous species of flora and fauna. Safeguarding natural capital has also positive global externalities. The financial community is only beginning to understand the value of ecosystem goods and services for economic activity and its sustainability. There is a close interlinkage between climate change and biodiversity loss (IPBES (2021)). In the transition to a sustainable economy it is essential to consider climate change and biodiversity loss in parallel, taking into account their specific characteristics. 3 Developing and emerging countries face an additional challenge, as some mistakenly believe that caring for biodiversity and ecosystems is an agenda that only advanced economies can afford. Losing biodiversity and natural capital makes countries poorer and less resilient. This is particularly challenging for developing and emerging economies with a large endowment of natural capital. Banco de Mexico is raising awareness on the importance of biodiversity within the general public. We have included images of the flora and the fauna of the most important ecosystems of Mexico on the back of the new six banknotes recently issued. 3. To preserve biodiversity, we must heed the advice of scientists The Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) has provided evidence of the risks we face due to the accelerated changes in nature that are being observed. In the case of Mexico, the National Commission for the Knowledge and Use of Biodiversity (CONABIO, for its Spanish acronym) provides important information on the trends and stock of natural capital.2 2 The general entry to the CONABIO portal is: / 4  Two thirds of the country have high levels of degradation.  Only 12 out of 31 states maintain sustainability conditions in ecosystems that preserve natural capital.  Nine states have high levels of natural capital depletion with a high probability of reaching unsustainable levels.  Eleven states have practically depleted all their natural capital.3 States with diminished natural capital tend to have greater soil erosion, be more prone to floods, and tend to suffer outsized negative economic impacts from droughts, tropical storms, and hurricanes. They face deterioration of development opportunities, declining productivity and reduced welfare. There is a growing conviction among international business and the financial community that nature should be explicitly considered as part of economic analysis and that it cannot be ignored or treated as a separate system as it entails serious sustainability implications. This is strongly supported by academic literature (Dasgupta, 2021), with a deeper understanding of the impacts of firms activities on natural 3 See: 5 ecosystems, and their interaction with physical and transition risks (see NGFS & INSPIRE, TNFD, WBCSD). As nature is impacted by human activities, businesses, the economy, and finance will be progressively affected and face increasing interrelated risks. 4. Importance of information systems and disclosure Nowadays, there are many tools that can be used by companies and market participants to assess the impact of ecosystem services on key economic sectors, such as agriculture, tourism, construction, electricity generation, and construction materials, among many others. During this conference we will address how some of these tools and frameworks provide relevant information to financial institutions on nature related financially material risks.4 To mention a few examples: 1. The science-based targets for nature (SBTN) aim to serve as a guidance for companies to align their business practices with ecosystems capacities. 4 Science-based Targets for Nature Initial Guidance for Business, September 2020. 6 2. Tools like Encore can help rank and prioritize financial exposures and dependencies of economic activities to ecosystem services. 3. The Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) currently under development, will complement the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) framework. It will provide recommendations on how firms should address naturerelated risks in their governance, strategy, risk management activities, and metrics and targets. These tools help financial and non-financial firms assess the risks they are exposed to from environmental degradation and move towards nature-positive outcomes. 5. Opportunities (nature-based solutions) As financial institutions understand better the benefits of ecosystems services and the potential for nature-based solutions, they will improve their pricing of loans and identify potential investment opportunities, unlocking capital towards these activities. 7 Innovative financial instruments are starting to be used for the conservation of ecosystems. For example:  Parametric insurance of coral reefs and beaches in Mexicos Yucatan peninsula. This insurance covers the damage done by hurricanes to coral reefs and beaches from Cancun to Tulum. This is part of the second largest coral reef in the world. Coral reefs preserve biodiverse marine life and help avoid the erosion of beaches caused by hurricanes.  Nature performance bonds (NPBs) aimed at emerging market nations to protect ecosystems and biodiversity (F4B report), are linked to pre-defined targets for nature and climate. Positive outcomes would bring about reductions in coupon payments, and even have the potential for adjustment of principal.  Financing sustainable and more efficient agriculture that restores soil fertility, nutrients and biodiversity can generate better longterm returns, especially in the context of climate-related physical risks. Countries or regions highly vulnerable to extreme climate events are finding that nature-based solutions can be a cost-effective way to 8 mitigate the damage from such events. For some, such investments are indispensable to maintain insurability and bankability. 6. Role of financial authorities and central banks With the support from the scientific and financial communities and other stakeholders, financial authorities can play a key role in addressing the risks and opportunities associated with restoring and preserving biodiversity and natural capital. This can be achieved by promoting metrics, standards, and disclosure practices, and integrating biodiversity-related risk factors into financial decision-making. By making sure financial institutions have access to information on ecosystem services and dependencies, promoting nature-related financial disclosures, and the integration of financially material information in their financial decisions, financial authorities can contribute to the preservation of natural capital. Financial authorities can also explore the role credit bureaus can have in collecting and providing data to credit institutions on the environmental compliance of borrowers. By providing this information in their reports, 9 credit bureaus could limit unlawful predatory behavior of firms that degrade the environment, particularly in emerging countries with a weak rule of law. Finally, central banks have been granted autonomy to insulate them from short-term political pressures, giving them the necessary space to pursue long-term objectives. Although central banks main mandate is the provision of money, safeguarding financial stability over time is also key. Under this long-term perspective, their actions require alignment with broadly defined social welfare and sustainability objectives. 10 References Dasgupta, P. 2021.
