Title: Impact of agri-food price volatility
text: "Impact of the volatility of agri-food prices" Conference of the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, at the international seminar "Food Security in a Context of High Food Price Volatility and Low Productivity in Latin America and the Caribbean: Challenges and Opportunities" March 27, 2014, Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico.  Mr. Arturo Zamora Jimenez, Secretary General of the Government of the State of Jalisco, to whom I ask to convey my attentive greetings to Governor Sandoval Diaz,  Dr. Fernando Aportela Rodriguez, Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit,  Engineer Ramiro Hernandez Garcia, Municipal President of Guadalajara,  Engineer Hector Padilla Gutierrez, Secretary of Rural Development of the state of Jalisco, 1  Dr. Rafael Gamboa Gonzalez, General Director of FIRA,  Dear colleagues of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico,  Distinguished panelists participating in this international seminar,  Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, good morning. I thank the State of Jalisco for its generous hospitality for the celebration of this important international seminar. It is worth remembering that the state of Jalisco is the federative entity of the country that contributes the most to the Gross Domestic Product of primary activities - this is in the line that groups: agriculture, breeding and exploitation of 2 animals, forestry, fishing and hunting -, with 10.5 percent of the national total. I am also grateful for the valuable participation of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Rural Development, Fisheries and Food (SAGARPA), for the celebration of this seminar, organized jointly by FIRA and the Government of the state of Jalisco. No one should be surprised by the great interest we have in the Bank of Mexico in having the problem of high volatility in agri-food prices addressed deeply and extensively. As is known, the main mandate of the Bank of Mexico, established in the Constitution, is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency. In short: fight inflation. For the full fulfillment of this objective, invaluable support would be to have a scenario in which the 3 frequent fluctuations in agri-food prices are effectively mitigated. I have no doubt that from these two days of intense dialogue and work between specialists will emerge proposals for public policies that attack this problem that seriously affects millions of consumers, especially those with less purchasing power. A problem that also harms tens of thousands of producers in Latin America and the Caribbean. In addition to proposals that help mitigate food price volatility, public policies that increase rural productivity and strengthen better functioning of agricultural markets need to be refined. There is clear evidence that in recent years the monetary policy implemented by the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, and an adequate communication of it, have 4 managed to anchor more and better inflation expectations. Thanks to this anchoring of expectations, relative price fluctuations - among which those of some foods and agricultural products usually stand out - are prevented from causing second-order effects. That is to say: that such variations do not infect the general dynamics of consumer prices. Thus, these oscillations have been transitory in nature and, once overcome, allow general inflation to resume its convergent trajectory towards the permanent objective of the Bank of Mexico. This means that, by itself, the high volatility of some agri-food prices does not normally represent a problem that should or can be addressed with monetary policy tools. However, such relative price volatility is a serious problem for millions of consumers, especially the poorest families, and seriously disrupts the economy of thousands of producers. 5 since just as such prices increase abruptly, in the same way they suddenly fall, upsetting any attempt by agricultural producers to carry out rational and efficient planning in their businesses. Figure 1 INPC and Agricultural Product Price Index Annual % change September 2007-March 2014 18 16 14 Agricultural 12 10 8 6 4 2 INPC 0 -2 */ Information as of the first half of March 2014. Source: Bank of Mexico and INEGI. 6 Sep-07 Mar-08 Sep-08 Mar-09 Sep-09 Mar-10 Sep-10 Mar-11 Sep-11 Mar-12 Sep-12 Mar-13 Sep-13 *Mar-14 Let me show you an eloquent graphic representation of this problem. The red line of the graph represents the annual variation, measured month by month, of the National Consumer Price Index - that is: general inflation - while the blue line represents the annual variations, also measured month by month, of the price index of agricultural products. As you can see, the price variations of agricultural products resemble the strong oscillations that a seismograph could register in the event of an earthquake. Note the gap between the biggest drop in agricultural prices in July 2010 (about minus two percent per year) and the rise in those same prices in February 2013 (which is about 17 percent per year). We are talking about an absolute variation of almost 20 percentage points in less than three years. And note, too, that we are not talking about the price of a single product (such as egg, chicken or lemon, in which case we would have records of variations 7 annual in terms of percentages up to three digits) but of the whole set of agricultural products. Undoubtedly, these brutal oscillations have a reflection in the changes in headline inflation, as clearly seen in the following graph: Figure 2 Headline Inflation and Inflation Excluding Products Agricultural Annual % change September 2007-March 2014 7 6 INPC 5 4 3 INPC Excluding Agricultural 2 1 0 */ Information as of the first half of March 2014. Source: Bank of Mexico and INEGI. 8 Sep-07 Mar-08 Sep-08 Mar-09 Sep-09 Mar-10 Sep-10 Mar-11 Sep-11 Mar-12 Sep-12 Mar-13 Sep-13 *Mar-14 This impact on the general price index is explained by the great weight that agri-food products have in the basic consumption basket of families. As we all know, the weight of these products in family spending is greater as household income is lower. Based on data from the National Household Income and Expenditure Survey, the Bank of Mexico has identified 14 agricultural products in which most of the spending made on food by lower-income families is concentrated. With these data, this graph was elaborated that shows the percentage of their income that each of the ten groups or deciles in which all Mexican households are divided allocates, first, to the acquisition of these products (which is the blue segment of each of the bars) and, second, the percentage of their income that each group allocates to the purchase of other foods. By the way, the prices of those 14 products, in addition to being those of 9 Higher consumption, usually register episodes of high volatility, caused by meteorological phenomena, epidemics and, in general, contingencies that severely affect their supply. Incomes range from the lowest to the highest, from left to right on the horizontal axis of the graph. Figure 3 Household Food Expenditure by Income Decile % of total expenditure 18.5 47.2 17.1 45.7 15.9 42.6 40.3 Other Foods Selected Products and Derivatives 37.1 36.0 33.7 30.6 50 45 40 35 12.7 13.4 13.8 15.2 25.9 30 25 11.7 9.4 6.7 15.5 10.4 18.8 21.0 22.6 23.3 25.1 26.7 28.5 28.7 16.1 20 15 10 5 0 I II III IV V VI VII VIII IX X Source: Bank of Mexico estimates with data from ENIGH 2010. The basket of selected products is made up of avocado, sugar, zucchini, pork, beef, onion, egg, tomato, milk, lemon, corn, chicken, green tomato and wheat. 10 The 14 products selected are: avocado, sugar, zucchini, pork, beef, onion, egg, tomato, milk, lemon, corn, chicken, green tomato and wheat. The graph itself is revealing. It highlights that for the first seven deciles of lower incomes, spending on these 14 foods alone represents more than 20 percent, becoming, for ten percent of the poorest households in Mexico, 28.7 percent of their total spending. And if we add to this the expenditure on other foods, it turns out that the percentages of total spending on food in households located in the first five deciles of income, that is, in the poorest households in the country, range from 37.1 percent to 47.2 percent of total spending. In contrast, households in the highest income decile only spend 16.1 percent of their total spending on food, and spend less than 10 percent of their total spending on the 14 selected foods. 11 It seems to me that in view of these data, the importance and justification of the national crusade against hunger proposed by the government of President Enrique Pena Nieto stands out. Within this crucial fight for the well-being of the country, the importance of applying correct and timely public policies to mitigate volatility in these prices and, along with it, increase the productivity and profitability of agricultural producers stands out. Therefore, and beyond even the impact of the volatility of these prices on general inflation, for the Bank of Mexico this is a matter of primary importance. As we have repeatedly pointed out: the priority objective of the Central Bank - price stability - is not an end in itself, but a requirement for a higher end that is the well-being of Mexicans, in an environment of accelerated and sustainable economic growth. 12 I am referring, now, to a relatively recent case that shows how an episode of abrupt volatility of a single agri-food price can weigh on the General Consumer Price Index. This case is that of the outbreak of avian influenza detected at the beginning of the summer of 2012. Before this outbreak, in June 2012, the price of eggs registered an annual increase of 5.9 percent, so it impacted the National Consumer Price Index (INPC) by only 0.04 percent. But three months later, in September 2012, the annual variation in the price of the egg was already 40.01 percent, which meant an impact on the INPC of 0.27 percentage points. As pointed out by the Bank of Mexico, in its Inflation Report for the July-September quarter of 2012, this implied that the increase in annual general inflation in the period June to September 2012 inclusive - which was 0.43 points 13 more than half was explained by the impact of the rise in the price of eggs. In addition, as I pointed out at the time in a newspaper interview, this rebound in general inflation was not going to subside even by applying a more restrictive monetary policy: chickens do not lay more eggs in response to a rise in interest rates. Undoubtedly, the high volatility of agri-food prices is influenced by various factors and practically each product presents a peculiar problem. For example, the impact that the global supply of grains has on numerous prices, along virtually the entire food production chain, is decisive. But it is also important, for some products whose prices show high volatility, such as tomato, the investment in cold nets. 14 In other cases, it is clear that producers diversify their investments in several products or even in the same product but in several regions, given that excessive concentration - as in investments in financial instruments - increases the risks, in this case the risks in the face of health crises or climatic events. In short, the importance of efficiently attacking the set of causes behind the high volatility of food prices is evident, so I congratulate the government of the state of Jalisco and FIRA for this valuable international seminar that, by the way, could be considered a preview of the celebrations for the 60th anniversary of FIRA, financial institution of promotion that was a visionary initiative of the Bank of Mexico and its then general director, Mr. Rodrigo Gomez. 15 Undoubtedly, with the celebration of this international seminar and with the punctual follow-up to the proposals that arise from it, FIRA will endorse its unalterable vocation of six decades at the service of the agricultural producers of Mexico and, ultimately, at the service of the well-being of all Mexicans. Thanks a lot. 16

Licenciado Arturo Zamora Jimnez, Secretario General de Gobierno del Estado de Jalisco, a quien pido transmitir mis atentos saludos al Gobernador Sandoval Daz,  Doctor Fernando Aportela Rodrguez, Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico,  Ingeniero Ramiro Hernndez Garca, Presidente Municipal de Guadalajara,  Ingeniero Hctor Padilla Gutirrez, Secretario de Desarrollo Rural del estado de Jalisco, 1  Doctor Rafael Gamboa Gonzlez, Director General de FIRA,  Estimados compaeros de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico,  Distinguidos panelistas participantes en este seminario internacional,  Seoras y seores: Antes que nada, muy buenos das. Title: Monetary policy in the pandemic: the Mexican experience
text: European Economics & Financial Centre Distinguished Speakers Seminar Monetary policy in the pandemic: the Mexican experience Jonathan Heath April 2021 Introduction Almost all countries in the world, if not all, have experienced the pandemic shock brought on by the propagation of the Covid-19 virus. The sudden stop in economic activity instigated by lockdown measures triggered massive disruptions in labor markets, together with a series of demand and supply shocks that had not been dealt with before. The common response from fiscal and monetary authorities worldwide has been countercyclical policies, which means sharp increases in government expenditures and significant expansionary monetary postures. While the health crisis is starting to succumb to vaccination efforts in parts of the world, progress has been vastly uneven throughout regions, while some countries have yet to see the beginning of the flattening of contagion curves and more than 40 countries have yet to apply a single vaccination. Most of the lessons learnt share a lot of common ground. Many countries, especially those with a profound financial deepening, have enacted massive fiscal stimuli aimed at minimizing job losses and avoiding business closures. The increase in sovereign debt around the world is most likely to be the next big issue to be faced once the pandemic is finally over. Exit strategies from the massive liquidity that is being injected into the world financial system will also likely be another branch in monetary studies. In the future, both fiscal and monetary policy responses will most likely be different from the typical recipes of the past, transformed into some sort of a new orthodoxy. Yet not all experiences have been the same. Some countries face idiosyncratic characteristics that make following typical recommendations much harder. Fiscal restrictions differ, risk perceptions vary, monetary independences contrast and political situations cannot be compared. Mexico is one these countries that stands out, that has been forced to follow different routes. For starters, the government has decided to enforce strict budget restrictions and not to use debt to finance any expansion of expenditures, which does not allow for any countercyclical fiscal policy. Monetary policy seems to be standing alone, trying to control inflation, inducing a more vigorous economic recovery and maintaining macro prudential conditions in order to preserve financial stability, all at the same time. 1 Is it possible to achieve these multiple objectives with only one policy instrument? Before trying to answer this question and speculate about the future, I will start by giving a brief background in order to understand how Mexico has arrived at where it is now. Background Between 1973 and 1993 Mexico went through two decades of great instability, with inflation averaging 43% per year. The main reason was very high fiscal dominance, created by chronic fiscal deficits that were financed through monetary expansion. In 1983, Mexico was the first country to manifest unmanageable external debt levels which triggered the world financial crisis of the eighties. Inflation soared into triple digit inflation levels and economic growth was absent for almost a decade. At the beginning of the nineties, Mexico slowly started correcting its disequilibrium, through fiscal retrenchment, the sell-off of public enterprises and the opening up its economy. Not only did it manage to balance the budget, but also to reduce its debt levels. Most of these reforms were deemed successful, but some were neither as transparent as they should have been nor truly solved some of their deep structural problems. For example, many public monopolies were substituted for private monopolies. At the beginning, it solved fiscal imbalances but never created a truly competitive economy, or worse, never corrected its crony capitalism. Massive corruption, weak judicial institutions and a weak regard for the rule of law persisted. Nevertheless, one very positive achievement was transforming the Central Bank into an autonomous institution, basically guaranteeing the end of fiscal dominance and the reintroduction of the price stability that has persisted over the past 25 years. The first five years were very difficult, but by the beginning of the century the inflation rate was only a one-digit number. Once this was achieved a transition phase towards inflation targeting started and was fully adopted in 2003. Price stability, monetary dominance and the new role of the Central Bank helped Mexico develop a local debt market and an extension of the governments yield curve. At the start of the century, this curve ended with a one-year bond, however, by 2006 it had extended to 30 years. Once this was achieved, starting in 2008, the Central Bank was able to begin using an interest rate target for the overnight funding market, very similar to what now prevails in most countries. Since 2003, the inflation rate has averaged 4.1% per year, together with very low volatility. There have only been two bouts of relatively high inflation, in 2008 and 2017, but in both cases the rate never reached 7%. In 2008, inflation peaked at 6.5% as a result of the increases in world commodity prices, while in 2017 it reached a high of 6.8% as a result of a huge once-and-for all increase in gasoline prices. Both cases were brought about by exogenous supply shocks and not by excessive aggregate demand. 2 Mexico has not truly achieved its inflation target of 3% on a consistent basis. Like most emerging economies, it has continuously faced supply shocks which are harder to control through traditional monetary management. This is evident when pointing out that non-core inflation has averaged 5.7% in the past 18 years, only ending up below 4% on five occasions. By contrast core inflation, which is much more responsive to monetary policy actions, has averaged 3.7% during the same period and has only been above 4% in 3 out of the past 18 years. Following the taper tantrum in 2013, Mexico faced a couple of years of a continuous weakening of the peso. In spite of this, not only was it able to contain inflation, but it even registered a historical low rate of 2.1%. This allowed it to continue with its monetary expansion phase, until the Federal Reserve started to hike rates in December 2015. However, it once again faced a series of exogenous shocks, including a significant drop in oil prices, forcing the Central Bank to not only replicate the Feds cycle, but to speed it up by hiking Mexicos rate at a faster pace. Mexicos risk perception increased sharply with Trumps arrival after which the government made a policy error by increasing gasoline prices by over 20% in one fell swoop, pushing inflation to 6.8% by the end of 2017. Even though inflation started coming down in 2018, Mexico faced political uncertainty starting with the 2018 elections and then the arrival of a new government at the end of that year. With inflation above its target and sovereign risk perception remaining high, the Central Bank responded by increasing rates from 3.0% in December 2015 to 8.25% three years later. Mexicos new government has a very different philosophy than any of the previous governments that it has had in almost a century. Self-described as left-wing, it has proved to be both populist and conservative all at the same time. Its main crusade has been an allout fight against corruption and the ingrown crony capitalism that has promoted extremely unequal income distribution and widespread poverty. It has tried to be very austere in government expenditures, avoiding financing fiscal expansion through debt and focusing most of its efforts on social programs aimed at lower income segments of the population. In its campaign to end crony capitalism, however, it has created a deep divide with the business sector, which in turn has all but stopped investing. It has created an overall sense of uncertainty and has shown little regard for the rule of law. This caused the economy to enter into a recession phase at some moment in 2019, before the pandemic started. However, this lack of investment problem existed before the current government arrived. In spite of many reforms carried out in 2013, total fixed investment peaked in 2015 and has failed to grow since. Among its many policies, the present government has pursued an aggressive minimum wage policy, through relatively high increases at the start of each of the last three years. As a result, real mean wages have also increased, something that must be seen as positive given the extremely low average wages that exist. Nevertheless, this policy led to higher price increases in food merchandise prices and other goods with prices susceptible to labor costs, causing core inflation to remain very persistent at levels only slightly below 4.0%. 3 This explanation reveals the backdrop behind monetary policy up through the end of 2019: a mild recession but increasing sovereign risk and a positive inflation gap. Nevertheless, once headline inflation dropped closer to its target and risk perception improved somewhat, together with the Fed reducing its own rate, the Central Bank felt time had come to start a downward cycle beginning in August 2019. According to my interpretation, this new cycle was initially aimed at moving from a restrictive stance towards neutral territory, not with an intention of transiting toward an outright expansionary phase as long as Mexico had a positive inflation gap. Thus, between August 2019 and February 2020, the Central Bank reduced its monetary policy rate by 25 basis points from 8.25% to 7.00% on five consecutive occasions - slowly, but continuously, with certain prudence as a result of still high risk perceptions. At the beginning, my thinking was that the Central Bank could reach a rate somewhere near 5.50%, which would have placed its monetary posture in a neutral real rate territory. However, economic activity fell slightly faster in the last quarter of 2019 while inflation ended the year at 2.8%. With headline inflation slightly below target and the economy falling into a recession, the time had perhaps come for an expansionary monetary phase; there seemed room to easily push the rate down further albeit with certain prudence. and then the pandemic arrived As was the case in most countries, lockdown policies followed, bringing economic activity to an abrupt halt. After a 1.0% drop in the first quarter, GDP fell 16.8% in the second. The Central Banks first reaction was to speed up the easing cycle by 50 basis points in March, followed up by an additional 50 basis points in an unscheduled announcement in April and coupled together with a ten-point list of additional measures aimed at increasing liquidity, assuring the well-functioning of the payments system and enticing credit expansion for small and medium sized firms. The largest decline in GDP that Mexico had registered in a single quarter had been a drop of 5.8% in the first quarter of 1995 at the height of the infamous Tequila Crisis. This time, however, the great lockdown caused a 16.8% fall, way beyond anything ever seen. I have been around for a while; I remember well the 1976 devaluation, the lost decade and external debt crisis of the eighties, the Tequila Crisis of 1995 and the Great Recession of 2009. This was far worse than all of that. In April alone, 12.5 million Mexicans lost their jobs and another 8 million were forced to work part-time, earning less than half their previous wages. The extended unemployment rate, equivalent to the U-4 definition used by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, surged above 33%, meaning that one out of every three Mexicans wanting a job did not have one. Worse still, the U-6 definition of unemployment, which includes part-time employment for economic reasons, went up past 50%. This meant that one out of every two Mexicans who wanted a fulltime job did not have one, equivalent to more than 20 million people. 4 The Bank of Mexico has one very clear priority mandate: price stability, meaning inflation at 3%, within a variability range of /- 1%. This means inflation should average 3%, but never be above 4%. Mexico does not have a dual mandate like the U.S. Federal Reserve; nevertheless, monetary policy decisions can never be made outside of the context of cyclical positioning, risk perceptions and financial stability considerations. This means always having to look at the balance of risks of growth and financial stability, together with that of inflation. Even in the context of a positive inflation gap, if one is looking at an almost 30% negative output gap, there is no alternative but to be dovish. Worse still, the federal government made it very clear that there was not going to be a countercyclical fiscal policy. Using debt to finance expansionary fiscal policies in the eighties ended up being a disaster: a decade without growth in a highly inflationary environment. In the years following the Tequila Crisis, the government used debt to bail out rich bankers. The current president remembers these experiences vividly and has promised to never again use debt under any circumstance. Mexico thus stayed with fiscal austerity in spite of what every other country was doing and against recommendations of all international institutions. This is without a doubt slowing down the recovery phase. However, Mexico may end up with the benefit of avoiding the major debt hangover that many countries will have to deal with in the upcoming years. Was this the right decision? Only time will let us know. Looking ahead, Mexico faces an uphill battle. In the first two years of this administration, the government used up all that was available in various fiscal stabilization funds. Oil revenues, which in the previous decades made up a large portion of fiscal income, have fallen to about half of what they used to be. Pemex and CFE, the two largest government enterprises, face huge debt and significant losses that will continue to increase. Expenditures such as pensions and debt service have kept on growing while available resources for public investment have declined for 11 years in a row. Public spending, as measured through national accounts, has failed to contribute to GDP growth. These fiscal restrictions will increase over the next years. Not only does this leave monetary policy on its own, but with a low level of effectiveness. Compared with most other countries, Mexico has a much lower level of financial inclusion, much less financial deepening, much lower credit penetration and a very high level of informality, all of which hinder the effectiveness of monetary policy. In addition, Mexicos banking system is highly concentrated among seven banks who control almost 80% of the market. The lockdown brought about both supply and demand disruptions causing huge changes in relative prices, very similar to most other countries. However, in most countries inflation diminished at the beginning of the pandemic, while in Mexico it increased. Changes in household consumption patterns increased the demand for food merchandise and certain non-food goods, while decreasing the demand for many services, especially in 5 entertainment, travel and restaurants. At the same time, many products faced restrictions in production, causing decreases in supply which in turn caused many prices to increase, in spite of the huge negative output gap. In contrast, in most other countries cyclical conditions prevailed in price formations, leading to negative inflation gaps. In Mexico, however, food prices increased more than in most other countries, while the drop in services was not as strong. Mexico also has higher weights for food merchandise and lower weights for services than other countries. All combined, Mexico has never experienced a negative inflation gap during the pandemic, while the traditional CPI weights underreported true inflation for households at the time. Part of the problem could well have been that health restrictions reduced potential GDP, making the negative output gap smaller than what models suggested. Even though monetary policy was left as the only tool, the Central Bank also had to consider that using an aggressive monetary policy response to stimulate the economy by lowering real interest rates, apart from preventing it from achieving its inflation target, could also create problems with the exchange rate and financial stability. It is important to remember that Mexico is a very open economy with almost no restrictions regarding capital flows. The Mexican peso is one of the few emerging market currencies that trades worldwide, 24 hours a day. Given the high interconnection that Mexico has with the U.S., it needs to maintain a higher differential between its monetary policy rate and that of the Federal Reserve, compared to other emerging markets. This means that the Central Bank has to monitor its balance of payment movements carefully and its financial system continuously. What is interesting is that in the second half of last year, exports rebounded to pre-pandemic levels, while imports only recovered partially. This led to a historically high current account surplus. In the third and fourth quarters of 2020, the current account surplus registered 6.6% and 5.8% of GDP, respectively, more than the previous high of 5.2% in the first quarter of 1983. Fortunately, the banking system was in robust conditions prior to the pandemic, with capitalization levels well above Basel III recommendations. As was pointed out above, the pandemic introduced large distortions in relative prices. Most of these changes, however, are not permanent. Many service prices that fell drastically last year have recovered one year later as lockdown restrictions have been lifted or at least eased. For example, the price of gasoline dropped drastically in April last year as a result of the dramatic decline in travel under lockdown. In April this year, it is expected that the year-over-year increase will be around 35%, pushing non-core inflation up to 12% or more. Combined with other price rebounds, the Bank anticipates headline inflation in April to register a rate somewhere near 6%. With inflation almost at twice its target and expectations for year-end on the rise, there was no choice but to put further easing on hold in the latest decision in March. 6 Final remarks Is this just a pause in this easing cycle or has it come to an end? If a terminal point of this cycle has been reached, how long can the pause last before having to make a new movement? Mexicos recovery phase can be described as difficult and fragile, and is estimated to last more than a couple of years. The most optimistic growth scenario places GDP increasing at 6% this year. Even though 6% sounds impressive and has not been observed yet this century, it is actually a mediocre rebound after falling 8.5% the previous year. It is estimated that the negative output gap, whatever it may be, will prevail throughout the rest of this year. This scenario seems consistent with the need for a continuous monetary expansive stance. Nevertheless, there has been a surge in inflation in many countries due to base comparison effects that is being labeled as temporary. However, is it really temporary? The balance of risks for inflation is definitely skewed to the upside. World financial volatility seems to have returned as a response to the U.S. fiscal stimulus program, casing yield curves to steepen and the dollar to strengthen. World commodity prices are on the rise and higher maritime transportation costs have been observed. The world economy is forecast to grow rapidly in the aftermath of the pandemic, causing negative output gaps to dissipate. Increased imported inflation with a higher exchange rate clearly poses further risk of inflation. On the domestic front, growing uncertainty pertaining to mid-term elections, real mean wage increases, further hikes in gasoline and electricity prices and an upward revision in mid-term inflation expectations are all evident. Again, this leads back to the possibility that there has been an over-estimation of the size of the negative output gap. In the context of an improving economy and an upward bias in the balance of inflation risks, it seems Mexico will most likely be on hold for a while. Obviously future decisions are datadriven. But for further easing to take place, core inflation would have to converge to the 3% target quickly and the country would need to experience financial stability on a consistent basis. A very important part of any decision going forward is what the Federal Reserve will do. If it decides to hike sometime before the two-year hiatus that has been promised, there is no doubt that Mexico will have to do the same. Monetary policy in the upcoming years will face many challenges. Fiscal weakening may eventually lead to country-risk downgrades and even the possibility of losing investment grade status. Higher risk aversion will limit capital inflows and the governments fight with the private sector will continue to prevent investment from growing. Mexico will face midterm elections in June and it is quite likely that the Bank will confront mounting political pressure from what was been an aggressive legislative body and an overly ambitious president. The Governor of the Central Bank finishes his term at the end of this year; obviously his replacement will be key. While the Banks main objective is price stability, it is also responsible for macro financial stability and a well-functioning payments system. 7 Decisions will be made to attempt to find a balance among all these factors, with the additional burden of somehow contributing to the post-pandemic recovery of the economy. Will it be possible to achieve these multiple objectives with only one policy instrument? Maybe, maybe not. Only time will tell. 8

Title: Presentation of the Cont@cto Banxico Award 2013
text: Remarks by Mr. Javier Guzman Calafell, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, on the occasion of the presentation of the Banxico Cont@cto Award 2013. November 27, 2013 Good night. It is a source of great satisfaction for me to address a few words to you on the occasion of the delivery of the Contacto Banxico award, a contest that is being held for the fifth consecutive year and whose core issue on this occasion has been "The autonomy of the central bank". On behalf of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, I thank all of you for your presence and extend a cordial welcome. I would first like to make a brief description of the objectives that the Bank of Mexico seeks to achieve by holding this event. On the one hand, the contest is an invaluable opportunity for the Bank of Mexico to know the opinions that high school students throughout the Mexican Republic, with the advice of their respective teachers, have on the most relevant issues. 1 for a central bank. This allows the Bank and its Governing Board to take note of the perception of this important segment of the population about our Institution and the legal framework in which our daily work takes place, and in general to collect the concerns of those who, without a doubt, will be responsible in the future, on the most diverse fronts, of Mexico's development. On the other hand, we are convinced that the contest is a splendid tool at the service of the financial education of our students, being a source of motivation for them to consult the available material on various central banking topics and, of course, to show their ability to understand and analyze these issues. As on previous occasions, the 2013 edition of the Prize has been characterized by a wide participation. This year we have more than 600 teams, from public and private schools in 28 states of the Republic. We are honored with their presence today by those who, after a careful and difficult evaluation process, were considered by the jury as the top five. 2 The theme around which the contest was designed this year is very significant for the Bank of Mexico, since in 2013 we celebrated the twentieth anniversary of the autonomy of our Central Institute. 20 years ago, first with a far-reaching constitutional reform and later with the enactment of a new law to regulate its performance, the Bank of Mexico became an autonomous institution of the Mexican State. With the distance that allows us the passage of these two decades, and in view of the results of this transformation, it is undoubted that the granting of autonomy to the Bank of Mexico has been one of the most important institutional reforms that have been implemented in the country in a long time. What are the pillars of the autonomy of our Central Bank? Firstly, the existence of a clear mandate. As a recognition that inflation represents an obstacle to economic development and affects the poorest sectors of the population more severely, the Mexican Constitution establishes that the priority objective of the Bank of Mexico will be "to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency." 3 Second, the definition, also at the constitutional level, that "no authority may order the Bank to grant financing." Why such an explicit prohibition? Because this makes it possible to separate the function of creating money from other tasks of the State, in which demands to increase spending are continually faced. In other words, because this is the best guarantee that users of the national currency can have, that said currency will not be subject to management that detracts from purchasing power. Thirdly, the formation of a capable Governing Board free of political pressures. Hence the staggering of the terms of its members, the establishment in the Bank Law of the requirements that they must meet, and the requirement that each of them be ratified by the Senate at the proposal of the President of the Republic. Fourthly, administrative independence, which protects the Central Bank from pressure from other institutions. It is important to clarify that this is not equivalent to giving the Central Institute a blank check, since there are criteria for the monitoring of the budget of the Institution by Congress and the Executive that are 4 established in the Law, in addition to the fact that the Bank is subject to different audit processes. Finally, the commitment to transparency and accountability. It is the responsibility and duty of the Bank to report in a clear and timely manner on its actions. In this regard, there are various instruments that allow a direct and accurate evaluation of the performance of the Central Bank, such as announcements of monetary policy decisions, minutes of the corresponding discussions, inflation reports and appearances before Congress, among others. Has the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico been beneficial to the country? Let me give you some figures. During the period of almost 20 years from July 1973 to April 1993, that is, before the autonomy of our Central Institute came into force, Mexico recorded inflation rates of at least two digits. In fact, a total of more than two years of this period saw triple-digit inflation rates. In contrast, today we can speak of more than 13 years in which our economy records annual rates of inflation in the single digits. 5 This has allowed families and businesses to plan their future with greater certainty. For example, families now have the possibility of accessing loans with terms of up to 30 years, at low and fixed rates, to acquire a home. For their part, companies can invest for the long term, without fear that their investments could become failed or ruinous because of runaway inflation. The government has also benefited from lower inflation, being able to finance itself at much lower interest rates and longer terms. Naturally, all of the above was unthinkable in the years when our economy was hit by high inflation rates. It is true that these achievements are not due exclusively to the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. However, it is also true that they would hardly have been viable in the absence of an autonomous central bank. Undoubtedly, the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico has contributed in a fundamental way to give greater stability, certainty and a horizon of confidence to our country, even in the midst of an international economic situation as difficult and uncertain as the one we are currently experiencing. In fact, this complicated global environment 6 underlines the importance of preserving the institutional arrangement that made the Bank of Mexico autonomous, which, by the way, is not a privilege granted to the Bank, but a guarantee for those who use the national currency. I would like to emphasize that the favorable experience with the autonomy of the central bank is not exclusive to Mexico. Today, it is widely accepted that the conduct of monetary policy by autonomous central banks makes it possible to isolate it from political influences that may guide it to objectives different from those set out in their mandates. In addition, autonomy protects monetary authorities from possible pressures to finance excessive fiscal deficits and the adoption of inconsistent measures over time. Ultimately, such schemes strengthen the credibility of the central bank and, therefore, the fight against inflation. In fact, empirical evidence at the international level shows that the effective autonomy of central banks has a negative relationship with inflation. In addition, the variability of nominal and real interest rates is lower, and the average real yield offered to depositors higher, in countries where central banks enjoy greater effective autonomy. 7 Because of the importance of this institutional arrangement for the present and for the future of our country, I think it is a great success that this year the theme of the Banxico Contact Award has been that of the autonomy of the central bank. In conclusion, I would like to congratulate the five finalist teams very warmly, both for the effort made and for the excellent quality of the work carried out. Undoubtedly, taking into account the strict criteria followed by the jury and the variety and quality of the participating teams, having reached this stage represents a triumph for all of them. I would also like to thank all the teams registered in the contest for their contributions and enthusiastic participation, the members of the jury, both from the Bank and external, for their very efficient reading and evaluation of the works presented, and of course the Bank team that made possible the organization of this edition of the contest. I hope that the Contacto Banxico Award will continue to be an incentive for the creativity and talent of our students for many years. Thanks a lot. 8 9
text_original: Palabras del licenciado Javier Guzmn Calafell, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, con motivo de la entrega del Premio Cont@cto Banxico 2013. 27 de noviembre de 2013 Buenas noches. Es para m motivo de gran satisfaccin dirigirles unas palabras con motivo de la entrega del premio Contacto Banxico, certamen que se celebra por quinto ao consecutivo y cuyo asunto medular en esta ocasin ha sido La autonoma del banco central. A nombre de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico agradezco la presencia de todos ustedes y les extiendo una cordial bienvenida. Deseara, en primer lugar hacer una somera descripcin de los objetivos que el Banco de Mxico busca lograr mediante la celebracin de este certamen. Por una parte, el concurso es una oportunidad invaluable para que el Banco de Mxico conozca las opiniones que los estudiantes de preparatoria de toda la Repblica Mexicana, con la asesora de sus respectivos profesores, tienen sobre los temas de mayor relevancia 1 para un banco central. Esto permite al Banco y a su Junta de Gobierno, tomar nota de la percepcin de este segmento tan importante de la poblacin sobre nuestra Institucin y el marco jurdico en el que se desenvuelve nuestra labor cotidiana, y en general recoger las inquietudes de quienes, sin duda, sern en un futuro responsables, en los ms diversos frentes, del desarrollo de Mxico. Por otra parte, estamos convencidos de que el certamen es una esplndida herramienta al servicio de la educacin financiera de nuestros estudiantes, al ser una fuente de motivacin para que consulten el material disponible sobre diversos temas de banca central y, por supuesto, para que muestren su capacidad para entender y analizar estos temas. Como en ocasiones anteriores, la edicin 2013 del Premio se ha caracterizado por una amplia participacin. Este ao contamos con ms de 600 equipos, provenientes de escuelas pblicas y privadas de 28 estados de la Repblica. Nos honran con su presencia el da de hoy aquellos que despus de un cuidadoso y difcil proceso de evaluacin, fueron considerados por el jurado como los cinco mejores. 2 El tema alrededor del cual se dise este ao el certamen resulta muy significativo para el Banco de Mxico, ya que en 2013 celebramos el vigsimo aniversario de la autonoma de nuestro Instituto Central. Hace 20 aos, primero con una trascendental reforma constitucional y ms tarde con la promulgacin de una nueva ley para normar su desempeo, el Banco de Mxico se convirti en una Institucin autnoma del Estado mexicano. Con la distancia que nos permite el paso de estas dos dcadas, y a la vista de los resultados de esta transformacin, es indudable que el otorgamiento de la autonoma al Banco de Mxico, ha sido una de las reformas institucionales de mayor trascendencia que se han implementado en el pas en mucho tiempo. Cules son los pilares de la autonoma de nuestro Banco Central? En primer lugar la existencia de un mandato claro. Como un reconocimiento de que la inflacin representa un obstculo para el desarrollo econmico y afecta con mayor severidad a los sectores ms pobres de la poblacin, la Constitucin mexicana establece que el objetivo prioritario del Banco de Mxico ser procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. 3 En segundo lugar, la definicin, tambin a nivel constitucional, de que ninguna autoridad podr ordenarle al Banco concederle financiamiento. Porqu esa prohibicin tan explcita? Porque esto permite separar la funcin de crear dinero de otras tareas del Estado, en las que continuamente se enfrentan demandas para aumentar el gasto. En otras palabras, porque esta es la mejor garanta que los usuarios de la moneda nacional pueden tener, de que dicha moneda no ser objeto de un manejo que le reste poder adquisitivo. En tercer lugar, la conformacin de una Junta de Gobierno capacitada y libre de presiones polticas. De ah el escalonamiento de los periodos de sus integrantes, el establecimiento en la Ley del Banco de los requisitos que estos deben cumplir, y la exigencia de que cada uno de ellos sea ratificado por el Senado a propuesta del Presidente de la Repblica. En cuarto lugar, la independencia administrativa, que protege al Banco Central de presiones de otras instituciones. Es importante aclarar que esto no es equivalente a darle al Instituto Central un cheque en blanco, ya que existen criterios para el seguimiento del presupuesto de la Institucin por parte del Congreso y del Ejecutivo que estn 4 establecidos en la Ley, adems de que el Banco est sujeto a distintos procesos de auditora. Por ltimo, el compromiso de transparencia y rendicin de cuentas. Es responsabilidad y deber del Banco informar de manera clara y oportuna sobre sus acciones. Al respecto, existen diversos instrumentos que permiten una evaluacin directa y precisa del desempeo del Banco Central, tales como anuncios de decisiones de poltica monetaria, minutas de las correspondientes discusiones, informes de inflacin y comparecencias ante el Congreso, entre otras. Ha sido benfica para el pas la autonoma del Banco de Mxico? Permtanme darles algunas cifras. Durante el periodo de casi 20 aos comprendido de julio de 1973 a abril de 1993, es decir antes de que entrara en vigor la autonoma de nuestro Instituto Central, Mxico registr tasas de inflacin de cuando menos dos dgitos. De hecho, en un total de ms de dos aos de este lapso se observaron tasas de inflacin de tres dgitos. En contraste, hoy en da podemos hablar de ms de 13 aos en que nuestra economa registra tasas anuales de inflacin de un solo dgito. 5 Esto ha permitido que familias y empresas puedan planear con mayor certidumbre su futuro. Por ejemplo, las familias tienen ahora la posibilidad de acceder a crditos con plazos de hasta 30 aos, a tasas bajas y fijas, para adquirir una vivienda. Por su parte, las empresas pueden invertir a largo plazo, sin temor a que sus inversiones puedan volverse fallidas o ruinosas a causa de una inflacin desbocada. Tambin el gobierno se ha beneficiado de la menor inflacin, al estar en posibilidades de financiarse a tasas de inters mucho ms bajas y a plazos ms largos. Naturalmente, todo lo anterior era impensable en los aos en que nuestra economa se vio afectada por tasas de inflacin elevadas. Es cierto que estos logros no obedecen exclusivamente a la autonoma del Banco de Mxico. Sin embargo, tambin es cierto que difcilmente habran sido viables en ausencia de un banco central autnomo. Indudablemente, la autonoma del Banco de Mxico ha contribuido de manera fundamental a darle mayor estabilidad, certidumbre y un horizonte de confianza a nuestro pas, incluso en medio de una situacin econmica internacional tan difcil e incierta como la que vivimos actualmente. De hecho, este entorno mundial complicado 6 subraya la importancia de preservar el arreglo institucional que hizo autnomo al Banco de Mxico, lo que, por cierto, no es un privilegio otorgado al Banco, sino una garanta para quienes usan la moneda nacional. Quisiera destacar que la favorable experiencia con la autonoma del banco central no es exclusiva de Mxico. Hoy en da, es ampliamente aceptado que la conduccin de la poltica monetaria por bancos centrales autnomos, permite aislarla de influencias de tipo poltico que puedan orientarla a objetivos diferentes de los fijados en sus mandatos. Adems, la autonoma protege a las autoridades monetarias de posibles presiones para el financiamiento de dficit fiscales excesivos y la adopcin de medidas inconsistentes en el tiempo. En ltima instancia, este tipo de esquemas fortalece la credibilidad del banco central y, por tanto, el combate a la inflacin. De hecho, la evidencia emprica a nivel internacional muestra que la autonoma efectiva de los bancos centrales tiene una relacin negativa con la inflacin. Adems, la variabilidad de las tasas de inters nominales y reales es ms baja, y el rendimiento real promedio ofrecido a los depositantes ms alto, en pases donde los bancos centrales disfrutan de una mayor autonoma efectiva. 7 Por la importancia de este arreglo institucional para el presente y para el futuro de nuestro pas, me parece un gran acierto que este ao el tema del Premio Contacto Banxico haya sido el de la autonoma del banco central. Deseo, para concluir, felicitar de manera muy calurosa a los cinco equipos finalistas, tanto por el esfuerzo realizado como por la excelente calidad de los trabajos elaborados. Indudablemente, tomando en cuenta los estrictos criterios seguidos por el jurado y la variedad y calidad de los equipos participantes, el haber llegado a esta etapa representa un triunfo para todos ellos. Tambin quisiera agradecer a todos los equipos inscritos en el concurso por sus contribuciones y su entusiasta participacin, a los miembros del jurado, tanto del Banco como externos, por su muy eficiente lectura y evaluacin de los trabajos presentados, y por supuesto al equipo del Banco que hizo posible la organizacin de esta edicin del certamen. Hago votos para que el Premio Contacto Banxico contine siendo por muchos aos un incentivo para la creatividad y el talento de nuestros estudiantes. Muchas gracias. 8 9

Title: Delivery of the Clean Industry Certificate to the Bank of Mexico (Complejo Legaria)
text: REMARKS BY DR. AGUSTiN GUILLERMO CARSTENS CARSTENS, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, ON THE OCCASION OF THE DELIVERY OF THE CLEAN INDUSTRY CERTIFICATE TO THE BANK OF MEXICO (COMPLEJO LEGARIA) LIC. JUAN JOSe GUERRA ABUD Secretary of Environment and Natural Resources LIC. GUILLERMO HARO BeLCHEZ Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection SENATOR RICARDO BARROSO AGRAMONT Member of the Committee on the Environment and Natural Resources of the Chamber of Senators LIC. CANEK VaZQUEZ GoNGORA Deputy Attorney General for Environmental Audit LIC. ALEJANDRO ALEGRE RABIELA General Director of Issuance of the Bank of Mexico Undersecretaries, Deputy Attorneys General, public servants of the Ministry of the Environment and Natural Resources, the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection and the Bank of Mexico. Page 1 of 9 Representatives of the media. Ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, the Bank of Mexico's vision is "To be an institution of excellence deserving of the trust of society for achieving the full fulfillment of its mission, for its transparent performance, as well as for its technical capacity and ethical commitment." Within the framework of this vision, at the Central Bank of the Mexican State we consider it very important that our actions are clearly aligned with the care of the environment. That is why for me it is a privilege to be at this event in which, for the second time, the Clean Industry Certificate will be delivered to the Bank of Mexico, Complejo Legaria, where the facilities of our Banknote Factory have been located for 45 years. Page 2 of 9 The "Certificate of Clean Industry Performance Level 2" to which the Banknote Factory was awarded, places it as the first "company" in the Federal District to obtain this level of performance and the thirteenth nationwide. As background, I tell you that in August 2012 the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection certified us, for the first time, as a Clean Industry, recognition with which the competent federal authority in the matter valued the effort and commitment that our Institution has with the care of the environment and motivated us to improve our environmental performance in the production processes we develop, mainly those related to the manufacture and distribution of Mexican banknotes. Since 2012 many of my colleagues in the General Directorate of Emission and in the Directorate of Material Resources assumed the challenge and commitment to endorse the certificate that is valid for two years, so they proposed and carried out measures and improvements Page 3 of 9 environmental, in terms of air, water, soil and subsoil, hazardous waste and environmental risk. My congratulations and thanks to all of you, especially the members of the Office of Industrial Safety and Environment. The implementation of these measures has meant the daily and sustained effort of you and many of our colleagues who do not accompany us, since you are currently manufacturing and processing banknotes, recognizing that in addition to developing activities directly linked to the provision of currency to the national economy, you have achieved greater awareness and shared responsibility regarding the institutional and personal contribution to the care of the environment, which has allowed us to carry out our work in a safer and cleaner place, offering the environment the confidence that the Bank of Mexico is committed to the conservation of natural resources. Page 4 of 9 Another example of this commitment to compliance with national and international agreements on sustainable and environmentally efficient products is the realization of the project called "Evaluation of the Environmental Performance of Mexican Banknotes and Generation of Environmental Indicators", which is being carried out with the support of the Institute of Engineering of the UNAM. Among its scope is the evaluation of the environmental performance of the processes involved in the issuance of banknotes, with a life cycle analysis approach in accordance with the specifications established in the ISO 14040 series of standards. This analysis ranges from obtaining the raw materials with which the banknotes manufactured and issued by the Bank of Mexico are printed, to their integral handling once they reach the end of their useful life. It highlights that we are the first Central Bank in Latin America and the sixth in the world to carry out work of this nature with a methodology based on life cycle analysis, before the Page 5 of 9 they made the European Central Bank, the Swiss, the Canadian, the English and the Australian. Other scopes defined for future stages of this project include the evaluation of various alternatives for the integral management of waste generated during the production and distribution process of banknotes, as well as the evaluation of the environmental performance of buildings and facilities involved in these processes. This study will generate objective information that supports the decision-making process from an environmental perspective, thus contributing to the provisions of the General Law on Climate Change and the National Strategy for Sustainable Production and Consumption. Research carried out in recent decades, of which Banco de Mexico has been attentive and promoting, has been dedicated to developing new materials to increase the useful life of banknotes, decreasing their replacement rate and therefore also their production, transport, and final disposal, reducing input costs, production and waste generation. Page 6 of 9 Consequently, actions have been taken to increase the wear resistance of banknotes at the circulation stage and thus increase their durability. In addition to the above, it is important to mention other day-to-day efforts for the care and saving of resources associated with the environment: ? In terms of electrical energy, the replacement of luminaires was carried out in all the exterior lighting of the Legaria Complex, by more efficient technologies, presence sensors were installed in general toilets, corridors, circulations, general offices and stairs and awareness actions were intensified to users for a rational use of energy. As a pilot project, cells were also installed in the Caja Regional Monterrey to take advantage of solar energy in the supply of part of our requirements of that installation of protection and distribution of values. Page 7 of 9 ? Regarding water, aerators were installed in the sinks of the general toilets and electric heaters in the service showers and a culture has been promoted among the staff in the best use and management of water. ? With technological development and continuous systematization of processes, the use of paper has been consistently reduced. Mr. Secretary, Mr. Attorney General, I want to thank the public servants of the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection, in particular the staff of the Metropolitan Area of the Valley of Mexico, for the great support they provided to this Central Institute, since their guidance, collaboration and professionalism with which they performed were fundamental for obtaining this clean industry certificate. Our next steps will be aimed at ensuring that the final disposal of banknotes contributes to eco-efficiency and that the distribution of banknotes and coins supports the reduction of environmental impacts. Page 8 of 9 Finally, the Bank of Mexico once again reaffirms its commitment to the protection of the environment and can proudly say that the manufacture of Mexican banknotes meets the highest standards in the field. Thank you very much for your attention. Page 9 of 9

Pgina 4 de 9 Otra muestra de dicho compromiso con el cumplimiento de acuerdos nacionales e internacionales en materia de productos sustentables y ambientalmente eficientes, es la realizacin del proyecto denominado Evaluacin del Desempeo Ambiental de Billetes de Banco Mexicanos y Generacin de Indicadores Ambientales, el cual se est llevando a cabo con el apoyo del Instituto de Ingeniera de la UNAM. Destaca que somos el primer Banco Central de Amrica Latina y el sexto en el mundo que realiza un trabajo de esta naturaleza con una metodologa basada en el anlisis de ciclo de vida, antes lo Pgina 5 de 9 hicieron el Banco Central Europeo, el suizo, el canadiense, el ingls y el australiano. Investigaciones realizadas en las ltimas dcadas, de las que Banco de Mxico ha estado atento y promoviendo, se han dedicado a desarrollar nuevos materiales para incrementar la vida til de los billetes, disminuyendo su tasa de reemplazo y por lo tanto tambin su produccin, transporte, y disposicin final, reduciendo costos de insumos produccin y generacin de residuos. Pgina 6 de 9 En consecuencia se han adoptado acciones tendientes a incrementar la resistencia al desgaste que presentan los billetes en la etapa de circulacin y as aumentar su durabilidad. Seor secretario, seor procurador, quiero agradecer a los servidores pblicos de la Procuradura Federal de Proteccin al Ambiente, en particular al personal de la Zona Metropolitana del Valle de Mxico, por el gran apoyo que proporcionaron a este Instituto Central, ya que su orientacin, colaboracin y el profesionalismo con el que se desempearon fueron fundamentales para la obtencin de este certificado de industria limpia.
