The Citibanamex Economics Award as a stimulus to economic research Over more than 60 years, the Citibanamex Economics Award has established itself as one of the most important and prestigious awards given to economic research in Mexico. With this recognition, the financial group Citibanamex contributes to extending the borders of the 1 economic knowledge and also encourages the generation of solid opinions on the most appropriate policies to face the problems that affect the economic development of our country. In this sense, the great merit of the Citibanamex Award has been to generate incentives for students and researchers to reflect on the main challenges facing our economy, formulate proposals arising from their research and begin to deliberate how they can contribute later in the solution of these challenges, either from the public sphere, the private, or the academic. 2. Economics, a science in constant evolution: Importance of continuously expanding and revising economic knowledge It should be remembered that economics is a discipline in constant evolution, and in that sense initiatives such as the Citibanamex Prize reveal its great importance since they promote the research eagerness of economists which, in the end, expands more and more the frontiers of economic science. 2 It is therefore important to remember that the list of economic issues and phenomena whose understanding still lacks consensus is long. There are numerous issues that are not yet explored and very varied are the unresolved questions or that, at least, do not have a single and definitive answer among economists. All this requires us, as social scientists, to focus our work and research on various fronts. First, to contribute to the expansion of the frontier of economic knowledge by generating new research agendas and innovations in the different fields covered by economics. Second, reviewing existing paradigms and theories, to discover whether it is pertinent to develop new ideas and methodologies that contribute to a better understanding of reality. to. The debate around the Phillips curve In this context and as an example, I will allow myself to speak of one of the central concepts of macroeconomics and that, although it has been widely studied in the past, continues to be one of the most relevant debates in our time. I'm referring to the Phillips Curve. 3 The Phillips Curve, which proposes a negative relationship between inflation and unemployment, has been widely used by economists as a guide to discuss the influence of aggregate demand growth on inflation. Understanding this is especially important today because of the low levels of inflation prevalent in many advanced countries and the fact that the relationship between economic slack and inflation appears to have weakened in a wider universe of countries. After the Great Recession in 2008, two puzzling phenomena have occurred, especially in advanced countries, which I would like to highlight. The first phenomenon, known as the "lack of disinflation" arises since during the Great Recession, inflation in advanced countries did not decline as much as the Phillips Curve would have predicted, given the magnitude and duration of the recession. On the other hand, more recently and equally disconcertingly, it is the enigma of the "lack of inflation" during the recovery period, since about a decade after that recession, despite the fact that the outlook for advanced economies has improved and that in some countries unemployment rates are already at the same level or even below their average level in years before the crisis, inflation continues in 4 low levels and wages are still lower than those observed before the recession. This behavior is also a matter of discussion in some emerging economies where growth has remained robust, working conditions have improved, but inflation remains low. In this way, the dynamics of inflation after the 2008 crisis and its apparent disconnection with real activity have led to the belief that the relationship between the two variables has weakened or could even have been broken. This phenomenon seems to have made it difficult to analyze the dynamics of inflation, with important consequences for the conduct of monetary policy. A weakened relationship between economic activity and inflation, i.e. a flatter slope of the Phillips Curve, would make converging to a given level of inflation target more costly in terms of the deviations of output from its potential. In this regard, contemporary economists have given themselves the task of offering explanations to the phenomena described above. However, there is still no consensus. In particular, in relation to the low levels of inflation observed in advanced economies and the weaker relationship between real activity and inflation, some economists 5 argue that this may be due to structural changes in the economy, while others point out that low inflation is a temporary phenomenon caused by idiosyncratic changes in the prices of some products. Among the main structural factors is, for example, a possible natural rate of unemployment lower than the current unemployment rate. Under this reasoning, inflation has been low because there is more slack than previously thought. A second explanation argues that central bankers have been successful in anchoring inflation expectations in such a way that firms do not seek to raise their prices and workers do not ask for wage increases. In relation to the latter, there is also talk of the decrease in the bargaining power of workers to demand wage increases as a possible factor. Globalization, greater trade integration, technological innovation and its effects on prices are also pointed out among the possible explanations. This is not the first time economists have debated the Phillips Curve as our understanding of pricing, the determinants of inflation, and the role of monetary policy has evolved considerably over the years. Thus, since its emergence at the end of the 6 In the 50s, the Phillips Curve has been subject to discussion and, along with the development of economic theory, has gone through a process of evolution. b. Academic evolution of the Phillips curve In the history of economic theory, a clear relationship between prices and real activity was not thought of until 1958, when using data for the United Kingdom, Phillips concludes the existence of a curve with a negative slope between changes in nominal wages and the unemployment rate, which in turn, it implied a positive relationship between inflation and real activity. Unlike the Classical school, which suggests perfectly flexible prices and a vertical supply curve, the Keynesian school holds the existence of rigid prices and a horizontal supply curve. The concept of the Phillips Curve is an intermediate point and derives in an aggregate supply curve with a positive slope. In this way, an increase in aggregate demand is not captured exclusively by price increases (Classical school) nor only by the growth of production (Keynesian school). These new ideas led to the era of Neoclassical Synthesis in which both Classical and Keynesian theory converge. While accepting the effectiveness of aggregate demand policies in 7 in the short run, the Neoclassical Synthesis holds that in the long run the economy converges to a steady-state level of flexible prices. However, in the seventies, a phenomenon of stagflation was observed in the developed world that could not be explained by the Phillips Curve. Despite the implementation of expansionary policies, both unemployment and inflation remained at high levels, breaking with the prevailing economic paradigm. This motivated economists of the time such as Phelps and Friedman to revisit existing ideas and theories, leading to various innovations that resulted in a new Phillips Curve augmented with a term that incorporates inflation expectations, while excess demand, formerly measured by unemployment, was expressed as the gap between unemployment and the natural rate of unemployment. Over the years, economists from different economic schools have continued to review and modify the Phillips Curve continuously in order to better explain economic phenomena such as those described above. This debate and analysis has also taken place in Mexico given the changes registered in the last decade in the inflationary process. In this context, some have been made 8 studies in recent years documenting a change in the relative importance of the components that determine the dynamics of inflation. Specifically, it is documented that the parameters of the Phillips Curve for Mexico have changed in such a way that the expectations of economic agents are increasingly important in determining the dynamics of inflation, while inflation observed in the past loses relevance. Let me dig a little deeper into this point, pointing out what has happened to inflation during 2017: it stood in mid-October at a level of 6.30 percent, reaching its highest level last August. This atypical increase in inflation is expected to be temporary, as it is very likely that gradual convergence to the 3 percent target will have already begun by the end of 2018. Inflation reached the high levels observed during 2017 as a result of various shocks. First, derived from the extremely complicated external environment that the country has faced since the end of 2014, pensions on inflation were generated as a result of the significant and persistent depreciation of the national currency. Secondly, the acceleration of inflation during 2017 was mainly due to the liberalisation of inflation prices. 9 energy in the country, and in particular, those of gasoline, as well as the increase in various prices of agricultural products and the minimum wage. While the effects of the shocks on the measurement of inflation that I have described have been significant in the short term, their effects are expected to be only temporary. Since these shocks are fundamentally changes in relative prices and since the Bank of Mexico has acted to avoid contagion effects in the process of price formation in the economy, they should not cause a generalized and sustainable increase in prices. This is consistent with the behavior of inflation expectations, where it is observed that the medium-term ones have increased to a much lesser extent than the short-term ones and the long-term ones remain anchored at 3.5 percent. This forecast reflects precisely the importance that in inflationary dynamics the role of inflation expectations is more relevant than with respect to that of past inflation. These results are important for the conduct of monetary policy since, in the presence of shocks to inflation due to changes in relative prices, such as those described, the anchoring of expectations allows the Central Bank to preserve an inflation environment. 10 low and stable efficiently, that is, at lower costs in economic activity. This highlights the importance of continuing to strengthen the anchoring of inflation expectations, being one of the main channels in the transmission mechanism of monetary policy, in order to consolidate the convergence of inflation to its objective more efficiently. The Phillips Curve is just one example of the multiple concepts and questions within economic thought that have been studied and debated over the years, demonstrating the importance of stimulating research and thus expanding the frontier of economic knowledge. In this sense, the work that you have developed over several months, or even years, of dedication and that take into account the realities and specific problems for Mexico, represent very important contributions and advances that allow us to close the gap between our understanding and reality. Therefore, I invite you to continue with this inquisitive work since our country, and the world, will always need new ideas that allow a better and more solid decision-making. 11 3. Final Considerations To conclude, I congratulate Citibanamex for these more than 60 years of promoting rigorous economic research and I congratulate the winners of this year's Prize, whose research covers diverse topics and is highly relevant to the current situation of our country. I assure you that through your research they improve our understanding of the functioning of the economy, favor better decision-making in both public administration and private initiative, and with it, contribute to generating greater well-being for our population. Today's laureates should be very proud of their achievements. I invite you to continue contributing to the development of Mexico, with a trajectory of excellence from each of its trenches. Mexico needs your talent and commitment. Thanks a lot. 12
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, en la entrega del Premio Citibanamex de Economa 2016 30 de octubre de 2017 - Ing. Ernesto Torres Cant, Director General del Grupo Financiero Citibanamex, - Alberto Gomez Alcal - Director Corporativo de Desarrollo Institucional, Estudios Econmicos y Comunicacin de Grupo Financiero Citibanamex, - Luis Madrazo, Jefe de la Unidad de Planeacin Econmica de la Secretaria de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, - Miembros del Presidium, 1. El Premio Citibanamex de Economa como estmulo a la investigacin econmica A lo largo de ms de 60 aos el Premio Citibanamex de Economa se ha consolidado como uno de los galardones ms importantes y prestigiosos que se otorga a la investigacin econmica en Mxico. Con este reconocimiento, el grupo financiero Citibanamex contribuye a extender las fronteras del 1 conocimiento econmico y adems propicia que se generen opiniones slidas sobre las polticas ms apropiadas para enfrentar los problemas que afectan el desarrollo econmico de nuestro pas. En este sentido, el gran mrito del Premio Citibanamex ha sido el de generar incentivos para que los estudiantes e investigadores reflexionen sobre los principales desafos que enfrenta nuestra economa, formulen propuestas surgidas de su investigacin y comiencen a deliberar la forma en que podrn contribuir ms adelante en la solucin de dichos retos, ya sea desde la esfera pblica, la privada, o la acadmica. 2. La economa, una ciencia en constante evolucin: Importancia de expandir y revisar continuamente el conocimiento econmico Hay que recordar que la economa es una disciplina en constante evolucin, y en ese sentido iniciativas como el Premio Citibanamex revelan su gran importancia ya que impulsan el afn de investigacin de los economistas lo que, a la postre, expande cada vez ms las fronteras de la ciencia econmica. 2 Por ello, es importante recordar que la lista de temas y fenmenos econmicos cuyo entendimiento carece an de consenso es larga. Numerosos son los asuntos que an no son explorados y muy variadas son las preguntas no resueltas o que, al menos, no cuentan con una respuesta nica y definitiva entre los economistas. Todo ello nos exige que, como cientficos sociales, enfoquemos nuestro trabajo y nuestra investigacin en diversos frentes. Primero, en contribuir a la expansin de la frontera del conocimiento econmico generando nuevas agendas de investigacin e innovaciones en los distintos campos que abarca la economa. Segundo, revisando los paradigmas y las teoras existentes, para descubrir si es pertinente desarrollar nuevas ideas y metodologas que contribuyan a un mejor entendimiento de la realidad. a. El debate en torno a la curva de Phillips En este contexto y a manera de ejemplo, me permitir hablar de uno de los conceptos centrales de la macroeconoma y que, aun cuando ha sido ampliamente estudiado en el pasado, contina siendo uno de los debates ms relevantes en nuestro tiempo. Me refiero a la Curva de Phillips. 3 La Curva de Phillips, que propone una relacin negativa entre la inflacin y el desempleo, ha sido ampliamente utilizada por los economistas como gua para discutir la influencia del crecimiento de la demanda agregada sobre la inflacin. Comprender lo anterior, resulta especialmente importante hoy en da debido a los bajos niveles de inflacin que prevalecen en muchos pases avanzados y el hecho de que la relacin entre la holgura de la economa y la inflacin parece haberse debilitado en un universo ms amplio de pases. Despus de la Gran Recesin en 2008 han ocurrido dos fenmenos desconcertantes, sobre todo en pases avanzados, que me gustara destacar. El primer fenmeno, conocido como la "falta de desinflacin surge ya que durante la Gran Recesin, la inflacin en los pases avanzados no disminuy tanto como la Curva de Phillips habra predicho, dada la magnitud y duracin de la recesin. Por otro lado, ms recientemente e igualmente desconcertante, es el enigma de la falta de inflacin durante el periodo de recuperacin, ya que cerca de una dcada despus de dicha recesin, a pesar de que las perspectivas para las economas avanzadas han mejorado y que en algunos pases las tasas de desempleo estn ya en el mismo nivel o incluso por debajo de su nivel promedio en aos previos a la crisis, la inflacin contina en 4 niveles bajos y los salarios son todava menores a aqullos observados antes de la recesin. Este comportamiento es tambin materia de discusin en algunas economas emergentes donde el crecimiento se ha mantenido robusto, las condiciones laborales han mejorado, pero la inflacin contina baja. De esta forma, la dinmica de la inflacin despus de la crisis de 2008 y su aparente desconexin con la actividad real han llevado a creer que la relacin entre ambas variables se ha debilitado o incluso podra haberse roto. Este fenmeno parece haber dificultado el anlisis sobre la dinmica de la inflacin, con importantes consecuencias para la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. Una relacin debilitada entre la actividad econmica y la inflacin, es decir, una pendiente ms plana de la Curva de Phillips hara que, converger a un nivel de inflacin objetivo determinado, sea ms costoso en trminos de las desviaciones de la produccin respecto a su potencial. Al respecto, economistas contemporneos se han dado a la tarea de ofrecer explicaciones a los fenmenos antes descritos. Sin embargo, an no existe un consenso. En particular, en relacin a los bajos niveles de inflacin observados en las economas avanzadas y la relacin ms dbil entre actividad real e inflacin, algunos economistas 5 sostienen que ello puede deberse a cambios estructurales en la economa, mientras que otros sealan que la baja inflacin es un fenmeno temporal causado por cambios idiosincrticos en los precios de algunos productos. Entre los principales factores estructurales se habla, por ejemplo, de una posible tasa natural de desempleo ms baja que la tasa actual de desempleo. Bajo este razonamiento, la inflacin ha sido baja porque existe mayor holgura de la que se pensaba. Una segunda explicacin sostiene que los banqueros centrales han sido exitosos en anclar las expectativas de inflacin de tal manera que las empresas no buscan aumentar sus precios y los trabajadores no piden aumentos salariales. En relacin a esto ltimo, tambin se habla de la disminucin en el poder de negociacin de los trabajadores para exigir aumentos salariales como un posible factor. La globalizacin, la mayor integracin comercial, la innovacin tecnolgica y sus efectos en precios tambin se sealan entre las posibles explicaciones. Esta no es la primera vez que los economistas debaten sobre la Curva de Phillips ya que nuestro entendimiento sobre la fijacin de precios, los determinantes de la inflacin y el papel de la poltica monetaria ha evolucionado considerablemente a lo largo de los aos. As, desde su surgimiento a finales de la 6 dcada de los aos 50, la Curva de Phillips ha estado sujeta a discusin y, junto con el desarrollo de la teora econmica, ha atravesado por un proceso de evolucin. b. Evolucin acadmica de la curva de Phillips En la historia de la teora econmica no se pensaba en una clara relacin entre los precios y la actividad real sino hasta 1958, cuando utilizando datos para el Reino Unido, Phillips concluye la existencia de una curva con pendiente negativa entre los cambios en salarios nominales y la tasa de desempleo, que a su vez, implicaba una relacin positiva entre inflacin y actividad real. A diferencia de la escuela Clsica, que sugiere precios perfectamente flexibles y una curva de oferta vertical, la escuela Keynesiana sostiene la existencia de precios rgidos y una curva de oferta horizontal. El concepto de la Curva de Phillips es un punto intermedio y se deriva en una curva de oferta agregada con una pendiente positiva. De esta forma, un aumento en la demanda agregada no se ve capturado exclusivamente por aumentos de precios (escuela Clsica) ni tampoco nicamente por el crecimiento de la produccin (escuela Keynesiana). Estas nuevas ideas llevaron a la era de la Sntesis Neoclsica en la cual convergen tanto la teora Clsica como la teora Keynesiana. Mientras que se acepta la efectividad de las polticas de demanda agregada en 7 el corto plazo, la Sntesis Neoclsica sostiene que en el largo plazo la economa converge a un nivel de estado estacionario de precios flexibles. Sin embargo, en los aos setenta, se observ un fenmeno de estanflacin en el mundo desarrollado que no poda ser explicado por la Curva de Phillips. A pesar de la implementacin de polticas expansionistas, tanto el desempleo como la inflacin se mantenan en niveles altos, rompiendo con el paradigma econmico prevaleciente. Esto motiv a los economistas del momento como Phelps y Friedman a revisitar las ideas y teoras existentes, dando lugar a diversas innovaciones que resultaron en una nueva Curva de Phillips aumentada con un trmino que incorpora las expectativas de inflacin, mientras que el exceso de demanda, antes medido por el desempleo, se expres como la brecha entre el desempleo y la tasa natural de desempleo. A lo largo de los aos, los economistas de las distintas escuelas econmicas han seguido revisando y modificando la Curva de Phillips continuamente a fin de explicar mejor fenmenos econmicos como los antes descritos. Este debate y anlisis tambin ha tenido lugar en Mxico dados los cambios registrados en la ltima dcada en el proceso inflacionario. En este contexto, se han realizado algunos 8 estudios en aos recientes que documentan un cambio en la importancia relativa de los componentes que determinan la dinmica de la inflacin. En especfico, se documenta que los parmetros de la Curva de Phillips para Mxico han cambiado de tal manera que las expectativas de los agentes econmicos son cada vez ms importantes para determinar la dinmica de la inflacin, mientras que la inflacin observada en el pasado pierde relevancia. Djenme ahondar un poco ms en este punto, sealando lo que ha pasado con la inflacin durante 2017: esta se situ a mediados de octubre en un nivel de 6.30 por ciento, alcanzando su nivel ms alto en agosto pasado. Este incremento atpico de la inflacin se espera que sea temporal, al ser muy factible que se haya iniciado ya la convergencia gradual al objetivo de 3 por ciento a finales de 2018. La inflacin alcanz los altos niveles observados durante 2017 como resultado de diversos choques. En primer lugar, derivado del entorno externo extremadamente complicado que ha enfrentado el pas desde finales de 2014, se generaron pensiones sobre la inflacin a raz de la significativa y persistente depreciacin registrada de la moneda nacional. En segundo lugar, el aceleramiento de la inflacin durante 2017se debi fundamentalmente a la liberalizacin de los precios de 9 los energticos en el pas, y en particular, de los de las gasolinas, as como el incremento de diversos precios de productos agropecuarios y del salario mnimo. Si bien los efectos de los choques sobre la medicin de la inflacin que he descrito han sido importantes en el corto plazo, se espera que sus efectos sean solamente temporales. Al ser los referidos choques fundamentalmente cambios en precios relativos y toda vez que el Banco de Mxico ha actuado para evitar efectos de contagio en el proceso de formacin de precios en la economa, no deberan causar un aumento generalizado y sostenible de los precios. Lo anterior es consistente con el comportamiento de las expectativas de inflacin, donde se observa que las de mediano plazo han aumentado en mucho menor medida que las de corto plazo y las de largo plazo permanecen ancladas en 3.5 por ciento. Esta previsin refleja precisamente la importancia de que en la dinmica inflacionaria el papel de las expectativas de inflacin sea ms relevante que con respecto al de la inflacin pasada. Estos resultados son importantes para la conduccin de la poltica monetaria ya que, en presencia de choques a la inflacin por cambios en los precios relativos, como los descritos, el anclaje de las expectativas permite al Banco Central preservar un ambiente de inflacin 10 baja y estable de manera eficiente, es decir, a menores costos en la actividad econmica. Esto resalta la importancia de continuar fortaleciendo el anclaje de las expectativas de inflacin, siendo uno de los principales canales en el mecanismo de transmisin de la poltica monetaria, para poder consolidar la convergencia de la inflacin a su objetivo de manera ms eficiente. La Curva de Phillips es slo un ejemplo de los mltiples conceptos y cuestionamientos dentro del pensamiento econmico que se han estudiado y debatido a lo largo de los aos, demostrando la importancia de estimular la investigacin y ampliar as la frontera del conocimiento econmico. En este sentido, los trabajos que ustedes han desarrollado a lo largo de varios meses, o incluso aos, de dedicacin y que toman en cuenta las realidades y problemticas especficas para Mxico, representan aportaciones y avances importantsimos que nos permiten ir cerrando la brecha existente entre nuestro entendimiento y la realidad. Por ello, los invito a continuar con esta labor inquisitiva ya que nuestro pas, y el mundo, siempre necesitarn ideas nuevas que permitan una mejor y ms slida toma de decisiones. 11 3. Consideraciones finales Para concluir, felicito a Citibanamex por estos ms de 60 aos de promover la investigacin econmica rigurosa y felicito a los ganadores del Premio de este ao, cuyas investigaciones abarcan temas diversos y sumamente relevantes para la coyuntura actual de nuestro pas. Les aseguro que mediante sus investigaciones mejoran nuestro entendimiento del funcionamiento de la economa, favorecen una mejor toma de decisiones tanto en la administracin pblica como en la iniciativa privada, y con ello, contribuyen a generar un mayor bienestar para nuestra poblacin. Los hoy galardonados deben sentirse muy orgullosos por sus logros. Los invito a seguir contribuyendo al desarrollo de Mxico, con una trayectoria de excelencia desde cada una de sus trincheras. Mxico necesita de su talento y compromiso. Muchas gracias. 12

Title: Mexico in the strange international environment
text: Mexico in the strange international environment Words of Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the Faculty of Economics Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon Monterrey, N.L. February 26, 2016 I wish to thank the Faculty of Economics of the Autonomous University of Nuevo Leon for the kind invitation to share with you some reflections on the situation and perspectives of the Mexican economy in the international context. For me it is very pleasant to return to this institution in which I had the privilege of participating as a teacher in the eighties, interacting with extraordinary colleagues and with students who have stood out for their professional performance. From the stage I spent in these classrooms I treasure magnificent academic experiences, as well as lasting friendships and affections. On this occasion, I would like to divide my comments into three parts. First, I will look at the implications of unusually expansionary monetary policies in advanced economies over the past eight years. I will argue that increasing international financial volatility and even pessimism about the prospects for global economic growth could be, to some extent, an unintended result of these stances. Secondly, I will comment on some challenges that Mexico faces in the international environment, highlighting the need to strengthen its economic fundamentals. Third, I will examine several factors that could determine our country's economic prospects. As always, my comments are of a personal nature and do not necessarily reflect the point of view of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 Since the eruption of the global crisis of 2008, advanced economies have applied monetary stances of increasing laxity, unprecedented in any other era. In particular, central banks cut their policy interest rates to near-zero levels, and even some of them have continued to lower them in negative territory. In addition, these authorities have considerably expanded their balance sheets, acquiring government securities and private securities, such as mortgage-backed assets, whose demand plummeted in the financial implosion, in order to boost their price. The measures carried out at the beginning of the crisis sought to meet the sudden demand for liquidity from the public. The central institutes acted appropriately, in their role as lenders of last resort, to mitigate panic and encourage a return to normal functioning of their financial systems and markets. In contrast to the effectiveness of these measures, the results of increasing monetary easing in subsequent years have been less clear. Central banks' overt goals have included higher economic growth and their inflation targets. In both cases, progress has been limited. 2 On the one hand, the ongoing economic recovery has been the slowest of all post-war cyclical upward phases. While there are indications of a favourable effect on economic activity, the extraordinary degree and prolonged duration of monetary easing contrasts with the weakness of the economic revival recorded.1 It must be recognized that the global financial crisis has been the most severe since the Great Depression. Therefore, the strengthening of the balance sheets of families and companies, as well as the recapitalization of financial institutions, have necessarily required more time than in other crises. However, even in countries such as the United States where financial consolidation has advanced considerably, there is a prevailing perception that economic improvement could be interrupted by monetary normalization, even if it is gradual. The dependence of growth expectations on monetary easing is even more significant in other regions, where further liquidity expansions are expected. This linkage has led to an anomalous financial environment. Often, by foreshadowing more monetary accommodation, unfavorable economic figures have induced 1 For comparison with previous cycles, see Sanchez, M. (2016). "Mexican Economy: Five Topical Topics", presentation at the College of Economists of Nuevo Leon, February. 3 rises in asset prices, while positive data have tended to depress them if less laxity is expected. Increasing monetary easing appears to reflect high expectations about the ability of monetary policy to generate growth. This is despite the fact that one of the conclusions most shared by economists is that of the long-term neutrality of monetary policy, that is, the recognition that the sustained expansion of any economy depends only on real factors, such as production inputs and its productivity. The monetary prominence could be raising doubts about the real drivers of the ongoing recovery, while it could have led to the postponement of imbalance adjustments and structural changes in some regions. On the other hand, central banks in developed countries have struggled to achieve their inflation targets, commonly defined as two percent per year. Price increases in recent years have fallen below this target and, in some cases, even fears of deflation have resurfaced. The above observation must be properly weighed. Inflations in advanced economies have remained moderately low, largely influenced by falling commodity prices, especially commodity prices. 4 Energy. Sooner or later these prices will stop falling so their impact on inflation will disappear. Additionally, there is no clear evidence of a negative association between deflation and economic growth. Hence, deflation, by itself, should not be a cause for concern.2 However, the apparent inability of the extraordinary monetary accommodation to generate more inflation is striking. In particular, even measures of core inflation, which exclude changes in food and energy prices, have declined somewhat, in some cases reaching negative territory. In addition, inflation expectations, reflected in market instruments and also recently in analysts' forecasts, have gone down in the United States and other nations. Among the possible explanations for low inflation and its expectations, I would like to highlight two that could be complementary. One concerns the current poor effectiveness of some monetary transmission mechanisms. For example, increased liquidity and low interest rates have not led to significant demand for credit. This could be due to the process of 2 Borio, C. et al. (2015). "The costs of deflations: a historical perspective," BIS Quarterly Review, marzo. 5 deleveraging after the crisis that has not yet ended, as well as uncertainty about the strength of the economic recovery. The other suggests that low inflation expectations could be the result of a poor balance brought about by extraordinarily expansionary monetary policy. Considering that real interest rates tend to reflect economic conditions, the persistence of near-zero or negative policy rates could be generating diminished inflation expectations. It is concluded that the normalization of monetary policy could increase inflation expectations.3 In sum, the results contrast with high expectations about the ability of monetary policy to solve problems beyond its scope. This can generate skepticism and loss of credibility of the same. Mexico's challenges in the international environment Since mid-2014, international financial markets have seen an increase in risk aversion, manifested in high volatility, as well as continued declines in the prices of commodities and many financial assets. Emerging economies have been 3 The approach is known as Neo-Fisherian, because it is based on the arbitration condition initially proposed by Irving Fisher. See, for example, Garcia-Schmidt, M. and M. Woodford (2015). "Are low interest rates deflationary? A paradox of perfect-foresight analysis," Institute for New Economic Thinking, Working Paper No. 18. 6 particularly affected, as reflected in the trend of widespread depreciation of their currencies against the dollar. At the same time, a net outflow of portfolio capital from these countries has been observed. Two factors contribute to explain this performance. On the one hand, approximately at the time in question, the perception that the beginning of the process of monetary normalization of the United States was approaching increased. The contrast with plans for further liquidity expansion in other advanced economies contributed to increasing capital preference for dollar-denominated assets, strengthening this currency. The U.S. Federal Reserve Bank's decision to finally raise the benchmark rate target by 25 basis points last December was widely anticipated, so its impact on assets was virtually imperceptible. However, during the current year, the economic figures of that country have been less favorable than expected, which has once again increased uncertainty about the future pace of monetary normalization. On the other hand, there was heightened concern about a possible sharp slowdown in China's economy, given the unsustainability of its expansionary policies, as well as about the interpretation of the increasingly frequent government interventions in financial markets. Although they seem to respond mainly to large capital outflows and the reduction of reserves. 7 In the international, the devaluations of the renminbi have also exacerbated fears about the country's economic weakness. In Mexico, market interest rates have remained relatively stable, having incorporated since 2013 the expectation of monetary normalization in the United States. Additionally, since that year the holding of government securities denominated in pesos by non-residents, with respect to the total in circulation, has remained approximately constant, which contrasts with the decline observed in other countries. As in other latitudes, the impact of increased risk aversion on Mexico has been absorbed primarily through the exchange rate. Over the past two years, the depreciation of the peso was similar to that observed on average by emerging economies. However, since last December, the peso has tended to register pressures higher than most of these currencies. In addition to continuing to reflect the broad use of the peso as a hedging vehicle against other emerging market currencies, it cannot be excluded that the weakening is also due to country-specific factors. One possible element could be the fiscal situation. In particular, the peso has shown a high correlation with oil prices. This relationship could be reflecting the adverse effect on 8 Pemex's financial conditions. In addition, it may incorporate, to some degree, the still high dependence of tax revenues on oil which, in the absence of a fiscal adjustment, could compromise public finances in the future. The rise in recent months of sovereign risk indicators, and in particular of Pemex, confirms this association. It cannot be ruled out that the international environment will continue to deteriorate in the coming months, with further falls in commodity prices and financial assets. Among the factors that could lead to this worsening are possible complications in the pace of normalization of monetary policy in the United States, a more significant economic slowdown in China, and the emergence of a financial crisis in that country. Faced with this adverse scenario, Mexico must continue to strengthen its economic fundamentals, at least in three aspects. The first concerns the macroeconomic stance, with the adequacy of public finances and Pemex to lower revenues, taking into account that oil prices are likely to remain low for a considerable period; as well as with monetary policy actions to preserve price stability. The second aspect is the maintenance of the soundness of the financial system, and the third is the proper implementation of structural reforms that increase the potential growth of our economy. 9 Mexico's Economic Outlook As of 2013, the Mexican economy has registered a slow recovery, driven, at first, by the rebound in industrial production, in sync with the greater vigor of that sector in the United States. The improvement in manufacturing and construction led to a positive change in the growth trend. Unfortunately, since mid-2014, GDP dynamism has stagnated, combining an industrial slowdown and upward leadership in the services sector. Recent manufacturing weakness is associated with the industrial loosening of the United States, affected, among other factors, by the resizing of the energy sector. In the same period, Mexico's manufacturing exports and investment have lost momentum. The main driver of demand has been private consumption, favoured by the increase in employment and the incipient improvement in real wages. Recent trends are of concern for three reasons. First, given the high correlation between industrial production in the United States and Mexico, the marked weakness of that sector in that country can severely impact ours. Secondly, if the decline in exports continues, it is difficult to foresee a significant recovery in private investment; and, third, historical data 10 suggest that services and consumption could deteriorate if industrial restoration is delayed. Global pessimism has been reflected in an expected recovery for the world and U.S. economy weaker than that calculated a few months ago. Consequently, expectations for the revival of Mexico's economic activity for 2016 and 2017 have been revised downwards.4 The above diagnosis suggests that the main downside risk to Mexico's dynamism is the U.S. industrial trajectory. Additionally, a further drop in oil prices could further restrict the country's financial conditions, limiting investment projects. Finally, since 2015 inflation in Mexico has been benign, falling below the Bank of Mexico's target, until reaching its historical minimum level at the end of the year. This evolution has been influenced by a smaller variation in some relative prices, as well as by a low transfer of the exchange rate to prices. During the current year, the reversal of some positive shocks has caused a moderate rebound in inflation. 4 For example, from January 2015 to January 2016, the average growth expectations for Mexico, reflected in the survey among analysts conducted by the Bank of Mexico, changed from 3.8 to 2.7 percent for 2016, and from 4.0 to 3.2 percent for 2017. See Bank of Mexico, Survey on the Expectations of Private Sector Economics Specialists. 11 Short- and medium-term expectations point to inflation equal to or slightly above the Bank of Mexico's target. It is worth noting the stability of these projections, despite the significant depreciation of the peso. In order to cope with the external environment, the Bank of Mexico adjusted last December and February the target of the reference interest rate by a total of 75 basis points. Considerations for these decisions included the preservation of the relative monetary stance vis-a-vis the United States; combating the possible contamination of exchange rate depreciation to inflation expectations; and the contribution to strengthening economic fundamentals, by accompanying, in the second decision, the announcement of the preventive adjustment of public spending. In any case, monetary policy must continue to act with all opportunity and flexibility to consolidate the convergence of inflation to the objective of the Bank of Mexico. Among the risks that must continue to be monitored, the following stand out. First, the event of a deeper depreciation of the peso against the dollar has materialized, so it could have increased the danger of second-round effects and misalignment of inflation expectations. Second, the growth of agricultural prices could pick up, within the historical pattern, whose average is much higher than recent observations, which could have effects on the general process of price formation; and third, as the economy recovers, demand pressures could arise. 12 aggregate, considering uncertainty about the economy's slack indicators, such as the output gap. Conclusions The unusual expansion of monetary policy in advanced economies has taken the world into territory whose possible implications are not known with certainty. So far, high expectations about potential benefits have contrasted with the results. Insistence on further stimulus could lead to unintended consequences in terms of financial instability and, sooner or later, disenchantment over monetary policy. The adverse international environment requires Mexico to seek to differentiate itself from other emerging markets, strengthening its economic fundamentals. In this regard, the Federal Government's commitment to a preventive adjustment in spending to adapt to the prospects of lower oil revenues is encouraging. The economic recovery faces downside risks coming mainly from abroad. Proper implementation of structural reforms can boost the potential growth of the economy. Finally, the good performance of inflation represents a unique opportunity to consolidate convergence to price stability. 13
text_original: Mxico en el extrao entorno internacional Palabras de Manuel Snchez Gonzlez Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico en la Facultad de Economa Universidad Autnoma de Nuevo Len Monterrey, N.L. 26 de febrero de 2016 Deseo agradecer a la Facultad de Economa de la Universidad Autnoma de Nuevo Len la amable invitacin para compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones sobre la situacin y perspectivas de la economa mexicana en el contexto internacional. Para m es muy grato regresar a esta institucin en la que tuve el privilegio de participar como maestro en los aos ochenta, interactuando con extraordinarios colegas y con alumnos que han destacado por su desempeo profesional. De la etapa que pas en estas aulas atesoro magnificas experiencias acadmicas, as como amistades y afectos perdurables. En esta ocasin, me gustara dividir mis comentarios en tres partes. En primer lugar, analizar las implicaciones de las polticas monetarias inusualmente expansivas de las economas avanzadas durante los ltimos ocho aos. Argumentar que la creciente volatilidad financiera internacional e, incluso, el pesimismo sobre las perspectivas de crecimiento econmico mundial podran ser, en alguna medida, resultado no deseado de estas posturas. En segundo lugar, comentar sobre algunos desafos que enfrenta Mxico en el entorno internacional, resaltando la necesidad de fortalecer sus fundamentos econmicos. En tercer lugar, examinar varios factores que podran determinar las perspectivas econmicas de nuestro pas. Como siempre, mis comentarios son de carcter personal y no necesariamente reflejan el punto de vista del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno. 1 Las polticas monetarias de las economas avanzadas A partir de la erupcin de la crisis global de 2008, las economas avanzadas han aplicado posturas monetarias de creciente laxitud, sin precedente en ninguna otra poca. En particular, los bancos centrales redujeron sus tasas de inters de poltica monetaria a niveles cercanos a cero, e incluso algunos de ellos las han continuado disminuyendo en terreno negativo. Adems, estas autoridades han expandido considerablemente sus balances, adquiriendo valores gubernamentales y ttulos privados, como activos respaldados por hipotecas, cuya demanda se desplom en la implosin financiera, con el fin de impulsar su precio. Las medidas llevadas a cabo al inicio de la crisis buscaron satisfacer la sbita demanda de liquidez por parte del pblico. Los institutos centrales actuaron adecuadamente, en su papel de prestamistas de ltima instancia, atenuando el pnico y propiciando el retorno al funcionamiento normal de sus sistemas y mercados financieros. En contraste con la efectividad de estas medidas, los resultados del creciente relajamiento monetario en los aos posteriores han sido menos claros. Los objetivos manifiestos de los bancos centrales han incluido el mayor crecimiento econmico y sus metas de inflacin. En ambos casos, el avance ha sido limitado. 2 Por una parte, la recuperacin econmica en curso ha sido la ms lenta de todas las fases cclicas alcistas de la posguerra. Si bien existen indicios de un efecto favorable sobre la actividad econmica, el extraordinario grado y la prolongada duracin del relajamiento monetario contrastan con la debilidad de la reanimacin econmica registrada.1 Debe reconocerse que la crisis financiera global ha sido la ms grave desde la Gran Depresin. Por lo tanto, el fortalecimiento de los balances de las familias y las empresas, as como la recapitalizacin de las instituciones financieras, necesariamente han requerido ms tiempo que en otras crisis. Sin embargo, incluso en pases como Estados Unidos donde el saneamiento financiero ha avanzado considerablemente, prevalece la percepcin de que la mejora econmica podra interrumpirse con la normalizacin monetaria, aun si sta es gradual. La dependencia de las expectativas de crecimiento respecto al relajamiento monetario es an ms significativa en otras regiones, donde se esperan ampliaciones adicionales de liquidez. Esta vinculacin ha propiciado un ambiente financiero anmalo. Con frecuencia, al presagiar ms acomodo monetario, cifras econmicas desfavorables han inducido 1 Para la comparacin con ciclos anteriores, vase Snchez, M. (2016). Economa mexicana: Cinco tpicos de actualidad, presentacin en el Colegio de Economistas de Nuevo Len, febrero. 3 alzas en los precios de los activos, mientras que datos positivos han tendido a deprimirlos si se prev menos laxitud. La creciente relajacin monetaria parece reflejar expectativas elevadas sobre la capacidad de la poltica monetaria de generar crecimiento. Ello a pesar de que una de las conclusiones ms compartidas por los economistas es la de la neutralidad de largo plazo de la poltica monetaria, es decir, el reconocimiento de que la expansin sostenida de cualquier economa depende solo de factores reales, como los insumos de produccin y de su productividad. El protagonismo monetario podra estar generando dudas sobre los motores reales de la recuperacin en marcha, al tiempo que podra haber propiciado la posposicin de ajustes de desbalances y de cambios estructurales en algunas regiones. Por otra parte, los bancos centrales de los pases desarrollados han tenido dificultades para alcanzar sus objetivos de inflacin, definidos comnmente como dos por ciento anual. El aumento de los precios durante los aos recientes ha descendido por debajo de esta meta y, en algunos casos, ha resurgido incluso el temor de la deflacin. La observacin anterior debe ponderarse adecuadamente. Las inflaciones en las economas avanzadas se han mantenido moderadamente bajas, influidas en gran medida por la cada en los precios de las materias primas, en especial de los 4 energticos. Tarde o temprano estos precios dejarn de descender por lo que su impacto sobre la inflacin desaparecer. Adicionalmente, no existe evidencia clara de una asociacin negativa entre deflacin y crecimiento econmico. De ah que la deflacin, por s misma, no debera ser motivo de preocupacin.2 No obstante, llama la atencin la aparente incapacidad del extraordinario acomodamiento monetario para generar ms inflacin. En particular, incluso las mediciones de inflacin subyacente, que excluyen las variaciones de precios de alimentos y energa, han registrado cierto descenso llegando en algunos casos a terreno negativo. Adems, las expectativas de inflacin, reflejadas en instrumentos de mercado y tambin recientemente en los pronsticos de los analistas, han ido a la baja en Estados Unidos y en otras naciones. Entre las posibles explicaciones sobre la reducida inflacin y sus expectativas, me gustara destacar dos que podran ser complementarias. Una se refiere a la escasa efectividad actual de algunos mecanismos de transmisin monetaria. Por ejemplo, el aumento de la liquidez y las mnimas tasas de inters no han propiciado una notable demanda por crdito. Ello podra deberse al proceso de 2 Borio, C. et al. (2015). The costs of deflations: a historical perspective, BIS Quarterly Review, marzo. 5 desendeudamiento posterior a la crisis que an no concluye, as como a la incertidumbre sobre la fortaleza de la recuperacin econmica. La otra apunta a que las expectativas de baja inflacin podran ser resultado de un mal equilibrio propiciado por la poltica monetaria extraordinariamente expansiva. Teniendo en cuenta que las tasas de inters reales tienden a reflejar las condiciones de la economa, la persistencia de tasas de poltica monetaria cercanas a cero o negativas podra estar generando expectativas de inflacin disminuidas. Se concluye que la normalizacin de la poltica monetaria podra aumentar las expectativas de inflacin.3 En suma, los resultados contrastan con las expectativas elevadas sobre la capacidad de la poltica monetaria para resolver problemas ms all de su mbito. Ello puede generar escepticismo y prdida de credibilidad de la misma. Desafos de Mxico ante el entorno internacional Desde mediados de 2014, los mercados financieros internacionales han registrado un aumento de la aversin al riesgo, que se ha manifestado en una elevada volatilidad, as como en continuos descensos en los precios de las materias primas y de numerosos activos financieros. Las economas emergentes han sido 3 El enfoque se conoce como Neo-Fisheriano, por basarse en la condicin de arbitraje inicialmente propuesta por Irving Fisher. Vase, por ejemplo, Garcia-Schmidt, M. y M. Woodford (2015). Are low interest rates deflationary? A paradox of perfect-foresight analysis, Institute for New Economic Thinking, Working Paper No. 18. 6 particularmente afectadas, como lo refleja la tendencia de depreciacin generalizada de sus monedas frente al dlar. Simultneamente, se ha observado una salida neta de capitales de cartera de esos pases. Dos factores contribuyen a explicar este desempeo. Por una parte, aproximadamente en la poca referida, aument la percepcin de que se acercaba el inicio del proceso de normalizacin monetaria de Estados Unidos. El contraste con planes de expansin adicional de liquidez en otras economas avanzadas contribuy a acrecentar la preferencia de los capitales por activos denominados en dlares, fortaleciendo a esta moneda. La decisin del Banco de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos de finalmente incrementar 25 puntos base el objetivo de la tasa de referencia en diciembre pasado fue ampliamente anticipada, por lo que su impacto en los activos fue prcticamente imperceptible. No obstante, durante el presente ao, las cifras econmicas de ese pas han sido menos favorables que las esperadas, lo que ha incrementado una vez ms la incertidumbre sobre el ritmo futuro de la normalizacin monetaria. Por otra parte, se acentu la preocupacin sobre una posible desaceleracin brusca de la economa de China, ante la insostenibilidad de sus polticas expansivas, as como sobre la interpretacin de las cada vez ms frecuentes intervenciones gubernamentales en los mercados financieros. Si bien parecen responder principalmente a las cuantiosas salidas de capital y a la reduccin de las reservas 7 internacionales, las devaluaciones del renminbi han exacerbado adems los temores sobre la debilidad econmica de ese pas. En Mxico, las tasas de inters de mercado han permanecido relativamente estables, tras haber incorporado desde 2013 la expectativa de la normalizacin monetaria de Estados Unidos. Adicionalmente, desde ese ao la tenencia de valores gubernamentales denominados en pesos por parte de no residentes, respecto al total en circulacin, se ha mantenido aproximadamente constante, lo que contrasta con el declive observado en otros pases. Como en otras latitudes, el impacto de la mayor aversin al riesgo sobre Mxico se ha absorbido primordialmente mediante el tipo de cambio. Durante los dos aos recientes, la depreciacin del peso fue semejante a la observada en promedio por las economas emergentes. No obstante, desde diciembre pasado, el peso ha tendido a registrar presiones superiores a la mayora de esas divisas. Adems de continuar reflejando la amplia utilizacin del peso como vehculo de cobertura contra otras monedas de mercados emergentes, no puede excluirse que el debilitamiento responda tambin a factores especficos del pas. Un posible elemento podra ser la situacin fiscal. En particular, el peso ha mostrado una elevada correlacin con los precios del petrleo. Esta relacin podra estar reflejando el efecto adverso sobre las 8 condiciones financieras de Pemex. Adems, es posible que incorpore, en algn grado, la todava alta dependencia de los ingresos fiscales respecto al petrleo lo que, en ausencia de un ajuste fiscal, podra comprometer las finanzas pblicas en el futuro. La elevacin en meses recientes de los indicadores de riesgo soberano, y en particular de Pemex, confirma esta asociacin. No puede descartarse que el entorno internacional contine deteriorndose en los prximos meses, con cadas adicionales en los precios de las materias primas y los activos financieros. Entre los factores que podran propiciar este empeoramiento se encuentran posibles complicaciones en el ritmo de normalizacin de la poltica monetaria de Estados Unidos, una desaceleracin econmica ms significativa en China, y el surgimiento de una crisis financiera en ese pas. Ante este escenario adverso, Mexico debe continuar fortaleciendo sus fundamentos econmicos, por lo menos, en tres vertientes. La primera se refiere a la postura macroeconmica, con la adecuacin de las finanzas pblicas y de Pemex a los menores ingresos, tomando en cuenta que los precios del petrleo probablemente se mantendrn bajos por un periodo considerable; as como con las acciones de poltica monetaria para preservar la estabilidad de precios. La segunda vertiente es el mantenimiento de la solidez del sistema financiero, y la tercera es la aplicacin adecuada de las reformas estructurales que aumenten el crecimiento potencial de nuestra economa. 9 Perspectivas econmicas de Mxico A partir de 2013, la economa mexicana ha registrado una recuperacin lenta, impulsada, al principio, por el repunte de la produccin industrial, en sincrona con el mayor vigor de ese sector en Estados Unidos. La mejora manufacturera y de la construccin propici un cambio positivo en la tendencia de crecimiento. Desafortunadamente, desde mediados de 2014, se ha estancado el dinamismo del PIB, combinando una desaceleracin industrial y un liderazgo ascendente del sector servicios. La debilidad manufacturera reciente est asociada con el aflojamiento industrial de Estados Unidos, afectado, entre otros factores, por el redimensionamiento del sector energtico. En igual lapso, las exportaciones manufactureras y la inversin de Mxico han perdido empuje. El principal motor de la demanda ha sido el consumo privado, favorecido por el aumento del empleo y la incipiente mejora de los salarios reales. Las recientes tendencias preocupan por tres razones. Primero, dada la elevada correlacin entre las producciones industriales de Estados Unidos y Mxico, la acentuada debilidad de ese sector en aquel pas puede impactar severamente al nuestro. Segundo, de continuar el decaimiento de las exportaciones, es difcil prever una recuperacin notable de la inversin privada; y, tercero, los datos histricos 10 sugieren que los servicios y el consumo podran deteriorarse si el restablecimiento industrial se demora. El pesimismo global se ha reflejado en una recuperacin prevista para la economa mundial y de Estados Unidos ms dbil que la calculada hace algunos meses. Consecuentemente, se han revisado a la baja las expectativas de reanimacin de la actividad econmica de Mxico para 2016 y 2017.4 El diagnstico anterior sugiere que el principal riesgo a la baja para el dinamismo de Mxico es la trayectoria industrial de Estados Unidos. Adicionalmente, una mayor cada de los precios del petrleo podra restringir ms las condiciones financieras del pas, limitando los proyectos de inversin. Finalmente, desde 2015 la inflacin en Mxico ha sido benigna, reducindose por abajo del objetivo del Banco de Mxico, hasta alcanzar su nivel mnimo histrico a finales de ao. Esta evolucin ha estado influida por una menor variacin en algunos precios relativos, as como por un bajo traspaso del tipo de cambio a los precios. Durante el presente ao, la reversin de algunos choques positivos ha causado un repunte moderado de la inflacin. 4 Por ejemplo, de enero de 2015 a enero de 2016, la media de las expectativas de crecimiento para Mxico, reflejada en la encuesta entre analistas conducida por el Banco de Mxico, cambi de 3.8 a 2.7 por ciento para 2016, y de 4.0 a 3.2 por ciento para 2017. Vase Banco de Mxico, Encuesta sobre las expectativas de los especialistas en economa del sector privado. 11 Las expectativas de corto y mediano plazo apuntan a una inflacin igual o ligeramente por arriba del objetivo del Banco de Mxico. Cabe destacar la estabilidad de estas proyecciones, a pesar de la significativa depreciacin del peso. Con el fin de enfrentar el entorno externo, el Banco de Mxico ajust en diciembre y febrero pasados el objetivo de la tasa de inters de referencia por un total de 75 puntos base. Las consideraciones para estas decisiones incluyeron la preservacin de la postura monetaria relativa respecto a Estados Unidos; el combate contra la posible contaminacin de la depreciacin cambiaria a las expectativas de inflacin; y la contribucin al fortalecimiento de los fundamentos econmicos, al acompaar, en la segunda decisin, el anuncio del ajuste preventivo del gasto pblico. En cualquier caso, la poltica monetaria deber seguir actuando con toda oportunidad y flexibilidad para consolidar la convergencia de la inflacin al objetivo del Banco de Mxico. Entre los riesgos que debern seguir vigilndose, sobresalen los siguientes. Primero, el evento de una depreciacin ms profunda del peso frente al dlar se ha materializado, por lo que podra haber aumentado el peligro de efectos de segunda vuelta y de desalineacin de las expectativas de inflacin. Segundo, el crecimiento de los precios agropecuarios podra repuntar, dentro del patrn histrico, cuya media es muy superior a las recientes observaciones, lo que podra tener efectos en el proceso general de formacin de precios; y tercero, a medida que se recupere la economa, podran surgir presiones de demanda 12 agregada, considerando la incertidumbre sobre los indicadores de holgura de la economa, tales como la brecha del producto. Conclusiones La expansin inusitada de la poltica monetaria en las economas avanzadas ha llevado al mundo a un territorio cuyas posibles implicaciones no se conocen con certeza. Hasta ahora, las expectativas elevadas sobre los posibles beneficios han contrastado con los resultados. La insistencia en un mayor estmulo podra conducir a consecuencias no deseadas en trminos de inestabilidad financiera y, tarde o temprano, al desencanto sobre la poltica monetaria. El entorno internacional adverso requiere que Mxico busque diferenciarse de otros mercados emergentes, fortaleciendo sus fundamentos econmicos. Al respecto, es alentador el compromiso del Gobierno Federal de realizar un ajuste preventivo en el gasto para adecuarse a las perspectivas de menores ingresos petroleros. La recuperacin econmica enfrenta riesgos a la baja provenientes principalmente del exterior. La implementacin adecuada de las reformas estructurales puede impulsar el crecimiento potencial de la economa. Finalmente, el buen desempeo de la inflacin representa una oportunidad nica para consolidar la convergencia a la estabilidad de precios. 13

Title: Closing of the seminar: The role of banking for stability and economic growth
text: 1 Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, during the closing of the Seminar "The role of banking for stability and economic growth". Thursday, June 10, 2010, Mexico City. ? Maria Teresa Fernandez Labardini, Executive Secretary of the Institute for the Protection of Bank Savings. ? Ignacio Deschamps Gonzalez, President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, ? IpAB Counselors ? Distinguished speakers at this Seminar ? Ladies and gentlemen Generating and maintaining confidence in the future, in turn, has been and will continue to be the perennial challenge facing all human societies to progress and aspire to a better future. The tremendous financial cataclysm that the world experienced in recent months, and whose aftermath will still generate concerns and difficulties for a long time, is ultimately explained as a deep crisis of confidence that was unleashed in full force in September 2008, when the unexpected bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers sent erratic and disconcerting signals about the handling of a financial crisis that until before that date was conjectured that could be reasonably under control. 1 2 That loss of confidence was enough for the crisis to spread beyond the strictly financial realm to the real economy in virtually the entire world and in a few hours. This crisis made reality, in a dramatic way, that famous sentence of Seneca: "When the navigator does not know which port he is going to, all the winds are contrary." When the delicate threads that sustain confidence in the permanence of contracts and in the effective fulfillment of payment promises are broken, even momentarily and by an erratic event, the markets lose their compass and all the winds seem to conspire against us. The banking business, as you all know, fulfills the essential function of reconciling liabilities that tend to be short-term, because depositors demand liquidity in the face of all kinds of uncertainties, with assets that need to be long-term, because productive investments require time to mature and to generate the desired returns. Such is this disparity between the needs and motivations of one party and another (which are savers, on the one hand, and entrepreneurs, on the other), that the probability of bank runs is not only high, but will surely materialize at some point, unless there are mechanisms that give certainty to depositors that their rights and interests will be preserved no matter what happens and according to certain parameters, known in advance. Precisely because of this is that finance is one of the few economic activities that must be highly regulated and 2 3 Supervised. What is sought is that intermediaries do not assume undue risks, do not have liquidity problems and, above all, that they do not fall into a situation of insolvency, which is the most serious danger. History, including of course recent history, has taught us, however, that regulation and supervision are not foolproof and that it has taken a lot of work to ensure that regulation and supervision do not constantly lag behind financial innovation. Because of all this, the guarantee mechanisms or trust vaccines that are required to consolidate the confidence of depositors and neutralize the uncertainty that encourages episodes of bank runs are only credible and viable when they are granted by the State. Only the State can give credibility to such guarantees and the State can do so only because it has the power to impose extraordinary levies and contributions, in case of extreme necessity, in order to preserve the functioning of the system as well as the rights of both. In this sense, it is no coincidence that on the way out of the global crisis that we have suffered we find ourselves with severe fiscal crises in several countries and even in entire regions of the world. As economies in trouble today unhesitatingly strengthen their fiscal balance sheets, dragging the cost that such a correction will inevitably entail, to that same extent the world will more quickly overcome this global upheaval and in that 3 4 World production and trade, along with jobs, can recover to the same extent. In Mexico we know this painful process well because we lived it after the outbreak of the crisis of 1994-1995 and we experienced all its aftermath and stages. From that sobering and difficult experience was born, precisely, the IPAB. Indeed, as has already been said several times today, insurance against bank deposits fulfils the crucial function of generating confidence, which is the most precious asset that must be counted not only by financial intermediation but also by the entire economic activity of a country. But the challenges do not end there, with the establishment of deposit insurance administered by a State institution and with the guarantee of the latter. There are three essential conditions for the proper functioning of a deposit insurance: 1. An efficient design. 2. A legal framework to give regulatory institutions and the agency administering the insurance broad and sufficient powers for timely crisis resolution, and 3. An equally sufficient capitalization that, however, does not unnecessarily make bank intermediation more expensive. Of course, it is much easier to enunciate these three conditions than to make them a reality. There is no single, infallible model. In fact, we find great disparities in the world regarding the design that different countries have applied to their deposit insurance modalities. And the persistence of different episodes of 4 5 crises and bank runs, in different regions and latitudes, shows us that we still have a lot to learn. The Northern Rock episode in the United Kingdom, for example, taught us that one of the causes of crisis may lie in the complexity of the rules for determining the amount of insurance from the perspective of the common depositor, as well as in the existence of a zone of uncertainty regarding the terms for the payment of insured deposits. The case of Icelandic banks, in turn, taught us that total certainty is required as to whether deposit coverage also includes depositors in branches of such banks established in other countries. This lack of definition caused serious international legal conflicts. Not all countries, for example, establish the same order of priority among creditors in the event of bank failure, especially in the case of foreign branches or non-resident depositors. That is why in Mexico, among other reasons, the establishment of branches of foreign banks has not been allowed, but only of subsidiaries of foreign parent companies that are, for all intents and purposes, Mexican banks. Incidentally, this feature completely dispels any conjecture about an alleged lack of sovereignty over the national payment system. As part of this global learning process, derived from recent experiences, some countries have expanded their deposit insurance coverage, through definitive increases in the amounts covered. Such have been the cases of 5 6 Ireland, Germany, the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Greece, Spain, the Netherlands, Italy and Austria. Other countries, such as Australia and New Zealand, have increased coverage, but have announced it only as a temporary measure. In turn, some other nations that did not have deposit insurance have established them. From these recent experiences in the field of deposit insurance in different countries, the lesson emerges that it is preferable that such changes be made in a coordinated manner at the global level. Otherwise, increasing the dispersion of coverage of bank deposits between different countries increases the risks of causing destabilizing episodes. Thus, the need to improve deposit insurance according to the three conditions I mentioned - design, defined attributions and sufficient capitalization - persists, which are those considered in the new "Basic Principles of Cash Deposit Insurance" released last year by the International Association of Deposit Insurers and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. I'll dwell a little on each of them. ? With regard to the design of the insurance, it should be perfectly clear which obligations will be covered by the insurance, especially when banks have a cross-border presence, either through branches or subsidiaries; and access to deposits covered by 6 7 the insurance must be expeditious, so that it does not generate any uncertainty in the depositors. ? The agencies that administer the insurance must have defined and sufficient legal powers to: 1. Act quickly, since the crisis taught us again that the problems of the banks must be solved immediately, ideally "in a weekend", 2. Carry out a resolution even if the capital of the bank in question is, in principle, positive. That is: the right of shareholders to be compensated does not mean that they have the right to stop the action of the authority, and 3. Coordinate efficiently with the rest of the agencies that constitute the safety net of the financial system, especially in "systemic" crises. In this regard, as I have said on other occasions, efficient coordination and cooperation mechanisms must be created to preserve the financial stability of the entire system, both at the national and international levels. ? Finally, there is the requirement of sufficient capitalization of the agencies that administer deposit insurance and that is the subject of many controversies, according to the interests of those involved. It should be understood, in any case, that the agency must have sufficient capital to expeditiously execute the payment of guaranteed deposits and for the execution of another type of bank resolution, such as the purchase of assets, the assumption of liabilities or the opening of a "bridge" bank that guarantees the continuity and fluidity of the financial system as a whole, among other examples. 7 8 Ten years after the creation of the IPAB, the balance sheet in Mexico is undoubtedly satisfactory: Our deposit insurance complies with the good principles recognized internationally, it was successfully and smoothly achieved to move from universal to limited coverage and an early warning system was established in the legal framework, as well as the methods for bank resolutions. However, we are left with several challenges in the immediate future. I mention the three that seem most important to me: 1. Define the collection of premiums according to the risk, 2. Establish a specific fund that allows bank resolutions to be carried out, and 3. Advance in the legal framework of the resolutions. The financial authorities have already designed a set of changes that complement and complete the framework of resolutions - for example, the shortening of the hearing periods for shareholders - as well as a legal framework for the judicial liquidation of banks. It is to be expected, as announced a few hours ago by the Secretary of Finance, that this set of modifications will be submitted to the Congress of the Union for consideration in the near future. Ladies and gentlemen: The financial authorities have the very delicate task of creating, transmitting, maintaining and increasing trust. This 8 9 it implies that we must foresee as far as possible, as well as provide today what tomorrow might demand of us. Experience always leaves us with valuable lessons to improve not only our forecasts, but also to strengthen the provisions we must make for future times that will always have a dose of uncertainty. The global crisis has also reminded us, once again in history, of the importance of the basic principles that enable the economic progress of societies and nations. Principles that today acquire even greater relevance: stability of the purchasing power of the currency through a responsible monetary policy; prudent management of public finances to avoid chronic and growing imbalances between revenues and expenditures; clear and certain rules that guarantee the fulfillment of contracts; judicious management of indebtedness; conditions that encourage long-term savings and that allow everyone to expect, with certain foundations, a better future. All this contains the value of the trust that we have, day by day, the obligation to maintain and increase. Thanks a lot. 9 10 10
text_original: 1 Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, durante la clausura del Seminario La funcin de la banca para la estabilidad y el crecimiento econmico. Jueves 10 de junio de 2010, ciudad de Mxico.  Mara Teresa Fernndez Labardini, Secretario Ejecutivo del Instituto para la Proteccin del Ahorro Bancario.  Ignacio Deschamps Gonzlez, Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico,  Seores Consejeros del IPAB  Distinguidos expositores en este Seminario  Seoras y seores Generar y mantener la confianza en el futuro, a su vez, ha sido y seguir siendo el perenne desafo que enfrentan todas las sociedades humanas para progresar y aspirar a un mejor porvenir. El tremendo cataclismo financiero que experiment el mundo en meses recientes, y cuyas secuelas an generarn inquietudes y dificultades por un largo tiempo, se explica en ltima instancia como una profunda crisis de confianza que se desat con toda su fuerza en septiembre de 2008, cuando la quiebra inesperada de Lehman Brothers envi seales errticas y desconcertantes acerca del manejo de una crisis financiera que hasta antes de esa fecha se conjeturaba que podra estar razonablemente bajo control. 1 2 Bast con esa prdida de confianza para que la crisis se extendiera ms all del mbito estrictamente financiero a la economa real en prcticamente todo el mundo y en unas cuantas horas. Esta crisis hizo realidad, de forma dramtica, aquella famosa sentencia de Sneca: Cuando el navegante no sabe a qu puerto se dirige, todos los vientos son contrarios. Al romperse los delicados hilos que sostienen la confianza en la permanencia de los contratos y en el cumplimiento efectivo de las promesas de pago, as sea momentneamente y por un evento errtico, los mercados pierden la brjula y todos los vientos parecen conspirar en nuestra contra. El negocio bancario, como todos ustedes saben, cumple la funcin esencial de conciliar pasivos que tienden a ser de corto plazo, porque los depositantes demandan liquidez ante todo tipo de incertidumbres, con activos que necesitan ser de largo plazo, porque las inversiones productivas requieren de tiempo para madurar y para generar los retornos deseados. Es tal esta disparidad entre las necesidades y motivaciones de una y otra parte (que son los ahorradores, por un lado, y los emprendedores, por otro), que la probabilidad de corridas bancarias no slo es elevada, sino que seguramente se materializar en algn momento, a menos que existan mecanismos que den certeza a los depositantes de que sus derechos e intereses sern preservados pase lo que pase y de acuerdo con parmetros ciertos, conocidos de antemano. Precisamente debido a esto es que la financiera es una de las pocas actividades econmicas que debe estar altamente regulada y 2 3 supervisada. Lo que se busca es que los intermediarios no asuman riesgos indebidos, no tengan problemas de liquidez y, sobre todo, que no caigan en una situacin de insolvencia, que es el peligro ms grave. La historia, incluida desde luego la historia reciente, nos ha enseado, sin embargo, que la regulacin y la supervisin no son infalibles y que ha costado mucho trabajo que la regulacin y la supervisin no se queden constantemente rezagadas frente a la innovacin financiera. Debido a todo esto es que los mecanismos de garanta o vacunas de confianza que se requieren para consolidar la confianza de los depositantes y neutralizar la incertidumbre que incentiva los episodios de corridas bancarias, slo son crebles y viables cuando son otorgados por el Estado. Slo el Estado puede dar credibilidad a tales garantas y el Estado puede hacerlo slo porque tiene la facultad de imponer gravmenes y contribuciones extraordinarias, en caso de necesidad extrema, para preservar el funcionamiento del sistema as como los derechos de unos y de otros. En este sentido, no es casual que en el camino de salida de la crisis global que hemos padecido nos encontremos con severas crisis fiscales en varios pases e incluso en regiones completas del mundo. Conforme las economas hoy en problemas fortalezcan sin titubeos sus balances fiscales, arrastrando el costo que esa correccin inevitablemente acarrear, en esa misma medida el mundo superar ms rpidamente este trastorno global y en esa 3 4 misma medida podrn recuperarse la produccin y el comercio mundiales, junto con los empleos. En Mxico conocemos bien este doloroso proceso porque lo vivimos tras el estallido de la crisis de 19941995 y experimentamos todas sus secuelas y etapas. De esa aleccionadora y difcil experiencia naci, precisamente, el IPAB. En efecto, como ya se ha dicho varias veces el da de hoy, el seguro a los depsitos bancarios cumple la funcin crucial de generar confianza, que es el activo ms preciado con que debe contar no slo la intermediacin financiera sino toda la actividad econmica de un pas. Pero los desafos no terminan ah, con el establecimiento de un seguro a los depsitos administrado por una institucin del Estado y con el aval de ste. Hay tres condiciones esenciales para el buen funcionamiento de un seguro de depsitos: 1. Un diseo eficiente. 2.
