Un marco jurdico que le de a las instituciones reguladoras y a la agencia que administra el seguro facultades amplias y suficientes para la resolucin oportuna de crisis, y 3. Una capitalizacin igualmente suficiente que, sin embargo, no encarezca de forma innecesaria la intermediacin bancaria. Por supuesto, es mucho ms fcil enunciar estas tres condiciones que hacerlas realidad. No hay un modelo nico e infalible. De hecho, encontramos grandes disparidades en el mundo respecto del diseo que diferentes pases han aplicado a sus modalidades de seguro de depsitos. Y la persistencia de diferentes episodios de 4 5 crisis y corridas bancarias, en diferentes regiones y latitudes, nos muestra que an tenemos mucho que aprender. El episodio de Northern Rock en el Reino Unido, por ejemplo, nos ense que una de las causas de crisis puede radicar en la complejidad de las reglas para determinar el monto del seguro desde la perspectiva del depositante comn, as como en la existencia de una zona de incertidumbre respecto de los plazos para el pago de los depsitos asegurados. El caso de los bancos de Islandia, a su vez, nos ense que se requiere de una total certidumbre acerca de si la cobertura de los depsitos tambin incluye a los depositantes de las sucursales de dichos bancos establecidas en otros pases. Esta indefinicin ocasion graves conflictos jurdicos internacionales. No todos los pases, por ejemplo, establecen el mismo orden de prelacin entre acreedores en caso de quiebra bancaria, en especial tratndose de sucursales extranjeras o de depositantes que no son residentes. Por eso en Mxico, entre otras razones, no se ha permitido el establecimiento de sucursales de bancos extranjeros, sino slo de subsidiarias de matrices extranjeras que son, para todo efecto, bancos mexicanos. Dicho sea de paso, esta caracterstica desvanece por completo cualquier conjetura acerca de una supuesta falta de soberana sobre el sistema de pagos nacional. Como parte de este proceso de aprendizaje mundial, derivado de las experiencias recientes, algunos pases han ampliado las coberturas de sus seguros de depsitos, mediante incrementos definitivos de los montos cubiertos. Tales han sido los casos de 5 6 Irlanda, de Alemania, de Estados Unidos, de Reino Unido, de Francia, de Grecia, de Espaa, de Holanda, de Italia y de Austria. Otros pases, como Australia y Nueva Zelanda, han incrementado la cobertura, pero lo han anunciado slo como una medida temporal. A su vez, algunas otras naciones que no contaban con seguros de depsitos los han establecido. De estas experiencias recientes en materia de seguros de depsito en diferentes pases se desprende la leccin de que es preferible que tales modificaciones se hagan de manera coordinada a nivel global. De otra forma, si aumenta la dispersin de las coberturas a los depsitos bancarios entre distintos pases se incrementan los riesgos de suscitar episodios desestabilizadores. Persiste, as, la necesidad de perfeccionar los seguros de depsito de acuerdo a las tres condiciones que mencion  diseo, atribuciones definidas y capitalizacin suficiente y que son las consideradas en los nuevos Principios Bsicos del Seguro de Depsitos en Efectivo que difundieron el ao pasado la Asociacin Internacional de Aseguradoras de Depsitos y el Comit de Basilea de Supervisin Bancaria. Me detendr un poco en cada una de ellas.  Respecto del diseo del seguro, debe quedar perfectamente claro qu obligaciones sern cubiertas por el seguro, especialmente cuando los bancos tienen presencia transfronteriza, ya sea a travs de sucursales o de subsidiarias; asimismo, el acceso a los depsitos cubiertos por 6 7 el seguro debe ser expedito, de forma que no genere ninguna incertidumbre en los depositantes.  Las agencias que administran el seguro deben tener atribuciones legales definidas y suficientes para: 1. Actuar con rapidez, ya que la crisis nos ense de nuevo que los problemas de los bancos deben resolverse de inmediato, idealmente en un fin de semana, 2. Llevar a cabo una resolucin aun cuando el capital del banco en cuestin sea, en principio, positivo. Esto es: el derecho de los accionistas a ser resarcidos no significa que tienen derecho a detener la accin de la autoridad, y 3. Coordinarse eficientemente con el resto de las agencias que constituyen la red de seguridad del sistema financiero, especialmente en crisis sistmicas. Al respecto, como ya he dicho en otras ocasiones, deben crearse mecanismos eficientes de coordinacin y cooperacin encargados de preservar la estabilidad financiera de todo el sistema, tanto en el mbito nacional como en el internacional.  Finalmente, est el requisito de la capitalizacin suficiente de las agencias que administran los seguros de depsito y que es objeto de no pocas polmicas, de acuerdo con los intereses de los involucrados. Debe entenderse, en todo caso, que la agencia debe contar con el capital suficiente para ejecutar de forma expedita el pago de los depsitos garantizados y para la ejecucin de otro tipo de resolucin bancaria, como la compra de activos, la asuncin de pasivos o la apertura de un banco puente que permita garantizar la continuidad y fluidez del sistema financiero en su conjunto, entre otros ejemplos. 7 8 A diez aos de la creacin del IPAB el balance en Mxico es indudablemente satisfactorio: Nuestro seguro de depsitos cumple con los buenos principios reconocidos internacionalmente, se logr de forma exitosa y sin sobresaltos transitar de una cobertura universal a una limitada y se estableci en el marco jurdico un sistema de alertas tempranas, as como los mtodos para resoluciones bancarias. Sin embargo, nos quedan varios desafos en el futuro inmediato. Menciono los tres que me parecen ms importantes: 1. Definir el cobro de primas de acuerdo con el riesgo, 2. Establecer un fondo especfico que permita llevar a cabo resoluciones bancarias, y 3. Avanzar en el marco legal de las resoluciones. Las autoridades financieras ya han diseado un conjunto de cambios que complementan y completan el marco de las resoluciones  por ejemplo, el acortamiento de los plazos de audiencia para los accionistas  as como un marco jurdico para la liquidacin judicial de bancos. Es de esperarse, como lo anunci hace unas horas el Secretario de Hacienda, que este conjunto de modificaciones sea sometido en fecha prxima a la consideracin del Congreso de la Unin. Seoras y seores: Las autoridades financieras tenemos la delicadsima encomienda de crear, transmitir, mantener y acrecentar la confianza. Esto 8 9 implica que debemos prever en la medida de lo posible, as como proveer hoy lo que podra demandarnos el maana. La experiencia nos deja siempre lecciones valiosas para mejorar no slo nuestras previsiones, sino tambin para fortalecer las provisiones que debemos hacer para tiempos futuros que siempre tendrn una dosis de incertidumbre. La crisis mundial tambin nos ha recordado, una vez ms en la historia, la importancia de los principios bsicos que permiten el progreso econmico de las sociedades y de las naciones. Principios que hoy adquieren an mayor relevancia: estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda a travs de una poltica monetaria responsable; administracin prudente de las finanzas pblicas que evite los desequilibrios crnicos y crecientes entre ingresos y egresos; reglas claras y ciertas que garanticen el cumplimiento de los contratos; manejo juicioso del endeudamiento; condiciones que propicien el ahorro de largo plazo y que permitan esperar a todos, con fundamentos ciertos, un futuro mejor. Todo eso encierra el valor de la confianza que tenemos, da con da, la obligacin de mantener y acrecentar. Muchas gracias. 9 10 10

Title: Mobile banking: regulatory simplification for the use of new technologies
text: "Mobile banking: regulatory simplification for the use of new technologies" Remarks by Agustin Carstens, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation ceremony of the regulatory simplification provisions to promote the use of new "mobile banking" technologies. July 21, 2010 - Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Ernesto Cordero Arroyo. - Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit, Gerardo Rodriguez Regordosa - President of the National Banking Commission, Guillermo Babatz Torres - Vice President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, Enrique Zorrilla Fullaondo - Senator Javier Castelo Parada - Deputy Jose Narro - Ladies and gentlemen, The current portrait of Mexican banking is as follows: it is an extraordinarily solid bank in terms of capital, liquidity and solvency; that, together with a macroeconomic framework of proven stability, gives it a formidable growth potential. However, it is also a bank that, despite countless attempts, to date has not made the great leap that allows it to bring financial services to the vast majority of Mexicans and cover the entire national territory. This is how great the challenge is for banks in Mexico in terms of financial inclusion, which allows us to measure the importance of the strategy behind this regulatory simplification that is announced today and in which we work together the 1 Ministry of Finance, the National Banking and Securities Commission and the Bank of Mexico. The ultimate objective is to definitively promote modalities of access and propagation of financial services through the use of new technologies, all encompassed in the denomination "mobile banking". Just a few facts to outline the potential of mobile banking: in Mexico there are approximately 85 million mobile phone lines and the mobile phone has become, thanks to technology, a secure means to make transactions or establish communication, through text messages, with banking institutions. They are, therefore, an ideal means to accelerate financial inclusion and for banks to offer, through mobile phones, channels of access to financial services, especially to people with low resources or who live in remote localities. Let's take into account that while there are, as I have already said, some 85 million mobile phone lines in Mexico, it is estimated that there are only about 30 million current bank accounts. For the Bank of Mexico, it is crucial that there is a greater participation of financial services throughout the country and for the entire population. Why? Firstly, because, together with the priority mandate in favour of price stability, the law has mandated us to promote the healthy development of the financial system, as well as the proper functioning of payment systems. 2 Secondly, because greater financial inclusion results in a better functioning of the markets and the system as a whole, contributes to reducing asymmetries in terms of information for users and facilitates, in short, that free competition between banks translates into lower costs and better products for consumers of financial services. Hence, the Bank of Mexico has participated decisively, and within the scope of its powers, in this strategy of regulatory simplification. I have no doubt that this effort will pave the way for the development of all the potential that, thanks to technological advances, mobile banking can reach in Mexico. Specifically, the Central Bank is the competent regulator to determine the characteristics of passive banking operations. Therefore, on June 17, the Bank of Mexico issued circular 14/2011 for multiple banking and on July 7 issued circular 1/2006 Bis 41 for development banking, which recognizes four types of collection accounts conducive to promoting access to financial services and their continued use with very few regulatory requirements in terms of information and monitoring of the same accounts. Once this framework has been established, the Ministry of Finance is able to issue provisions relating, especially to the prevention and combating of money laundering and the financing of terrorism; at the same time that the National Banking and Securities Commission may exercise the regulation that corresponds to it 3 in the field of electronic banking and banking commission agents, which will include telecommunications companies. It is worth drawing attention to the logical scheme that was followed to identify and design these four types of accounts: the lower the transactional capacity of the accounts corresponds to a lower risk of illegitimate operations and the lower the reporting and monitoring requirements. This makes it possible to offer basic financial products - collection accounts with amounts and modalities of use more or less restricted according to the type of account - to the access of anyone in practically any place of the Mexican Republic. In addition to this regulatory simplification, an ideal response to the need to promote electronic money linked to mobile phones is consolidated, all focused on the banking system. With this regulatory framework, security is given to the resources allocated by users to these innovative mechanisms, since they will be protected by all the prudential regulation of the banking system and will then qualify for the protection of the IPAB. The interests of the public are fully guaranteed because payments made through mobile phones and other electronic means will be laid on the foundations of the banking system, and this gives users all the benefits of the regulation issued by the Central Bank on transparency in characteristics and costs, the application of the rules relating to the fight against money laundering and financing of terrorism, as well as the use of systems 4 of robust, well-regulated and supervised payments, in which the final nature of payments is foreseen. In this way, an ideal and creative response is being given to the great challenge represented by the need to increase financial inclusion. It is, in short, a great boost for the Mexican banking system to develop its full potential. An opportunity to integrate tens of millions of people into the financial system in a relatively short time who today do not have access to it. An opportunity, in short, that we cannot and should not miss. Thanks a lot. 5
text_original: Banca mvil: simplificacin regulatoria para el uso de nuevas tecnologas Palabras de Agustn Carstens, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la ceremonia de presentacin de las disposiciones de simplificacin regulatoria para propiciar el uso de nuevos tecnologas de banca mvil. 21 de julio de 2010 - Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, Ernesto Cordero Arroyo. - Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, Gerardo Rodrguez Regordosa - Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria, Guillermo Babatz Torres - Vicepresidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, Enrique Zorrilla Fullaondo - Senador Javier Castelo Parada - Diputado Jose Narro - Seoras y seores: El retrato actual de la banca mexicana es el siguiente: es una banca extraordinariamente slida en capital, en liquidez y en solvencia; eso, sumado a un marco macroeconmico de probada estabilidad, le da un formidable potencial de crecimiento. Sin embargo, es tambin una banca que, a pesar de innumerables intentos, hasta la fecha no ha dado el gran salto que le permita llevar los servicios financieros a la inmensa mayora de los mexicanos y cubrir todo el territorio nacional. As de grande es el reto para la banca en Mxico en materia de inclusin financiera, lo cual nos permite dimensionar la importancia de la estrategia que hay detrs de esta simplificacin regulatoria que se anuncia hoy y en la que trabajamos conjuntamente la 1 Secretara de Hacienda, la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores y el Banco de Mxico. El objetivo ltimo es impulsar de forma definitiva modalidades de acceso y propagacin de los servicios financieros mediante el uso de nuevas tecnologas, todo ello englobado en la denominacin banca mvil. Slo unos datos para bosquejar el potencial de la banca mvil: en Mxico hay aproximadamente 85 millones de lneas de telefona mvil y el telfono mvil se ha convertido, gracias a la tecnologa, en un medio seguro para hacer transacciones o establecer comunicacin, mediante mensajes de texto, con instituciones bancarias. Son, por lo tanto, un medio ideal para acelerar la inclusin financiera y para que los bancos ofrezcan, a travs de los telfonos celulares o mviles, canales de acceso a los servicios financieros en especial a personas de bajos recursos o que viven en localidades apartadas. Tomemos en cuenta que mientras existen, como ya he dicho, unas 85 millones de lneas de telefona mvil en Mxico se estima que slo hay alrededor de 30 millones de cuentas bancarias corrientes. Para el Banco de Mxico es crucial que exista una mayor participacin de los servicios financieros en todo el pas y para toda la poblacin. Por qu? En primer lugar porque, junto con el mandato prioritario a favor de la estabilidad de precios, la ley nos ha encomendado promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero, as como el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. 2 En segundo lugar porque una mayor inclusin financiera redunda en un mejor funcionamiento de los mercados y del sistema en su conjunto, contribuye a reducir las asimetras en materia de informacin para los usuarios y facilita, en fin, que la libre competencia entre los bancos se traduzca en costos ms bajos y mejores productos para los consumidores de servicios financieros. De ah que el Banco de Mxico haya participado decididamente, y dentro del mbito de sus facultades, en esta estrategia de simplificacin regulatoria. No me cabe duda que este esfuerzo dejar allanado el terreno para el desarrollo de todo el potencial que, merced a los avances tecnolgicos, puede alcanzar la banca mvil en Mxico. En concreto, el Banco Central es el regulador competente para determinar las caractersticas de las operaciones pasivas de la banca. Por eso, el pasado 17 de junio el Banco de Mxico emiti la circular 14/2011 para la banca mltiple y el 7 de julio emiti la circular 1/2006 Bis 41 para la banca de desarrollo, en las que se reconocen cuatro tipos de cuentas de captacin propicias para fomentar el acceso a los servicios financieros y su uso continuo con muy pocos requisitos regulatorios en cuanto a informacin y monitoreo de las mismas cuentas. Una vez establecido este marco, la Secretara de Hacienda est en posibilidad de emitir las disposiciones relativas sobre todo en materia de prevencin y combate al lavado de dinero y al financiamiento del terrorismo; al tiempo que la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores podr ejercer la regulacin que le compete 3 en materia de banca electrnica y de comisionistas bancarios, entre los cuales quedarn incluidas las empresas de telecomunicaciones. Conviene llamar la atencin sobre el esquema lgico que se sigui para identificar y disear estos cuatro tipos de cuentas: a menor capacidad transaccional de las cuentas corresponde un menor riesgo de operaciones ilegtimas y son menores los requisitos de informacin y monitoreo. Esto posibilita ofrecer productos financieros bsicos  cuentas de captacin con montos y modalidades de uso ms o menos restringidas de acuerdo con el tipo de cuenta- al acceso de cualquier persona en prcticamente cualquier sitio de la Repblica Mexicana. Adems de esta simplificacin regulatoria, se consolida una respuesta idnea a la necesidad de fomentar el dinero electrnico vinculado a los telfonos mviles, todo ello centrado en el sistema bancario. Con este marco de regulacin se da seguridad a los recursos que destinan los usuarios a estos novedosos mecanismos, pues quedarn resguardados por toda la regulacin prudencial del sistema bancario y entonces calificarn para la proteccin del IPAB. Los intereses del pblico quedan plenamente garantizados porque los pagos realizados a travs de telfonos mviles y otros medios electrnicos estarn sentados sobre las bases del sistema bancario, y ello les da a los usuarios todos los beneficios de la regulacin que emite el Banco Central acerca de transparencia en caractersticas y costos, la aplicacin de las reglas relativas al combate al lavado de dinero y financiamiento al terrorismo, as como el uso de sistemas 4 de pagos robustos, bien regulados y supervisados, en los que se prev el carcter definitivo de los pagos. De esta forma, se est dando una respuesta idnea y creativa al gran desafo que representa la necesidad de aumentar la inclusin financiera. Es, en suma, un gran impulso para que el sistema bancario mexicano desarrolle todo su potencial. Una oportunidad de integrar al sistema financiero en un plazo relativamente corto a decenas de millones de personas que hoy no tienen acceso a l. Una oportunidad, en fin, que no podemos ni debemos desaprovechar. Muchas gracias. 5

Title: Inauguration of the XI Conference on Financial Education and Inclusion for Latin America and the Caribbean/CEMLABanco de Mxico
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the inauguration of the XI Conference on Education and Financial Inclusion for Latin America and the Caribbean / CEMLA - Bank of Mexico. November 20, 2019 Manuel Ramos Francia, Director of the Center for Latin American Studies; Jessica Serrano, Director of Financial Education and Cultural Development at the Bank of Mexico; Distinguished and distinguished participants of this Seminar; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 It is an honor to participate in the inauguration of this Eleventh Conference on Financial Education and Inclusion for Latin America and the Caribbean, organized by CEMLA and the Bank of Mexico. For almost seven decades, CEMLA has been the multilateral organization that has channeled cooperation between the central banks of the region and has contributed, in an invaluable way, to identifying and solving common challenges. This Conference is a magnificent opportunity to, together with the prestigious experts convened, exchange ideas and experiences on a core issue for our countries. Indeed, inclusion and financial education are two notions that, although they have independent elements, are closely interrelated and are decisive for protecting the well-being of individuals and promoting the development of nations. I. Financial Inclusion and Education: Simultaneous Needs It is widely known that financial inclusion can more effectively meet the basic economic needs of every individual, 2 such as: i) transferring values in a safe, agile and cheap way; (ii) manage liquidity flows in an orderly and safe manner; iii) deal with unforeseen events with mechanisms such as credit or insurance and iv) achieve long-term goals with effective planning, savings and capitalization mechanisms. Despite the tangible advantages of financial inclusion, its progress has been insufficient in most countries in our region. Certainly, problems remain such as the lack of infrastructure in remote locations, or regulatory limitations for the expansion of correspondent networks, or the scarcity of relevant supply by intermediaries for certain social strata. However, even though in some cases access problems are overcome, significant lags in the use of financial services persist. In particular, in surveys on the use of financial services, one of the most frequent reasons why citizens in emerging economies do not seek access to financial services has to do with a lack of skills and 3 information on this subject, as well as with deep-rooted behavioral biases. Thus, it is clear that education and access to financial services are elements that reinforce or weaken each other, so both strategies must be promoted simultaneously and harmoniously. Thus, inclusion and financial education are processes that, when provided in a coordinated manner, result in greater tangible benefits for the individual and society. On the side of the individual, inclusion and financial education are an imperative of justice and equity, since they allow them to access more effective mechanisms to enhance their savings or investment operations, as well as having greater support to respond to eventualities or channel their initiative and talent. In terms of benefits to society, greater inclusion and financial education contribute to the efficiency of the financial system, which is the most effective resource allocation mechanism in modern societies. Thus, the broader the financial inclusion 4 among the population, the resources available to a country can be better used. II. The role of technology in reducing the lags of inclusion and financial education Until a few years ago, geographical dispersion and the prohibitive costs of operating on a small scale made it unfeasible for formal financial services to spread to certain places or social strata. This condemned significant sectors of the population to lack these services or to resort to informal instances, which are generally more expensive and less secure. However, today there are tools to bridge the gap and address the lags in terms of inclusion and financial education. Technology can break down geographical barriers and lower costs. Technology also makes it possible to design financial services that better fit the needs of different segments of the public. Today, through a smartphone, it is possible to make from the payment of a service to the contracting of a mortgage loan. 5 Also, in addition to traditional intermediaries, new players have emerged that offer specialized or niche services. All this can be beneficial for both the system and the consumer. However, at the same time as opportunities, technological developments generate risks. Therefore, to make the most of opportunities and minimize dangers, it is essential to strengthen both inclusion and financial education, as well as consumer safety and protection and encourage technological development to be channeled in favor of the user. An example of the way in which technology can be used to promote financial inclusion is the platform called Digital Collection (CoDi), which means an evolutionary leap in payments in our country, as well as a great opportunity to expand financial inclusion. Using the infrastructure of the Interbank Electronic Payments System, SPEI, operated by the Bank of Mexico, and with the use of QR and NFC technologies for the realization of electronic payments, the CoDi 6 it allows anyone who has a smartphone and opens a bank account to make electronic payments in seconds, 24 hours a day, free of charge and with the highest security standards. The CoDi implies for its users enormous benefits in terms of cost reduction, security and transparency. To mention a few examples, it has a very positive impact for small businesses that can receive immediate electronic payments; it also promotes the streamlining and simplification of many daily transactions and the reduced possibility of illicit or corruption by generalizing payments that are recorded electronically. Moreover, given that the universe of mobile device users almost doubles that of those who have bank accounts, accessing this platform can encourage the use of other financial services, which can play a key role in inclusion and strengthens the financial system. As of November 15, more than one million forty-seven thousand accounts have been enabled to receive payments by CoDi, carrying out more than 63 thousand operations with more than 34 thousand different recipients of payments for an aggregate amount of 37.1 million pesos. 7 III. Importance of financial inclusion and education for central banks There is a potential virtuous circle between financial inclusion and education and the fulfillment of the typical objectives of a central bank, which are to promote price stability, the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of the payment system. For starters, price stability promotes savings and credit. On the other hand, a healthy financial system, by promoting openness, competition and mobility, is conducive to inclusion. The good performance of the financial system, in turn, allows the public to have infrastructure and open networks to carry out their transactions. Financial inclusion and education also have a positive impact on the work of central banks. Thus, among other benefits, both contribute to a better understanding and transmission of monetary policy; to make the financial system deeper and more competitive and to generate fewer aggregate risks. 8 For central banks, there is a growing need to fully understand the opportunities, interconnections and risks of the new modalities in which financial services can be provided. In particular, the central bank should promote that users achieve the greatest benefits, in a sustainable manner, with quality financial services, on appropriate terms and conditions and with wide coverage. For this, it is essential to maintain the stability and strength of the financial system and promote a regulatory framework that promotes the adoption of new technologies, competition and that protects and empowers users for their better decision-making. All this hand in hand with an offer of financial education that helps to break inertia and behavioral lags. IV. Role of the Bank of Mexico in financial inclusion and education Allow me to refer very briefly to some actions of financial education and inclusion, as well as consumer protection, that the Bank of Mexico has been carrying out. 9 For several years, the central bank has been forming a wide range of outreach and training aimed at the most diverse audiences. Within the Bank's website there is a section called, "BANXICO educa" with attractive and interactive information aimed at children, young people and adults. In addition, a series of calculators have been developed so that the public can know and compare costs of credits, cards and other banking products and services. In addition, extremely useful applications have been established to have all the updated information generated by the bank. Apart from this wide range of dissemination tools, chairs, diplomas and other forms of educational extension have been created to interact with students in secondary and higher education. In addition, Awards have been established, at the baccalaureate and higher education level, which call for essays on a central banking topic and have exercised a great convening power. Moreover, the Bank of Mexico has enthusiastically promoted other initiatives related to financial education and encouraged the creation of a one-of-a-kind project, such as the Interactive Museum of Economics. 10 As a way to complement this educational offer and promote the best conditions of equity, transparency and user protection, the Bank has promoted various measures to strictly safeguard the rights of the consumer and guarantee their mobility. Ladies and gentlemen: It is rare to find areas in which actions can be promoted that transform people's lives, and that in turn entail profound social benefits. This is the case of actions in the field of inclusion and financial education, since they are instruments of progress and economic leveling; they awaken initiatives and capacities in individuals and contribute to breaking vicious circles of marginalization and poverty. That is why I warmly welcome the holding of this Conference and wish you every success in the course of your work. Thanks a lot. 11

Title: 74 Banking Convention
text: 1 Remarks by the Governor of Banco de Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, on the occasion of the 74th Banking Convention, Acapulco, Guerrero. April 7, 2011.  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, teacher Ernesto Cordero Arroyo;  Isabel Trejo Reyes, President of the Finance Committee of the Senate;  Ladies and gentlemen Legislators;  Mr. President of the National Banking and Securities Commission, Doctor Guillermo Babatz Torres;  Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, engineer Ignacio Deschamps Gonzalez; Ladies and gentlemen: Good afternoon. As every year it is a great honor to attend this Banking Convention. This occasion is particularly pleasing because in the last 12 months in macroeconomic matters things have gone well for Mexico, better than expected, and because the outlook for 2011, in terms of inflation and economic growth, is also favorable, although they are not without risks. 1 2 For central banks, a good year is one in which the economy grows beyond expectations and at the same time the inflation rate is lower than expected. So was 2010 for Mexico, despite the complexities prevailing in the global economic environment. A year ago in this same framework of the Banking Convention I pointed out that we were facing a panorama that forced us to qualify optimism with caution. The reason for the caution was that we were then facing unusual events in the international financial markets. Essentially, these disturbing phenomena persist, so that even today we see the future with optimism tempered by prudence. I will try to summarize the main reasons for concern generated by the external environment: 1st. High fiscal vulnerability in several of the developed economies. This risk factor is still present and the strategies and times to overcome it, as well as the mechanisms to mitigate its undesirable effects, have yet to be defined. 2nd. The extremely loose monetary stance by the central banks of advanced economies, which is not 2 3 sustainable over time due to the inflationary risks it raises. The imminent correction of this position could induce a sharp adjustment in external interest rates, reversal of capital that has been channeled to emerging economies and turbulence in international financial markets. 3rd. Global imbalances, which after a cyclical correction have worsened again, could have a negative impact on the growth prospects of the world economy. 4th. In addition, there is great uncertainty about whether the recent recovery in some advanced economies, and in particular in the United States, will be sustainable in the near future once monetary and fiscal stimuli in those economies are reduced. 5th. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and North Africa, the disaster in Japan and weak financial systems in some European countries could also generate turbulence in markets. Finally, 6th. For some emerging countries, the above risks are combined with a strong expansion in spending and with the fact that they have already entered the high phase of their spending cycle. 3 4 business, which means a limitation to be able to continue growing at accelerated rates without increasing inflationary pressures. All this sets up an uncomfortable external environment, as it combines prospects of persistent weakness in developed economies with threats of inflation and overheating in several emerging economies. I return now to the particular case of Mexico during 2010. Any annual balance, whether good or bad, leaves lessons. What happened to inflation in 2010, why did we have to lower our inflation forecasts as the year progressed? There were several factors behind this fact: 1. As foreseen by the Bank of Mexico, the tax and public tariff adjustments that entered into force in 2010 had a one-time effect and their impact on inflation records was transitory. I said a year ago that, given such a forecast, the Governing Board of the Central Bank considered it inadvisable to adjust monetary policy, not only because the increases in inflation would be short-lived, but because the effects of any change in policy 4 5 Monetary occur with several months of lag. Time has proved the monetary policy right: the effects of fiscal and tariff adjustments, in terms of inflation, have completely dissipated since the first month of 2011. 2. On the other hand, the appreciation of the exchange rate was a determining factor in the reduction of inflation, mitigating possible pressures on the prices of tradable goods and the costs of production of those goods and services that use imported inputs. This appreciation was the result of the favorable performance of our external sector, characterized by the great dynamism of exports, both oil and non-oil, and the important capital inflows, especially those channeled to medium and long-term investments in government securities. These capital inflows, in turn, responded both to the good prospects for economic growth in Mexico, as well as to the substantial easing of U.S. monetary policy, which made ours more restrictive in relative terms. The strength of the price of the national currency had a particular influence on the good performance of core inflation. 5 6 3. In addition, while it is true that the Mexican economy grew more than expected, the output gap continued to be negative. This means that GDP is below its potential, that is, in reference to GDP that would be consistent with full employment of factors of production. This gap measures the economy's ability to grow without accelerating inflationary pressures. Undoubtedly, this factor contributed to the fact that the transfer of the increase in taxes and public prices to final prices has been lower than expected. 4. Associated with the above, wage revisions were consistent with a fall in unit labor costs, which favorably impacted inflation of non-tradable goods and services, as well as promoting rapid employment growth. 5. Another factor that contributed during 2010 to lower inflation than we expected at the beginning of the year was that in the Bank of Mexico significant improvements in public information and transparency were consolidated. Communication is a key element in the conduct of a monetary policy such as ours, aimed at anchoring inflation expectations in the medium term. During that year, 2010, the Board 6 7 The Government took particular care to ensure that monetary policy announcements and inflation reports became increasingly clear and analytical. Also last year we announced with opportunity the schedule of communications related to monetary policy to which the Central Bank would adjust and we anticipate that in 2011 we would begin the dissemination of the minutes of the sessions of the Governing Board convened to make monetary policy decisions. All of this has provided financial market participants, analysts and the general public with greater elements of judgment about the factors that Board members weigh in making their decisions. This improvement in the communication strategy of the Bank of Mexico facilitated the adjustment of expectations in the face of a better performance of inflation observed during 2010 itself, which in turn reinforced its favorable behavior. Like the previous year, 2011 is already shaping up to be good in terms of economic growth and inflation control. Indeed, the economy continues to advance at rates. 7 8 in addition to the fact that aggregate demand has been showing a more balanced development. External demand continues with the great dynamism shown since the second half of 2009, but since recent quarters this behavior has been accompanied by a more favorable one of domestic demand: private consumption has consolidated to the extent that employment recovers, while productive investment shows clear signs of reactivation. Inflation, meanwhile, continues to decline, approaching the permanent target of 3 percent per year. As you know, this morning the March inflation data was released, which was 0.19 percent compared to the previous month, which yields an annual headline inflation of 3.04 percent and an annual core inflation of 3.21 percent. However, it is still necessary to temper optimism with caution. Latent risks should not be disregarded. In recent months, some inflation concerns have arisen domestically, mainly due to two elements: the increases in international commodity prices and the likelihood of an accelerated closing of the output gap. That is, that soon the Mexican economy could 8 9 exhaust the capacity it has today to grow rapidly, without accelerating inflation. I think it is necessary to pause to comment on these elements of concern. As far as commodity price rises are concerned, these have so far not been reflected in substantial increases in headline inflation. In fact, its impact on the national consumer price index has been lower than most forecasts anticipated and significantly lower than that observed in other countries. This minor impact in terms of inflation is explained by several factors. On the one hand, in the case of energy, and specifically gasoline, public policy in Mexico in recent years has allowed us to isolate ourselves from the great volatility in international prices, although we should recognize the fiscal costs that the measure represents and the challenges that derive from it. With regard to grain prices, the existence of inventories has mitigated the severity of external shocks in our economy, while the appreciation of the exchange rate has diminished the increases in international prices translated into national currency; no less important is the fact that the specific price increases of some 9 10 agricultural products have been offset by declines in others. Notwithstanding the above, adverse climatic factors and the increase in demand for raw materials and commodities by emerging countries will continue to put pressures on these prices, so we must be vigilant in this regard. The recent reduction in inflation in Mexico is partly attributable to non-core inflation, so it should not be ruled out that there will be a rebound in subsequent months. In this regard, given the possibility of further increases in commodity prices, it would be appropriate to bear in mind the following considerations. As long as attempts continue to be made to raise the prices of primary commodities in response to clearly identifiable exogenous shocks, monetary policy will not have to be modified, since doing so in such circumstances would be a decision that could lead to more costs than benefits, in addition to keeping in mind the lag of several months with which monetary policy adjustments affect inflation. However, if the aforementioned variations in the prices of primary goods begin to affect inflation expectations, thus modifying 10 11 More deeply, the process of price formation in the economy would be appropriate, if a timely and decisive response by the Bank of Mexico would be appropriate. Precisely the margin of variability of plus / minus one percentage point with respect to the permanent inflation target of 3 percent, was established by the Governing Board to put into perspective the deviations that arise from that objective, such as those referring to variations in relative prices of some goods and services. Of course, the existence of such margins of variation at no time should be interpreted as an invitation to laxity or indifference on the part of the Governing Board regarding the relevance of pursuing its permanent objective. The Bank's monetary policy bulletins have been emphatic in this regard. The Governing Board will be very vigilant to detect if the relative price variations of some goods or services, especially agricultural products, have affected the price formation process, in order to, if necessary, act in a timely manner. As for the product gap, it is also worth making some reflections. If we define this gap as the difference 11 12 between current production and the potential that the economy could reach under conditions of full employment, it is obvious that we are talking about a concept that is not directly observable, since potential GDP is not. Although there are widely accepted theoretical models for the estimation of the latter concept, it is well known that the accuracy of these models is lost especially after sudden and unexpected variations in economic growth, as happened in Mexico in 2009. From a practical point of view, this represents the following challenge for the Central Institute: the difficulty of knowing whether the disappearance of the output gap, as traditionally measured, really implies the cancellation of the economy's ability to grow without accelerating inflation. Precisely because of these considerations, the Bank of Mexico complements the diagnosis by studying other indicators. This in order to be able to determine more precisely if the economy is already close to or in full employment. Suitable complementary indicators are the situation in the country's labor market, the performance of financing, the utilization of installed capacity, the behavior of the current account, among others. 12 13 If the analysis of these complementary indicators were carried out in the case of Mexico, it would seem that it is not imminent that during the coming months the Mexican economy will present generalized pressures on prices. Namely: 1st. While it is true that labour employment has been growing at very rapid rates, both the unemployment and underemployment rates remain at levels significantly above those prevailing during 2008, before the crisis. In addition, the different opinion surveys collected by the Central Institute among entrepreneurs indicate that the availability of skilled labor does not represent, for the moment, an impediment for their production to continue increasing. 2nd. Just at the end of last year, the extension of bank credit to families and businesses began to show positive real growth rates, after more than two years of showing the opposite. Hence, one could hardly think that the availability of credit in the foreseeable future will be a bottleneck and a margin of pressure on the costs of companies. Nor is it expected that the foreseeable credit expansion could lead to overheating in the economy on the aggregate demand side. 13 14 3rd. The utilization of installed capacity in the country has not yet recovered to pre-crisis levels in 2008. In fact, this is a possible explanation for the slow recovery of private investment. 4th. Finally, in 2010 we observed one of the smallest current account deficits since 1990, indicating that there is not even a near overflow in the country's aggregate demand. All the above indicators seem to indicate that we are still far from the dynamism of the economy generating, by itself, pressures on core inflation. This, in turn, makes automatic monetary policy responses inadvisable. The observation of all the indicators as a whole shows that the Mexican economy still has enough slack to grow as it has been doing, without generating inflationary pressures for that reason. And it is also for these reasons that I believe that, under the current circumstances, it is foreseeable that the gradual process of convergence of inflation towards the permanent target of 3 per cent will continue. This does not exempt, of course, that the Bank of Mexico remains vigilant and reacts in case the expected phenomena do not materialize. 14 15 Even a scenario in which the output gap does not close as quickly as anticipated should not be ruled out, in light of the uncertainty that exists about the sustainability of the recovery in the United States. In addition to the challenges posed by the increases in commodity prices and the dynamics with which the output gap could be closed, the Bank of Mexico faces a third challenge of great importance: the growing flows of external capital entering the Mexican economy. As I mentioned, exchange rate appreciation has been a relevant factor in reducing inflationary pressures. And the appreciation of the exchange rate has been due, to a large extent, to the flows of external capital invested mainly in government securities. This phenomenon has several facets. On the one hand, these capital inflows represent the favorable perception aroused by the Mexican economy but, on the other, it should not be ignored that a good part of them have been the result of the extraordinarily loose monetary policy implemented by the Federal Reserve of the United States. In particular, since last September the central bank launched liquidity easing 15 16 known as QE2, monetary policy in Mexico was made, de facto and in relation to the external economy that most influences the Mexican economy, more astringent. That is why this factor has helped us, through the appreciation of the exchange rate, to combat inflation. Therefore, the Bank of Mexico must be vigilant about any changes in the Monetary Policy of the Federal Reserve and the impact that such changes, when verified, will have on its relative monetary stance. We all know that for the current good conditions in the Mexican economy to be maintained, even in the event of a sudden or gradual change in U.S. monetary policy, two key strengths must be preserved: first, a sound macroeconomic framework, characterized by prudent fiscal and monetary policies; and, second, a healthy financial system in terms of capitalization, solvency and liquidity. I should also mention that Mexico has accumulated international reserves deliberately and in unprecedented amounts, while negotiating and contracting with the International Monetary Fund a flexible line of credit for an approximate amount of 73 billion dollars for a term extended to 16 17 Two years. These actions are intended to maintain the confidence of domestic and foreign investors, even in light of higher interest rates abroad as a result of a potential tighter monetary policy in the United States. In the same vein, I welcome the establishment of the Financial System Stability Council, in which the Bank of Mexico was invited to participate. As the recent report released by the Council reveals, the Mexican financial system is in an enviable position, since the factors that could lead to systemic risks are currently under control. Rather than boasting about this fact, it seems to me that the authorities and banks should take advantage of it and act accordingly. The position of Mexican banks in terms of capitalization and liquidity, together with a favorable regulatory framework and economic environment, must translate into an increasingly important contribution to the growth of the economy in this and in the coming years. Mexico's banking system is one of the few in the world that has the potential available to drive growth. In other emerging countries, as I already mentioned, the credit cycle is very advanced, in some cases even at the limit of its capacity to 17 18 expansion. Not to mention economies whose banking systems are still in serious trouble. That is why I conclude my speech with this exhortation: let us not waste this opportunity. Both from the structural point of view and for conjunctural reasons, all the conditions seem ready for us to see in the immediate future an extraordinary contribution of the banking system to the development of Mexico. Thanks a lot. 18
text_original: 1 Palabras del Gobernador de Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, con motivo de la 74 Convencin Bancaria, Acapulco, Guerrero. 7 de abril de 2011.  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, maestro Ernesto Cordero Arroyo;  Isabel Trejo Reyes, Presidente de la Comisin de Hacienda de la Cmara de Senadores;  Seoras y seores Legisladores;  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, doctor Guillermo Babatz Torres;  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, ingeniero Ignacio Deschamps Gonzlez; Seoras y seores: Tengan ustedes muy buenas tardes. Como todos los aos es un gran honor acudir a esta Convencin Bancaria. Esta ocasin es particularmente grata porque en los ltimos 12 meses en materia macroeconmica las cosas han ido bien para Mxico, mejor de lo esperado, y porque las perspectivas para 2011, en lo que respecta a la inflacin y el crecimiento econmico, tambin son favorables, aunque no estn exentas de riesgos. 1 2 Para los bancos centrales un buen ao es aqul en el cual la economa crece ms all de lo esperado y al mismo tiempo la tasa de inflacin resulta menor que la prevista. As fue 2010 para Mxico, a pesar de las complejidades prevalecientes en el entorno econmico mundial. Hace un ao en este mismo marco de la Convencin Bancaria seal que estbamos ante un panorama que obligaba a matizar el optimismo con la cautela. La razn de la cautela fue que entonces enfrentbamos hechos inusitados en los mercados financieros internacionales. En lo esencial esos fenmenos inquietantes persisten, de forma que tambin hoy vemos el futuro con optimismo atemperado por la prudencia. Tratar de resumir los principales motivos de preocupacin que genera el entorno externo: 1. Una elevada vulnerabilidad fiscal en varias de las economas desarrolladas. Este factor de riesgo sigue presente y an estn por definirse las estrategias y los tiempos para superarlo, as como los mecanismos para atenuar sus efectos indeseables. 2. La postura monetaria extremadamente laxa por parte de los bancos centrales de economas avanzadas, la cual no es 2 3 sostenible en el tiempo por los riesgos inflacionarios que suscita. La inminente correccin de dicha postura podra inducir un ajuste brusco de las tasas de inters externas, reversin de capitales que se han canalizado a economas emergentes y turbulencia en los mercados financieros internacionales. 3. Los desequilibrios globales, que despus de una correccin cclica han vuelto a agudizarse, podran repercutir negativamente sobre las perspectivas de crecimiento de la economa mundial. 4. Adems, existe la gran incertidumbre sobre si la reciente recuperacin en algunas economas avanzadas, y en particular en Estados Unidos, ser sostenible en el futuro cercano una vez que se reduzcan los estmulos monetarios y fiscales en dichas economas. 5. Las tensiones geopolticas en Medio Oriente y frica del Norte, el desastre en Japn y la debilidad en los sistemas financieros de algunos pases de Europa tambin podran generar turbulencia en los mercados. Por ltimo, 6. Para algunos pases emergentes los riesgos mencionados se combinan con una fuerte expansin del gasto y con el hecho de que ya han entrado a la fase alta de su ciclo de 3 4 negocios, lo cual significa una limitante para poder seguir creciendo a tasas aceleradas sin presiones inflacionarias cada vez mayores. Todo esto configura un entorno externo nada cmodo, pues conjuga perspectivas de persistente debilidad en las economas desarrolladas con amenazas de inflacin y sobrecalentamiento en varias economas emergentes. Regreso ahora al caso particular de Mxico durante 2010. Cualquier balance anual, sea bueno o malo, deja enseanzas. Qu pas con la inflacin en 2010?, por qu tuvimos que reducir nuestras previsiones de inflacin conforme avanzaba el ao? Hubo varios factores detrs de este hecho: 1. Como haba previsto el Banco de Mxico los ajustes tributarios y de tarifas pblicas que entraron en vigor en 2010 tuvieron un efecto de una sola vez y su impacto en los registros de inflacin fue transitorio. Dije hace un ao que, dada tal previsin, la Junta de Gobierno del Banco Central consideraba desaconsejable ajustar la poltica monetaria, no slo porque las alzas en la inflacin seran efmeras, sino porque los efectos de cualquier cambio en la poltica 4 5 monetaria ocurren con varios meses de rezago. El tiempo le ha dado la razn a la poltica monetaria adoptada: los efectos de los ajustes fiscales y de tarifas, en trminos de inflacin, se han disipado por completo desde el primer mes de 2011. 2. Por otro lado, la apreciacin del tipo de cambio fue un factor determinante en el abatimiento de la inflacin, al mitigar las posibles presiones sobre los precios de bienes comerciables y los costos de produccin de aquellos bienes y servicios que utilizan insumos importados. Dicha apreciacin fue el resultado del favorable desempeo de nuestro sector externo, caracterizado por el gran dinamismo de las exportaciones, tanto petroleras como no petroleras, y de las importantes entradas de capital, sobre todo las canalizadas a inversiones de mediano y largo plazo en valores gubernamentales. Dichos influjos de capital, a su vez, respondieron tanto a las buenas perspectivas de crecimiento econmico en Mxico, como tambin al relajamiento sustancial de la poltica monetaria de Estados Unidos, lo cual hizo que, en trminos relativos, la nuestra se convirtiera en ms restrictiva. La fortaleza de la cotizacin de la moneda nacional influy en particular en el buen comportamiento de la inflacin subyacente. 5 6 3. En adicin, si bien es cierto que la economa mexicana creci ms de lo esperado, la brecha del producto contino siendo negativa. Esto significa que el PIB se encuentra por debajo de su potencial, es decir, en referencia al PIB que sera consistente con el pleno empleo de los factores de produccin. Dicha brecha mide la capacidad que tiene la economa de crecer sin acelerar las presiones inflacionarias. Sin duda, este factor contribuy a que el traspaso del aumento en impuestos y precios pblicos a precios finales haya sido menor a lo esperado. 4. Asociado a lo anterior, las revisiones salariales fueron congruentes con una cada en los costos unitarios de la mano de obra, lo cual impact favorablemente la inflacin de los bienes no comerciables y de los servicios, adems de que ha promovido el rpido crecimiento del empleo. 5. Otro factor que coadyuv durante 2010 a una inflacin menor a la que preveamos al principio del ao, fue que en el Banco de Mxico se consolidaron importantes mejoras en materia de informacin pblica y transparencia. La comunicacin es un elemento clave en la conduccin de una poltica monetaria como la nuestra, encaminada al anclaje de las expectativas de inflacin en el mediano plazo. Durante ese ao, 2010, la Junta 6 7 de Gobierno cuid en particular que los anuncios de poltica monetaria y los informes relativos a la inflacin fueran cada vez ms claros y con mayor contenido analtico. Tambin el ao pasado anunciamos con oportunidad el calendario de las comunicaciones relativas a la poltica monetaria al que se ajustara el Banco Central y anticipamos que en 2011 iniciaramos la difusin de las minutas de las sesiones de la Junta de Gobierno convocadas para tomar decisiones de poltica monetaria. Todo esto ha proporcionado a los participantes en los mercados financieros, a los analistas y al pblico en general, mayores elementos de juicio acerca de los factores que ponderan los miembros de la Junta al tomar sus decisiones. Esta mejora en la estrategia de comunicacin del Banco de Mxico facilit el ajuste de expectativas ante un mejor desempeo de la inflacin observada durante el propio 2010, lo que a su vez reforz el comportamiento favorable de sta. Al igual que el ao anterior, 2011 ya se est perfilando para ser bueno en materia de crecimiento econmico y de control de la inflacin. En efecto, la economa sigue avanzando a tasas 7 8 aceleradas, adems de que la demanda agregada ha venido mostrando un desarrollo ms balanceado. La demanda externa contina con el gran dinamismo mostrado desde la segunda mitad de 2009, pero a partir de los ltimos trimestres dicho comportamiento ha venido acompaado por uno ms favorable de la demanda interna: el consumo privado se ha consolidado en la medida que en que se recupera el empleo, a la vez que la inversin productiva muestra claros signos de reactivacin. La inflacin, por su parte, sigue disminuyendo, acercndose al objetivo permanente de 3 por ciento anual. Como ustedes saben, hoy en la maana se dio a conocer el dato de la inflacin de marzo, que fue de 0.19 por ciento respecto del mes anterior, lo que arroja una inflacin general anual de 3.04 por ciento y una inflacin anual subyacente de 3.21 por ciento. Sin embargo, sigue siendo necesario atemperar el optimismo con la cautela. Los riesgos latentes no deben desdearse. En los ltimos meses, en el mbito interno han surgido algunas preocupaciones en materia de inflacin, debido bsicamente a dos elementos: las alzas en los precios internacionales de materias primas y la probabilidad de que se cierre aceleradamente la brecha del producto. Esto es, que pronto la economa mexicana pudiese 8 9 agotar la capacidad que hoy tiene de crecer rpidamente, sin acelerar la inflacin. Considero preciso detenerme a comentar estos elementos de preocupacin. Por lo que hace a las alzas de los precios de las materias primas, hasta el momento stas no se han reflejado en incrementos sustanciales en la inflacin general. De hecho, su repercusin en el ndice nacional de precios al consumidor ha sido menor al que anticipaba la mayora de las previsiones y significativamente menor al observado en otros pases. Este impacto menor en trminos de inflacin se explica por varios factores. Por un lado, en el caso de los energticos, y especficamente de las gasolinas, la poltica pblica en Mxico durante los ltimos aos ha permitido aislarnos de la gran volatilidad en los precios internacionales, aunque habra que reconocer los costos fiscales que la medida representa y los retos que de ello se derivan. Respecto de los precios de los granos, la existencia de inventarios ha mitigado la severidad de los choques externos en nuestra economa, a la vez que la apreciacin del tipo de cambio ha disminuido las alzas de los precios internacionales traducidas a moneda nacional; no menos importante es el hecho de que los incrementos especficos de los precios de algunos 9 10 productos agropecuarios han sido compensados por disminuciones en otros. No obstante lo anterior, factores climticos adversos y el aumento de la demanda de materias primas y productos bsicos por parte de pases emergentes, seguirn imprimiendo presiones sobre dichos precios, por lo que debemos estar vigilantes al respecto. La reduccin reciente de la inflacin en Mxico es atribuible en parte a la inflacin no subyacente, por lo que no debe descartarse que se presente un rebote en meses subsecuentes. Al respecto, ante la posibilidad de aumentos adicionales en los precios de las materias primas, sera pertinente tener presentes las consideraciones siguientes. Mientras se siga tratando de alzas en precios de mercancas primarias en respuesta a choques exgenos claramente identificables, no habr que modificar la poltica monetaria, ya que hacerlo en tales circunstancias sera una decisin que podra provocar ms costos que beneficios, adems de que habra que tener en mente el rezago de varios meses con el que los ajustes de poltica monetaria inciden sobre la inflacin. Sin embargo, si las referidas variaciones en los precios de mercancas primarias comienzan a afectar las expectativas de inflacin, modificando as 10 11 de manera ms profunda el proceso de formacin de precios en la economa, s sera procedente una respuesta oportuna y decidida por parte del Banco de Mxico. Precisamente el margen de variabilidad de ms/menos un punto porcentual con respecto al objetivo permanente de inflacin de 3 por ciento, fue establecido por la Junta de Gobierno para poner en perspectiva las desviaciones que se presenten de dicho objetivo, como las referentes a variaciones en precios relativos de algunos bienes y servicios. Por supuesto, la existencia de tales mrgenes de variacin en ningn momento se debe interpretar como una invitacin a la laxitud o indiferencia por parte de la Junta de Gobierno respecto de la pertinencia de procurar su objetivo permanente. Los boletines de poltica monetaria del Banco han sido enfticos a este respecto. La Junta de Gobierno estar muy vigilante para detectar si las variaciones de precios relativos de algunas mercancas o servicios, sobre todo de productos agropecuarios, han afectado el proceso de formacin de precios, para, de ser el caso, actuar oportunamente. Por lo que hace a la brecha del producto tambin conviene hacer algunas reflexiones. Si definimos esta brecha como la diferencia 11 12 entre la produccin actual y la potencial que podra alcanzar la economa en condiciones de pleno empleo, salta a la vista que estamos hablando de un concepto que no es directamente observable, pues el PIB potencial no lo es. Si bien existen modelos tericos de amplia aceptacin para la estimacin de este ltimo concepto, es bien sabido que la exactitud de esos modelos se pierde sobre todo despus de variaciones bruscas e inesperadas en el crecimiento econmico, tal como sucedi en Mxico en 2009. Desde un punto de vista prctico, esto representa el siguiente reto para el Instituto Central: la dificultad de saber si la desaparicin de la brecha del producto, como tradicionalmente se mide, realmente implica la cancelacin de la capacidad de la economa de crecer sin acelerar la inflacin. Precisamente debido a estas consideraciones, el Banco de Mxico complementa el diagnstico mediante el estudio de otros indicadores. Esto con el objeto de poder determinar con mayor precisin si la economa ya se encuentra cerca de o en pleno empleo. Indicadores complementarios idneos son la situacin en el mercado de trabajo del pas, el desempeo del financiamiento, la utilizacin de la capacidad instalada, el comportamiento de la cuenta corriente, entre otros. 12 13 Si se efectuara el anlisis de estos indicadores complementarios en el caso de Mxico, parecera que no es inminente que durante los prximos meses la economa mexicana presente presiones generalizadas sobre los precios. A saber: 1. Si bien es cierto que el empleo de mano de obra ha venido creciendo a tasas muy aceleradas, tanto la tasa de desempleo como la de subocupacin siguen a niveles significativamente por arriba de los prevalecientes durante 2008, antes de la crisis. Adems, las diferentes encuestas de opinin recabadas por el Instituto Central entre empresarios sealan que la disponibilidad de mano de obra calificada no representa, por el momento, un impedimento para que su produccin contine aumentando. 2. Apenas a finales del ao pasado, la extensin de crdito bancario a las familias y empresas empez a mostrar tasas de crecimiento reales positivas, despus de ms de dos aos de mostrar lo contrario. De ah que difcilmente se podra pensar que la disponibilidad de crdito en el futuro previsible ser un cuello de botella y un margen de presin sobre los costos de las empresas. Tampoco se prev que la expansin de crdito previsible pueda conducir a un sobrecalentamiento en la economa por el lado de la demanda agregada. 13 14 3. La utilizacin de la capacidad instalada en el pas aun no recupera los niveles previos a la crisis de 2008. De hecho esto es una posible explicacin de la lenta recuperacin de la inversin privada. 4. Por ltimo, en 2010 observamos uno de los menores dficit de cuenta corriente desde 1990, lo que indica que no hay un desbordamiento, ni siquiera cercano, de la demanda agregada del pas. Todos los indicadores anteriores parecen sealar que estamos an lejos de que el dinamismo de la economa genere, por s mismo, presiones en la inflacin subyacente. Esto, a su vez, hace desaconsejable respuestas automticas de poltica monetaria. La observacin de todos los indicadores en su conjunto deja ver que la economa mexicana todava tiene holgura suficiente para crecer como lo viene haciendo, sin generar presiones inflacionarias por ese motivo. Y tambin por esas razones considero que, en las circunstancias actuales, sea previsible que contine el proceso gradual de convergencia de la inflacin hacia el objetivo permanente de 3 por ciento. Esto no exime, por supuesto, de que el Banco de Mxico se mantenga pendiente y reaccione en caso de que los fenmenos esperados no se materialicen. 14 15 Incluso no se debera descartar un escenario en que la brecha del producto no se cierre con la celeridad anticipada, a la luz de la incertidumbre que existe sobre la sostenibilidad de la recuperacin en los Estados Unidos. Adems de los desafos que representan las alzas de los precios de materias primas y de la dinmica con la que podra cerrarse la brecha del producto, el Banco de Mxico enfrenta un tercer desafo de gran importancia: los crecientes flujos de capitales externos que ingresan a la economa mexicana. Como ya mencion, la apreciacin del tipo de cambio ha sido un factor relevante para reducir presiones inflacionarias. Y la apreciacin del tipo de cambio ha obedecido, en gran medida, a los flujos de capitales externos invertidos sobre todo en valores gubernamentales. Este fenmeno tiene varias facetas. Por un lado, estos ingresos de capitales representan la favorable percepcin que despierta la economa mexicana pero, por otro, no se debe soslayar que buena parte de ellos han sido consecuencia de la poltica monetaria extraordinariamente laxa implantada por la Reserva Federal de los Estados Unidos. En particular, desde que en septiembre pasado dicho banco central puso en marcha la relajacin de liquidez 15 16 conocida como QE2, la poltica monetaria en Mxico se hizo, de facto y en relacin con la economa externa que ms influye en la economa mexicana, ms astringente. De ah que este factor nos haya ayudado, por la va de la apreciacin del tipo de cambio, a combatir la inflacin. Por lo anterior, el Banco de Mxico debe estar vigilante respecto de cualquier cambio en la poltica monetaria de la Reserva Federal y del impacto que dichos cambios, cuando se verifiquen, tendrn sobre su postura monetaria relativa. Todos sabemos que para que las actuales condiciones bonancibles en la economa mexicana se mantengan, an en la eventualidad de una modificacin, repentina o gradual, en la poltica monetaria de Estados Unidos, es preciso preservar dos fortalezas clave: primero, un marco macroeconmico slido, caracterizado por polticas fiscal y monetarias prudentes; y, segundo, un sistema financiero sano en trminos de capitalizacin, solvencia y liquidez. Tambin debo mencionar que Mxico ha acumulado reservas internacionales deliberadamente y en montos sin precedente, a la vez que negociamos y contratamos con el Fondo Monetario Internacional una lnea de crdito flexible por un monto aproximado de 73 mil millones de dlares a un plazo extendido a 16 17 dos aos. Mediante estas acciones se pretende mantener la confianza de los inversionistas nacionales y extranjeros, aun a la luz de mayores tasas de inters en el exterior producto de una potencial poltica monetaria ms restrictiva en Estados Unidos. En la misma lnea, celebro que se haya constituido el Consejo de Estabilidad del Sistema Financiero, en el que el Banco de Mxico fue invitado a participar. Como revela el reciente Informe difundido por el Consejo, el sistema financiero mexicano est en una envidiable posicin, pues los factores que podran derivar en riesgos sistmicos se encuentran por el momento bajo control. Ms que vanagloriarnos por este hecho, me parece que las autoridades y los bancos debemos aprovecharlo y actuar en consecuencia. La posicin de la banca mexicana en trminos de capitalizacin y liquidez, junto con un marco regulatorio y entorno econmico favorable, debe traducirse en una contribucin cada vez ms importante al crecimiento de la economa en este y en los prximos aos. El sistema bancario mexicano es uno de los pocos en el mundo que tiene potencial disponible para impulsar el crecimiento. En otros pases emergentes, como ya mencion, el ciclo crediticio est muy avanzado, en algunos casos incluso en el lmite de su capacidad de 17 18 expansin. Ello, por no hablar de las economas cuyos sistemas bancarios estn an en serios problemas. De ah que concluya mi intervencin con este exhorto: no desperdiciemos esta oportunidad. Tanto desde el punto de vista estructural como por razones coyunturales, todas las condiciones parecen dispuestas para que veamos en el futuro inmediato una extraordinaria contribucin del sistema bancario al desarrollo de Mxico. Muchas gracias. 18

Title: Payment systems and new technologies
text: Welcoming remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, for the Seminar of the 25th anniversary of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico on "Payment Systems and New Technologies". Mexico City, August 19, 2019. Good morning, everyone. On behalf of the Bank of Mexico and its Governing Board, it is an honor to welcome all of you to the Seminar "Payment Systems and New Technologies." This is the first in a series of seminars to commemorate the Twenty-Fifth Anniversary of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. We appreciate the presence of recognized leaders and experts in the field, who will analyze the challenges and opportunities that new technologies offer to the payments ecosystem, from an international and national point of view. The purpose of the Bank of Mexico is to provide the country's economy with national currency, which must fulfill three basic functions: to serve as a medium of exchange, a unit of account and a store of value. That is why the Constitution gives the Bank of Mexico the priority objective of maintaining the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. The Act also assigns two additional purposes, closely linked to the main objective: (i) to promote the healthy development of the financial system; and (ii) to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. 1 Providing national currency, in our case the peso, involves two fundamental elements. On the one hand, to issue and put into circulation banknotes and coins that constitute a full means of payment, that is, that are widely accepted and free the person who delivers them from the obligation to pay even for their face value; on the other hand, that they constitute a unit of reference for all types of economic transactions, without requiring the physical exchange of banknotes and coins for many of these operations. In this sense, the development of payment systems is fundamental, which make the exchange of flows in national currency more agile and efficient, while facilitating the full incorporation of the entire population into economic activity. The faster, safer, and more imperceptible a payment is, the less friction or costs individuals face in making their transactions, making it easier to make economic decisions. In recent years, technological advances around the world have revolutionized the way people transact their transactions. For example, the internet and the widespread use of telephones 2 Smart and other mobile devices allow multiple transactions to be made remotely and instantly. Having open architectures and access to information allows processing a large amount of data, for example on the financial behavior of customers, and facilitates the development of innovative technological solutions appropriate to the requirements of different types of users in terms of financial and payment services. Technological advances also make it possible to lower entry barriers, promote an environment of greater competition and increase positive network externalities in payment services, with the consequent reduction of costs. This environment has allowed significant productivity gains for financial institutions, which have significantly reduced their operating costs, and improved the agility and quality of their services. This environment has also enabled the emergence of a new type of companies, such as financial technology institutions (Fintech), 3 that exploit the various technological advances and their application in the provision of financial services for specific sectors or niches. The new developments generate a fundamental change in the very conception of the architecture of financial services. If for decades it was considered that the formation of financial conglomerates, even global, was an irreversible trend, technological progress has opened the door to new participants and ways of interacting. All this could lead to more open financial systems, with the participation of new service providers and a scheme where the greatest gains in efficiency are not necessarily within a single institution, but in the interaction of various participants. We could say that just as manufacturing value chains have become more open and competitive, the same could be happening with value chains in the provision of financial services. The possibilities offered by new technologies and their applications in financial services generate important opportunities in 4 terms of competition and coverage. These opportunities differ depending on the level of maturity of the financial markets. Those countries with greater maturity and financial depth often already have: (i) a broad client base receiving financing and services; (ii) easy access to transactional and consumer information; and, (iii) a solid infrastructure capable of generating credits and various services. In this environment, new technologies allow for greater competition and new financial services of greater added value among a population that is already, in general terms, served with financial services. In emerging economies, or with less mature financial systems, new technologies, in addition to promoting more and better services and greater competition, offer the opportunity - as never before in history - to reduce lags in terms of financial inclusion, by inducing a penetration of new services towards the unbanked population. Thus, technological advances in countries like ours can play a crucial factor in equal opportunities, economic growth and social development. 5 Therefore, regulatory authorities in emerging economies face unique challenges and opportunities, at an unprecedented juncture to promote the better adoption of new technologies, for the benefit of both regular users of financial services and those who are not yet banked. This must be achieved within the framework of the responsibilities traditionally held by the financial authorities and in particular the Central Banks. In particular, two major challenges have been faced in recent years. The first concerns financial stability since, in the wake of the 2008-09 financial crisis, policies have been required to strengthen the resilience of the financial system and reduce taxpayers' exposure to potential shocks. The second is related, precisely, to finding the best uses and applications of new information technologies in financial services. 6 Thus, there is a growing need to fully understand the opportunities, interconnections and risks of the new modalities in which financial services can be provided. In particular, the Central Bank should promote that users achieve the greatest benefits, in a sustainable manner, with quality financial services, on appropriate terms and conditions and with wide coverage. For this, it is essential to maintain the stability and strength of the financial system and promote a regulatory framework that promotes the adoption of new technologies, economic competition and that protects and empowers users for their better decision-making. This implies moving away from the approach based on the regulation of institutions and adopting a modular approach, in which activities are regulated according to the risks they represent from a point of view of "same risk same regulation." In addition, regulation must be technologically neutral and must be designed in such a way as to establish an "even floor" for all participants providing the same services. 7 In the effort to create the right regulatory conditions, Central Banks must seek a balance sheet on different fronts: i) innovation and risks; (ii) economies of scale and competition; (iii) efficiency and safety; (iv) standardization and diversity; and finally; v) privacy and efficiency. In a world where new developments come from a large number of providers with different objectives and technologies, Central Banks must promote payment systems that serve as a space conducive to the interaction of different participants. In particular, it is necessary that payment systems enable the attraction of a wide range of participants, the interoperability of services, the reduction of costs, the immediacy in transactions with high security standards and that they consider mechanisms and contingency plans that ensure operational continuity 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Central Banks should encourage the positive externalities associated with payment systems; reduce information asymmetries; internalize network effects by allowing, with clear rules, 8 a wide variety of participants; exploit economies of scale for the benefit of all network users and stimulate an open architecture that benefits the whole of society.
