Title: Stability and economic growth: the role of the central bank
text: STABILITY AND ECONOMIC GROWTH: THE ROLE OF THE CENTRAL BANK Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, at the Meeting of the ITAM Alumni Association, ITAM, May 14, 2010 I want to thank the invitation of Maestro Guillermo Zuniga, president of the ITAM Alumni Association, to share with you, distinguished professionals, some ideas about the role of central banks in the economy and society. It is an honor to be back at this university institution with which I have been attached for a long time as a professor and friend of many of its students. On this occasion, I will address the issue of economic stability and growth, which are social objectives to which every central bank and, in particular, the Bank of Mexico must contribute. I will do so by dividing my presentation into two parts: in the first I will seek to describe how central banks, by taking care of price stability, foster an environment that protects well-being and fosters economic growth. The central message is that the goal of ensuring price stability is both a goal that promotes well-being and growth. In the second part of my presentation I will analyze how by promoting the healthy development of the financial system, central banks further strengthen the conditions necessary for the dynamism of the economy. Price stability and economic growth The basic function of central banks is to issue the currency that serves as legal tender. The use of money as a unit of measurement and storehouse of 1 Reliable value makes it essential that issuing institutes seek to preserve their purchasing power. In our country, the Constitution assigns this responsibility to the Bank of Mexico as a priority objective. Now, the goodness of price stability is an idea clearly accepted by all societies today. Regardless of their income level, citizens know that it is better not to have inflation than to have it. This truth is corroborated every day, without exaggeration, by one's own experience. The ravages of periods of high inflation have been dramatic confirmations of this reality for many Mexicans. Economists have documented in detail the economic and social costs of inflation. This is equivalent to an unlegislated tax on monetary balances, so that by discouraging its use it generates inefficiencies in the allocation of resources. When unexpected, inflation also causes errors in economic decisions and uncertainty that inhibits planning, saving and investment. These and other costs have two implications. First and foremost and contrary to what is sometimes claimed, price stability is a good in itself and can therefore be considered an end. The reason is that inflation is a confiscation of wealth that undermines people's property rights. Unless money is not used even as a contractual reference, inflation can arbitrarily redistribute significant proportions of wealth. This tax especially affects people with less income, who keep a high proportion of their savings in cash. Second, price stability is a prerequisite for economic growth. Avoiding the distortions and insecurity associated with inflation facilitates business creation and investment projects. Empirical studies have confirmed that there is an inverse relationship between inflation and long-term economic growth. In particular, financial instability related to the uncontrolled inflation was largely responsible for the unfavourable economic performance of 2 our country in the last three decades of the last century. This damage is even more evident when the causes of Mexico's disadvantage vis-a-vis economies with high rates of per capita income expansion, such as East Asian countries, are explored.1 This leads us to the conclusion that price stability is beneficial twice: it preserves well-being and promotes development. On the other hand, I am not aware of any empirical studies that show that inflation alone produces benefits. At best, statistical studies conclude that for low inflations, a concept that varies between investigations, the effects may be minor or imperceptible, but they are never favorable. That is why, since 2003, the Bank of Mexico has pursued the objective of seeking annual inflation of 3%. This reference has been considered to be consistent with price stability, after considering the common imperfections of inflation measurement. The imperfections referred to arise from the failure of price indices to capture essential aspects such as improvements in the quality of goods, technological changes and changes in consumption structures, and these omissions skew the measurement of inflation upwards. The inflation target in Mexico refers to the annual variation of the National Consumer Price Index (INPC) and not to that of one of its components, since this general index is the most appropriate indicator to reflect the deterioration of the purchasing power of the currency. The validity of using the general index, for example, instead of the "underlying" is exemplified by the fact that the "non-underlying" component, which contains elements such as fruit and vegetable prices, can most severely affect the lower-income population. 1 For an estimate of the effect of inflation on long-term growth see Barro, Robert J., Determinants of Economic Growth, Cambridge: The MIT Press, 1997 and for an assessment of the effect of instability in Mexico compared to East Asia, see De Gregorio, Jose and Jong-Wha Lee, "Growth and Adjustment in East Asia and Latin America", LAEBA Working Paper No. 17, December 2003. 3 On the other hand, it is well known that lasting price stability requires the support of a sound fiscal position. Growing fiscal imbalances may lead the public to fear that the central bank will finance them in the future and thus betray their commitment to controlling inflation. And it is not an unfounded perception, on the contrary: historical experience shows that in the face of persistent fiscal imbalances, central banks are more pressured to relax their monetary policy, to the detriment of price stability. Indeed, such a situation could complicate perceptions about the future management of monetary policy by some central banks in industrialized nations that currently have high fiscal deficits. To mitigate these risks, in Mexico the Constitution has granted autonomy to the Central Bank so that no authority can force it to grant financing. This is the raison d'etre of autonomy; it is not a privilege of a central bank or its governing board, but a guarantee that the State grants to the users of the national currency that it will not resort to the file of financing deficit expenses through the degradation of the currency and the consequent dispossession of wealth from society. Despite the consensus in favor of stability, the agreement seems minor when considering choosing between two actions that, at times, could seem in conflict: the stabilization of prices and the stabilization of economic activity in the short term. This supposed dilemma is usually expressed by the public through two arguments: first, that combating an outbreak of inflation can cause an economic retraction, and second, that it is possible to stimulate economic activity by accepting higher inflation. Although the dilemma described could arise in the short term, it is possible to minimize and even eliminate it with a prudent monetary policy. First, to be efficient in the short term, monetary policy must be part of a long-term strategy based on public expectations that inflation, on average, will remain low. It 4 it requires a long record of price stability and a great deal of credibility of the commitment to maintain it. Secondly, monetary policy consistent with stability always takes into account the conditions of the economy, in particular the phase of the business cycle. Thus, when the economy has some slack in its productive capacity, monetary policy can be relaxed since the situation contributes to the decline in price dynamism, and the opposite happens when inflationary pressures occur as a result of economic activity exceeding its potential for a sufficient time. This implies that in the face of various macroeconomic shocks, the stabilization of prices and the stabilization of economic activity are not opposed. The monetary policy response described can be theoretically justified. A simple approach is that of monetary rules, inspired by the original contribution of the economist John B. Taylor, according to which the authority adjusts the interest rate responding to deviations of inflation from the target and according to the magnitude of the gap between the economic activity actually carried out and its potential level.2 In this and other formulations, monetary decisions do not seek to induce arbitrary manipulations of economic activity. The fundamental assumption is that monetary policy helps the economy to adapt to various shocks, to return to the path of sustained growth in an environment of long-term price stability. This premise differs profoundly from the purpose of stimulating economic activity by jeopardizing stability. When stability and growth goals are framed as antagonistic, active gains, if they occur, tend to be fleeting. On the contrary, allowing inflation to worsen raises the real costs of future stabilizations. 2 Vease Taylor, John B., "Discretion versus Rules in Practice", Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy, vol. 39, pp. 195-214, 2007. 5 In short, price stability favours growth in the long run and there is no irremediable contradiction between economic growth and inflation control in the short term if monetary policy is conducted autonomously and prudently. Thus, based on the widening of the estimated output gap, the Bank of Mexico was able to lower its benchmark interest rate by 375 basis points during the first seven months of 2009. It did so in a preventive manner by assessing that this slack would allow the decrease in inflation, which effectively occurred at the end of the year at 3.6%. This result must be inscribed in the light of the evolution of inflation in the last decade. While the decline in inflation during that period has been significant, to which the formal adoption of the inflation targeting strategy since 2001 has contributed, annual inflation in recent years has averaged above 4 per cent. In addition, the specialist surveys collected by Banxico reflect medium-term inflation expectations still above 3%. These data pose a challenge to ensure that inflation and inflation expectations converge towards the bank of Mexico's target. It is sometimes claimed that, in the face of this task, it would be preferable to raise the inflation target. This modification faces at least two drawbacks. The first and obvious is that a higher goal would be inconsistent with the notion of price stability as estimated by Banxico itself. The second has to do with the clear risk of loss of credibility on which monetary policy is based. If the target is changed once, the public might validly wonder how many more times in the future the monetary authorities will change the target, turning what was offered as a permanent endeavor into a reference subject to circumstances. 6 Central Bank and Financial Stability The pursuit of price stability is not the only thing central banks do for welfare. In the case of the Bank of Mexico, two complementary legal purposes to its priority objective stand out: to promote the healthy development of the financial system and to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. In the first purpose, Banxico shares with other authorities the task of establishing rules and ensuring that financial intermediaries expand under solid and competitive conditions. In the second, the Bank of Mexico operates and promotes the use of payment systems to make all transactions carried out through intermediaries more efficient. In both functions, it is sought that financial penetration increases and is sustainable so that a greater number of Mexicans benefit from financial services. Empirical evidence reveals that there is a positive association between different measures of "financial depth" and economic development. Although inconclusive, the data suggest that, at least in part, causality can range from the former to the latter.3 In this context, I would like to comment on some lessons from the recent global crisis, the critical manifestation of which was a serious instability of the financial systems of developed nations, which spread to the rest of the world. This volatility took the form of a sudden adjustment in the price of assets and an increase in the perception of risk and, therefore, the aversion associated with it, which caused a large contraction of credit markets and a wide demand for liquidity. The antecedent of the crisis was an excessive adoption of risks by the public, a process in which financial institutions played not only a role as intermediaries but also as significant risk claimants. 3 Vease Levine, Ross, "Finance and Growth: Theory and Evidence" en Philippe Aghion and Steven N. Durlauf, eds., The Handbook of Economic Growth, chapter 12, Elsevier North Holland, 2005. 7 The magnitude of the crisis, whose consequences have not yet been concluded, has highlighted the need to have an objective diagnosis of its causes, in order to carry out the reforms that will reduce the probability of future instabilities and, where appropriate, face them adequately. The financial system is vital to the functioning of any economy and its soundness depends on price stability and vice versa. Hence, central banks have a central role in preserving financial stability. Although it is not possible to have a definitive diagnosis of the crisis, it is not risky to say that it was the result of several factors. Within these elements, some authors have pointed out that certain public measures contributed to shaping an environment conducive to excessive risk-taking. They highlight, for example, the government's "affordable housing" financing targets and low interest rates during the years preceding the U.S. debacle. Regardless of the validity of this diagnosis, the widespread failure of supervisors to detect risks is striking.4 As you know, the response of the authorities of the countries affected by the crisis has been firm. Other measures have included unprecedented fiscal and monetary policy actions to provide liquidity, promote the normalization of credit operations and mitigate recessionary effects. The large monetary and fiscal expansion carried out in the United States and other advanced nations poses the challenge of a timely strategy of withdrawing such stimuli. It should be done to prevent possible inflationary pressures and not to unduly pressure interest rates in the future. Considering the above, at least two major lessons can be drawn from the recent crisis. On the one hand, it is essential to ensure that economic policy does not create incentives for over-indebtedness and, on the other, there must be an adequate framework for the regulation and supervision of the system and of financial intermediaries. In this second aspect, the international agenda has incorporated proposals for changes in the 4 See, for example, Taylor, John B. Getting Off Track, Hoover Institution Press, 2009. 8 regulations and the supervisory architecture. In particular, amendments to the institutions' capital, liquidity and pre-emptive reserve requirements are envisaged, as well as procedures for greater transparency on risk exposure. In addition, the mechanisms for providing liquidity to solvent institutions and for expeditious resolution of insolvent institutions, especially those considered "too big to fail", are reviewed in order to mitigate the "moral hazard" and, at the same time, promote the continuation of the operation of the markets even in critical situations. Finally, Mexico did not face notable problems with financial institutions, so it was possible to maintain a prudent fiscal and monetary stance. The absence of serious complications reflects, to a large extent, some direct or indirect benefits of the crisis of the mid-nineties. Three elements stand out: first, better financial regulation and supervision, for example, rules on capitalization and foreign currency operations of banks; second, the application of sound business models by intermediaries, for example, lower-risk mortgage credit products; and third, the still incipient development in Mexico of some sophisticated financial products, which were the conduit for much of the risk overexposure in developed nations. As a consequence, the Bank of Mexico did not have to expand its balance sheet as the central banks of those countries did and the fiscal authority, far from following an excessively expansionary fiscal policy, was able to promote a reform that improved the situation of public finances with an advantage over other nations. While the country has many tasks to do in the area of the financial system, particularly with regard to greater banking, the progress made is a good starting point. 9 Conclusion With the pursuit of price stability, central banks contribute to an environment that protects well-being and promotes economic growth. Even in the short term, there need not be an irremediable conflict between economic growth and inflation control if monetary policy is conducted prudently. Thus, in 2009, the Bank of Mexico was able to lower its reference interest rate by 375 basis points in a preventive manner, by estimating that the slack of the economy would allow inflation to decrease, which indeed happened. However, the challenge remains of achieving convergence of inflation to the 3% inflation target on a permanent basis. On the other hand, by promoting the development of the financial system, central banks further strengthen the conditions necessary for economic dynamism. There is a positive relationship between different measures of "financial depth" and economic development. Mexico faced no problems with financial institutions in the recent global crisis, which largely reflected the drawing on some lessons from the mid-nineties crisis. The resulting progress is a good starting point for the country's remaining financial tasks, such as inclusion in financial services and a healthy expansion of credit to the private sector. 10
text_original: ESTABILIDAD Y CRECIMIENTO ECONOMICO: EL PAPEL DEL BANCO CENTRAL Palabras del Dr. Manuel Snchez Gonzlez, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, en la Reunin de la Asociacin de ex Alumnos del ITAM, ITAM, Mayo 14 de 2010 Quiero agradecer la invitacin del maestro Guillermo Ziga, presidente de la Asociacin de ex Alumnos del ITAM, para compartir con ustedes, distinguidos profesionistas, algunas ideas sobre el papel de los bancos centrales en la economa y la sociedad. Es un honor estar de regreso en esta institucin universitaria con la que he estado unido por largo tiempo como profesor y amigo de muchos de sus estudiantes. En esta ocasin abordar el tema de la estabilidad y el crecimiento econmicos, los cuales son objetivos sociales a los que todo banco central y, en particular, el Banco de Mxico deben contribuir. Lo har dividiendo mi ponencia en dos partes: en la primera buscar describir cmo los bancos centrales al cuidar la estabilidad de los precios propician un entorno que protege el bienestar y fomenta el crecimiento econmico. El mensaje central es que el objetivo de procurar la estabilidad de los precios es a la vez un objetivo que favorece el bienestar y el crecimiento. En la segunda parte de mi exposicin analizar la forma en que al promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero los bancos centrales fortalecen adicionalmente las condiciones necesarias para el dinamismo de la economa. Estabilidad de precios y crecimiento econmico La funcin bsica de los bancos centrales es emitir la moneda que sirve de curso legal. La utilizacin del dinero como unidad de medida y almacn de 1 valor confiables hace indispensable que los institutos emisores busquen preservar su poder adquisitivo. En nuestro pas la Constitucin asigna al Banco de Mxico esta responsabilidad como objetivo prioritario. Ahora bien, la bondad de la estabilidad de los precios es una idea claramente aceptada por todas las sociedades actuales. Independientemente de su nivel de ingresos, los ciudadanos saben que es mejor no tener inflacin que tenerla. Esta verdad se corrobora todos los das, dicho sea sin exageracin, con la propia experiencia. Los estragos de los perodos de alta inflacin han sido confirmaciones dramticas de esta realidad para muchos mexicanos. Los economistas han documentado con detalle los costos econmicos y sociales de la inflacin. sta equivale a un impuesto no legislado sobre los saldos monetarios, por lo que al desincentivar su uso genera ineficiencias en la asignacin de recursos. Cuando es inesperada, la inflacin provoca adems errores en las decisiones econmicas e incertidumbre que inhibe la planeacin, el ahorro y la inversin. Estos y otros costos tienen dos implicaciones. En primer lugar y contrario a lo que a veces se afirma, la estabilidad de los precios es un bien en s mismo y, por lo tanto, puede considerarse un fin. La razn es que la inflacin es una confiscacin de riqueza que atenta contra los derechos de propiedad de las personas. A menos de que no se use el dinero ni siquiera como referencia contractual, la inflacin puede redistribuir arbitrariamente proporciones significativas de riqueza. Este impuesto afecta en especial a las personas con menos ingreso, las cuales mantienen una elevada proporcin de sus ahorros en efectivo. En segundo lugar, la estabilidad de los precios es un prerrequisito para el crecimiento econmico. Al evitarse las distorsiones y la inseguridad asociadas con la inflacin se facilitan la creacin de negocios y los proyectos de inversin. Los estudios empricos han confirmado que existe una relacin inversa entre inflacin y crecimiento econmico de largo plazo. En particular, la inestabilidad financiera relacionada con el descontrol de la inflacin fue responsable, en una buena parte, del desempeo econmico desfavorable de 2 nuestro pas en las tres ltimas dcadas del siglo pasado. Este dao es an ms evidente cuando se exploran las causas de la desventaja que manifiesta Mxico respecto de las economas con elevadas tasas de expansin del ingreso por habitante, como por ejemplo los pases de Asia del Este.1 Lo anterior nos lleva a la conclusin de que la estabilidad de los precios es benfica por partida doble: preserva el bienestar y favorece el desarrollo. Por otra parte, no conozco algn estudio emprico que demuestre que la inflacin por s misma produzca beneficios. En el mejor de los casos, los estudios estadsticos concluyen que para bajas inflaciones, concepto que vara entre investigaciones, los efectos podran ser menores o imperceptibles, pero nunca son favorables. Por eso, desde 2003 el Banco de Mxico ha perseguido como objetivo procurar una inflacin anual del 3%. Se ha estimado que esta referencia es congruente con la estabilidad de los precios, una vez consideradas las imperfecciones comunes de la medicin de la inflacin. Las imperfecciones referidas surgen al no captar los ndices de precios aspectos esenciales como las mejoras en la calidad de los bienes, los cambios tecnolgicos y las modificaciones en las estructuras de consumo, y estas omisiones sesgan al alza la medicin de inflacin. La meta de inflacin en Mxico se refiere a la variacin anual del ndice Nacional de Precios al Consumidor (INPC) y no a la de uno de sus componentes, ya que este ndice general es el indicador ms adecuado para reflejar el deterioro del poder adquisitivo de la moneda. La validez de usar el ndice general, por ejemplo, en lugar del subyacente se ejemplifica por el hecho de que el componente no subyacente, que contiene elementos como los precios de frutas y verduras, puede afectar de forma ms severa a la poblacin de menos ingresos. 1 Para una estimacin del efecto de la inflacin sobre el crecimiento de largo plazo vase Barro, Robert J., Determinants of Economic Growth, Cambridge: The MIT Press, 1997 y para una evaluacin del efecto de la inestabilidad en Mxico en comparacin con Asia del Este, vase De Gregorio, Jos y Jong-Wha Lee, Growth and Adjustment in East Asia and Latin America, LAEBA Documento de trabajo No. 17, diciembre 2003. 3 Por otra parte, es sabido que una estabilidad de los precios duradera requiere el apoyo de una posicin fiscal solvente. Los desequilibrios fiscales crecientes pueden conducir al pblico a temer que el banco central los financiar en el futuro y traicionar as su compromiso con el control de la inflacin. Y no es una percepcin infundada, por el contrario: la experiencia histrica demuestra que ante persistentes desequilibrios fiscales, los bancos centrales se ven ms presionados para relajar su poltica monetaria, en detrimento de la estabilidad de los precios. Por cierto, una situacin semejante podra complicar la percepcin sobre el futuro manejo de la poltica monetaria de algunos bancos centrales en naciones industrializadas que actualmente tienen elevados dficit fiscales. Para mitigar estos riesgos, en Mxico la Constitucin ha otorgado autonoma al Banco Central por lo que ninguna autoridad puede obligarlo a otorgar financiamiento. Esta es la razn de ser de la autonoma; no se trata de un privilegio de un banco central o de su junta de gobierno, sino de una garanta que el Estado otorga a los usuarios de la moneda nacional de que no recurrir al expediente de financiar gastos deficitarios mediante la degradacin de la moneda y el consecuente despojo de riqueza a la sociedad. A pesar del consenso a favor de la estabilidad, el acuerdo parece menor cuando se plantea elegir entre dos acciones que, en ocasiones, podran parecer en conflicto: la estabilizacin de los precios y la estabilizacin de la actividad econmica en el corto plazo. Este supuesto dilema suele expresarse por el pblico a travs de dos argumentos: primero, que combatir un brote de inflacin puede causar una retraccin econmica, y segundo, que es posible estimular la actividad econmica aceptando una mayor inflacin. Aunque la disyuntiva descrita podra presentarse en el corto plazo, es posible minimizarla e incluso eliminarla con una poltica monetaria prudente. En primer lugar, para ser eficiente en el corto plazo, la poltica monetaria debe ser parte de una estrategia de largo plazo fincada en las expectativas por parte del pblico de que la inflacin, en promedio, se mantendr baja. Ello 4 requiere un rcord largo de estabilidad de los precios y una gran credibilidad del compromiso de mantenerla. En segundo lugar, la poltica monetaria congruente con la estabilidad siempre toma en cuenta las condiciones de la economa, en particular la fase del ciclo econmico. As, cuando la economa presenta cierta holgura respecto de su capacidad productiva, la poltica monetaria puede relajarse ya que la situacin contribuye al descenso del dinamismo de los precios, y sucede lo contrario cuando se presentan presiones inflacionarias como resultado de que la actividad econmica rebasa por suficiente tiempo su potencial. Lo anterior implica que ante diversos choques macroeconmicos, la estabilizacin de los precios y la estabilizacin de la actividad econmica no estn contrapuestas. La respuesta de la poltica monetaria descrita puede justificarse tericamente. Un enfoque sencillo es el de reglas monetarias, inspiradas en la contribucin original del economista John B. Taylor, segn las cuales la autoridad ajusta la tasa de inters respondiendo a desviaciones de inflacin respecto de la meta y segn la magnitud de la brecha entre la actividad econmica efectivamente realizada y su nivel potencial.2 En esta y otras formulaciones, las decisiones monetarias no buscan inducir manipulaciones arbitrarias de la actividad econmica. El supuesto fundamental es que la poltica monetaria ayuda a la economa a adaptarse ante diversas perturbaciones, para retomar la senda del crecimiento sostenido en un ambiente de estabilidad de largo plazo de los precios. Esta premisa difiere profundamente del propsito de estimular la actividad econmica poniendo en peligro la estabilidad. Cuando los objetivos de estabilidad y crecimiento se plantean como antagnicos, las ganancias en actividad, si ocurren, tienden a ser pasajeras. Por el contrario, permitir el agravamiento de la inflacin eleva los costos reales de futuras estabilizaciones. 2 Vase Taylor, John B., Discretion versus Rules in Practice, Carnegie-Rochester Conference Series on Public Policy, vol. 39, pp. 195-214, 2007. 5 En suma, la estabilidad de los precios favorece el crecimiento en el largo plazo y no existe contradiccin irremediable entre crecimiento econmico y control de la inflacin en el corto plazo si la poltica monetaria se conduce con autonoma y prudencia. As, con base en la ampliacin de la brecha estimada del producto, el Banco de Mxico pudo bajar 375 puntos base su tasa de inters de referencia durante los siete primeros meses de 2009. Lo hizo de manera preventiva al evaluar que esta holgura permitira el descenso de la inflacin, lo cual efectivamente ocurri al cerrar el ao en un 3.6%. Este resultado, debe inscribirse a la luz de la evolucin de la inflacin en la pasada dcada. Si bien ha sido importante el descenso de la inflacin durante ese lapso, al que ha contribuido la adopcin formal de la estrategia de objetivos de inflacin desde 2001, la inflacin anual de los ltimos aos se ha ubicado en promedio por encima del 4%. Adems, las encuestas de especialistas recabadas por Banxico reflejan expectativas de inflacin de mediano plazo an superiores al 3%. Estos datos plantean un desafo para lograr que la inflacin y las expectativas de la misma converjan hacia la meta del Banco de Mxico. En ocasiones se afirma que, en presencia de esta tarea, sera preferible elevar la meta de inflacin. Esta modificacin enfrenta por lo menos dos inconvenientes. El primero y obvio es que una meta mayor sera incongruente con la nocin de estabilidad de los precios segn la ha estimado el propio Banxico. El segundo tiene que ver con el claro riesgo de prdida de la credibilidad sobre la cual se sustenta la poltica monetaria. Si se modifica una vez la meta, el pblico podra vlidamente preguntarse cuntas veces ms en el futuro las autoridades monetarias cambiarn la meta, convirtiendo lo que se ofreci como empeo permanente en una referencia sujeta a las circunstancias. 6 Banco central y estabilidad financiera La bsqueda de la estabilidad de los precios no es lo nico que hacen los bancos centrales a favor del bienestar. En el caso del Banco de Mxico, destacan dos finalidades legales complementarias a su objetivo prioritario: promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. En la primera finalidad, Banxico comparte con otras autoridades la tarea de establecer reglas y vigilar que los intermediarios financieros se expandan en condiciones slidas y de competencia. En la segunda, el Banco de Mxico opera y promueve el uso de los sistemas de pagos para hacer ms eficiente todas las transacciones que se realizan mediante intermediarios. En ambas funciones, se busca que la penetracin financiera aumente y sea sostenible a fin de que un mayor nmero de mexicanos se beneficie de los servicios financieros. La evidencia emprica revela que existe una asociacin positiva entre las diferentes mediciones de profundidad financiera y el desarrollo econmico. Aunque no son concluyentes, los datos sugieren que, por lo menos en parte, la causalidad puede ir de la primera al segundo.3 En este contexto, me gustara comentar sobre algunas lecciones de la reciente crisis global, cuya manifestacin crtica fue una grave inestabilidad de los sistemas financieros de las naciones desarrolladas, que se contagi al resto del mundo. Esta volatilidad tom la forma de un sbito ajuste en el precio de los activos y una elevacin de la percepcin del riesgo y, por lo tanto, de la aversin asociada al mismo, lo que provoc una gran contraccin de los mercados crediticios y una amplia demanda de liquidez. El antecedente de la crisis fue una adopcin excesiva de riesgos por parte del pblico, proceso en el que las instituciones financieras jugaron no slo un papel de intermediarios sino tambin de demandantes significativos de riesgo. 3 Vase Levine, Ross, Finance and Growth: Theory and Evidence en Philippe Aghion and Steven N. Durlauf, eds., The Handbook of Economic Growth, chapter 12, Elsevier North Holland, 2005. 7 La magnitud de la crisis, cuyas secuelas an no concluyen, ha puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de contar con un diagnstico objetivo de sus causas, para realizar las reformas que permitan reducir la probabilidad de futuras inestabilidades y, en su caso, enfrentarlas adecuadamente. El sistema financiero es vital para el funcionamiento de cualquier economa y su solidez depende de la estabilidad de precios y viceversa. De ah que los bancos centrales tengan un papel central para preservar la estabilidad financiera. Si bien no es posible contar con un diagnstico definitivo de la crisis, no es arriesgado afirmar que fue resultado de varios factores. Dentro de estos elementos algunos autores han sealado que ciertas medidas pblicas contribuyeron a configurar un ambiente propicio para la toma excesiva de riesgos. Destacan, por ejemplo, las metas gubernamentales de financiamiento de vivienda asequible y las bajas tasas de inters durante los aos precedentes a la debacle en Estados Unidos. Independientemente de la validez de este diagnstico, llama la atencin la falla generalizada en la deteccin de riesgos por parte de los supervisores.4 Como saben, la respuesta de las autoridades de los pases afectados por la crisis ha sido firme. Entre otras medidas, se han incluido acciones de poltica fiscal y monetaria sin precedente para proveer liquidez, propiciar la normalizacin de las operaciones crediticias y mitigar los efectos recesivos. La gran expansin monetaria y fiscal llevada a cabo en Estados Unidos y otras naciones avanzadas plantea el reto de una estrategia oportuna de retiro de tales estmulos. Deber realizarse para prevenir posibles presiones inflacionarias y no presionar indebidamente las tasas de inters en el futuro. Considerando lo anterior, por lo menos dos grandes lecciones pueden desprenderse de la crisis reciente. Por una parte, es esencial asegurar que la poltica econmica no genere incentivos para el sobreendeudamiento y por otra, debe contarse con un marco adecuado de regulacin y supervisin del sistema y de los intermediarios financieros. En esta segunda vertiente la agenda internacional ha incorporado propuestas de cambios en las 4 Vase por ejemplo, Taylor, John B. Getting Off Track, Hoover Institution Press, 2009. 8 regulaciones y la arquitectura de supervisin. En particular, se contemplan modificaciones de los requisitos de capital, liquidez y reservas preventivas de las instituciones, as como procedimientos de mayor transparencia sobre la exposicin a riesgos. Se revisan, adems, los mecanismos de provisin de liquidez a las instituciones solventes y de resolucin expedita de las insolventes, sobre todo las consideradas demasiado grandes para quebrar, esto con el fin de mitigar el riesgo moral y, al mismo tiempo, propiciar la continuacin de la operacin de los mercados an en situaciones crticas. Finalmente, Mxico no enfrent problemas notables con las instituciones financieras, por lo que fue posible mantener una postura fiscal y monetaria prudente. La ausencia de graves complicaciones refleja, en gran medida, algunos beneficios directos o indirectos de la crisis de mediados de los noventa. Sobresalen tres elementos: primero, la mejor regulacin y supervisin financiera, por ejemplo, reglas de capitalizacin y de operaciones en moneda extranjera de los bancos; segundo, la aplicacin de sanos modelos de negocio por parte de los intermediarios, por ejemplo, productos de crdito hipotecario de menor riesgo; y tercero, el an incipiente desarrollo en Mxico de algunos productos financieros sofisticados, que fueron el conducto de gran parte de la sobreexposicin al riesgo en las naciones desarrolladas. Como consecuencia, el Banco de Mxico no tuvo que ampliar su balance como lo hicieron los bancos centrales de esos pases y la autoridad fiscal, lejos seguir una poltica fiscal excesivamente expansiva, pudo promover una reforma que mejor la situacin de las finanzas pblicas con ventaja respecto de otras naciones. Si bien el pas tiene muchas tareas pendientes en el mbito del sistema financiero, en particular con relacin a una mayor bancarizacin, los avances alcanzados son un buen punto de partida. 9 Conclusin Con la bsqueda de la estabilidad de precios los bancos centrales contribuyen a propiciar un ambiente que protege el bienestar y promueve el crecimiento econmico. Aun en el corto plazo no tiene por qu existir un conflicto irremediable entre el crecimiento econmico y el control de la inflacin si la poltica monetaria se conduce prudentemente. As, en 2009, el Banco de Mxico pudo bajar 375 puntos base su tasa de inters de referencia de manera preventiva, al estimar que la holgura de la economa permitira el descenso de la inflacin, lo cual efectivamente ocurri. No obstante, persiste el desafo de lograr la convergencia de la inflacin a la meta de inflacin del 3% de forma permanente. Por otra parte, al promover el desarrollo del sistema financiero, los bancos centrales fortalecen adicionalmente las condiciones necesarias para el dinamismo econmico. Existe una relacin positiva entre las diferentes mediciones de profundidad financiera y el desarrollo econmico. Mxico no enfrent problemas con las instituciones financieras en la reciente crisis global, lo que en gran medida reflej el aprovechamiento de algunas lecciones de la crisis de mediados de los noventa. Los resultantes avances constituyen un buen punto de partida para las tareas pendientes del pas en materia financiera, como es la inclusin en los servicios financieros y una sana expansin del crdito al sector privado. 10

Title: Inauguration of the sixth edition of the National Financial Education Week
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the inauguration of the sixth edition of the National Financial Education Week. September 23, 2013, Mexico City.  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso,  Mr. Secretary of Public Education, Dr. Emilio Chuayffet Chemor,  Mr. Head of Government of the Federal District, Dr. Miguel Angel Mancera,  Mr. President of the National Commission for the Protection and Defense of Users of Financial Services, Mr. Mario Alberto Di Constanzo Armenta,  Mr. Head of Delegation of Iztapalapa, Mr. Jesus Valencia Guzman,  Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, and representative in this ceremony of the whole 1 of financial institutions in the country, Javier Arrigunaga Gomez del Campo,  Distinguished members of the presidium, presidents and directors of institutions, regulatory agencies, public bodies, banks and trade associations of the Mexican financial system,  Representatives of the media,  Ladies and gentlemen Good morning. I am honored to be present again at another annual edition of National Financial Education Week. And it is also a source of great satisfaction to see how much progress we have made in Mexico in this important task in just a few years. On previous occasions I have had the opportunity to list several of the many financial outreach, linkage and education tasks that the Bank of Mexico has carried out and is undertaking. Today I would like to refer, in addition, to the way in which our Bank 2 Central contributes to providing an adequate framework for users of financial services to make increasingly sound decisions, for their own benefit and for the better functioning of the financial system as a whole. I will also refer, if only in a specific aspect, to how much the Financial Reform, already approved by the Chamber of Deputies, could contribute in the same sense. For a financial system to function properly, in addition to prudential supervision and regulation, users are required to have the capacity and tools to make sound decisions in the use and choice of financial products and services. How to achieve this? First, with a good understanding of financial practices and how financial services and products can meet the specific needs of users in terms of savings, investment, credit, insurance and means of payment, among others. 3 It is clear that timely and transparent information is key to achieving this good understanding. Users need to know which intermediaries have the services that meet their needs and also need to identify who are the best, in terms of quality, price and availability, among those intermediaries. Assuming all of the above, that is: that people already have such information, it is also necessary to be offered the greatest possible mobility from one intermediary to another or to other intermediaries, so that the user can optimally take advantage of the market opportunities that arise from greater competition on an even or level playing field. The construction of this set of elements: formal financial instruction, comprehensive and timely information and facilitating the mobility of users to choose the best options, I reiterate, not only results in a greater well-being of the individual user but in a better functioning of the financial system as a whole. In this way, by making better decisions, the consumer of financial services and products generates a collective benefit, even greater than 4 the sum of individual benefits, because it contributes to making the financial system as a whole more competitive and efficient. There are many reasons to welcome the Financial Reform, but for the moment I would like to highlight only what the Reform contemplates to facilitate the mobility of users of the financial system, because I am convinced that by forcefully encouraging users of the financial system to move unhindered from one intermediary to another, as it suits their interests, financial reform will generate strong incentives both for greater competition in financial markets and also to stimulate a much greater interest of Mexicans in acquiring a solid financial education. Thanks to greater mobility, the user's effort to obtain more and better information about financial products and services will be rewarded immediately. If one analyses the proposed financial reform as a whole, one will find a common thread in terms of mobility: thus, from different angles and in different legal systems, 5 it is promoting a basic mechanism that will make it possible to break down many of the barriers that still exist for mobility. This basic mechanism, at the same time simple and forceful, consists of granting the clients of the financial system all the facilities so that, in case of agreeing to them, they change their credits or their deposits or investments from one institution to another, without the user having to assume cumbersome, time-consuming and discouraging procedures, since it will be the financial institution that leaves the user responsible for the cancellation of the old contracts and the new one. receiving entity is responsible for carrying out all the necessary procedures before the entity with which the client has decided to terminate the contractual relationship. All this, in addition, in peremptory terms, such as three working days, for example, in the case of consumer credits, and only the express request of the client is enough to make the change of Institution. I have no doubt that these provisions, if approved by the H. Congress of the Union, will provoke: 1. A powerful stimulus to competition between intermediaries to offer 6 the best rates, the best conditions and the best treatment of customers and 2. A growing interest of users to take advantage of these opportunities - which will tangibly benefit their assets - through greater information and greater knowledge about the advantages, limitations and characteristics of financial products and services. That is: a formidable complement to financial education, which should stimulate the interest of the entire population to deepen it. By the way, as you all know, promoting the healthy development of the financial system is one of the missions that the Constitution orders the Bank of Mexico. In accordance with this mandate and with the different legal provisions that concern the Central Bank, it has focused on complementing financial education in several aspects, of which I highlight four here: 1. The regulation of commissions, interest rates and, in short, any other concept of collection of the operations concluded by financial institutions with their customers. 2. The issuance of rules that prohibit or limit those practices that detract from the clarity and transparency of the 7 operations that are carried out in the financial markets. 3. Generate, regularly and in a timely manner, accurate information on financial intermediaries, interest rates and commissions in force in different segments of the financial markets, which guide users for better decision making, and 4. Promote greater competition in the financial system, for the benefit of users. This translates for the Central Institute, day by day, into tasks aimed at the protection of the consumer of financial products and services as well as the generation of the greatest possible transparency in the information related to commissions, charges, rights of users, conditions of competition and availability of financial services and products. Without pretending to be exhaustive, here are some of the measures that the Bank of Mexico has taken in recent years in this regard: In terms of consumer protection, the Bank of Mexico designed basic deposit and savings products, accounts 8 basic both payroll and personal, for which no commission can be charged to users. These basic accounts are associated with the following services, for which no commission can be charged: opening and maintaining the account; granting of a debit card; crediting resources to the account by any means; unlimited withdrawals and consultations at own ATMs; payment of goods and services by debit card and direct debit services. Likewise, the Bank of Mexico regulated the minimum payment in credit cards, to avoid negative amortizations and ensuring that the debt is paid in a reasonable time, no longer in endless terms. In terms of transparency, the Bank of Mexico has issued the following provisions:  At ATMs, the fees to be charged must be clearly disclosed on the screen and the collection of fees on withdrawals and inquiries at own ATMs is prohibited.  The Bank of Mexico periodically publishes reports of basic credit card and credit card indicators for the acquisition of automobiles. 9  Once every six months, in April and October, banks must publish comparative tables on credit card statements, so that the user knows the costs charged by other institutions for similar products. In this area, the participation of CONDUSEF stands out, which has been decisive.  Since 2009 the Total Annual Cost or CAT formula was established that incorporates all the costs that the credit applicant cannot avoid allowing a homogeneous basis of comparison between products and between institutions, which facilitates the best decision making for the user. In addition, the Bank of Mexico published last May its first study evaluating the credit card issuance market in Mexico. The study analyses not only possible barriers to entry, but also the profitability and concentration of markets, as well as the diversity of competition instruments, and issues certain recommendations. In the near future, the Bank will publish similar studies on competition in the credit market for small and medium-sized enterprises, for the 10 acquisition of automobiles, and payroll and personnel credits, among others. Ladies and gentlemen: The country's various financial authorities have made substantial progress in recent years in strengthening the financial system. This also results in greater incentives to promote financial education and a growing interest of users to learn more about the different ways in which the financial system can benefit them. However, we are still a long way from our financial system benefiting the vast majority of Mexicans on a daily basis. Millions of compatriots pay a very high opportunity cost due to the low financial penetration and inclusion registered in Mexico. It is both an urgent and most important task to correct this lag and we are at a crucial, perhaps unique, moment to do so. In that sense, the financial reform to come could not be more timely and indispensable. Let's know it, take advantage of it and support it, each one from his field of responsibility. The stakes are high and one of them 11 the best tools to consolidate these efforts is, precisely, financial education. It concerns us all, it benefits us all and for those of us who are here today it is an inescapable commitment. Thanks a lot. 12

Title: Opening remarks at the World Bank's Annual Conference on Development Economics (ABCDE): Productivity, Growth and the Law
text: Opening remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens WORLD BANK ANNUAL CONFERENCE ON DEVELOPMENT ECONOMICS (ABCDE) "Productivity, Growth and Law" June 15, 2015 ? Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso. ? Mr. Senior Vice President and Chief Economist of the World Bank, Kaushik Basu. ? Mr. Vice President for Latin America and the Caribbean of the World Bank, Jorge Familiar. ? Ladies and gentlemen. ? Good morning to all of you. The Bank of Mexico is honored to host, together with the World Bank, this Annual Conference on Development Economics, this year with the theme "Productivity, Growth and Law". This conference, in particular for the theme chosen, seeks to contribute to a greater understanding of the fundamental aspects that affect the promotion of economic growth. It is obvious the relevance of discussing this issue given the international context faced by the economies of the so-called emerging markets and the challenges that arise from this context. Since the second half of the nineties, several emerging market economies began to strengthen their macroeconomic policy frameworks and improve their economic fundamentals. Moreover, for most of the current century these economies faced a favourable external environment. International commodity prices were rising and 1 interest rates in international financial markets were at low levels. The combination of this benign international environment, together with sound macroeconomic policies, resulted in a prolonged period of relatively high growth in many of these economies. However, today the situation has changed and emerging economies face a very difficult external environment. The era of prosperity for these economies, characterized by high commodity prices, low interest rates and ample liquidity in international financial markets, is being reversed. The impacts of this change in trend are beginning to be felt. Economic growth in East Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe has been lower than initially expected. This has led to a general downward revision of the growth outlook. In many of these economies, the recovery in productivity has been weak during the period after the 2009 financial crisis, even in an environment of loose monetary conditions that, in this case, have not translated into a strong boost to private investment. Going forward, it will be paramount for emerging market economies to continue to strengthen their macroeconomic policy frameworks and improve their economic fundamentals. Keeping inflation under control and fiscal discipline are objectives that cannot be ignored. Additionally, the strengthening of the external sector, supporting the implementation of policies such as flexible exchange rate regimes, sustainable external accounts and free capital mobility, among others, is also necessary. However, these same economies must adequately prepare for an environment in which there will no longer be high commodity prices, in which external financing will be 2 relatively scarce and in which, therefore, the impulse derived from the economic growth of the main economies will not be very vigorous. In this sense, the adoption of a broad set of economic and public policy reforms with the purpose of strengthening the institutional and regulatory framework, and providing incentives for the adoption of modern technologies and investment in human and physical capital, are crucial to respond adequately to the challenge of desired growth. The contribution of this conference lies in bringing together both academics and those in charge of the design of public policies, to discuss and learn about the challenges and policy experiences acquired in different parts of the world, as well as to know and disseminate the most recent advances in research in order to expand our understanding of these and other aspects related to economic growth, such as: I. Productivity of Enterprises, II. Human Capital and Skills Training, III. Infrastructure and Growth, IV. Investment Law and Climate, V. Law, Control of Corruption and Efficiency, VI. Access to the Financial System, and VII. Trade, Foreign Direct Investment and Technology. This diversity in the topics analyzed reflects the different points towards which efforts to increase productivity and promote growth should be directed. Mexico, by the way, in recent years has concretized, through a valuable political effort between powers to achieve consensus, a set of structural reforms that address precisely the points I mentioned. Needless to say, our country has not concluded this process of transformation, but is immersed in its most laborious stage, that of implementing these reforms. Some of these reforms aim to correct the functioning of specific markets - such as telecommunications - improve the investment climate in the energy sector, create a flexible labour market, lay the foundations for higher quality. 3 in public education, and strengthening the role of the financial sector in supporting economic growth, among others. These reforms are important steps in the right direction. To the extent that society can track its progress through proper and transparent implementation, positive expectations will be generated, which will contribute to a virtuous circle that will accelerate the beneficial effects of the reforms themselves. There are two aspects that, due to their impact on the general functioning of the economy and on the improvement in the quality of life of people, require special mention: The current context of innovation and accelerated technological changes raises the need to keep up with the generation of high value-added jobs to replace those routine and low productivity, which will tend to disappear. To make the benefits of such transformation reach the population, emerging market economies must act promptly by implementing reforms aimed at boosting human capital development. It is essential to encourage such development to occur from early educational stages and to be as inclusive as possible so that, in addition to increasing the productivity of the economy, it results in a decrease in income inequality through the access of more people to better paid jobs. Without systematic efforts to generalize the creation of specialized human capital, many will be left behind. It is also imperative to strengthen the rule of law. A weak rule of law generates high costs by increasing uncertainty in day-to-day interactions and economic transactions, by inducing a reallocation of private resources to the protection of property and people, and by delaying the administration of justice. Strengthening the rule of law can involve a difficult and gradual process as it involves improvements in both the design of legal provisions and the procedures for enforcing them. However, since the institutional framework permeates every aspect of the daily life of the population, small advances at a sustained pace can accumulate and become an important trigger for growth. 4 I cannot conclude without first thanking the World Bank for its invitation to participate in the organization of this event. In the same way, I also recognize and appreciate the participation of such distinguished panelists and academics and the audience. I am sure that the reflection and discussions that will take place during these two days will generate substantial benefits for all of us. Thanks a lot 5
text_original: Palabras de apertura del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens CONFERENCIA ANUAL DEL BANCO MUNDIAL SOBRE ECONOMA DEL DESARROLLO (ABCDE) Productividad, Crecimiento y Derecho 15 de junio de 2015  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Luis Videgaray Caso.  Seor Vicepresidente Senior y Economista Jefe del Banco Mundial, Kaushik Basu.  Seor Vicepresidente para Latinoamrica y el Caribe del Banco Mundial, Jorge Familiar.  Seoras y seores.  Muy buenos das tengan todos ustedes. Para el Banco de Mxico es un honor ser anfitrin, junto con el Banco Mundial, de esta Conferencia Anual sobre Economa del Desarrollo, este ao con el tema "Productividad, Crecimiento y Derecho". Esta conferencia, en particular por el tema elegido, busca contribuir a una mayor comprensin de los aspectos fundamentales que inciden en la promocin del crecimiento econmico. Es obvia la relevancia que tiene discutir este asunto dado el contexto internacional que enfrentan las economas de los llamados mercados emergentes y los desafos que de dicho contexto se derivan. Desde la segunda mitad de la dcada de los aos noventa, varias economas de mercados emergentes comenzaron el fortalecimiento de sus marcos de poltica macroeconmica y la mejora de sus fundamentos econmicos. Adems, durante la mayor parte del siglo actual estas economas enfrentaron un entorno externo favorable. Los precios internacionales de las materias primas estaban creciendo y 1 las tasas de inters en los mercados financieros internacionales se encontraban en niveles bajos. La combinacin de este ambiente internacional benigno, junto con polticas macroeconmicas slidas, dio por resultado un perodo prolongado de crecimiento relativamente elevado en muchas de estas economas. Sin embargo, hoy la situacin ha cambiado y las economas emergentes enfrentan un entorno externo muy difcil. La era de prosperidad para estas economas, caracterizada por precios elevados de las materias primas, tasas de inters bajas y amplia liquidez en los mercados financieros internacionales, se est revirtiendo. Los impactos de este cambio de tendencia empiezan a sentirse. El crecimiento econmico en Asia Oriental, en Amrica Latina y en Europa Oriental ha sido menor que lo previsto inicialmente. Esto ha llevado a que, en general, se revisen a la baja las perspectivas de crecimiento. En muchas de estas economas la recuperacin de la productividad ha sido dbil durante el periodo despus de la crisis financiera de 2009, an en un entorno de condiciones monetarias laxas que, en este caso, no se han traducido en un fuerte impulso a la inversin privada. Sin duda, hacia adelante ser primordial para las economas de mercados emergentes continuar fortaleciendo sus marcos de poltica macroeconmica y mejorando sus fundamentos econmicos. Mantener la inflacin bajo control y la disciplina fiscal son objetivos que no pueden ser prescindibles. Adicionalmente, el fortalecimiento del sector externo, apoyando la implementacin de polticas tales como regmenes cambiarios flexibles, cuentas externas sostenibles y libre movilidad de capitales, entre otras, tambin es necesario. Sin embargo, estas mismas economas deben prepararse adecuadamente para un entorno en el que ya no habr precios elevados de las materias primas, en el que el financiamiento externo ser 2 relativamente escaso y en el cual, por tanto, el impulso derivado del crecimiento econmico de las principales economas no ser muy vigoroso. En este sentido, la adopcin de un amplio conjunto de reformas econmicas y de polticas pblicas con el propsito de fortalecer el marco institucional y regulatorio, y de proveer incentivos para la adopcin de tecnologas modernas y la inversin en capital humano y fsico, son cruciales para responder adecuadamente al desafo del crecimiento deseado. La contribucin de esta conferencia radica en reunir tanto a acadmicos como a encargados del diseo de polticas pblicas, para discutir y aprender sobre los retos y experiencias de poltica adquiridas en diferentes partes del mundo, as como para conocer y difundir los avances ms recientes en la investigacin con el fin de ampliar nuestra comprensin sobre stos y otros aspectos relacionados con el crecimiento econmico, tales como: I. Productividad de las Empresas, II. Capital Humano y Formacin de Habilidades, III. Infraestructura y Crecimiento, IV. Derecho y Clima de Inversin, V. Derecho, Control de la Corrupcin y Eficiencia, VI. Acceso al Sistema Financiero, y VII. Comercio, Inversin Extranjera Directa y Tecnologa. Esta diversidad en los temas analizados refleja los diferentes puntos hacia donde los esfuerzos para aumentar la productividad y promover el crecimiento deben ser dirigidos. Mxico, por cierto, en los aos recientes ha concretado, mediante un valioso esfuerzo poltico entre poderes para lograr consensos, un conjunto de reformas estructurales que abordan justamente los puntos que mencion. Huelga advertir que nuestro pas no ha concluido este proceso de transformacin, sino que est inmerso en su etapa ms laboriosa, la de implementacin de dichas reformas. Algunas de estas reformas tienen por objeto corregir el funcionamiento de mercados especficos como el de telecomunicaciones, mejorar el clima de inversin en el sector energtico, crear un mercado laboral flexible, establecer las bases para una mayor calidad 3 en la educacin pblica, y fortalecer el papel del sector financiero en apoyo del crecimiento econmico, entre otros. Estas reformas son pasos importantes en la direccin correcta. En la medida en que la sociedad pueda seguir su progreso a travs de una implementacin adecuada y transparente, se generarn expectativas positivas, las cuales contribuirn a un crculo virtuoso que acelerar los efectos benficos de las propias reformas. Hay dos aspectos que, por su impacto en el funcionamiento general de la economa y en la mejora en la calidad de vida de las personas, requieren mencin especial: El contexto actual de innovacin y cambios tecnolgicos acelerados plantea la necesidad de mantenerse al da con la generacin de puestos de trabajo de alto valor agregado para sustituir a aquellos rutinarios y de baja productividad, que tendern a desaparecer. Para hacer que los beneficios de dicha transformacin lleguen a la poblacin, las economas de mercados emergentes deben actuar con prontitud mediante la implementacin de reformas orientadas a impulsar el desarrollo del capital humano. Es imprescindible fomentar que dicho desarrollo se d desde etapas educativas tempranas y que sea lo ms inclusivo posible para que, adems de incrementar la productividad de la economa, resulte en una disminucin de la desigualdad de ingresos a travs del acceso de ms personas a trabajos mejor remunerados. Sin esfuerzos sistemticos para generalizar la creacin de capital humano especializado, muchos quedarn rezagados. Asimismo, es imprescindible fortalecer el estado de derecho. Un estado de derecho dbil genera altos costos al aumentar la incertidumbre en las interacciones cotidianas y en las transacciones econmicas, al inducir una reasignacin de recursos privados a la proteccin de bienes y personas, y al retrasar la administracin de la justicia. El fortalecimiento del estado de derecho puede implicar un proceso difcil y gradual dado que implica mejoras tanto en el diseo de disposiciones legales, como en los procedimientos para hacerlas cumplir. Sin embargo, dado que el marco institucional permea cada aspecto de la vida cotidiana de la poblacin, pequeos avances a paso sostenido pueden acumularse y convertirse en un detonante importante para el crecimiento. 4 No puedo concluir sin antes agradecer la invitacin del Banco Mundial para participar en la organizacin de este evento. Del mismo modo, reconozco y agradezco tambin la participacin de tan distinguidos panelistas y acadmicos y del pblico asistente. Estoy seguro de que la reflexin y las discusiones que se llevarn a cabo durante estos dos das generarn beneficios sustanciales para todos nosotros. Muchas gracias 5

Title: Mexico, business summit
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, at the ninth edition of "Mexico, business summit", Queretaro, Queretaro. October 23, 2011 Good evening, I thank Mr. Miguel Aleman Velasco, president of "Mexico, business summit", for his kind invitation to participate in this opening dinner of the summit. I warmly greet Jose Calzada Rovirosa, Constitutional Governor of this beautiful state of Queretaro, in which so many fundamental events in the history of Mexico have taken place. Distinguished speakers at this summit meeting, ladies and gentlemen, The global crisis that erupted in September 2008 with the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers substantially changed the perception of economic and financial risk in the world. Investors, entrepreneurs, governments, financial authorities around the world now perceive high risks of a global nature where until September 2008, and 1 in the darkest of cases, we saw moderate risks limited to a region, a country or a branch of economic activity. This radical change in the perception of risks generates, in turn, great uncertainty. Today, October 23, the world awaits the definitive answer that the main countries of the European Monetary Union will give to the sovereign debt crisis that this region is going through, as well as to the pollution suffered by the banks and in general the financial system in that continent. There have been important advances in recent times, but not enough to reduce global uncertainty, nor to scare away the fear that at any moment these turbulences will infect the world economy. To this difficult panorama in Europe are added the great dilemmas that the United States faces in fiscal matters, unemployment, over-indebtedness of families and depression of its housing market, which has led to a 2 expectation of very low economic growth in the coming years. Thus, three years away from the most acute point of the crisis, and more than four years after its beginning by the chain of defaults on so-called low-quality mortgages in the United States, uncertainty continues to reign. Not surprisingly, at the recent meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors in Paris, many of us insisted on demanding clear and immediate responses from the European Monetary Union and the United States. While it is true that the serious problems of over-indebtedness of families, banks and governments in most advanced countries generate a huge burden on the possibilities of economic growth, these have been even more affected by the negative effect that the poor management of the crisis has had on expectations. This negative effect that has undermined confidence has caused many profitable investment projects to be postponed, just as families not affected by the crisis prefer to save cautiously instead of making spending commitments that in another environment they would. 3 There is no doubt, then, that the first scale on the long road to a recovery of the pace of growth of the world economy, in a sustained and stable manner, must be that of the restoration of confidence, the generation of basic certainties by the leaders of the advanced economies. Restoring confidence would allow us to enter a virtuous circle: as markets stabilized, risk premiums would fall, leading to higher investment and consumer spending, which in turn would lead to higher economic growth. This, in turn, would tend to improve the health of Public Finances and European banks, which in turn would result in greater confidence in the recovery. This virtuous circle has been observed time and again in the processes of overcoming crises in several emerging countries, including Mexico. But to kick-start this process, it is essential that the authorities take the necessary strong measures, in a timely manner. Strong and bitter medicine yes, but potentially very profitable in the short term by the virtuous process it can trigger. 4 In the meantime, what is the outlook in Mexico? A fact that distinguishes our country is that in recent years, and especially during the government of President Felipe Calderon, a constant in the field of economic policy has been the insistence on generating certainty. A responsible fiscal policy has been sustained, against all odds; a well-regulated and supervised banking system has been maintained, extraordinarily sound and solvent compared to the banking system of many other countries. In this regard, our banking system will be among the first to meet the stricter prudential requirements that the international community has agreed to as a result of the crisis. In turn, the Central Bank has fully exercised its autonomy without departing from the constitutional mandate that orders it to pursue price stability. Even though the recent volatility in international financial markets has been reflected in a depreciation of the national currency, inflation is close to our permanent target of 3 percent, while inflation expectations at all times are anchored below four percent. This is because, 5 from my point of view, that market participants expect an upcoming appreciation of the peso, given the strong fundamentals of the Mexican economy, and that for several years now the transfer of exchange rate movements to prices has been considerably reduced, partly due to the credibility of the inflation targeting scheme implemented by the Bank of Mexico. A comparison that is most illustrative of the progress we have made in Mexico in terms of financial stabilization, and that reflects the responsibility for the fiscal and monetary policies that we have followed, is what we can make between the weighted average term of government debt in Mexico and the same debt for the case of the United States. In 1994, the weighted average term of government debt in pesos in Mexico was 0.63 years (230 days). That same year, 1994, the weighted average term of government debt in the United States was 5.08 years (about 1,854 days). 6 Today, in Mexico, the weighted average term of government debt in pesos is 7.4 years (2,674 days) while the weighted average term of U.S. government debt is 5.2 years (1,898 days). This means that in Mexico we have not only extended that term more than eleven times from 1994 to date, but we have outsold the government debt of the United States in those same terms of term, by more than two years. This comparison certainly reflects the confidence that investors are giving the government of Mexico in macroeconomic management, to the extent that they are willing to entrust their money to it for a period even longer than the term in which they entrust their money to the Government of the United States. And it also reflects the decisive importance of the pension reform initiated in Mexico at the end of the last century, since over time it has created a solid base of long-term institutional investors, which contribute to the stability of the financial system and give certainty to domestic savings. 7 Another international comparison that is eloquent in reference to the fiscal strengths of our country is the following: consider that Mexico's public debt to GDP is approximately 32 percent while in the European Union it is more than 85 percent, with several of its countries above 100 percent, and in the United States that reason will surpass that mark in the coming months. That is, Mexico's public debt-to-GDP ratio is only about a third of that of the United States and Europe. I would like here to acknowledge the H. Chamber of Deputies for having approved last Thursday a Responsible Revenue Law for 2012, with a fiscal deficit target of only 0.4 percent of GDP, which will allow our debt to GDP to continue falling during the coming year. It is precisely with the same commitment to generate and guarantee certainty that has been done in the specific area of national financial markets through multiple reforms. I will not dwell on the details of these, but I do consider it necessary to highlight what concerns the 8 changes, given the concerns that, for reasons of historical memory, this issue usually causes. ? The peso has become one of the few currencies of emerging countries that operates continuously 24 hours a day, which gives it great liquidity. ? Today the Mexican peso occupies the 13th place among the most traded currencies in the world, which places us, within the emerging countries, only below Korea and Singapore. ? The bid-sell spreads in the interbank markets are comparable to those observed in the main currencies of the world: dollar, yen, euro or pound sterling. ? Most foreign exchange operations are carried out today through electronic platforms, ensuring greater transparency in the price formation process and in the ability to execute. The decisive factor behind all these advances has been the free floating of weight since the end of 1994. 9 The sporadic interventions of the Bank of Mexico in the foreign exchange market have generally occurred under predefined rules, transparent and known in advance by all participants. In addition, our interventions have been made mainly with a single objective: to guarantee the orderly functioning of the market, trying to avoid generating situations of illiquidity that lead to excessive volatility in the price of the national currency. This implies that for many years the country's financial authorities have stopped intervening in the foreign exchange market by pursuing a specific level of the exchange rate. Our thesis has been that the only way to guarantee an adequate and stable level of exchange rate parity is to keep the fundamentals of our economy healthy. And this is precisely what we have dedicated ourselves to in recent years both the Federal Government through the Ministry of Finance, and the Bank of Mexico. Hence my expectation that once the dust of the recent episode of international financial turbulence settles, the 10 The price of our national currency appreciates considerably. In conclusion, I would like to return to the opening theme of my speech. Certainty, as we know, is a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for ensuring sustained and accelerated economic growth. What certainty and stability offer is a formidable platform to undertake the much-carried and brought, but not yet crystallized, structural reforms that our country needs. We therefore have the foundations to undertake without further delay those indispensable structural reforms that we require to grow at rates that are much higher than the current ones and constantly, rates that I have no doubt would be higher than 5 percent per year. This imperative becomes more urgent today than ever given the prospect that the economies of the United States and Europe, which generate more than 45% of the world's GDP, will live through difficult times and will have, at best, a very high 11 low growth for the coming years, which will result in a lower boost to the national economy. It is precisely in order to compensate for this lack of external impetus in the future that the need for the already much-mentioned structural reforms has become extremely urgent. Only in this way can we close the great gap we have in terms of job creation and poverty reduction. The country can no longer afford inaction. Thanks a lot. 12
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, en la novena edicin de Mxico, cumbre de negocios, Quertaro, Quertaro. 23 de octubre de 2011 Muy buenas noches, agradezco al licenciado Miguel Alemn Velasco, presidente de Mxico, cumbre de negocios, su amable invitacin a participar en esta cena de inauguracin de la cumbre. Saludo afectuosamente a Jos Calzada Rovirosa, Gobernador Constitucional de este bello estado de Quertaro, en el que tantos acontecimientos fundamentales de la historia de Mxico han tenido lugar. Distinguidos expositores en esta reunin cumbre, seoras y seores: La crisis global que estall en septiembre de 2008 con la quiebra de Lehman Brothers cambi sustancialmente la percepcin de riesgo econmico y financiero en el mundo. Inversionistas, empresarios, gobiernos, autoridades financieras en todo el planeta percibimos ahora elevados riesgos de carcter global donde hasta septiembre de 2008, y 1 en el ms sombro de los casos, veamos riesgos moderados y acotados a una regin, a un pas o a una rama de la actividad econmica. Este cambio radical en la percepcin de los riesgos genera, a su vez, una gran incertidumbre. Al da de hoy, 23 de octubre, el mundo espera la respuesta definitiva que los principales pases de la Unin Monetaria Europea darn a la crisis de deuda soberana por la que atraviesa esa regin, as como a la contaminacin que por dicha crisis sufren los bancos y en general el sistema financiero en ese continente. Ha habido avances importantes a ltimas fechas, pero no los suficientes para abatir la incertidumbre global, ni para ahuyentar el temor de que en cualquier momento estas turbulencias contagien a la economa mundial. A este difcil panorama en Europa se adicionan los grandes dilemas que enfrenta Estados Unidos en materia fiscal, desempleo, sobreendeudamiento de las familias y depresin de su mercado de vivienda, lo cual ha conducido a una 2 expectativa de crecimiento econmico muy bajo en los aos venideros. As pues, a tres aos de distancia del punto ms agudo de la crisis, y a ms de cuatro aos de su inicio por la cadena de incumplimientos en pagos de las llamadas hipotecas de baja calidad en los Estados Unidos, la incertidumbre sigue reinando. No en vano, en la reciente reunin de ministros de finanzas y gobernadores de bancos centrales del G-20 en Pars, muchos insistimos en demandar respuestas claras e inmediatas de la Unin Monetaria Europea y Estados Unidos. Si bien es cierto que los graves problemas de sobreendeudamiento de familias, bancos y gobiernos de la mayora de los pases avanzados generan un lastre enorme sobre las posibilidades de crecimiento econmico, stas se han visto an ms afectadas por el efecto tan negativo que el pobre manejo de la crisis ha tenido sobre las expectativas. Este efecto negativo que ha minado la confianza ha provocado que muchos proyectos de inversin rentables se pospongan, al igual que las familias no afectadas por la crisis prefieran ahorrar precautoriamente en lugar de hacer compromisos de gastos que en otro entorno haran. 3 No cabe duda, entonces, que la primera escala en el largo camino hacia una recuperacin del ritmo de crecimiento de la economa mundial, de forma sostenida y estable, tiene que ser la del restablecimiento de la confianza, la generacin de certidumbres bsicas por parte de los lderes de las economas avanzadas. El restablecimiento de la confianza permitira entrar en un crculo virtuoso: al estabilizarse los mercados, bajaran las primas de riesgo, lo que llevara a un mayor gasto de inversin y de consumo, lo que a su vez conducira a un mayor crecimiento econmico. Este, a su vez, tendera a mejorar la salud de las finanzas pblicas y de los bancos europeos, lo que a su vez redundara en una mayor confianza en la recuperacin.
