Este crculo virtuoso se ha observado una y otra vez en los procesos de superacin de crisis en varios pases emergentes, incluidos Mxico. Pero para echar andar este proceso, es indispensable que las autoridades tomen las medidas fuertes necesarias, de manera oportuna. Medicina fuerte y amarga s, pero potencialmente muy redituable en el corto plazo por el proceso virtuoso que puede desencadenar. 4 Mientras tanto, cul es el panorama en Mxico? Un hecho que distingue a nuestro pas es que en los ltimos aos, y especialmente durante el gobierno del Presidente Felipe Caldern, una constante en el mbito de la poltica econmica ha sido la insistencia en generar certidumbre. Se ha sostenido, contra viento y marea, una poltica fiscal responsable; se ha mantenido un sistema bancario bien regulado y supervisado, extraordinariamente slido y solvente en comparacin con la banca de muchos otros pases. En esta materia, nuestro sistema bancario ser de los primeros en cumplir los requisitos prudenciales ms estrictos que la comunidad internacional ha acordado como resultado de la crisis. A su vez, el Banco Central ha ejercido a plenitud su autonoma sin apartarse del mandato constitucional que le ordena procurar la estabilidad de precios. An a pesar de la reciente volatilidad en los mercados financieros internacionales que se ha reflejado en una depreciacin de la moneda nacional, la inflacin se encuentra cercana a nuestro objetivo permanente de 3 por ciento, mientras que las expectativas de inflacin a todos los plazos se encuentran ancladas por debajo del cuatro por ciento. Esto se debe, 5 desde mi punto de vista, a que los participantes en los mercados esperan una prxima apreciacin del peso, dados los fuertes fundamentos de la economa mexicana, y a que desde hace ya varios aos el traspaso de movimientos cambiarios a precios se ha reducido considerablemente, en parte debido a la credibilidad del esquema de objetivos de inflacin que ha implementado el Banco de Mxico. Una comparacin que resulta de lo ms ilustrativa del progreso que hemos logrado en Mxico en materia de estabilizacin financiera, y que refleja la responsabilidad de las polticas fiscal y monetaria que hemos seguido, es la que podemos hacer entre el plazo promedio ponderado de la deuda gubernamental en Mxico y la misma deuda para el caso de Estados Unidos. En 1994, el plazo promedio ponderado de la deuda gubernamental en pesos en Mxico era de 0.63 aos (230 das). Ese mismo ao, 1994, el plazo promedio ponderado de la deuda gubernamental en Estados Unidos era de 5.08 aos (alrededor de 1,854 das). 6 Hoy, en Mxico el plazo promedio ponderado de la deuda gubernamental en pesos es de 7.4 aos (2,674 das) en tanto que el plazo promedio ponderado de la deuda del gobierno de Estados Unidos es de 5.2 aos (1,898 das). Esto significa que en Mxico no slo hemos ampliado ms de once veces dicho plazo de 1994 a la fecha, sino que superamos a la deuda gubernamental de los Estados Unidos en esos mismos trminos de plazo, por ms de dos aos. Esta comparacin sin duda refleja la confianza que los inversionistas le estn otorgando al gobierno de Mxico en materia de manejo macroeconmico, al grado de que estn dispuestos a confiarle su dinero por un plazo incluso mayor al plazo en el que le confan su dinero al gobierno de los Estados Unidos. Y tambin refleja la importancia decisiva que tuvo la reforma al sistema de pensiones iniciada en Mxico a fines del siglo pasado, ya que con el paso del tiempo ha creado una slida base de inversionistas institucionales de largo plazo, que contribuyen a la estabilidad del sistema financiero y le dan certidumbre al ahorro interno. 7 Otra comparacin internacional que resulta elocuente en referencia a las fortalezas fiscales de nuestro pas es la siguiente: considrese que la deuda pblica sobre PIB de Mxico es de aproximadamente 32 por ciento mientras que en la Unin Europea es de ms de 85 por ciento, con varios de sus pases por arriba del 100 por ciento, y en Estados Unidos esa razn superar dicha marca en meses prximos. Es decir, la razn deuda pblica sobre PIB de Mxico es tan slo una tercera parte aproximadamente que la de Estados Unidos y de Europa. Quisiera aqu hacerle un reconocimiento a la H. Cmara de Diputados por haber aprobado el jueves pasado una Ley de Ingresos para 2012 responsable, con un objetivo de dficit fiscal de tan slo 0.4 por ciento del PIB, lo que permitir que durante el ao entrante nuestra deuda sobre PIB contine cayendo. Justo con el mismo empeo de generar y garantizar certidumbre es lo que se ha hecho en el mbito especfico de los mercados financieros nacionales a travs de mltiples reformas. No me voy a detener en los detalles de stas, pero s considero necesario destacar lo relativo al mercado de 8 cambios, dadas las inquietudes que, por razones de memoria histrica, este tema suele causar.  El peso se ha convertido en una de las pocas divisas de pases emergentes que opera de manera continua las 24 horas del da, lo que le da una gran liquidez.  Hoy el peso mexicano ocupa el lugar nmero 13 entre las divisas ms operadas en el mundo, lo que nos sita, dentro de los pases emergentes, slo por debajo de Corea y Singapur.  Los diferenciales de compra-venta en los mercados interbancarios son comparables a los que se observan en las principales divisas del mundo: dlar, yen, euro o libra esterlina.  La mayor parte de las operaciones cambiarias se realizan hoy mediante plataformas electrnicas, garantizando una mayor transparencia en el proceso de formacin de precios y en la capacidad de ejecucin. El factor decisivo detrs de todos estos avances ha sido la libre flotacin del peso desde finales de 1994. 9 Las espordicas intervenciones del Banco de Mxico en el mercado cambiario se han dado en general bajo reglas predefinidas, transparentes y conocidas de antemano por todos los participantes. Adems, nuestras intervenciones se han hecho fundamentalmente con un solo objetivo: garantizar el funcionamiento ordenado del mercado, procurando evitar que se generen situaciones de iliquidez que lleven a una volatilidad excesiva en la cotizacin de la moneda nacional. Esto implica que desde hace muchos aos las autoridades financieras del pas hemos dejado de intervenir en el mercado cambiario persiguiendo un nivel especfico del tipo de cambio. Nuestra tesis ha sido que la nica manera de garantizar un nivel adecuado y estable de la paridad cambiaria, es manteniendo sanos los fundamentos de nuestra economa. Y precisamente a esto es a lo que nos hemos dedicado en los ltimos aos tanto el Gobierno Federal a travs de la Secretara de Hacienda, como el Banco de Mxico. De ah mi expectativa de que una vez que se asiente el polvo del reciente episodio de turbulencia financiera internacional la 10 cotizacin de nuestra moneda nacional se aprecie de manera considerable. Para concluir, quisiera regresar a la temtica de inicio de mi intervencin. La certidumbre, ya lo sabemos, es una condicin necesaria, pero no suficiente, para garantizar el crecimiento econmico sostenido y acelerado. Lo que ofrecen la certidumbre y la estabilidad es una formidable plataforma para emprender las tan llevadas y tradas, pero an no cristalizadas, reformas estructurales que nuestro pas necesita. Tenemos pues los cimientos para emprender sin ms dilaciones esas indispensables reformas estructurales que requerimos para crecer a tasas que sean mucho mayores que las actuales y de manera constante, tasas que no me cabe duda seran superiores al 5 por ciento anual. Este imperativo se hace hoy ms urgente que nunca ante la perspectiva de que las economas de Estados Unidos y Europa, que generan ms del 45% del PIB mundial, vivirn tiempos difciles y tendrn, en el mejor de los casos, un muy 11 bajo crecimiento para los prximos aos, lo cual redundar en un menor impulso a la economa nacional. Precisamente para poder compensar esta falta de impulso externo en el futuro, es que se ha vuelto sumamente urgente la necesidad de hacer las ya muy mentadas reformas estructurales. Slo as podremos abatir el gran rezago que tenemos en materia de creacin de empleo y de reduccin de la pobreza. El pas ya no se puede dar el lujo de la inaccin. Muchas gracias. 12

Title: 79th National Banking Convention
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, on the occasion of the 79th National Banking Convention. March 10, 2016 Acapulco, Guerrero ? Mr. President of the United Mexican States, Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto, ? Mr. Governor of the State of Guerrero, Mr. Hector Astudillo Flores, ? Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso, ? Mr. Secretary of Social Development, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena, ? Mr. President of the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Senators, Mr. Roberto Gil Zuarth, ? Mr. President of the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Deputies, Mr. Jesus Zambrano Grijalva, 1 ? Mr. President of the Finance and Public Credit Committee of the Chamber of Senators, Mr. Jose Francisco Yunes Zorrila, ? Ladies and Gentlemen Legislators; ? Mr. President of the National Banking Commission and Values, teacher Jaime Gonzalez Aguade, ? Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, Mr. Luis Robles Miaja, ? Ladies and gentlemen, Good afternoon. It is a real privilege to participate in this Session Plenary and Inauguration of the 79th National Banking Convention, with the honorable presence of the Constitutional President of the United Mexican States, Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto. This occasion is particularly pleasing to me, as it is seen at the stage in which our country has achieved the highest inflation. 2 down since a national register of consumer prices was kept 47 years ago. Indeed, the efforts made by the Bank of Mexico to achieve low and stable inflation in accordance with its constitutional mandate contributed to the fact that in the first months of 2015 general inflation converged to our permanent target of 3 percent and, since May of that year, was below this figure. closing 2015 at 2.13 percent, a historical minimum level since the INPC is measured. In the intervening period of 2016, inflation had a rebound associated mainly with transitory increases in the prices of a small number of fruits and vegetables, but always remaining below 3 percent. In achieving this achievement, the monetary policy measures adopted for many years by this Central Institute have been of paramount importance, but it is also pertinent to mention that in the last 18 months they have been 3 Fundamental are the reductions in several prices of inputs in widespread use, such as energy and telecommunications services, which have been the result of the structural reforms promoted by the current administration. The favourable behaviour of inflation has been achieved despite an otherwise complex situation. During 2015 and early 2016, moderate economic growth prevailed domestically, with no aggregate demand pressure on prices and with a solid anchoring of inflation expectations. However, the international environment that Mexico has faced has been characterized for several years by a notorious weakness in the pace of expansion of global economic activity. Since 2008, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has consecutively revised down its global growth forecasts. A more recent manifestation of this widespread sluggishness in economic growth, which already borders on 4 in a recessionary environment in several regions of the world, it is the unusual slowdown in the volume of international trade. The following data are very eloquent in this regard: in December 2013, only 5 of the 34 OECD member countries had negative annual rates of variation in their exports; in December 2015, two years later, that figure rose to 32 countries, meaning that 94 percent of OECD member countries had falls in the volume of their exports last year. The same can be said of emerging countries as important as Brazil, China, India, Russia, South Africa, Indonesia and Colombia. This deep slowdown in global economic activity has been reflected in a sustained fall in commodity prices for several years; it certainly highlights the precipitous reduction in the price of oil, which has also been greatly affected by geopolitical problems. 5 complex and by a rupture of the industrial organization of the sector worldwide, which suggests that the recent dynamics of prices are more structural than transitory. Thus, in 2015 the price of the Mexican export mix suffered a fall of 39.8 percent, while in the first weeks of 2016 it reached up to 31 percent, and then recover the lost ground. This erratic behavior of the price of crude oil, which undoubtedly represents a major external shock in the real sector of the economy, has contributed to the depreciation of the national currency. In fact, a depreciation of the real exchange rate is part of the process of adjustment of the Mexican economy in the face of the magnitude of the disturbance received, so the authorities must help make this process as orderly as possible. As if the above had not been enough, during 2015 and so far this year there have been recurrent episodes of 6 unusual volatility in international financial markets, manifested mainly in sharp falls in stock market quote indices and in a generalized appreciation of the United States dollar against the currencies of the main advanced and emerging countries, including the Mexican peso. I can think of three fundamental factors, in addition to oil price dynamics, low global economic activity and geopolitical problems, that have contributed to this wave of periods of financial instability, which I would like to address in detail: First. Divergent monetary policies among the main advanced countries. By this I am referring to the fact that, on the one hand, the Federal Reserve Bank of the United States has already begun the process of normalizing its monetary policy, starting with suspending the massive purchase of securities in the market, and more recently. 7 increasing the federal funds rate to nearly 0 percent. This in response to the fact that after several years of convalescence from the global financial crisis, the American economy has already resumed the path of growth, although not very accelerated, and its inflation has been increasing from very low levels. At the other extreme are the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan, to name the two most important in this field, which have not only been expanding their money supply through the massive purchase in the markets of all kinds of securities, but have also reduced their reference interest rates to levels even below zero. This has been reflected in the yield curves of several countries, to the extent that 41 percent of OECD countries have negative rates on government securities up to five years. The larger rate differential in favour of the United States has attracted a very significant amount of resources to that country, contributing to the appreciation already 8 mentioned of your currency. But perhaps more important has been the signal of fragility sent by countries whose central banks are forced to venture into such unconventional monetary policies that take interest rates into negative territory, given the lack of fiscal policies and structural reforms that help them get out of the quagmire in which they find themselves. Negative rates have affected the profitability of the banks that are subject to them, and have increased the perception of financial stability risk. These reactions have led global investors to privilege assets that are considered "safeguards of value," which has undoubtedly affected their appetite for risk in emerging countries, including Mexico. The above moral is that central banks alone cannot lead an economy into a situation of accelerated and sustained growth with financial stability; proper coordination with fiscal policy and structural reforms is indispensable. 9 Second. Unwanted side effects of regulatory reform on the international financial system. This reform has been designed with great care through the G-20 Financial Stability Board, with the ultimate goal of minimizing the possibility of global financial institutions failing, and that taxpayer resources do not have to be used to rescue these institutions. The resulting changes in international banking regulation contemplate higher capital requirements on emerging country debt instruments that institutions can maintain, along with specific rules in some countries, such as the United States, that limit them from retaining exchange positions, among others. This has affected the depth and liquidity of financial markets in countries where global banks play an important role, exacerbating the responses of financial variables in those countries, such as the exchange rate. 10 to various clashes. This has undoubtedly been perceived in our country. Finally, participation of some agents in the foreign exchange market through the use of high-frequency automated trading models. In particular, the strategies adopted with such models take advantage of exchange rate volatility to make a profit, which in turn affects its level and feeds back into its volatility. In the Mexican environment, at the beginning of the year this type of strategy was used to activate the dollar auctions that the Bank of Mexico executed by agreement of the Exchange Commission to soften the volatility in the exchange market, which allowed these agents to continue pressuring the price of the national currency on the day, without the fear that the central bank would re-enter the market to try to stabilize it. Undoubtedly, this type of operation using algorithms eroded the capacity 11 stabilizing non-discretionary interventions in the foreign exchange market of the Bank of Mexico. Thus, for all these reasons, during January and the first half of February 2016 volatility in international financial markets continued to increase. In addition, pressures on the national currency increased further in response to the collapse of the price of oil. This increased the likelihood that inflation expectations would emerge inconsistent with the consolidation of the permanent 3 percent target set by the Bank of Mexico. Thus, given the complicated external environment, the high risk aversion in the markets and the perception of threats to public finances, it became essential to strengthen the macroeconomic framework of the Mexican economy. Therefore, on February 17, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Bank of Mexico decided 12 strengthen the country's economic fundamentals, each within the scope of their respective responsibilities: (i) at an extraordinary meeting, the Governing Board of the Central Institute decided to increase the target for the benchmark interest rate by 50 basis points to a level of 3.75 per cent, clarifying that this action did not represent the beginning of a cycle of monetary contraction; (ii) the Foreign Exchange Commission, chaired by the Secretary of Finance and with the participation of the Bank, decided to suspend the mechanisms for selling dollars through daily auctions, without ruling out the possibility of discretionary interventions in the event of exceptional conditions in the foreign exchange market, while ratifying that the key element in ensuring the anchoring of the national currency will be the preservation of sound macroeconomic fundamentals. Finally, the Ministry of Finance announced a cut to public spending by 132.3 billion pesos. 13 This joint action of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Bank of Mexico has yielded the expected results. In the last nearly four weeks, the peso has appreciated about nine percent; short-term rates rose, but not long-term rates, producing the desired flattening of our yield curve; the Mexican Stock Exchange's price and quote index rose 3.2 percent, while the measure of sovereign credit risk as measured by CDSs fell 48 basis points, or 22 percent. The coordinated strategy of the country's financial authorities took some market participants by surprise. This should not have been the case. The measures adopted were not improvised, but the result of a meticulous process of analysis between the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Mexico. It simply represents the use of the stabilization instruments that we have to our 14 disposition, and that, speaking for the Bank of Mexico, we will not hesitate to use them again in case it is necessary. In addition, I must admit that during the administration of President Pena Nieto we have found in the Federal Government a constant willingness to collaborate and coordinate with the Bank of Mexico. Wherever relevant to preserving the country's macroeconomic soundness, fiscal policy has responded in a timely manner. This coordination of fiscal and monetary policies has in no way been detrimental to the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. On the contrary, the efficient coordination - provided for in the law of the Bank of Mexico - has strengthened the autonomous character of our institution, since it has allowed to expand the degrees of freedom to exercise a monetary policy absolutely aligned with the constitutional mandate to ensure low and stable inflation. 15 The coordination between the Federal Government and the Bank of Mexico also extends, as it should, to the regulatory space of the financial system. This coordination has pursued the objective, among others, that Mexican banks have all the conditions to be a protagonist of the first order in the promotion of growth, while observing a strict prudential scheme. We have acted in a coordinated manner so that - each within the scope of its powers and competences - financial penetration and inclusion are increased. Specifically, the Bank of Mexico has continued to make the most of the legal tools that Congress has provided it with in recent years to encourage greater competition for the benefit of users, reducing costs and commissions and, in general, opening spaces of opportunity for the benefits of a macroeconomy. 16 Through Mexican banking, more and more households and companies are reaching. In this regard, I would like to take this opportunity to announce that the system of interbank payments in dollars, baptized as SPID and developed by the Bank of Mexico, will enter into operation from next April. The SPID arises from the importance of dollar-denominated transfers in the country. This is partly a consequence of Mexico's greater integration into the global economy, as a fraction of transactions in various production chains are denominated in dollars, even when related activities occur within the national territory. The regulation allows banks to offer dollar accounts in Mexico to certain types of customers, mainly legal entities. Therefore, the SPID will allow electronic transfers in dollars between companies in very short times, at most one day, and will avoid 17 inefficient procedures for performing each transaction. In addition, the requirements to operate in the system imply that the dollar operations carried out in the country will be more transparent, and that banks will implement reviews in accordance with a strict risk-based scheme. This will contribute to improving the credibility of the preventive processes of credit institutions, and of the Mexican financial system in general, compared to the rest of the world. Mr President, Ladies and gentlemen: In the face of an extraordinarily challenging global environment such as the one we are experiencing, it is imperative that State institutions carefully attend to the fulfillment of their specific mandates and the use of the policies that correspond to them. You can rest assured that the Bank of Mexico, as an autonomous institution, will continue to do so. But it is also necessary that such State policies act in coordination. 18 to achieve a higher goal, that of increasing the well-being of all Mexicans. We are on the right track and, in the face of the setbacks and vicissitudes of such a complex world environment, we cannot be discouraged but, on the contrary, redouble our efforts and persevere in the final goal we pursue. Thanks a lot. 19
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, con motivo de la 79 Convencin Nacional Bancaria. 10 de marzo de 2016 Acapulco, Guerrero  Seor Presidente de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto,  Seor Gobernador del Estado de Guerrero, licenciado Hctor Astudillo Flores,  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Luis Videgaray Caso,  Seor Secretario de Desarrollo Social, doctor Jos Antonio Meade Kuribrea,  Seor Presidente de la Mesa Directiva de la Cmara de Senadores, licenciado Roberto Gil Zuarth,  Seor Presidente de la Mesa Directiva de la Cmara de Diputados, licenciado Jess Zambrano Grijalva, 1  Seor Presidente de la Comisin de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico de la Cmara de Senadores, licenciado Jos Francisco Yunes Zorrila,  Seoras y seores Legisladores;  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, maestro Jaime Gonzlez Aguad,  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, licenciado Luis Robles Miaja,  Seoras y seores: Muy buenas tardes. Es un verdadero privilegio participar en esta Sesin Plenaria e Inaugural de la 79 Convencin Nacional Bancaria, con la honrosa presencia del Presidente Constitucional de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, Licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto. Esta ocasin es particularmente grata para m, pues se verifica en la etapa en la que nuestro pas ha logrado la inflacin ms 2 baja desde que se lleva un registro nacional de los precios al consumidor, hace 47 aos. En efecto, los esfuerzos que ha realizado el Banco de Mxico para lograr una inflacin baja y estable conforme a su mandato constitucional, contribuyeron a que en los primeros meses de 2015 la inflacin general convergiera a nuestra meta permanente de 3 por ciento y, desde mayo de ese ao, se ubicara por debajo de esta cifra, cerrando 2015 en 2.13 por ciento, nivel mnimo histrico desde que se mide el INPC. En el periodo transcurrido de 2016 la inflacin tuvo un repunte asociado principalmente a incrementos transitorios en los precios de un nmero pequeo de frutas y verduras, pero siempre mantenindose por debajo del 3 por ciento. En la consecucin de este logro ha sido de importancia toral las medidas de poltica monetaria adoptadas ya por muchos aos por este Instituto Central, pero tambin es pertinente mencionar que en los ltimos 18 meses han sido 3 fundamentales los abatimientos de varios precios de insumos de uso generalizado, tales como los energticos y los servicios de telecomunicaciones, los cuales han sido el resultado de las reformas estructurales impulsadas por la actual administracin. El comportamiento favorable de la inflacin se ha logrado a pesar de una coyuntura por dems compleja. Durante 2015 e inicios de 2016, en el mbito interno predomin un crecimiento econmico moderado, sin que se presentaran presiones de demanda agregada sobre los precios y con un slido anclaje de las expectativas de inflacin. No obstante, el entorno internacional que ha enfrentado Mxico se ha caracterizado desde hace ya varios aos por una notoria debilidad en el ritmo de expansin de la actividad econmica global. Desde 2008 el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) ha revisado consecutivamente a la baja sus pronsticos de crecimiento mundial. Una manifestacin ms reciente de esta atona generalizada en el crecimiento econmico, que ya raya 4 en un ambiente recesionario en varias regiones del orbe, es la inusitada desaceleracin del volumen del comercio internacional. Los siguientes datos son muy elocuentes al respecto: en diciembre de 2013, slo 5 de los 34 pases miembros de la OCDE tuvieron tasas anuales negativas de variacin de sus exportaciones; en diciembre de 2015, es decir dos aos despus, esa cifra se elev a 32 pases, lo que significa que 94 por ciento de los pases miembros de la OCDE tuvieron cadas en el volumen de sus exportaciones el ao pasado. Lo mismo se puede decir de pases emergentes tan importantes como Brasil, China, India, Rusia, Sudfrica, Indonesia y Colombia. Esta profunda desaceleracin de la actividad econmica mundial se ha reflejado en una cada sostenida por ya varios aos en los precios de las materias primas; destaca sin duda la precipitosa reduccin del precio del petrleo, el cual tambin se ha visto afectado por problemas geopolticos sumamente 5 complejos y por una ruptura de la organizacin industrial del sector a nivel mundial, lo cual hace pensar que la dinmica reciente de los precios es ms estructural que transitoria. As, en 2015 el precio de la mezcla mexicana de exportacin sufri una cada de 39.8 por ciento, mientras que en las primeras semanas de 2016 sta lleg a ser de hasta 31 por ciento, para despus recuperar el terreno perdido. Este comportamiento tan errtico del precio del crudo, que sin duda representa un choque externo de gran magnitud en el sector real de la economa, ha contribuido a la depreciacin de la moneda nacional. De hecho, una depreciacin del tipo de cambio real es parte del proceso de ajuste de la economa mexicana ante la magnitud de la perturbacin recibida, por lo que las autoridades debemos coadyuvar a que dicho proceso sea lo ms ordenado posible. Por si lo anterior no hubiera sido suficiente, durante 2015 y lo que va del ao se han suscitado episodios recurrentes de 6 inusitada volatilidad en los mercados financieros internacionales, manifestndose principalmente en cadas pronunciadas en los ndices de cotizacin de los mercados de valores y en una apreciacin generalizada del dlar de los Estados Unidos frente a las divisas de los principales pases avanzados y emergentes, incluido el peso mexicano. Puedo pensar en tres factores fundamentales, adems de la dinmica del precio del petrleo, de la baja actividad econmica mundial y de problemas geopolticos, que han contribuido a esta oleada de periodos de inestabilidad financiera, los cuales quisiera abordar en detalle: Primero. Polticas monetarias divergentes entre los principales pases avanzados. Por esto me refiero al hecho de que, por un lado, el Banco de la Reserva Federal de los Estados Unidos ha iniciado ya el proceso de normalizacin de su poltica monetaria, empezando con suspender la compra masiva de ttulos en el mercado, y ms recientemente 7 aumentando la tasa de fondos federales que se encontraba prcticamente en 0 por ciento. Esto en respuesta a que despus de varios aos de convalecencia de la crisis financiera global, la economa americana ya ha retomado la senda de crecimiento, aunque no muy acelerado, y su inflacin ha venido aumentando de niveles muy bajos. En el otro extremo se sitan el Banco Central Europeo y el Banco de Japn, por citar a los dos ms importantes que se encuentran en ese campo, los cuales no slo han venido expandiendo su masa monetaria mediante la compra masiva en los mercados de todo tipo de valores, sino que tambin han reducido sus tasas de inters de referencia a niveles incluso inferiores a cero. Esto se ha reflejado en las curvas de rendimiento de varios pases, al grado que el 41 por ciento de los pases de la OCDE tienen tasas negativas en valores gubernamentales hasta de un plazo de cinco aos. El mayor diferencial de tasas a favor de los Estados Unidos ha atrado una cantidad de recursos muy importante hacia ese pas, abonando a la apreciacin ya 8 mencionada de su moneda. Pero quiz ms importante ha sido la seal de fragilidad que mandan los pases cuyos bancos centrales se ven obligados a incursionar en polticas monetarias tan poco convencionales que llevan las tasas de inters a terreno negativo, ante la falta de polticas fiscales y de reformas estructurales que los ayuden a salir del atolladero en que se encuentran. Las tasas negativas han afectado la rentabilidad de los bancos que estn sujetas a ellas, y han aumentado la percepcin de riesgo de estabilidad financiera. Estas reacciones han llevado a inversionistas globales a que privilegien activos que se consideran resguardos de valor, lo que sin duda ha afectado su apetito por riesgo de pases emergentes, entre ellos Mxico. La moraleja anterior es que los bancos centrales por si solos no pueden llevar a una economa a una situacin de crecimiento acelerado y sostenido con estabilidad financiera; es indispensable una adecuada coordinacin con la poltica fiscal y las reformas estructurales. 9 Segundo. Efectos colaterales no deseados de la reforma regulatoria al sistema financiero internacional. Dicha reforma ha sido diseada con gran esmero a travs del Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera del G-20, con el objetivo final de minimizar la posibilidad de que instituciones financieras globales quiebren, y que no se tengan que utilizar recursos de los contribuyentes para rescatar a dichas instituciones. Los cambios en la regulacin bancaria internacional resultante contemplan mayores requerimientos de capital sobre los instrumentos de deuda de pases emergentes que pueden mantener las instituciones, junto con reglas especficas en algunos pases, como Estados Unidos, que les limitan conservar posiciones cambiarias, entre otras. Esto ha afectado la profundidad y liquidez de los mercados financieros en los pases en donde los bancos globales juegan un papel importante, lo que ha exacerbado las respuestas de las variables financieras de dichos pases, como el tipo de cambio, 10 a diversos choques. Esto sin duda se ha percibido en nuestro pas. Por ltimo, participacin de algunos agentes en el mercado cambiario mediante el uso de modelos de operacin automatizada de alta frecuencia. En particular, las estrategias adoptadas con dichos modelos aprovechan la volatilidad del tipo de cambio para obtener ganancias, lo que a su vez afecta su nivel y retroalimenta su volatilidad. En el entorno mexicano, al inicio del ao este tipo de estrategias se utiliz para activar las subastas de dlares que el Banco de Mxico ejecutaba por acuerdo de la Comisin de Cambios para suavizar la volatilidad en el mercado cambiario, lo que les permita a estos agentes seguir presionando a la cotizacin de la moneda nacional en el da, sin el temor que el banco central volviera a entrar al mercado para intentar estabilizarlo. Sin lugar a dudas, este tipo de operaciones mediante algoritmos erosion la capacidad 11 estabilizadora de las intervenciones no discrecionales en el mercado cambiario del Banco de Mxico. As pues, por todas estas razones, durante enero y la primera mitad de febrero de 2016 la volatilidad en los mercados financieros internacionales continu aumentando. Adems, las presiones sobre la moneda nacional se incrementaron an ms en respuesta al colapso del precio del petrleo. Esto aument la probabilidad de que surgieran expectativas de inflacin incongruentes con la consolidacin del objetivo permanente del 3 por ciento establecido por el Banco de Mxico. As, ante el complicado entorno externo, la elevada aversin al riesgo en los mercados y la percepcin de amenazas sobre las finanzas pblicas, se hizo indispensable fortalecer el marco macroeconmico de la economa mexicana. Por ello, el 17 de febrero pasado la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico y el Banco de Mxico decidieron 12 reforzar los fundamentos econmicos del pas, cada uno en el mbito de sus respectivas responsabilidades: i) en una reunin extraordinaria, la Junta de Gobierno del Instituto Central determin incrementar en 50 puntos base el objetivo para la tasa de inters de referencia a un nivel de 3.75 por ciento, aclarando que esta accin no representaba el inicio de un ciclo de contraccin monetaria; ii) la Comisin de Cambios, presidida por el Secretario de Hacienda y con la participacin del Banco, decidi suspender los mecanismos de venta de dlares mediante subastas diarias, sin descartar la posibilidad de intervenciones discrecionales en caso de que se presenten condiciones excepcionales en el mercado cambiario, ratificando a la vez que el elemento clave para procurar el anclaje de la moneda nacional ser la preservacin de fundamentos macroeconmicos sanos. Por ltimo, la Secretara de Hacienda anunci un recorte al gasto pblico por 132.3 miles de millones de pesos. 13 Este accionar conjunto de la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico y del Banco de Mxico ha rendido los resultados esperados. En las ltimas casi cuatro semanas, el peso se ha apreciado aproximadamente nueve por ciento; las tasas de corto plazo subieron, mas no las de largo, produciendo el aplanamiento deseado de nuestra curva de rendimientos; el ndice de precios y cotizaciones de la Bolsa Mexicana de Valores subi 3.2 por ciento, mientras que la medicin del riesgo crediticio soberano medido por los CDS baj 48 puntos base, equivalentes a 22 por ciento. La estrategia coordinada de las autoridades financieras del pas tom por sorpresa a algunos participantes en los mercados. Esto no debera haber sido el caso. Las medidas adoptadas no fueron improvisadas, sino el resultado de un meticuloso proceso de anlisis entre la Secretara de Hacienda y el Banco de Mxico. Simplemente representa el uso de los instrumentos de estabilizacin que tenemos a nuestra 14 disposicin, y que, hablando por el Banco de Mxico, no dudaremos en volverlos a usar en caso de que sea necesario. Adems, debo reconocer que durante la administracin del Presidente Pea Nieto hemos encontrado en el Gobierno Federal una constante disposicin de colaboracin y coordinacin con el Banco de Mxico. Siempre que ha sido pertinente para preservar la solidez macroeconmica del pas, la poltica fiscal ha respondido de forma oportuna. Esta coordinacin de las polticas fiscal y monetaria de ninguna manera ha sido en detrimento de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico. Por el contrario, la coordinacin eficiente  prevista en la ley del Banco de Mxico-, ha fortalecido el carcter autnomo de nuestra institucin, ya que ha permitido ampliar los grados de libertad para ejercer una poltica monetaria absolutamente alineada al mandato constitucional de procurar una inflacin baja y estable. 15 La coordinacin entre el Gobierno Federal y el Banco de Mxico tambin se extiende, como debe de ser, al espacio regulatorio del sistema financiero. Esta coordinacin ha perseguido el objetivo, entre otros, de que la banca mexicana tenga todas las condiciones para ser un protagonista de primer orden en el impulso al crecimiento, observando a la vez un esquema prudencial estricto. Hemos actuado de forma coordinada para que  cada cual en el mbito de sus atribuciones y competencias- se incrementen la penetracin y la inclusin financieras. Especficamente, el Banco de Mxico ha seguido aprovechando al mximo las herramientas jurdicas de las que le ha dotado el Congreso en aos recientes para fomentar una mayor competencia en beneficio de los usuarios, abatiendo costos y comisiones y, en general, abriendo espacios de oportunidad para que los beneficios de una macroeconoma 16 slida lleguen, a travs de la banca mexicana, a cada vez ms hogares y empresas. En este sentido, quisiera aprovechar la ocasin para anunciar que el sistema de pagos interbancarios en dlares, bautizado como SPID y desarrollado por el Banco de Mxico, entrar en operacin a partir de abril prximo. El SPID surge de la importancia que han adquirido las transferencias denominadas en dlares en el pas. Esto en parte es consecuencia de la mayor integracin de Mxico en la economa global, ya que una fraccin de las transacciones en varias cadenas de produccin se denomina en dlares, incluso cuando las actividades relacionadas ocurren dentro del territorio nacional. La regulacin permite que los bancos ofrezcan cuentas en dlares en Mxico a cierto tipo de clientes, principalmente a personas morales. Por ello, el SPID permitir realizar transferencias electrnicas en dlares entre empresas en tiempos muy reducidos, de a lo ms un da, y evitar 17 procedimientos ineficientes para realizar cada transaccin. Adems, los requerimientos para operar en el sistema implican que las operaciones en dlares que se realicen en el pas sern ms transparentes, y que los bancos implementarn revisiones acordes con un estricto esquema basado en riesgos. Esto contribuir a mejorar la credibilidad de los procesos preventivos de las instituciones de crdito, y del sistema financiero mexicano en general, frente al resto del mundo. Seor Presidente, Seoras y seores: Ante un entorno global extraordinariamente retador como el que vivimos es imperativo que las instituciones del Estado atiendan con esmero el cumplimiento de sus mandatos especficos y el uso de las polticas que les corresponden. Pueden tener la seguridad de que el Banco de Mxico, como institucin autnoma, lo seguir haciendo. Pero adems es preciso que tales polticas de Estado acten coordinadamente 18 para lograr un fin ms elevado, el de acrecentar el bienestar de todos los mexicanos. Vamos por el camino correcto y, ante las contrariedades y vicisitudes propias de un entorno mundial tan complejo, no podemos desalentarnos sino, por el contrario, redoblar el esfuerzo y perseverar en el objetivo final que perseguimos. Muchas gracias. 19

Title: Economic developments and monetary policy in Mexico
text: "ECONOMIC EVOLUTION AND MONETARY POLICY IN MEXICO", WORDS OF MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO.- AMERICAS SOCIETY/COUNCIL OF THE AMERICAS CFO MEXICO CITY FORUM. Mexico City, May 17, 2016.1 I would first of all like to thank the organizers for their kind invitation to present to you my views on the Mexican economy and the monetary policy that is being implemented in the country. After a start to the year surrounded by great uncertainty and volatility in international financial markets, it has been observed, although with ups and downs, a lower nervousness propitiated, among other factors, by expectations of a very relaxed monetary policy stance in the United States and other advanced economies for a prolonged period, the recovery in the price of oil and other raw materials, and some improvement in the Chinese economy. However, the global economic and financial situation remains fragile, and the risk of further outbreaks of market turbulence is high. It should be noted, due to its importance for Mexico, that the US economy has shown resistance to this problem, which has allowed it to achieve economic growth rates higher than those of the rest of the advanced economies considered as a whole. However, the appreciation of the dollar, the weakness of external demand and the problems in the energy sector have been reflected in its industrial production, which has remained stagnant since the beginning of 2015. The manufacturing sector, of 1 The opinions contained herein are the sole responsibility of the author. 1 With very close ties with the Mexican economy, it is also in a situation of weakness, although to a lesser degree than the industrial sector in general. On the other hand, analysts continue to anticipate a gradual recovery in industrial production over the coming months. After registering in January 2016 the lowest levels in almost 14 years, the prices of the Mexican oil mix have gradually recovered. In the opinion of the International Energy Agency (IEA), an improvement in the global balance between supply and demand of crude oil could be observed since the second half of this year, which would give additional support to energy prices. However, these prices remain at low levels and, in general, future markets continue to anticipate a gradual recovery in the coming years, probably as a result of the stimulus that higher prices would represent for the supply of crude oil. Despite this challenging external environment, the Mexican economy has continued to expand at a moderate pace. During the period 2011-2015, GDP recorded an average annual growth rate of 2.8 percent. Notably, these results are similar to those observed in Mexico during the years prior to the global financial crisis (2.7 percent per year from 2000 to 2007). It is true that these growth rates are low considering the needs of the population. However, it is also important to evaluate them objectively in the appropriate context, particularly taking into account that during that period a significant decrease in the 2 global economic growth. For example, the average annual rate of GDP growth in the United States fell by 0.6 percentage points from 2000-2007 to 2011-2015, and today the level of manufacturing output in this country is still lower than that observed at the end of 2007. The Latin American and Caribbean region (excluding Mexico) showed a more drastic decline in its expansion rate, of about 1.6 percentage points, in those years. In addition, an economic contraction was observed in the area in 2015, with a further fall expected in 2016. More generally, the Mexican economy is one of the few among the emerging economies that managed to maintain its stable pace of economic growth in the periods indicated. As is logical to assume, Mexican exports have suffered the effect of the stagnation of industrial production in the United States and weak global economic activity. Thus, GDP growth has been supported by domestic demand, and especially by private consumption, as investment has continued to show lassitude. On the other hand, as a result of the gradual recovery of the economy, a negative output gap continues to be observed. In this regard, it should be noted that the unemployment rate is still above the levels observed before the crisis, the demands for wage increases are moderate, as we will see later the inflation rate is below the target and, although bank credit shows a recovery, this has occurred from low levels. 3 In the case of the external sector, there has been a widening of the current account deficit as a proportion of GDP, from 0.5 percent in 2010 to 2.8 percent in 2015. This is not explained by demand pressures on imports, but mainly by the transition from a surplus to an oil deficit, a result in turn of the deterioration of the terms of trade and lower production in the sector.2 The Mexican economy is expected to continue to show a gradual recovery in the coming months. The anticipated rebound in U.S. industrial production should be reflected in manufacturing exports. In this regard, it is important to consider that, as evidenced by the fact that Mexican exports have continued to gain share in the US market, they remain very competitive.3 This would allow a more balanced growth of the different components of aggregate demand, which would strengthen the fundamentals of the recovery. On the other hand, it is important to make two clarifications. First, taking into account the circumstances of both the external and internal environments, the output gap is expected to close slowly; it could even remain in negative territory over the next year. Secondly, downside risks to economic activity in Mexico persist, among which I find particularly important. 2 After posting a surplus equivalent to 2.0% of GDP in 2006, the oil trade balance showed a continuous deterioration until it became a deficit in 2015, at a magnitude equivalent to 0.9% of GDP. 3 During the first quarter of 2016, Mexican exports (excluding crude oil) reached an average share of 13.92 percent in non-oil imports from the United States, up from 12.81 percent in the same quarter of 2015. 4 the possibility of a new episode of turbulence in international financial markets, which affects the performance of the markets and the real sector, as well as a slower than expected recovery in US industrial production, although there are also risks of a domestic nature. In the case of inflation, the facts speak for themselves: ? Despite a depreciation of the peso against the dollar that from September 2014 to date accumulates around 40 percent, inflation registered in 2015 historical lows for 8 consecutive months, and in April 2016 it stood at a level of 2.5 percent, below the target of 3 percent. ? Mexico is one of the countries in Latin America with the lowest transfer from exchange rate to prices.4 ? Long-term inflation expectations based on surveys have declined and show greater convergence with the target, although they are still slightly above the target.5 The above achievements are the result of a combination of factors. The most important among these is the implementation of prudent macroeconomic policies over many years. It is noteworthy, in particular, that the conduct of monetary policy by an independent central bank, with the constitutional mandate to achieve a low and stable inflation rate, and 4 See Bank of Mexico, Quarterly Report, July-September 2015 and International Monetary Fund (2016): "Exchange Rate Transfer in Latin America",Chapter 4 of the Economic Outlook for the Americas, April. 5 Based on the results of the Bank of Mexico's April 2016 "Survey on the Expectations of Specialists in Private Sector Economics," the median expectation for horizons of 1 to 4 years and 5 to 8 years is 3.3 percent. In June 2015 alone, the median for the 1-4 year horizon was 3.5%, while that for the 5-8 year horizon was at that level in September last year. 5 the context of an inflation targeting scheme has considerably strengthened the credibility of the authorities' commitment to price stability. The recent trajectory of inflation has also benefited from the structural reforms put in place in recent years, which have led to significant declines in the prices of several key goods in the economy, including telecommunications and electricity. To this can be added the effect of the decrease in international quotations of various inputs and the absence of demand pressures on prices. Inflation is likely to fluctuate for the rest of this year and the next around 3 percent. This is largely explained by the expected behavior of gasoline prices. As of January 2016, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit modified the mechanism to determine these prices, temporarily introducing a fluctuation band, based on its international quotes, as a transition to its complete liberalization in January 2018. In this way, inflation in Mexico will be affected this year and next, both by the seasonality of international prices of this product, and by the formula used to determine its domestic quotations recently announced by the SHCP. It should be noted that a trajectory of inflation characterized by movements of this around 3 percent would be normal and consistent with the fulfillment of the target. In fact, if economic agents perceive that in the long run the inflation rate would have a pattern of this nature, they would 6 facilitate the anchoring of the various measures of inflation expectations by 3 percent. However, a situation characterized by a negative output gap, low inflation and expectations for this well anchored, the interest rate of reference was increased in December 2015 and again in February 2015 This year. This responded to the increase in the federal funds rate in The United States, in the first of these cases, and an excessive adjustment of the rate of exchange that threatened to affect inflation and its expectations in the second.6 I think it is important to point out that in the implementation of the policy The Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico has sought the efficient convergence of inflation to target, i.e. at lower cost possible for economic activity. In this regard, it should be noted that notwithstanding the above-mentioned increases in the reference rate, such as result of exchange rate depreciation, monetary conditions in Mexico remains relaxed. It should also be taken into account that the the impact of the higher reference rate has been offset, when 6 In December 2015, the U.S. Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee decided to increase by 25 basis points the target range for the federal funds rate, which had remained virtually zero since late 2008. Given the risks to the exchange rate and inflation of a potential disorderly adjustment of capital flows, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico decided to do the same at its monetary policy meeting that same month. In early 2016, conditions deteriorated. In particular, increased volatility in international financial markets and falling oil prices affected the economy through different channels. This, combined with other factors, especially the use of the peso as a risk hedging mechanism in other emerging economies, led to a sharp depreciation of the national currency, reaching parity with respect to the dollar at an all-time high during February. At the same time, the effectiveness of the foreign exchange intervention mechanisms in place since the end of 2014 was diminished, while expectations for the exchange rate deteriorated. Faced with the risk of increased inflationary pressures and inflation expectations, the Bank of Mexico decided to increase the target for the overnight interbank interest rate by 50 basis points to 3.75 percent as part of a coordinated policy effort to overcome the difficulties facing the economy. 7 less partially, due to the favourable effect on various risk premia of the timely change in the monetary policy stance. Likewise, the impact of the higher policy rate has been concentrated on short-term interest rates. For example, from December 16, 2015 to date, the yield on 10-year government bonds has shown a fall of more than 30 basis points, despite the 75 basis point increase in the benchmark rate. More generally, it should be remembered that achieving low and stable inflation represents the best contribution our Central Institute can make to the growth of the economy. What are the factors that are likely to determine the course of monetary policy in the coming months? As I mentioned earlier, the Mexican economy is expected to continue to face a negative output gap during the period of monetary policy influence. Therefore, the risk of demand pressures on prices, although present, seems at the moment of minor relative importance. In this way, the implementation of monetary policy is likely to be influenced to a greater extent by factors of an external nature. In this regard, I think it is important to highlight two of them. First, it is well known that there is a wide divergence of opinion on the precise timing at which the U.S. Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee will raise the federal funds rate again. Notwithstanding the above, the predominant expectation remains that of an increase in this rate in the short term. I believe that the 8 Circumstances today for monetary authorities in Mexico are not very different from those they faced when the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate last December. That is, taking into account the degree of openness of the Mexican economy, its close ties with the US and the atmosphere of nervousness in international financial markets, a narrowing of the differential of the reference interest rates between the two countries, could generate disorderly movements of capital and risks for inflation and financial stability. Second, regardless of the normalization of monetary policy in the United States, as I noted in previous paragraphs, in my view there is a high risk of further outbreaks of uncertainty in international financial markets. In particular, the lower nervousness that has been observed recently is not supported by an improvement in underlying conditions, so that the fragility of the global economic and financial situation persists. To this should be added the growing doubts about the effectiveness of monetary policy actions in some advanced economies. It should also be taken into account that events such as the possible exit of the United Kingdom from the European Union or geopolitical conflicts can affect the behavior of international financial markets. Naturally, monetary policy would have to be adjusted with opportunity in the event that any of these events would result in pressures on the exchange rate, inflation and expectations for it. The evolution of inflation in the coming months could also be affected by supply shocks, such as those observed at the beginning of this year, derived from increases in the prices of agricultural products. This 9 risk is always present, since the prices of these goods have a very volatile behavior. While it is true that shocks of this type can affect the trajectory of inflation, they do not justify a monetary policy response, since the experience of recent years in Mexico shows that their impact is short-term and does not affect the process of price formation in the economy. In any case, the Bank of Mexico has clearly stated that it will closely monitor all the determinants of inflation and its expectations, and will adjust its monetary policy stance with all flexibility and at the time when conditions require it, to consolidate the efficient convergence of inflation to the 3 percent target. In sum, despite difficult external conditions, the Mexican economy has continued to show stable growth rates and low inflation. However, the importance of strengthening the country's economic fundamentals and domestic sources of growth has increased in the current challenging circumstances. From Mexico's recent experience, it is clear that this requires coordinated actions in different areas. Therefore, in addition to the efforts in monetary matters, it will be essential to continue with the fiscal consolidation measures, in order to ensure compliance with the goals that have been set for the financial requirements of the public sector and public debt in the coming years. Likewise, it will be necessary to maintain financial stability, and ensure an adequate implementation of the structural change and institutional transformation actions underway to increase, in accordance with our needs, the country's economic growth potential. 10

En segundo lugar, persisten riesgos a la baja para la actividad econmica en Mxico, entre los que me parecen particularmente importantes 2 Tras registrar un supervit equivalente a 2.0 por ciento del PIB en 2006, la balanza comercial petrolera mostr un continuo deterioro hasta volverse deficitaria en 2015, en una magnitud equivalente a 0.9 por ciento del PIB. 3 Durante el primer trimestre de 2016, las exportaciones mexicanas (excluyendo petrleo crudo) alcanzaron una participacin promedio de 13.92 por ciento en las importaciones no petroleras de Estados Unidos, cifra superior a la de 12.81 por ciento registrada en el mismo trimestre de 2015. 4 la posibilidad de un nuevo episodio de turbulencia en los mercados financieros internacionales, que incida en el desempeo de los mercados y del sector real, as como una recuperacin de la produccin industrial estadounidense ms lenta de lo previsto, aunque tambin existen riesgos de naturaleza interna.
