Asimismo, la incidencia de la mayor tasa de poltica monetaria se ha concentrado en las tasas de inters de corto plazo. Por ejemplo, del 16 de diciembre de 2015 a la fecha, el rendimiento de los bonos gubernamentales a 10 aos ha mostrado una cada de ms de 30 puntos base, a pesar del incremento de 75 puntos base en la tasa de referencia. En trminos ms generales, cabe recordar que el logro de una inflacin baja y estable representa la mejor contribucin que nuestro Instituto Central puede hacer al crecimiento de la economa. Cules son los factores que probablemente determinarn el curso de la poltica monetaria en los prximos meses? Como mencion anteriormente, se espera que la economa mexicana siga enfrentando una brecha negativa del producto durante el periodo de influencia de la poltica monetaria. Por tanto, el riesgo de presiones de demanda sobre los precios, aunque presente, parece en este momento de una importancia relativa menor. De esta forma, es probable que la implementacin de la poltica monetaria se vea influida en mayor medida por factores de naturaleza externa. Al respecto, me parece importante destacar dos de ellos. Primero, es bien conocido que existe una amplia divergencia de opiniones sobre el momento preciso en el que el Comit Federal de Mercado Abierto de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos aumentar nuevamente la tasa de fondos federales. No obstante lo anterior, la expectativa predominante sigue siendo la de un incremento de dicha tasa en el corto plazo. Considero que las 8 circunstancias en la actualidad para las autoridades monetarias en Mxico, no son muy distintas de las que se enfrentaban cuando la Reserva Federal aument su tasa de referencia en diciembre pasado. Es decir, tomando en cuenta el grado de apertura de la economa mexicana, sus cercanos vnculos con la estadounidense y el ambiente de nerviosismo en los mercados financieros internacionales, un estrechamiento del diferencial de las tasas de inters de referencia entre los dos pases, podra generar movimientos desordenados de capital y riesgos para la inflacin y la estabilidad financiera. En segundo lugar, independientemente de la normalizacin de la poltica monetaria en Estados Unidos, como seal en prrafos anteriores, en mi opinin existe un riesgo elevado de nuevos brotes de incertidumbre en los mercados financieros internacionales. En particular, el menor nerviosismo que se ha observado recientemente no est respaldado por una mejora en las condiciones subyacentes, por lo que la fragilidad de la situacin econmica y financiera mundial persiste. A lo anterior caber agregar las dudas crecientes sobre la efectividad de las acciones de poltica monetaria en algunas economas avanzadas. Tambin debe tomarse en cuenta que eventos tales como la posible salida del Reino Unido de la Unin Europea o conflictos de orden geopoltico, pueden incidir en el comportamiento de los mercados financieros internacionales. Naturalmente, la poltica monetaria tendra que ajustarse con oportunidad en caso de que alguno de estos eventos diera lugar a presiones sobre el tipo de cambio, la inflacin y las expectativas para esta. La evolucin de la inflacin en los prximos meses tambin podra verse afectada por choques de oferta, como los observados a principios de este ao, derivados de aumentos en los precios de los productos agropecuarios. Este 9 riesgo siempre est presente, ya que los precios de estos bienes tienen un comportamiento muy voltil. Si bien es cierto que choques de este tipo pueden afectar la trayectoria de la inflacin, no justifican una respuesta de la poltica monetaria, ya que la experiencia de los ltimos aos en Mxico muestra que su impacto es de corto plazo y no afecta el proceso de formacin de precios en la economa. En todo caso, el Banco de Mxico ha manifestado con claridad que seguir de cerca todos los determinantes de la inflacin y sus expectativas, y ajustar su postura de poltica monetaria con toda flexibilidad y en el momento en que las condiciones lo requieran, para consolidar la convergencia eficiente de la inflacin al objetivo de 3 por ciento. En suma, a pesar de las difciles condiciones externas, la economa mexicana ha continuado mostrando tasas de crecimiento estables y una baja inflacin. No obstante, la importancia de fortalecer los fundamentos econmicos del pas y las fuentes internas de crecimiento se ha acrecentado en las complicadas circunstancias actuales. De la experiencia reciente de Mxico, es evidente que lo anterior requiere de acciones coordinadas en distintos mbitos. Por ello, adems de los esfuerzos en materia monetaria, ser indispensable continuar con las medidas de consolidacin fiscal, a fin de asegurar el cumplimiento de las metas que se han fijado para los requerimientos financieros del sector pblico y la deuda pblica en los prximos aos. Asimismo, ser necesario mantener la estabilidad financiera, y asegurar una implementacin adecuada de las acciones de cambio estructural y transformacin institucional en marcha para incrementar, de conformidad con nuestras necesidades, el potencial de crecimiento econmico del pas. 10

Title: Convention of the Mexican Association of Stock Exchange Institutions (AMIB)
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the Convention of the Mexican Association of Stock Exchange Institutions (AMIB). Mexico City, October 5, 2021; alvaro Garcia Pimentel Caraza, President of the Board of Directors of the Mexican Association of Stock Exchange Institutions (AMIB); Gabriel Yorio Gonzalez, Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit; Juan Pablo Graf Noriega, President of the National Banking and Securities Commission (CNBV) Alejandro Aguilar Ceballos, Vice President of the Board of Directors of the Mexican Association of Stock Exchange Institutions (AMIB); Roberto Valdes Acra, Vice President of the Board of Directors of the Mexican Association of Stock Exchange Institutions (AMIB); Distinguished members of the Presidium; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 Good afternoon. I thank the Mexican Association of Stock Exchange Institutions (AMIB) for the invitation to participate in this Convention. Throughout its more than four decades of existence, the AMIB has managed to be an effective coordination body that has made it possible to reconcile interests, unify efforts and align incentives in favor of the development of the stock market sector, financial markets and the country's economy. The AMIB has been a representative body of its guild and has brought together the most outstanding leaders of the stock market sector. Therefore, I want to express my deepest and sincere condolences for the recent death of Javier Alvarado, a prominent economist and executive who, at the time of his death, headed the Monex brokerage house and served as vice president of this association. Javier will be an irreplaceable absence in the financial sector where he made so many contributions. In my particular case, I will not only miss him as a professional interlocutor, but as a dear friend. 2 I also want to highlight the management of alvaro Garcia Pimentel, since thanks to his extensive knowledge of the financial environment, his leadership and his ability to work as a team, he has promoted a comprehensive diagnosis of the challenges of the stock market sector, which will be very useful to identify opportunities and continue adopting the best practices in the field. 2020 was an unprecedented year in history and all economic agents faced unprecedented challenges as a result of the global health emergency. The solidity and resilience of the institutions of the stock exchange union allowed them to overcome the challenges and continue contributing to the development of the country. Currently, the AMIB associates the 36 brokerage houses that operate in Mexico and has as affiliates 32 investment fund operators, 3 money brokerage companies and 1 independent investment advisor. 3 Stock market institutions play a very important role in the Mexican economy. At the end of June 2021, the custody of securities of brokerage houses amounted to 29.2% of GDP and the resources managed by investment fund operators exceeded 10.90% of GDP. The AMIB and the authorities share the purpose of achieving more efficient and competitive financial markets. The openness and dialogue that has been maintained with the AMIB over the last few years has been fundamental to advance in the objective of deepening the development of the stock market in our country, both in terms of operability and security. On this occasion, I would like to refer, first of all, to the effects of the pandemic on financial markets and the actions of the central bank in order to mitigate them; secondly, to develop a joint agenda between the central institute, intermediaries and other authorities for the development of markets, and to address future challenges. 4 Actions of the Bank of Mexico during the pandemic The effect of the COVID-19 health crisis was very unfavorable for the assets of emerging countries, including Mexico. The sharp increase in risk aversion caused a significant depreciation in the exchange rate and outflows, especially in fixed income assets. The gradual adjustment of monetary policy in Mexico allowed a more orderly behavior in interest rates in Mexico than in other emerging economies, which facilitated a reduction in long-term rates, and in the risk premiums associated with them. Throughout the year, the peso has shown an orderly behavior and a market with depth, with a reduction in the levels of volatility registered in 2020, both in realized terms and in levels implicit in the prices of options. On the other hand, interest rates on government securities registered a stable behavior throughout the year. In recent weeks there have been adjustments in the foreign exchange market and an increase in interest rates. This in response to the effects and associated volatility 5 the process of withdrawal of monetary stimulus by the Fed, which in the coming weeks could announce the beginning of the process of reducing asset purchases. The previous movements have occurred in a context of better operation in these markets, although the pre-pandemic levels have not yet been reached. During the pandemic, the Bank of Mexico and other authorities announced measures aimed at providing liquidity to improve the functioning of domestic markets; strengthen credit channels in the economy; and promoting the orderly behaviour of debt and foreign exchange markets. This is in order to create the conditions that would facilitate that financial intermediaries could fulfill their priority role of providing financing to the economy. The set of actions approved by the Bank of Mexico contemplated support for up to 750 billion pesos (equivalent to 3.3% of GDP in 2019). 6 Let me detail these actions: o In terms of liquidity provision. 1. The Ordinary Additional Liquidity Facility, aimed at multiple banking institutions through secured loans or reports on an expanded range of eligible securities, was reactivated and made more accessible. 2. A facility associated with government securities reporting operations was adopted that reached the maximum use in its capacity of 100 mmp and currently the reports are for 34.5 billion pesos. The total cumulative use of this facility during the period that was in force was 465 billion pesos. 3. A facility related to reporting operations with corporate securities was adopted, with which operations were carried out for a total amount of 44.83 billion pesos. 4. A facility associated with the temporary exchange of securities that can be used in financing guarantees was implemented, which reached a total amount allocated of 63.2 billion pesos. 7 o With regard to actions to promote the orderly behaviour of markets, 1. Both the SHCP and the Bank of Mexico swapped long-term instruments for short-term securities, allowing participants to reduce their sensitivity to abrupt movements in interest rates. 2. The SHCP modified the figure of market trainers, extending the term of validity of the option of placement and special swaps for these intermediaries. 3. The Foreign Exchange Commission expanded the size of the foreign exchange hedge program from 20 to 30 billion dollars and approved the possibility of concluding these operations with foreign entities and liquidating them in dollars. 4. The Bank of Mexico has held several dollar financing auctions with the resources of the swap line with the Federal Reserve of New York up to an amount of 60,000 million dollars, of which a cumulative total of 15.2 billion dollars were allocated via auction. o With regard to the strengthening of credit channels, the use of facilities associated with the provision of resources for the 8 MSMEs and individuals affected by the COVID-19 health crisis, considering the most recent applications, the total amount allocated would exceed 50 billion pesos. Since its announcement, this whole set of measures has contributed to a more orderly behavior of the markets, by providing additional liquidity support and a signal of certainty. In this context, the institutions used resources from these facilities for a total amount allocated of approximately 683.4 billion pesos, while those instrumented by agreement of the Exchange Commission have been for 17.2 billion dollars. The holding of new operations under the measures implemented by the Bank of Mexico came to an end on September 30. 9 Joint actions for the development of financial markets and future challenges The Bank of Mexico and other financial authorities, together with the main associations of the financial market, have designed a work agenda with a series of deliverables and times. In this agenda, the participation of the AMIB and its members has been essential to identify those initiatives that can boost the debt and stock market in our country. The groups in which the work has been concentrated include: reporting operations under international standards; real-rate securities, derivatives, corporate securities and government debt lending operations; central securities counterparty and, transition to the new reference rates. Some of the deliverables, which are already visible on a day-to-day basis, include: 1. New reference for 20-year term udibonos. Publication of the value of the UDI one hour before, at 8 am with the aim of extending the hours of operations. 10 2. Exchange hedges that can be settled for differences on a daily basis, to avoid the asymmetric delivery of collateral to the Bank of Mexico. 3. Amendments to the Securities Lending Rules (published on Wednesday, September 22, 2021), which authorizes various improvements, including the possibility for stock brokers to make loans on indexed fiduciary stock certificates (ETFs) and real estate (Fibras), as well as the participation of insurers and guarantors in these operations. 4. At the Bank we enter the final phase of the analysis on credit derivatives operations (Credit Default Swaps and Total Return Swaps), in order to issue the corresponding rules. In addition, the Bank of Mexico will update the circulars on the requirements to enter into derivative transactions on its own account (31 requirements) and the margination rules for derivative transactions that are not settled with central counterparties. 5. Since January 2020, Banco de Mexico formally began the process of transition to the new rates of 11 reference through the publication of the TIIE of Fondeo. Subsequently, MexDer and CME launched futures contracts linked to this new benchmark in the market. 6. An additional step in this transition is the placement of government securities with this new reference rate for financing from the Federal Government, and for monetary regulation purposes in the case of the Bank of Mexico. The first bond F auction was held today (Tuesday, October 5). A thank you to the AMIB that allowed us through its extensive network of contacts to be able to transmit the relevant messages to the main intermediaries (in particular a videoconference was held with 350 participants from the institutions represented in the AMIB) so that they could be ready in terms of approvals and system for the placement of this new family of titles. Today's auction of Bondes F had a total demand of 41.4 billion pesos, with 20 bidders that included market makers, commercial banks, development banks and brokerage houses. This demand was also reflected in good placement conditions for the SHCP when surcharges were presented at levels. 12 similar to the previous primary auction of Bondes D (1 year surcharge of 0.10, 2 years in 0.14 and 3 years in 0.17). At the Bank, we are confident that this new title will facilitate the process of adoption and consolidation of the new Funding TIIE as a reference in the placement of securities and credit operations. 7. Additionally, on September 30, 2020, the Bank of Mexico published the "General provisions applicable to the electronic issuance of securities representing securities subject to deposit in institutions for the deposit of securities". Other notable joint projects that are being worked on are: 1. Update of the rules applicable to reports under international standards. 2. Securities lending that includes the possibility of holding open loan operations, through a "tripartite" scheme, among other elements that should deepen the development of our markets. 13 3. The new rules for central securities counterparties (in conjunction with the CNBV). All these elements of improvement and clarity in the regulatory aspect will undoubtedly be key to the development of our markets. Moving forward, several challenges remain that need to be addressed: 1. Liquidity and depth in the stock market government; a key element will be the electronification of that market. It is necessary to work together to find the mechanisms that accelerate this transition process and promote greater liquidity and depth to the markets. 2. Create elements that continue to attract foreign capital to our markets, with a comprehensive perspective and continue to deepen the development of these markets to continue being a recipient of capital flows. 14 The institutional work agendas that have been proposed have as a priority to unblock those elements that have prevented the growth of the corporate debt market in our country and the issuance of shares. It is necessary that both financial authorities and private sector institutions continue to collaborate for the development of our capital market, encouraging companies to strengthen their corporate governance and thus obtain stock market financing and strengthen their financial structure and competitiveness. It is essential that more and more Mexican companies can go out to place on the stock exchange, in the first instance stock certificates and in the background, shares. In addition, it is convenient to visualize the opportunities that open up for the national financial markets and the stock market sector in areas such as pension savings. The recent pension reforms implemented can be a key element in the growth of the capital market in our country. These reforms will result in: 1. An increase in the pension due to the increase in contributions to the individual accounts of workers and the greater flexibility of the guaranteed minimum pension. 15 2. Higher recovery rates for workers who for some reason do not meet the requirements for a pension. 3. A greater number of workers with access to a pension, by reducing the weeks of contribution required before the IMSS. 4. Regarding the assets under management of the SIEFORES, the approved reform entails a sustained growth of domestic savings that will allow a greater availability of resources that could be channeled to the financial assets of our country, both public and private with a long-term perspective. This valuable opportunity for growth in forced savings will be invaluable for the well-being of workers and the comprehensive development of financial markets in our country. Ladies and gentlemen: I would like to close this speech by alluding to a historic anniversary. Just last week we celebrated the Bicentennial of the Consummation of Mexican Independence. This event, which ended more than a decade of war, was possible thanks to the fact that a society, deeply divided with divergent positions, knew 16 overcome their differences and establish agreements in search of a common goal. This event has a very clear and topical message: the economic and social progress of a country only occurs if basic consensus and a shared vision of the future are achieved, which allow catalyzing and converging individual efforts with the common good. The AMIB has been a paradigmatic organism of this positive and proactive attitude. Over the years, it has led to a more adequate channeling of financing in the economy, through an effective, solid and resilient stock market sector. Thank you for everything and I wish you every success in the course of the work of this important Convention. 17
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la Convencin de la Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones Burstiles (AMIB). Ciudad de Mxico, 5 de octubre de 2021; lvaro Garca Pimentel Caraza, Presidente del Consejo Directivo de la Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones Burstiles (AMIB); Gabriel Yorio Gonzlez, Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico; Juan Pablo Graf Noriega, Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV) Alejandro Aguilar Ceballos, Vicepresidente del Consejo Directivo de la Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones Burstiles (AMIB); Roberto Valds Acra, Vicepresidente del Consejo Directivo de la Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones Burstiles (AMIB); Distinguidos miembros del Presidium; Seoras y seores: 1 Muy buenas tardes. Agradezco a la Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones Burstiles (AMIB) la invitacin para participar en esta Convencin. A lo largo de sus ya ms de cuatro dcadas de existencia, la AMIB ha logrado ser una instancia eficaz de coordinacin que ha permitido conciliar intereses, unificar esfuerzos y alinear incentivos en favor del desarrollo del sector burstil, de los mercados financieros y de la economa del pas. La AMIB ha sido un organismo representativo de su gremio y ha reunido a los ms destacados lderes del sector burstil. Por eso, quiero expresarles mi ms sentido y sincero psame por el reciente fallecimiento de Javier Alvarado, prominente economista y ejecutivo que, al momento de su muerte, encabezaba la casa de bolsa Monex y funga como vicepresidente de esta asociacin. Javier ser una ausencia irremplazable en el sector financiero donde hizo tantas aportaciones. En mi caso particular, no slo lo extraar como interlocutor profesional, sino como entraable amigo. 2 Tambin quiero destacar la gestin de lvaro Garca Pimentel, ya que gracias a su amplio conocimiento del medio financiero, a su liderazgo y a su capacidad de trabajo en equipo ha impulsado un diagnstico integral de los retos del sector burstil, que ser muy til para identificar oportunidades y seguir adoptando las mejores prcticas en la materia. El 2020 fue un ao indito en la historia y todos los agentes econmicos enfrentaron retos sin precedentes a raz de la emergencia sanitaria global. La solidez y resiliencia de las instituciones del gremio burstil les permiti superar los desafos y seguir contribuyendo al desarrollo del pas. Actualmente, la AMIB asocia a las 36 casas de bolsa que operan en Mxico y tiene como afiliados a 32 operadoras de fondos de inversin, 3 empresas de corretaje de dinero y 1 asesor en inversiones independiente. 3 Las instituciones burstiles juegan un papel muy relevante en la economa mexicana. Al cierre de junio de 2021, la custodia de valores de las casas de bolsa ascendi al 29.2% del PIB y los recursos administrados por las operadoras de fondos de inversin superaron el 10.90% del PIB. La AMIB y las autoridades compartimos el propsito de alcanzar mercados financieros ms eficientes y competitivos. La apertura y el dilogo que se ha mantenido con la AMIB a lo largo de los ltimos aos ha sido fundamental para avanzar en el objetivo de profundizar el desarrollo del mercado de valores en nuestro pas, tanto en trminos de operatividad como de seguridad. En esta ocasin, me quiero referir, en primer lugar, a los efectos de la pandemia en los mercados financieros y las acciones del banco central para mitigarlos; en segundo lugar, al desarrollo de una agenda conjunta entre el instituto central, los intermediarios y otras autoridades para el desarrollo de los mercados, y hacer frente a retos futuros. 4 Acciones del Banco de Mxico durante la pandemia El efecto de la crisis sanitaria de COVID-19 fue muy desfavorable para los activos de pases emergentes, entre ellos Mxico. El abrupto aumento en la aversin al riesgo provoc una significativa depreciacin en el tipo de cambio y flujos de salida, especialmente en activos de renta fija. El ajuste gradual de la poltica monetaria en Mxico permiti un comportamiento ms ordenado en las tasas de inters en Mxico que en otras economas emergentes, lo que facilit una reduccin en las tasas de largo plazo, y en las primas de riesgo asociadas a las mismas. A lo largo del ao, el peso ha mostrado un comportamiento ordenado y un mercado con profundidad, con una reduccin en los niveles de volatilidad registrados en 2020, tanto en trminos realizados como en niveles implcitos en los precios de opciones. Por su parte, las tasas de inters de valores gubernamentales, registraron un comportamiento estable a lo largo del ao. En las ltimas semanas se han presentado ajustes en el mercado cambiario y un aumento en las tasas de inters. Ello en respuesta a los efectos y volatilidad asociada 5 al proceso de retiro del estmulo monetario por parte de la FED, que en las prximas semanas podra anunciar el inicio del proceso de reduccin de compras de activos. Los movimientos anteriores se han dado en un contexto de mejor operacin en estos mercados, aunque an no se han alcanzado los niveles previos a la pandemia. Durante la pandemia, el Banco de Mxico y otras autoridades, anunciaron medidas orientadas a proveer liquidez para mejorar el funcionamiento de los mercados internos; fortalecer los canales de otorgamiento de crdito en la economa; y promover el comportamiento ordenado de los mercados de deuda y de cambios. Lo anterior, a fin de crear las condiciones que facilitaran que los intermediarios financieros pudieran cumplir su funcin prioritaria de proveer financiamiento a la economa. El conjunto de acciones aprobadas por el Banco de Mxico contemplaba apoyos hasta por 750 mil millones de pesos (equivalente al 3.3% del PIB de 2019). 6 Permtanme detallar estas acciones: o En materia de provisin de liquidez. 1. Se reactiv y se hizo ms accesible la Facilidad de Liquidez Adicional Ordinaria, dirigida a las instituciones de banca mltiple a travs de crditos garantizados o reportos sobre una gama ampliada de ttulos elegibles. 2. Se adopt una facilidad asociada a operaciones de reporto de ttulos gubernamentales que alcanz el uso mximo en su capacidad de 100 mmp y actualmente los reportos son por 34.5 mil millones de pesos. El uso total acumulado de esta facilidad durante el plazo que estuvo vigente fue de 465 mil millones de pesos. 3. Se adopt una facilidad relacionada con operaciones de reporto con ttulos corporativos, con la que se celebraron operaciones por un monto total de 44.83 mil millones de pesos. 4. Se instrument una facilidad asociada al intercambio temporal de ttulos susceptibles de utilizarse en garantas de financiamientos, que alcanz un monto total asignado de 63.2 mil millones de pesos. 7 o En lo que atae a las acciones para promover el comportamiento ordenado de los mercados, 1. Tanto la SHCP como el Banco de Mxico realizaron permutas de instrumentos de largo plazo por ttulos de corto plazo, permitindole a los participantes reducir su sensibilidad a movimientos abruptos en tasa de inters. 2. La SHCP modific la figura de formadores de mercado, ampliando el plazo de vigencia de la opcin de colocacin y permutas especiales para estos intermediarios. 3. La Comisin de Cambios ampli el tamao del programa de coberturas cambiarias de 20 a 30 mil millones de dlares y aprob la posibilidad de celebrar estas operaciones con entidades del extranjero y liquidarlas en dlares. 4. El Banco de Mxico ha celebrado diversas subastas de financiamiento en dlares con los recursos de la lnea swap con la Reserva Federal de Nueva York hasta por un monto de 60,000 millones de dlares, de los cuales se asignaron va subasta un total acumulado de 15.2 miles de millones de dlares. o En lo que atae al fortalecimiento de los canales de crdito, el uso de las facilidades asociadas a la provisin de recursos para las 8 MiPyMes y personas fsicas afectadas por la crisis sanitaria de COVID-19, considerando las solicitudes ms recientes el monto total asignado superara 50 mil millones de pesos. Desde su anuncio, todo este conjunto de medidas coadyuvaron a propiciar un comportamiento ms ordenado de los mercados, al proveer un soporte de liquidez adicional y una seal de certidumbre. En este contexto, las instituciones utilizaron recursos de estas facilidades por un monto total asignado de aproximadamente 683.4 mil millones de pesos, mientras que los instrumentados por acuerdo de la Comisin de Cambios han sido por 17.2 miles de millones de dlares. La celebracin de nuevas operaciones al amparo de las medidas implementadas por el Banco de Mxico lleg a su fin el pasado 30 de septiembre. 9 Acciones conjuntas para el desarrollo de los mercados financieros y retos futuros El Banco de Mxico y otras autoridades financieras, en conjunto con las principales asociaciones del mercado financiero han diseado una agenda de trabajo con una serie de entregables y tiempos. En esta agenda, la participacin de la AMIB y sus agremiados ha sido esencial para identificar aquellas iniciativas que pueden dinamizar el mercado de deuda y accionario en nuestro pas. Los grupos en los que se han concentrado los trabajos abarcan: operaciones de reporto bajo estndares internacionales; operaciones de prstamo de valores, derivados, ttulos corporativos y deuda gubernamental a tasa real; contraparte central de valores y, transicin a las nuevas tasas de referencia. Algunos de los entregables, que ya son visibles en el da a da, incluyen: 1. Nueva referencia para Udibonos a plazo de 20 aos. Publicacin del valor de la UDI una hora antes, a las 8 am con el objetivo de ampliar el horario de operaciones. 10 2. Coberturas cambiarias liquidables por diferencias de manera diaria, para evitar la entrega asimtrica de colateral al Banco de Mxico. 3. Modificaciones a las Reglas de Prstamo de Valores (publicada el mircoles 22 de septiembre de 2021), la cual autoriza diversas mejoras, incluida la posibilidad de que los intermediarios burstiles puedan realizar prstamos sobre certificados burstiles fiduciarios indizados (ETFs) e inmobiliarios (Fibras), as como la participacin de aseguradoras y afianzadoras en estas operaciones. 4. En el Banco entramos en la fase final del anlisis sobre operaciones de derivados de crdito (Credit Default Swaps y Total Return Swaps), a fin de emitir las reglas correspondientes. De manera adicional, el Banco de Mxico actualizar las circulares sobre los requisitos para celebrar operaciones derivadas por cuenta propia (31 requerimientos) y las reglas de marginacin para operaciones de derivados que no se liquidan con contrapartes centrales. 5. Desde enero de 2020, Banco de Mxico comenz de manera formal el proceso de transicin hacia las nuevas tasas de 11 referencia a travs de la publicacin de la TIIE de Fondeo. Posteriormente, MexDer y CME lanzaron contratos de futuros vinculados a esta nueva referencia en el mercado. 6. Un paso adicional en esta transicin es la colocacin de valores gubernamentales con esta nueva tasa de referencia para financiamiento del Gobierno Federal, y con fines de regulacin monetaria en el caso del Banco de Mxico. La primera subasta de Bondes F se realiz el da de hoy (martes 5 de octubre). Un agradecimiento a la AMIB que nos permiti a travs de su extensa red de contactos poder transmitir los mensajes relevantes a los principales intermediarios (en particular se realiz una videoconferencia con 350 participantes de las instituciones representadas en la AMIB) para que pudieran estar listos en trminos de aprobaciones y sistema para la colocacin de esta nueva familia de ttulos. Title: Reserve management and FX intervention in Mexico
text: RESERVE MANAGEMENT AND FX INTERVENTION IN MEXICO1 Javier Guzman Calafell2 This note outlines Mexicos recent experience with three closely interrelated issues. First, on the basis of a legal framework regulating transactions in foreign currency between the central bank and government entities, and preannounced market-based mechanisms, the stock of international reserves has reached adequate levels. Second, interventions have been made to restore orderly operating conditions in the FX market whenever this has been needed, with satisfactory results and consistent at all times with the free-floating exchange rate regime in place. Third, the continuous improvement of standards and practices has been instrumental in achieving the objectives set for reserve management at the Banco de Mexico (ie liquidity, capital preservation and return enhancement). Keywords: International reserve management, FX intervention mechanisms, portfolio allocation. JEL classification: E58, F31, G11. 1 This is a slightly edited and updated version of a note prepared for the 2019 BIS Annual Meeting of Deputy Governors, hosted by the Bank for International Settlements in Basel, Switzerland, on 1415 February 2019. It was published on 31 October 2019 as part of BIS Paper No. 104 Reserve management and FX intervention. 2 Deputy Governor at the Banco de Mexico. The views and opinions expressed in this document are the sole responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Banco de Mexico or of its Governing Board. 1 The Banco de Mexicos international reserves have increased significantly, although with fluctuations, in recent decades. The current stock, of around USD 181 billion, represents a tenfold increase from early 1997. At the same time, the level of reserves has remained roughly constant over the last three years. This is explained by a combination of factors. Given the uncertainty regarding the optimal level of reserves, a tendency to err on the side of caution is desirable. In fact, evidence in the economic literature shows that large stocks of international reserves enhance an economys resilience to external shocks, including through the diminished probability or cost of potential sudden stops of capital inflows. Decisions by Mexicos Foreign Exchange (FX) Commission3 regarding the level of the stock of international reserves, take into account a range of tests and metrics. However, in view of their varying nature and at times diverging results, these are used only as a reference and never as an explicit goal. In fact, no single metric is uniquely relied upon to gauge international reserves adequacy, thus rendering the FX Commissions judgment crucial in this task. Reserve accumulation in Mexico has originated from two sources. On the one hand, as per the Banco de Mexicos Law, all non-financial entities of the Federal Public Administration are required to operate with foreign currencies following the rules and policies set forth by the central bank, as well as to sell them directly to the latter under prevailing market conditions. 3 The FX Commission, the body responsible of Mexican foreign exchange policy, includes three members of the Ministry of Finance (the Minister and two Deputy Ministers) and three from the Bank of Mexico (the Governor and two Deputy Governors). The Minister of Finance chairs the Commission and has the casting vote. In his or her absence, the Governor of the central bank takes on these roles. 2 Naturally, the motivation for such a requirement rests on those institutions potentially large trade surpluses or deficits. Due to this regulatory framework, international reserves were sourced, for many years, to a significant extent from Pemex, the national oil company. The Federal Government has been another important driver of the international reserves stock. On the other hand, when the level of reserves has been deemed insufficient, the FX Commission has resorted to a rules-based approach to buy US dollars from the market, in the form of preannounced auction mechanisms with relevant terms and conditions (such as timing and size) made public in advance. Specifically, these have consisted in the sale of US dollar put options to the market through monthly auctions during the periods August 1996June 2001 and February 2010November 2011. These instruments give financial institutions the right to sell US dollars to the central bank over the course of the following month, conditional on two requirements. First, the options strike price is the FIX exchange rate determined by the Banco de Mexico on the business day prior to the exercise.4 Second, the option can be executed only when the exchange rate of exercise has appreciated with respect to its 20-day moving average. Of course, the benefits of holding an ample stock of international reserves come at a cost. In order to avoid potential pressures that could weaken monetary policy, the Banco de Mexico has sterilized the added liquidity injected into the economy, as foreign currency is purchased with domestic 4 The FIX exchange rate is determined by the Banco de Mexico as an average of quotes in the wholesale foreign exchange market for operations payable in 48 hours. The central bank reports the FIX from 12:00PM onward each banking day. It is published in the Official Gazette (Diario Oficial de la Federacion) one banking business day after its determination date, and it is used to settle liabilities denominated in US dollars payable in Mexico on the day after its publication in the Official Gazette. 3 currency, by issuing interest-bearing liabilities. The cost of accumulating international reserves arises from the fact that the return on investing international reserves is typically lower than the interest paid on said central bank liabilities. In view of the above-mentioned trade-off, the FX Commission has at times decided to reduce the pace of accumulation when international reserves have reached levels at which the benefits of future expected accumulation have started to be surpassed by their financial costs (ie the cost of carry). For instance, from May 2003 through July 2008, following a period of rapid reserve accumulation owing mainly to large US dollar sales from Pemex to the central bank, the FX Commission introduced a mechanism through which the Banco de Mexico sold, via preannounced daily auctions over the course of a given quarter, half the net amount accumulated during the previous quarter.5 Notwithstanding the merits of holding adequate levels of international reserves, as underscored by the experience of recent years, it is worthwhile to consider additional measures. In Mexicos case, these include an IMF Flexible Credit Line (FCL), which since 2009 has enhanced the economic position of the country in the event of external shocks, at a financial cost lower than that of holding international reserves. Currently at around USD 74 billion, this FCL yields, among other benefits, potential additional resources in foreign currency to face any contingency in the foreign exchange market, an 5 Nearly a year after the introduction of this mechanism, the previous quarter reference was changed to a moving average of the previous four quarters to smooth out the seasonality inherent in international reserve accumulation and thus avoid large fluctuations in amounts sold. 4 endorsement by the IMF of Mexicos economic policies, and another mechanism of discipline for the authorities. In addition, Mexico has negotiated several regional arrangements. For instance, under the North American Framework Agreement (NAFA), and with the purpose of promoting orderly currency exchange markets, the Banco de Mexico has a bilateral currency swap line with the US Federal Reserve and a parallel agreement with the US Department of the Treasury. The former, amounting to USD 3 billion, has been renewed annually since it was established in 1994, with Mexico drawing upon the line for the last time in 1995. In the case of the latter, the resources available were tripled in 2018 to USD 9 billion. Further to these, reciprocal currency arrangements (swap lines) for an amount of up to USD 30 billion were temporarily established between the Banco de Mexico and the Federal Reserve at the height of the global financial crisis (from 29 October 2008 to 1 February 2010), to help provide US dollar funding to financial institutions in Mexico. It is important to note that neither the FCL nor the other arrangements are to be seen as a substitute for international reserves, but rather as a complement to them. The second issue under consideration in this note relates to intervention in the foreign exchange market.6 The Mexican economy operates under a flexible exchange rate regime. In this context, market forces determine the equilibrium real rate, the exchange rate plays a key role as a shock absorber, 6 For a detailed account of Mexicos experience with FX intervention under the current free-floating exchange rate regime, see R. Cano, D. Gallardo and J. Acosta, Mexico: free-floating exchange regime, in M. Chamon, D. Hofman, N. Magud and A. Werner (eds), Foreign exchange intervention in inflation targeters in Latin America, International Monetary Fund, 2019, Chapter 11. 5 and the value of the currency is supported mainly by economic fundamentals. At the same time, mechanisms for intervention in the foreign exchange market have been used to manage the level of international reserves, as already described, or to foster orderly market operating conditions. In line with those related to the management of the level of international reserves, Mexicos FX Commission has relied mainly on preannounced, rulesbased tools for interventions to smooth volatility or to provide liquidity to the market. These include the daily US dollar auctions (both with and without a minimum bid price) held on a number of occasions in the past,7 as well as the previously mentioned USD-denominated credit lines offered to banks (also allocated through auctions), which they could on-lend to corporates.8 Although the vast majority of Mexicos experience in this regard has taken place in the spot market, interventions through derivatives have also been carried out. In fact, the FX Commission recently introduced auctions of nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) which, by being settled in MXN, protect the stock of international reserves. In place since February 2017, the size of this program is USD 20 billion, of which only USD 5.5 billion has been auctioned and subsequently rolled over. Although the FX Commission has typically resorted to rules-based and preannounced operations like the ones described above to intervene in the FX market, extraordinary measures to provide it with liquidity and restore its 7 Auctions with a minimum bid price were used during February 1997June 2001, October 2008April 2010, November 2011April 2013, and December 2014February 2016, while corresponding mechanisms without a minimum bid price were in place during March 2009September 2009 and March 2015November 2015. 8 This mechanism was resorted to in April 2009, when USD 3.2 billion were allocated via auction. It is noteworthy that international reserves were not used, as the resources came from the above-noted swap line established with the Federal Reserve. 6 smooth functioning have also been harnessed, although only in exceptional circumstances. These include the USD auctions of October 2008, as well as four episodes9 of discretionary outright sales of US dollars, the last of which (in January 2017) was conducted, for the first time, with institutions located outside the country, thereby attesting to the Banco de Mexicos capabilities to intervene at any time, through several mechanisms (including both electronic and more traditional platforms), and not only via domestic counterparties. Mexicos experience with interventions has been positive, not only as a result of the expertise gained through their execution, but also in terms of their effectiveness in containing surges of volatility in the FX market. On the one hand, when the Banco de Mexico has sought to accumulate international reserves or to reduce the pace of accumulation through purchases or sales of US dollars, respectively, the interventions have served their intended purpose. On the other hand, when the aim of interventions has been to provide liquidity to the market to ensure adequate operating conditions, the evidence suggests that, in most cases, they have reduced extremely high volatility and bid-ask spreads (a proxy for illiquidity). However, caution should be used when arriving at conclusions derived from analyses of the effectiveness of interventions, as this is not a straightforward question. For example, even if volatility does not diminish after an intervention, it is not necessarily the case that the intervention was ineffective. The problem is that, in practice, central banks have no counterfactual scenario against which to compare the outcome of a given intervention. 9 September 1998, February 2009, February 2016 and January 2017. 7 Since the impact of FX interventions on liquidity has been sterilized by the Banco de Mexico, they have had no implications for the implementation of monetary policy. This is evidenced, for instance, by the fact that the interbank funding rate has been very close to the central banks target since its adoption in 2008 (Graph 1). Interbank funding rate and monetary policy objective (%) Interbank funding rate Monetary policy objective Graph 1 9.0 8.0 7.0 6.0 5.0 4.0 3.0 2.0 1.0 0.0 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 Source: Banco de Mexico. It is important to stress that the actions described above have been taken without setting a target for the exchange rate. As a result, FX interventions 8 have been implemented in a way fully consistent with the free-floating exchange rate regime. Regarding the Banco de Mexicos standards and practices in reserves management, the Bank has three main objectives: liquidity, capital preservation and return enhancement. The balance among these aims is determined, to a significant extent, by the interplay between the international environment and the Mexican economy, ongoing perspectives on financial markets, and the central banks needs. Liquidity stands out as the most important of these objectives, and it is taken into account in any context to determine the composition of the reserves portfolio, while the relative focus on capital preservation vis-a-vis return enhancement  usually conflicting objectives  may change depending on the economic and financial context. For example, between 2000 and 2012, Mexicos international reserves grew rapidly, from USD 31 billion to USD 164 billion. Naturally, given the amount of accumulated reserves and the low levels of international interest rates, the cost of carry was significant. In this context, the Banco de Mexico focused its strategic asset allocation on enhancing the return of the portfolio to mitigate carry costs. This was achieved by including new asset classes and currencies that allowed the central bank to increase the expected return of the international reserves portfolio without significantly increasing market risk, thereby harvesting the benefits of diversification. In contrast, starting in 2013, the looming normalization of the Federal Reserves monetary policy stance was expected to result in an appreciation of the US dollar and an increase in interest rates, which could pose a significant 9 risk to the returns of the international reserves portfolio, and give rise to capital losses. In addition, the price of gold could drop due to the higher opportunity cost of holding the precious metal, while reserve accumulation had come to a halt given lower oil prices and, as previously described, the need to use the Banco de Mexicos reserves on several occasions to provide liquidity to the FX market and restore its adequate functioning. As a result, the Bank shifted the balance of objectives towards capital preservation, which was achieved by identifying the main risk factors of its portfolio, and adding forward-looking measures to its optimization models. All in all, the efforts made were successful in mitigating capital losses, and the measures taken allowed the Banco de Mexico to successfully diminish the volatility of returns on the reserves portfolio. Currently, in view of the uncertainty surrounding the path for US monetary policy going forward and other factors, the focus of the Banco de Mexicos asset allocation strategy is still to preserve capital while maintaining a more balanced portfolio that should be less affected by different economic and financial outcomes. Within this context, the Banco de Mexico significantly adjusted its strategic asset allocation methodology. Firstly, changes in financial markets dynamics after the global financial crisis made apparent that the usage of historical data had to be revamped. Thus, the models of the central bank were adapted to use the information embedded in market prices as their primary source. This provided a forward-looking element to the methodology, and allowed for a more intuitive and sound estimation of the expected distribution of returns, while minimizing subjective elements within the decision-making process. 10 Secondly, the inputs used in the portfolios optimization were enhanced by enabling them to match empirical facts, such as the non-normality of asset returns, in view of the evidence suggesting that their actual distributions tend to be fatter at the tails than would be predicted under the previously held assumption of a normal distribution. Lastly, the Banco de Mexico redefined the risk metric of the portfolio altogether. From using volatility, and thereby the typical mean-variance approach (Markowitz), towards optimizing the portfolio using a risk metric that focuses on the left-hand side of the distribution of returns, such as the conditional value-at-risk, thus explicitly matching the objective function of the portfolio with the objective of capital preservation. In tandem with these and other practices adopted internally, the Banco de Mexicos framework for reserves management has been further enhanced in recent years through the incorporation of non-benchmarked mandates, awarded to external managers. These provide direct diversification benefits derived from uncorrelated investment strategies which, on the basis of absolute returns but within the boundaries of eligible asset classes, construct portfolios that can be deemed unusual for a central bank. In addition, this type of mandates allow part of the reserves portfolio to adjust rapidly to changing market conditions, while the external managers capability to implement investment strategies having a low correlation with other portfolios positions effectively expands the investment efficiency frontier. Lastly, our staffs increased exposure to novel approaches and methodologies as part of this process has been of great value, not least due to the resulting learning and insights. 11 Some important challenges remain. Among these, a most significant one relates to the general publics understanding and perception about the broader contours of the issues at hand, including the rationale behind the FX Commissions directives, as well as their implementation by the Banco de Mexico. Particularly, in spite of the assessed adequacy of the current level of international reserves as per a variety of objective metrics, there is a risk that public opinion could deem them excessive and/or invested sub-optimally from a social standpoint. Should views like these become entrenched, the central bank could face pressures to generate higher returns or distribute the reserves to meet other objectives. In such a situation, a direct and clear communication strategy is important, to better explain the purpose, scope and usage of international reserves, especially their role in the financial and economic stability of the country. In this regard, further to the mandated disclosures derived from Mexicos transparency law, the Banco de Mexico has been working on different projects to provide more clarity to the public, including efforts to increase awareness and understanding of international reserves management practices. 12

Title: Art and matter: a walk through sculpture
text: Art and matter: a walk through the sculpture Words of Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the opening of the exhibition Sculpture: A window to the materialized creative process Banco de Mexico Mexico Library, Mexico City December 5, 2013 On behalf of the Bank of Mexico, I am honored to welcome you to the exhibition: "Sculpture: A window to the materialized creative process". It has already become a warm tradition that, every end of the year, distinguished personalities, friends and collaborators of this central bank coexist around an artistic activity organized in this library. The Bank of Mexico, in addition to fulfilling the objectives entrusted to it by the Constitution, has deployed a solid cultural vocation, either by participating in urban rescue projects, protecting an appreciable pictorial heritage, or by publishing books of great historical and testimonial value. Our library is an axis of this task of cultural promotion. With this exhibition, the seventh in this space, the library ratifies its desire to dialogue with avant-garde culture and strengthen ties with key institutions in the generation of art and knowledge. The exhibition that we will see today arises from the cooperation between the National Autonomous University of Mexico and the Bank of Mexico and fills us with satisfaction because it brings together two of the Schools with the greatest trajectory: the National School of Plastic Arts and the National School of Music. 2 The art of sculpture On this occasion, the art of sculpture has played the leading role, an ancient profession that has fulfilled various functions, whether magical, religious, funerary, civic or aesthetic. In this way, through a sculptural work you can represent an image of popular devotion, commemorate an important event for the collective memory or express an aesthetic intention. Sculpture implies an intimate contact with matter, in which all faculties and senses participate, and the individual becomes a creator, both with his imagination and with his hands. These constraints require, in addition to inspiration, a refined technique, discipline and constant effort. Therefore, it is known that the great sculptor must be, at the same time, a great artist and a great craftsman. Perhaps it is because of these features of the craft that in the history of sculpture a continuity in rigor is manifested, there are relatively well-established traditions and canons and more or less objective forms of judgment can be resorted to. Like the rest of the arts, sculpture allows the world to be modeled according to the highest aesthetic, social and moral visions. Perhaps this creative act implies a gift of observation that tends to glimpse, in the landscape or inert matter, the desired figure or form, that figure or form that in the opinion of the artist is missing in the world, and sculpt it. 3 As the art scholar, Henri Focillon, said in his "Praise of the Hand": But the greatest gift of the human species consists in the creation of a concrete universe different from nature. The animal without hands, even at the most attainment levels, creates nothing but a monotonous industry and does not transcend the boundaries of art. He has not been able to build either a magical world or a useless world.1 Sculpture in Mexico In Mexico, the art of sculpture has ancient antecedents and monumental works acquired great political and religious relevance in pre-Hispanic culture. Pieces such as "The Stone of the Sun", already stripped of their ritual function, still convey their imposing aesthetic value. After the Conquest, the needs of evangelization led to the flourishing of a statuary of a religious nature, which still amazes with its richness, imagination, beauty and variety. Subsequently, secular themes were popularized with characters from Greek mythology, allegories and heroes of Mexican history, until reaching the trends of the twentieth century, where increasingly innovative languages and expressions gained ground. 1 Henri Focillon (2010), in La vida de las formas, followed by Elogio de la mano, Mexico, UNAM-Escuela Nacional de Artes Plasticas, p. 125. 4 From the anonymous pre-Hispanic masters or colonial religious statuary, through Manuel Tolsa or the classics of the twentieth century, to the most recent generations, the Mexican sculptural tradition has been very fruitful and heterogeneous. Content of the exhibition This exhibition has sought to represent the diversity that characterizes the sculptural language. On the one hand, reproductions of classical pieces are exhibited, guarded by the Academy of San Carlos and, on the other, samples of the life-giving contemporary Mexican sculpture, created by seventeen young artists, who develop their work presided over by renowned masters. It is evident that, in each of the workshops, the artists give bases to their inspiration, polish their craft and learn to master the most different materials and sculptural techniques, from the traditional ones, based on stone and metal, to the newest, which incorporate waste materials and innovations in form and function. The choice of raw material involves different technical challenges and aesthetic approaches; but, without a doubt, the common challenge is similar and consists in combining volume, space and meaning, in making matter more eloquent. There are many artistic and technical virtues that the trade demands; however, I sense that a human virtue must also be highly valued: patience, because we must 5 invest a lot of time and mood to learn to listen to the elements. As the great poet Rainer Maria Rilke said about Michelangelo: Would the stones have a soul? Why did that man hear the stones?2 Because the sculptor manifests a spirit, sometimes simultaneous, to differentiate or merge with the world, the contemplation of this art not only delights the viewer, but sometimes refines his senses. I am sure that, on this journey through sculpture, we will find not only an aesthetic enjoyment, but we will feel more perceptive around the forms, images and volumes that surround us. Invitation to travel The arts open horizons, generate intuitions and connect with the most genuinely human. Because we know that decision-making in any field has much to learn from the humanistic and artistic imagination, the Bank of Mexico has sought to incorporate the cultural offer as part of a closer relationship with society. For this central institute and its library, it is a pride to host such a valuable exhibition. I want to express a warm congratulations to all those who participated in the organization, as well as ratify to the artists our gratitude for sharing the rigor and refinement of their craft. 2 Rainer Maria Rilke (2000), "De uno que escucha las piedras" in Historias del Buen Dios, Mexico, Jus, p.78. 6 In a few more moments we can enjoy a toast and walk through the exquisite and surprising art of sculpture. To accompany us on this trip we have the participation of the Touche Magique Quartet, which promises to enter us in a very original way in this journey. In the meantime, let's open the exhibition. I appreciate the distinguished presence of all of you and I convey to you, on behalf of myself and the Bank of Mexico, my best wishes for health and prosperity for these holidays and for next year. 7

Piezas como La piedra del sol, ya despojadas de su funcin ritual, an trasmiten su imponente valor esttico. Tras la Conquista, las necesidades de evangelizacin propiciaron el florecimiento de una estatuaria de ndole religiosa, que todava asombra por su riqueza, imaginacin, belleza y variedad. Ulteriormente, se popularizaron los temas laicos con personajes de la mitologa griega, alegoras y hroes de la historia mexicana, hasta llegar a las tendencias del siglo XX, donde ganaron terreno lenguajes y expresiones cada vez ms innovadoras. 1 Henri Focillon (2010), en La vida de las formas, seguida de Elogio de la mano, Mxico, UNAM-Escuela Nacional de Artes Plsticas, p. 125. 4 Desde los annimos maestros prehispnicos o de la estatuaria religiosa colonial, pasando por Manuel Tols o los clsicos del siglo XX, hasta llegar a las ms recientes generaciones, la tradicin escultrica mexicana ha sido muy fecunda y heterognea. Contenido de la muestra En la presente exposicin se ha buscado representar la diversidad que caracteriza el lenguaje escultrico. Por un lado, se exhiben reproducciones de piezas clsicas, resguardadas por la Academia de San Carlos y, por el otro, muestras de la vivificante escultura contempornea mexicana, creadas por diecisiete jvenes artistas, quienes desarrollan su trabajo presididos por connotados maestros. Es evidente que, en cada uno de los talleres, los artistas dan bases a su inspiracin, pulen su oficio y aprenden a dominar los ms distintos materiales y tcnicas escultricas, desde las tradicionales, basadas en la piedra y el metal, hasta las ms nuevas, que incorporan materiales de desecho e innovaciones en forma y funcin. La eleccin de la materia prima implica distintos retos tcnicos y enfoques estticos; pero, sin duda, el desafo comn es semejante y consiste en conjugar volumen, espacio y significado, en hacer ms elocuente a la materia. Son muchas las virtudes artsticas y tcnicas que demanda el oficio; sin embargo, intuyo que tambin debe ser muy valorada una virtud humana: la paciencia, pues hay que 5 invertir mucho tiempo y disposicin anmica para aprender a escuchar a los elementos. Como deca el gran poeta Rainer Maria Rilke a propsito de Miguel Angel: Tendran alma las piedras? Por qu escuchaba las piedras aquel hombre?2 Debido a que el escultor manifiesta un nimo, a veces simultneo, de diferenciarse o de fusionarse con el mundo, la contemplacin de este arte no slo deleita al espectador, sino que, en ocasiones, afina sus sentidos. Estoy seguro que, en este viaje por la escultura, encontraremos no solo un goce esttico, sino que nos sentiremos ms perceptivos en torno a las formas, imgenes y volmenes que nos rodean. Invitacin al viaje Las artes abren horizontes, generan intuiciones y conectan con lo ms genuinamente humano. Porque sabemos que la toma de decisiones en cualquier mbito tiene mucho que aprender de la imaginacin humanstica y artstica, el Banco de Mxico ha buscado incorporar la oferta cultural como parte de una relacin ms estrecha con la sociedad. Para este instituto central y su biblioteca, es un orgullo albergar tan valiosa muestra. Quiero expresar una calurosa felicitacin a todos los que participaron en la organizacin, as como ratificar a los artistas nuestro agradecimiento por compartirnos el rigor y refinamiento de su oficio. 2 Rainer Maria Rilke (2000), De uno que escuchaba las piedras en Historias del Buen Dios, Mxico, Jus, p.78. 6 En unos momentos ms podremos disfrutar de un brindis y pasear por el arte exquisito y sorprendente de la escultura. Para acompaarnos en este viaje contamos con la participacin del Cuarteto Touche Magique, el cual promete adentrarnos de una forma muy original en este recorrido. Mientras tanto, demos por inaugurada la exposicin. Aprecio la distinguida presencia de todos ustedes y les transmito, a nombre mo y del Banco de Mxico, mis mejores deseos de salud y prosperidad para estas fiestas y para el ao que viene. 7

Title: Welcome remarks of the seminar: the opportunity of the Pacific Alliance
text: Seminar: The Opportunity of the Pacific Alliance Welcoming Words Agustin Carstens - Governor of Banco de Mexico D.F., December 11, 2013 Governor Agustin Carstens will share the welcoming words with Javier Leon Olavarria (Ambassador of Peru to Mexico) and Jose Antonio Blanco (Executive President, inPERu). ? I am grateful for the invitation of my colleague Julio Velarde to address such a distinguished audience on the occasion of the seminar "The Opportunity of the Pacific Alliance".1 It is an honor to share these opening words with Ambassador Javier Leon Olavarria and Jose Antonio Blanco, Executive President of inPERu. ? The Pacific Alliance has been consolidated as an important mechanism for cooperation and economic and commercial integration. The four countries that make up the bloc are characterized by giving high priority to macroeconomic stability. We have much in common and a great affinity of goals, scopes and challenges. It couldn't be any other way: we share a story that unites us. ? From an economic perspective, it can be said that for decades we suffered together the onslaught of several episodes of crisis. Our countries were partners during very turbulent times. From these periods we have certainly learned and become stronger, and we have 1 As an economic bloc, the Pacific Alliance has a population of more than 209 million inhabitants, which represents 36% of the total in Latin America. The GDP of this bloc represents 35% of the total of Latin America and 50% of the region's trade. 1 stronger institutions with more appropriate regulatory frameworks. Today, I consider the situation to be very different. Experience puts the bloc as a whole in a privileged position. Today, we can agree that together we have graduated and that our countries are now companions of a new reality that offers a more promising vision for the future. ? An excellent example of the new reality is Peru, whose economy has been one of the most dynamic within the Latin American region, with an average growth of 6.4% in the last 10 years. This performance is explained both by sound macroeconomic policies and by the implementation of structural reforms that have provided greater flexibility and efficiency to the Peruvian economy, making it an important recipient of foreign investment. It is, so to speak, the fruit of years of investing in improving and making more effective the institutional framework and scaffolding for the proper functioning of markets. ? Let me also highlight the role that monetary policy has played in Peru. The Central Reserve Bank of Peru has implemented a transparent and independent monetary policy that is conducted under an explicit inflation targeting scheme. The results of this effort stand out: during the last 10 years, the Peruvian economy has presented one of the lowest average inflation rates in the region.2 ? Like other emerging countries in Latin America and the rest of the world, Peru will face an uncertain and volatile global environment. In fact, and in 2 The average inflation rate is only 2.75% over the last 10 years. 2 In contrast to past times, several Latin American countries have recently been able to face these adverse events with a battery of counter-cyclical policies without this translating into a loss of market confidence; a situation unthinkable a few decades ago, in which imbalances in public or external accounts prevented the economic authorities from implementing this type of policy. Peru is an example of this too, it has even received, as you all know, an increase in its credit rating3 by the main rating agencies, which shows the confidence of the markets in the solidity of its economy. ? While the Countries of the Alliance have been able to cope with the recent crises in a satisfactory manner, the volatile external environment does not allow any complacency. This year's experience showed us that markets have differentiated between emerging economies with better economic fundamentals and lower vulnerabilities, as the latter have coped better with recent bouts of volatility. In this sense, the current environment makes it a necessity to have a solid external position, adequate international reserves, responsible public finances, as well as the credibility of monetary policy aimed at maintaining moderate inflation. Similarly, further progress is needed on structural reforms to strengthen and boost competitiveness and growth; and 3 Peru's ratings rose to BBB on: S&P August 19, 2013, Fitch October 23, 2013 3 at the same time, reduce vulnerabilities to the fragile external environment. On this front, Peru is also doing its homework. ? Finally, it is good to know that we will not face the important challenges for our countries alone. In the past, we shared our crises; now with the Pacific Alliance we share the construction of a framework and a system that will make us stronger in the face of external volatility. We will share in the creation of a more promising future. 4
text_original: Seminario: La Oportunidad de la Alianza del Pacfico Palabras de bienvenida Agustn Carstens  Gobernador del Banco de Mxico Mxico D.F., 11 de diciembre de 2013 El Gobernador Agustn Carstens compartir las palabras de bienvenida con Javier Len Olavarra (Embajador de Per en Mxico) y con Jos Antonio Blanco (Presidente Ejecutivo, inPER). El Banco Central de Reserva del Per ha implementado una poltica monetaria transparente e independiente que se conduce bajo un esquema de metas explcitas de inflacin. Los resultados de este esfuerzo sobresalen: durante los ltimos 10 aos, la economa peruana ha presentado una de las tasas de inflacin promedio ms bajas de la regin.2  Al igual que otros pases emergentes de Amrica Latina y del resto del mundo, Per enfrentar un entorno global incierto y voltil. En este frente, Per tambin est haciendo su tarea.  Finalmente, es bueno saber que no enfrentaremos solos los importantes retos para nuestros pases. En el pasado, compartimos nuestras crisis; ahora con la Alianza del Pacfico compartimos la construccin de un marco y de un sistema que nos har ms fuertes ante la volatilidad externa.
