Title: Inauguration of the seminar Financial stability and central banks
Subtitle: Remarks by Alejandro Daz de Len, Governor of Banco de Mxico, at the Inauguration of the Seminar
text: Remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of Banco de Mexico, at the Inauguration of the Seminar Financial Stability and Central Banks.* Mexico City, November 1, 2019 Opening remarks Good morning. Welcome to the Seminar. It is an honor for Banco de Mexico to receive such renowned national and international officials and leading experts who have gathered here today to exchange ideas and experiences. This Seminar is part of a set of activities seeking to reflect on the functions and challenges of contemporary central banks, which we have organized to commemorate 25 years of Banco de Mexicos autonomy. On this occasion, our meeting addresses the issue of the central banks role in financial stability. I would like to talk about the interaction between monetary policy and financial stability and Banco de Mexicos measures to detect, prevent and mitigate financial risks, along with its actions to encourage inclusion and to promote competition, with a permanent focus on citizens. * English translation made by Banco de Mexicos staff. Discrepancies may possibly arise between the original document in Spanish and its English translation. For this reason, the original version in Spanish is the only official document. 1 I. Background of the central banks role in financial stability. Since the beginning, central banks have monopolized the issuance of fiat money and the consequent role of lender of last resort. To successfully fulfill these functions, societies need to have confidence that their central banks will use the issuance of primary money prudently to attain their goals of preserving the purchasing power of the money they provide to society and of fostering financial stability and the smooth functioning of the payment systems. For many years, considerations on financial stability have permeated the central banks decision-making process. However, the 2008 crisis forced these institutions to take further steps and to coordinate efforts in an unprecedented way. Such actions have dealt with both mitigating the impact of such crisis and detecting and preventing new systemic risk events. Thus, the 2008 crisis contributed to the largest global financial collaboration effort on record. Multilateral consensus were established to adopt regulatory and supervisory standards at the international level that would effectively limit the possibility of new crisis episodes. Among 2 these standards, a broader adoption of the so-called macroprudential measures and the reduction of systemic risk stand out, as, unlike microprudential regulation and supervision based on individual entities, the former recognize the close and complex interaction among the players and networks of the financial system and seek to identify and prevent risks to the financial systems stability, as a whole. As an example of this effort, I should mention that yesterday, the 17th Meeting of the Financial Stability Board (FSB) Regional Consultative Group for the Americas was held here in Mexico City. Challenges faced by the regions financial systems were shared. The meeting also included the analysis of the work carried out by the FSB regarding cybernetic and technological risks, risks related to virtual assets, climate risks, international coordination, and possible market fragmentation. The Consultative Group, in which the Ministry of Finance and the National Banking and Securities Commission participated, also checked on the progress made during this financial year regarding the measurement of non-bank financial intermediaries in the region. 3 Thus, around the world, albeit under different institutional arrangements, central banks have renewed their participation in assessing and framing financial stability measures. II. Monetary policy and financial stability The benefits of attaining monetary policy and financial stability goals tend to strengthen. In this regard, the instruments to achieve such goals are characterized by a certain degree of interaction, but also by clear differences that must be considered. Following this line, a central bank must take three elements into account: 1. Separability between monetary policy and financial stability goals. Although monetary policy actions can contribute to stabilize the economic cycle, it is key to keep in mind the differences between these and the financial cycle, since they are generally not synchronized and have different time frames or temporality. There are also clear differences between the best instruments to achieve price stability and financial stability, given that the regulatory and supervisory policies can address the specific challenges of financial stability. 4 2. Interconnection between monetary and financial policies. Despite their distinct character, there is also a close interconnection between monetary policy and financial stability that must not be underestimated. Many emerging economies have experienced episodes of macroeconomic weakening, which have intensified due to the financial crisis. As a result, financial stability considerations have become a very important component of risk assessment for monetary policy decisions and macroeconomics in such countries. Meanwhile, in advanced economies, financial stability prior to the 2008 global crisis was taken for granted. Only after the emergency had occurred, considerations on such stability played a predominant role once again and currently interact with monetary policy via the financial risks channel. For this reason, it is imperative that challenges and risks associated with the interconnection between monetary policy and financial stability are considered. 3. Carry out an integrated policy assessment. In order to size stress scenarios to which an economys financial system is subject, it is essential to thoroughly analyze and assess the interaction between several policies. In particular, the 5 interrelation and side effects of aspects such as monetary policy, exchange rate regime, fiscal policy and macroprudential measures. For such purpose, it is necessary to comprehensively model the risks to which the economy is subject so as to adopt the most appropriate policies. Such comprehensive approach is especially valuable for emerging countries with small and open economies and less mature financial systems, which are subject to multiple shocks, both external and domestic. Although several multilateral organizations have proposed efforts in this matter, much work remains to be done as to the development of a multifactorial approach that provides improved analytical and empirical tools to generate better policies. In sum, considering these three dimensions of the analysis can lead to a more effective central bank decision-making process and help attain the central bank price stability and financial stability objectives. 6 III. Banco de Mexico and the healthy development of the financial system. Banco de Mexicos efforts to promote the healthy development of the Mexican financial system unfold along three main axes. The first axis pertains to its regulatory and supervisory powers, key elements of financial stability. The second one has to do with its role as promoter of regulations and best practices to stimulate competition and empower citizens, for them to have access to better financial services. The third one refers to Banco de Mexicos actions to take on new challenges, benefit from the opportunities related to technological change, and to mitigate risks. As to the first axis, concerning the improvement of regulations and supervision over more than two decades, a sound financial system with high levels of capital, liquidity and solvency, able to withstand possible adverse scenarios, is being built in Mexico. In this regard, Banco de Mexico participates in the Financial System Stability Council, a body created in 2010 in which all sector authorities interact to timely monitor potential vulnerabilities and reduce risks, and 7 that has sought to incorporate the best international practices, not only regarding regulation and supervision, but also in matters of disclosure and transparency. In addition, for the past ten years, Banco de Mexico has released annually a Financial System Report, which, as of this year, will be published every six months. In addition to addressing traditional risks, Banco de Mexico considers it very important to assess the nature and magnitude of certain financial challenges that have been gaining relevance, such as environmental and ecological sustainability issues. These issues are not only crucial for sustainable global development, but can lead to credit risks with systemic consequences. In this regard, the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors to Green the Financial System (NGFS), of which Banco de Mexico is a founding member, has identified the systemic financial risks to certain environmental and climatic issues and seeks to incorporate them in the strategic decisions of all financial institutions, developing methodologies to measure and manage such issues. 8 The second major axis implies that the financial system is not only stable, but also efficient and inclusive, allowing to safely and rapidly channel public savings into the most profitable projects for society. It is essential to emphasize that financial stability is not an end in itself, but rather a means that allows to offer financial services to which citizens have access under the best conditions of quality, accessibility and extent, and to ensure that they are provided sustainably in the long term. In this regard, there are two fronts of action. The first one is to promote greater efficiency and competition in the provision of services, reducing user mobility costs, eliminating entry barriers for new participants and developing an open architecture for information and payment networks. The second one is to strengthen education and information, as well as consumer protection, since greater quality and clarity of public information about the products and services offered by intermediaries helps to reverse information asymmetries or correct behavioral biases and allows to make better decisions. Transparency directly benefits 9 consumers and encourages greater competition among intermediaries. Also, the most informed and appropriate decisions taken at the individual level contribute to prevent excessive acquisition of risks at the collective level and, thereby, to limit systemic risk factors. Finally, the third major axis has to do with Banco de Mexicos actions that allow it to fully benefit from the possibilities of the revolution in information technologies. Thanks to technological change, today there is an opportunity, unthinkable in the past, especially in emerging countries, to put an end to the lags in financially attending the population and to improve the payment systems, based on technological innovations and creative partnerships. An example of how technological development can be exploited in projects rendering significant social benefits is the Request to Pay scheme CoDi (acronym in Spanish for Cobro Digital), which was recently launched in our country. Using the infrastructure of the Interbank Electronic Payment System (SPEI, for its acronym in Spanish), operated by Banco de Mexico, and using QR and NFC technologies for electronic 10 payments, CoDi allows anyone who has a smartphone and a bank account or an account with a financial institution participating in SPEI, to make electronic payments in seconds, free of charge. In the first month of its launch, more than 600 thousand people have downloaded this payment service. CoDi reflects how technological advance offers new alternatives to make user transactions more efficient, lower their costs, and foster greater inclusion, competition, and transparency. Technological advance brings along great opportunities, but also implies challenges. For this reason, just like all central banks and financial authorities in the world, Banco de Mexico faces the challenge of fully understanding the new structure and activities of financial systems, characterized by the incorporation of new business models and participants, such as the so-called Fintech companies, and by the new penetration capabilities and specialization trends. This is essential to design optimal regulation and supervision frameworks, less dependent on individual institutions and more on a modular approach that allows to 11 properly align incentives, establish an even floor between different types of intermediaries, empower consumers, and balance the goals of financial stability and inclusion. Ladies and Gentlemen: To face this stage of continuous transformation, we must rely on a forward-looking vision that not only addresses the immediate challenges, but also those deep trends that are emerging in a less visible way. In this regard, organizing this "Seminar on financial stability and central banks" is very useful and set at the proper timing, given that in recent decades central banks have evolved very rapidly and dynamically. Today, we will have two panels of great interest. The first one related with Financial stability and central bank independence, and the second one with Financial stability and macroprudential policy. 12 In the case of Banco de Mexico, its mandates to promote price stability, stimulate the healthy development of the financial system and foster the proper functioning of the payment systems are strongly interconnected and have complementarities. Indeed, these three objectives constitute public goods that are reflected directly in the economic opportunities and standards of living of citizens. Price stability is a public good that, by preserving the purchasing power of money, grants basic certainty to citizens and directly affects their wellbeing. Similarly, financial stability is a public good that allows citizens to have, in a sustained manner, better financial services and access instruments to deploy more fully their talents and initiatives. Finally, the proper functioning of the payment systems is a public good that allows citizens to carry out all their transactions in a fast and secure way and, currently, is the gateway for millions of Mexicans to access a wide range of financial services. 13 The central bank seeks to provide these key public goods and thus contribute to a more robust, equitable and sustained growth over time. Thank you once again for attending this venue, which I expect to be a very productive seminar. 14

Title: Olympics: economy and values
text: Olympics: Economy and Values Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the opening of the exhibition "London 2012: Economy and Green Olympic Games" at the Interactive Museum of Economics, in Mexico City, on July 26, 2012. I am very pleased to participate in the opening of this exhibition around the London 2012 Olympics organized jointly by the British Embassy in Mexico and the Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE). Presented in the most important and innovative space for economic dissemination in our country that is the MIDE, this exhibition emphasizes the economic effect of the Olympic Games, its sustainability and its social impact. Archaeology of the Olympic Games The celebration of the Olympics every four years seeks to recover an old civilizing function of sport. As we know, the current games are inspired by the religious and sports festivals that took place in several cities of ancient Greece, mainly in the sanctuary of Olympia. In these competitions the religious, ethical and sporting dimensions converged, since it was conceived that physical dexterity was closely linked to moral virtue and the ability to govern. It is not surprising that these games monopolized the widespread interest in Greece, were considered a subject for poetry and animated a celebratory genre of which some testimonies remain. 1 Prominently the lyric poet Pindar, who devoted a substantial part of his work to singing athletic feats and merging them with myth, left written in one of his well-known odes:1 If celebrating victories is your attempt at the Olympic lid take your lyre that another will not be more worthy of your accent. The games served several functions, including: celebrating the gods and emulating heroic archetypes through sports competition; to promote the Greek educational ideal which advised the integral training of the body and spirit of citizens; and ratify the Panhellenic zeal that conceived the Greeks as a single civilization. Hence, even if there were wars between the cities, they temporarily ceased for the celebration of the festivities. A similar yearning for concord guided the restitution of the Olympic Games in the modern era. Its simple but eloquent symbol, the five interlocking rings, represents the perennial aspiration to union and friendship between the five continents. Possible economic and social impact For the third time in the modern era, it is up to the city of London to host this festival of sport, culture and world brotherhood. In addition to their symbolic aspect, the Olympic Games involve an enormous mobilization of economic resources. Therefore, many wonder about the economic and social impact of being its headquarters. In this regard, there is no unequivocal consensus. In each case, the promotion and business opportunities that are generated, the tourist flow that is propitiated, and the temporary jobs that are created with 1 Pindar (1984). Odas, (translated by Ipandro Acaico), Secretaria de Educacion Publica, Mexico. 2 the large public investments in infrastructure required. Hence, the net economic benefit for an Olympic games host country depends on aspects such as how it subsequently leverages infrastructure or uses Olympic promotion to permanently increase tourism or investment. What studies are conclusive about is that hosts tend to get more medals than they usually earn.2 It is therefore foreseeable that Britain will further improve its already splendid sporting performance and provide many reasons for solace and joy to its inhabitants. Intangible gains Regardless of the quantifiable benefits, there are certainly intangible gains for the participants and viewers of an event like this. Perhaps the most valuable is that feeling of universal communion with the values of self-improvement and conciliation that sport promotes. Because, despite the shadows that have sometimes hung over these games, the Olympics are a celebration of fraternity and harmony among human beings. This fair is eagerly awaited not only by athletes but by millions of fans around the world. And is that although the nature of sport is essentially playful, it is also paradigmatic for the role played by rules and values, for the discipline that imprints on its practitioners and for the effort, initiative and intelligence that high competition requires. That's why Olympic sport 2 Vease, por ejemplo, Goldman Sachs (2012) The Olympics and Economics 2012; y Lui, H.K. y W. Suen (2008) "Men, Money, and Medals: An Econometric Analysis of the Olympic Games" Pacific Economic Review 13(1): 1-16 3 it continues to function as inspiration and as a representation of individual virtues and social values. Certainly, sports achievements can become human achievements of the first order that border on aesthetics for their display of imagination, technique and tactics or are linked to ethics for their show of fair competence and spirit of solidarity. Thus, in each Olympic Games, we witness with hope the possibility of channelling sport as a source of self-esteem, as a promoter of values of perseverance and as a form of social integration and reconciliation between peoples. In light of the above, I congratulate the organizers of this exhibition for allowing us a trip to the Olympic world and, in particular, to the splendor and enthusiasm that floods the city of London this 2012. It is a well-designed exhibition that offers information, reflection material and interactive fun. Here visitors will be able to learn about the history of the Olympic Games and appreciate picturesque aspects, such as pets or some posters and uniforms, of these Olympics. Thanks to the variety of tools available, I am sure that the exhibition will be attractive to diverse audiences, from children to specialists. Finally, the exhibition of MIDE is a reason for satisfaction that the Olympics give us, even before officially starting. Hopefully throughout the competition, both Great Britain and Mexico will have, in the performance of their athletes, many more reasons to celebrate. For now, congratulations to the organizers, thank you very much to all of you for joining us and I invite you to enjoy this exhibition. 4

Title: Ceremony for the circulation of the commemorative coin of Senator Belisario Domnguez
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the ceremony of the circulation of the commemorative coin of Senator Belisario Dominguez (for his luctuous centenary and the 150th anniversary of his birth) issued by the Bank of Mexico. Ceremony held in the Senate of the Republic on the occasion of the annual delivery of the Belisario Dominguez medal. November 5, 2013  Mr. President of the Republic, Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto;  Mr. President of the Board of Directors of the Senate of the Republic, Senator Raul Cervantes Andrade;  Mr. Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Honorable Chamber of Deputies, Deputy Ricardo Anaya Cortes;  Mr. President of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation, Minister Juan Silva Meza;  Head of Government of the Federal District, Dr. Miguel angel Mancera Thorny;  Mr. Constitutional Governor of the State of Chiapas, Licensed Manuel Velasco Coello  Ladies and gentlemen legislators;  Ladies and gentlemen, It is a source of great pride for the Bank of Mexico to participate in this event in which, to the delivery that every year is made of the Belisario Dominguez award to a distinguished Mexican selected by the Senate of the Republic, today it is put into circulation in honor of such an illustrious hero, a coin that is issued on the initiative of the Belisario Dominguez Commission of this Collegiate Body. I would like to thank the Senators of the Republic for receiving us in this historic legislative precinct on the occasion of the circulation of this new currency. Page 1 of 5 With its issuance, the Bank of Mexico fulfills the constitutional mandate that orders it to provide the country's economy with national currency and, additionally, pays tribute to the illustrious and courageous Chiapas senator. So significant for our political life and for the construction of democracy was the contribution of this famous senator, that since 1954 the Senate of the Republic has honored him by conferring his name on the highest distinction he bestows on the most eminent Mexicans. Thus, this ceremony of putting into circulation the legal tender that bears the effigy of Senator Belisario Dominguez has several aspects that fill the Bank of Mexico with particular satisfaction. Indeed, in this year 2013, by a fortunate coincidence, the distinction of the Belisario Dominguez medal will fall on Mr. Manuel Gomez Morin, who was the first president of the board of directors of the Bank of Mexico and one of the architects of the foundation of our Central Bank promoted by the then President of the Republic Mr. Plutarco Elias Calles. Another aspect, which also fills the Central Bank with satisfaction, is to bring to fruition, as on many other occasions, an initiative of the Honorable Congress of the Union that contributes to twinning the issuance of coins with the wise idea of promoting civic education and veneration to outstanding characters of our history, such as in this case Belisario Dominguez Palencia, on the 150th anniversary of his birth and 100 years after his tragic but fruitful death. Page 2 of 5 This coin, for its meaning and for the exemplary character it represents, we are sure that it will enjoy full acceptance. I share with you an element of policy that represents a relevant but very pleasant challenge for our Central Bank. We require that the designs and motifs of our coins, for their beauty and for the values they transmit, find a favorable reception from all users. That is why its theme seeks to collect these elements of which we can be proud: historical events, such as the one that summons us today; tribute to our heroes, such as those of Hidalgo and Morelos; antecedents of our pre-Hispanic culture or a sample of federalism such as the collection of coins of each of the States. Numismatic presence, which has allowed us to obtain international awards, such as those of the Aztec Calendar or the Railway alluding to the Centennial of the Mexican Revolution. Reasons of great cultural prestige such as that of our Nobel Octavio Paz or the Centenary of the UNAM. Or the one that with great justice we have just issued in the Centennial of the Mexican Army, also by Initiative of Congress. And always on the obverse, the eagle on a nopal devouring the snake, evoking our roots and our vocation for independence and freedom framed by the words "United Mexican States". The third element that I want to emphasize is the wide space for collaboration and understanding that our Central Institute maintains with the Honorable Congress of the Union and that goes beyond the decisions that accompany the issuance of coins. Page 3 of 5 Indeed, for the Bank of Mexico, this institutional relationship is indispensable in fulfilling the priority objective given to it by the Constitution, that is, to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency. The pillar of this strategy is the adequate communication with all the actors that requires to inform society in a timely and transparent manner each of its monetary policy decisions that are also accompanied by the accumulation of information that was considered to reach these decisions, as well as the content of the intense deliberations that were carried out within its Governing Board. By making this information public, we are among the very few central banks that make the content of their minutes known with this breadth. We know that this way of acting is a key element so that the expectations of low and stable inflation can be anchored among the public. It is fair to recognize that in the Senate of the Republic we find inspiration and support to act in this framework of transparency. A few days ago, we held a public event to commemorate our 20 years of autonomy, in which we had the distinguished presence of the President of the Republic, the President of the Senate and various legislators, precisely underlining that, in the exercise of our constitutional mandate, respect for autonomy and adequate coordination between Powers are part of the same vision and responsibility. Page 4 of 5 In taking each of our decisions, in fulfilment of this mandate, we must prevent the national currency or the payment system, which we are obliged to preserve, from being subjected to speculative attacks, destabilisation manoeuvres or any other manipulation. To this end, we have always found in the Congress of the Union, as it has also been with the Federal Executive, this clear commitment and understanding of our objective and functions. That is why I take this opportunity to make this well-deserved recognition, which accurately reflects the respectful and harmonious character of the very broad and close cooperation and collaboration between the Bank of Mexico and the Powers of the Union. I conclude by expressing my gratitude and recognition also to the Mint of Mexico, responsible for the issuance of this current coin with a face value of twenty pesos, which can be used for any payment but which we are sure will be preserved by users as a memory and testimony of recognition of the life and example of Don Belisario Dominguez, whose effigy is included in this coin. In this way, the Bank of Mexico once again fulfills its legal mandate and, at the same time, pays a sincere and well-deserved tribute to one of the most recognized Mexican democrats, Don Belisario Dominguez. text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la ceremonia de la puesta en circulacin de la moneda conmemorativa del Senador Belisario Domnguez (por su centenario luctuoso y el 150 aniversario de su nacimiento) emitida por el Banco de Mxico. Ceremonia efectuada en el Senado de la Repblica con motivo de la entrega anual de la medalla Belisario Domnguez. 5 de noviembre de 2013  Seor Presidente de la Repblica, licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto;  Seor Presidente de la Mesa Directiva del Senado de la Repblica, Senador Ral Cervantes Andrade;  Seor Presidente de la Mesa Directiva de la honorable Cmara de Diputados, Diputado Ricardo Anaya Corts;  Seor Presidente de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nacin, Ministro Juan Silva Meza;  Jefe de Gobierno del Distrito Federal, Doctor Miguel ngel Mancera Espinosa;  Seor Gobernador Constitucional del Estado de Chiapas, Licenciado Manuel Velasco Coello  Seoras y seores legisladores;  Seoras y seores: Es un motivo de gran orgullo para el Banco de Mxico participar en este evento en el que, a la entrega que cada ao se hace de la presea Belisario Domnguez a un mexicano distinguido seleccionado por el Senado de la Repblica, el da de hoy se ponga en circulacin en honor de tan ilustre prcer, una moneda que se emite por Iniciativa de la Comisin Belisario Domnguez de este cuerpo Colegiado. Quiero agradecer a las seoras y a los seores senadores de la Repblica el hecho de recibirnos en este histrico recinto legislativo con motivo de la puesta en circulacin de esta nueva moneda. Pgina 1 de 5 Con su emisin, el Banco de Mxico cumple con el mandato constitucional que le ordena proveer a la economa del pas de moneda nacional y, adicionalmente, rinde homenaje al ilustre y valeroso senador chiapaneco. Tan significativa para nuestra vida poltica y para la construccin de la democracia fue la contribucin de este clebre senador, que desde 1954 el Senado de la Repblica lo ha honrado confiriendo su nombre a la mxima distincin que otorga a los mexicanos ms eminentes. As, esta ceremonia de puesta en circulacin de la moneda de curso legal que lleva la efigie del senador Belisario Domnguez tiene diversas vertientes que llenan de particular satisfaccin al Banco de Mxico. En efecto, en este ao 2013, por una afortunada coincidencia, la distincin de la medalla Belisario Domnguez recaer en don Manuel Gmez Morn, quien fue el primer presidente del consejo de administracin del Banco de Mxico y uno de los artfices de la fundacin de nuestro Banco Central impulsada por el entonces Presidente de la Repblica don Plutarco Elas Calles. Otra vertiente, que asimismo llena de satisfaccin al Banco Central, es llevar a buen trmino, como en muchas otras ocasiones, una iniciativa del Honorable Congreso de la Unin que contribuye a hermanar la emisin de monedas con la atinada idea de fomentar la educacin y la veneracin cvicas a personajes seeros de nuestra historia, como es en este caso Belisario Domnguez Palencia, en el 150 aniversario de su natalicio y a 100 aos de su trgico pero fecundo fallecimiento. Pgina 2 de 5 Esta moneda, por su significado y por la ejemplaridad del personaje que representa, estamos seguros que gozar de plena aceptacin. Comparto con ustedes un elemento de poltica que significa un desafo relevante pero muy grato para nuestro Banco Central. Requerimos que los diseos y motivos de nuestras monedas, por su belleza y por los valores que transmiten, encuentren una recepcin favorable de todos los usuarios. Por eso su temtica busca recoger estos elementos de los que podamos sentirnos orgullosos: eventos histricos, como el que hoy nos convoca; homenaje a nuestros hroes, como las de Hidalgo y Morelos; antecedentes de nuestra cultura prehispnica o una muestra del federalismo como la coleccin de monedas de cada uno de los Estados. Presencia numismtica, que nos ha permitido obtener premios internacionales, como las del Calendario Azteca o la del Ferrocarril alusiva al Centenario de la Revolucin Mexicana. Motivos de gran prestigio cultural como la de nuestro Nobel Octavio Paz o la del Centenario de la UNAM. O la que con gran justicia acabamos de emitir en el Centenario del Ejrcito Mexicano, tambin por Iniciativa del Congreso. Y siempre en el anverso, el guila sobre un nopal devorando a la serpiente, evocando nuestras races y nuestra vocacin por la independencia y la libertad enmarcadas por las palabras Estados Unidos Mexicanos. El tercer elemento que quiero subrayar es el amplio espacio de colaboracin y entendimiento que mantiene nuestro Instituto Central con el Honorable Congreso de la Unin y que va ms all de las decisiones que acompaan la emisin de monedas. Pgina 3 de 5 En efecto, para el Banco de Mxico esta relacin institucional es indispensable en el cumplimiento del objetivo prioritario que le ha dado la Constitucin, esto es, procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda. Pilar de esta estrategia es la adecuada comunicacin con todos los actores que exige informar de forma oportuna y transparente a la sociedad cada una de sus decisiones de poltica monetaria que adems se acompaan del cmulo de informacin que fue considerada para llegar a dichas decisiones, as como del contenido de las intensas deliberaciones que se efectuaron al interior de su Junta de Gobierno. Al hacer pblica esta informacin nos ubicamos entre los muy pocos bancos centrales que dan a conocer con esta amplitud el contenido de sus minutas. Sabemos que esta forma de actuar es elemento clave para que las expectativas de una inflacin baja y estable puedan anclarse entre el pblico. Es de justicia reconocer que en el Senado de la Repblica encontramos inspiracin y apoyo para actuar en este marco de transparencia. Hace unos das, realizamos un evento pblico al conmemorar nuestros 20 aos de autonoma, en el que contamos con la distinguida presencia del Presidente de la Repblica, del Presidente del Senado y de diversos legisladores, precisamente subrayando que, en el ejercicio de nuestro mandato constitucional, el respeto a la autonoma y la adecuada coordinacin entre Poderes forman parte de una misma visin y responsabilidad. Pgina 4 de 5 Al adoptar cada una de nuestras decisiones, en cumplimiento de este mandato, debemos evitar que la moneda nacional o el sistema de pagos, que estamos obligados a preservar, sean objeto de ataques especulativos, maniobras de desestabilizacin o de cualquier otra manipulacin. Para ello, siempre hemos encontrado en el Congreso de la Unin, como ha sido tambin con el Ejecutivo Federal, este claro compromiso y entendimiento de nuestro objetivo y funciones. De ah que aproveche la ocasin para hacer este merecido reconocimiento, que refleja con precisin el carcter respetuoso y armnico de la muy amplia y estrecha cooperacin y colaboracin entre el Banco de Mxico y los Poderes de la Unin. Concluyo expresando mi gratitud y reconocimiento tambin a la Casa de Moneda de Mxico, responsable de la emisin de esta moneda de cuo corriente con valor facial de veinte pesos, que podr utilizarse para cualquier pago pero que estamos seguros ser conservado por los usuarios como un recuerdo y testimonio de reconocimiento a la vida y ejemplo de Don Belisario Domnguez, cuya efigie se incluye en esta moneda. De esta forma, el Banco de Mxico cumple una vez ms con su mandato legal y, al mismo tiempo, rinde un sincero y bien merecido homenaje a uno de los ms reconocidos demcratas mexicanos, Don Belisario Domnguez.
