Title: 78 Banking Convention
text: Remarks by the Governor of Banco de Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, on the occasion of the 78th Banking Convention. March 19, 2015 ? Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso, ? Mr. President of the National Banking and Securities Commission, teacher Jaime Gonzalez Aguade, ? President of the Finance and Public Credit Commission, of the Honorable Chamber of Deputies, Deputy Aurora de la Luz Aguilar Rodriguez ? Vice President of the Board of Directors, of the Honorable Chamber of Deputies, Deputy Tomas Torres Mercado ? Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, Mr. Luis Robles Miaja, ? Mr. Executive President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, teacher Alberto Gomez Alcala, ? Distinguished Vice Presidents of the Association of Banks of Mexico, ? Ladies and gentlemen, 1 Good afternoon. As in previous years for me it represents not only an honor but a great pleasure to be present at this banking convention. I welcome the fact that the Association of Banks of Mexico has chosen as the general theme of this convention "Banking, prepared for a great opportunity for development". Various actions by the government, legislators, commercial and development banks, as well as financial authorities have come together to make it so. I also welcome the fact that Mexican banks are willing to be a major player in shaping a promising stage of accelerated and sustained economic development for our country. Mexican banks are solidly capitalized, and enjoy a regulatory framework that seeks at the same time to promote growth, as well as to timely prevent any risk of a systemic nature. Just on Monday of this week, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision rated Mexico as approved with respect to our adoption of the new capitalization and liquidity rules, a maximum rating that few countries have received today. However, it would be wrong to take a promising future without its problems for granted. There is still much to be done 2 to match the growth potential of the Mexican economy with a greater participation of banks as the engine of this development. We all know that there are still obstacles that need to be removed, both on the demand and supply side of credit. It is a constant task that requires adding to the perseverance in maintaining a solid macroeconomic framework, the constant improvement of public policies and of regulatory and supervisory actions of a microeconomic nature that affect financial intermediation so that it is more timely, accessible and efficient. The Bank of Mexico plays a strategic role in achieving this objective, in two major areas. On the one hand, through a monetary policy that maintains the necessary conditions for banks to make more and more contributions to development. The first and inescapable requirement not only for the growth of banking but for the economic well-being of the whole country is to have a solid and stable monetary unit and that is precisely the mandate and priority objective of the Bank of Mexico: to preserve the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. On the other hand, the Bank of Mexico also has the mandates, complementary and in harmony with its priority objective, to promote the healthy development of the financial system and promote the proper functioning of the systems. 3 of payments. In this area, the Bank of Mexico has the unwavering objective of promoting competition, transparency and operational efficiency, in institutions and financial markets, so that its products and services reach a greater number of users in the best possible terms. Due to time constraints, this afternoon I will focus my words on highlighting the importance that the framework for conducting monetary policy has had for Mexico's economy, as well as the challenges we will face in this area in the future. Since 2001, the Bank of Mexico has conducted monetary policy through an inflation targeting scheme. This framework, together with responsible fiscal policies, has contributed significantly to the great progress that our country has achieved in terms of controlling inflation. Indeed, from a long-term perspective, headline inflation has declined from triple-digit levels in the '80s to levels of 3 percent today. Thus, inflation has practically converged to the permanent target that the Central Institute has set. This remarkable progress in the creation of an environment of low and stable inflation, has allowed to consolidate, over the years, a greater credibility of the commitment of the authority. 4 monetary with its objective of price stability, which has resulted in a more solid anchoring of medium- and long-term inflation expectations. And this has resulted in the Bank of Mexico having greater degrees of freedom to conduct monetary policy. This greater room for manoeuvre of monetary policy was evident during 2013 and 2014 when the Bank of Mexico was able to implement reductions in the objective of the reference interest rate without compromising the process of efficient convergence of inflation towards its target, that is, at the lowest cost in terms of economic activity. Thus, our central bank lowered the target for the overnight interbank interest rate from 4.50 percent in March 2013 to 3 percent in June last year. This adjustment in the target rate was reflected in a reduction in practically all interest rates in Mexico, both for active and passive operations. In this way, the Bank was able to implement a counter-cyclical monetary policy. That is, the policy actions implemented contributed to supporting economic activity at a time when it had been showing weakness. But the road has not been without its difficulties. We have repeatedly experienced adverse supply shocks, such as changes in relative prices of some 5 goods and services, such as agricultural products, gasoline and public transport, which have had an impact on the behavior of inflation in the short term. Although these shocks have been recurrent, medium- and long-term inflation expectations have not been affected, so the impact on inflation has been moderate and transitory. This is a clear proof of the greater credibility of the Central Bank, which is understood as the fact that economic agents do not feel the need to adjust the practices with which they establish their prices, since they trust that the Bank of Mexico will adjust its monetary policy in case of fundamental factors that persistently divert inflation from its target. Looking ahead, the great challenge for monetary policy is to strengthen the convergence of inflation to its permanent target of 3 percent and, in this way, consolidate the environment of low and stable inflation in Mexico. To achieve the above, the Governing Board will be aware of all those factors that could affect the evolution of inflation and its expectations. These factors include: (i) the relative monetary policy stance between Mexico and the United States; (ii) exchange rate performance; and (iii) the evolution of the degree of slack in the economy in the face of the expected recovery in growth. 6 Generally speaking, the outlook for inflation is favourable. However, it is pertinent to note that the Mexican economy and, consequently, monetary policy, face a particularly complex external situation, characterized by: (i) a significant decrease in international oil prices due, mainly, to supply factors, and the expectation that these prices will remain at low levels for a relatively long period; ii) after nearly eight years of maintaining an extremely loose and unconventional monetary policy, the United States is expected to begin the normalization of its stance during 2015; to complicate matters further, this would presumably happen when the monetary stances of the Eurozone and Japan would be going in diametrically opposite directions; and (iii) global economic activity continues to perform very weakly, although differentiated between countries and regions. During the last months, great volatility has prevailed in the international financial markets caused by the aforementioned factors. Undoubtedly, the one that has contributed the most to this volatility has been the expectation that the US Federal Reserve will begin to increase its benchmark interest rate sometime in 2015 from its current historically low level. Analyzing this 7 In perspective, I think it should not be a cause for surprise. When in past years the Federal Reserve created unprecedented international liquidity and lowered its rate to levels of almost zero percent, with the aim of facilitating the consolidation of the balance sheets of financial institutions and families in the United States, stimulating investment and economic recovery, great incentives were generated for capital from that country to flow to others that offered a higher risk-adjusted return. Mexico has undoubtedly been a recipient of some of these capitals, which at the time was reflected in an appreciation of the national currency, in a reduction in domestic interest rates and in some accumulation of international reserves. In particular, Mexico avoided intermediating these resources to finance consumer or real estate bubbles, as did other countries that unfortunately today are in a situation of great vulnerability to the possible reversal of these capitals. However, both the Federal Government and multiple Mexican companies took advantage of the ample international liquidity to contract new external debt or refinance the existing one at lower rates and with a longer duration, without having incurred a situation of overleveraging. 8 A good part of the capital inflows was carried out by institutional investors that have a medium and long-term horizon, so the securities they acquired are in firm hands. A smaller proportion of these inflows were channelled to short-term securities, managed by operators with a short horizon, so these represent more unstable investments. It is not surprising, therefore, that given the imminence of the Federal Reserve initiating the normalization of its monetary policy stance, a reallocation of portfolios has been generated and that this phenomenon, together with the precipitous fall in the price of oil, has been reflected mainly in a significant depreciation in the national currency against the dollar, and to a lesser extent, an increase in interest rates along the yield curve. It is essential to point out that the appreciation of the dollar has not only been against the Mexican peso, but in relation to practically all the currencies of both advanced and emerging countries. In fact, over the past eight months the dollar has seen the largest appreciation against a broad basket of currencies in a similar span since 1973. This undoubtedly means that the depreciation of the peso against the dollar has been caused mainly by external factors of global scope, and not by internal problems. Even if one considers a broad sample of 9 Quotes of currencies of emerging countries against the dollar, the peso has been one of those that has depreciated the least in recent months. This is in response to the fact that Mexico has maintained its solid macroeconomic fundamentals, has a solvent external position and we have undertaken unprecedented structural reforms in the country. A positive phenomenon has been that the recent depreciation of the national currency has had a very limited impact on inflation. Although this pattern is consistent with the degree of transfer that has been observed in the country for more than a decade, this does not necessarily imply that the Central Institute can remain oblivious to this situation. In general, determining factors of the degree of pass-through are how durable the depreciation itself is, the slack of the economy, in particular of the labor market and, above all, the fact that the Central Bank consistently does not allow exchange rate depreciations to have second-order effects by polluting inflation expectations, wages and, ultimately, price formation in the economy. This explains why the Governing Board has reiterated more than once that it will remain very attentive to the evolution of the exchange rate and its impact on inflation, in order to be able to adjust the monetary stance in a timely manner if necessary. 10 For its part, the Exchange Commission, made up of officials from the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Bank of Mexico, have made clear their concern that the foreign exchange market operates efficiently, which requires, at least, that there is sufficient liquidity. This is because in the absence of this, very pronounced variations in the exchange rate could occur that do not reflect the fundamentals of the economy, and that could put us in a pernicious dynamic in the behavior of inflation. Hence, since last December the Commission has introduced two types of daily foreign currency auctions, one with a minimum price and one without, to ensure an acceptable level of liquidity in the foreign exchange market. It is pertinent to underline that these sales of international reserves by the Bank of Mexico do not seek to defend a specific level of the price of the national currency. As this stage of volatility in international financial markets caused by the expectation of reversal of the monetary stance in the United States, and partly also by the fall in the price of oil, is not surprising, it would be expected that the authorities would have a planned action plan. This is the case. In monetary and exchange matters, the lines of defense are as follows: 11 - Allow the absorption of imbalances and/or disturbances to be carried out mainly through market adjustments of the exchange rate and interest rates, as these variations are normally stabilising. - However, in the absence of adequate liquidity in the foreign exchange market or in the presence of erratic exchange rate behaviour, it is appropriate to intervene in that market, preferably through transparent and rule-based mechanisms. The large accumulation of international reserves since 2009 gives us sufficient degrees of freedom to act in this way. In addition, there is the Flexible Credit Line of the International Monetary Fund for about 75,000 million dollars, which, it should be noted, reinforces the incentives to maintain a solid macroeconomic framework. Finally, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico could adjust its monetary stance by increasing the overnight interbank interest rate target, should it perceive that the consolidation of inflation convergence to our permanent target of 3 percent is in jeopardy, which could happen in the event that the Federal Reserve initiates the normalization of its policy. 12 An indispensable complement to the potential actions in exchange and monetary matters mentioned above is that the Federal Government perseveres in maintaining healthy public finances. This is particularly relevant in a foreseeable scenario in which there would be lower liquidity globally and higher external interest rates, at least in dollars. In the new constellation in the international financial markets, it is essential that the sustainability of public debt be guaranteed. In this sense, the cuts to public spending recently announced by the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit represent a strong signal about the commitment to fiscal responsibility on the part of the Federal Government. Such an adjustment should strengthen market participants' confidence in Mexico's economy and is consistent with the depreciation of the equilibrium real exchange rate necessary after the collapse in the price and the oil production platform. Likewise, its impact on economic activity should be marginal. This is because the adjustment will take place mainly through current public sector spending. In all this narrative we must not allow short-term considerations to blind us and prevent us from seeing the implications of certain phenomena in the medium and long term. I have repeatedly pointed out in my speech as the main risk to the financial stability of the country. 13 in the short term at the beginning of the process of normalization of monetary stance in the United States. But we should not forget that this would happen in response to a more favorable perception of the contemporary and future evolution of the US economy by the Federal Reserve, which would be a strong incentive for the Mexican economy. In particular, our exports to our neighbouring country to the North would be stimulated, which would undoubtedly bring about greater economic growth. This should help prop up the value of the national currency and limit financial volatility in Mexico. Moreover, this is a factor that would set us apart from other emerging countries, given our close integration with the United States. * * * In conclusion, Mexico, and emerging economies in general, must adapt to the changing global reality, persevering in maintaining a solid macroeconomic framework. In addition, in the face of a more complex international environment such as the one described, it is essential to promote domestic sources of growth. In this area, Mexico has made significant progress in the design, approval and implementation of structural reforms aimed at increasing the productivity and competitiveness of the economy. Part of these effects we have already begun to see in the fall in prices of certain strategic inputs. 14 for production, such as electricity and telecommunications. To achieve faster potential economic growth, an institutional framework is required that generates an incentive scheme that favors the creation of value. That is why it is of the utmost importance to continue working on the institutional transformation of the country, in such a way that there is greater competition and less extraction of rents in the economy, for which it is necessary to achieve a more solid rule of law and to grant legal certainty to the members of society. Ultimately, the purpose is to improve the well-being of the entire population of the country, achieve social harmony and overcome the lags that, unfortunately, still afflict millions of Mexicans. Thank you very much for your attention. 15
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador de Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, con motivo de la 78 Convencin Bancaria. 19 de marzo de 2015  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Luis Videgaray Caso,  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, maestro Jaime Gonzlez Aguad,  Presidenta de la Comisin de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, de la Honorable Cmara de Diputados, diputada Aurora de la Luz Aguilar Rodrguez  Vicepresidente de la Mesa Directiva, de la Honorable Cmara de Diputados, diputado Toms Torres Mercado  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, licenciado Luis Robles Miaja,  Seor Presidente Ejecutivo de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, maestro Alberto Gmez Alcal,  Distinguidos Vicepresidentes de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico,  Seoras y seores: 1 Muy buenas tardes. Como en aos anteriores para m representa no slo un honor sino un gran gusto estar presente en esta convencin bancaria. Celebro que la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico haya elegido como tema general de esta convencin La banca, preparada ante una gran oportunidad de desarrollo. Diversas acciones del gobierno, de los legisladores, de la banca comercial y de desarrollo, as como de las autoridades financieras han concurrido para que as sea. Tambin celebro que la banca mexicana se manifieste dispuesta a ser un actor de primer orden en la configuracin de una promisoria etapa de desarrollo econmico acelerado y sostenido para nuestro pas. La banca mexicana est slidamente capitalizada, y disfruta de un marco regulatorio que busca al mismo tiempo promover el crecimiento, como prevenir oportunamente cualquier riesgo de carcter sistmico. Apenas el lunes de esta semana, el Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea calific a Mxico como aprobado respecto a nuestra adopcin de las nuevas reglas de capitalizacin y liquidez, calificacin mxima que hoy pocos pases han recibido. Sin embargo, sera errneo dar por descontado un futuro promisorio exento de problemas. An hay mucho por hacer 2 para empatar el potencial de crecimiento de la economa mexicana con una mayor participacin de la banca como motor de ese desenvolvimiento. Todos sabemos que an persisten obstculos que deben removerse, tanto del lado de la demanda como de la oferta de crdito. Es una tarea constante que requiere sumar a la perseverancia en mantener un marco macroeconmico slido, el constante perfeccionamiento de polticas pblicas y de acciones de regulacin y supervisin de carcter microeconmico que incidan en la intermediacin financiera para que sta sea ms oportuna, accesible y eficiente. El Banco de Mxico desempea un papel estratgico para lograr este objetivo, en dos grandes vertientes. Por una parte, mediante una poltica monetaria que mantenga las condiciones necesarias para que la banca haga cada vez ms contribuciones al desarrollo. El primer e ineludible requisito no slo para el crecimiento de la banca sino para el bienestar econmico de todo el pas es contar con una unidad monetaria slida y estable y se es, precisamente, el mandato y el objetivo prioritario del Banco de Mxico: preservar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. Por otra parte, el Banco de Mxico tambin tiene los mandatos, complementarios y en armona con su objetivo prioritario, de promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas 3 de pagos. En ese terreno el Banco de Mxico tiene el inquebrantable objetivo de fomentar la competencia, la transparencia y la eficiencia operativa, en las instituciones y en los mercados financieros, para que sus productos y servicios lleguen a un mayor nmero de usuarios en los mejores trminos posibles. Por limitaciones de tiempo, esta tarde centrar mis palabras en resaltar la importancia que el marco de conduccin de la poltica monetaria ha tenido para la economa de Mxico, as como los retos que enfrentaremos en esa materia en el futuro. Desde 2001 el Banco de Mxico conduce la poltica monetaria mediante un esquema de objetivos de inflacin. Este marco, junto con polticas fiscales responsables, ha contribuido de manera significativa al gran avance que en materia de control de la inflacin ha logrado nuestro pas. En efecto, desde una perspectiva de largo plazo, la inflacin general ha disminuido de niveles de tres dgitos en los aos 80 hasta niveles del 3 por ciento en la actualidad. As, la inflacin ha prcticamente convergido a la meta permanente que el Instituto Central se ha fijado. Este notable avance en la creacin de un entorno de inflacin baja y estable, ha permitido ir consolidando, a lo largo de los aos, una mayor credibilidad del compromiso de la autoridad 4 monetaria con su objetivo de estabilidad de precios, lo que ha derivado en un anclaje ms slido de las expectativas de inflacin de mediano y largo plazo. Y esto ha dado lugar a que el Banco de Mxico cuente con mayores grados de libertad para conducir la poltica monetaria. Este mayor margen de maniobra de la poltica monetaria qued de manifiesto durante 2013 y 2014 cuando el Banco de Mxico fue capaz de implementar reducciones en el objetivo de la tasa de inters de referencia sin comprometer el proceso de convergencia eficiente de la inflacin hacia su meta, es decir, al menor costo en trminos de actividad econmica. As, nuestro banco central disminuy el objetivo para la tasa de inters interbancara a un da desde 4.50 por ciento en marzo de 2013 hasta 3 por ciento en junio del ao pasado. Dicho ajuste en la tasa objetivo se reflej en una reduccin en prcticamente todas las tasas de inters en Mxico, tanto para operaciones activas como pasivas. De esta manera, el Banco pudo instrumentar una poltica monetaria contra-cclica. Es decir, las acciones de poltica implementadas contribuyeron a apoyar la actividad econmica en un momento en que sta vena mostrando debilidad. Pero el camino no ha estado exento de dificultades. En repetidas ocasiones hemos experimentado choques de oferta adversos, como cambios en precios relativos de algunos 5 bienes y servicios, como productos agropecuarios, gasolinas y transporte pblico, que han incidido sobre el comportamiento de la inflacin en el corto plazo. A pesar de que estas perturbaciones han sido recurrentes, las expectativas de inflacin de mediano y largo plazo no se han visto afectadas, por lo que el impacto sobre la inflacin ha sido moderado y transitorio. Ello es una prueba fehaciente de la mayor credibilidad del Banco Central, entendindose por sta el hecho de que los agentes econmicos no sienten la necesidad de ajustar las prcticas con las que establecen sus precios, ya que confan que el Banco de Mxico ajustar su poltica monetaria en caso de que se presenten factores fundamentales que desven de manera persistente a la inflacin de su meta. De cara al futuro, el gran reto para la poltica monetaria es afianzar la convergencia de la inflacin a su meta permanente de 3 por ciento y, de esta manera, consolidar el entorno de inflacin baja y estable en Mxico. Para lograr lo anterior la Junta de Gobierno estar pendiente de todos aquellos factores que pudieran incidir sobre la evolucin de la inflacin y sus expectativas. Entre dichos factores destacan: i) la postura de poltica monetaria relativa entre Mxico y Estados Unidos; ii) el desempeo del tipo de cambio; y iii) la evolucin del grado de holgura en la economa ante la recuperacin prevista del crecimiento. 6 En trminos generales, las perspectivas para la inflacin son favorables. No obstante, es pertinente sealar que la economa mexicana y, en consecuencia, la poltica monetaria, enfrentan una coyuntura externa particularmente compleja, caracterizada por: i) una disminucin significativa de los precios internacionales del petrleo debido, principalmente, a factores de oferta, y la expectativa de que dichos precios permanezcan en niveles bajos por un periodo relativamente prolongado; ii) despus de cerca de ocho aos de mantener una poltica monetaria sumamente laxa y no convencional, se anticipa que Estados Unidos inicie la normalizacin de su postura durante 2015; para complicar an ms las cosas, esto sucedera presumiblemente cuando las posturas monetarias de la Zona del Euro y de Japn estaran yendo en direccin diametralmente opuesta; y iii) la actividad econmica global contina mostrando un comportamiento muy dbil, aunque diferenciado entre pases y regiones. Durante los ltimos meses ha prevalecido una gran volatilidad en los mercados financieros internacionales causada por los factores arriba mencionados. Sin duda el que ms ha contribuido a dicha volatilidad ha sido la expectativa de que la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos comience a aumentar en algn momento de 2015 su tasa de inters de referencia a partir de su nivel actual histricamente bajo. Analizando este 7 fenmeno en perspectiva, creo que no debera ser causa de sorpresa. Cuando en aos pasados la Reserva Federal cre liquidez internacional sin precedente y baj su tasa a niveles prcticamente de cero por ciento, con el objetivo de facilitar el saneamiento de los balances de las instituciones financieras y de las familias de los Estados Unidos, estimulando la inversin y la recuperacin econmica, se generaron grandes incentivos para que capitales de dicho pas fluyeran a otros que ofrecieran un mayor rendimiento ajustado por riesgo. Mxico ha sido sin duda receptor de parte de dichos capitales, lo que en su momento se reflej en una apreciacin de la moneda nacional, en una reduccin en las tasas de inters internas y en cierta acumulacin de reservas internacionales. En particular, Mxico evit intermediar dichos recursos para financiar burbujas de consumo o inmobiliarias, como lo hicieron otros pases que lamentablemente hoy se encuentran en una situacin de gran vulnerabilidad ante la posible reversin de dichos capitales. Sin embargo, tanto el Gobierno Federal como mltiples empresas mexicanas aprovecharon la amplia liquidez internacional para contratar nueva deuda externa o refinanciar la existente a tasas ms bajas y con una duracin mayor, sin haber incurrido en una situacin de sobreapalancamiento. 8 Una buena parte de los influjos de capitales fue llevada a cabo por inversionistas institucionales que tienen un horizonte de mediano y largo plazo, por lo que los ttulos que adquirieron estn en manos firmes. Una menor proporcin de dichos influjos se canaliz a ttulos de corto plazo, gestionados por operadores con un horizonte reducido, por lo que stas representan inversiones ms inestables. No sorprende, por tanto, que ante la inminencia de que la Reserva Federal inicie la normalizacin de su postura de poltica monetaria, se haya generado una reasignacin de carteras y que este fenmeno, junto con la precipitosa cada del precio del petrleo, se haya reflejado principalmente en una depreciacin significativa en la moneda nacional frente al dlar, y en menor proporcin, en un aumento de las tasas de inters a lo largo de la curva de rendimientos. Resulta esencial apuntar que la apreciacin del dlar no slo ha sido contra el peso mexicano, sino con relacin a prcticamente todas las divisas de pases tanto avanzados como emergentes. De hecho, durante los ltimos ocho meses el dlar ha registrado la mayor apreciacin con respecto a una canasta amplia de divisas en un lapso similar desde 1973. Esto indudablemente significa que la depreciacin del peso respecto al dlar ha sido causada fundamentalmente por factores externos de alcance global, y no por problemas internos. Incluso si uno considera una muestra amplia de 9 cotizaciones de monedas de pases emergentes frente al dlar, el peso ha sido de las que menos se ha depreciado durante los ltimos meses. Esto en respuesta a que Mxico ha mantenido sus fundamentos macroeconmicos slidos, tiene una posicin externa solvente y hemos emprendido reformas estructurales sin precedente en el pas. Un fenmeno positivo ha sido que la depreciacin reciente de la moneda nacional ha tenido un impacto muy limitado sobre la inflacin. Si bien este patrn es congruente con el grado de traspaso que se ha venido observando en el pas ya por ms de una dcada, ello no implica necesariamente que el Instituto Central pueda mantenerse ajeno a dicha situacin. En general, factores determinantes del grado de traspaso son qu tan perdurable es la propia depreciacin, la holgura de la economa, en particular del mercado laboral y, sobre todo, el que el Banco Central de manera consistente no permita que las depreciaciones cambiarias tengan efectos de segundo orden mediante la contaminacin de las expectativas de inflacin, los salarios y, a la postre, la formacin de precios en la economa. Ello explica que la Junta de Gobierno haya reiterado ms de una vez que se mantendr muy atenta de la evolucin del tipo de cambio y de su impacto sobre la inflacin, con el objeto de poder ajustar la postura monetaria oportunamente en caso de ser necesario. 10 Por su parte, la Comisin de Cambios, formada por funcionarios de la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico y del Banco de Mxico, han hecho patente su preocupacin de que el mercado cambiario opere eficientemente, lo que requiere, cuando menos, que haya suficiente liquidez. Esto porque en ausencia de sta podran ocurrir variaciones muy pronunciadas en el tipo de cambio que no reflejen los fundamentos de la economa, y que nos pudieran meter en una dinmica perniciosa en el comportamiento de la inflacin. De ah que a partir de diciembre pasado la Comisin haya introducido dos tipos de subastas diarias de moneda extranjera, una con precio mnimo y otra sin l, para procurar un nivel aceptable de liquidez en el mercado cambiario. Es pertinente subrayar que estas ventas de reservas internacionales por parte del Banco de Mxico no persiguen defender un nivel especfico de la cotizacin de la moneda nacional. Al no ser sorpresiva esta etapa de volatilidad en los mercados financieros internacionales causada por la expectativa de reversin de la postura monetaria en Estados Unidos, y en parte tambin por la cada en el precio del petrleo, sera de esperarse que las autoridades tuvieran un plan de accin previsto. Este es el caso. En materia monetaria y cambiaria, las lneas de defensa son las siguientes: 11 - Permitir que la absorcin de desequilibrios y/o perturbaciones se lleve a cabo principalmente a travs de ajustes de mercado del tipo de cambio y de las tasas de inters, pues normalmente estas variaciones son estabilizadoras. - Sin embargo, ante la ausencia de liquidez adecuada en el mercado cambiario o ante la presencia de un comportamiento errtico del tipo de cambio, procede intervenir en dicho mercado, de preferencia a travs de mecanismos transparentes y basados en reglas. La gran acumulacin de reservas internaciones desde 2009 nos otorga los suficientes grados de libertad para actuar de esta manera. Adems, se cuenta con la Lnea de Crdito Flexible del Fondo Monetario Internacional por cerca de 75,000 millones de dlares, que, debe resaltarse, refuerza los incentivos para mantener un marco macroeconmico slido. - Por ltimo, la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico podra ajustar su postura monetaria mediante aumentos en el objetivo de la tasa de inters interbancaria a un da, en caso de que perciba que est en peligro la consolidacin de la convergencia de la inflacin a nuestro objetivo permanente de 3 por ciento, lo cual podra suceder en caso de que la Reserva Federal inicie la normalizacin de su poltica. 12 Un complemento indispensable a las acciones potenciales en materia cambiaria y monetaria anteriormente citadas, es que el Gobierno Federal persevere en mantener finanzas pblicas sanas. Esto reviste particular relevancia en un escenario previsible en el que se tendra menor liquidez a nivel mundial y mayores tasas de inters externas, cuando menos en dlares. En la nueva constelacin en los mercados financieros internacionales es indispensable que se garantice la sostenibilidad de la deuda pblica. En este sentido, los recortes al gasto pblico que anunci recientemente la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico representan una fuerte seal sobre el compromiso con la responsabilidad fiscal por parte del Gobierno Federal. Dicho ajuste debera reforzar la confianza de los participantes en los mercados sobre la economa de Mxico y es congruente con la depreciacin del tipo de cambio real de equilibrio necesaria despus del desplome del precio y de la plataforma de produccin del petrleo. Asimismo, su impacto en la actividad econmica debera ser marginal. Ello debido a que el ajuste se dar principalmente a travs del gasto corriente del sector pblico. En toda esta narrativa no debemos permitir que consideraciones de corto plazo nos cieguen y eviten que veamos las implicaciones de ciertos fenmenos en el mediano y largo plazo. He sealado reiteradamente en mi intervencin como el principal riesgo para le estabilidad financiera del pas 13 en el corto plazo al inicio del proceso de normalizacin de la postura monetaria en Estados Unidos. Pero no se nos debe olvidar que esto sucedera en respuesta a una percepcin ms favorable de la evolucin contempornea y futura de la economa de Estados Unidos por parte de la Reserva Federal, lo que sera un fuerte aliciente para la economa mexicana. En particular, nuestras exportaciones al vecino pas del Norte se veran estimuladas, lo que sin duda traera consigo un mayor crecimiento econmico. Esto debera ayudar a apuntalar el valor de la moneda nacional y limitar la volatilidad financiera en Mxico. Adems, este es un factor que nos distinguira de los dems pases emergentes, dada nuestra estrecha integracin con Estados Unidos. * * * En conclusin, Mxico, y en general las economas emergentes, deben adaptarse a la cambiante realidad mundial, perseverando en mantener un marco macroeconmico slido. Adems, ante un entorno internacional ms complejo como el descrito, es fundamental promover las fuentes internas de crecimiento. En esta materia, Mxico ha avanzado significativamente en el diseo, aprobacin e implementacin de reformas estructurales encaminadas a aumentar la productividad y competitividad de la economa. Parte de estos efectos ya hemos comenzado a verlos en la cada de precios de ciertos insumos estratgicos 14 para la produccin, tales como la electricidad y las telecomunicaciones. Para lograr un crecimiento econmico potencial ms acelerado, se requiere de un marco institucional que genere un esquema de incentivos que favorezca la creacin de valor. Es por ello que es de suma importancia continuar trabajando en la transformacin institucional del pas, de tal manera que se tenga mayor competencia y menor extraccin de rentas en la economa, para lo cual es necesario que se alcance un estado de derecho ms slido y que se otorgue certeza jurdica a los miembros de la sociedad. En ltima instancia, la finalidad es mejorar el bienestar de toda la poblacin del pas, lograr armona social y superar los rezagos que, desafortunadamente, todava aquejan a millones de mexicanos. Muchas gracias por su atencin. 15

Title: Presentation of the book Readings in what the indicators indicate
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of the book Readings in what the indicators indicate.1 CDMX, October 26, 2021. Dear Silvia, dear Julio and Jonathan; Friends who attend in person and virtually: Introduction It is an honor to participate in the presentation of the three volumes of the book Readings in what the indicators indicate. How to use statistical information to understand the economic reality of Mexico, devised and coordinated by Jonathan Heath. It gives me great pleasure to share the table with three eminent promoters of economic education and the improvement of statistical information. On the one hand, our host and editor of the book, Silvia Singer, has turned MIDE into an international reference in terms of economic dissemination. On the other hand, Julio Santaella, 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 respected economist and former colleague at the Bank of Mexico, which currently directs INEGI and, of course, my esteemed colleague on the Governing Board of the central bank, Jonathan Heath, a pioneer and reference in the analysis of national economic indicators. This editorial effort, to which Jonathan generously summoned us, responds to his marked vocation to improve the quantity, quality and consistency of national statistical information that, in 2012, led him to publish his magnificent book What the indicators indicate. With its rigorous scrutiny of the country's pool of indicators, it helped to determine, with greater clarity and accuracy, what makes an indicator useful, reliable and relevant. From that book, a successful "Diploma in Macroeconomic Indicators of Conjuncture in Mexico" was conceived, coordinated by Jonathan himself and taught by specialists that he convenes. This academic program, which was hosted by Silvia Singer at MIDE, offers valuable tools for statistical analysis and has benefited numerous students. Now, that effort is reflected in this series of volumes in which several authors, who had the 2 Privilege of participating in the diploma, we reflect on the nature of the data we handle in our field of specialty. The importance of indicators It is undeniable that having a reliable and solid system of indicators is essential for the growth of a country, since this information contributes to economic agents being able to make better decisions. Having timely, well-organized and clearly arranged data allows you to identify and distinguish between correlations and causalities, establish comparisons over time and determine trends, projections and forecasts. This is essential to understand the economic situation, have a more complete historical picture, anticipate plausible scenarios and, of course, make better decisions. For economic authorities and institutions it is essential to clearly identify information needs, ensure their 3 greater opportunity and quality, promote its homogeneity, harmonize it with the best practices at an international level, make its methodologies transparent and promote its wider dissemination, according to the requirements of the different economic actors. This last aspect is fundamental, since information is an input that needs to be distributed properly in order to achieve a greater social impact. Therefore, institutions must resort to imaginative and flexible strategies, which allow them to reach diverse audiences. The Bank of Mexico and the production and dissemination of information In the case of the Bank of Mexico, for more than 25 years it has made continuous efforts to improve the quality, timeliness and modalities of dissemination of both the various economic indicators we produce, as well as the information on our main actions. In particular, under the scheme of inflation targets based on forecasts, which is characterized, among other aspects, by: the announcement of explicit medium-term inflation targets and the implementation of 4 Transparent monetary policy, as well as the periodic provision of forecasts, therefore, communication between the central bank and the public is paramount. In this scheme, the central bank generates confidence and contributes to the fact that, in the medium and long term, inflation expectations are around the institutional objective. Therefore, proactive communication and a wide dissemination of information are essential. Consequently, we have made an effort, which has intensified in recent years, to improve our indicators and find new channels and means to disseminate them, which are in tune with the consultation habits of different audiences and that allow the entire public to closely monitor the performance of the central bank. Let me mention some of the main measures of transparency, accountability and linkage with society that we have been adopting in recent years: 1. Since February 2018, timely forecasts for the average quarterly inflation of 5 the next eight quarters, for both headline and core inflation. 2. Both the monetary policy announcements and the minutes include the meaning of the vote of the members of the Governing Board. 3. The full transcripts of the meetings of the Governing Board at which the monetary policy decision is taken shall be made available to the public, three years after the corresponding meeting, a period shorter than that used by most central banks. 4. The central bank has ventured into social networks and has generated new communication products such as visual summaries, infographics, webinars and blogs, in order to dialogue with wider audiences. 5. To promote a broader discussion on the financial regulations issued by the Bank of Mexico, a mechanism for public, open and transparent consultations was adopted. 6. Our main building, which now houses the Banco de Mexico Museum, was opened to the public as an exercise in linking the central institute and society, in which the essence is addressed 6 of money, the role of central banks and the fundamental role of the public's confidence that the issuing institute will preserve the value of money, and will seek at all times the sustained well-being of society. Ladies and gentlemen, information is a public good that benefits the whole of society. Today, economic indicators are fundamental tools not only for those who make public policy or business decisions, but for any citizen who must make fundamental determinations for their own economic future. It is critical that institutions adopt the user's point of view and offer better information to more audiences. This implies serving both specialists who make intensive use of information, and citizens with specific requirements, who only sporadically turn to indicators. 7 Likewise, it is necessary to have reference sources to learn how to use data and extend a statistical culture, necessary for the population to make more efficient consumption or investment decisions. Hence the importance of this series of volumes presented today. Undoubtedly, this titanic effort of reflection to which Jonathan Heath has summoned us will have broad social benefits and I am sure that, in the future, it will help more citizens find in the use of statistical information a useful instrument in their decision-making and will promote a more prosperous future for the country. Congratulations to Jonathan and everyone who participated in these volumes. 8
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la presentacin del libro Lecturas en lo que indican los indicadores.1 CDMX, 26 de octubre de 2021. Querida Silvia, muy estimados Julio y Jonathan; Amigas y amigos que atienden de manera presencial y virtual: Introduccin Es un honor participar en la presentacin de los tres volmenes del libro Lecturas en lo que indican los indicadores. Cmo utilizar la informacin estadstica para entender la realidad econmica de Mxico, ideado y coordinado por Jonathan Heath. Me da mucho gusto compartir la mesa con tres eminentes promotores de la educacin econmica y el mejoramiento de la informacin estadstica. Por un lado, nuestra anfitriona y editora del libro, Silvia Singer que ha convertido al MIDE en una referencia internacional en materia de divulgacin de la economa. Por otro lado, Julio Santaella, 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad del autor y no necesariamente representan la posicin institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno. 1 respetado economista y antiguo compaero en el Banco de Mxico, que dirige actualmente al INEGI y, por supuesto, mi estimado colega en la Junta de Gobierno del banco central, Jonathan Heath, un pionero y referente en el anlisis de los indicadores econmicos nacionales. Este esfuerzo editorial, al que generosamente nos convoc Jonathan, responde a su marcada vocacin por mejorar la cantidad, calidad y consistencia de la informacin estadstica nacional que, en 2012, lo llev a publicar su magnfico libro Lo que indican los indicadores. Con su riguroso escrutinio del acervo de indicadores con que contaba el pas, contribuy a determinar, con mayor claridad y exactitud, qu es lo que hace a un indicador til, confiable y relevante. A partir de ese libro, se concibi un exitoso Diplomado en Indicadores Macroeconmicos de Coyuntura en Mxico, que coordina el propio Jonathan y que es impartido por especialistas que l convoca. Este programa acadmico, que fue alojado por Silvia Singer en el MIDE, ofrece valiosas herramientas para el anlisis estadstico y ha beneficiado a numerosos alumnos. Ahora, ese esfuerzo se plasma en esta serie de volmenes en la que varios autores, que tuvimos el 2 privilegio de participar en el diplomado, reflexionamos sobre la naturaleza de los datos que manejamos en nuestro mbito de especialidad. La importancia de los indicadores Es innegable que disponer de un sistema de indicadores confiable y slido resulta fundamental para el crecimiento de un pas, pues esa informacin contribuye a que los agentes econmicos puedan tomar mejores decisiones. Contar con datos oportunos, bien organizados y dispuestos con claridad, permite identificar y distinguir entre correlaciones y causalidades, establecer comparaciones en el tiempo y determinar tendencias, proyecciones y pronsticos. Ello es fundamental para entender la coyuntura econmica, tener un panorama histrico ms completo, anticipar escenarios plausibles y, por supuesto, tomar mejores decisiones. Para las autoridades e instituciones econmicas es imprescindible identificar claramente las necesidades de informacin, asegurar su 3 mayor oportunidad y calidad, promover su homogeneidad, armonizarla con las mejores prcticas a nivel internacional, transparentar sus metodologas y promover su difusin ms amplia, de acuerdo a los requerimientos de los distintos actores econmicos. Este ltimo aspecto es fundamental, pues la informacin es un insumo que requiere distribuirse adecuadamente para que logre un mayor impacto social. Por eso, las instituciones deben acudir a estrategias imaginativas y flexibles, que permitan alcanzar diversas audiencias. El Banco de Mxico y la produccin y difusin de informacin En el caso del Banco de Mxico, desde hace ms de 25 aos ha realizado esfuerzos continuos para mejorar la calidad, oportunidad y modalidades de difusin tanto de los diversos indicadores econmicos que producimos, como de la informacin sobre nuestras principales acciones. En particular, bajo el esquema de objetivos de inflacin con base en pronsticos, que se caracteriza, entre otros aspectos, por: el anuncio de objetivos explcitos de inflacin de mediano plazo y la aplicacin 4 transparente de la poltica monetaria, as como por la provisin peridica de pronsticos, por ello, la comunicacin entre el banco central y el pblico es primordial. En este esquema, el banco central genera confianza y contribuye a que, en el mediano y largo plazo, las expectativas de inflacin estn alrededor del objetivo institucional. Por lo cual es indispensable una comunicacin proactiva y una amplia divulgacin de informacin. En consecuencia, hemos hecho un esfuerzo, que se ha intensificado en los ltimos aos, por mejorar nuestros indicadores y encontrar nuevos canales y medios para difundirlos, que estn en sintona con los hbitos de consulta de distintas audiencias y que permitan a todo el pblico un seguimiento estrecho del desempeo del banco central. Permtanme mencionar algunas de las principales medidas de transparencia, rendicin de cuentas y vinculacin con la sociedad que hemos venido adoptando en los ltimos aos: 1. Desde febrero del 2018 se publican en cada Informe Trimestral los pronsticos puntuales para la inflacin promedio trimestral de 5 los prximos ocho trimestres, tanto para inflacin general como la subyacente. 2. Tanto los anuncios de poltica monetaria como las minutas incluyen el sentido del voto de los integrantes de la Junta de Gobierno. 3. Las transcripciones ntegras de las reuniones de la Junta de Gobierno en las que se adopta la decisin de poltica monetaria se ponen a disposicin del pblico, tres aos despus de la reunin correspondiente, plazo menor al utilizado por la mayora de bancos centrales. 4. El banco central ha incursionado en las redes sociales y ha generado nuevos productos de comunicacin como resmenes visuales, infografas, webinars y blogs, a fin de dialogar con audiencias ms amplias. 5. Para propiciar una discusin ms amplia sobre la normatividad en materia financiera que emite el Banco de Mxico, se adopt un mecanismo de consultas pblicas, abiertas y transparentes. 6. Se abri al pblico nuestro edificio principal, que ahora alberga al Museo Banco de Mxico, como un ejercicio de vinculacin entre el instituto central y la sociedad, en el que se aborda la esencia 6 del dinero, el rol de los bancos centrales y el papel fundamental que tiene la confianza del pblico en que el instituto emisor preservar el valor del dinero, y buscar en todo momento el bienestar sostenido de la sociedad. Seoras y seores: La informacin es un bien pblico que beneficia a toda la sociedad. En la actualidad, los indicadores econmicos son herramientas fundamentales no slo para quienes toman decisiones de poltica pblica o empresariales, sino para cualquier ciudadano que debe adoptar determinaciones fundamentales para su propio futuro econmico. Es fundamental que las instituciones adopten el punto de vista del usuario y ofrezcan mejor informacin a ms audiencias. Esto implica servir tanto a los especialistas que hacen uso intensivo de la informacin, como a los ciudadanos con requerimientos especficos, que slo acuden espordicamente a indicadores. 7 Igualmente, es necesario contar con fuentes de referencia para aprender a utilizar los datos y extender una cultura estadstica, necesaria para que la poblacin tome decisiones de consumo o inversin ms eficientes. De ah la importancia de esta serie de volmenes que se presenta hoy. Sin duda, este titnico esfuerzo de reflexin al que nos ha convocado Jonathan Heath tendr amplios beneficios sociales y estoy seguro de que, en el futuro, ayudar a que ms ciudadanos encuentren en el uso de la informacin estadstica un instrumento til en su toma de decisiones y propiciar un futuro ms prspero para el pas. Felicidades a Jonathan y a todos los que participaron en estos volmenes. 8

Title: Second National Thematic Forum for Debate on a New National Development Project
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, at the Second National Thematic Forum for Debate on a New National Development Project, convened by the National College of Economists September 7, 2011 Good afternoon, fellow economists. I would especially like to greet Deputy Jesus Alberto Cano Velez, President of the National College of Economists and Dr. Rogelio Montemayor Seguy, Coordinator of the Special Commission of the National Project of the National College of Economists, as well as all of you, fellow economists. Ladies and gentlemen: It is a great honor for me to participate in this Forum convened by the National College of Economists. I especially thank Beto Cano Velez, President of the College, for his kind invitation to present my views on the present and future of the national economy. It is certainly a very valuable exercise to reflect on the situation and prospects of our economy. But if there has been a moment in which it has been essential to consider the international environment when talking about the present and the future of the Mexican economy, it is just this, since we are living unprecedented phenomena that will inexorably mark the future of the world economy for many years. 1 I mention some of these unprecedented facts. The credit valuation of the sovereign debt of the United States for the first time in its history has been downgraded in the opinion of one of the rating agencies. And this has happened in the context of one of the most tense negotiations that have been experienced in the Congress of that country to achieve an extension in the ceiling of its public indebtedness; as we all know, the end result of these discussions was a tight political compromise seen as unencouraging by much of the economic analysts. Another unprecedented fact: from the opinion of many observers, it is clear that there are voices, which I do not share, that call into question the integrity of European Monetary Union. At the same time, many of its financial institutions are very fragile and suffering deeply. Finally, we are living through an unusual period in which most European economies face excessive indebtedness. Consider as evidence that many of the member countries of the European Monetary Union (EMU) today have a significantly lower credit rating than that of Mexico and many other emerging countries. 2 As an immediate result of these unprecedented developments, great uncertainty has been generated in international financial markets. And that uncertainty, along with the turbulence that accompanies it, is undoubtedly one of the biggest obstacles to the world's economy regaining its dynamism. However, in order to try to understand what the immediate future of the world economy might be, it is very important to identify the origins and causes of the international financial crisis; review what economic policy measures were taken in the different countries and regions to face the crisis and with what results. From this diagnosis we will be able to see more clearly what the perspectives are in the case of the Mexican economy. In analyzing the causes of the crisis, it must be recognized that there were significant market failures, but it is also true, and this fact is often overlooked, that States and governments have failed in the same way. In the United States, an over-extension of the financial system took place, based on excessive permissive regulation; regulation that was not adjusted to the evolution of the risks. At the origin of the crisis of the mortgages called sub-prime we find an uncontrolled and uncoordinated impulse of its development banking. 3 Financial institutions such as Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, government-backed, encouraged as a development bank a granting of credits without order or concert. All this, in addition, in the context of an excessively loose monetary policy, which contributed to the unbridled leverage of many families. Consequently, while the markets failed, there is no doubt that mistakes were also made in the actions and policies of the State. This global crisis reminded advanced economies of a lesson that we in Mexico and other emerging economies have well learned: governments can manufacture crises or aggravate them through an irresponsible credit policy supported by development banks without adequate controls and a loose monetary policy, as happened in the United States. History not very different from the one that Mexico had already experienced in the crises of the eighties and 1994-1995, in which regulation and internal controls in the granting of credit also failed. It is not idle to remember that in Mexico during those episodes of crisis most of our development banks reached a situation of bankruptcy, from which they had to be rescued with public resources, a situation very similar to that experienced today by the two financial institutions referred to in the United States. 4 In Europe, for its part, the fundamental problem was that, in an environment of high liquidity and encouraged by the initial success of monetary union, European governments forgot to observe several basic economic principles for the sustainability of their exchange rate regime, such as the need for fiscal convergence among the countries that make up the Union and to manage the risks of an excessively extended or leveraged financial system. This is in order to make the best monetary policy in the Union compatible with monetary policies that would be equally optimal in each country. In short, in Europe too, it was disdained to consider the margins and conditions under which the state can operate without seriously disturbing economic balances. From the above, and it must be said, it turns out that a large part of the global financial crisis has been the result of bad public policies and lessons from the past that in advanced economies were not heeded. In this matter, Mexico did learn the lessons that successive financial crises left it and that is why we have not suffered the severe consequences that these advanced economies are suffering today. 5 In 2008, once the crisis broke out in all its magnitude with the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers, the international response was aimed at restoring the conditions for markets to return to normal functioning and, above all, to avoid the negative impact on economic growth. Although the first objective has been moderately met, three years after the outbreak of the crisis, the result is that the policies adopted have not produced what was promised in terms of the evolution of economic activity. The promise was, specifically, that public policies could avoid the recessionary economic cycle and, above all, that painful and difficult decisions could be avoided. In other words, responses to the crisis in the United States and Europe have not generated the sustained economic growth that was thought. Why? Because all the problems of over-indebtedness need to be addressed, through the necessary correction of the balance sheets of families, banks and governments, which cannot be achieved with continuous fiscal and monetary stimulus actions. On the contrary, fiscal and monetary activism has generated uncertainty in the markets about the sustainability of the short-lived recovery and has made achieving the desirable response of the private sector in these countries, so that through their consumption and investment spending they bear the brunt of the recovery, a much more complex challenge to conquer today. 6 In Europe, in a process similar but not identical to that which took place in the United States, the incongruity between an exchange rate regime embodied in the Monetary Union and the problems of fiscal solvency and weakness of the financial system became obvious. This situation was aggravated by the economic policy response. Fiscal activism has not made it possible to restore economic growth, but it has induced a structural weakening of its public finances by exploiting the debt-to-GDP ratio in most European countries. Thus, in the case of Europe, the degree of uncertainty has also increased. I give a clear example: 2 years ago, sovereign debt insurance instruments - which measures the risk premium of countries - were quoted at 24 basis points for France, 78 basis points for Italy and 71 basis points for Spain, while for Mexico they stood at 171 basis points; that is, Mexico then had a risk perspective almost three times higher than those countries. Today the situation is very different; these instruments are quoted at 175 basis points for France, 392 for Spain, 433 for Italy and in the case of Mexico, they are quoted at 152 as of today. Now, Mexico's risk premium is at least half that of three European countries and is even lower than the risk premium of Europe's second-largest economy, France. It is pertinent to note that these risk premiums tend to affect the level of interest rates, the financing capacity of economies and the desire to undertake new ones. 7 Investments. Hence, it is concluded that fiscal and monetary activism in Europe was as harmful as the disease it was trying to remedy: it has generated the uncertainty that prevents the private sector from establishing a pattern of sustainable and accelerated growth. In these circumstances, the best scenario we can expect is that little by little countries establish measures that generate certainty and confidence. It would seem that many of them still do not realize the inevitability of making difficult decisions, so it is possible that the process will take a while. A new recession can be avoided at best, but given that there are several countries in a frankly weak situation, difficult and long times of low economic growth, particularly in the United States and Europe, cannot be avoided. In addition, the mistrust generated by the lack of appropriate solutions to the problems of the advanced countries has permeated the rest of the world. This has further compromised the chances of an early and vigorous recovery in global economic activity. In contrast, and entering the case of Mexico, a constant of our macroeconomic policy during the last years has been precisely the objective of generating certainty. In this regard, we can advance some conclusions: first, that maintaining macroeconomic prudence has paid well and has paid well. 8 Resisting the temptation of fiscal and monetary activism in 2009 and 2010 yielded good results, as evidenced by the fact that we have had a vigorous and relatively rapid recovery from the crisis, thanks to the strength of the country's macroeconomic variables. Mexico does not show the structural weaknesses, of a fiscal and financial nature, that many advanced economies suffer today. As I said a few days ago: we have a strong and solid boat to navigate solvently in extremely turbulent waters. I mention in detail some of these strengths. We have maintained fiscal discipline, supported by a law of fiscal responsibility approved by the Congress of the Union since 2005. During the most acute stage of the global crisis, Mexico did not join the furor for fiscal stimulus, which became in other latitudes a real maelstrom and a sword of Damocles in the end. We were one of the few countries that in the midst of the crisis made fiscal reforms to strengthen public revenues and today we are seeing the results: Mexico's public debt-to-GDP ratio is only 31.1 percent, one of the lowest in the world, which gives the country access to credit in international financial markets in very good conditions. Practically on the same day that the European Central Bank announced the massive emergency purchase of sovereign debt bonds of Spain and Italy in order to alleviate the strong pressures suffered by those countries to 9 Because of its excessive indebtedness, Mexico made another placement of one billion dollars with a term of 100 years and with a fixed rate of only 5.96 percent. Let us also remember that in 1994-1995 the government of Mexico could only finance itself for two weeks at rates that reached levels of up to 92.5 percent per year. Today, in the midst of severe global financial turbulence, Mexico's government can obtain financing in the domestic market at 30-year terms and at rates of only 7.3 percent. In the same vein of generating certainty, hedges against the risk of variations in the price of Mexico's oil have continued, thus protecting a very important proportion of the country's public revenues. For its part, monetary policy has also been consistent with the objective of reducing uncertainty. The responsibility with which it has conducted itself over the years allowed the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico in its most recent monetary policy announcement to send a signal of tranquility and certainty to the markets, by anticipating that if the economic slowdown in the world worsens or if monetary positions in advanced countries become even more accommodating, we would be in a position to adjust the monetary stance 10 without jeopardizing the objective of price stability. Indeed, very few central banks in the world today have such room for manoeuvre. And in fact, speaking of unprecedented phenomena, I would like to point out that today the entire structure of interest rates of Cetes up to a year is below 4.5 percent, historically low levels that reflect the credibility of monetary policy. This, without a doubt, is yielding lower rates throughout the country and for all types of credit, consequently boosting consumption, investment and favoring public finances. This result, by the way, confirms the great vision that was had more than 16 years ago when the Congress of the Union gave autonomy to the Bank of Mexico and established with all certainty in the Constitution its priority objective, which is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency. Also within this trend of generating certainty, the Bank of Mexico has made an extraordinary effort in terms of transparency and communication. We are one of the few central banks in the world that make public the minutes of the Governing Board regarding the meetings in which monetary policy is discussed and decided. 11 Of course, another element of our financial strength has been the central institute's international reserves. This week it was announced that its amount already reaches more than 137,000 million dollars. This level of reserves is the result of the decision taken by the Foreign Exchange Commission to accumulate supplies for difficult times since the first months of 2010. Again, this helps eliminate factors of uncertainty, as does the flexible credit line of more than 75 billion that the International Monetary Fund gave us in recognition of our sound macroeconomic policies. Far away are the years of the eighties and nineties in which not in a single occasion we ran out of reserves, with the dramatic consequences that we already know. We also have a healthy financial system, with a capitalization of 16.5 percent as of June 2011 and that meets practically all the new requirements established globally for banking, the Basel III agreements. Mexican banks, in fact, will fully comply with each and every one of these requirements several years in advance of the date on which the vast majority of banks established in other countries will be able to do so. The strength of our financial system means that banks in Mexico today have the leeway to continue stimulating growth 12 of credit and the economy, something that, again, very few countries in the world today can do. In July 2011, credit to companies in real terms grew 10.6 percent annually, consumer credit 14.3 percent annually and housing credit 6.2 percent real annually. For its part, development banking in Mexico at the most acute stage of the global crisis played an important countercyclical role. This could be done precisely because - unlike its equivalents in the United States - it was healthy, capitalized and with operating rules consistent with a policy of fiscal and financial responsibility. It is necessary, of course, to make reforms to development banking in our country, to give it more flexibility and remove regulatory and surveillance obstacles that make such banking more regulated even than commercial banking. It is necessary to eliminate the regulatory handbrake to which development banking has been subject for more than ten years, after its crisis of 1994-95, as proposed by the initiative that President Calderon submitted to the H. Congress of the Union since 2009, but it would not be desirable to impose a greater bureaucratic and organizational structure that would make it less agile and effective. In summary, what has been done in Mexico is: 13 ? First, maintain a responsible monetary policy, ? Second, resist in the most acute stages of the crisis the song of the sirens that exhorted us to engage in fiscal and monetary activism, and ? Finally, systematically reduce the factors of uncertainty. These three points have proven to be, in fact, the best formula for not inhibiting growth. And they are a solid foundation that, in these times of global uncertainty, distinguish us from most of the economies of the planet. However, we must not indulge in complacency. There are still many things to solve going forward, we still have several pending issues, and it would not be healthy to minimize the risks of the global environment. For the time being, it is clear that macroeconomic consistency and the slogan of reducing factors of uncertainty must remain the basis for the future. 14 Development banks will also need to be given greater flexibility to fulfil their role as a complement to private banking more efficiently. And we have to reiterate the lesson - to learn it now in someone else's head, in view of the serious imbalances that we see today in advanced economies - that the capacity for government intervention and activism has narrow limits that must not be exceeded. Much is put at risk in doing so, and it is not easy, nor quick, to remedy the damage that such exacerbated activism causes. But what we must mostly concentrate on immediately is addressing the pending issue that we have already had for many decades: establishing the effective conditions to be able to aspire to a much more vigorous, sustainable economic growth, which allows us to significantly reduce unemployment, reduce income inequality and eradicate poverty. We economists know that macroeconomic stability and congruence is a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for achieving these goals. What is required in addition are the already much mentioned structural reforms, the only ones that can make us more competitive, will allow us to eliminate extraordinary monopolistic rents and that will open markets that today can only be served through the actions of the State. 15 The difference with the past is that today it is much more urgent to address these pending issues, given the poor expectations of external growth. This implies that Mexico will not receive the boost from abroad to which we have been accustomed, so only through boosting the domestic economy will the greatest growth and job creation to which we aspire be achieved. And the latter will only be achieved in an ideal way if structural reforms are accelerated, this same six-year period. I mention some of these reforms, which you all already know well: we need labor reform, to reduce the costs of creating formal jobs in the economy and give more opportunities to young people; we need to deepen and ground the reforms that Congress has recently made in the area of competition, particularly in the area of telecommunications; we need to reduce uncertainty about energy prices and tariffs with a thorough reform of the sector; we need an educational reform that contributes to providing our population with better human capital so that we can defend ourselves from the greatest demands of a globalized world; we need to give more leeway to private investment through the passage of the Public-Private Partnerships Act; and, of course, we need to substantially improve our legal framework so that it is a factor that generates certainty, confidence and gives security to economic agents. 16 I repeat, in the face of such a turbulent international economic environment, the need to make these reforms becomes even more pressing. Therefore, our obligation is to carry out these reforms now to give certainty to Mexico and Mexicans in the face of a global environment that has become deeply uncertain. Thanks a lot. 17
