Por su parte, la banca de desarrollo en Mxico en la etapa ms aguda de la crisis global desempe un importante papel contracclico. Esto se pudo hacer precisamente porque  a diferencia de sus equivalentes en los Estados Unidos- estaba saneada, capitalizada y con reglas de operacin congruentes con una poltica de responsabilidad fiscal y financiera. Es necesario, por supuesto, hacer reformas a la banca de desarrollo en nuestro pas, para darle ms flexibilidad y quitarle trabas de carcter regulatorio y de vigilancia que hacen que dicha banca est ms regulada incluso que la banca comercial. Se necesita eliminar el freno de mano regulatorio al que ha estado sujeta la banca de desarrollo por ms de diez aos, despus de su crisis de 1994  95, tal como lo propone la iniciativa que someti el Presidente Caldern al H. Congreso de la Unin desde 2009, mas no sera deseable imponerle una mayor estructura burocrtica y organizacional que la hara menos gil y efectiva. En resumen, lo que se ha hecho en Mxico es: 13  Primero, mantener una poltica monetaria responsable,  Segundo, resistir en las etapas ms agudas de la crisis el canto de las sirenas que nos exhortaba a incurrir en el activismo fiscal y monetario, y  Por ltimo, reducir sistemticamente los factores de incertidumbre. Estos tres puntos han demostrado ser, en los hechos, la mejor frmula para no inhibir el crecimiento. Y son una base slida que, en estos tiempos de incertidumbre global, nos distinguen respecto de la mayor parte de las economas del planeta. Sin embargo, no debemos incurrir en la autocomplacencia. Hay an muchas cosas que resolver hacia delante, tenemos todava varias asignaturas pendientes, y no sera sano minimizar los riesgos del entorno global. Por lo pronto, est claro que la congruencia macroeconmica y la consigna de reducir factores de incertidumbre deben seguir siendo la base para el futuro. 14 Habr tambin que dotar de mayor flexibilidad a la banca de desarrollo para que cumpla ms eficientemente su papel de complemento de la banca privada. Y tenemos que reiterar la leccin  aprenderla ahora en cabeza ajena, a la vista de los graves desajustes que hoy vemos en las economas avanzadas- de que la capacidad de intervencin y activismo gubernamental tiene estrechos lmites que no deben sobrepasarse. Es mucho lo que se pone en riesgo al hacerlo y no es nada sencillo, ni rpido, remediar los daos que tal activismo exacerbado causa. Pero en lo que mayormente nos debemos concentrar de inmediato es en atender la asignatura pendiente que tenemos ya desde hace muchas dcadas: establecer las condiciones efectivas para poder aspirar a un crecimiento econmico mucho ms vigoroso, sustentable, que nos permita abatir significativamente el desempleo, reducir la desigualdad del ingreso y erradicar la pobreza. Nosotros economistas sabemos que la estabilidad y congruencia macroeconmica es condicin necesaria, mas no suficiente, para lograr dichas metas. Lo que se requiere en complemento son las ya muy mentadas reformas estructurales, las nicas que nos pueden hacer ms competitivos, nos permitirn eliminar rentas monoplicas extraordinarias y que abrirn mercados que hoy slo puedan ser atendidos a travs del accionar del Estado. 15 La diferencia con el pasado es que hoy es mucho ms urgente atender estas asignaturas pendientes, dadas las pobres expectativas de crecimiento externo. Esto implica que Mxico no va a recibir el impulso del exterior al que hemos estado acostumbrados, por lo que slo a travs de dinamizar la economa interna se lograr el mayor crecimiento y creacin de empleos al que aspiramos. Y esto ltimo slo se alcanzar de manera idnea si se aceleran, este mismo sexenio, las reformas estructurales. Menciono algunas de estas reformas, que todos ustedes ya conocen de sobra: necesitamos la reforma laboral, para reducir los costos de crear empleos formales en la economa y darles ms oportunidades a los jvenes; necesitamos profundizar y aterrizar las reformas que recientemente ha hecho el Congreso en materia de competencia, particularmente en el rea de las telecomunicaciones; necesitamos disminuir la incertidumbre respecto de los precios y tarifas de los energticos con una reforma profunda del sector; necesitamos una reforma educativa que contribuya a dotar de mejor capital humano a nuestra poblacin para que podamos defendernos de las mayores exigencias de un mundo globalizado; necesitamos dar ms margen de accin a la inversin privada a travs de aprobar la Ley de Asociaciones Pblico Privadas; y, desde luego, necesitamos mejorar sustancialmente nuestro marco jurdico para que sea un factor que genere certidumbre, confianza y otorgue seguridad a los agentes econmicos. 16 Repito, ante un entorno econmico internacional tan agitado la necesidad de hacer estas reformas se vuelve an ms acuciante. Por ello, nuestra obligacin es llevar a cabo ya estas reformas para dar certidumbre a Mxico y a los mexicanos frente a un entorno mundial que se ha vuelto profundamente incierto. Muchas gracias. 17

Title: 77 Banking Convention
text: Remarks by the Governor of Banco de Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, on the occasion of the 77th Banking Convention, held in Acapulco, Guerrero. April 3, 2014 ? Mr. President of the National Banking and Securities Commission, teacher Jaime Gonzalez Aguade, ? Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, teacher Javier Arrigunaga Gomez del Campo, ? Mr. President of the Business Coordinating Council, Mr. Gerardo Gutierrez Candiani ? Distinguished Vice Presidents of the Association of Banks of Mexico, ? Ladies and gentlemen, Good afternoon, all of you. As in previous years it is an honor for me to be present in this banking convention. I thank the Association of Banks of Mexico, and in particular its 1 Mr. President, your kind invitation to participate in this distinguished event. I would like to begin my speech with a series of reflections on the world economy, with particular emphasis on the prevailing situation and prospects of the emerging economies, of which Mexico is a part. About a year ago, the global financial cycle was more clearly transmitted to emerging economies, largely due to the beginning of the process of monetary policy normalization in the United States. The beginning of the end of a long era of low interest rates and ample liquidity in international financial markets, together with the downward correction of most commodity prices that has occurred as a result of the sluggish global economy and, markedly, in response to the recent slowdown in China, have invited a major reassessment of the outlook for emerging economies. As a result of this exercise, vulnerabilities have been discovered in 2 the economic fundamentals of a number of countries, particularly those where their public and private sectors are highly leveraged, which has been reflected in high fiscal and current account deficits in the balance of payments. More astringent financial conditions, together with the correction in the terms of trade and a loss of international competitiveness for an already prolonged period, have in turn manifested themselves in a significant and generalized reduction in growth in emerging economies. To be fair, it also hasn't helped that advanced economies, which account for about 50 percent of global GDP, have been growing continuously below their potential since 2008. From the point of view of financial stability, and given the underlying conditions described, the main risk of emerging countries is that they are confronted with massive outflows of foreign capital, which could arise in response to the vulnerabilities of the aforementioned countries, in 3 combination with abrupt changes in the monetary policy stance in the major advanced countries, particularly in the United States. Thus, the fundamental challenge facing emerging countries is how to stimulate their economic growth without compromising financial stability, in an external environment fraught with uncertainty. One possibility would be to invoke international cooperation, trying to put together a package of responses where both emerging and advanced countries would collaborate. In fact, this kind of solution has been tried in forums like the G-20. But to be very frank, I'm skeptical about this kind of solution. Advanced countries today find themselves in a more complicated situation than emerging countries, so it is difficult to think that they would divert or adjust their economic policies to pursue a goal of global well-being. The governments of advanced countries have to deal with their own problems, which are by no means negligible. In fact, if they surpass them, the world economy would be in 4 better conditions. Hence, emerging countries must take the circumstances and policies of advanced countries as given, and forge their way forward. In this sense, it would be advisable that, in order to face the dilemma posed, the emerging countries follow a strategy that has three fundamental pillars. First Pillar: Maintaining sound macroeconomic fundamentals. There is no room for mediocre fundamentals. In particular, it is very relevant for emerging countries to limit their financial requirements to what would be affordable in stress scenarios. This calls for a moderate fiscal stance and, if necessary, using aggregate demand management to avoid ballooning current account deficits. Monetary policy should concentrate on keeping inflation under control, as the latter is a prerequisite for flexible exchange rates to effectively serve as external shock absorbers. Local banking systems must be strictly supervised, and subject as soon as possible to the 5 international regulatory standards, such as those sponsored by the Basel Committee and the G20 Financial Stability Board. Second Pillar: Ensure the strength of the external sector also under stress scenarios. For starters, a future trajectory of sustainable balance of payments balances is essential. Flexibility of domestic interest rates and the exchange rate, anchored by sound economic fundamentals, should be part of the adjustment process in the event of external shocks. But given the sheer magnitude of capital inflows emerging economies have seen in recent years, those elements may not be enough. Therefore, having high international reserves and other support instances, such as the flexible credit line of the International Monetary Fund, would be highly recommended. At the same time, the public and private sectors must adopt proactive debt management strategies, seeking 6 increase their duration and prudently manage exposure to foreign exchange risk. Third Pillar: Promote economic growth by making economies more competitive, increasing total factor productivity and thus potential GDP. This leads us inexorably to the path of structural reforms, which have great potential in emerging economies. This is the difficult path to achieving higher sustainable GDP growth, but it is the only one that is reliable. Thus, in short, the first and second pillars are designed to ensure financial stability, without necessarily inhibiting economic growth. But the real lever to promote growth lies in the third pillar. It is my opinion that in the case of Mexico, a plan has been put in place that fully satisfies the need for these three pillars. Macroeconomic fundamentals have remained solid, we have a well-equipped external position, even under scenarios 7 stressed, and unprecedented structural reforms have been undertaken in the country. Moving forward we must strive to preserve this situation. * ** I would be ignorant in this participation if I do not make some specific comments on the monetary policy in our country, even more so if we remember that the first of this month marked twenty years since the operational beginning of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. Such full autonomy, together with good macroeconomic fundamentals and external stability - although not exempt from some episodes of temporary turbulence - have given this Central Institute the degrees of freedom necessary to consolidate a credible monetary policy and effectively anchor inflation expectations. Thus, last year the Governing Board had room to reduce the objective of its reference interest rate on three occasions: in March, in recognition of the progress made. 8 structural in the process of lowering inflation; and in September and October, in response to slack in the economy, in the context of inflation converging to the permanent target of 3 per cent, and even with core inflation below that level. This means that in the case of monetary policy we have entered a new stage that allows us not only to move more clearly towards the convergence of inflation to the permanent objective of the Bank of Mexico, but also to seek that this convergence is verified in an even more efficient way. In that context, efficiency should be understood as the fact that the permanent objective can be achieved at the lowest possible cost in terms of the dynamism of economic growth. By the way, the extensive and profound process of structural change in which the Mexican economy has been immersed for a few months will allow, if it comes to fruition, that the application of monetary policy to be even more efficient, that is: that Mexico can grow much more 9 accelerated and sustainable without this meaning that inflationary pressures are generated. However, in recent months this process of convergence towards the permanent objective of low and stable inflation experienced two major shocks that have meant a short-term challenge for monetary policy. The first was the sudden rise in relative prices that was registered in the last months of last year, both in some agricultural prices, and in public transport fares in the largest cities of the country. To this disturbance was added, at the beginning of this year, the impact also on relative prices that had the tax and public price modifications for fiscal year 2014. These changes meant one-time increases in specific prices for some products, which is the case for several high-calorie products, as in some regions, given the homogenization of the VAT rate to 16 percent at borders. 10 I wish to make it clear that the Bank of Mexico undoubtedly supports reforms that, by increasing revenues, strengthen public finances, since the latter is a necessary structural factor to have low inflations in a sustainable way. All these shocks contributed to the fact that at the beginning of this year the measurement of inflation was notoriously over 4 percent per year. However, subsequent data have confirmed the diagnosis made at the time by the Bank of Mexico: in the first half of March the measurement of inflation had already returned to the range of variability acceptable to our permanent target, specifically at 3.89 percent, while core inflation was below three percent, by 2.84 percent. In this case, core inflation is a lower annual rate than those recorded in the same period of 2013 and 2012. This reflects the credibility with respect to the anchoring of nominal variables that the Bank of Mexico has achieved. 11 An important ingredient for this achievement has been the communication policy followed by the Central Institute, which has made it possible to anticipate shocks in relative prices and has indicated, with the greatest possible clarity and transparency, the diagnoses on which monetary policy decisions are being based and what will be the courses of action that the Bank of Mexico would follow in the face of different events. Undoubtedly, this guide has been useful for participants in the financial markets and for the general public, and has made it possible to regulate the decisions of economic agents with lower margins of uncertainty. I reiterate, as I have done on other occasions, that these relative price shocks do not in themselves represent an inflationary phenomenon, as they are not a sustained rise in all prices in the economy. For the same reason, they are not events that can or should be fought with monetary policy tools. In any case, the fundamental challenge has been that these relative price changes, which are themselves transitory, do not contaminate other prices of the 12 economy. The evidence we have to this day is that the latter has not happened and hence we have not had to modify the monetary policy stance. Inflation is expected to remain below or close to 4 percent per year for the remainder of this year, close the year below that upper limit and begin rapid convergence to 3 percent from 2015. Of course, as we have repeatedly pointed out in our monetary policy announcements, the Governing Board will remain vigilant to detect any deviations from this roadmap, and will not hesitate to act accordingly to correct it. It is not idle to emphasize that within the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico we have no doubt that our objective and priority mission is to ensure low and stable inflation. Also, to the extent that financial stability exists and is consolidated on an increasingly firm basis, monetary policy works better and in harmony with economic activity. 13 In this sense, the set of initiatives integrated in the recent financial reform combine the elements to give greater strength to the financial sector with the appropriate incentives in terms of competition, and thus promote greater growth and penetration of financial intermediation. But beyond its particularities, already known to all of you, financial reform acquires a decisive dimension for the future economic growth of the country, when it is framed as one more gear of all the structural transformation that we have undertaken in recent months. This ambitious reform process, which is underway, seeks to change the structure of the Mexican economy and increase the total productivity of the factors of production in the country. If this transformation is successful, it will mean raising Mexico's potential GDP by several percentage points and doing so in a period that would be historically short. 14 It is not a more or less ephemeral enthusiasm, or a circumstantial impulse. Borrowing a fortunate description by Octavio Paz about the processes of change, we should not lose sight of the fact that we are talking about a transformation that is part of what the poet and essayist called "the long count" in the history of peoples and nations. If from a distance we evaluate the economic policy of the last 20 years in Mexico, we will find a common thread that has been establishing the bases for the current reforms in which we are immersed to be feasible and so that they are fully understood in their logic: they are the history of how a country forges, by successive approaches, its destiny for many decades. In any case, and returning to a shorter horizon, that of the coming years, Mexico will obtain, if we know how to consolidate and implement this ambitious process of structural change, great benefits, among others that of the Domestic Product 15 Gross can grow sustainably at rates of 5 percent or higher, with low and stable inflation. Thanks a lot. 16
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador de Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, con motivo de la 77 Convencin Bancaria, celebrada en Acapulco, Guerrero. 3 de abril de 2014  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, maestro Jaime Gonzlez Aguad,  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, maestro Javier Arrigunaga Gmez del Campo,  Seor Presidente del Consejo Coordinador Empresarial, Lic. Gerardo Gutirrez Candiani  Distinguidos Vicepresidentes de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico,  Seoras y seores: Muy buenas tardes tengan todos ustedes. Como en aos anteriores es para m un honor estar presente en esta convencin bancaria. Agradezco a la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, y en particular a su 1 Presidente, su amable invitacin para participar en este distinguido evento. Quisiera iniciar mi intervencin con una serie de reflexiones sobre la economa mundial, poniendo particular nfasis en la situacin prevaleciente y perspectivas de las economas emergentes, de las cuales Mxico forma parte. Hace aproximadamente un ao, el ciclo financiero global se transmiti de manera ms clara a las economas emergentes, en buena medida debido al inicio del proceso de normalizacin de la poltica monetaria en los Estados Unidos. El comienzo del fin de una larga era de tasas de inters reducidas y de amplia liquidez en los mercados financieros internacionales, junto con la correccin a la baja de la mayora de los precios de mercancas bsicas que se ha dado como resultado de la atona de la economa global y, marcadamente, en respuesta a la reciente desaceleracin en China, han invitado a una importante reevaluacin de las perspectivas de las economas emergentes. Como resultado de este ejercicio, han sido descubiertas vulnerabilidades en 2 los fundamentos econmicos de varios pases, en particular en aquellos en los que sus sectores pblico y privado se encuentran altamente apalancados, lo que se ha reflejado en elevados dficits fiscales y de cuenta corriente de la balanza de pagos. Condiciones financieras ms astringentes, junto con la correccin en los trminos de intercambio y una prdida de competitividad internacional por un periodo ya prolongado, se han manifestado a su vez en una reduccin significativa y generalizada del crecimiento en las economas emergentes. Para ser justos, tampoco ha ayudado el hecho de que las economas avanzadas, que representan cerca del 50 por ciento del PIB mundial, hayan estado creciendo continuamente por debajo de su potencial a partir de 2008. Desde el punto de vista de la estabilidad financiera, y dadas las condiciones subyacentes descritas, el principal riesgo de los pases emergentes es que se vean confrontados con salidas masivas de capitales forneos, las cuales se podran suscitar en respuesta a las vulnerabilidades propias de los pases aludidos, en 3 combinacin con cambios abruptos en la postura de poltica monetaria en los principales pases avanzados, en particular en los Estados Unidos. As pues, el reto fundamental que enfrentan los pases emergentes es como estimular su crecimiento econmico sin comprometer la estabilidad financiera, en un entorno externo plagado de incertidumbre. Una posibilidad sera invocar a la cooperacin internacional, tratando de armar un paquete de respuestas donde colaboraran tanto pases emergentes como avanzados. De hecho, este tipo de solucin se ha intentado en foros como el G-20. Pero siendo muy franco, yo soy escptico sobre este tipo de solucin. Los pases avanzados hoy se encuentran en una tesitura ms complicada que los pases emergentes, por lo que es difcil pensar que desviaran o ajustaran sus polticas econmicas para perseguir un objetivo de bienestar global. Los gobiernos de pases avanzados tienen que lidiar con sus propios problemas, que no son en lo absoluto despreciables. De hecho, si los superan, la economa mundial estara en 4 mejores condiciones. De ah que los pases emergentes deban tomar las circunstancias y las polticas de los pases avanzados como dadas, y forjar por si mismos su camino hacia delante. En este sentido, sera recomendable que, para afrontar el dilema planteado, los pases emergentes siguieran una estrategia que contara con tres pilares fundamentales. Primer Pilar: mantener fundamentos macroeconmicos sanos. No hay espacio para fundamentos mediocres. En particular, es muy relevante para pases emergentes limitar sus requerimientos financieros a lo que sera asequible en escenarios de estrs. Esto exige una postura fiscal moderada y, si es necesario, usar el manejo de la demanda agregada para evitar dficits abultados en la cuenta corriente. La poltica monetaria se debe concentrar en mantener la inflacin bajo control, puesto que esto ltimo es un prerrequisito para que los tipos de cambio flexibles puedan fungir de manera efectiva como amortiguadores de choques externos. Los sistemas bancarios locales deben ser supervisados estrictamente, y sujetarlos a la brevedad a los 5 estndares regulatorios internacionales, tales como los auspiciados por el Comit de Basilea y el Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera del G-20. Segundo Pilar: Asegurar la fortaleza del sector externo tambin bajo escenarios de estrs. Para empezar, una trayectoria futura de saldos sostenibles de la balanza de pagos es esencial. Flexibilidad de las tasas de inters domsticas y del tipo de cambio, anclados por fundamentos econmicos slidos, debe formar parte del proceso de ajuste en casos de perturbaciones del exterior. Pero dada la gran magnitud de las entradas de capital que han observado las economas emergentes durante los ltimos aos, esos elementos podran no ser suficientes. Por tanto, contar con reservas internacionales altas y otras instancias de apoyo, como la lnea de crdito flexible del Fondo Monetario Internacional, sera altamente recomendable. A la vez, los sectores pblico y privado deben adoptar estrategias proactivas de administracin de sus deudas, procurando 6 aumentar la duracin de las mismas y administrar de manera prudente la exposicin al riesgo cambiario. Tercer Pilar: Promover el crecimiento econmico a travs de hacer las economas ms competitivas, aumentando la productividad total de los factores y por esta va el PIB potencial. Esto nos lleva inexorablemente a la avenida de las reformas estructurales, las cuales tienen gran potencial en las economas emergentes. Este es el camino difcil para alcanzar un mayor crecimiento sostenible del PIB, pero es el nico que es confiable. As pues, en resumen, el primer y segundo pilares estn diseados para garantizar la estabilidad financiera, sin inhibir necesariamente el crecimiento econmico. Pero la palanca real para promover el crecimiento radica en el tercer pilar. Es mi opinin que en el caso de Mxico, se ha puesto en marcha un plan que satisface cabalmente la necesidad de contar con estos tres pilares. Los fundamentos macroeconmicos se han mantenido slidos, tenemos una posicin externa bien pertrechada, an bajo escenarios 7 estresados, y se han emprendido reformas estructurales sin precedente en el pas. Hacia delante nos debemos esforzar para que esta situacin se preserve. * ** Sera omiso en esta participacin si no hago algunos comentarios especficos sobre la poltica monetaria en nuestro pas, ms aun si recordamos que el primero de este mes se cumplieron veinte aos del inicio operativo de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico. Dicha autonoma plena, junto con buenos fundamentos macroeconmicos y estabilidad externa  aunque no exenta de algunos episodios de turbulencia pasajera , le han dado a este Instituto Central los grados de libertad necesarios para consolidar una poltica monetaria creble y anclar de manera efectiva las expectativas de inflacin. As, el ao pasado la Junta de Gobierno tuvo espacio para reducir el objetivo de su tasa de inters de referencia en tres ocasiones: en marzo, como reconocimiento del avance 8 estructural en el en el proceso de abatimiento de la inflacin; y en septiembre y octubre, en respuesta a la holgura en la economa, en el contexto de una inflacin convergente al objetivo permanente de 3 por ciento, e incluso, con una inflacin subyacente inferior a dicho nivel. Esto significa que en el caso de la poltica monetaria hemos entrado en una nueva etapa que nos permite no slo avanzar con mayor claridad hacia la convergencia de la inflacin al objetivo permanente del Banco de Mxico, sino buscar tambin que dicha convergencia se verifique de una manera an ms eficiente. En ese contexto debe entenderse por eficiencia el hecho de que el objetivo permanente se pueda conseguir al menor costo posible en trminos del dinamismo del crecimiento econmico. Por cierto, el extenso y profundo proceso de cambio estructural en el que desde hace unos meses est inmersa la economa mexicana permitir, de llegar a buen puerto, que la aplicacin de la poltica monetaria sea an ms eficiente, es decir: que Mxico pueda crecer de forma mucho ms 9 acelerada y sostenible sin que ello signifique que se generen presiones inflacionarias. Sin embargo, en los meses recientes este proceso de convergencia hacia el objetivo permanente de inflacin baja y estable experiment dos perturbaciones importantes que han significado un desafo coyuntural para la poltica monetaria. La primera fue el alza sbita en precios relativos que se registr en los ltimos meses del ao pasado, tanto en algunos precios agropecuarios, como en las tarifas de transporte pblico en las ciudades ms grandes del pas. A esta perturbacin se sum, al inicio de este ao, el impacto tambin en precios relativos que tuvieron las modificaciones tributarias y de precios pblicos para el ejercicio fiscal 2014. Estos cambios significaron alzas de una sola vez en precios especficos de algunos productos, lo cual es el caso de varios de alto contenido calrico, como en algunas regiones, dada la homogenizacin de la tasa del IVA a 16 por ciento en las fronteras. 10 Deseo dejar claro que el Banco de Mxico apoya, sin duda, las reformas que al incrementar la recaudacin fortalezcan las finanzas pblicas, pues esto ltimo es un factor estructural necesario para tener inflaciones bajas de manera sostenible. El conjunto de estas perturbaciones contribuy a que al inicio de este ao la medicin de la inflacin rebasara de manera notoria el 4 por ciento anual. Sin embargo, los datos subsecuentes han confirmado el diagnstico que hizo en su momento el Banco de Mxico: en la primera quincena de marzo la medicin de la inflacin ya haba regresado al rango de variabilidad aceptable para nuestra meta permanente, especficamente a 3.89 por ciento, en tanto que la inflacin subyacente se ubic abajo del tres por ciento, en 2.84 por ciento. En este caso, el de la inflacin subyacente, es una tasa anual ms baja que las registradas en el mismo periodo de 2013 y de 2012. Esto refleja la credibilidad respecto del anclaje de las variables nominales que ha alcanzado el Banco de Mxico. 11 Un ingrediente importante para este logro ha sido la poltica de comunicacin que ha seguido el Instituto Central, la cual ha permitido anticipar choques en los precios relativos y ha sealado, con la mayor claridad y transparencia posibles, los diagnsticos sobre los que se estn fundando las decisiones de poltica monetaria y cules sern los cursos de accin que seguira el Banco de Mxico ante diferentes eventos. Sin duda esta gua ha sido til para los participantes en los mercados financieros y para el pblico en general, y ha permitido normar las decisiones de los agentes econmicos con menores mrgenes de incertidumbre. Reitero, como en otras ocasiones lo he hecho, que estos choques de precios relativos no representan por s mismos un fenmeno inflacionario, al no ser una elevacin sostenida de todos los precios en la economa. Por lo mismo, no son eventos que puedan o deban combatirse con herramientas de poltica monetaria. En todo caso, el reto fundamental ha sido que esas alteraciones de precios relativos, que son de suyo transitorias, no contaminen otros precios de la 12 economa. La evidencia que tenemos hasta el da de hoy es que esto ltimo no ha sucedido y de ah que no hayamos tenido que modificar la postura de poltica monetaria. La previsin es que la inflacin permanezca por lo que resta de este ao por debajo o cerca del 4 por ciento anual, que cierre el ao debajo de ese lmite superior y que inicie una rpida convergencia al 3 por ciento a partir de 2015. Por supuesto, como repetidamente hemos sealado en nuestros anuncios de poltica monetaria, la Junta de Gobierno se mantendr vigilante para detectar cualquier desviacin respecto de esta hoja de ruta, y no dudar en actuar en consecuencia para corregirla. No es ocioso enfatizar que dentro de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico no tenemos dudas de que nuestro objetivo y misin prioritaria es procurar una inflacin baja y estable. Asimismo, en la medida que exista estabilidad financiera y que sta se consolide sobre bases cada vez ms firmes, la poltica monetaria funciona mejor y en armona con la actividad econmica. 13 En este sentido, el conjunto de iniciativas integradas en la reciente reforma financiera combinan los elementos para dar una mayor solidez al sector financiero con los incentivos adecuados en materia de competencia, y as impulsar un mayor crecimiento y penetracin de la intermediacin financiera. Pero ms all de sus particularidades, ya conocidas por todos ustedes, la reforma financiera adquiere una dimensin decisiva para el futuro crecimiento econmico del pas, cuando se enmarca como un engranaje ms de toda la transformacin estructural que hemos emprendido en los ltimos meses. Este ambicioso proceso reformador, que est en curso, busca cambiar la estructura de la economa mexicana y aumentar la productividad total de los factores de la produccin en el pas. De lograrse bien esta transformacin significar elevar en varios puntos porcentuales el PIB potencial de Mxico y hacerlo en un plazo que sera histricamente corto. 14 No se trata de un entusiasmo ms o menos efmero, o de un impulso circunstancial. Tomando prestada una afortunada descripcin de Octavio Paz acerca de los procesos de cambio, no deberamos perder de vista que estamos hablando de una transformacin que se inscribe en lo que el poeta y ensayista llamaba la cuenta larga en la historia de los pueblos y de las naciones. Title: The enigma of economic development
text: The Enigma of Economic Development Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, on the occasion of the inauguration of the exhibition "Sustainable Development: Images of the World", at the Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE), in Mexico City, on January 31, 2012. It is an honor for me to have the opportunity to address a few words to you on the occasion of the inauguration of the photographic exhibition "Sustainable Development: Images of the World" at the Interactive Museum of Economics. I congratulate the organizers of this exhibition and, in particular, the French Development Agency for this splendid initiative that coincides with the celebration of its seventieth anniversary. The theme of the exhibition that opens today is of great importance, since development is the way in which societies can increase their level of well-being. Although not exclusively, quality of life is associated with the quantity of goods and services produced, which ultimately makes it an economic phenomenon. Only with a higher income can people eat better, buy medicines, become more educated, travel, and have access to other means of material and spiritual satisfaction. Despite the inevitable economic cycles, development implies the maintenance, for prolonged periods, of an upward trend in production. Its sustainability requires ensuring that physical, natural or financial resources are not compromised limiting future prosperity, hence it is natural to qualify development as "sustainable". Moreover, only with lasting economic growth can poverty and marginalization be effectively combated. This exhibition reminds us that driving development is challenging. Perhaps there is no more troubling task for economists and for economists. 1 Policymakers understand why some nations have prospered and others have lagged behind and, more specifically, why today the per capita income level of the richest societies is more than thirty times that of the poorest. Immediately it is clear that we are facing some questions whose answer can be complex. Undoubtedly, long-term growth is a mysterious process in which multiple factors must interact harmoniously, although not unique, much less mechanically. For progress there are no panaceas or recipes for two or three magical actions. To be fair, I must clarify that economists have identified with relative clarity three major symptomatic elements that tend to underpin long-term material development: first, investment in physical capital, i.e. in machines and factories; second, growth in human capital, i.e. increases in health and education, which, incidentally, may include schooling and job training; and third, technological change, expressed in the generation or absorption of knowledge that makes us more productive. My list of factors is simple and hopefully useful, but clearly not enough to understand development. In particular if, as confirmed by economic science and data, the elements referred to are the pillars of progress, why have less advanced societies not adopted them or, at least, not done so with sufficient intensity or perseverance? This deeper question increases the complexity of the topic. Development scholars have tried several responses, but the one that seems most grounded is the one that identifies the real causes of development with the institutions and policies that generate appropriate incentives for the factors I mentioned. The constitution of such an environment conducive to growth is a choice of society and its implementation is a non-transferable task of the State. Although the 2 The configuration of such rules of the game depends on each country and there is no single model, I would like to cite two elements that seem to have played a crucial role in strengthening the pillars of development in many countries. The first is respect for property rights, which, for example, means that each person can enjoy, without being unjustifiably robbed, of the fruits of their productive effort. This principle is the raison d'etre of the priority objective of the Bank of Mexico and many central banks in the world, to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. Inflation operates as an unlegislated tax on savings which, by the way, tends to affect the poorest the most. Respect for property rights, which also includes public safety and the equal application of laws, creates incentives to educate, work, invest and innovate which, as I mentioned, are the foundation of development. In addition, the definition of property rights is an efficient way to combat some of the problems that endanger the preservation of nature and the environment and, therefore, sustainable development. With definition and respect for property rights, the exploitation without renewal of forests or fishing without cultivation of aquatic species is unthinkable. A second element of the enabling environment is competition in economic transactions. Free entry to participate in productive activities and openness to the outside world promote efficiency, while allowing people living in other countries to enjoy the fruits of ingenuity, such as electronic tablets and telephones. 3 smart today, and incorporate new technologies that make us more productive.1 Finally, for the development process to be sustainable, it is necessary to maintain a social consensus in favor of growth, which implies facilitating the access of the entire population to the possibilities of progress. This may include, for example, transitional support to the poorest population in basic education, in such a way as to strengthen incentives to work, through transfers aimed at families sending their children to school. The photographic exhibition that we will appreciate today is an interesting account of some of the programs that the French Development Agency has carried out in solidarity in seven countries of the Southern Hemisphere in favor of sustainable development. Through the eyes of seven photographers we can imagine how the promotion of maternal and child health, the use of soils, the interconnection of villages, education and the transfer of knowledge can activate, along with other elements, the opportunities for progress. I conclude by reiterating my congratulations to those who made it possible for us to enjoy this exhibition and to the French Development Agency on its anniversary, wishing it many more years of fruitful work contributing to understanding the conditions that explain the mysterious process of economic development. 1 For a review of the empirical evidence supporting the importance of economic institutions and policies on development, see Daron Acemoglu, Introduction to Modern Economic Gowth, Princeton: Princeton University Press, 2009, especially Chapter 4. 4

De inmediato se constata que estamos frente a unos interrogantes cuya respuesta puede ser compleja. La constitucin de ese ambiente favorable al crecimiento es una eleccin de la sociedad y su aplicacin es una tarea intransferible del Estado. Aunque la 2 configuracin de tales reglas del juego depende de cada pas y no existe un modelo nico, me gustara citar dos elementos que parecen haber desempeado un papel crucial en el robustecimiento de los pilares del desarrollo en muchos pases. La inflacin opera como un impuesto no legislado sobre el ahorro que, por cierto, tiende a afectar ms a los ms pobres. El respeto a los derechos de propiedad, que incluye tambin la seguridad pblica y la aplicacin igualitaria de las leyes, genera incentivos para educarse, trabajar, invertir e innovar que, como mencion, son el basamento del desarrollo. Adems, la definicin de los derechos de propiedad es una forma eficiente de combatir algunos de los problemas que ponen en peligro la preservacin de la naturaleza y el medio ambiente y, por lo tanto, el desarrollo sustentable. Con definicin y respeto a los derechos de propiedad es impensable la explotacin sin renovacin de los bosques o la pesca sin cultivo de las especies acuticas. Un segundo elemento del entorno favorable es la competencia en las transacciones econmicas. La libre entrada a participar en las actividades productivas y la apertura al exterior propician la eficiencia, a la vez que permiten disfrutar los frutos del ingenio de las personas que viven en otros pases, como es el caso de las tabletas electrnicas y los telfonos 3 inteligentes en la actualidad, e incorporar nuevas tecnologas que nos hacen ms productivos.1 Finalmente, para que el proceso de desarrollo sea sostenible se requiere mantener un consenso social a favor del crecimiento, lo que implica facilitar el acceso de toda la poblacin a las posibilidades de progreso. Esto puede incluir, por ejemplo, el apoyo transicional a la poblacin ms pobre en materia de educacin bsica, de forma tal que se fortalezcan los incentivos al trabajo, mediante transferencias orientadas a que las familias enven a sus hijos a la escuela. La muestra fotogrfica que hoy apreciaremos es un interesante recuento de algunos de los programas que la Agencia Francesa de Desarrollo ha llevado a cabo solidariamente en siete pases del Hemisferio Sur a favor del desarrollo sustentable. A travs de la mirada de siete fotgrafos podremos imaginar cmo el impulso a la salud materno-infantil, el aprovechamiento de los suelos, la interconexin de los poblados, la educacin y la transferencia de conocimientos puede activar, junto con otros elementos, las oportunidades de progreso. Title: Putting into circulation the 500 peso banknote of the new family of Mexican banknotes
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, on the occasion of the circulation of the 500 peso note of the new family of Mexican banknotes. Ladies and gentlemen, members of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico; Distinguished representatives of educational institutions and research centers; Ladies and gentlemen: On behalf of the Bank of Mexico, and in the company of all the members of the Governing Board, it is an honor to welcome you to the Interactive Museum of Economy to announce the new family of Mexican banknotes and, on this occasion, put into circulation the banknote corresponding to the denomination of 500 pesos. Central banks have as one of their primary functions to issue the currency of a country, as well as to preserve its purchasing power. In our case, the corresponding law is very clear and states in its article 2 that: "The purpose of the Bank of Mexico shall be to provide the country with national currency. In achieving this purpose, its priority objective will be to preserve the purchasing power of said currency". By not having an intrinsic value, the issuance and circulation of fiat money fulfills its purpose when the population trusts that the authority that issues that currency will generate the conditions to make it effective as a store of value and means of payment. This confidence in the value of the currency is key to the evolution of economies because, to the extent that it is consolidated as a generally accepted means of payment, it facilitates the realization of transactions of all kinds, while expanding the coverage of such operations. In modern times, periods of high inflation erode confidence in money, because by undermining the purchasing power of the 2 banknotes and coins, their effectiveness as a store of value is hindered and their capacity as a means of payment is uncertain. In particular, there are numerous episodes in history and in various countries, even recent ones, in which uncontrolled inflation reduces the acceptance and social esteem of money, with disastrous consequences. That is why, since the end of the last century, the international consensus has advanced that the national currency issuing authority should concentrate on ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the currency, with a sustained approach and alien to political cycles. Consequently, a large number of countries decided to give their central banks the task of ensuring price stability and empowering them to achieve that important objective. Throughout its history, Mexico has also recorded episodes in which confidence in money has deteriorated. For example, in the nineteenth century internal wars caused a significant delay in the adoption and acceptance of paper money. Likewise, during the Mexican Revolution, the anarchic issuance of money by the different factions in conflict, led to the rejection of the banknotes of that time. To reverse this deterioration in confidence in the means of payment, the Constitution of 1917 contemplated the creation of a central bank, as an institution of the State, with the exclusive power to provide 3 currency to the nation's economy. Since its founding in 1925, the Bank of Mexico has provided banknotes and coins to the Mexican economy. Over the years, the Bank of Mexico has managed to consolidate public confidence in paper money. Thus, and especially since its autonomy, the Bank of Mexico has made substantial progress in the stability of the purchasing power of the Mexican currency and has gone from very high and persistent inflation figures, which were presented in some stages of the past, to levels close to the permanent target of 3 percent. Our country has also forged a rich numismatic tradition. This has allowed, on the one hand, that some of the Mexican coins and banknotes are recognized among the most beautiful in the world. On the other hand, the use of these coins and banknotes has generated identification and strengthened the feeling of belonging and unity among the population. For all the above, I am very pleased to announce the new family of banknotes and put into circulation their first denomination. This new family has new and better standards of safety and durability and, at the same time, with iconographic elements that highlight the historical identity and natural heritage of our country. 4 Due to technological advances, security requirements, the wear and tear of paper money in circulation or the new needs of users, banknote families are usually renewed periodically. These renovations are planned well in advance, given that the process of designing and manufacturing a banknote family takes several years. According to the powers granted by law, the Bank of Mexico has the power to determine the design and characteristics of the banknotes. In this case, the decision to print a new family of banknotes was taken more than five years ago, when in 2013 the Governing Board instructed the General Directorate of Issuance to start work to gradually replace the banknotes that circulate today. With this new family of banknotes, the Bank of Mexico seeks to face various challenges. The use of new technologies provides banknotes with better security measures, which will make them more difficult to counterfeit. Likewise, the identification elements that these banknotes have will make them easier for users to authenticate, including people with visual weakness and blindness. Likewise, the use of state-of-the-art materials will allow to extend its useful life. 5 For the rest, these banknotes will highlight the historical, cultural and natural heritage of the country, through images that represent the most important stages and events of our history, as well as the varied natural wealth of our territory. The choice of theme and particular motifs illustrating the new banknote family was part of a meticulous process of analysis and consultation. The Bank of Mexico collected data on the population's preferences for banknotes through studies, surveys and focus groups. Based on this, it was decided to focus the new banknotes on two themes "Historical identity and natural heritage". On the one hand, the choice of the theme "historical identity", which will occupy the obverse of the banknotes, responds to the fact that, traditionally, the appearance on paper money of heroes and notable characters contributes to the population strengthening its sense of community and identifying with figures who, by their actions and virtues, have left an important mark on the national memory. On the other hand, the theme of the reverse, related to Mexican ecosystems, was chosen because it will help to disseminate, appreciate and preserve one of our most valuable and, sometimes, little disseminated collections, which is the natural heritage. Its appearance on the banknotes will allow to know in greater detail the diverse ecosystems of the country, to assess its 6 importance for economic and social development, and contribute to preserving this extraordinary legacy. In this way, in the choice of this dual theme, past, present and future converge: pride in history and a sense of responsibility for the sustainable development of the next generations. To define the historical figures that will appear on the obverses of the banknotes, as well as the elements of fauna and flora that will illustrate the reverses, a consultation process was carried out that allowed to identify the representativeness of the motifs, as well as their accuracy and historical and scientific rigor. In this regard, the Bank of Mexico deeply appreciates the participation of experts from renowned educational institutions and research centers. Among the institutions that were consulted, and of which some of their members do us the honor of joining us on this occasion, are:  the Mexican Academy of Language;  the Centre for Research and Higher Studies in Social Anthropology (CIESAS);  the Colegio de Mexico;  the National College;  the National Commission of Natural Protected Areas;  the National Commission for the Knowledge and Use of the Biodiversity; 7  the National Council for Culture and the Arts, now the Ministry of Culture;  the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH);  the National Institute of Statistics and Geography;  the National Institute of Historical Studies of the Revolutions of Mexico (INEHRM);  the Mexican Society of Authors of the Plastic Arts,  and the National Autonomous University of Mexico, through various study centers. In addition, this Central Institute organized an international seminar with banknote designers to discuss new trends and technologies in this field. Various tests were also carried out to select the best quality raw materials and safety elements. With the results obtained, the new banknotes were manufactured, ensuring that, in addition to being functional and safe, they strengthen identification and highlight the shared values among Mexicans. The obverses of the new banknotes address six fundamental historical stages: one, The Old Mexico; two, the Colony; three, Independence, four, reform and restoration of the Republic; five, the Mexican Revolution and, six, Contemporary Mexico. The 8 Stages were ordered chronologically, as the value of the denomination increased. The new banknotes also exalt the diversity and natural wealth of the country and, on their reverses, allude to the six most representative ecosystems of Mexico: one, rivers and lakes; two, temperate forests; three, thickets and deserts; four, coasts, seas and islands; five, humid forests and, six, dry forests; through sites recognized in the "World Heritage" list of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Today we present the first banknote of this new family, which corresponds to the denomination of 500 pesos. The decision to manufacture this denomination first responds to the fact that it is the banknote that circulates the most and, therefore, the one that suffers the most counterfeiting attempts, so its introduction was the most convenient. According to the established program, the design and manufacture of this new 500 peso note began in the first half of 2016. Today, the circular was published instructing credit institutions to start the circulation of this banknote. With this, the gestation cycle of this first denomination of the new family is completed. 9 The predominant color of the new 500 peso banknote is blue and, following the chronological order established by denomination, it corresponds to refer to the historical process of the Reform and Restoration of the Republic, whose indisputable reference is Benito Juarez. In particular, this banknote shows the effigy of President Juarez, accompanied by the fragment of the engraving of the Mexican artist Alberto Beltran that alludes to his triumphal entry into Mexico City on July 15, 1867, the date that marks the end of the Second Empire and the restoration of the Republic. The figure of Don Benito Juarez, who has repeatedly illustrated the national currency, is one of the most unanimously admired for his example of self-improvement; for its defense of national sovereignty and liberal and republican values; as well as, for its unwavering effort to move from a country of confrontations to one of laws and institutions. The reverse of this same note illustrates the ecosystem of coasts, seas and islands, represented by the Biosphere Reserve of El Vizcaino, located in Baja California Sur. This reserve was declared a protected natural area in 1988 and considered "Natural Heritage of Humanity" by UNESCO. With its five kilometers of coastal strip, 10 The El Vizcaino Biosphere Reserve is an important sanctuary for the species known as "Grey Whale". In the following stages of this issuance program, it is scheduled that in the second half of 2019 and 2020, respectively, the banknotes corresponding to the denominations of 200 and 1,000 pesos will be put into circulation. The 200 peso bill will refer to Independence, with the figures of Miguel Hidalgo and Jose Maria Morelos on the obverse; while its reverse will illustrate the ecosystem of thickets and deserts, with the heritage of the El Pinacate Reserve and Gran Desierto del Altar, and the Golden Eagle. For its part, the 1,000 peso bill will allude to the Mexican Revolution, with Francisco I. Madero, Carmen Serdan and Hermila Galindo on its obverse, while on the reverse they will have a representation of the system of humid jungles, the heritage of the ancient Mayan city Calakmul and the jaguar. To elaborate on the new family of banknotes, I invite you to visit the microsite on the subject that is available on the website of the Bank of Mexico. There you will find detailed information on the powers of the central bank in the issuance of currency, the decision-making process on the new family of banknotes, the characteristics of the different denominations of banknotes and the periodicity of their appearance. 11 Ladies and gentlemen, the stability of the purchasing power of coins and banknotes and full confidence in their use are an indispensable imperative to generate conditions for economic growth and the well-being of the population. Therefore, it is appropriate to redouble the effort to achieve and sustain this objective. In Mexico, with the Constitutional mandate of the Bank of Mexico, to maintain the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, the public is given an element of certainty about the value of banknotes and coins and their use as a means of payment. With this new family, the Bank of Mexico seeks to make Mexican banknotes safer and more functional, to continue to reinforce the trust and pride of those who use them daily, and to contribute to strengthening our national identity. Thank you all very much. 12

Por eso, desde finales del siglo pasado, avanz el consenso internacional de que la autoridad emisora de moneda nacional se concentrara en procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda, con un enfoque sostenido y ajeno a los ciclos polticos.
