Desde que el Banco de Mxico es autnomo se han bajado los niveles de inflacin de niveles de 3 dgitos a uno solo y se ha logrado una menor persistencia inflacionaria, un anclaje de las expectativas en niveles prximos a la meta y un menor traspaso de las variaciones de precios relativos, en particular de las fluctuaciones cambiarias, al nivel de inflacin. Seoras y seores: El Premio Reto BANXICO es muy importante para el Banco de Mxico, pues contribuye a que muchos de los estudiantes universitarios ms talentosos, con mejor formacin y con mayor influencia futura se involucren con los objetivos prioritarios de nuestra institucin. La respuesta a la convocatoria de este ao implica, ya por s misma, un xito. Para la tercera edicin del Premio Reto Banxico se inscribieron 303 equipos y se recibieron 190 trabajos escritos, lo que equivale a una 9 participacin total de 1361 participantes entre estudiantes y profesores asesores. Participaron 110 instituciones educativas y se inscribieron equipos pertenecientes a 28 entidades federativas. Las presentaciones se destacaron por el conocimiento, soltura y profesionalismo con que se manejaron los equipos y por lo pertinente y fundado de sus recomendaciones de poltica. Acabamos de escuchar, la deliberacin del jurado y la nominacin del ganador. Felicidades tanto al triunfador como a los equipos finalistas. Para el Banco de Mxico es un motivo de satisfaccin el grado de participacin y calidad en este certamen. Los magnficos trabajos que ustedes realizaron constituyen una aportacin original y contribuyen a que haya un mayor consenso social en torno a la tarea del banco central, lo que contribuye a que sus objetivos se alcancen de mejor manera. Gracias a todos y, otra vez, muchsimas felicidades. 10

Title: 76 Banking Convention
text: Remarks by the Governor of Banco de Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, on the occasion of the 76th Banking Convention, held in Acapulco, Guerrero, April of 2013. ? Mr. Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Fernando Aportela Rodriguez ? Mr. President of the National Banking and Securities Commission, teacher Jaime Gonzalez Aguade ? Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, Mr. Jaime Ruiz Sacristan ? Mr. President-Elect of the ABM, Mr. Javier Arrigunaga Gomez del Campo Ladies and gentlemen: Good afternoon, all of you. As on previous occasions, it is a privilege for me to have the opportunity to address a few words to such a distinguished audience. Today I would like to share with you some reflections on the remarkable institutional progress we have achieved in the conduct of macroeconomic policy in Mexico. A sign of this progress is the great structural change in the control of inflation that has been achieved over the last few years. 1 In addition, it is pertinent to recognize that we continue to face a very complicated external environment. The crisis that began in 2008 in the financial system of the United States and that quickly spread to other latitudes, has taken much longer than anticipated for its resolution, so that the advanced countries have been running out of the degrees of freedom to adopt countercyclical policies. Hence, it has fallen on monetary policy to mitigate recessionary pressures on the economy and open a window of time for structural reforms that effectively have the potential to accelerate economic growth to be implemented. Emerging countries, including Mexico, quickly outweighed the initial impact of the crisis thanks to their macroeconomic strength, but more recently we have resented the global economic slowdown and the externalities of unconventional monetary policies of advanced countries. It is therefore of the utmost importance to analyse the impact that the prolongation of extremely loose monetary policies in the main advanced countries could have on the country. I will develop this theme in the second part of my speech. 1. Framework for the Conduct of Macroeconomic Policy The conduct of macroeconomic policy in Mexico is based on four pillars: fiscal policy, monetary policy, the exchange rate regime, and financial regulation and supervision. These are four pillars that are congruent with each other and whose objective is to shape 2 a solid and stable platform for economic growth and the well-being of the population. In the first place, the prudent and responsible management of fiscal policy has made it possible to eradicate the large and persistent imbalances in public finances that our country suffered in the past. As a result of fiscal discipline, public sector debt as a share of GDP has remained low and has improved its profile considerably (Figure 1). Among the measures taken in recent years is the entry into force of the Federal Law on Budget and Financial Responsibility in March 2006, which establishes, among other rules, a balanced budget rule. Likewise, the tax reforms of 2008 and 2010 that contributed to further strengthening the fiscal position of our country also stand out, along with the fact that, after the space was used in this last year to have moderate deviations from the fiscal balance for temporary reasons, the current Government returned to a draft fiscal balance for 2013. All of the above has significantly reduced the vulnerability of public finances in Mexico and improved its relative position in the global economy. 3 Figure 1 Public Debt 1/ % of GDP 165 Prognosis 145 125 EEUUA 105 Spain 85 65 Brazil 45 Mexico 25 Balance Fiscal 2/ % of GDP 4 Forecast 2 Mexico 00 Brazil -2 -4 -6 EEUUA -8 -10 Spain -12 -14 5 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 -16 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 1/ For Mexico it refers to the Historical Balance of the Financial Requirements of the Public Sector. Source: World Economic Outllok (IMF) and Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (SHCP). 2/ For Mexico, it refers to PEMEX's Public Balance Sheet without Investment. Source: World Economic Outllok (IMF) and Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (SHCP). Secondly, with regard to monetary policy, since 1993 Mexico has had an autonomous central bank which, in accordance with the Constitution, has as its priority objective to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. The fundamental element of autonomy is to maintain the separation between fiscal and monetary policies, through prohibiting the financing of fiscal imbalances through primary issuance. Within this framework of autonomy, since 2001 the Bank of Mexico adopted an inflation targeting regime for the conduct of monetary policy. The effort to strengthen this scheme has been permanent. Thus, for example, in 2011 the minutes on the monetary policy decision meetings began to be published, which has further improved the transparency and communication of the Central Institute, key 4 to anchor inflation expectations among both market participants and the general public. The ordering of public finances and monetary policy adopted by the Issuing Institute has resulted in a significant reduction in inflation, reaching low and stable levels, which in recent years has fluctuated between 3 and 4 per cent in general. (Graph 2). The figures for 2013 are forecast. Source: INEGI and Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (SHCP). Third, with regard to exchange rate policy, since the mid-nineties Mexico has maintained a flexible exchange rate regime. The floating regime has been a fundamental element for macroeconomic policy, since it has functioned as a buffer mechanism against the external shocks that Mexico's economy has experienced. In this sense, the depreciation that the real exchange rate had after the crisis that 5 it began in 2008, induced rapid export growth and a rebound in our economic growth (Chart 3). It should be noted that among the currencies of the emerging countries the peso has managed to maintain its real depreciation for a longer time since 2008, largely due to the appropriate mix of fiscal and monetary policy that we have followed. Figure 3 Multilateral Real Exchange Rate Index Jun-08100 Depreciation 2008 2009 Source: Bank for International Settlements. 2010 2011 120 115 110 Chile Colombia 105 100 Brazil Korea 95 90 Mexico 85 80 2012 75 2013 The fourth major pillar of macroeconomic stability enjoyed by Mexico is a healthy and well-capitalized financial system. Adequate financial regulation and supervision has contributed to this. In this regard, it should be noted that Mexico has made significant progress in adopting the provisions relating to Basel III (Figure 4). Likewise, our country has, like other nations, a Financial System Stability Council, in which various authorities participate, including the Bank of Mexico and 6 the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, which aims to detect in a timely manner possible vulnerabilities within the financial system, as well as the preparation of recommendations to address them. All of the above has contributed to Mexico being one of the few countries that has a healthy and well-capitalized banking system with the ability to contribute to economic growth with solid regulatory bases. Figure 4 Bank Capitalization Index 1/ % 24 22 ICAP Current Regulatory Minimum 20 18 Previous Regulatory Minimum 16 14 12 10 8 6 4 2 0 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 1/ Current Regulatory Minimum in force as of January 2013. Source: CNBV and Banco de Mexico. 2. Achievements in Terms of Inflation Thanks to all the above, the Mexican economy enjoys a an environment of stability and certainty, within which the control that has been achieved over inflation stands out. The result has been a more than significant reduction in the level, volatility and persistence of inflation in Mexico. 7 To illustrate the structural progress achieved in this area, it should be noted that we have managed to reduce general inflation from levels above 100 percent in some years of the eighties to levels close to 3 percent today. In this way, for more than ten years inflation has been fluctuating in an orderly manner around a level that is the lowest since the National Consumer Price Index is calculated (Graph 5). Figure 5 Headline Inflation 1/ % Per Year 200 150 100 50 0 -50 1976 1979 1982 1985 1988 1991 1994 1997 2000 2003 2006 2009 2013 1/ Information as of the first half of April 2013. Source: INEGI and Banco de Mexico. The degree of persistence of inflation has also decreased. Generally speaking, inflation is said to be persistent when shocks affecting it, such as changes in certain relative prices, for example for some agricultural products, have a prolonged impact. On the contrary, if such 8 Shocks have only a transitory effect on inflation, which is described as non-persistent. This lower persistence has been reflected in a lower effect of passing on variations, both in the exchange rate and in the prices of agricultural goods to inflation (Graph 6A and 6B). Figure 6A General Inflation and Exchange Rate Change 1/% Per Year 300 Figure 6B General Inflation and Agricultural Inflation 2/ % Annual 300 250 Exchange Rate Change 200 150 250 200 Agricultural Inflation 150 100 Headline Inflation 50 100 Headline Inflation 50 0 0 -50 -50 1976 1982 1988 1994 2000 2006 2013 1976 1982 1988 1994 2000 2006 2013 1/ General inflation at the first half of April 2013. Source: INEGI and Banco de Mexico. 2/ Information as of the first half of April 2013. Source: INEGI and Banco de Mexico. In the evidence presented, it stands out that in the past the general inflation rate was very closely correlated with changes in the exchange rate and agricultural prices, while more recently this correlation has been substantially reduced. As a result of the favorable results in terms of combating inflation, monetary policy in Mexico has enjoyed a 9 high degree of credibility. This has made it possible to anchor the inflation expectations of economic agents within the range of variability defined by the Bank of Mexico, and close to the permanent inflation target. In this way, a virtuous circle is generated, since efforts to consolidate price stability feed back into a favorable evolution of inflation expectations (Graph 7), and vice versa. Figure 7 Annual Headline Inflation Expectations % 6.0 5.0 Average Next 4 years 4.0 3.0 Average Next 5-8 years 2.0 1.0 2003 2004 2005 2005 2006 2007 2008 2008 2009 2010 2011 2011 2012 Source: Banco de Mexico Survey. Thus, inflationary risk premiums have been reduced in our country, which has resulted in lower interest rates. This reduction has been substantial. In fact, current rates at virtually any term are at historically low levels (Figure 8). 10 Figure 8 91-day Cetes Short-Term Interest Rates, % 160 140 120 100 80 60 40 20 0 1980 1983 1986 1989 1992 1995 1998 2001 2004 2007 2010 2013 Source: Banco de Mexico. In addition, the sustained and credible decline in inflation has manifested itself not only in reductions in interest rates, but also in an extension of the terms at which financial transactions are made in the country. For several years now we have had a yield curve of government securities that reaches 30 years, when in 1995 the maximum term was just 6 months (Graph 9). 11 Graph 9 Government Bond Yield Curve % 60 1995 50 40 1998 30 2000 20 2006 10 2013 0 1 day 1 Month 3 Months 6 Months 1 Year 2 Years 3 Years 5 Years 7 Years 10 Years 20 Years 30 Years Source: Bank of Mexico. This makes it clear that keeping inflation at low and stable levels is not a goal in itself. It is a means to conquer higher goals. The resulting low interest rates result in greater investment, greater job creation and a faster reduction in poverty. Hence, it is important that the intermediaries involved in the credit channel of transmission of monetary policy, notoriously commercial banks, are ready to take advantage of the very favorable conditions prevailing in interest rates. Of course, another purpose of keeping inflation low is to avoid the most regressive tax, since it is well known that high inflation rates erode workers' wages and the 12 income of pensioners. This confirms that the benefits of price stability are many and varied. Thus, the decision of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico last March to reduce by 50 basis points the target for the Overnight Interbank Interest Rate should be interpreted as a recognition of the structural achievements that have been achieved in terms of controlling inflation. In this context, it is important and timely to mention the recent increase in inflation observed in March and in the first half of April. Indeed, annual headline inflation recently stood above 4 percent and is expected to remain at similar levels in the next two months and then, starting in June, resume a downward trajectory. It should be noted that the current rebound, predicted at the time by Banco de Mexico, is due to supply disturbances associated with climatic and phytosanitary factors, increases in public transport fares, as well as a low comparison base in fruit and vegetable prices. Given the nature of the factors that have caused this rebound in inflation, it is considered that this episode of changes in relative prices will not affect the process of convergence of inflation towards the permanent target that we have set. In fact, in the horizon in which monetary policy has an impact on the economy, about 18 months, it is expected that headline inflation will be close to 3 percent. It should also be noted that despite 13 The shocks that have had an impact on headline inflation, core inflation, which largely reflects the medium-term trend in inflation, has behaved very favourably. During the first quarter of the year it averaged below 3 percent, and most likely for the rest of 2013 and for 2014 it will remain close to or even below that level. It is worth highlighting the differentiated behavior of core and non-core inflation. The first records the price variation of 77 per cent of the basket used as a reference in the INPC, and is mainly comprised of processed foods, tobacco, alcohol, non-food goods and services. The prices of this collection of goods and services are fundamentally determined by market forces and have the capacity to respond, with certain lags, to the monetary policy measures adopted by the Bank of Mexico. The basket of products whose prices are used to calculate non-core inflation are agricultural products and services and commodities whose prices are determined by federal or other government authorities, which is why they do not respond to monetary policy actions. In recent years, the main factor preventing the permanent headline inflation target of 3% from being achieved in a durable manner is the high volatility of non-core inflation (Chart 10). 14 Figure 10 Headline, Core and Non-Core Inflation 1/ % 15 13 Non-Core 11 Headline Inflation 9 7 5 3 Underlying 1 2000 2001 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 1/ Information as of the first half of April 2013. Source: INEGI and Banco de Mexico. This does not prevent the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico from remaining attentive, as it has always done, to the behavior of all the determinants of inflation, as well as to the evolution of its prospects. This is in order to ensure that the process of price and wage formation in the economy is not effectively contaminated, and gradually converges to the permanent inflation target of 3 per cent. 3. Challenges of the International Situation I now proceed to comment on some of the challenges that the international situation poses to the macroeconomic policy of our country. 15 As we know, in recent years the international environment has been very complicated. Several advanced economies have faced the worst economic crisis since the time of the Great Depression. In response to the crisis, the central banks of these economies have adopted highly accommodative monetary policies, bringing their benchmark interest rates to levels close to zero since the end of 2008. In addition to the above, some of these economies have adopted various unconventional monetary policy actions in order to provide greater monetary stimulus (Figure 11). Figure 11 Central Bank Balance Sheets % of GDP 70 Prognosis 60 50 European Central Bank 40 Bank of Japan 30 Bank of England Federal Reserve I 2008 IV 2008 III 2009 II 2010 Source: Central Banks and Haver Analytics. I 2011 IV 2011 III 2012 II 2013 I 2014 20 10 0 IV 2014 This high monetary policy lassitude at the global level has contributed to an environment of exceptionally low interest rates in advanced economies. While it fits 16 To point out that in the immediate future a withdrawal of monetary stimulus in these economies is not contemplated, since global economic growth continues to be weak and dependent on the aforementioned stimulus, this scenario cannot be considered in any way as permanent. Therefore, the environment of very low interest rates will not last indefinitely and eventually advanced economies will have to normalize monetary conditions. This can have important repercussions for the rest of the world, so it is appropriate to discuss this issue from the perspective of an emerging economy such as Mexico. Accommodative monetary policies in advanced countries have been aimed at stabilizing financial markets and supporting economic activity. In the case of our main trading partner, the United States, both purposes are being achieved, which has brought benefits to our country. Considering the high degree of trade and financial integration between the economies of Mexico and the United States, greater economic dynamism in the latter has undoubtedly had a favorable impact on our economy. In addition to the above, the environment of exceptionally low interest rates in advanced economies has also contributed to an episode of significant capital flows to emerging economies, from which Mexico has not escaped. 17 Generally speaking, capital inflows provide significant benefits for host economies. For example, they supplement domestic savings with resources from abroad, which makes it possible to finance higher rates of investment. However, there are also certain challenges associated with such flows, especially when they occur in an environment of high volatility and high speed. In particular, capital inflows tend to generate pressures towards the appreciation of the national currency. In the case of Mexico, the exchange rate appreciation to date has been consistent with the strength shown by the national economy, reflecting the differentials in economic growth rates, as well as monetary policy stances, between Mexico and our main trading partners. However, the volatility that has been observed in capital flows can lead to an overreaction of the exchange rate that must be carefully monitored by the authority (Graph 12). 18 Figure 12 Holding of Government Securities of Foreigners Billions of Pesos 1,200 Bonuses 1,100 1,000 900 800 700 600 CETES 500 400 300 200 100 0 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2008 Exchange Rate 1/ Pesos per Dollar 2009 2010 2011 2012 16 15 14 13 12 11 10 2013 Source: Bank of Mexico. 1/ The observed exchange rate is the daily data of the FIX exchange rate. The last data of the observed exchange rate corresponds to April 25, 2013. Source: Bank of Mexico. In addition to their impact on the exchange rate, the international financial flows to which I have referred can also lead to excessive increases in domestic asset prices and excessive credit expansions, which often lead to the formation of financial imbalances. There is also a risk that a reversal of capital flows will occur in the event of a possible withdrawal of monetary stimulus, which, in principle, may have significant consequences for financial stability and economic activity. 19 It is important to emphasize that given the strength of the institutional framework of macroeconomic policy in Mexico, today the national economy is in good condition to face a scenario such as the one described. Indeed, considering the improvement in the economic fundamentals of our country, the remarkable resistance that the Mexican economy has shown in the face of the shocks it has suffered recently, and the permanent emphasis of the authorities on identifying vulnerabilities and strengthening financial regulation and supervision, it is possible to argue that an environment of confidence currently prevails over our economy. In addition, we have a historically high level of international reserves along with the flexible credit line of the International Monetary Fund for more than 70,000 million dollars (Graph 13), resources that would be, in their case, extremely useful to face some contingency. Figure 13 International Reservations 1/ Billions of Dollars 260 240 IMF Flexible Credit Line 220 200 180 160 140 120 International Reserves 100 80 60 40 20 2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 0 2013 1/ Information as of April 19, 2013. Source: Bank of Mexico. 20 However, we cannot be complacent. The international situation imposes problems on us that we should not underestimate. The normalization of monetary conditions in advanced economies can have important repercussions for the world economy and, consequently, for our economy. In particular, it can lead to a massive reallocation of investments globally and lead to a sudden reversal of capital flows that have reached emerging economies. Overall, economies with strong fundamentals are expected to be relatively less affected by the potential phenomena described than those with a relatively more compromised position. In this scenario, continuing to strengthen the environment of trust in the Mexican economy is an imperative. That is why the effort to continue improving the institutional framework for macroeconomic policy in our country must be permanent. We must also make even more progress in the process of structural reforms to make our economy increasingly competitive. That has borne fruit in the past and is to be expected to bear fruit in the future. Thanks a lot. 21
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador de Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, con motivo de la 76 Convencin Bancaria, celebrada en Acapulco, Guerrero, abril de 2013.  Seor Subsecretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Fernando Aportela Rodriguez  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, maestro Jaime Gonzlez Aguad  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, licenciado Jaime Ruz Sacristn  Seor Presidente Electo de la ABM, licenciado Javier Arrigunaga Gmez del Campo Seoras y seores: Muy buenas tardes tengan todos ustedes. Como en ocasiones anteriores es para m un privilegio tener la oportunidad de dirigir algunas palabras a tan distinguida audiencia. El da de hoy me gustara compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones en torno al notable progreso institucional que hemos alcanzado en la conduccin de la poltica macroeconmica en Mxico. Signo de dicho progreso es el gran cambio estructural en el control de la inflacin que se ha conseguido a lo largo de los ltimos aos. 1 Adems, es pertinente reconocer que continuamos enfrentando un entorno externo muy complicado. La crisis que inici en 2008 en el sistema financiero de los Estados Unidos y que rpidamente se propag a otras latitudes, ha llevado mucho ms tiempo del que se anticipaba para su resolucin, por lo que a los pases avanzados se les han ido agotando los grados de libertad para adoptar polticas contracclicas. De ah que haya recado sobre la poltica monetaria mitigar las presiones recesivas sobre la economa y abrir una ventana de tiempo para que se puedan implementar las reformas estructurales que efectivamente tengan el potencial de acelerar el crecimiento econmico. Los pases emergentes, entre ellos Mxico, superaron rpidamente el impacto inicial de la crisis gracias a su fortaleza macroeconmica, pero ms recientemente hemos resentido la desaceleracin econmica mundial y las externalidades de las polticas monetarias no convencionales de los pases avanzados. Por tanto, es de suma importancia analizar el impacto que podra tener sobre el pas la prolongacin de las polticas monetarias extremadamente laxas en los principales pases avanzados. Esta temtica la desarrollar en la segunda parte de mi intervencin. 1. Marco para la Conduccin de la Poltica Macroeconmica La conduccin de la poltica macroeconmica en Mxico se sustenta en cuatro pilares: la poltica fiscal, la poltica monetaria, el rgimen cambiario y la regulacin y supervisin financieras. Se trata de cuatro pilares congruentes entre s y cuyo objetivo es conformar 2 una plataforma slida y estable para el crecimiento econmico y el bienestar de la poblacin. En primer trmino, el manejo prudente y responsable de la poltica fiscal ha permitido erradicar los abultados y persistentes desbalances en las finanzas pblicas que nuestro pas padeci en el pasado. Como resultado de la disciplina fiscal, la deuda del sector pblico como proporcin del PIB se ha mantenido baja y ha mejorado su perfil considerablemente (Grfica 1). Entre las medidas que se tomaron en los ltimos aos destaca la entrada en vigor de la Ley Federal de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria en marzo de 2006 que establece, entre otras normas, una regla de presupuesto balanceado. Asimismo, tambin sobresalen las reformas tributarias de 2008 y 2010 que contribuyeron a fortalecer todava ms la posicin fiscal de nuestro pas, junto con el hecho de que, despus de que se us en este ltimo ao el espacio para tener desviaciones moderadas del equilibrio fiscal por razones temporales, el actual Gobierno retorn a un proyecto de balance fiscal para 2013. Todo lo anterior ha reducido significativamente la vulnerabilidad de las finanzas pblicas en Mxico y ha mejorado su posicin relativa en la economa global. 3 Grfica 1 Deuda Pblica 1/ % del PIB 165 Pronstico 145 125 EEUUA 105 Espaa 85 65 Brasil 45 Mxico 25 Balance Fiscal 2/ % del PIB 4 Pronstico 2 Mxico 00 Brasil -2 -4 -6 EEUUA -8 -10 Espaa -12 -14 5 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 -16 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 1/ Para Mxico se refiere al Saldo Histrico de los Requerimientos Financieros del Sector Pblico. En segundo trmino, en lo referente a la poltica monetaria, desde 1993 Mxico cuenta con un banco central autnomo que, de acuerdo con la Constitucin, tiene como objetivo prioritario procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. El elemento fundamental de la autonoma es mantener la separacin entre las polticas fiscal y monetaria, a travs de prohibir el financiamiento de los desbalances fiscales mediante emisin primaria. En ese marco de autonoma, desde 2001 el Banco de Mxico adopt un rgimen de objetivos de inflacin para la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. El esfuerzo por fortalecer dicho esquema ha sido permanente. As, por ejemplo, en 2011 se empezaron a publicar las minutas sobre las reuniones de decisin de poltica monetaria, lo cual ha mejorado an ms la transparencia y la comunicacin del Instituto Central, claves 4 para anclar las expectativas de inflacin tanto entre los participantes en los mercados como entre el pblico en general. El ordenamiento de las finanzas pblicas y la poltica monetaria adoptada por el Instituto Emisor ha dado por resultado un abatimiento significativo de la inflacin, llegando sta a niveles bajos y estables, que en los ltimos aos ha fluctuado entre el 3 y 4 por ciento por lo general. (Grfica 2). En tercer lugar, respecto de la poltica cambiaria, desde mediados de los aos noventa Mxico ha mantenido un rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible. El rgimen de flotacin ha sido un elemento fundamental para la poltica macroeconmica, ya que ha funcionado como mecanismo amortiguador de los choques externos que ha experimentado la economa de Mxico. En este sentido, la depreciacin que tuvo el tipo de cambio real despus de la crisis que 5 se inici en 2008, indujo un rpido crecimiento de las exportaciones y el repunte de nuestro crecimiento econmico (Grfica 3). Es de notarse que entre las monedas de los pases emergentes el peso ha logrado mantener por mayor tiempo su depreciacin real desde 2008, en buena medida debido a la apropiada mezcla de poltica fiscal y monetaria que hemos seguido. A ello ha contribuido una adecuada regulacin y supervisin financiera. En este sentido, cabe sealar que Mxico ha avanzado de manera notable en la adopcin de las disposiciones referentes a Basilea III (Grfica 4). Asimismo, nuestro pas cuenta, al igual que otras naciones, con un Consejo de Estabilidad del Sistema Financiero, en el cual participan diversas autoridades, entre ellas el Banco de Mxico y 6 la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, y que tiene como propsito detectar de manera oportuna posibles vulnerabilidades dentro del sistema financiero, as como la elaboracin de recomendaciones para hacerles frente. Todo lo anterior ha contribuido a que Mxico sea uno de los pocos pases que cuente con un sistema bancario sano y bien capitalizado con la capacidad de contribuir al crecimiento econmico con bases regulatorias slidas. Logros en Materia de Inflacin Gracias a todo lo anterior la economa mexicana disfruta de un ambiente de estabilidad y certidumbre, dentro del cual sobresale el control que se ha logrado sobre la inflacin. El resultado ha sido una reduccin ms que significativa en el nivel, la volatilidad y la persistencia de la inflacin en Mxico. 7 Para ilustrar el avance estructural logrado en esta materia, cabe sealar que hemos conseguido reducir la inflacin general de niveles por arriba del 100 por ciento en algunos aos de la dcada de los ochentas a niveles cercanos a 3 por ciento en la actualidad. De esta manera, desde hace ms de diez aos la inflacin ha venido fluctuando de manera ordenada alrededor de un nivel que es el ms bajo desde que se calcula el ndice Nacional de Precios al Consumidor (Grfica 5). En trminos generales, se dice que una inflacin es persistente cuando las perturbaciones que la afectan, como las variaciones en ciertos precios relativos, por ejemplo de algunos productos agropecuarios, tienen un impacto prolongado. Por el contrario, si tales 8 choques tienen tan slo un efecto transitorio sobre la inflacin, sta es calificada como no persistente. Esta menor persistencia se ha reflejado en un menor efecto de traspaso de variaciones, tanto del tipo de cambio como de los precios de los bienes agropecuarios a la inflacin (Grfica 6A y 6B). En la evidencia presentada destaca que en el pasado la tasa de inflacin general guardaba una correlacin muy estrecha con las variaciones del tipo de cambio y de los precios agropecuarios, mientras que ms recientemente dicha correlacin se ha reducido sustancialmente. Como consecuencia de los resultados favorables en materia de combate a la inflacin, la poltica monetaria en Mxico ha gozado un 9 alto grado de credibilidad. Ello ha permitido anclar las expectativas de inflacin de los agentes econmicos dentro del intervalo de variabilidad definido por el Banco de Mxico, y cerca del objetivo permanente de inflacin. De esta manera se genera un crculo virtuoso, ya que los esfuerzos por consolidar la estabilidad de precios retroalimentan una evolucin favorable de las expectativas de inflacin (Grfica 7), y viceversa.
