Adems, el Banco se ha esforzado por disear un marco regulatorio que no slo resulte adecuado a las necesidades del sistema financiero, sino que tambin procure su estabilidad ante escenarios adversos. Asimismo, ms all de proveer a la economa nacional de un instrumento tan bsico para la facilitacin de las transacciones que en ella tienen lugar como lo es el dinero, el Banco de Mxico ha impulsado el desarrollo de la infraestructura, las reglas y los medios que permiten la transferencia de recursos mediante un sistema de pagos eficiente y confiable. Me parece importante tambin destacar las contribuciones del Banco de Mxico al desarrollo de capital humano y a la investigacin en nuestro pas. Ante la carencia de mano de obra calificada en materia monetaria y financiera, aprovechando los programas de capacitacin del Instituto Central, en 1928 se fund en el Banco la Escuela Bancaria y Comercial, que en una etapa posterior pas a manos privadas. Algunos aos despus, estos esfuerzos se complementaron con la creacin del programa de becas del Banco de Mxico, vigente hasta la actualidad. El aporte del banco central a la formacin de personal de alto nivel en nuestro pas queda de manifiesto al considerar el elevado nmero de cuadros formados en la Institucin que han ocupado posiciones prominentes tanto en el sector pblico como privado. Asimismo, el 8 Banco le ha asignado una alta prioridad al fomento de la investigacin desde etapas tempranas en su existir. Esto no se ha limitado a la investigacin econmica y financiera, ya que durante varios aos el Banco fungi como uno de los centros ms importantes de investigacin industrial en Mxico. La importancia del Banco en el establecimiento de condiciones de estabilidad econmica se hizo patente desde su creacin. En efecto, la necesidad de contar con una institucin que velara por la estabilidad del valor de nuestra moneda estuvo presente inclusive durante la etapa en que este funcion como banco comercial, ya que en esa poca el Banco slo poda emitir billetes a cambio de oro o a travs del redescuento con sus bancos asociados. Posteriormente, ya con el Banco concentrado exclusivamente en sus funciones de banco central, la Ley Orgnica de 1936 se enfoc en darle a la Institucin un marco operativo libre de toda nota inflacionista, para lo cual se crearon varios candados precautorios.10 Sin embargo, desde muy poco tiempo despus, los intereses polticos predominaron, por lo que el marco legal de operacin del Banco se ajust, convirtindolo en diversas etapas de su existencia en un mecanismo de financiamiento del gasto gubernamental. Dichos episodios se caracterizaron, inevitablemente, por elevados niveles de inflacin y bajas, o incluso negativas, tasas de crecimiento econmico. La obtencin de la autonoma a partir de 1994 marca un parteaguas en la historia del Banco de Mxico. Con esta reforma se dio al Banco una autonoma tanto de jure como de facto, sobre la base de cimientos slidos: 10 Turrent, Eduardo (2015): Historia del Banco de Mxico, Volumen II, Captulo 7. 9 1. El objetivo prioritario, establecido a nivel de la Constitucin, de procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda, es decir, de combatir la inflacin. Las razones de este mandato constitucional estn fundamentadas en slida evidencia emprica a nivel nacional e internacional, que ha demostrado los efectos nocivos de la inflacin para el crecimiento econmico, el empleo y la distribucin del ingreso. 2. La salvaguarda, tambin a nivel constitucional, de que ninguna autoridad podr ordenarle al Banco conceder financiamiento. Lo anterior se enfoca en evitar la posibilidad de que por motivos polticos las autoridades monetarias pongan en marcha medidas que puedan resultar en un repunte de la inflacin. 3. Un rgano colegiado de toma de decisiones, la Junta de Gobierno, cuyos integrantes estn libres de presiones polticas y deben cumplir con requisitos estrictos. Si bien su designacin le corresponde al Presidente de la Repblica, la independencia en su actuar se garantiza mediante mecanismos previstos en la Ley, tales como la aprobacin de su nombramiento por el Senado de la Repblica, el escalonamiento en la rotacin de sus miembros, y su inamovilidad salvo por causas graves especificadas en la ley. 4. La independencia administrativa, que elimina la posibilidad de coercin por parte de otras entidades mediante presiones indirectas de tipo presupuestal. 10 Es importante resaltar que este cambio fundamental en el marco legal del Banco de Mxico fue respaldado por la conciencia generalizada de la sociedad sobre los efectos nocivos de la inflacin y la necesidad de contar con una institucin que permitiera hacer frente a este problema. Naturalmente, la autonoma del Banco de Mxico va acompaada de responsabilidades de transparencia y rendicin de cuentas para el Instituto Central. Para este propsito, el Banco cuenta con una diversidad de canales y herramientas para informar a la sociedad, de manera clara y oportuna, sobre sus decisiones, acciones y resultados. Es as como mediante la publicacin de comunicados de las decisiones de poltica monetaria y las minutas correspondientes a cada discusin, los informes trimestrales sobre la inflacin y comparecencias peridicas ante el Congreso, entre otros mecanismos, se pone bajo el escrutinio pblico el actuar del Banco. Adems, la Institucin est legalmente obligada a cumplir con distintos procesos de auditora, en lo que al ejercicio de su presupuesto y prcticas administrativas se refiere. La trayectoria de la inflacin en los ltimos aos pone en evidencia los mritos de una poltica monetaria conducida por un banco central autnomo. Durante un largo periodo previo a la entrada en vigor de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico, nuestro pas registr ndices inflacionarios de dos y hasta tres dgitos. En contraste, a lo largo de los ltimos 16 aos, la tasa de inflacin en Mxico ha sido de un solo dgito. De hecho, el ndice nacional de precios al consumidor ha mostrado tasas anuales de crecimiento por debajo de 3 por ciento, la meta desde 2003, de manera consecutiva durante los ltimos 15 meses, resultado 11 sin precedente desde que existe dicho ndice. Si bien estos logros no pueden atribuirse exclusivamente a la autonoma del banco central, tambin es cierto que difcilmente se hubieran alcanzado en ausencia de esta. La disminucin de la inflacin ha acarreado beneficios a familias, empresas, gobierno y al propio Banco de Mxico. Merece destacarse, por ejemplo, que en la actualidad las familias tienen acceso a crditos hipotecarios a tasas fijas, en pesos, a plazos de hasta 30 aos, lo cual era imposible durante las pocas de inflacin elevadas. Asimismo, la recuperacin que hemos observado recientemente en los salarios reales ha sido determinada no por mayores aumentos nominales, sino por una inflacin ms baja. La menor inflacin ha beneficiado a las empresas no solo a travs de un acceso al crdito a plazos ms largos y con tasas de inters ms bajas, sino que tambin les ha permitido una planeacin de sus operaciones en un entorno de mayor certidumbre. Para el gobierno los beneficios han sido, entre otros, la posibilidad de poner en marcha una poltica de endeudamiento menos onerosa, extender el plazo de la curva de rendimientos gubernamental y mejorar el perfil de la deuda pblica. En cuanto al Banco, el reforzamiento de la credibilidad de su compromiso con la estabilidad de precios derivado de estos resultados ha redundado a su vez en una mayor efectividad y eficiencia de la poltica monetaria, facilitando as la continuidad en el logro de este objetivo. En suma, el Banco de Mxico ha tenido un papel de relevancia en el desarrollo econmico del pas, a travs de canales que han ido modificndose con el curso del tiempo de conformidad con los requerimientos de la economa. En 12 su ajuste ms reciente, la autonoma del Banco elimin la posibilidad de usar a la Institucin como ventana de financiamiento del gasto gubernamental, lo que ha permitido avanzar de manera importante en el combate a la inflacin, condicin necesaria aunque no suficiente para sentar las bases de un crecimiento econmico sostenido. Los esfuerzos de fortalecimiento del Banco y adaptacin a las nuevas necesidades deben continuar. Tambin es importante tener presente que el Banco de Mxico representa solamente una pieza del entramado institucional requerido para apoyar de manera adecuada el desarrollo econmico del pas. Indudablemente, deberemos seguir esforzndonos para lograr este objetivo. Para finalizar quisiera hacer un ltimo comentario. El desarrollo de un marco institucional adecuado en cualquier pas requiere de la voluntad y la visin de las autoridades para identificar las medidas a implementar y las prioridades de accin. Sin embargo, como ya seal, dada la naturaleza y el alcance de cambios de esta magnitud, estos esfuerzos generalmente enfrentan resistencias de algunos sectores de la sociedad. De ah que frecuentemente ser necesario, adems de un liderazgo fuerte, lograr niveles adecuados de apoyo de la clase poltica e incluso de la sociedad civil, para llevarlos a cabo. Es probable que las dificultades que a menudo se enfrentan para lograr estos respaldos contribuyan a explicar por qu, a pesar de la importancia evidente de las instituciones para el desempeo econmico, numerosos pases siguen adoleciendo de debilidades considerables en este frente. 13

Title: Award ceremony of the tenth edition of the Contacto Banxico Award
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the Award Ceremony of the tenth edition of the BANXICO Contact Award. Mexico City, November 28, 2018 Teacher Irene Espinosa, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico; Dear participants of the BANXICO Contact Award; Colleagues from the Bank of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen: It gives me great pleasure to attend the award ceremony of the tenth edition of the "Contacto BANXICO" award and give you a warm welcome. This Award was conceived to meet three primary objectives in the field of financial education: first, to establish a direct link between the Bank of Mexico and the upper secondary education segment; second, to encourage, from high school, research and debate on issues of monetary policy and central banking and, third, to promote greater knowledge and social consensus on the priority objectives and the contribution of the Bank of Mexico to the development of the country. As you know, this is a national competition aimed at high school students on a topic of monetary policy or finance that is renewed every year. The participants form teams of three or four students and a teacher from the same institution, who advises them in the preparation of a written essay. Over ten years, the BANXICO Contact Award has been consolidated, generating great interest among the student population and offering remarkable results. For example, during this decade, more than 10 thousand teams from all the states of the Republic have registered. 2 Mexican, which have completed almost 5700 essays on various aspects of the economy, which have been qualified by experts through a rigorous and transparent process. It should be noted that, as of this edition, and with the purpose of updating in the new discussion and dissemination platforms, the BANXICO Contact Award, in addition to rewarding a written text, also grants recognition to a video made on the designated topic. In 2018 the Contacto Banxico Award celebrates its tenth edition with the theme "The Autonomy of the Central Bank: How does it contribute to maintaining low and stable inflation?". The theme of this occasion is fundamental to understand the institutional design of modern central banking. Throughout the twentieth century, inflation constituted a kind of epidemic phenomenon, which affected numerous countries on various continents, generated historical stagnation and setbacks and harmed the quality of life of several generations. 3 You, who were born in the twenty-first century, fortunately have not experienced firsthand the impact of inflation. The inflationary phenomenon causes a sense of desolation and uncertainty in individuals, as well as a harmful effect on economic activity, the health of companies and the well-being of families. Surely, you who have studied this topic to elaborate your work know the way in which inflation tends, among other effects, to distort the decisions of economic actors, to inhibit medium- and long-term productive projects and to favor speculation. The great writer Elias Canetti, winner of the Nobel Prize for literature, and who lived various inflationary experiences, especially the hyperinflation of the Weimar Republic in Germany in the twenties, is very eloquent about the negative effects of inflation. Canetti points out: "What happens in case of inflation? The monetary unit suddenly loses its personality. It transforms into a growing mass of units; these will be worth less and less as their mass increases. The millions, which one so desired 4 To have them, he holds them suddenly in his hands, but they are no longer such, they are just called that. It is as if the sharp increase has deprived of all value to what is increased." 1 Among the anecdotes of that time, one of them tells that the few who could go to a restaurant, before sitting at the table, had to agree on the price of food and pay it in advance, because it could go up during the meal. Thus, periods of hyperinflation erode the usefulness of money and return the economy to primitive practices such as barter. While inflation is a malaise that affects the whole of the social body, its impact damages even more severely those who have the least, that is, those who live up to date with their income and do not have ways to protect their few assets from the loss of value. Inflation manifests itself in this case in a more dramatic way, since the increase in prices implies that with the same income it will be possible to 1 Canetti, Elijah, Mass and power. Barcelona, Galaxia Gutenberg, 2002, p.231 5 buy fewer elementary satisfiers, such as food, and there will be a palpable and immediate consequence on the quality of life. One of the usual causes of inflation tends to be the excessive issuance of primary money to correct other imbalances. Therefore, the exclusive power of central banks to issue money must be exercised with enormous responsibility and prudence. When a central bank does not have clear and verifiable mandates and objectives for its actions, its powers can be misused. At different points in the last century, it was thought that monetary policy was possible to stimulate economic activity and various governments and central banks undertook an unjustifiably expansionary monetary policy. This use of monetary policy, together with other imbalances, caused crises. The painful experience, as well as the evidence of economic theory, gave rise, in the last decades of the last century, to a broad consensus regarding the advisability of the power of issuing primary money to be isolated from political cycles and that central banks, 6 as state institutions, they will concentrate on trying to maintain low and stable inflation with a long-term horizon. Thus, many countries granted autonomy to their central banks, guaranteeing them independence from the fiscal needs of governments and the political cycle. Today, most central banks have legal autonomy and the priority mandate is to fight inflation. Likewise, a significant number of central banks make their monetary policy decisions, through a collegial, expert and functional body, which is provided with various conditions to act with full independence in pursuit of its primary objective. Our country also experienced the phenomenon of inflation at various stages. In particular, in the seventies and eighties of the last century excessive public spending policies were applied and the Central Bank was obliged to extend credit to finance the consequent fiscal deficits. This led to inflations that were profoundly harmful to society, resulting in economic recession and deterioration of welfare levels. 7 After these experiences, in 1993 the reform of Article 28 of the Constitution was proposed, which granted the Bank of Mexico autonomy in its administration and functions, assigning it the priority objective of maintaining the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency and indicating, explicitly, that no authority can order it to grant financing. The autonomy of the Bank of Mexico has been an institutional design that has worked: inflation has fallen from the two- and even triple-digit levels it reached to levels close to the permanent target of 3 percent. The autonomy of monetary policy has not only led to a lower persistence of inflation, but also to anchor medium- and long-term expectations at levels close to the target, and a lower transfer to inflation of relative price changes, such as exchange rate fluctuations. In short, the lowering of inflation is not a dogma, nor an end in itself, but a means to achieve a higher goal, which is 8 the growth of the economy. Price stability is a condition that has taken a lot of time and effort to take root and that should be preserved as a precious social good. In addition, it is the best proven use that can be given to the power of central banks to provide the country with national currency. Hence the importance of stimulating, among students, reflection on this topic. I am sure that, throughout your research exercises, you have found many reasons and evidences to explain the benefits of low inflation and the existence of an autonomous institution focused on this objective. Dear participants of the Award: For the Bank of Mexico it is essential to establish a link with the population of upper secondary education, for its social influence, its indisputable role in the economic future of our country, and its potential as an engine of development and progress. The BANXICO Contact Award is one of our institute's oldest and most successful initiatives in financial education and outreach. Undoubtedly, throughout its decade of existence, this 9 the award has more than fulfilled the objectives for which it was created. It has generated enthusiasm and interest among the student population, has produced remarkable pieces of research and reflection, has fostered teamwork and has awakened and consolidated vocations in the areas of economics and finance. The achievements of this pioneering award led the Bank of Mexico to create, in 2016, another contest, called "BANXICO Challenge", aimed at undergraduate students, which has also yielded magnificent results. I have no doubt that some of you, in some years, participated in the "Banxico Challenge". We are very happy and satisfied with the response of middle and higher education students that has made the BANXICO Contact Award a well-attended and successful contest. I wish to congratulate very sincerely the participants and winners of this edition and urge them to continue committing their talent to analyze the challenges and opportunities of the Mexican economy and to continue providing realistic diagnoses and constructive proposals. Congratulations to all. 10
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la ceremonia de Premiacin de la dcima edicin del Premio Contacto BANXICO. Ciudad de Mxico, 28 de noviembre de 2018 Maestra Irene Espinosa, Subgobernadora del Banco de Mxico; Estimados participantes del Premio Contacto BANXICO; Colegas del Banco de Mxico; Seoras y seores: Me da mucho gusto acudir a la premiacin de la dcima edicin del premio Contacto BANXICO y darles una calurosa bienvenida. Este Premio se concibi para atender tres objetivos primordiales en materia de educacin financiera: primero, establecer un vnculo directo entre el Banco de Mxico y el segmento de educacin media superior; segundo, incentivar, desde el bachillerato, la investigacin y el debate sobre temas de poltica monetaria y banca central y, tercero, fomentar el mayor conocimiento y consenso social sobre los objetivos prioritarios y la aportacin del Banco de Mxico al desarrollo del pas. Como ustedes saben, este es un concurso nacional dirigido a estudiantes de educacin media superior sobre un tpico de poltica monetaria o finanzas que se renueva cada ao. Los participantes forman equipos de tres o cuatro alumnos y un profesor de su misma institucin, que los asesora en la elaboracin de un ensayo escrito. A lo largo de diez aos, el Premio Contacto BANXICO se ha consolidado, generando gran inters entre la poblacin estudiantil y ofreciendo notables resultados. Por ejemplo, durante esta dcada, se han inscrito ms de 10 mil equipos de todos los estados de la Repblica 2 Mexicana, los cuales han culminado casi 5700 trabajos ensaysticos sobre diversos aspectos de la economa, que han sido calificados por expertos mediante un proceso riguroso y transparente. Cabe resaltar que, a partir de esta edicin, y con el propsito de actualizarse en las nuevas plataformas de discusin y divulgacin, el Premio Contacto BANXICO, adems premiar un texto escrito, tambin otorga un reconocimiento a un video elaborado sobre el tema designado. En 2018 el Premio Contacto Banxico celebra su dcima edicin con el tema La Autonoma del Banco Central Cmo contribuye a mantener una inflacin baja y estable?. La temtica de esta ocasin es fundamental para entender el diseo institucional de la banca central moderna. A lo largo del siglo XX, la inflacin constituy una especie de fenmeno epidmico, que afect numerosos pases en diversos continentes, gener estancamientos y retrocesos histricos y perjudic la calidad de vida de varias generaciones. 3 Ustedes, que nacieron en el siglo XXI, afortunadamente no han experimentado en carne propia el impacto de la inflacin. El fenmeno inflacionario provoca una sensacin de desolacin e incertidumbre en los individuos, as como un efecto nocivo sobre la actividad econmica, la salud de las empresas y el bienestar de las familias. Seguramente, ustedes que han estudiado este tema para elaborar sus trabajos conocen la forma en que la inflacin tiende, entre otros efectos, a distorsionar las decisiones de los actores econmicos, a inhibir los proyectos productivos de mediano y largo plazo y a favorecer la especulacin. El gran escritor Elas Canetti, ganador del Premio Nobel de literatura, y quien vivi diversas experiencias inflacionarias, especialmente la hiperinflacin de la Repblica de Weimar en la Alemania de los aos veinte, es muy elocuente sobre los efectos negativos de la inflacin. Seala Canetti: qu sucede en caso de inflacin? La unidad monetaria pierde repentinamente su personalidad. Se transforma en una masa creciente de unidades; estas valdrn cada vez menos a medida que aumente su masa. Los millones, que uno tanto deseaba 4 tener, los sostiene de pronto en las manos, pero ya no son tales, slo se llaman as. Es como si el incremento brusco hubiese privado de todo valor a lo que se incrementa.1 Entre las ancdotas de esa poca, una de ellas cuenta que los pocos que podan acudir a algn restaurante, antes de sentarse a la mesa, deban acordar el precio de los alimentos y pagarlo por adelantado, pues ste poda subir durante la comida. As, los periodos de hiperinflacin, erosionan la utilidad del dinero y regresan a la economa a prcticas primitivas como el trueque. Si bien la inflacin es un malestar que afecta el conjunto del cuerpo social, su impacto daa todava ms severamente a quienes menos tienen, es decir, a quienes viven al da de sus ingresos y no cuentan con formas de proteger sus pocos activos de la prdida de valor. La inflacin se manifiesta en este caso de manera ms dramtica, pues el aumento de precios implica que con los mismos ingresos se podrn 1 Canetti, Elas, Masa y poder. Barcelona, Galaxia Gutenberg, 2002, p.231 5 comprar menos satisfactores elementales, como los alimentos, y habr una consecuencia palpable e inmediata en la calidad de vida. Una de las causas habituales de la inflacin tiende a ser la emisin excesiva de dinero primario para subsanar otros desequilibrios. Por eso, la facultad exclusiva de emitir dinero de los bancos centrales debe ejercerse con una enorme responsabilidad y prudencia. Cuando un banco central no cuenta con mandatos y objetivos claros y verificables para su accionar, sus facultades pueden llegar a ser mal utilizadas. En distintos momentos del siglo pasado, se pens que mediante la poltica monetaria era posible estimular la actividad econmica y diversos gobiernos y bancos centrales emprendieron una poltica monetaria injustificadamente expansiva. Esta utilizacin de la poltica monetaria, aunada a otros desequilibrios, provoc crisis. La dolorosa experiencia, as como la evidencia de la teora econmica, dio lugar, en las ltimas dcadas del siglo pasado, a un amplio consenso respecto a la conveniencia de que la facultad de emisin de dinero primario se aislara de los ciclos polticos y de que los bancos centrales, 6 como instituciones del Estado, se concentraran en tratar de mantener una inflacin baja y estable con un horizonte de largo plazo. As, numerosos pases otorgaron autonoma a sus bancos centrales, garantizndoles independencia de las necesidades fiscales de los gobiernos y del ciclo poltico. Hoy, la mayora de los bancos centrales tienen autonoma legal y el mandato prioritario es combatir la inflacin. Igualmente, un nmero significativo de bancos centrales toma sus decisiones de poltica monetaria, por medio de un rgano colegiado, experto y funcional, que est provisto de diversas condiciones para actuar con plena independencia en busca de su objetivo primordial. Nuestro pas tambin experiment en diversas etapas el fenmeno de la inflacin. En particular, en los aos setenta y ochenta del siglo pasado se aplicaron polticas de gasto pblico excesivo y se impuso al Banco Central la obligacin de extender crdito para financiar los consecuentes dficits fiscales. Esto propici inflaciones profundamente dainas para la sociedad, que redundaron en recesin econmica y deterioro de los niveles de bienestar. 7 Tras estas experiencias, en 1993 se plante la reforma al Artculo 28 de la Constitucin, que concedi al Banco de Mxico autonoma en su administracin y funciones, asignndole el objetivo prioritario de mantener la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional y sealando, explcitamente, que ninguna autoridad puede ordenarle conceder financiamiento. La autonoma del Banco de Mxico ha sido un diseo institucional que ha funcionado: la inflacin ha descendido de los niveles de dos, y hasta tres dgitos que lleg a alcanzar, a niveles cercanos a la meta permanente de 3 porciento. La autonoma de la poltica monetaria no slo ha propiciado una menor persistencia de la inflacin, sino un anclaje de las expectativas de mediano y largo plazo en niveles prximos a la meta, y un menor traspaso a la inflacin de modificaciones de precios relativos, como las fluctuaciones cambiarias. En suma, el abatimiento de la inflacin no es un dogma, ni un fin en s mismo, sino un medio para conseguir un objetivo ms elevado, que es 8 el crecimiento de la economa. La estabilidad de precios es una condicin que ha costado mucho tiempo y esfuerzo arraigar y que conviene preservar como un preciado bien social. Adems, es el mejor uso probado que se puede dar a la facultad de los bancos centrales de proveer al pas de moneda nacional. De ah la importancia de que se estimule, entre los estudiantes, la reflexin sobre este tema. Estoy seguro que, a lo largo de sus ejercicios de investigacin, ustedes han encontrado muchas razones y evidencias para explicar los beneficios de una inflacin baja y de la existencia de una institucin autnoma enfocada en este objetivo. Estimados participantes del Premio: Para el Banco de Mxico es fundamental establecer un vnculo con la poblacin de educacin media superior, por su influencia social, su papel indiscutible en el futuro econmico de nuestro pas, y su potencial como motor de desarrollo y progreso. El Premio Contacto BANXICO es una de las iniciativas ms antiguas y exitosas de nuestro instituto en materia de educacin y divulgacin financiera. Sin duda, a lo largo de su dcada de existencia, este 9 galardn ha cumplido sobradamente con los objetivos para los que fue creado. Ha generado entusiasmo e inters entre la poblacin estudiantil, ha producido piezas notables de investigacin y reflexin, ha fomentado el trabajo en equipo y ha despertado y consolidado vocaciones en las reas de economa y finanzas. Los logros de este premio pionero llevaron al Banco de Mxico a crear, en 2016, otro concurso, denominado Reto BANXICO, dirigido a estudiantes de licenciatura, que tambin ha arrojado magnficos resultados. No tengo duda de que algunos de ustedes, en algunos aos, participaran en el Reto Banxico. Estamos muy contentos y satisfechos con la respuesta de los estudiantes de educacin media y superior que ha hecho del Premio Contacto BANXICO un certamen concurrido y exitoso. Deseo felicitar muy sinceramente a los participantes y ganadores de esta edicin e instarlos a que sigan empeando su talento para analizar los retos y oportunidades de la economa mexicana y a que sigan aportando diagnsticos realistas y propuestas constructivas. Enhorabuena a todos. 10

Title: Unwinding public interventions in the financial sector: an emerging market economys perspective
text: Unwinding Public Interventions in the Financial Sector: An Emerging Market Economys Perspective Remarks by Manuel Sanchez Deputy Governor The Bank of Mexico at the IMF High-Level Conference Unwinding Public Interventions, Preconditions and Practical Considerations Washington D.C. December 3, 2009 During the last two years, governments and central banks have undertaken unprecedented measures to face the risks stemming from the global financial crisis. Most measures were interpreted as extraordinary actions to avoid an economic and financial collapse. At the same time, it was accepted that some costs and risks would need to be controlled. These include tax burdens and possible unintended consequences such as distortions of market participants behaviour from reinforced moral hazard. Due to these costs and perils, exit strategies have become a crucial issue. This conference is exceptionally timely as it addresses the issue of unwinding public interventions in the financial system. In my comments, I will focus on some questions related to the adoption of adequate exit strategies from an emerging market economys (EME) perspective, with reference to the Mexican experience in the recent and previous crises. Before moving to the core of the subject, an initial warning seems in order. Exit strategies should not be used as a means to return to a business as usual scenario. Just as important as disengagement by the public sector from extraordinary interventions is the governments engagement in order to prevent future crises. Essential tasks to achieve this goal include sound macroeconomic policies and a renewed regulatory and supervisory framework for financial institutions. EMEs and the global crisis The recent global financial crisis did not initially have a major impact on EMEs. At a certain stage, a commonly held view was that these economies were decoupling from developed countries. Financial systems in EMEs were solvent and profitable, with high domestic net interest margins having dissuaded local banks from investing in more risky assets. At that stage, the impact of the crisis in EMEs 1 worked through the real side of the economy: a decrease in international trade, a fall in commodity prices, and lower remittances. However, the worsening of the global turmoil after Lehmans bankruptcy had major effects. Investment inflows suddenly shrank and the massive asset sell-off that followed had an adverse impact on exchange rates, domestic interest rates, and local stock markets. Subsidiaries of foreign banks in EMEs constituted an important source of liquidity for their parent firms, which in some cases restricted credit in host countries. Some evidence suggests that since the end of 2008, credit growth in EMEs with large foreign banks presence has been smaller than in other EMEs. The financial instability and contraction of output and employment led to the adoption of emergency measures in several EMEs. However, these regions still depend on the recovery of the developed world in order to return to full health. The actions adopted in advanced countries to support their financial systems, together with their fiscal and monetary stimuli, have set the stage for the upturn. Proper exit strategies are crucial in order to maintain the improvement of economic prospects. Preconditions and the unwinding strategy Governments measures to support financial systems in many countries have been multiple, including deposit insurance, guarantees of non-deposit liabilities, asset purchases or asset guarantees, special lending facilities and extraordinary central bank liquidity facilities, and capital injections and emergency loans. Exit from these interventions should aim at restoring sustainable financial stability and economic growth. 2 To achieve a durable and safe disengagement by the public sector, certain preconditions seem desirable. In particular, it is necessary to verify that intermediaries no longer need support, as reflected in their decreased demand for assistance, available access to market sources of funding, and reconstructed balance sheets. This implies the strengthening of capital, reserve, and provisioning ratios under fair value conditions. Also, macroeconomic stability should be guaranteed in terms of sound monetary and fiscal policies, so that no undue future financial instability is built into current stimulus measures. On the other hand, economic recovery should clearly be underway, allowing banks to return to normal lending. Given these preconditions, several elements may contribute to a successful exit strategy. The first one is to price the measures in such a way that a market-based exit is a natural outcome. The incentives of market participants should lead them to draw less on support measures as markets normalize, for example in the cases of debt guarantees, central bank lending facilities, or haircuts to the assets exchanged in a balance-sheet cleanup plan. A second element is that the timing and sequencing of exit plans should depend on the progress of the preconditions mentioned above, which implies that the timing of withdrawal is partly endogenous and cannot be completely fixed in advance. Although some measures might have been established for a specific time period, others need to be flexible to accommodate unforeseen developments. A third element is to reconcile the steps of the exit plan with the implementation of any new regulatory and supervisory measures. The combination of higher requirements and lower support should not destabilize banks. A fourth element is to explore possible cross-border effects so that adequate internationally coordinated measures can be taken. For example, developing 3 countries have been shown to be highly sensitive to relatively smaller changes in the global economic environment. Exit strategies from firm-specific actions may affect countries where those firms play a significant role. A fifth element is an adequate communication of plans to the public to avoid unnecessary surprises and gain social support. The advance notice of exit strategies, their objectives and timelines, will facilitate adjustment in the regions that expect some indirect impacts or spill-over effects. Transparency and time consistency greatly increase a plans credibility. These elements uncover interdependencies among measures that may make the unwinding process particularly complex. For example, highly accommodative monetary policy in place for too long may incentivize carry-trade transactions causing asset price bubbles in EMEs; removal of public-sector support without enhanced regulatory rules may facilitate excessive risk-taking; and lack of international coordination may lead banks and their creditors to arbitrage facilities at different countries. Mexicos experience in times of crisis Let me now turn to Mexicos experience with public-sector interventions during the last two crises, which may be useful to policy-makers in other countries. The 1995 crisis brought about a sharp depreciation of the peso, a drastic rise in inflation and interest rates, and a deep recession. As a result, the capacity of borrowers to honor their debts was severely impaired, causing a deterioration of banks balance sheets. The authorities responded with a series of measures to stabilize the financial system. 4 In the wake of the crisis, a dollar-credit window was established at the central bank to help banks service their obligations and reduce the volatility in a highly illiquid foreign exchange market. This facility charged a high dollar interest rate in order to ensure that the resources were used only for temporary liquidity shortages. The outstanding amount of dollar loans from the central bank peaked in April 1995 and by September of that year all banks had repaid them in full. Thus, the high rates charged on the facility gave financial institutions an incentive to exit, allowing for the facilitys quick termination. At the same time, to avoid panic, the government announced a blanket guarantee on banks liabilities. With the establishment of the new deposit insurance agency (IPAB) in 1999, the coverage was gradually reduced and by 2005 it had reached its current coverage level of about US130,000 per depositor and institution. Also, a program was implemented for banks to sell their non-performing loans (NPLs) in exchange for the injection of new capital. The deposit insurance agency bought two pesos of NPLs for each peso of new capital injected by shareholders. The NPLs acquired by the agency would still be managed by the selling bank. The scheme included a loss-sharing agreement under which after 10 years, losses would be assumed by the banks at 30% and the deposit insurance agency at 70%. Unfortunately, measures to fully capitalize the banking system and build conditions for a return to lending activities took several years. One reason was that NPLs were acquired with promissory notes that were non-tradable and, hence, banks could not sell them to finance lending. More importantly, capitalization was limited by legal restrictions on foreign ownership of banks, which were not completely abolished until 1999. Finally, it took three more years to approve reforms to improve the protection of creditors rights. 5 In contrast, during the recent crisis, the emergency measures were milder and, in general, regarded as temporary, with the imposition of explicit deadlines and limits on the amounts of resources committed. An important difference with the previous crisis was the relative strength of the current banking system. Specifically, in the foreign exchange market the Bank of Mexico conducted extraordinary interventions as well as daily auctions of dollars with and without a minimum price. The amount offered in the daily auctions was gradually reduced to zero in the case of those with no minimum price. Additionally, the Bank of Mexico and the Federal Reserve agreed on a currency swap line for up to US30 billion, with a deadline extended to February 2010. Finally, the IMF granted a oneyear contingent credit line to Mexico for about US47 billion. Both facilities are good examples of internationally coordinated measures. On another front, in order to address the negative effects of the sharp steepening of the yield curve on institutional investors portfolios, the Bank of Mexico conducted interest rate swap auctions. Also, the government and the IPAB reduced the placement of medium- and long-term securities and increased the placement of short-term issues. At the same time, the central bank introduced an auction mechanism to acquire IPAB bonds and implemented the buyback of long-term debt. These measures have begun to see a gradual unwinding. In addition, regulation was amended so that, for a period of six months, investment funds were allowed to carry out purchases and sales of government debt securities with any financial firm belonging to their financial group. Finally, government-owned development banks launched temporary guarantee programs to facilitate the refinancing of commercial paper issued by businesses and non-bank, non-mortgage-related financial firms for up to 50%, a program that closed to new access in July 2009. These guarantees were adequately collateralised and their pricing reflected the firms debt ratings. Another guarantee 6 program was implemented for mortgage non-bank financial institutions for up to 65%, which will conclude in 2010. In short, in comparison with the previous crisis episode, emergency measures in the recent crisis were considerably less extensive mainly because Mexico had a more resilient financial system, which, in turn, reflected a stronger and more efficient regulatory and supervisory framework as well as improvements in banks risk management and macroeconomic fundamentals. Concluding remarks In conclusion, careful consideration on the timing of the unwinding of the various public-sector interventions is needed. The magnitude of the global crisis, the interdependency of implemented measures, and the needed reforms of the financial system will likely make the exit a long process. Given that support measures may have undesirable effects in terms of moral hazard, it is imperative to implement new rules of the game that induce responsible risk-taking in the future. This effort should devote special attention to minimizing the size of the too-big-to-fail problem, a subject that deserves a whole conference in and of itself. Clear leadership and social consensus around exit strategies and pending reforms will be essential. 7

Title: Inauguration of the new banknote factory of the Bank of Mexico
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the inauguration of the new banknote factory of the Bank of Mexico. Guadalajara, Jalisco, November 7, 2018 Dear members of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico Irene Espinosa Javier Guzman Manuel Ramos France Ladies and gentlemen special guests, builders, consultants and suppliers of this project; Friends and colleagues of the Bank of Mexico: It is an honor to welcome you to inaugurate, on behalf of the Governing Board present here, the second Banknote Factory of the Bank of Mexico. Central banks have as their main purpose to issue the national currency and preserve its purchasing power. In the case of our country, this mission was raised in 1917, when the Constituent Assembly defined the need to create a central bank that would be the sole issuer of the national currency, which would consolidate the public's confidence in fiat money. Since the Constitutional Reform of August 1993, article 28 of the Magna Carta establishes that "The State shall have a Central Bank that shall be autonomous in the exercise of its functions and in its administration" and whose "priority objective shall be to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency". According to this standard, it is the exclusive responsibility of the Bank of Mexico to issue banknotes, defining their characteristics, and to order the minting of metallic currency. It is also responsible for putting these means of payment into circulation. 2 For paper money to function fully as a means of payment, store of value and unit of account and thus to be widely accepted by the public, two fundamental characteristics are required. First, confidence in the preservation of their purchasing power, avoiding inflationary episodes that violate their purchasing power. Second, the ability of the issuer to provide banknotes and coins in the quantity, variety, quality, opportunity and security criteria that are required. Let me elaborate on both aspects. First, the introduction of fiat money, i.e. banknotes and coins without intrinsic value, constituted a transformative means of payment that eliminated a wide range of clashes with the so-called money-commodity or precious metals. However, in some countries, their historical process of social acceptance was slow and difficult. Since it lacks intrinsic value and constitutes a mere promise of payment, for fiat money to circulate widely and perform its function in the economy, the public is required to perceive that 3 an economic and institutional climate conducive to the fulfilment of such a promise of payment shall prevail. When this does not happen and trust begins to erode, money ceases to effectively fulfill its function, which can cause great damage to the economy and society. Episodes of inflation have been a recurring factor of uncertainty towards fiat money, as they erode its functionality as a means of payment, unit of account and store of value. Thus, throughout the twentieth century, and even in our days, the experience of numerous nations can be observed in which uncontrolled inflation reduces the usefulness and social acceptance of money, affecting commercial operations, falling into disuse, and in extreme cases even promoting barter; hindering planning and investment; favoring speculation and causing famine, especially among those who have less. It is not surprising that, given the obvious effects of these affectations, in the last decades of the last century a solid consensus has been formed around the benefits of low and stable inflation. In 4 As a result, in a large number of countries, legislators or authorities conferred autonomy on their central banks and focused their mission on ensuring price stability. In the case of Mexico, the consolidation of fiat money was also a complex process. Paper money in Mexico was introduced after Independence, due to the shortage of metals for coins. However, the frequent periods of political and economic instability, which resulted in multiple issuance, high inflation and loss of the value of the banknotes, reduced the confidence of the population in these means of payment. Although during the Porfiriato the banknote reached a certain circulation and credibility, the armed struggles during the Mexican Revolution led to an abundant and disorderly issuance of paper money, which again undermined confidence in this medium. It was not until 1925, with the founding of the central bank and the determination that it would be the sole issuer of currency, that the foundations were laid to begin to restore the credibility of the note as a means of payment. 5 Trust in the currency has been built over several decades. Certainly, during the seventies and eighties, the phenomenon of so-called fiscal dominance and the bank's dependence on other authorities led to the financing of fiscal deficits with the issuance of primary money, which caused inflation and severe economic damage. To eradicate this phenomenon, and in line with the international trend, the constituent assembly gave autonomy to the Bank of Mexico in 1994 and established as its priority objective to maintain price stability. The autonomy of the Bank of Mexico has clearly allowed to break with a stage of acute, disorderly and persistent inflations and has allowed inflation figures to fall to levels increasingly closer to its permanent target of 3 percent. All this has provided an environment of greater certainty and has expanded the temporal range for the planning of the activities of economic agents and the decision-making of consumers. Thus, by seeking the stability of the purchasing power of the currency, the Bank of Mexico contributes to entrenching an indispensable condition for money to fully fulfill its functions. Of course, stability is not an end in itself, but a 6 a fundamental requirement to, together with other policies, underpin any process of sustainable and equitable growth. Secondly, over time, the Bank of Mexico has been developing the infrastructure and capacity to provide coins and banknotes in the denominations and quantities that the public requires, provide a higher level of security about their authenticity and guarantee their distribution throughout the national territory. Although for several decades the banknotes that circulated in Mexico were printed abroad, from 1969 a new chapter in the history of the Mexican banknote was opened, when the activities of the Banknote Factory of the Bank of Mexico, located in Legaria, in Mexico City, began. The activity of this well-known factory, which is about to complete its first fifty years, has fulfilled its function of providing paper money to the economy. Thus, it has gone from producing 201 million pieces in 1970 to producing around 1450 million pieces in 2017, more than 7 times the production of 1970. In addition, these banknotes have improved 7 constantly its quality to maximize its circulation time, as well as its security elements to limit its counterfeiting. Likewise, the distribution tasks have been fulfilled throughout the national territory. In recent years, however, the Legaria factory has been approaching the limit of its production capacity. Taking into account the prospective growth of both population growth and the Mexican economy, for about 8 years, the Bank of Mexico decided to start work on the development of a plan for the construction, equipment and commissioning of a banknote factory complementary to that of Mexico City. This new factory, located in another city, should contribute to the provision of the increased demand for national currency and, at the same time, mitigate the risks of concentrating currency production and inventories in one place. After carefully analyzing several scenarios and conducting feasibility studies, it was decided that the new factory would be located in the state of Jalisco, for several reasons: 8 (i) Jalisco is a pole of economic development; ii) in Guadalajara, the Bank of Mexico has a regional ATM which allows synergies; iii) is a city with extensive road infrastructure and airport, which facilitates communication with Mexico City and distribution to other regions; (iv) because of its geographical equidistance, it prevents concentration and, at the same time, facilitates coordination and an optimal division of functions, as well as a greater effectiveness of the distribution. To carry out this project, in 2012 the Bank acquired the properties adjacent to the Guadalajara regional bank, with an approximate area of 38 thousand square meters and began the projection of the work. On October 14, 2015, the act of laying the first stone of the construction of the work was carried out, which included not only the construction of a factory that in the future could house two production lines, but also the construction of a reserve vault 9 with a capacity of 5,500 containers, that is about 35% more than our current storage capacity. Thanks to the location of the acquired properties, it was possible to consolidate, in a single building, the new facilities with the existing ones of the Regional Fund and place, in the middle of these, the reserve vault, in which the Factory delivers the pieces of banknotes produced and the box receives them and enters its stocks, in a highly efficient and controlled process. It is worth noting that the factory uses state-of-the-art equipment, both in the production processes and in the security and support systems. It is also important to note that equipment that is friendly to the environment and that allows minimizing the generation of hazardous waste or special management were privileged. Moreover, this factory has the capacity to produce banknotes in polymer and paper and, therefore, to print all denominations. 10 With the entry into operation of this new complex, the distribution of the tickets will become more efficient and, from here, it will be supplied mainly to the northwest and western regions of the country, including the states of Aguascalientes, Baja California, Baja California Sur, Chihuahua, Durango, Jalisco, Michoacan, Nayarit, Sinaloa, Sonora and Zacatecas. In short, the factory that we inaugurate today constitutes a cutting-edge space, which is housed in a safe and functional building, which has the most modern equipment and has a staff of around 250 highly trained workers. Undoubtedly, this factory will contribute to continue consolidating the prestige of our country in the production of banknotes. On the Banco de Mexico website, a micro-site will be opened in which the main phases and critical decisions of the project are documented, which will allow any interested party to verify the planning process and the transparent use of the resources invested. 11 Ladies and gentlemen: Through the obligation to provide national currency to the economy, the Bank of Mexico establishes a close link with all citizens, since a large proportion of the population uses coins and banknotes. Thus, millions of citizens have a direct and daily relationship with the banknotes printed by the Bank of Mexico, because they use them to carry out their transactions and deposit in them part of their assets. This implies a great responsibility for the issuing institute. In that sense, the stability of the purchasing power of banknotes and coins and full confidence in their use are key elements for an economy to perform properly, facilitate economic exchange, stimulate individual and social initiatives and can open more opportunities for well-being to all citizens. The Bank of Mexico has sought, throughout its history and especially since its autonomy, to preserve the purchasing power of our currency and provide it efficiently, which has resulted in 12 a wide acceptance among the public. In addition, our currency is not only a reliable means of payment, but an object of great quality, beauty and representativeness with which many users develop a clear identification. For all the above, the formal entry into operation of this new banknote factory is great news for the Bank of Mexico. Congratulations to those who have participated in this work and to those who will work in this space. All of you will contribute to consolidating the services that the Bank of Mexico is obliged to provide to our country and to strengthening security and confidence in the use of our banknotes. Thanks a lot 13

En suma, la fbrica que hoy inauguramos constituye un espacio de vanguardia, que se alberga en una edificacin segura y funcional, que dispone del equipo ms moderno y que cuenta con un personal de alrededor de 250 trabajadores altamente capacitados. Ello implica una gran responsabilidad para el instituto emisor. En ese sentido, la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de los billetes y monedas y la confianza plena en su uso, son elementos clave para que una economa se desempee adecuadamente, facilite el intercambio econmico, estimule las iniciativas individuales y sociales y pueda abrir ms oportunidades de bienestar a todos los ciudadanos. El Banco de Mxico ha procurado, a lo largo de su historia y especialmente desde su autonoma, preservar el poder adquisitivo de nuestra moneda y proveerla eficientemente, lo que ha redundado en 12 una amplia aceptacin entre el pblico. Adems, nuestra moneda no slo es un medio de pago confiable, sino un objeto de gran calidad, belleza y representatividad con el que muchos usuarios desarrollan una clara identificacin. Por todo lo anterior, la entrada formal en operacin de esta nueva fbrica de billetes es una gran noticia para el Banco de Mxico. Felicidades a quienes han participado en esta obra y a quienes laborarn en este espacio. Todos ustedes habrn de contribuir a consolidar los servicios que el Banco de Mxico est obligado a prestar a nuestro pas y a fortalecer la seguridad y la confianza en el uso de nuestros billetes. Muchas gracias 13

Title: The importance of central bank autonomy: the Mexican experience, from the seminar for the twenty-fifth anniversary of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the closing of the First Session, "The Importance of the Autonomy of the Central Bank: The Mexican Experience", of the Seminar for the Twenty-Fifth Anniversary of the Autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. Already the former governors Mancera, Ortiz and Carstens have made an extraordinary account of the nature, history and evolution of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico, on which I would like to recapitulate around some aspects. -The aspiration to stability and certainty in monetary issuanceThe stability in the provision of national currency and the maintenance of its purchasing power constitute a fundamental indicator of the institutional development of a country. From the beginning of independent life in Mexico, a recurring aspiration was the creation of an instance of issuance that would provide currency to the national economy and, in that function, seek the acceptance of its circulation and the stability of its purchasing power. Given the constant political instability and warlike clashes that Mexico experienced during most of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, 1 it was extremely complex to create a stable system of monetary issuance. Therefore, fiat money did not take root and was frequently rejected, forcing, at times, to retreat to the most archaic modes of exchange. It was not until the Constitution of 1917 that a social consensus could be reached to incorporate the mandate to create a state bank with a monopoly on the issuance of banknotes. From its beginnings, a balance was sought between its character as an institution of the State and the possibility of maintaining independence in its actions with respect to the most immediate governmental needs. In fact, in the explanatory memorandum of the Constitutive Law of the Bank of Mexico of 1925 it was recognized: "There is indeed, in a bank controlled by the Government, the very serious danger that the political interest may predominate at any given time over the public interest, that is, that the government represents the interest of the men who belong to the party that constitutes it and dispenses with the national interest." 2 Therefore, this Law incorporated a certain independence between the Bank and the federal government. Thus, for example, it was stipulated that the members of the board of directors could not be public officials, measures were established to ensure prudence in the creation of money and a clear limit was determined on the financing of the Bank of Mexico to the government. In both 1928 and 1936, stricter requirements were established so that the Bank could increase the issuance of working capital or grant loans to the federal government. However, these restrictions met with strong opposition in the public power and led to reforms that, in 1938 and 1941, significantly reversed that independence in its management, and even gave the government powers to appoint and remove discretionary officials of the central institute. 3 This episode reflects how sometimes, despite being clear about the most convenient institutional arrangement, it can take a back seat to the political imperatives of the moment. Although the legal and institutional arrangement in force at that time was not favorable to price stability, during the decades known as the stabilizing development, from the mid-fifties to 1970, there was agreement between the fiscal and monetary authorities and prudent and coordinated macroeconomic policies were maintained, that allowed a long stage of sustained growth with low inflation. In these years, the Director of the central bank, Rodrigo Gomez and the Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Antonio Ortiz Mena, conceived price stability as a fundamental requirement of sustainable development. With the application of this vision, it was possible to maintain low inflation and it was possible that, for just over three decades, the country grew to 4 rates above 6 percent per year, with extensive job creation. This sustained period of growth illustrates the importance of pursuing price stability as a State policy aimed at creating a solid and long-term foundation for more dynamic and inclusive economic development. Unfortunately, this strategy was reversed in the following years, making it clear that price stability cannot depend only on possible coincidences between the people responsible for fiscal and monetary policy. -The crises of the seventies and eighties and the road to autonomyAfter, in the seventies and eighties the Mexican economy experienced a turbulent stage, which originated in the application of excessively expansionary policies, as well as in the obligation imposed on the central bank to extend credit to finance the fiscal deficit. 5 This led to the deterioration of price stability, generating acute, prolonged and profoundly damaging inflations for society - which exceeded 100% between 1982 and 1988. It was not a phenomenon unique to our country, in many economies, especially emerging economies, where the central bank lacked effective independence, the government used monetary policy for different purposes and contrary to price stability. Thus, the excessive monetary expansion produced, in different latitudes, recurrent inflationary episodes, distrust in money and crises with severe economic consequences and social affectations. For this reason, and in the face of the extended rebound in inflation, various proposals to promote price stability began to circulate. Many academic texts, from friedman's to those of Lucas, Kydland, Prescott, Barro, Gordon, and Rogoff, to name a few of the most influential, abounded on the nature of the inflationary phenomenon, demonstrated the limitations of monetary expansion to foster growth, and supported the desirability of a more independent central bank. 6 Thus, both the theory and the international experience, and the history of Mexico itself, show the risks of not having an autonomous central bank: (i) creates an environment where pressure from governments on central bankers may be more frequent to meet very short-term objectives, making inflationary episodes more likely; (ii) fosters an environment more likely to face a situation of fiscal dominance over monetary policy; and (iii) by tolerating that monetary policies may be inconsistent over time, agents' expectations and economic activity are adversely affected. In addition, various empirical studies began to show that countries where central banks showed greater independence had better inflationary performance and a better sustenance for sustained economic growth. Even, the credibility they gained 7 these banks made it possible to reduce the costs of combating inflation by consolidating and clarifying the objectives and strategies of the central bank. All this generated a widespread awareness of the importance of having an autonomous central bank, aimed at permanently promoting price stability. Among its main features, the autonomy of the central bank implied: (i) Having a clear legal mandate with specific objectives; ii) Limit the discretion of the government in the appointment and permanence of the bank's board of directors or governing board; (iii) Explicitly limit the capacity of any authority to use the central bank as a means of financing; iv) Consolidate collegiate decision-making bodies, with proven technical capacity and guarantees to act independently; and (v) Allow the bank to choose the best means to achieve the objectives set by law. 8 During the nineties, these notions in favor of the autonomy of central banks began to materialize in dozens of advanced and emerging countries. -The autonomy of the Bank of MexicoFrom its own historical experience, and in line with the international trend aimed at modifying the legal arrangement between the State and the central bank, as well as giving it greater clarity and certainty, it was proposed to change the legal nature of the Bank of Mexico, transforming it into an autonomous State agency and with the priority purpose of seeking price stability with a long-term commitment. The 1993 amendment to Article 28 of the Constitution, which entered into force in 1994, granted the Bank of Mexico full autonomy, noting that "[...] The State shall have a central bank which shall be autonomous in the exercise of its functions and in its administration. Its priority objective will be to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, thereby strengthening the leadership of national development that 9 it is up to the State. No authority may order the bank to grant financing." The Law gives the Bank two additional purposes, closely related to the primary objective, which are to promote the healthy development of the financial system and to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. The Bank's management autonomy provided for in the Law also implies the formation of a collegiate decision-making body, the Governing Board, composed of five members who are appointed in a staggered manner and have the conditions to act with total independence. The autonomy of the Bank of Mexico is an institutional design that has worked: the priority criterion according to which the Bank must operate, maintain low and stable inflation, offers the public a clear measure to evaluate its performance. This makes monetary policy more 10 predictable, reducing uncertainty and facilitating the decisions of economic agents. Thus, inflation left behind the levels of two, and up to three digits that it reached, currently standing around the permanent target of 3%. The conduct of monetary policy with this objective has also led to a lower persistence of inflation and a lower transfer of changes in relative prices, especially exchange rate fluctuations, to this inflation. This has made it possible to face various and severe external shocks that have required significant exchange rate adjustments with less impact on economic activity. Of course, autonomy does not imply isolation, on the contrary, it obliges and links the institution to a greater extent with the citizenry, so it requires substantive progress in transparency and information openness. 11 Moreover, these factors are not only an indispensable part of the central bank's accountability to society, but are a fundamental requirement for the better functioning of monetary policy itself and the better achievement of its aims. Since gaining its autonomy, the bank has increased the frequency, quality and timeliness of its reports and indicators, improved the methodologies for calculating its data and modernized the formats for its dissemination, gradually adopting the best international practices of disclosure and transparency. Throughout 2018, additional measures were adopted, allowing the public to assess in greater detail the nature, evolution and results of the institution's policies. i) To reinforce the inflation targeting scheme based on forecasts, since February 2018 the specific forecasts for average inflation have been published in each Quarterly Report 12 quarterly for the next eight quarters, for both headline and core inflation. (ii) The minutes of monetary policy decisions include the identity of the voters and, in the event of any dissent, add an explanation for such dissent. In addition, this can occur both on the monetary policy decision and on what is expressed in the communique. (iii) The full transcripts of the meetings of the Governing Board at which the monetary policy decision is taken shall be available to the public three years after the relevant meeting, a shorter period than that used by most central banks. (iv) To promote a broader discussion of the financial regulations issued by the Bank of Mexico, a mechanism for open and transparent public consultations was adopted, which addresses the principle that all actors should be aware of draft provisions with equal opportunity and can comment on them. 13 Autonomy has shown its advantages as an effective means for central banks to provide society with important public goods. However, autonomy is not a finished issue, but a condition that must continuously respond to new challenges. For example, since the 2008 financial crisis, in addition to the priority objective of price stability, central banks have renewed their role in preventing, detecting and mitigating risks to the stability of the financial system. Similarly, central banks must react with agility to the changes that technological progress brings to the configuration of financial services. With what has been learned in recent decades and considering the costs to society, both of not having price stability, and those associated with financial crises, the arguments in favor of having an autonomous central bank have been reinforced. 14 However, the autonomy of central banking faces new challenges. We have witnessed a growing polarization in economic and political narratives, both in advanced and emerging economies. This is the result of profound and complex transformations, which are related to: (i) the rapid integration of labour-rich economies and regions into a globalised world; (ii) the direct and indirect costs of the major financial crisis; (iii) the information technology revolution and its effect on the world of work and everyday life; their development opportunities. This environment has been fertile ground for public policies with short-term horizons, such as protectionism and trade tensions. That is why institutions with long-term objectives, both multilateral and national, face greater and new challenges. 15 In this circumstance, central banks face the challenge both of fulfilling their objectives and of communicating more effectively the tangible impact they have, their mandate, their condition of autonomy and their actions on the well-being of citizens and on the possibilities of development. Meetings like this are an extraordinary space to strengthen this communication. Ladies and gentlemen, the history of the Bank of Mexico over the past 25 years confirms the importance of autonomy as an ideal condition for achieving its priority mandate, maintaining low and stable inflation, which is the best contribution of monetary policy to promote a more dynamic, sustainable and equitable development. Indeed, the objectives of promoting price stability, stimulating the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of the payment system pursued by the Bank of Mexico are public goods, which have a concrete impact on the well-being of citizens. 16 For example, so far in the twenty-first century, there has been one of the longest periods of price stability in Mexico's history as an independent nation. Confidence in the effectiveness of our currency as a means of payment, store of value and unit of account has a direct influence on the economic opportunities and quality of life of citizens. Therefore, the Constitutional amendment that 25 years ago conferred autonomy on the Bank of Mexico, can be considered as one of the most important economic reforms in the contemporary history of Mexico, which deserves to be preserved for the following generations. Thanks a lot 17
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante el cierre de la Primera sesin, La importancia de la autonoma de la Banca Central: la experiencia mexicana, del Seminario por el Vigsimo Quinto Aniversario de la autonoma del banco de Mxico. Ya los exgobernadores Mancera, Ortiz y Carstens han hecho un extraordinario recuento de la naturaleza, historia y evolucin de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico, sobre lo cual me gustara recapitular en torno a algunos aspectos. -La aspiracin a la estabilidad y certidumbre en la emisin monetariaLa estabilidad en la provisin de moneda nacional y el mantenimiento de su poder adquisitivo constituyen un indicador fundamental del desarrollo institucional de un pas. Desde los inicios de la vida Independiente en Mxico, una aspiracin recurrente era la creacin de una instancia de emisin que dotara de moneda a la economa nacional y que, en esa funcin, procurara la aceptacin de su circulacin y la estabilidad de su poder adquisitivo. Dada la constante inestabilidad poltica y enfrentamientos blicos que vivi Mxico durante la mayor parte del siglo XIX y principios del XX, 1 resultaba sumamente complejo crear un sistema estable de emisin monetaria. Por eso, el dinero fiduciario no lleg a arraigarse y fue frecuentemente rechazado, obligando, en ocasiones, a retroceder a las modalidades de intercambio ms arcaicas. Fue hasta la Constitucin de 1917 cuando se pudo alcanzar un consenso social para incorporar el mandato de crear un banco del Estado con el monopolio de la emisin de billetes. Desde sus inicios, se buscaba un equilibrio entre su carcter de institucin del Estado y la posibilidad de que mantuviera independencia en su accionar respecto a las necesidades gubernamentales ms inmediatas. De hecho, en la exposicin de motivos de la Ley Constitutiva de Banco de Mxico de 1925 se reconoca: Hay efectivamente, en un banco controlado por el Gobierno, el gravsimo peligro de que el inters poltico pueda predominar en un momento dado sobre el inters pblico, es decir, que el gobierno represente el inters de los hombres que pertenecen al partido que lo constituye y prescinda del inters nacional. 2 Por eso, dicha Ley incorporaba cierta independencia entre el Banco y el gobierno federal. As, por ejemplo, se estipul que los miembros del consejo de administracin no podran ser funcionarios pblicos, se establecieron medidas para procurar la prudencia en la creacin de dinero y se determin un lmite claro al financiamiento del Banco de Mxico al gobierno. Tanto en 1928, como en 1936, se establecieron requisitos ms estrictos para que el Banco pudiera aumentar la emisin de circulante o conceder crditos al gobierno federal. Sin embargo, estas restricciones encontraron fuerte oposicin en el poder pblico y propiciaron reformas que, en 1938 y 1941, revirtieron significativamente esa independencia en su gestin, e inclusive se otorgaron facultades al gobierno para nombrar y remover discrecionalmente a los funcionarios del instituto central. 3 Este episodio refleja cmo en ocasiones, a pesar de tener claro el arreglo institucional ms conveniente, ste puede llegar a pasar a segundo plano respecto a los imperativos polticos del momento. -La etapa de concurrencia de enfoques y autonoma de factoA pesar de que el arreglo legal e institucional vigente en ese entonces no era favorable a la estabilidad de precios, durante las dcadas conocidas como el desarrollo estabilizador, de mediados de los cincuenta hasta 1970, hubo coincidencia entre las autoridades fiscales y monetarias y se mantuvieron polticas macroeconmicas prudentes y coordinadas, que permitieron una larga etapa de crecimiento sostenido con baja inflacin. En estos aos, el Director del banco central, Rodrigo Gmez y el Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, Antonio Ortiz Mena, conceban la estabilidad de precios como un requisito fundamental del desarrollo sostenible. Con la aplicacin de esta visin se logr mantener una inflacin baja y fue posible que, durante poco ms de tres lustros, el pas creciera a 4 tasas superiores al 6 por ciento anual, con amplia generacin de empleos. Este periodo sostenido de crecimiento ilustra la importancia de procurar la estabilidad de precios como poltica de Estado, tendiente a crear cimientos slidos y de largo plazo para un desarrollo econmico ms dinmico e inclusivo. Desgraciadamente, esta estrategia fue revertida en los aos siguientes, dejando en claro que la estabilidad de precios no puede depender slo de las posibles coincidencias entre las personas responsables de la poltica fiscal y monetaria. -Las crisis de los aos setenta y ochenta y el camino a la autonomaPosteriormente, en los aos setenta y ochenta la economa mexicana experiment una etapa turbulenta, que se origin en la aplicacin de polticas excesivamente expansivas, as como en la obligacin que se impuso al banco central de extender crdito para financiar el dficit fiscal. 5 Esto condujo al deterioro de la estabilidad de precios, generando inflaciones agudas, prolongadas y profundamente perjudiciales para la sociedad las cuales llegaron a rebasar el 100% entre 1982 y 1988. No se trat de un fenmeno nico de nuestro pas, en numerosas economas, sobre todo emergentes, donde el banco central careca de independencia efectiva, el gobierno utiliz la poltica monetaria para fines distintos y contrarios a la estabilidad de precios. As, la excesiva expansin monetaria produjo, en distintas latitudes, episodios inflacionarios recurrentes, desconfianza en el dinero y crisis con severas secuelas econmicas y afectaciones sociales. Por ello, y ante el repunte extendido de la inflacin, comenzaron a circular diversas propuestas para promover la estabilidad de precios. Muchos textos acadmicos, desde los de Friedman hasta los de Lucas, Kydland, Prescott, Barro, Gordon y Rogoff, por mencionar algunos de los ms influyentes, abundaban sobre la naturaleza del fenmeno inflacionario, demostraban las limitaciones de la expansin monetaria para fomentar el crecimiento y sustentaban la conveniencia de una banca central ms independiente. 6 As, tanto la teora como la experiencia internacional, y la propia historia de Mxico, muestran los riesgos de no contar con un banco central autnomo: i) crea un ambiente donde pueden ser ms frecuentes las presiones de los gobiernos a los banqueros centrales, a fin de que atiendan objetivos de muy corto plazo, haciendo ms probable sufrir episodios inflacionarios; ii) propicia un entorno ms propenso a enfrentar una situacin de dominancia fiscal sobre la poltica monetaria; y iii) al tolerar que las polticas monetarias pudieran ser inconsistentes en el tiempo, se afectan negativamente las expectativas de los agentes y la actividad econmica. Adicionalmente, diversos estudios empricos comenzaron a mostrar que los pases donde los bancos centrales mostraban mayor independencia tenan un mejor desempeo inflacionario y un mejor sustento para el crecimiento econmico sostenido. Inclusive, la credibilidad que ganaban 7 dichos bancos permita disminuir los costos del combate a la inflacin al consolidar y clarificar los objetivos y estrategias del banco central. Todo ello, gener una extendida conciencia sobre la importancia de contar con un banco central autnomo, orientado a promover permanentemente la estabilidad de precios. Entre sus principales rasgos, la autonoma del banco central implicaba: i) Contar con un mandato jurdico claro y con objetivos concretos; ii) Acotar la discrecionalidad del gobierno en el nombramiento y permanencia del directorio o junta de gobierno del banco; iii) Limitar explcitamente la capacidad de cualquier autoridad para utilizar al banco central como medio de financiamiento; iv) Consolidar rganos colegiados de toma de decisiones, con probada capacidad tcnica y garantas para actuar con independencia; y v) Permitir al banco elegir los mejores medios para alcanzar los objetivos que le marca la ley. 8 Durante los aos noventa, estas nociones a favor de la autonoma de los bancos centrales comenzaron a materializarse en decenas de pases avanzados y emergentes. -La autonoma del Banco de MxicoA partir de la propia experiencia histrica, y en consonancia con la tendencia internacional orientada a modificar el arreglo jurdico entre el Estado y el banco central, as como a darle mayor claridad y certidumbre, se plante cambiar la naturaleza jurdica del Banco de Mxico, transformndolo en un organismo del Estado autnomo y con la finalidad prioritaria de procurar la estabilidad de precios con un compromiso de largo plazo.
