The fifth place corresponded to the team from the Technical and Banking Institute San Carlos de Ecatepec, State of Mexico, with the essay entitled "Economic certainty and price stability". Its members are Kevin Rogaciano Flores Sanchez, Gustavo Reyes Garcia, Zully Julieta Vazquez Mateos, Diana Paola Ugalde Soto and as advisor Professor Gerardo Soria Maldonado. The work recalls Mexico's own economic history, particularly that of the eighties, when people could not afford to buy a chocolate in the corner store due to such high inflation. The fourth place was assigned to the team of the Alexander Von Humboldt University Institute, Preparatory school of the Springfield College of Toluca, State of Mexico, with the article entitled "Taking care of it is worth it". Its members are Adriana Elizabeth de Lucas Aguirre, Karla Carely Reyna Gonzalez, Julia Isabel Serrato Fonseca and Juan Carlos Talavera Nieto and as advisor The Professor Maritza Pena Becerril. The essay talks concretely about how in the eighties in Mexico people could not be sure how many kilos of tortillas they would be able to buy. The different experiences raised agree that stability provides certainty and more possibilities to make plans in any term for families. 5 Creditors to the third place with a prize of 50,000 pesos, we have the team of Instituto Highlands del Pedregal of the Federal District composed of Elsa Behar Gomez, Gloria Romina Celis Gonzalez, Celia Gomez del Campo Neme, Maria Alejandra Pliego Zermeno and as an advisor professor Maria Isabel de Haas Torres. The title of his work is "Stable Prices: Benefit for All". In the essay, the young Vero is affected in her life projects by price instability. Vero's intention to buy a computer had to be postponed, thus delaying the acquisition of a tool that would allow him to receive a better education. The second place, with a prize of 75,000 pesos, was awarded to the team of the Ameyalli School of the Federal District, its members are Mariana Blanco Uriarte, Rodrigo Cal and Mayor Bachtold, Ernesto Diaz Lozano Patino and Alejandro Soto Fernandez and its advisor is Professor Cesar Ivan Quiroz Trejo. His document "An unfounded suspicion", takes place in Acambaro and presents us in an entertaining way how an excess of money without economic foundation deteriorates the quality of life of the population. Undoubtedly, his example of an excessive level of water for flowers can be associated with monetary excesses and price instability. Finally, the winning essay with a prize of 100,000 pesos, entitled "Our professional future and price stability" corresponds to the team of the Alexander Von Humboldt University Preparatory Institute of the Springfield College of Toluca, State of Mexico. Its members are Luis Rodrigo Arce Valdes, Luis Felipe Galicia alvarez, Jessica Marlene Mosso Ruiz and Jessica Ramos Sanchez and the advisory professor is Maritza Pena Becerril. The work presents in an original and creative way, the effects it has and will have on the lives of the authors, an economy with and without price stability. It shows that inflation does not distinguish professions or lifestyles, it can frustrate personal development plans, affecting everyone negatively. Thank you very much and congratulations. 6

Title: Launch of the TCFD Consortium
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the Launch of the TCFD Consortium.1 December 7, 2021 I am very pleased to participate in the launch of the TCFD consortium of Mexico, established at the initiative of industry and academic leaders, which seeks, through dialogue between the financial and non-financial sectors, to deepen the effective and efficient corporate disclosure of relevant financial information related to climate change. This, to have more information and promote the use of it by financial markets and economic agents. The TCFD consortium, a private sector platform, will promote awareness, the exchange of good practices, the issuance of guides and training in the field to companies and investors. The Sustainable Finance Committee of the Financial System Stability Council has been invited to participate as an observer in the work of the consortium. 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 Globally, the TCFD's recommendations have become an obligatory reference for climate-related disclosures. They consist of a set of risk management tools and best practices, which help companies understand, assess and mitigate the risks and exposures they have related to the climate in order to make better capital allocation decisions. The TCFD Consortium will play a key role in promoting the voluntary adoption of its recommendations. Due to its complexity, it is convenient to develop practical guidance and implementation capacity. This is particularly relevant in the case of medium-sized companies, for which the recommendations should not imply an excessive burden. For companies that want or are already contributing to positive environmental and climate change, the transparency promoted by the TCFD provides a path to consolidate alternatives for greater growth and profitability. The adoption of the recommendations of the TCFD, grouped into 4 pillars that are Governance, Strategy, 2 Risk Management and Metrics and Objectives, allows organizations to show the commitment of senior management to the achievement of positive climate results, a strategic vision of sustainability, and consolidate factors of attraction of consumers, better human capital and investors with long-term horizons. In closing, let me highlight the importance of the recent announcement at COP26 of the creation of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) of the IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards Foundation). The ISSB is developing a comprehensive global foundation of sustainability-related disclosure standards. The goal is to provide investors and other capital market participants with information on the risks and opportunities related to the sustainability of companies, in order to help them make better informed decisions. These standards will be based on the 4 pillars of the TCFD. 3 The ISSB will recommend measuring the impact of companies in terms of carbon emissions, water consumption, biodiversity or labor practices, as this information is relevant to identify value in companies. Its disclosure will be key so that it can be used by investors. Transparency induces better behavior and will have important effects on companies which will avoid being labeled as highly polluting or with inadequate labor practices. In addition, transparency will promote greater awareness among entrepreneurs about how to improve their practices and promote innovation in sustainable products and services. Initiatives such as the one we are celebrating today are the initial steps of a strategy of profound transformation, necessary for our economy to maintain and increase its competitiveness, based on producing goods and services that are in tune with the environment, with its employees and with society. Congratulations on the launch of the TCFD Consortium of Mexico. 4

Title: Presentation of the book: The relevance of public information for economic-social decision-making
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of the book The relevance of public information for economic-social decision-making. Mexico City, September 18, 2018 Dr. Francisco Javier Acuna, Commissioner President of INAI; Dr. oscar Guerra, Commissioner and President of the Editorial Committee of INAI; Dr. Gerardo Esquivel, coordinator of the volume The relevance of public information for economic-social decision-making; Dr. Maria Elena Estavillo, Commissioner of the Federal Institute of Telecommunications; Mr. Ricardo Fuentes, Executive Director of OXFAM; Ladies and gentlemen: It is a pleasure to participate in the presentation of the book: "The relevance of public information for economic-social decision-making", edited by the National Institute of Transparency, Access to Information and Protection of Personal Data (INAI) and coordinated by Dr. Gerardo Esquivel. I deeply appreciate the opportunity to collaborate in this collective effort of reflection and to share pages with very distinguished personalities. The focus of this book highlights the importance of transparency in improving the public policy decision-making process, and making them more effective. The result is a volume that offers specialized approaches to the role of transparency in the areas of monetary, fiscal, telecommunications, energy and anti-poverty policy. A fundamental feature of contemporary democracy is the social demand for greater transparency with regard to the work of public institutions. This social requirement generates broad benefits, on the one hand, it forces institutions to be accountable and provide concrete information to be able to comprehensively evaluate their performance and, on the other, the permanent scrutiny of citizens promotes greater efficiency in their operation. 2 Thus, access to information and transparency are not only a means of surveillance and citizen control that strengthens the rule of law and democracy, they also contribute to better economic performance. InAI's generous invitation to collaborate on this volume was an opportunity to highlight the importance of transparency to achieve the objectives that the law entrusts to the Bank of Mexico, as well as to recount the steps that have been taken in this area, and some of the pending challenges. Transparency has become fundamental for every central bank, consolidating itself as a way to reinforce the confidence of citizens that the issuance of primary money will be done responsibly and seeking the fulfillment of its mandate, which in the case of the Bank of Mexico is to preserve the purchasing power of the currency, that is, to maintain low and stable inflation. Periods of high and persistent inflation damage confidence in money, because by eroding its purchasing power, its effectiveness as a store of value is reduced and its capacity as a means of payment becomes uncertain. There are numerous episodes in history, including recent, and in various countries, in which uncontrolled inflation reduces the acceptance and social esteem of money, with disastrous consequences for the economy. That is why, since the final decades of the twentieth century, an international consensus advanced for the national currency issuing authority 3 ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency. Thus, a large number of countries decided to give their central banks the objective of seeking price stability and providing them with autonomy to achieve it. In our country, in 1993 the Constituent Assembly decided to grant autonomy to the Bank of Mexico for the realization of its institutional mission. Since then, a clear awareness has been consolidated within the Institute that transparency and accountability are practices that go hand in hand with autonomy and that they are essential to consolidate credibility in institutional action and achieve stability. Since those years, measures began to be taken to enable economic agents to better monitor the actions of the central bank, and new technologies, such as the Internet, began to be used to disseminate public data. For example, in 1996, several years before legislation on transparency and access to information, the Bank of Mexico established a "one-stop shop" on the website to enable citizens to submit questions and requests for information. In line with a robust academic evidence, from the nineties a new international paradigm was consolidated in the conduct of the monetary policy of central banks: the so-called inflation targeting regime, which bases its effectiveness, largely on: i) the communication of explicit inflation targets, ii) the 4 dissemination of methods and procedures to achieve them; When the public has confidence that the central bank will react to shocks that could steadily divert inflation from its target, its expectations and price formation will be better aligned with the inflation target. Thus, the credibility of the central bank is built through constant and consistent efforts, and cannot be taken for granted. Therefore, monetary policy must be carried out in an environment of transparency and be based on a strategy of clear communication with society regarding its objectives, plans and decisions. In this sense, the advantages of making decision-making transparent in the conduct of monetary policy are clear. With the dissemination of the communiques and minutes of the monetary policy meetings of the Bank of Mexico, anyone interested can know the way in which the monetary authority interprets, analyzes and uses public data. This transparency strategy has recently been strengthened in order to adopt best practices in the dissemination of information in central banks. In particular, the following measures were taken in the first four months of this year: (1) Quarterly publication of timely forecasts for inflation quarterly average for the next eight quarters. This will lead to 5 provides a reference for timely monitoring of compliance with the inflation target. (2) It was decided that the minutes of monetary policy decisions should include the identity of the voters and, in the event of any dissent, should add an explanation of the reasons for such dissent. (3) To support accountability and contribute to the historical narrative of the country's economy, it was decided that the full transcripts of the Governing Board meetings at which the monetary policy decision is taken will be made available to the public, three years after the relevant meeting, shorter than that used by most central banks. It is also a purpose of the Bank of Mexico to promote the healthy development of the financial system. In this regard, the Bank deploys this task in two main aspects. The first, as a regulator and supervisor, which seeks to promote the stability of the financial system, detecting and mitigating possible systemic risks that could affect the sector. The second, as a promoter of provisions and best practices to protect the interests of the public using financial services. In both aspects, the Bank of Mexico conceives transparency as a fundamental tool. On the one hand, with the exhaustive supervision and with the wide dissemination of significant data and reports regarding the health of the intermediaries and the system. This promotes, 6 directly and indirectly, the adoption of best financial practices, contributing to the soundness and stability of the financial system. On the other hand, through the protection and dissemination of consumer rights, as well as through the extensive dissemination of information on the characteristics and comparative costs of financial services, the Bank of Mexico seeks to promote competition and help intermediaries offer better services. It should be noted that transparency and access to information efforts and financial inclusion and education efforts present clear synergies. In addition, advances in information technologies offer an invaluable opportunity to overcome long-standing problems in the financial system, such as: i) the complexity and multiplicity of financial products, ii) high costs and barriers to obtain reliable information and compare services, and iii) prevent behavioral biases and other distortions from preventing users from making their best financial decisions. Among the recent actions to strengthen transparency and accountability, in March of this year, the Bank of Mexico significantly modified the process for issuing provisions to financial intermediaries. In particular, regulatory improvement includes the 7 carrying out different forms of public consultations, through open, homogeneous and transparent procedures. In all cases, the comments received are made public and a mechanism for communication, monitoring and evaluation of the regulatory framework that favors social participation is inaugurated. As an example, one of the first provisions that used this format refers to the use of payroll accounts as a source of payment of various credits for the benefit of employees. * * * In short, for the Bank of Mexico, autonomy does not imply isolation, but, on the contrary: i) a clear institutional mandate; (ii) with a attribution of specific responsibilities; Of course, transparency actions can never be concluded, as they are a process in constant evolution. Particularly in central banking and the financial sector, technological progress generates constant innovations and, therefore, new needs to regulate, disclose and make transparent. Therefore, the bank expresses its willingness to continue detecting opportunities to strengthen the transparency framework and, with it, strengthen its most important asset: public trust and credibility. 8 It is worth mentioning that this book proposes a very useful dialogue between academics and public officials, contrasting visions and perspectives around the advances in transparency in certain areas of public activity. In this regard, I would like to thank Dr. Gerardo Esquivel and Gabriela Orozco for their constructive approach in this book to the progress and challenges of transparency in monetary policy. Your views are appreciated and very useful in improving our work. At the Bank of Mexico, we are convinced that the more and better informed society is about the specific objectives pursued by the institution, the benefits they imply and the factors that influence monetary policy decision-making, the better the results with respect to these objectives and the better anchored will be the expectations of economic agents around low and stable inflation. Such price stability is far from an end in itself and, rather, constitutes an indispensable condition for sustaining the processes of growth and improvement of social welfare that we all desire. Thanks a lot 9

Ciudad de Mxico, 18 de septiembre de 2018 Dr. Francisco Javier Acua, Comisionado Presidente del INAI; Dr. scar Guerra, Comisionado y Presidente del Comit Editorial del INAI; Dr. Gerardo Esquivel, coordinador del volumen La relevancia de la informacin pblica para la toma de decisiones econmico-sociales; Dra. Mara Elena Estavillo, Comisionada del Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones; Mtro. Ricardo Fuentes, Director Ejecutivo de OXFAM; Seoras y seores: Es un gusto participar en la presentacin del libro: La relevancia de la informacin pblica para la toma de decisiones econmicosociales, editado por el Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Informacin y Proteccin de Datos Personales (INAI) y coordinado por el Dr. Gerardo Esquivel. El enfoque de este libro permite destacar la importancia que tiene la transparencia para mejorar el proceso de toma de decisiones de poltica pblica, y que stas sean ms eficaces. El resultado es un volumen que ofrece enfoques especializados sobre el papel de la transparencia en los mbitos de la poltica monetaria, fiscal, telecomunicaciones, energtica y de combate a la pobreza. Un rasgo fundamental de la democracia contempornea es la demanda social de mayor transparencia con respecto al quehacer de las instituciones pblicas. Esta exigencia social genera amplios beneficios, por un lado, obliga a las instituciones a rendir cuentas y brindar informacin concreta para poder evaluar integralmente su desempeo y, por el otro, el escrutinio permanente de los ciudadanos promueve una mayor eficacia en su funcionamiento. 2 As, el acceso a la informacin y la transparencia, no slo son un medio de vigilancia y control ciudadano que fortalece el estado de derecho y la democracia, tambin contribuyen a un mejor desempeo econmico. La generosa invitacin del INAI a colaborar en este volumen fue una oportunidad para destacar la importancia de la transparencia para alcanzar los objetivos que la ley le encomienda al Banco de Mxico, as como para hacer un recuento de los pasos que se han dado en esta materia, y de algunos de los retos pendientes. La transparencia se ha vuelto fundamental para todo banco central, consolidndose como una va para reforzar la confianza de la ciudadana en que la emisin de dinero primario, se har con responsabilidad y buscando el cumplimiento de su mandato, que en el caso del Banco de Mxico es el de preservar el poder adquisitivo de la moneda, es decir, mantener una inflacin baja y estable. Los periodos de inflacin alta y persistente daan la confianza en el dinero, pues al erosionar su poder adquisitivo, se merma su eficacia como depsito de valor y se vuelve incierta su capacidad como medio de pago. Existen numerosos episodios en la historia, incluso reciente, y en diversos pases, en los que la inflacin descontrolada reduce la aceptacin y estima social del dinero, con desastrosas consecuencias para la economa. Por eso, desde las dcadas finales del siglo XX, avanz un consenso internacional para que la autoridad emisora de moneda nacional 3 procurara la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda. As, un gran nmero de pases decidi otorgar a sus bancos centrales el objetivo de procurar la estabilidad de precios y dotarlos de autonoma para alcanzarlo. En nuestro pas, en 1993 el Constituyente decidi otorgar autonoma al Banco de Mxico para la realizacin de su misin institucional. Desde entonces, se ha consolidado al interior del Instituto una clara conciencia de que la transparencia y la rendicin de cuentas, son prcticas que van de la mano con la autonoma y que son indispensables para consolidar la credibilidad en el actuar institucional y alcanzar la estabilidad. Desde esos aos, comenzaron a adoptarse medidas a fin de que los agentes econmicos pudieran dar mejor seguimiento a las acciones del banco central y se comenzaron a utilizar las nuevas tecnologas, como Internet, para difundir datos pblicos. Por ejemplo, en 1996, varios aos antes de que se legislara en materia de transparencia y acceso a la informacin, el Banco de Mxico estableci una ventanilla nica en el sitio de Internet para que los ciudadanos pudieran presentar dudas y peticiones de informacin. En lnea con una robusta evidencia acadmica, a partir de los aos noventa se consolid un nuevo paradigma internacional en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria de los bancos centrales: el rgimen denominado de metas de inflacin, el cual basa su efectividad, en gran parte en: i) la comunicacin de metas explcitas de inflacin, ii) la 4 divulgacin de los mtodos y procedimientos para alcanzarlas, y iii) la rendicin de cuentas sobre los resultados. Cuando el pblico tiene confianza en que el banco central reaccionar ante los choques que pudieran desviar de manera sostenida a la inflacin de su objetivo, sus expectativas y la formacin de precios estarn mejor alineadas con la meta de inflacin. As, la credibilidad del banco central se construye a travs de esfuerzos constantes y consistentes, y no puede darse por sentada. Por ello, la poltica monetaria debe llevarse a cabo en un entorno de transparencia y estar sustentada en una estrategia de comunicacin clara con la sociedad respecto de sus objetivos, planes y decisiones. En este sentido, son claras las ventajas de transparentar la toma de decisiones en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. Con la difusin de los comunicados y de las minutas de las reuniones de poltica monetaria del Banco de Mxico, todo interesado puede conocer la forma en que la autoridad monetaria interpreta, analiza y utiliza los datos pblicos. Esta estrategia de transparencia se ha reforzado recientemente a fin de adoptar mejores prcticas en materia de difusin de informacin en la banca central. En particular, en los primeros cuatro meses del presente ao se adoptaron las siguientes medidas: 1) Publicacin trimestral de los pronsticos puntuales para la inflacin promedio trimestral de los prximos ocho trimestres. Con ello se 5 proporciona una referencia para dar seguimiento puntual al cumplimiento de la meta de inflacin. 2) Se decidi que las minutas de las decisiones de poltica monetaria incluyan la identidad de los votantes y, en caso de que exista algn disentimiento, aadan una explicacin de las razones de dicho disentimiento. 3) Para respaldar la rendicin de cuentas y contribuir a la narrativa histrica de la economa del pas, se decidi que las transcripciones ntegras de las reuniones de la Junta de Gobierno en las que se adopta la decisin de poltica monetaria estn disponibles al pblico, tres aos despus de la reunin correspondiente, plazo menor al utilizado por la mayora de bancos centrales. Tambin es una finalidad del Banco de Mxico el promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero. Al respecto, el Banco despliega esta tarea en dos grandes vertientes. La primera, como regulador y supervisor, que busca promover la estabilidad del sistema financiero, detectando y mitigando los eventuales riesgos sistmicos que pudieran afectar al sector. La segunda, como promotor de disposiciones y mejores prcticas para proteger los intereses del pblico usuario de servicios financieros. En ambas vertientes, el Banco de Mxico concibe la transparencia como una herramienta fundamental. Por un lado, con la supervisin exhaustiva y con la amplia divulgacin de datos significativos y reportes respecto a la salud de los intermediarios y del sistema. Ello promueve, 6 directa e indirectamente, la adopcin de mejores prcticas financieras, contribuyendo a la solidez y estabilidad del sistema financiero. Por otro lado, mediante la proteccin y difusin de los derechos de los consumidores, as como mediante la divulgacin extensiva de informacin en torno a las caractersticas y costos comparativos de los servicios financieros, el Banco de Mxico busca promover la competencia y contribuir a que los intermediarios ofrezcan mejores servicios. Cabe sealar que los esfuerzos de transparencia y acceso a la informacin y los esfuerzos en materia de inclusin y educacin financiera presentan claras sinergias. Adems, los avances en las tecnologas de la informacin ofrecen una oportunidad invaluable para superar problemas aejos en el sistema financiero, como lo son: i) la complejidad y multiplicidad de productos financieros, ii) altos costos y barreras para obtener informacin confiable y comparar servicios, y iii) evitar que sesgos conductuales y otras distorsiones impidan a los usuarios tomar sus mejores decisiones en materia financiera. Entre las acciones recientes para fortalecer la transparencia y rendicin de cuentas, en marzo de este ao, el Banco de Mxico modific significativamente el proceso para emitir disposiciones a los intermediarios financieros. En particular, la mejora regulatoria incluye la 7 realizacin de distintas modalidades de consultas pblicas, mediante procedimientos abiertos, homogneos y transparentes. En todos los casos, los comentarios recibidos se hacen pblicos y se inaugura un mecanismo de comunicacin, monitoreo y evaluacin del marco regulatorio que favorece la participacin social. A manera de ejemplo, una de las primeras disposiciones que utilizaron este formato se refiere al uso de las cuentas de nmina como fuente de pago de diversos crditos en beneficio de los asalariados. * * * En suma, para el Banco de Mxico la autonoma no implica aislamiento, sino, al contrario: i) un mandato institucional claro; ii) con una atribucin de responsabilidades concretas, y iii) un proceso de rendicin de cuentas basado en amplios criterios de transparencia. Por supuesto, las acciones en materia de transparencia nunca pueden darse por concluidas, pues son un proceso en permanente evolucin. Particularmente, en materia de banca central y en el sector financiero, el avance tecnolgico genera constantes innovaciones y, por ende, nuevas necesidades de regular, divulgar y transparentar. Por eso, el banco manifiesta su disposicin a seguir detectando las oportunidades para reforzar el marco de transparencia y, con ello, fortalecer su activo ms importante: la confianza y la credibilidad del pblico. 8 Cabe mencionar que este libro plantea un dilogo de gran utilidad entre acadmicos y funcionarios pblicos, contrastando visiones y perspectivas en torno a los avances en la transparencia en determinados mbitos de la actividad pblica. Al respecto, quiero agradecer el enfoque constructivo con que el doctor Gerardo Esquivel y Gabriela Orozco se refirieron en este libro a los avances y retos de transparencia en materia de poltica monetaria. Sus puntos de vista son apreciados y muy tiles para mejorar nuestra labor. En el Banco de Mxico estamos convencidos de que mientras ms y mejor informada est la sociedad sobre los objetivos concretos que persigue la institucin, los beneficios que stos implican y los factores que influyen en la toma de decisiones de poltica monetaria, mejores sern los resultados respecto a dichos objetivos y mejor ancladas estarn las expectativas de los agentes econmicos en torno a una inflacin baja y estable. Dicha estabilidad de precios est lejos de ser un fin en s misma y, ms bien, constituye una condicin indispensable para sustentar los procesos de crecimiento y mejoramiento del bienestar social que todos deseamos. Title: Celebration of the 90th Anniversary of the Bank of Mexico, in which the construction of the Banknote Factory in the state of Jalisco began and the circulation of the commemorative coin of 20 pesos alluding to the Centennial of the Mexican Air Force
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the celebration of the 90th Anniversary of the Bank of Mexico, in which the construction of the Banknote Factory in the state of Jalisco began and the circulation of the commemorative coin of 20 pesos alluding to the Centennial of the Mexican Air Force El Salto, Jalisco, October 14, 2015  Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto, Constitutional President of the United Mexican States,  Maestro Jorge Aristoteles Sandoval Diaz, Constitutional Governor of the State of Jalisco,  Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso, Secretary of Finance and Public Credit,  General Salvador Cienfuegos Zepeda, Secretary of Defense National,  Admiral Vidal Francisco Soberon Sanz, Secretary of the Navy,  Mr. Gerardo Ruiz Esparza, Secretary of Communications and Transport,  Francisco Guzman Ortiz, Head of the Office of the Presidency of the Republic,  Deputy Jorge Enrique Hernandez Bielma, President of the Bureau Board of Directors of the Congress of the State of Jalisco,  Magistrate Dr. Luis Carlos Vega Pamanes, President of the Supreme Court Court of Justice of the State of Jalisco,  General Carlos Antonio Rodriguez Munguia, Force Commander Aerea Mexicana,  Guillermo Hopkins Gamez, General Director of the Casa de Moneda de Mexico,  Mr. Joel Gonzalez Diaz, Municipal President of El Salto, Jalisco,  Members of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, 1  Mr. Arturo Zamora Jimenez, Senator of the Republic,  Mr. Luis Robles Miaja, President of the Association of Banks of the Republic Mexico,  Ladies and gentlemen, On the first of September, the Bank of Mexico celebrated ninety years of having started operations in 1925. However, the genesis of our Central Bank goes back years, when in 1917 our Political Constitution established that the Mexican State founded a Single Bank of Issuance. The denomination given by the Constituents to that long-awaited Central Bank could not be more eloquent: not only did it have to be an issuer of currency, it had to be the sole issuer of the national currency, since the main reason for creating a Central Bank controlled by the State was to end the diversity of issues of banknotes and coins that, during the peak years of the revolutionary struggle, they caused monetary and substantial chaos. 2 economic losses, which in turn generated among Mexicans a widespread distrust and even an open rejection of banknotes and coins that were not minted in precious metals. The Constituents were clearly aware that eradicating this distrust was indispensable not only for Mexico to prosper, but even to undertake the reconstruction of a country disarticulated and devastated by armed struggle, as well as to create modern institutions in accordance with the purposes of change and progress embodied in the new Constitution. It was certainly not an easy task. It took the creation of the Bank of Mexico eight more years, especially because the new Institution, to be successful, would have to have a solid livelihood, which could not be other than a constant and sound capital, with intrinsic value, backed by gold or silver. And this, in those very difficult years of reconstruction of the country, only 3 it could be achieved through large savings by the federal government. This effort of savings and austerity is reflected in the reports of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit corresponding to the period 1923-1925, so that in August 1925 in the coffers of the Treasury of the Federation had been accumulated, through notable savings in public spending, 45 million gold pesos. So aware were President Plutarco Elias Calles and the Secretary of Finance Alberto J. Pani of the need for the Bank of Mexico to be born endorsed before all society as a solid and reliable institution, that, as the surpluses resulting from the savings of the federal government were accumulated, they gave in the habit of visiting the Treasury accompanied by journalists and photographers, in order to spread the news about the crystallization of the surplus. These public visits sought, of course, to accredit in advance in front of 4 to the citizens the solidity and reliability that the future Central Bank would have and the currency it would issue. Thus, the Bank of Mexico was born thanks to what could have been the first fiscal surplus - of 45 million gold pesos - that a Mexican government registered after the Revolution. That surplus would represent 51% of the capital contributed by the federal government for the creation of the Bank of Mexico, which was complemented at that time by 49% of private capital. During a good part of its first years of life, our Central Institute faced various setbacks, from powerful pressures to become a source of financing for wasteful and deficit public spending to an adverse world environment, of a recessionary nature, which would lead to the so-called great depression, through the incomprehension and hostility of some private banks that saw the Bank of Mexico as a competitor, since in 5 initially, the Bank effectively provided window services to the public. When the Mexican peso was transformed into fiat currency, starting with a new Law of the Bank of Mexico in July 1931, and paper money was definitively rooted as the main means of payment in the country, the requirement to be a trust-generating entity for the Issuing Bank became even more imperative. To achieve this, the Central Bank required, in addition to exercising a responsible monetary policy, the help of an equally judicious fiscal policy, which did not incur chronic fiscal deficits, and which did not resort to the Issuing Bank as a source of financing for deficit public spending. After a long period of coordination between both policies, which was approximately from 1954 to 1970 and which has been known as the stage of stabilizing development - and during which our country registered high growth rates with 6 In the 70s and 80s, Mexico suffered from growing fiscal deficits that, since the Central Bank lacked autonomy, were financed with monetary issuance. The terrible experience of recurrent crises in the balance of payments, accompanied by high inflations that impoverished millions of Mexicans in a very short time, forged a broad social consensus in the country in favor of the Bank of Mexico being the Institution within the State whose sole mandate was to take care of the purchasing power of the currency. To achieve this, and this conviction was key in this social consensus, it was necessary that such an institution be autonomous, in such a way that no one could force it to grant financing to the State or to someone else, to the detriment of its mandate. Thus, in 1993 and 1994, one of the most successful and exemplary structural reforms of contemporary Mexico was forged: that of granting constitutional autonomy. 7 to the Bank of Mexico. The essence of this autonomy is precisely the express prohibition on the Central Bank granting financing to the government. The direct beneficiary of this autonomy is society, the users of the national currency. And the final result of this autonomy is that the Bank of Mexico has all the monetary policy instruments to achieve low and stable inflation, as has indeed happened. Today we have an annual inflation of 2.52 percent, the lowest in Mexico since consumer price movements are measured at the national level. In December 1995, barely a year after the Bank of Mexico's autonomy came into force, annual inflation was more than 25 times that of now, as a result of the balance of payments crisis that erupted in December 1994 and caused us to abandon a semi-fixed exchange rate policy, of pre-established flotation bands. 8 Thanks to the low and stable inflation that we enjoy today, interest rates are also at the lowest levels in history, there is a wide range of loans for people and companies at fixed rates, long terms and in pesos; the same for the savings of families as for the investment of companies, the planning horizon has been extended to decades, providing certainty. All this affects a growth in real wages and protects the purchasing power of retirees and pensioners. In turn, it stimulates - together with an environment of greater competition - that productivity is the lever to generate profits, and not the speculative calculation based on the misaligned price rises characteristic of periods of high inflation. Also, thanks to the effective anchoring of inflation, the incomes of Mexican families have retained their purchasing power even in the midst of a global financial environment of great volatility. 9 All these results make it abundantly clear that the pursuit of low and stable inflation is not at odds with higher economic growth. Quite the opposite. Low and stable inflation is a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for accelerated and sustainable economic activity, more well-paid jobs and greater well-being for the entire population. It is fair to recognize that President Enrique Pena Nieto has been clearly respectful of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico in all its senses. It should even be noted that, as part of the fiscal package for 2016 that your Government has submitted to the consideration of Congress, it contemplates an initiative to include in the Budget and Financial Responsibility Law the obligation that most, at least 70 percent, of the remnants of operation that the Bank of Mexico generates in its case and that 10 by law deliver to the Federal Government, which allocates them to the reduction of public debt. This initiative, in my opinion, is a clear demonstration of the conviction of the government of President Pena Nieto that the deliveries that the Bank of Mexico, where appropriate, makes to the Federal Government of its remnants of operation, are destined for purposes that adhere as closely as possible to the spirit of the autonomy of the Central Bank, and of course to strengthen macroeconomic stability. Moving forward, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico is committed to ensuring that the achievement of low and stable inflation continues. Particularly in these times of great volatility and uncertainty in the international financial markets, we have indicated in our communiques that if required, we will act with all flexibility and in a timely manner to consolidate the convergence of inflation to the 3 percent target. 11 * * * Now, perhaps there are those who wonder why we are celebrating the first 90 years of the life of the Bank of Mexico here. The reason is that the Bank's second banknote factory will be built on this land. Taking advantage of the honorable presence of the President of the Republic, we will unveil an allusive plaque that will remain as a testimony of the beginning of the construction work of this new banknote factory, in the thriving State of Jalisco. Today the banknote factory established in 1969 in Mexico City is close to its maximum production capacity limit, given that the demand for banknotes from the public has grown remarkably, due of course to the growth of both the population and the economy and, of course, by the same price stability. In the period from January 2001 to December 2014 the number of banknotes in circulation (measured in pieces, regardless of their 12 denomination) has recorded an average annual growth rate of 7.5 percent. Faced with this reality, the Bank of Mexico must be prepared, since it cannot fail in its task of providing society with the cash it demands, even more so if we consider that meeting that demand does not create inflationary pressures. It would be unthinkable that in the medium and long term the Bank would not be able to respond in a timely manner to society's demands for this specific means of payment, which are banknotes. It is estimated that the construction of this factory will last 24 months and it is expected that the start of operations will be between November 2017 and February 2018. The total investment, of course financed with bank resources given its budgetary autonomy, is estimated at approximately three billion pesos, of which about one billion correspond to the construction of the 13 building and about two billion pesos to the equipment and commissioning of the factory. A social witness, of impeccable honorability, will accompany us throughout the process of this work. It is, I repeat, an investment to be in a position to meet the demand for banknotes that society will make in the coming years, so it will not be inflationary. From what I have already said about the essence of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico, it will in no way be a banknote factory to finance the government. * * * We are also proud to share this event with the beloved Mexican national army and, specifically, with the Mexican Air Force, which celebrates its first hundred years of life. On this occasion, a commemorative coin of 20 pesos will begin to circulate today that gives honor and recognition to the Mexican Air Force in its centenary. This coin was 14 approved by the H. Congress of the Union, its design arose at the proposal of the Ministry of National Defense and was minted by the Mint of Mexico. I must also mention, and to reiterate the historic and harmonious relationship of our armed forces with the Bank of Mexico, that the Air Transport Unit of the Bank itself began operations in 1947 thanks largely to the initiative and support of the Mexican Air Force. For the creation of this Air Transport Unit, the efforts of the captain of the Mexican Air Force, Radames Gaxiola Andrade, who was previously in command of the glorious 201 squadron that participated in World War II, were decisive. Congratulations to the Mexican Air Force for its centenary and for the commemorative coin that will begin to circulate today; there will be those who wish to treasure it for its meaning, but also, like all other commemorative coins of 15 20 pesos, will serve without limitation as a means of payment in any type of operations. * * * Mr. President, I do not want to end without mentioning that, in the face of the difficult environment generated by the global economic crisis that we have faced since 2008, your government has laid the foundations for Mexico to be one of the few countries in the world that can simultaneously offer two factors that seem to be elusive: macroeconomic stability along with the potential for sustained and accelerated growth. Responsibility for the management of fiscal, financial and monetary policies generates stability, while structural reforms are allowing us to have the potential to grow rapidly and with increasing equity. Thanks a lot. 16
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la celebracin del 90 Aniversario del Banco de Mxico, marco en el cual se dio inicio a la construccin de la Fbrica de Billetes en el estado de Jalisco y la puesta en circulacin de la moneda conmemorativa de 20 pesos alusiva al Centenario de la Fuerza Area Mexicana El Salto, Jalisco, 14 de octubre de 2015  Seor licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto, Presidente Constitucional de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos,  Maestro Jorge Aristteles Sandoval Daz, Gobernador Constitucional del Estado de Jalisco,  Doctor Luis Videgaray Caso, Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico,  General Salvador Cienfuegos Zepeda, Secretario de la Defensa Nacional,  Almirante Vidal Francisco Sobern Sanz, Secretario de Marina,  Licenciado Gerardo Ruz Esparza, Secretario de Comunicaciones y Transportes,  Licenciado Francisco Guzmn Ortiz, Jefe de la Oficina de la Presidencia de la Repblica,  Diputado Jorge Enrique Hernndez Bielma, Presidente de la Mesa Directiva del H. Congreso del Estado de Jalisco,  Magistrado doctor Luis Carlos Vega Pmanes, Presidente del Supremo Tribunal de Justicia del Estado de Jalisco,  General Carlos Antonio Rodrguez Mungua, Comandante de la Fuerza Area Mexicana,  Licenciado Guillermo Hopkins Gmez, Director General de la Casa de Moneda de Mxico,  Seor Joel Gonzlez Daz, Presidente Municipal de El Salto, Jalisco,  Miembros de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico, 1  Licenciado Arturo Zamora Jimnez, Senador de la Repblica,  Licenciado Luis Robles Miaja, Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico,  Seoras y seores: El pasado primero de septiembre el Banco de Mxico celebr noventa aos de haber iniciado operaciones en 1925. Sin embargo, la gnesis de nuestro Banco Central se remonta aos atrs, cuando en 1917 nuestra Constitucin Poltica estableci que el Estado mexicano fundara un Banco nico de Emisin. La denominacin que le dieron los Constituyentes a ese anhelado Banco Central no poda ser ms elocuente: no slo tena que ser emisor de moneda, tena que ser el emisor nico de la moneda nacional, dado que el principal de los motivos para crear un Banco Central controlado por el Estado fue terminar con la diversidad de emisiones de billetes y de monedas que, durante los aos ms lgidos de la lucha revolucionaria, ocasionaron un caos monetario y cuantiosas 2 prdidas econmicas, lo que a su vez gener entre los mexicanos una generalizada desconfianza y hasta un abierto rechazo hacia los billetes y ante las monedas que no fuesen acuadas en metales preciosos. Los Constituyentes tenan clara conciencia de que erradicar esa desconfianza era indispensable ya no slo para que Mxico pudiese prosperar, sino incluso para emprender la reconstruccin de un pas desarticulado y devastado por la lucha armada, as como para crear instituciones modernas acordes a los propsitos de cambio y progreso plasmados en la nueva Constitucin. No fue, desde luego, tarea sencilla. Demor la creacin del Banco de Mxico ocho aos ms, sobre todo porque la nueva Institucin, para tener xito, debera tener un sustento slido, que no poda ser otro ms que un capital contante y sonante, con valor intrnseco, respaldado por oro o por plata. Y esto, en aquellos dificilsimos aos de reconstruccin del pas, slo 3 poda lograrse mediante grandes ahorros por parte del gobierno federal. De este esfuerzo de ahorro y austeridad dan cuenta las memorias de la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico correspondientes al periodo 1923-1925, de tal suerte que en agosto de 1925 en las arcas de la Tesorera de la Federacin se haban logrado acumular, mediante notables ahorros en el gasto pblico, 45 millones de pesos oro. Tan conscientes estaban el Presidente Plutarco Elas Calles y el Secretario de Hacienda Alberto J. Pani de la necesidad de que el Banco de Mxico naciese avalado ante toda la sociedad como Institucin slida y confiable, que, conforme se fueron acumulando los excedentes producto del ahorro del gobierno federal, dieron en la costumbre de visitar la Tesorera acompaados de periodistas y fotgrafos, con el objeto de que se difundiera la noticia sobre la cristalizacin del supervit. Esas visitas pblicas buscaban, desde luego, acreditar de antemano frente 4 a la ciudadana la solidez y confiabilidad que tendran el futuro Banco Central y la moneda que emitira. As pues el Banco de Mxico naci gracias al que podra haber sido el primer supervit fiscal  de 45 millones de pesos oro  que registr un gobierno mexicano despus de la Revolucin. Ese excedente representara el 51% del capital aportado por el gobierno federal para la creacin del Banco de Mxico, lo que se complement en ese entonces con un 49% de capital privado. Durante buena parte de sus primeros aos de vida nuestro Instituto Central enfrent diversas contrariedades, desde poderosas presiones para convertirse en fuente de financiamiento de un gasto pblico dispendioso y deficitario hasta un entorno mundial adverso, de carcter recesivo, que desembocara en la llamada gran depresin, pasando por la incomprensin y hostilidad de algunos bancos privados que vean al Banco de Mxico como un competidor, dado que en 5 un principio el Banco efectivamente brindaba servicios de ventanilla al pblico. Cuando el peso mexicano se transform en moneda fiduciaria, a partir de una nueva Ley del Banco de Mxico en julio de 1931, y se arraig definitivamente el papel moneda como el principal medio de pago en el pas, el requisito de ser una entidad generadora de confianza para el Banco Emisor se hizo an ms imperativo. Para lograrlo, el Banco Central requera, adems de ejercer una poltica monetaria responsable, del concurso de una poltica fiscal igualmente juiciosa, que no incurriera en dficits fiscales crnicos, y que no recurriera al Banco Emisor como fuente de financiamiento de un gasto pblico deficitario. Tras un largo periodo de coordinacin entre ambas polticas, que fue aproximadamente de 1954 a 1970 y que se ha conocido como la etapa del desarrollo estabilizador  y durante el cual nuestro pas registr altas tasas de crecimiento con 6 estabilidad de precios-, Mxico padeci en los aos 70 y 80 episodios de crecientes dficits fiscales que, dado que el Banco Central careca de autonoma, fueron financiados con emisin monetaria. La terrible experiencia de crisis recurrentes en la balanza de pagos, acompaadas de elevadas inflaciones que empobrecieron en muy poco tiempo a millones de mexicanos, forj un amplio consenso social en el pas a favor de que el Banco de Mxico fuese la Institucin dentro del Estado cuyo mandato nico fuese cuidar el poder adquisitivo de la moneda. Para lograrlo, y esta conviccin fue clave en dicho consenso social, era preciso que tal Institucin fuese autnoma, de tal forma que nadie pudiese obligarla a otorgar financiamiento al Estado o a alguien ms, en detrimento de su mandato. As se forj, en los aos 1993 y 1994, una de las reformas estructurales del Mxico contemporneo ms exitosas y ejemplares: la del otorgamiento de la autonoma constitucional 7 al Banco de Mxico. La esencia de dicha autonoma es precisamente la prohibicin expresa a que el Banco Central le otorgue financiamiento al gobierno. El beneficiario directo de esa autonoma es la sociedad, los usuarios de la moneda nacional. Y el resultado final de dicha autonoma es que el Banco de Mxico cuenta con todo el instrumental de poltica monetaria para lograr una inflacin baja y estable, como en efecto ha sucedido. Hoy tenemos una inflacin anual de 2.52 por ciento, la ms baja en Mxico desde que se miden a nivel nacional los movimientos de los precios al consumidor. En diciembre de 1995, cuando apenas tena un ao de haber entrado en vigor la autonoma del Banco de Mxico, la inflacin anual fue ms de 25 veces que la de ahora, como resultado de la crisis de balanza de pagos que estall en diciembre de 1994 y que hizo que abandonramos una poltica de tipo de cambio semifijo, de bandas de flotacin preestablecidas. 8 Gracias a la inflacin baja y estable de la que hoy gozamos, las tasas de inters tambin estn en los niveles ms bajos de la historia, hay una amplia oferta de crditos para personas y empresas a tasas fijas, a plazos largos y en pesos; lo mismo para el ahorro de las familias que para la inversin de las empresas, el horizonte de planeacin se ha extendido a dcadas, brindando certidumbre. Todo esto incide en un crecimiento de los salarios reales y protege el poder adquisitivo de jubilados y pensionados. A su vez, estimula  junto con un entorno de mayor competencia- que la productividad sea la palanca para generar utilidades, y no el clculo especulativo en funcin de las alzas desalineadas de precios caractersticas de los perodos de alta inflacin. Tambin, gracias al efectivo anclaje de la inflacin, los ingresos de las familias mexicanas han conservado su poder de compra aun en medio de un entorno financiero global de gran volatilidad. 9 Todos estos resultados dejan ms que claro que la persecucin de una inflacin baja y estable no est reida con un mayor crecimiento econmico. Todo lo contrario. Una inflacin baja y estable es condicin necesaria, ms no suficiente, para tener una actividad econmica acelerada y sostenible, ms empleos bien remunerados y un mayor bienestar para toda la poblacin. Es de justicia reconocer que el Presidente Enrique Pea Nieto ha sido claramente respetuoso de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico en todos sus sentidos. Incluso, debe advertirse, que, como parte del paquete fiscal para 2016 que su Gobierno ha sometido a la consideracin del Congreso, contempla una iniciativa para incluir en la Ley de Presupuesto y Responsabilidad Hacendaria la obligacin de que la mayor parte, cuando menos el 70 por ciento, de los remanentes de operacin que en su caso genere el Banco de Mxico y que 10 por mandato de ley entregue al Gobierno Federal, ste los destine a la reduccin de la deuda pblica. Esta iniciativa, a mi juicio, es una clara demostracin de la conviccin del gobierno del Presidente Pea Nieto de que las entregas que el Banco de Mxico, en su caso, haga al Gobierno Federal de sus remanentes de operacin, se destinen a fines que se apeguen lo ms posible al espritu de la autonoma del Banco Central, y por supuesto a fortalecer la estabilidad macroeconmica. Hacia adelante, la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico se ha comprometido en procurar la permanencia del logro de una inflacin baja y estable. Particularmente en estos tiempos de gran volatilidad e incertidumbre en los mercados financieros internacionales hemos sealado en nuestros comunicados que en caso de requerirse, actuaremos con toda flexibilidad y oportunamente para consolidar la convergencia de la inflacin al objetivo de 3 por ciento. 11 * * * Ahora bien, tal vez haya quien se pregunte por qu estamos realizando esta celebracin de los primeros 90 aos de vida del Banco de Mxico aqu. La razn es que en estos terrenos se construir la segunda fbrica de billetes del Banco. Aprovechando la honrosa presencia del seor Presidente de la Repblica, develaremos una placa alusiva que quedar como testimonio del inicio de los trabajos de construccin de esta nueva fbrica de billetes, en el pujante Estado de Jalisco. Hoy da la fbrica de billetes establecida en 1969 en la Ciudad de Mxico est cerca de su lmite de capacidad mxima de produccin, dado que la demanda de billetes del pblico ha crecido notablemente, a causa desde luego del crecimiento tanto de la poblacin como de la economa y, desde luego, por la misma estabilidad de precios. En el perodo que va de enero de 2001 a diciembre de 2014 el nmero de billetes en circulacin (medido en piezas, independientemente de su 12 denominacin) ha registrado una tasa de crecimiento anual promedio de 7.5 por ciento. Ante esta realidad, el Banco de Mxico debe estar preparado, ya que no puede fallar en su tarea de proveer a la sociedad del efectivo que demande, ms aun si consideramos que al atender esa demanda no se crean presiones inflacionarias. Sera impensable que en el mediano y largo plazos el Banco no est en posibilidad de responder oportunamente a las demandas de la sociedad de este medio de pago especfico que son los billetes. Se estima que la construccin de esta fbrica durar 24 meses y se prev que el inicio de operaciones sea entre noviembre de 2017 y febrero de 2018. La inversin total, sufragada desde luego con recursos del Banco dada su autonoma presupuestal, se estima en aproximadamente tres mil millones de pesos, de los cuales cerca de mil millones corresponden a la construccin del 13 edificio y alrededor de dos mil millones de pesos al equipamiento y puesta en operacin de la fbrica. Un testigo social, de honorabilidad intachable, nos acompaar en todo el proceso de esta obra. Es, repito, una inversin para estar en condiciones de satisfacer la demanda de billetes que har la sociedad en los prximos aos, por lo cual no ser inflacionaria. Por lo que ya he dicho respecto de la esencia de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico, de ningn modo ser una fbrica de billetes para financiar al gobierno. * * * Tambin nos enorgullece compartir este evento con el entraable ejrcito nacional mexicano y, especficamente, con la Fuerza Area Mexicana, que cumple sus primeros cien aos de vida. Con este motivo hoy empezar a circular una moneda conmemorativa de 20 pesos que da honor y reconocimiento a la Fuerza Area Mexicana en su centenario. Esta moneda fue 14 aprobada por el H. Congreso de la Unin, su diseo surgi a propuesta de la Secretara de la Defensa Nacional y fue acuada por la Casa de Moneda de Mxico. Debo mencionar tambin, y para reiterar la histrica y armoniosa relacin de nuestras fuerzas armadas con el Banco de Mxico, que la Unidad de Transportes Areos del propio Banco, inici operaciones en 1947 gracias en gran medida a la iniciativa y apoyo de la Fuerza Area Mexicana. Para la creacin de esta Unidad de Transportes Areos fueron decisivas las gestiones del capitn de la Fuerza Area Mexicana, Radams Gaxiola Andrade, quien antes estuvo al mando del glorioso escuadrn 201 que particip en la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Muchas felicidades a la Fuerza Area Mexicana por su centenario y por la moneda conmemorativa que hoy empezar a circular; habr quien desee atesorarla por su significado, pero tambin, como todas las dems monedas conmemorativas de 15 20 pesos, servir sin limitacin alguna como medio de pago en cualquier tipo de operaciones. * * * Seor Presidente: No quiero terminar sin hacer mencin de que, ante el difcil entorno generado por la crisis econmica global que enfrentamos desde 2008, su gobierno ha sentado las bases para que Mxico sea uno de los pocos pases en el mundo que pueda ofrecer simultneamente dos factores que parecen ser elusivos: estabilidad macroeconmica junto con el potencial de un crecimiento sostenido y acelerado. La responsabilidad en el manejo de las polticas fiscal, financiera y monetaria genera la estabilidad, en tanto que las reformas estructurales estn permitiendo que contemos con el potencial para crecer de forma acelerada y cada vez con mayor equidad. Muchas gracias. 16

Title: Thanks to the recognition of his career granted by the Board of Directors of the Mexican Institute of Finance Executives (IMEF)
text: Words of the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, to thank the recognition of his career granted by the Board of Directors of the Mexican Institute of Finance Executives (IMEF). Friday, March 23, 2012  Mr. Accountant Jose Antonio Quesada Palacios, President of the National Board of Directors of the IMEF.  Mr. Contador Daniel Calleja Pineda, President of IMEF Mexico City  Mr. Accountant Javier Soni Ocampo, Managing Partner Pricewaterhouse Coopers, PwC  Mr. Alberto Espinosa Desigaud, President of the Employers' Confederation of the Mexican Republic (Coparmex) and former President of the National Board of Directors of the IMEF.  Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, I thank the IMEF and its President, Jose Antonio Quesada, for this recognition that, in justice and without false modesty, should be extended to many Mexicans who, for decades, have struggled, against all odds, to consolidate the macroeconomic stability that we enjoy today. In particular, I would like this recognition that you kindly grant me today to be considered addressed to all those who form and have formed, to the 1 long of more than eight decades, the Bank of Mexico. An institution that today is, for most Mexicans, synonymous with trust and solidity. A crucial element of the design that was given to the current Bank of Mexico along with its autonomy, in April 1994, is the constitutional mandate that establishes as a priority mission of the Bank to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency. I do not think it necessary to commend to you, experts in finance, the decisive nature of this mandate for the healthy development of the economy and for the well-being of individuals, families and companies. It is worth mentioning that today we have well-behaved inflation, below 4 percent per year; that core inflation has been lower in Mexico for several of the recent months than that registered in the United States and, as a background and concurrent cause to achieve these results, that inflation expectations in the markets, among analysts and in the general public increasingly seem more solidly anchored and aligned with the permanent objective of the Bank of Mexico. We all know that stability is a prerequisite for economic growth, but we also know that it is not a sufficient condition. Along with stability, accelerated and sustained economic growth requires an institutional scaffolding that fosters the productivity of all the factors that concur in economic activity. To this scaffolding we refer precisely when we talk about the much-talked about structural reforms that the country requires: starting with the labor reform and the educational reform, going through the reforms in the 2 Telecommunications and energy matters, as well as the reform that makes our agricultural activities more competitive and raises the standard of living of those who live in the countryside and, of course, I am also referring to the necessary reform to strengthen the rule of law, promote respect for property rights and guarantee the fulfillment of contracts in all cases and at all levels. These great transformations, which we must see with a sense of urgency, will allow Mexico to obtain all the benefit that derives from an environment of economic stability. It would be a terrible mistake to consider that economic stability is a conquest that once achieved is preserved by mere inertia. That is not the case. This is an ongoing task. Hence, the Bank of Mexico, starting with its Governing Board, monitors day by day the evolution of numerous economic variables and scrutinizes in detail the behavior of national and global markets to attend and counteract in a timely manner any threat to price stability. We cannot afford to put it at risk, distracting ourselves in tasks of another nature, not even in tasks that seem seductively noble and desirable in terms of growth, but which, by strict logic, correspond to other areas of the State or society. History and life itself teach us that whoever proposes two or more priorities at the same time, in fact ends up not having any priority and losing the compass that gave direction and credibility to their actions. 3 Well understood, the autonomy of the Central Bank is a necessity that derives from its priority objective. Autonomy is not a privilege of those of us who work in the Bank of Mexico, nor is it an itch for the Central Institute to single out before the government. Autonomy is, above all, a guarantee for each and every user of the national currency that the Bank of Mexico will not violate the purchasing power of that currency, for example by financing government spending with the creation of means of payment. That is why the Bank of Mexico Law expressly prohibits this practice that, despite sometimes presenting itself as a seductive temptation, has proven to be a source of countless and serious damages to the country's economy. The importance of the Bank's autonomy, crystallized in the constitutional reforms of 1994, was always a desire of the founders of the Institution since 1925. Being, as it is, a guarantee for all users of the national currency, autonomy also obliges the Bank of Mexico to be an example of transparency and clarity in its monetary policy decisions. Therefore, in 2011 we decided to join a handful of central banks in the world that publish punctually the minutes that explain in detail the background, reasoning and forecasts that the Governing Board weighs to define its monetary policy stance. 4 This allows market trainers, investors, companies, analysts and researchers and the general public to know in a timely manner and in detail what the Bank is doing to take care of the purchasing power of the currency and to know why the Bank decided to do what it does. You, as finance executives, know like few others the importance of having reliable, sufficient and timely information to make sound decisions. Among the accumulation of pertinent information that the Bank of Mexico disseminates, I will take just one other example - in addition to the minutes - which may be particularly interesting: Every week, the Bank publishes its Consolidated Statement of Accounts in an executive format. A careful reading of this information allows not only to know the amount of the Bank's international reserves - which constitute the majority of its assets - or the amount of banknotes and coins in circulation - which make up most of its liabilities - but also to have an accurate idea of where such reserves come from (for example, of the sale of dollars that Pemex makes to the Bank of Mexico to obtain the national currency that allows the oil company to operate in Mexico and comply with its tax obligations). The Bank's Statement of Accounts also gives us weekly timely information on the open market operations carried out by the Bank, for example, to neutralize excess liquidity or to soften the effects of cyclical fluctuations that usually occur in the financial markets. 5 These operations are nothing more than a daily, consistent and practical, instrumental expression of the monetary policy stance established by the Bank's Governing Board. Since its foundation, banco de Mexico has placed particular emphasis on being an exemplary institution in terms of the accuracy and relevance of its own accounting information. It cannot be otherwise, given the eminently public nature that an issuing bank must have and due to the importance that such information has for the evolution of the national economy. That is why the Bank, since its inception, has approached the most competent professionals in financial and accounting information, to collaborate directly or indirectly with the Institution or to be, for example, its external auditors. Tonight, I am pleased on behalf of Banco de Mexico to make a kind of recognition to Mexican finance executives, yesterday and today. To the accounting information professionals who have always been so close to the Central Bank, giving them a facsimile reproduction of the balance sheet of the Bank of Mexico of 1930. This document goes beyond the historical anecdote, revealing punctually the fruitful collaboration and complementarity that has occurred in Mexico, for decades, between experts in expressing and interpreting financial and accounting information and the Central Bank. 6 You will notice that the bank's external auditor on this 1930 balance sheet was none other than Mr. Roberto Casas Alatriste, who has been rightly described as a key figure in the development of Mexico in the twentieth century. Don Roberto accompanied and supported the tasks of the Bank of Mexico for many years. Together with Manuel Gomez Morin he participated in the Liquidation Committee of the old banks of issue, a task in which his dedication and good judgment shone. Don Roberto was also a prominent part of the founding group of the Banking School of the Bank of Mexico on March 10, 1929, aimed at training and training the employees of the Central Institute. Later, this school would be replaced by the Banking and Commercial School, a fertile training quarry for hundreds of current and retired employees of the Bank of Mexico. For me it is an honor to be recognized by an institution like the IMEF that, I have no doubt, keeps alive the mood and willingness to serve Mexico that characterized characters such as Mr. Roberto Casas Alatriste (who, by the way, was also founder of what is now in Mexico Pricewaterhouse Coopers, PwC), and many other professionals and experts in financial and accounting information. All of them, dear colleagues of the Central Bank throughout many decades of fruitful work for Mexico. Thank you very much. 7
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, al agradecer el reconocimiento a su trayectoria que le otorg el Consejo Directivo del Instituto Mexicano de Ejecutivos de Finanzas (IMEF). Viernes 23 de marzo de 2012  Seor Contador Jos Antonio Quesada Palacios, Presidente del Consejo Directivo Nacional del IMEF.  Seor Contador Daniel Calleja Pineda, Presidente del IMEF Ciudad de Mxico  Seor Contador Javier Soni Ocampo, Socio Director Pricewaterhouse Coopers, PwC  Seor Licenciado Alberto Espinosa Desigaud, Presidente de la Confederacin Patronal de la Repblica Mexicana (Coparmex) y ex presidente del Consejo Directivo Nacional del IMEF.  Seoras y seores: Antes que nada agradezco al IMEF y a su Presidente, Jos Antonio Quesada, este reconocimiento que, en justicia y sin falsa modestia, debiera extenderse a muchos mexicanos que, durante dcadas, han pugnado, contra viento y marea, por consolidar la estabilidad macroeconmica que hoy disfrutamos. En particular deseara que este reconocimiento que hoy amablemente me otorgan se considerase dirigido a todos los que forman y han formado, a lo 1 largo de ms de ocho dcadas, el Banco de Mxico. Una Institucin que hoy es, para la mayora de los mexicanos, sinnimo de confianza y de solidez. Un elemento crucial del diseo que se le dio al actual Banco de Mxico junto con su autonoma, en abril de 1994, es el mandato constitucional que establece como misin prioritaria del Banco procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda. No creo necesario encomiar ante ustedes, expertos en finanzas, el carcter decisivo que tiene este mandato para el sano desenvolvimiento de la economa y para el bienestar de personas, familias y empresas. Vale la pena mencionar que hoy tenemos una inflacin bien comportada, por debajo del 4 por ciento anual; que la inflacin subyacente ha sido en Mxico durante varios de los meses recientes menor a la registrada en los Estados Unidos y, como trasfondo y causa concurrente para lograr estos resultados, que las expectativas de inflacin en los mercados, entre los analistas y en el pblico en general cada vez parecen ms slidamente ancladas y alineadas con el objetivo permanente del Banco de Mxico. Todos sabemos que la estabilidad es condicin indispensable para el crecimiento econmico, pero tambin sabemos que no es una condicin suficiente. Junto con la estabilidad, el crecimiento econmico acelerado y sostenido requiere de un andamiaje institucional que propicie la productividad de todos los factores que concurren en la actividad econmica. A ese andamiaje precisamente nos referimos cuando hablamos de las tan comentadas reformas estructurales que el pas requiere: empezando por la reforma laboral y la reforma educativa, pasando por las reformas en los 2 terrenos de las telecomunicaciones y de los energticos, as como la reforma que haga a nuestras actividades agropecuarias ms competitivas y eleve el nivel de vida de quienes viven en el campo y, por supuesto, me refiero tambin a la necesaria reforma para fortalecer el estado de Derecho, fomentar el respeto a los derechos de propiedad y garantizar el cumplimiento de los contratos en todos los casos y en todos los rdenes. Estas grandes transformaciones, que debemos ver con sentido de urgencia, permitirn que Mxico obtenga todo el provecho que se deriva de un entorno de estabilidad econmica. Sera un terrible error considerar que la estabilidad econmica es una conquista que una vez alcanzada se conserva por mera inercia. No es as. Se trata de una tarea permanente. De ah que el Banco de Mxico, empezando por su Junta de Gobierno, vigile da con da la evolucin de numerosas variables econmicas y escudrie con detalle el comportamiento de los mercados nacionales y globales para atender y contrarrestar oportunamente cualquier amenaza a la estabilidad de precios. No podemos darnos el lujo de ponerla en riesgo, distrayndonos en tareas de otra naturaleza, ni siquiera en tareas que parezcan seductoramente nobles y deseables en trminos de crecimiento, pero que, por estricta lgica, corresponden a otras reas del Estado o de la sociedad. La historia y la vida misma nos ensean que quien se propone dos o ms prioridades a la vez, en los hechos termina por no tener prioridad alguna y por perder la brjula que le daba direccin y credibilidad a sus acciones. 3 Bien entendida, la autonoma del Banco Central es una necesidad que se deriva de su objetivo prioritario. La autonoma no es un privilegio de quienes trabajamos en el Banco de Mxico ni es un prurito del Instituto Central para singularizarse ante al gobierno. La autonoma es, ante todo, una garanta para todos y cada uno de los usuarios de la moneda nacional de que el Banco de Mxico no vulnerar el poder adquisitivo de esa moneda, por ejemplo financiando el gasto gubernamental con la creacin de medios de pago. Es por ello que la Ley del Banco de Mxico prohbe expresamente esa prctica que, a pesar de presentarse en ocasiones como una seductora tentacin, ha probado ser fuente de incontables y graves daos a la economa del pas. La importancia de la autonoma del Banco, cristalizada en las reformas constitucionales de 1994, fue siempre un anhelo de los fundadores de la Institucin desde 1925. Tratndose, como se trata, de una garanta para todos los usuarios de la moneda nacional, la autonoma obliga tambin al Banco de Mxico a ser ejemplo de transparencia y de claridad en sus decisiones de poltica monetaria. Por eso, en 2011 decidimos sumarnos a un puado de bancos centrales en el mundo que publican puntualmente las minutas que explican a detalle los antecedentes, los razonamientos y las previsiones que sopesa la Junta de Gobierno para definir su postura de poltica monetaria. 4 Ello permite a los formadores de los mercados, a los inversionistas, a las empresas, a los analistas e investigadores y al pblico en general, conocer oportunamente y a detalle qu est haciendo el Banco para cuidar el poder adquisitivo de la moneda y saber por qu el Banco decidi hacer lo que hace. Ustedes, como ejecutivos de finanzas, conocen como pocos la importancia de contar con informacin confiable, suficiente y oportuna para tomar decisiones acertadas. De entre el cmulo de informacin pertinente que el Banco de Mxico difunde tomar slo otro ejemplo  adems del de las minutas  que puede ser particularmente interesante: Cada semana, el Banco publica en un formato ejecutivo su Estado de Cuenta Consolidado. Una lectura atenta de esa informacin permite no slo conocer el monto de las reservas internacionales del Banco  que constituyen la mayor parte de su activo  o el monto de los billetes y monedas en circulacin  que conforman la mayor parte de su pasivo- sino tambin tener una idea precisa de dnde provienen tales reservas (por ejemplo, de la venta de dlares que Pemex le hace al Banco de Mxico para obtener la moneda nacional que le permite a la empresa petrolera operar en Mxico y cumplir con sus obligaciones tributarias). El Estado de Cuenta del Banco nos da tambin cada semana informacin puntual de las operaciones de mercado abierto llevadas a cabo por el Banco, por ejemplo, para neutralizar un exceso de liquidez o para suavizar los efectos de oscilaciones cclicas que suelen presentarse en los mercados financieros. 5 Esas operaciones no son otra cosa que una expresin cotidiana, congruente y prctica, instrumental, de la postura de poltica monetaria establecida por la Junta de Gobierno del Banco. Desde su fundacin el Banco de Mxico le ha dado particular nfasis a ser una institucin ejemplar en lo que hace a la precisin y pertinencia de su propia informacin contable. No puede ser de otra manera, dado el carcter eminentemente pblico que debe tener un banco emisor y debido a la trascendencia que dicha informacin tiene para la evolucin de la economa nacional. Por eso el Banco, desde sus orgenes, se ha acercado a los ms competentes profesionales de la informacin financiera y contable, para que colaboren directa o indirectamente con la Institucin o para que sean, por ejemplo, sus auditores externos. Esta noche, me complace a nombre de Banco de Mxico hacer una suerte de reconocimiento a los ejecutivos de finanzas mexicanos, de ayer y de hoy. A los profesionales de la informacin contable que tan cercanos han sido siempre al Banco Central, entregndoles una reproduccin facsimilar del balance del Banco de Mxico de 1930. Este documento va ms all de la ancdota histrica, revela puntualmente la fructfera colaboracin y complementacin que se ha dado en Mxico, por dcadas, entre los expertos en expresar e interpretar la informacin financiera y contable y el Banco Central. 6 Notarn que el auditor externo del Banco en este balance de 1930 fue nada menos que don Roberto Casas Alatriste, a quien se ha calificado, con toda justicia, como un personaje clave del desarrollo de Mxico en el siglo XX. Don Roberto acompa y apoy las tareas del Banco de Mxico durante muchos aos. Junto con Manuel Gmez Morn particip en el Comit Liquidador de los antiguos bancos de emisin, tarea en la que brillaron su dedicacin y su buen juicio. Don Roberto tambin form parte destacada del grupo fundador de la Escuela Bancaria del Banco de Mxico el 10 de marzo de 1929, dirigida a formar y capacitar a los empleados del Instituto Central. Ms tarde, esta escuela sera sustituida por la Escuela Bancaria y Comercial, fecunda cantera de formacin para cientos de empleados, actuales y jubilados, del Banco de Mxico. Para m es un honor ser reconocido por una institucin como el IMEF que, no me cabe duda, mantiene vivo el talante y la disposicin de servicio a Mxico que caracteriz a personajes como don Roberto Casas Alatriste (quien, por cierto, fue tambin fundador de lo que hoy es en Mxico Pricewaterhouse Coopers, PwC), y a muchos otros profesionales y expertos de la informacin financiera y contable. Todos ellos, compaeros entraables del Banco Central a lo largo de muchas dcadas de trabajo fructfero para Mxico. Muchas gracias. 7

Title: CFI-UNSGSA workshop: balancing financial inclusion & exclusion in AI-driven DFS
Subtitle: Remarks by Alejandro Daz de Len, Governor of Banco de Mxico at the CFI-UNSGSA Workshop:
text: Remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of Banco de Mexico at the CFI-UNSGSA Workshop: Balancing Financial Inclusion & Exclusion in AI-Driven DFS.1 3 December 2021  Technological change and digitization present a huge opportunity to expand financial inclusion. The first dimension has been about access to financial services and the second is related to better pricing (from credit bureaus to behavioral bureaus).  Adopting new technologies should go hand in hand with safeguarding consumer protection, which underpins trust.
