Title: Presentation of the book Foreign exchange intervention in inflation targeters in Latin America
text: Remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of Banco de Mexico, at the presentation of the book Foreign Exchange Intervention in Inflation Targeters in Latin America Mexico City, March 8th 2019 Good morning, everyone. On behalf of Banco de Mexico, I am pleased to welcome the IMF delegation, especially of David Lipton, First Deputy Managing Director and Alejandro Werner, Director of the Western Hemisphere Department, as well as this distinguished group of experts and authorities, that includes Jose de Gregorio former governor of Banco Central de Chile and Alexandre Tombini former governor of Banco Central de Brasil, who all have met today to present the book Foreign Exchange Intervention in Inflation Targeters in Latin America. For Banco de Mexico, it is an honor to host this event. The book that is being presented today is a valuable analytical and empirical effort, divided into two sections. The first section outlines a theoretical framework and a comparative study on Foreign Exchange (FX) intervention in some Latin American economies which have adopted an Inflation Targeting (IT) regime. The second section presents detailed case studies from seven countries, including Mexico (Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Mexico, Peru and Uruguay). The book offers a comprehensive overview of this issue and is useful for policy makers, market participants and academics. From a historical perspective, when societies went from using money with intrinsic value to fiat money, adopting the right monetary standard was crucial to preserve peoples confidence in the functions of money as a deposit of value, as a unit of account and as a mean of exchange. At that time, monetary standards were mainly based on the direct or indirect convertibility of the currency into a merchandise of intrinsic value, such as gold. This was the prevailing standard during the nineteenth and a large part of the twentieth century, until 1971, when the U.S. suspended the convertibility of the dollar into gold. Thus, the US dollar began fluctuating with respect to other currencies, and other major advanced economies also shifted to more flexible exchange rates. 2 In the case of emerging market economies (EMEs), authorities continued with a fixed exchange rate with respect to the US dollar. However, in many cases, macroeconomic mismanagement led to unsustainable external imbalances that ended in currency crises. During the 1990s, several emerging markets, faced currency crisis and a depletion of international reserves, forcing in several cases the adoption of a floating exchange rate regime with a monetary anchor that gradually moved towards the adoption of an inflation targeting regime. In that process, Latin American economies adopted different FX intervention strategies that have been updated in the last years. This book presents the strategies and operational tactics that were being followed and raises very important questions. For example, what motivates FX interventions? What are the strategies and levels of transparency of FX interventions? How effective have FX interventions been? I would like to talk briefly about the adoption and results of the floating exchange regime and the IT framework in Mexico. After the crisis of 199495, Banco de Mexico was forced to adopt a flexible exchange rate regime. 3 The central bank faced two main challenges. First, we had to adopt a new nominal anchor, instead of the exchange rate, and, second, we needed to develop a deep and liquid FX market with an efficient price discovery process. As to the first challenge, that is, replacing the exchange rate as the nominal anchor of the economy, inflation targets began to be the new anchor for economic agents expectations, a condition that gradually led to the full adoption of IT. To develop a deep and liquid foreign exchange market, Banco de Mexico needed to make significant adjustments to the regulatory framework. For instance: 1. A full convertibility of the Mexican peso was adopted, even today the peso is one of the few fully convertible EM currencies. 2. A derivatives market was developed, providing market participants the possibility to hedge against exchange rate fluctuations, which is essential to manage FX risks. 3. Regulation was strengthened to avoid the dollarization of the financial system, to reduce currency mismatches and tail risks. In this regard, 4 bank accounts in foreign currency are only available for corporations, foreign government representations, and citizens living at the border. Also, banks net long-short FX exposures were limited, currently those limits are of 15% of their capital and long term dollar loans required long term financing. 4. In 2008, the Mexican peso has been included in the Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) system, allowing the currency to trade every day on a 24-hr basis. As a result of all of these actions, the Mexican foreign exchange market has become one of the most liquid and deep markets among emerging economies. According to the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), the Mexican peso is the second most traded currency among emerging countries, just below the Chinese renminbi. The daily turnover of the Mexican peso is 112 billion US dollars (including both spot and derivatives markets) and most of the volume is traded abroad. In fact, only 20% of the volume is traded with at least one Mexican counterparty. This means that, today, the Mexican peso is more a global than a local currency. 5 In an exchange market like the one I described, there is a lesser need for FX interventions. Since the adoption of a flexible exchange rate regime, Mexicos FX Commission (which includes the Ministry of Finance and Banco de Mexico), fully committed with the regime and avoided giving signals about desired levels for the exchange rate, and defined two clear goals for FX interventions. First, to adjust the pace of foreign reserve accumulation under preannounced rule-based mechanisms in order to achieve a desired stock. Second, to provide liquidity in high volatility episodes where the price discovery process could be compromised. The most important principle is that interventions do not aim at a particular level of the exchange rate. An overall assessment of the effectiveness of these type of interventions is hard to obtain; however, FX interventions have contributed to attain its objectives, both on the international reserve management component and to promote better FX market conditions during episodes of stress. The path to development followed by many emerging markets implies the consolidation of an open economy, both in terms of trade and capital flows. 6 Having an open capital account requires the continuous adoption of sound macroeconomic measures, in which a strong monetary policy anchor (such as the IT framework) and a market-based flexible exchange rate play a key role. In order for these measures to be effective, it is crucial to: i) develop a deep and liquid foreign exchange market, with a strong investor base (both domestic and external); ii) build a strong financial and corporate FX resilience; and iii) consider FX interventions and capital flow management measures as exceptions. Before I conclude, I would like to share some reflections on Mexicos macroeconomic response to a recent sequence of shocks. In the case of small and open emerging market economies, authorities may implement the so called "leaning against the wind interventions". That is, in the presence of transitory shocks that either lead to an appreciation or depreciation of the currency, authorities intervene against the direction in which the currency is moving. However, this assumes that authorities can identify in real time the nature of the shocks, whether transitory or permanent. In the presence of shocks 7 of the latter type, policy actions should facilitate rather than impede the real exchange rate adjustment and the consequent change in relative prices. In Mexico, during the last years the economy has faced a sequence of adverse and persistent shocks, which led to a tighter external financing constraint. It was necessary to adjust the current account deficit to the lower availability of foreign financial resources and to cope with other structural changes in the external accounts (passing from a large oil trade surplus to a large oil trade deficit). These required a significant real exchange rate depreciation. In order to contribute to an orderly adjustment of the economy, the macroeconomic policy response involved strengthening public finances and tightening monetary policy. If macroeconomic policy had not been adjusted, inflation would have been significantly higher and economic growth would have been lower than observed. Ladies and gentlemen: Banco de Mexico has gladly joined other central banks in this effort led by the IMF to promote a better understanding of FX interventions in Latin 8 America. This comparative study provides valuable information on the decision making processes involving FX interventions and on the best way of bringing into line such interventions with the transparency and credibility of the IT framework. I am sure that in the following presentations more policy lessons can be derived. It is a great honor for Banco de Mexico to host this meeting as a continuation of our long-standing collaboration with the IMF to disseminate new ideas and policy references on a wide range of issues. Thank you very much and, once more, welcome to Banco de Mexico. 9

Title: Challenges for the Mexican economy in a complex external environment
text: "CHALLENGES FOR THE MEXICAN ECONOMY IN THE FACE OF A COMPLEX EXTERNAL ENVIRONMENT". REMARKS BY MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, AT THE 7TH INFORMATIVE BREAKFAST OF COPARMEX 2015. Queretaro, Queretaro, June 30, 2015.1 I would like first of all to thank the Board of Directors of COPARMEX Queretaro, for the invitation to participate in this seventh Informative Breakfast of the Confederation. In addition to allowing me to discuss with you issues of great relevance to our country, this visit has given me the opportunity to enjoy again the charms of this beautiful city. I would like to take this opportunity to address some of the challenges facing the Mexican economy, both in the short and long term, in a complicated international environment. Like other emerging economies, Mexico has been hit by a combination of external shocks in recent months. The first of these stems from the decline in international oil prices. In the particular case of the Mexican blend, its price registered a drop of more than 60 percent from mid-2014 to the beginning of this year. While crude oil prices have subsequently risen and a gradual recovery is expected in the coming years, the widespread perception is that they will not return for an extended period. 1 The opinions contained in this document are the sole responsibility of the author and do not necessarily coincide with those of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico. 1 to levels such as those reached relatively few months ago. As you know, oil has a modest share of both GDP and our country's exports, but sales for this concept represent about a third of tax revenues, so its recent decline has had a significant impact on public finances. The second external shock relates to the existence of high levels of volatility in international financial markets. This is explained by a variety of factors, such as the difficult situation in Greece, conflicts of a geopolitical nature and, especially, the expectation that, by virtue of the improvement that the US economy has been showing, during the second half of this year an upward cycle of interest rates in that country will begin. Given the persistent weakness of other advanced economies, and especially those of the euro area and Japan, the central banks of these economies are expected to maintain very low interest rates for an extended period. The consequent divergence in the monetary conditions of the main advanced economies has led to capital movements between them with the consequent effect on their exchange rates, which has contributed to accentuate the nervousness in the markets. A third shock that has hit emerging economies stems from the slowdown in global economic activity. In this case, the characteristics of our country's trade links have allowed the impact to be of a smaller magnitude than in other emerging economies. Suffice it to recall that about 80 percent of the 2 Mexican merchandise exports are directed to the United States, and that global economic activity is currently characterized by a slowdown in the Chinese economy, a still considerable weakness of the economies of the eurozone and Japan, and a relative strengthening of those of the United States and the United Kingdom. In addition to these external shocks, the Mexican economy has been affected by the fall in oil production. During the period 2004-2014, crude oil production in our country registered a cumulative contraction of almost 30 percent. In addition, an additional reduction is expected for 2015, which could even be accentuated as a result of the accidents on the coasts of Campeche that occurred in recent months. The policy response adopted by the Mexican authorities to these clashes has had three components. First, it has been announced that federal public spending, both in 2015 and 2016, will be downward adjusted for amounts equivalent to 0.7 percent of GDP. This is intended to compensate for lower revenues from the sale of oil and ensure the strength of public finances. Second, the implementation of monetary policy has been focused on achieving the convergence of headline inflation to the permanent target of 3 percent. In this regard, it should be noted that the annual growth rate of consumer prices has been around this target during 2015, and that inflation records for both May and the first half of June show figures even below 3 percent. It is worth noting that a 3 The trajectory of inflation such as that observed throughout this year has no historical precedent in Mexico. Finally, the Foreign Exchange Commission, composed of representatives of the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Mexico, has been implementing, on the basis of previously announced rules, measures aimed at providing additional liquidity to the foreign exchange market, in order to mitigate the volatility of the international price of our currency. As a result of the difficult external environment, like the currencies of other emerging economies, the peso's exchange rate against the dollar has weakened significantly in recent months, having accumulated from September 2014 to the end of June 2015 a depreciation of around 20 percent. However, the actions implemented have allowed such an adjustment to take place in an orderly manner. Thus, the volatility of the peso's exchange rate has been located at levels that compare favorably with those observed in other emerging economies. Domestic interest rates have also shown moderate increases, while the level of sovereign credit risk indicators is below those of most emerging economies. Let me elaborate on the challenges that monetary policy will have to face in the coming months. The implementation of monetary policy in Mexico rests on four pillars. The first of these is the autonomy of the central bank, an attribute that 4 our Central Institute acquired in 1994, in what undoubtedly represents one of the most important institutional reforms in the recent history of Mexico. The second pillar, erected in 2001, is an inflation targeting scheme for the conduct of monetary policy, which has among its central elements a permanent objective for the inflation rate,2 as well as a systematic assessment of price determinants based on a wide range of variables and tools. Thirdly, the search for an efficient convergence of inflation to the target, that is, at the lowest possible cost in terms of economic activity. And fourth, a strict commitment to transparency and accountability. This monetary policy approach, together with the strengthening of public finances, have allowed a substantial decrease in the inflation rate. Since the beginning of this century, both headline and core inflation have shown a downward trend, reaching, as already mentioned, the target of 3 percent during 2015. It should be noted that progress in the fight against inflation goes far beyond the decline in the rate of price growth. In particular, as a result of the efforts made, the pricing mechanisms in the economy have shown structural change. In this regard, it is worth noting, for example, the drastic fall in the transfer of depreciations from the exchange rate to inflation, as well as a much lower response of inflation expectations and their dispersion to different types of shocks. In this context, 2 It should be remembered that there is a variability range of /- 1 percent around the permanent target of 3 percent. 5 it is not surprising that the exchange rate depreciation of recent months has coexisted with a decline in inflation, nor that various supply shocks - such as the tax changes of 2014 or the increases frequently shown by the prices of agricultural products - only temporarily affect inflation, without giving rise to second-order effects. By virtue of these results, the credibility of monetary policy has been strengthened. This has made it possible to reduce inflation, in the context of a considerable fall in interest rates. From March 2013 to June 2014, the benchmark interest rate for the conduct of monetary policy fell by 150 percentage points, to its lowest level on record, remaining constant ever since. A handling of monetary policy of this nature would have been unthinkable a few years ago. Undoubtedly, the main challenge for monetary policy in the current situation is to consolidate the progress made in reducing inflation. What are the risks faced in this regard? To answer this question, it is necessary to consider, first of all, that despite the gradual strengthening of our economy, it still presents a high degree of slack. This is clearly reflected in the unemployment rate, which although it has shown a downward trend in recent months, continues to register figures higher than those prior to the global financial crisis, as well as in the fact that there are no pressures in credit markets, in the external sector or wages. In fact, the calculations 6 of the output gap (that is, of the difference between the observed GDP and that which can be achieved without generating inflationary pressures) show a negative figure that allows to rule out demand pressures on prices in the coming months. In addition to the above, as already noted, supply shocks, although frequent, have been shown to have a only temporary impact on prices, without translating into upward adjustments in medium- and long-term inflation expectations. In a context of the absence of inflationary pressures on the demand side, as well as a transitory impact of supply shocks on prices, the process of normalization of monetary policy in the United States probably represents the main source of risk for inflation in Mexico in the coming months. This is due to its potential effect on volatility in financial markets and capital flows to our country and, consequently, on the exchange rate of the peso against the dollar. While, as explained above, the transfer from the exchange rate to inflation is currently very low, the risk of a period of turbulence in financial markets leading to pressures on the peso exchange rate and prices cannot be ruled out. It can be argued that the challenges for the Mexican economy arising from the normalization of monetary policy in the United States are accentuated by virtue of the high level of financial openness of our economy and the holdings of government securities in pesos by investors. 7 Foreigners.3 In this regard, the following should be noted: (a) although a greater openness to capital flows implies a greater exposure of our country to episodes of international financial turbulence, long-term benefits of this measure (access to external savings, risk diversification, greater depth of the financial system, etc.) rather than outweigh the risks; b) foreigners' holdings of government bonds in pesos as by one hundred of the total are very similar to the average of the main emerging economies;4 c) in the case of Mexico, these holdings have a nature of the long term, not only for its duration, but for the fact that in its most of them are in the hands of institutional investors, which by their nature makes them more stable;5 d) in recent months a change in the composition of these holdings, from short-term securities to long-term bonds, which supports the conclusion that these investments in most of them are not speculative in nature. In any case, in the face of the imminent tightening of financial conditions Overall, the monetary policy stance in Mexico will have to be adjusted. Without However, the precise timing faces several factors of uncertainty. In 3 The financial openness index constructed by Professors Chinn and Ito, based in turn on information from the International Monetary Fund, gives a rating for Mexico in 2013 on par with economies such as Korea and Chile, and significantly higher than other emerging economies such as Turkey, Brazil, India, China and South Africa. For more details, see The Chinn-Ito Index (latest update available on ). 4 As of June 18, 2015, non-resident holdings of Mexican government securities were equivalent to 30.3 percent of the total outstanding, slightly lower than that observed at the end of April 2015 for the average of a sample of ten emerging economies (Brazil, Hungary, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, Poland, Russia, South Africa, Thailand and Turkey), weighted by the dollar value of non-resident holdings in each country (30.5 per cent). 5 As of March 31, 2015, it was possible to identify an amount equivalent to about 53 percent of the total of these holdings held by institutional investors. No information is available on the composition of the remaining 47 percent, but it is reasonable to assume that a portion of these resources are also in the hands of institutional investors. 8 First, the precise date on which the upward cycle of interest rates in the United States will begin is unknown. Secondly, it is impossible to know in advance to what extent the normalization of monetary policy in that country will affect the peso-dollar parity and other financial variables in Mexico. Finally, there is also uncertainty about when monetary policy actions in the United States will be reflected in these variables. In particular, markets may pre-empt the Federal Reserve's decisions and make adjustments before the federal funds rate target is raised. By virtue of the above, monetary policy must be prepared to respond in a timely and flexible manner to the extent that circumstances so require. There is no doubt that the normalization of monetary policy in the United States poses significant challenges for emerging economies. However, it is possible to affirm, with a reasonable level of confidence, that Mexico is well prepared to face them, and in general to overcome episodes of turbulence in international financial markets regardless of their origin. On the one hand, our country has a solid macroeconomic position, based on prudent monetary and fiscal policies, a moderate current account deficit, a flexible exchange rate that has shown a very efficient operation, and levels of international reserves close to historical highs, in addition to a flexible credit line with the International Monetary Fund for an amount equivalent to almost 70 billion dollars. On the other hand, the system 9 Banking is well capitalized, there are no perceived bubbles in asset prices, and both the financial regulation and supervision scheme and the institutional framework for the coordination of the different authorities responsible for financial stability in the country have been strengthened. In addition, it is important to note that the growth potential of the economy should be strengthened by the recent adoption and implementation of structural change measures in a wide range of sectors. I would now like to make a few comments on economic growth in Mexico from a long-term perspective. The notion that an environment of high inflation is harmful to economic growth has broad support, both empirical and theoretical. However, there is also consensus that achieving low inflation rates on a sustained basis, while indispensable, is not sufficient for an economy to enjoy adequate economic growth rates. Mexico's experience is illustrative in this regard. Despite the significant progress made in combating inflation, the pace of economic growth in our country has continued to register relatively modest figures. There are good reasons to expect a reversal of trend in Mexico's economic growth over the next few years. The productive potential of the economy is already evident in the general evolution of our exports, which has allowed our entrepreneurs to increase significantly. 10 its market share in the U.S. economy, even in the face of competition from economies such as China.6 It particularly highlights the recent and prospective performance of sectors such as automotive and auto parts.7 Naturally, the challenge is to generalize these advances to the rest of the economy. This is precisely the objective of the structural reform process recently undertaken in our country. To get a clearer idea of the importance of the efforts made, it is worth noting that, based on a comparative methodology, the OECD classifies the structural reform measures approved in Mexico during the period 2013-2014, as the most ambitious among its member countries.8 It is also noteworthy that, unlike other economies that also launched important structural change actions in recent years, in the case of Mexico, these were not triggered by a crisis. Economic growth in the coming years should also be supported by favorable demographic conditions, since the expected evolution of our country's population will allow us to benefit from high labor force growth rates in relation to other economies. 6 U.S. imports from Mexico increased from 9.1 percent to 12.9 percent of the total, from July 2005 to April 2015. 7 According to the International Organization of Automobile Manufacturers (OICA), in 2014 Mexico ranked seventh in the world in total vehicle production (including commercial and passenger vehicles). Likewise, the World Trade Organization ranks Mexico as the fourth largest global exporter of automotive products in 2013. In addition, the installed capacity in this industry is expected to increase considerably in the coming years. 8 See Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (2015): OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico, January. 11 Emerging. It is also important to consider that while emerging economies are likely to continue to face a complex global economic situation in the coming years, it is expected that this external environment will be less unfavorable for Mexico. On the one hand, U.S. potential growth has been less affected by the global financial crisis and faces fewer downside risks than those of other major economies, including China and the euro area.9 On the other hand, the low share of raw materials in our total exports could become an additional differentiating factor. given the current context of low international prices for these products and the expectation that they will continue to be depressed in the coming years.10 The implementation of structural reform measures in Mexico has already begun, and some of the expected results of them are already evident. In this regard, they highlight, to cite some examples, the falls in the prices of telecommunications services, reflecting in turn the greater competition in the sector; the broad interest of private companies, both domestic and foreign, in participating in the bidding processes for contracts in the energy sector; and the perception among the private sector that recent changes have resulted in a regulatory framework in the labour sector that is more conducive to investment. The important actions carried out to improve the institutional framework of our country are also noteworthy, including 9 See International Monetary Fund (2015): "Where Are We Headed? Perspectives on Potential Output", Chapter 3, World Economic Outlook, April. 10 The share of raw materials in total merchandise exports is about 15 per cent in Mexico, compared with 86, 85, 82 and 62 per cent in Chile, Peru, Colombia and Brazil, respectively. 12 the recently approved General Law on Transparency and Access to Public Information, and the constitutional reform that creates the National Anti-Corruption System. However, it is necessary to recognize that while the efforts made so far are of enormous relevance, they are only the beginning of a long process. Undoubtedly, the impact of structural reforms on the productivity of our economy will take time. In addition, achieving higher rates of potential economic growth will require sustained efforts to ensure both macroeconomic and financial stability, as well as adequate implementation of structural reforms. It is also necessary to consider that any additional action necessary to address other possible obstacles to the expansion of the economy will need to be put in place. Is it possible to achieve greater potential growth in Mexico? It seems to me that the State of Queretaro is a tangible example of the feasibility of achieving this objective. The GDP of Queretaro registered during the period 20052013 an average annual growth of 4.8 percent, the highest among the country's entities and close to double that observed at the national level. This expansion has been supported by a solid growth of the export industry and a diverse economic structure, which among other things is characterized by hosting one of the largest concentrations of companies in the aerospace sector in Mexico. Likewise, Queretaro has consolidated its position as a manufacturing cluster in recent years. I trust that 13 Similar to what has been achieved in this entity, our country will be able to begin a new stage characterized by higher and sustained rates of economic growth. Thanks a lot. 14

As, la volatilidad del tipo de cambio del peso se ha ubicado en niveles que se comparan favorablemente con los observados en otras economas emergentes. Asimismo, las tasas de inters internas han mostrado incrementos moderados, mientras que el nivel de los indicadores de riesgo de crdito soberano se ubica por debajo de los de la mayora de las economas emergentes. Permtanme profundizar en los retos a los que deber hacer frente la poltica monetaria en los prximos meses. La implementacin de la poltica monetaria en Mxico descansa en cuatro pilares. El primero de ellos es la autonoma del banco central, atributo que 4 nuestro Instituto Central adquiri en 1994, en lo que indudablemente representa una de las reformas institucionales de mayor relevancia en la historia reciente de Mxico. En tercer lugar, la bsqueda de una convergencia eficiente de la inflacin a la meta, es decir, al menor costo posible en trminos de actividad econmica. Y en cuarto lugar, un compromiso estricto con la transparencia y la rendicin de cuentas. Este enfoque de poltica monetaria, junto con el fortalecimiento de las finanzas pblicas, han permitido un descenso sustancial de la tasa de inflacin. Desde principios de este siglo, tanto la inflacin general como la subyacente han mostrado una tendencia a la baja, alcanzndose, como ya se ha mencionado, la meta de 3 por ciento durante 2015. En particular, a raz de los esfuerzos realizados, los mecanismos de determinacin de precios en la economa han mostrado un cambio estructural. Al respecto, cabe sealar por ejemplo la drstica cada del traspaso de depreciaciones del tipo de cambio a la inflacin, as como una respuesta mucho menor de las expectativas de inflacin y su dispersin ante diferentes tipos de choques. En este contexto, 2 Cabe recordar que existe un intervalo de variabilidad de +/- 1 por ciento alrededor del objetivo permanente de 3 por ciento. 5 no es sorprendente que la depreciacin del tipo de cambio de meses recientes haya coexistido con un descenso de la inflacin, ni que distintos choques de oferta como los cambios impositivos de 2014 o los incrementos que frecuentemente muestran los precios de los productos agropecuarios solo afecten de manera transitoria la inflacin, sin dar lugar a efectos de segundo orden. De marzo de 2013 a junio de 2014, la tasa de inters de referencia para la conduccin de la poltica monetaria se redujo en 150 puntos porcentuales, a su nivel ms bajo en los registros, permaneciendo constante desde ese entonces. Un manejo de la poltica monetaria de esta naturaleza habra sido impensable hace algunos aos. Indudablemente, el principal reto para la poltica monetaria en la coyuntura actual es consolidar los avances logrados en la reduccin de la inflacin. Cules son los riesgos que se enfrentan a este respecto? Para responder a esta pregunta, es necesario considerar, en primer lugar, que no obstante el gradual fortalecimiento de nuestra economa, sta presenta todava un elevado grado de holgura. Lo anterior se refleja con claridad en la tasa de desempleo, que si bien ha mostrado una tendencia a la baja en meses recientes, contina registrando cifras superiores a las previas a la crisis financiera global, as como en el hecho de que no se observan presiones en los mercados de crdito, en el sector externo o los salarios. La experiencia de Mxico es ilustrativa a este respecto. El crecimiento econmico en los prximos aos tambin debera verse apoyado por condiciones demogrficas favorables, ya que la evolucin esperada de la poblacin de nuestro pas nos permitir beneficiarnos de tasas de crecimiento de la fuerza laboral elevadas en relacin a otras economas 6 Las importaciones de Estados Unidos provenientes de Mxico aumentaron de 9.1 a 12.9 por ciento del total, de julio de 2005 a abril de 2015. 7 Segn la Organizacin Internacional de Fabricantes de Automviles (OICA, por sus siglas en francs), en 2014 Mxico ocup el sptimo lugar mundial en la produccin total de vehculos (incluyendo comerciales y de pasajeros). Tambin es importante considerar que si bien es probable que las economas emergentes sigan enfrentando una situacin econmica mundial compleja en los prximos aos, es de esperarse que dicho entorno externo sea menos desfavorable para Mxico. Por una parte, el crecimiento potencial de Estados Unidos se ha visto menos afectado por la crisis financiera global y enfrenta menos riesgos a la baja que los de otras economas importantes, entre ellas China y la zona del euro.9 Por otra parte, la baja participacin de las materias primas dentro de nuestras exportaciones totales podra convertirse en un factor adicional de diferenciacin, dado el contexto actual de bajas cotizaciones internacionales para estos productos y la expectativa de que continen deprimidas en los prximos aos.10 La implementacin de las medidas de reforma estructural en Mxico ya ha iniciado, y algunos de los resultados esperados de las mismas ya son evidentes. Al respecto, destacan, por citar algunos ejemplos, las bajas en los precios de los servicios de telecomunicacin, reflejo a su vez de la mayor competencia en el sector; el amplio inters de empresas privadas, tanto nacionales como extranjeras, por participar en los procesos de licitacin de contratos en el sector energtico; y la percepcin entre el sector privado de que los cambios recientes han redundado en un marco regulatorio en el sector laboral ms propicio para la inversin. Son de destacarse tambin las importantes acciones llevadas a cabo para mejorar el marco institucional de nuestro pas, entre ellas 9 Ver International Monetary Fund (2015): Where Are We Headed? Perspectives on Potential Output, Chapter 3, World Economic Outlook, April. 10 La participacin de las materias primas en las exportaciones totales de mercancas es de alrededor de 15 por ciento en Mxico, cifra que se compara con las de 86, 85, 82 y 62 por ciento en Chile, Per, Colombia y Brasil, respectivamente. 12 la recientemente aprobada Ley General de Transparencia y Acceso a la Informacin Pblica, y la reforma constitucional que crea el Sistema Nacional Anticorrupcin. Sin embargo, es necesario reconocer que si bien los esfuerzos hasta ahora realizados son de enorme relevancia, constituyen tan slo el inicio de un largo proceso. Indudablemente, el impacto de las reformas estructurales en la productividad de nuestra economa tomar tiempo. Adicionalmente, el logro de mayores tasas de crecimiento econmico potencial requerir de esfuerzos sostenidos para garantizar la estabilidad tanto macroeconmica como financiera, as como de una adecuada implementacin de las reformas estructurales. Tambin es preciso considerar que ser necesario poner en marcha cualquier accin adicional necesaria para hacer frente a otros posibles obstculos a la expansin de la economa. Es posible alcanzar un mayor crecimiento potencial en Mxico? Me parece que el Estado de Quertaro constituye un ejemplo palpable de la viabilidad de alcanzar este objetivo. El PIB de Quertaro registr durante el periodo 20052013 un crecimiento anual medio de 4.8 por ciento, el ms alto entre las entidades del pas y cerca del doble del observado a nivel nacional. Title: Fourth edition of the biennial conference on financial stability, organized by the Bank of Canada, CEMLA, the University of Zurich, and Banco de Mxico
Subtitle: Opening Remarks by Alejandro Daz de Len, Governor of Banco de Mxico, at the 4 th Conference on Financial Stability
text: Opening Remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of Banco de Mexico, at the 4th Conference on Financial Stability.1 Mexico City, November 23, 2021 It is a pleasure to meet you all at this fourth edition of the biennial Conference on Financial Stability, jointly organized by the Bank of Canada, CEMLA, the University of Zurich, and Banco de Mexico. This is a special forum where academics, policy makers and practitioners in general gather, although virtually this time, to discuss topics which expand the frontier of financial stability policy. The Great Financial Crisis contributed to the largest global regulatory and supervisory financial collaboration effort on record. Multilateral consensus enabled to adopt standards at the international level to limit the occurrence of new crisis episodes. Key among these standards is a broader adoption of macroprudential measures that recognizes close and complex interactions among intermediaries and networks of the financial system. 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the sole responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Banco de Mexico or of its Governing Board. 1 Financial authorities, international standard setters, and market participants have learned a lot from this episode and have worked together to create a more robust micro and macroprudential framework through methodological advances, identification of vulnerabilities, and assessment of upcoming risks. Recently, we had the opportunity to successfully test our progress. The swift and coordinated response to the COVID-19 pandemic providing liquidity in a wide range of fronts was key to preserve financial stability. The financial system was resilient and is playing a key role in the recovery. Many of the advances that were key to strengthening the financial system were the result of coordinated efforts by academics and policy makers to understand the origins, dynamics, and how to manage systemic risks. This research agenda allowed us to understand and develop policy work on relevant topics to enhance financial stability, such as: 2 i. designing a framework to deal with too-big-to-fail; ii. developing the right incentives, and a credible message, that banks wont be bailed out; iii. determining the amount and type of capital that banks should hold at an entity level to absorb potential losses; iv. identifying when credit is growing too fast and may increase systemic risk; and v. disentangling the interaction and feedback loop that exists between monetary and macroprudential policy, among others. To foster high quality research and discussion, forums like todays conference are of paramount importance. The financial stability paradigm relies on key elements, some of which are reflected in this conference: i. macroprudential policy; ii. stress testing as a tool to monitor systemic risk; iii. interconnectedness as a shock amplifier; iv. financial system and banking regulation; v. potential systemic risk from financial innovations; 3 vi. interaction among price, macroeconomic and financial stability; and vii. risks originating outside the financial system. However, it is important to recognize pending areas and emerging risks ahead, such as those stemming from financial and technological innovations or from climate-related risks, and the need to better communicate to the public at large the role of financial stability and the needed actions to preserve it. Recent advances in technology and innovation have created the potential for a structural transformation in payment and financial services (platform payments and platform finance). The inclusion of networks with a wide customer base in financial ecosystems, the so-called Bigtechs and Fintechs, seeks to link customers with financial services, either provided by financial intermediaries or themselves. This raises key issues for public policy, in terms of competition, consumer protection, and financial stability. 4 An open finance ecosystem could render several benefits such as better services, lower costs, and deeper financial inclusion, but authorities should avoid potential suboptimal results, for example concentration, vertical integration, lack of interoperability, among others. An open finance ecosystem without adequate regulation will not deliver the desired public goods. To attain this, research and new ideas coming from academia, think tanks and authorities would be of relevance. As for climate-related risks, this is a highly complex, infrequent but material risk, which affects all countries and sectors. We need to develop more detailed plans and a deeper understanding of its impact on the economy and the financial system. Climate change can have major effects on our economies and financial systems. Central banks, which have price, output and financial stability mandates, have been active in assessing these risks, and developing tools and analysis to address these risks. While work is being undertaken on both of these areas, it is important to devote more efforts to continue analyzing them. In particular, it is key to 5 better understand the role of the financial system in mitigating or amplifying the impact of such risks. The session on overlooked systemic risks is a step in this direction. One last topic to develop, is the need to improve communication by sending a clear message that financial system users are always at the center of our regulatory and intervention decisions. We must make sure that if there is a shock to the financial system, the public is informed and has clarity about our objectives and policies to intertemporally minimize the shocks impact to the real economy and, therefore, to the publics welfare. This is a great opportunity to reflect on financial stability on a broader sense, acknowledging what has been achieved, digging deeper to better understand the relevant topics already identified, and continue working on pending issues. 6

Title: XLIX National Convention IMEF
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the XLIX National Convention IMEF.1 Mexico City, November 19, 2021 Introduction Good afternoon. I greet you again and I reiterate my pleasure to participate in this meeting organized by the IMEF. I thank Mr. angel Garcia-Lascurain for his invitation and my friend and colleague Federico Rubli for their participation in the moderation. The assigned theme, on the role that the Bank of Mexico must play in the future of the Mexican economy, is very relevant, since it refers both to the essential and historical functions of central banking, as well as to emerging challenges and opportunities. Central banks serve basic functions in modern economies. Since their origins, central banks have served as the institutions that provide certainty to the process of issuance and circulation of money and their priority mission is to seek the 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 stability of the purchasing power of the currency they provide to society. Similarly, since their inception, central banks have had responsibilities for the stability and healthy development of the financial and payment system. In recent years, new circumstances have emerged, which affect the basic functions of central banking. We have witnessed technological innovations and trends that radically change the economy and everyday life. These, on the one hand, increase the possibilities of economic progress and well-being of citizens. On the other hand, they pose challenges of global scope, in various dimensions, such as financial, cyber, environmental challenges and, of course, health emergencies. Central banks must adapt to fulfill their essential functions in this new environment. In this speech, I would like to refer, first of all, to the importance of institutional mandates to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, as well as to promote the healthy development of the financial and payment system that the law entrusts to the Bank of Mexico; and, secondly, to some of the challenges 2 more important emerging economies, which require the intervention and leadership of the central bank. 1.1 The importance of price stability With the inauguration of the Bank of Mexico on September 1, 1925, an aspiration materialized, which can be traced back to our beginnings as an independent nation, to have a single instance that would give certainty to the issuance and circulation of money and that, in addition, would contribute to the development of the financial and payment system. Since, in historical retrospect, it is clear that the stages in which the Bank of Mexico had greater room for maneuver to implement a prudent monetary policy coincide with periods of growth with low inflation and financial stability, from 1994 onwards, autonomy was conferred on the central bank. This is the ideal framework to achieve the priority objective of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, as well as promoting the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of the payment system. 3 The autonomy of the Bank of Mexico has worked: inflation has fallen from the two- and even triple-digit levels it reached to levels around the permanent target. The autonomy of the Bank of Mexico has been accompanied by a consistent effort in terms of transparency, accountability and communication with the market and society. This policy of openness is essential to promote the broadest social knowledge about the bank's actions, as well as to raise its credibility and, therefore, achieve its objectives more expeditiously and efficiently. Since 2020, the Bank of Mexico has faced one of the most complex challenges in its autonomy stage. The pandemic has implied an unexpected economic scenario, which has generated new challenges that have required, first the agile and determined use of its powers to grant financing and, subsequently, the fight against global inflationary pressures not seen in decades. In its initial stage, the health emergency led to an abrupt closure of activities that induced companies to reduce costs, inventories, 4 investment and workforce. This produced profound effects on the labor market and employment, as well as a decrease in income and a recomposition in household spending, which due to the pandemic redirected their spending from services to goods. In response to the population's income and employment losses, many governments adopted fiscal stimulus and support, especially in advanced economies. In addition, with the advance of vaccines, it has been possible to reopen economies and a gradual, albeit heterogeneous, global economic recovery. In particular, the reopening of productive activity has led to a more accelerated recovery than those that usually occur cyclically. Likewise, fiscal support and transfers to households in the United States increased, which led to a significant increase in the demand for durable consumer goods globally, pressuring their prices and generating bottlenecks in production lines and supply chains. 5 The labor market also has considerable challenges, as the pandemic rebuilt the labor force, is leading to a change in relative wages with greater risk of contagion and greater pressures are to be expected for wages to rise above inflation. The effects of the pandemic described above have had differentiated effects between countries and sectors, and important inflationary pressures, which although it is expected to be mainly transitory, the horizon in which they could affect inflation is uncertain. In addition, they have impacted a wide range of products and their magnitude has been considerable. All this has increased the risks to price formation and inflation expectations. Therefore, it has been considered necessary to strengthen the monetary policy stance to promote the convergence of inflation to its target and an orderly adjustment in the financial markets and the economy. Small, open emerging economies that supplement their domestic savings with external sources must maintain a sound macroeconomic stance at all times, both with sustainable public finances and inflation-focused monetary policy. 6 low and stable, and strength in the financial system. All three are indispensable elements that we must preserve in order to maintain stability and the foundations of growth. 1.2 Promote the healthy development of the financial and payment system. In addition to its main objective, which is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, the law entrusts the Bank of Mexico with the purposes of promoting the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of payment systems. To achieve these goals, the Bank of Mexico works on two aspects: stability and the promotion of greater efficiency, competition and inclusion of the financial system. On the one hand, the bank promotes regulation and supervision that identifies, reduces and mitigates systemic risks. On the other hand, the financial system must not only be stable, but also efficient and inclusive, in order to channel public savings in a safe and agile way towards the most profitable projects for society. 7 One way to establish an even floor and promote greater equity between different social sectors is to promote the possibility of financing, in the best conditions of quality, accessibility and scope, the talent, productivity and projects of the entire population. Therefore, it is essential to continue promoting greater transparency, efficiency and competition in the provision of services, offering consumers adequate information to make better decisions, as well as actions to protect their interests. 2. Emerging risks Let me now turn to emerging risks and opportunities, in which central banks must play a significant role. 2.1 Climate-related financial risks. Climate change and environmental degradation represent significant and growing challenges at the national and global levels and bring risks but also opportunities for the financial system. The various catastrophic, acute or chronic climatic events and the degradation of ecosystems affect productivity, cause disruptions in the 8 value chains and produce phenomena of great social, economic and geopolitical impact. The adoption of technologies for adaptation to climate change and the mitigation of pollutant emissions represent an important source of investment and development opportunities. An adequate assessment of environmental and social risks and opportunities helps to guide the allocation of resources towards more economically efficient activities, more consistent with the preservation of the environment and with sustainable growth with greater social impact. Central banks and supervisory bodies should incentivise and ensure that the financial system becomes increasingly aware and resilient to these risks. Since historical information tends to be of little relevance to assessing climate risks, it is important for financial and non-financial firms to develop prospective instruments such as stress testing and evaluation of alternative scenarios. 9 For an adequate consideration of the relevant physical and transition risks, it is necessary to have internationally homogeneous schemes of information, disclosure and accounting standards by financial and non-financial companies. It is also imperative to work on building a common framework of reference for green/sustainable investments, including a coherent classification system for these activities. In addition, in the case of emerging economies, it is necessary to develop portfolios of credits and green projects that meet international criteria and that allow resources to be captured at low costs. The Bank of Mexico has been early aware of these challenges and is the founder of the network of central banks and supervisors to green the financial system (NGFS) and collaborates with various international organizations in projects to promote sustainable finance. 10 2.2 Technological and operational risks. The pandemic has deepened the digital divide within countries and internationally, making technological updating and financial inclusion an imperative for all. Technological advances create the possibility of a structural transformation of financial services and payment systems, in favour of citizens. Central banks play a key role in this transition given their role as regulators, supervisors and operators of the payments infrastructure. In particular, the incorporation of new actors in the financial ecosystem, such as the so-called Fintech and Bigtech, generates new opportunities to improve the quality, coverage and variety of services, but it can also generate risks likely to affect competition and operational continuity, and can even become systemic. These payment networks should not be developed outside the financial ecosystem. It is necessary to work on regulatory conditions and 11 technologies needed to ensure that they are part of our financial systems and achieve better services and inclusion on a solid basis. Therefore, its constructive incorporation into the financial and payment system should be promoted following principles such as: 1) same risk/same-regulation; 2) interoperability and net neutrality; 3) boost competition and avoid mergers and alliances between dominant companies; 4) ensure operational continuity with large suppliers; 5) global coordination to deal with jurisdictional gaps; (6) full consumer protection and; 7) strengthen cybersecurity standards. Central banks play a key role in ensuring and providing certain basic functions that are indispensable for a healthy ecosystem, in which they highlight: 1) a robust infrastructure for the clearing and settlement of low, medium and high value payments; 12 2) a robust authentication and validation infrastructure for individuals; 3) arrangements to provide access to new participants (APIs); and 4) ability to operate account services. Likewise, central banks in the world must move quickly in the task of extending the functions of money to their digital versions, which are compatible with the intermediation carried out by commercial banks and offer more efficient payment services. Crypto assets seeking to be used as means of payment should be extensions of the current monetary and financial architecture, and serve as a substitute for cash, not as an alternative currency. Some of these alternatives, which could partially function as a medium of exchange, largely fail as a store of value, unit of account, and as an efficient and generally accepted payment instrument. To consolidate these new services for the benefit of users without jeopardizing the financial architecture, global coordination, investment in systems, processes and technologies, as well as the 13 commitment to work together with the private sector. Failure to address these concerns can severely affect public goods provided by the central bank, jeopardize financial stability, and weaken consumer protection. In short, the central bank has a fundamental role in channeling technological innovations in favor of a more efficient and inclusive financial and payment system, capable, especially in emerging economies, of reducing historical lags and benefiting all sectors of the population. Ladies and gentlemen, in the following decades we will face, as never before, a changing environment in which many opportunities are looming but also unusual challenges. To face this stage, it is essential to deploy a prospective vision, which not only addresses the immediate challenges, but also those long-term trends that are being configured in a less visible way. 14 For the Bank of Mexico, its mandates to promote price stability, stimulate the healthy development of the financial system and promote the proper functioning of the payment system are public goods that are directly reflected in the economic opportunities and quality of life of citizens. Likewise, the Bank of Mexico is called to exercise leadership in crucial aspects for growth and financial stability in the coming decades, such as responses to climate change and the optimal and safe incorporation of technological innovation into the financial and payment system. Because of its tradition, its history and, above all, the clarity of its institutional mandate, I am sure that the Bank of Mexico will live up to its urgent mission in the future of the Mexican economy. Thanks a lot 15
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la XLIX Convencin Nacional IMEF.1 Ciudad de Mxico, 19 de noviembre de 2021 Introduccin Muy buenas tardes. Los saludo nuevamente y les reitero el gusto que me da participar en este encuentro que organiza el IMEF. Agradezco la invitacin del Mtro. ngel Garca-Lascurin, y a mi amigo y colega Federico Rubli por su participacin en la moderacin. El tema asignado, sobre el papel que debe cumplir el Banco de Mxico en el futuro de la economa mexicana, resulta muy relevante, ya que remite tanto a las funciones esenciales e histricas de la banca central, como a desafos y oportunidades emergentes. Los bancos centrales cumplen funciones bsicas en las economas modernas. Desde sus orgenes, los bancos centrales han fungido como las instituciones que brindan certidumbre al proceso de emisin y circulacin de dinero y su misin prioritaria consiste en procurar la 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad del autor y no necesariamente representan la posicin institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno. 1 estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda que proveen a la sociedad. Igualmente, desde sus inicios, los bancos centrales han tenido responsabilidades relativas a la estabilidad y el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y de pagos. En los ltimos aos han surgido nuevas circunstancias, que inciden en las funciones bsicas de la banca central. Hemos atestiguado innovaciones tecnolgicas y tendencias que modifican radicalmente la economa y la vida cotidiana. stas, por un lado, incrementan las posibilidades de progreso econmico y bienestar de los ciudadanos. Por el otro, plantean desafos de alcance global, en diversas dimensiones, como son la financiera, la ciberntica, los retos ambientales y, desde luego, las emergencias sanitarias. Los bancos centrales deben adaptarse para cumplir sus funciones esenciales en este nuevo entorno. En esta intervencin, quiero referirme, en primer lugar, a la importancia de los mandatos institucionales de procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional, as como promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y de pagos que la ley encomienda al Banco de Mxico; y, en segundo lugar, a algunos de los retos 2 emergentes ms importantes, que requieren la intervencin y el liderazgo del banco central. 1.1 La importancia de la estabilidad de precios Con la inauguracin del Banco de Mxico, el 1 de septiembre de 1925, se materializaba una aspiracin, que puede remontarse a nuestros inicios como nacin independiente, de contar con una instancia nica que diera certidumbre a la emisin y circulacin de dinero y que, adicionalmente, contribuyera al desarrollo del sistema financiero y de pagos. Dado que, en retrospectiva histrica, es claro que las etapas en que el Banco de Mxico tuvo mayor margen de maniobra para implementar una poltica monetaria prudente coinciden con periodos de crecimiento con baja inflacin y estabilidad financiera, a partir de 1994, se confiri autonoma al banco central. Este es el marco idneo para lograr el objetivo prioritario de procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional, as como promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. 3 La autonoma del Banco de Mxico ha funcionado: la inflacin ha descendido de los niveles de dos, y hasta tres dgitos que lleg a alcanzar, a niveles de alrededor de la meta permanente. La autonoma del Banco de Mxico ha sido acompaada de un consistente esfuerzo en materia de transparencia, rendicin de cuentas y comunicacin con el mercado y la sociedad. Esta poltica de apertura es fundamental para propiciar el ms amplio conocimiento social sobre las acciones del banco, as como para elevar su credibilidad y, por ende, alcanzar sus objetivos de manera ms expedita y eficiente. Desde 2020, el Banco de Mxico ha enfrentado uno de los retos ms complejos en su etapa de autonoma. La pandemia ha implicado un escenario econmico inesperado, que ha generado nuevos desafos que han requerido, primero el uso gil y decidido de sus facultades para otorgar financiamiento y, posteriormente, el combate a presiones inflacionarias globales no vistas en dcadas. En su etapa inicial la emergencia sanitaria propici un cierre abrupto de actividades que indujo a las empresas a reducir costos, inventarios, 4 inversin y plantilla laboral. Ello produjo afectaciones profundas en el mercado laboral y el empleo, as como una disminucin en el ingreso y una recomposicin en el gasto de los hogares, los cuales por la pandemia reorientaron su gasto de los servicios a las mercancas. Como respuesta a las prdidas de ingreso y empleo de la poblacin, muchos gobiernos adoptaron estmulos y apoyos fiscales, especialmente en las economas avanzadas. Adicionalmente, con el avance de las vacunas ha sido posible una reapertura de las economas y una recuperacin econmica mundial gradual, aunque heterognea. En particular, la reapertura de la actividad productiva ha propiciado una recuperacin ms acelerada que las que usualmente se presentan cclicamente. Igualmente, se incrementaron los apoyos fiscales y las transferencias a los hogares en Estados Unidos, lo que propici un aumento significativo en la demanda de bienes de consumo duradero a nivel global, presionando sus precios y generando cuellos de botella en las lneas de produccin y en las cadenas de suministro. 5 El mercado laboral tambin tiene retos considerables, pues la pandemia recompuso la fuerza laboral, est propiciando un cambio en los salarios relativos con mayor riesgo de contagio y son de esperarse mayores presiones para que los salarios aumenten por encima de la inflacin. Las afectaciones de la pandemia antes descritas han tenido efectos diferenciados entre pases y sectores, e importantes presiones inflacionarias, las cuales si bien se prev que sean principalmente transitorias, el horizonte en el que podran incidir sobre la inflacin es incierto. Adems, han impactado a un amplio rango de productos y su magnitud ha sido considerable. Todo ello ha incrementado los riesgos para la formacin de precios y las expectativas de inflacin. Por ello, se ha considerado necesario reforzar la postura de poltica monetaria para propiciar la convergencia de la inflacin a su meta y un ajuste ordenado en los mercados financieros y la economa. Las economas emergentes pequeas y abiertas que complementan su ahorro interno con fuentes externas deben mantener en todo momento una postura macroeconmica slida, tanto con finanzas pblicas sostenibles como con una poltica monetaria enfocada en una inflacin 6 baja y estable, y fortaleza en el sistema financiero. Los tres son elementos indispensables que debemos preservar para mantener la estabilidad y las bases del crecimiento. 1.2 Promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y de pagos. Adems de su objetivo principal, que es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional, la ley le encarga al Banco de Mxico las finalidades de promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Para alcanzar estas finalidades, el Banco de Mxico trabaja en dos vertientes: la estabilidad y la promocin de mayor eficiencia competencia e inclusin del sistema financiero. Por un lado, el banco promueve una regulacin y supervisin que identifique, reduzca y mitigue riesgos sistmicos. Por otro lado, el sistema financiero no slo debe ser estable, sino tambin eficiente e inclusivo, a fin de encauzar de manera segura y gil el ahorro pblico hacia los proyectos ms rentables para la sociedad. 7 Una manera de establecer un piso parejo y promover una mayor equidad entre distintos sectores sociales es propiciando la posibilidad de financiar, en las mejores condiciones de calidad, accesibilidad y alcance, el talento, productividad y los proyectos de toda la poblacin. Por eso, resulta indispensable seguir impulsando la mayor transparencia, eficiencia y competencia en la provisin de servicios, ofreciendo a los consumidores informacin adecuada para tomar mejores decisiones, as como con acciones para proteger sus intereses. 2. Los riesgos emergentes Permtanme ahora hablar de los riesgos y oportunidades emergentes, en los que los bancos centrales deben jugar un papel significativo. 2.1 Riesgos financieros relacionados con el clima. El cambio climtico y la degradacin ambiental representan retos importantes y crecientes a nivel nacional y global y conllevan riesgos pero tambin oportunidades para el sistema financiero. Los diversos eventos climticos catastrficos, agudos o crnicos y la degradacin de los ecosistemas afectan la productividad, provocan disrupciones en las 8 cadenas de valor y producen fenmenos de gran impacto social, econmico y geopoltico. La adopcin de tecnologas para la adaptacin al cambio climtico y la mitigacin de emisiones de contaminantes representan una fuente importante de oportunidades de inversin y de desarrollo. Una evaluacin adecuada de los riesgos ambientales y sociales y de las oportunidades contribuye a orientar la asignacin de recursos hacia actividades ms eficientes desde el punto de vista econmico, ms congruentes con la preservacin del medio ambiente y con un crecimiento sustentable y con mayor derrama social. Los bancos centrales y los organismos supervisores deben incentivar y procurar que el sistema financiero sea cada vez ms consciente y resiliente ante estos riesgos. Dado que la informacin histrica tiende a ser poco relevante para evaluar los riesgos climticos, es importante que las empresas financieras y no financieras desarrollen instrumentos prospectivos como pruebas de estrs y evaluacin de escenarios alternativos. 9 Para una consideracin adecuada de los riesgos fsicos y de transicin relevantes, es necesario contar con esquemas homogneos a nivel internacional de informacin, divulgacin y estndares contables por parte de las empresas financieras y no financieras. Tambin es imprescindible trabajar en la construccin de un marco de referencia comn para inversiones verdes/sostenibles, que incluya un sistema de clasificacin coherente para estas actividades. Adems, en el caso de las economas emergentes, se necesita desarrollar portafolios de crditos y proyectos verdes que cumplan con criterios internacionales y que permitan captar recursos a costos bajos. El Banco de Mxico ha estado tempranamente alerta de estos retos y es fundador de la red de bancos centrales y supervisores para enverdecer el sistema financiero (NGFS, por sus siglas en ingls) y colabora con diversos organismos internacionales en proyectos de promocin de finanzas sustentables. 10 2.2 Riesgos tecnolgicos y operativos. La pandemia ha profundizado la brecha digital al interior de los pases y a nivel internacional, haciendo a la actualizacin tecnolgica y la inclusin financiera un imperativo para todos. Los avances tecnolgicos generan la posibilidad de una transformacin estructural de los servicios financieros y los sistemas de pagos, en favor de los ciudadanos. Los bancos centrales juegan un papel clave en esta transicin dada su funcin como reguladores, supervisores y operadores de la infraestructura de pagos. En particular, la incorporacin de nuevos actores en el ecosistema financiero, como los llamados Fintech y Bigtech, genera nuevas oportunidades para mejorar la calidad, cobertura y variedad de los servicios, pero tambin puede generar riesgos susceptibles de afectar la competencia y la continuidad operativa, e incluso pueden llegar a ser sistmicos. Estas redes de pago no deben desarrollarse fuera del ecosistema financiero. Es necesario trabajar en las condiciones regulatorias y 11 tecnolgicas necesarias para asegurarnos de que formen parte de nuestros sistemas financieros y lograr mejores servicios e inclusin sobre una base slida. Por eso, debe promoverse su incorporacin constructiva al sistema financiero y de pagos siguiendo principios como: 1) mismo riesgo/misma-regulacin; 2) interoperabilidad y neutralidad de la red; 3) impulsar la competencia y evitar fusiones y alianzas entre empresas dominantes; 4) asegurar continuidad operativa con grandes proveedores; 5) coordinacin global para lidiar con brechas jurisdiccionales; 6) plena proteccin del consumidor y; 7) fortalecer los estndares de ciberseguridad. Los bancos centrales desempean un papel clave en garantizar y proveer ciertas funciones bsicas que son indispensables para contar con un ecosistema saludable, en las que destacan: 1) una infraestructura robusta para la compensacin y liquidacin de pagos de bajo, mediano y alto valor; 12 2) una slida infraestructura de autenticacin y validacin para individuos; 3) arreglos para proporcionar acceso a nuevos participantes (APIs); y 4) capacidad para operar servicios de cuentas. Igualmente, los bancos centrales en el mundo deben avanzar con celeridad en la tarea de extender las funciones del dinero hacia sus versiones digitales, que sean compatibles con la intermediacin que realizan los bancos comerciales y que ofrezcan servicios de pago ms eficientes. Los criptoactivos que busquen ser utilizados como medios de pago deben ser extensiones de la arquitectura monetaria y financiera actual, y fungir como un sustituto del efectivo, no como una moneda alternativa. Algunas de estas alternativas, que podran funcionar parcialmente como un medio de intercambio, fracasan ampliamente como depsito de valor, unidad de cuenta y como un instrumento de pago eficiente y generalmente aceptado. Para consolidar estos nuevos servicios en beneficio de los usuarios sin poner en riesgo la arquitectura financiera, se requiere de coordinacin global, inversin en sistemas, procesos y tecnologas, as como el 13 compromiso de trabajar junto con el sector privado. No atender estas preocupaciones puede afectar gravemente los bienes pblicos que provee el banco central, poner en peligro la estabilidad financiera y debilitar la proteccin al consumidor. En suma, el banco central tiene un papel fundamental en encauzar las innovaciones tecnolgicas en favor de un sistema financiero y de pagos ms eficiente e inclusivo, capaz, sobre todo en economas emergentes, de abatir rezagos histricos y beneficiar a todos los sectores de la poblacin. Seoras y seores: En las dcadas siguientes enfrentaremos, como nunca antes, un entorno cambiante en el que se avizoran numerosas oportunidades pero, tambin, retos inusitados. Para hacer frente a esta etapa es imprescindible desplegar una visin prospectiva, que no slo atienda los retos inmediatos, sino tambin aquellas tendencias de largo plazo que van configurndose de manera menos visible. 14 Para el Banco de Mxico, sus mandatos de promover la estabilidad de precios, estimular el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y fomentar el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos constituyen bienes pblicos que se reflejan directamente en las oportunidades econmicas y la calidad de vida de los ciudadanos. Igualmente, el Banco de Mxico est llamado a ejercer un liderazgo en aspectos cruciales para el crecimiento y la estabilidad financiera en las prximas dcadas, como son las respuestas al cambio climtico y la incorporacin ptima y segura de la innovacin tecnolgica en el sistema financiero y de pagos. Por su tradicin, por su historia y, sobre todo, por la claridad de su mandato institucional, estoy seguro de que el Banco de Mxico estar a la altura de su impostergable misin en el futuro de la economa mexicana. Muchas gracias 15

Title: A window to Cyprus
text: A Window to Cyprus Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, on the occasion of the inauguration of the exhibition "Cyprus, reflections of its history and culture: ten thousand years of civilization", at the Bank of Mexico Library, in Mexico City, on November 29, 2012. It is an honor for me to participate, on behalf of the Bank of Mexico, in the inauguration of the exhibition "Cyprus, reflections of its history and culture: ten thousand years of civilization". In addition to primarily addressing its substantive activities, the Bank of Mexico has sponsored and promoted various cultural projects. Within these, the library has become a space for interdisciplinary dialogue where exhibitions on different countries and cultures have been promoted. In fact, the current thematic exhibition is the sixth annual one offered in this venue. The exhibition that we are inaugurating today opens a window to Cyprus, a small country in size but owner of a great symbolic heritage, rich historical legacy and thriving vision of the future. These traits are fundamental to understanding the resilience of a nation: the symbolic heritage traces a horizon of values, the historical legacy generates direction and identity and the vision of the future channels energies. When thinking of Cyprus it is inevitable to evoke the dawn of Greek civilization, its most persistent and significant root, and to go back to one of the most fascinating figures in mythology: Aphrodite. 1 As the great Mexican writer, Alfonso Reyes, pointed out: Aphrodite is a goddess steeped in Asian flavors that reveal her Eastern ancestry, but she was worshipped without exception throughout the world of Greek communion.1 According to the most widespread version, this goddess was born from some members of Uranus torn off by her own son and thrown into the sea. From such dispossession sprang white foam, and from it arose the goddess who was pushed placidly by the waves to Cyprus, where she touched the earth and from her footsteps sprouted grass and flowers. Literature has exposed Aphrodite's temperament and adventures: her affairs with the god of war, her dalliances with mortals, her determining role in the initiation of the Trojan War, and the abysmal passions she used to induce in some Greek heroines. However, as Alfonso Reyes himself points out, beyond the picturesque character of mythology, the tutelary presence of Aphrodite refers, above all, to a set of values that celebrate life in all its dimensions. The spirit of luminous vitalism is what characterizes Cyprus, whose temperament and landscape incite to enjoy from earthly gifts to ideal objects. The radiant desire to live makes the everyday sacred and gives meaning to every moment. Thus, in this beautiful and millenary island a refined art of living has been cultivated ancestrally, verified in the opulence of its cuisine, in the sober beauty of traditional clothing, in the harmony of vernacular architecture with the natural environment, in the role occupied by good conversation, in social life or in the sensitivity of its inhabitants to the most different manifestations of art. It is not surprising that this territory is so present in the artistic imagination of the West and has inspired and attracted numerous creators. 1 Reyes, A. (1989), Obras Completas, tomo XVI, p. 459, Fondo de Cultura Economica, Mexico, Segunda reimpresion. 2 The historical legacy Located in a meeting point between Europe, Africa and Asia, Cyprus has been a crossroads of civilizations and has received, throughout its history, different cultural influences. The Phoenician, Egyptian, Persian, Greek, Roman, Frankish, Venetian, Ottoman and British presences, among others, have implied a very rich confluence that Cyprus has managed to assimilate in a multifaceted and open character. This town has known times of stability and splendor that have allowed it to generate progress and provide significant cultural contributions, but also, as a small and prosperous territory, it has been the object of the conflicting interests of different powers and has suffered periods of turbulence. However, after each onslaught, Cyprus has been able to overcome, recover its forces, rebuild its social fabric and safeguard its identity. It is no coincidence that it was the Cypriot philosopher, Zeno of Citium (335-263.C BC), who founded in Athens the imperishable philosophical school of Stoicism, which prescribes serenity in the face of triumph and fortitude in the face of adversity, and points out that the greatest degree of freedom of man is found in the dominion of himself and his passions and excessive ambitions.2 The vision of the future Today, after a historical itinerary as rich as it is complex, Cyprus is a democracy and an economy that is part of the European community and occupies a privileged position due to its geographical location, its infrastructure, its human resources and its legal framework. For several years now, this country has carried out a programme aimed at the market economy, which was strengthened by its accession to the Union. 2 See Sharples, R.W. (2009), Stoics, Epicureans, and Skeptics. Introduction to Hellenistic Philosophy, UNAM, Institute of Philosophical Research, Mexico. 3 European in 2004, and with the adoption of the euro on the first day of 2008. Cyprus currently has liberalized trade and a framework that encourages competition and investment. Thus, this nation has gone from being an eminently agricultural economy to developing an industrial sector and, above all, services.
