A majority of the population depends on tourism and another notable item is maritime transport, with a fleet of ships with international prestige. The global crisis has hit the Cypriot economy by contracting demand from its main trading partners, such as Greece, Germany, the United Kingdom and Italy. Also, as in the case of the whole of Europe, the crisis has revealed economic imbalances in Cyprus that require adjustments. However, thanks to its comparative advantages and human capital, this country has the capacity to, in the near future, resume its path of progress and well-being. Panoramic view of a country It is natural for Cypriots and Mexicans to experience immediate identification and sympathy: both peoples have a thousand-year-old history; we have been a crossroads of roads and cultures; we have waged long struggles for our independence, territorial integrity and self-determination; and we have sought to reconcile tradition and modernity. Like Mexico, Cyprus is a multicultural country whose deepest roots lie in ancient civilizations. The exhibition that we present today, with the generous and invaluable support of the Embassy of Cyprus, provides a panoramic view of this country: from archaeological pieces of Hellenic origin with centuries of antiquity to moving Byzantine icons; from ritual objects to everyday instruments; from clothing and textiles to old maps. I would like to thank in a special way His Excellency Ambassador Vasilis Philippou for his deference to share with us some pieces from his private collection. 4 In the balanced set of objects and works of art exhibited, we can observe a fruitful cultural mixture assimilated with an original spirit. Precisely, to evoke more vividly the atmosphere of that country, maestro Basilio Mavridis will share with us a selection of his music. For the duration of the exhibition, Cyprus comes alive in this enclosure and becomes an affable host who serves his guests with proverbial hospitality. It only remains for me to congratulate those who have participated in the successful organization, election, curatorship and assembly of this exhibition, both on behalf of the Embassy and the Bank of Mexico. And of course, on behalf of this institution, I would like to reiterate to the Ambassador our gratitude for having brought this beloved corner of Cyprus to our facilities. 5
text_original: Una Ventana a Chipre Palabras del Dr. Manuel Snchez Gonzlez, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, con motivo de la inauguracin de la exposicin Chipre, reflexiones de su historia y cultura: diez mil aos de civilizacin, en la Biblioteca del Banco de Mxico, en la Ciudad de Mxico, el 29 de noviembre de 2012. Es un honor para m participar, a nombre del Banco de Mxico, en la inauguracin de la exposicin Chipre, reflexiones de su historia y cultura: diez mil aos de civilizacin. Adems de ocuparse primordialmente de sus actividades sustantivas, el Banco de Mxico ha patrocinado e impulsado diversos proyectos culturales. Dentro de estos, la biblioteca se ha constituido en un espacio de dilogo interdisciplinario donde se han promovido exposiciones sobre diferentes pases y culturas. De hecho, la actual muestra temtica es la sexta anual que se ofrece en este recinto. La exposicin que hoy inauguramos nos abre una ventana a Chipre, pas pequeo en dimensiones pero dueo de un gran patrimonio simblico, rico legado histrico y pujante visin de futuro. Estos rasgos son fundamentales para entender la reciedumbre de una nacin: el patrimonio simblico traza un horizonte de valores, el legado histrico genera rumbo e identidad y la visin de futuro encauza energas. El patrimonio simblico Al pensar en Chipre es inevitable evocar el alba de la civilizacin griega, su raz ms persistente y significativa, y remontarse a una de las figuras ms fascinantes de la mitologa: Afrodita. 1 Como apunt el gran escritor mexicano, Alfonso Reyes: Afrodita es diosa impregnada de sabores asiticos que revelan su ascendencia oriental, pero fue adorada sin excepcin en todo el orbe de la comunin griega.1 Segn la versin ms extendida, esta diosa naci de algunos miembros de Urano arrancados por su propio hijo y arrojados al mar. De tal despojo brot espuma blanca, y de ella surgi la diosa que fue empujada plcidamente por las olas hasta Chipre, donde toc la tierra y de sus pisadas brotaron hierba y flores. La literatura ha puesto al descubierto el temperamento y las aventuras de Afrodita: sus amoros con el dios de la guerra, sus devaneos con mortales, su papel determinante en la iniciacin de la guerra de Troya, y las pasiones abismales que sola inducir en algunas heronas griegas. Sin embargo, como seala el propio Alfonso Reyes, ms all del carcter pintoresco de la mitologa, la presencia tutelar de Afrodita remite, sobre todo, a un conjunto de valores que celebran la vida en todas sus dimensiones. El espritu de luminoso vitalismo es el que caracteriza a Chipre, cuyo temperamento y paisaje incitan a gozar desde los dones terrenales hasta los objetos ideales. El deseo radiante de vivir vuelve sacro lo cotidiano y brinda significado a cada instante. As, en esta bella y milenaria isla se ha cultivado ancestralmente un refinado arte de vivir, constatado en la opulencia de su cocina, en la sobria belleza de la indumentaria tradicional, en la armona de la arquitectura verncula con el entorno natural, en el papel que ocupa la buena conversacin, en la vida social o en la sensibilidad de sus habitantes ante las ms distintas manifestaciones de arte. No es extrao que este territorio se encuentre tan presente en la imaginacin artstica de Occidente y haya inspirado y atrado a numerosos creadores. 1 Reyes, A. (1989), Obras Completas, tomo XVI, p. 459, Fondo de Cultura Econmica, Mxico, Segunda reimpresin. 2 El legado histrico Ubicada en un punto de encuentro entre Europa, frica y Asia, Chipre ha sido un cruce de civilizaciones y ha recibido, a lo largo de su historia, distintas influencias culturales. Las presencias fenicia, egipcia, persa, griega, romana, franca, veneciana, otomana y britnica, entre otras, han implicado una riqusima confluencia que Chipre ha logrado asimilar en un carcter multifactico y abierto. Este pueblo ha conocido pocas de estabilidad y esplendor que le han permitido generar progreso y brindar significativas aportaciones culturales, pero tambin, como un territorio pequeo y prspero, ha sido objeto de los intereses encontrados de distintas potencias y ha sufrido periodos de turbulencia. Sin embargo, tras cada embate, Chipre ha sabido sobreponerse, resarcir sus fuerzas, recomponer su tejido social y resguardar su identidad. No es casual que haya sido el filsofo chipriota, Zenn de Citio (335-263 a.C.), el que fundara en Atenas la imperecedera escuela filosfica del estoicismo, que prescribe la serenidad ante el triunfo y la entereza ante la adversidad, y seala que el mayor grado de libertad del hombre se encuentra en el dominio de s mismo y de sus pasiones y ambiciones desmesuradas.2 La visin de futuro Hoy, despus de un itinerario histrico tan rico como complejo, Chipre es una democracia y una economa que forma parte de la comunidad europea y ocupa una posicin privilegiada por su localizacin geogrfica, su infraestructura, sus recursos humanos y su marco legal. Desde hace varios aos este pas ha llevado adelante un programa orientado a la economa de mercado, que se fortaleci con su ingreso a la Unin 2 Vase Sharples, R.W. (2009), Estoicos, epicreos y escpticos. Introduccin a la filosofa helenstica, UNAM, Instituto de Investigaciones Filosficas, Mxico. 3 Europea en 2004, y con la adopcin del euro el primer da de 2008. Actualmente, Chipre cuenta con un comercio liberalizado y un marco que fomenta la competencia y la inversin. As, esta nacin ha pasado de ser una economa eminentemente agrcola a desarrollar un sector industrial y, sobre todo, de servicios. Una parte mayoritaria de la poblacin depende del turismo y otro rubro notable es la trasportacin martima, con una flota de buques con prestigio internacional. La crisis mundial ha afectado a la economa chipriota al contraer la demanda de sus principales socios comerciales, como Grecia, Alemania, Reino Unido e Italia. Asimismo, como en el caso de toda Europa, la crisis ha revelado desequilibrios econmicos en Chipre que precisan ajustes. Sin embargo, gracias a sus ventajas comparativas y su capital humano, este pas cuenta con la capacidad para, en el futuro prximo, retomar su camino de progreso y bienestar. Visin panormica de un pas Es natural que chipriotas y mexicanos experimentemos una identificacin y simpata inmediatas: ambos pueblos tenemos una historia milenaria; hemos sido encrucijada de caminos y culturas; hemos empeado largas luchas por nuestra independencia, integridad territorial y autodeterminacin; y hemos buscado conciliar la tradicin y la modernidad. Como Mxico, Chipre es un pas multicultural cuyas races ms profundas se encuentran en antiguas civilizaciones. La muestra que hoy presentamos, con el apoyo generoso e invaluable de la Embajada de Chipre, brinda una visin panormica de este pas: desde piezas arqueolgicas de origen helnico con siglos de antigedad hasta conmovedores iconos bizantinos; desde objetos rituales hasta instrumentos de uso cotidiano; desde prendas de vestir y textiles hasta mapas antiguos. Deseo agradecer de forma especial al Excelentsimo Sr. Embajador Vasilis Philippou por su deferencia de compartir con nosotros algunas piezas de su coleccin privada. 4 En el equilibrado conjunto de objetos y obras de arte exhibidas, podemos observar una fecunda mezcla cultural asimilada con un espritu original. Precisamente, para evocar ms vvidamente el ambiente de ese pas, el maestro Basilio Mavridis compartir con nosotros una seleccin de su msica. Por el tiempo que dure la exposicin, Chipre adquiere vida en este recinto y se vuelve un afable anfitrin que atiende a sus huspedes con proverbial hospitalidad. A m slo me resta felicitar a quienes han participado en la acertada organizacin, eleccin, curadura y montaje de esta muestra, tanto de parte de la Embajada como del Banco de Mxico. Y por supuesto, en nombre de esta Institucin, quiero reiterarle al seor Embajador nuestro agradecimiento por haber trado a nuestras instalaciones este entraable rincn de Chipre. 5

Title: Celebration of the 50th anniversary of Grupo Financiero Inbursa (S.A.B. de C.V.)
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the celebration of the 50th anniversary of Grupo Financiero Inbursa (S.A.B. de C.V.). November 30, 2015 ? Engineer Carlos Slim Helu, Honorary and Life President of the Board of Directors of Grupo Carso, ? Mr. Marco Antonio Slim Domit, President of Grupo Financiero Inbursa, ? Mr. Javier Foncerrada Izquierdo, General Director of Grupo Financiero Inbursa ? Family and friends of engineer Carlos Slim Helu, ? Officials and employees of Grupo Financiero Inbursa, ? Distinguished guests, ? Ladies and gentlemen: Good evening. First of all I thank Grupo Financiero Inbursa for inviting me to share this celebration that, without a doubt, will be emotional and endearing for all of you. Congratulations on this fiftieth anniversary. 1 What today, in 2015, is Grupo Financiero Inbursa began to take shape when in 1965 the brokerage house Inversora Bursatil was born, founded by the engineer Carlos Slim who was then only 25 years old. The year 1965 was a very interesting and promising year for Mexico. Our country then had just over 45 million inhabitants. Life expectancy was only 59 years. That year, 1965, saw the highest population growth rate that Mexico would reach in the second half of the twentieth century: 3.5% per year. Also in 1965 Mexico would achieve exceptionally low inflation of only 1.9 percent. The data was so unique that the Bank of Mexico in its Annual Report highlighted it with great emphasis, warning that it contrasted with the inflation of 4.2% per year of the previous year, 1964, and that the low inflation of 1965 was verified despite the fact that for several months a strong increase in demand had been detected driven by private investment and spending. It should be clarified that at that time the best tool available to Mexico to measure inflation was the wholesale price index of Mexico City, since it would not be until 1969 when a more accurate and more representative national consumer price index would be available. 2 In that year of 1965, the Bank of Mexico, under the direction of Mr. Rodrigo Gomez, celebrated its first 40 years of life and in its Annual Report stated that the Gross Domestic Product of the country grew 5.4%, despite being the first year of a new administration, that of President Gustavo Diaz Ordaz, in which according to the six-year cycles there was a retraction of public investment. In addition to highlighting the good figures of inflation and growth of the economy, the Annual Report of the Bank of Mexico of 1965 noted a surprising expansion of bank financing, which that year grew 17.4%, as well as the good performance of the main export product of Mexico at that time, which was cotton, whose sales abroad advanced 24.7% in the year, despite a slight fall in international prices of that commodity. Another point on which the Annual Report of the Bank of Mexico of 1965 based its optimistic tone was the reference to the gross international reserves of the Central Institute itself that closed that year with the bulky figure of 575.2 million dollars. This was a long-awaited fact by the markets and by the general public, since in those times the data of international reserves was only 3 he disclosed on three occasions a year: in the aforementioned annual report of the Bank of Mexico, during the Presidential Report and on the occasion of the annual convention of the bankers. As if this good news were not enough, the multi-cited Report of the Bank of Mexico also commented, and I quote: "An outstanding fact is that public interest in equities continued to be accentuated, which was reflected in the higher relative growth in equity transactions." Thus, Inversora Bursatil, the germ of what is now Grupo Financiero Inbursa, was born at a time that, in light of these data, seems unbeatable: in a country in full growth, with great price stability, with an expanding financial system and a stock market - both in fixed income and equities - taking off at full speed. There is no doubt that the young engineer Carlos Slim and his partners correctly deciphered the growth potential that the Mexican economy offered at that time and acted without delay in accordance with that diagnosis. An attitude that has 4 he was a constant in the various ventures that in these 50 years the engineer Slim has carried out. Considering all this information about the year 1965 one cannot but exclaim: "It was another world!", "it was another Mexico! True, but it wasn't necessarily a better Mexico than the one we have now. It's not just anything to go from a life expectancy at birth of 59 years to a life expectancy of 78 years, as we have now. It is not just anything, despite all that we often lament our unsatisfactory rates of economic growth, that the Gross Domestic Product per capita is today more than six times what it was in 1965. Nor is it anything that today the volume of Mexico's industrial production more than sextuplies what it was in 1965. The differences between yesterday, 50 years ago, and the present are undeniable. And overwhelmingly those differences tell us that we are a better country today than we were in 1965. Even 5 we are an even more promising country than the Mexico of 1965 was. Suffice it to say that the opportunities today for those entering the labor market are exponentially greater, in quantity and quality, than those available 50 years ago. We can list many causes behind this progress: technological and scientific advances, progress in the art and science of running and managing businesses, achievements in designing adequate institutional and governance frameworks, results in terms of democracy and transparency and accountability, fruitful learning in terms of the better functioning of monetary policy - than central banks almost everywhere in the world. we have incorporated into our daily work the globalization of world trade and financial markets; just to mention the most prominent of such causes. The truth is that these differences between the past and the present have not occurred in a magical way or by the inexplicable 6 intervention of some unknown force outside the will of human beings. To a large extent, and for the specific case of Mexico, these differences are the result of the effort, of responsibility, of the talent of millions of Mexicans. These remarkable and undeniable advances must be paid into our balance in favor as a country and as people. Accompanying those factors that have driven change, and basically giving them cohesion and meaning, we can detect a few fundamental principles and values, which have allowed us to progress, despite errors of judgment, temporary setbacks and various adversities. I am referring to principles such as the conviction that there is no achievement without effort, that it is only worth investing in assets that produce greater value in the future, that we must be austere and far-sighted in times of prosperity so that in adverse times the adjustments are less severe and painful, that we must privilege investment in the skills and talents of people to be more productive as 7 society, that episodes of crisis are also times of great opportunity. I do not think I am wrong if I say that these are principles and values, common sense guides, that we share both in the Bank of Mexico and in Inbursa. Nor do I think it is boastful to acknowledge that such principles and values explain, to a large extent, that the respective histories of Grupo Financiero Inbursa on its 50th anniversary, and of Banco de Mexico, on its 90th anniversary, are genuine success stories. With these principles and values, which remain over time, we must face the new challenges of an increasingly complex and uncertain global scenario. Those principles and values remain the best guide as financial markets around the world navigate hitherto uncharted waters. Congratulations on this fiftieth anniversary! Congratulations to Grupo Financiero Inbursa. Thanks a lot. 8
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la celebracin del 50 aniversario de Grupo Financiero Inbursa (S.A.B. de C.V.). 30 de noviembre de 2015  Ingeniero Carlos Slim Hel, Presidente Honorario y Vitalicio del Consejo de Administracin de Grupo Carso,  Licenciado Marco Antonio Slim Domit, Presidente de Grupo Financiero Inbursa,  Licenciado Javier Foncerrada Izquierdo, Director General de Grupo Financiero Inbursa  Familiares y amigos del ingeniero Carlos Slim Hel,  Funcionarios y empleados de Grupo Financiero Inbursa,  Distinguidos invitados,  Seoras y seores: Muy buenas noches. Antes que nada agradezco a Grupo Financiero Inbursa haberme invitado a compartir esta celebracin que, sin duda, resultar emotiva y entraable para todos ustedes. Felicidades por este quincuagsimo aniversario. 1 Lo que hoy, en 2015, es Grupo Financiero Inbursa empez a gestarse cuando en 1965 naci la casa de bolsa Inversora Burstil, fundada por el ingeniero Carlos Slim quien entonces tena slo 25 aos de edad. El ao de 1965 fue para Mxico un ao muy interesante y promisorio. Nuestro pas tena entonces poco ms de 45 millones de habitantes. La esperanza de vida era de slo 59 aos. Ese ao, 1965, se registr la tasa de crecimiento de la poblacin ms alta que Mxico alcanzara en la segunda mitad del siglo XX: 3.5% anual. Tambin en 1965 Mxico lograra una inflacin excepcionalmente baja de slo 1.9 por ciento. El dato fue tan singular que el Banco de Mxico en su Informe Anual lo destac con gran nfasis, advirtiendo que contrastaba con la inflacin de 4.2% anual del ao anterior, 1964, y que la baja inflacin de 1965 se verificaba pese a que desde hace varios meses se haba detectado un fuerte incremento de la demanda impulsado por la inversin y el gasto privados. Debe aclararse que en ese entonces la mejor herramienta de la que dispona Mxico para medir la inflacin era el ndice de precios al mayoreo de la ciudad de Mxico, ya que no sera sino hasta 1969 cuando se dispondra de un ndice nacional de precios al consumidor, ms preciso y ms representativo. 2 En ese ao de 1965, el Banco de Mxico, bajo la direccin de don Rodrigo Gmez, cumpli sus primeros 40 aos de vida y en su Informe Anual consign que el Producto Interno Bruto del pas creci 5.4%, a pesar de ser el primer ao de una nueva administracin, la del Presidente Gustavo Daz Ordaz, en el cual de acuerdo con los ciclos sexenales se registraba una retraccin de la inversin pblica. Adems de destacar las buenas cifras de inflacin y de crecimiento de la economa, el Informe Anual del Banco de Mxico de 1965 haca notar una sorprendente expansin del financiamiento bancario, que ese ao creci 17.4%, as como el buen desempeo del principal producto de exportacin de Mxico en ese entonces, que era el algodn, cuyas ventas al exterior avanzaron 24.7% en el ao, a pesar de una ligera cada en los precios internacionales de ese producto bsico. Otro punto en el que el Informe Anual del Banco de Mxico de 1965 fund su tono optimista fue el referente a las reservas internacionales brutas del propio Instituto Central que cerraron ese ao con la abultada cifra de 575.2 millones de dlares. Este era un dato muy esperado por los mercados y por el pblico en general, ya que en aquellos tiempos el dato de las reservas internacionales slo se 3 divulgaba en tres ocasiones al ao: en el citado informe anual del Banco de Mxico, durante el Informe Presidencial y con motivo de la convencin anual de los banqueros. Como si estas buenas noticias no fuesen suficientes, el multicitado Informe del Banco de Mxico comentaba tambin, y cito textual: Un hecho sobresaliente es que el inters del pblico en los valores de renta variable continu acentundose, lo que se reflej en el mayor crecimiento relativo de las operaciones con esos ttulos. As pues, Inversora Burstil, el germen de lo que hoy es Grupo Financiero Inbursa, naci en un momento que, a lo luz de estos datos, parece inmejorable: en un pas en pleno crecimiento, con gran estabilidad de precios, con un sistema financiero en expansin y un mercado de valores  tanto en renta fija como en renta variable- despegando a toda velocidad. No cabe duda que el joven ingeniero Carlos Slim y sus socios descifraron correctamente el potencial de crecimiento que en ese entonces ofreca la economa mexicana y actuaron sin dilacin de acuerdo con ese diagnstico. Una actitud que ha 4 sido una constante en los diversos emprendimientos que en estos 50 aos ha realizado el ingeniero Slim. Considerando toda esta informacin sobre el ao 1965 uno no puede sino exclamar: Era otro mundo!, era otro Mxico! Cierto, pero no necesariamente era un Mxico mejor que el que ahora tenemos. No es cualquier cosa pasar de una esperanza de vida al nacer de 59 aos a una esperanza de vida de 78 aos, como tenemos ahora. No es cualquier cosa, pese a todo lo que solemos lamentar nuestras poco satisfactorias tasas de crecimiento econmico, que el Producto Interno Bruto per cpita sea hoy ms de seis veces el que era en 1965. Tampoco es cualquier cosa que hoy el volumen de la produccin industrial de Mxico ms que sextuplique el que era en 1965. Las diferencias entre el ayer, de hace 50 aos, y el presente son innegables. Y abrumadoramente esas diferencias nos dicen que somos hoy un mejor pas que en 1965. Incluso 5 somos un pas an ms promisorio de lo que fue el Mxico de 1965. Baste advertir que las oportunidades hoy para quienes se incorporan al mercado laboral son exponencialmente mayores, en cantidad y en calidad, que las que se disponan hace 50 aos. Podemos enumerar muchas causas detrs de este progreso: Los avances tecnolgicos y cientficos, el progreso en el arte y la ciencia de dirigir y administrar empresas, los logros en el diseo de adecuados marcos institucionales y de gobierno, los resultados en materia de democracia y de transparencia y rendicin de cuentas, el fructfero aprendizaje en lo que se refiere al mejor funcionamiento de la poltica monetaria  que los bancos centrales en casi todo el mundo hemos incorporado a nuestro quehacer cotidiano-, la globalizacin del comercio mundial y de los mercados financieros; por slo mencionar las ms destacadas de tales causas. Lo cierto es que esas diferencias entre el pasado y el presente no se han dado de forma mgica o por la inexplicable 6 intervencin de alguna fuerza desconocida al margen de la voluntad de los seres humanos. En gran medida, y para el caso especfico de Mxico, esas diferencias son el resultado del esfuerzo, de la responsabilidad, del talento de millones de mexicanos. Estos avances notables e innegables deben abonarse en nuestro saldo a favor como pas y como personas. Acompaando a esos factores que han impulsado el cambio, y en el fondo dndoles cohesin y sentido, podemos detectar unos cuantos principios y valores fundamentales, que nos han permitido progresar, a pesar de errores de juicio, de retrocesos temporales y de variadas adversidades. Me refiero a principios tales como la conviccin de que no hay logro sin esfuerzo, de que slo vale la pena invertir en activos que produzcan en el futuro mayor valor, de que debemos ser austeros y previsores en tiempos de prosperidad para que en pocas adversas los ajustes sean menos severos y dolorosos, de que debemos privilegiar la inversin en las capacidades y en los talentos de las personas para ser ms productivos como 7 sociedad, de que los episodios de crisis son tambin los tiempos de grandes oportunidades. No creo equivocarme si digo que estos son principios y valores, guas de sentido comn, que compartimos tanto en el Banco de Mxico como en Inbursa. Tampoco creo que sea jactancioso reconocer que tales principios y valores explican, en gran medida, que las respectivas historias de Grupo Financiero Inbursa en su 50 aniversario, y de Banco de Mxico, en su 90 aniversario, sean genuinas historias de xito. Con esos principios y valores, que permanecen a lo largo del tiempo, hemos de afrontar los nuevos desafos de un escenario global cada vez ms complejo e incierto. Esos principios y valores siguen siendo la mejor gua cuando los mercados financieros en todo el mundo navegan en aguas hasta ahora desconocidas. Enhorabuena por este quincuagsimo aniversario! Muchas felicidades a Grupo Financiero Inbursa. Muchas gracias. 8

Title: The contribution of monetary policy to economic stability
text: "THE CONTRIBUTION OF MONETARY POLICY TO ECONOMIC STABILITY". SPEECH BY MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, DURING THE MEETING OF THE INSTITUTE OF BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT OF THE ANAHUAC UNIVERSITY. Mexico City, November 25, 2016.1 I appreciate the kind invitation of the Anahuac University to participate in this event of its Institute of Business Development. The Political Constitution of the United Mexican States establishes that the Bank of Mexico shall be autonomous in the exercise of its functions and its administration, and that its priority objective shall be to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, that is, low and stable inflation. The reasons for this constitutional mandate are based on solid empirical evidence at the national and international levels. An environment of high inflation generates uncertainty and hinders planning over long horizons, adversely affecting investment. In addition, by leading to greater variability in relative prices, the information content of these decreases, leading to higher search costs and marketing margins, and a less efficient allocation of resources. The latter is also impacted by the fact that in an inflationary environment companies and households tend to allocate a greater part of their income to protect themselves from the costs of inflation, at the expense of activities aimed at promoting innovation or increases in productivity. The ability of the financial system to support economic development is affected in an inflationary environment. By virtue of the risks caused by inflation, savers demand higher interest rates and shorter terms for their deposits, which has an impact on more expensive and scarce credit, with the consequent adverse effects on the productive apparatus. Inflation also deteriorates the purchasing power of the population, with even more pernicious effects on fixed-income segments, such as wage earners and pensioners, and the poorest, who are the least 1 The opinions contained herein are strictly personal. 1 trained to defend themselves from this evil. In this way, inflation has a negative impact on the distribution of income. In short, by virtue of the harmful effects of inflation on economic growth, employment and income distribution, and the characteristics of the instruments at the disposal of the Bank of Mexico, the best contribution that our Central Institute can make to the economic development of the country is to strictly comply with its mandate. In other words, price stability is not an objective in itself, but the means through which the Bank of Mexico contributes to the ultimate goal of economic policy, which is to improve the welfare levels of the population. Naturally, the objective of maintaining low and stable inflation also implies that the Bank of Mexico must be prepared to act during episodes of deflation, that is, of generalized and prolonged contraction of prices. As recent experience in many advanced economies shows, such episodes can lead to high costs in terms of output and employment. On the other hand, it is obvious that the above does not represent a cause for concern for the Mexican economy today. The autonomy of a central bank lays the foundation for it to fulfill its mandate in an appropriate manner. This is because it roots credibility in the anti-inflationary commitment and clears up doubts about the possibility that, for political or other reasons, the authorities of a country will implement measures that may result in a rebound in inflation. The international evidence is clear. In both advanced and emerging economies, effective central bank autonomy has a negative relationship with inflation and a positive relationship with economic growth. Likewise, the variability of interest rates, both nominal and real, is lower, and the average real yield offered to depositors is higher, in countries where central banks enjoy greater effective autonomy. It is for this reason that the autonomy granted to the Bank of Mexico since 1994 represents one of the most important institutional changes in the country's recent history. In conducting monetary policy, the Bank of Mexico has relied since 2001 on an inflation-targeting regime. These types of regimes began to gain acceptance among advanced and emerging economies from 2 of the nineties, by virtue of the fact that they allow for a more efficient nominal anchor in the economy, by providing guidance to inflation expectations through a numerical target; assign a central role to transparency, accountability and communication with the public; and in general promote the strengthening of the institutional framework for the implementation of monetary policy. In the case of Mexico, the inflation target has been set at 3 percent, with a variability range of plus/minus one percentage point, given the uncertainty surrounding the fulfillment of the specific target. The conduct of monetary policy in Mexico has been supported by efforts in other areas and, in particular, by fiscal policy. In this regard, it is important to remember that in the mid-eighties the fiscal deficit registered figures around 14 percent of GDP, while public debt came to represent more than 100 percent of this aggregate.2 The trajectory of inflation in Mexico highlights the merits of the strategy adopted to protect the purchasing power of our currency. For most of the period from July 1973 to March 2000, inflation recorded rates of at least two digits, and inflation records of up to three digits were observed for part of that period. In contrast, during the 17 months ending in September 2016, inflation was below 3 percent, an unprecedented achievement in our country, and in the first half of November of this year it registered levels of 3.29 percent. It is important to note that progress in combating inflation goes far beyond the decline in inflation. On the one hand, its volatility, whose effects on confidence and consumption and investment decisions are pernicious, has been considerably reduced. But, in addition, the process of price formation in our economy has shown a structural change, reflected in a sharp decrease in the transfer of the exchange rate to prices, a decrease in the persistence of inflation, and a lower level and dispersion of expectations for it. Thus, the economy has been able to absorb considerable shocks at different stages, without affecting medium- and long-term inflation expectations and, consequently, without being reflected in 2 Figures corresponding to the economic cash deficit and the total net debt of the public sector, whose coverage is lower than those of the Financial Requirements of the Public Sector (RFSP) and its historical balance currently used. 3 a permanent increase in the rate of price growth. In this regard, it should be noted the favorable results that have been obtained in the fight against inflation, despite the fact that from September 2014 to date the peso has depreciated by almost 60 percent against the dollar. Naturally, lower inflation has been accompanied by the benefits to which I referred earlier. It should be noted, by way of example, the collapse in the costs of credit to both households and companies that has resulted from the fall in the inflation rate. In addition, the environment of greater certainty has made it possible to extend the term of these loans and grant them with a fixed interest rate. A similar situation is observed in the case of the government, which not only faces lower borrowing costs, but also a curve of government values whose term has increased from just 3 years in 2000, to 30 today. The environment of lower inflation has also been a determining factor in the development of the financial system and, consequently, in greater and better diversified access of the private sector to sources of financing. I think it is also worth emphasising that the recovery in real wages that we have seen recently is not due to higher nominal increases, but precisely to the decline in inflation. What are the main challenges facing monetary policy at the moment? Economic activity in Mexico is experiencing growth rates below its potential and is in a phase of slowdown. During the first nine months of this year, GDP showed annual growth of 2 percent, which compares with a figure of 2.7 percent in 2015. In this context, our economy is expected to show moderate growth in 2016, although lower than the previous year. It is very difficult at this time to estimate the trajectory of the Mexican economy in 2017 and in subsequent years, given that the result of the presidential elections in the United States and its possible implications have generated an environment of uncertainty particularly marked for the future evolution of the Mexican economy. In this regard, it should be recalled that the new US administration has contemplated the introduction of measures that could affect trade flows and 4 remittances between our two countries. In addition, it has also considered the implementation of an expansionary fiscal policy that, through its effect on inflation expectations, could lead to a cycle of interest rate hikes in the United States faster than anticipated until recently. In any case, the outlook for economic activity in Mexico in 2017 is one of moderate growth, below its potential and with downside risks. Given the phase of the cycle in which the economy finds itself and the rate of economic growth that can reasonably be anticipated for the year, it is not expected that throughout 2017 there will be demand pressures on prices. Meanwhile, headline inflation in Mexico has risen to levels slightly above target, due to an increase in both its core and non-core components. The first has been affected by the transfer of the depreciation of the peso to the prices of goods, while the behavior of the second has been significantly influenced by higher gasoline prices on the northern border and increases in the prices of some agricultural products. Inflation is expected to close the year at levels just above 3 percent. Due to the recent behavior of the exchange rate and the liberalization of gasoline prices, inflation is expected to register higher figures during 2017, although remaining throughout the year within the range of variability established around 3 percent, to converge to levels close to the target in 2018. In this context, inflation expectations from surveys for 2017 have increased, while those of the medium and long term remain relatively stable, although at levels above the target. For their part, the spreads between nominal and real interest rates on long-term government bonds have widened significantly in recent weeks, but it is difficult to extract a precise signal from these indicators, given the deterioration in trading conditions in the bond market, and the difficulties in separating the component of inflation expectations from the different risk factors that also affect this differential. 5 What are the main risks to inflation? As I explained a moment ago, the cyclical position of the economy and the scenario it faces do not make us expect demand pressures on prices in the coming months. On the other hand, the possibility of a rebound in the prices of agricultural products or gasoline, the latter especially under the liberalization measures for the price of this product announced for 2017, is latent. It should be noted that, as observed at previous stages, a shock of this nature should be reflected only temporarily in price behaviour, without giving rise to second-order effects. In this way, the evolution of the exchange rate continues to represent the main risk to inflation. As I will discuss later, these risks have increased in the face of the prospect of a permanent adjustment of the exchange rate to a higher level. The depreciation of the peso's exchange rate against the dollar throughout 2016 is explained by a combination of factors, both external and internal in nature. Among the external ones are the expectation of an increase in interest rates in the United States, events of a geopolitical nature, fluctuations in the price of oil, and the use of the peso as a risk hedging mechanism in other emerging economies or for purely speculative purposes. With regard to domestic factors, the nervousness resulting from the current and prospective state of public finances, and to a lesser extent from the widening of the current account deficit, has also been reflected in the weakening of the peso. More recently, however, the most relevant factor has been the concern stemming from the results of the U.S. presidential election and its potential implications for Mexico. This external shock has affected the parity of our currency through two channels. First, the expectation that the new US administration will carry out an expansionary fiscal policy has given rise to the prospect of downward pressures on bond prices and higher inflation, causing a sharp increase in interest rates in that country. To get a clearer picture of the magnitude of this shock, it is worth noting that the observed increase in 10-year Treasury yields from November 8 to date is greater than that recorded in the equivalent periods of the onset of the global financial crisis in 2008-2009 and the 2013 episode known as "Taper Tantrum". Secondly, 6 has generated a marked increase in uncertainty regarding the direction of economic policy in the United States in the coming years and its possible impact on Mexico. This new scenario makes us expect a depreciation of the real equilibrium exchange rate of the peso, whose magnitude will be more evident as there is greater clarity about the actions that the new US administration intends to carry out, particularly in macroeconomic, commercial and migratory matters. Markets in Mexico have adjusted in response to this shock through movements in interest rates and, as already noted, the exchange rate. Thus, the former have shown a significant increase along the yield curve. The peso's exchange rate against the dollar depreciated by about 12 percent from Nov. 8 to 24, representing its biggest drop for an equivalent period since October 2008. Although the electoral phase in the United States has affected the financial markets of emerging economies in general, its impact on Mexico has been of greater magnitude due to its close ties with the United States. In short, monetary policy in Mexico faces a panorama of economic growth below potential and with a slowdown in economic activity that could even be accentuated in 2017; increased pressures on inflation; and an unusual situation of uncertainty about the outlook for the economy due to external factors. Under these circumstances, and taking into account the mandate of the Bank of Mexico, which as I have already pointed out rests on the premise that the best contribution that our Central Institute can make to the growth of the economy is to maintain low and stable inflation, the Governing Board of the Bank decided at its meeting on November 17 to increase the objective for the overnight interbank interest rate by 50 basis points to a level of 5.25 percent. This measure reinforces the actions, mainly of a preventive nature, that the Institution has been implementing over the last few months, which resulted in 4 previous increases in the reference rate for a total of 175 basis points. Clearly, the magnitude of the external shock we are currently facing highlights the merits of that strategy. 7 What are the factors that are likely to determine the direction of monetary policy in Mexico in the coming months? I would highlight two. Firstly, for the reasons mentioned above, I consider that one of the most important is linked to the risks to inflation arising from the behaviour of the exchange rate. Thus, one of the main challenges will be to ensure that the adjustment of the real exchange rate to a new equilibrium situation is consistent with the convergence of inflation to the target. Secondly, it seems to me that monetary policy in our country is expected to be greatly influenced by the evolution of interest rates in the United States. Considering the close relationship between the two economies, the degree of openness of the Mexican economy and the situation of nervousness in the national and international financial markets, under current conditions an adjustment of the reference rate in the United States without a response from monetary policy in Mexico, could lead to disorderly capital outflows and the consequent risks to inflation and financial stability. The Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico has clearly stated that in the management of monetary policy, all the determinants of inflation must continue to be carefully monitored, in order to respond flexibly and in a timely manner if risks are perceived for the fulfillment of the target. Macroeconomic stability does not depend exclusively on the management of monetary policy. Fiscal policy also plays a key role in this regard. As noted above, the increase in public debt in recent years has led to nervousness in the markets, affecting the trajectory of the exchange rate. The tax authorities have announced a program to adjust public finances for 2017, the implementation of which will stabilize and subsequently reduce the ratio of public debt to GDP. Undoubtedly, the new business plan for PEMEX recently announced plays a central role in these efforts. In addition to the actions taken or in the process of being implemented in fiscal and monetary matters, the Mexican economy has adequate levels of international reserves and a Flexible Credit Line with the Monetary Fund. 8 International that not only gives access, if necessary, to resources of around 84 billion dollars, but also stimulates the adoption of a healthy economic policy framework. Additionally, the Foreign Exchange Commission, composed of representatives of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Bank of Mexico, has announced that it could resort to intervention operations in the exchange market if exceptional conditions arise that justify it, although emphasizing that the anchoring of the value of the national currency will continue to be sought through the preservation of solid economic fundamentals. I think it is worth noting that, as has become clear in the wake of the global financial crisis, macroeconomic stability does not ensure financial stability. This has led to the conclusion that it is imperative that both central banks and other authorities seek mechanisms to efficiently achieve that goal. While monetary policy can make an important contribution to financial stability, it often does not represent the right instrument for this purpose. In fact, this will normally require the coordinated effort of the various authorities responsible for macroeconomic governance and the regulation and supervision of the financial system. In order to address the risks arising from this front, the Financial System Stability Council was created in Mexico in mid-2009. This is an instance of evaluation, analysis and coordination between the various financial authorities of the country, aimed at both identifying risks to financial stability and proposing policies to prevent them or, where appropriate, minimize their impact. It should be noted that as part of these efforts, the Bank of Mexico has significantly strengthened its monitoring and analysis capacity in the area of financial stability. The various episodes of turbulence that have been observed in recent years have not compromised financial stability in Mexico. Banks have sufficient levels of capital and liquidity to face even extreme situations, while the levels of indebtedness of families and companies remain at moderate levels. On the other hand, the indebtedness of the corporate sector abroad does not give rise to a systemic risk, by virtue of the fact that most of the issues have been at long terms and fixed rates, and that in general these companies have natural coverage or 9 financial institutions that mitigate foreign exchange risk. It is also pertinent to note that intermediation through entities and platforms not subject to traditional banking regulation does not represent a significant proportion of total financing. In any case, it will be important to continue to carefully monitor possible risks and vulnerabilities to respond with opportunity, especially taking into account the challenges arising from the external environment in the current conjuncture. To conclude, I would just like to emphasize that although the progress made in combating inflation and in general in macroeconomic stability in Mexico over the last decades has been considerable, the need to strengthen the country's economic fundamentals has increased. Not only do we face a very difficult external environment, but the degree of uncertainty surrounding it is unusually high. In addition, there has been a deterioration in the solvency indicators of our economy. It is therefore imperative that the Bank of Mexico continue to adhere to a prudent monetary policy. Under the current circumstances, strengthening public finances is particularly important. The implementation of the fiscal adjustment package announced for next year, together with PEMEX's new business plan, represent fundamental elements to meet this need. In addition, in the face of an uncertain and changing environment, the authorities must be prepared to make additional efforts if necessary. However, macroeconomic stability is a necessary but not sufficient condition for achieving adequate and sustained economic growth. This will also require maintaining financial stability, and continuing structural adjustment efforts aimed at increasing the efficiency of the economy and strengthening its domestic sources of growth. 10

Para tener una idea ms clara de la magnitud de este choque, vale la pena sealar que el aumento observado en los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 aos del 8 de noviembre a la fecha, es mayor al registrado en los periodos equivalentes del inicio de la crisis financiera global en 2008-2009 y del episodio de 2013 conocido como Taper Tantrum. En segundo lugar, se 6 ha generado un marcado aumento de la incertidumbre respecto del rumbo de la poltica econmica en Estados Unidos en los prximos aos y su posible impacto en Mxico. Este nuevo escenario hace esperar una depreciacin del tipo de cambio real de equilibrio del peso, cuya magnitud ser ms evidente conforme se tenga mayor claridad sobre las acciones que la nueva administracin estadounidense pretende llevar a cabo, particularmente en materia macroeconmica, comercial y migratoria. Los mercados en Mxico se han ajustado en respuesta a este choque a travs de movimientos de las tasas de inters y, como ya se seal, del tipo de cambio. As, las primeras han mostrado un aumento importante a lo largo de la curva de rendimientos. Por su parte, el tipo de cambio del peso frente al dlar se depreci en alrededor de 12 por ciento del 8 al 24 de noviembre, lo que representa su mayor cada para un periodo equivalente desde octubre de 2008. Si bien la fase electoral en Estados Unidos ha incidido en los mercados financieros de las economas emergentes en general, su impacto en la mexicana ha sido de mayor magnitud debido a sus estrechos vnculos con la estadounidense. En suma, la poltica monetaria en Mxico enfrenta un panorama de un crecimiento econmico por debajo de potencial y con una desaceleracin de la actividad econmica que incluso podra acentuarse en 2017; mayores presiones sobre la inflacin; y una situacin inusual de incertidumbre sobre las perspectivas de la economa derivada de factores externos. Bajo estas circunstancias, y tomando en cuenta el mandato del Banco de Mxico, que como ya seal descansa en la premisa de que la mejor contribucin que puede hacer nuestro Instituto Central al crecimiento de la economa es mantener una inflacin baja y estable, la Junta de Gobierno del Banco decidi en su reunin del 17 de noviembre aumentar el objetivo para la tasa de inters interbancaria a un da en 50 puntos base a un nivel de 5.25 por ciento. Esta medida refuerza las acciones, fundamentalmente de naturaleza preventiva, que ha venido implementando la Institucin a lo largo de los ltimos meses, que resultaron en 4 aumentos previos de la tasa de referencia por un total de 175 puntos base. Claramente, la magnitud del choque externo que estamos enfrentando en la actualidad, pone de manifiesto los mritos de esa estrategia. 7 Cules son los factores que probablemente determinarn el rumbo de la poltica monetaria en Mxico en los prximos meses? Yo destacara dos. En primer lugar, por los motivos antes sealados, considero que uno de los ms importantes est vinculado a los riesgos para la inflacin derivados del comportamiento de la paridad cambiaria. As, uno de los retos principales ser asegurar que el ajuste del tipo de cambio real a una nueva situacin de equilibrio, sea congruente con la convergencia de la inflacin a la meta. En segundo lugar, me parece que es de esperarse que la poltica monetaria en nuestro pas se vea muy influida por la evolucin de las tasas de inters en Estados Unidos. Considerando la estrecha relacin entre las dos economas, el grado de apertura de la economa mexicana y la situacin de nerviosismo en los mercados financieros nacionales e internacionales, bajo las condiciones actuales un ajuste de la tasa de referencia en Estados Unidos sin una respuesta de la poltica monetaria en Mxico, podra dar lugar a salidas desordenadas de capital y los consecuentes riesgos para la inflacin y la estabilidad financiera. La Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico ha manifestado con claridad que en el manejo de la poltica monetaria se deber continuar dando un seguimiento cuidadoso a todos los determinantes de la inflacin, para responder con flexibilidad y de manera oportuna de percibirse riesgos para el cumplimiento de la meta. La estabilidad macroeconmica no depende exclusivamente del manejo de la poltica monetaria. La poltica fiscal tambin cumple un papel fundamental a este respecto. Como se seal con anterioridad, el aumento de la deuda pblica en aos recientes ha dado lugar a nerviosismo en los mercados, incidiendo en la trayectoria del tipo de cambio. Las autoridades hacendarias han anunciado un programa de ajuste de las finanzas pblicas para 2017, cuya implementacin permitir estabilizar y posteriormente disminuir el cociente de deuda pblica a PIB. Indudablemente, el nuevo plan de negocios para PEMEX anunciado recientemente desempea un papel central en estos esfuerzos. Adems de las acciones tomadas o en vas de implementacin en materia fiscal y monetaria, la economa mexicana cuenta con niveles adecuados de reservas internacionales y una Lnea de Crdito Flexible con el Fondo Monetario 8 Internacional que no solamente da acceso, en caso de ser necesario, a recursos por alrededor de 84 mil millones de dlares, sino que estimula la adopcin de un marco de poltica econmica sano. Adicionalmente, la Comisin de Cambios, integrada por representantes de la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico y del Banco de Mxico, ha anunciado que podra recurrir a operaciones de intervencin en el mercado cambiario de presentarse condiciones excepcionales que lo justifiquen, si bien enfatizando que el anclaje del valor de la moneda nacional continuar procurndose mediante la preservacin de fundamentos econmicos slidos. Creo que vale la pena sealar que, como se ha hecho patente a raz de la crisis financiera global, la estabilidad macroeconmica no asegura la estabilidad financiera. Esto ha llevado a la conclusin de que es indispensable que tanto los bancos centrales como otras autoridades busquen mecanismos para lograr de manera eficiente ese objetivo. Si bien la poltica monetaria puede contribuir de manera importante a la estabilidad financiera, con frecuencia no representa el instrumento idneo con este fin. De hecho, lo anterior requerir normalmente del esfuerzo coordinado de las diversas autoridades encargadas de la conduccin macroeconmica y de la regulacin y supervisin del sistema financiero. Con el fin de hacer frente a los riesgos que se derivan de este frente, a mediados de 2009 se cre en Mxico el Consejo de Estabilidad del Sistema Financiero. Esta es una instancia de evaluacin, anlisis y coordinacin entre las diversas autoridades financieras del pas, orientada tanto a identificar riesgos para la estabilidad financiera como a proponer polticas para prevenirlos o, en su caso, minimizar su impacto. Cabe sealar que como parte de estos esfuerzos, el Banco de Mxico ha reforzado considerablemente su capacidad de seguimiento y anlisis en el mbito de la estabilidad financiera. Los distintos episodios de turbulencia que se han observado en los ltimos aos no han comprometido la estabilidad financiera en Mxico. La banca cuenta con niveles suficientes de capital y liquidez para enfrentar incluso situaciones extremas, a la vez que los niveles de endeudamiento de familias y empresas se mantienen en niveles moderados. Por su parte, el endeudamiento del sector corporativo en el exterior no da lugar a un riesgo sistmico, en virtud de que la mayor parte de las emisiones han sido a plazos largos y tasas fijas, y de que en general estas empresas cuentan con coberturas naturales o 9 financieras que mitigan el riesgo cambiario. Tambin es pertinente sealar que la intermediacin a travs de entidades y plataformas no sujetas a la regulacin bancaria tradicional no representa una proporcin importante del financiamiento total. En todo caso, ser importante continuar dando un seguimiento cuidadoso a los posibles riesgos y vulnerabilidades para responder con oportunidad, especialmente tomando en cuenta los retos que se derivan del entorno externo en la coyuntura actual. Para concluir, solo quisiera enfatizar que si bien los avances en materia de combate a la inflacin y en general de estabilidad macroeconmica en Mxico a lo largo de las ltimas dcadas han sido considerables, la necesidad de fortalecer los fundamentos econmicos del pas se ha incrementado. No solamente enfrentamos un entorno externo muy difcil, sino que el grado de incertidumbre que lo rodea es inusualmente elevado. Adems, se ha observado un deterioro de los indicadores de solvencia de nuestra economa. Por tanto, es indispensable que el Banco de Mxico contine apegndose a una poltica monetaria prudente. Bajo las circunstancias actuales, el fortalecimiento de las finanzas pblicas es particularmente importante. La implementacin del paquete de ajuste fiscal anunciado para el ao entrante, junto con el nuevo plan de negocios de PEMEX, representan elementos fundamentales para atender esta necesidad. Adems, ante un entorno incierto y cambiante, las autoridades deben estar preparadas para realizar esfuerzos adicionales en caso de ser necesario. Ahora bien, la estabilidad macroeconmica es una condicin necesaria pero no suficiente para lograr un crecimiento econmico adecuado y sostenido. Para ello, se requerir tambin mantener la estabilidad financiera, y continuar con los esfuerzos de ajuste estructural encaminados a incrementar la eficiencia de la economa y fortalecer sus fuentes internas de crecimiento. 10

Title: Awards ceremony: BRAVO Business Awards 2011
text: Remarks by Agustin Carstens, Governor of Banco de Mexico, at the Latin Trade Bravo Business Awards 2011, Miami (Florida), October 28, 2011 Good evening. The Bravo Business Awards is one of the most prestigious, lauded events in Latin America and the Caribbean. This yearly initiative of Latin Trade magazine, which salutes those men and women who have contributed to the regions well-being and growing development, surely deserves to be celebrated. I am truly flattered to be standing with the other fellow recipients of this award, a woman and seven men from the most diverse fields of specialization, and which are part of the mainstays of development in Latin America and the Caribbean. Their daily contributions to our countries health and prosperity are exemplary. I receive this distinction as an incentive to emulate their commitment and diligence. For some it may be surprising, and even unbelievable, the extreme contrast between the turbulent situation some of the worlds main economies are currently facing and the strength the Latin American and Caribbean nations have exhibited during these harsh times. It should really come as no surprise. We have done our job, and we have done it responsibly and diligently. The fruits borne from such efforts are reflected in many of our countries now having stronger fundamentals to face adverse situations. Of course, there is still much to be done and we cannot take anything for granted. The global crisis has indeed affected the region and we cannot isolate ourselves from the turmoil in world financial markets. Let us persevere in everything that has proven us right and that works, such as fiscal responsibility, prudent monetary policy, and strict supervision and intelligent regulation of financial markets. These are the strong foundations 1 on which we need to build the growth and well-being tahat all of our people deserve. The Bravo Business Awards pay tribute to those men and women in Latin America and the Caribbean working to consolidate the underlying strengths of our countries. On this occasion, this event reasserts the message our region can legitimately deliver to the world nowadays: we have not gone wrong and we will persevere in our efforts to continue on the same path. We are not the problem but an important contributor to the solution. Thank you very much for your attention and congratulations. 2

Title: Monetary policy in an environment of inflationary pressures
text: "MONETARY POLICY IN AN ENVIRONMENT OF INFLATIONARY PRESSURES". SPEECH BY MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, AT THE "MEXICO ENERGY AND INFRASTRUCTURE FORUM" OF SCOTIABANK. Mexico City, May 23, 2017.1 Allow me before I begin my presentation to thank the organizers for the invitation to participate in this important forum. The Mexican economy continues to face an international situation that, although it has improved recently, remains complicated and presents a series of challenges of consideration. On the one hand, world economic activity and, of particular importance to Mexico, both global industrial production and international trade, seem to be entering a phase of more accelerated recovery. In addition, the IMF's most recent projections anticipate that from this year there will be a gradual rebound in the global GDP growth rate, which had been trending downward in recent years, to register in 2016 its lowest reading since 2009. The volume of international trade in goods and services is expected to follow a similar pattern, while oil and other energy prices, and in general commodity prices, have continued to recover after reaching multi-year lows in early 2016. 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board as a whole. 1 In the United States, after the slowdown recorded in the first months of this year, the pace of GDP expansion seems to be strengthening, a trend that is expected to continue during the coming quarters. In addition, industrial production is projected to return to positive growth rates from this year, after having contracted during 2015 and 2016. The above, in a context of greater dynamism of its external sector, both on the side of imports and exports. The latter is of great relevance to our country, by virtue of the close ties between Mexico's industrial sector and industrial activity and foreign trade in the United States.2 It is also important to take into account that the signals regarding the direction of economic policy by the current administration of that country have improved, generally perceived a lower probability of extreme scenarios. Despite the above, a high level of uncertainty persists regarding the future evolution of the world economy, as a result of a variety of factors. At the global level, the main concerns revolve around the united Kingdom's exit from the European Union, the potential strengthening of protectionist and anti-globalization positions, macroeconomic and financial vulnerabilities in China and other emerging economies, as well as the latent possibility of geopolitical conflicts in various regions of the world. In relation to the United States, the main sources of uncertainty stem from the process of normalization of policy 2 In the latter case, either through the purchase of inputs for U.S. exports or direct imports of Mexican goods. 2 Monetary by the Federal Reserve and that, despite the improvement observed recently, there is not enough clarity on the future actions of the administration of that country in different areas. Economic activity in Mexico showed during the first quarter of 2017 a better performance than anticipated in the face of the complexities presented by the external environment. On the aggregate demand side, a uniform trajectory of its main components was not observed. Private consumption continued to grow, albeit with signs of slowing, while investment spending continued to weaken. Simultaneously, exports continued to rebound, driven by the recovery of industrial production and foreign trade in the United States, as well as the depreciation that the peso has accumulated in recent years. This divergent trajectory was also observed among the components of aggregate supply, as illustrated by the expansion of the services sector and the stagnation of industrial production, albeit with an upward trend in manufacturing output. Assessing the cyclical position of the economy is made difficult by virtue of the fact that the results of the first quarter are influenced by factors of an arithmetic nature. As this effect fades, the slowdown in economic activity should become more apparent. Overall, projections for GDP growth in 2017 point to a gradual slowdown of the economy year-on-year, but with growth rates for the last 9 months of 2017 significantly lower than those observed throughout 2016. Of 3 In this way, although the slack in the economy seems to have practically disappeared, the anticipated weakening of economic activity should contain the emergence of demand pressures in the coming months. The slowdown in the economy is influenced by several factors. Private consumption spending could be adversely affected by the decline in real wages resulting from the increase in the inflation rate, combined with low levels of household confidence. At the same time, high levels of uncertainty could continue to weigh on the confidence of the business sector, affecting the performance of investment throughout the year. On the other hand, given the expectation of a rebound in industrial production in the United States, including manufacturing, Mexican exports should continue with their recovery process. This would imply a more balanced growth of the different components of aggregate demand, although at a slower pace than that observed in 2016. It should also be noted that a gradual rebound in economic activity is expected in 2018. The pace of price growth has increased significantly during 2017. Both headline and core inflation have shown an upward trend, registering higher-than-expected readings. Thus, so far this year, headline inflation has been well above the upper limit of the range of variability associated with the permanent target of 3 per cent, mainly as a result of a more evident effect of exchange rate depreciation on prices, the adjustment of the quotations of the 4 energy, higher prices of agricultural products, the increase in the minimum wage and, more recently, increases in public transport fares. It should be noted that the percentage of the INPC basket that registers growth rates greater than 4 percent has continued to increase, reaching in April a figure higher than 60 percent in the case of the general and around that figure in the underlying one. Annual inflation is expected to continue to rise in the coming months, to fall in the second half of the year and more sharply from the beginning of 2018. This as a result of the monetary policy actions implemented since the end of 2015, which have resulted in a cumulative increase in the reference interest rate of 375 basis points; the gradual disappearance of the impact of the shocks that have affected inflation; the slowdown in economic activity; and effects of an arithmetic nature. Inflation expectations derived from surveys show a pattern of behavior consistent with this trajectory. However, it should be clarified that expectations for the end of this year have increased significantly and by the end of 2018 are at levels above the target. Long-term inflation expectations obtained through surveys have remained stable at around 3.5 percent. On the other hand, the spreads between nominal and real interest rates on securities 5 Governments have shown volatile behaviour over the past few months, and while they have fallen from the high levels reached at the end of last year and the beginning of last year, they continue to register relatively high figures. It is difficult to obtain an accurate estimate of inflation expectations from market instruments, as these incorporate, in addition to inflation expectations, different risk factors. However, these metrics currently suggest concern in the markets about the evolution of inflation in the long term. In my opinion, the balance of risks for the behavior of inflation during this year and the next retains an upward bias. To date, there appears to have been no second-rate effects on inflation. On the one hand, as I have already pointed out, long-term inflation expectations remain stable. In addition, while the pace of growth in services prices has increased, this is mainly due to the cost effects of higher energy prices, smaller reductions in telecommunications prices and seasonal factors. However, by virtue of the unfavourable trajectory of inflation and the diversity of shocks that have affected it, the risk of second-order effects has been accentuated. To this can be added the possibility of additional pressures on the exchange rate or even a higher transfer coefficient. For its part, the exchange rate of the peso against the dollar has shown a significant appreciation during 2017. In addition to adjustments to the rate of 6 Reference that has been carried out by the Bank of Mexico, to the above has also contributed the implementation of the program of hedges against exchange risks by the Exchange Commission, as well as the perception of lower risks derived from possible actions of the United States administration with harmful effects for Mexico and the situation of public finances in our country. However, the parity of the peso against the dollar continues to show a high sensitivity to information in different areas, and especially to the possible evolution of the economic relationship between Mexico and the United States. By virtue of the above, and the presence of other risk factors, both external and internal, the potential for pronounced fluctuations in the exchange rate of the peso in the coming months remains latent. It is also necessary to take into account that the accumulated depreciation of the peso since September 2014 amounts to more than 40 percent, so the possibility of a lagging effect on prices cannot be ruled out. The factors that have influenced the appreciation of the peso throughout 2017 have also reflected favorably on other financial variables in the economy. In particular, medium- and long-term domestic interest rates, as well as their spread over those of the United States, have declined throughout the year, resulting in a flattening of the yield curve. Likewise, the sovereign solvency indicators of our country have achieved more than reversing the deterioration registered after the completion of last year's electoral process in the United States, although 7 they are still at high levels relative to other economies with similar credit ratings. In short, monetary policy in Mexico faces a scenario with conflicting implications. In one sense, economic activity shows signs of slowing down, so it seems unlikely that there will be demand pressures on prices in the coming months, while long-term inflation expectations remain stable. Conversely, price growth has exceeded expectations, pressures on inflation have continued to generalize, and upside risks to inflation have been heightened. In an environment of this nature, a prudent monetary policy approach is indispensable. Otherwise, the possibility of a loosening of inflation expectations and a loss of credibility in the monetary authority may materialize. In fact, given a scenario in which inflation is expected to remain significantly above the upper limit of the variability range associated with the Bank of Mexico's target for the rest of this year, that further increases in the federal funds rate will be observed in the United States and that an environment of high uncertainty persists with potential effects on the exchange rate and prices, in my view, further adjustments to the reference rate in Mexico are likely to be required in the coming months. 8 On the other hand, the margins of maneuver for the implementation of monetary policy should be expanded as a trajectory of convergence of inflation towards the target becomes evident and the strengthening of public finances derived from the adjustments announced by the fiscal authorities is consolidated. 9
text_original: POLTICA MONETARIA EN UN ENTORNO DE PRESIONES INFLACIONARIAS. INTERVENCIN DEL LIC. JAVIER GUZMN CALAFELL, SUBGOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE MXICO, EN EL MEXICO ENERGY AND INFRASTRUCTURE FORUM DE SCOTIABANK. Ciudad de Mxico, 23 de mayo de 2017.1 Permtanme antes de iniciar mi presentacin agradecer a los organizadores la invitacin a participar en este importante foro. La economa mexicana sigue enfrentando una situacin internacional que, si bien ha mejorado recientemente, se mantiene complicada y presenta una serie de retos de consideracin. Por una parte, la actividad econmica mundial y, de particular importancia para Mxico, tanto la produccin industrial global como el comercio internacional, parecen estar iniciando una fase de recuperacin ms acelerada. Adems, las proyecciones ms recientes del FMI anticipan que a partir de este ao se observe un gradual repunte de la tasa de crecimiento del PIB mundial, misma que haba venido presentando una tendencia a la baja en aos recientes, para registrar en 2016 su menor lectura desde 2009. Se espera que el volumen de comercio internacional de bienes y servicios siga un patrn similar, al tiempo que los precios del petrleo y otros energticos, y en general de las materias primas, han continuado recuperndose tras alcanzar niveles mnimos multianuales a principios de 2016. 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad del autor y no necesariamente representan la postura institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno en conjunto. 1 En Estados Unidos, despus de la desaceleracin registrada en los primeros meses de este ao, el ritmo de expansin del PIB parece estar fortalecindose, tendencia que se espera se mantenga durante los prximos trimestres. Adems, se proyecta que la produccin industrial vuelva a registrar tasas de crecimiento positivas a partir de este ao, tras haberse contrado durante 2015 y 2016. Lo anterior, en un contexto de mayor dinamismo de su sector externo, tanto por el lado de las importaciones como de las exportaciones. Esto ltimo es de gran relevancia para nuestro pas, en virtud de los estrechos vnculos existentes entre el sector industrial de Mxico y la actividad industrial y el comercio exterior en Estados Unidos.2 Tambin es importante tomar en cuenta que las seales en cuanto al rumbo de la poltica econmica por parte de la actual administracin de ese pas han mejorado, percibindose en general una menor probabilidad de escenarios extremos. A pesar de lo anterior, persiste un elevado nivel de incertidumbre respecto de la evolucin futura de la economa mundial, como resultado de una diversidad de factores. A nivel global, las principales preocupaciones giran en torno a la salida del Reino Unido de la Unin Europea, el potencial fortalecimiento de posturas proteccionistas y en contra de la globalizacin, las vulnerabilidades macroeconmicas y financieras en China y otras economas emergentes, as como la latente posibilidad de conflictos de orden geopoltico en diversas regiones del mundo. En relacin a Estados Unidos, las principales fuentes de incertidumbre se derivan del proceso de normalizacin de la poltica 2 En este ltimo caso, ya sea a travs de la compra de insumos para las exportaciones estadounidenses o de importaciones directas de bienes mexicanos. 2 monetaria por parte de la Reserva Federal y de que, no obstante la mejora observada recientemente, no existe suficiente claridad sobre las futuras acciones de la administracin de ese pas en distintos mbitos. La actividad econmica en Mxico mostr durante el primer trimestre de 2017 un desempeo mejor de lo anticipado ante las complejidades que presenta el entorno externo. Por el lado de la demanda agregada, no se observ una trayectoria uniforme de sus principales componentes. El consumo privado continu creciendo, si bien con indicios de desaceleracin, mientras que el gasto en inversin sigui debilitndose. De manera simultnea, las exportaciones continuaron repuntando, impulsadas por la recuperacin de la produccin industrial y el comercio exterior en Estados Unidos, as como la depreciacin que durante los ltimos aos ha acumulado el peso. Esta trayectoria divergente tambin se observ entre los componentes de la oferta agregada, como lo ilustra la expansin del sector de servicios y el estancamiento de la produccin industrial, aunque con una tendencia alcista de la produccin manufacturera. La evaluacin de la posicin cclica de la economa se dificulta en virtud de que los resultados del primer trimestre estn influidos por factores de naturaleza aritmtica. Al diluirse este efecto, la desaceleracin de la actividad econmica debera hacerse ms evidente. En general, las proyecciones para el crecimiento del PIB en 2017 apuntan a una desaceleracin gradual de la economa ao con ao, pero con tasas de crecimiento para los ltimos 9 meses de 2017 significativamente inferiores a las observadas a lo largo de 2016. De 3 esta forma, si bien la holgura en la economa parece haber prcticamente desaparecido, el anticipado debilitamiento de la actividad econmica debera contener el surgimiento de presiones de demanda en los prximos meses. En la desaceleracin de la economa influyen varios factores. El gasto privado en consumo podra verse adversamente afectado por la disminucin de los salarios reales derivada del incremento de la tasa de inflacin, en combinacin con los bajos niveles de confianza de los hogares. Al mismo tiempo, los elevados niveles de incertidumbre podran continuar pesando sobre la confianza del sector empresarial, incidiendo en el comportamiento de la inversin a lo largo del ao. Por otra parte, ante la expectativa de un repunte de la produccin industrial en Estados Unidos, incluyendo la manufacturera, las exportaciones mexicanas deberan continuar con su proceso de recuperacin. Lo anterior implicara un crecimiento ms balanceado de los distintos componentes de la demanda agregada, aunque a un ritmo menor que el observado en 2016. Cabe sealar tambin que se prev un repunte gradual de la actividad econmica en 2018. El ritmo de crecimiento de los precios ha aumentado de manera importante durante 2017. Tanto la inflacin general como la subyacente han mostrado una tendencia al alza, registrando lecturas mayores a las previstas. As, en lo que va del ao, la inflacin general se ha ubicado muy por encima del lmite superior del intervalo de variabilidad asociado al objetivo permanente de 3 por ciento, en lo fundamental como resultado de un efecto ms evidente de la depreciacin cambiaria sobre los precios, el ajuste de las cotizaciones de los 4 energticos, los mayores precios de los productos agropecuarios, el aumento al salario mnimo y, ms recientemente, alzas de las tarifas del transporte pblico. Cabe sealar que el porcentaje de la canasta del INPC que registra tasas de crecimiento mayores a 4 por ciento ha seguido incrementndose, alcanzando en abril una cifra superior a 60 por ciento en el caso de la general y de alrededor de esa cifra en la subyacente. Se espera que la inflacin anual siga aumentando en los prximos meses, para descender en la segunda mitad del ao y ms pronunciadamente a partir de inicios de 2018.
