Title: Accounting as a tool for a central bank
text: ACCOUNTING AS A TOOL FOR A CENTRAL BANK I am pleased to attend the invitation to participate in this important forum organized by the National Banking and Securities Commission, the Mexican Council of Financial Reporting Standards (CINIF) and the International Accounting Standards Board, which as is well known, is the entity that issues the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) in which the best accounting practices at the international level are established. In recent years, the global trend has been oriented to use the aforementioned Standards as a basis for the issuance of financial information, so we can conclude that they have become the global accounting language. Especially since 2008, when the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) accepted that foreign companies that have debt registered in the United States of America can present their Financial Statements in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards and, with it, avoid the reconciliation that is 1 carried out with the American Accounting Principles (USGAAP). To date, 114 countries use this regulatory framework to prepare and issue their financial information, which constitutes 62% of world GDP, in addition to the above, there is a public commitment from other countries to adopt the aforementioned regulatory framework, which with current figures, would represent 96% of world GDP. There is no doubt that the accounting information issued with solid bases is important for the decision-making of the different participants of the economic activity. Central banks are no exception since they are also users who benefit from it and occupy it in their daily work. I will focus on highlighting three different aspects in which accounting information is important for a central bank: (i) First, as a tool that facilitates the promotion of the healthy development of the financial system, by providing more and better information for decision-making; (ii) Second as a tool to be used by the central bank in exercising its role as regulator; and 2 iii) Third party in its capacity as generator and user of its own financial information. I. ACCOUNTING INFORMATION THAT PROMOTES THE HEALTHY DEVELOPMENT OF THE FINANCIAL SYSTEM Our times have been characterized by a growing global economic integration, in a context in which financial markets have been important protagonists, being the channel of communication between the various economies. One of the phenomena linked to this integration is the increasing mobility of capital and the way in which it is transferred with lower costs and frictions. The dynamics of these integration mechanisms encompass not only the purely economic, but also regulation and transparency. In this last point, the quantity and quality of the information that is generated is of vital importance, as well as the ability of the market to make decisions based on it. In this regard, it should be noted that decision-making based on incomplete information could lead to significant costs in terms of social welfare. 3 Comparable financial information across borders and the adoption of best practices at the international level, provide confidence in the financial markets and reduce the costs in the issuance of the same, by not requiring the elaboration of reconciliations between different accounting regulations. In short, International Financial Reporting Standards contribute to the efficient functioning of capital markets. For example, foreign investors interested in investing in debt of a Mexican corporation will be able to obtain better information about the solvency of the issuer if it publishes its financial information in accordance with global standards. In this way, our country is in a position to attract more investors. Ultimately, this positively impacts countries' economic growth by helping capital to be allocated to projects that are most profitable internationally. II. ACCOUNTING INFORMATION AS A TOOL OF THE CENTRAL BANK IN ITS CAPACITY AS REGULATOR In order to maintain the integrity of the markets and the financial system of the different countries, they have chosen to 4 adopt best practices, which translate into requirements, restrictions and guidelines. Derived from the above, it is how the formulation of the Basel Accords arises. This generated a series of national and international regulatory reforms, and initiated the design and implementation of public policies to mitigate risks to financial stability and, in this way, contribute to minimizing uncertainty in the markets. The objective of these agreements is to establish the minimum conditions that a financial institution must satisfy to ensure its permanence and stability. That is why the Bank of Mexico, in the exercise of its powers and in coordination with other authorities, analyzes several aspects of the information of financial institutions, among which are: the minimum levels of accounting capital; the degree of indebtedness; determine responsiveness to operational, credit and market risks; financial costs, and exposure to changes in the fair values of financial instruments. Therefore, accounting is an indispensable tool used by the Bank of Mexico to perform its role as 5 regulatory entity, thus complying with the provisions of its Law, which indicates as purposes to promote the healthy development of the financial system and promote the proper functioning of payment systems. As for payment systems, the Bank of Mexico seeks their proper functioning and focuses on their quality and the necessary actions to promote their use among the population, seeking to make them safe, efficient and cheap. The accounting information derived from payment systems complements the set of elements necessary to make monetary policy decisions, for example, the information on the current assets available to participants in payment systems allows the establishment of optimal mechanisms for injecting liquidity into the market. In this way, by maintaining a stable, efficient, competitive and innovative financial system, as well as an efficient and secure payment system, the Bank of Mexico contributes to sustained economic growth and the general well-being of the population. 6 III. BANCO DE MeXICO AS GENERATOR AND USER OF ACCOUNTING INFORMATION. International Financial Reporting Standards are not fully applicable to central banks, since they carry out operations of a nature different from those of a private company, highlighting in general terms: 1. That the performance of central banks is evaluated primarily in relation to the stability of the purchasing power of the currency and not in relation to the maximization of its assets; 2. That their legal systems impose a particular treatment on specific concepts such as the creation of reserves, delivery of remnants to the Federal Government, valuation of assets, among others, and 3. That they are entrusted with the manufacture of banknotes and metallic coin for their subsequent circulation (not sale). 7 In summary, I can establish that the soundness and efficiency of a central bank's operation is measured with indicators different from those of any other entity. Although there is a growing interest in the information they generate, they are not object, nor could they be regulated with national or international standards, applicable to other types of organizations. This same conclusion was reached by the Central Bank Accounting and Budget Committee1, of the Center for Latin American Monetary Studies (CEMLA)2.Even at the last meeting of the Committee, held this year, a representative of the International Accounting Standards Board attended, who emphasized that the International Financial Reporting Standards were not designed for a central bank, since their objective is that they are adopted by companies that can access capital markets. 1 The current members of the Committee are: Central Bank of the Argentine Republic, Central Bank of Brazil, Bank of the Republic (Colombia), Central Bank of Chile, Central Reserve Bank of Peru, Central Bank of the Dominican Republic, Bank of Spain, Bank of Mexico. 2 Institution that emerged in 1952, during the second Meeting of Technicians of Central Banks of the American Continent, a forum whose purpose serves to exchange information between the monetary authorities. 8 However, in 2013 the Bank of Mexico completed a project called "Strengthening the Regulatory Framework and Transparency of Financial Information of the Bank of Mexico", which managed to incorporate the best accounting practices in the bank's operation, in full compliance with the legal mandate of this Central Institute. The benefits achieved with the aforementioned project are: ? Have an Accounting Regulatory Framework endorsed by the Mexican Council of Financial Reporting Standards, A.C. (CINIF); ? Improve the quantity and quality of the information that is disseminated, in order to make it more accessible to all those interested in it, which helps them to better understand the actions of the Bank of Mexico. The project consisted of the analysis of the operations carried out by the Bank of Mexico according to the following grouping: Corporate operations.- those that in general terms, are common among the different types of entities, including 9 belonging to different sectors of the economy; for example, the purchase of a batch of real estate, machinery and equipment. Particular operations of Central Banking.- those of a Central Bank; for example, monetary issuance and management of international reserves. For this group of operations, a very deep technical analysis was required, bearing in mind at all times the nature of the operation and the legal mandate. In particular, within the Balance Sheet of the Bank of Mexico, the reserve of international assets stands out as the most important asset, which, in accordance with the provisions of its Law, aims to contribute to the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency by compensating for imbalances between the country's foreign exchange income and expenditure. Likewise, these reserves generate certainty and confidence in the country, benefits that cannot be reflected in the Bank's balance sheet. An example is the reduction of country risk, which attracts investors to our market and tends to decrease financing costs. 10 The implementation of the Financial Reporting Standards of the Bank of Mexico took place on January 1, 2014, so currently the priority task is to disseminate its understanding. I would not like to end without first mentioning that this is not the only effort that the Bank of Mexico has made in the matter that brings us together today. Indeed, as I have already mentioned, the dynamics of the integration mechanisms in the markets cause, among other needs, that of having more and better information. Under this premise, the Bank of Mexico seeks to maintain the balance between timely, consistent, comparable and methodologically rigorous information and the elements of judgment on which the general user bases their decisions. In addition, the Bank of Mexico has observed that providing more information, far from generating uncertainty, encourages the confidence of the general public. In this sense, so that the user knows our work, the Central Bank currently publishes on its Web portal, the time series with the weekly and monthly values of international reserves, the main lines of the balance sheet, liquidity in currency 11 foreign, documents that explain what international reserves are their sources and uses, the exchange rate regime, the weekly bulletin on the consolidated statement of account, also called the balance sheet and, quarterly in addition to this, the statements of income and changes in the accounting capital, with their respective notes. In addition, the Bank of Mexico has substantially improved the editing of its financial statements and has adopted best practices at the national and international levels in full compliance with its legal mandate. In this way, the Bank now has, as I have already pointed out, an accounting scheme endorsed by a third party expert in the field, and of recognized prestige: the Mexican Council of Financial Reporting Standards (CINIF), which places it at the forefront of the world, providing information with greater disclosure, detail and frequency than other central banks. Thus, it can be said that as a result of the entry into force of its constitutional autonomy, the Bank of Mexico developed a profound transformation in its dissemination and accountability schemes, in addition to the mechanisms on these matters. 12 the law imposes on him. Due to the above, it has a systematic and poridiodic production of reports, bulletins, surveys, tables and statistical series that make available to the interested public a collection of information, much of it daily update, which helps society evaluate and weigh the performance of the Central Institute. Prior to the constitutional reform that gave it autonomy, the Bank of Mexico made public a minimum proportion of the information it discloses today. To cite one example, the level of international reserves was disclosed only twice a year, while today that level is published weekly and it is even possible to infer it daily. It is also very illustrative to point out the determinations adopted by the Governing Board, in the sense of publishing quarterly reports (on inflation, economic evolution and the behavior of economic indicators in the country, as well as the execution of monetary policy) and the Report on the Financial System (analysis of the risks that could constitute a threat to the stability of the Financial System), as well as the minutes of the sessions in which decisions related to monetary policy are made. 13 IV. CONCLUSION I am convinced that the constant work of the Bank of Mexico to fully comply with its mandate and seek to adopt and develop best practices in various areas has given important benefits to the country. Aware of the challenges ahead, as well as the importance of having complete and robust information for the proper functioning of the markets, the Bank of Mexico is at the forefront of the world by having an accounting scheme endorsed by a third party expert in the field and of recognized prestige, as well as for having implemented a policy of disclosure of information even more detailed and frequent than that followed by other central banks. 14
text_original: LA CONTABILIDAD COMO HERRAMIENTA PARA UN BANCO CENTRAL Me complace atender la invitacin a participar en este importante foro organizado por la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, el Consejo Mexicano de Normas de Informacin financiera (CINIF) y el International Accounting Standards Board, que como es bien sabido, es la entidad que emite las Normas Internacionales de Informacin Financiera (IFRS por sus siglas en ingls) en las cuales se establecen las mejores prcticas contables a nivel internacional. En los ltimos aos, la tendencia mundial se ha orientado a utilizar las citadas Normas como base para la emisin de la informacin financiera, por lo que podemos concluir que se han convertido en el lenguaje contable mundial. Mxime a partir de 2008, fecha en la cual la Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) acept que las empresas extranjeras que tienen deuda registrada en los Estados Unidos de Amrica puedan presentar sus Estados Financieros ajustndose a las Normas Internacionales de Informacin Financiera y, con ello, evitar la conciliacin que se 1 llevaba a cabo con los Principios Contables Americanos (USGAAP por sus siglas en ingls). Al da de hoy, 114 pases utilizan este marco normativo para elaborar y emitir su informacin financiera, lo cual constituye el 62% del PIB mundial, aunado a lo anterior, existe el compromiso pblico de otros pases para adoptar el referido marco normativo, lo que con cifras actuales, representara el 96% del PIB mundial. No cabe duda que la informacin contable emitida con bases slidas, es importante para la toma de decisiones de los distintos participantes de la actividad econmica. Los bancos centrales no son la excepcin puesto que tambin son usuarios que se benefician de la misma y la ocupan en su quehacer cotidiano. Me enfocar a resaltar tres distintas vertientes en las cuales la informacin contable es importante para un banco central: i) Primero como herramienta que facilita la promocin del sano desarrollo del sistema financiero, al contar con mayor y mejor informacin para la toma de decisiones; ii) Segundo como herramienta a ser utilizada por el banco central al ejercer su funcin de regulador, y 2 iii) Tercero en su calidad de generador y usuario de su propia informacin financiera. I. LA INFORMACIN CONTABLE QUE PROMUEVE EL SANO DESARROLLO DEL SISTEMA FINANCIERO Nuestros tiempos se han caracterizado por una creciente integracin econmica mundial, en un contexto en el cual los mercados financieros han sido protagonistas importantes, al ser la va de comunicacin entre las diversas economas. Uno de los fenmenos vinculados a esta integracin, es la creciente movilidad de capitales y la forma en que stos se transfieren con menores costos y fricciones. La dinmica de estos mecanismos de integracin abarca no slo lo meramente econmico, sino tambin la regulacin y la transparencia. En este ltimo punto es de vital importancia la cantidad y calidad de la informacin que se genera, as como la capacidad del mercado para tomar decisiones con base en ella. En este sentido, cabe sealar que la toma de decisiones basadas en informacin incompleta podra dar lugar a importantes costos en trminos de bienestar social. 3 La informacin financiera comparable a travs de las fronteras y la adopcin de las mejores prcticas a nivel internacional, proveen confianza en los mercados financieros y disminuyen los costos en la emisin de la misma, al no requerir la elaboracin de conciliaciones entre distintas normatividades contables. En sntesis, las Normas Internacionales de Informacin Financiera contribuyen al funcionamiento eficiente de los mercados de capitales. Por ejemplo, los inversionistas extranjeros interesados en invertir en deuda de un corporativo mexicano, podrn allegarse de mejor informacin sobre la solvencia del emisor si ste publica su informacin financiera de acuerdo con estndares mundiales. De este modo, nuestro pas est en posicin de atraer a ms inversionistas. En ltima instancia, esto impacta positivamente en el crecimiento econmico de los pases al contribuir a que el capital se asigne a los proyectos que tienen mayor rentabilidad a nivel internacional. II. LA INFORMACIN CONTABLE COMO HERRAMIENTA DEL BANCO CENTRAL EN SU CARCTER DE REGULADOR Con el objetivo de mantener la integridad de los mercados y del sistema financiero de los distintos pases, stos han optado por 4 adoptar las mejores prcticas, mismas que se traducen en requisitos, restricciones y directrices. Derivado de lo anterior, es como surge la formulacin de los Acuerdos de Basilea. Ello gener una serie de reformas regulatorias nacionales e internacionales, e inici el diseo e implementacin de polticas pblicas para mitigar los riesgos para la estabilidad financiera y, de esa manera, contribuir a minimizar la incertidumbre en los mercados. El objetivo de estos acuerdos es establecer las condiciones mnimas que una entidad financiera debe satisfacer para asegurar su permanencia y estabilidad. Es por ello que el Banco de Mxico, en el ejercicio de sus atribuciones y en coordinacin con otras autoridades analiza varios aspectos de la informacin de las entidades financieras, entre los cuales destacan: los niveles mnimos de capital contable; el grado de endeudamiento; determinar la capacidad de respuesta ante los riesgos operativos, de crdito y de mercado; los costos financieros, y la exposicin ante variaciones en los valores razonables de los instrumentos financieros. Por tanto, la contabilidad es una herramienta indispensable que utiliza el Banco de Mxico para desempear su funcin como 5 entidad reguladora, cumpliendo as con lo establecido en su Ley, misma que seala como finalidades el promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. En cuanto a los sistemas de pagos, el Banco de Mxico procura su buen funcionamiento y se enfoca en su calidad y en las acciones necesarias para promover su uso entre la poblacin, buscando que stos sean seguros, eficientes y baratos. La informacin contable derivada de los sistemas de pagos complementa el conjunto de elementos necesarios para tomar decisiones de poltica monetaria, por ejemplo, la informacin sobre los activos circulantes con que cuentan los participantes en los sistemas de pagos permite establecer mecanismos ptimos de inyeccin de liquidez en el mercado. De esta forma, manteniendo un sistema financiero estable, eficiente, competitivo e innovador, as como un sistema de pagos eficiente y seguro, el Banco de Mxico contribuye al crecimiento econmico sostenido y al bienestar general de la poblacin. 6 III. BANCO DE MXICO COMO GENERADOR Y USUARIO DE LA INFORMACIN CONTABLE. Las Normas Internacionales de Informacin Financiera no le son aplicables de manera ntegra a los bancos centrales, toda vez que realizan operaciones de naturaleza distinta a las de una empresa de la iniciativa privada, destacando en trminos generales: 1. Que el desempeo de los bancos centrales se evala fundamentalmente en relacin con la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda y no respecto a la maximizacin de su patrimonio; 2. Que sus ordenamientos legales les imponen un tratamiento particular a conceptos especficos tales como creacin de reservas, entrega de remanentes al Gobierno Federal, valuacin de activos, entre otros, y 3. Que tienen encomendada la fabricacin de billetes y moneda metlica para su posterior puesta en circulacin (no venta). 7 En sntesis, puedo establecer que la solidez y eficiencia de la operacin de un banco central se mide con indicadores distintos a los de cualquier otra entidad. Si bien hay un inters creciente en la informacin que generan, no son objeto, ni podran ser normados con los estndares nacionales o internacionales, aplicables a otro tipo de organizaciones. A esta misma conclusin arrib el Comit de Contabilidad y Presupuesto de Banca Central1, del Centro de Estudios Monetarios Latinoamericanos (CEMLA)2.Incluso, en la ltima reunin del Comit, realizada en el presente ao, asisti un representante del International Accounting Standards Board , quien enfatiz que las Normas Internacionales de Informacin Financiera no fueron diseadas para un banco central, toda vez que su objetivo es el que sean adoptados por empresas que puedan acceder a mercados de capital. 1 Los miembros Actuales del Comit son: Banco Central de la Repblica Argentina, Banco Central de Brasil, Banco de la Repblica (Colombia), Banco Central de Chile, Banco Central de Reserva del Per, Banco Central de la Repblica Dominicana, Banco de Espaa, Banco de Mxico. 2 Institucin surgida en 1952, durante la segunda Reunin de Tcnicos de Bancos Centrales del Continente Americano, foro cuyo objeto sirve para intercambiar informacin entre las autoridades monetarias. 8 No obstante, el Banco de Mxico concluy en 2013 un proyecto denominado Fortalecimiento del Marco Normativo y de la Transparencia de la Informacin Financiera del Banco de Mxico, el cual logr incorporar las mejores prcticas contables en la operacin del Banco, con pleno apego al mandato legal que tiene este Instituto Central. Los beneficios alcanzados con el citado proyecto son:  Contar con un Marco Normativo Contable avalado por el Consejo Mexicano de Normas de Informacin Financiera, A.C. (CINIF);  Mejorar la cantidad y calidad de la informacin que se difunde, con el fin de hacerla ms accesible a todos los interesados en ella, lo que coadyuva a que comprendan mejor el actuar del Banco de Mxico. El proyecto consisti en el anlisis de las operaciones realizadas por el Banco de Mxico conforme a la siguiente agrupacin: Operaciones corporativas.- aqullas que en trminos generales, son comunes entre los diferentes tipos de entidades, incluso 9 pertenecientes a distintos sectores de la economa; por ejemplo, la compra de una partida de inmuebles, maquinaria y equipo. Operaciones particulares de Banca Central.- aqullas propias de un Banco Central; por ejemplo, la emisin monetaria y administracin de reservas internacionales. Para este grupo de operaciones se requiri de un anlisis tcnico muy profundo, teniendo en todo momento presente la naturaleza de la operacin y el mandato legal. En particular, dentro del Balance General del Banco de Mxico, destaca la reserva de activos internacionales como el activo de mayor importancia, la cual, conforme a lo establecido en su Ley, tiene por objeto coadyuvar a la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional mediante la compensacin de desequilibrios entre los ingresos y egresos de divisas del pas. Asimismo, estas reservas generan certeza y confianza en el pas, beneficios que no se pueden reflejar en el balance general del Banco. Un ejemplo es la reduccin del riesgo pas, que atrae inversionistas a nuestro mercado y tiende a disminuir los costos de financiamiento. 10 La implantacin de las Normas de Informacin Financiera del Banco de Mxico, tuvo lugar el 1 de enero de 2014, por lo que actualmente la tarea prioritaria es difundir su entendimiento. No quisiera terminar sin antes mencionar que este no es el nico esfuerzo que ha hecho el Banco de Mxico en la materia que hoy nos congrega. Efectivamente, como ya lo he mencionado anteriormente, la dinmica de los mecanismos de integracin en los mercados provoca entre otras necesidades, la de contar con ms y mejor informacin. Bajo esta premisa, el Banco de Mxico busca mantener el equilibrio entre la informacin oportuna, consistente, comparable y elaborada con rigor metodolgico y los elementos de juicio en los que el usuario general sustenta sus decisiones. Aunado a ello, el Banco de Mxico ha observado que el proporcionar mayor informacin lejos de generar incertidumbre, incentiva la confianza del pblico en general. En este sentido para que el usuario conozca nuestro quehacer, el Banco Central publica actualmente en su portal Web, las series tiempo con los valores semanales y mensuales de las reservas internacionales, los principales renglones del balance general, la liquidez en moneda 11 extranjera, documentos que explican qu son las reservas internacionales sus fuentes y usos, el rgimen cambiario, el boletn semanal sobre el estado de cuenta consolidado, tambin llamado balance general y, trimestralmente de manera adicional a ste, los estados de resultados y de cambios en el capital contable, con sus respectivas notas. Adicionalmente, el Banco de Mxico ha mejorado sustantivamente la edicin de sus estados financieros y ha adoptado las mejores prcticas a nivel nacional e internacional con pleno apego a su mandato legal. De este modo, el Banco cuenta ahora, como ya lo seal, con un esquema contable avalado por un tercero experto en la materia, y de reconocido prestigio: el Consejo Mexicano de Normas de Informacin Financiera (CINIF), lo que lo coloca a la vanguardia mundial, proporcionando informacin con mayor revelacin, detalle y frecuencia que otros bancos centrales. As, puede afirmarse que a raz de la entrada en vigor de su autonoma constitucional, el Banco de Mxico desarroll una profunda transformacin en sus esquemas de difusin y rendicin de cuentas, en adicin a los mecanismos que sobre esas materias 12 le impone la ley. En razn de lo anterior, cuenta con una produccin sistemtica y poridica de informes, boletines, encuestas, cuadros y series estadsticas que ponen al alcance del pblico interesado un acervo de informacin, mucha de ella de actualizacin diaria, que coadyuva a que la sociedad evale y pondere la actuacin del Instituto Central. Previo a la reforma constitucional que le dio autonoma, el Banco de Mxico haca pblica una mnima proporcin de la informacin que hoy divulga. Por citar un ejemplo, el nivel de las reservas internacionales se daba a conocer slo dos veces por ao, mientras que hoy ese nivel se publica semanalmente e incluso es posible inferirlo diariamente. Tambin resulta muy ilustrativo, sealar las determinaciones que adopt la Junta de Gobierno, en el sentido de publicar informes trimestrales (sobre la inflacin, la evolucin econmica y el comportamiento de indicadores econmicos del pas, as como la ejecucin de la poltica monetaria) y el Reporte Sobre el Sistema Financiero (anlisis de los riesgos que podran constituir una amenaza para la estabilidad del Sistema Financiero), as como las minutas de las sesiones en las que se toman decisiones relacionadas con la poltica monetaria. 13 IV. CONCLUSIN Estoy convencido de que el trabajo constante del Banco de Mxico para dar cabal cumplimiento a su mandato y procurar adoptar y desarrollar las mejores prcticas en diversos mbitos, le ha dado importantes beneficios al pas. Consciente de los retos por delante, as como de la importancia de contar con informacin completa y robusta para el correcto funcionamiento de los mercados, el Banco de Mxico est a la vanguardia mundial al tener un esquema contable avalado por un tercero experto en la materia y de reconocido prestigio, as como por haber implementado una poltica de divulgacin de informacin incluso ms detallada y frecuente que la seguida por otros bancos centrales. 14

Title: Presentation of the Rodrigo Gmez 2011 Central Banking Award, awarded by the Center for Latin American Monetary Studies (CEMLA) to Dr. Daniel Smano
text: 1 Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, at the presentation of the Rodrigo Gomez Central Banking Award 2011, awarded by the Center for Latin American Monetary Studies (CEMLA) to Dr. Daniel Samano. Thursday, July 19, 2012, Mexico City  Dear Governors and Central Bank Officials.  Representatives of international organizations, financial institutions, research centers and universities.  Mr. Javier Guzman Calafell, General Director of CEMLA.  Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, I thank CEMLA and its Director General, Javier Guzman, for organizing this ceremony to award the Rodrigo Gomez Central Banking Award 2011, instituted by this Center in 1970 in order to stimulate research and better knowledge of substantive central banking issues for the Latin American and Caribbean region. As Mr. Guzman already mentioned, this Award was created by CEMLA in order to honor the memory of Don Rodrigo Gomez, just in the year in which that enthusiastic promoter of the creation of CEMLA died and who was, as Mr. Guzman also recalled, not only General Director of the Bank of Mexico from 1952 to 1970, but perhaps the main architect of a long period of accelerated economic growth in Mexico with great price stability. To such a degree is recognized the contribution of Don Rodrigo Gomez to the so-called Mexican miracle that years later Arnold Harberger - great economist and teacher of several Nobel Prizes in Economics at the University of Chicago -, wrote: "For more than a decade before the death of Rodrigo Gomez, the Mexican economy grew much more, had much lower inflation, greater social mobility and greater improvements in the benefits of the poor, and greater social peace - with Rodrigo Gomez and without oil - than it had in its subsequent period of equality. 1 2 duration - with oil and without Rodrigo Gomez". Don Rodrigo Gomez was also an enthusiastic promoter of integration and cooperation in Latin America and a great promoter of economic research, and that it was complemented by teaching. Hence, one of his main initiatives was to create an organization aimed at studying monetary and financial problems from the perspective and circumstances prevailing in the countries of the region, which bore fruit with the establishment of CEMLA in 1952, an event that endorsed the Latin American vocation of Don Rodrigo. Having decided that this Central Banking Award bears the name of Don Rodrigo Gomez, as well as the fact that the Auditorium of the CEMLA headquarters building bears the name of this illustrious Mexican central banker, is clearly a fair recognition of who had the vision and enthusiastically encouraged the establishment of this Institution, as a center that radiates knowledge, experiences and cooperation among all the central banks of Latin America. We have seen with pleasure that, as part of the Strategic Plan 2011-2013 of CEMLA, the Rodrigo Gomez Award has been strengthened and given new impetus, which has resulted in a growth in the quantity of the works presented and their quality. For the Bank of Mexico, it is a source of pride that one of its officials, Dr. Daniel Samano, has obtained this Award on this occasion. This highlights the importance of economic research activities for this Central Institute and is a recognition of the quality of its human capital. The institution that I chair is convinced, as was Mr. Rodrigo Gomez, that a better understanding of the economic and financial issues of relevance to the activities of central banks requires, on the one hand, to have researchers with a solid academic background of vanguard, and on the other, that they have the ability to adapt the analysis and evaluation. 2 3 from these topics to the reality and circumstances of each country. That this knowledge be translated into public policies and, specifically in the field of monetary policy, into initiatives that are both practical and solidly founded. These are precisely the essential aspects that have guided the Rodrigo Gomez Central Banking Award since its creation. The article "In the Search for Macro-Prudential Policy Tools" by Daniel Samano explores in the framework of a macroeconomic model whether two policy instruments, specifically, a rule on the capital requirements of banks in combination with a Taylor rule, lead to better macroeconomic performance than a Taylor rule alone. The results of the article suggest that with the inclusion of a second instrument, in this case of a macro-prudential nature, the authority can obtain significant gains in terms of the macroeconomic and financial performance of the economy. Specifically, the use of two instruments of economic policy, used in a coordinated manner, allows the authority to efficiently mitigate deviations of the product from its potential and inflation from its objective in addition to reducing the volatility of financial variables in the economy. Moreover, the article exposes how through the use of the macro-prudential instrument it is possible for the authority to partially isolate shocks that are brewing in the financial sector of the economy, thus reducing their adverse effects on macroeconomic variables. This issue, without a doubt, is of great interest and topicality for central banks, not only in the region but throughout the world. Here is a brief portrait of the winner of the 2011 Rodrigo Gomez Award: Dr. Daniel Samano Penaloza has a degree in Economics from the Autonomous Technological Institute of Mexico (ITAM), and a Master's Degree in Theory 3 4 Economics at ITAM, as well as a Master's Degree in Economics at the University of Minnesota. He also obtained a Ph.D. in Economics from the University of Minnesota in 2009 under the advice of Dr. Narayana Kocherlakota. He currently teaches Monetary Theory and Policy at ITAM and in the past has taught various courses, including Macroeconomic Policy at the University of Minnesota. Also, during 2010 he was a member of the "Macroeconomic Assessment Group" of the Bank for International Settlements in Basel, Switzerland. Dr. Samano has also been a Visiting Researcher at the Federal Reserve in Minneapolis, United States. Since 2001 he has worked at the Bank of Mexico in various responsibilities and positions as an Economic Analyst, Economic Researcher and currently holds the position of Manager of Monetary Research in the General Directorate of Economic Research. Dr. Samano has participated in seminars in national and international forums. The latter include presentations at the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic, Central Bank of Brazil, Bank of Canada, Central Bank of South Korea, Central Bank of Costa Rica, Bank of France, Bank of England and the Bank of Italy. Dr. Samano is the author of several working papers for the Bank of Mexico. I congratulate Dr. Samano on this important recognition and I hope that he will continue to deepen the analysis of monetary and financial issues relevant to the activities of central banking. I take this opportunity to reiterate the support of the Bank of Mexico for the activities of CEMLA and to continue strengthening this Award as well as the promotion of research and information exchange activities among the monetary and financial authorities of the region. Thanks a lot. 4
text_original: 1 Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, en la entrega del Premio de Banca Central Rodrigo Gmez 2011, otorgado por el Centro de Estudios Monetarios Latinoamericanos (CEMLA) al doctor Daniel Smano. Jueves 19 de julio de 2012, Mxico, D.F.  Estimados Gobernadores y funcionarios de bancos centrales.  Representantes de organismos internacionales, instituciones financieras, centros de investigacin y universidades.  Seor licenciado Javier Guzmn Calafell, Director General del CEMLA.  Seoras y seores: Antes que nada agradezco al CEMLA y a su Director General, Javier Guzmn, por organizar esta ceremonia de entrega del Premio de Banca Central Rodrigo Gmez 2011, instituido por este Centro en 1970 con el fin de estimular la investigacin y el mejor conocimiento de temas sustantivos de banca central para la regin de Amrica Latina y el Caribe. Como ya mencion el licenciado Guzmn este Premio fue creado por el CEMLA con el fin de honrar la memoria de Don Rodrigo Gmez, justo en el ao en que falleci ese entusiasta promotor de la creacin del CEMLA y quin fue, como tambin record el licenciado Guzmn, no slo Director General del Banco de Mxico de 1952 a 1970, sino tal vez el principal artfice de una larga poca de crecimiento econmico acelerado en Mxico con gran estabilidad de precios. A tal grado es reconocida la aportacin de don Rodrigo Gmez al llamado milagro mexicano que aos ms tarde Arnold Harberger  gran economista y maestro de varios premios Nobel de Economa en la Universidad de Chicago-, escribi: Por ms de una dcada anterior a la muerte de Rodrigo Gmez, la economa mexicana creci mucho ms, tuvo mucho menor inflacin, mayor movilidad social y mayores mejoras en los beneficios de los pobres, y mayor paz social  con Rodrigo Gmez y sin petrleo-, del que tuvo en su periodo subsiguiente de igual 1 2 duracin con petrleo y sin Rodrigo Gmez. Don Rodrigo Gmez, adems, fue un promotor entusiasta de la integracin y cooperacin en Amrica Latina y un gran impulsor de la investigacin econmica, y de que sta fuese complementada por la enseanza. De ah que una de sus principales iniciativas fuese la de crear un organismo orientado a estudiar los problemas monetarios y financieros desde la perspectiva y las circunstancias prevalecientes en los pases de la regin, la cual fructific con el establecimiento del CEMLA en 1952, evento que refrend la vocacin latinoamericanista de Don Rodrigo. El haber decidido que este Premio de Banca Central lleve el nombre de Don Rodrigo Gmez, as como el hecho de que el Auditorio del edificio sede del CEMLA lleve el nombre de este banquero central mexicano ilustre, es a todas luces un justo reconocimiento a quin tuvo la visin y alent con entusiasmo el establecimiento de esta Institucin, como un centro que irradie conocimientos, experiencias y cooperacin entre todos los bancos centrales de Amrica Latina. Hemos visto con agrado que, como parte del Plan Estratgico 2011-2013 del CEMLA, se ha fortalecido y dado nuevo mpetu al Premio Rodrigo Gmez, lo que ha redundado en un crecimiento de la cantidad de los trabajos presentados y de la calidad de los mismos. Para el Banco de Mxico es motivo de orgullo que uno de sus funcionarios, el doctor Daniel Smano, haya obtenido en esta ocasin este Premio. Ello pone de relieve la importancia que para este Instituto Central tienen las actividades de investigacin econmica y es un reconocimiento a la calidad de su capital humano. La institucin que presido est convencida, como lo estuvo don Rodrigo Gmez, de que una mejor comprensin de los temas econmicos y financieros de relevancia para las actividades de los bancos centrales requiere, por una parte, de contar con investigadores con una slida formacin acadmica de vanguardia, y por la otra, de que stos tengan la capacidad de adaptar el anlisis y evaluacin 2 3 de estos tpicos a la realidad y circunstancias de cada pas. Que dichos conocimientos se traduzcan en polticas pblicas y, especficamente en el mbito de la poltica monetaria, en iniciativas que a la vez resulten prcticas y slidamente fundadas. Estos son justamente los aspectos esenciales que han guiado al Premio de Banca Central Rodrigo Gmez desde su creacin. En el artculo En la Bsqueda de Herramientas de Poltica Macro-prudencial de Daniel Smano se explora en el marco de un modelo macroeconmico si dos instrumentos de poltica, especficamente, una regla sobre los requerimientos de capital de la banca en combinacin con una regla de Taylor, conllevan a un mejor desempeo macroeconmico que una regla de Taylor sola. Los resultados del artculo sugieren que con la inclusin de un segundo instrumento, en este caso de ndole macro-prudencial, la autoridad puede obtener ganancias significativas en trminos del desempeo macroeconmico y financiero de la economa. Especficamente, el uso de dos instrumentos de poltica econmica, empleados de manera coordinada permite a la autoridad mitigar eficientemente desviaciones del producto de su potencial y de la inflacin de su objetivo adems de lograr disminuir la volatilidad de las variables financieras en la economa. Ms aun, el artculo expone cmo mediante el uso del instrumento macro-prudencial es posible que la autoridad logre aislar parcialmente choques que se gestan en el sector financiero de la economa reduciendo as sus efectos adversos sobre las variables macroeconmicas. Este tema, sin duda, es de sumo inters y actualidad para los bancos centrales, no solamente de la regin sino de todo el mundo. A continuacin les ofrezco una breve semblanza del ganador del Premio Rodrigo Gmez 2011: El doctor Daniel Smano Pealoza es licenciado en Economa por el Instituto Tecnolgico Autnomo de Mxico (ITAM), realiz una Maestra en Teora 3 4 Econmica en el ITAM, as como una Maestra en Economa en la Universidad de Minnesota. Adems obtuvo el Doctorado en Economa por la Universidad de Minnesota en 2009 bajo la asesora del Dr. Narayana Kocherlakota. Actualmente imparte la clase de Teora y Poltica Monetaria en el ITAM y en el pasado se ha desempeado como profesor de diversos cursos, entre ellos Poltica Macroeconmica en la Universidad de Minnesota. Asimismo, durante 2010 fue Miembro del Macroeconomic Assessment Group del Banco de Pagos Internacionales en Basilea, Suiza. El doctor Smano tambin ha sido Investigador Visitante en la Reserva Federal de Minneapolis, Estados Unidos. A partir de 2001 ha laborado en el Banco de Mxico en diversas responsabilidades y posiciones como Analista Econmico, Investigador Econmico y actualmente desempea el cargo de Gerente de Investigacin Monetaria en la Direccin General de Investigacin Econmica. El doctor Smano ha participado en seminarios en foros nacionales e internacionales. Entre estos ltimos destacan ponencias en el Banco Central de la Repblica Argentina, Banco Central de Brasil, Banco de Canad, Banco Central de Corea del Sur, Banco Central de Costa Rica, Banco de Francia, Banco de Inglaterra y el Banco de Italia. El doctor Smano es autor de varios documentos de trabajo del Banco de Mxico. Felicito al doctor Smano por este importante reconocimiento y hago votos porque contine profundizando en el anlisis de los temas monetarios y financieros relevantes para las actividades de la banca central. Aprovecho la ocasin para reiterar el apoyo del Banco de Mxico a las actividades del CEMLA y continuar fortaleciendo este Premio as como la promocin de las actividades de investigacin y de intercambio de informacin entre las autoridades monetarias y financieras de la regin. Muchas gracias. 4

Title: Objective and operation of the Bank of Mexico
text: OBJECTIVE AND OPERATION OF THE BANK OF MEXICO Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, at the closing of the Banco de Mexico Chair, held at the Autonomous Metropolitan University, July 1, 2010. It is an honor to exhibit at the closing of the Banco de Mexico Chair taught in recent weeks at the Autonomous Metropolitan University (UAM). I appreciate the opportunity to participate in this program aimed at explaining the activities of our Central Bank to the students of this prestigious house of studies. With only 35 years of having started its work, the UAM is widely recognized as an academic institution of excellence, training professionals who occupy key positions in the public and private sectors. As its motto expresses it, "Open House to Time", the UAM confirms that learning and the dissemination of knowledge are the essential components for people to grow and transcend in the environment of the common home, which is the homeland, and which is also, ultimately, our planet. I would like to share with you some reflections on the way in which the Bank of Mexico carries out the task of ensuring price stability, which is an indispensable condition for raising the well-being of the population and promoting sustained economic growth. As in other parts of the world, Mexico has a fiat currency whose acceptance is not based on its intrinsic value or the convertibility of the same currency to some precious metal, such as gold or silver, at a predetermined price. Confidence in the Mexican peso is based on the public's expectation that its holding allows it to buy a certain set of goods and services and that, over time, it will continue to retain that purchasing power. The purchasing power of money serves as a reference for many exchanges and contracts in the economy, and makes it possible project our future, through savings and investment, so it is convenient to stability. Since monetary issuance is a purpose of central banks, it is natural that such a power should be accompanied by the responsibility to ensure the preservation of its value. Now, we know that, as with other State institutions, the actions of the Bank of Mexico have effects on people. Specifically, by achieving price stability, the Central Bank creates an environment that allows us to better anticipate and plan for the future. So families can make better decisions about buying a car or a home, and companies about when and how much to invest, open businesses and create jobs. That is why with high inflations economies tend to grow less. As inflation rises, its volatility also tends to increase, obscuring relative price signals and increasing public uncertainty. Among other damages, inflation causes economic distortions and errors, discourages saving and investment, weakens the financial system and complicates the functioning of the economy. Conversely, when there is price stability, the economy can expand steadily. The recognition of these effects and the social support in favor of such stability have allowed great advances in the control of inflation during the last decades in the world. For many years Mexico suffered the ravages of high and volatile inflations. Not so long ago, from 1973 to the late nineties, price instability was dramatic. In this period annual inflation averaged more than 38 percent and peaked at 180 percent. The economic disorder of that time included the permanent lag of wages with respect to inflation, despite frequent wage revisions that in some years became quarterly; the distraction of many human and material resources in the search for means to protect themselves and perhaps benefit from inflation; devaluations 2 recurrent weight against the dollar; the prolonged contraction in investment and economic growth; Fortunately, through responsible and judicious monetary and fiscal policies, annual inflation fell from 12 per cent in 1999 to an average of 4.5 per cent over the past six years. With this, nominal interest rates have been reduced. This environment of greater certainty, together with fiscal discipline and the proper management of public debt, allowed the Government to extend the yield curve up to 30 years, which has facilitated the emergence, for the first time, of long-term private debt issuances and mortgage loans at fixed interest rates in pesos. How does the Bank of Mexico seek to control inflation? To a large extent, the fight against inflation has been possible thanks to the institutional bases of the Central Bank. I would like to highlight three fundamental elements. The first has to do with the fact that the priority objective of the Bank of Mexico, established by the Constitution, is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. This mandate leaves no room for doubt as to the basic direction of the Tasks of the Bank of Mexico. The Law establishes as other purposes to promote the healthy development of the financial system and to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. A second basis is that, also by constitutional provision, the Bank of Mexico is autonomous in the exercise of its functions and administration. This autonomy should not be understood as a privilege to do as you please, but as a means to promote the achievement of the priority objective. A frequent cause of high inflation in Mexico and other nations has been the use of governments to finance their deficits monetarily. One consequence of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico is that no authority can force it to provide financing. As a way to strengthen autonomy, the Bank of Mexico is led by a Governing Board that is composed of five members, appointed 3 by the President of the Republic and approved by the Chamber of Senators or the Permanent Commission of Congress, as the case may be. Of the five members, the President appoints a Governor to preside over the Governing Board and the other four members are called Deputy Governors. The position of the first lasts six years and that of the second, eight. They are appointed in a staggered manner and may be appointed more than once, if they meet, among other requirements, not having reached more than 65 years of age on the date of their appointment. The members of the Governing Board may not be removed, except for serious cause established in the Law. The five members of the Governing Board have the same voting power and the Governor has a casting vote in the event of a tie. In addition, the latter is responsible for the administrative structure of the Central Bank, within its field of competence. In this regard, the autonomy of the Central Institute and the formation of its Governing Board make it possible to direct efforts to the priority objective without other considerations. A third institutional pillar is increasing transparency in the conduct of monetary policy. Like any public body, the Bank of Mexico is held accountable for the performance of its powers. In addition, the exercise of its powers, and in particular the determination of monetary policy, requires clear external communication. To this end, the Bank of Mexico prepares and disseminates statistics and research documents. It also issues provisions to fulfil its role as a regulatory authority. With regard to its priority objective, the Law obliges it to send to the Executive and Legislative Branches a statement on monetary policy at the beginning of each year and a report every six months on its implementation. On the other hand, since 1995 the Bank of Mexico publishes its weekly statement of accounts, which among other elements contains the level of the international reserve, as well as the main accounts of its balance sheet, whose 4 movements allow to know their market operations to satisfy the demand for money from the public. In addition, since 2000 the Bank of Mexico has published a quarterly report explaining the evolution of inflation and the bases of monetary policy. It should be remembered that central banks do not determine prices, but that prices are the result of the interaction of companies and consumers in the markets for different goods and services. However, when the general level of prices registers persistent growth, there is inflation. Ultimately, inflation is a monetary phenomenon, so it is up to the Central Bank to guide the expectations and price formation of the economy through its actions to control it. Since 2001, the Bank of Mexico has formally applied a strategy based on inflation targets, which means that monetary policy is "anchored" in the commitment of this Central Bank that it will apply its tools to achieve the announced objectives. In the monetary program of that year, the Bank of Mexico established that the annual inflation target is three percent as of December 2003. This rate is consistent with price stability, once the upward bias of the corresponding indices is considered, which do not consider aspects such as increases in the quality of products and changes in consumption patterns. The three percent target represents an ongoing commitment. However, a range of variability of plus minus one percentage point is included around this target, in order to incorporate transitory deviations from factors beyond the scope of monetary policy, such as highly volatile price fluctuations. Since 2008, the Bank of Mexico has expressed its monetary policy stance through a reference interest rate, which is currently the overnight interbank interest rate. The changes in this rate seek to influence the expectations of the public and, through this and other channels, on the future evolution of inflation. 5 We know that the effects of monetary policy occur with long and variable lags, so decisions in this area must be based primarily on future forecasts and, therefore, be preventive. The problem is that no one knows the future and therefore the transmission channels of monetary policy can have an uncertain impact. Therefore, central banks take into account all available information. They seek to identify inflation pressures and their nature by seeking to distinguish whether they are transitory or permanent, whether they come from aggregate supply or demand pressures, and at what stage of the cycle the economy is. How do you publicize your monetary policy decisions? As a result of the monetary policy meetings, which are held according to a previously published schedule, the Bank of Mexico issues a concise communication in which it announces its decision and the reasons behind it. This statement and other publications seek to influence the course of inflation. Typically, the bulletin includes an interpretation of economic conditions, an analysis of the trajectory and outlook for inflation, and an assessment of the risks to meeting the target. Finally, it should be recognized that communication is a dynamic process, in which the Bank of Mexico seeks to improve the clarity and timeliness of its reports. In the future, new forms of communication will surely be incorporated that will contribute to improving the public's understanding of the Central Bank's decisions. 6 Final comments Over the past decade, Mexico has made considerable progress in controlling inflation. The reduction in inflation has been possible thanks to the institutional bases of the Bank of Mexico, among which the priority objective of stability, autonomy and greater transparency stand out. Progress towards price stability represents a favourable condition for economic growth and social welfare. Without ignoring this achievement, it is essential to continue efforts to converge to the three percent annual inflation target that serves as the anchor of monetary policy. In addition, challenges remain for central banks in other areas. In particular, the recent global crisis has been a wake-up call to remember that price stability is not sufficient for economic stability and that adequate regulation and supervision of the financial system are essential for the steady expansion of the economy. 7
text_original: OBJETIVO Y FUNCIONAMIENTO DEL BANCO DE MEXICO Palabras del Dr. Manuel Snchez Gonzlez, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, en la clausura de la Ctedra Banco de Mxico, impartida en la Universidad Autnoma Metropolitana, 1 de julio de 2010. Es un honor exponer en la clausura de la Ctedra Banco de Mxico impartida durante las ltimas semanas en la Universidad Autnoma Metropolitana (UAM). Agradezco la oportunidad de participar en este programa orientado a explicar las actividades de nuestro Banco Central a los estudiantes de esta prestigiada casa de estudios. Con slo 35 aos de haber iniciado sus labores, la UAM es ampliamente reconocida como una institucin acadmica de excelencia, formadora de profesionales que ocupan puestos clave en los sectores pblico y privado. Como su lema lo expresa, Casa Abierta al Tiempo, la UAM confirma que el aprendizaje y la difusin del conocimiento son los componentes esenciales para que las personas crezcan y trasciendan en el entorno de la casa comn, que es la patria, y que es tambin, en ltimo trmino, nuestro planeta. Quisiera compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones sobre la forma en que el Banco de Mxico lleva a cabo la tarea de procurar la estabilidad de los precios, la cual es una condicin indispensable para elevar el bienestar de la poblacin y propiciar un crecimiento econmico sostenido. Como sucede en otras partes del mundo Mxico cuenta con una moneda fiduciaria cuya aceptacin no se sustenta en su valor intrnseco o en la convertibilidad de la misma moneda a algn metal precioso, como el oro o la plata, a un precio predeterminado. La confianza en el peso mexicano se basa en la expectativa del pblico de que su tenencia le permite comprar un cierto conjunto de bienes y servicios y que, pasado el tiempo, seguir conservando esa capacidad de compra. El poder adquisitivo del dinero sirve de referencia para muchos intercambios y contratos en la economa, y hace posible proyectar nuestro futuro, mediante el ahorro y la inversin, por lo que es conveniente su estabilidad. Al ser la emisin monetaria una finalidad de los bancos centrales, es natural que tal facultad se acompae con la responsabilidad de procurar la preservacin de su valor. Ahora bien, sabemos que, como sucede con otras instituciones del Estado, las acciones del Banco de Mxico tienen efectos sobre las personas. Especficamente, al lograr la estabilidad de los precios el Banco Central genera un entorno que permite prever y planear mejor el futuro. As las familias pueden tomar mejores decisiones sobre la compra de un automvil o una casa, y las empresas sobre cundo y cunto invertir, abrir negocios y crear empleos. Es por eso que con inflaciones altas las economas tienden a crecer menos. Al elevarse la inflacin suele incrementarse adems su volatilidad, lo que oscurece las seales de los precios relativos y aumenta la incertidumbre del pblico. Entre otros daos, la inflacin causa distorsiones y errores econmicos, desalienta el ahorro y la inversin, debilita el sistema financiero y complica el funcionamiento de la economa. Por el contrario, cuando hay estabilidad de precios, la economa puede expandirse de forma sostenida. El reconocimiento de estos efectos y el apoyo social a favor de dicha estabilidad han permitido grandes avances en el control de la inflacin durante las ltimas dcadas en el mundo. Por muchos aos Mxico padeci los estragos de las inflaciones elevadas y voltiles. No hace mucho tiempo, de 1973 a finales de los aos noventa, la inestabilidad de precios fue dramtica. En este perodo la inflacin anual promedi ms de 38 por ciento y alcanz un mximo de 180 por ciento. El desorden econmico de esa poca incluy el rezago permanente de los salarios respecto de la inflacin, a pesar de las frecuentes revisiones salariales que en algunos aos llegaron a ser trimestrales; la distraccin de muchos recursos humanos y materiales en la bsqueda de medios para protegerse y tal vez beneficiarse de la inflacin; las devaluaciones 2 recurrentes del peso frente al dlar; la prolongada contraccin de la inversin y del crecimiento econmico, y el doloroso aumento de la pobreza. Por fortuna, y mediante polticas monetarias y fiscales responsables y juiciosas, la inflacin anual disminuy de 12% en 1999 a un promedio de 4.5% en los ltimos seis aos. Con ello, se han reducido las tasas de inters nominales. Este ambiente de mayor certeza, junto con la disciplina fiscal y el manejo adecuado de la deuda pbica, permiti al Gobierno ampliar la curva de rendimientos hasta 30 aos, lo que ha facilitado el surgimiento, por primera vez, de emisiones de deuda privada de largo plazo y de crditos hipotecarios a tasas de inters fijas en pesos. Cmo busca el Banco de Mxico controlar la inflacin? En buena medida, el combate de la inflacin ha sido posible gracias a las bases institucionales del Banco Central. Me gustara destacar tres elementos fundamentales. El primero tiene que ver con que el objetivo prioritario del Banco de Mxico, establecido por la Constitucin, es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. Este mandato no deja lugar a dudas respecto de la orientacin bsica de las tareas del Banco de Mxico. La Ley establece como otras finalidades promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Un segundo fundamento es que, tambin por disposicin constitucional, el Banco de Mxico es autnomo en el ejercicio de sus funciones y de su administracin. Esta autonoma no debe entenderse como un privilegio para hacer lo que se plazca, sino como un medio para propiciar la consecucin del objetivo prioritario. Una causa frecuente de los episodios de elevada inflacin en Mxico y otras naciones ha sido el recurso de los gobiernos a financiar monetariamente su dficit. Una consecuencia de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico es que ninguna autoridad puede obligarlo a otorgar financiamiento. Como una forma de afianzar la autonoma, el Banco de Mxico es conducido por una Junta de Gobierno que se integra por cinco miembros, designados 3 por el Presidente de la Repblica y aprobados por la Cmara de Senadores o la Comisin Permanente del Congreso, segn sea el caso. De los cinco miembros, el Presidente designa un Gobernador que preside la Junta de Gobierno y los otros cuatro miembros se llaman Subgobernadores. El cargo del primero dura seis aos y el de los segundos, ocho. Se nombran de forma escalonada y pueden ser designados ms de una vez, si cubren, entre otros requisitos, no haber cumplido ms de 65 aos de edad en la fecha de su nombramiento. Los miembros de la Junta de Gobierno no pueden ser removidos, salvo por causa grave establecida en la Ley. Los cinco miembros de la Junta de Gobierno tienen el mismo poder de voto y el Gobernador tiene voto de calidad en caso de empate. Adems, este ltimo tiene a su cargo la estructura administrativa del Banco Central, en su mbito de competencia. En ese sentido, la autonoma del Instituto Central y la conformacin de su Junta de Gobierno permiten orientar los esfuerzos al objetivo prioritario sin consideraciones de otra ndole. Un tercer pilar institucional es la creciente transparencia en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. Como todo rgano pblico, el Banco de Mxico est obligado a rendir cuentas sobre el desempeo de sus atribuciones. Adems, el ejercicio de sus facultades y, en especial, la determinacin de la poltica monetaria, requieren una clara comunicacin externa. Para este efecto, el Banco de Mxico elabora y difunde estadsticas y documentos de investigacin. Asimismo, emite disposiciones para cumplir con su funcin como autoridad reguladora. En materia de su objetivo prioritario, la Ley lo obliga a enviar al Poder Ejecutivo y al Legislativo una exposicin sobre la poltica monetaria a principio de cada ao y un informe cada semestre sobre su ejecucin. Por otra parte, desde 1995 el Banco de Mxico publica su estado de cuenta semanal, que entre otros elementos contiene el nivel de la reserva internacional, as como las principales cuentas de su balance, cuyos 4 movimientos permiten conocer sus operaciones de mercado para satisfacer la demanda de dinero del pblico. Adems, desde 2000 el Banco de Mxico divulga un informe trimestral en el que explica la evolucin de la inflacin y las bases de la poltica monetaria. Debe recordarse que los bancos centrales no determinan los precios, sino que stos son resultado de la interaccin de las empresas y los consumidores en los mercados de los diferentes bienes y servicios. Sin embargo, cuando el nivel general de los precios registra un crecimiento persistente existe inflacin. En ltima instancia, la inflacin es un fenmeno monetario, por lo que corresponde al Banco Central orientar las expectativas y la formacin de los precios de la economa mediante sus acciones para controlarla. Desde 2001 el Banco de Mxico aplica formalmente una estrategia basada en objetivos de inflacin, lo que significa que la poltica monetaria se ancla en el compromiso de este Banco Central de que aplicar sus herramientas para alcanzar los objetivos anunciados. En el programa monetario de ese ao el Banco de Mxico estableci que el objetivo de inflacin anual es tres por ciento a partir de diciembre de 2003. Esta tasa es congruente con la estabilidad de los precios, una vez considerado el sesgo al alza de los ndices correspondientes, los cuales no consideran aspectos como los aumentos en la calidad de los productos y los cambios en los patrones de consumo. El objetivo de tres por ciento representa un compromiso continuo. Sin embargo, se incluye un intervalo de variabilidad de ms menos un punto porcentual alrededor de esta meta, con el fin de incorporar desviaciones transitorias provenientes de factores fuera del alcance de la poltica monetaria, tales como fluctuaciones de precios altamente voltiles. Desde 2008 el Banco de Mxico expresa su postura de poltica monetaria mediante una tasa de inters de referencia, que en la actualidad es la tasa de inters interbancaria a un da. Con los cambios de esta tasa se busca influir sobre las expectativas del pblico y, mediante ste y otros canales, sobre la evolucin futura de la inflacin. 5 Sabemos que los efectos de la poltica monetaria ocurren con rezagos largos y variables, por lo que las decisiones en esta materia deben sustentarse primordialmente en las previsiones del futuro y, por ende, ser preventivas. El problema es que nadie conoce el futuro y, por tanto, los canales de transmisin de la poltica monetaria pueden tener un impacto incierto. Por ello, los bancos centrales toman en cuenta toda la informacin disponible. Buscan identificar las presiones de inflacin y su naturaleza procurando distinguir si son transitorias o permanentes, si provienen de presiones de la oferta o la demanda agregadas, y en qu fase del ciclo se encuentra la economa. Cmo da a conocer sus decisiones de poltica monetaria? Como resultado de las reuniones de poltica monetaria, que se llevan a cabo conforme a un calendario previamente publicado, el Banco de Mxico emite una comunicacin concisa en la que da a conocer su decisin y las razones que la sustentan. Este comunicado y otras publicaciones buscan influir en el rumbo de la inflacin. Tpicamente, el boletn incluye la interpretacin de las condiciones de la economa, el anlisis de la trayectoria y las perspectivas de la inflacin, y una evaluacin de los riesgos respecto del cumplimiento del objetivo. Por ltimo, debe reconocerse que la comunicacin es un proceso dinmico, en el que el Banco de Mxico procura mejorar la claridad y la oportunidad de sus informes. En el futuro con seguridad se incorporarn nuevas formas de comunicacin que contribuyan a perfeccionar el entendimiento del pblico sobre las decisiones del Banco Central. 6 Comentarios finales Durante la dcada reciente Mxico ha avanzado de manera considerable en el control de la inflacin. La disminucin de la inflacin ha sido posible gracias a las bases institucionales del Banco de Mxico, entre las que destacan el objetivo prioritario de la estabilidad, la autonoma y la mayor transparencia. El progreso hacia la estabilidad de los precios representa una condicin favorable para el crecimiento econmico y el bienestar social. Sin desconocer este logro, es indispensable continuar los esfuerzos para convergir a la meta de inflacin de tres por ciento anual que sirve de ancla de la poltica monetaria. Adems, persisten desafos para los bancos centrales en otras materias. En especial, la reciente crisis global ha sido una llamada de atencin para recordar que la estabilidad de los precios no es suficiente para la estabilidad econmica y que una adecuada regulacin y supervisin del sistema financiero son esenciales para la expansin firme de la economa. 7

Title: Opening remarks
text: Challenges to Achieving Price Stability Annual IJCB Research Conference Hosted by the Banco de Mexico November 23-24, 2015. Manuel Ramos-Francia1 Opening Remarks Good morning, I am Manuel Ramos-Francia, a Vice-Governor and Member of the Governing Board at Banco de Mexico. Also, I am currently the Chairman of the Deputies of the International Monetary and Financial Committee (IMFC) of the International Monetary Fund (IMF). I mention this because at the end of my remarks, I will briefly touch upon some of the topics that are being discussed at the IMFC concerning the role of the IMF in the global economy. On behalf of Banco de Mexico, I would like to extend everyone a warm welcome to the Annual International Journal of Central Banking Research Conference Challenges to Achieving Price Stability. I would also like to express my gratitude to the conference organizers, the IJCB, and our host Banco de Mexico, in particular, its Research Division. As all of you know, in response to the global financial crisis, central banks in major advanced economies adopted a series of unconventional monetary policies (UMPs) with two main objectives. First, to restore the functioning of financial markets and intermediation. This goal included all the way from liquidity provision to a sort of market maker of last resort, and comprised purchases of private and public assets. Second, to provide further monetary accommodation at the zero lower bound (zlb). This objective included purchases of government bonds, as well as forward guidance. There has been an enduring and heated debate on the topic of capital flows and/or controls. As I mentioned, it has taken place amidst the unprecedented monetary policy stances that have been set in place in many advanced economies. In what follows, I will briefly review three of the main recent papers. First, Farhi and Wernings (2013) consider the possible occurrence of a sudden stop. In their model, capital controls are set as subsidies on capital inflows and as taxes on outflows. The authorities have as an objective to mitigate the archetypal consequences of a sudden stop: exchange rate depreciations, interest rate increases, current account reversals, and drops in consumption. Thus, the rationale they put forward for capital controls is to smooth the stabilization process when a sudden stop takes place. Second, in Bengui and Bianchi (2014) households are occasionally subject to a credit constraint. Hence, their access to credit depends on the value of their current income, which in turn is a function of tradable and non-tradable goods. Then, if sufficient debt stock accumulates and a sudden stop takes place, the contraction of capital flows and the depreciation of the real exchange rate feed each other through the credit constraint. In their model, a pecuniary externality exists precisely because agents ignore that as their debt increases, they are more exposed to a sudden stop. They maintain that their externality can be addressed with capital controls.29 The gist in their model is that controls cannot be enforced on a fraction of agents. Thus, as authorities tighten the financial regulation, the fraction of unregulated agents know there is less probability of a sudden stop, and take on additional debt. While the planner cannot control unregulated agents, she does account for these leakages when solving for her planning problem. The authors find that, notwithstanding the imperfect enforcement, capital controls are welfare improving. But when implemented, their cost essentially falls on the regulated fraction of agents, while their benefits are shared by both fractions. Yet, in the last few years there has been an unprecedented degree of monetary policy accommodation in advanced economies. The search for yield, given the low levels of interest rates in advanced economies, has led to enormous problems in policy making in some emerging market economies in both of its facets: at first the large capital inflow stage and, afterwards, the possibility of large, abrupt capital outflows when the perception is generated that the core country could start the process of normalizing monetary policy. To conclude, let me mention two set of points. The first set pertains to some of the key policies emerging economies can individually pursue. The second set, to the need of taking international cooperation to a higher level. First, going forward, emerging markets as I have said, face potentially daunting challenges. In this context, it is very difficult to overemphasize that nothing can substitute for solid macroeconomic fundamentals. Fiscal policy should be tightened. Monetary policy should be adjusted depending on different issues, but there may be complicated trade-offs present in this case. Financial authorities have to foster conditions under which financial markets can grow as deep, and as complete, as possible. Policy makers have to design, plan and implement the necessary structural reforms. Crucially, these policies have to be seen and implemented as a package. In effect, there are neither silver bullets, nor fail-safe reforms. Equally important is that emerging market economies that have consistently implemented more prudent macroeconomic policies should try to differentiate themselves from their peers as 13 much as possible, especially now that the asset class seems to be under a lot of strain. Second, regarding international cooperation, my contention is that for it to gain traction, we need to reassess its benefits and, in tandem, the eventual costs of continuing with the current system (or non-system). This is not to say that cooperation can be easily achieved. In effect, in the words of the late Anna Schwartz cooperation: is a fair-weather instrument because countries have independent interests that they will not sacrifice for the sake of the collectivity. 41 Rather, it is motivating cooperation what is necessary given the otherwise potential dire consequences. The theory on non-cooperative repeated games can tell us about why and where has there been cooperation, and where we can expect to see it in the future. More specifically, in such games the players willingness to cooperate closely depends on: 1) their subjective discount factors, 2) the level of economic activity, and 3) the prevailing economic uncertainty. Thus, it is a fragile equilibrium, and cooperation can be brought to a halt in various instances.42 In short, such cooperation has to be called for by the realization that it is in the economies interests to cooperate, and not doing so could bring about significant and long-lasting costs. Yet, the world should advance much more quickly on cooperative/coordinated solutions to some of these problems. Financial institutions such as the worlds central banks have advanced along these lines, e.g., successfully implementing swap lines during the global financial crisis. In addition, the IMF, as a key multilateral institution, has made available several types of credit lines to countries with a strong record of economic policies but that, nonetheless, could face challenges in the current environment. In particular, at the IMFC and also at fora like the G20, important policy tools such as the design and architecture of Global Financial Safety Nets are considered to be essential for the world economy to achieve a better equilibrium. Indeed, these policy tools are fundamental towards creating a more resilient International Monetary System and, thus, securing better global economic growth. Some solid steps have been taken in the right direction, but much work remains to be done. Thank you for your attention.
