Title: 75 Banking Convention
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, at the 75th (seventy-fifth) Banking Convention, held in Acapulco, Guerrero, on May 17, 2012.  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena,  Mr. President of the National Banking and Securities Commission, Dr. Guillermo Babatz Torres,  Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, Mr. Jaime Ruiz Sacristan,  Ladies and gentlemen legislators,  Conventionist ladies and gentlemen I think it is a success that the theme of this seventy-fifth Banking Convention has been chosen as the "Political and Economic Stability: The Variables of Success in the Face of Global Uncertainty". In recent years, Mexico has managed, in terms of macroeconomic policy, to successfully navigate one of the most uncertain and complicated economic environments the world has suffered in many decades. It is certainly worth analyzing the 1 elements that have contributed to this performance and evaluate not only what we must maintain from this strategy, but also the challenges that we will have to undertake in the short and medium term. * * * It is well known that the first worrying signs of the crisis in the most advanced countries, particularly in the United States and Europe, were manifested since mid-2007, but it was not until late 2008 when this financial and economic crisis broke out with all harshness and spread to all the economies of the world. Despite the fact that our country had healthy foundations, the deep interconnection between economies and the global financial system, together with the magnitude of the external shocks, made Mexico immediately resent the contagion of the crisis. The impact was brutal in 2 the first two quarters of 2009, when we suffered a significant reduction in the demand for our exports of around 23 percent, the abrupt fall in oil prices and a severe contraction in external financing to Mexican companies. To this adverse environment must be added the appearance in Mexico of an unusual pandemic due to its novelty and virulence, which additionally affected economic activity. However, only a few months later, and thanks to the sound fundamentals and the measures adopted to face the crisis, Mexico entered a period of frank recovery, to such an extent that today, within the G-20, it is likely that we are one of the countries with the best macroeconomic foundations. This is based on the following reasons: 1. We have low and stable inflation. In the last 16 months only once has inflation exceeded the upper limit of the 3 variability set by the Bank of Mexico, of plus or minus one percentage point around the three percent target. That month was last January, with an annual measurement of 4.05 percent and, as we have all seen, that deviation responded to temporary variations in relative prices of some goods and services. Recall that the inflation corresponding to last April was 3.41 percent. The maintenance of low and stable inflation has benefited the entire population, not only because the incidence of the most regressive tax that exists has been minimized, but also because it has allowed us to enjoy interest rates at historically low levels in all terms. 2. The free-floating exchange rate regime has shown its suitability to absorb external shocks without the episodic depreciations, due to turbulence in international markets, having generated 4 lasting inflationary consequences. This is because, over the years, the nominal anchors of the Mexican economy have strengthened, thanks to the credibility of both monetary and fiscal policy. In turn, the possibility of the real exchange rate adjusting without major inflationary repercussions allows economic activity in the country to respond quickly to external shocks through higher net exports. This adjustment mechanism is very similar to that enjoyed by stable and open advanced economies, such as Canada and Australia, and to which we could not aspire in the past. 3. We have a record level of international reserves today. This maintains and increases confidence in the value of the national currency, which facilitates the access of the government and companies to international financial markets in 5 favorable conditions and is also an additional factor of confidence for attracting external investments. 4. Throughout this prolonged global crisis our financial system has remained healthy and remarkably strong. Mexican banks have a capitalization that is high compared to any other banking system, and we will be one of the first countries to meet the most demanding prudential requirements embodied in the Basel III Principles. This makes Mexico one of the few G20 countries whose financial system is clearly capable of driving economic growth. 5. A strong fiscal discipline has been maintained, which has made it possible to sustain a ratio of debt to Gross Domestic Product that is equivalent to approximately one third of the levels presented by several advanced countries and that have been 6 source of the serious problems that keep these nations in crisis. By themselves all these results are meritorious. But, at the end of the day, they are not the ultimate goal we pursue as a country, but only the intermediate and necessary steps to achieve higher goals, such as:  Faster and more sustained economic growth, and  A generation of jobs increasingly in line with the great needs of the country. In this sense, it should be noted that immediately after the peak of the global crisis, in 2010 GDP in Mexico grew 5.5 percent real; the following year, growth was 3.9 percent and the most recent estimates for 2012 show a figure slightly below 4 percent. It is not idle to note that this growth for three consecutive years is something remarkable in the current global context, characterized by 7 crisis and recession. Of course, it is above growth in advanced countries, global growth, and even above growth in emerging countries that are considered emblematic, such as Brazil. Job creation has also shown a favourable trend during the years following the global crisis. It does not seem remote that in the period from 2010 to 2012 2 million new jobs will be created. These results come from the joint and coordinated action of several factors, which are: fiscal policy, monetary policy, exchange rate policy, regulation and supervision of the financial system and the vitality of an entrepreneurial private sector, underpinned by a solid and dynamic financial system. Within this coordinated and joint work, I would like to deepen the role that monetary policy has played. 8 Specifically, monetary policy has focused on four key elements: 1. We have consistently guided its actions towards the objective of achieving convergence of inflation at 3 per cent per annum, with its range of variability of plus or minus one percentage point, and to keeping inflation expectations well anchored, preferably in line with the aforementioned inflation target. 2. The Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico has also remained very vigilant about the performance of the main determinants of inflation. This in order to be in a position to identify in a timely manner the most incipient signals that could make adjustments to the monetary stance advisable, either towards greater laxity or restriction, as required by the precise circumstance. One of these determinants is the so-called 9 product, which basically represents the difference between observed GDP and potential GDP if all production resources are being used efficiently. Although this concept of the output gap is difficult to quantify (moreover, after an abrupt and unexpected fall such as that experienced by GDP in 2009), it is estimated that to this day this gap remains negative and inflationary pressures are not perceived on the aggregate demand side of the economy. In a complementary way, we carefully analyze the prevailing situation in the input markets of the economy, the most relevant for these purposes being labor and credit. 10 Despite significant growth in employment, there are no perceived inflationary pressures in the labour market as unit labour costs continue to fall. Something similar can be said about the credit market: there is a healthy growth of credit to households and companies, but the level of interest rates and delinquency rates, together with the high capitalization of banks, rule out that the credit market is overheated. This perception is confirmed in the Bank of Mexico's surveys of entrepreneurs about credit conditions, in which it is clear that the main limitations to contracting new loans are on the demand side and not on the supply side of credits. 11 3. The Governing Board also monitors that changes in relative prices, often induced by changes in the exchange rate or the prices of some specific goods such as gasoline and agricultural products, among others, do not manifest themselves in greater permanent inflation. It should be remembered that changes in relative prices usually happen once and for all and do not represent a sustained increase in all prices in the economy. Hence, monetary policy does not have to respond to them, unless they generate second-order impacts on the rest of the prices. Recently we have observed a great volatility of the exchange rate and in the prices of several basic commodities, but these phenomena have not affected the dynamics of inflation, which is why an adjustment in the 12 monetary policy stance. The reduction that has occurred over the years in the intensity of transfers of exchange rate variations and specific prices to inflation reflects the solidity of the disinflation process in Mexico and the credibility that the Central Institute has acquired. In addition, it is pertinent to mention that in the recent past the exchange rate has tended to appreciate after abrupt depreciations of the national currency as a result of external financial turbulence. This is because, in the end, the solid fundamentals of the Mexican economy in terms of growth, public finances, monetary control, health of the financial system and balance of external accounts, end up imposing. 13 4. Finally, the Governing Board carefully analyzes the evolution of monetary policy in Mexico in relation to monetary policy abroad, and in particular with respect to the corresponding monetary policy in the United States. An excessive easing of monetary policy abroad could eventually generate a tighter monetary stance in Mexico than desirable, considering that the rest of the variables remain the same. This, because this external monetary easing could induce an excessive inflow of resources from abroad, such as those we have observed in recent years, and a very strong appreciation of the exchange rate, which for all practical purposes would translate into more restrictive monetary conditions in Mexico. It should be noted, however, that in recent months this phenomenon has become 14 compensated by other factors such as the different episodes of international financial turbulence. But that does not prevent the Bank of Mexico from remaining very vigilant about such an eventuality. The simultaneous consideration of all these key elements has led to the Bank of Mexico maintaining its benchmark interest rate at 4.5 percent over the past 33 months, which has not been an obstacle to more than significant reductions in all interest rates in the country. As evidenced, rates on all government securities, from 28-day to 30-year rates, have reached historically low levels, which has reduced the cost of financing for the Federal Government, allowing the reallocation of fiscal resources to other, more socially pressing objectives. This has also been reflected in a significant reduction in the cost of financing extended by banks, which, at the 15 increasing the amount demanded for credit has had an impact on greater consumption and investment in the country, which translates into greater economic growth. * * * All of the above has been achieved through strict observance of the constitutional mandate assigned to the Bank of Mexico to ensure the sustained abatement of inflation. I stress this, because it is often mentioned that the Bank of Mexico should also have the objective of promoting greater economic growth. However, theory and evidence have shown that a systematically expansionary monetary policy only generates higher and higher inflations. For the sake of completeness, the results of the last three years in terms of growth in our country make it clear that it is fully compatible to obtain growth. 16 accelerated economic policy with a monetary policy aimed at achieving an inflation target, such as that followed by the Bank of Mexico. I would like to end with the following reflection: the economic growth that we have achieved through prudent macroeconomic management is a solid platform, a firm floor, so that, from there, Mexico grows in the future at even more accelerated rates. What remains for us, as I have repeated on numerous occasions, is to promote and achieve a greater social spillover of that growth, through the structural reforms already more than identified, but which we have not yet been able to crystallize. At a time when uncertainty is deepening in the international environment, and when mediocre economic growth is predicted in the economies of our main trading partners, it becomes even more important to undertake those reforms that strengthen domestic sources of growth, by contributing to 17 to encourage savings and investment, increase the competitiveness of enterprises and improve the productivity of workers. Only in this way can we translate the progress of stability that we have already achieved, in a stage of sustained growth that generates more jobs, sustainable wage improvements and greater well-being for all Mexicans. Thanks a lot. 18
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, en la 75 (septuagsima quinta) Convencin Bancaria, realizada en Acapulco, Guerrero, el 17 de mayo de 2012.  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Jos Antonio Meade Kuribrea,  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, doctor Guillermo Babatz Torres,  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, licenciado Jaime Ruz Sacristn,  Seoras y seores legisladores,  Seoras y seores convencionistas Me parece un acierto que se haya elegido como tema de esta septuagsima quinta Convencin Bancaria la Estabilidad poltica y econmica: Las variables de xito ante la incertidumbre global. En los ltimos aos, Mxico ha logrado, en trminos de poltica macroeconmica, sortear con xito uno de los entornos econmicos ms inciertos y complicados que ha padecido el mundo en muchas dcadas. Sin duda vale la pena analizar los 1 elementos que han contribuido a este desempeo y evaluar no slo aquello que debemos mantener de dicha estrategia, sino tambin los desafos que deberemos acometer en el corto y en el mediano plazo. * * * Es por dems sabido que los primeros signos preocupantes de la crisis en los pases ms avanzados, en particular en Estados Unidos y en Europa, se manifestaron desde mediados de 2007, pero no fue sino hasta avanzado 2008 cuando esta crisis financiera y econmica estall con toda crudeza y se extendi a todas las economas del mundo. Pese a que nuestro pas contaba con fundamentos sanos, la profunda interconexin entre las economas y el sistema financiero global, junto con la magnitud de los choques externos, hicieron que Mxico resintiera de inmediato el contagio de la crisis. El impacto fue brutal en 2 los primeros dos trimestres de 2009, cuando sufrimos una reduccin importante en la demanda de nuestras exportaciones de alrededor de 23 por ciento, la abrupta cada de los precios del petrleo y una severa contraccin en el financiamiento externo a empresas mexicanas. A este entorno adverso debe agregarse la aparicin en Mxico de una pandemia inslita por su novedad y virulencia, que afect de manera adicional la actividad econmica. Empero, tan slo unos meses despus, y gracias a los sanos fundamentos y las medidas adoptadas para enfrentar la crisis, Mxico entr en un perodo de franca recuperacin, a tal grado que hoy, dentro del G-20, es probable que seamos uno de los pases con mejores cimientos macroeconmicos. Esto se sustenta en las siguientes razones: 1. Tenemos una inflacin baja y estable. En los ltimos 16 meses slo en una ocasin la inflacin ha superado el lmite superior del intervalo de 3 variabilidad establecido por el Banco de Mxico, de ms o menos un punto porcentual alrededor del objetivo de tres por ciento. Ese mes fue enero pasado, con una medicin anual de 4.05 por ciento y, como todos hemos podido comprobar, esa desviacin respondi a variaciones temporales en precios relativos de algunos bienes y servicios. Recordemos que la inflacin correspondiente a abril pasado fue de 3.41 por ciento. El mantenimiento de una inflacin baja y estable ha beneficiado a toda la poblacin, no slo porque se ha minimizado la incidencia del impuesto ms regresivo que existe, sino tambin porque nos ha permitido gozar de tasas de inters a niveles histricamente bajos a todos los plazos. 2. El rgimen cambiario de libre flotacin ha mostrado su idoneidad para absorber choques externos sin que las episdicas depreciaciones, por turbulencias en los mercados internacionales, hayan generado 4 consecuencias inflacionarias perdurables. Esto se debe a que, a travs de los aos, las anclas nominales de la economa mexicana se han fortalecido, gracias a la credibilidad tanto de la poltica monetaria como de la fiscal. A su vez, la posibilidad de que el tipo de cambio real se ajuste sin mayores repercusiones inflacionarias permite que la actividad econmica en el pas responda rpidamente ante choques externos mediante mayores exportaciones netas. Este mecanismo de ajuste es muy similar al que gozan economas avanzadas estables y abiertas, como Canad y Australia, y al cual nosotros no podamos aspirar en el pasado. 3. Contamos hoy con un nivel rcord de reservas internacionales. Esto mantiene y acrecienta la confianza en el valor de la moneda nacional, lo cual facilita el acceso del gobierno y de las empresas a los mercados financieros internacionales en 5 condiciones favorables y es tambin un factor adicional de confianza para la atraccin de inversiones externas. 4. A lo largo de esta prolongada crisis global nuestro sistema financiero se ha mantenido saludable y notablemente slido. La banca mexicana tiene una capitalizacin que es elevada comparada con cualquier otro sistema bancario, y seremos uno de los primeros pases en satisfacer los requisitos ms exigentes en materia prudencial plasmados en los Principios de Basilea III. Esto hace de Mxico uno de los pocos pases del G-20 cuyo sistema financiero est en clara capacidad de impulsar el crecimiento econmico. 5. Se ha mantenido una frrea disciplina fiscal, lo que ha permitido sostener una razn de deuda a Producto Interno Bruto que equivale aproximadamente a un tercio de los niveles que presentan varios pases avanzados y que han sido 6 fuente de los graves problemas que mantienen en crisis a dichas naciones. Por s mismos todos estos resultados son meritorios. Pero, al final del da, no son el objetivo ltimo que perseguimos como pas, sino slo los pasos intermedios y necesarios para lograr metas ms elevadas, como son:  Un crecimiento econmico ms acelerado y sostenido, y  Una generacin de empleos cada vez ms acorde con las grandes necesidades del pas. En este sentido, cabe recalcar que inmediatamente despus de la etapa ms lgida de la crisis global, en 2010 el PIB en Mxico creci 5.5 por ciento real; al ao siguiente, el crecimiento fue de 3.9 por ciento y las ms recientes estimaciones para 2012 arrojan una cifra ligeramente inferior a 4 por ciento. No es ocioso advertir que este crecimiento por tres aos consecutivos es algo notable en el actual contexto mundial, caracterizado por 7 crisis y recesin. Desde luego est por encima del crecimiento en pases avanzados, del crecimiento mundial, e inclusive por arriba del crecimiento en pases emergentes que se consideran emblemticos, como Brasil. La creacin de empleos tambin ha mostrado una tendencia favorable durante los aos posteriores a la crisis global. No parece remoto que en el lapso de 2010 a 2012 se vayan a crear 2 millones de empleos nuevos. Estos resultados provienen de la accin conjunta y coordinada de varios factores, que son: la poltica fiscal, la poltica monetaria, la poltica cambiaria, la regulacin y supervisin del sistema financiero y la vitalidad de un sector privado emprendedor, apuntalado por un sistema financiero slido y dinmico. Dentro de este trabajo coordinado y conjunto quisiera profundizar en el papel que ha desempeado la poltica monetaria. 8 Especficamente, la poltica monetaria se ha centrado en cuatro elementos clave: 1. Hemos guiado constantemente sus acciones hacia el objetivo de lograr la convergencia de la inflacin al 3 por ciento anual, con su intervalo de variabilidad de ms o menos un punto porcentual, y a mantener bien ancladas las expectativas de inflacin, de preferencia en lnea con el referido objetivo de inflacin. 2. La Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico se ha mantenido muy vigilante, tambin, sobre el desempeo de los principales determinantes de la inflacin. Esto con el objeto de estar en condiciones de identificar oportunamente las ms incipientes seales que podran hacer recomendables ajustes a la postura monetaria, ya sea hacia una mayor laxitud o restriccin, segn lo requiera la circunstancia precisa. Uno de esos determinantes es la llamada brecha del 9 producto, que bsicamente representa la diferencia entre el PIB observado y el PIB potencial en caso de que se estn empleando eficientemente todos los recursos de la produccin. Si bien este concepto de la brecha del producto es difcil de cuantificar (ms an, despus de una cada abrupta e inesperada como la que experiment el PIB en 2009), se estima que al da de hoy dicha brecha contina siendo negativa y no se perciben presiones inflacionarias por el lado de la demanda agregada de la economa. De manera complementaria analizamos minuciosamente la situacin prevaleciente en los mercados de insumos de la economa, siendo los ms relevantes para estos efectos el laboral y el de crdito. 10 A pesar de un crecimiento significativo en el empleo, en el mercado laboral no se perciben presiones inflacionarias dado que los costos unitarios de la mano de obra continan cayendo. Algo similar podemos decir del mercado de crdito: se registra un crecimiento saludable del crdito a los hogares y empresas, pero el nivel de las tasas de inters y de los ndices de morosidad, junto con la elevada capitalizacin de la banca, descartan que el mercado crediticio se encuentre sobrecalentado. Esta percepcin se ratifica en las encuestas del Banco de Mxico a empresarios acerca de las condiciones del crdito, en las cuales queda claro que las principales limitantes para contratar nuevos crditos estn del lado de la demanda y no del lado de la oferta de crditos. 11 3. La Junta de Gobierno tambin vigila que cambios en precios relativos, frecuentemente inducidos por variaciones del tipo de cambio o de los precios de algunas mercancas especficas como gasolinas y productos agropecuarios, entre otros, no se manifiesten en mayor inflacin permanente. Hay que recordar que las variaciones en precios relativos normalmente suceden de una vez por todas y no representan un aumento sostenido de todos los precios de la economa. De ah que la poltica monetaria no tenga que responder a ellos, salvo que generen impactos de segundo orden sobre el resto de los precios. Recientemente hemos observado una gran volatilidad cambiaria y en los precios de varias mercancas bsicas, pero estos fenmenos no han afectado la dinmica de la inflacin, razn por lo cual no se ha requerido un ajuste en la 12 postura de poltica monetaria. La reduccin que se ha dado a travs de los aos de la intensidad de los traspasos de variaciones cambiarias y de precios especficos a la inflacin refleja la solidez del proceso de desinflacin en Mxico y la credibilidad que el Instituto Central ha adquirido. En adicin es pertinente mencionar que en el pasado reciente el tipo de cambio ha tendido a apreciarse despus de depreciaciones abruptas de la moneda nacional como resultado de la turbulencia financiera externa. Esto debido a que, a la postre, los slidos fundamentos de la economa mexicana en trminos de crecimiento, finanzas pblicas, control monetario, salud del sistema financiero y balance de las cuentas externas, se terminan imponiendo. 13 4. Por ltimo, la Junta de Gobierno analiza con todo detenimiento la evolucin de la poltica monetaria en Mxico en relacin con la poltica monetaria en el exterior, y en particular respecto a la correspondiente de los Estados Unidos. Un relajamiento excesivo de la poltica monetaria en el exterior podra generar, eventualmente, una postura monetaria en Mxico ms estricta de lo deseable, considerando que el resto de las variables permanecen igual. Esto, debido a que esa relajacin monetaria externa podra inducir una entrada excesiva de recursos del exterior, como las que hemos observado durante los ltimos aos, y una apreciacin muy fuerte del tipo de cambio, lo que para todo fin prctico se traducira en condiciones monetarias ms restrictivas en Mxico. Debe advertirse, sin embargo, que en los ltimos meses este fenmeno se ha 14 compensado por otros factores como son los diferentes episodios de turbulencia financiera internacional. Pero eso no obsta para que el Banco de Mxico se mantenga muy vigilante respecto de tal eventualidad. La consideracin simultnea de todos estos elementos clave ha llevado a que en los ltimos 33 meses el Banco de Mxico haya mantenido su tasa de inters de referencia en 4.5 por ciento, lo cual no ha sido obstculo para que se dieran reducciones ms que significativas de todas las tasas de inters en el pas. Como muestra de ello, las tasas de todos los valores gubernamentales, desde aquellos a 28 das hasta los de un plazo de 30 aos, han llegado a niveles histricamente bajos, lo que ha reducido el costo de financiamiento para el Gobierno Federal, permitiendo la reasignacin de recursos fiscales a otros objetivos socialmente ms apremiantes. Esto tambin se ha reflejado en una reduccin notable del costo del financiamiento extendido por la banca, lo cual, al 15 incrementar la cantidad demandada por crdito, ha repercutido en mayor consumo e inversin en el pas, lo que se traduce en mayor crecimiento econmico. * * * Todo lo anterior se ha logrado mediante la estricta observancia del mandato constitucional que tiene asignado el Banco de Mxico de procurar el abatimiento sostenido de la inflacin. Recalco esto, porque con cierta frecuencia se menciona que el Banco de Mxico debera tener tambin el objetivo de promover un mayor crecimiento econmico. Sin embargo, la teora y la evidencia han mostrado que una poltica monetaria sistemticamente expansiva solamente genera inflaciones cada vez ms altas. Para mayor abundamiento, los resultados de los ltimos tres aos en materia de crecimiento en nuestro pas dejan por dems claro que es plenamente compatible obtener crecimiento 16 econmico acelerado con una poltica monetaria orientada a la consecucin de una meta inflacionaria, como la que sigue el Banco de Mxico. Quisiera terminar con la siguiente reflexin: el crecimiento econmico que hemos logrado por el prudente manejo macroeconmico es una slida plataforma, un piso firme, para que, a partir de ah, Mxico crezca en el futuro a tasas an ms aceleradas. Lo que nos resta, como lo he repetido en numerosas ocasiones, es potenciar y lograr una mayor derrama social de ese crecimiento, mediante las reformas estructurales ya ms que identificadas, pero que an no hemos podido cristalizar. En estos momentos en que la incertidumbre se agudiza en el entorno internacional, y en los que se augura un crecimiento econmico mediocre en las economas de nuestros principales socios comerciales, se vuelve ms importante todava emprender esas reformas que refuercen las fuentes internas de crecimiento, al contribuir 17 a fomentar el ahorro y la inversin, elevar la competitividad de las empresas y mejorar la productividad de los trabajadores. Solo as podremos traducir los avances de la estabilidad que ya hemos logrado, en una etapa de crecimiento sostenido que genere ms empleos, mejoras salariales sostenibles y mayor bienestar para todos los mexicanos. Muchas gracias. 18

Title: Statement to IMF Governors and Executive Directors
text: Statement by Agustin Carstens, Governor of Banco de Mexico, to IMF Governors and Executive Directors May 23, 2011 Governors, Members of the Executive Board, The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was established in the spirit of cooperation for the well-being of all member countries. Towards that end, I firmly believe that transparency and fairness in the selection of its Managing Director (MD) is essential for the Funds legitimacy, cohesion, and effectiveness. To facilitate the transparent and merit-based selection process, I hereby offer an overview of my professional background; economic policymaking record; managerial and diplomatic skills, with particular attention to multilateral cooperation; understanding of the Fund and the policy challenges facing the Funds diverse membership; and, in closing, my strategic vision for the institution. PROFESSIONAL BACKGROUND I am an economist, having received my bachelors degree from the Instituto Tecnologico Autonomo de Mexico (ITAM) and a masters degree (MA) and PhD from the University of Chicago. My fields of specialization were international economics and finance, and economic development. I have over 30 years of public service. I started my career in late 1980 in Banco de Mexico (Mexicos Central Bank) and was associated with the institution until mid-1999 (including 3 years I spent at the University of Chicago to earn my MA and PhD). In these 19 years I went through the ranks, from foreign exchange trader to treasurer, chief of staff to the Governor, and head of the Economic Research Department. 1 From mid-1999 to late 2000 I had the honor to serve as Executive Director at the Fund, representing Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Venezuela, and Spain. The chair I was privileged to represent covers the whole range of countries that participate in the Fund: low income (Honduras, Nicaragua), middle income (Mexico, Venezuela, El Salvador, Guatemala, and Costa Rica), and advanced (Spain). From late 2000 to mid-2003 I served in Mexicos Ministry of Finance as Undersecretary. I was responsible for macroeconomic planning, financial sector regulation and supervision, coordination and oversight of our development banks, Mexicos relationship with international financial institutions, and debt management. In August 2003 I returned to the IMF as Deputy Managing Director (DMD). This provided me with the opportunity to work closely with two distinguished European Managing Directors: Horst Kohler and Rodrigo de Rato. In my purview as DMD, among other issues, I had the responsibility of managing the Funds relationship with over 70 countries. These included countries from Europe (among them, Italy, Spain, Greece, Portugal, and Belgium); North Africa and the Middle East (including Tunisia, Morocco, and Lebanon); Africa (Mali, Senegal, Tanzania, Burundi, and others); Asia (including Philippines, Malaysia, Cambodia, and Pakistan); Latin America (from Uruguay and the Dominican Republic to most of the Caribbean nations); and several other countries as varied as Armenia and Australia. In December 2006 I was designated by President Felipe Calderon as Mexicos Minister of Finance. I was responsible for tax policy, tax administration, customs, expenditure and debt management, and financial sector regulation and supervision. In December 2009 I was nominated by President Calderon and ratified by the Mexican Senate for a six year term as Governor of Banco de Mexico, the countrys autonomous Central Bank. I am not a member, and never have been, of any political party. 2 ECONOMIC POLICY RECORD When I started as an economist in 1980 Mexico was experiencing severe economic problems: very high inflation, disorderly public finances, monetary policy dominated by fiscal considerations, an unsustainable fixed exchange rate, a weak balance of payments, excessive public debt, and a poorly supervised and regulated financial system. Even though Mexico continues to confront challenges in terms of economic and human development, poverty alleviation and income distribution, today the country is enjoying rapid economic growth, low and controlled inflation, no balance of payments problems, record levels of international reserves, near balanced public finances, a debt to GDP ratio of approximately 35 percent, and a solid banking system which to a large extent is already Basel III compliant. This structural transformation required a major overhaul in the economic policymaking in my country. Since early on in my career I have had the opportunity to participate in the policymaking relevant to this transformation, with more of a direct and substantial contribution as my responsibilities have increased. Among the most significant policy transformations in Mexico that I have participated in, I would like to highlight the following: 1. The establishment of the autonomy of Banco de Mexico; 2. The external debt renegotiation in 1989, under the Brady Plan; 3. The shift from fixed to a managed, and finally to a freely floating exchange rate regime; 4. The reform of Mexicos pension fund system, in several stages; 5. The strengthening the regulation and supervision of Mexicos financial system, from a situation where we had sequential banking crises (up to 1995) to todays situation where we have a strong, well-capitalized banking system; 6. Several fiscal reforms, including two under my watch as Minister of Finance; 7. Also as Minister of Finance the approval of four Federal Budgets presented by a minority government, which required extensive political negotiations; 8. The inclusion of collective action clauses in Mexicos external debt in 2002; 9. The recent creation of a Financial Stability Council; 3 10. Strengthening of the inflation targeting regime followed by Banco de Mexico since 2001; 11. The design and implementation of the hedging program for Mexicos public finances oil price exposure through derivative markets; and 12. The use of the IMFs Flexible Credit Line (FCL) as a commitment vehicle to assure solid macroeconomic management. Let me stress that all these reforms have been the result of successful teamwork, which is essential, particularly in situations of crisis management, where I have ample experience. MANAGERIAL SKILLS My responsibilities in the Central Bank, Ministry of Finance, and the IMF have allowed me to acquire the skills to manage very complex institutions, including one with multinational and diverse staff, and with international operations, such as the Fund. I have worked closely with the Funds staff and I know they are its most important asset. DIPLOMATIC SKILLS AND APPRECIATION OF MULTILATERAL COOPERATION Very early in my career I recognized the importance of diplomacy. Mexico has traditionally been an active participant in multilateral affairs (indeed, Mexico is a proud founding member of the Fund, having participated in the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference). I acquired diplomatic skills on the job in my country, which were further shaped and enhanced during the time I served in the Fund as Executive Director (ED) and as DMD. In fact, in my purview as DMD, I was responsible for managing the IMFs relationship with other international financial institutions (excluding the World Bank), and the United Nations system, which gave me both experience and profound appreciation for effective coordination among multilateral organizations. 4 In addition, I have also played important roles in several fora designed to enhance multilateral cooperation: a) Active participant in the G-20 process since its inception; b) Chairman of the Joint IMF-World Bank Development Committee, 2007  2009; c) Governor of Mexico in the IMF, World Bank and IDB; d) Current member of the Financial Stability Board (FSB) Steering Committee and Cochair of the Americas FSB Regional Consultative Group; and e) BIS Board Member. PROVEN UNDERSTANDING OF THE FUND AND THE POLICY CHALLENGES FACING THE FUNDS DIVERSE MEMBERSHIP I have the advantage of knowing the Fund from three different points of view, given the responsibilities I have had: as a member country authority, as Executive Director, and as a member of the management team and staff (DMD). Thanks to this I have a thorough understanding of the Fund as an institution, and its challenges. At the same time, given the composition of the chair to which Mexico belongs, the broad purview I had as DMD and my engagement for so many years with the IMF, I have a clear understanding of the challenges of the Funds diverse membership. STRATEGIC VISION TO ADVANCE THE GOALS OF THE FUND The global financial crisis has vividly demonstrated how interconnected our world has become in the 21st century. While globalization has lead to unprecedented growth for many countries, be they advanced, emerging, or low income, the crisis reminded us that in an interconnected world maintaining stability and avoiding and resolving crisis is a collective responsibility. The IMF plays a unique role as the platform for global economic collaboration. With 187 member countries, it has a truly global representation, and with a staff that is both high- 5 caliber and diverse, it has the intellectual firepower and credibility to deliver objective, quality analysis and practical solutions, in short, to serve as the trusted advisor to member governments. In the last few years, the international community has taken some important steps to strengthen the IMF: The representation in particular of dynamic emerging market economies was increased to better reflect their economic weight in the world, while poorer countries were protected. These adjustments required substantial political effort on the part of many countries, and the success of the reform is testament to the international communitys recognition of the importance of the Funds legitimacy. The global financial safety net was revamped and new instruments were developed to avoid and resolve crises. My country, Mexico, benefitted from liquidity insurance that the IMF provided which helped us contain the spillovers of the global crisis. And the IMFs financial resources were increased to make its crisis fighting capacity commensurate with the size of the challenges in a globalized world. While much has been achieved by this joint effort of the international community, the reform agenda remains unfinished. Unfortunately, with countries emerging from the global crisis with diverging problems, incentives and enthusiasm for joint action is fading. Advanced countries are focusing on fiscal reforms to ensure medium-term fiscal sustainability; many emerging market countries in Asia and Latin America are struggling with managing large capital inflows and a few are starting to face overheating; and middle and low income countries in particular have been hit hard by commodity price increases. At the same time, Europe is focused on the crisis in some Eurozone members, and many countries in the Middle East and North Africa are at the beginning of a long political and economic transformation. There is no doubt that the Fund has to serve all its membership. Needless to say there always will be urgent country-member issues (such as the recent crises in the Eurozone and in the Middle East and North Africa) that will need to take precedent, and will absorb the 6 attention of the Managing Director, irrespective of his/her nationality. Precisely one of the challenges that any MD faces is to identify the issues that require the most prompt and appropriate response by the institution. This would allow the deployment of resources (human, technical and, in given cases, financial) to support the member-countries in greatest need, but this should be done without disregarding the rest of the membership. Always there will be countries with other issues to tackle, and the Fund should be in a position to respond to their needs also. We know where the current crises and urgent matters are today (Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa), but we do not know with certainty where the next ones will erupt. Therefore we need a Managing Director who can best serve all of the member countries, not merely those experiencing challenges at one particular point in time. While all crises erupt locally, in todays interconnected world they have the potential to affect us all. But for us to act, we need a legitimate global framework so that the international community can effectively support individual countries in their own reform efforts. And therefore the governance reforms that have begun need to be solidified and completed. To remain relevant, the Fund will have to deliver on improving the international monetary system, whose deficiencies were once again made evident during the crisis. Fund work on global imbalances and capital flows will require bold consensus building and the will of its membership to move forward. The Fund must also pay special attention to its members from low income countries (LIC). While the current crisis has diverted global attention from the fight against poverty, LIC assistance through appropriately funded programs is essential for crisis resolution, and in this capacity, the Fund is also in a unique position to make a significant contribution toward the fight. As for crisis prevention in LIC and middle income countries, I cannot think of a better instrument than the Technical Assistance (TA) provided by the Fund. During my tenure as Deputy Managing Director I heard firsthand from many of you about the benefits TA had brought to your countries. I also know from you that more work by the Fund is needed during the implementation phases of its TA recommendations. 7 At the same time, while emerging markets representation has been strengthened in global economic decision making, it is imperative that they have a stronger voice in the design and implementation of the Funds policies. This should come with their sharing more fully the responsibility of being stewards of the global economy. Finally, the Fund must remain legitimate in its three operational dimensions: staff, Executive Board, and Management. A diverse staff enhances legitimacy by providing a more balanced perspective and by being more attuned with member countries. The 2010 voice and representation reforms go a long way in addressing Executive Board imbalances. In the future, this process needs to continue. The next Managing Director of the IMF must serve the member countries by leading the institution and its staff and, in accordance with the Funds mission, help forge political consensus amongst members for policies that maximize global welfare. 8

Title: 80th National Banking Convention
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the inauguration of the 80th National Banking Convention March 22, 2017 Acapulco, Guerrero ? Mr. President of the United Mexican States, Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto, ? Mr. Governor of the State of Guerrero, Mr. Hector Astudillo Flores, ? Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena, ? Secretaries of State, ? Ladies and Gentlemen Legislators, ? Mr. Municipal President of Acapulco de Juarez, Licenciado Jesus Evodio Velazquez Aguirre, ? Mr. President of the National Banking and Securities Commission, teacher Jaime Gonzalez Aguade, ? Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, graduate Luis Robles Miaja, 1 ? Mr. President-Elect of the Association of Banks of Mexico, engineer Marcos Martinez Gavica, ? Distinguished members of the Presidium, ? Ladies and gentlemen, It is a great honor for me to participate in this Eightieth National Banking Convention. The mere fact that this is the 80th of the annual meetings that have been held in our country between authorities and financial institutions, is of historical importance. To this is added the unique complexity of the moment that the world economy and that of our country are experiencing. These are times of great challenges that demand from us not only effort and talent, but also to assess, in all that is worth, the strength of our institutions. Undoubtedly, the Bank of Mexico is one of the great institutional strengths that our country has. Since 1994, when its autonomy became fully operational with an unequivocal constitutional mandate to ensure low and stable inflation, and especially since 2001 when it adopted the inflation targeting scheme for the conduct of monetary policy, the Issuing Institute has fully complied with this mandate. 2 Thus, during the last fifteen years an average annual inflation rate of less than 5 percent has been achieved, while during the present decade this has been 3.6 percent. These data compare very favorably with an average annual inflation of 14.6 percent during the first ten years of the Bank's autonomy, that is, from 1994 to 2004. Hence, it is claimed that a substantial reduction in inflation has been achieved structurally. The gradual consolidation of average annual inflation at low levels has protected the purchasing power of all Mexicans' incomes, and has led to lower real and nominal interest rates, which in turn has allowed for greater credit growth and financial inclusion. The Bank of Mexico, in fulfilling its priority mandate, contributes crucially to the country's development and economic stability. Having a clear and unequivocal constitutional mandate is, for the Bank of Mexico, one of the most important pillars of its institutional strength, among other reasons because it allows society to evaluate punctually and timely the performance of the Institution and its challenges. Key in the process of institutional maturation has been the emphasis that has been given to transparency. In this spirit, the Governing Board has translated, for practical purposes, its unique constitutional mandate into 3 the achievement of an annual inflation of 3 per cent, allowing a range of variability of plus/minus one percentage point around that target. This interval considers the fact that there is a wide range of factors that are not within the control of the monetary authority and that in the short term can affect the behavior of inflation. It follows that if the observed inflation were outside the target range, or if expected inflation deviated substantially and steadily from that range, it would be expected that the Bank of Mexico would adjust its monetary policy stance, making use of the instruments at its disposal in this regard. In particular, you can vary your target from the overnight interbank interest rate, thereby inducing changes in the interest rate structure of the entire economy. In this way, the Issuing Institute sends a clear signal of its disagreement with the performance of inflation, and in this way seeks to influence the behavior of this and that the inflationary expectations of society are not overwhelmed. This process has worked very well in the past, and I am confident that it will continue to do in the future, including at the juncture we are going through. 4 In this sense, it should be remembered that inflation reached the 3 percent target in May 2015 and remained for 17 consecutive months below that target until October 2016, when it rebounded to close 2016 at 3.36 percent. It is currently at 4.86 percent. The latter figure is clearly outside the Bank's range of variability. We have come here as a result, first, of the extremely complicated external environment that the country has faced for several years now, which created the potential for higher inflation that has been gradually manifesting itself. Secondly, the acceleration of inflation during 2017 has been due to a fundamental change in the Mexican economy: the liberalization of energy prices in the country, and in particular, those of gasoline. Let us consider in greater detail these factors and their impact on inflation. As for the external elements, it is pertinent to highlight three: First, the abrupt fall in the international price of oil that occurred from mid-2014, represented an external shock of great magnitude in the real sector of the Mexican economy, as well as in public finances, which contributed to the depreciation of the national currency from the end of 2014. 5 Second, the uncertainty about the process of normalization of the monetary stance in the United States, which has caused substantial adjustments in capital flows to the country; and Third, high volatility in domestic financial markets as a result of the electoral process in the United States, as well as its outcome. The repercussions that some of the elements of the possible economic policy of the new administration of the northern neighbour could have on our country have undoubtedly led to an adjustment in the real exchange rate of our currency. These external shocks have manifested themselves in a significant depreciation of the national currency against the dollar. Although this trend began at the end of 2014, what has been surprising is the low transfer of the aforementioned exchange rate dynamics to inflation. This has been due to the fact that, even though the observed inflation was within the Bank's range of variability, the expected inflation for the future was increasing, so the monetary authority decided to react in advance. Thus, as of December 2015 the Bank of Mexico has been increasing its reference rate, by 325 basis points to date, which has undoubtedly softened the transfer of the 6 depreciation to the evolution of the general price level, and increased the credibility of the Central Institute. It should be clarified that the Bank of Mexico has responded to the depreciation of the exchange rate not because it has a target for the level of this, but because its behavior can affect the observed and expected inflation. Thus, it highlights that the fact that in 2016, when inflation was below 3 percent at historic lows, the Bank of Mexico continued with the adjustment of its monetary stance. It should also be borne in mind that under a floating exchange rate regime, such as to which the Mexican peso is subject, there is the possibility that the exchange rate will overreact in the short term and there will be subsequent corrections. A good example is what happened during this year. At a time of exacerbated uncertainty in mid-January, the peso traded above 22 pesos to the dollar. As this level is not compatible with the country's macroeconomic fundamentals, there has subsequently been a very significant correction, as evidenced by the fact that the national currency was quoted today at levels of 19.06 pesos per dollar. This correction will help reduce the inflation rate, facilitating its convergence to the objective. 7 Now let's consider the main domestic factor that has affected the dynamics of inflation. Adjustments in gasoline prices in January 2017, as a result of its liberalization, had clear effects on measured inflation, exacerbating its upward trend. It is important to note that although the liberalization of these prices has a transitory effect on inflation, it represents an advance for the consolidation of public finances, since it is not sustainable to maintain public prices misaligned from their international reference. In this context, as is well known, a sound fiscal stance contributes to strengthening the macroeconomic framework and helps to reduce risks in the economy, creating a more growth-friendly environment. In this way, this liberalization lays the foundations, through greater sustainability of public finances, so that the process of price formation of the economy in the medium term is more consistent with the inflation target of the Central Bank. However, given the recent behavior of inflation, it is very important to make the distinction between changes in relative prices and generalized and sustained price increases. Headline inflation data, as measured, does not in itself distinguish whether the impulse comes from supply shocks (which induce change). 8 in relative prices) or demand pressures, which induce generalized and sustained increases in prices, which is, precisely, the definition of inflation. It is precisely up to those responsible for monetary policy, the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, to discern carefully, and with the greatest possible collection of relevant information, if it is facing an episode of change in relative prices derived from a supply shock or, if it is facing a more persistent phenomenon that gives rise to a genuine inflationary trend. In the first case, the record of a rise in inflation will tend to dissipate, as long as inflation expectations remain anchored. This highlights the decisive role of anchoring inflation expectations in the process of price and wage formation. If, in the face of an adjustment of relative prices, second-order effects are presented, and some prices of goods not related to the original shock begin to rise, a contamination in inflation expectations is generated, leading them to lose their anchorage. Thus, if a supply shock that would have to affect a reduced set of prices ends, for one reason or another, generating generalized increases in prices, it is clearly a phenomenon. 9 inflationary. In this way, it is clear that it is essential that monetary policy reacts in a timely manner to any sign that inflation expectations could be unanchored. While the effects of the shocks on the short-term measurement of inflation that I have described have been significant, their effects are expected to be only temporary, since the Bank of Mexico has remained vigilant and has acted to avoid spillover effects in the process of price formation in the economy. This is consistent with the behavior of inflation expectations, where it is observed that those of the medium term have increased to a much lesser extent than those of the short term. In summary, for 2017 inflation is expected to be above the upper level of the variability range associated with the objective established by the Bank of Mexico, resuming a convergent trend towards the target during the last months of the year, to stand at about 3 percent at the end of 2018. In this sense, it could not be said that the Bank of Mexico has overreacted throughout 2016 and 2017. On the contrary, since monetary policy operates with certain lags on the economy, the Bank has acted preventively, so that the adjustment is 10 orderly and expectations (particularly those of the medium and long term) remain anchored. It is very important that the public has full confidence that the Bank of Mexico will do its job without hesitation, providing not only the discernment to distinguish the nature and possible effects of price variations, but also by paying extreme attention to react in a timely manner and keep inflation expectations anchored. * * * Allow me to make a final reflection. It is relevant to note that monetary policy does not operate in a vacuum, but is part of the economic policy of the State as a whole. The fact that decisions related to monetary policy are in the hands of the central bank does not imply that complementarity with other economic policies should not be sought. In fact, if there is greater synergy between the different policies of the State, the Bank of Mexico will be able to achieve its objective in a more efficient way, that is, at a lower cost to society. It must be remembered that low and stable inflation is not the ultimate goal of economic policy, but is the best contribution than the central bank. 11 it can make the ultimate goals of higher growth, better income distribution and greater well-being for the population. To the extent that we have a sound fiscal policy, which helps to contain the transfer of nominal exchange rate movements to consumer prices, there will be less pressure on interest rates. That is why in the face of an adverse external environment, the right balance must be found between the adjustment in the real exchange rate and in real interest rates. This balance sheet must be the result of an appropriate combination of fiscal policy and monetary policy, in order to obtain the best result from a macroeconomic point of view. In addition, Mexico must continue to increase its competitiveness abroad and boost the growth potential of its domestic market through greater productivity. It is essential that the commitment to correctly and timely implement the structural reforms promoted by President Pena Nieto prevail. In addition, it is essential to strengthen the rule of law and guarantee legal certainty in order to create a more favourable environment for growth. The strengthening of both the microeconomic functioning of the economy and macroeconomic soundness will allow the country to become a more attractive destination for investment. 12 In this way we will achieve greater potential growth of the economy, which will allow us to achieve a greater and more sustainable pace of economic activity, without generating pressures on inflation. Thanks a lot. 13
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la inauguracin de la 80 Convencin Nacional Bancaria 22 de marzo de 2017 Acapulco, Guerrero  Seor Presidente de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto,  Seor Gobernador del Estado de Guerrero, licenciado Hctor Astudillo Flores,  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Jos Antonio Meade Kuribrea,  Seores Secretarios de Estado,  Seoras y Seores Legisladores,  Seor Presidente Municipal de Acapulco de Jurez, Licenciado Jess Evodio Velzquez Aguirre,  Seor Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores, maestro Jaime Gonzlez Aguad,  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, licenciado Luis Robles Miaja, 1  Seor Presidente Electo de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, ingeniero Marcos Martnez Gavica,  Distinguidos miembros del Presdium,  Seoras y seores: Es para m un gran honor participar en esta Octogsima Convencin Nacional Bancaria. El Banco de Mxico, al cumplir con su mandato prioritario, contribuye de manera crucial al desarrollo y estabilidad econmica del pas. Por esta va, el Instituto Emisor manda una clara seal de su inconformidad con el desempeo de la inflacin, y de esta forma procura incidir sobre el comportamiento de sta y que no se desbordan las expectativas inflacionarias de la sociedad. Este proceso ha funcionado muy bien en el pasado, y estoy confiado de que lo que seguir haciendo en el futuro, incluyendo en la coyuntura por la que estamos atravesando. 4 En este sentido, cabe recordar que la inflacin alcanz la meta de 3 por ciento en mayo de 2015 y se mantuvo por 17 meses consecutivos por debajo de dicho objetivo hasta octubre de 2016, cuando repunt para cerrar 2016 en 3.36 por ciento. Actualmente se encuentra en 4.86 por ciento. Esta ltima cifra se situa claramente fuera del intervalo de variabilidad del Banco. Hemos llegado aqu como resultado, primero, del entorno externo extremadamente complicado que ha enfrentado el pas desde hace ya varios aos, el cual cre el potencial de una mayor inflacin que se ha venido manifestando gradualmente. En segundo lugar, el aceleramiento de la inflacin durante 2017 se ha debido a un cambio fundamental en la economa mexicana: la liberalizacin de los precios de los energticos en el pas, y en particular, de los de las gasolinas. Consideremos con mayor detalle estos factores y su incidencia sobre la inflacin. En cuanto a los elementos externos, es pertinente resaltar tres: Primero, la abrupta cada en el precio internacional del petrleo que se dio a partir de mediados de 2014, represent un choque externo de gran magnitud en el sector real de la economa mexicana, as como en las finanzas pblicas, lo que contribuy a la depreciacin de la moneda nacional a partir de finales de 2014. 5 Segundo, la incertidumbre sobre el proceso de normalizacin de la postura monetaria en Estados Unidos, lo cual ha provocado ajustes sustanciales en los flujos de capitales hacia el pas; y Tercero, una alta volatilidad en los mercados financieros domsticos como consecuencia del proceso electoral en Estados Unidos, as como de su resultado. Las repercusiones que podran tener en nuestro pas algunos de los elementos de la posible poltica econmica de la nueva administracin del vecino pas del norte sin duda han dado lugar a un ajuste en el tipo de cambio real de nuestra moneda. Estos choques externos se han manifestado en una depreciacin significativa de la moneda nacional con respecto al dlar. Si bien esta tendencia inici a finales de 2014, lo que ha sorprendido es el bajo traspaso de la referida dinmica cambiaria a la inflacin. Esto se ha debido a que, aun cuando la inflacin observada se encontraba dentro del intervalo de variabilidad de Banco, la inflacin esperada para el futuro se fue incrementando, por lo que la autoridad monetaria decidi reaccionar con anticipacin. As, a partir de diciembre de 2015 el Banco de Mxico ha venido incrementando su tasa de referencia, en 325 puntos base hasta la fecha, lo que sin duda ha suavizado el traspaso de la 6 depreciacin a la evolucin del nivel general de precios, e incrementado la credibilidad del Instituto Central. Cabe aclarar que el Banco de Mxico ha respondido a la depreciacin del tipo de cambio no porque tenga un objetivo para el nivel de ste, sino porque su comportamiento puede afectar la inflacin observada y esperada. As, destaca que el hecho de que en 2016, cuando la inflacin se encontraba por debajo de 3 por ciento en mnimos histricos, el Banco de Mexico prosigui con el ajuste de su postura monetaria. Tambin hay que tener en mente que bajo un rgimen cambiario de flotacin, como al que est sujeto el peso mexicano, hay la posibilidad de que el tipo de cambio sobrereaccione en el corto plazo y haya correcciones subsecuentes. Un buen ejemplo es lo sucedido durante este ao. En un momento de incertidumbre exacerbada a mediados de enero, el peso se cotiz por arriba de 22 pesos por dlar. Al no ser compatible este nivel con los fundamentos macroeconmicos del pas, posteriormente ha habido una correccin muy significativa, como lo evidenca el hecho de que la moneda nacional se cotiz hoy a niveles de 19.06 pesos por dlar. Esta correccin, ayudar a reducir la tasa de inflacin, facilitando su convergencia al objetivo. 7 Ahora consideremos el principal factor interno que ha afectado la dinmica de la inflacin. Los ajustes en los precios de las gasolinas en enero de 2017, producto de su liberalizacin, tuvieron claros efectos en la inflacin medida, exacerbando su tendencia al alza. Es importante sealar que si bien la liberalizacin de estos precios tiene un efecto transitorio en la inflacin, representa un avance para la consolidacin de las finanzas pblicas, ya que no es sostenible mantener precios pblicos desalineados de su referencia internacional. En este contexto, como es bien sabido, una postura fiscal slida contribuye a fortalecer el marco macroeconmico y coadyuva a reducir los riesgos en la economa, crendose un entorno ms propicio para el crecimiento. De esta forma, dicha liberalizacin sienta las bases, a travs de una mayor sostenibilidad de las finanzas pblicas, para que el proceso de formacin de precios de la economa en el mediano plazo sea ms congruente con la meta de inflacin del Banco Central. Ahora bien, dado que el comportamiento reciente de la inflacin, es muy importante hacer la distincin entre cambios en precios relativos y aumentos generalizados y sostenidos de los precios. El dato de inflacin general, tal y como se mide, no distingue por s mismo si el impulso proviene de choques de oferta (que inducen cambios 8 en precios relativos) o de presiones de demanda, que inducen aumentos generalizados y sostenidos en los precios, que es, justamente, la definicin de inflacin. Corresponde precisamente a los responsables de la poltica monetaria, la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico, discernir cuidadosamente, y con el mayor acopio posible de informacin pertinente, si se enfrenta un episodio de cambio en precios relativos derivado de un choque de oferta o, si se est ante un fenmeno ms persistente que d lugar a una genuina tendencia inflacionaria. En el primer caso, el registro de un alza en la inflacin tender a disiparse, siempre y cuando las expectativas de inflacin permanezcan ancladas. Esto destaca el papel decisivo que tiene el anclaje de las expectativas de inflacin en el proceso de formacin de precios y de salarios. Si ante un ajuste de precios relativos se presentan efectos de segundo orden, y algunos precios de bienes no relacionados con el choque original se empiezan a elevar, se genera una contaminacin en las expectativas de inflacin, conduciendo a que las mismas pierdan su anclaje. As, si un choque de oferta que tendra que afectar a un conjunto reducido de precios, termina, por una u otra razn, generando aumentos generalizados en los precios, se trata de un fenmeno claramente 9 inflacionario. De esta forma, queda claro que es primordial que la poltica monetaria reaccione oportunamente ante cualquier seal de que las expectativas de inflacin pudiesen desanclarse. Si bien los efectos de los choques sobre la medicin de corto plazo de la inflacin que he descrito han sido importantes, se espera que sus efectos sean solamente temporales, toda vez que el Banco de Mxico se ha mantenido vigilante y ha actuado para evitar efectos de contagio en el proceso de formacin de precios en la economa. Lo anterior es consistente con el comportamiento de las expectativas de inflacin, donde se observa que las de mediano plazo han aumentado en mucho menor medida que las de corto plazo. En resumen, para 2017 se espera que la inflacin se ubique por encima de la cota superior del intervalo de variabilidad asociado al objetivo establecido por el Banco de Mxico, retomando una tendencia convergente hacia la meta durante los ltimos meses del ao, para situarse cerca de 3 por ciento al cierre de 2018. En este sentido, no podra decirse que el Banco de Mxico haya sobrerreaccionado a lo largo de 2016 y 2017. Por el contrario, dado que la poltica monetaria opera con ciertos rezagos sobre la economa, el Banco ha actuado de manera preventiva, de manera que el ajuste sea 10 ordenado y las expectativas (en particular las de mediano y largo plazo) se mantengan ancladas. Es por dems importante que el pblico tenga plena confianza en que el Banco de Mxico har su trabajo sin titubeos, aportando no slo el discernimiento para distinguir la naturaleza y efectos posibles de las variaciones en los precios, sino extremando su atencin para reaccionar oportunamente y mantener ancladas las expectativas de inflacin. * * * Me permito hacer una reflexin final. Es relevante destacar que la poltica monetaria no opera en el vaco, sino que es parte de la poltica econmica del Estado en su conjunto. El que las decisiones relacionadas con la poltica monetaria estn en manos del banco central, no implica que no se deba buscar una complementariedad con otras polticas econmicas. De hecho, de existir mayor sinergia entre las distintas polticas del Estado, el Banco de Mxico podr lograr su objetivo de una manera ms eficiente, es decir, a un menor costo para la sociedad. Hay que recordar que una inflacin baja y estable no es el objetivo final de la poltica econmica, sino que es la mejor contribucin que el banco central 11 puede hacer a los objetivos supremos de mayor crecimiento, mejor distribucin del ingreso y mayor bienestar para la poblacin. En la medida en que contemos con una poltica fiscal sana, y que ayude a contener el traspaso de los movimientos del tipo de cambio nominal a los precios del consumidor, habr menores presiones sobre las tasas de inters. Es por ello que ante un entorno externo adverso, se debe encontrar el balance adecuado entre el ajuste en el tipo de cambio real y en las tasas de inters reales. Este balance debe ser resultado de una combinacin idnea entre la poltica fiscal y la poltica monetaria, para obtener el mejor resultado desde el punto de vista macroeconmico. En adicin, Mxico debe continuar incrementando su competitividad frente al exterior e impulsar el potencial de crecimiento de su mercado interno mediante una mayor productividad. Es esencial que prevalezca el compromiso de implementar correcta y oportunamente las reformas estructurales promovidas por el Presidente Pea Nieto. Adicionalmente, resulta indispensable fortalecer el estado de derecho y garantizar la seguridad jurdica con el fin de propiciar un entorno ms favorable para el crecimiento. El robustecimiento tanto del funcionamiento microeconmico de la economa, como de la solidez macroeconmica, permitir al pas convertirse en un destino ms atractivo para la inversin. 12 De esta manera lograremos un mayor crecimiento potencial de la economa, que nos permitir alcanzar un mayor y ms sostenible ritmo de actividad econmica, sin generar presiones sobre la inflacin. Muchas gracias. 13

Title: What is financial education?
text: What is Financial Education? Words from Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the Seventh Symposium Economic and Financial Education, Theory and Practice Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE) Mexico, D.F. September 25, 2015 It is an honor to participate, on behalf of the Bank of Mexico, in the opening of the symposium "Economic and financial education, theory and practice" organized by the Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE). In recent years, the concept of financial education has been very present in institutions, intermediaries and authorities around the world. Such a notion tends to relate to knowledge and skills to make good decisions in the matter. However, the definitions of financial education usually vary, there is no generally accepted one and many suffer from theoretical and operational vagueness. Therefore, often under the same term, it is possible to find references to actions that pursue heterogeneous purposes.1 This ambivalence invites us to delve into the possible nature and scope of financial education. In addition, a careful evaluation of the results of the programmes undertaken is needed to identify their contributions and contribute to focusing them on the greatest benefit of society. 1 Vease Remund, D. (2010). "Financial Literacy Explicated: The Case for a Clearer Definition in an Increasingly Complex Economy," Journal of Consumer Affairs, Special Issue: Financial Literacy, 44(2). 2 Given its breadth, it would be useful to identify some fundamental dimensions of the subject, among which I highlight three. Financial intuition The first plane would be financial intuition, which consists of that spontaneous tendency of any individual to respond adequately to market signals and the institutional framework that provides incentives of different kinds. Thanks to this propensity, people, regardless of their social status and schooling, have the intrinsic ability to prioritize their needs and preferences, set goals and make decisions that favor them. The mechanisms of choice are not exclusive to the educated or the rich. Intuition allows the average individual to choose, within a group of existing alternatives, the most convenient option for their interests. Therefore, I believe that we must reject the tutelary or paternalistic notion of financial education that, sometimes, rather than providing information and tools, aims to teach. A broad body of research confirms that, in the right environment, people make sensible decisions according to their goals.2 2 For a seminal reference to the rationality of poor farmers, see Schultz, T. (1964). Transforming Traditional Agriculture, New Haven: Yale University Press. 3 Information, regulation and competition A second dimension concerns financial reporting. The availability of data that affects opportunities and constraints around the goals of individuals, families, and businesses is critical. Prices and the institutional framework send clear signals that guide savings, consumption and investment, among others. These decisions are enriched by timely information. In this sense, it is an inescapable obligation of the authorities and intermediaries to ensure that information, which must be a public good, is widely distributed and timely, truthful, relevant and intelligible. In particular, the information must ensure that the individual not only knows the nature of the financial products but also their rights and obligations when contracting one. Thus, the conditions of the services must be made totally transparent, including enlarging the so-called small letters of the contracts and evidencing the possible hidden costs. In addition, it is desirable that comparative statistics be provided to assess the desirability of the various options. To mention one example, cat comparison charts published in account statements facilitate the evaluation of a credit product and an institution against other alternatives. Another example should be the obligation to communicate to the customer the total costs of sales in subscriptions and not only the monthly payments. 4 Competition and regulation help to prevent fraudulent practices and promote customer certainty. This eliminates some of the biggest barriers to financial inclusion, such as distrust of intermediaries and the high cost of solving problems and differences with some of them. Formal instruction The third scope refers to formal instruction, which ranges from knowledge of elementary personal finance topics to more specialized preparation in aspects of budgeting or accounting. Such instruction can support determinations such as purchasing child education insurance or starting a business. Instruction has its natural space in classrooms and it would be important to incorporate it as part of educational programs from the initial grades. However, in order to reduce training failures and lags, it might be desirable to design programmes for certain social or age groups. For example, in Mexico we are living through a transitional stage in the pension system, in which we move from a collective scheme to an individual one. Familiarization with such simple notions as compound interest or present value can have a significant impact on decisions that increase quality of life during retirement. Likewise, instruction and training can be encouraged to potentiate the spirit of enterprise present in many individuals. 5 The offer of financial education offered by some intermediaries starts from a laudable purpose and can have a significant social spillover. However, for it to bear fruit, its limits must be considered. In particular, while customer search, as part of the competition, is positive to the extent that it disseminates truthful information, customer acquisition should not be confused with financial education. In short, I believe that those of us who participate in this work must do so with pragmatism and modesty. On the one hand, we must choose concrete and measurable objectives. On the other hand, we must remember that our function does not involve indoctrinating or changing mentalities, but supporting and stimulating latent competences and initiatives in people. The MIDE an experience in financial education The MIDE, which today offers us hospitality, is an ideal place to hold this seminar, not only for the majesty of its facilities, but for its role in financial education. In this enclosure the different dimensions of this activity meet harmoniously. There are innovative technological and pedagogical resources to introduce young people to economic dilemmas and exercise their intuition. Its permanent rooms provide didactic information about the system and the main financial products. It also has a specialized training offer, 6 which includes courses and seminars or special events, such as the symposium that brings us together today. There are those who, like Alain de Botton, have pointed out that a museum should not be a place of exhibition of objects ordered in a conventional way, but a space of revelation and reflection where the individual raises and finds answers to his deepest concerns and needs. Undoubtedly, MIDE fulfills this condition for financial education.3 Finally, I wish to reiterate my gratitude to this great museum for its hospitality, to welcome the distinguished participants in the symposium and to wish them every success in their work. 3 Vease de Botton, A. (2012). Religion for Atheists: A Non-believer's Guide to the Uses of Religion, New York: Vintage Books, capitulo VIII, Art. 7
