Palabras de Manuel Snchez Gonzlez Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico en el Sptimo Simposio Educacin Econmica y Financiera, Teora y Prctica Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE) Mxico, D.F. 25 de septiembre de 2015 Es un honor participar, a nombre del Banco de Mxico, en la apertura del simposio Educacin econmica y financiera, teora y prctica organizado por el Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE). En los aos recientes, el concepto de educacin financiera ha estado muy presente en las instituciones, intermediarios y autoridades de todo el mundo. Tal nocin tiende a relacionarse con conocimientos y habilidades para tomar buenas decisiones en la materia. Sin embargo, las definiciones de educacin financiera suelen variar, no hay una generalmente aceptada y muchas adolecen de vaguedades tericas y operativas. Por eso, a menudo bajo el mismo trmino, es posible encontrar referencias a acciones que persiguen propsitos heterogneos.1 Esta ambivalencia invita a profundizar en la posible naturaleza y alcance de la educacin financiera. Adems, se necesita una evaluacin cuidadosa de los resultados de los programas emprendidos que permita identificar sus aportaciones y contribuya a enfocarlos al mayor beneficio de la sociedad. 1 Vase Remund, D. (2010). Financial Literacy Explicated: The Case for a Clearer Definition in an Increasingly Complex Economy, Journal of Consumer Affairs, Special Issue: Financial Literacy, 44(2). 2 Dada su amplitud, convendra identificar algunas dimensiones fundamentales del tema, entre las que destaco tres. Intuicin financiera El primer plano sera la intuicin financiera, la cual consiste en esa tendencia espontnea de cualquier individuo a responder adecuadamente a las seales del mercado y al marco institucional que brinda incentivos de diferente ndole. Gracias a esta propensin, las personas, independientemente de su condicin social y escolaridad, tienen la capacidad intrnseca de jerarquizar sus necesidades y preferencias, proponerse metas y tomar decisiones que les favorezcan. Los mecanismos de eleccin no son privativos de los instruidos ni de los ricos. La intuicin permite que el individuo promedio elija, dentro de un grupo de alternativas existentes, la opcin ms conveniente para sus intereses. Por eso, considero que debemos rechazar la nocin tutelar o paternalista de la educacin financiera que, en ocasiones, ms que brindar informacin y herramientas, pretende aleccionar. Un amplio cuerpo de investigacin confirma que, en un ambiente adecuado, la gente toma decisiones sensatas de acuerdo con sus objetivos.2 2 Para una referencia seminal sobre la racionalidad de los agricultores pobres, Vase Schultz, T. (1964). Transforming Traditional Agriculture, New Haven: Yale University Press. 3 Informacin, regulacin y competencia Una segunda dimensin se refiere a la informacin financiera. Resulta fundamental la disponibilidad de datos que afectan las oportunidades y restricciones en torno a los objetivos de los individuos, las familias y las empresas. Los precios y el marco institucional emiten seales claras que orientan el ahorro, el consumo y la inversin, entre otros. Esas decisiones se enriquecen con la informacin puntual. En este sentido, es una obligacin ineludible de las autoridades y los intermediarios propiciar que la informacin, que debe ser un bien pblico, est ampliamente distribuida y sea oportuna, veraz, pertinente e inteligible. En particular, la informacin debe asegurar que el individuo no solo conozca la naturaleza de los productos financieros sino adems sus derechos y obligaciones al contratar alguno. As, se debe hacer totalmente transparentes las condiciones de los servicios, incluyendo agrandar las llamadas letras chiquitas de los contratos y evidenciar los posibles costos ocultos. Adems, es deseable que se proporcionen estadsticas comparativas para evaluar la conveniencia de las distintas opciones. Por mencionar un ejemplo, los cuadros comparativos del CAT publicados en los estados de cuenta facilitan la evaluacin de un producto de crdito y de una institucin respecto de otras alternativas. Otro ejemplo debera ser la obligacin de comunicar al cliente los costos totales de las ventas en abonos y no solo las mensualidades. 4 La competencia y la regulacin contribuyen a evitar prcticas fraudulentas y favorecer la certidumbre del cliente. Ello elimina algunas de las mayores barreras a la inclusin financiera, como son la desconfianza ante las intermediarias y el alto costo de resolver problemas y diferencias con alguno de ellos. Instruccin formal El tercer alcance alude a la instruccin formal, que va desde el conocimiento de temas elementales de finanzas personales hasta la preparacin ms especializada en aspectos de presupuesto o contabilidad. Dicha instruccin puede apoyar determinaciones como la compra de un seguro para la educacin de los hijos o el inicio de un negocio. La instruccin tiene su espacio natural en las aulas y sera importante que se incorporara como parte de los programas educativos desde los grados iniciales. Sin embargo, para aminorar fallas y rezagos de formacin, podra resultar deseable disear programas para determinados grupos sociales o de edad. Por ejemplo, en Mxico vivimos una etapa de transicin en el sistema de pensiones, en el que pasamos de un esquema colectivo a uno individual. La familiarizacin con nociones tan sencillas como el inters compuesto o el valor presente pueden tener una repercusin significativa para las decisiones que aumenten la calidad de vida durante el retiro. Igualmente, se puede fomentar la instruccin y capacitacin para potencializar el espritu de empresa presente en muchos individuos. 5 La oferta de educacin financiera que ofrecen algunos intermediarios parte de un propsito loable y puede tener una derrama social significativa. Sin embargo, para que rinda frutos deben considerarse sus lmites. En particular, si bien la bsqueda de clientes, como parte de la competencia, es positiva en la medida en que difunda informacin veraz, la captacin de clientes no debe confundirse con la educacin financiera. En suma, creo que quienes participamos en esta labor debemos hacerlo con pragmatismo y modestia. Por un lado, debemos escoger objetivos concretos y mensurables. Por el otro, debemos recordar que nuestra funcin no implica adoctrinar o cambiar mentalidades, sino apoyar y estimular competencias e iniciativas latentes en las personas. El MIDE una experiencia en educacin financiera El MIDE, que hoy nos brinda hospitalidad, es un lugar ideal para realizar este seminario, no solo por lo majestuoso de sus instalaciones, sino por su papel en la educacin financiera. En este recinto se renen armnicamente las distintas dimensiones de esta actividad. Existen novedosos recursos tecnolgicos y pedaggicos para introducir a los jvenes en los dilemas econmicos y ejercitar su intuicin. Sus salas permanentes brindan informacin didctica sobre el sistema y los principales productos financieros. Cuenta tambin con una oferta de formacin especializada, 6 que incluye cursos y seminarios o eventos especiales, como el simposio que hoy nos rene. Hay quienes, como Alain de Botton, han sealado que un museo no debe ser un lugar de exhibicin de objetos ordenados de forma convencional, sino un espacio de revelacin y reflexin donde el individuo se plantea y encuentra respuestas a sus ms profundas inquietudes y necesidades. Sin duda, el MIDE cumple esta condicin para la educacin financiera.3 Finalmente, deseo reiterar mi agradecimiento a este gran museo por su hospitalidad, dar la bienvenida a los distinguidos participantes en el simposio y desearles mucho xito en sus trabajos. 3 Vase de Botton, A. Title: Celebration of the fifty years of the establishment of FIDERH
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the celebration of the fifty years of the establishment of FIDERH. Mexico City, July 13, 2021 It gives me great pleasure to participate in this celebration for the fifty years of the Fund for the Development of Human Resources of the Bank of Mexico (FIDERH). As you all know, FIDERH was established on a day like today, July 13, half a century ago, by the Federal Government and the Bank of Mexico. The mandate of FIDERH is to support, through the granting of educational credits, the training of specialists in those scientific, technological and administrative disciplines that can contribute significantly to the economic and social development of the country. Since 1971, FIDERH has contributed to the progress of Mexico through the formation of human capital of excellence. The Bank of Mexico as a fiduciary institution has monitored, during all this time, the full scope of the purpose of FIDERH, with measurable, transparent and effective results, always seeking to comply with this 1 fiduciary entrustment, which in the legal origin of the term refers to acting as a "good father of a family". A fundamental principle of social equity is equal opportunities, among which educational opportunities are of great importance. Greater education and professional specialization benefit the individuals who have access to them and, at the same time, raise the productivity and development possibilities of a country. Investment in education and training has a proven individual, social and economic profitability. Educational credit is an effective mechanism to promote the training of human resources, since it consists of the loan so that a student pays partially or completely for his studies and, when he acquires the degree and is more productive, he can gradually cover said credit. Recovered resources are used to provide more opportunities and credit to other students. In this way, the educational credit, which for fifty years has been granted by FIDERH is a 2 solidarity mechanism, where the rotation of resources allows to support the successive specialization of different generations. The training of human and professional resources is a permanent necessity of national development. During the last century, after the Mexican Revolution, the reconstruction of the country required raising the educational level of the general population and having well-prepared specialists who could bridge the development gaps and assume positions of responsibility. In the Bank of Mexico, for many decades, there has been a clear awareness of the need to promote the training of human resources both in areas of interest of the bank itself, and in other priority areas of the economy. In 1965 the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Bank of Mexico decided to create a fund for the promotion of higher education through educational credits, giving rise in 1966 to the "Credit Program for Specialization Studies". The experience that was acquired with the administration of this program, as well as the contribution to the country of many of the students 3 benefited in different institutional areas, they made evident the convenience of giving institutional sustainability and permanence to such a valuable effort. In this way, in 1971 the aforementioned "Credit Program for Specialization Studies" was transformed into the trust that today is FIDERH. With FIDERH, the Bank of Mexico has been a significant participant in the process of training students who, most likely, would not have been able to achieve their specialization otherwise. This has helped to level educational opportunities and has supported the modernization and economic development of the country. Specifically, in the last 50 years FIDERH has benefited more than 20,000 graduate students to study at the best universities in Mexico and the world, granting, on average, 400 educational credits per year. 4 Throughout its history, FIDERH has granted loans for an amount at present value close to 6,000 million pesos. Currently, this fund has a total portfolio amount under administration that exceeds one billion pesos (1,103.2 million pesos) and, as of May 31, 2021, manages more than 6,600 loans. About 80% of our accredited students study their postgraduate studies abroad. While approximately the remaining 20% study at the best universities in Mexico. Most of those accredited study their postgraduate studies in the area of Social and Administrative Sciences and, recently, the preference for postgraduate courses within the area of Engineering and Technology has increased. The Human Resources Development Fund has more than 100 collaboration agreements with universities in 13 countries. These agreements offer their accredited discounts and scholarships that increase the benefits for the student and help him choose the 5 best program. In 2020, 43% of those accredited (271 out of 630) chose a university with a FIDERH agreement. In the face of the COVID-19 pandemic, in 2020, electronic contract signing options were implemented and online and mixed programs were authorized to be financed. In 2020, despite the health emergency situation, FIDERH managed to grant 630 credits (in 2019 it granted 929), by 2021 it is projected to finance at least 720 students. Thus, a recovery in the placement of educational credits is underway, which has special value when considering the situation in which we find ourselves. In 2021, the points assessment system was redesigned to determine credit awarding in order to give more weight to academic quality. Credit analysis was also strengthened from a retrospective approach to the creditor and its guarantees, to a prospective approach, in accordance with the best financial and banking practices. 6 It is very important to note that the variable interest rate of the FIDERH credit is very competitive (75% of CPP) and, additionally, those accredited are encouraged with the reduction (from 75 to 25% of CPP) for those who prove that their professional practice is for the benefit of Mexico, or even the elimination of the interest rate and only the payment of capital for those who prove that they are full-time researchers within the Mexican Republic or who provide their services in an institution of higher education or in the public sector outside the metropolitan areas of Mexico City, Guadalajara or Monterrey. Among the high-quality postgraduate studies and specialization funded are cutting-edge scientific and technological areas, such as Data Science, Aerospace and Computer Engineering, Robotics, Biomedical and Health Sciences, and Economics and Business, among others. FIDERH is a public policy instrument that has helped Mexico to strengthen the professional training that the country needs. In addition, the revolving and sustainability of its resources, and its ability to 7 adaptation to the needs of applicants, together with the efficient use of credit and the timely and responsible payment of the vast majority of accredited, allow that each year new credits can be granted. Ladies and gentlemen, the bodies in charge of educational financing must preserve the balance between their social character and their financial sustainability. To this end, a strategic approach that is quickly oriented to the priority sectors for national development is essential; a transparent administration and a prudent and efficient management of credit, as well as building co-responsibility among the entire community of beneficiaries. With this, it is sought that the educational credit mechanism generates a virtuous circle. The strategic focus in the areas of study makes it possible to multiply the effect of educational credit on the national economy and its social profitability. The efficient management of resources ensures the financial viability of the credit mechanism and builds trust. The co-responsibility of the beneficiaries strengthens solidarity 8 intergenerational, since the fulfillment of the accredited generates resources that will be used in the future to continue deepening in the specialization and the improvement of the knowledge and competences of the new generations. The granting of educational credits is a public policy of broad and proven benefits. Proof of this is the permanence and growing relevance of FIDERH, which today celebrates fifty years, and which has driven generations of students who seek to achieve academic excellence and their best professional version, for the benefit of their loved ones and their country. Thousands of Mexicans benefiting from an educational credit from FIDERH, who have contributed and contribute to national growth, are the best testimony to the effectiveness and benefits of this mechanism. For all the above, it is a pleasure for me to extend the widest congratulations to all the fellows and administrators of the program, who have made possible this exemplary instrument, which has transformed the lives of thousands of students and improved our country, I wish you to celebrate many more anniversaries. 9 At the same time, I am pleased to announce the opening of the fourth call 2021, which is available from today, July 13 on the FIDERH website where interested people can consult the bases and register to start the process of applying for educational credit. Thank you and congratulations. 10
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la celebracin de los cincuenta aos del establecimiento del FIDERH. Ciudad de Mxico, 13 de julio de 2021 Me da mucho gusto participar en esta celebracin por los cincuenta aos del Fondo para el Desarrollo de Recursos Humanos del Banco de Mxico (FIDERH). Como todos ustedes saben, el FIDERH fue constituido un da como hoy, 13 de julio, hace medio siglo, por el Gobierno Federal y el Banco de Mxico. El mandato del FIDERH es apoyar, a travs del otorgamiento de crditos educativos, la formacin de especialistas en aquellas disciplinas cientficas, tecnolgicas y administrativas que puedan contribuir destacadamente al desarrollo econmico y social del pas. Desde 1971, FIDERH ha aportado al progreso de Mxico a travs de la formacin de capital humano de excelencia. El Banco de Mxico como institucin fiduciaria ha vigilado, durante todo este tiempo, el cabal alcance de la finalidad del FIDERH, con resultados medibles, transparentes y efectivos, buscando siempre cumplir con esta 1 encomienda fiduciaria, que en el origen jurdico del trmino se refiere a actuar como un buen padre de familia. *** Un principio fundamental de la equidad social es la igualdad de oportunidades, entre las cuales las educativas son de gran importancia. La mayor educacin y la especializacin profesional benefician a los individuos que tienen acceso a ellas y, a la vez, elevan la productividad y las posibilidades de desarrollo de un pas. La inversin en educacin y adiestramiento tiene una probada rentabilidad individual, social y econmica. El crdito educativo es un mecanismo eficaz para promover la formacin de recursos humanos, pues consiste en el prstamo para que un estudiante pague de manera parcial o completa sus estudios y, cuando adquiera el grado y sea ms productivo, pueda cubrir gradualmente dicho crdito. Los recursos recuperados se utilizan para brindar ms oportunidades y crdito a otros estudiantes. De esta manera, el crdito educativo, que por cincuenta aos ha otorgado el FIDERH es un 2 mecanismo solidario, en donde la rotacin de recursos permite apoyar la especializacin sucesiva de diversas generaciones. La formacin de recursos humanos y profesionales es una necesidad permanente del desarrollo nacional. Durante el siglo pasado, despus de la Revolucin Mexicana, la reconstruccin del pas requera elevar el nivel educativo de la poblacin en general y contar con especialistas bien preparados que pudieran zanjar las brechas de desarrollo y asumir puestos de responsabilidad. En el Banco de Mxico, desde hace muchas dcadas, ha existido una clara conciencia de la necesidad de fomentar la formacin de recursos humanos tanto en reas de inters del propio banco, como en otros mbitos prioritarios de la economa. En 1965 la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico y el Banco de Mxico decidieron la creacin de un fondo destinado a la promocin de la educacin superior a travs de crditos educativos, dando lugar en 1966 al Programa de crdito para estudios de especializacin. La experiencia que se adquiri con la administracin de este programa, as como la aportacin al pas de muchos de los estudiantes 3 beneficiados en diferentes mbitos institucionales, hicieron evidente la conveniencia de dar sustentabilidad institucional y permanencia a tan valioso esfuerzo. De esta manera, en 1971 el mencionado Programa de crdito para estudios de especializacin se transform en el fideicomiso que hoy es FIDERH. Con el FIDERH, el Banco de Mxico ha sido un partcipe significativo en el proceso de formacin de estudiantes que, muy probablemente, no hubieran podido lograr su especializacin de otra manera. Con ello, se ha contribuido a nivelar oportunidades educativas y se ha apoyado a la modernizacin y el desarrollo econmico del pas. En concreto, en los ltimos 50 aos el FIDERH ha beneficiado a ms de 20,000 estudiantes de posgrado para que estudien en las mejores universidades de Mxico y el mundo, otorgando, en promedio, 400 crditos educativos por ao. 4 A lo largo de su historia, FIDERH ha otorgado crditos por un monto a valor presente cercano a los $6,000 millones de pesos. Actualmente, este fondo cuenta con un monto de cartera total en administracin que supera los mil millones de pesos ($1,103.2 mdp) y, al 31 de mayo de 2021, administra ms de 6,600 crditos. Alrededor del 80% de nuestros acreditados estudian su posgrado en el extranjero. Mientras que aproximadamente el 20% restante estudia en las mejores universidades de Mxico. La mayora de los acreditados estudia su posgrado en el rea de Ciencias Sociales y Administrativas y, recientemente, ha aumentado la preferencia por posgrados dentro del rea de Ingeniera y Tecnologa. El Fondo para el Desarrollo de Recursos Humanos cuenta con ms de 100 convenios de colaboracin con universidades en 13 pases. Dichos convenios, ofrecen a sus acreditados descuentos y becas que incrementan los beneficios para el estudiante y le ayudan a elegir el 5 mejor programa. En 2020, el 43% de los acreditados (271 de 630) eligieron una universidad con convenio FIDERH. Ante la pandemia del COVID-19 en 2020 se implementaron opciones electrnicas de firma de contrato y se autoriz financiar programas en lnea y mixtos. En 2020, a pesar de la situacin de emergencia sanitaria, FIDERH logr otorgar 630 crditos (en 2019 otorg 929), para 2021 se proyecta financiar al menos a 720 estudiantes. As, est en marcha una recuperacin en la colocacin de crditos educativos, que tiene especial valor al considerar la coyuntura en que nos encontramos. En 2021, se redise el sistema de evaluacin por puntos para determinar el otorgamiento de crditos a fin de otorgar ms peso a la calidad acadmica. Tambin se fortaleci el anlisis crediticio pasando de un enfoque retrospectivo del acreditado y sus avales, a un enfoque prospectivo, acorde con las mejores prcticas financieras y bancarias. 6 Es muy importante destacar que la tasa variable de inters del crdito FIDERH es muy competitiva (75% de CPP) y, adicionalmente, se incentiva a los acreditados con la reduccin (de 75 a 25% de CPP) para aquellos que comprueban que su ejercicio profesional es en beneficio de Mxico, o inclusive la eliminacin de la tasa de inters y slo el pago de capital para aquellos que comprueben que son investigadores de tiempo completo dentro de la Repblica Mexicana o que presten sus servicios en alguna institucin de educacin superior o en el sector pblico fuera de las reas metropolitanas de la ciudad de Mxico, Guadalajara o Monterrey. Entre los estudios de posgrado de alta calidad y especializacin financiados destacan reas cientficas y tecnolgicas de vanguardia, como Ciencia de Datos, Ingeniera Aeroespacial y en Computacin, Robtica, Ciencias Biomdicas y de la Salud, y Economa y Negocios, entre otras. FIDERH es un instrumento de poltica pblica que ha servido a Mxico para reforzar la formacin profesional que necesita el pas. Adems, la revolvencia y la sustentabilidad de sus recursos, y su capacidad de 7 adaptacin a las necesidades de los solicitantes, junto con el uso eficiente del crdito y el pago puntual y responsable de la inmensa mayora de acreditados, permiten que cada ao se puedan otorgar nuevos crditos. Seoras y seores: Las instancias encargadas del financiamiento educativo deben preservar el equilibrio entre su carcter social y su sustentabilidad financiera. Para ello, es imprescindible un enfoque estratgico que con agilidad se oriente a los sectores prioritarios para el desarrollo nacional; una administracin transparente y un manejo prudente y eficiente del crdito, as como construir corresponsabilidad entre toda la comunidad de beneficiarios. Con esto, se busca que el mecanismo de crdito educativo genere un crculo virtuoso. El enfoque estratgico en las reas de estudio permite multiplicar el efecto del crdito educativo en la economa nacional y su rentabilidad social. El manejo eficiente de los recursos asegura la viabilidad financiera del mecanismo de crdito y genera confianza. La corresponsabilidad de los beneficiarios fortalece la solidaridad 8 intergeneracional, ya que el cumplimiento de los acreditados genera recursos que sern aprovechados en el futuro para seguir profundizando en la especializacin y el perfeccionamiento de los conocimientos y competencias de las nuevas generaciones. El otorgamiento de crditos educativos es una poltica pblica de amplios y probados beneficios. Prueba de ello es la permanencia y creciente relevancia del FIDERH, que hoy cumple cincuenta aos, y que ha impulsado a generaciones de estudiantes que buscan alcanzar la excelencia acadmica y su mejor versin profesional, en beneficio de sus seres queridos y de su pas. Miles de mexicanas y mexicanos beneficiados con un crdito educativo del FIDERH, que han contribuido y contribuyen al crecimiento nacional, son el mejor testimonio de la efectividad y los beneficios de este mecanismo. Por todo lo anterior, es un gusto para m extender la ms amplia felicitacin a todos los becarios y administradores del programa, que han hecho posible este ejemplar instrumento, el cual ha transformado la vida de miles de estudiantes y mejorado a nuestro pas, les deseo que celebren muchos aniversarios ms. 9 Al mismo tiempo, me complace anunciar la apertura de la cuarta convocatoria 2021, la cual se encuentra disponible a partir del da de hoy 13 de julio en el sitio web de FIDERH donde las personas interesadas podrn consultar las bases y realizar su registro para iniciar el proceso de solicitud del crdito educativo. Gracias y enhorabuena. 10

Title: Presentation of the commemorative coins, in gold and silver, of the Bicentennial of Independence and the Centennial of the Mexican Revolution
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Dr. Agustin Guillermo Carstens Carstens, during the presentation in the Banking Room of the Bank of Mexico of the commemorative coins, in gold and silver, of the Bicentennial of Independence and the Centennial of the Mexican Revolution. Thursday, September 23, 2010  Mr. President of the Republic, Maestro Felipe de Jesus Calderon Hinojosa,  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Maestro Ernesto Cordero Arroyo,  Mr. Secretary of Public Education, Maestro Alonso Lujambio Irazabal,  Mr. Legal Counsel of the Federal Executive, Mr. Miguel Alessio Robles Landa,  Mr. Director of the Mint of Mexico, Public Accountant Marcelo de los Santos Fraga,  Legislators,  Deputy Governors and colleagues of the Bank of Mexico,  Ladies and gentlemen, 1 For the Bank of Mexico, it is a real privilege to receive the President of the Republic in our main building. The Governing Board is very grateful that it has agreed to preside over this ceremony in which the Bank, together with the Mint of Mexico, unveil the new gold and silver coins minted to commemorate the Bicentennial of Independence and the Centennial of the Revolution. His visit, without a doubt, will become part of the endearing memories of the Bank of Mexico, even more so because it occurs in the month and year in which we commemorate the 85th anniversary of our Issuing Institute. In addition to their universally known functions as a means of payment, unit of account, and store of value, coins are also a singular testament to historical experiences. Thus, two great events, complex and multiform, of immense transcendence, as were the 2 Movements of Independence and Revolution in Mexico, also admit a particularly evocative chronicle from the perspective of the currency. Originally, the minting of coins in precious metals was due to the need that, even if it was due to its intrinsic value, money had acceptance. As a result of the evolution of central banks, and to the extent that the population consolidated its confidence in the liberatory power of the money issued by them, coins minted in precious metals ceased to be ordinary means of payment. However, they have retained a great appreciation as a store of value and are a source of hoarding; to their intrinsic value is added their value as artistic objects and expression of culture. Not coincidentally, coins have also served as commemorative items in our national history. It should be remembered that in 1910 the first 3 commemorative Mexican coin whose purpose was to celebrate the centenary of Independence. With the same intention, in 1921 the famous gold coin widely known as Centenario was launched, to remember the consummation of Independence. The metallic coin has evolved since those years. Thus, the Centennial was the starting point for the formation of a great Mexican tradition that is that of collector and savings coins minted in precious metals. To this tradition, already old, will be added from today the very beautiful pieces stamped in gold and silver that we make known in the context of the celebrations for the Bicentennial of Independence and the Centenary of the Revolution. Among the five commemorative coins that we unveil today, four of them will be produced in silver. 4 These pieces should be seen as a continuation of another great and ancient tradition of Mexican argentiferous currency that became known practically all over the world but especially in the Far East. Of these silver coins, two allude to the feat of Independence and the other two to the movement of the Mexican Revolution. The first of the coins related to Independence, pays tribute to its two most outstanding and well-known heroes, Don Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla and Generalissimo Jose Maria Morelos y Pavon, who holds with his right hand a saber and with his left the document "Feelings of the Nation". This piece has the numismatic peculiarity that in it both characters appear in full body and standing. The second of the silver coins commemorating Independence shows on its reverse, on the right side, the facade and towers of the Parish of Dolores, where Hidalgo pronounced his 5 known "scream" in the early morning of September 16, 1810, while ringing the bell of that temple, now known as the bell of Dolores, whose relief image is the one that, precisely, appears in the upper left of the coin, As for the coins that commemorate the Revolution, they reproduce two powerful images, captured in photographs of the time that have already become memorable for Mexicans; one, that of a locomotive, on the front of which sit four anonymous revolutionaries dressed in straw hats and armed with rifles; the other, the expressive image of a "soldadera" on the steps of a railroad car and in an attitude of attentive observation. On the other hand, and in a prominent place, there is the gold coin of the Bicentennial, which will most likely end up being popularly known as "Bicentennial", heir to the 6 beautiful tradition of the highly appreciated Centenarians. Like its predecessor, this coin reproduces the sculpture of the Winged Victory that crowns the column of Independence in Mexico City. Belonging to those two deep-rooted traditions of Mexican gold and silver coins, the pieces we launch today have the same legal attributes as their illustrious predecessors. In addition to presenting a face value - which is obviously much lower than their market value - all the pieces of the issue have the legal quality of coins and therefore should not be considered simply as commemorative medals. I would like to recognize the work of excellence that the Mexican Mint has carried out in the production of these coins, which without a doubt, and like their predecessors, will become part of the traditions and historical legacy of Mexico. 7 Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, the presentation that brings us together today takes place after a prolonged period during which significant progress has been made in the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, since the Bank of Mexico has consolidated itself as a solid and modern institution, a generator of confidence. To the extent that the autonomy enjoyed by the central bank has been strengthened day by day, the immense importance of this autonomous condition as a guarantee of economic stability and as a platform for Mexico to face the challenges of the future with confidence has also been confirmed. We have today in Mexico a low inflation but not as a fortuitous effect of the severe crisis that collapsed economic activity around the world during 2008 and much of the 8 2009, but as a deliberate fruit of a persevering monetary policy. It is necessary to recognize that the monetary policy of the Central Bank has found a very powerful ally, in this battle for economic stability, in the responsible and constant fiscal policy adopted by the Federal Government, headed by President Calderon. It would be obtuse to spare the merits of this fiscal policy when today it is widely recognized that Mexico knew how to anticipate in a timely manner the strong adjustment that would follow after the global crisis. Not all the governments of the world had, in the most acute moments of the crisis, the political will to defend a strong fiscal position, even at the cost of misunderstandings and criticisms. Fiscal strength that must be preserved to give continuity to an accelerated economic recovery without pressure 9 inflationary, such as what we have observed during 2010. Among the main benefits that this combination of responsible fiscal and monetary policies has produced, I must mention a substantial reduction in inflation expectations, as well as interest rates. Ten years ago it would have been unimaginable for the Federal Government to finance itself, as it does now, for a term of 30 years at a fixed rate, in pesos, of only 7.23 percent. All the more so this was impossible, 85 years ago, when the Bank of Mexico was inaugurated. The benefits of low and stable interest rates, and of fixed-rate, long-term financing, extend to households and businesses as well. On the other hand, it should be remembered that stability tends to improve the distribution of income in the country, since it is 10 it is well known that high inflations usually hurt the lower-income population more severely. The Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico and I, in my capacity as Governor, took this opportunity to confirm that we will continue to persevere in the task of consolidating price stability in the country. The autonomy of the Central Bank must be, above all, a guarantee of trust for the users of the national currency. Increasing this confidence day by day and consolidating an increasingly broad horizon of price stability is the best way in which the Bank of Mexico can and should contribute to the sustained growth of the country, the generation of jobs and the reduction of poverty. To conclude, and in order to be recorded in the historical memory of the country and the Bank of Mexico, the Governing Board has ordered that it deliver to you Lord 11 President the first case with the coins that today are made available to all Mexicans. Thanks a lot. 12
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Guillermo Carstens Carstens, durante la presentacin en la Sala Bancaria del Banco de Mxico de las monedas conmemorativas, en oro y en plata, del Bicentenario de la Independencia y del Centenario de la Revolucin Mexicana. Jueves 23 de septiembre de 2010  Seor Presidente de la Repblica, Maestro Felipe de Jess Caldern Hinojosa,  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, Maestro Ernesto Cordero Arroyo,  Seor Secretario de Educacin Pblica, Maestro Alonso Lujambio Irazbal,  Seor Consejero Jurdico del Ejecutivo Federal, Licenciado Miguel Alessio Robles Landa,  Seor Director de la Casa de Moneda de Mxico, Contador Pblico Marcelo de los Santos Fraga ,  Seores Legisladores,  Seores Subgobernadores y compaeros del Banco de Mxico,  Seoras y seores: 1 Para el Banco de Mxico es un verdadero privilegio recibir en nuestro edificio principal al Seor Presidente de la Repblica. La Junta de Gobierno est muy agradecida de que haya aceptado presidir esta ceremonia en la que el Banco, junto con la Casa de Moneda de Mxico, damos a conocer las nuevas monedas de oro y plata acuadas para conmemorar el Bicentenario de la Independencia y el Centenario de la Revolucin. Su visita, sin duda, pasar a formar parte de las memorias entraables del Banco de Mxico, ms an porque se da en el mes y ao en que conmemoramos el 85 aniversario de nuestro Instituto Emisor. Adems de sus funciones universalmente conocidas como medio de pago, unidad de cuenta y almacn de valor, las monedas tambin son un singular testimonio de experiencias histricas. As, dos grandes eventos, complejos y multiformes, de inmensa trascendencia, como fueron los 2 movimientos de Independencia y de Revolucin en Mxico, admiten tambin una crnica particularmente evocadora desde la perspectiva de la moneda. En su origen la acuacin de moneda en metales preciosos obedeci a la necesidad de que, aun cuando fuese en razn de su valor intrnseco, el dinero tuviese aceptacin. Como resultado de la evolucin de los bancos centrales, y en la medida que la poblacin consolid su confianza en el poder liberatorio del dinero emitido por stos, las monedas acuadas en metales preciosos dejaron de ser medios ordinarios de pago. Sin embargo, han conservado un gran aprecio como almacn de valor y son motivo de atesoramiento; a su valor intrnseco se suma su vala como objetos artsticos y expresin de cultura. No por casualidad las monedas tambin han servido como elementos conmemorativos en nuestra historia nacional. Cabe recordar que en 1910 se cre la primera 3 moneda mexicana conmemorativa cuya finalidad fue celebrar el centenario de la Independencia. Con igual intencin, en 1921 se lanz la famosa moneda de oro ampliamente conocida como Centenario, para recordar la consumacin de la Independencia. La moneda metlica ha evolucionado desde aquellos aos. As, el Centenario fue punto de partida para la conformacin de una gran tradicin mexicana que es la de las monedas de coleccin y ahorro acuadas en metales preciosos. A esa tradicin, ya aeja, se sumarn a partir de hoy las muy hermosas piezas troqueladas en oro y plata que damos a conocer en el contexto de las celebraciones para el Bicentenario de la Independencia y el Centenario de la Revolucin. Entre las cinco monedas conmemorativas que hoy damos a conocer, cuatro de ellas sern producidas en plata. 4 Estas piezas deben verse como una continuacin de otra gran y antigua tradicin de la moneda argentfera mexicana que lleg a ser conocida prcticamente en todo el mundo pero en especial en el Lejano Oriente. De estas monedas de plata, dos hacen alusin a la gesta de Independencia y las otras dos al movimiento de la Revolucin Mexicana. La primera de las monedas relativas a la Independencia, rinde tributo a sus dos hroes ms destacados y conocidos, Don Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla y el Generalsimo Jos Mara Morelos y Pavn, quien sostiene con la mano derecha un sable y con la izquierda el documento Sentimientos de la Nacin. Esta pieza tiene la peculiaridad numismtica de que en ella aparecen ambos personajes en cuerpo completo y de pie. La segunda de las monedas de plata que conmemora la Independencia muestra en su reverso, del lado derecho, la fachada y las torres de la Parroquia de Dolores, lugar donde Hidalgo pronunci su 5 conocido grito en la madrugada del 16 de septiembre de 1810, al tiempo que tocaba la campana de ese templo, ahora conocida como campana de Dolores, cuya imagen en relieve es la que, precisamente, aparece en la parte superior izquierda de la moneda, Por lo que hace a las monedas que conmemoran la Revolucin reproducen dos poderosas imgenes, capturadas en sendas fotografas de la poca que ya se han vuelto memorables para los mexicanos; una, la de una locomotora, en cuyo frente estn sentados cuatro revolucionarios annimos ataviados con sombreros de paja y armados con fusiles; la otra, la expresiva imagen de una soldadera en la escalinata de un carro de ferrocarril y en actitud de atenta observacin. Por otra parte, y en lugar destacado, est la moneda de oro del Bicentenario, que muy probablemente terminar por conocerse popularmente como Bicentenario, heredera de la 6 hermosa tradicin de los muy apreciados Centenarios. Al igual que su antecesora, esta moneda reproduce la escultura de la Victoria Alada que corona la columna de la Independencia en la ciudad de Mxico. Al pertenecer a esas dos arraigadas tradiciones de monedas mexicanas de oro y plata, las piezas que hoy lanzamos poseen iguales atributos jurdicos que sus ilustres antecesoras. Adems de presentar un valor nominal el cual es obviamente muy inferior a su valor de mercado todas las piezas de la emisin tienen la calidad legal de monedas y por lo tanto no deben considerarse simplemente como medallas conmemorativas. Quisiera reconocer la labor de excelencia que ha llevado a cabo la Casa de Moneda de Mxico en la produccin de estas monedas, las cuales sin duda, y al igual que sus antecesoras, pasarn a ser parte de las tradiciones y del legado histrico de Mxico. 7 Seor Presidente, seoras y seores: La presentacin que hoy nos congrega tiene lugar despus de un periodo prolongado durante el cual se ha avanzado notablemente en la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional, ya que el Banco de Mxico se ha consolidado como una Institucin slida y moderna, generadora de confianza. En la medida en que se ha afianzado da a da la autonoma de la que goza el banco central, se ha confirmado tambin la inmensa importancia de esa condicin autnoma como garanta de estabilidad econmica y como plataforma para que Mxico enfrente con confianza los desafos del futuro. Tenemos hoy en Mxico una inflacin baja pero no como efecto fortuito de la severa crisis que desplom la actividad econmica en todo el mundo durante 2008 y buena parte de 8 2009, sino como fruto deliberado de una poltica monetaria perseverante. Es preciso reconocer que la poltica monetaria del Banco Central ha encontrado un poderossimo aliado, en esta batalla por la estabilidad econmica, en la poltica fiscal responsable y constante que ha adoptado el Gobierno Federal, encabezado por el Presidente Caldern. Sera obtuso escatimar los mritos de dicha poltica fiscal cuando hoy es ampliamente reconocido que Mxico supo anticipar oportunamente el fuerte ajuste que seguira tras la crisis global. No todos los gobiernos del mundo tuvieron, en los momentos ms agudos de la crisis, voluntad poltica para defender una posicin fiscal fuerte, aun a costa de incomprensiones y crticas. Fortaleza fiscal que es imprescindible preservar para darle continuidad a una recuperacin econmica acelerada y sin presiones 9 inflacionarias, tal como la que hemos observado durante 2010. Entre los principales beneficios que ha producido esta combinacin de polticas fiscales y monetarias responsables debo mencionar un abatimiento sustancial de las expectativas de inflacin, as como de las tasas de inters. Hace diez aos hubiera sido inimaginable que el Gobierno Federal se financiase, como sucede ahora, a un plazo de 30 aos a una tasa fija, en pesos, de slo 7.23 por ciento. Con mayor razn esto resultaba imposible, hace 85 aos, cuando se inaugur el Banco de Mxico. Los beneficios de las tasas de inters bajas y estables, y del financiamiento a tasas fijas y a largo plazo, se extienden tambin a las familias y a las empresas. Por otro lado, habr que recordar que la estabilidad tiende a mejorar la distribucin del ingreso en el pas, pues es 10 bien sabido que las inflaciones altas usualmente perjudican ms severamente a la poblacin de menores ingresos. La Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico y yo en mi calidad de Gobernador, aprovechamos la ocasin para confirmar que continuaremos perseverando en la tarea de consolidar la estabilidad de precios en el pas. La autonoma del Banco Central debe ser, sobre todo, garanta de confianza para los usuarios de la moneda nacional. Acrecentar da a da esa confianza y consolidar cada vez ms un horizonte amplio de estabilidad de precios es la mejor forma en la que el Banco de Mxico puede y debe contribuir al crecimiento sostenido del pas, a la generacin de empleos y a la reduccin de la pobreza. Title: Presentation of the book: Autonomy of central banking in Mexico. Historical vision
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the presentation of the book "Autonomy of Central Banking in Mexico. Historical Vision" by Eduardo Turrent, at the Club de Industriales. Wednesday, May 22, 2013 Good evening. ? Mr. Miguel Mancera Aguayo, first governor of the Bank of Mexico, fully autonomous; ? Doctor Pedro Aspe Armella, former Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, decided promoter, together with Mr. Miguel Mancera, of the granting of full autonomy to the Bank of Mexico; ? Mr. Jose Carral Escalante, director of this prestigious Club of Industrialists and generous host who proposed with great wisdom the presentation of this book; ? Mr. Eduardo Turrent y Diaz, author of the splendid book that we present today, and who was until a few weeks ago, and for several decades, a careful official 1 of the Bank of Mexico as well as an attentive chronicler as well as as a diligent communicator, ? Ladies and gentlemen 20 years ago, in 1993, in the text of the explanatory statement of the initiative sent by the then President Carlos Salinas de Gortari to the Chamber of Deputies, to modify three constitutional articles in order to grant autonomy to the Bank of Mexico, a creepy fact was mentioned and that I quote: "Let's remember that about 45 million Mexicans have been born since we began to suffer inflations of two or more digits." Terrible: 20 years ago, in 1993, more than half of the population in Mexico had not known inflation below double digits. A year later, in April 1994, the long-awaited autonomy of the Bank of Mexico would begin to fully govern. 2 Just a month ago, also in April, Mexico completed 13 uninterrupted years of recording, month by month, single-digit annual inflations. In this way, today all Mexicans aged 13 and under, who are more than 31 million compatriots, have not known inflations higher than 9.7 percent per year - which has been the record of the highest inflation that Mexico has had since April 2000. This historic and forceful change achieved in just 20 years would not have been possible without an autonomous Central Bank. When recently the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico has spoken of a structural, profound and definitive change, in the fight against inflation is what we are referring to. Today, unlike 20 years ago, Mexicans can access mortgage loans, in pesos, at fixed rates even in the single digits, something unthinkable, illusory, two decades ago, and with terms of up to 30 years. Cetes have reached historically low rates in their history, below 4 percent per year. 3 Within the framework of its autonomy, the Bank of Mexico adopted in 2001 an inflation targeting regime for the conduct of monetary policy. This effort to strengthen this scheme has been permanent, in 2011 the minutes on the meetings in which the Governing Board makes its decisions on the monetary policy stance began to be published. This has further improved the transparency of the Bank of Mexico's communication, which has undoubtedly contributed to the fact that inflation expectations, both of market makers and the general public, remain anchored. Which brings me back to the same explanatory statement already cited, which explains with crystal clarity the very close relationship between the autonomy of the Central Bank and an effective fight against inflation. I quote again: Throughout the history of our central institute, this is since 1925, there has been a constant concern to "somehow moderate the flow of credit from the central bank. This, probably for two reasons. One, that for a long time it has been perceived the existence of a link between this flow and evolution. 4 of prices. Another, that the laxity in the credit control of the central institute, has resulted in innumerable evils that inflation has brought with it, still very much alive in our memory." And it is concluded in that explanatory statement: "Therefore, if we are to have a permanent policy of fighting inflationary forces, it is clear that it is advisable to separate the function of creating money from other tasks of the State, in which repeated demands to increase spending are continually faced." Today, 20 years away, and this is the profound message of Eduardo Turrent's book, it has been demonstrated in a forceful way that the granting of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico and the consequent institutional architecture that was reflected in its Law in December 1993, were a great success. A historic feat, dare I say, exemplary on the world stage. It should be noted - and also on this key point Turrent has been emphatic - that the essence of autonomy is to prevent the Central Bank from granting direct financing to the Government. And the reason why it is sought with 5 so much effort this separation between the public administration, prone to exercise an increasing expenditure for the benefit of the population, and the issuing bank is to avoid at all costs that the legal tender, that the money of the Mexicans, is degraded and debased because of inflation. Once again, it is worth recalling the careful explanatory statement with which the Executive justified in 1993 the constitutional changes leading to an autonomous Central Bank. That text read: "Undoubtedly, acute and prolonged inflations have been closely linked both in Mexico and in the rest of the world with considerable fiscal deficits financed by central bank credit." Hence, then, the need to close once and for all the possibility that fiscal deficits would be financed with the credit of the Central Bank. But also from there, the explanatory statement itself warns: 6 "But this separation is feasible until now, when the consolidation of public finances has been achieved. Before, such a measure would not have been consistent with reality." This warning not only introduces an indispensable tone of pragmatic realism into the initiative, it also prevents for the future how the harmonious and consistent relationship between fiscal policy and monetary policy, the two great pillars of macroeconomic stability, should be. Years later, with the approval, in 2006, of the Federal Law on Budget and Financial Responsibility, which obliges us to maintain a balanced budget rule, this virtuous circle of stability would be closed. We must congratulate ourselves as a country because we have completed thirteen consecutive years with single-digit inflations and with enviable macroeconomic stability. We must also recognize and applaud the insight, talent and conviction with which people like Don Miguel Mancera and Pedro Aspe, among others, pushed and carefully cared for the institutional design of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. 7 In addition, the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico also contemplates budgetary independence, which has allowed, with a scrupulous and prudent administration of the resources generated by the Bank's own operation, to sustain the investment in human capital that throughout its history the Central Bank has made and that allows it to maintain not only proverbial analytical rigor and the intellectual integrity of its economic analyses, but the formation of cadres of excellence in economic research for which the Bank of Mexico is widely known and recognized throughout the world. The reform granted autonomy by the Bank of Mexico is a central part of the construction of democratic institutions of excellence in our country. In fact, Mexico is one of the few countries with autonomous central banks, if not the only one, that has embodied in its constitutional text the autonomy of its issuing bank. It is a fact that the autonomy of the Central Bank in Mexico has been a decisive factor in consolidating low inflation and a horizon of macroeconomic stability, but we must not forget that such 8 Objectives are not in themselves an end, but means to a higher purpose: to establish a platform for economic growth and, therefore, for the fight against poverty and for the well-being of all Mexicans. This book captures, with the good prose that characterizes Eduardo Turrent, one of the most important conquests of modern Mexico, a success story in the design, architecture and effective functioning of democratic, transparent, reliable and so solid institutions that remain beyond the particular circumstances and that transcend those who have the honor of serving them in some stretch of their history. Thanks a lot. 9

Title: Inauguration of the second International Forum on Financial Inclusion
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the inauguration of the Second International Forum on Financial Inclusion. Mexico City, June 22, 2016  Mr. President of the United Mexican States, Mr. Enrique Pena Nieto,  Her Majesty: Maxima, Queen of the Netherlands, Special Adviser on Financial Inclusion for Development to the Secretary-General of the United Nations,  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Luis Videgaray Caso,  Distinguished participants in this Second International Forum on Financial Inclusion,  Ladies and gentlemen, It is a great honour for me to speak before two characters who, each in their field of action, have made great contributions to financial inclusion. 1 On the one hand, for the President of the Republic, Enrique Pena Nieto, the task of promoting greater financial inclusion in our country has been a constant of his performance as Head of State. Indeed, President Pena Nieto has emphatically referred to the "importance of democratizing the formal financial system in Mexico" and the determined purpose of his government, embodied in the National Development Plan, to ensure that "more and more Mexicans can save, invest, have a loan or be protected by insurance." In response to that call and within the framework of financial reform, Mexico has consolidated important advances to combat that great obstacle to growth and development that is the exclusion of millions of Mexicans from the benefits offered by financial intermediation. Precisely to deepen these advances is that it was designed 2 the National Financial Inclusion Policy, whose launch today brings us together. On the other hand, Queen Maxima of the Netherlands has been, for many years, a talented, enthusiastic and tireless promoter of financial inclusion. Recall that in 2009, the Secretary-General of the United Nations, Ban Kimoon, appointed her as Special Counsel for "financing for inclusive development", which has led Queen Maxima to work closely with leaders of governments around the world, with financial institutions, with authorities and regulators of the financial system, with intergovernmental organizations, with parliaments, the media, civil society and private sector organizations. All with the sole purpose of achieving greater financial inclusion, for the benefit of the poorest and most vulnerable sectors on the planet. * * * 3 The importance of a National Financial Inclusion Policy lies in its ability to support, in a sustained and unrelenting manner, those who still do not enjoy all the advantages and benefits that a solid financial system can grant, at the forefront in the use of more modern technologies, well capitalized, regulated and growing. It also aims to empower the population, through adequate education, so that they can effectively use and have access to a system that can lead them to modernity. As we all know, these millions of Mexicans - whom our financial system, for various reasons, does not yet include - are precisely the most vulnerable group of the population, that is, they are the ones who can gain the most by joining the system, and to whom the Mexican financial system itself, from a point of view of social obligation and justice, more must. 4 Of course, greater financial inclusion represents multiple benefits for the system itself: it reinforces its soundness and reduces its exposure to risk, by diversifying and extending its products and services; generates operational synergies that, in turn, trigger greater productivity not only in the financial system itself, but throughout the economy. But beyond these benefits for the consolidation and growth of the financial system, we must focus the effort, motivation and message of this National Financial Inclusion Policy on the benefit of all those for whom financial inclusion can mean the most important gateway to a better life, in which credit and savings - and in general the use of financial products and services. are the ideal tools for the achievement of long-cherished goals and dreams. In this sense, it is key to achieving greater financial inclusion that the authorities always have in mind, and 5 first, precisely the needs and objectives of those who are still outside the system. It is not so much they who must adapt to the financial system, it is the financial system that must adapt to them. No doubt this principle was present in the design of national policy. The Bank of Mexico, in particular, contributes to financial inclusion at different levels ranging from the most general and substantive, such as the maintenance of price stability, to the most specific, through regulatory provisions aimed at creating easily accessible, easy to understand, safe and reliable financial products and services. At the foundation of financial inclusion is price stability. We know well from the grim experiences of the second half of the last century that episodes of high inflation with all their consequences of instability, uncertainty and loss of well-being, not only do 6 Greater financial inclusion is unthinkable but in fact promotes the exclusion of millions of people from the benefits of financial intermediation. More seriously, those who suffer most from the perverse effects of high inflation are precisely those who have the least, because lacking access to formal financial services cannot protect themselves against inflationary risk. That is why inflation is the most unfair and cruel of taxes. In this regard, full compliance with the Bank of Mexico's priority objective, which is to ensure price stability, is crucial to any serious and sustained effort at financial inclusion. How good that more than half of Mexico's population, the youngest, has not suffered the experience of annual inflations of two or three digits. In fact, last May we celebrated thirteen consecutive months with inflation observed by 7 below the Bank of Mexico's permanent target of 3 percent, and June is shaping up to be the fourteenth. But it would be a grave mistake to erase from our memory the lessons that, as a warning, the history of crises characterized by high inflation left us. In addition, financial inclusion is also part of the other objectives that the law sets for Banco de Mexico, which are to promote the healthy development of the financial system and promote the proper functioning of payment systems. Based on the premise that inclusion products must be appropriate for the needs and capacities of users, the Bank of Mexico has fostered, through regulation and coordination with other authorities, important advances in the financial inclusion strategy. I would like to give a few illustrative examples in this regard. To make the means of payment more accessible, the obligation of banks to allow their account holders was regulated. 8 associate the cell phone number with your deposit account, which in addition to avoiding the use of complex and diverse alphanumeric keys and access codes, allows practically immediate interbank mobile payments using the robust infrastructure of the Interbank Electronic Payments System (SPEI) of the Bank of Mexico. In practice, then, the SPEI is the mechanism that allows interconnection between the various mobile payment schemes in a single network. Likewise, the Bank of Mexico has adopted measures that allow the growth of the network of merchants that accept payment cards, in particular through the figure of "aggregators", so that the growth rate of Point of Sale Terminals (POS) has doubled in the last two years. With the same objective, the Bank of Mexico has made transparent and revealed the costs or discount rates that banks 9 they charge merchants for the "acquisition" service (acceptance of payments from consumers by credit or debit card), so that merchants can compare such costs by institution and choose the one that suits them best, lowering their costs. Additionally, an application has been developed for smartphones (Ubicajero) that allows to know, in addition to the location, the commissions in external ATM that all institutions charge at the level of individual cashier; this puts users in a position to choose the CASHIER that suits them best. By law, the Bank of Mexico publishes reports of indicators of the interest rates that each regulated intermediary charges for various credit services; these indicators, on the one hand, have fostered competition between intermediaries and, on the other, have empowered users to negotiate better credit terms. This 10 promotes a more competitive system and with it, the offer of cheaper products that are achievable for the low-income population. One aspect that I would not like to fail to mention is that a constant of the time we live in is the continuous appearance of new technologies and financial business models to encourage the opening of deposit accounts, massify credits and facilitate payments. We are convinced that we must encourage and accompany these innovations, but we strive to ensure that they have the appropriate regulatory framework that minimizes the risks, which, if materialized, would make it more difficult to promote the desired financial inclusion. * ** In conclusion, at the Bank of Mexico we know that the task of generating more and more financial inclusion is permanent. But given the immensity of the task, we also understand that we must act in a complementary and 11 coordinated with the other authorities of our country, under the leadership of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit. Undoubtedly, the National Financial Inclusion Policy that President Pena Nieto rightly presents today gives us the appropriate frame of reference for all those involved to join forces in the consequence of the common good. There is no doubt that the Bank of Mexico will do its part to maximize financial inclusion in our country, for the direct benefit of those most in need. Thanks a lot. 12
