Ciudad de Mxico, 22 de junio de 2016  Seor Presidente de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, licenciado Enrique Pea Nieto,  Su Majestad: Mxima, Reina de los Pases Bajos, asesora especial sobre inclusin financiera para el desarrollo del Secretario General de la Organizacin de las Naciones Unidas,  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Luis Videgaray Caso,  Distinguidos participantes en este Segundo Foro Internacional de Inclusin Financiera,  Seoras y seores: Es para m un gran honor hacer uso de la palabra ante dos personajes que, cada cual en su mbito de accin, han hecho grandes contribuciones a la inclusin financiera. 1 Por una parte, para el Presidente de la Repblica, Enrique Pea Nieto, la tarea de promover una mayor inclusin financiera en nuestro pas ha sido una constante de su actuacin como Jefe de Estado. En efecto, el Presidente Pea Nieto se ha referido enfticamente a la trascendencia de democratizar el sistema financiero formal en Mxico y al decidido propsito de su gobierno, plasmado en la Plan Nacional de Desarrollo, de lograr que cada vez ms mexicanos puedan ahorrar, invertir, tener un crdito o estar protegidos por un seguro. En respuesta a ese llamado y en el marco de la reforma financiera, Mxico ha consolidado importantes avances para combatir ese gran obstculo para el crecimiento y para el desarrollo que es la exclusin de millones de mexicanos de los beneficios que ofrece la intermediacin financiera. Precisamente para profundizar esos avances es que se dise 2 la Poltica Nacional de Inclusin Financiera, cuyo lanzamiento hoy nos rene. Por otra parte, la Reina Mxima de los Pases Bajos es, desde hace muchos aos, una promotora talentosa, entusiasta e incansable de la inclusin financiera. Recordemos que en 2009, el Secretario General de las Naciones Unidas, Ban Kimoon, la design como Abogada Especial de la financiacin para el desarrollo inclusivo, lo que ha llevado a la Reina Mxima a trabajar estrechamente con lderes de gobiernos de prcticamente todo el mundo, con instituciones financieras, con autoridades y reguladores del sistema financiero, con organizaciones intergubernamentales, con parlamentos, medios de comunicacin, la sociedad civil y con organizaciones del sector privado. Todo, con el nico propsito de alcanzar una mayor inclusin financiera, en beneficio de los sectores ms pobres y vulnerables en el planeta. * * * 3 La trascendencia de una Poltica Nacional de Inclusin Financiera radica en su capacidad de apoyar, de forma sostenida y sin reticencias, a quienes an no gozan de todas las ventajas y beneficios que puede otorgar un sistema financiero slido, de vanguardia en el uso de tecnologas ms modernas, bien capitalizado, regulado y en crecimiento. Tambin pretende empoderar a la poblacin, a travs de una educacin adecuada, para que efectivamente puedan usar y tener acceso a un sistema que les puede llevar a la modernidad. Como todos sabemos, estos millones de mexicanos  a quienes nuestro sistema financiero, por diversas razones, an no incluye-, son precisamente el grupo ms vulnerable de la poblacin, es decir, son quienes ms pueden ganar al incorporarse al sistema, y a quienes el propio sistema financiero mexicano, desde un punto de vista de obligacin social y de justicia, ms debe. 4 Desde luego, una mayor inclusin financiera representa mltiples beneficios para al propio sistema: refuerza su solidez y disminuye su exposicin al riesgo, al diversificar y extender sus productos y servicios; genera sinergias de operacin que, a su vez, detonan una mayor productividad no slo en el propio sistema financiero, sino en toda la economa. Pero ms all de estos beneficios para la consolidacin y el crecimiento del sistema financiero, debemos centrar el esfuerzo, la motivacin y el mensaje de esta Poltica Nacional de Inclusin Financiera en el beneficio de todos aquellos para quienes la inclusin financiera puede significar la ms importante puerta de acceso a una vida mejor, en la cual el crdito y el ahorro  y en general el uso de productos y servicios financieros-, sean las herramientas idneas para el logro de metas y sueos largamente anhelados. En este sentido, es clave para lograr una mayor inclusin financiera que las autoridades tengamos siempre en mente, y 5 en primer lugar, justamente las necesidades y los objetivos de quienes an estn fuera del sistema. No son tanto ellos quienes deben adaptarse al sistema financiero, es el sistema financiero el que debe adaptarse a ellos. Sin duda este principio estuvo presente en el diseo de la poltica nacional. El Banco de Mxico, en particular, contribuye a la inclusin financiera en distintos niveles que van desde lo ms general y sustantivo, como es el mantenimiento de la estabilidad de precios, hasta lo ms especfico, mediante disposiciones regulatorias encaminadas a crear productos y servicios financieros de fcil acceso, sencillos de entender, seguros y confiables. En la base de la inclusin financiera est la estabilidad de precios. Bien sabemos, por las aciagas experiencias de la segunda mitad del siglo pasado, que los episodios de elevada inflacin con todas sus secuelas de inestabilidad, incertidumbre y prdida de bienestar, no slo hacen 6 impensable una mayor inclusin financiera sino que promueven de hecho la exclusin de millones de personas de los beneficios de la intermediacin financiera. Ms grave an, aquellos que sufren ms los efectos perversos de una inflacin elevada son precisamente quienes menos tienen, pues al carecer de acceso a los servicios financieros formales no se pueden proteger contra el riesgo inflacionario. Es por ello que la inflacin es el ms injusto y cruel de los impuestos. En este sentido, el cumplimiento cabal del objetivo prioritario del Banco de Mxico, que es procurar la estabilidad de precios, es crucial para cualquier esfuerzo serio y sostenido de inclusin financiera. Qu bueno que ms de la mitad de la poblacin de Mxico, la ms joven, no ha sufrido la experiencia de inflaciones anuales de dos o tres dgitos. De hecho, en mayo pasado cumplimos trece meses consecutivos con una inflacin observada por 7 debajo del objetivo permanente del Banco de Mxico de 3 por ciento, y junio se perfila como el catorceavo. Pero sera un grave error borrar de nuestra memoria las lecciones que, como advertencia, nos dej la historia de las crisis caracterizadas por una elevada inflacin. Adems, la inclusin financiera tambin est inserta en los otros objetivos que la ley marca a Banco de Mxico y que son promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. A partir de la premisa de que los productos de inclusin deben ser apropiados para las necesidades y capacidades de los usuarios, el Banco de Mxico ha propiciado, mediante la regulacin y coordinacin con otras autoridades, avances importantes en la estrategia de inclusin financiera. Me gustara dar unos cuantos ejemplos ilustrativos al respecto. Para hacer ms accesibles los medios de pago se regul la obligacin de los bancos para permitir a sus cuentahabientes 8 asociar el nmero de telfono celular a su cuenta de depsito, lo que adems de evitar el uso de complejas y diversas claves alfanumricas y cdigos de acceso, permite los pagos mviles interbancarios prcticamente inmediatos utilizando la robusta infraestructura del Sistema de Pagos Electrnicos Interbancarios (SPEI) del Banco de Mxico. En la prctica, entonces, el SPEI es el mecanismo que permite la interconexin entre los diversos esquemas de pagos mviles en una red nica. Asimismo, el Banco de Mxico ha adoptado medidas que permiten el crecimiento de la red de comercios que aceptan tarjetas de pago, en particular a travs de la figura de los agregadores, de forma tal que la tasa de crecimiento de las Terminales Punto de Venta (TPV) se ha duplicado en los ltimos dos aos. Con el mismo objetivo, el Banco de Mxico ha transparentado y revelado los costos o tasas de descuento que los bancos 9 cobran a los comercios por el servicio de adquirencia (aceptacin de pagos de los consumidores con tarjeta de crdito o de dbito), de forma que los comercios puedan comparar tales costos por institucin y elegir la que ms les convenga, abatiendo sus costos. Adicionalmente, se ha desarrollado una aplicacin para telfonos inteligentes (Ubicajero) que permite conocer, adems de la ubicacin, las comisiones en cajero ajeno que cobran todas las instituciones a nivel de cajero individual; esto hace que los usuarios estn en posicin de elegir el cajero que ms les convenga. Por mandato de ley, el Banco de Mxico publica reportes de indicadores de las tasas de inters que cada intermediario regulado cobra por diversos servicios crediticios; estos indicadores, por un lado, han fomentado la competencia entre los intermediarios y, por otro, han empoderado a los usuarios para que negocien mejores condiciones de crdito. Esto 10 promueve un sistema ms competitivo y con ello, la oferta de productos ms baratos que resulten alcanzables para la poblacin de bajos recursos. Un aspecto que no quisiera dejar de mencionar es que una constante del tiempo que vivimos es la continua aparicin de nuevas tecnologas y modelos de negocios financieros para fomentar la apertura de cuentas de depsitos, masificar los crditos y facilitar los pagos. Estamos convencidos que debemos alentar y acompaar estas innovaciones, pero esmerndonos en que tengan el marco regulatorio apropiado que minimice los riesgos, los cuales, de materializarse, haran ms complicado propulsar la anhelada inclusin financiera. * ** En conclusin, en el Banco de Mxico sabemos que la tarea por generar cada vez ms una mayor inclusin financiera es permanente. Pero dada la inmensidad de la tarea, tambin entendemos que debemos actuar en forma complementaria y 11 coordinada con las dems autoridades de nuestro pas, bajo el liderazgo de la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico. Sin duda, la Poltica Nacional de Inclusin Financiera que el Presidente Pea Nieto atinadamente hoy presenta nos da el marco de referencia adecuado para que todos los involucrados sumemos esfuerzos en la consecuencia del bien comn. No les quede duda que el Banco de Mxico har lo que le corresponda para maximizar la inclusin financiera en nuestro pas, para beneficio directo de los ms necesitados. Muchas gracias. 12

Title: Inauguration of the XVI Symposium on Risk Management of the Association of Banks of Mexico
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the inauguration of the XVI Symposium on Risk Management of the Association of Banks of Mexico.1 Mexico City, October 25, 2021 Lic. Daniel Becker Feldman, President de la ABM; Dr. Alfredo Navarrete Martinez, Head of the Banking, Securities and Savings Unit of the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit; Mr. Juan Pablo Graf Noriega, President of the National Banking and Securities Commission; Juan Carlos Jimenez Rojas, Director General of the ABM; Eng. Heleodoro Ruiz Santos, President of the Risk Management Committee of the ABM; Act. Javier Tellez Lugo, Chairman of the Risk Management Committee of the ABM; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 Introduction I am very pleased to participate in another edition of the Risk Management Symposium, organized by the Association of Banks of Mexico. In a world characterized by accelerated change, it is natural for opportunities to increase, but also risks. We have observed, in recent years, changes and innovations that modify the face of the economy and daily life and that increase the possibilities of addressing old lags and generating greater well-being for societies. However, we have also witnessed the emergence of unprecedented challenges, ranging from global financial crises and cyber threats to climate change and health emergencies. In particular, the institutions that are part of the financial system are highly exposed to the impact of these phenomena. For the financial sector, globalization, technological change, cybersecurity, environmental risks or unexpected affectations, 2 like the current pandemic, they entail new challenges, which are added to the traditional ones of this activity. To respond to these challenges, it is necessary to work in two dimensions. The first implies having a prospective and panoramic vision, which allows to identify the main points of alert, their possibility of occurrence and their eventual solutions. The second refers to building institutional resilience and response capacity to cope with the eventual materialization of challenges, giving viability and adjustment options to our institutions. For this reason, this analytical exercise carried out annually by the Association of Banks of Mexico is especially important, which allows updating the risk map, sharing experiences and improving coordination and response capacity to unexpected situations. In this speech, I would like to refer, first of all, to the importance of the stability, competitiveness and efficiency of the financial system, as well as to the current situation of banks in the face of the health emergency that we have faced in the last two years; and, secondly, to 3 some of the most important challenges facing the sector, such as, among others, climate change, as well as technological change and cybersecurity. 1. Situation of the Mexican financial system In addition to its main objective, which is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, the law entrusts the Bank of Mexico with the purposes of promoting the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of payment systems. Both purposes provide public goods fundamental to economic growth and the quality of life of citizens. In a healthy financial system, intermediaries provide end-users with quality financial services on appropriate terms and conditions and in a sustainable manner. Likewise, a healthy financial system must be accessible and serve the entire population. Even the stability of the financial system itself must be understood as an indispensable characteristic for citizens to have financial services in a sustained manner. 4 For the Bank of Mexico, the healthy development and stability of the financial system, as well as its efficiency and competitiveness, are a fundamental objective, given the high costs that financial instability or the inefficiency of the system usually imposes on society as a whole, by negatively affecting the pace of economic activity and levels of employment and income. In addition, a stable and competitive financial system contributes to the more efficient implementation of monetary policy and, with it, to achieving the priority objective of a central bank, which is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. The Bank of Mexico seeks to promote the stability of the financial system through various actions. On the one hand, through the detection and correction of vulnerabilities and, on the other, by promoting resilience to the materialization of risk events for the proper functioning of the financial system (in terms of both the intermediation of financial resources, as well as the aggregation and distribution of risks). 5 Thus, the Bank of Mexico maintains a macroprudential vision of the Mexican financial system, seeking to detect risks in the various sectors that compose it and reduce the channels of contagion that could lead to systemic risk. In this regard, due to its magnitude and relative importance, the banking sector, which accumulates about 44% of the total assets of the financial system and is a key player in the payment system, deserves particular attention. For the financial system to contribute to raising economic growth and the well-being of the population, in addition to having stability, it must be efficient, competitive and inclusive. On the one hand, efficiency allows financial institutions to safely mediate the public's savings and direct them to the most profitable projects. On the other hand, greater competition allows financial services to be provided at better prices. Likewise, an inclusive financial system helps financial services reach the entire population, allowing more people to have opportunities to diversify their savings or receive credit. 6 safely. While this is very relevant, it must be carried out without relaxing risk management standards, but through technological innovations and innovative partnerships that make credit risk analysis and mitigation processes more efficient and that allow the incorporation of significant segments of the population, little attended in the past. To achieve these objectives, the Bank of Mexico has promoted a solid institutional framework and financial regulation and supervision that, at the same time, safeguard the integrity of the system, promote efficiency and competition, and protect the interests of the public. To the extent that financial services are offered in better quality conditions, with the greatest accessibility and coverage, and in a sustainable manner over time, it is possible to solidly underpin economic growth and social well-being. As a result of the shock represented by the COVID-19 pandemic, the Mexican financial system has faced, since the beginning of 2020, stressed operating conditions, derived from a global environment 7 uncertain and complex. However, the Mexican financial system and, in particular, the banking sector, have shown remarkable resilience in the face of such shocks. This is based both on the characteristics of the affectation, which suddenly went from a massive closure to the reopening, and on the solid position of the levels of capital and liquidity. This solidity is the result of a series of efforts that, consistently, have been carried out for more than two decades. During the pandemic, the Bank of Mexico adopted a comprehensive package of measures and coordinated with other authorities to promote the orderly behavior of the debt and exchange markets; improve the functioning of domestic markets, and strengthen the channels of granting credit in the economy, from those of wholesale to that received by households and micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. The set of approved actions contemplated support for up to 750 billion pesos (equivalent to 3.3% of GDP in 2019). 8 Given the significant economic contraction that was registered as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, it is relevant to highlight that the granting of credit plays a key role for the economic recovery. Despite the fact that this year economic activity has been recovering at a higher rate than originally expected, there is still no reactivation in the granting of credit, which could contribute to strengthening it and giving it greater support. 2. The risks ahead. The pandemic showed the importance of having a resilient financial system capable of facing various shocks. Due to its importance, some of the risks we could face in the future include: 1. Climate-related financial risks. Climate risks imply a unique challenge, since unlike most of the risks faced by banking, in this one there is no data and historical information that allows to make a probabilistic inference about their occurrence and accurately evaluate the potential. 9 of damage. In this environment, it is especially important to develop climate risk management tools through stress testing and evaluation of alternative scenarios. The scale and severity of climate risks do not allow us to wait to address them until their effects materialize, prevention and mitigation are essential and represent an immediate task. Central Banks should incorporate the assessment of risks associated with climate change into the risk measurement of the financial system. This requires proper consideration of the relevant physical and transition risks. To assess these risks, it is necessary to have the following: 1) Disclosure schemes by financial and non-financial companies. In particular, promote the adoption of useful standards and metrics to understand and address these risks. Ifrs (International Financial Reporting Standards Foundation) is developing a global reference standard for reporting, based on the framework of the TCFD (Task Force on Climate-related FInancial 10 Disclosures) and the work of sustainability standard issuers. 2) An adequate understanding and integration of physical and transition risks in financial decision-making to reorient capital flows in order to improve and preserve the competitiveness of the economy, and align our transition to a low-carbon future with that of our trading partners. 3) In emerging markets, there are additional challenges to mobilizing resources on a scale that fosters a transition to a low-carbon economy. This is despite the fact that in these economies, sustainable investments replace technologies that are more carbon-intensive than those of advanced economies, so their potential for mitigation and positive externalities is much greater. 4) The cost of capital faced by emerging and developing economies is significantly higher than in advanced economies. It is essential to move from a bad balance with high financing costs and insufficient green investment, to a good balance with large-scale climate-friendly financing sources for these countries and financing costs. 11 really low. It is necessary for the entire financial system and banking in particular to evaluate how to develop portfolios of credits and green projects that meet international criteria and that allow to capture very low-cost resources through multilateral development banks and the Ex-Im Banks of developed countries. In this, the active participation of all is indispensable, not the accompaniment in the efforts of someone else. 2. Cyber, technological and operational risks. In the face of this growing risk, it is important to strengthen our response protocols to address cyber incidents in a timely and coordinated manner and prevent them from spreading to other participants. Computer security and the proper adoption of state-of-the-art technology have become a core issue for the stability of the financial system. Additionally, since the affectation can be at the infrastructure level, in data, or materialize monetarily, confidence 12 of users in a correct functioning of financial institutions can be severely affected by cybersecurity events. Therefore, it is essential to take into account the following considerations. 1) In the financial system, cyber risks face conditions that are not necessarily present in other markets. The existence of network economies and the presence of externalities, as a result of the high levels of interconnection of the different participants in the financial system, can generate market failures that result in levels of investment and socially suboptimal risk prevention measures. 2) The financial system is prone to so-called "herd" behaviors if users consider that their resources and operations are exposed to third-party risks and contagion. 3) Cybersecurity regulation and supervision should address the system as a whole over a long-term horizon, foster cooperation and communication between authorities and financial institutions. 13 4) The strength of computer security depends on the most vulnerable link in the chain. This applies both at the level of an institution, and in terms of the system as a whole. Therefore, risk mitigation actions should be aimed at ensuring operational continuity, understood as a network, both at the level of the institutions and the system as a whole. 5) Within this area, one of the issues that has been gaining greater relevance is the participation of the "Technological Giants" in the provision of financial services globally, as well as in the provision of technological services to financial companies, including the storage, transmission or analysis of data. In their direct or indirect participation in the financial system, the following principles must be preserved: (i) equal risk, equal regulation; (ii) full interoperability of networks, avoiding the formation of silos and partial networks; (iii) maintain operational continuity and technological neutrality; and (iv) full consumer protection. 6) One aspect in which there has been a considerable increase in the concentration of risk is in the provision of technological services by a few companies. This can 14 represent a high risk to financial stability in the event of an operational failure or cyberattack, which can become a systemic event. As we saw in the episode of October 5 with the fall of one of the most relevant social networks, these companies are not exempt from significant operational risks. 7) It is necessary to continue developing mechanisms for monitoring and identifying risks and vulnerabilities in a timely manner and to have adequate policy responses to the materialization of such risks. Ladies and gentlemen: We face, as never before, a changing environment in which numerous opportunities and, also, unusual challenges are foreseen. Given this panorama, it will be essential that the financial institutions of our country and, especially the banks and their risk management areas, play their strategic role in defining the perimeter of action of their institutions. Which must be consistent over time with its model of generating value for its users, and not be subject to stumbling into the inertia and short-term profitability myopia to which they could sometimes be subject. 15 the business areas. The role of risk areas in defining the vision and strategies of their institutions has never been more important. In particular, in the face of some of the new challenges I have mentioned here, it will be desirable for institutions to expand and strengthen their schemes for monitoring, administration and risk management. For this, a key element will be that the areas and departments responsible for such management and administration are adequately equipped, not only in the aspect of infrastructure and technology but, above all, in terms of their human capital. While the more direct and immediate impact of the above will be reflected in greater protection for financial institutions themselves, in the face of the risks they face individually, it will also contribute to the resilience of the system as a whole. We all face this challenge. 16 Therefore, as the recent experience with the COVID-19 crisis has once again shown, effective communication and coordinated action between financial institutions and authorities is an indispensable tool to face challenges and adversities, as well as to promote the strength and development of the financial system, always for the benefit of those who are at the center of all our efforts, the user and society. Thanks a lot. 17

Alejandro Daz de Len, gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la inauguracin del XVI Simposio de Administracin de Riesgos de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico.1 Ciudad de Mxico, 25 de octubre de 2021 Lic. Daniel Becker Feldman, Presidente de la ABM; Dr. Alfredo Navarrete Martnez, Titular la Unidad de Banca, de Valores y Ahorro de la Secretara de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico; Mtro. Juan Pablo Graf Noriega, Presidente de la Comisin Nacional Bancaria y de Valores; Lic. Juan Carlos Jimnez Rojas, Director General de la ABM; Ing. Heleodoro Ruiz Santos, Presidente de la Comisin de Administracin de Riesgos de la ABM; Act. Javier Tllez Lugo, Presidente de la Comisin de Administracin de Riesgos de la ABM; Seoras y seores: 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad del autor y no necesariamente representan la posicin institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno. 1 Introduccin Me da mucho gusto participar en otra edicin del Simposio de Administracin de Riesgos, que organiza la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico. En un mundo caracterizado por el cambio acelerado resulta natural que aumenten las oportunidades, pero tambin los riesgos. Hemos observado, en los ltimos aos, cambios e innovaciones que modifican el rostro de la economa y la vida cotidiana y que incrementan las posibilidades de atender antiguos rezagos y generar mayor bienestar para las sociedades. Sin embargo, tambin hemos atestiguado la emergencia de desafos inditos, que van desde las crisis financieras globales y las amenazas cibernticas hasta el cambio climtico y las emergencias sanitarias. En particular, las instituciones que forman parte del sistema financiero estn altamente expuestas al impacto de estos fenmenos. Para el sector financiero la globalizacin, el cambio tecnolgico, la ciberseguridad, los riesgos ambientales o afectaciones inesperadas, 2 como la actual pandemia, entraan nuevos retos, que se suman a los tradicionales de esta actividad. Para responder a estos retos, se requiere trabajar en dos dimensiones. La primera implica contar con una visin prospectiva y panormica, que permita identificar los principales puntos de alerta, su posibilidad de ocurrencia y sus eventuales soluciones. La segunda se refiere a construir resiliencia institucional y capacidad de respuesta para sobrellevar la eventual materializacin de los retos, dndole viabilidad y opciones de ajuste a nuestras instituciones. Por ello, es especialmente importante este ejercicio analtico que anualmente lleva a cabo la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico y que permite actualizar el mapa de riesgos, compartir experiencias y mejorar la coordinacin y capacidad de respuesta ante situaciones inesperadas. En esta intervencin, quiero referirme, en primer lugar, a la importancia de la estabilidad, competitividad y eficiencia del sistema financiero, as como a la situacin actual de la banca ante la emergencia sanitaria que hemos enfrentado en los ltimos dos aos; y, en segundo lugar, a 3 algunos de los retos ms importantes que enfrenta el sector, como son, entre otros, el cambio climtico, as como el cambio tecnolgico y la ciberseguridad. 1. Situacin del sistema financiero mexicano Adems de su objetivo principal, que es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional, la ley le encarga al Banco de Mxico las finalidades de promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Ambas finalidades proveen bienes pblicos fundamentales para el crecimiento econmico y la calidad de vida de los ciudadanos. En un sistema financiero sano, los intermediarios suministran a los usuarios finales de servicios financieros de calidad en trminos y condiciones adecuadas y de manera sostenible. Asimismo, un sistema financiero sano debe ser accesible y atender a toda la poblacin. Inclusive, la propia estabilidad del sistema financiero debe ser entendida como una caracterstica indispensable para que la ciudadana cuente de manera sostenida con servicios financieros. 4 Para el Banco de Mxico, el sano desarrollo y la estabilidad del sistema financiero, as como su eficiencia y competitividad, son un objetivo fundamental, dados los elevados costos que la inestabilidad financiera o la ineficiencia del sistema, suele imponer a la sociedad en su conjunto, al afectar negativamente el ritmo de la actividad econmica y los niveles de empleo e ingreso. Adems, un sistema financiero estable y competitivo contribuye a instrumentar de manera ms eficiente la poltica monetaria y, con ello, a alcanzar el objetivo prioritario de un banco central, que es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. El Banco de Mxico busca promover la estabilidad del sistema financiero, mediante diversas acciones. Por una parte, mediante la deteccin y correccin de vulnerabilidades y, por otra, promoviendo la resiliencia ante la materializacin de eventos de riesgo para el adecuado funcionamiento del sistema financiero (en trminos tanto de la intermediacin de recursos financieros, como de la agregacin y distribucin de riesgos). 5 As, el Banco de Mxico mantiene una visin macroprudencial del sistema financiero mexicano, procurando la deteccin de riesgos en los diversos sectores que lo componen y la reduccin de los canales de contagio que pudieran derivar en riesgo sistmico. Al respecto, por su magnitud e importancia relativa, el sector bancario, que acumula alrededor del 44% de los activos totales del sistema financiero y es pieza toral en el sistema de pagos, merece particular atencin. Para que el sistema financiero pueda contribuir a elevar el crecimiento econmico y el bienestar de la poblacin, adems de contar con estabilidad, debe ser eficiente, competitivo e incluyente. Por un lado, la eficiencia permite que las instituciones financieras intermedien de manera segura el ahorro del pblico y lo orienten a los proyectos de mayor rentabilidad. Por su parte, una mayor competencia permite que los servicios financieros puedan proveerse a mejores precios. Asimismo, un sistema financiero incluyente contribuye a que los servicios financieros lleguen a toda la poblacin, permitiendo que ms personas tengan oportunidades de diversificar su ahorro o recibir crdito 6 de manera segura. Si bien esto es muy relevante, se debe llevar a cabo sin relajar los estndares de gestin de riesgos, sino a travs de la innovaciones tecnolgicas y asociaciones novedosas que vuelvan ms eficientes los procesos de anlisis y mitigacin de riesgos de crdito y que permitan incorporar a significativos segmentos de la poblacin, poco atendidos en el pasado. Para lograr dichos objetivos, el Banco de Mxico ha impulsado un marco institucional slido y una regulacin y supervisin financiera que, al mismo tiempo, salvaguarden la integridad del sistema, promuevan la eficiencia y competencia y protejan los intereses del pblico. En la medida en que los servicios financieros sean ofrecidos en mejores condiciones de calidad, con la mayor accesibilidad y cobertura, y de manera sostenible en el tiempo, es posible apuntalar de manera slida el crecimiento econmico y el bienestar social. A raz del choque que ha representado la pandemia por COVID-19, el sistema financiero mexicano ha enfrentado, desde inicios de 2020, condiciones de operacin estresadas, derivadas de un entorno global 7 incierto y complejo. No obstante, el sistema financiero mexicano y, en particular, el sector bancario, han mostrado una destacable resiliencia ante dicho choques. Ello se fundamenta tanto en las caractersticas de la afectacin, que pas sbitamente de un cierre masivo a la reapertura, como en la slida posicin de los niveles de capital y de liquidez. Dicha solidez es el resultado de una serie de esfuerzos que, de manera consistente, se han llevado a cabo desde hace ms de dos dcadas. Durante la pandemia el Banco de Mxico adopt un amplio paquete de medidas y se coordin con otras autoridades para promover el comportamiento ordenado de los mercados de deuda y de cambios; mejorar el funcionamiento de los mercados internos, y fortalecer los canales de otorgamiento de crdito en la economa, desde los de mayoreo hasta el que reciben los hogares y las micro, pequeas y medianas empresas. El conjunto de acciones aprobadas contemplaron apoyos hasta por 750 mil millones de pesos (equivalente al 3.3% del PIB de 2019). 8 Ante la importante contraccin econmica que se registr a raz de la pandemia de COVID-19, es relevante destacar que el otorgamiento de crdito juega un papel clave para la recuperacin econmica. A pesar de que en el presente ao la actividad econmica se ha ido recuperando a un ritmo mayor al previsto originalmente, contina sin observarse una reactivacin en el otorgamiento del crdito, la cual podra contribuir a fortalecerla y darle mayor soporte. 2. Los riesgos hacia delante. La pandemia mostr la importancia de contar con un sistema financiero resiliente y capaz de enfrentar choques diversos. Por su importancia, entre algunos de los riesgos que podramos enfrentar en el futuro destacan: 1. Riesgos financieros relacionados con el clima. Los riesgos climticos implican un reto singular, ya que a diferencia de la mayora de los riesgos a los que se enfrenta la banca, en ste no hay datos e informacin histrica que permitan hacer una inferencia probabilstica sobre su ocurrencia y evaluar con precisin el potencial 9 de dao. En este entorno, es especialmente importante desarrollar herramientas de gestin de riesgos climticos a travs de pruebas de estrs y evaluacin de escenarios alternativos. La escala y gravedad de los riesgos climticos no permiten esperar a abordarlos hasta que sus efectos se materialicen, la prevencin y mitigacin son esenciales y representan una tarea inmediata. Los Bancos Centrales deben incorporar la evaluacin de los riesgos asociados al cambio climtico en la medicin de riesgos del sistema financiero. Esto requiere una consideracin adecuada de los riesgos fsicos y de transicin relevantes. Para evaluar estos riesgos, es necesario contar con lo siguiente: 1) Esquemas de divulgacin de informacin por parte de las empresas financieras y no financieras. En particular, promover la adopcin de estndares y mtricas tiles para comprender y abordar estos riesgos. La IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards Foundation) est desarrollando una norma de referencia global para la presentacin de informes, basada en el marco del TCFD (Task Force on Climate-related FInancial 10 Disclosures) y el trabajo de los emisores de normas de sostenibilidad. 2) Una adecuada comprensin e integracin de los riesgos fsicos y de transicin en la toma de decisiones financieras para reorientar los flujos de capital a fin de mejorar y preservar la competitividad de la economa, y alinear nuestra transicin hacia un futuro bajo en carbono con la de nuestros socios comerciales. 3) En los mercados emergentes, existen desafos adicionales para la movilizacin de recursos a una escala que fomente una transicin hacia una economa baja en carbono. Ello a pesar de que en estas economas, las inversiones sustentables sustituyen tecnologas que son ms intensivas en carbono que las de las economas avanzadas, por lo que su potencial de mitigacin y externalidades positivas es mucho mayor. 4) El costo del capital que enfrentan las economas emergentes y en desarrollo es significativamente ms alto que en las economas avanzadas. Es esencial pasar de un mal equilibrio con altos costos de financiamiento e inversin verde insuficiente, a un buen equilibrio con fuentes de financiamiento amigables con el clima a gran escala para estos pases y costos de financiamiento 11 realmente bajos. Es necesario que todo el sistema financiero y la banca en particular, evalen cmo desarrollar portafolios de crditos y proyectos verdes que cumplan con criterios internacionales y que permitan captar recursos de muy bajo costo a travs de bancos multilaterales de desarrollo y los Ex-Im Banks de pases desarrollados. En ello, es indispensable la activa participacin de todos, no el acompaamiento en los esfuerzos de alguien ms. 2. Riesgos cibernticos, tecnolgicos y operativos. Ante este riesgo creciente, es importante fortalecer nuestros protocolos de respuesta para abordar oportuna y coordinadamente los incidentes cibernticos y evitar que se propaguen a otros participantes. La seguridad informtica y la adecuada adopcin de tecnologa de punta se han convertido en un tema medular para la estabilidad del sistema financiero. Adicionalmente, dado que la afectacin puede ser a nivel de infraestructura, en datos, o materializarse monetariamente, la confianza 12 de los usuarios en un funcionamiento correcto de las entidades financieras puede verse severamente afectada ante eventos de ciberseguridad. Por eso, es fundamental tener en cuenta las siguientes consideraciones. 1) En el sistema financiero, los riesgos cibernticos enfrentan condiciones que no necesariamente estn presentes en otros mercados. La existencia de economas de red y la presencia de externalidades, producto de los niveles elevados de interconexin de los distintos participantes en el sistema financiero, pueden generar fallas de mercado que resultan en niveles de inversin y medidas de prevencin de riesgos socialmente subptimas. 2) El sistema financiero es propenso a los denominados comportamientos en manada si los usuarios consideran que sus recursos y operaciones estn expuestos a riesgos de terceros y contagios. 3) La regulacin y supervisin en materia de ciberseguridad debe atender al sistema en su conjunto en un horizonte de largo plazo, fomentar la cooperacin y comunicacin entre autoridades y entidades financieras. 13 4) La fortaleza de la seguridad informtica depende del eslabn ms vulnerable de la cadena. Esto aplica tanto a nivel de una institucin, como en trminos del sistema en su conjunto. Por ello, las acciones de mitigacin de riesgos deben orientarse a garantizar la continuidad operativa, entendida como una red, tanto a nivel de las instituciones como del sistema en su conjunto. 5) Dentro de este mbito, uno de los temas que ha ido ganando mayor relevancia es la participacin de los Gigantes Tecnolgicos en la provisin de servicios financieros a nivel global, as como en el suministro de servicios tecnolgicos a empresas financieras, incluido el almacenamiento, transmisin o anlisis de datos. En su participacin directa o indirecta en el sistema financiero se deben preservar los siguientes principios: i) a igual riesgo, igual regulacin; ii) plena interoperabilidad de redes, evitando la conformacin de silos y redes parciales; iii) mantener continuidad operativa y neutralidad tecnolgica; y, iv) plena proteccin al consumidor. 6) Un aspecto en el que se ha visto un considerable aumento en la concentracin de riesgo es en la provisin de servicios tecnolgicos por parte de unas cuantas empresas. Esto puede 14 representar un riesgo alto para la estabilidad financiera ante alguna falla operativa o ciberataque, pudiendo convertirse en un evento sistmico. Como vimos en el episodio del 5 de octubre con la cada de una de las redes sociales ms relevantes, estas empresas no estn exentas de riesgos operativos importantes. 7) Es necesario seguir desarrollando mecanismos de monitoreo e identificacin de riesgos y vulnerabilidades de manera oportuna y tener respuestas de poltica adecuadas ante la materializacin de dichos riesgos. Seoras y seores: Enfrentamos, como nunca antes, un entorno cambiante en el que se avizoran numerosas oportunidades y, tambin, retos inusitados. Ante este panorama, ser esencial que las instituciones financieras de nuestro pas y, de manera especial los bancos y sus reas de administracin de riesgos, desempeen su papel estratgico en definir el permetro de accin de sus instituciones. El cual, debe ser consistente a lo largo del tiempo con su modelo de generacin de valor para sus usuarios, y no estar sujeto a tropezar en la inercia y miopa de rentabilidad de corto plazo a la que en ocasiones podran estar sujetas 15 las reas de negocio. La funcin de las reas de riesgos en la definicin de la visin y estrategias de sus instituciones nunca haba sido tan importante. En particular, ante algunos de los nuevos desafos que aqu he mencionado, ser deseable que las instituciones amplen y refuercen sus esquemas para el monitoreo, la administracin y la gestin de riesgos. Para ello, un elemento clave ser que las reas y departamentos responsables de dicha gestin y administracin se encuentren adecuadamente equipados, no slo en el aspecto de infraestructura y tecnologa sino, sobre todo, en cuanto a su capital humano. Si bien el impacto ms directo e inmediato de lo anterior se reflejar en una mayor proteccin para las instituciones financieras mismas, ante los riesgos que en lo individual enfrentan, tambin contribuir a la resiliencia del sistema en su conjunto. Este reto lo enfrentamos todos. 16 Por ello, tal como la experiencia reciente con la crisis del COVID-19 ha vuelto a poner de manifiesto, la comunicacin efectiva y la accin coordinada entre las instituciones financieras y las autoridades es una herramienta indispensable para hacer frente a retos y adversidades, as como para impulsar la fortaleza y el desarrollo del sistema financiero, siempre en beneficio de quien est al centro de todos nuestros esfuerzos, el usuario y la sociedad. Muchas gracias. 17

Title: Financial inclusion: a world to discover
text: "Financial inclusion: a world to discover" Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the inauguration of the Chair of Financial Inclusion "Agustin Carstens" Mexico City, November 17, 2017  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade Kuribrena,  Madam Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit, teacher Vanessa Rubio Marquez,  Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico, engineer Marcos Martinez Gavica,  Mr. Rector of the Autonomous Technological Institute of Mexico, Dr. Arturo Fernandez Perez,  Ladies and gentlemen, 1 Good morning. I am grateful, excited, for the great honor that, at the initiative of the Secretary of Finance, Dr. Jose Antonio Meade, this nascent chair on financial inclusion has been baptized with my name. Really, thank you very much. In addition to an overwhelming distinction, the fact that my name is associated with the study of an issue as important to enhance well-being as financial inclusion, represents, in my eyes, a fascinating challenge. Financial inclusion is an issue of borders that are widening as we explore its vast territory and is, at the same time, a crucial topic for the economic well-being of people. In a personal note I would like on this occasion to pay tribute to my wife, Catherine Mansell Mayo, who 22 years ago (1995) wrote the book "Popular Finance in Mexico: The Rediscovery of a Forgotten Financial System", which 2 was a pioneering research on the subject of inclusion and financial education in our country. I will not stop on this occasion to list the progress that we have made in recent years in Mexico in terms of financial inclusion. They are in no way negligible or minor and, although there is still much to be done and we would do badly to be satisfied, neither can we haggle over the financial authorities, nor the intermediaries, nor the institutions, much less the disseminators of financial education and society as a whole, credit for all that has been achieved. For my part, I would like to share with you some reflections on the conceptual and research challenges that the issue of financial inclusion represents and that, without a doubt, will be the object of the intellectual inquisitions of those who gather around this chair. I am convinced that, to put it colloquially, 3 we have only just begun to "sink our teeth into the issue of financial inclusion". Let's start with something that may seem obvious: financial inclusion is not an end in itself, but a propitious condition for the human being to enhance his economic well-being. It is therefore something extremely desirable, but subordinate to a higher end which is well-being. Let us not confuse, then, the achievement of such and such indicators of financial inclusion with the ultimate goal. And here arises another question that must be the subject of discussion and careful study: From what point can we talk about a person being a beneficiary of full financial inclusion?, even more: is there a "full financial inclusion" as something already established or rather it is a desirable goal that constantly, thanks to financial and technological innovation, is it moving forward? 4 We can talk about four pillars, generally accepted and used in Mexico, to characterize financial inclusion. These pillars are: First: access, which refers to all those points - physical or virtual - that allow a viable contact between the public and financial institutions and intermediaries. Secondly, the use, as regards the demand and effective use of financial services. Third: the protection of the user of financial services; obviously it refers to the consumer getting a fair deal, for which we all know that transparency and everything that helps to eliminate or reduce asymmetric information is crucial. Fourth: financial education, which refers to the acquisition by the public of the skills, abilities and knowledge that contribute effectively to the making of financial decisions that maximize their well-being. 5 In these four pillars we have registered in Mexico undoubted advances in the last two decades, but there is also much to be done. But that is why these four pillars represent vast territories for exploration. When talking about access, for example, the undoubted synergy between technology, connectivity and financial inclusion is obvious. In this area, I have no doubt that the proposal of the so-called Fintech Law will be an ideal platform to enhance this synergy. But also, unfortunately, the lags in connectivity that we still have are obvious. According to data from the Federal Telecommunications Institute1, at the national level we have just over 49 fixed broadband connections for every hundred households; however, that average is misleading: In Mexico City there are-almost 95 (94.9) fixed broadband connections. 1 Telecommunications Information Bank of the Federal Telecommunications Institute: / 6 while in Chiapas there are only 16 connections for every hundred households. The same inequality is overwhelming in the case of cell phone lines for every hundred households. The national average is 90 lines; in Mexico City there are 125 lines for every hundred households, but in Oaxaca there are only less than half: 54 cell phone lines for every hundred households. It is clear that we are here, as a country, facing a great challenge in terms of infrastructure for connectivity. In this regard, the progress that the promising Shared Network project, led by the Federal Government, has already made, augurs well and I hope that its objectives will fully materialize in the not too distant future, since it could undoubtedly allow a quantum leap in terms of financial inclusion. But that is only one face in the multifaceted world of financial inclusion challenges we must face. It seems to me that, from the point of view of analysis and research on financial inclusion, where more territory 7 we have to explore, between different branches of the social sciences, it is in the second pillar that I mentioned: the one that refers to the use of financial services. There is an old saying that can help me share with you my concern about it. It is said that you can take the horse to the river but you can not force it to drink water if. Why, in the case of Mexico, are there still vast sectors of the population that have the resources and means of access to formal financial intermediation do not take advantage of its advantages and prefer to remain in financial exclusion? From a strictly rational point of view it would be said that it is, for the vast majority of these people, an erroneous perception, because there is no doubt that the security, flexibility and comfort in the management of financial resources that financial inclusion brings would give them greater benefits than those they have today outside of it. 8 However, the problem may be more complex than it seems. Perhaps we have failed to convincingly show the benefits of financial inclusion to these population groups; or perhaps from the point of view of the supply of financial services, and of ourselves as authorities, we have started from an erroneous assumption about the behavior of economic agents. This erroneous assumption is to consider that rationality predominates in all the decisions that, in matters of economy and finance, human beings make. Not necessarily so. Here we enter the field of behavioral sciences and their intersection with economic decisions. It turns out that, as Richard H. Thaler, the 2017 Nobel Prize in Economics, has eloquently said, the "homo economicus" that always acts rationally to maximize its profit, does not exist or, at least, is not as common as we had believed. 9 Phenomena such as the existence of inconsistent preferences over time or the problems of "self-control" of individuals in their decisions to borrow or save for retirement or to face catastrophic events, belie the assumption that always and in all cases rationality prevails in financial decision-making. The unfortunate earthquakes that devastated Mexico in recent months have highlighted one of these irrationalities: nationwide only 6.5% of homes have damage insurance2. Of course, when comparing the benefit of having insurance of this kind against its cost over time, this figure seems inexplicably low, but in reality it is that we must give space, in our inquisitions about financial decisions, to that wide swath of behaviors that we human beings incur that are not 100 percent rational: either by a deficient perception, or by 2 Estimate of the Mexican Association of Insurance Institutions. 10 the "animal spirits" of which Keynes spoke, that is, simply because we all, in certain circumstances, can be victims of fatal presumptions, which are illusory; presumptions such as "this time will be different", "that will not happen to me"... In Thaler's own words: "Unless you are Mr. Spock (the character from 'Star Treek' or 'Star Trek' who as you know is an alien who lacks emotions and always acts rationally) irrelevant things do matter in economic behavior" (see Thaler op-ed in The New York Times, May 8, 2015). The first preliminary conclusion is that also when it comes to financial inclusion, and the use or non-use of formal financial intermediation, in no way should we disdain what the behavioral sciences can tell us about those things that we sometimes consider "irrelevant" I have already mentioned some data about connectivity in our country, but beyond the challenges posed by the 11 Technological lags, and which are dramatic in certain regions, we can detect radical differences, in terms of the use or not of technology for transactions and financial operations, according to the age of the users. Obviously here we are not talking about the pillar of "access" to financial institutions, but the "use" of a service that, from a rational point of view, is more efficient. As with the media, there is no doubt that also in financial intermediation we have had to live a sharp transition between the materially tangible and the virtual; between face-to-face personal interaction and remote electronic interaction; between the paper entry and the cyber record. And this technological transition seems to have widened the gap between generations. In the last century it was considered that the inhabitant of a city who wished to be well informed was subscribed to a printed newspaper that he received and read every morning; today it is difficult 12 to find, in the big cities, someone under the age of forty who is subscribed to a printed newspaper to inform himself at home. In this sense, the Internet has ruthlessly displaced the print media. Something similar must happen in the case of financial services, that is: we should assume that for millions of people under 40 the contact with financial institutions - what we call access - will be remote, virtual, electronic, cyber. It will not be physical or face-to-face, and may be provided by institutions of a different nature than traditional banks. Is this the case or, rather, in this field the supply and demand for services walk more slowly than in the field of news and information?, and if so, why this different pace of acceptance and use of new technologies? This is another aspect of discussion, analysis and research for scholars of financial inclusion. 13 In short, these questions are just a few of the many that, as an object of analysis and study, financial inclusion poses to us. I have mentioned them only as a sample of the immense field of research that we have in front of us and trying to make these words fulfill the purpose of inspiring, in the Chair of Financial Inclusion, many more questions that, probably, will be more acute and pressing than those I have asked today. By beginning to solve those unknowns with study, research, and talent, the results will translate into greater financial inclusion. In conclusion, at the risk of being repetitive, I would like to thank the Secretary of finance once again for this initiative, which should contribute, in an effective manner, to fulfilling the objective that brings us all together here today: the desire that financial services contribute more and more to the well-being of all Mexicans. 14 Thanks a lot. I proceed now to formally declare the Chair of Financial Inclusion "Agustin Carstens" formally inaugurated at 10:00 a.m. on November 17, 2017. 15
text_original: La inclusin financiera: un mundo por descubrir Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, durante la inauguracin de la Ctedra de Inclusin Financiera Agustn Carstens Ciudad de Mxico, 17 de noviembre de 2017  Seor Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, doctor Jos Antonio Meade Kuribrea,  Seora Subsecretaria de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico, maestra Vanessa Rubio Mrquez,  Seor Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, ingeniero Marcos Martnez Gavica,  Seor Rector del Instituto Tecnolgico Autnomo de Mxico, doctor Arturo Fernndez Prez,  Seoras y seores: 1 Buenos das. La inclusin financiera es un tema de fronteras que se van ensanchando conforme exploramos su vasto territorio y es, a la vez, un tpico crucial para el bienestar econmico de las personas. En un apunte personal me gustara con este motivo dar tributo a mi esposa, Catherine Mansell Mayo, quien hace 22 aos (1995) escribi el libro Las Finanzas Populares en Mxico: El Redescubrimiento de un Sistema Financiero Olvidado, el cual 2 fue una investigacin pionera en el tema de la inclusin y la educacin financiera en nuestro pas. Estoy convencido de que, por decirlo coloquialmente, 3 al tema de la inclusin financiera apenas le hemos empezado a hincar el diente. Empecemos por algo que puede parecer obvio: la inclusin financiera no es una finalidad en s misma, sino una condicin propicia para que el ser humano potencie su bienestar econmico. Es pues, algo sumamente deseable, pero subordinado a un fin superior que es el bienestar. No confundamos, entonces, el logro de tales o cuales indicadores de inclusin financiera con la meta final. Y aqu surge otra pregunta que debe ser objeto de discusin y de esmerado estudio: A partir de qu punto podemos hablar de que una persona es beneficiaria de una plena inclusin financiera?, ms an: existe una plena inclusin financiera como algo ya establecido o ms bien se trata de una meta deseable que constantemente, gracias a la innovacin financiera y tecnolgica, se est moviendo hacia delante? 4 Podemos hablar de cuatro pilares, generalmente aceptados y utilizados en Mxico, para caracterizar la inclusin financiera. Esos pilares son: Primero: el acceso, lo que se refiere a todos aquellos puntos  fsicos o virtuales- que permiten un contacto viable entre el pblico y las instituciones e intermediarios financieros. Segundo: el uso, lo que se refiere a la demanda y a la utilizacin efectiva de los servicios financieros. Tercero: la proteccin del usuario de los servicios financieros; obviamente se refiere a que el consumidor obtenga un trato justo, para lo cual todos sabemos que es crucial la transparencia y todo lo que colabore a eliminar o reducir la informacin asimtrica. Cuarto: la educacin financiera, que se refiere a la adquisicin por el pblico de las habilidades, destrezas y conocimientos que contribuyan eficazmente a la toma de decisiones financieras que maximicen su bienestar. 5 En estos cuatro pilares hemos registrado en Mxico indudables avances en las ltimas dos dcadas, pero tambin queda mucho por hacer. Pero por eso estos cuatro pilares representan vastos territorios para la exploracin. Al hablar de acceso salta a la vista, por ejemplo, la indudable sinergia entre tecnologa, conectividad e inclusin financiera. En este terreno, no me cabe duda que la propuesta de la llamada Ley Fintech ser una plataforma idnea para potenciar esta sinergia. Pero tambin, lamentablemente, saltan a la vista los rezagos en conectividad que an tenemos. Segn datos del Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones1, a nivel nacional tenemos poco ms de 49 conexiones de banda ancha fija por cada cien hogares; sin embargo ese promedio es engaoso: En la Ciudad de Mxico soncasi 95 (94.9) conexiones de banda ancha fija 1 Banco de Informacin de Telecomunicaciones del Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones: https://bit.ift.org.mx/ 6 mientras que en Chiapas slo son 16 conexiones por cada cien hogares. La misma desigualdad es abrumadora en el caso de lneas de telefona celular por cada cien hogares. El promedio nacional es de 90 lneas; en la Ciudad de Mxico hay 125 lneas por cada cien hogares, pero en Oaxaca slo hay menos de la mitad: 54 lneas de telefona celular por cada cien hogares. Es evidente que estamos aqu, como pas, ante un gran reto en materia de infraestructura para la conectividad. Al respecto, el avance que ya ha tenido el promisorio proyecto de Red Compartida, encabezado por el Gobierno Federal, es un buen augurio y espero que se materialicen plenamente sus objetivos en un futuro no muy lejano, pues sin duda, podra permitir un salto cuntico en materia de inclusin financiera. Pero esa es slo una cara en el polifactico mundo de los desafos de la inclusin financiera que debemos plantearnos. Me parece que, desde el punto de vista del anlisis y la investigacin sobre la inclusin financiera, donde ms territorio 7 tenemos que explorar, entre distintas ramas de las ciencias sociales, es en el segundo pilar que mencion: el que se refiere al uso de los servicios financieros. Hay un viejo refrn que me puede ayudar a compartir con ustedes mi inquietud al respecto. Se dice que puedes llevar el caballo al ro pero no puedes obligarlo a que beba agua si. Por qu, en el caso de Mxico, an hay vastos sectores de la poblacin que teniendo los recursos y los medios de acceso a la intermediacin financiera formal no aprovechan sus ventajas y prefieren permanecer en la exclusin financiera? Ser que perciben ventajas en permanecer fuera de la formalidad?, desde un punto de vista estrictamente racional se dira que se trata, para la inmensa mayora de esas personas, de una percepcin errnea, porque es indudable que la seguridad, flexibilidad y comodidad en el manejo de recursos financieros que trae consigo la inclusin financiera les dara mayores beneficios que los que hoy tienen al margen de ella. 8 Sin embargo, el problema puede ser ms complejo de lo que parece. Tal vez no hemos sabido mostrar convincentemente los beneficios de la inclusin financiera a esos grupos de la poblacin; o quiz desde el punto de vista de la oferta de los servicios financieros, y de nosotros mismos como autoridades, hemos partido de un supuesto errneo sobre el comportamiento de los agentes econmicos. Dicho supuesto errneo es considerar que la racionalidad predomina en todas las decisiones que, en materia de economa y finanzas, tomamos los seres humanos. No necesariamente es as. Aqu entramos al terreno de las ciencias de la conducta y su interseccin con las decisiones econmicas. Resulta que, como elocuentemente ha dicho Richard H. Thaler, Premio Nobel de Economa 2017, el homo economicus que siempre acta racionalmente para maximizar su beneficio, no existe o, al menos, no es tan comn como habamos credo. 9 Fenmenos como la existencia de preferencias inconsistentes a travs del tiempo o los problemas de autocontrol de los individuos en sus decisiones de endeudamiento o de ahorro para el retiro o para afrontar eventos catastrficos, desmienten el supuesto de que siempre y en todos los casos prevalece la racionalidad en la toma de decisiones financieras. Los lamentables sismos que en meses recientes asolaron a Mxico han resaltado una de estas irracionalidades: a nivel nacional slo 6.5% de las viviendas cuenta con un seguro de daos2. Por supuesto, al comparar el beneficio de tener un seguro de este tipo contra su costo a lo largo del tiempo, esta cifra parece inexplicablemente baja, pero en realidad es que debemos dar espacio, en nuestras inquisiciones acerca de las decisiones financieras, a esa ancha franja de comportamientos en que incurrimos los seres humanos que no son 100 por ciento racionales: sea por una percepcin deficiente, sea por 2 Estimacin de la Asociacin Mexicana de Instituciones de Seguros. 10 los espritus animales de los que habl Keynes, o sea simplemente porque todos, en determinadas circunstancias, podemos ser vctimas de presunciones fatales, que son ilusorias; presunciones como esta vez ser diferente, a m no me pasar eso En palabras del propio Thaler: A menos que t seas el seor Spock (el personaje de Star Treek o Viaje a las Estrellasquien como ustedes saben es un extraterrestre que carece de emociones y siempre acta racionalmente) las cosas irrelevantes s importan en el comportamiento econmico (ver op-ed de Thaler en The New York Times, 8 de mayo de 2015). La primera conclusin preliminar es que tambin tratndose de inclusin financiera, y del uso o no uso de la intermediacin financiera formal, de ninguna manera debemos desdear lo que nos puedan decir las ciencias del comportamiento sobre esas cosas que a veces consideramos irrelevantes Ya he mencionado algunos datos acerca de la conectividad en nuestro pas, pero ms all de los desafos que representan los 11 rezagos tecnolgicos, y que resultan dramticos en determinadas regiones, podemos detectar diferencias radicales, en cuanto al uso o no de la tecnologa para transacciones y operaciones financieras, de acuerdo con la edad de los usuarios. Obviamente aqu no estamos hablando del pilar de acceso a las instituciones financieras, sino del uso de un servicio que, desde un punto de vista racional, es ms eficiente. Al igual que sucede con los medios de comunicacin no hay duda que tambin en la intermediacin financiera nos ha tocado vivir una tajante transicin entre lo materialmente tangible y lo virtual; entre la interaccin personal cara a cara y la interaccin electrnica a distancia; entre el asiento anotado en papel y el registro ciberntico. Y esta transicin tecnolgica pareciera que ha ensanchado la brecha entre generaciones. En el siglo pasado se consideraba que el habitante de una ciudad que deseaba estar bien informado estaba suscrito a un diario impreso que reciba y lea cada maana; hoy da es difcil 12 encontrar, en las grandes ciudades, a alguien menor de cuarenta aos que est suscrito a un diario impreso para informarse en su hogar. En este sentido la Internet ha desplazado sin piedad a los medios impresos. Algo similar debe suceder en el caso de los servicios financieros, es decir: deberamos suponer que para millones de personas menores de 40 aos el contacto con las instituciones financieras lo que denominamos acceso- va a ser a distancia, virtual, electrnico, ciberntico. No ser fsico, ni presencial, y tal vez ser prestado por instituciones de un cuo distinto a los bancos tradicionales. Title: Signing ceremony of the closing act of the inter-institutional work Bank of Mexico-INEGI for the transfer of responsibility for measuring price indices
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, at the end of the signing ceremony of the closing act of the inter-institutional work banco de Mexico - INEGI for the transfer of responsibility for measuring price indices. July 14, 2011. I thank INEGI for its support and collaboration and I congratulate the joint teams for having brought the transfer to fruition. I will not elaborate on the process, for Dr. Sojo described it more than accurately and eloquently. If I would like to point out that the culmination of this transfer process that we are celebrating today, with the formal and solemn surrender to INEGI of this responsibility, means much more than the satisfaction of a legal mandate. For the Bank of Mexico, it is an opportunity to endorse its full autonomy and to crown a long and successful process of institutional modernization that began in April 1994 when the Bank obtained, precisely, its autonomous character. From the explanatory statement of the Autonomy Initiative of the Bank of Mexico, it was emphatically pointed out that, and I quote, "... if the proposed constitutional reform were approved, it would not be appropriate for the statistics on price indices to continue to be carried out by the central bank." In such a way that it can be said that with this transfer of the measurement of price indices to INEGI, the Bank of Mexico perfects its autonomy to the last detail. By the way, it was a very fortunate fact that on July 7, the last occasion on which the Bank of Mexico disseminated, as a source of origin, the evolution of the national consumer price index, it resulted in a monthly variation of 0.0 percent and that, with it, the accumulated inflation of the first half of the year reaches only 0.3 percent. This opens a space for reflection on the role of the Central Bank as guarantor of price stability in the country, because that is the priority mandate of the Bank established by the Constitution and the full fulfillment of that mandate is the foundation of its autonomy. Indeed, the downward trajectory that inflation has shown in recent months confirms in fact that we continue to move forward to bring headline inflation towards the permanent target of 3 percent per year, considering an interval 1 of variation of plus/minus one percent. But no one should be confused by these satisfactory results in terms of price stability, nor assume that for this reason the Governing Board of the Central Bank is experiencing a stage of carelessness or partial abandonment of its priority task. The fight against inflation is permanent and inalienable. The term "monetary pause" is often used in some commentaries to refer to the period during which the Central Bank's benchmark interest rate remains unchanged. Such an expression is misleading because it seems to erroneously suggest that, by not modifying its reference rate, the Central Bank and/or its Governing Board are enjoying a kind of vacation with respect to the fight against inflation. Nothing more false. It is enough to read carefully the minutes of the meetings of the Governing Board on monetary policy to verify that the priority concern of each and every one of its members is precisely price stability. There are divergent opinions and approaches among the members of the Board, and the minutes give an exhaustive account of these differences, but the conviction remains a constant in all of us who form that collegiate body that our task and our most important responsibility is precisely to seek price stability. Therefore, due to the importance of the full fulfillment of this mandate in favor of price stability, this ceremony is particularly significant for the Central Bank: once the measurement of price indices has been totally in the hands of INEGI, it should also be clear to everyone that the task of the Central Bank in terms of prices is solely and exclusively to apply the tools of monetary policy to combat inflation. And that mission is not subject to variation. I reiterate, because it is a permanent message from the Bank of Mexico, some of the great benefits that price stability throws for society as a whole, and I will comment later on some of the factors that have allowed us to advance in the convergence towards the inflation target. Both economic theory and international experience have shown that an environment of low and stable inflation makes resource allocation more efficient, which in turn contributes to improving the productive capacity of the economy. In addition, an environment is generated that facilitates decision-making 2 long term, primarily those related to the accumulation of physical and human capital. Price stability therefore creates an environment conducive to economic activity. It should also be noted that to the extent that inflation is a regressive tax that harms the poorest segments of society to a greater extent, its decrease leads to an improvement in the distribution of income. Precisely because of the benefits that a low and stable inflation environment gives to the economy, in Mexico, as in an increasing number of countries, price stability has been defined by law as the priority objective of the monetary authority. As for the progress we have made in terms of inflation in Mexico, these have occurred in the context of a strengthening in the framework of the conduct of macroeconomic policy and, in general, in an environment of improvement in the economic fundamentals of our country. First, prudent fiscal policy has helped eliminate the persistent fiscal deficits that the country suffered in the past. This same prudence has contributed to a significant reduction in public indebtedness in relation to gross domestic product. In addition, not only has the ratio of public debt to GDP been reduced, but proper debt management has generated a better debt profile, in terms of terms and rates. On the other hand, since the mid-1990s Mexico adopted a flexible exchange rate regime. This has helped to cushion the negative effects on the domestic economy of adverse external shocks, especially if we consider that Mexico is an open and relatively small economy. In addition to the above, the strengthening of financial regulation and supervision has preserved us from episodes of banking crises and risks of insolvency in the financial system, which in Mexico remains remarkably healthy both in capitalization and in solvency and liquidity, and in comparison with the tribulations suffered by the financial systems of some other countries and regions. An additional element is that the Bank of Mexico since 2001 formally implemented an inflation targeting regime. This monetary regime is based on an institutional commitment to price stability, as well as on a 3 active and transparent strategy of communication with the public. Key steps have been taken to advance this communication strategy, including the decision to publish the minutes of the sessions of the Governing Board convened to make decisions on the monetary policy stance. This is how this monetary regime, supported by a prudent fiscal policy, has allowed a significant reduction in both inflation levels and their volatility and persistence. This, in a virtuous process, has increased the credibility of the Central Institute, which has anchored inflation expectations, and decisively helps us to advance in convergence towards the inflation target. In order to illustrate the benefits of strengthening the macroeconomic framework of our country, and in particular of the growing credibility of the Central Institute, it is worth highlighting the recent evolution of inflation in emerging economies. As is well known, in the first months of the year international commodity prices showed significant increases, contributing to an increase in inflation around the world. Those economies with relatively less solid macroeconomic fundamentals and signs of overheating were hit hardest. In this international environment, Mexico has differentiated itself from other emerging economies. Overall, inflation has continued its downward trend and is expected to continue in the process of convergence towards the permanent inflation target. Thus, it has not been necessary to modify the monetary policy stance. In particular, various factors such as the public policy of energy prices, the appreciation of the exchange rate, the slack in the input markets, and the absence of inflationary pressures on the side of aggregate demand mitigated the impact of several external shocks on inflation in our country. In addition to the above, an element that also contributed significantly to preventing a substantial increase in inflation is the growing credibility of the Central Institute's commitment to price stability, which has helped to anchor inflation expectations. In this context, inflation has followed a gradual downward trend which has 4 allowed, unlike other countries with a less solid macroeconomic framework, to maintain the monetary policy stance unchanged. I reiterate, because this is an extremely important clarification: the fact that the Bank's monetary stance has not changed for many months should in no way be interpreted as a complacent position towards inflation. On the contrary, the firm commitment of the Bank and its Governing Board to price stability has been a decisive factor in keeping inflation and its expectations under control, without the need to restrict the monetary policy stance. Of course, as we have said in all the monetary policy announcements, we remain scrupulously vigilant and I have no doubt that in the Governing Board we will act without hesitation and without delay in case of detecting generalized pressures on prices. From now on, the price indices prepared and disseminated by INEGI will measure the performance of the Bank of Mexico precisely with respect to its priority objective. By virtue of everything that both institutions have done during this process to guarantee the best of transfers, we believe that INEGI has all the elements so that the measurement of inflation in Mexico remains thorough and exemplary. I believe that the calculation of the INPC and the INPP cannot be in better hands than in those of the INEGI Thank you very much. 5

Con la finalidad de ilustrar los beneficios del fortalecimiento en el marco macroeconmico de nuestro pas, y en particular de la creciente credibilidad en el Instituto Central, conviene destacar la evolucin que recientemente ha tenido la inflacin en las economas emergentes.
