Title: The Bank of Mexico: strategies against the volatility of agricultural prices
text: The Bank of Mexico: strategies against the volatility of agricultural prices Remarks by the Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Roberto Del Cueto, during the opening of the International Forum "Towards a Public Policy for the Development of the Agricultural Sector". August 2, 2011 Good morning, everyone. I thank the Senate of the Republic and the National Agricultural Council for the honorable invitation they have extended to me to participate in the inauguration of this important international forum on public policies for the development of the agricultural sector. The exchange of experiences, knowledge and concerns about the present and future of food production in the world is essential to find creative solutions to the challenges we are facing, every day and from the most diverse perspectives, in the production and markets of agricultural goods. It is no secret to anyone that agricultural markets in the world are experiencing a period of great uncertainty. The Elevated 1 Price volatility affects producers and consumers alike, disrupts financial markets, distorts the allocation of resources and discourages investment, makes financing for agricultural producers more expensive and hinders, and makes it difficult for policymakers to make appropriate and timely decisions. Therefore, combating the volatility of agricultural prices and mitigating its negative effects should be a focus of priority attention. I will not dwell on a detailed examination of the varied and complex factors that concur to generate this problem. I would like to limit my message to commenting, first, on how this volatility of agricultural prices influences the core tasks of the Bank of Mexico, and then to point out some of what the Central Bank is doing to underpin the development of the agricultural sector, either directly through its powers to regulate markets and financial instruments. or indirectly, for example through FIRA, that is: through the four trusts established in relation to agriculture, of which the Bank of Mexico has been a trustee for 55 years. At the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico we experience every day the challenge of interpreting price trends 2 Agricultural. The challenge is not simple because it is about scrutinizing its possible effects on inflation. To do this, we must discern whether we are facing episodes of ephemeral price increases due to supply shocks, or if we are dealing with permanent trends that will have lasting and negative effects on inflation. This task of analysis and informed discussion is reflected in the minutes of the Governing Board itself that we are publicly disseminating since the beginning of this year. Airing before public opinion the data and arguments that support our rich exchanges of opinions, prior to monetary policy decisions, is something that contributes decisively to a better functioning of the markets. Information is like the oxygen that allows the right decision-making to all market participants: producers, commercial intermediaries, financial intermediaries, consumers, investors, accredited. Abundant and timely information is also the best weapon we have to reduce uncertainty and thereby lessen the effects of price volatility. Since the priority objective of the Bank of Mexico is to ensure price stability, you can imagine that the markets of 3 Agricultural goods from Mexico and the world are for us, both for the Governing Board and for the Bank's technical team, a constant reason for analysis and concern. In addition to the tools of monetary policy, the Bank uses its powers to participate, within the scope of its competence, in the design of policies and instruments that contribute to mitigating this volatility of agricultural prices. Thus, at the end of last year the Bank of Mexico expanded the spectrum of goods that can be considered as underlying derivative operations. This allows producers and marketers of certain agricultural goods such as yellow corn, soybeans, wheat, sugar and pork to operate derivative contracts on them since last April both in the Mexican derivatives market and in the respective market of Chicago. What does this mean?, that we have opened more options of coverage contracts for agricultural producers, which translates into greater certainty for them, as well as operating in a more suitable environment for planning and decision-making. 4 On the other hand, in its role as trustee of FIRA, the Bank promotes the strengthening of the technical capacities of this institution to deepen the knowledge and analysis of agricultural markets as well as the evolution of the prices of these goods. In addition to the fact that this information is one of the valuable inputs that FIRA provides to its clients, it constitutes the raw material for the design of the financial products offered by its trusts, articulating the credit, guarantees, insurance and price coverage program of FIRA itself in its different modalities. Since its establishment in 1954 FIRA has been, especially for agricultural producers in Mexico, a valuable tool to increase the supply of agricultural goods, underpinning the development of the countryside and its producers. Just to measure the contribution of FIRA to agricultural development in Mexico I mention that during 2010 the loan portfolio granted by the different institutions that make up the Development Bank and Development Entities amounted to 444,500 million pesos, and of that amount the credit portfolio of FIRA represented approximately 13 percent, that is: almost 58 billion pesos. 5 Today, out of every three pesos of financing that the Mexican countryside receives, one peso comes from FIRA. But FIRA has not been limited to being a second-tier bank. For many years it has encompassed its task of financial intermediation in a broader objective: to provide genuine and practical business solutions and propose development alternatives for the field. Hence, the human capital accumulated in FIRA through many years of dedicated and responsible work is today its main asset. Throughout its history FIRA has been adapting opportunely to the growing complexity posed by the development of the field and the boost to its productivity. Therefore, it has a long catalog of success stories. Concrete, tangible and sobering stories. To its credit programs - whether in the form of discount or loan through financial intermediaries - FIRA added from the beginning guarantee programs, as well as technological support. Later, it established special programs, based on the specific needs of climatic regions, agricultural products with peculiar characteristics, or the maturation times of certain projects. In many cases, as you know, these programs have been developed. 6 with SAGARPA and in other cases on a par with other development banking institutions, such as Financiera Rural. As an additional and increasingly necessary step in this architecture of financial intermediation services and technical assistance, FIRA has a price hedging program designed with simple rules and under three basic principles: technical support, operational viability and total transparency. The price hedging program allows the producer to set the price of his harvest in the market conditions of the time the hedging is made. Specifically, it grants the right to sell or buy at a certain price for a certain volume in exchange for an accessible premium. This, of course, provides the long-awaited certainty to both the creditor and the financial intermediary just in the face of the scenario of persistent volatility in agricultural prices. In the case of FIRA, the program is focused on the smallest producers, who are those who usually find insurmountable barriers to access price coverage schemes. On the other hand, the Bank of Mexico permanently supports FIRA in the design of public policies aimed at improving the channels and infrastructure of collection, storage and 7 marketing of products. These policies not only contribute to reducing the volatility of agricultural prices, but also improve the competitiveness of the agri-food sector. By generating greater confidence in agricultural market participants and the intermediaries that finance these activities, credit to the sector is increased and granted on better terms for producers. The challenge of increasingly promoting the development of the agricultural sector through better public policies is immense and requires the active participation of authorities and financial intermediaries, governments, legislators and, obviously, producers and marketers of agricultural goods. Specifically, the volatility of agricultural prices must be faced with creative solutions based on four premises that I consider key: first, information and transparency are crucial to reduce uncertainty and, with it, mitigate price volatility. Second, greater competition in the markets by lowering all kinds of barriers to entry, so that we have more and more 8 participants and a greater supply of agricultural goods for the benefit of all of us. Thirdly, a continued effort to increase agricultural productivity through the dissemination and use of the best available technology and through technical assistance; It seems to me that in this sense the task of FIRA has been exemplary throughout its history. And fourth, to harness and develop for the benefit of better functioning markets, the full potential of financial intermediation, to develop innovative credit and hedging products, as well as new specific financial markets. In this sense, we must read well the experience of the recent global financial crisis: there were clear omissions and failures of financial regulation that led to the crisis, but it would be a terrible mistake to fall into the opposite extreme and suffocate the markets with excessive controls and with an accumulation of prohibitions. Examples of this virtuous balance that financial regulation must have, between the two extremes, are the FIRA price hedging programs that I have already mentioned or the new regulation of the Bank of Mexico extending to agricultural goods the option of being used as underlying products in derivative contracts that benefit 9 producers, intermediaries and, ultimately, millions of consumers through better prices, more quality and greater supply of agricultural products. Thanks a lot. 10
text_original: El Banco de Mxico: estrategias frente a la volatilidad de los precios agropecuarios Palabras del Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, Roberto Del Cueto, durante la inauguracin del Foro Internacional Hacia una Poltica Pblica para el Desarrollo del Sector Agropecuario. 2 de agosto de 2011 Muy buenos das a todos. Agradezco al Senado de la Repblica y al Consejo Nacional Agropecuario la honrosa invitacin que me han hecho para participar en la inauguracin de este importante foro internacional sobre polticas pblicas para el desarrollo del sector agropecuario. El intercambio de experiencias, conocimientos e inquietudes acerca del presente y el futuro de la produccin de alimentos en el mundo, es primordial para encontrar soluciones creativas a los desafos que estamos enfrentando, todos los das y desde las perspectivas ms diversas, en la produccin y en los mercados de los bienes agropecuarios. Para nadie es un secreto que los mercados agropecuarios en el mundo viven una etapa de gran incertidumbre. La elevada 1 volatilidad de los precios afecta por igual a productores y a consumidores, perturba los mercados financieros, distorsiona la asignacin de recursos y desalienta la inversin, encarece y obstaculiza el financiamiento para los productores agropecuarios, dificulta, en fin, que los hacedores de polticas pblicas tomen decisiones adecuadas y oportunas. Por todo ello, combatir la volatilidad de los precios agropecuarios y mitigar sus efectos negativos debe ser un foco de atencin prioritario. No me detendr en un examen detallado de los variados y complejos factores que concurren para generar este problema. Deseo limitar mi mensaje a comentar, primero, cmo esta volatilidad de los precios agropecuarios influye en las tareas torales del Banco de Mxico y, despus apuntar algo de lo que hace el Banco Central para apuntalar el desarrollo del sector agropecuario, ya sea directamente mediante sus facultades de regulacin de los mercados y de los instrumentos financieros, o de manera indirecta, por ejemplo a travs de FIRA, esto es: a travs de los cuatro fideicomisos instituidos en relacin con la agricultura, de los cuales el Banco de Mxico ha sido fiduciario desde hace ya 55 aos. En la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico experimentamos todos los das el desafo de interpretar las tendencias de los precios 2 agropecuarios. El reto no es sencillo porque se trata de escudriar sus posibles efectos sobre la inflacin. Para ello debemos discernir si estamos ante episodios de alza efmera de precios por choques de oferta, o si estamos lidiando con tendencias permanentes que tendrn efectos perdurables y negativos sobre la inflacin. De esta tarea de anlisis y discusin informada dan cuenta las minutas de la propia Junta de Gobierno que estamos difundiendo pblicamente desde que comenz este ao. Ventilar ante la opinin pblica los datos y los argumentos que sustentan nuestros nutridos intercambios de opiniones, previos a las decisiones de poltica monetaria, es algo que contribuye de forma decisiva a un mejor funcionamiento de los mercados. La informacin es como el oxgeno que permite la toma de decisiones adecuadas a todos los participantes en los mercados: productores, intermediarios comerciales, intermediarios financieros, consumidores, inversionistas, acreditados. La informacin abundante y oportuna es tambin la mejor arma de la que disponemos para disminuir la incertidumbre y, de esa manera, aminorar los efectos de la volatilidad de los precios. Dado que el objetivo prioritario del Banco de Mxico es procurar la estabilidad de los precios, pueden imaginar que los mercados de 3 bienes agropecuarios de Mxico y del mundo son para nosotros, tanto para la Junta de Gobierno como para el equipo tcnico del Banco, un motivo constante de anlisis y preocupacin. Adems de las herramientas propias de la poltica monetaria, el Banco recurre a sus facultades para, en el mbito de su competencia, participar en el diseo de polticas e instrumentos que contribuyan a mitigar esta volatilidad de los precios agropecuarios. As, a fines del ao pasado el Banco de Mxico ampli el espectro de mercancas que pueden considerarse como subyacentes en las operaciones de derivados. Esto permite que desde abril pasado productores y comercializadores de ciertas mercancas agropecuarias como el maz amarillo, la soya, el trigo, el azcar y la carne de puerco puedan operar contratos de derivados sobre las mismas tanto en el mercado mexicano de derivados como en mercado respectivo de Chicago. Qu significa esto?, que hemos abierto ms opciones de contratos de cobertura para los productores agropecuarios, lo que se traduce en una mayor certidumbre para ellos, as como operar en un entorno ms idneo para la planeacin y la toma de decisiones. 4 Por otra parte, en su papel de fiduciario de FIRA, el Banco impulsa el fortalecimiento de las capacidades tcnicas de dicha institucin para profundizar en el conocimiento y anlisis de los mercados agropecuarios as como de la evolucin de los precios de dichos bienes. Adems de que esta informacin es uno de los valiosos insumos que proporciona FIRA a sus clientes, constituye la materia prima para el diseo de los productos financieros que ofrecen sus fideicomisos, articulando el crdito, las garantas, los seguros y el programa de cobertura de precios del propio FIRA en sus distintas modalidades. Desde su constitucin en 1954 FIRA ha sido, en especial para los productores agropecuarios en Mxico, una herramienta valiosa para aumentar la oferta de bienes agropecuarios, apuntalando el desarrollo del campo y de sus productores. Slo para dimensionar el aporte de FIRA al desarrollo agropecuario en Mxico menciono que durante 2010 la cartera de crdito otorgada por las diferentes instituciones que conforman la Banca de Desarrollo y Entidades de Fomento ascendi a $444 mil 500 millones de pesos, y de ese monto la cartera de crdito de FIRA represent aproximadamente el 13 por ciento, esto es: casi $58 mil millones de pesos. 5 Hoy da, de cada tres pesos de financiamiento que recibe el campo mexicano un peso proviene de FIRA. Pero FIRA no se ha limitado a ser un banco de segundo piso. Desde hace muchos aos ha englobado su tarea de intermediacin financiera en un objetivo ms amplio: brindar genuinas y prcticas soluciones de negocios y proponer alternativas de desarrollo para el campo. De ah que el capital humano acumulado en FIRA a travs de muchos aos de trabajo dedicado y responsable sea hoy en da su principal activo. A lo largo de su historia FIRA ha ido adaptndose oportunamente a la creciente complejidad que plantean el desarrollo del campo y el impulso a su productividad. Por ello, tiene un largo catlogo de historias de xito. Historias concretas, tangibles y aleccionadoras. A sus programas de crdito  sea en la modalidad de descuento o de prstamo a travs de intermediarios financieros-, FIRA sum desde un principio programas de garanta, as como apoyos tecnolgicos. Ms tarde, estableci programas especiales, en funcin de necesidades especficas de regiones climticas, de productos agropecuarios con caractersticas peculiares, o de los plazos de maduracin de determinados proyectos. En muchos casos, como ustedes saben, estos programas se han desarrollado 6 con la SAGARPA y en otros casos a la par de otras instituciones de banca de fomento, como Financiera Rural. Como un escaln adicional y cada vez ms necesario en esta arquitectura de servicios de intermediacin financiera y asistencia tcnica, FIRA tiene un programa de cobertura de precios diseado con reglas sencillas y bajo tres principios bsicos: sustento tcnico, viabilidad operativa y total transparencia. El programa de cobertura de precios permite al productor fijar el precio de su cosecha en las condiciones del mercado del momento en que se realiza la cobertura. Especficamente, otorga el derecho de venta o de compra a un determinado precio por un volumen determinado a cambio de una prima accesible. Esto, desde luego, proporciona la ansiada certidumbre tanto al acreditado como al intermediario financiero justo ante el escenario de una persistente volatilidad de los precios agropecuarios. En el caso de FIRA el programa est enfocado a los ms pequeos productores que son aquellos que usualmente encuentran barreras infranqueables para acceder a esquemas de cobertura de precios. Por otra parte, el Banco de Mxico apoya de forma permanente a FIRA en el diseo de las polticas pblicas destinadas a mejorar los canales y la infraestructura de acopio, almacenamiento y 7 comercializacin de los productos. Estas polticas no slo contribuyen a reducir la volatilidad de los precios de los productos agropecuarios, sino que mejoran la competitividad del sector agroalimentario. Al generar una mayor confianza en los participantes de los mercados agropecuarios y en los intermediarios que financian estas actividades, se induce que el crdito al sector se eleve y se otorgue en mejores condiciones para los productores. El desafo de potenciar cada vez ms el desarrollo del sector agropecuario mediante mejores polticas pblicas es inmenso y requiere de la participacin activa de autoridades e intermediarios financieros, de los gobiernos, de los legisladores y, obviamente, de los productores y comercializadores de los bienes agropecuarios. Especficamente, la volatilidad de los precios agropecuarios debemos enfrentarla con soluciones creativas sustentadas en cuatro premisas que considero claves: primera, la informacin y la transparencia son cruciales para disminuir la incertidumbre y, con ello, atenuar la volatilidad de los precios. Segundo, una mayor competencia en los mercados abatiendo todo tipo de barreras de entrada, de forma que tengamos cada vez ms 8 participantes y una mayor oferta de bienes agropecuarios en beneficio de todos nosotros. Tercero, un constante empeo por incrementar la productividad agropecuaria mediante la difusin y el uso de la mejor tecnologa disponible y a travs de la asistencia tcnica; me parece que en este sentido la tarea de FIRA ha sido ejemplar a lo largo de su historia. Y cuarto, aprovechar y desarrollar en beneficio de un mejor funcionamiento de los mercados, todo el potencial de la intermediacin financiera, para desarrollar productos de crdito y de cobertura innovadores, as como nuevos mercados financieros especficos. En este sentido, debemos leer bien la experiencia de la reciente crisis financiera global: hubo claramente omisiones y fallas de la regulacin financiera que propiciaron la crisis, pero sera un terrible error caer en el extremo contrario y asfixiar a los mercados con controles excesivos y con un cmulo de prohibiciones. Ejemplos de este balance virtuoso que debe tener la regulacin financiera, entre los dos extremos, son los programas de cobertura de precios de FIRA que ya coment o la nueva regulacin del Banco de Mxico ampliando a bienes agropecuarios la opcin de ser usados como productos subyacentes en contratos de derivados que benefician a 9 productores, a intermediarios y, a la postre, a millones de consumidores a travs de mejores precios, ms calidad y mayor abasto de productos agropecuarios. Muchas gracias. 10

Title: Signing of the decree for the creation of the Financial System Stability Council
text: REMARKS BY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, DR. AGUSTIN CARSTENS, ON THE OCCASION OF THE SIGNING OF THE DECREE FOR THE CREATION OF THE STABILITY COUNCIL OF THE FINANCIAL SYSTEM Mexico, Federal District, July 28, 2010  Mr. President of the Republic, Mr. Felipe Calderon Hinojosa  Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit, Maestro Ernesto Cordero Arroyo  Mr. President of the Mexican Association of Banks, Engineer Ignacio Deschamps Gonzalez  Ladies and gentlemen members of the Presidium,  Ladies and gentlemen, Since the beginning of 2008, the world economy has been afflicted by an unprecedented international financial crisis that caused a collapse in economic activity, employment and the volume of foreign trade and that, with varying intensity, affected practically all the countries of the world. Financial crises - unlike others such as exchange rate, balance of payments or fiscal crises - are 1 particularly pernicious, because they usually produce sequelae that take a long time to overcome completely. This happens because, after all, financial crises reflect a situation of unsustainable over-indebtedness in one or more sectors of the economy. Resolving this over-indebtedness, as well as the allocation of the losses that result from this process, usually generates great complications in political, social and economic terms. These include serious problems of equity in the population, since costs can be unfairly transferred from one sector to another and from one generation to the next. More than two years after the beginning of the crisis, it can be said that Mexico has had the capacity and strength to adequately face this cataclysm that came to us from abroad. There is no doubt that this phenomenon has temporarily affected the country's growth dynamics and the 2 job creation, but thanks to the macroeconomic strength we had at the beginning of the crisis and the timely measures adopted by the Federal Government and the Bank of Mexico, our financial system was practically unaffected. This is very important because now we do not require a sanitation of the system as it happens in other countries. This indispensable sanitation will be a drag on the process of recovery of productive activity and employment in these economies. In our case, the national financial system, rather than representing a burden, has been emerging as one of the elements that could accelerate growth and employment. The fact that Mexico has been able to navigate this difficult environment generated by the international financial crisis does not exempt us from drawing useful lessons that will help us to further strengthen the strength of our system. 3 One of the great lessons derived from the recent international crisis, among others, is that if there had been no weakness in financial regulation and supervision in some countries, and if there had been no lack of coordination mechanisms between the different authorities, the crisis could have been avoided. Even if it had arisen, it would have been addressed and resolved with greater opportunity and effectiveness. A peculiarity of this global crisis was the sudden appearance of severe discontinuities in financial flows. These ruptures, unlike other crises, were not preceded by severe alterations in price indices or by inflationary spikes in the main industrial economies. However, such shocks were clearly the result of inappropriate credit expansion; expansion that the central banks of these countries could not neutralize or combat in a timely manner, in 4 largely because it did not have a clear reflection or correlate in the price indices that were commonly used to detect inflationary pressures. But also because the prudential framework in force until before the crisis did not serve to detect this risk in a timely manner and prevent it. Thus, the real great challenge that the global crisis has left central banks is to broaden their perspective to also include the preservation of the country's financial stability, understood in a broad sense. Preserving financial stability is not an objective unrelated to that of combating inflation, but closely related to it. Both responsibilities support each other. Just as inflation has a clear corrosive effect on the wealth of families and nations, so financial instability cancels out sources of wealth creation. In both cases, instability - whether price or financial - is an insurmountable obstacle. 5 to achieve sustained economic growth. Even financial instability sooner or later can lead to a problem of higher inflation, and vice versa. Of course, the pursuit of financial stability cannot and should not be the sole function of the central bank, but also of the tax authorities, regulatory commissions and savings protection institutes. Precisely, meeting the challenge of ensuring financial stability requires great collaboration and cooperation between the different authorities and regulators in the country. In this regard, I welcome the initiative of the President of the Republic to create by decree the Financial System Stability Council, which will operate as a collegiate body headed by the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and formed by the Supervisory Commissions, the IPAB and the Bank of Mexico. 6 Mr President, I thank the Central Institute for the invitation extended to us, respectful of our autonomy, to join the Council. An invitation that we gladly accept, because we appreciate the great value of formalizing a space for coordination and dialogue between the different financial authorities, which, incidentally, will at all times preserve their powers and powers of law. The creation of the Financial System Stability Council leads Mexico to adopt international best practices, which is important in itself, but is even more important because, through the Council, the possibility of a financial crisis is reduced and the possibilities for more accelerated economic development are expanded. vigorous and sustainable for Mexico. Thanks a lot. 7

Title: Announcement of the circulation of the new 100 peso banknote
text: Message from Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, governor of the Bank of Mexico, on the occasion of the announcement of the circulation of the new 100 peso note. Mexico City, November 12, 2020 Dear Deputy Governor and Esteemed Deputy Governors of the Bank of Mexico; Mtra. Carmen Beatriz Lopez-Portillo Romano, rector of the University of the Cloister of Sor Juana; Representatives of the media; Comrades of the Bank of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen: On behalf of the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, I am pleased to welcome you to this ceremony to put into circulation the 100 peso banknote, the third denomination of the new family of Mexican banknotes. It is a privilege to meet today in the magnificent Ex Convento de San Jeronimo, whose construction dates from the sixteenth century and which was the home of Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz for much of her life. I thank the authorities of the University of the Cloister of Sor Juana for allowing us to announce the issuance of the new ticket in this space, precisely on the day on which the anniversary of the birth of this great writer is commemorated, which gives even greater emphasis to this act. 1 The Bank of Mexico, like most of the world's central banks, has the priority objective of providing the economy with national currency and preserving its purchasing power. The successful issuance and circulation of fiat money depends on the population having full confidence that that currency will effectively function as a means of payment, unit of account and store of value. Therefore, it is essential that the issuer of national currency, the central bank, has clear legal mandates and objectives, which allow it to concentrate on combating the cause that most affects the public's confidence in money, inflation. This is necessary in order to prevent the central bank's powers to issue primary money from being used to expand short-term spending capacity, leading to inflationary processes that erode the purchasing power of the currency. Throughout the twentieth century, in the world and in Mexico, there were numerous cases in which inflation seriously affected confidence. 2 in money, with dramatic consequences on economic activity and social welfare. This consolidated, in the last decades of the last century, the international consensus around the importance of central banks being focused on ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the currency they provide. In line with this consensus, a large number of nations entrusted their central banks with the priority objective of pursuing price stability and gave them autonomy to achieve that objective. In the case of our country, more than 25 years ago the Constituent Assembly decided to grant autonomy to the Bank of Mexico to achieve its main objective of maintaining price stability and, with it, preserving the purchasing power of the national currency. The purposes of the Bank of Mexico are also to promote the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of the payment system. From its autonomy, the Bank of Mexico has managed to consolidate public confidence in the national currency and, so far in the twenty-first century, we have had low inflations, and in recent years 3 around the permanent target of 3%. Thus, in the last two decades we have had one of the longest periods of price stability in our history as an independent nation. As a supplier of the national currency, the law empowers the Bank of Mexico to determine the design and characteristics of paper money. This, in order to provide Mexicans with effective and secure means of payment. In August 2018, the Bank of Mexico presented a new family of banknotes, of which those corresponding to the denominations of 500 and 200 pesos have already been issued. This family is characterized by modern, robust and easy-to-use security elements, as well as more durable materials and a unique graphic identity that reflects the historical, natural and cultural wealth of our country. To develop this new family of banknotes, whose planning began more than 7 years ago, it has had the invaluable collaboration of renowned academic institutions and national research centers. In particular, an in-depth study of the 4 thematic motifs of greater identity and meaning for Mexicans. From this exercise, the historical processes and ecosystems with their flora and fauna were selected, which are being reflected in each of the banknotes that make up the new family and that allow us to take a tour of the coordinates of time and space of our country. I would like to acknowledge the institutions that generously supported us in this work:  The Mexican Academy of History,  The Mexican Academy of Language,  The National Commission of Protected Natural Areas,  The National Commission for the Knowledge and Use of the Biodiversity (CONABIO),  The National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH),  The National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI),  The National Autonomous University of Mexico, through its various study centres, 5  The Center for Research and Higher Studies in Social Anthropology (CIESAS) of the National Council of Science and Technology (CONACyT),  The College of Mexico,  The College of San Ildefonso,  The National College,  The Ministry of Culture of the Government of Mexico,  The University of the Cloister of Sor Juana,  The National Institute of Historical Studies of the Revolutions of Mexico (INEHRM), and  The Mexican Society of Authors of the Plastic Arts. The new 100 peso note is predominantly red, printed in polymer, has a vertical format and unique security features. On its obverse, it alludes to the historical process of the Colony in Mexico, a period that covers three centuries of history, in which the fusion of two cultures took place and the emergence of a complex social, political, economic and religious structure, and of an enormous cultural wealth. 6 During the Colony, architecture, sculpture, painting, music, literature and other arts flourished, which were carefully practiced by distinguished New Hispanic artists. Among them, Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz stands out, who is represented on the obverse of the banknote. Her figure is prominent for being a scholarly and combative writer, who fought to overcome the obstacles that limited women's access to culture and who managed to become one of the maximum protagonists of the Latin American letters of the seventeenth century. From her earliest childhood, Sor Juana showed an unusual passion for knowledge. In the autobiographical sketches, contained in her famous Response to Sister Filotea de la Cruz, the writer points out that she learned to read at the age of three and that, when she was six, she begged her mother to take her to university. He also recounts the rigid self-discipline with which he forced himself to learn the subjects he studied, on his own, in his grandfather's library.1 1 De la Cruz, Sister Juan Ines, "Respuesta a Sor Filotea de la Cruz" in Obras completas, 16th ed., Mexico, Porrua, 2018, pp. 827-848. 7 Due to the conventions of the time, Sor Juana could not fulfill her aspiration to study at a university; however, her passion and self-taught rigor put her at the height of the greatest minds of her time. When, as a teenager, she entered the viceregal court, she was already known as a young prodigy. As Amado Nervo points out: "There, he soon captivated all hearts, won all the votes, chained all the admirations. For this he had two invincible ways: the goodness of his character, sweet and kind, and his amazing wisdom and discretion."2 Sor Juana cultivated the most varied literary forms of her time, from the philosophical poem, such as her famous "Primero sueno", to her popular carols, passing through the sacramental cars, the lyric of loving tone or numerous compositions of occasion. With Sor Juana, Baroque poetry reached one of its highest peaks and, not in vain, came to be known as the "Tenth Muse". Ernesto de la Pena says: "He deserves this title for the enormous, very high quality of his poetry and, also, for the universality 2 Nervo, Amado, Juana de Asbaje, Madrid, 1910, p. 28. Available in: file:///C:/Users/Dell/AppData/Local/Temp/juana-de-asbaje-contribucion-al-centenariode-la-independencia-de-mexico--0.pdf. 8 of her knowledge".3 Thus, with great pride, we can say that it was a Mexican writer who made the Spanish language sing and think simultaneously in its Golden Age. It accompanies the effigy of Sor Juana, the central courtyard of the Old College of San Ildefonso, located in the Historic Center of Mexico City, one of the most important educational institutions in New Spain and an example of the architectural heritage of the colonial period. Its origin goes back to the educational work of the Jesuits in the capital of New Spain, which marked their vocation, as later it was the headquarters of the National Preparatory School and place where the National Autonomous University of Mexico was inaugurated in 1910. The back of the note is dedicated to the ecosystem of temperate forests, one of the most important in Mexico, which is populated mostly by pines, oaks, oyameles and other species of trees that integrate imposing and green landscapes. This ecosystem makes up about 16% of the Mexican territory and has a significant contribution to the megadiversity that 3De la Pena, Ernesto, "Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz, 3" in Al hilo del tiempo (radio program), available at: . 9 characterizes our country, as it has 50% of the species of pines in the world and about 33% of the oaks. To allude to the temperate forests, the banknote represents the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve, located east of the state of Michoacan and west of the State of Mexico. This Reserve was listed in 2008 as a natural asset on the UNESCO World Heritage List. This region is the destination of the wonderful migration of the monarch butterfly, which every autumn undertakes a long journey from southern Canada and the north of the United States to reach our country. In this ideal place, the butterfly nests and dyes the trees of the forests orange until, at the end of March, it undertakes the journey back to its place of origin. On the banknote, the composition is complemented by the milkweed flower, on whose leaves the eggs of the monarch butterfly are deposited and after four to eight days tiny caterpillars with white, black and yellow stripes are born that feed on the same flower, which is also the food of adult butterflies. 10 In short, this banknote alludes to figures and cultural venues, as well as landscapes, which are deeply precious and endearing. For the reasons of its design, as well as for its improved security and durability features, the new 100 peso bill is not only a better means of payment, it is also a sample of our cultural and natural wealth that fills us with pride. For all this, I reiterate my deepest gratitude to all those who, despite the unprecedented challenges we have faced, made it possible for the third banknote of the new family to be presented to the public today. Thank you for helping us to put in the hands of Mexicans this new banknote that, like others manufactured in our country, aspires to be as useful and safe as it is beautiful. Thanks a lot. 11
text_original: Mensaje del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, gobernador del Banco de Mxico, con motivo del anuncio de la puesta en circulacin del nuevo billete de 100 pesos. Ciudad de Mxico, 12 de noviembre de 2020 Estimada subgobernadora y estimados subgobernadores del Banco de Mxico; Mtra. Carmen Beatriz Lpez-Portillo Romano, rectora de la Universidad del Claustro de Sor Juana; Representantes de los medios de comunicacin; Compaeras y compaeros del Banco de Mxico; Seoras y seores: A nombre de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de Mxico, me complace darles la bienvenida a esta ceremonia para poner en circulacin el billete de 100 pesos, tercera denominacin de la nueva familia de billetes mexicanos. Es un privilegio encontrarnos el da de hoy en el magnfico Ex Convento de San Jernimo, cuya construccin data del siglo XVI y que fue el hogar de Sor Juana Ins de la Cruz durante gran parte de su vida. Agradezco a las autoridades de la Universidad del Claustro de Sor Juana por permitirnos anunciar la emisin del nuevo billete en este espacio, precisamente el da en que se conmemora el aniversario del natalicio de esta gran escritora, lo que brinda an mayor realce a este acto. 1 *** El Banco de Mxico, como la mayora de los bancos centrales del mundo, tiene el objetivo prioritario de proveer a la economa de moneda nacional y preservar su poder adquisitivo. La emisin y circulacin exitosa del dinero fiduciario depende de que la poblacin tenga plena confianza en que esa moneda funcionar efectivamente como medio de pago, unidad de cuenta y depsito de valor. Por eso, es fundamental que el emisor de moneda nacional, el banco central, cuente con mandatos legales y objetivos claros, que le permitan concentrarse en combatir la causa que ms afecta la confianza del pblico en el dinero, la inflacin. Esto es necesario a fin de evitar que las facultades del banco central para emitir dinero primario pueden ser utilizadas para expandir la capacidad de gasto de corto plazo, lo que propicia procesos inflacionarios que erosionan el poder adquisitivo de la moneda. A lo largo del siglo XX, en el mundo y en Mxico, se presentaron numerosos casos en los que la inflacin afect gravemente la confianza 2 en el dinero, con dramticas consecuencias sobre la actividad econmica y el bienestar social. Ello consolid, en las ltimas dcadas del siglo pasado, el consenso internacional en torno a la importancia de que los bancos centrales estuvieran concentrados en procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda que proveen. En concordancia con este consenso, un gran nmero de naciones encomend a sus bancos centrales el objetivo prioritario de procurar la estabilidad de precios y les brind autonoma para lograr dicho objetivo. En el caso de nuestro pas, hace ms de 25 aos el Constituyente determin otorgarle autonoma al Banco de Mxico para alcanzar su objetivo principal de mantener la estabilidad de precios y, con ello, preservar el poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. Tambin constituyen finalidades del Banco de Mxico promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. A partir de su autonoma, el Banco de Mxico ha logrado consolidar la confianza del pblico en la moneda nacional y, en lo que va del siglo XXI, hemos tenido inflaciones bajas, y en los ltimos aos 3 alrededor de la meta permanente de 3%. As, en las ltimas dos dcadas hemos tenido uno de los periodos ms prolongados de estabilidad de precios en nuestra historia como nacin independiente. *** Como proveedor de la moneda nacional, la ley faculta al Banco de Mxico para determinar el diseo y las caractersticas del papel moneda. Ello, a fin de proveer a los mexicanos de medios de pago eficaces y seguros. En agosto de 2018 el Banco de Mxico hizo la presentacin de una nueva familia de billetes, de la cual se han emitido ya los correspondientes a las denominaciones de 500 y 200 pesos. Esta familia se caracteriza por tener elementos de seguridad modernos, robustos y de uso sencillo, as como materiales ms duraderos y una identidad grfica nica que refleja la riqueza histrica, natural y cultural de nuestro pas. Para elaborar esta nueva familia de billetes, cuya planeacin inici hace ms de 7 aos, se ha contado con la invaluable colaboracin de reconocidas instituciones acadmicas y centros de investigacin nacionales. En particular, se llev a cabo un profundo estudio de los 4 motivos temticos de mayor identidad y significado para los mexicanos. A partir de este ejercicio, se seleccionaron los procesos histricos y los ecosistemas con su flora y fauna, que estn siendo plasmados en cada uno de los billetes que conforman la nueva familia y que nos permiten hacer un recorrido por las coordenadas del tiempo y el espacio de nuestro pas. Quiero reconocer a las instituciones que generosamente nos apoyaron en esta labor:  La Academia Mexicana de la Historia,  La Academia Mexicana de la Lengua,  La Comisin Nacional de reas Naturales Protegidas,  La Comisin Nacional para el Conocimiento y Uso de la Biodiversidad (CONABIO),  El Instituto Nacional de Antropologa e Historia (INAH),  El Instituto Nacional de Estadstica y Geografa (INEGI),  La Universidad Nacional Autnoma de Mxico, a travs de sus diversos centros de estudio, 5  El Centro de Investigaciones y Estudios Superiores en Antropologa Social (CIESAS) del Consejo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnologa (CONACyT),  El Colegio de Mxico,  El Colegio de San Ildefonso,  El Colegio Nacional,  La Secretara de Cultura del Gobierno de Mxico,  La Universidad del Claustro de Sor Juana,  El Instituto Nacional de Estudios Histricos de las Revoluciones de Mxico (INEHRM), y  La Sociedad Mexicana de Autores de las Artes Plsticas. El nuevo billete de 100 pesos es de color predominantemente rojo, est impreso en polmero, tiene formato vertical y elementos de seguridad nicos. En su anverso, alude al proceso histrico de la Colonia en Mxico, perodo que abarca tres siglos de historia, en el que tuvo lugar la fusin de dos culturas y el surgimiento de una compleja estructura social, poltica, econmica y religiosa, y de una enorme riqueza cultural. 6 Durante la Colonia florecieron la arquitectura, la escultura, la pintura, la msica, la literatura y otras artes, que fueron practicadas con esmero por distinguidos artistas novohispanos. Entre ellos destaca Sor Juana Ins de la Cruz, a quien se representa en el anverso del billete. Su figura es prominente por ser una escritora erudita y combativa, que luch por superar los obstculos que limitaban el acceso de las mujeres a la cultura y que logr convertirse en una de las mximas protagonistas de las letras hispanoamericanas del siglo XVII. Desde su ms temprana infancia, Sor Juana mostr una inusual pasin por el conocimiento. En los esbozos autobiogrficos, contenidos en su famosa Respuesta a Sor Filotea de la Cruz, la escritora seala que aprendi a leer a los tres aos y que, teniendo seis, le suplic a su madre llevarla a la universidad. Tambin relata la rgida autodisciplina con la que se obligaba a aprender las materias que estudiaba, por su cuenta, en la biblioteca de su abuelo.1 1 De la Cruz, Sor Juan Ins, Respuesta a Sor Filotea de la Cruz en Obras completas, 16va ed., Mxico, Porra, 2018, pp. 827-848. 7 Por los convencionalismos de la poca, Sor Juana no pudo cumplir su aspiracin de estudiar en una universidad; sin embargo, su pasin y rigor autodidacta la pusieron a la altura de las mayores mentes de su tiempo. Cuando, apenas adolescente, ingres a la corte virreinal, ya era conocida como una joven prodigio. Como seala Amado Nervo: All, pronto cautiv todos los corazones, se granje todos los sufragios, encaden las admiraciones todas. Para ello tena dos arbitrios invencibles: la bondad de su carcter, dulce y amable, y su sorprendente sabidura y discrecin.2 Sor Juana cultiv las ms variadas formas literarias de su tiempo, desde el poema filosfico, como su clebre Primero sueo, hasta sus populares villancicos, pasando por los autos sacramentales, la lrica de tono amoroso o numerosas composiciones de ocasin. Con Sor Juana, la poesa barroca alcanz una de sus ms altas cumbres y, no en balde, lleg a ser conocida como la Dcima Musa. Dice, al respecto, Ernesto de la Pea: Merece este ttulo por la enorme, altsima calidad de su poesa y, tambin, por la universalidad 2 Nervo, Amado, Juana de Asbaje, Madrid, 1910, p. 28. Disponible en: file:///C:/Users/Dell/AppData/Local/Temp/juana-de-asbaje-contribucion-al-centenariode-la-independencia-de-mexico--0.pdf. 8 de su conocimiento.3 As, con gran orgullo, podemos decir que fue una escritora mexicana la que hizo cantar y pensar simultneamente a la lengua espaola en su Siglo de Oro. Acompaa a la efigie de Sor Juana, el patio central del Antiguo Colegio de San Ildefonso, ubicado en el Centro Histrico de la Ciudad de Mxico, una de las instituciones educativas ms importantes de la Nueva Espaa y ejemplo de la herencia arquitectnica del periodo colonial. Su origen se remonta a la labor educativa de los jesuitas en la capital novohispana, que marc su vocacin, pues posteriormente fue sede de la Escuela Nacional Preparatoria y lugar donde se inaugur la Universidad Nacional Autnoma de Mxico en 1910. El reverso del billete se dedica al ecosistema de bosques templados, uno de los ms importantes en Mxico, el cual est poblado mayormente por pinos, encinos, oyameles y otras especies de rboles que integran imponentes y verdes paisajes. Este ecosistema conforma alrededor del 16% del territorio mexicano y tiene una aportacin significativa a la megadiversidad que 3De la Pea, Ernesto, Sor Juana Ins de la Cruz, 3 en Al hilo del tiempo (programa de radio), disponible en: https://youtu.be/IrkyYyVECgM. 9 caracteriza a nuestro pas, pues posee el 50% de las especies de pinos del mundo y cerca del 33% de los encinos. Para hacer alusin a los bosques templados, en el billete se representa la Reserva de la Bisfera Mariposa Monarca, ubicada al oriente del estado de Michoacn y al poniente del Estado de Mxico. Esta Reserva fue catalogada en 2008 como bien natural en la Lista del Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO. Esta regin es el destino de la maravillosa migracin de la mariposa monarca, la cual cada otoo emprende un largo viaje desde el sur de Canad y el norte de Estados Unidos hasta llegar a nuestro pas. En este sitio idneo, la mariposa anida y tie los rboles de los bosques de color naranja hasta que, a finales de marzo, emprende el viaje de retorno a su lugar de origen. En el billete, complementa la composicin la flor de algodoncillo, en cuyas hojas son depositados los huevos de la mariposa monarca y despus de cuatro a ocho das nacen unas diminutas orugas con rayas blancas, negras y amarillas que se alimentan de la misma flor, que es tambin el alimento de las mariposas adultas. 10 *** En suma, este billete alude a figuras y recintos culturales, as como a paisajes, que resultan profundamente preciados y entraables. Por los motivos de su diseo, as como por sus caractersticas de seguridad y durabilidad mejoradas, el nuevo billete de 100 pesos no slo es un mejor medio de pago, tambin es una muestra de nuestra riqueza cultural y natural que nos llena de orgullo. Por todo ello, reitero mi ms profundo agradecimiento a todos quienes, a pesar de los retos inditos que hemos enfrentado, hicieron posible que hoy se presente al pblico el tercer billete de la nueva familia. Gracias por ayudarnos a poner en manos de los mexicanos este nuevo billete que, al igual que otros fabricados en nuestro pas, aspira a ser tan til y seguro como bello. Muchas gracias. 11

Title: Inauguration of the numismatic exhibition: A peso per kilo. Supply, market and currency in Mexico (XVI to XX centuries)
text: March 11, 2014 Words of the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, in the framework of the inauguration of the numismatic exhibition "A peso el kilo. Supply, market and currency in Mexico (XVI to XX centuries)" that will be exhibited in the Interactive Museum of Economy-MIDE.  Alberto Gomez Alcala, Executive Director of Economic Studies and Communication of Grupo Financiero Banamex and Executive President of the Association of Banks of Mexico,  Mr. Bruno Newman, President of the Board of Trustees and Founder of the "Museum of the Object of the Object" (MODO),  Silvia Singer Sochet, General Director of the "Interactive Museum of Economics" (MIDE),  Distinguished guests,  Ladies and gentlemen. Good morning! Thank you for joining us and welcome to the Interactive Museum of Economics. Today we present the exhibition of a sample of the extensive numismatic collection of the Bank of Mexico, which is the result of a joint effort between MIDE, MODO and the Central Bank itself. As you will have noticed both the acronyms of the respective participating museums (the MIDE and the MODO), and the full name of the latter museum, Museum of the Object of the Object 1 and the very name of the exhibition that we inaugurate today, which is "A peso el kilo, oferta, mercado y moneda en Mexico, de los siglos XVI al XX", lend themselves to making ingenious puns that, hopefully, are memorable and contribute to this exhibition being very visited and obtaining a great diffusion. It's worth it, really. With the minting of the first Mexican coins during the spring of 1536, as arranged by Queen Juana and her coadjutor King Carlos I, the numismatic history of Mexico began. Thanks to this, there are now almost five centuries of monetary issuance documented by the Numismatic Collection of the Bank of Mexico, which is integrated today by about 60 thousand pieces between coins, banknotes and medals, from different eras of our history. In this collection there are viceregal pieces, such as the coins of Carlos and Juana, which were the first minted in Mexico; the machines made manually, with the hammer blow, and of crude appearance, despite which they enjoyed full acceptance in much of the world; and the 2 round pieces stamped in ruffle press such as the beautiful and baroque columnariums, the so-called gold peluconas and the neoclassical pieces of silver bust. Of the War of Independence there is a great variety of copies manufactured in the royalist provisional mints and the insurgent coinages of the Junta de Zitacuaro and General Morelos, as well as numerous stamps and countermarks of the time. From independent Mexico and its difficult gestation period, in this collection there are coins and banknotes of the First Empire and the nascent Mexican Republic. From this same period, in which the country was torn between federalism and centralism, and suffered foreign invasions, there are eighth coins of gold, silver and copper from the mint of Mexico and also from the thirteen foreign houses that operated throughout the nineteenth century in different parts of our territory. The decimal coin, whose minting began in 1863 inspired by liberal ideals, is documented both with pieces of the Second Empire and with the so-called republican balance weights. For its part, the Porfirian era is represented by the large issuance of banknotes from private banks and, of course, 3 with the currency born as a result of the monetary reform of 1905, motivated by the volatility of the value of silver in the world market in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The numerous issues of the Mexican Revolution are also an important part of this collection in which we find villista, Zapatista and Oaxacan coins, and of course the famous and justly despised bilimbiques that in the dark days of the revolutionary struggle proliferated throughout the national territory. Precisely the disorder and the cauda of economic evils that led to the multiple and even capricious issuance of banknotes at that time was an experience that influenced, without a doubt, the spirit of the Constituents of 1917 to establish in our Magna Carta the need to create a Single Bank of Issuance, which would end once and for all with the plural and disorderly proliferation of banknotes to be used as means of payment and allow for the need to create a Single Bank of Issuance, which would end once and for all with the plural and disorderly proliferation of banknotes to be used as means of payment and allow Mexico has a single bank responsible for the issuance of a single monetary unit of legal tender throughout the territory. All this would culminate in 1925 with the foundation of the Bank of Mexico, the Central Bank of the Mexican State and the only issuer of legal tender and daily use in our country. 4 Already in this contemporary era, the Bank of Mexico is present in this exhibition, first with the banknotes that were printed in New York by the American Bank Note Company, and later with the banknotes produced entirely in Mexico, in the Banknote Factory of the Bank of Mexico inaugurated in 1969. The exhibition, of course, also shows us the richness of the contemporary minting of coins of both current use and commemorative character, made of fine and industrial metals. I cannot fail to mention as an important part of this collection, the Mexican pieces that circulated abroad, from the sixteenth century until the end of the nineteenth century, in places as distant as China, the Philippines, the Caribbean and Central America; as well as in England, Portugal and Oceania where they were stamped with stamps and countermarks that testify to the international course of our silver coin. At the Bank of Mexico we believe that exhibitions like this will encourage the public to reflect on the importance of having a Central Bank dedicated to providing legal tender in the country, and whose priority objective is to ensure that this currency retains its purchasing power to 5 over time. This priority objective established in the Constitution, and which orders us to combat inflation, is crucial for the well-being of all Mexicans and by directing all our efforts to fulfill it we contribute efficiently to the growth and progress of the national economy. To this end, as has been demonstrated in the last 20 years, the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico established in 1993 in the Constitution and which became effective just 20 years ago, in 1994, has been fundamental. So important has been this autonomy - for the fight against inflation - that today we already find remote (and for many even known events only by hearsay) the times when we suffered annual inflations of double digits or more and in which prices in general increased by a fortnight which today would hardly increase in a whole year. While we must recognize the great success of granting full autonomy to the Bank of Mexico as an institution of the Mexican State and the undeniable progress in achieving price stability, we cannot declare ourselves totally satisfied with what has been achieved; we still need to consolidate, as a stable and lasting condition, the goal 6 permanent annual inflation of 3 percent with a range of variation of one percentage point. We are on the right track, as shown by the so-called core inflation that in February was 2.98 percent per year and the decrease in the general inflation rate, after the temporary increase it showed at the beginning of 2014, due to the introduction of new taxes and the increase in urban transport fares in the largest cities of the country. We know that this deviation in the convergent trajectory of the price indices towards the target of the Bank of Mexico will be of a temporary nature, but the Governing Board of the Bank remains vigilant to stop any contagion effects at other prices (that is, the so-called second-order effects) or any pressure on prices coming from the demand side that moves us away from said convergence towards our permanent goal. I return to the central theme of the exhibition that we present today: The exhibition is also an invitation for us to look at the fascinating world of numismatics and the fact that it reflects with more or less fidelity our history. 7 Economic. Thus, the visitor to the exhibition will be able to observe, in the coins, crucial epochs of our past such as that of the Habsburgs or the Bourbons, or, he will glimpse in these pieces the vicissitudes of independent, modern and contemporary Mexico. In short, it is a kind, fun and nostalgic way to delve into numismatics and the economy itself, as is the purpose of MIDE. Therefore, for me it is a source of pride to inaugurate today together with you the exhibition A peso el kilo. Supply, market and currency in Mexico (XVI to XX centuries), the result of the joint effort made by the Interactive Museum of Economy, the Museum of the Object of the Object and the Bank of Mexico. I want to end with my thanks to MIDE for their hospitality, to the Museum of the Object object, for their generous collaboration, and to all the people who participated in this project for their enthusiastic and creative contribution. Thanks a lot. 8
text_original: 11 de marzo de 2014 Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, Agustn Carstens, en el marco de la inauguracin de la muestra numismtica A peso el kilo. Oferta, mercado y moneda en Mxico (siglos XVI a XX) que se exhibir en el Museo Interactivo de Economa-MIDE .  Licenciado Alberto Gmez Alcal, Director Ejecutivo de Estudios Econmicos y Comunicacin de Grupo Financiero Banamex y Presidente Ejecutivo de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico,  Licenciado Bruno Newman, Presidente del Patronato y Fundador del Museo del Objeto del Objeto (MODO),  Licenciada Silvia Singer Sochet, Directora General del Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE),  Distinguidos invitados,  Seoras y seores. Muy buenos das! Gracias por acompaarnos y bienvenidos al Museo Interactivo de Economa. Hoy presentamos la exhibicin de una muestra de la extensa coleccin numismtica del Banco de Mxico, que es resultado de un esfuerzo conjunto entre el MIDE, el MODO y el propio Banco Central. Como habrn notado tanto los acrnimos de los respectivos museos participantes (el MIDE y el MODO), como el nombre completo de este ltimo museo, Museo del Objeto del Objeto 1 y el nombre mismo de la exposicin que hoy inauguramos, que es A peso el kilo, oferta, mercado y moneda en Mxico, de los siglos XVI al XX, se prestan para hacer ingeniosos juegos de palabras que, esperemos, sean memorables y contribuyan a que esta muestra sea muy visitada y obtenga una gran difusin. Vale la pena, en verdad. Con la acuacin de las primeras monedas mexicanas durante la primavera de 1536, conforme a lo dispuesto por la Reina Juana y su coadjutor el Rey Carlos I, se inici la historia numismtica de Mxico. Gracias a ello, ahora son casi cinco siglos de emisin monetaria los que documenta la Coleccin Numismtica del Banco de Mxico, la cual est integrada el da de hoy por cerca de 60 mil piezas entre monedas, billetes y medallas, procedentes de diferentes pocas de nuestra historia. En esta coleccin se cuenta con piezas virreinales, como las monedas de Carlos y Juana, que fueron las primeras acuadas en Mxico; las macuquinas hechas manualmente, a golpe de martillo, y de burdo aspecto, a pesar de lo cual gozaron de plena aceptacin en gran parte del mundo; y las 2 piezas redondas troqueladas en prensa de volante como los hermosos y barrocos columnarios, las llamadas peluconas de oro y las neoclsicas piezas de plata de busto. De la guerra de Independencia se tienen una gran variedad de ejemplares fabricados en las casas de moneda provisionales realistas y las acuaciones insurgentes de la Junta de Zitcuaro y del general Morelos, as como numerosos resellos y contramarcas de la poca. Del Mxico independiente y de su difcil periodo de gestacin, en esta coleccin se dispone de monedas y billetes del Primer Imperio y de la naciente Repblica Mexicana. De este mismo periodo, en el que el pas se debati entre el federalismo y el centralismo, y sufri sendas invasiones extranjeras, se cuenta con monedas octavales de oro, plata y cobre provenientes en la ceca de Mxico y tambin de las trece casas forneas que operaron a lo largo del siglo XIX en distintos puntos de nuestro territorio. La moneda decimal, cuya acuacin inici en 1863 inspirada en los ideales liberales, se documenta tanto con piezas del Segundo Imperio como con los llamados pesos de balanza republicanos. Por su parte, la poca porfiriana se representa con la nutrida emisin de billetes de los bancos privados y, desde luego, 3 con la moneda nacida a raz de la reforma monetaria de 1905, motivada por la volatilidad del valor de la plata en el mercado mundial a finales del siglo XIX y principios del XX. Las numerosas emisiones de la Revolucin Mexicana tambin forman parte importante de este acervo en el que encontramos monedas villistas, zapatistas y oaxaqueas, y desde luego los famosos y justamente menospreciados bilimbiques que en los aciagos das de la lucha revolucionaria proliferaron por todo el territorio nacional. Justamente el desorden y la cauda de males econmicos que acarre la emisin mltiple y hasta caprichosa de billetes en esa poca fue una experiencia que influy, sin duda, en el nimo de los Constituyentes de 1917 para establecer en nuestra Carta Magna la necesidad de crear un Banco nico de Emisin, que terminase de una vez por todas con la plural y desordenada proliferacin de billetes para usarse como medios de pago y permitiese a Mxico contar con un solo Banco responsable de la emisin de una nica unidad monetaria de curso legal en todo el territorio. Todo ello culminara en 1925 con la fundacin del Banco de Mxico, el Banco Central del Estado mexicano y el nico emisor de la moneda de curso legal y de uso cotidiano en nuestro pas. 4 Ya en esta poca contempornea, el Banco de Mxico est presente en esta muestra, primero con los billetes que se impriman en Nueva York por la American Bank Note Company, y ms tarde con los billetes producidos ntegramente en Mxico, en la Fbrica de Billetes del Banco de Mxico inaugurada en 1969. La exhibicin, desde luego, tambin nos muestra la riqueza de la acuacin contempornea de monedas tanto de uso corriente como de carcter conmemorativo, hechas en metales finos e industriales. No puedo dejar de mencionar como parte importante de este acervo, las piezas mexicanas que circularon en el extranjero, desde el siglo XVI y hasta finales del XIX, en lugares tan distantes como China, Filipinas, el Caribe y Centroamrica; as como en Inglaterra, Portugal y Oceana donde se les estamparon resellos y contramarcas que testimonian el curso internacional de nuestra moneda de plata. En el Banco de Mxico creemos que exhibiciones como sta propiciarn en el pblico una reflexin sobre la importancia de contar con un Banco Central dedicado a proveer la moneda de curso legal en el pas, y cuyo objetivo prioritario es procurar que dicha moneda conserve su poder adquisitivo a 5 lo largo del tiempo. Este objetivo prioritario establecido en la Constitucin, y que nos ordena combatir la inflacin, es crucial para el bienestar de todos los mexicanos y al orientar todos nuestros esfuerzos a cumplirlo contribuimos eficientemente al crecimiento y al progreso de la economa nacional. Para ello, como se ha demostrado en los ltimos 20 aos, ha sido fundamental la autonoma del Banco de Mxico establecida en 1993 en la Constitucin y que se hizo vigente justamente hace 20 aos, en 1994. Tan importante ha sido dicha autonoma  para el combate a la inflacin  que hoy ya nos parecen remotas (y para muchos incluso se trata de sucesos conocidos slo de odas) las pocas en que padecimos inflaciones anuales de dos dgitos o ms y en las que los precios en general aumentaban en una quincena lo que hoy difcilmente aumentaran en todo un ao. Si bien debemos reconocer el gran acierto que fue otorgar la autonoma plena al Banco de Mxico como Institucin del Estado mexicano y los innegables avances para lograr la estabilidad de precios, tampoco podemos declararnos totalmente satisfechos con lo alcanzado; an nos falta consolidar, como una condicin estable y duradera, la meta 6 permanente de una inflacin anual de 3 por ciento con un intervalo de variacin de un punto porcentual. Vamos por el camino correcto, como lo muestra la llamada inflacin subyacente que al mes de febrero fue de 2.98 por ciento anual y el descenso de la tasa de inflacin general, tras el temporal aumento que mostr al inicio de 2014, debido a la introduccin de nuevos gravmenes y al incremento de tarifas de transporte urbano en las ciudades ms grandes del pas. Sabemos que esta desviacin en la trayectoria convergente de los ndices de precios hacia la meta del Banco de Mxico ser de carcter temporal, pero la Junta de Gobierno del Banco permanece vigilante para atajar cualquier efecto de contagio a otros precios (es decir, los llamados efectos de segundo orden) o cualquier presin sobre los precios proveniente del lado de la demanda que nos aleje de dicha convergencia hacia nuestra meta permanente. Vuelvo al tema central de la muestra que hoy presentamos: La muestra es tambin una invitacin para que nos asomemos al fascinante mundo de la numismtica y al hecho de que sta refleja con ms o menos fidelidad nuestra historia 7 econmica. As, el visitante a la muestra podr observar, en las monedas, pocas cruciales de nuestro pasado como la de los Habsburgo o la de los Borbn, o bien, vislumbrar en estas piezas las vicisitudes del Mxico independiente, moderno y contemporneo. En fin, es una forma amable, divertida y nostlgica, para adentrarse en la numismtica y en la misma economa, como es la finalidad del MIDE. Por lo anterior, para m es motivo de orgullo inaugurar hoy junto con ustedes la muestra A peso el kilo. Oferta, mercado y moneda en Mxico (siglos XVI a XX), resultado del esfuerzo conjunto realizado por el Museo Interactivo de Economa, el Museo del Objeto del Objeto y el Banco de Mxico. Quiero terminar con mi agradecimiento al MIDE por su hospitalidad, al Museo del Objeto del Objeto, por su generosa colaboracin, y a todas las personas que participaron en este proyecto por su entusiasta y creativa contribucin. Muchas gracias. 8

Title: Importance of central bank autonomy
text: "IMPORTANCE OF CENTRAL BANK AUTONOMY". INTERVENTION OF MR. JAVIER GUZMaN CALAFELL, DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MEXICO, IN THE CHAIR DON HUMBERTO MARTiNEZ DE LEoN OF THE AUTONOMOUS UNIVERSITY OF AGUASCALIENTES. October 2, 2019.1 I am very honored to be with you in this edition of the Don Humberto Martinez de Leon Chair of the Autonomous University of Aguascalientes. I sincerely thank Dr. Francisco Javier Avelar Gonzalez, Rector of this House of Studies, for the invitation to participate as a speaker in this important event. As you know, this year marks the XXV anniversary of the autonomy of the Bank of Mexico. I therefore think it is appropriate to concentrate my intervention on the factors that led this institutional arrangement to acquire a very important role in the world economy, as well as on some of the challenges that are currently being faced. The antecedents of the widespread trend towards granting autonomy to central banks date back to the 1970s and 1980s as a consequence, to a large extent, of two closely related events. On the one hand, a number of countries were experiencing episodes of persistently high inflation, involving significant economic costs. Likewise, during these periods, and partly as a result of the situation described, the academic literature began to pay increasing attention to the solution of the problem of "temporal inconsistency" inherent in monetary policy, that is, the risk that those in charge of its implementation will assign greater importance to it, for example. 1 The opinions and views expressed in this document are the responsibility of the author and do not necessarily represent the institutional position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. 1 political reasons, to the short-term benefits that could be derived from the adoption of expansionary positions, since the corresponding costs would not be evident until later. Proposals to strengthen the autonomy of such institutions emerged, therefore, as a viable alternative to meet such challenges.2 Despite the theoretical arguments and empirical evidence supporting the autonomy of central banks, as well as the consolidation of a widespread view during the nineties and early first decade of this century regarding the importance of such an institutional arrangement for the successful stabilization of inflation, in recent years there have been important questions regarding its benefits. These views originate from a variety of sources, both political and academic, and are present in a large number of economies of varying degrees of development. A first wave of criticism of central bank autonomy stemmed directly from the experience of the Global Financial Crisis, and in particular from the monetary policy response implemented to address it, mainly in the major advanced economies. First, given that the mechanisms that provide autonomy to the monetary authority were designed, in principle, to counteract high and persistent inflation rates, in a context such as that of recent years in which they show resistance to the rise or have even registered readings. 2 Ver, por ejemplo, Kydland, Finn E. y Edward C. Prescott (1977): "Rules Rather than Discretion: The Inconsistency of Optimal Plans", Journal of Political Economy, Vol. 85(3):473-492; y Barro, Robert J. y David B. Gordon (1983): "Rules, Discretion and Reputation in a Model of Monetary Policy", Journal of Monetary Economics, Vol. 12(1):101-121. 2 Some analysts have pointed out that such an institutional arrangement is no longer justifiable. Second, as major central banks were forced to deploy unconventional monetary policy measures (mainly through large-scale purchases of government securities) once benchmark interest rates had fallen to levels around zero, concern arose that such institutions were taking action outside their strict sphere of responsibility. adopting tasks that would correspond to fiscal policy and, in this way, diluting the dividing line between it and monetary policy. For example, when buying government securities, the costs of financing for the public sector are affected to a greater extent than with the traditional management of monetary policy. Thus, spaces are generated for fiscal policy that would not otherwise exist and, simultaneously, decisions on the management of public debt are affected, not only in terms of the amounts, but also with respect to the structure of their maturities. On the other hand, the expansion and subsequent contraction of central banks' balance sheets is subject to potentially significant losses, which could have implications for consolidated public sector finances. Third, also as a direct consequence of the Global Financial Crisis, central banks have placed greater emphasis on other responsibilities, particularly in areas related to financial stability. However, by virtue of the complexity of trying to fulfill a 3 A task in itself that is difficult to define and evaluate, especially in cases where conflicts with the objective of price stability may arise, the congruence between the autonomy of the central bank and its participation in functions related to financial stability has been questioned. At the same time, the desirability of delegating such responsibility to unappointed officials through electoral processes has been questioned. Fourth, its detractors have pointed to the autonomy of the central bank as an obstacle to the coordination of monetary actions with other policies, particularly fiscal, especially during extremely disruptive episodes such as the aforementioned Global Financial Crisis, in which it may be essential to adopt multidimensional approaches to stimulate the economy and help inflation return to a trajectory consistent with the objective. Fifth, the autonomy of central banks has been subject to more rigorous scrutiny by virtue of the potential redistributive effects of some of the unconventional measures, such as quantitative easing, implemented after the crisis. While it is generally recognized that conventional monetary policy, typically implemented through adjustments in reference interest rates, has always had redistributive effects (e.g., between creditors and debtors), the potential magnitude of those stemming from quantitative easing measures has heightened concern about the differentiated effects that active central bank intervention in financial markets may have on specific segments of the financial market. the population. Thus, it has been argued that 4 Decisions of this kind should fall on officials elected through democratic processes and therefore accountable to their voters. In my opinion, these and other arguments in the same sense are hardly justifiable. To begin with, I find it paradoxical to hear this type of questioning of the autonomy of central banks, when there is a widespread opinion that, given the lack of an adequate and timely reaction of fiscal and structural policies, the actions taken on the monetary front became the only viable alternative to the Global Financial Crisis. Rather than focusing on monetary policy, it would be reasonable to expect that attention would have been focused on the inadequate fiscal policy response, as well as the inadequacy - or even absence - of structural reform efforts in many countries. On the other hand, is the autonomy of central banks unnecessary in an environment of low inflation? The answer to this question might be yes, if we were willing to assume that such an environment is a permanent feature of the world economy. However, it is obvious that such an assumption would be extremely risky. On the one hand, the fall in inflation levels that we have witnessed in recent years is, in part, the result of the recessionary effects of one of the most severe global economic crises of modern times. On the other hand, although other factors have contributed to containing upward pressures on prices, their nature is not yet fully understood and, consequently, their potential impact on the future is uncertain. 5 The need for autonomous central banks is even more evident if we consider that, given the criticisms of the quantitative easing measures mentioned above, had they lacked autonomy, it is likely that these central institutes would not have been able to take the necessary action to deal with the crisis. In other words, autonomy is important in situations of both high and low inflation. With regard to the additional objectives and mandates assigned to central banks, although in the strict sense it is true that they may restrict the degrees of freedom with which those institutions formulate monetary policy, it must be considered that, regardless of how narrow the definition of the objective of price stability is, monetary policy has always faced trade-offs which, in general, they have been taken into account. This has been particularly the case for financial stability, as monetary policy is transmitted to the rest of the economy largely through markets and financial institutions. In fact, the current challenge is mainly related to the additional emphasis that has been given to such an objective, as risks to financial stability have always been an important factor in central bank decision-making. With regard to the coordination of monetary and fiscal policies, it should be noted, first of all, that their close interrelationship necessarily implies that the actions implemented on one front will have consequences for the other, and vice versa. Coordination of monetary and fiscal policy actions often brings benefits, as the achievement of the objectives of the former also depends on the latter. Of course, this does not justify the loss of 6 autonomy for the monetary authority. Indeed, the risk of fiscal over monetary policy dominance, a situation that has proven incompatible with price stability in the long run, requires greater autonomy from central banks. Finally, the view that central banks should be less autonomous in light of the redistributive implications of their policy decisions is questionable, since in addition to the fact that there is empirical evidence to suggest that there have been no major changes in the distribution of income as a result of the implementation of quantitative easing measures, 3 this aspect has to be compared with its counterfactual. As already noted, in the absence of autonomy, the actions put in place in the monetary sphere to deal with the crisis would probably not have been implemented, which would have led to even more acute economic problems. Clearly, the segments of the population most affected in circumstances like these are precisely those with the lowest incomes, who have fewer or no options to protect themselves against events of this nature.
