In addition to the arguments against central bank autonomy described above, more recently a second wave of criticism has emerged which, while lacking technical justification and essentially politically motivated, may be even more alarming in view of its wide spread across a variety of economies, both advanced and emerging. 3 Ver, por ejemplo, Ampudia, Miguel et al. (2018): "Monetary Policy and Household Inequality", ECB Working Paper No. 2170, julio. 7 The emergence of this challenge to the current institutional framework has also been nourished by the events arising from the Global Financial Crisis, and has been strongly supported by sectors of the population disappointed with the results of greater economic and financial integration at the global level. The situation is even more worrying in the case of emerging economies, since their institutional frameworks are more fragile and they have fewer tools to withstand such attacks. Undermining the independence of our central banks would be a highly costly mistake for the world economy. The achievement of the primary mandate of these institutions, price stability, would be in jeopardy, since the perception of temporarily inconsistent policies in the monetary field would result, sooner rather than later, in a deanchoring of inflation expectations, carrying the risk of returning results similar to those that prevailed in the seventies and eighties of the last century. Undoubtedly, the arguments in favor of the autonomy of central banks remain valid today: those institutions with a long-term perspective, isolated from political pressures, capable of responding quickly to changing conditions in national and international financial markets, and with sufficient technical competence and credibility to fulfill their mandates, they will be much better prepared to meet the challenges arising from price pressures, whether upward or downward. 8 The autonomy of central banks has been a key factor in containing price changes and stabilizing long-term inflation expectations in many countries, and of paramount importance in overcoming episodes of acute financial difficulties, such as those that occurred a decade ago. So under what logic could the criticisms of recent years of the institutional framework that has made such achievements possible be justified? On the other hand, it is also true that the autonomy of central banks must be accompanied by an adequate scheme of checks and balances. In order to provide such institutions with the legitimacy they require to perform their functions effectively and efficiently, clear and transparent objectives and mandates are necessary, and society at large must have at its disposal the necessary means to hold central banks accountable for their actions and decisions. Therefore, central banks cannot simply ignore the questions about their autonomy that have proliferated in recent years. On the contrary, it is essential to reflect on what additional actions are necessary to allow the public to better understand the role of our central institutes and the importance of autonomy in the fulfillment of the functions assigned to them. While it is the congresses of each country that typically define both the scope of mandates and the mechanisms to ensure the accountability of central banks, these same institutions must ensure that the policies they implement are fully consistent with their mandates, and maintain an ongoing evaluation of the measures they implement. 9 can contribute to improving both their transparency and accountability. In view of the experience of a diversity of economies that have put it into practice, including Mexico, it is clearly clear that the autonomy of the central bank is a critical piece of an institutional scaffolding conducive to stability and, therefore, to lay the foundations for a path of sustained economic growth in the medium and long term. 10
text_original: IMPORTANCIA DE LA AUTONOMA DEL BANCO CENTRAL. INTERVENCIN DEL LIC. JAVIER GUZMN CALAFELL, SUBGOBERNADOR DEL BANCO DE MXICO, EN LA CTEDRA DON HUMBERTO MARTNEZ DE LEN DE LA UNIVERSIDAD AUTNOMA DE AGUASCALIENTES. 2 de octubre de 2019.1 Me siento muy honrado de estar con ustedes en esta edicin de la Ctedra Don Humberto Martnez de Len de la Universidad Autnoma de Aguascalientes. Agradezco sinceramente al Dr. Francisco Javier Avelar Gonzlez, Rector de esta Casa de Estudios, la invitacin a participar como conferencista en este importante evento. Como ustedes saben, este ao se conmemora el XXV aniversario de la autonoma del Banco de Mxico. Por ello, me parece pertinente concentrar mi intervencin en los factores que llevaron a este arreglo institucional a adquirir un papel de gran trascendencia en la economa mundial, as como en algunos de los retos que se estn enfrentado en la actualidad. Los antecedentes de la tendencia generalizada hacia el otorgamiento de autonoma a los bancos centrales se remontan a las dcadas de 1970 y 1980 como consecuencia, en gran medida, de dos eventos estrechamente relacionados. Por una parte, diversos pases estaban experimentando episodios de inflacin persistentemente elevada, lo que implicaba costos econmicos significativos. Asimismo, durante dichos periodos, y en parte como resultado de la situacin descrita, la literatura acadmica comenz a prestar creciente atencin a la solucin del problema de inconsistencia temporal inherente a la poltica monetaria, es decir, el riesgo de que los encargados de su implementacin le asignen una mayor importancia, por 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad del autor y no necesariamente representan la postura institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno. 1 razones polticas, a los beneficios de corto plazo que podran derivarse de la adopcin de posturas expansivas, en virtud de que los costos correspondientes no seran evidentes sino hasta ms adelante. Las propuestas para fortalecer la autonoma de dichas instituciones surgieron, por lo tanto, como una alternativa viable para enfrentar tales desafos.2 A pesar de los argumentos tericos y la evidencia emprica que respaldan la autonoma de los bancos centrales, as como la consolidacin de una opinin generalizada durante los aos noventa y principios de la primera dcada de este siglo respecto de la importancia de dicho arreglo institucional para la exitosa estabilizacin de la inflacin, en aos recientes se han observado cuestionamientos importantes respecto de sus beneficios. Estos puntos de vista se originan de una diversidad de fuentes, tanto del mbito poltico como acadmico, y se encuentran presentes en un amplio nmero de economas de distintos grados de desarrollo. Una primera ola de crticas a la autonoma de los bancos centrales se deriv directamente de la experiencia de la Crisis Financiera Global, y en particular de la respuesta de poltica monetaria implementada para hacerle frente, fundamentalmente en las principales economas avanzadas. En primer lugar, dado que los mecanismos que proveen de autonoma a la autoridad monetaria fueron diseados, en principio, para contrarrestar tasas de inflacin altas y persistentes, en un contexto como el de aos recientes en el que estas muestran resistencia al alza o incluso han registrado lecturas 2 Ver, por ejemplo, Kydland, Finn E. y Edward C. Prescott (1977): Rules Rather than Discretion: The Inconsistency of Optimal Plans, Journal of Political Economy, Vol. 85(3):473-492; y Barro, Robert J. y David B. Gordon (1983): Rules, Discretion and Reputation in a Model of Monetary Policy", Journal of Monetary Economics, Vol. 12(1):101-121. 2 negativas, algunos analistas han sealado que dicho arreglo institucional ya no es justificable. En segundo lugar, al verse los principales bancos centrales obligados a desplegar medidas de poltica monetaria no convencionales (principalmente mediante compras a gran escala de valores gubernamentales) una vez que las tasas de inters de referencia haban descendido a niveles alrededor de cero, surgi la preocupacin de que dichas instituciones estuvieran llevando a cabo acciones fuera de su estricto mbito de responsabilidad, adoptando tareas que le corresponderan a la poltica fiscal y, de esa manera, diluyendo la lnea divisoria entre esta y la poltica monetaria. Por ejemplo, al comprar valores gubernamentales los costos del financiamiento para el sector pblico se afectan en mayor medida que con el manejo tradicional de la poltica monetaria. As, se generan espacios para la poltica fiscal que de otra manera no existiran y, simultneamente, las decisiones sobre el manejo de la deuda pblica se ven afectadas, no solo en trminos de los montos, sino tambin respecto de la estructura de sus vencimientos. Por otro lado, la expansin y posterior contraccin de las hojas de balance de los bancos centrales est sujeta a prdidas potencialmente significativas, lo que podra tener implicaciones para las finanzas del sector pblico consolidado. En tercer lugar, tambin como consecuencia directa de la Crisis Financiera Global, los bancos centrales han puesto un mayor nfasis en otras responsabilidades, sobre todo en reas relacionadas con la estabilidad financiera. Sin embargo, en virtud de la complejidad de tratar de cumplir una 3 tarea en s difcil de definir y evaluar, especialmente en casos en los que pueden presentarse conflictos con el objetivo de estabilidad de precios, se ha cuestionado la congruencia entre la autonoma del banco central y su participacin en funciones relacionadas con la estabilidad financiera. Al mismo tiempo, se ha puesto en duda la conveniencia de delegar tal responsabilidad a funcionarios no designados mediante procesos electorales. En cuarto lugar, sus detractores han sealado a la autonoma de la banca central como un obstculo para la coordinacin de las acciones en materia monetaria con otras polticas, particularmente la fiscal, especialmente durante episodios extremadamente disruptivos como la citada Crisis Financiera Global, en los que puede ser indispensable adoptar enfoques multidimensionales para estimular la economa y coadyuvar a que la inflacin retome una trayectoria congruente con el objetivo. En quinto lugar, la autonoma de los bancos centrales ha estado sometida a un escrutinio ms riguroso en virtud de los posibles efectos redistributivos derivados de algunas de las medidas no convencionales, tales como el relajamiento cuantitativo, implementadas tras la crisis. Aunque en general se reconoce que la poltica monetaria convencional, tpicamente instrumentada mediante ajustes en las tasas de inters de referencia, siempre ha tenido efectos redistributivos (por ejemplo, entre acreedores y deudores), la potencial magnitud de aquellos derivados de las medidas de relajamiento cuantitativo ha incrementado la preocupacin por los efectos diferenciados que la activa intervencin del banco central en los mercados financieros puede tener en segmentos especficos de la poblacin. As, se ha argumentado que 4 decisiones de este tipo deberan recaer en funcionarios elegidos mediante procesos democrticos y, por tanto, obligados a rendir cuentas a sus votantes. En mi opinin, estos y otros argumentos en el mismo sentido son difcilmente justificables. Para empezar, me parece paradjico escuchar este tipo de cuestionamientos a la autonoma de los bancos centrales, cuando existe la opinin generalizada de que, dada la falta de una adecuada y oportuna reaccin de las polticas fiscal y estructural, las acciones tomadas en el frente monetario se convirtieron en la nica alternativa viable ante la Crisis Financiera Global. En lugar de enfocarse en la poltica monetaria, lo razonable sera esperar que la atencin se hubiera concentrado en la inadecuada respuesta de la poltica fiscal, as como en la insuficiencia o incluso la ausencia de esfuerzos de reforma estructural en muchos pases. Por otra parte, es innecesaria la autonoma de los bancos centrales en un entorno de baja inflacin? La respuesta a esta pregunta podra ser afirmativa, si estuviramos dispuestos a suponer que dicho entorno es una caracterstica permanente de la economa mundial. Sin embargo, es obvio que tal supuesto sera sumamente arriesgado. Por un lado, la cada de los niveles de inflacin que hemos presenciado en los ltimos aos es, en parte, resultado de los efectos recesivos de una de las crisis econmicas mundiales ms severas de los tiempos modernos. Por otro lado, aunque otros factores han contribuido a contener las presiones al alza sobre los precios, su naturaleza an no es entendida en su totalidad y, en consecuencia, su impacto potencial en el futuro es incierto. 5 La necesidad de contar con bancos centrales autnomos resulta incluso ms evidente si consideramos que, dadas las crticas a las medidas de relajamiento cuantitativo antes mencionadas, de haber carecido de autonoma, es probable que estos institutos centrales no hubieran podido emprender las acciones necesarias para enfrentar la crisis. En otras palabras, la autonoma es importante en situaciones tanto de alta como de baja inflacin. Con respecto a los objetivos y mandatos adicionales asignados a los bancos centrales, aunque en estricto sentido es cierto que pueden restringir los grados de libertad con que dichas instituciones formulan la poltica monetaria, debe considerarse que, independientemente de qu tan acotada sea la definicin del objetivo de estabilidad de precios, la poltica monetaria siempre ha enfrentado disyuntivas que, en general, se han tomado en cuenta. Este ha sido el caso en particular de la estabilidad financiera, en virtud de que la poltica monetaria se transmite al resto de la economa en buena medida a travs de los mercados e instituciones financieras. De hecho, el desafo actual se relaciona principalmente con el nfasis adicional que se le ha dado a dicho objetivo, ya que los riesgos para la estabilidad financiera siempre han sido un factor importante en la toma de decisiones de los bancos centrales. En cuanto a la coordinacin de las polticas monetaria y fiscal, cabe sealar, ante todo, que su estrecha interrelacin implica forzosamente que las acciones implementadas en un frente tendrn consecuencias para el otro, y viceversa. Por tanto, con frecuencia, la coordinacin de las acciones de poltica monetaria y fiscal acarrea beneficios, ya que la consecucin de los objetivos de la primera tambin depende de la segunda. Desde luego, esto no justifica la prdida de 6 autonoma para la autoridad monetaria. De hecho, el riesgo de dominancia de la poltica fiscal sobre la monetaria, situacin que ha demostrado ser incompatible con la estabilidad de precios en el largo plazo, exige una mayor autonoma de los bancos centrales. Por ltimo, el punto de vista de que los bancos centrales deben ser menos autnomos a la luz de las implicaciones redistributivas de sus decisiones de poltica es cuestionable, ya que adems de que existe evidencia emprica que sugiere que no ha habido cambios importantes en la distribucin del ingreso como resultado de la implementacin de medidas de relajamiento cuantitativo,3 este aspecto tiene que ser comparado con su contrafactual. Como ya se seal, en ausencia de autonoma, las acciones puestas en marcha en el mbito monetario para hacer frente a la crisis probablemente no se habran implementado, lo que habra llevado a problemas econmicos aun ms agudos. Claramente, los segmentos de la poblacin ms afectados en circunstancias como estas son precisamente los de ms bajos ingresos, que tienen menores o nulas opciones para protegerse ante eventos de esta naturaleza. Adems de los argumentos en contra de la autonoma de los bancos centrales arriba descritos, ms recientemente ha surgido una segunda oleada de crticas que, aunque carece de justificacin tcnica y en lo esencial tiene una motivacin poltica, puede ser aun ms alarmante en vista de su amplia difusin en una diversidad de economas, tanto avanzadas como emergentes. 3 Ver, por ejemplo, Ampudia, Miguel et al. (2018): Monetary Policy and Household Inequality, ECB Working Paper No. 2170, julio. 7 El surgimiento de este desafo al marco institucional vigente se ha nutrido tambin de los eventos derivados de la Crisis Financiera Global, y se ha visto fuertemente apoyado por sectores de la poblacin decepcionados con los resultados de la mayor integracin econmica y financiera a nivel global. La situacin es incluso ms preocupante en el caso de las economas emergentes, ya que sus marcos institucionales son ms frgiles y cuentan con menos herramientas para resistir tales embates. Menoscabar la independencia de nuestros bancos centrales sera un error altamente costoso para la economa mundial. La consecucin del mandato primordial de estas instituciones, la estabilidad de precios, peligrara, ya que la percepcin de polticas temporalmente inconsistentes en el mbito monetario resultara, ms temprano que tarde, en un desanclaje de las expectativas de inflacin, conllevando el riesgo de que reaparezcan resultados similares a los que prevalecieron en los aos setenta y ochenta del siglo pasado. Sin duda, los argumentos a favor de la autonoma de los bancos centrales se mantienen vigentes en la actualidad: aquellas instituciones con una perspectiva de largo plazo, aisladas de presiones polticas, capaces de responder rpidamente a condiciones cambiantes en los mercados financieros nacionales e internacionales, y con la competencia tcnica y credibilidad suficientes para cumplir con sus mandatos, estarn mucho mejor preparadas para enfrentar los desafos derivados de las presiones sobre los precios, ya sea al alza o a la baja. 8 La autonoma de los bancos centrales ha sido un factor fundamental para contener las variaciones de precios y estabilizar las expectativas de inflacin de largo plazo en numerosos pases, y de suma importancia para superar episodios de agudas dificultades financieras, como los ocurridos hace una dcada. Entonces, bajo qu lgica podran justificarse las crticas de aos recientes al marco institucional que ha hecho posible tales logros? Por otra parte, tambin es cierto que la autonoma de los bancos centrales debe ir acompaada de un adecuado esquema de pesos y contrapesos. Con el fin de dotar a dichas instituciones de la legitimidad que requieren para realizar sus funciones de manera eficaz y eficiente, es necesario contar con objetivos y mandatos claros y transparentes, y la sociedad en general debe tener a su disposicin los medios necesarios para exigir que los bancos centrales rindan cuentas de sus acciones y decisiones. Por tanto, los bancos centrales no pueden simplemente ignorar los cuestionamientos que sobre su autonoma han proliferado en los ltimos aos. Por el contrario, es indispensable reflexionar sobre qu acciones adicionales son necesarias para permitir que el pblico comprenda mejor cul es el papel de nuestros institutos centrales y la importancia de la autonoma en el cumplimiento de las funciones que les han sido asignadas. Si bien son los congresos de cada pas quienes tpicamente definen tanto el alcance de los mandatos como los mecanismos para garantizar la rendicin de cuentas de los bancos centrales, estas mismas instituciones deben asegurarse de que las polticas que implementen sean plenamente consistentes con sus mandatos, y mantener una evaluacin permanente de las medidas que 9 puedan contribuir a mejorar tanto su transparencia como su rendicin de cuentas. En vista de la experiencia de una diversidad de economas que la han puesto en prctica, incluyendo a Mxico, es a todas luces claro que la autonoma del banco central es una pieza crtica de un andamiaje institucional conducente a la estabilidad y, por tanto, a sentar las bases para una senda de crecimiento econmico sostenido en el mediano y largo plazos. 10

Title: Views and priorities of the G20 presidency on financial regulation
text: Eurofi High Level Seminar 2012 Thursday, March 29 - Gala dinner Keynote Speech of Governor Carstens Views and Priorities of the G20 Presidency on Financial Regulation It is a pleasure to have the opportunity to discuss with you the priorities of the G20 Presidency regarding financial regulation. Before I jump into the subject allow me to put into context the regulatory agenda by commenting on the role the G20 plays in assuring sustainable global growth and financial stability. Although there are some indications that economic activity is on the path to recovery, we have not been able to fully break the adverse feedback loop between low economic growth, unsustainable fiscal positions and the fragility of financial institutions. In advanced economies, there is still great uncertainty regarding the impact on economic activity derived from the adjustment of domestic expenditures to sustainable levels, which makes more urgent the implementation of structural reforms. In fact, growth expectations for 2012 are moderate and downside risks continue to be high. Thus there is no room to be complacent. Given the high degree of interconnection in the world economy, policy actions require cooperation and coordination among authorities from different countries and international institutions in order to be effective. In this context, the G20 is expected to play a key role in enhancing the required measures, agreements and reforms. In fact, this is one of the main elements of our agenda. 1 In particular, we have agreed to enhance monitoring and accountability to ensure that our previous policy commitments can be achieved, including those on fiscal, financial and exchange rate policies. In the context of the Framework for Strong, Sustainable and Balanced Growth we will continue to ensure that developments in the global economy and associated risks are properly assessed, and that corrective policy actions are identified and undertaken. A second fundamental part of the G20 agenda refers to the International Financial Architecture. In the lead-up to the Los Cabos Summit, we are reviewing the options which would allow mobilizing resources for the IMF in a timely manner. At this point let me emphasize that these resources will be available for the whole membership of the IMF and are not earmarked for any particular region. We have given some indications regarding the possible modalities to complement existing IMF resources and will consider the buildup of the European firewalls as an essential element in our deliberations. It is in this context that Mexico has established the strengthening of the financial system as one of its priorities in the G20. We acknowledge that in order to secure a balanced and sustainable growth it is necessary to restore credit flows. We must avert the negative cycle between reduced confidence in sovereign debt, banks deleveraging and weak economic activity. In fact, Mexicos financial regulatory agenda cannot be fully understood without considering the dual objective of achieving financial stability and securing growth. 2 As this years chairs of the G20 we will be moving towards a smooth adoption of the financial regulatory agenda. In an effort led by the FSB, we have already been working very hard on each stream of this broad plan. We have advanced expeditiously on many different fronts of the reform agenda and now we are emphasizing the implementation of our hard reached agreements. We could summarize our priorities in the financial arena as: the timely and consistent implementation of reforms; increasing the resilience of financial institutions; strengthening continuous markets; improving the institutional footing of the Financial Stability Board; and assessing the implications of post-crisis reforms on Emerging Markets and Developing Economies. Now, turning to implementation, we have spent a lot of time designing a regulatory and supervisory framework that provides the proper setting for the efficient and stable functioning of the international financial system. This effort led to several regulatory initiatives, from Basel III to measures to address SIFIs. While supervision and regulation are dynamic endeavors with constant adjustments, there comes a time when all these new initiatives have to be implemented. That time is now. It is fundamental that in all jurisdictions we strive for a rigorous implementation of the new regulation in a timely and consistent manner. Many countries, FSB and G20 members, have acknowledged the importance of this objective and we have committed to pursue its achievement firmly and without hesitation. 3 However, we must recognize that implementation also brings new challenges. For instance, it is important to assess the consistency of national initiatives (like the ones being pursued in the United States, the European Union and Japan) with global standards, like Basel III. The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision is working towards this effort and preliminary findings are expected by the middle of this year. Given the wide range of initiatives and commitments, an important aspect of these global efforts is accountability. In this regard, most countries are cooperating to monitor progress and have regular assessments. One key date for reviewing this progress will be at the G20 Leaders Summit in Los Cabos, Mexico in June 2012. While authorities and market participants may not always agree on the way forward, I think we all share one common goal, which is building resilient financial institutions. To this end, we need to carefully balance the intensity and effectiveness of supervision. We need to keep progressing in several aspects, for example, Basel III liquidity standards need to be finalized, a decision on the liquidity coverage ratio by the second half of 2012 is desirable, and we should try to finalize discussions on the net stable funding ratio. Also, the recent financial crisis painfully highlighted the costs of having too-big-tofail institutions. Thus, at the G20 we have progressed in elaborating a resolution framework for global systemically important banks and we are moving to gradually extend this framework to domestic banks, global insurance companies and global non-banks. 4 Regarding the operation of the international financial system, several measures are being taken in order to strengthen continuous markets. For example, it is expected that implementation of over-the-counter derivatives reforms will be ready by end2012. This includes putting in place safeguards for a global central counterparty clearing house framework, including multilateral cooperative oversight, crossborder liquidity, resolution and fair and open access. As you know, one key player in our efforts to improve the international financial system is the Financial Stability Board. Actions to strengthen the governance and capacity of the FSB are ongoing. The Reconstitution of the Steering Committee has already been completed along with the establishment of a High-level group on this issue. These initiatives will provide a stronger institutional footing to this organism, thereby contributing to its better functioning. As I mentioned earlier, the implementation phase of financial reforms will generate challenges and we should be ready to react swiftly in order to adapt or come up with solutions to unforeseen issues. In this regard, the FSB will work together with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank to assess the implications of post-crisis reforms on Emerging Markets and Developing Economies. In this aspect, let me be very clear, the objective is to identify the extent of any unintended consequences and to consider recommendations, which facilitate implementation without diluting or delaying the global reform agenda; no backtracking, no re-negotiating of previous accords. 5 Emerging markets and developing economies were not at the center of this crisis, but they have inevitably been affected by adverse developments since its outbreak. These developments include heightened financial system fragilities in many advanced economies, changes in the business models of globally operating banks, which had to adjust to more demanding funding and capital conditions, international and national regulatory responses developed to increase the global financial systems resilience to adverse shocks, and lately, the knock-on effects from sovereign debt concerns. International policies, which have been designed in the aftermath of the crisis, reflect the objective of strengthening the resilience of the international financial system in the face of identified shortcomings. These policies have intended consequences, such as raising the level and quality of capital and the amount of liquidity in the global banking system, as well as deterring business models that relied on excessive leverage and maturity mismatches. They have been designed with the appropriate transition arrangements where needed. However, they may also have unintended consequences that might arise from the way banks have responded and countries have implemented the rules. A number of measures taken at national or regional levels may also have cross-border impacts on emerging market economies; in particular in those countries that are hosts of global banks. 6 In this context, one of Mexicos priorities in the G20 is to analyze the effect of the international regulatory agenda and other post-crisis developments on emerging market economies with the aim of identifying areas that may need policies to support a swift and consistent implementation of the agreed financial reform agenda. Last but not least, Financial Inclusion is another important aspect that we are pursuing under the G20 agenda. Inclusion into the financial system, regardless of the populations social and economic conditions, can be reached by creating adequate policies and adapting the legal framework to the current needs. With the aim of achieving the greatest positive impact, the agenda covers expanding the access and fostering the use of formal financial services, and developing financial education and consumer protection policies. Furthermore, Mexico is promoting various actions like the creation of the G20 Financial Inclusion Peer Learning Program where participant countries commit to raise financial inclusion to the highest level in the national agenda and support the design of policies to push it forward. In a nutshell, the approach that Mexico has taken is comprehensive not only regarding financial regulation, but also with respect to growth and financial stabilization. Nevertheless, we have resisted the temptation of introducing new issues for discussion that could overburden the agenda. So regarding financial regulation, during our G20 Presidency in 2012 we will continue the ongoing work program of the FSB mainly focusing on implementation. 7 We know that from the industrys point of view there are different perspectives and we acknowledge that this has been a difficult and complex reform process. We are emphasizing the need to have a transparent and open process and we are working very hard to deliver on the regulatory agenda in a timely fashion. As you all know, these are not trivial issues and we are working as expedite as prudence allows. There are many different points of view that have to be considered. To conclude, Mexico has proposed a very ambitious agenda but we firmly believe that the priorities we have put forward are highly relevant at the global level. They cover a range of issues where actions are needed in order to establish the conditions for a more stable international financial and economic environment. We still have a lot of work ahead of us. In order to succeed in this endeavor, Mexico will strive to foster useful and fruitful discussions, always acknowledging the existence of different points of view but with the main objective of reaching consensus and concrete commitments. Thank you very much. 8

Title: Monetary and credit policy in the context of the crisis
text: Virtual seminar "Economy and society from the pandemic" Monetary and credit policy in the context of the crisis Senate of the Republic and Chamber of Deputies July 29, 2020 Jonathan Heath Good morning and thank you very much for the invitation to be here today with you, especially Don Porfirio Munoz Ledo and Senator Ifigenia Martinez and also Alfredo Navarrete, our moderator. 1. It is clear to all that we are currently experiencing an unprecedented crisis, the result of the great global lockdown that occurred in response to the Covid-19 pandemic. ? This pandemic has caused an economic crisis not seen in at least the last 90 years. The expectation of a fall in GDP for this year is close to a double-digit rate, while it is not clear how the recovery will take shape. ? This has generated a very deep labor crisis, in which the greatest weight has fallen on those who can least assimilate it: the lower income classes and the segment of the population that lived in precarious situations. ? Let me delve even deeper into this topic. Alfredo Navarrete said at the beginning in his speech that Mexico's open unemployment rate, at 4.7 percent in April of this year, was below many other countries. However, this is not the relevant rate, since it does not even begin to describe the labor imbalance we live. ? The Telephone Survey of Employment and Occupation (ETOE) of the INEGI, reported that in the months of April and May 20.1 million full-time jobs were lost, of which 12.2 million were displaced from the labor force, which is disguised unemployment, and 7.9 million were reclassified as underemployed, that is, they kept their jobs but now work fewer hours and obviously, with less income. 1 ? If we consider unemployment disguised as genuine unemployment, the extended unemployment rate reached 33 percent. If we consider that the underemployed also need a full-time job as before, the labor gap registered a rate of 53 percent. These figures reflect another dimension. ? As Norma Samaniego pointed out, of the 12.2 million people who completely lost their jobs, 75 percent were informal occupations, that is, without the benefits established by law and surely without adequate medical protection, something truly tragic in times of a health crisis. ? A large part of the jobs lost will not be replenished, as many companies and establishments suffered the definitive closure in the face of the great confinement, while the markets will face structural changes derived from the post-pandemic ravages. At this point it is not clear how many years the labor recovery will take us. 2. Faced with this crisis, the Bank of Mexico has responded with all the instruments at its disposal to mitigate the impact of the crisis: accelerate the lowering of the monetary policy interest rate, take additional measures to inject liquidity into the system for an amount of 800 billion pesos, along with forecasts to maintain the ordering of the markets and ensure the proper functioning of the economy's payment system. ? Indeed, the cycle of lowering interest rates began almost a year ago, when we saw that the conditions of idiosyncratic risks facing the economy began to dissipate, inflation was approaching the target set and economic activity experienced an uncomfortable slowdown. ? In that regard, the central bank has shown concern about poor economic performance long before the pandemic. ? At the time, a cycle of interest rate reduction was implemented, which, in my opinion, is not yet over. ? However, in the face of the pandemic, the Bank accelerated the monetary transition towards an expansionary stance, proceeding with some caution in the face of the unusual increase in global risk aversion. Between August and 2 last year and February of the present, a steady pace was maintained in the reduction of the monetary policy rate of 25 basis points in each scheduled monetary decision. ? When the pandemic was declared to exist, the cycle accelerated in the face of the sudden deterioration of the economic outlook to half a percentage point, first by advancing the March decision and then by means of an additional reduction not scheduled in April. This pace has been maintained with similar decisions in May and June, so that we have changed the restrictive monetary stance expressed with a monetary policy rate of 8.25 percent in the middle of last year, to an expansionary of 325 basis points less to stand at 5.0 percent in June. ? The objective of these reductions is to stimulate the economy as far as possible, as the negative effects on economic activity and employment have taken on top priority. I emphasize, which is my personal opinion, that the cycle is not yet over, so we will seek to bring the monetary stance to an expansionary level according to the current economic situation. 3. However, the road is not easy given that we face several risks along the way. It is in this context that there are two main challenges to monetary policy: ? First, we must recognize the limitations to monetary policy. Low financial inclusion, a large informal sector and high banking concentration reduce the effectiveness of a lower interest rate. ? Second, the great integration of our economy into the global economy. At any given time, interest rates that are too low, especially in a context of high risk, can lead to an even greater depreciation of our currency and to the continuation of capital outflows, which from March to date already registered 17 billion dollars. To be precise, from February 28 to July 16, an outflow of 391 billion pesos has been registered, equivalent to 17.7 billion dollars. Price stability is conditioned on the stability of our currency, so its accelerated depreciation could 3 generate a substantial loss in the purchasing power of our household income. If the less protected classes face a precarious situation, we cannot see it even more deteriorated. In the last year and a half we have seen a recovery, albeit incipient, in the purchasing power of wages. This is a primordial and social justice advance, which we cannot lose. Therefore, the Bank of Mexico will make every effort to ensure that this wage recovery maintains its purchasing power. 4. The constitutional mandate of the Bank of Mexico has as a priority objective price stability, but it is not a single objective or a final one. It is an intermediate objective that ultimately seeks, as Article 25 of the Constitution indicates, national development through the promotion of economic growth and employment. How? Creating the best possible conducive environment for its promotion. ? Headline inflation is estimated to be within the target range, but core inflation has upward pressures from distortions caused by the pandemic and exchange rate depreciation. In particular, inflation of "food commodities" ranks well above all other major sub-indices of the national price index. For example, in June, inflation of non-food goods, services and the component known as non-core inflation were below the bank's target of 3.0 percent, while that of food commodities more than doubled. ? Although this is a phenomenon that was observed before the arrival of the pandemic, due to international price pressures, it was exacerbated by distortions in supply and demand conditions and exchange rate pressures caused by the pandemic. It must be remembered that this is precisely the segment of inflation that most affects the less protected classes and those who today find themselves without income due to the labor crisis. ? The problem with this scenario that we face is that being the product of a supply shock has practically no sensitivity to the economic cycle and the monetary stance. There is not much we can do, other than be careful that it does not represent a deterioration in the 4 inflation expectations and remember that the best defense of workers' nominal income is low inflation. Without forgetting this, for now, our institution has already joined forces to combat head-on the brutal fall in economic activity and the tragic loss of jobs. 5. The Bank of Mexico also aims to promote the healthy development of the financial system and to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. This implies that the financial system is part of the solution and not part of the problem. ? At this time, what we must take care of most and ensure is that the economy has enough liquidity to operate in the best possible conditions taking into account the restrictions imposed by the pandemic. For this, the Bank has implemented complementary measures for 800 billion pesos. These measures announced in March and April are equivalent to around 3.3 percent of 2019 GDP. ? The objectives are to provide greater liquidity to institutions, preserve the functioning of the market and above all strengthen the credit granting channel. While the first two measures are traditional and seek to preserve the health of the financial system, the third aims to increase the room for maneuver of banks so that they can give credit to micro, small and medium enterprises, thereby benefiting the thousands of workers who work in them. ? It is clear that the ideal complement to the proper functioning of these measures is to continue with the downward cycle of the interest rate of overnight interbank funding and extending the expansionary stance of monetary policy, always closely monitoring the potential risks that could derail us. ? The Bank is and will continue to monitor these actions to ensure that the measures are functional and sufficient. We will be correcting, increasing, extending and improving these measures on the fly, seeking to contribute in the best possible way to the economic recovery. We will do this by encouraging activity 5 economic and employment, but always within a framework that ensures the continuity of financial stability, the proper functioning of our payment systems and price stability. ? It is sought that the financial system is an effective vehicle that provides solvency to companies and enough working capital for them to survive. Without companies, there is simply no employment. This support is vital to this day. 6. In summary: ? The Bank of Mexico is committed to price stability, but it does not stop having a policy committed to growth and the functionality of the economy to generate employment. ? In this crisis, the most effective defense for the classes that have less is to protect their purchasing power and mitigate as much as possible the impact on employment. ? It remains to be said that the policies of the Bank of Mexico must be understood from the context of its legal powers. In these times of uncertainty, it is essential for the Bank of Mexico to show itself as a solid institution, attached to its regulatory framework and at the same time with inventiveness to face the challenge of this crisis. This contribution is essential to maintain credibility and remain one of the pillars of the confidence of the financial sector and Mexican society in the capacity of its institutions. ? Similarly, the scope of the implemented policies must be understood. The Bank of Mexico alone cannot be the solution to economic problems whose attention requires the joint participation of all the institutions of the Mexican State and the private sector. So that each of these, within their attributions, puts their grain of sand. ? However, within its institutional perimeter, the Bank will seek to actively support these public and private sectors to achieve the rapid economic recovery we so desperately need. Thanks a lot. 6
text_original: Seminario virtual Economa y sociedad a partir de la pandemia Poltica monetaria y crediticia en el contexto de la crisis Senado de la Repblica y Cmara de Diputados 29 de julio de 2020 Jonathan Heath Buenos das y muchas gracias por la invitacin para estar aqu el da de hoy con ustedes, en especial a Don Porfirio Muoz Ledo y a la Senadora Ifigenia Martinez y tambin a Alfredo Navarrete, nuestro moderador. 1. Queda claro a todos que vivimos en estos momentos una crisis sin precedentes, resultado del gran confinamiento a nivel mundial que se dio como respuesta a la pandemia del Covid-19.  Esta pandemia ha causado una crisis econmica no vista por lo menos en los ltimos 90 aos. La expectativa de cada del PIB para este ao se sita cercana a una tasa de doble dgito, mientras que no queda claro cmo se conformar la recuperacin.  Esto ha generado una crisis laboral muy profunda, en la cual el peso ms grande ha recado sobre quienes menos pueden asimilarlo: las clases de ms bajos ingresos y el segmento de la poblacin que viva en situaciones precarias.  Permtame ahondar todava ms en este tema. Alfredo Navarrete dijo al principio en su intervencin que la tasa de desempleo abierto de Mxico, de 4.7 por ciento en abril de este ao, se ubic por debajo de muchos otros pases. Sin embargo, esta no es la tasa relevante, ya que ni siquiera empieza a describir el desequilibrio laboral que vivimos.  La Encuesta Telefnica de Empleo y Ocupacin (ETOE) del INEGI, report que en los meses de abril y mayo se perdieron 20.1 millones de empleos de tiempo completo, de los cuales 12.2 millones quedaron desplazados de la fuerza laboral, lo cual es desempleo disfrazado, y 7.9 millones fueron reclasificados como subempleados, es decir, mantuvieron su empleo pero trabajan ahora menos horas y obviamente, con menos ingresos. 1  Si consideramos el desempleo disfrazado como desempleo genuino, la tasa de desempleo extendido lleg a 33 por ciento. Si consideramos que los subempleados tambin necesitan un trabajo de tiempo completo como antes, la brecha laboral registr una tasa de 53 por ciento. Estas cifras reflejan otra dimensin.  Como apunt Norma Samaniego, de los 12.2 millones de personas que perdieron por completo su trabajo, 75 por ciento eran ocupaciones informales, es decir, sin las prestaciones que marca la ley y seguramente sin una adecuada proteccin mdica, algo verdaderamente trgico en tiempos de una crisis sanitaria.  Una gran parte de los empleos perdidos no se repondrn, ya que muchas empresas y establecimientos sufrieron el cierre definitivo ante el gran confinamiento, mientras que los mercados enfrentarn cambios estructurales derivados de los estragos post-pandemia. A estas alturas no queda claro cuntos aos nos tomar la recuperacin laboral. 2. Ante esta crisis, el Banco de Mxico ha respondido con todos los instrumentos de que dispone para mitigar el impacto de la crisis: acelerar la baja de la tasa de inters de poltica monetaria, tomar medidas adicionales para inyectar liquidez en el sistema por un monto de 800 mil millones de pesos, junto con previsiones para mantener el ordenamiento de los mercados y asegurar el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos de la economa.  En efecto, se inici el ciclo de baja de tasas de inters desde hace casi un ao, cuando vimos que las condiciones de riesgos idiosincrticos que enfrentaba la economa empezaban a disiparse, la inflacin se acercaba al objetivo trazado y la actividad econmica experimentaba una desaceleracin incmoda.  En ese sentido, el banco central ha mostrado una preocupacin por el pobre desempeo econmico mucho antes de la pandemia.  En su momento, se instrument un ciclo de reduccin de tasas de inters, el cual, de acuerdo a mi opinin, an no ha terminado.  No obstante, ante la pandemia, el Banco aceler la transicin monetaria hacia una postura expansiva, procediendo con cierta cautela ante el incremento inusitado en la aversin al riesgo mundial. Entre agosto del 2 ao pasado y febrero del presente, se mantuvo un ritmo constante en la reduccin de la tasa de poltica monetaria de 25 puntos base en cada decisin monetaria calendarizada.  Cuando se declar la existencia de la pandemia, se aceler el ciclo ante el sbito deterioro de las perspectivas econmicas a medio punto porcentual, primero adelantando la decisin de marzo y despus mediante una reduccin adicional no programada en abril. Este ritmo se ha mantenido con decisiones similares en mayo y junio, de tal forma que hemos cambiado la postura monetaria restrictiva expresada con una tasa de poltica monetaria de 8.25 por ciento a mediados del ao pasado, a una expansiva de 325 puntos base menos para situarnos en 5.0 por ciento en junio.  El objetivo de estas reducciones, es dar, hasta donde sea posible, un estmulo a la economa, ya que los efectos negativos sobre la actividad econmica y el empleo han cobrado mxima prioridad. Subrayo, que es mi opinin personal, que el ciclo todava no termina, por lo que buscaremos llevar la postura monetaria a un nivel expansivo acorde a la situacin econmica actual. 3. Sin embargo, el camino no es fcil dado que enfrentamos varios riesgos en el camino. Es en este contexto, que hay dos retos principales a la poltica monetaria:  Primero, debemos reconocer las limitaciones a la poltica monetaria. La baja inclusin financiera, un sector informal grande y la elevada concentracin bancaria, reducen la efectividad de una baja de la tasa de inters.  Segundo, la gran integracin de nuestra economa a la economa global. En un momento dado, tasas de inters demasiado bajas, en especial en un contexto de riesgo elevado, pueden inducir a una todava mayor depreciacin de nuestra moneda y a que contine la salida de capitales, que de marzo a la fecha ya registr 17 mil millones de dlares. Para ser precisos, del 28 de febrero al 16 de julio se ha registrado una salida de 391 mil millones de pesos, equivalente a 17.7 miles de millones de dlares. La estabilidad de precios est condicionada a la estabilidad de nuestra moneda, por lo que su depreciacin acelerada podra 3 generar una prdida sustantiva en el poder adquisitivo de los ingresos de nuestros hogares. Si de por si las clases menos protegidas enfrentan una situacin precaria, no podemos verla todava ms deteriorada. En el ltimo ao y medio hemos visto una recuperacin, aunque incipiente, en el poder adquisitivo de los salarios. Este es un avance primordial y de justicia social, que no podemos perder. Por lo que el Banco de Mxico har todo los esfuerzos que estn a su alcance para que dicha recuperacin salarial mantenga su poder de compra. 4. El mandato constitucional del Banco de Mxico tiene como objetivo prioritario la estabilidad de precios, ms no es un objetivo nico ni uno final. Es un objetivo intermedio que al final de cuentas busca, como lo seala el Artculo 25 Constitucional, el desarrollo nacional mediante el fomento del crecimiento econmico y el empleo. Cmo? Creando el mejor ambiente propicio posible para su fomento.  La inflacin general se estima dentro del rango objetivo, pero la inflacin subyacente tiene presiones al alza por distorsiones causadas por la pandemia y la depreciacin cambiaria. En particular, la inflacin de mercancas alimenticias se ubica muy por encima de todos los dems subndices principales del ndice nacional de precios. Por ejemplo, en junio la inflacin de mercancas no alimenticias, de servicios y el componente conocido como la de inflacin no subyacente se ubicaban por debajo del objetivo del banco de 3.0 por ciento, mientras que la de mercancas alimenticias se situ a ms de lo doble.  Si bien, este es un fenmeno que se observaba antes de la llegada de la pandemia, debido a presiones de precios internacionales, se exacerb por las distorsiones en las condiciones de oferta y demanda y las presiones cambiarias originadas por la pandemia. Hay que recordar que este es justamente el segmento de la inflacin que ms afecta a las clases menos protegidas y a las que hoy se encuentran sin ingresos por la crisis laboral.  El problema de este escenario que enfrentamos es que al ser producto de un choque de oferta tiene prcticamente nula sensibilidad al ciclo econmico y a la postura monetaria. No hay mucho que podemos hacer, ms que estar atentos a que no represente un deterioro en las 4 expectativas de inflacin y recordar que la mejor defensa del ingreso nominal de los trabajadores es una baja inflacin. Sin olvidarnos de esto, por lo pronto, nuestra institucin ya uni fuerzas para combatir frontalmente la cada brutal de la actividad econmica y la prdida trgica de empleos. 5. El Banco de Mxico tiene tambin como objetivos promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Esto implica que el sistema financiero sea parte de la solucin y no parte del problema.  En estos momentos, lo que ms debemos cuidar y asegurar es que la economa tenga la liquidez suficiente para operar en las mejores condiciones posibles tomando en cuenta las restricciones impuestas por la pandemia. Para esto, el Banco ha instrumentado medidas complementarias por 800 mil millones de pesos. Estas medidas anunciadas en marzo y en abril son equivalentes a alrededor de 3.3 por ciento del PIB de 2019.  Los objetivos son proveer una mayor liquidez a las instituciones, preservar el funcionamiento del mercado y sobre todo fortalecer el canal de otorgamiento de crdito. Mientras las dos primeras medidas son tradicionales y buscan preservar la salud del sistema financiero, la tercera tiene el objetivo de incrementar el margen de maniobra de los bancos para que estos puedan dar crdito a las micro, pequeas y medianas empresas beneficiando con ello a los miles de trabajadores que en ellas laboran.  Queda claro que el complemento ideal al buen funcionamiento de estas medidas es continuar con el ciclo a la baja de la tasa de inters del fondeo interbancaria a un da y extendiendo la postura expansiva de la poltica monetaria, siempre vigilando de cerca los riesgos potenciales que nos pudieran descarrilar.  El Banco est y continuara estando vigilando estas acciones para asegurar que las medidas sean funcionales y suficientes. Estaremos corrigiendo, aumentando, extendiendo y mejorando estas medidas sobre la marcha, en busca de contribuir en la mejor forma posible a la recuperacin econmica. Lo haremos fomentando la actividad 5 econmica y el empleo, pero siempre dentro de un marco que asegura la continuidad de la estabilidad financiera, el buen funcionamiento de nuestros sistemas de pago y la estabilidad de precios.  Se busca que el sistema financiero sea un vehculo efectivo que otorgue solvencia a las empresas y suficiente capital de trabajo para que sobrevivan. Sin empresas, simplemente, no hay empleo. Este apoyo es vital al da de hoy. 6. En resumen:  El Banco de Mxico est comprometido con la estabilidad de precios, pero no por ello deja de tener una poltica comprometida con el crecimiento y la funcionalidad de la economa para generar empleo.  En esta crisis, la defensa ms efectiva para las clases que menos tienen es proteger su poder adquisitivo y mitigar en lo posible la afectacin del empleo.  Queda por decir que las polticas del Banco de Mxico deben entenderse desde el contexto de sus atribuciones de ley. En estos momentos de incertidumbre, es esencial para el Banco de Mxico mostrase como una institucin slida, apegada a su marco normativo y al mismo tiempo con inventiva para enfrentar el reto de esta crisis. Dicha contribucin es esencial para mantener la credibilidad y seguir siendo uno de los pilares de la confianza del sector financiero y de la sociedad mexicana en la capacidad de sus instituciones.  De igual forma, se tienen que entender los alcances de las polticas implementadas. El Banco de Mxico, por s solo no puede ser la solucin a problemas econmicos cuya atencin requiere de una participacin conjunta de la todas las instituciones del Estado mexicano y del sector privado. Para que cada uno de stos, dentro de sus atribuciones ponga su grano de arena.  Sin embargo, dentro su permetro institucional, el Banco buscara apoyar de manera activa a estos sectores pblicos y privados para que alcancemos la rpida recuperacin econmica que tanto necesitamos. Muchas gracias. 6

Title: Mexicos economic outlook: challenges and opportunities
text: Mexicos Economic Outlook: Challenges and Opportunities Remarks by Manuel Sanchez Deputy Governor The Bank of Mexico at the Conference Latin America 2010: Economic, Business and Trade Forecast Center for Hemispheric Policy University of Miami February 5, 2010 I would like to thank the Center for Hemispheric Policy of the University of Miami for the invitation to speak at this conference addressing the growth and trade prospects for Latin America. In my talk, I will focus on the short- and medium-term outlook for the Mexican economy. My central message will be the following: The deep recession suffered by Mexico during the past two years was mainly due to external factors, but its impact was somewhat mitigated by the soundness of the countrys macroeconomic fundamentals. Although the world and Mexico have recently started to show signs of an economic recovery, sustainable growth will require prudent economic management. To elaborate on these issues, I will divide my presentation into three parts. First, I will analyze how the global financial crisis affected Mexico and how this recession was different from previous ones. Second, I will discuss the economic outlook for Mexico in the international context. Finally, I will comment on some policy challenges for the global economy and Mexico. The impact of the global crisis in Mexico During the last two years, Mexico experienced a harsh economic downturn. Official data suggest that the economic contraction started during the second quarter of 2008 and probably ended in the same quarter of 2009. During this five-quarter period, per-capita GDP plummeted by approximately 10%, a fall similar to the one observed in the first half of 1995. In modern history, the depth of the recent recession has been clearly surpassed only during the Great Depression, when the countrys per-capita GDP collapsed 26% between 1928 and 1932. The loss of per-capita income and employment in the recent recessionary period has significantly damaged the wellbeing of many Mexicans. 1 By far, the most distinct feature of this modern contraction relative to others in the post-war period was that it comprised two adverse external shocks that fed back into each other and led to a dangerous deterioration of economic and financial conditions. As was the case for other emerging economies, Mexico was affected by the global crisis through the financial sector in the form of substantial market volatility and a generalized fall in asset prices. However, the Mexican economy was most deeply disturbed through the real sector, as seen in the contraction of international flows of goods and services, especially to and from the United States, Mexicos main trading partner. As we know, the widespread increase in risk aversion triggered by the problems derived from the previous lending boom in the housing and real estate sectors of the United States caused substantial financial turbulence worldwide. In particular, the Lehman Brothers collapse in September 2008 sparked major volatility which started falling only seven months later. Massive monetary injections in several countries and an official bailout program for troubled financial institutions in the United States allowed international financial markets a gradual return to normal conditions. To cushion the effects of the financial blow, Mexican authorities implemented several actions, especially geared to providing liquidity in the foreign exchange and credit markets. Given the relative resilience of the Mexican financial system, most measures were relatively modest and designed as temporary, and thus have already ended or will soon end.1 Moreover, the real economic disturbance, which in April 2009 was aggravated by the eruption of swine flu epidemics, had a deeper and more lasting effect on Mexico. Its manifestation included a contraction of tourism in Mexican destinations and the worsening of an already declining trend in worker remittances from abroad. However, the most important driving force of the 1 For a review of the measures taken by Mexico during the crisis, see Manuel Sanchez, Impacto de la Crisis Internacional en Mexico, Respuesta de Politica y Perspectivas speech at the Reserve Bank of El Salvador, November 2009: . 2 economic slump was the sharp fall in the demand for Mexicos exports, especially manufacturing goods oriented to the United States, which during the last ten years accounted for over 80% of the countrys total non-oil exports. According to the national income accounts, Mexicos total exports of goods and services in the second quarter of 2009 were 24% lower than those at their peak level six quarters earlier. It is worth noting that this last recession in Mexico exhibited substantial differences from previous ones. Past crises were typically linked to major macroeconomic and financial disequilibria, in the form of high fiscal deficits, large current account imbalances and fragile financial intermediaries. Given a predetermined exchange rate system, these weaknesses eventually led to a speculative attack on the currency. The sequence of events was a significant burst in inflation and interest rates, a sudden drop in investment and output, major job losses, and a dramatic fall in real wages. Restoration of macroeconomic equilibrium usually required the implementation of tight fiscal and monetary policies. In contrast, the recent recession occurred in the presence of sound macroeconomic fundamentals, including a solvent fiscal position, a floating exchange rate system, and an independent central bank committed to price stability. In addition, the construction of a strong regulatory and supervisory framework together with openness to foreign investment yielded a solid banking system. The development of long-term loan products at fixed nominal interest rates offered by banks reduced the vulnerability of consumers and firms to sudden changes in financial conditions. These elements proved valuable in ameliorating the effects of the external shock on domestic spending. Of particular note, exports of goods and services fell dramatically whereas they had either remained relatively stable or boomed in previous recessions. However, private consumption was more resilient than it was in the mid-1990s crisis, and the fall in private investment was lower than that in the 1982 and 3 1995 recessions. Additionally, public expenditures grew at higher rates than in any previous contraction, thus exerting some countercyclical effect on output. The main lesson to be drawn from Mexicos experience with crises is that there are no substitutes for good and well-coordinated economic policies. Prudent macroeconomic measures together with a well-capitalized financial system and flexible exchange rates are suitable elements to preserve the confidence of market participants and facilitate an orderly adjustment to external disturbances. Mexicos economic outlook Let me now turn to the economic outlook for Mexico. Given this countrys openness to foreign trade and investment, its prospects naturally depend on the expected evolution of the world economy and, in particular, that of the United States. So allow me to first briefly comment on the international scenario. Most forecasters share the view that the global economy will perform better in 2010 and 2011 than in the previous two years. On the one hand, GDP and international trade are expected to increase, in clear contrast with their corresponding contractions in 2009. A characteristic feature of this outlook is that recovery will exhibit a more gradual pace than in previous expansions. For example, the IMF forecasts that global GDP will grow 3.9% in 2010 and 4.4% on average from 2011 to 2014. The latter figure is half a percentage point lower than that observed in the 2004-2007 period. Additionally, emerging market economies are expected to continue to grow faster than developed countries. For the U. S. economy, the IMF estimates 2.7% growth in 2010 and 2.4% in 4 2011. At the same time, world inflation is estimated to remain fairly subdued in the near future.2 Prospects for better world economic performance are based on different factors, among which recent data stand out. Since the second quarter of 2009, the global economy has shown increasingly clearer signs of a rebound. While growth has been widespread, the recovery has been more vigorous in specific emerging economies, especially China, India and Brazil. In the case of Latin America, during the second half of 2009 the region experienced a mild recuperation supported by an increase in government spending, lower interest rates, and an improvement in external demand. In the United States, favorable developments included a 5.7% annualized quarterly increase in GDP in the fourth quarter of 2009, the fastest pace in six years and the second consecutive quarter of growth after four quarters of decline. Moreover, during the fourth quarter, liquidation of inventories by firms slowed and their investment in equipment and software started to show signs of recovery. Similarly, real estate indicators continued an upturn observed in the previous quarter. Given substantial excess capacity, global inflationary pressures have remained relatively contained. In the advanced economies, inflation turned positive during the last quarter of 2009 after being negative for several months. In the United States, inflation ticked up recently mainly as a result of higher energy prices. In developing countries, although consumer inflation also took a downward path, it has generally remained positive, with some exceptions such as China and Chile. In general, the monetary stance in most countries is expected to continue to be accommodative for some time, although some central banks have already started their tightening cycles. 2 For the IMF forecasts, see IMF, World Economic Outlook, October 2009 : ) and World Economic Outlook Update, January 2010: . 5 In the financial system, the risk of a widespread collapse of international markets has significantly narrowed. While initially the main source of improvement was constituted by the measures implemented by the authorities in various countries, the more recent upturn in the financial system seems to reflect a positive feedback loop between the growth prospects of the real economy and financial conditions. However, certain factors suggest that the economic recovery in the United States will be sluggish. One is that consumers and firms will likely continue deleveraging their financial positions, which may imply higher saving rates than pre-crisis levels. Another is that banks will continue cleansing their balance sheets and seeking to replenish capital before resuming lending. Finally, although some recent housing-sector indicators such as construction orders and sales point toward further progress, full adjustment of inventories may still take time. These elements may, in turn, contribute to an explanation of why employment has been responding somewhat more slowly than in previous expansions. Furthermore, low interest rates in the United States and in other advanced countries, together with the expectation that they will remain low for an extended period as well as a weak dollar, have led to the proliferation of the carry trade. This type of trade consists in investors seeking higher returns in risky assets by borrowing cheaply in the money markets of advanced countries, seizing opportunities from a lax monetary stance. These transactions have resulted in a notable increase of capital flows into emerging market economies, a trend which implies a possible source of future financial instability. In particular, as the Fed and other major central banks begin to tighten their monetary policies and the dollar starts to appreciate, risky positions in a number of assets should begin to unwind, affecting the financial markets and reversing capital flows into developing countries. In this event, volatility could return to international financial markets and the U. S. economy could grow less than anticipated. 6 How will Mexico fare in the future? The consensus forecast is for a gradual economic recovery, proceeding hand in hand with the improvement of the world economy. Specifically, the Bank of Mexico estimates that, after a contraction of a little less than 7% in 2009, the Mexican economy will grow between 3.2% and 4.2% in 2010 and 2011.3 The main engine of growth will be the continued greater dynamism of the U. S. economy, particularly its industrial sector. As is well known, the correlation between the industrial outputs of these two countries exceeds 0.9, reflecting the high share of manufacturing exports going to the United States out of Mexicos total exports. As is the case for other counties, the Mexican economy has already begun to show signs of resurgence. After five consecutive quarters of contraction, thirdquarter GDP posted a 2.9% seasonally adjusted, non-annualized change. Additionally, some economic indicators for the fourth quarter of last year also support the view that growth has continued. For example, last November, the Economic Activity Indicator (IGAE) showed a monthly seasonally adjusted rise of 1.5%, which corresponds to a third consecutive month of positive change. Perhaps the most encouraging factor is the reversal of the external-sector troubles which, as I mentioned, were the main source of the economic slump. In particular, annual dollar growth rates of non-oil and auto-industry exports have recently followed a rising trend, reaching more than 15% and 31%, respectively, in December 2009. Although domestic demand indicators still show a mixed picture, with reviving consumption and stagnant investment, these variables may respond with a lag to the external impetus. This hypothesis seems to be confirmed by the positive recent trend of leading indicators such as the Purchasing Managers and Consumer Confidence Indexes, and the reduction in the unemployment rate by the end of last year. Notwithstanding the latest return of business to market 3 Banco de Mexico, Informe sobre la Inflacion Octubre  Diciembre 2009 y Programa Monetario para 2010, January 2010: . 7 financing, the revival of bank lending, especially consumer credit, will probably take time. Economic policy challenges The sustained growth scenario I have just described depends on the appropriate management of crucial challenges faced by advanced economies, which are related to the timely reversal of the extraordinary monetary and fiscal actions that were undertaken to counter the global crisis. The resulting expansionary stance is reflected in the unprecedented enlargement of the major central banks balance sheets and the high fiscal deficits in many developed countries. Adequate exit strategies need to be planned and properly implemented.4 These policies are widely expected to be maintained until growth consolidates and gains more momentum. There is concern that if the various stimulus measures are retired too early or too rapidly, this withdrawal might adversely affect consumers and firms that are still too leveraged. In addition, many financial institutions may still be too fragile to handle liquidity or solvency problems on their own. In fact, in accordance with this preoccupation, the U.S. government announced last November a new package of fiscal stimulus to support growth and employment. Unfortunately, maintenance of these measures over the medium term is clearly unsustainable. High fiscal deficits may exert upward pressure on interest rates, crowding out private spending and hampering economic activity. This may also 4 For a discussion of possible principles guiding exit strategies, see IMF, Global Economic Prospects and Principles for Policy Exit, Meetings of G-20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors, November 6 7, 2009: . Prospects and Principles for Policy Exit 8 limit the access of emerging economies to international capital markets. On the other hand, if maintained for too long, highly expansionary monetary policies may cause deterioration of inflation expectations, fueling inflation and weakening the recovery. On both fiscal and monetary counts, the key issue ahead is when and how to retire stimulus without letting these risks materialize. Finally, Mexico has important tasks ahead. One relates to the improvement of the fiscal and monetary framework to continue supporting growth prospects. In response to the foreseen decline of oil-related fiscal revenues, at the end of last year, the Mexican Congress approved a fiscal reform that included certain higher tax rates. Additionally, some public-sector prices at the federal and local levels will be revised upward in 2010, particularly those such as for gasoline and gas that were frozen during 2009 to support the economy. Notwithstanding some possible short-term undesirable effects on economic activity,5 these adjustments may be justified as a means to maintain the longterm sustainability of public finances, ameliorating Mexicos country risk perception. Additionally, a strong fiscal position contributes to the anchoring of inflation expectations and the lowering of both short- and long-term interest rates. Since April 1994, the Bank of Mexico has, as its Constitutional mandate, the main objective of preserving the purchasing power of the currency, which means price stability. To fulfill its obligation, since 2001, the central bank has conducted its monetary policy under an inflation-targeting regime and established as its medium-term objective a 3% annual inflation rate. Price stability is a highly commendable objective as it represents a necessary condition for sustainable economic growth. As you know, inflation is one of the 5 For an estimation of the possible effects of the fiscal package on the real economic activity, see Banco de Mexico, Addendum al Informe sobre la Inflacion Julio  Septiembre 2009, December 2009: . 9 worst maladies that can affect any economic system, and Mexico has suffered its catastrophic consequences during long periods in the past. Inflation acts as one of the most regressive taxes, wiping out the financial wealth of the poor. It introduces a wide range of inefficiencies in the form of diversion of economic resources from their most productive uses. Its associated uncertainty shortens the planning horizons for savings, investment and job creation. In short, inflation dramatically lowers the possibilities for growth and poverty alleviation. So particularly for us, it is essential to fight against inflation.6 After many years of severe price instability, during the past decade inflation in Mexico has been reduced to relatively low levels. In 2009, to accommodate the shock of the global crisis, the Bank of Mexico reduced its policy interest rate by 375 basis points. As the effects of previous currency depreciation subsided and economic slack remained substantial, annual inflation came down to 3.6% by year-end. For 2010, the increases in taxes and public-sector prices will likely have a direct, once-and-for-all impact on inflation that is expected to dissipate early in 2011. It is not advisable for any central bank to try to offset these kinds of effects, as this would require an overly restrictive monetary policy in order to exert downward pressure on other prices. In fact, the likely outcome of such an attempt could be a negligible effect on inflation and downward pressure on economic activity. However, the central bank should be ready to act when these kinds of price adjustments appear to affect the medium-term dynamics of inflation or lead to a deterioration of inflation expectations. Therefore, in 2010 the Bank of Mexico will remain vigilant to prevent likely transitory pressures on inflation from becoming widespread or from raising inflation expectations, so that its inflation target of 3% may be reached by 2011. If the Mexican central bank determines that the behavior of these variables is 6 For an exposition of the benefits of price stability, see Ben Bernanke, The Benefits of Price Stability speech at the Center for Economic Studies, Princeton University, February 24 2006: . 10 inconsistent with its inflation target, it will not hesitate to adjust its policy interest rate to induce inflation and inflation expectations towards the 3% target. A second type of challenge is the need to implement structural reforms in order to increase the potential growth rate of the economy. These include changes to make the use of labor and investment more attractive, enhance total factor productivity, and take advantage of worldwide technological progress. In the pursuit of this agenda, there is no panacea and a wide range of transformations is desirable. These include a fiscal reform that efficiently broadens the tax base and focuses public expenditure to the better provision of public goods, such as public security, protection of property rights and physical infrastructure, as well as the liberalization of barriers to entrepreneurial activities, which take the form of red tape and limitations or prohibitions to production, investment, and market flexibility and competition. Concluding remarks The recent deep recession had its origin abroad, but its impact was somewhat mitigated by the sound macroeconomic fundamentals prevalent in the country. Fortunately, the global economy has begun to recover, a trend which is already benefiting Mexico. The sustainability of economic growth will depend on the appropriate management of crucial challenges in advanced economies related to removing the extraordinary measures undertaken to handle the crisis. Mexico will need to continue strengthening its framework for macroeconomic and financial stability, as well as pursue structural reforms that would increase its potential economic growth. With these changes, Mexico will be able to improve its prospects for higher living standards and achieve substantial poverty reduction. 11

Title: The never-ending task of price stability
text: The never-ending task of price stability Remarks by Dr. Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, at the Financial Conference Cycle of the ITESM Campus Mexico City on January 26, 2011. I very much appreciate the invitation of the Tecnologico de Monterrey Campus Mexico City to participate in its cycle of financial conferences. As an alumnus of Tec, it is a great pleasure to return to this institution and to be able to share with you some ideas related to the Mexican economy and, in particular, to the Bank of Mexico. Recently our central bank celebrated its 85th anniversary. That is why the occasion is propitious to reflect on their challenges and achievements. The history of the Bank of Mexico can be analyzed from different perspectives. I would like to explore one of them today: the struggle for price stability; this has usually been underserved by analysts and researchers. Inflation is an evil that violates families and the economy. Sustained growth in the general price level, which is the definition of inflation, deteriorates the purchasing power of income. To adapt to this phenomenon, people put in place mechanisms that, obviously without intending to, waste productive resources, which generates inefficiencies. One example is the constant change of prices in shops and restaurants. In addition, individuals and businesses look for financial or contractual ways to protect themselves against this danger. Those who do not or cannot do so, such as pensioners and wage earners, are especially affected by inflation. On the other hand, when inflation persistently rises, it tends to be more volatile, implying greater uncertainty and making savings and investment decisions even more difficult. 1 While those who have led the Bank of Mexico have always intended to fight inflation, price stability has not necessarily been the characteristic that has marked all stages of the national economy since the Bank opened its doors in 1925. Below I will give a brief account of the most outstanding episodes of the struggle for price stability in our country.
