In certain circumstances the conditions and strategy of this fight were unfavorable and this explains, in general terms, the periods of high inflation in Mexico. Since the search for permanent price stability is, by definition, an unfinished task that extends to the present day, the subject of this talk is fully topical. For convenience, I will distinguish five epochs. I. First contributions towards price stability (1925-1935) The Mexican Revolution severely affected the country in every way. There were banknotes and coins in circulation from various issuers, for example Venustiano Carranza, Francisco Villa, Emiliano Zapata and state banks. All this discredited the use of money. In 1914 there was a high inflation due to the uncontrolled increase in the circulation and the shortage of goods. Reflecting this environment, between July 1914 and July 1915 corn increased 2400 percent, beans 2200 percent, rice 1420 percent, sugar 940 percent and flour 900 percent. In 1916 the government resorted to collecting taxes on gold and silver, and not on paper money, which signaled to the public that the banknotes were no longer worthy. In the years that followed, the country was demonetized and without an institutional framework of banking, which led to a monetary disorder with a high cost to the population.1 1 See Del angel Mobarak, Gustavo A. (2010). "The Socialization of the Economic Cost of the Mexican Revolution" in Inflation and Revolution: The Mexican Experience from 1912 to 1917. Bank of Mexico. Mexico. 2 The road to monetary order began in September 1925 with the founding of the Bank of Mexico. One of the first key actions in defense of price stability was led by the Chairman of its Board of Directors, Manuel Gomez Morin and the Secretary of Finance, Alberto J. Pani. Both agreed on the desirability of the central bank having independence. Gomez Morin's thesis in this regard was that in this way you could have a healthy and stable currency.2 It should be clarified that from 1925 to 1994 the Bank operated under various predetermined exchange rate regimes that were interrupted by periods of floating of the currency. These suspensions were the result of incongruous monetary policies that were, to a large extent, due to the financing of public spending by the central institute. In turn, this phenomenon - turning the Bank of Mexico into the source of financing government spending through the issuance of currency - derives from the lack of independence from the Government that the Bank suffered during that long period. In early 1927 there were two particularly unfavorable trends for the central bank. The first was the inclination of the Bank's management to take it more and more down the path of commercial banking and neglect its vocation as a central bank. The second was related to a sharp weakening of the institution's independence by allowing funding to the government to exceed the established legal limit. The main expression of the battle given by Gomez Morin to avoid these two tendencies materialized in his report to the Shareholders' Meeting in 1928: The Bank of Mexico... it was not founded to give the country a new bank placed on the same level as the other credit institutions of the Republic. No 2 See Mendez Reyes, Jesus. (2001). The Economic Thought of Manuel Gomez Morin (1913-1936). Faculty of Economics, UNAM. Mexico. 3 it will be able to function fully, therefore, or yield the fruits that should be expected of it, as long as it does not have the character that should be its own: that of a central institution in all the economic bodies of the Country. ... The law of its creation gives the Bank the character of a central institution of issuance and rediscounting, thus entrusting it with the double task of maintaining a healthy currency in Mexico and of regulating banking trade, the functioning of the credit institutions that should be the exponent and summary of the economic organization of the Republic.3 In 1931 and 1932 there was the first major reform of the Bank of Mexico. In July 1931 gold was demonetized in the country through the enactment of the Monetary Law and in March 1932 another major change was carried out: a reform of the aforementioned Monetary Law and the promulgation of a new Organic Law for the Bank of Mexico. With these modifications, the Bank ceased to operate as a commercial bank and consolidated itself as a central bank, that is, it acquired the exclusivity of monetary issuance and the association of commercial banks with the central institute became mandatory. During those years there was a huge shortage of currency, which gave way to a widespread movement in favor of the acceptance of the banknote of the Bank of Mexico. The advance was very significant if we consider the history of distrust that the population had about paper money, so the task carried out by the central bank was crucial. In fact, Alberto J. Pani considered inflation "Mexico's supreme problem."4 With the new Law and the beginning of a period of free floating, so that the exchange rate reached its equilibrium level, the Bank was authorized to buy gold at market prices. Consequently, the central bank's reserve was increased and one of the main channels for the issuance of 3 See Bank of Mexico, Annual Report, 1927. 4 See Pani, Alberto J. (1955). "Mexico's Supreme Problem." Essay on constructive criticism of financial policy. Manuel Casas Press. Mexico 4 ticket. This formula, together with the recovery of the economy after the great contraction of 1929, rooted paper money as the main payment instrument in the country. As a result, during those first ten years inflation was virtually zero.5 II. Defence and loss of progress achieved (1936-1954) In early 1936, Finance Secretary Eduardo Suarez contacted lawyer Miguel Palacios Macedo to entrust him with the drafting of a new Organic Law for the Bank of Mexico. Palacios Macedo set out to prepare an order to ensure that price stability was consolidated in the country. Or to put it in that character's own words, that the operation of the Bank of Mexico "was free of any inflationary note."6 His anti-inflationary motivation and the attempt to strengthen the independence of the Bank of Mexico made the Organic Law of the Bank of Mexico promulgated in 1936 a nuisance for the authorities of the Federal Executive, since an ambitious public spending program had been established that could only be financed from the central bank. Thus began the era of government financing through the Bank of Mexico. The central bank's defense reaction was led by its general director, Luis Montes de Oca, and the same drafter of the Law, Palacios Macedo. In the debate with government representatives, Palacios Macedo wrote a memorandum explaining the inflationary and destabilizing implications of financing the government: The very gravity that from one moment to the next can cover the situation demands a treatment as serious as the evils and dangers that this situation carries in germ. Hence, they are not more or less ingenious files 5 See Oxford Economic History Database, available in / 6 See Explanatory Memorandum, Organic Law of the Bank of Mexico, 1936. 5 but real remedies, background remedies, those that must be applied... To this end, what matters above all is to radically suppress the phenomena of deficit economy that have been occurring and worsening with alarming frequency and intensity and that in summary consist in the fact that the country seems determined to lead a 'life train' that is not related to the real value of its national income and the need to form capital for its economic development.7 However, the inflationism represented by the Government prevailed: in 1938 reforms to the Organic Law of the Bank of Mexico were sent to Congress to remove from its articles the ceilings and locks established for monetary expansion and, specifically, the credit that the central bank could grant to the Government. As a result, fiscal and monetary expansionism was resorted to on several occasions in the following years with the aim of boosting economic growth. The main consequence was that, with this approach, the country led to several balance of payments crises, highlighting the devaluations of 1938, 1948-49 and 1954. In addition, in the period from 1936 to 1954, average annual inflation reached almost 10 percent. The former general director himself, Luis Montes de Oca, wrote in 1954: It should not be forgotten that currency conditions are reflected throughout the economy and that the economy is reflected in currency conditions... The lack of security in the value of the national currency is today the most urgent problem and the one that has the greatest impact on the life of the country. If a solution is to be found within the term and to the extent demanded by the public, it will be essential to subordinate economic policy and the other acts of the Government to the convenience of having a healthy and stable currency. This purpose would not be a mere wish, because a policy of this scope can be printed with all the effectiveness that is needed. 8 7 See Palacios Macedo, Miguel "Dos Documentos sobre Politica Hacendaria Mexicana" in Problemas Agricolas e Industriales de Mexico, volume V, number I, January-March, 1953. 8 See Montes de Oca, Luis. (1954). Five Articles on Monetary Devaluation. Mexico 6 III. Low inflation (1955-1972) Maintaining exchange rate stability required strict monetary discipline, which was applied by the general director of the Bank of Mexico from 1952 to 1970, Rodrigo Gomez. This manager always opposed what he called "a path of roses", consisting of obtaining money in the short term and spending it, since for him the only way to sustained progress is saving, productive investment and persistent effort. Nor did he accept the idea that "the stabilization sought by the central bank slows down the country's progress."9 To achieve price stability, Rodrigo Gomez and the Secretary of Finance from 1958 to 1970, Antonio Ortiz Mena, applied responsible fiscal discipline and prudent monetary policy. Regarding the latter, both agreed on the convenience of getting the Bank of Mexico to operate without political interference. This stage would be called that of a "charismatic autonomy" or de facto, which depended mainly on the great negotiating capacity and leadership of Rodrigo Gomez.10 The authorities of the Bank of Mexico, headed by Rodrigo Gomez, observed with great care the behavior of two variables: the price level and the international reserve. If inflation showed signs of rising above the level it presented in the United States or the international reserve fell continuously, monetary containment measures were immediately taken: the reserve requirement rate was raised to send a signal of greater restriction. In this way, Mexico became a pioneer in the application of the "monetary approach to the balance of payments".11 9 See Petricioli, Gustavo. (1991). "Semblanza de un gran mexicano" in Rodrigo Gomez: Vida y Obra. Bank of Mexico and Fondo de Cultura Economica. Mexico. 10 See Turrent, Eduardo. (2005). "The three stages of the autonomy of the Central Bank in Mexico". Economic Analysis 20, 43: 47-81. 11 Among other aspects, this approach focuses on the analysis of the total balance of payments rather than one of its parts (e.g. the trade balance) and interprets the problems of the balance of payments. 7 Rodrigo Gomez and Ortiz Mena were the architects of the exceptional period of the Mexican economy known as Stabilizing Development characterized by high economic growth and low inflation. During those years the average annual inflation was close to 3 percent, very similar to that of the United States. IV. Stability interrupted (1973-1995) The next 23 years were a period of great threats to monetary stability. In that period, practically everything that had been gained in the fight against inflation was lost. The main cause was the fiscal policy applied in the country. Public finances proved to be very vulnerable to external shocks and under a highly unstable financial environment. Thus, very high and volatile government spending, and very high public debt, especially dollar-denominated debt, caused recurrent crises characterized by recession, high inflation and devaluations. During the seventies and early eighties the fiscal deficit was largely financed by the central bank. Beginning in 1973, such financing began to rise rapidly, as did inflation, and led the country to a significant devaluation three years later. The monetization of the fiscal deficit continued until 1982, when a severe external debt crisis erupted. Rising international interest rates and falling oil prices exposed the fragility of public finances. In April 1983 inflation closed at just over 117 percent. payments as monetary phenomena; see Johnson, Harry G. (1977) "The Monetary Approach to Balance of Payments Theory and Policy: Explanation and Policy Implications", Economica 44, 175: 217-229. For the case of Mexico, see Gil Diaz, Francisco (1991) "Don Rodrigo Gomez, Visionary of the Economy" in Rodrigo Gomez: Vida y Obra. Bank of Mexico and Fondo de Cultura Economica. Mexico. 8 Although the practice of monetary financing of the fiscal deficit was abandoned in 1983, in the next four years a measure was put in place that would cause even more inflation: a continuous slide of the peso against the dollar to keep it "competitive". The intention was to counter the fall in oil revenues and promote exports and, presumably, economic growth. However, the dynamism of economic activity was very low: average annual growth from 1983 to 1987 was 1.0 percent, and the highest inflation records in modern history reached almost 180 percent. This dishonourable mark on inflation was observed in February 1988, despite the fact that a couple of months earlier, at the end of 1987, an economic stability pact had been established; such an annual inflation rate was a deferred consequence of inadequate economic policies prior to the stability pact. In fact, this social agreement, based on a fixed exchange rate regime, made it possible to lower annual inflation to 7% in 1994. However, various political developments and a fragile dollar-linked public debt strategy, among other factors, led the country into a new currency crisis and a considerable rebound in inflation. Annual inflation in December 1995 was almost 52 per cent, bringing the average during this period to 41 per cent. V. Towards permanent price stability (1996- ) The legal autonomy of the Bank of Mexico entered into force in April 1994 and was established on solid bases as it was embodied in article 28 of the Constitution. It was determined that the priority objective of the central bank is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. The conduct of monetary policy was entrusted to a Governing Board whose members are replaced in a staggered manner and cannot be dismissed at their discretion. 9 The most important thing about autonomy is that it allows to avoid that in the country there are new episodes of inflation with all its pernicious consequences. The greatest danger posed by the forces of inflation stems from their subtlety, as Rodrigo Gomez once called it.12 Arguments for using the ability to create money to boost growth or to expand the supply of loanable funds can be seductive to many ears. The truth is that if economic growth could be accelerated just by creating means of payment and throwing them into circulation, poor countries would no longer exist in the world. The transition in Mexico to the current monetary policy regime called "Inflation Targets" was gradual from its announcement in 2000. This regime requires the central bank to guide its actions by goals announced to the public. In addition, for monetary policy to work, the exchange rate needs to be flexible. Thus, the anchor of the strategy is the commitment of the central bank to achieve its own goal, which in the case of Mexico is 3 percent per year since the end of 2003. The results of this approach have been encouraging as suggested by the fact that annual inflation rose from 19 per cent in January 1999 to an average moderately above 4 per cent from 2004 to date. Conclusion The road to price stability in Mexico has been full of challenges and vicissitudes. Outbreaks of inflation characterized prolonged periods of our history, severely affected the well-being of the population and curbed the chances of further economic development. Thus, this brief tour of the history of the Bank of Mexico indicates that monetary discipline is not easy to achieve and, in addition, that when it is lost it is even more difficult to recover. A common root 12 See "The Bank of Mexico and Inflationary Policy" in Texts by Rodrigo Gomez. (1967). Grafica Panamericana, Mexico. 10 of economic instability has been the subordination of monetary policy to other misguided objectives. The recent progress in combating inflation is positive and puts Mexico close to consolidating price stability. The target of 3 per cent annual inflation is perfectly achievable, as evidenced by the experience of other economies and that of the country itself. The fight against inflation is an ongoing task that requires broad social support, sound public finances as well as a firm commitment and a lot of perseverance. 11
text_original: La interminable tarea de la estabilidad de precios Palabras del Dr. Manuel Snchez Gonzlez, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico, en el Ciclo de Conferencias Financieras del ITESM Campus Ciudad de Mxico el 26 de enero de 2011. Agradezco mucho la invitacin del Tecnolgico de Monterrey Campus Ciudad de Mxico para participar en su ciclo de conferencias financieras. Como exalumno del Tec, es un enorme gusto regresar a esta institucin y poder compartir con ustedes algunas ideas relacionadas con la economa mexicana y, en particular, con el Banco de Mxico. Recientemente nuestro banco central celebr su aniversario 85. Por eso la ocasin es propicia para reflexionar sobre sus desafos y sus logros. La historia del Banco de Mxico puede analizarse desde diversas perspectivas. Quisiera explorar hoy una de ellas: la lucha por la estabilidad de precios; sta ha sido, usualmente, poco atendida por analistas e investigadores. La inflacin es un mal que vulnera a las familias y a la economa. El crecimiento sostenido en el nivel general de precios, que es la definicin de la inflacin, deteriora el poder adquisitivo del ingreso. Para adaptarse a este fenmeno las personas ponen en marcha mecanismos que, obviamente sin proponrselo, desperdician recursos productivos, lo que genera ineficiencias. Un ejemplo es el cambio constante de los precios en las tiendas y los restaurantes. Adems, las personas y los negocios buscan formas financieras o contractuales para protegerse contra este peligro. Los que no lo hacen o no lo pueden hacer, como los pensionados y asalariados, son especialmente afectados por la inflacin. Por otra parte, cuando aumenta persistentemente la inflacin tiende a ser ms voltil, lo que implica una mayor incertidumbre y dificulta an ms las decisiones de ahorro e inversin. 1 Si bien quienes han dirigido al Banco de Mxico han tenido siempre la intencin de luchar contra la inflacin, la estabilidad de precios no necesariamente ha sido la caracterstica que ha marcado a todas las etapas de la economa nacional desde que el Banco abri sus puertas en 1925. A continuacin har un breve recuento de los episodios ms sobresalientes de la lucha en favor de la estabilidad de precios en nuestro pas. En ciertas circunstancias las condiciones y la estrategia de este combate fueron desfavorables y ello explica, en trminos generales, los periodos de alta inflacin en Mxico. Toda vez que la bsqueda de una estabilidad de precios permanente es, por definicin, una tarea inacabada que se extiende hasta nuestros das, el tema de esta pltica tiene una actualidad plena. Por conveniencia, distinguir cinco pocas. I. Primeras contribuciones hacia la estabilidad de precios (19251935) La Revolucin mexicana afect severamente al pas en todos los sentidos. Existan billetes y monedas en circulacin de diversos emisores, por ejemplo Venustiano Carranza, Francisco Villa, Emiliano Zapata y los bancos estatales. Todo ello desprestigi el uso del dinero. En 1914 se registr una elevada inflacin debido al aumento descontrolado del circulante y al desabasto de mercancas. Como reflejo de este ambiente, entre julio de 1914 y julio de 1915 el maz aument 2400 por ciento, el frijol 2200 por ciento, el arroz 1420 por ciento, el azcar 940 por ciento y la harina 900 por ciento. En 1916 el Gobierno recurri a cobrar los impuestos en oro y plata, y no en papel moneda, lo cual dio una seal al pblico de que los billetes ya no tenan valor. En los aos posteriores, el pas estuvo desmonetizado y sin un marco institucional de la banca, lo que llev a un desorden monetario con un alto costo para la poblacin.1 1 Vase Del ngel Mobarak, Gustavo A. (2010). La socializacin del costo econmico de la Revolucin Mexicana en Inflacin y Revolucin: La experiencia mexicana de 1912 a 1917. Banco de Mxico. Mxico. 2 El camino hacia el orden monetario inici en septiembre de 1925 con la fundacin del Banco de Mxico. Una de las primeras acciones clave en defensa de la estabilidad de precios fue encabezada por el presidente de su Consejo de Administracin, Manuel Gmez Morin y el secretario de Hacienda, Alberto J. Pani. Ambos coincidieron en la conveniencia de que el banco central tuviera independencia. La tesis de Gmez Morin al respecto fue que de esta manera se podra tener una moneda sana y estable.2 Debe aclararse que desde 1925 hasta 1994 el Banco oper con diversos regmenes de tipo de cambio predeterminado que se interrumpan por periodos de flotacin de la moneda. Estas suspensiones eran resultado de polticas monetarias incongruentes que lo eran, en gran medida, por el financiamiento del gasto pblico por parte del instituto central. A su vez, este fenmeno convertir al Banco de Mxico en la fuente de financiamiento del gasto gubernamental a travs de la emisin de moneda deriva de la falta de independencia respecto del Gobierno que padeci el Banco durante ese largo periodo. A principios de 1927 se registraron dos tendencias particularmente desfavorables para el banco central. La primera fue la inclinacin de la administracin del Banco a llevarlo cada vez ms por el camino de la banca comercial y descuidar su vocacin como banco central. La segunda estuvo relacionada con un agudo debilitamiento de la independencia de la institucin al permitirse que el financiamiento al Gobierno superase el lmite legal establecido. La principal expresin de la batalla dada por Gmez Morin para evitar esas dos tendencias se materializ en su informe a la Asamblea de Accionistas en 1928: El Banco de Mxico no se fund para dar al Pas un nuevo banco colocado en el mismo nivel de las dems instituciones de crdito de la Repblica. No 2 Vase Mndez Reyes, Jess. (2001). El Pensamiento Econmico de Manuel Gmez Morn (1913 1936). Facultad de Economa, UNAM. Mxico. 3 podr funcionar plenamente, en consecuencia, ni rendir los frutos que de l deben esperarse, mientras no llegue a tener el carcter que debe serle propio: el de una institucin central en el conjunto de los cuerpos econmicos del Pas.  La ley de su creacin da al Banco el carcter de institucin central de emisin y redescuento, confindole as la doble tarea de mantener en Mxico una moneda sana y de regular el comercio bancario, el funcionamiento de las instituciones de crdito que deben ser el exponente y el resumen de la organizacin econmica de la Repblica.3 En 1931 y 1932 se dio la primera gran reforma del Banco de Mxico. En julio de 1931 se desmonetiz el oro en el pas por medio de la promulgacin de la Ley Monetaria y en marzo de 1932 se llev a cabo otro cambio de envergadura: una reforma a la mencionada Ley Monetaria y la promulgacin de una nueva Ley Orgnica para el Banco de Mxico. Con estas modificaciones el Banco dej de operar como banco comercial y se consolid como banco central, esto es, adquiri la exclusividad de la emisin monetaria y se hizo obligatoria la asociacin de los bancos comerciales con el instituto central. Durante esos aos se present una enorme escasez de moneda, lo que dio paso a un movimiento generalizado a favor de la aceptacin del billete del Banco de Mxico. El avance fue muy significativo si consideramos los antecedentes de desconfianza que tena la poblacin sobre el papel moneda por lo que la tarea realizada por el banco central fue crucial. De hecho, Alberto J. Pani consideraba a la inflacin como el problema supremo de Mxico.4 Con la nueva Ley y el inicio de un periodo de libre flotacin, para que el tipo de cambio alcanzara su nivel de equilibrio, se autoriz al Banco a comprar oro a precios de mercado. En consecuencia, aument la reserva del banco central y se consolid uno de los principales canales para la emisin de 3 Vase Banco de Mxico, Informe Anual, 1927. 4 Vase Pani, Alberto J. (1955). El problema supremo de Mxico. Ensayo de crtica constructiva de la poltica financiera. Imprenta Manuel Casas. Mxico 4 billete. Esta frmula, junto con la recuperacin de la economa despus de la gran contraccin de 1929, arraig al papel moneda como el principal instrumento de pago en el pas. Como resultado, durante esos primeros diez aos la inflacin fue virtualmente nula.5 II. Defensa y prdida de los avances alcanzados (19361954) A principios de 1936, el secretario de Hacienda Eduardo Surez contact al abogado Miguel Palacios Macedo para encomendarle la redaccin de una nueva Ley Orgnica para el Banco de Mxico. Palacios Macedo se propuso preparar un ordenamiento para garantizar que en el pas se consolidara la estabilidad de precios. O para decirlo en las propias palabras de ese personaje, que la operacin del Banco de Mxico estuviese libre de toda nota inflacionista.6 Su motivacin antiinflacionaria y el intento de fortalecer la independencia del Banco de Mxico convirtieron a la Ley Orgnica del Banco de Mxico promulgada en 1936 en una molestia para las autoridades del Ejecutivo Federal, ya que se haba establecido un ambicioso programa de gasto pblico que slo podra financiarse con cargo al banco central. Se inici as la poca del financiamiento del Gobierno a travs del Banco de Mxico. La reaccin de defensa del banco central la encabezaron su director general, Luis Montes de Oca, y el mismo redactor de la Ley, Palacios Macedo. En el debate con los representantes del Gobierno, Palacios Macedo escribi un memorndum explicando las implicaciones inflacionistas y desestabilizadoras del financiamiento al Gobierno: La gravedad misma que de un momento a otro puede revestir la situacin reclama un tratamiento tan serio como los males y peligros que esa situacin lleva en germen. De ah que no sean expedientes ms o menos ingeniosos 5 Vase Oxford Economic History Database, disponible en http://oxlad.qeh.ox.ac.uk/ 6 Vase Exposicin de Motivos, Ley Orgnica del Banco de Mxico, 1936. 5 sino remedios reales, remedios de fondo, los que deben aplicarse Para ello, lo que importa sobre todo es suprimir radicalmente los fenmenos de economa deficitaria que vienen producindose y agravndose con frecuencia e intensidad alarmantes y que en sntesis consisten en que el Pas parece empeado en llevar un tren de vida que no guarda relacin con el valor real de su renta nacional y con la necesidad de formar los capitales para su desarrollo econmico.7 No obstante, prevaleci el inflacionismo representado por el Gobierno: en 1938 se enviaron al Congreso reformas a la Ley Orgnica del Banco de Mxico para remover de su articulado los topes y candados establecidos para la expansin monetaria y, en lo especfico, el crdito que el banco central pudiera conceder al Gobierno. Como resultado, en los siguientes aos se recurri en diversas ocasiones al expansionismo fiscal y monetario con la pretensin de impulsar el crecimiento econmico. La consecuencia principal fue que, con ese enfoque, el pas desemboc en varias crisis de balanza de pagos, destacando las devaluaciones de 1938, 194849 y 1954. Adems, en el lapso que corre de 1936 a 1954 la inflacin promedio anual alcanz casi 10 por ciento. El propio ex director general, Luis Montes de Oca, escribi en 1954: No debe olvidarse que las condiciones de la moneda se reflejan en toda la economa y que la economa se refleja en las condiciones de la moneda La falta de seguridad en el valor de la moneda nacional constituye hoy da el problema ms urgente y el que repercute con mayores consecuencias en la vida del Pas. Si quiere hallrsele solucin dentro del trmino y en la medida que demanda el pblico, ser indispensable subordinar la poltica econmica y los dems actos del Gobierno a la conveniencia de tener una moneda sana y estable. No sera este propsito un mero buen deseo, porque a una poltica de estos alcances puede imprimrsele toda la efectividad que se necesite. 8 7 Vase Palacios Macedo, Miguel Dos Documentos sobre Poltica Hacendaria Mexicana en Problemas Agrcolas e Industriales de Mxico, volumen V, nmero I, enero marzo, 1953. 8 Vase Montes de Oca, Luis. (1954). Cinco Artculos sobre la Devaluacin Monetaria. Mexico 6 III. Inflacin baja (19551972) El mantenimiento de la estabilidad del tipo de cambio requera de una disciplina monetaria estricta, la cual fue aplicada por el director general del Banco de Mxico de 1952 a 1970, Rodrigo Gmez. Este directivo siempre se opuso a lo que llamaba un camino de rosas, consistente en obtener dinero a corto plazo y gastarlo, ya que para l la nica va hacia el progreso sostenido la forman el ahorro, la inversin productiva y el esfuerzo persistente. Tampoco aceptaba la idea de que la estabilizacin que busca el banco central frena el progreso del pas.9 Para alcanzar la estabilidad de precios, Rodrigo Gmez y el Secretario de Hacienda de 1958 a 1970, Antonio Ortiz Mena, aplicaron una disciplina fiscal responsable y una poltica monetaria prudente. Respecto a esta ltima, ambos coincidieron en la conveniencia de conseguir que el Banco de Mxico operase sin interferencias polticas. A esta etapa se le llamara como la de una autonoma carismtica o de facto, la cual dependi principalmente de la gran capacidad negociadora y del liderazgo de Rodrigo Gmez.10 Las autoridades del Banco de Mxico, encabezadas por Rodrigo Gmez, observaban con gran cuidado el comportamiento de dos variables: el nivel de precios y la reserva internacional. Si la inflacin mostraba indicios de aumentar por arriba del nivel que presentaba en Estados Unidos o la reserva internacional descenda de manera continua, inmediatamente se tomaban medidas de contencin monetaria: se elevaba la tasa del encaje legal para mandar una seal de mayor restriccin. De esta manera, Mxico se convirti en un pionero de la aplicacin del enfoque monetario de la balanza de pagos.11 9 Vase Petricioli, Gustavo. (1991). Semblanza de un gran mexicano en Rodrigo Gmez: Vida y Obra. Banco de Mxico y Fondo de Cultura Econmica. Mxico. 10 Vase Turrent, Eduardo. (2005). Las tres etapas de la autonoma del Banco Central en Mxico. Anlisis Econmico 20, 43: 4781. 11 Entre otros aspectos, este enfoque se centra en el anlisis de la balanza pagos total en lugar de una de sus partes (por ejemplo, la balanza comercial) e interpreta los problemas de la balanza de 7 Rodrigo Gmez y Ortiz Mena fueron los artfices del periodo excepcional de la economa mexicana conocido como Desarrollo Estabilizador caracterizado por un elevado crecimiento econmico y una inflacin baja. Durante esos aos la inflacin promedio anual fue cercana al 3 por ciento, muy similar a la de Estados Unidos. IV. Estabilidad interrumpida (19731995) Los siguientes 23 aos fueron un periodo de grandes amenazas para la estabilidad monetaria. En ese lapso se perdi prcticamente todo lo que se haba ganado en la lucha contra la inflacin. La principal causa fue la poltica fiscal aplicada en el pas. Las finanzas pblicas resultaron ser muy vulnerables ante choques externos y bajo un ambiente financiero sumamente inestable. As, un gasto gubernamental muy elevado y voltil, y una deuda pblica muy alta, especialmente deuda denominada en dlares, provocaron crisis recurrentes caracterizadas por recesin, inflacin alta y devaluaciones. Durante los aos setenta y principios de los ochenta el dficit fiscal fue financiado en gran medida por el banco central. A partir de 1973 dicho financiamiento empez a aumentar rpidamente, al igual que la inflacin, y condujo al pas a una devaluacin significativa tres aos despus. La monetizacin del dficit fiscal se mantuvo hasta 1982, cuando estall una severa crisis de deuda externa. La elevacin de las tasas de inters internacionales y los decrecientes precios del petrleo expusieron la fragilidad de las finanzas pblicas. En abril de 1983 la inflacin cerr en poco ms de 117 por ciento. pagos como fenmenos monetarios; vase Johnson, Harry G. (1977) The Monetary Approach to Balance of Payments Theory and Policy: Explanation and Policy Implications, Economica 44, 175: 217229. Para el caso de Mxico, vase Gil Daz, Francisco (1991) Don Rodrigo Gmez, Visionario de la Economa en Rodrigo Gmez: Vida y Obra. Banco de Mxico y Fondo de Cultura Econmica. Mxico. 8 Aunque la prctica del financiamiento monetario del dficit fiscal se abandon en 1983, en los siguientes cuatro aos se puso en marcha una medida que causara an ms inflacin: un deslizamiento continuo del peso frente al dlar para mantenerlo competitivo. La intencin era contrarrestar la cada de los ingresos petroleros y promover las exportaciones y, presumiblemente, el crecimiento econmico. Sin embargo, el dinamismo de la actividad econmica fue muy bajo: el crecimiento promedio anual de 1983 a 1987 fue del 1.0 por ciento, y se tuvieron los registros de inflacin ms elevados de la historia moderna que alcanzaron casi un 180 por ciento. Esta deshonrosa marca en materia de inflacin se observ en febrero de 1988 no obstante que un par de meses antes, a finales de 1987, se haba establecido un pacto de estabilidad econmica; tal tasa de inflacin anual fue una consecuencia diferida de las inadecuadas polticas econmicas anteriores al pacto de estabilidad. De hecho, este acuerdo social, basado en un rgimen de tipo de cambio fijo, hizo posible el descenso de la inflacin anual hasta 7 por ciento en 1994. No obstante, diversos acontecimientos polticos y una frgil estrategia de deuda pblica ligada al dlar, entre otros factores, condujeron al pas a una nueva crisis de la moneda y a un repunte considerable de la inflacin. La inflacin anual en diciembre de 1995 fue casi 52 por ciento, con lo que el promedio durante esta poca alcanz 41 por ciento. V. Hacia la estabilidad permanente de los precios (1996 ) La autonoma legal del Banco de Mxico entr en vigor en abril de 1994 y se estableci sobre bases solidas al quedar plasmada en el artculo 28 Constitucional. Se determin que el objetivo prioritario del banco central es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. La conduccin de la poltica monetaria se encarg a una Junta de Gobierno cuyos integrantes se reemplazan de manera escalonada y no pueden ser destituidos discrecionalmente. 9 Lo ms importante de la autonoma es que permite evitar que en el pas haya nuevos episodios de inflacin con todas sus consecuencias perniciosas. El mayor peligro que presentan las fuerzas de la inflacin deriva de su sutileza, como alguna vez la calific Rodrigo Gmez.12 Los argumentos en favor de que se utilice la capacidad de crear dinero para impulsar el crecimiento o para ampliar la oferta de fondos prestables pueden resultar seductores para muchos odos. La verdad es que si el crecimiento econmico se pudiera acelerar con tan slo crear medios de pago y arrojarlos a la circulacin ya no existiran en el mundo pases pobres. La transicin en Mxico al actual rgimen de poltica monetaria denominado Objetivos de Inflacin fue gradual a partir de su anuncio en el ao 2000. Este rgimen requiere que el banco central guie sus acciones por metas anunciadas al pblico. Adems para que funcione la poltica monetaria, se necesita que el tipo de cambio sea flexible. As, el ancla de la estrategia es el compromiso del banco central por alcanzar la propia meta, la cual en el caso de Mxico es 3 por ciento anual desde finales de 2003. Los resultados de este enfoque han sido alentadores como lo sugiere el hecho de que la inflacin anual pas de 19 por ciento en enero de 1999 a un promedio moderadamente superior a 4 por ciento desde 2004 a la fecha. Conclusin El camino hacia la estabilidad de los precios en Mxico ha estado lleno de desafos y vicisitudes. Los brotes de inflacin caracterizaron prolongados perodos de nuestra historia, afectaron severamente el bienestar de la poblacin y frenaron las posibilidades de un mayor desarrollo econmico. As, este breve recorrido por la historia del Banco de Mxico indica que la disciplina monetaria no es nada fcil de alcanzar y, adems, que cuando sta se llega a perder es todava mucho ms difcil de recuperar. Una raz comn 12 Vase El Banco de Mxico y la Poltica Inflacionaria en Textos de Rodrigo Gmez. (1967). Grfica Panamericana, Mxico. 10 de la inestabilidad econmica ha sido la subordinacin de la poltica monetaria a otros objetivos mal encaminados. El reciente avance en el combate de la inflacin es positivo y coloca a Mxico cerca de consolidar la estabilidad de precios. La meta del 3 por ciento de inflacin anual es perfectamente alcanzable, como lo demuestra la experiencia de otras economas y la del propio pas. La lucha contra la inflacin es una tarea continua que requiere un amplio apoyo social, finanzas pblicas sanas as como un firme compromiso y mucha perseverancia. 11

Title: Japan: millenary modernity
text: Japan: millenary modernity Words of Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico at the opening of the exhibition Japan to 400 Years of the Hasekura Mission: A Commercial and Cultural Vision Mexico City, November 27, 2014 It is an honor to participate in this traditional toast organized by the library of the Bank of Mexico, and to have the presence of His Excellency the Ambassador of Japan, Akira Yamada. On this occasion, the building of Bolivar 19 serves as a venue to meet and appreciate this magnificent exhibition on Japanese history and culture. The importance of the Hasekura mission Throughout 2014, we have been celebrating 400 years of the Hasekura mission, which is considered Japan's first commercial and diplomatic approach to New Spain. This expedition, despite natural obstacles and changes in the Japanese political environment, marks a desire for international openness and symbolically initiates the relationship between the two nations. The Hasekura mission was a formidable undertaking, sponsored by the Lord of Sendai, Masamune Date, with the consent of the Tokugawa shogunate. Date sponsored a vessel, headed by the samurai Tsunenaga Hasekura, whose first destination was the port of Acapulco. He then continued his journey to Spain, France and Italy, to establish economic and political relations, as well as to spread Christianity. The mission did not achieve its mission at that time. When, after seven years, Hasekura returned to Japan, the political and religious environment had changed radically, Christianity was already repressed and a certain tendency to isolationism had been strengthened. However, this pioneering feat had already sown the roots of great Japanese diplomacy. 1 The heroic characteristics of this exploration and its various adventures are not only an extraordinary historical event, but have fed the narrative imaginary. For example, the great writer Shusaku Endo published in 1980 his novel The Samurai, based on the Hasekura mission. Since that initial contact until now, multiple developments have occurred in Japan-Mexico relations. We can say that, centuries later, the ideal of the Hasekura mission has been fulfilled. Today, we are two dynamic, forward-thinking nations and we maintain vigorous ties. For example, bilateral trade, facilitated by the Agreement for the Strengthening of the Economic Partnership, in force since 2005, is around 20 billion dollars annually. In addition, Japan is the first Asian investor in Mexico and about 800 companies from that nation have a presence here. Much could be said about the new potential for cooperation, which is increased by Mexico's structural reforms, which are in the process of being implemented. However, on this very special occasion, I would like to focus on a coincidence that we have maintained over the centuries, and that lies, more than in the material field, in that of the spirit. Empathy for culture Indeed, Japan and Mexico have two cultures that have been decisively inserted into modernity, and that have not forgotten their millenary roots. Our countries have known 2 assimilate various influences and adapt to the rhythm of the times, without affecting their most profoundly distinctive features. Despite being one of the paradigms of economic progress, Japan remains faithful to many traditions that make it unique. For example, courtesy, consideration for the other, attachment to the family and respect for the elderly are fundamental features of their social relationships. It is a worldview that combines individual initiative and entrepreneurial spirit with a strong sense of belonging to the community. Since the nineteenth century, Japanese culture has exerted a fruitful irradiation in the West and has had a special weight in Mexico. Let us remember the fondness for Japan of certain Mexican intellectual elites of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, which gravitated in various aspects of art and customs. This influence ranges from the fascination of the poet Jose Juan Tablada for the calligraphic character and the capacity of synthesis of Japanese poetry, to the art of the florist or the design of the gardens in some large houses. In fact, and to illustrate these happy coincidences of culture, it should be noted that in 1952, when our governments agreed to resume relations, Mexico appointed a young diplomat as charge d'affaires to Japan, with the mission of carrying out all the operational tasks to install our Embassy in that country.1 1 See Asiain, A. (2014), "Octavio Paz, diplomat in Japan." In Revista Mexicana de Politica Exterior, special issue 2014, dedicated to Octavio Paz, pp. 53-77. 3 The young man, impressed by Japan, immediately wrote to a friend, that the brief days of his stay: (...) they have made me glimpse a very beautiful country and an admirable, courteous and cheerful people and for whom poetry, painting and life do not constitute separate worlds.2 That diplomat of modest rank was Octavio Paz, who spent a short but decisive stay in Japan, which consolidated his former fascination with this country and expanded his universalist vocation. This fruitful exchange has been mutual. The great Japanese novelist Kenzaburo Oe, also a Nobel laureate and author of some of the most moving autobiographical records of contemporary literature, such as the novel A Personal Question, was a visiting professor at El Colegio de Mexico during 1976. The fusion of art and everyday life in Japan Paz was right when he pointed out that in Japan there is no difference between art and everyday life, because the fusion of civilization and nature, as well as the cult of beauty, are reflected in each and every one of the customs of that nation. From architecture to calligraphy, through poetry, painting, theater, decoration or design, we can observe a harmonization with the cycles and 2 See Paz, O. (2008), Wandering Gardens: Letters to J.C. Lambert. Barcelona: Seix-Barral. p. 12. 4 natural materials, a sober rituality and a sense of altruism and gratitude to life. Of course, in the refined asceticism that characterizes part of the Japanese character, a renunciation should not be sought, but, on the contrary, a call to enjoy the joys of the world and its great and small wonders. As evident is the famous traveling poet of the seventeenth century, Matsuo Basho, who on his way was able to marvel at a banquet, at the majesty of a temple or at the bud of an herb, with a traditional verse like this: Sacred place: on the green leaves the sun rests or another such as: I've walked a long way to see you, cherry blossom.3 The exhibition that we inaugurate today illustrates the will for harmony and the search for transcendence in the simplest and most spontaneous. In addition to the informative material about the Hasekura mission, we will see a collection of utensils of daily life, 3 See Basho, M. (2011), On the Way to Oku and Other Travel Diaries. Version of Jesus Aguado, Barcelona: DVD Ediciones, pp. 60 and 91. 5 decorative objects, toys and dolls. All of them respond to an elaborate procedure and use ancient techniques, as is the case of hakata dolls, made of clay, and kokeshi, of wood. The use of these articles responds to protocols related to the season of the year, the range or gender of the user. Thus, the most common activities, such as eating, grooming or playing, acquire an ancestral weight and a deep meaning. Likewise, we will have a music concert for koto, this ancient and versatile Japanese string instrument, which will be conducted by the master Yoshiko Nishimura. She lives in Mexico and with her group, Kasou Kai, has created a fertile fusion school that combines koto with other instruments and repertoires. Undoubtedly, both the exhibition and the concert will transport us to the spell that life in Japan implies. I invite you to enjoy this immersion in a culture where an ordinary day recovers its ritual dimension, all acts have a meaning, and both words and silences are revealing. We will appreciate in its fullness the forms and sounds that will accompany us in this evening and that, without a doubt, will make us leave this enclosure a little more conscious and a little happier. 6
text_original: Japn: modernidad milenaria Palabras de Manuel Snchez Gonzlez Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico en la inauguracin de la exposicin Japn a 400 Aos de la Misin Hasekura: Una Visin Comercial y Cultural Mxico, D.F. 27 de noviembre de 2014 Es un honor participar en este tradicional brindis organizado por la biblioteca del Banco de Mxico, y contar con la presencia del excelentsimo Embajador de Japn, Akira Yamada. En esta ocasin, el edificio de Bolvar 19 nos sirve de sede para reunirnos y apreciar esta magnfica exposicin sobre la historia y la cultura japonesa. La importancia de la misin Hasekura A lo largo de 2014, hemos estado celebrando los 400 aos de la misin Hasekura, que se considera el primer acercamiento comercial y diplomtico por parte de Japn a la Nueva Espaa. Dicha expedicin, pese a los obstculos naturales y los cambios en el ambiente poltico japons, marca una voluntad de apertura internacional e inicia de manera simblica la relacin entre las dos naciones. La misin Hasekura constituy una formidable empresa, auspiciada por el seor de Sendai, Masamune Date, con la anuencia del shogunato Tokugawa. Date patrocin una embarcacin, encabezada por el samuri Tsunenaga Hasekura, cuyo primer destino fue el puerto de Acapulco. Luego prosigui su viaje a Espaa, Francia e Italia, para establecer relaciones econmicas y polticas, as como para extender el cristianismo. La misin no logr su cometido en ese momento. Cuando, tras siete aos, Hasekura regres a Japn, el entorno poltico y religioso haba cambiado radicalmente, el cristianismo ya era reprimido y se haba fortalecido cierta tendencia al aislacionismo. Sin embargo, esta hazaa pionera ya haba sembrado las races de la gran diplomacia japonesa. 1 Las caractersticas heroicas de esta exploracin y sus diversas peripecias no slo son un extraordinario acontecimiento histrico, sino que han alimentado el imaginario narrativo. Por ejemplo, el gran escritor Shsaku End public en 1980 su novela El samuri, basada en la misin Hasekura. Desde ese contacto inicial hasta ahora, han ocurrido mltiples acontecimientos en las relaciones entre Japn y Mxico. Podemos decir que, siglos despus, el ideal de la misin Hasekura se ha cumplido. Hoy, somos dos naciones dinmicas, con visin de futuro, y mantenemos vnculos vigorosos. Por ejemplo, el comercio bilateral, facilitado por el Acuerdo para el Fortalecimiento de la Asociacin Econmica, en vigor desde 2005, ronda los 20 mil millones de dlares anuales. Adems, Japn es el primer inversionista asitico en Mxico y cerca de 800 empresas de esa nacin tienen presencia aqu. Mucho podramos extendernos sobre los nuevos potenciales para la cooperacin, que se acrecientan con las reformas estructurales de Mxico, en proceso de implementacin. Sin embargo, en esta ocasin tan especial, quisiera enfocarme en una coincidencia que hemos mantenido a lo largo de los siglos, y que radica, ms que en el terreno material, en el del espritu. La empata por la cultura En efecto, Japn y Mxico poseen dos culturas que se han insertado con decisin en la modernidad, y que no han olvidado sus races milenarias. Nuestros pases han sabido 2 asimilar diversas influencias y adaptarse al ritmo de los tiempos, sin afectar sus rasgos ms profundamente distintivos. Pese a ser uno de los paradigmas del progreso econmico, Japn sigue fiel a muchas tradiciones que lo hacen nico. Por ejemplo, la cortesa, la consideracin hacia el otro, el apego a la familia y el respeto a los mayores son rasgos fundamentales de sus relaciones sociales. Se trata de una cosmovisin que combina la iniciativa individual y el nimo empresarial con el acendrado sentido de pertenencia a la comunidad. A partir del siglo XIX, la cultura japonesa ha ejercido una fructfera irradiacin en Occidente y ha tenido un peso especial en Mxico. Recordemos la aficin por Japn de ciertas lites intelectuales mexicanas de finales del siglo XIX y principios del XX, que gravit en diversos aspectos del arte y las costumbres. Dicha influencia va desde la fascinacin del poeta Jos Juan Tablada por el carcter caligrfico y la capacidad de sntesis de la poesa japonesa, hasta el arte de la florera o el diseo de los jardines en algunas grandes casonas. De hecho, y para ilustrar estas felices coincidencias de la cultura, cabe resaltar que en 1952, cuando nuestros gobiernos acordaron reanudar relaciones, Mxico design a un joven diplomtico como encargado de negocios ante Japn, con la misin de realizar todas las tareas operativas para instalar nuestra Embajada en ese pas.1 1 Vase Asiain, A. (2014), Octavio Paz, diplomtico en Japn. En Revista Mexicana de Poltica Exterior, nmero especial 2014, dedicado a Octavio Paz, pp. 53-77. 3 El joven, impresionado por Japn, escribi de inmediato a un amigo, que los breves das de su estancia: () me han hecho vislumbrar un pas muy hermoso y un pueblo admirable, corts y alegre y para el que poesa, pintura y vida no constituyen mundos aparte.2 Ese diplomtico de rango modesto, era Octavio Paz, quien pas una corta pero decisiva estancia en Japn, la cual consolid su antigua fascinacin por este pas y ampli su vocacin universalista. Este fecundo intercambio ha sido mutuo. El gran novelista japons Kenzabur e, tambin premio Nobel y autor de algunos de los registros autobiogrficos ms conmovedores de la literatura contempornea, como la novela Una cuestin personal, fue profesor visitante en El Colegio de Mxico durante 1976. La fusin del arte y la vida cotidiana en Japn Paz tena razn cuando sealaba que en Japn no hay una diferencia entre el arte y la vida cotidiana, pues la fusin de la civilizacin y la naturaleza, as como el culto a la belleza, se reflejan en todas y cada una de las costumbres de esa nacin. Desde la arquitectura hasta la caligrafa, pasando por la poesa, la pintura, el teatro, la decoracin o el diseo, podemos observar una armonizacin con los ciclos y 2 Vase Paz, O. (2008), Jardines errantes: Cartas a J.C. Lambert. Barcelona: Seix-Barral. p. 12. 4 materiales naturales, una sobria ritualidad y un sentido de altruismo y agradecimiento a la vida. Por supuesto, en el refinado ascetismo que caracteriza parte del carcter japons no debe buscarse una renuncia, sino, al contrario, un llamado a disfrutar los goces del mundo y sus grandes y pequeos prodigios. Como lo hace evidente el clebre poeta viajero del siglo XVII, Matsuo Bash, quien en su trayecto lo mismo era capaz de maravillarse ante un banquete, ante la majestuosidad de un templo o ante el brote de una hierba, con un verso tradicional como este: Lugar sagrado: sobre las hojas verdes se posa el sol u otro como: He caminado bastante para verte, cerezo en flor.3 La muestra que hoy inauguramos ilustra la voluntad de armona y la bsqueda de trascendencia en lo ms sencillo y espontneo. Adems del material informativo sobre la misin Hasekura, veremos una coleccin de utensilios de la vida diaria, 3 Vase Bash, M. (2011), De camino a Oku y otros diarios de viaje. Versin de Jess Aguado, Barcelona: DVD Ediciones, pp. 60 y 91. 5 objetos decorativos, juguetes y muecos. Todos ellos responden a un elaborado procedimiento y emplean tcnicas antiqusimas, como es el caso de los muecos hakata, de arcilla, y los kokeshi, de madera. La utilizacin de estos artculos responde a protocolos relacionados con la estacin del ao, el rango o gnero del usuario. As, las actividades ms habituales, como comer, asearse o jugar, adquieren un peso ancestral y un profundo significado. Igualmente, tendremos un concierto de msica para koto, este antiguo y verstil instrumento de cuerda japons, que ser conducido por la maestra Yoshiko Nishimura. Ella reside en Mxico y con su grupo, Kasou Kai, ha creado una fecunda escuela de fusin que combina el koto con otros instrumentos y repertorios. Sin duda, tanto la exposicin como el concierto nos transportarn al sortilegio que implica la vida en Japn. Los invito a disfrutar de esta inmersin en una cultura donde una jornada ordinaria recupera su dimensin ritual, todos los actos tienen un significado, y tanto las palabras como los silencios son reveladores. Apreciaremos en su plenitud las formas y sonidos que nos acompaarn en esta velada y que, sin duda, nos harn salir de este recinto un poco ms conscientes y un poco ms felices. 6

Title: Delivery of the eleventh edition of the Contacto-BANXICO Award
text: Remarks by Mr. Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the delivery of the Eleventh Edition of the Contacto-BANXICO Award. Mexico City, November 25, 2019 Irene Espinosa Cantellano, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico; Jonathan Heath, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico; Jessica Serrano, Director of Financial Education and Cultural Development at the Bank of Mexico; Distinguished members of the Jury of the Contacto-BANXICO Award; Dear finalists of the Contact-BANXICO Award and esteemed University Links; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 It gives me a lot to attend this award ceremony of the Eleventh Edition of the Contacto-BANXICO contest. This is the dean of our competitions and has the purpose of strengthening the contact of the central bank with institutions and students of upper secondary education. Significance of the Contact-BANXICO Award For the Bank of Mexico, communication with society is crucial so that there is a better understanding of its objectives, mandates and results, as well as the concrete benefits, at the individual and social level, that its work entails. That is why, over the years, a broad communication strategy has been forged with messages and information for various audiences, from children who begin their learning to the most specialized academics and economic agents. For their ongoing academic training, for their imminent vocational definition and incorporation into the labor market and for their influence on their family and social environment, high school and education students 2 they constitute a segment of the public whose dialogue is of particular interest to the Bank of Mexico. For this reason, various forms of linkage have been established with this segment, such as chairs, diplomas and the University Links program, whose participants as we have seen have become true strategic allies in the dissemination of the Bank. Of course, within these forms of connection with the student community, our ContactoBANXICO and Reto BANXICO contests occupy an important place, which have become a catalyst for reflection and a hotbed of talents. Throughout its history, the Contacto-Banxico Award has met three primary objectives:  To constitute an attractive vehicle to bring the Bank of Mexico closer to the segment that attends upper secondary education;  Encourage teachers and students at the baccalaureate level to know the purposes, priority objective and operation of the Bank of Mexico; 3  Encourage schools, teachers and students to review and use the wide range of information disseminated by the Bank of Mexico and that serves all kinds of purposes, from preparing a school work to making a practical economic decision. As is known, in the Contacto-BANXICO contest the participants form teams of three or four students with a teacher from the same institution. These teams produce a written paper or a video on a select topic of economics, finance or monetary policy that is proposed in each edition. The work of the teams is thoroughly evaluated by a first-class jury, all of them recognized experts in economic matters and from institutions of excellence in academia, banking or the public sector. This jury selects the 6 best works (3 for each category: written work or video). The selected teams are presented in Mexico City to argue their work before a Qualifying Jury. 4 The Theme of the 2019 Edition of this contest was entitled "Financial inclusion in one click" and sought to promote reflection on:  How technology facilitates access to the financial system for the entire population;  What are the social advantages of participating in the financial system and,  What are electronic means of payment and what is their role in financial inclusion. This topic seemed ideal because, on the one hand, the revolution in digital technologies provides a unique opportunity to advance in the pending tasks of financial inclusion and, on the other, you were literally born in the digital world and are spontaneous and experienced users of this type of technology. Technology and financial inclusion Until a few years ago, problems such as geographical dispersion; the high costs of operating on a small scale or the difficulty of designing specialized products for certain strata that were 5 Profitable ones made it unfeasible for formal financial services to spread to certain sites or social sectors. This condemned significant portions of the population to lack these services or, alternatively, to resort to informal instances, generally more expensive and less secure. This lack of inclusion exacerbates inequalities and wastes potential initiatives and talents. Today, thanks to the technological revolution, there are tools to bridge the gap and address the lags in terms of inclusion and financial education. Technology can break down geographical barriers and lower costs to promote access to financial services on sites that were previously unaffordable or cost-effective. Technology also makes it possible to design financial services that better fit the needs of different segments of the public. Since the universe of internet or smartphone users outpaces users of formal financial services, there is a huge 6 potential for those who use these instruments on a daily basis to access the benefits of formal financial services. The policies of the Bank of Mexico to link technology and inclusion An example of the way in which technology can be used to promote financial inclusion is the platform called Cobro Digital (CoDi), which means a significant advance in the operations of purchase-sale or payment of services in our country, as well as a great opportunity to expand financial inclusion. The CoDi is a platform that allows you to carry out 24 hours a day, seven days a week, expeditiously, and without commissions, electronic payment operations through mobile devices. Using the infrastructure of the Interbank Electronic Payments System, SPEI, operated by the Bank of Mexico, and with the use of QR and NFC technologies for making electronic payments, the CODI allows anyone who has a smartphone and opens a bank account, to make electronic payments in seconds, free of charge and with the highest security standards. 7 The CoDi implies for its users enormous benefits in terms of cost reduction, security and transparency. To mention a few examples, it will have a very positive impact for small businesses that will be able to receive immediate electronic payments; it will also lead to the streamlining and simplification of many day-to-day transactions and the reduced possibility of illicit or corrupt by making payments that are recorded electronically. This payment scheme, which can mean a turning point in terms of economic efficiency and financial inclusion in our country, is just one example of the way in which technology can be directed to create an environment more conducive to the deployment of the spirit of improvement and the initiatives of all Mexicans. I am sure that you young students, natural users of digital technology and future professionals, will be able to imagine many other ways to channel technology for the benefit of society and, in a single click, open new expectations and solutions to recurring problems. 8 Friends participating in the Contacto-BANXICO Award; Ladies and gentlemen: Throughout the eleven editions of this contest, we have seen the professionalism and creativity of the participants in the contest and we feel very proud and enriched by the response to this call. In these eleven years, for example, we have received the participation of schools from all the States of the Mexican Republic, more than 11 thousand teams have been registered and we have reviewed more than 6 thousand works. In particular, in this edition 857 teams were registered (3,505 people, 54% women and 46% men). 206 registered schools participated, of which 54% were public and 46% private and 525 materials were received (412 written and 113 videos). For us, the response of the students to this call is very satisfactory. For the jurors, whom I would especially like to acknowledge, deliberation involves a workload and an always difficult dilemma, given the abundant participation, as well as the excellent academic and intellectual level and creativity, of the texts and videos. 9 Participants. For the Bank of Mexico, as always, it is a pride to convene some of the most brilliant high school students in the country and undertake this enriching and fruitful exercise of reflection. Thank you very much and congratulations. 10
text_original: Palabras del Lic. Alejandro Daz de Len, Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, durante la entrega de la Dcima Primera Edicin del Premio Contacto-BANXICO. Ciudad de Mxico, 25 de noviembre de 2019 Irene Espinosa Cantellano, Subgobernadora del Banco de Mxico; Jonathan Heath, Subgobernador del Banco de Mxico; Jessica Serrano, Directora de Educacin Financiera y Fomento Cultural del Banco de Mxico; Distinguidos miembros del Jurado del Premio Contacto-BANXICO; Estimados finalistas del Premio Contacto-BANXICO y estimados Enlaces Universitarios; Seoras y seores: 1 Me da mucho acudir a esta ceremonia de premiacin de la Dcima Primera Edicin del certamen Contacto-BANXICO. Este es el decano de nuestros concursos y tiene el propsito de estrechar el contacto del banco central con las instituciones y estudiantes de educacin media superior. Significacin del Premio Contacto-BANXICO Para el Banco de Mxico es crucial la comunicacin con la sociedad a fin de que haya una mejor comprensin de sus objetivos, mandatos y resultados, as como de los beneficios concretos, en el plano individual y social, que conlleva su labor. Por eso, a lo largo de los aos, se ha venido forjando una amplia estrategia de comunicacin con mensajes e informacin para diversas audiencias, desde los nios que comienzan su aprendizaje hasta los acadmicos y agentes econmicos ms especializados. Por su formacin acadmica en marcha, por su inminente definicin vocacional e incorporacin al mercado laboral y por su influencia en su medio familiar y social, los estudiantes de bachillerato y educacin 2 superior constituyen un segmento del pblico cuya interlocucin interesa especialmente al Banco de Mxico. Por eso, se han establecido diversas formas de vinculacin con este segmento, como son ctedras, diplomados y el programa de Enlaces Universitarios, cuyos participantes como hemos visto se han convertido en verdaderos aliados estratgicos en la difusin del Banco. Por supuesto, dentro de estas formas de vinculacin con la comunidad estudiantil ocupan un lugar importante nuestros concursos ContactoBANXICO y Reto BANXICO, que se han convertido en un catalizador para la reflexin y en un semillero de talentos. A lo largo de su historia, el Premio Contacto-Banxico ha atendido tres objetivos primordiales:  Constituir un vehculo atractivo para acercar al Banco de Mxico al segmento que cursa la educacin media superior;  Estimular a profesores y estudiantes de nivel bachillerato a que conozcan las finalidades, objetivo prioritario y operacin del Banco de Mxico; 3  Incentivar a escuelas, profesores y estudiantes a revisar y utilizar la amplia gama de informacin que difunde el Banco de Mxico y que sirve para todo tipo de propsitos, desde elaborar un trabajo escolar hasta tomar una decisin econmica prctica. Como es sabido, en el concurso Contacto-BANXICO los participantes forman equipos de tres o cuatro alumnos con un profesor de su misma institucin. Estos equipos elaboran un trabajo escrito o un video sobre algn tema selecto de economa, finanzas o poltica monetaria que se propone en cada edicin. Los trabajos de los equipos son evaluados exhaustivamente por un jurado de primer nivel, todos ellos expertos reconocidos en materia econmica y provenientes de instituciones de excelencia de la academia, la banca o el sector pblico. Este jurado selecciona a los 6 mejores trabajos (3 por cada categora: trabajo escrito o video). Los equipos seleccionados se presentan en la Ciudad de Mxico para argumentar sus trabajos ante un Jurado Calificador. 4 El Tema de la Edicin 2019 de este certamen se titul Inclusin financiera en un clic y buscaba propiciar la reflexin sobre:  Cmo la tecnologa facilita el acceso al sistema financiero a toda la poblacin;  Cules son las ventajas sociales de participar en el sistema financiero y,  Qu son los medios electrnicos de pago y cul es su papel en la inclusin financiera. Este tema nos pareci idneo porque, por un lado, la revolucin en las tecnologas digitales brinda una oportunidad nica para avanzar en las tareas pendientes de la inclusin financiera y, por el otro, ustedes literalmente nacieron en el mundo digital y son usuarios espontneos y avezados de ste tipo de tecnologas. Tecnologa e inclusin financiera Hasta hace algunos aos, problemas como la dispersin geogrfica; los altos costos de operar a pequea escala o la dificultad para disear productos especializados para determinados estratos que fueran 5 rentables hacan inviable que los servicios financieros formales se extendieran a determinados sitios o sectores sociales. Ello condenaba a porciones significativas de la poblacin a no contar con estos servicios o, bien, a recurrir a instancias informales, generalmente ms costosas y menos seguras. Esta falta de inclusin agrava las desigualdades y desaprovecha iniciativas y talentos potenciales. Hoy, gracias a la revolucin tecnolgica, se cuenta con herramientas para zanjar la brecha y atender los rezagos en materia de inclusin y educacin financiera. La tecnologa puede romper barreras geogrficas y abatir costos para promover el acceso a los servicios financieros en sitios que anteriormente no resultaban asequibles o rentables. Asimismo, la tecnologa permite disear servicios financieros que se ajusten mejor a las necesidades de los distintos segmentos del pblico. Dado que el universo de usuarios del internet o los telfonos inteligentes supera a los usuarios de servicios financieros formales, existe un gran 6 potencial para que quienes utilizan estos instrumentos cotidianamente accedan a las ventajas de los servicios financieros formales. Las polticas del Banco de Mxico para enlazar tecnologa e inclusin Un ejemplo de la forma en que puede utilizarse la tecnologa para promover la inclusin financiera es la plataforma denominada Cobro Digital (CoDi), que significa un avance significativo en las operaciones de compra-venta o pago de servicios en nuestro pas, as como una gran oportunidad para ampliar la inclusin financiera. El CoDi es una plataforma que permite realizar las 24 horas del da, los siete das de la semana, de manera expedita, y sin comisiones, operaciones electrnicas de pago a travs de dispositivos mviles. Utilizando la infraestructura del Sistema de Pagos Electrnicos Interbancarios, SPEI, que opera el Banco de Mxico, y con el uso de las tecnologas QR y NFC para la realizacin de pagos electrnicos, el CODI permite a cualquiera que tenga un telfono inteligente y abra una cuenta bancaria, realizar pagos electrnicos en segundos, de manera gratuita y con los ms altos estndares de seguridad. 7 El CoDi implica para sus usuarios enormes beneficios en materia de abatimiento de costos, seguridad y transparencia. Por mencionar algunos ejemplos, tendr un impacto muy positivo para los pequeos comercios que podrn recibir pagos electrnicos inmediatos; tambin propiciar la agilizacin y simplificacin de muchas transacciones cotidianas y la menor posibilidad de ilcitos o corrupcin al generalizarse los pagos que se registran electrnicamente. Este esquema de pagos, que puede significar un punto de inflexin en materia de eficiencia econmica e inclusin financiera en nuestro pas, es slo un ejemplo de la manera en que la tecnologa puede dirigirse para crear un ambiente ms propicio para el despliegue del nimo de superacin y las iniciativas de todos los mexicanos. Estoy seguro que ustedes los jvenes estudiantes, usuarios naturales de la tecnologa digital y futuros profesionistas, podrn imaginar muchas otras formas de encauzar la tecnologa en beneficio de la sociedad y, en un solo clic, abrir nuevas expectativas y soluciones a problemas recurrentes. 8 Amigos participantes del Premio Contacto-BANXICO; Seoras y seores: A lo largo de las once ediciones de este concurso, hemos constatado el profesionalismo y la creatividad de los participantes en el certamen y nos sentimos muy orgullosos y enriquecidos por la respuesta a esta convocatoria. En estos once aos, por ejemplo, hemos recibido la participacin de escuelas de todos los Estados de la Repblica Mexicana, se han inscrito ms de 11 mil equipos y hemos revisado ms de 6 mil trabajos. En particular, en esta edicin se inscribieron 857 equipos (3,505 personas, 54% mujeres y 46% hombres). Participaron 206 escuelas inscritas de las cuales el 54 % fueron pblicas y 46% privadas y se recibieron 525 materiales (412 escritos y 113 videos). Para nosotros, la respuesta de los estudiantes a esta convocatoria es muy satisfactoria. Para los jurados, a quienes quiero reconocer especialmente, la deliberacin implica una carga de trabajo y un dilema siempre difcil, dada la abundante participacin, as como el excelente nivel acadmico e intelectual y la creatividad, de los textos y videos 9 participantes. Para el Banco de Mxico, como siempre, es un orgullo convocar a algunos de los estudiantes de bachillerato ms brillantes del pas y emprender este enriquecedor y fecundo ejercicio de reflexin. Muchas gracias y muchas felicidades. 10

Title: The communion of art
text: The Communion of Art Words of Manuel Sanchez Gonzalez Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico in the exhibition Art and Inclusion John Langdon Down Foundation, A.C. Banco de Mexico Mexico, Mexico City June 26, 2014 Good evening ladies and gentlemen. For the Bank of Mexico it is a great pride to host the exhibition "Art and inclusion" with works by artists from the Mexican School of Art Down, sponsored by the John Langdon Down Foundation. The Bank of Mexico seeks to stimulate cultural activities that, in addition to guaranteeing a high artistic quality, imply a positive social impact. Therefore, we are especially pleased to host this exhibition in which excellent artists with different abilities give us an example of initiative, talent and creative joy. I give the warmest and most cordial welcome to the creators who accompany us, to their families and to all of you who, today, have the opportunity to open up to the communion of art, beyond any border. Art beyond the artistic Art constitutes both a means of individual expression and a space for social encounter. Through art it is possible to overcome the most diverse physical and cultural barriers, whether of time, languages or customs, and establish revealing forms of communication. Thus, art manages to transcend the particular circumstances of human experience and usually generates affinities between very different beings. 1 Hence the importance of understanding the function of art not only as an object of delight and aesthetic contemplation, but also as an instrument to promote empathy and inclusion among various human groups. Indeed, in addition to its intrinsic aesthetic function, art, both in its practice and in its appreciation, promotes the social integration and emotional well-being of individuals. The use of art as an auxiliary instrument in different forms of psychological and language therapy, or the usufruct of this activity in some experiments of regeneration of the social fabric in nations ravaged by violence, are examples of the practical potential of the artistic. In particular, it has been widely proven that art can contribute to more fully developing faculties and promote the socialization and integration of people with disabilities, such as those living with Down syndrome. Therefore, at present many care centers for people with different abilities have experts in the plastic, musical or performing arts, as well as workers trained in different artistic therapies, who are aware that art is a vigorous means of self-knowledge and improvement. 2 The Mexican School of Art Down, sponsored by the John Langdon Down Foundation that for several decades has provided comprehensive care to people living with the syndrome, arises precisely from this conviction in the therapeutic and transformative power of art. As stated on its website, this School has gone from being a modest workshop to becoming a real hotbed of plastic talents, which has presented multiple exhibitions in various spaces in the country and abroad. Now, the Bank of Mexico has the opportunity to show some examples of the outstanding work of its students. Different art?
