Title: Presentation of the new era of the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance (REMEF) of the Research Foundation of the Mexican Institute of Finance Executives (IMEF)
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the presentation of the new era of the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance (REMEF) of the Research Foundation of the Mexican Institute of Finance Executives (IMEF) July 2, 2015 ? Mr. President of the IMEF Research Foundation, Accountant Jose Antonio Quesada, ? Teacher Nelly Molina, National President of the Mexican Institute of Finance Executives (IMEF), ? Doctor Gerardo Dubcovsky, Senior Editor of the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance (REMEF), ? Mr. Contador Carlos Mendez, Managing Partner of PwC Mexico, sponsoring firm of this important research journal, ? Ladies and gentlemen, Good evening. First of all, congratulations. In my own name and also on behalf of the entire Bank of Mexico I can only extend my widest recognition to the very important work carried out by the IMEF Research Foundation and specifically to the very valuable contribution represented by the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance (REMEF), in this new era, for the progress and well-being of Mexico. Unfortunately, it is not common in our country for trade union organizations of the relevance and representativeness of the IMEF to value and attend with such enthusiasm and dedication to research and knowledge. 1 scientist in economics and finance. That is why we must congratulate, support and applaud this effort. Scientific knowledge in the field of economics and finance constitutes a major input for the development of a country, especially when such knowledge comes from rigorous and careful research and when it is applied to scrutinize current issues related to public policy decisions and actions. This has been a permanent conviction in the Bank of Mexico, since its foundation 90 years ago, hence the weight that our Central Institute has always given to economic research and hence, also, the prestige that the Bank of Mexico has achieved in this matter. In fact, the findings arising from the work of the General Directorate of Economic Research are a constant input for the decision-making of the Governing Board of the Bank itself. We are pleased, therefore, that the knowledge of our economic reality is enriched by the results of this initiative of the IMEF Research Foundation, which is the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance. Every six months, the journal has published works of great relevance, as well as detailed analyses on the effectiveness of the Basel III agreements to mitigate risks in derivative positions related to "commodities" or basic goods, as well as research on transparency and corporate governance or on the possible impact of delinquency indicators on the granting of bank loans, to mention just a few of the recent articles. 2 I am certain that in the future the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance, by increasing its research collection, will be able to consolidate itself as an indispensable reference, both for deliberation prior to decision-making in the field of public policies, and for evaluating with objectivity and rigor the effectiveness and efficiency of the same. All this, as Jose Antonio Quesada pointed out in a recent editorial of the journal itself, with a determined practical spirit, always seeking that research in the economic-financial field is applied and applicable research. Thus, the Mexican Institute of Finance Executives (IMEF) will continue to play a leading role in promoting economic and financial research in our country. This is not only through the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance, to which I have already referred and which represents an important forum for the dissemination of research carried out by professionals in these areas in our country on issues of finance, economics and business activity. In addition to the above, I would like to emphasize that the IMEF has also contributed significantly to the promotion and dissemination of economic and financial research through the publication of specialized books and through the realization of the Financial Research Congress of the IMEF, an event that allows a fruitful exchange of ideas and experiences between researchers. Likewise, we cannot fail to mention the IMEF-EY Financial Research Award (Ernst & 3 Young) which, given the prestige it has acquired over time, has been an important incentive for the promotion of research in the economic and financial field in our country. Likewise, having a category dedicated to thesis work and applied research contributes to encourage research activities among students and young professionals. Generally speaking, such research helps us to achieve a deeper and more complete understanding of the functioning of the economy and, in particular, of the financial sector. Such knowledge, together with the judgment and experience of decision-makers in both the private and public sectors, can be extremely beneficial for the design of more efficient business and financial practices, as well as better public policies that translate into benefits for the population as a whole. I would like to emphasize that this is precisely the objective to which any research agenda must be oriented, whether in the economic-financial field or in other areas of knowledge. In this regard, I welcome the fact that the IMEF successfully promotes both the implementation and dissemination of research projects from different fronts. I would also like to stress the importance of redoubling our efforts to make further decisive progress in that direction. In particular, I would like to emphasize an area where we can work together the private sector, the public sector and institutions. 4 academics with the purpose of continuing to promote top-level economic and financial research in Mexico. As we all know, such research uses economic and financial data as one of its main inputs. Therefore, the availability of quality databases is a factor of primary importance for the development of research projects that are timely, relevant and of quality. There is no doubt that to the extent that we have more timely and accurate information and more extensive and detailed databases, we will be able to carry out an economic and financial research that is even more relevant and profitable for the productive sector, including of course the financial sector, for the public sector and in general for Mexican society as a whole. In this context, it should be noted that due to the accelerated and remarkable progress in information technology that has been achieved in recent years around the world, it is now possible to have large databases containing increasingly detailed and accurate information (Big Data). Databases that just a few decades ago were simply unthinkable, but that today are feasible and a reality in various countries. This, from the perspective of economic and financial research, opens a unique window of opportunity to carry out novel research projects. In particular, they allow us to have better elements to answer questions that have long been 5 is part of the economic-financial research agenda. Questions and questions for which satisfactory answers have not yet been found but which continue to capture the attention of academics and policymakers. In addition to the above, they also provide an opportunity to raise new questions, as well as explore issues that due to lack of adequate economic and financial data had not been able to be addressed with sufficient analytical rigor in the past. All this allows us to be in a position to assess more accurately the impact of certain events and/or policies on the economy and, in particular, on the financial sector. In this context, economic and financial research in Mexico cannot and should not remain oblivious to the advantages offered by this technological revolution that the world is experiencing in terms of information technologies. In this sense, Banco de Mexico, like other institutions in our country, has a firm commitment to collect and process economic and financial information in a timely manner and thereby generate better databases. It is important to continue moving in this direction and to redouble our efforts to lay the foundations for better research. To the extent that the above contributes to the design and implementation of good public policies, as well as best business and financial practices, we will be in a position to promote a better functioning of the economy in general and the financial system in particular. Seeking that the above translates into greater well-being for the population of our country. 6 Regarding the practical approach to scientific knowledge, I would like to share with you tonight some reflections on the characteristics that define the environment in which public policies are designed and implemented. In the first place, it is an imperfect environment, very different from the theoretical and ideal framework of the "ceteris paribus", far from the assumption in which all the diverse variables of which we are studying remain the same, unperturbed. On the contrary, one of the roots of the complexity of the practical world in which public policies operate is precisely the dynamic and multiple interrelationship, often unfathomable, of numerous variables, many of them known only partially or whose behavior is by definition unpredictable. In this way, it would be naive to expect that public officials, when making decisions, would mechanically resort to this or that theoretical model and follow a kind of rigid form known in advance. Moreover, often those of us with such responsibilities are confronted with unexplored, unknown, totally new territories. For example, the global financial crisis that erupted and dispersed throughout the world in September 2008, at the time of the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers, suddenly put us in unprecedented situations for which there were no solutions embodied in advance in a theoretical model or in a paradigm of economic science. Faced with this, unusual decisions were also taken dictated by a sense of urgency, such as those followed by the main advanced economies relaxing 7 extraordinarily their monetary policy stances. This certainly prevented a definitive collapse of the global financial system by providing it with liquidity never before seen and never before sought as a deliberate purpose, but it also introduced us to unknown seas and confronted us with entirely new challenges. In a way, at that time the best reference to which decision-makers could resort was to avoid the mistakes that were made decades ago during the Great Economic Depression, mistakes - by the way - that humanity as a whole could only identify as such "ex post facto", or, as we would say colloquially, "a bull past". I refer specifically to the mistake of acting pro-cyclically by restricting liquidity. There is no doubt that the president of the federal reserve banking system of the United States at that time, Ben Bernanke, had such a reference in mind, being as he is one of the most thorough connoisseurs of the episode of the Great Depression and its aftermath. However, the Great Depression is still a distant reference and only comparable in a very limited way to the situation of 2008, not to mention the extraordinary multiplicity and complexity of financial instruments and mechanisms characteristic of the global economy of the XXI century and that, obviously, were not even sketched by the most visionary of theorists in the 30s of the last century. I turn to this example precisely because we continue to sail in those unknown seas, now faced with the challenge of how a normal monetary policy will be restored while activity. 8 global economic recovery; the challenge involves defining, largely on the fly and with a more than attentive look at numerous economic and financial indicators, the speed, sequence, pace and even the way to communicate as clearly as possible the steps to follow to markets justifiably troubled by uncertainty. In those we are also in the Bank of Mexico as a monetary authority that, being national, cannot escape, however, the condition of strong interdependence that we keep with the economy of the United States. But while it is true that we are facing an unprecedented situation that will be decisive for the world's economy, it is also true that today, in Mexico, we have many more and better elements than in past decades to face uncertainty. And we have that arsenal largely because economic research and reflection on grim experiences of past crises have allowed us, as a country, to design and build stronger and more reliable institutional arrangements. Such is the case, of course, of the structural reform that more than 20 years ago gave full autonomy to the Bank of Mexico, which includes particularly fortunate institutional arrangements, such as the collegial nature of its Governing Board (which fosters a rich exchange of views, perspectives and knowledge to inform decision-making), as well as the staggered sequence in the appointment of its members, which guarantees the independence of criteria of those who make up the Board with respect to the guidelines 9 specific action that the public administration could have in turn. I have no doubt that this solid institutional arrangement - which today is one of the ingredients that give Mexico greater strength and confidence in an extremely uncertain and volatile international economic environment - is largely the product of reflection and research applied intelligently, and with practical sense, to the economy and finance. An additional reflection in this same line is that - unlike the theoretical world, from which models and paradigms emerge in principle immovable, as well as univocal definitions - in the practical world of public policies there are no perfect and unique solutions, but more or less opportune responses, more or less correct, more or less favorable to stability and economic growth. Therefore, precisely because there are no single or perfect answers, it is so valuable that in matters such as monetary policy, deliberation and decision-making they are based on a collegiate body and therefore, also, it is so important that the markets and the general public know, through the dissemination that we make of the minutes of the Governing Board on the occasion of monetary policy decisions, the exchange of views and arguments among the members of the Board, as well as the weightings that give rise to the final decisions. A careful reading of the most recent of these minutes, for example, allows us to notice that above differences of opinion and opinions, those of us who are members of the Governing Board of the Bank of 10 Mexico fully agrees that - given that our priority objective is to ensure price stability - the Bank must act in a timely manner in the event that would unanchor the expectations of low and stable inflation that we have today. And this, even regardless of the monetary policy actions taken by the Federal Reserve of the United States. I have no doubt that for the markets and for the general public to know this type of clear definitions about the course of action that we will eventually follow, thanks to the dissemination of our minutes, generates certainties that compensate - to a large extent - the accumulation of uncertainties caused by the fact that the world economy navigates seas not yet known. And these institutional arrangements that build trust - and ultimately allow for a better functioning economy and, with it, greater well-being - ultimately come, as I have already said, from the findings of economic research. That is to say: of useful but rigorous and grounded knowledge such as those disseminated and will continue to be disseminated by the Mexican Journal of Economics and Finance. Congratulations and thank you very much. 11

En trminos generales, dicha investigacin nos ayuda a lograr un entendimiento ms profundo y completo sobre el funcionamiento de la economa y, en particular, del sector financiero. Todo ello permite estar en condiciones de evaluar con mayor precisin el impacto de ciertos eventos y/o polticas sobre la economa y, en particular, sobre el sector financiero. En este contexto, la investigacin econmica y financiera en Mxico no puede ni debe permanecer ajena a las ventajas que ofrece esta revolucin tecnolgica que en materia de tecnologas de la informacin est viviendo el mundo. En este sentido, Banco de Mxico, al igual que otras instituciones en nuestro pas, tiene un compromiso firme por recolectar y procesar de manera oportuna informacin econmicofinanciera y con ello generar mejores bases de datos. Es importante seguir avanzando en esta direccin y redoblar esfuerzos para sentar las bases que permitan una mejor investigacin. En la medida en que lo anterior contribuya al diseo e implementacin de polticas pblicas idneas, as como de mejores prcticas empresariales y financieras, estaremos en condiciones de propiciar un mejor funcionamiento de la economa en general y del sistema financiero en particular. Buscando que lo anterior se traduzca en un mayor bienestar para la poblacin de nuestro pas. 6 Respecto del enfoque prctico del conocimiento cientfico quisiera compartir con ustedes esta noche algunas reflexiones acerca de las caractersticas que definen el entorno en el cual se disean y ponen en marcha las polticas pblicas. En primer lugar, se trata de un entorno imperfecto, muy diferente del entramado terico e ideal del ceteris paribus, muy lejos del supuesto en el que todas las variables diversas de la que estamos estudiando permanecen iguales, imperturbables. Por el contrario, una de las races de la complejidad del mundo prctico en el que se desenvuelven las polticas pblicas es precisamente la interrelacin dinmica y mltiple, frecuentemente inabarcable, de numerosas variables, muchas de ellas conocidas slo parcialmente o cuyo comportamiento es por definicin impredecible. De esta forma, pecara de ingenuidad quien esperase que los funcionarios pblicos, al momento de tomar decisiones, recurriesen mecnicamente a tal o cual modelo terico y siguiesen a pe juntillas una suerte de formulario rgido conocido de antemano. Ms an, con frecuencia quienes tenemos tales responsabilidades nos enfrentamos a territorios inexplorados, desconocidos, totalmente nuevos. Por ejemplo, la crisis financiera global que estall y se dispers por todo el orbe en septiembre de 2008, al momento de la quiebra de Lehman Brothers, nos puso de sbito ante situaciones inditas para las cuales no haba soluciones plasmadas de antemano en un modelo terico o en un paradigma de la ciencia econmica. Ante ello, se tomaron tambin decisiones inslitas dictadas por un sentido de urgencia, como fueron las que siguieron las principales economas avanzadas relajando de 7 manera extraordinaria sus posturas de poltica monetaria. Ello evit ciertamente un colapso definitivo del sistema financiero global dotndolo de una liquidez nunca antes vista y nunca antes buscada como un propsito deliberado, pero tambin nos introdujo en mares ignotos y nos enfrent a desafos totalmente nuevos. En cierta forma, en esos momentos la mejor referencia a la cual pudieron recurrir los tomadores de decisiones fue evitar los errores que se cometieron dcadas atrs durante la Gran Depresin econmica, errores  por cierto- que la humanidad en su conjunto slo pudo identificar como tales ex post facto, o, como diramos coloquialmente, a toro pasado. Me refiero especficamente al error de actuar de forma pro-cclica restringiendo la liquidez. No cabe duda que el presidente del sistema de bancos de la Reserva Federal de los Estados Unidos en ese momento, Ben Bernanke, tuvo en mente tal referencia, siendo como es uno de los conocedores ms minuciosos del episodio de la Gran Depresin y de sus secuelas. Sin embargo, la Gran Depresin no deja de ser una referencia lejana y slo equiparable de forma muy limitada a la situacin del ao 2008, por no mencionar la extraordinaria multiplicidad y complejidad de instrumentos y mecanismos financieros caractersticos de la economa global del siglo XXI y que, obviamente, ni siquiera estaban bosquejados por el ms visionario de los tericos en los aos 30 del siglo pasado. Recurro a este ejemplo justamente porque seguimos navegando en esos mares ignotos, ahora frente al desafo de cmo habr de restaurarse una poltica monetaria normal al tiempo que la actividad 8 econmica mundial se recupera; el desafo implica definir, en buena medida sobre la marcha y con una mirada ms que atenta sobre numerosos indicadores econmicos y financieros, la velocidad, la secuencia, el ritmo y hasta el modo de comunicar lo ms claramente posible los pasos a seguir a unos mercados justificadamente atribulados por la incertidumbre. En esas estamos tambin nosotros en el Banco de Mxico como autoridad monetaria que, siendo nacional, no puede sustraerse, sin embargo, a la condicin de fuerte interdependencia que guardamos con la economa de los Estados Unidos. Pero si bien es cierto que estamos ante una situacin indita que ser decisiva para la economa del mundo, tambin es cierto que hoy, en Mxico, contamos con muchos ms y mejores elementos que en dcadas pasadas para hacer frente a la incertidumbre. Y contamos con ese arsenal en gran medida gracias a que la investigacin econmica y la reflexin sobre experiencias aciagas de crisis pasadas nos han permitido, como pas, disear y construir arreglos institucionales ms slidos y confiables. Tal es el caso, desde luego, de la reforma estructural que hace ms de 20 aos dot de autonoma plena al Banco de Mxico, que incluye arreglos institucionales particularmente afortunados, como es el carcter colegiado de su Junta de Gobierno (lo que propicia un rico intercambio de pareceres, perspectivas y conocimientos para fundamentar la toma de decisiones), as como la secuencia escalonada en la designacin de sus miembros, lo que garantiza la independencia de criterio de quienes integran la Junta respecto de las orientaciones 9 especficas de accin que pudiese tener la administracin pblica en turno. No me cabe duda que este slido arreglo institucional  que hoy da es uno de los ingredientes que le dan mayor solidez y confianza a Mxico en un entorno econmico internacional sumamente incierto y voltil-, es en buena medida producto de la reflexin y la investigacin aplicadas inteligentemente, y con sentido prctico, a la economa y a las finanzas. Una reflexin adicional en esta misma lnea es que  a diferencia del mundo terico, del cual surgen modelos y paradigmas en principio inamovibles, as como definiciones unvocas-, en el mundo prctico de las polticas pblicas no existen soluciones perfectas y nicas, sino respuestas ms o menos oportunas, ms o menos correctas, ms o menos favorecedoras de la estabilidad y del crecimiento econmico. Por ello, justamente porque no hay respuestas nicas o perfectas, es tan valioso que en asuntos tales como la poltica monetaria, la deliberacin y la toma de decisiones se sustenten en un rgano colegiado y por ello, tambin, es tan importante que los mercados y el pblico en general conozcan, a travs de la difusin que hacemos de las minutas de la Junta de Gobierno con ocasin de las decisiones de poltica monetaria, el intercambio de opiniones y argumentos entre los miembros de la Junta, as como las ponderaciones que dan pie a las decisiones finales. Una lectura atenta de la ms reciente de estas minutas, por ejemplo, permite advertir que por encima de diferencias de opinin y de pareceres, quienes integramos la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de 10 Mxico coincidimos plenamente en que dado que nuestro objetivo prioritario es procurar la estabilidad de precios  el Banco deber actuar oportunamente ante cualquier evento que llegase a desanclar las expectativas de inflacin baja y estable que hoy tenemos. Y esto, aun con independencia de las acciones de poltica monetaria que tome la Reserva Federal de los Estados Unidos. No me cabe duda que para los mercados y para el pblico en general conocer este tipo de definiciones claras sobre el rumbo de accin que eventualmente seguiremos, gracias a la difusin de nuestras minutas, genera certidumbres que compensan  en buena medida- el cmulo de incertidumbres provocadas por el hecho de que la economa mundial navega por mares an no conocidos. Y estos arreglos institucionales que generan confianza  y a la postre permiten un mejor funcionamiento de la economa y, con ello, un mayor bienestar- provienen en ltima instancia, como ya he dicho, de los hallazgos de la investigacin econmica. Es decir: de conocimientos tiles pero rigurosos y fundamentados como los que difunde y seguir difundiendo la Revista Mexicana de Economa y Finanzas. Felicidades y muchas gracias. 11

Title: Signing of the collaboration agreement between the Federal Economic Competition Commission and the Bank of Mexico
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Agustin Carstens, during the signing of the collaboration agreement between the Federal Commission of Economic Competition and the Bank of Mexico. February 6, 2014 ? Dear teacher Alejandra Palacios Prieto, Commissioner President of the Federal Commission of Economic Competition, ? Dear Commissioners and officials of the Federal Economic Competition Commission, ? Dear Members of the Governing Board and colleagues of the Bank of Mexico, ? Distinguished guests of the media, ? Ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of myself and the Governing Board of the Bank of Mexico, I am pleased to welcome you to this emblematic banking room that distinguishes and beautifies, for more than eight decades, our Central Institute. As the Commissioner President of the Federal Economic Competition Commission has eloquently expressed, the signing of this collaboration agreement goes far beyond a protocol act between two autonomous institutions of the Mexican State. Indeed, both institutions share a clear and inescapable mandate of service in favor of Mexicans, which undoubtedly generates wide avenues of collaboration and opportunities for synergy. Each of the institutions has clearly defined, in the Constitution, its object and its areas of activity. And, well seen, the specific missions entrusted to each one, 1 they complement and harmonize in a single and superior purpose that is the economic well-being of all Mexicans. The Bank of Mexico has in the Constitution as a priority objective to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. It also has the responsibility, shared with other authorities, to promote the healthy development of the financial system and promote the proper functioning of payment systems. In accordance with the Law on Transparency and Regulation of Financial Services, the Bank of Mexico can evaluate whether there are reasonable conditions of competition in the services provided by financial institutions, which we have done, or request the opinion of the Commission. In turn, the Commission has the power to assess the conditions of competition in the financial markets, regardless of whether or not it receives a request to this effect. In the immediate term, the recently enacted financial reform mandates the Commission to carry out, within a peremptory period, an investigation into the conditions of competition in the financial system and its markets. On the basis of this investigation, the Commission may make recommendations in order to improve competition in the system. The Commission's investigation will undoubtedly provide a fresh and complementary insight into competition in the financial system. Precisely, this Agreement that we are signing today will facilitate the Commission to have the information and advice of the Bank of Mexico to bring to fruition this specific mandate that does not fit. 2 doubt, arouses great interest in the Bank and has our full support. On the other hand, it is very important to emphasize that the collaboration that we formalize today goes far beyond the system and the financial markets. In fact, as the Strategic Plan 20142017 which the Commission has submitted for public consultation has expressed very well, the Commission's own commitment to substantially improve the efficiency of the markets of the economy is crucial for the Bank of Mexico to be able to better meet its priority objective of preserving the purchasing power of the national currency. All this because, in the words of the aforementioned Strategic Plan: "competition between companies brings with it lower prices, greater efficiency, better quality of goods and services and innovation in the markets". Recently I have referred to the importance that we in the Bank of Mexico attach to the need to achieve the convergence of inflation to the permanent objective of three percent per year, in the most efficient way possible, which means, in plain words, the lowest cost for society. To fully fulfill this purpose, it is of great help that we are getting closer and closer in Mexico to an environment of full competition in the markets. This, fundamentally because the power of monetary policy tools is greatly reduced when markets lacking healthy competition prevail. 3 On the one hand, it is clear that increased competition in financial markets makes it easier for monetary policy transmission channels to operate more efficiently. Hence the importance for the Bank of Mexico of the investigation into the conditions of competition in the financial system and its markets that has already been initiated by the Federal Economic Competition Commission. But also, on the other hand, the greater competition in all markets, not only in financial ones, has a direct impact on an improvement in the purchasing power of consumers. And this has a great relevance for the fulfillment of the priority objective of the Central Bank. Let me dwell on a slightly more detailed explanation of this phenomenon: We all know that there are prices for certain goods and services that are not determined in competitive markets. When this is so, prices exhibit distortions that have adverse effects on consumer welfare. Such markets affected by non-competitive structures or practices can have an effect similar to that of taxes: they tend to cause a rise in prices and to decrease, at the same time, the quantities offered, but with an ominous aggravating factor: we are not talking about taxes collected by the State to apply them to public spending for the benefit of society, but of income extracted by third parties to the detriment of the benefit that should correspond to consumers. 4 This price distortion due to anti-competitive practices has even more adverse effects when it comes to generalized consumer goods because they damage the purchasing power of the poorest households to a greater extent. Along these lines, the Bank of Mexico wishes to offer the Federal Economic Competition Commission the widest possible cooperation and, where appropriate, access to the knowledge and experience it has accumulated in this area. It is for all this that I see a very wide potential for cooperation and synergy between both institutions, each preserving their specific objectives and mandates, their attributions and the modalities that the law dictates for their respective actions. In this way, cooperation between the Commission and the Bank of Mexico will make it easier for this Central Institute to fulfil both its priority mandate in favour of price stability and its specific obligations to promote the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of payment systems. At the same time, we are convinced that the Commission will always find in the Bank of Mexico a determined collaborator for the fulfillment of its mandate, which is to monitor free competition and the free competition of agents in the markets. Thanks a lot. 5

Y esto tiene una gran relevancia para el cumplimiento del objetivo prioritario del Banco Central. Permtanme detenerme en una explicacin un poco ms detallada de este fenmeno: Todos sabemos que hay precios de ciertos bienes y servicios que no se determinan en mercados competitivos. Cuando esto es as, los precios exhiben distorsiones que tienen efectos adversos sobre el bienestar de los consumidores. Tales mercados afectados por estructuras o prcticas nocompetitivas pueden tener un efecto similar al de los impuestos: tienden a provocar un alza en los precios y a disminuir, a la vez, las cantidades ofertadas, pero con un agravante ominoso: no estamos hablando de impuestos que recaude el Estado para aplicarlos al gasto pblico en beneficio de la sociedad, sino de rentas que extraen terceros en detrimento del beneficio que debiera corresponder a los consumidores. 4 Esta distorsin de precios a causa de prcticas contrarias a la competencia tiene efectos an ms adversos cuando se trata de bienes de consumo generalizado porque lesionan en una mayor proporcin el poder adquisitivo de los hogares ms pobres. En esta lnea, el Banco de Mxico desea ofrecer a la Comisin Federal de Competencia Econmica la ms amplia cooperacin y, en su caso, el acceso a los conocimientos y experiencias que en esta materia ha acumulado. Title: Delivery of the Financial Markets Award 2012
text: Delivery of the Financial Markets Award 2012 Mexican Stock Exchange December 10, 2012 Remarks by Dr. Manuel Ramos-France Good afternoon. Dear Dr. Luis Tellez, Dear Mr. Jose Manuel Allende, Dear winners and guests, It is a pleasure for me to be here at the presentation of an award that has become in a few years one of the most important in the country in economic and financial matters. I congratulate each of the winners who should feel very honored and at the same time be aware of the great responsibility that the Financial Markets Award and the associated awards confer on them. Before speaking properly about the content of some of the research papers distinguished with these awards, I would like to address two issues that certainly concern us at this great event. The first topic is the importance of financial market research. It is very likely that today we will take the existence of financial markets for granted. Although with the recent global crisis the implications of its inadequate functioning were seen, on a day-to-day basis it is very likely that we will take for granted its vital role within the economy and its importance for the development and growth of the country. Thus, it is no exaggeration to say that the great progress of humanity experienced in recent centuries is largely due to the development of financial markets. For example, Walter Bagehot in his work Lombard Street of 1873 describes the enormous advantage that England had over other nations due to the great development of the financial system that it had at that time. It had the capacity to capture and allocate, respectively, English capital from areas of the country where there was a surplus of it, to those where such capital was scarce. In practice, this process made it easier for capital to be allocated to projects where it would be best used. Moreover, several countries turned to the English financial system for capital. Paradoxically, these countries did have capital at home. However, it does not 1 they had adequate access to it because of the poor capacity of their financial system to gather it and, therefore, allocate it. However, managing the financial system is not an easy task. Thus, I believe that a very powerful reason why there is an urgent need for high-level research is to know the functioning and characteristics of the financial markets, in particular that of Mexico. The above, not only to have a better understanding of the financial markets themselves, the positive aspect of the matter, but also to have the ability to implement incessantly improvements in terms of the design and regulation of the aforementioned markets, the regulatory aspect of it. In this context, although the existence of finance as a modern discipline of study is relatively recent, its young trajectory has had very distinguished results. It can be considered that this discipline began with markowitz's (1952) article on portfolio formation, and with arrow's (1953) who provided the fundamentals of the general equilibrium approach to the valuation of financial assets. The impetus continued with the contribution of Modigliani and Miller (1958), who formulated the well-known theorem in corporate finance, and to which their surnames gave it a name. There was also a key contribution to the valuation model for capital assets (CAPM) of Sharpe (1964) and Lintner (1965). Years later the now famous article by Black and Scholes (1973) on the valuation of financial options was published. This methodology is also used for the valuation of companies, and its results are used on a daily basis by financial institutions everywhere. In this context, it is central that you realize that you are part of this great legacy. This entails the enormous responsibility of continuing to research, and maintaining an active dialogue with other researchers and the community in general, on this very important discipline. The second issue I will address, albeit more briefly, is the importance of awards in our society. At least since Plato in his classic work The Republic there was already mention of the importance of prizes in a society. The awards are to recognize those people who have provided society with a benefit or service. Naturally, there are several institutions, both public and private, that in our country have established awards of different kinds. In our context, you have provided society with an invaluable benefit in the form of new knowledge in the field of financial markets, work for which you have been awarded these distinctions. An additional reason why research awards exist is as follows. In the case of applied research, there is a patent mechanism to provide people with incentives to stimulate activity in such work. 2 In contrast, in the case of basic research there are no patents. Indeed, Messrs. Harry Markowitz, Kenneth Arrow or Franco Modigliani were not granted patents for their contributions. On the contrary, for them each one was deserving of a well-known award. Thus, in basic research, such as that associated with the Financial Markets Award, the Mexican Stock Exchange, MexDer and Asigna provide through the aforementioned award incentives so that researchers like you have an additional reason to contribute with their best effort in their work as researchers. Additionally, an award acts as a catalyst to make known in a more expeditious and extensive way the research carried out by experts in the field. In particular, it is crucial that such research is known to decision-makers and economic policymakers. Remember that the value of your research grows as it becomes better known. Therefore, an award such as the Financial Markets award also aims to disseminate high-level research such as that carried out by you. In short, an award exists for at least three reasons, first, as a recognition by society of its work; second, as an additional incentive to their work as researchers; and third, to facilitate the process of disseminating their findings. Finally, let me highlight some of the features and benefits of the major award-winning research papers. In the first instance, I want to highlight the winning work of the Financial Markets Award.1 It is entitled: "Tests of macroeconomic stress and contagion in the Mexican financial system", written by Juan Pablo Solorzano Margain, who works at the Bank of Mexico. In his work Juan Pablo proposes a methodology to measure systemic risk. To this end, it estimates the distribution of losses in the Mexican financial system given different stress tests. What's more, their model considers the possibility of contagion effects captured through a network model. This allows for better policy design to prevent and mitigate risks, particularly with regard to regulatory improvements. The recent global crisis was a clear testimony to the relevance of understanding the phenomenon of contagion in financial markets. I would also like to highlight the following three works. 1 The first place of the National Mexican Stock Exchange Award was for the work: "Tests of macroeconomic stress and contagion in the Mexican financial system", by Juan Pablo Solorzano Margain. This work considered better than the first place of the National Derivatives Award became the winning work of the Financial Markets Award. 3 The second place of the National Mexican Stock Exchange Award was awarded to the work entitled: "A statistical arbitrage strategy" by Juan Jose Sanchez Azcarate, affiliated with the Autonomous Technological Institute of Mexico. It explains how statistical arbitrage is a useful tool for the valuation of financial instruments. Statistical arbitration can be considered as a generalization of arbitration. While the former refers to the existence of profits with a favorable probability, the latter refers to the existence of secure profits, in both cases in the context of a financial market. It should be noted that the absence of arbitrage is equivalent to the existence of equilibrium in the market, one of the pillars of economic theory. Regarding the winners of the National Derivatives Award: The work deserving of the first place in this case was entitled: "Use of Copulations, series, numerical approximations and logistic regression in the valuation of Debt obligations with Collateral: Extension proposal to adapt the methodology of Glasserman & Suchintabandid to the Mexico case" by Juan Carlos alvarez Campero, also affiliated with the Autonomous Technological Institute of Mexico. This paper proposes an improvement in the valuation of Collateralized Debt Obligations (CDOs). Its model involves the valuation of credit risks and highlights the fact that it applies to the case of a Collateral Debt Obligation formed by mortgage loans in Mexico. Methodologically, the use of copulations allows to recover the joint density function from the marginal density functions of the stochastic variables in the models. I also want to mention in this same area the work worthy of the second place entitled: "The self-regulation of the derivatives market in Mexico" by Alfredo Nieves Cisneros of the National Autonomous University of Mexico. This issue is undoubtedly of great validity and key in the debate on the effectiveness of self-regulation and, therefore, on the scope of regulation in the financial system. In short, there is no doubt about the high quality and relevance of each of the works distinguished in this contest. I reiterate my congratulations to the organizers of the award and especially to all the winners. I also urge you to continue to contribute to financial research in the country for the benefit of all. Thanks a lot. 4 Referencias [1.] Arrow, Kenneth (1953). "The Role of Stock Market Values for Distribution la Meilleure des Risques". Econometrie. Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique. [2.] Bagehot, Walter (1873, 1999). "Lombard Street: A Description of the Money Market". Wiley Investment Classics. [3.] Black, Fischer y Myron Scholes (1973). "The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities". Journal of Political Economy 81 (3): 637-654. [4.] Lintner, John (1965). "The valuation of risk assets and the selection of risky investments in stock portfolios and capital budgets". Review of Economics and Statistics 47 (1), 13-37. [5.] Markowitz, Harry (1952). "Portfolio Selection". The Journal of Finance 7 (1): 77-91. [6.] Modigliani, Franco y Merton H. Miller (1958). "The Cost of Capital, Corporation Finance and the Theory of Investment". American Economic Review 48 (3): 261-297. [7.] Sharpe, William F. (1964). "Capital asset prices: A theory of market equilibrium under conditions of risk". Journal of Finance 19 (3), 425-442. 5

Title: 84th National Banking Convention
text: Remarks by Alejandro Diaz de Leon, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the 84th Banking Convention. March 11, 2021 Maestro Arturo Herrera Gutierrez, Secretary of Finance and Public Credit; Maestro Gabriel Yorio Gonzalez, Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit; Maestro Juan Pablo Graf Noriega, President of the National Banking and Securities Commission; Mr. Luis Nino de Rivera, outgoing President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Mr. Carlos Salazar Lomelin, President of the Business Coordinating Council; Mr. Carlos Rojo Macedo, outgoing Executive President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen: 1 Introduction. It is an honor to participate in the Eighty-Fourth Banking Convention, with the theme "Banking as a driver of development". In my speech, I will address two issues. First of all, I will highlight the raison d'etre of the Bank of Mexico and its contribution to the development of the country. Secondly, I will address the actions that the Bank of Mexico has taken, in the context of the pandemic, to continue procuring the public goods that the law obliges it to provide: price stability, the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of the payment system. 1. The Central Bank and its raison d'etre. The thematic axis of this year's convention refers to a recurring question of the economy: how to promote sustained and inclusive development? The answer can be sought from different angles, one of them is the pragmatic. From observation and international experience of many decades it is possible to infer that a market economy, with the right public institutions, norms and incentives, can be a factor of prosperity, in which the common good and the individual interest fully coincide. 2 Among the elements necessary to achieve this result are indispensable public goods, which must be provided by the State and its institutions. These public goods include: (i) an effective rule of law that generates certainty about essential aspects such as personal safety, ownership and contract compliance; (ii) strong foundations in education and health for all, in order to level opportunities and break down ancestral circles of inequality and poverty; (iii) public policies that stimulate efficiency and competition for the benefit of consumers and promote long-term investment; Central banks have the function of providing some of these public goods, in particular, they have the priority task of providing national currency to their economies and of promoting the stability of power. 3 acquisitive of that currency. In addition, because of their role in this role, they are also given responsibilities for the development and stability of the financial system and for the proper functioning of payment systems. In any society, money must best fulfill three essential functions: i) as a means of payment, ii) as a store of value, and iii) as a unit of account. In modern economies, central banks have the power to issue and place fiat money, with no intrinsic value. Therefore, the terms and conditions with which national currency is provided and the objectives pursued therein play a key role in laying the necessary foundations for development and economic growth. Fiat money, more than other forms of money, depends on the trust of the public in three dimensions: i) that it can be redeemed at any time, at any time. buying and selling; 4 (ii) which shall serve as a safeguard of value; and (iii) that it will function as a numerary and reference to facilitate the trade and the determination of prices of goods and services. It should be noted that these functions of money apply not only to banknotes and coins, but to all units of value denominated or referred to in national currency, and that public confidence is even more necessary when there is a free-floating exchange rate regime. When the issuance of primary money is used for other purposes, it begins to lose confidence among the public, thereby effectively failing to perform its functions. Therefore, the tasks of issuing money of the central bank must be carried out with clear objectives, with a long-term horizon and with the greatest responsibility and prudence, always taking care of its greatest asset, the trust of the public. In the last century, in different countries, there was a frequent propensity to use the central bank's emission powers to create money in order to increase the spending capacity of governments. This equivocal use of the central bank's issuing powers was one of the 5 more frequent sources of inflation, as well as the generation of economic crises with serious social consequences. These were particularly adverse in emerging economies. These dramatic experiences generated a widespread awareness of the counterproductive effects of the use of monetary expansion to finance public deficits and of the need for a central bank focused on the fulfillment of its functions in a sustained manner over time and endowed with autonomy, as the ideal structure for the achievement of its objectives. With this institutional arrangement, central banks are in a better position to serve their societies. 2. The central bank and the provision of public goods. 2.1 The effect of the pandemic on the global economy. Let me now elaborate on how the Bank of Mexico has driven the achievement of its institutional objectives, even in a circumstance as complex as the one we experienced last year. The COVID 19 pandemic generated intense repercussions in all the 6 economies, especially emerging economies and posed considerable challenges to monetary policy. Since the end of February 2020, as the pandemic spread around the world, serious effects on global economic activity have been observed. Likewise, the pandemic led to a significant deterioration in global financial conditions, mainly in March and April, causing a recomposition in investors' portfolios towards lower risk assets, with significant capital outflows from emerging economies. The second quarter of last year saw a sudden and deep global economic contraction, which led to a revision of economic expectations and a decline in the prices of raw materials, mainly oil. In this context, the central banks of advanced and emerging economies implemented extraordinary measures to prevent the hoarding of liquidity and the accelerated liquidation of risk positions, in order to restore the orderly functioning of the markets. 7 Financial. Central banks also adjusted their monetary stances to cope with this adverse environment and governments in several countries adopted fiscal measures to mitigate the effects of the pandemic on employment and household and business incomes. During the third quarter, a gradual global economic recovery began to be observed, in the face of stimulus measures and the reopening of various productive activities. However, this recovery process has been partial and heterogeneous between countries and sectors. In addition, the global economy has not yet reached pre-pandemic levels of activity. As for international financial markets, after the episode of high risk aversion in March and April last year, they improved, although they remained subject to periods of volatility. The global economy and financial markets remain exposed to a number of risks, including the evolution of the pandemic, possible delays in vaccination and, recently, significant increases in medium- and long-term interest rates in the world. 8 The United States in response to the effects of the recently approved large fiscal stimulus. If marked differences in recovery rates prevail in global economic activity, episodes of volatility will become more frequent and global financial conditions will be tightened in advance. 2.2 The effects of the pandemic on national economic activity and inflation. In the wake of the pandemic, the Mexican economy faced the combination of three shocks: 1) A financial shock, with a sudden increase in aversion to risk in international financial markets. It faced the risk of an overreaction in the foreign exchange market, in risk premiums and in capital outflows. 2) A supply shock, propitiated by measures to contain the spread of the virus, such as the paralysis in the production of various goods and services. There were also effects on global value chains and the provision of inputs for domestic production. 9 3) A demand shock. The spread of the pandemic globally reduced external demand; while the social distancing measures adopted in the country, as well as the lower incomes of households and companies, led to a significant contraction in domestic demand. Starting in March, domestic economic activity suffered from global weakness and domestic measures to contain the spread of the pandemic, which caused strong contractions in output and employment in the second quarter. During the second half of the year, a gradual economic recovery was observed as a result of the resumption of productive activities in various sectors and the significant reactivation of external demand. However, economic activity registered an annual contraction of 8.2% in all of 2020, the largest since 1932. In addition, the new social distancing measures, adopted in December and January, once again affected economic activity, which remains clearly below pre-pandemic levels. 10 The effects of the pandemic on the labor market were very marked, with significant contractions in labor participation and losses in formal and informal employment. In 2020, inflation was also affected by the effects of the pandemic and the combination of the three shocks described, the financial, the supply and the demand, which led to: i) an exchange rate adjustment, ii) deep effects on the supply of goods and services, and iii) changes in consumption patterns. These shocks have put pressure on production costs and led to a significant reallocation of household spending, in favour of goods and reducing that allocated to services. Among the initial effects of the pandemic, there was a significant drop in international energy prices, which led to a decrease in general inflation and that in April it registered its second historically lowest level, standing at 2.15%. 11 However, headline inflation began to rise from May, due to the recovery in international energy prices and a rebound in goods in core inflation. Thus, headline inflation increased to reach a level of 4.09% in October 2020, while core inflation registered 3.98%. In the last two months of the year, headline and core inflation decreased, standing at the end of 2020 at 3.15% and 3.80%, respectively. In February 2021, headline inflation was 3.76% and core inflation 3.87%, highlighting the increase in the annual variation in merchandise prices and the slowdown in services, which registered 5.54% and 2.06%, respectively. In all this, it is clear that there are multiple changes in relative prices that are taking place in the economy, under a particularly complex environment: i) with a very significant economic contraction, ii) with the additional challenge of an exchange rate adjustment, and iii) with difficulties in retaining capital. 12 In this context, it is essential to have a solid macroeconomic framework, which favors an adjustment of the economy with price stability and strength in the financial system. In an environment such as the one described, one of the greatest challenges for the conduct of monetary policy is to assimilate the significant change in relative prices, without affecting the process of price formation and inflation expectations. Given the severity of the shock, it was important that the foreign exchange market, risk premiums and medium- and long-term interest rates, after cushioning the initial shock, present an orderly behavior and gradually corrected. This, in turn, would contribute to an adjustment of the economy in better conditions. For all the above, the strategy of the Bank of Mexico has been to conduct monetary policy in a timely and prudent manner, seeking a consistent and sustained convergence of inflation towards its target and contributing to an orderly adjustment in national financial markets and economic activity. 13 During 2020, the Bank of Mexico reduced the target for the overnight Interbank Interest Rate by 300 basis points, reaching 4.25% in September. On February 11 of this year, that rate was reduced by 25 points to a level of 4%. In turn, in the second half of the year, 10- and 30-year interest rates also decreased significantly from the high levels reached in March and April 2020. However, in recent weeks the increase in medium- and long-term interest rates on US Treasuries has suffered. It should be noted that since the beginning of the pandemic, the yield curve in Mexico has behaved favorably compared to that of other emerging economies. By maintaining low and stable inflation, with reduced inflationary risk premia, monetary policy contributes significantly to a sustained reduction of the entire yield curve, which is a key factor for the economy to adequately adjust to the shocks associated with the pandemic. In this regard, the 14 Last week the Bank of Mexico announced its GDP growth forecast for 2021, which in the central scenario, is 4.8% and 3.3% for 2022. 2.3 The public good of financial stability and the proper functioning of the payment system. As I mentioned, in addition to price stability, the Bank of Mexico is charged with promoting the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of payment systems, indispensable elements for the progress of any nation and its individuals. To promote greater efficiency and competition in the provision of financial services to the population, it has sought to empower the consumer, facilitating their mobility between institutions, promoting an open architecture in information and payment networks, providing them with more comparative information to make better decisions and protecting their rights. 15 On the other hand, the financial shock caused by the pandemic posed considerable risks to the Mexican financial system. Therefore, in March and April of last year, the Bank of Mexico announced extraordinary measures to promote an orderly behavior of the financial markets, provide liquidity and strengthen all credit granting channels, including small and medium-sized companies, as well as households affected by the pandemic. These actions include operations authorized by the Bank of Mexico Law, the support for the operation of the financial system in national currency contemplates resources up to 800 billion pesos, a figure equivalent to 3.3% of GDP in 2019. Since their announcement, these measures have helped to promote a more orderly behavior of the national financial markets, by providing additional liquidity support and a signal of confidence to financial intermediaries, which modify their behavior by being able to have such measures. 16 Despite the greater stability of our country's financial markets, risks persist that could have a negative impact on the Mexican economy and financial system. Therefore, on February 25, the Bank of Mexico announced, with some adjustments, the extension of these measures until September 30, 2021. This seeks to promote that financial markets maintain an orderly behavior and that intermediaries play their priority role in providing financing to the economy. Due to their systemic importance for the economy and the financial system, market infrastructures and in particular payment systems, must provide their services and operate, under any type of condition and scenario, at any time and from anywhere, even in the face of health contingencies, such as COVID-19. With regard to the participants in the payment systems, in particular in the SPEI, they have clear rules to implement operational continuity protocols and were required to validate that they have the appropriate procedures, instruments and personnel to maintain their operation safely and efficiently in any eventuality. 17 These measures have allowed that during 2020 the payment systems administered by Banco de Mexico operate under normal conditions; in particular for the SPEI, a service availability of 99.99% was observed. In addition, this instrument is increasingly used: the volume of payments less than 8 thousand pesos in the SPEI reached 885 million operations in 2020 and registered a growth of 90.2% in the last twelve months. These payment systems have been a key tool to mitigate the effects of the pandemic and avoid further paralysis in many activities. In addition, it was especially useful in the transactions of small and medium-sized enterprises and households. In the field of financial services and payment systems, technology has made it possible for many people to continue to carry out their operations remotely, efficiently and securely despite the pandemic. However, those who do not have such remote means have faced significant restrictions on their activities. Therefore, the 18 Access to financial services by digital means has become a public policy imperative for all financial authorities. One of the new technological applications for digital payments is the platform called Digital Collection (CoDi), which uses the SPEI infrastructure. CoDi allows anyone with a smartphone and bank account to make electronic payments, 24 hours a day, free of charge and with the highest security standards. This payment network is a reality, to date there are more than 8 million validated accounts to make payments. Now, the challenge is for banks to focus their efforts on greater use of payment networks that offer the greatest benefits for their users and that can also have a decisive impact on financial inclusion, and reach more than 40 million Mexicans who have a smartphone and do not have banking services. 19 Ladies and gentlemen, the pandemic has implied unprecedented conditions and challenges, both globally and for the Mexican economy. In this environment, the Bank of Mexico has adapted its instruments and strategies in order to comply with its Constitutional mandate, to maintain low and stable inflation, and in order to promote the healthy development of the financial system and promote the proper functioning of payment systems. These elements constitute public goods that benefit all social actors and that are reflected in a concrete way in the economic opportunities and quality of life of all citizens, particularly those who have less. This is the Central Institute's best contribution to national development, and to more vigorous, equitable and sustained economic growth over time. Thanks a lot. 20
