Otra medida muy importante adoptada por el IMEF, en febrero de este ao, es la instalacin del Comit de Fechado de los Ciclos de la 4 Economa de Mxico, el cual se integra por 7 expertos en materia macroeconmica y estadstica. Este Comit tiene su origen en los trabajos de un grupo de expertos que establecieron el INEGI y el CIDE en 2019, el cual determin la conveniencia de contar con una instancia de esta naturaleza, a fin de fijar y mantener actualizada una cronologa de los ciclos econmicos en nuestro pas. El IMEF, con extraordinaria disposicin, decidi instalar, alojar y ofrecer apoyo logstico a este Comit, cuya composicin y reconocimiento profesional brinda credibilidad, independencia y neutralidad Con todo esto, el IMEF aporta instrumentos valiosos de informacin y anlisis, as como una opinin fundada sobre la coyuntura y las perspectivas econmicas que tiene significativa influencia en la toma de decisiones empresariales. En suma, este organismo, adems de que constituye un instrumento de actualizacin y mejora profesional para sus miembros, a lo largo de su historia ha emprendido tareas que han dejado una invaluable huella social. As, el IMEF ha sido un catalizador de los 5 esfuerzos de los profesionales de las finanzas en favor de la evolucin del gremio y del desarrollo del pas. *** Aunque con orgenes y vocaciones distintas, el Banco de Mxico y el IMEF persiguen objetivos permanentes y despliegan una visin de largo plazo del desarrollo nacional. Por lo que toca al Banco de Mxico, su fundacin fue la consumacin de un anhelo largamente acariciado por el pas. Desde sus inicios como nacin independiente se intent la emisin de dinero fiduciario y se buscaron alternativas para tener un emisor nico que procurara la certidumbre en la provisin de circulante y la estabilidad en el poder adquisitivo de la moneda. Esto se alcanz en la Constitucin de 1917 y con la fundacin del Banco de Mxico en 1925. En sus inicios, el Banco de Mxico tuvo que enfrentar diversas dificultades, como la arraigada desconfianza de la poblacin hacia el uso del dinero fiduciario. Desde esa poca, pero con mayor claridad una 6 vez que le fue concedida autonoma, ha concentrado todos sus esfuerzos en consolidar el activo ms valioso de cualquier institucin emisora, la credibilidad de que invariablemente se conducir con el objetivo de preservar el poder adquisitivo del dinero que coloca entre el pblico. En sus orgenes la institucin pudo proveer de moneda a la economa y consolidar el dinero fiduciario como medio de pago, y desde su autonoma ha podido enfocar mejor sus esfuerzos en mantener la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo del dinero de los mexicanos. La conduccin autnoma de la poltica monetaria ha sido un elemento determinante para lograr una disminucin importante en el nivel, volatilidad y persistencia de la inflacin en las ltimas dcadas. La evidencia emprica muestra que, desde 2001, podemos hablar de un proceso estacionario de la inflacin, que la ha vuelto estable, baja y predecible. Se trata de la etapa ms larga de estabilidad de precios en la historia de nuestro pas, lo que implica beneficios tangibles para la poblacin y una base firme para el crecimiento y el desarrollo. 7 La estabilidad de precios es indispensable para permitir una correcta planeacin y funcionamiento de las empresas. Por la naturaleza de su actividad, los ejecutivos de finanzas conocen de manera directa las distorsiones que generan los episodios inflacionarios en la planeacin y ejecucin de proyectos y, por ello, identifican cabalmente los beneficios que conlleva un entorno de estabilidad de precios para la actividad econmica. De hecho, probablemente muchos de ustedes atestiguaron o experimentaron en carne propia, algunas dcadas atrs, la incertidumbre que acarrea la inflacin y su efecto devastador sobre la inversin y el empleo, as como sobre el patrimonio y el salario de las personas. Entre los beneficios concretos del descenso de la inflacin en Mxico destaca la tendencia a la baja de las tasas de inters, lo que ha contribuido a un mayor acceso de las empresas y los individuos al crdito con menor costo y plazos ms largos. Por ejemplo, en 1995, el mayor plazo de financiamiento del gobierno federal a tasa fija era de 6 meses y, desde 2003, llega hasta 30 aos. Esta extensin de la curva de rendimientos ha permitido el financiamiento de largo plazo a tasa fija 8 con beneficios notables tanto para la inversin productiva de las empresas como para el crdito hipotecario de los hogares. Otro ejemplo de los efectos positivos de procurar la estabilidad de precios es la menor respuesta de la inflacin a choques, como una depreciacin de la moneda nacional, que sola tener un severo impacto en los precios. En el siglo pasado eran comunes los episodios de pronunciada depreciacin cambiaria y procesos inflacionarios voltiles y con niveles de dos dgitos. El haber consolidado una inflacin baja y estable ha permitido un ajuste ordenado en los mercados financieros y en la economa. Esto ha sido patente ante los choques por la crisis global de 2008 y 2009, por los cuestionamientos al TLCAN que iniciaron en 2016 o por la pandemia que hemos enfrentado recientemente. As, ha sido posible sortear episodios de turbulencia considerable con una menor afectacin a la economa real y se ha mitigado su efecto en la inflacin y en los ingresos y patrimonio de los mexicanos, particularmente de aquellos con menores ingresos, evitando mayor pobreza y desigualdad. 9 Actualmente, el entorno para la inflacin se presenta complejo. Despus de una profunda y sbita contraccin econmica en 2020, la actividad econmica global se recupera, a un ritmo heterogneo entre sectores y pases. En todo el mundo, las cadenas de suministro se han visto afectadas, particularmente las de los procesos productivos ms complejos y extendidos. Adems, en las economas ms avanzadas, se han adoptado cuantiosos estmulos a la expansin del gasto. Esto ha acentuado los cuellos de botella en la produccin y provocado presiones inflacionarias globales. En esta circunstancia, el Banco de Mxico ha buscado conducir la poltica monetaria de manera oportuna y prudente, propiciando un ajuste ordenado tanto en los mercados financieros como en la economa en su conjunto, y evitando riesgos de contaminacin en la formacin de precios ante las recientes presiones inflacionarias. El Banco tambin adopt diversas medidas, inditas pero necesarias, para promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. De esta manera, en el 10 mbito de sus posibilidades y finalidades, ha contribuido a mitigar los efectos adversos de la pandemia sobre las familias mexicanas. Seoras y seores: Estamos a unos cuantos das de la celebracin del Bicentenario de la consumacin de la Independencia de Mxico. Ese acontecimiento histrico representa un ejemplo de que, cuando los distintos actores dejamos de lado nuestras diferencias y nos reunimos en torno a un mismo objetivo, podemos alcanzar logros y metas trascendentales y que pareceran impensables. Hoy, estamos convocados para celebrar al IMEF que ha logrado convertirse en una institucin ejemplar gracias a un conjunto de visiones y aspiraciones compartidas entre el gremio de los ejecutivos de finanzas. Esa unidad les ha permitido realizar aportes slidos a sus agremiados y a la sociedad en general. De manera anloga, el Banco de Mxico refleja cmo, gracias a grandes acuerdos y consensos nacionales, se ha podido construir un slido basamento constitucional y legal para tener una institucin 11 completamente comprometida con su objetivo prioritario de proveer al pas de moneda nacional y mantener su poder adquisitivo. A esto tambin se agrega el promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. Estos tres mandatos permiten consolidar bienes pblicos fundamentales para el bienestar de los individuos y familias, as como para propiciar un desarrollo econmico ms slido y equilibrado. En el marco de las celebraciones de estos das, esta ocasin es ms que propicia para destacar la importancia de la generacin de acuerdos e instituciones que procuren el mejor balance entre el inters individual y el bien comn, como lo realiza destacadamente el IMEF. Muchas gracias de nuevo por este reconocimiento que recibo a nombre de todo el equipo del banco central y, desde luego, muchas, muchsimas felicidades por estos 60 aos de fecunda labor. Enhorabuena. 12

Title: Opening of the Eleventh International Conference on Payment Systems
text: Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, at the opening of the Eleventh International Conference on Payment Systems in Mexico City, May 24, 2010  Mr. Luis Robles Miaja, Executive President of the Association of Banks of Mexico.  Mr. Accountant Emilio Lujan Vallado, General Director of Cecoban.  Dear colleagues at the Bank of Mexico  Distinguished speakers at this international conference on payment systems.  Ladies and gentlemen .... I am grateful for the invitation extended to me by the Association of Banks of Mexico to participate in the inauguration of this eleventh international conference on payment systems. 1 Every two years this forum is a unique opportunity to exchange experiences, as well as to know and discuss the advances of payment systems in the world. Today, as the global economy and financial markets face unprecedented challenges, the role of payment systems in underpinning certainty and confidence is becoming uniquely important. * * * The purpose of the Bank of Mexico is to provide the economy with a national currency and, in the fulfillment of this mandate, the Constitution orders it to ensure the stability of its purchasing power. Priority mandate to which are added the tasks of promoting the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of payment systems. To meet this last objective, the central bank has paid permanent attention throughout its history to the constant improvement of payment systems in the country. If we remember, a few decades ago the payment system in Mexico basically consisted of the exchange of banknotes and coins. However, thanks to the advances 2 The payment system has spread, more and more rapidly, to electronic exchanges that for most financial and commercial transactions are the safest, most efficient and economical. Rightly, this international conference focuses precisely on electronic payment systems. In this area and in recent years, the Bank of Mexico has undertaken actions in two main areas: first, it has worked intensively, and with excellent results, to consolidate the proper functioning of payment systems that, due to their high value and / or the number of their daily transactions, are considered of "systemic importance". Secondly, a number of innovations have been launched using the best scientific and technological resources to promote the widespread use of increasingly efficient payment instruments among the broader population. An exemplary case of these actions is the evolution of the Interbank Electronic Payment System - the SPEI - of the Bank of Mexico. It is a state-of-the-art system that follows international best practices; it's safe, fast, and costly costly 3 Low. In addition, its design and the provisions that regulate it have led participating financial institutions to automate their payment processes, reduce their operating costs and expand the offer of electronic payment services to the user public. One of the characteristics that distinguishes the SPEI from other payment systems in other countries is that it processes both very high value payments as well as retail transfers made daily by the general public. On a typical day, in the SPEI payments are made for a total of approximately 500 billion pesos through 300 thousand operations, of which 67% are for amounts less than 20 thousand pesos. The average commission charged by Internet banking, for transferring resources through the SPEI, amounts to less than 6 pesos, no matter how high or low the amount of the transfer. This rate is one of the lowest in the world. On the other hand, in order to promote greater competition between financial institutions for the benefit of users, the Bank of Mexico has been allowing non-bank financial institutions to participate directly in the SPEI for some years. 4 Currently, more than 30 institutions of this nature, such as insurers, brokerage houses and exchange houses, are connected to the SPEI, which allows them to offer better services to their clients. Additionally, the Treasury of the Federation has been making a great effort to avoid the use of cash and checks in its operations. Its goal is to fully migrate its operations to electronic payments in a few years. Thus, the Treasury of the Federation already pays a good part of the payrolls of the federal public sector through the SPEI, the same happens in payments to suppliers of several public entities. This has resulted in significant savings for the Federal Government, while increasing the transparency and timeliness of its transactions. It is clear that transfers by the SPEI are becoming more common, which has been reflected in the fact that the growth rate in the use of this system has exceeded expectations. However, there is still opportunity to continue improving. Therefore, shortly the Bank of Mexico will issue rules for banks to extend service hours to their customers. In this way, from next September the SPEI service will be offered through the 5 Internet banking from 6 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.; currently, the SPEI's hours of operation are from half past eight in the morning to 5 in the afternoon. In addition, the Bank of Mexico will require banks to substantially reduce the period between a client's request for the transfer until the crediting of resources to the beneficiary's account. Currently this period can be up to 20 minutes but from June next year payments must be credited in no more than one minute. * * * I will now turn to another payment system that is considered systemically important: the system that manages the deposit and settlement of government-issued securities, banks, private sector companies, as well as the shares of companies listed on the capital market. Daily in this payment system, operations are carried out for almost three trillion pesos with securities, which is equivalent to more than three quarters of the total amount of payments that are settled in our financial system. Therefore, it is fair. 6 highlight the constant effort of INDEVAL and its depositors to keep this system at the forefront. The current system, called DALI, has a modern technological platform and processes that allow it to clear and settle operations practically in real time. Trade clearing reduces the cash and securities required by depositors to settle their trades, which is reflected in lower costs for intermediaries, makes it easier to settle many transactions and is extremely valuable in providing transaction reliability, particularly in times of high market turbulence. In addition, timely settlements during the day allow market participants to release cash and/or securities very quickly, making it easier for them to better manage their risks. For all this, today we can say that DALi meets the desirable characteristics of a good payment system: it is safe, reliable and efficient. It is, in short, a system on par with the most important securities deposit systems in the world. 7 A clear example of this is the international award that DALI obtained last April by the most recognized Institute worldwide in the area of Operations Research. DALI received the 2010 "Franz Edelman" award. It is important to note that the central component of the DALi uses an optimization model designed at the Bank of Mexico, which is the basic algorithm for the operation of the system. * * * The Bank of Mexico is not only concerned with the benefits that efficient payment systems generate for financial intermediation or for high-value operations. In fact, the most important challenge we have set ourselves is to bring better, efficient and accessible payment services to the general population. Undoubtedly, the direct costs of transaction, as well as those of transportation, time and others, are considerably reduced with the increasingly widespread use of electronic systems to settle payments, especially for people with lower incomes. Therefore, the Bank of Mexico will intensify the promotion of these means of payment 8 through various strategies and with all the instruments at its disposal. Obviously, coordination and collaboration with the rest of the country's financial authorities is crucial in this effort. There are some specific challenges in this area to which I will briefly address. First, with regard to the use of cards as a means of payment, we are convinced that the main problem continues to be that the number of establishments that accept cards in Mexico is relatively low. For every thousand inhabitants there are less than five shops that accept cards, while in Brazil there are 17 and in Spain 33 establishments that receive plastics per thousand inhabitants. On the other hand, with regard to electronic transfers, the main obstacle we have detected is that most of the population does not have secure computers connected to the Internet, despite the fact that this is the most appropriate channel to instruct such transfers. Therefore, at the end of 2009 the Bank of Mexico issued the provisions on mobile bank accounts, whose objective is to promote that cell phones can be used, instead and 9 in addition to computers, as a channel for electronic transfers. Through these provisions, mobile phone users will be able to manage mobile bank accounts from their cell phones and instruct transfers in favor of other users. Here, in the use of the cell phone as a generalized instrument of payment between natural persons, and for operations between natural persons and commercial establishments, we see a very promising field of action that should have a substantial, and certainly beneficial, impact on the economy of the population in general. Some banks already offer financial services via cell phone, but we hope that in the near future making money transfers using mobile accounts on the cell phone will be as easy and as common as texting. We also hope that in a short time paying for various consumptions in shops will be as simple a process as bringing the cell phone closer to another device. * * * We know that there is still a long way to go and that the active participation of the financial authorities will continue to be necessary if the country's payment services are to continue to expand and reach 10 more sectors of the population. For our part, at the Bank of Mexico we will continue to work decisively in our field of action to realize the broad objectives that we have set ourselves. Thanks a lot. 11
text_original: Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, en la inauguracin de la Dcimo Primer Conferencia Internacional sobre Sistemas de Pago en la Ciudad de Mxico, 24 de mayo de 2010  Seor licenciado Luis Robles Miaja, presidente ejecutivo de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico.  Seor Contador Emilio Lujn Vallado, Director General de Cecoban.  Estimados colegas del Banco de Mxico  Distinguidos expositores en esta conferencia internacional sobre sistemas de pago.  Seoras y seores . Agradezco la invitacin que me hizo la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico a participar en la inauguracin de esta dcimo primera conferencia internacional sobre sistemas de pago. 1 Cada dos aos este foro es una oportunidad nica para intercambiar experiencias, as como para conocer y discutir los avances de los sistemas de pagos en el mundo. El da de hoy, cuando la economa mundial y los mercados financieros enfrentan desafos inslitos, adquiere singular importancia el papel que desempean los sistemas de pago para apuntalar la certidumbre y la confianza. * * * El Banco de Mxico tiene la finalidad de proveer a la economa de una moneda nacional y, en el cumplimiento de esa encomienda, la Constitucin le ordena procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la misma. Mandato prioritario al que se suman las tareas de promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y de propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pago. Para cumplir este ltimo objetivo el banco central ha prestado a lo largo de su historia una atencin permanente a la constante mejora de los sistemas de pago en el pas. Si hacemos memoria, hace unas dcadas el sistema de pagos en Mxico consista bsicamente en el intercambio de billetes y monedas. Sin embargo gracias a los avances 2 tecnolgicos el sistema de pagos se ha extendido, cada vez con mayor rapidez, a intercambios de carcter electrnico que para la mayora de las transacciones financieras y comerciales son los ms seguros, eficientes y econmicos. Atinadamente, esta conferencia internacional se centra precisamente en los sistemas de pago electrnicos. En esta materia y en los ltimos aos el Banco de Mxico ha emprendido acciones en dos grandes vertientes: primero, se ha trabajado intensamente, y con excelentes resultados, en consolidar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pago que, por su alto valor y/o por el nmero de sus transacciones diarias, se consideran de importancia sistmica. Segundo, se han puesto en marcha diversas innovaciones echando mano de los mejores recursos cientficos y tecnolgicos, para promover entre lo ms amplio de la poblacin el uso generalizado de instrumentos de pago cada vez ms eficientes. Un caso ejemplar de dichas acciones es la evolucin que ha tenido el Sistema de Pagos Electrnicos Interbancarios - el SPEI- del Banco de Mxico. Es un sistema de vanguardia que sigue las mejores prcticas internacionales; es seguro, es rpido y tiene costos notablemente 3 bajos. Adems, su diseo y las disposiciones que lo regulan han propiciado que las instituciones financieras participantes automaticen sus procesos de pago, reduzcan sus costos de operacin y amplen la oferta de servicios de pagos electrnicos al pblico usuario. Una de las caractersticas que distingue al SPEI respecto de otros sistemas de pago en otros pases, es que en l se procesan tanto los pagos de muy alto valor as como transferencias al menudeo que realiza cotidianamente el pblico en general. En un da tpico, en el SPEI se realizan pagos por un total aproximadamente de 500 mil millones de pesos mediante 300 mil operaciones, de las cuales 67% son por montos menores a 20 mil pesos. La comisin promedio que cobra la banca mediante Internet, por transferir recursos a travs del SPEI, asciende a menos de 6 pesos, sin importar qu tan alto o bajo sea el monto de la transferencia. Dicha tarifa es de las ms bajas del mundo. Por otro lado, para promover una mayor competencia entre instituciones financieras en beneficio de los usuarios, el Banco de Mxico permite desde hace algunos aos que instituciones financieras no bancarias participen tambin directamente en el SPEI. 4 Actualmente, ms de 30 instituciones de esta naturaleza, como aseguradoras, casas de bolsa y casas de cambio, estn conectadas al SPEI, lo que les permite ofrecer mejores servicios a sus clientes. Adicionalmente, la Tesorera de la Federacin ha venido haciendo un gran esfuerzo para evitar el uso de efectivo y de cheques en sus operaciones. Su meta es migrar totalmente en algunos aos sus operaciones a pagos electrnicos. As, la Tesorera de la Federacin ya paga una buena parte de las nminas del sector pblico federal a travs del SPEI, sucediendo lo mismo en pagos a proveedores de varias entidades pblicas. Esto ha redundado en significativos ahorros para el Gobierno Federal, y ha aumentado a la vez la transparencia y oportunidad de sus transacciones. Es claro que las transferencias por el SPEI son cada vez ms comunes, lo que se ha reflejado en que la tasa de crecimiento en el uso de este sistema ha superado las expectativas. Sin embargo, todava hay oportunidad para seguir mejorando. Por eso, en breve el Banco de Mxico emitir reglas para que los bancos amplen los horarios de servicio a su clientela. De esta forma, a partir de septiembre prximo el servicio de SPEI se ofrecer a travs de la 5 banca por Internet desde las 6 de la maana hasta las 5:30 de la tarde; actualmente, el horario de operaciones del SPEI es de las ocho y media de la maana a las 5 de la tarde. Adems, el Banco de Mxico requerir a los bancos reducir sustancialmente el lapso que transcurre entre la solicitud de la transferencia por parte de un cliente hasta la acreditacin de los recursos en la cuenta del beneficiario. Actualmente este lapso puede ser de hasta 20 minutos pero a partir de junio del prximo ao los pagos debern acreditarse en no ms de un minuto. * * * Me referir ahora a otro sistema de pagos que se considera de importancia sistmica: el sistema que administra el depsito y la liquidacin de valores emitidos por el gobierno, bancos, empresas del sector privado, as como de las acciones de empresas que se cotizan en el mercado de capitales. Diariamente en dicho sistema de pagos se realizan operaciones por casi tres billones de pesos con valores, lo que equivale a ms de tres cuartas partes del monto total de los pagos que se liquidan en nuestro sistema financiero. Por ello, es justo 6 destacar el esfuerzo constante del INDEVAL y de sus depositantes para mantener a la vanguardia dicho sistema. El actual sistema, denominado DALI, cuenta con una plataforma tecnolgica moderna y con procesos que le permiten compensar y liquidar operaciones prcticamente en tiempo real. La compensacin de operaciones reduce el efectivo y los valores que requieren mantener los depositantes para liquidar sus operaciones, lo cual se refleja en menores costos para los intermediarios, hace ms fcil la liquidacin de muchas operaciones y es sumamente valioso para dar confiabilidad a las transacciones, en particular, en momentos de elevada turbulencia en los mercados. Adems, las liquidaciones oportunas durante el da permiten que los participantes del mercado liberen efectivo y/o valores muy rpidamente, facilitndoles administrar mejor sus riesgos. Por todo esto, hoy podemos afirmar que DAL rene las caractersticas deseables de un buen sistema de pagos: es seguro, es confiable y es eficiente. Es, en fin, un sistema a la par con los sistemas de depsito de valores ms importantes del mundo. 7 Una muestra clara de ello es el premio internacional que obtuvo DALI en abril pasado por parte del Instituto ms reconocido mundialmente en el rea de Investigacin de Operaciones. El DALI recibi el premio "Franz Edelman" de 2010. Es importante destacar que el componente central del DAL utiliza un modelo de optimizacin diseado en el Banco de Mxico, el cual es el algoritmo base para el funcionamiento del sistema. * * * El Banco de Mxico no slo se preocupa por los beneficios que los sistemas de pago eficientes generan para la intermediacin financiera o para las operaciones de alto valor. De hecho, el desafo ms importante que nos hemos trazado es llevar mejores servicios de pago, eficientes y accesibles, a la poblacin en general. Sin duda, los costos directos de transaccin, as como los de transportacin, tiempo y otros, se abaten considerablemente con el uso cada da ms generalizado de sistemas electrnicos para liquidar pagos, en especial para las personas de menores ingresos. Por eso, el Banco de Mxico intensificar la promocin de estos medios de pago 8 mediante diversas estrategias y con todos los instrumentos de que dispone. Obviamente, en este esfuerzo es crucial la coordinacin y la colaboracin con el resto de las autoridades financieras del pas. Hay algunos desafos concretos en esta materia a los que me referir brevemente. Primero, respecto de la utilizacin de tarjetas como medio de pago estamos convencidos de que la principal problemtica contina siendo que el nmero de establecimientos que aceptan tarjetas en Mxico es relativamente bajo. Por cada mil habitantes hay menos de cinco comercios que aceptan tarjetas, mientras que en Brasil hay 17 y en Espaa 33 establecimientos que reciben plsticos por millar de habitantes. Por otro lado, en lo concerniente a las transferencias electrnicas, el principal obstculo que hemos detectado es que la mayor parte de la poblacin no cuenta con computadoras seguras conectadas a Internet, a pesar de que ese es el canal ms adecuado para instruir esas transferencias. Por ello, a finales de 2009 el Banco de Mxico emiti las disposiciones sobre cuentas mviles bancarias, cuyo objetivo es promover que los telfonos celulares puedan ser utilizados, en lugar y 9 adems de las computadoras, como canal para realizar transferencias electrnicas. Mediante esas disposiciones los usuarios de telefona mvil podrn administrar cuentas mviles bancarias desde el celular e instruir transferencias a favor de otros usuarios. Aqu, en el uso del telfono celular como instrumento generalizado de pago entre personas fsicas, y para las operaciones entre personas fsicas y establecimientos comerciales, vemos un muy prometedor campo de accin que debe tener una incidencia sustancial, y desde luego benfica, sobre la economa de la poblacin en general. Algunos bancos ya ofrecen servicios financieros a travs de telfono celular, pero esperamos que en el futuro cercano hacer transferencias de dinero mediante cuentas mviles en el telfono celular sea tan fcil y tan comn como enviar mensajes de texto. Tambin esperamos que en poco tiempo pagar diversos consumos en comercios sea un proceso tan simple como aproximar el celular a otro dispositivo. * * * Sabemos que an falta camino por recorrer y que seguir siendo necesaria la participacin activa de las autoridades financieras para que los servicios de pago del pas sigan extendindose y lleguen a 10 ms sectores de la poblacin. Por nuestra parte, en el Banco de Mxico seguiremos trabajando decididamente en nuestro mbito de accin para hacer realidad los objetivos tan amplios que nos hemos planteado. Muchas gracias. 11

Title: Forum 2010: Remittances for the Future (Remes Americas)
text: 1 Remarks by the Governor of the Bank of Mexico, Dr. Agustin Carstens, at the 2010 Forum Remittances for the Future ("Remes Americas") organized by the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) in Mexico City, May 6, 2010.  Mr. President of the Inter-American Development Bank, highly esteemed Luis Alberto Moreno  Dear Julie T. Katzman, General Manager of the IDB's Multilateral Investment Fund.  Members of the IDB Board of Directors  Ambassador Carlos Garcia de Alba, Executive Director of the Idb Institute Mexicans Abroad (IME)  Distinguished participants in this important analysis forum  Ladies and gentlemen I thank the IDB for its kind invitation to participate in this session, which begins this forum of analysis on the decisive role that remittances play for the development of our countries. I would like to begin by acknowledging the great work that the IDB's Multilateral Investment Fund has done with the remittance program. The IDB has pertinently focused this event on the multiple challenges that we will have to face to ensure that the contribution of migrant workers to development, materialized in remittances, generates its full potential in 1 2 Latin America as a factor of integration and regional development. For many of our countries, family remittances constitute a substantial part of national income. In some cases, they are equivalent to 20 percent of the Gross Domestic Product, as is the case in Honduras, or to percentages of the Product greater than 10 percent, as is the case in El Salvador or Guatemala. Given these data, the importance of remittances for the economic development of the region is obvious even to those who have only a vague notion about this phenomenon. On the other hand, we all know that the global crisis severely affected the incomes of migrant workers. To the same extent that remittances have decreased during this crisis, the families of these workers, who live in our countries, have suffered a deterioration in their welfare conditions. Although during the first months of this year it began to verify, in most statistics, and certainly in Mexico, an incipient recovery in the amount and number of remittances, the figures are still far away. 2 3 to reach the levels recorded before the outbreak of the crisis. In addition, recent events in Greece in particular and in the European Union in general, as well as their impact on markets, have reminded us that significant vulnerabilities persist in several countries and regions. It is not yet a guaranteed fact that there will be a vigorous recovery of economic dynamism in the world. Specifically in the United States, which is the source economy for the vast majority of remittances on the continent, signs of weakness in demand persist and the great unknown remains about what the reactions of private consumption and investment will be when the withdrawal of the large fiscal and monetary stimuli put in place to mitigate the consequences of the recessionary shock begins. This uncertainty, as well as the unusual experience of the global crisis itself, make the careful analysis of the phenomenon of family remittances from all angles even more urgent. From this analysis, strategies and public policies must emerge that allow us to exploit the full potential of remittances for the benefit of development. No doubt 3 4 the program that the IDB has designed for this meeting fully fulfills this purpose. For Latin American central banks, remittances from migrant workers represent an extensive and challenging work agenda. First of all, it should be remembered that in the case of family remittances, monetary stability is crucial so that the great daily effort of migrant workers translates into well-being for them, for their families and for their communities. Central banks have a very serious responsibility to these migrants, and to society at large, to ensure that the fruit of their labour is not lost to inflation or macroeconomic instability, but is transformed into opportunities for growth, investment, savings and a better life. In particular, we have that serious responsibility to millions of Latin American families who still live in conditions of extreme poverty or misery. Families for whom in many cases remittances constitute their substantial income. Second, we need to step up and accelerate the work that most of America's central banks do. 4 5 Latina we have already started, in collaboration with other financial authorities, to lower the costs of money transfers for workers and their families every day. In this sense, we must find the right means in terms of regulation and supervision so that transactions are becoming cheaper and, at the same time, safer every day. A third challenge for all financial authorities is to generate legal and regulatory frameworks that favor innovation in financial products - credit, investment, savings, securitization and coverage, among others - designed so that family remittances can spill their full beneficial potential. In particular, central banks have much to contribute in this area as procurators of the healthy development of our financial systems and the proper functioning of our payment systems. In the same vein, the great issue of family remittances also imposes on us the need to efficiently link the immense needs of our nations, in housing, in education, in health, in infrastructure for development and 5 6 for well-being, with the powerful flow that family remittances constitute. It is no secret to anyone that banking is still a major pending issue in many of the countries of the continent. Facing that challenge implies promoting greater banking competition that translates into products and services of better price and quality for users. Increased competition will lead to the emergence of efficient savings and credit modalities designed precisely to address what has been called "the base of the social pyramid." That is where most of the families of migrant workers are located and that is also, in general, where the insufficient banking is most noticeable. No less decisive is to promote the efficient use of the great technological advances in telecommunications to reduce the costs associated with remittance transfers. Here, too, increased competition will stimulate the timely adoption of state-of-the-art technologies in our countries, which will have a decisive impact on a reduction in the costs associated with remittances. As a permanent and indispensable accompaniment of all these efforts is the task of financial education. 6 7 There are numerous efforts in this area in virtually all the countries of the continent, but they need to be intensified and more synergies generated between them. It is up to all of us, from our respective responsibilities, to harmonize the various financial education ventures in the region, enhance them and share a robust conceptual framework, from the point of view of the contents, that gives a coherent direction to the propagation of financial culture throughout the continent and in all social strata. To this must be added that the new stage that is just being configured for the future of the planet's economy, after the episode of the crisis, will modify the outlook for migrant remittances. Inevitably, U.S. immigration policies, as is already the case in other advanced economies, will tend to be more selective and strict. And this trend in migration policies, as President Moreno has already said, will surely modify the phenomenon of family remittances. It will be very important, in this regard, for the U.S. government to move forward with the passage of reform. 7 8 migration that is beneficial to workers throughout the region. But, the final and most important challenge is to generate more and more highly competitive and well-paid jobs. And that generation of jobs will not happen, we all know, by decree or through voluntary wishes. We need to create the conditions conducive to this definitive take-off through fundamental, structural, educational, labor, competitive environment and numerous strategic sectors of economic activity reforms. Our goal must be to create the development opportunities to retain within our countries those enterprising and high-productivity workers who are forced to emigrate today. Let's not settle for less. Thanks a lot. 8
text_original: 1 Palabras del Gobernador del Banco de Mxico, doctor Agustn Carstens, en el Foro 2010 Remesas para el Futuro (Remes Amricas) organizado por el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) en la Ciudad de Mxico, 6 de mayo de 2010.  Seor Presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo, muy estimado Luis Alberto Moreno  Estimada Julie T. Katzman, Gerente General del Fondo Multilateral de Inversiones del BID.  Seores miembros del Consejo Directivo del BID  Seor embajador Carlos Garca de Alba, Director Ejecutivo del Instituto de Mexicanos en el Exterior (IME)  Distinguidos participantes en este importante foro de anlisis  Seoras y seores Agradezco al BID su amable invitacin a participar en esta sesin, con la que se inicia este foro de anlisis acerca del papel decisivo que desempean las remesas para el desarrollo de nuestros pases. Deseo empezar haciendo un reconocimiento al gran trabajo que ha llevado a cabo el Fondo Multilateral de Inversiones del BID con el programa de remesas. Con pertinencia el BID ha centrado este evento en los mltiples desafos que deberemos enfrentar para lograr que el aporte de los trabajadores migrantes al desarrollo, materializado en las remesas, genere todo su potencial en 1 2 Amrica Latina como factor de integracin y desarrollo regional. Para muchos de nuestros pases, las remesas familiares constituyen una parte sustancial del ingreso nacional. Equivalen en algunos casos al 20 por ciento del Producto Interno Bruto, como sucede en Honduras, o a porcentajes del Producto superiores al 10 ciento, como acontece en El Salvador o en Guatemala. Ante estos datos la importancia de las remesas para el desarrollo econmico de la regin salta a la vista incluso para quienes slo tienen una vaga nocin acerca de este fenmeno. Por otra parte, todos sabemos que la crisis global afect gravemente los ingresos de los trabajadores migrantes. En la misma medida en que han disminuido las remesas durante esta crisis las familias de estos trabajadores, que viven en nuestros pases, han sufrido un deterioro en sus condiciones de bienestar. Aun cuando durante los primeros meses de este ao se empez a verificar, en la mayora de las estadsticas, y ciertamente en Mxico, una incipiente recuperacin en el monto y en el nmero de las remesas, las cifras siguen lejos 2 3 de alcanzar las cotas registradas antes del estallido de la crisis. Adems, los recientes eventos en Grecia, en particular, y en la Unin Europea, en general, as como sus repercusiones en los mercados nos han recordado que persisten importantes vulnerabilidades en varios pases y regiones. An no es un hecho garantizado que habr una recuperacin vigorosa del dinamismo econmico en el mundo. Especficamente en los Estados Unidos, que es la economa de origen de la inmensa mayora de las remesas en el continente, persisten signos de debilidad en la demanda y permanece la gran incgnita acerca de cules sern las reacciones del consumo y de la inversin privadas cuando se inicie el retiro de los cuantiosos estmulos fiscales y monetarios puestos en marcha para mitigar las consecuencias del choque recesivo. Esta incertidumbre, as como la experiencia inslita de la misma crisis global, hacen an ms urgente el anlisis cuidadoso del fenmeno de las remesas familiares desde todos los ngulos. De dicho anlisis deben surgir estrategias y polticas pblicas que nos permitan explotar todo el potencial de las remesas en beneficio del desarrollo. Sin duda 3 4 el programa que ha diseado el BID para esta reunin cumple cabalmente este propsito. Para los bancos centrales de Amrica Latina las remesas de los trabajadores migrantes representan una extensa y desafiante agenda de trabajo. En primer lugar, habr que recordar que en el caso de las remesas familiares la estabilidad monetaria es crucial para que el gran esfuerzo cotidiano de los trabajadores migrantes se traduzca en bienestar para ellos, para sus familias y para sus comunidades. Los bancos centrales tenemos la gravsima responsabilidad ante esos migrantes, y ante la sociedad en general, de garantizar que el fruto de su trabajo no se pierda a causa de la inflacin o de la inestabilidad macroeconmica, sino que se transforme en oportunidades de crecimiento, de inversin, de ahorro y de una vida mejor. En especial, tenemos esa seria responsabilidad ante millones de familias latinoamericanas que an viven en condiciones de pobreza extrema o de miseria. Familias para las cuales en muchos casos las remesas constituyen su ingreso sustancial. En segundo lugar, tenemos que intensificar y acelerar el trabajo que la mayora de los bancos centrales de Amrica 4 5 Latina ya hemos iniciado, en colaboracin con otras autoridades financieras, para abatir cada da ms los costos de las transferencias de dinero para los trabajadores y para sus familias. En este sentido hay que encontrar el justo medio en materia de regulacin y supervisin para que las transacciones sean cada da ms baratas y, a la vez, cada da ms seguras. Un tercer desafo para el conjunto de las autoridades financieras es generar los marcos jurdicos y de regulacin que favorezcan la innovacin en materia de productos financieros  de crdito, de inversin, de ahorro, de bursatilizacin y de cobertura, entre otros- diseados para que las remesas familiares puedan derramar todo su potencial benfico. En concreto, los bancos centrales tenemos mucho que aportar en esta materia como procuradores del sano desarrollo de nuestros sistemas financieros y del buen funcionamiento de nuestros sistemas de pagos. En la misma lnea, el gran tema de las remesas familiares tambin nos impone la necesidad de vincular con eficiencia las inmensas necesidades de nuestras naciones, en vivienda, en educacin, en salud, en infraestructura para el desarrollo y 5 6 para el bienestar, con el poderoso caudal que constituyen las remesas familiares. Para nadie es un secreto que la bancarizacin sigue siendo una gran asignatura pendiente en muchos de los pases del continente. Enfrentar ese desafo implica promover una mayor competencia bancaria que se traduzca en productos y servicios de mejor precio y calidad para los usuarios. La mayor competencia propiciar el surgimiento de modalidades eficientes de ahorro y crdito diseadas precisamente para atender a lo que se ha dado en llamar la base de la pirmide social. Ah es donde se ubican la mayora de las familias de los trabajadores migrantes y ah tambin es, por lo general, donde ms notoria es la insuficiente bancarizacin. No menos decisivo es propiciar el aprovechamiento eficiente de los grandes avances tecnolgicos en materia de telecomunicaciones para abaratar los costos asociados a las transferencias de remesas. Tambin aqu una mayor competencia estimular la adopcin oportuna en nuestros pases de tecnologas de punta, lo que incidir decisivamente en un abatimiento de los costos asociados a las remesas. Como un acompaamiento permanente e indispensable de todos estos esfuerzos est la tarea de educacin financiera. 6 7 Existen numerosos esfuerzos en esta materia prcticamente en todos los pases del continente, pero es preciso intensificarlos y generar ms sinergias entre ellos. Nos corresponde a todos, desde nuestras respectivas responsabilidades, armonizar los diversos emprendimientos de educacin financiera en la regin, potenciarlos y compartir un marco conceptual robusto, desde el punto de vista de los contenidos, que le de un rumbo coherente a la propagacin de la cultura financiera en todo el continente y en todos los estratos sociales. A esto debe aadirse que la nueva etapa que apenas se est configurando para el futuro de la economa del planeta, tras el episodio de la crisis, modificar el panorama para las remesas de los migrantes. Inevitablemente las polticas migratorias de Estados Unidos, como ya sucede en otras economas avanzadas, tendern a ser ms selectivas y estrictas. Y esta tendencia en las polticas migratorias, como ya dijo el presidente Moreno, seguramente modificar el fenmeno de las remesas familiares. Ser muy importante, en este sentido, que el gobierno de los Estados Unidos avance en la aprobacin de una reforma 7 8 migratoria que sea beneficiosa para los trabajadores de toda la regin. Pero, el desafo final y el ms importante, es generar cada vez ms empleos altamente competitivos y bien remunerados. Y esa generacin de empleos no se dar, todos lo sabemos, por decreto o mediante deseos voluntariosos. Requerimos crear las condiciones propicias para ese despegue definitivo mediante reformas de fondo, estructurales, en lo educativo, en lo laboral, en el entorno de competencia y en numerosos sectores estratgicos de la actividad econmica. Nuestra meta debe ser crear las oportunidades de desarrollo para retener dentro de nuestros pases a esos trabajadores emprendedores y de alta productividad que hoy se ven forzados a emigrar. No nos conformemos con menos. Muchas gracias. 8

Title: 5th Annual Conference of the Center on Capitalism & Society: Economic dynamism and inclusion
text: 5th Annual Conference of the Center on Capitalism & Society: Economic Dynamism and Inclusion November 24, 2008 Introductory Remarks Dr. Guillermo Ortiz I would like to start my talk by thanking Edmund and the Center on Capitalism and Society for inviting me to share with you some thoughts about the conferences topic, economic dynamism and inclusion. The main concern at the Center on Capitalism and Society is an old and fundamental issue in economics: to understand what drives the economic success of nations. The premise of the Center is that the creation, development and adoption of good innovations and ideas that promote productivity are the force behind high economic performance. Given this premise, the question reduces to understand what determines a countrys ability to generate and adopt these ideas. Todays topic is indeed very related to this fundamental question: A countrys economic dynamism will be determined by the rate at which it develops or adopts new ideas and technologies to boost its productivity. Inclusion, on the other hand, could be understood as the likelihood that a specific individual in society will participate and take full advantage of the economic and social opportunities and benefits that its country may offer, and will be able to achieve a minimum level of quality of life. A relevant question concerning the relationship between dynamism and inclusion is to what extent there may be or not a trade-off between these two objectives: Do faster-growing economies achieve this by sacrificing inclusion or, on the contrary, growth and inclusion can be seen as two features that may feedback in a virtuous circle? Indeed, as opposed to a trade-off view, an alternative hypothesis is that while growth may provide resources for improving inclusion, at the same time inclusion may 1 increase the growth opportunities of a country by increasing the productive potential of its citizens. To try to answer this question, it is important first to acknowledge that, as has been documented in the literature, the dynamism of an economy and the inclusion of its participants reflects the institutional framework. What is more difficult to do is to understand which institutions are the main drivers of economic growth and how these institutions interact with each other to boost dynamism. The people at the Center on Capitalism and Society have set their minds to the task of uncovering these issues and provide a full evaluation of the costs and benefits of each institutional arrangement, within the set of market economies. At this point, it is relevant to contextualize this quest for finding the best institutions. As is stated in the Centers mission, even the most primitive market economies require such social institutions as property rights and the rule of law. Concerning this point I would like to recognize that in many developing countries these basic institutions to sustain a healthy market-oriented economy are still very deficient. In this context, the main question for economies such as mine is, how should we modify our institutions to improve dynamism and inclusion in our countries? What I will like to do in the remaining minutes of my talk, is to give some perspective regarding this last question. To focus the discussion, I will exemplify my ideas with the country I know best, which is Mexico. Mexico cannot be characterized as a dynamic economy. In the last five decades, it has registered a poor performance in terms of economic growth, if compared to other regions that started the period at similar or lower development levels. Indeed, from 1960 to 2007, Mexicos per capita GDP growth rate was only of 1.9% per year. In contrast, East Asias average per capita growth rate was 5.2% per year, while the European countries of most recent development, such as Greece, Ireland, Portugal and Spain, achieved 3.3% growth per year.1 1 The Asian countries considered includes South Korea, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Taiwan. 2  As a result of this poor performance, Mexico has significantly stagnated in terms of the living standards of its population. In the 60s Mexico had similar per capita GDP levels to those of Spain and Ireland, and higher than Korea. In 2007, Mexico is far below from all these countries. This stagnation has clearly limited the scope to advance in the inclusion of the most unprotected sectors of the population into the economic and social opportunities that the country offers.  The comparison between Mexico and Korea illustrates the former idea. In 1960, Koreas per capita GDP level represented only 42% of Mexicos. In 2007, the situation was exactly the opposite: Mexicos per capita GDP represented 42% of that of Korea. The poor performance that, on average, was observed in the Mexican economy from 1960 to 2007, can partially be explained from the stagnation experienced during the lost decade of the 80s and the financial crises that the country has suffered. However, there is also a problem related to a low potential growth.  In Banco de Mexico we have made several studies in order to calculate the countrys potential growth. This growth rate seems to be within an interval that goes from 3% to 3.5% per year. This potential growth must be considered as low, given Mexicos current development level.  Given its current population growth, Mexico would require to grow around twice its current potential growth in order to reach in 2020 Koreas present per capita GDP level. The most immediate causes of Mexicos low potential growth would be a deficient accumulation of factors, an inefficient allocation of these factors and the technology used in production. Let me review these issues in turn:  Physical and human capital accumulation: During the 1960-2007 period, Mexico has registered a much lower saving and fixed-capital investment 3 rates, than those of other developing countries. For instance, in that period, Mexico invested about 20% of its GDP, while the aforementioned European countries of recent development and the East Asian countries invested 26% and 28% of their GDPs, respectively. In the same way, Mexico also shows an unfavorable performance in terms of human capital accumulation, which has limited the countrys possibility to ascend in the value chain. The deficiency in human capital accumulation has been both in terms of quantity as well as in terms of quality. While these figures do provide a clear contrast with faster-growing economies, as will be clear in the following minutes, my main argument is that the low accumulation of productive resources has been itself a consequence of deeper factors shaping the economy.  Efficient allocation of resources: Indeed, even given our current resource endowments, these could be allocated more efficiently. In particular, there are several barriers and distortions that obstruct the dynamic and efficient allocation of resources in Mexico, which imply an ineffective exploitation of the existing comparative advantages the country has, as well as a low growth in productivity. Two of them seem to be of particular importance. First, there has been an inefficient use of labor as a consequence of important rigidities and adverse incentives existing in this market. In fact, Mexico stands out negatively in various international comparisons due to the high existing barriers to labor mobility. These rigidities, that interact with other adverse incentives that tend to reward the informal sector, have direct consequences in terms of dynamism and inclusion. In particular, they: i) complicate labor mobility to sectors or regions where productivity is higher; ii) discourage the adoption of modern technologies and human capital investment; and, iii) promote the growth of a low-productivity informal sector, where labor does not enjoy the benefits of the formal social security system. Evidently, the high bargaining power that labor unions in some 4 important sectors of non tradable goods enjoy has also become a rentextracting mechanism and has contributed to restrict the mobility of labor and the adoption of more productive technologies. The other type of distortions that also affect the efficient use of factors of production and reduce competitiveness of the Mexican economy are regulatory problems in sectors that supply inputs through networks, such as financial services, telecommunications, energy and transportation. In the absence of an appropriate regulation, high prices, low quality of service, restrictions to generalized use of basic inputs and, in general, a loss of competitiveness may be observed. Indeed, in the absence of a pro-competitive regulation, the appearance of dominant suppliers that take over a significant market share and exploit their market power to extract rents is generally observed, damaging consumers and competitiveness of industries that use intensively these inputs.  Modern production technologies: As a consequence of the barriers of entry to some strategic sectors and to the free movement of factors just mentioned, Mexico presents low rates in adoption of advanced technologies and efficient work practices. If the adoption of state-of-the-art technologies is low, the production of new ideas is almost inexistent. Dated technologies and inefficient work practices, coupled with the other distortions mentioned and with a deficient accumulation of productive factors, have caused a low rate of total factor productivity growth and, thus, a low competitiveness of the Mexican economy. Given these immediate causes, the relevant questions are: Why Mexico has not being accumulating factors of production at a faster rate? Why Mexico has not being allocating more efficiently its factors of production towards their most productive sectors and its comparative advantages? Why does Mexico tend to produce with dated technologies? The answer to these questions is the same: 5 the current institutional framework does not provide enough incentives to boost innovation and the adoption of modern technologies, to accumulate resources and to allocate them efficiently. Indeed, the performance of total factor productivity, factor accumulation and the efficiency with which factors are allocated to different productive activities must not be taken as exogenous elements that determine the economys growth but, on the contrary, these are endogenous consequences of the system of incentives in which the economic agents and policymakers interact. In this circumstance we need to work on improving those features that make an economy more competitive. Within these, I may highlight the following:  Promote contestability conditions in markets of generalized-use inputs, network supplied inputs and final goods. Economic theory, as well as international experience, show that when an economy operates under competitive conditions: 9 a higher innovation rate is stimulated and firms are encouraged to adopt modern technologies and the most efficient work practices; 9 consumers have access to higher-quality and more-diverse goods and services, at lower prices; and, 9 people have more opportunities of having a job that pays according to their productivity. Particularly, when there are no barriers to entry in markets, agents that decide entering to an activity would do it by investing in modern technologies. Barriers to entry, in contrast, allow those firms that dominate the market to obtain monopoly rents using inefficient technologies and, as a consequence, they face small incentives to adopt more efficient technologies. In this context, it is noteworthy to state that, according to the OECD, Mexico stands out negatively in terms of the imposed barriers to competition. 6  Increase flexibility in allocation of resources. As mentioned before, market rigidities, such as in the labor market, cause an inefficient allocation of resources by limiting factor movement towards more productive activities. Additionally, these rigidities also tend to avoid the adoption of modern technologies and human capital investment.  Efficient implementation of public policies. A third relevant factor is the efficient implementation of public policies. These have an important role to play since they actively take part in those areas of the economy where the social return is higher than the private one. Evidently, their efficient implementation depends on making the agents in charge of their design and execution, to face the adequate incentives that could maximize these policies social return. In order to obtain the desired results from these changes, we need to work on the improvement of an environment were property rights are respected and the rule of law prevails. To conclude, it is clear that, in order to enhance the much needed economic dynamism and inclusion in Mexico, as well as in other developing countries with similar characteristics, a deep change in the economys basic system of incentives is necessary. This change must substitute the current structures that have allowed rent-seeking activities to new ones aimed to promote competitiveness, transparency and respect for the rule of law and property rights. It is especially relevant to decidedly advance in actions that contribute to a higher economic competition as well as having more flexibility in resource allocation. Thank you very much. I am sure that we will have a very productive conference that will provide us with relevant insights related to the points Edmund and I have highlighted. 7

Title: Simulation in Computational Finance and Economics: Tools and Emerging Applications
text: Simulation in Computational Finance and Economics: Tools and Emerging Applications. Book Presentation Manuel Ramos-Francia Deputy Governor Banco de Mexico October 18, 2012 Good evening. I am very pleased to be here tonight. I would like to thank the organizers of this event for the invitation and, on behalf of Banco de Mexico, extend a warm welcome to all the participants that are here with us -in particular those that came from overseas- to share some of their insights, experiences, and knowledge. The subject that occupies us today is the intersection of three fascinating disciplines, namely, simulation, computer science, and economics. They have all achieved impressive results; and have, jointly, got a lot of attention from academics, policy makers, and practitioners. Having said that, as a way of introduction, let me first very briefly talk about the early stages of these three disciplines, and then I will talk more concretely about the book. One can argue that simulation started in 1947 with the polish mathematician Stanislaw Ulam playing solitaire.1 It occurred to him that by playing several times one could estimate the probability of various outcomes. After having access to one of the first computers, due to his participation in the Manhattan project, he realized that his approach could be implemented in practice. Mr. Ulam and his co-author, Nicolas Metropolis, published the first paper on the subject in 1949 and, thus, simulation was born, leading to an array of applications.2 Second, for many years any method that required several calculating steps was of no practical interest. In fact, it was not until computers were actually constructed that a systematic study of algorithms began. Computer science certainly includes 1 As with many inventions and discoveries it is difficult to attribute them solely to one person. For instance, in this case, one can also think of Buffons needle problem to estimate in the 18th century as a prelude to simulation. 2 The name Monte Carlo derives from the fact that Ulams uncle went gambling to the casinos in that city. 1 areas such as programming, numerical analysis, and what has been called, for a lack of a better name, non-numerical analysis.3 This last area refers to the study of algorithms, in terms of their efficiency and complexity. This discipline immediately brings to mind intellectual giants like Charles Babbage, Alan Turing, and Donald Knuth, to name only a few.4 Third, modern economics, which I am going to count as encompassing finance, was born with the well-known Scottish economist Adam Smith. Little did he know at the time about the different branches that would in due course develop from his brainchild. In economic modeling, if one just considers the more general case and, in particular, the stochastic case, one is forced to leave the world of analytical closed solutions or, at times, is unable to solve the model at all. In this context, simulation in computational economics (and finance) lets us solve a greater set of models, which generally involve stochastic elements. In other words, with it, tractability for an important set of models has been and is being significantly extended. Allow me now to present the book entitled: Simulation in Computational Finance and Economics: Tools and Emerging Applications. It is divided into three sections, having a total of eighteen chapters. I will very briefly talk about each section and, in the interest of time, underscore a few selected chapters from each section. I apologize in advance to the authors of the papers that I will not be mentioning. Payments systems are crucial to the conduct of monetary policy. In fact, in many cases, central banks have as an aim -by law- bringing about their adequate functioning.5 They are -so to speak- the set of pipes and drains in the transmission of monetary policy. Thus, their study is of special interest to monetary economists and policy makers alike. There are several issues on payment systems one should be concerned about, from methodological to regulatory ones. In this context, consider first the paper: The use of simulations as an analytical tool for payments systems by Martin Diehl. This is an excellent introduction to the material, explaining to the uninitiated reader in a straightforward way the use of simulations for payments systems. It lucidly compares the use of simulations vis-avis the use of analytical tools. 3 Programming can be thought as the design, formulation, and execution of algorithms. Numerical analysis refers, loosely speaking, to the study of the behavior of numbers and operations in a computer. 4 Babbage (1791 -1871) originated the concept of a programmable computer. Turing (1912  1954) is considered the father of computer science. Knuth (1938-?) can be considered the father of the analysis of algorithms. 5 For example, part of Article 2 of the Banco de Mexicos Law states: Seran tambien finalidades del Banco promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. 2 As for the article Preparing simulations in large value payment systems using historical data, Heijmans and Heuver explain how the data associated to such systems could be used in the creation of stress scenarios. This study is aimed at the inexperienced researcher. In addition, it describes what can be called the best practices in the use of data in the simulation of large value payments systems. In Simulation Approaches to Risk, Efficiency, and Liquidity Usage in Payment Systems, Laine, Korpinen, and Hellqvist propose the use of payment systems simulation as a regular activity in the analysis of payment systems stability. This is based on the fact that in modern economies nearly all the transactions are settled through payment systems. They consider key aspects in the study of payment systems such as: the liquidity usage by participants, the design mechanisms of liquidity requirements, and the identification of risks in payment systems. The authors are affiliated to an institution which has been a leader in the use of simulation in payment systems, the Bank of Finland. In the article Liquidity management in the Large Value Payment Systems (LVPS): need for an agent based models complex approach Arciero and Picillo, make the case for the use of agent-based simulations to study complexity in the context of liquidity management for banks which interact in a LVPS. The authors highlight three areas in which agent based simulations are applicable, namely: i) the commercial banks strategies in a LVPS; ii) the design of LVPS, in particular, the evaluation of new and current policies; and, iii) the financial stability assessment of LVPS, as part of the financial infrastructure. Finally, in this section, the article Liquidity Saving in CHAPS (Clearing House Automated Payment System): A Simulation Study, by McLafferty and Denbee, proposes a simulation methodology to assess the liquidity efficiency in the UK large payment system by the implementation of a Liquidity Saving Mechanism.6 This type of simulations allows one to conduct experiments in policy variations, as part of a large payment system, to assess the extent to which a given change, in this case, the introduction of a Liquidity Saving Mechanism, might be economically beneficial. In the second section, risk management is considered. This subject has a long and truly interesting history, perhaps starting with an epistolary exchange between a lawyer and a mathematician -Fermat and Pascal- on pricing a game with uncertain outcomes.7 Nowadays, it encompasses a plethora of subjects. Within this section, I would like to emphasize one article: Systemic Risk, Stress Testing and Financial Contagion: Their Interaction and Measurement, by 6 The Clearing House Automated Payment System (CHAPS) is a sterling payments scheme that processes and settles both systemically important and time-dependent payments. 7 For an interesting narrative on the topic see Bernstein, P.L. (1996). Against the Gods, The Remarkable Story of Risk. John Wiley and Sons, N.Y. For a translation of some of the actual letters see, for example, 3 Martinez, Lopez and Lopez. These authors present a network model for which a distribution of the losses for the banking system as a whole is obtained. It accounts for contagion and second round effects. Thus, they are able to estimate a plethora of risk measurements, in particular, those capturing systemic risk, as well as their dynamics. More generally, network modeling has gained prominence in the area of systemic risk. It has deemed to be particularly suitable due to its flexibility and, in addition, the need to model complex phenomena. In effect, network models are akin to the structure some financial systems have. Thus, although in this type of models some elements are lost in terms of the incentives financial institutions face, it is their complex interaction -as captured by networks- that can potentially shed additional light on the properties of systemic risk and its propagation. Agents based simulation is currently a popular modeling approach. It focuses on understanding the interactions effects of many independent agents in a welldefined system. It has found applications in several subjects. In my opinion two articles stand out. First, consider the paper Optimal Patent Design by Brabazon. As economists we know the main justification for the existence of patents: to incentivize technological invention. Nonetheless, as the author himself claims, little is known regarding how patent policy affects the rate of technological advancement.8 In this context, relevant questions are the extent to which a patent holder should be given market power and for how long. A conventional answer is that these should be commensurate with the costs involved in the research process leading to the inventions. Nonetheless, empirical research in this area is difficult, as results are highly model-dependent and, particularly, because it is difficult to quantify the scope and protection across patents. In this context, this paper proposes an agents-based model which, by simulating, is capable of assessing various policies, and their impact on the rate of technical advancement. The second paper, Modeling the FX market Traders Behavior, by Edward Tsang and Olsen, studies the collective behavior of foreign exchange traders using an agent-based model. The study of foreign exchange markets using different approaches is essential, as it is nowadays widely recognized that much of their behavior in the short run is not completely explained by ordinary asset pricing models.9 8 Additional relevant policies are subsidizes and preferential tax treatments for a company or individual involved in applied research. Furthermore, as known, basic research cannot be patented. Thus, governments typically provide generous resources to that end. 9 As in the microstructure of foreign exchange markets literature, for example see Sarno, L. and Taylor, M. (2006). The Economics of Exchange Rates. Cambridge University Press, U.K. 4 In effect, agents based models in some cases have more flexibility to capture more closely some of the features of the organization of FX markets, which are typically mute in more conventional models. Two features of these markets that are adequately captured by this type of models are: first, the fact that some of these markets are essentially decentralized and, second, accordingly, information is only sluggishly conveyed across market participants. As for my final remarks, let me mention three points. First, although these disciplines are interesting by themselves and intellectually challenging, at the end of the day they are only means to an end. They should allow us to have a better understanding of economic and financial phenomena. Thus, they should put us in a vantage point to design better policy and regulation, which, in turn, should provide us all with economic welfare. Second, simulation in computational economics and finance is a very useful tool. Yet, it is in their complementarity that their usefulness increases. For instance, a network model is well served by supporting it with economic assumptions. In other words, it is in the interaction of these disciplines that one finds the cross-fertilization of ideas, which allows for a deeper and broader understanding of the challenging policy and regulatory difficulties we currently face. Third, some have said that in the field of economics, well-established methods failed by not predicting and, perhaps, not preventing the crisis.10 I beg to differ. I believe that most, if not all, of the phenomena that were conducive to the crisis, such as adverse selection, moral hazard, asymmetric information, mechanism design, price bubbles, herding behavior, liquidity risk, among many others, had been closely and intensely studied for quite a long time before the crisis. I think it was rather the misplaced belief in the markets self-regulation capabilities, where externalities were known to exist that, to a great degree, sowed the seeds of the last global financial crisis. In effect, some members of the profession did raise their voices warning us of the incoming peril. Without further ado, I applaud everyone for their efforts towards a better understanding of the subject and sharing your thoughts on the matter. Thank you! 10 For example, in the Motivation of the book, it says In the field of economics, the application of simulation models has permeated slowly due to the preference of well-established methods over simulation, although these have failed to predict the recent financial crisis.
