text: REMARKS BY GALIA DEPUTY GOVERNOR BORJA GoMEZ ON INTERNATIONAL WOMEN'S DAY March 7, 2023, at the Institutional Stock Exchange, CDMX. Good morning, it is an honor for me to speak on this day, accompanied by such distinguished guests. I am particularly grateful to Maria Ariza for the invitation to participate in this event organized by the Institutional Stock Exchange. Within the framework of International Women's Day, I celebrate the "Letter of Commitment to Equal Pay", an initiative that invites Afores, investment funds and representatives of the business sector in Mexico to commit to promoting conditions of equal pay within their institutions. Private organizations create jobs, offer products that meet people's needs, and create community. Thus, they contribute in various ways to society, not only because they bring stability to regional economies but also because they innovate and contribute to technological development. However, no company can be truly successful in an unequal society. Despite the fact that, in recent years, significant actions have been promoted in Mexico to promote equality, we continue to face challenges that do not allow us to completely eliminate gender gaps. There is evidence that women's participation in the labor market is fundamental for the country's economic development and entails numerous benefits for society, such as: an increase in productivity, greater innovation, better decision-making, and worker retention. However, female labor participation in Mexico continues to be among the lowest in Latin America and the Caribbean. There are multiple barriers that hinder women's entry into the labor force, one of the most important is the inequality in the division of unpaid domestic work, since the burden falls to a greater extent on us. According to INEGI, in Mexico a woman spends an average of 47 hours a week on domestic and care work, which reduces her time available to work and can prevent her from accessing positions of greater responsibility. The double shift that women have could be the reason why many take informal, self-employed or part-time jobs that can be more easily adapted to their schedules. Women still face challenges, biases and barriers that do not allow us to be included equally in the public, social and economic spheres. Aware of this, the Bank of Mexico has promoted a research agenda on the behavior of different variables with a gender perspective. In particular, during the last two years, when we had the COVID-19 health emergency, 5 boxes were published in Quarterly Reports; 3 boxes in the Regional Economies Report and a Research Document. Next, I will refer to the most outstanding results of these investigations. On the labor market side:  In one of the boxes, it was found that the loss of employment during the initial phase of the pandemic affected both genders in a similar way, but the recovery occurred differently between women and men. The reincorporation of women into the labor market happened more slowly. This could be influenced by the following factors:  On the one hand, the closure of the economy had a longer impact on sectors in which women have a greater participation and sectors whose recovery was more gradual, as was the case of various services, such as restaurants and accommodation, and the informal sector as a whole.  On the other hand, the increase in the demand for home care, both due to the closure of schools and the tasks of caring for the sick and elderly, could be an important factor behind the slower reincorporation of women into the labor market.  Likewise, with the health emergency there was an increase of around 1.5 million women who reported not being interested in obtaining a job, even if they were offered one.  In this last aspect, another of the findings of this Box is that the proportion of women who reported dedicating themselves exclusively to household chores increased by more than double among those who have two or more children compared to the rest. Women who had at least two children accounted for 68% of the total female population unavailable for work in 2020.  In another study, it was found that return to work also had differences by gender, due to geographical and sectoral adjustment costs. In the center and north of the country, women showed a greater propensity to remain outside the formal labor market than men, while the percentage of women who changed sectors or locations was lower than the percentage corresponding to men. This lower frequency of transitions between employer sectors and job location suggests that labor market adjustments represent higher costs for women workers in the country.  As a consequence of the above, a third study found that the gender gap in terms of the probability of employment, that is, the probability of finding a given job if one is a man or a woman, widened during the pandemic. Regarding inflation: 1. In one of the Boxes and in the Research Document, it was found that, although the vast majority of households have been affected by the rise in prices that we have experienced for the last two years, the effects of inflation can be heterogeneous according to the composition of the consumption basket of each household, which in turn depends on factors related to the income and demographic composition of each family. In this regard, these studies suggest that women can influence household spending patterns if they have a greater possibility of reflecting their preferences in the consumption of goods and services that are acquired: i. On the one hand, when women increase their share of family income, household risk aversion increases, which in turn leads to an increase in precautionary savings. Thus, to the extent that extra savings are encouraged in families, household assets increase, and with this, wealth inequality is reduced, the effect of which tends to be more favourable among lower-income households. i. On the other hand, when women's contribution to household income exceeds 40%, there is a smaller increase in the cost of the consumption basket, due to a greater diversification of the goods and services purchased. In this sense, it has been observed that although the vast majority of households have been affected by inflation, it has had less impact on nuclear households where women participate more, since, for example, their preferences increase food intake in households. Of course, these results are completely conditional on the nature of the shocks we have experienced, but to a large extent, they exemplify the potential effects of seeking gender equality, equal pay and show the attention we should have on the issue. Finally, I would like to point out that, despite all the progress made in terms of the role of women in society, in the economy and in the labour market, it is clear that there is still much to be done and there is still a long way to go, despite the efforts of each and every one of us in our areas of competence, it will allow us to continue breaking barriers and changing paradigms. Thanks a lot.
text_original: PALABRAS DE LA SUBGOBERNADORA GALIA BORJA GMEZ EN EL MARCO DEL DA INTERNACIONAL DE LA MUJER 7 de Marzo de 2023, en la Bolsa Institucional de Valores, CDMX. Buenos das, es un honor para m hablar en este da, acompaada por tan distinguidos invitados. Agradezco en particular a Mara Ariza por la invitacin a participar en este evento organizado por la Bolsa Institucional de Valores. En el marco del Da Internacional de las Mujeres, celebro la "Carta Compromiso por la Igualdad Salarial", iniciativa que invita a Afores, fondos de inversin y representantes del sector empresarial de Mxico a comprometerse en promover condiciones de equidad salarial dentro de sus instituciones. Las organizaciones privadas crean empleos, ofrecen productos que satisfacen las necesidades de la gente, y crean comunidad. As, contribuyen de diversas formas a la sociedad, no slo porque aportan estabilidad a las economas regionales sino tambin porque innovan y contribuyen al desarrollo tecnolgico. No obstante, ninguna empresa puede tener verdadero xito en una sociedad desigual. A pesar de que, en los ltimos aos, en Mxico se han impulsado acciones significativas para promover la igualdad, continuamos enfrentando desafos que no permiten eliminar completamente las brechas de gnero. Existe evidencia de que la participacin de las mujeres en el mercado laboral es fundamental para el desarrollo econmico del pas y conlleva numerosos beneficios para la sociedad, como: un incremento en la productividad, mayor innovacin, mejor toma de decisiones, y retencin de trabajadores. Sin embargo, la participacin laboral femenina en Mxico contina siendo de las ms bajas de Amrica Latina y el Caribe. Hay mltiples barreras que dificultan el ingreso de las mujeres a la fuerza laboral, una de las ms importantes es la desigualdad en la divisin del trabajo domstico no remunerado, ya que la carga recae en mayor medida en nosotras. i De acuerdo con el INEGI, en Mxico una mujer dedica en promedio 47 horas semanales a labores domsticas y de cuidado, lo que le reduce su tiempo disponible para trabajar y puede impedir su acceso a puestos de mayor responsabilidad. La doble jornada que tenemos las mujeres podra ser la causa por la cual, muchas toman trabajos informales, por cuenta propia o a tiempo parcial que puedan adaptase ms fcilmente a sus horarios. Las mujeres an enfrentamos retos, sesgos y barreras que no permiten nuestra inclusin paritaria en las esferas pblica, social y econmica. Conscientes de ello, desde el Banco de Mxico se ha impulsado una agenda de investigacin sobre el comportamiento de distintas variables con una perspectiva de gnero. En particular, durante los ltimos dos aos, en que tuvimos la emergencia sanitaria por la COVID-19, se publicaron 5 recuadros en Informes Trimestrales; 3 recuadros en el Reporte de Economas Regionales y un Documento de Investigacin. A continuacin, voy a referirme a los resultados ms sobresalientes de estas investigaciones. Por parte del lado del mercado laboral: 1. En uno de los recuadros se encontr que la prdida de empleo durante la fase inicial de la pandemia afect de manera similar a ambos gneros, pero la recuperacin ocurri de manera diferenciada entre mujeres y hombres. La reincorporacin de las mujeres al mercado laboral sucedi de manera ms lenta. Esto pudo ser influenciado por los siguientes factores: i. Por un lado, el cierre de la economa impacto por ms tiempo a sectores en los que las mujeres tienen una mayor participacin y sectores cuya recuperacin fue ms gradual, como fue el caso de diversos servicios, como los de restaurantes y alojamiento, y el sector informal en su conjunto. 2 ii. Por otro lado, el incremento en la demanda de cuidados en el hogar, tanto por el cierre de las escuelas como por las tareas de asistencia a enfermos y adultos mayores, pudo ser un factor importante detrs de la reincorporacin ms lenta de las mujeres al mercado laboral. iii. Asimismo, con la emergencia sanitaria existi un aumento de alrededor de 1.5 millones de mujeres que reportaron no estar interesadas en obtener un empleo, aun si se les ofreciera uno. iv. En este ltimo aspecto, otro de los hallazgos de este Recuadro es que la proporcin de mujeres que report dedicarse exclusivamente a los quehaceres domsticos aument en ms del doble entre las que tienen dos o ms hijos respecto del resto. Las mujeres que tenan al menos dos hijos representaban 68% del total de la poblacin femenina no disponible para trabajar en 2020. 2. En otra investigacin, se encontr que la reincorporacin laboral tambin tuvo diferencias por gnero, debido a costos de ajuste geogrfico y sectorial. En el centro y norte del pas, las mujeres mostraron una propensin mayor a permanecer fuera del mercado de trabajo formal que los hombres, al tiempo que el porcentaje de mujeres que cambi de sector o de ubicacin, fue menor que el porcentaje correspondiente a hombres. Esta menor frecuencia de transiciones entre sectores empleadores y ubicacin del trabajo, sugiere que los ajustes del mercado laboral representan costos ms altos para las trabajadoras del pas. 3. Como consecuencia de lo anterior, en un tercer trabajo se encontr que la brecha de gnero en trminos de la probabilidad de ocupacin, esto es, la probabilidad de encontrar un empleo dado si se es hombre o mujer, se ampli durante la pandemia. 3 En cuanto a la inflacin: 1. En uno de los Recuadros y en el Documento de Investigacin se encontr que, aunque la gran mayora de los hogares se ha visto afectada por el alza de precios que hemos vivido desde hace dos aos, los efectos de la inflacin pueden ser heterogneos de acuerdo con la composicin de la canasta de consumo de cada hogar, lo cual depende a su vez de factores relacionados al ingreso y a la composicin demogrfica de cada familia. Al respecto, estos estudios sugieren que las mujeres pueden influir en los patrones de gasto del hogar si tienen una mayor posibilidad de reflejar sus preferencias en el consumo de bienes y servicios que se adquieren: i. Por una parte, cuando las mujeres incrementan su participacin en el ingreso familiar, aumenta la aversin al riesgo de los hogares, lo que a su vez genera un incremento en los ahorros precautorios. As, en la medida en que se propicia un ahorro extra en las familias, los activos del hogar aumentan, y con ello, se ayuda a reducir la desigualdad de riqueza, cuyo efecto tiende a ser ms favorable entre los hogares de menores recursos. i. Por otra parte, cuando la contribucin de las mujeres al ingreso del hogar supera el 40% se aprecia un menor incremento en el costo de la canasta de consumo, debido a una mayor diversificacin de los bienes y servicios adquiridos. En este sentido, se ha observado que si bien la gran mayora de los hogares se han visto afectados por la inflacin, sta ha impactado menos en los hogares nucleares donde participan ms las mujeres, pues por ejemplo sus preferencias aumentan la ingesta de alimentos en los hogares. 4 Por supuesto, estos resultados son completamente condicionales a la naturaleza de los choques que hemos vivido, pero en buena medida, ejemplifican los efectos potenciales en buscar la igualdad de gnero, la igualdad salarial y muestran la atencin que debemos tener en el tema. Finalmente, me gustara sealar que, a pesar de todos los avances logrados en trminos del rol de las mujeres en la sociedad, en la economa y en el mercado laboral, es evidente que an falta mucho por hacer y es todava extenso el camino por recorrer, sin embargo, el esfuerzo de todos y cada una de nosotros en nuestros mbitos de competencia, nos permitir seguir rompiendo barreras y cambiando paradigmas. Muchas gracias. 5

text: REMARKS BY DEPUTY GOVERNOR GALIA BORJA GoMEZ at the Forum "Financial Health for Women" March 22, 2023, Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE), CDMX Good morning, it is an honor for me to speak on this day, accompanied by such distinguished guests, friends and colleagues. I thank Lie. Oscar Rosado Jimenez, president of CONDUSEF for his very kind invitation. I very much celebrate this initiative of CONDUSEF that seeks to contribute to promoting the empowerment of women and raise awareness of the importance of building their financial independence and with it, without a doubt, a better Mexico for all. Being aware of the situation under which many women live in the country, today I want to share with you a reflection based on my years of professional experience, which has been in the financial sector. I would like to begin by acknowledging that unfortunately in our country there is still a long way to go because gender differences persist, are significant and affect the development of women in a multidimensional way. To contextualize the depth of the challenges and difficulties we face, I want to briefly share with you four facts that I find worrying:  Of all women between the ages of 15 and 65 in the country, only 46% participate in the labor market, which is in contrast to the 76% of men who participate in the labor market for the same age group.  As a result, female labor participation in Mexico is one of the lowest in the Latin American and Caribbean region.  Likewise, of employed women, 56% are employed in the informal sector.  At the same time, almost 28% of Mexican women over the age of 15 have reported having suffered some type of economic and patrimonial violence and discrimination throughout their lives. The different barriers and gaps that operate in our country generate negative synergies that limit development. By not having a permanent job, or having it in the informal market, women are limited in their access to financial products and services, which in turn affects their economic independence. The lack of these services makes it more difficult for us to build wealth, to be financially independent and makes us more vulnerable to situations of family violence. In this context, being a woman in the labor market has great challenges. The gender stereotypes that are still prevalent make us feel insecure about our abilities and limit our growth to positions of greater responsibility. These same stereotypes make us have to try harder. Our academic or work credentials are not enough, day by day we have to demonstrate more than and repeatedly that we deserve to be in the position we have, whether with our superiors, our peers or even with our work teams. As a result, we tend to be less tolerant of failure and usually only apply for a promotion when we feel overqualified. Today I have the privilege of being here giving this speech as Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico. Which I have achieved in addition to the great effort and discipline, and the support of decision-makers, in part thanks to the fact that:  I grew up in a family that supported me at all times, that motivated me to have a solid academic background and gave me the freedom to choose the degree of my choice.  Throughout my professional career, I had the privilege of having bosses and mentors who encouraged me in my professional development by giving me their trust, recognizing my work, offering me greater responsibilities and, for example, giving me a job promotion to a management position in my first months of motherhood.  By becoming a mother, I did not have to sacrifice my work life. I was able to count on the maternity leave granted by law, and access to a care network that allowed me to continue working. Although I have to admit that it has been a challenge to reconcile work life while being in the care of a family. These personal opportunities that I have had are not representative for the majority of Mexican women, so we must continue working to promote human resources policies that favor the personal, family and professional development of women. It is important to recognize that a big step was taken in Mexico in 2019 when the constitutional reform of gender pandad was approved, which stipulates that half of the political decision-making positions be held by women. Thanks to this reform, we have come closer to achieving gender equality at all three levels of government. I firmly believe that women who play a managerial role have the responsibility to be mentors with the women in our work team and with the collaborators of our institutions. Sharing our story, with successes and difficulties, helps to set real expectations based on experience, which can inspire new leadership. Thus, all of us who play a leadership role have the responsibility to continue breaking barriers and changing paradigms, so that as a country we can overcome sticky floors, broken stairs and glass ceilings. In the future, the statistics I mentioned should be only an echo of a distant past. Thanks a lot!
text_original: PALABRAS DE LA SUBGOBERNADORA GALIA BORJA GMEZ en el Foro "Salud Financiera para Mujeres" 22 de marzo de 2023, Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE), CDMX Buenos das, es un honor para m hablar en este da, acompaada por tan distinguidos invitados, amigos y compaeros. Agradezco al Lie. Oscar Rosado Jimnez, presidente de la CONDUSEF por su muy amable invitacin. Celebro mucho esta iniciativa de la CONDUSEF que busca contribuir a impulsar el empoderamiento de las mujeres y generar conciencia de la importancia de construir su independencia financiera y con ello, sin lugar a dudas, un mejor Mxico para todos. Siendo consciente de la situacin bajo la que viven muchas mujeres en el pas, el da de hoy quiero compartirles una reflexin basada en mis aos de experiencia profesional, la cual ha sido en el sector financiero. Me gustara iniciar reconociendo que lamentablemente en nuestro pas an existe un lago camino por recorrer pues las diferencias de gnero persisten, son significativas y afectan el desarrollo de las mujeres de manera multidimensional. Para contextualizar la profundidad de los retos y dificultades a los que nos enfrentamos, quiero compartirles brevemente cuatro datos que me parecen preocupantes:  De todas las mujeres que tienen entre 15 y 65 aos en el pas, slo el 46% participan en el mercado laboral, lo que es contrastante con el 76% de los hombres que participa laboralmente para el mismo grupo de edad.  Como consecuencia, la participacin laboral femenina en Mxico es una de las ms bajas de la regin de Amrica Latina y el Caribe.  Asimismo, de las mujeres ocupadas, el 56% se encuentran empleadas en la informalidad. 1  Al tiempo que casi el 28% de las mexicanas mayores de 15 aos han reportado haber sufrido algn tipo de violencia econmica, patrimonial y discriminacin a lo largo de su vida. Las distintas barreras y brechas que operan en nuestro pas generan sinergias negativas que limitan el desarrollo. Al no contar con un trabajo fijo, o que ste sea en el mercado informal, se limita a las mujeres en el acceso a productos y servicios financieros, lo que a su vez afecta su independencia econmica. La falta de estos servicios nos lleva a una mayor dificultad para construir un patrimonio, ser financieramente independientes y nos hace ms vulnerables ante situaciones de violencia familiar. En este contexto, ser una mujer dentro del mercado laboral tiene grandes retos. Los estereotipos de gnero que an prevalecen hacen que nos sintamos inseguras sobre nuestras capacidades y nos limitan el crecimiento a posiciones de mayor responsabilidad. Estos mismos estereotipos hacen que tengamos que esforzarnos ms. No basta con nuestras credenciales acadmicas o laborales, da con da tenemos que demostrar con creces y de manera reiterada que merecemos estar en la posicin que tengamos, ya sea con nuestros superiores, nuestros pares o incluso con nuestros equipos de trabajo. Por ello, tendemos a ser menos tolerantes con el fracaso y, por lo general, slo solicitamos un ascenso cuando nos sentimos sobrecalificadas. El da de hoy tengo el privilegio de estar aqu dando este discurso como Subgobernadora del Banco de Mxico. Lo cual he logrado adems de por el mucho esfuerzo y disciplina, y el apoyo de personas tomadoras de decisin, en parte gracias a que:  Crec en una familia que me apoy en todo momento, que me motiv a tener una slida formacin acadmica y me dio la libertad de elegir la licenciatura de mi preferencia.  A lo largo de mi carrera profesional, tuve el privilegio de contar con jefes, jefas y mentores que me impulsaron en mi desarrollo profesional al brindarme su confianza, al reconocer mi trabajo, al ofrecerme mayores responsabilidades y, por ejemplo, otorgarme una promocin laboral a un puesto directivo en mis primeros meses de maternidad. 2  Al convertirme en madre no tuve que sacrificar mi vida laboral. Pude contar con la licencia de maternidad que otorga la ley, y el acceso a una red de cuidados que me permiti seguir trabajado. Aunque he de admitir que ha sido un reto conciliar la vida laboral a la par de estar al cuidado de una familia. Estas oportunidades personales con las que he contado, no son representativas para la mayora de las mujeres mexicanas, por lo que debemos seguir trabajando para promover polticas de recursos humanos que favorezcan el desarrollo personal, familiar y profesional de las mujeres. Es importante reconocer que en Mxico se dio un gran paso en 2019 cuando se aprob la reforma constitucional de pandad de gnero, la cual estipula que la mitad de los cargos de decisin poltica sean ocupados por mujeres. Gracias a esta reforma, nos hemos acercado ms a lograr la igualdad de gnero en los tres niveles de gobierno. Creo firmemente que las mujeres que desempeamos un rol directivo tenemos la responsabilidad de ser mentoras con las mujeres de nuestro equipo de trabajo y con las colaboradoras de nuestras instituciones. El compartir nuestra historia, con xitos y dificultades, ayuda a establecer expectativas reales basadas en la experiencia, lo que puede inspirar nuevos liderazgos. As, todos y todas los que desempeamos un rol directivo tenemos la responsabilidad de seguir rompiendo barreras y cambiando paradigmas, para que como pas logremos superar los pisos pegajosos, las escaleras rotas y los techos de cristal. Title:
"The role of institutions in Mexico in promoting the "S" within ESG, Second Santander Sustainable Forum", Irene Espinosa, Deputy Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

Full text
text: THE ROLE OF INSTITUTIONS IN MEXICO IN THE PROMOTION OF THE 'S' WITHIN ASG Face-to-face conference by Irene Espinosa Cantellano, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico, at the Second Sustainable Santander Forum, held in Mexico City, on October 13, 2022 Good morning to all of you. I would like to begin by thanking Hector Grisi and Felipe Garcia for the invitation to this second edition of the Sustainable Santander Forum. Initiatives like this are of paramount importance, as environmental, social and corporate governance, or ESG, principles are the only path to achieving a sustainable recovery. i Congratulations to Santander for the leadership! Spaces like these are necessary to achieve greater internalization, awareness and dissemination of the benefits of ensuring clean and inclusive development in all dimensions and, with it, contribute to our own subsistence as a species. This topic is very fascinating due to its recent dizzying development, since the COVID-19 Pandemic. Emanating from the ethical investment philosophy of the 1960s, ESG principles have become cornerstones in the sustainable development of investment projects and an inclusive and sustainable economy. In recent years, there have been important advances in the field of environmental risks and vulnerabilities arising from climate change. Of course, that is to be applauded. However, there are two aspects that often go unnoticed or take a back seat when talking about ESG principles; I am referring to social and governance factors. This happens, most likely, because if the measurement and analysis of climatic factors are already complicated, they are usually even more so when we talk about the "S" and the "G". Today in particular, I want to address the Social factor and reflect on how it is that the ambiguity or lack of precision in the definition of this factor, causes it to be often undervalued. By definition, it is a very general factor, as it has to cover multiple aspects of the human being as a social being; from issues of human rights, communication, decent working conditions, equitable remuneration, gender and diversity issues, social justice and transparency, to mention a few. The challenge is precisely to incorporate these elements into the traditional performance measurements of institutions and to define their social impact contributions aimed at improving people's lives. Although the current ESG principles originated in the S, the path of their incorporation into investments has been guided over the decades by climate risk. Consequently, a natural way to proceed with the inclusion of Social criteria in investment principles is to follow the same steps that were used at the time to define the measurement of the environmental sphere:  First, the use of standardized quantitative data and metrics is crucial. This makes it possible to compare and classify the results of different actions and policies, in order to have robust social impact studies. These measurements help investors assess the relative contribution level of institutions or companies to key social issues, similar to the assessment of their environmental profile.  The next step is to develop an adequate framework for data reporting and dissemination of actions and statistics, so that the information is transparent and accessible for decision-making by economic agents. In short, the focus should be on closing the data and information gap available for the Social factor. Following this line, the intention would be to create a market similar to the one that exists for the carbon market, in which the positive social impact of projects and companies becomes a real generator of value. Without a doubt, the social factor within the ESG universe is a very complex issue, but we must begin to lay the foundations for its incorporation to be deeper and move from discourse to action. Today many companies have joined and committed to sustainability efforts, but many managers still see those efforts as costs and not as sources of value. This makes it difficult to release the capital and domestic financing needed to give impetus to these issues. A survey collected by KPMG on ESG issues this year indicates that 83% of those consulted recognize that focusing on ESG criteria will bring benefits to their business areas; however, only 30% feel that they are only in the early stages of defining a clear strategy to report progress in meeting their ESG commitments. In another survey, also by KPMG, it is highlighted that 91% of CEOs of large corporations in the United States believe that there will be a recession in the next twelve months and that, in preparation, 59% indicate plans to pause or reconsider their ESG efforts. It is here that failures to recognize the close link between sustainability and financial performance emerge, in addition to the reputational risk that this implies. One of the causes may be that few institutions adequately track and record returns from their existing sustainable investments, or carefully analyze those from future investments because of the complexity of the measurements. To address this problem, there are efforts such as the one developed by the Center for Sustainable Business at New York University (NYU Stern), in which they propose a five-step model to link financial returns with sustainability actions:  Design current sustainability strategies;  Identify related operational and managerial changes;  Determine the yields obtained;  Quantify the benefits; and  Calculate the monetary value. It may sound simple, but this structure is the first step we must take as institutions. From a central bank's perspective, ESG principles are crucial to ensure the smooth functioning and stability of the financial system. In recent years, Banco de Mexico has made significant efforts to incorporate the analysis of climate risks and their impact on financial stability and the economic environment into our framework of action and operation. We have internalized in our analysis of climate-related risks that could become risks to the proper functioning of the financial system. For this reason, central banks are taking a proactive and preventive role. The good judge for his house begins. For this reason, at Banco de Mexico we have taken actions to improve our management in terms of social impact and governance structure. In 2017 we were the first central bank to be recognized for its commitment to gender equality through the EDGE Certification, and this year we have endorsed that commitment, achieving the EDGE Move certification, the second level of evaluation that recognizes an organization's progress in achieving a balance of gender and equity. In addition to recognizing the progress made with the commitment to gender equality at all levels, especially in leadership roles, the strengthening of flexible work practices implemented during the pandemic and that have already permeated our work culture was also recognized. On the other hand, in 2018, the Governing Board renewed its commitment and pronounced itself in favor of labor equality and non-discrimination as normative ethical principles that should guide the actions of public servants and that are key factors for our institutional strengthening and for the economic development of Mexico. This is also a way to strengthen our talent pool and to promote the efficient use of human capital. Undoubtedly, the incorporation of environmental, social and governance criteria are part of a joint strategy that must be addressed on numerous fronts and, definitely, these criteria are not exclusive. The joint recognition and strengthening of these aspects places us in a better position to achieve the proper fulfillment of our functions and objectives as a central bank, always with a social perspective. For a society as a whole, where sectors are highly interrelated, and actions have an amplifying effect on the rest of the system, it goes without saying the extraordinary benefits of having an inclusive and sustainable economy, since it makes it possible to combat entrenched socioeconomic inequalities, and trigger economic development to reach its full potential. At the level of organizations, having great diversity in their human capital offers a wider range of perspectives and ideas, which promote innovation, competitiveness, decision-making and, therefore, governance, thus favoring a favorable work environment, which allows talent to be retained. All of the above contributes to the achievement of the functional objectives of the institution, which results in economic benefits in a sustainable way and is key to its survival and permanence over time. However, building human capital requires a holistic approach across sectors. The more women take on senior leadership positions, the more progress can be made in designing policies, regulations, products, and services that promote gender-inclusive finance to support sustainable and resilient growth. Research in 2019 by the International Finance Corporation found that private and venture capital with gender-balanced senior investment teams generated 10-20% higher returns compared to funds with unbalanced decision-making teams, as a diverse board is also diverse in terms of solutions and prudence in its risk management. Likewise, investors are today highly interested in strengthening gender diversity in their investment operations, with the Social aspect predominating with much greater importance. Definitely, ESG principles, and especially those corresponding to the "S" are an issue that is here to stay. Therefore, it is imperative that more women access key and decision-making positions. Significant progress has been made in women's political participation, both in the formal sphere of laws and in the composition of legislatures. However, in the economic and financial sphere, women's participation in leadership spaces presents a very different picture. For example, in the financial industry, women are often overrepresented at the lower end of the corporate ladder, in branches or administrative roles. But the real test of a level playing field is whether a company is balanced at its highest levels. We have seen in Mexico great efforts by institutions in the promotion of female talent, as well as their promotion in key decision-making positions, although it is clear that there is still a long way to go. The results obtained are not only visible within organizations, but the reflection of this important work is also palpable in terms of the creation of financial products that comply with ESG principles. In recent years, we have witnessed various financial innovations. For example, in October 2020, we witnessed the first issuance of a Gender Social Bond in Mexico, by FIRA, a concrete and exemplary initiative, which demonstrates that it is possible to design financial instruments with cutting-edge environmental and social sustainability incentives and criteria. The issue reaffirms the importance of taking affirmative action in favor of women, which effectively contributes to the financial profitability of productive projects, as well as to equal opportunities between men and women in the agri-food and rural sectors. This not only affects the well-being of women, their families and their communities, but also places the entire economy of the national rural sector on a higher path of progress and development. The bond allows granting loans to small agricultural producers, as well as expanding and strengthening the investment portfolio in projects and companies with exclusive or majority participation by women. This placement, followed by a second one in April last year, confirms the great interest that gender bonds aroused in the stock certificate market in our country, as they obtained an overdemand at more favorable rates than other traditional financial instruments of the same issuer on previous dates. I would like to emphasize a quote from Hillary Clinton that I find incredibly enlightening: "[diversity and inclusion] ... In fact, it's not just the right thing to do, it's the smart thing to do." It is imperative to recognize that actions aimed at generating a positive social impact carry an economic and financial value that improves the profile of companies in all dimensions. We also have to recognize that both the planet and those who live on it are important. This is why the framework of analysis and action must necessarily be comprehensive and multidimensional, giving equal relevance to each of the letters of the ESG criteria. And that is precisely the pending task of institutions, both private and public, the internalization of these concepts in our frameworks of action. Just as we are being able to put a price on carbon emissions, we should also be able to put a price on positive social impact and raise awareness that this is a win-win strategy, generating profits and not only in the financial field. Undoubtedly, the experience lived during the COVID-19 pandemic significantly reconfigured our way of relating to each other and the social aspect has regained ground in the global concept of sustainability. The potential is enormous and we have the opportunity and the generational responsibility to take advantage of it. Once again, I would like to congratulate Grupo Santander for the brilliant initiative to open spaces like this and to be part of the efforts that imply a before and after in the sustainable development of our country. Thank you very much and congratulations!

Title:
"Economic Outlook for Mexico and its Regions, Agribusiness Forum 2023", Irene Espinosa, Deputy Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

Full text
text: Economic Outlook for Mexico and its Regions Agribusiness Forum 2023, Deloitte FEBRUARY 15, 2023 PPTX presentation offered by Irene Espinosa Cantellano, Deputy Governor, Bank of Mexico, on the occasion of the 2023 Agribusiness Forum, organized by Deloitte. I would like to thank Deloitte for the invitation, which, through Salvador Sanchez, extended this invitation to me to talk with you about the economic outlook for Mexico and its regions at this important event. Considering that the objective of my talk is to publicize the international, national and regional panorama, I prepared a presentation that tries to follow that order, from the point of view of the central bank. As you know, the priority objective of the Bank of Mexico in the conduct of its monetary policy is price stability, since that is the best contribution we can make to promote sustained growth and the well-being of the population. However, what is less known is that the analysis of regional economies provides very valuable elements to better understand the economic reality of our country and, in this way, contribute to better economic policy decision-making. Following this idea, in the first part I will briefly comment on the macro environment, both internationally and nationally, in order to lay the foundations to address the center of the exhibition, which is the added value of our quarterly reports of regional economies. Before I begin, however, I must remind you that I am participating in this event in a personal capacity, so what I express in this forum should not be interpreted as an official position of the Bank of Mexico or its Governing Board. * * * I would like to begin the presentation by underlining that the environment in which the Bank of Mexico has conducted monetary policy remains complex and uncertain. The shocks resulting from the pandemic and the war continue to affect the inflationary outlook, which is a challenge for the central bank. On the one hand, in the external sphere, global inflation remains at high levels. As a result, several central banks have continued to increase their benchmark rates. Against this backdrop, for most of 2022, interest rates tended to rise and the U.S. dollar strengthened, so financial conditions tightened. Likewise, the outlook for global activity deteriorated. Domestically, the dynamics of headline and core inflation have continued to suffer from the effects of the pandemic and the war. In this environment, the Bank of Mexico implemented firm monetary policy actions to maintain the anchoring of longer-term inflation expectations, as well as to contribute to an orderly behavior of the national financial markets. I would like to emphasize that, considering the actions taken, the monetary stance is in restrictive territory, and it is foreseeable that it will remain so for a long period, which is necessary to bring down inflation. During 2022, global economic activity moderated and a slowdown is expected in 2023. As for the external environment, as can be seen in the graph on the left, global economic activity is expected to have moderated in the fourth quarter of 2022 compared to the previous quarter, albeit with heterogeneity between countries. Going forward, several timely indicators suggest a slowdown in different sectors of economic activity, as well as a slower pace in world trade. As for forecasts for global economic growth, the International Monetary Fund's outlook published last January continues to point to a slowdown in global economic activity in 2023 and a slight recovery in 2024. Moving on to the behavior of global inflation, inflation increased during 2022 to reach levels not seen in more than two decades. Recently, in several economies, there has been a decline. This can be explained, in part, by the moderation in energy and food inflation. Despite this, global inflation remains elevated. Thus, in most economies, headline inflation remains significantly above the targets of their central banks. The greatest inflationary pressures came from the increase in the prices of food raw materials, but non-food also contributed to the inflationary problem. As can be seen in the graph on the left, the prices of food commodities began to increase during the first months of the pandemic and their increase accelerated with the beginning of the geopolitical conflict. From the second half of 2022 these prices have moderated; however, they remain at a high level. On the other hand, the prices of non-food raw materials initially had a considerable decrease due to the slowdown in the global economy caused by the pandemic. Subsequently, the recovery of the world's main economies put pressure on international references of various products. In addition, the war meant additional pressures to these references on already high levels. In this context, during 2022, central banks increased their reference rates. Recently, in the face of signs of easing some of the inflationary shocks, some central banks moderated the magnitude of their hikes, although they indicated that additional hikes are still likely to be required, and that rates will remain high for an extended period. During 2022, national economic activity continued to recover. Thus, it is already at levels slightly higher than those of Q4-2019, prior to the health emergency. In Mexico, for 2022, GDP grew 3.0% in its annual comparison. With this result, GDP stands at a level similar to that reported in the last quarter of 2019, prior to the pandemic. The growth of the domestic economy was encouraged by domestic demand, especially private consumption, and by the favorable performance of external demand during most of 2022. Growth has been supported by the three main groups of activity. Likewise, various labor market indicators improved their performance throughout 2022. In particular, national and urban unemployment rates are already below their pre-pandemic levels. In Mexico, inflation remains high and has shown no signs of having reached its tipping point. National Consumer Price Index Annual % Change In Mexico, inflation remains high and has shown no signs of having reached its tipping point. Of particular concern is core inflation, which in January 2023 increased again to close at 8.45%, and seems to be reluctant to decrease. This behavior is explained by a slower-than-expected decline in food commodity inflation and the rebound in services inflation. The latter, on the one hand, continues to feel the effects of the pandemic and the war. However, it also shows a certain inertia that cannot be explained exclusively by external factors. Thus, we cannot yet speak of a more generalized reduction in the pressures that we have been observing in the goods and services that make up the price index basket. To combat persistent inflationary pressures, since June 2021 the reference rate has increased by 700 basis points to reach the current level of 11.00%. Regarding monetary policy actions, I would like to emphasize that we continue in a complex and uncertain environment, in which higher inflationary pressures have implied a greater challenge for the conduct of monetary policy. The current hiking cycle began with increases of 25 basis points at the June, August, September and November 2021 meetings. Subsequently, the Governing Board accelerated the pace of adjustment to 50 basis points at its meetings in December 2021, February, March and May 2022. Again, in each of its meetings in June, August, September and November 2022, the Governing Board had to accelerate the pace of increase to 75 basis points. Finally, in December 2022 and February 2023, the pace of increase decreased to 50 basis points on each occasion, to place the rate at its current level of 11.00%. The cycle accumulates 700 basis points of increases, a situation that is unprecedented since the Bank of Mexico began to set its reference rate in 2008, nor has such high inflation since then. Monetary policy actions finally made it possible to reach a restrictive monetary stance as of August 2022, as required by the inflationary outlook. Increased cost pressures. Regarding economic growth, growth is expected to slow down during 2023 to between 1 and 2.6% according to our latest Quarterly Report, however, market forecasts, which are more recent, suggest that we should probably revise this range downwards. * * * I would now like to turn to the outlook for regional economies. The Bank of Mexico monitors the evolution of the different regions of the country. It provides a broader and deeper understanding of the national economy. Regional analysis complements the view of the economic situation, and provides information for analysis and forecasting, so it is important for monetary policy decision-making. The regional study is particularly useful because it recognizes regional specialization and thus the different dynamics that can be observed. To analyze the regions, different sources of data are used, including statistical information from INEGI or other sources, for example, the Agricultural and Fisheries Information Service, and consultation instruments with entrepreneurs and specialists, since the Bank of Mexico implements a monthly survey of companies and a program of interviews with business executives on a quarterly basis. These instruments provide information on the factors that are determining behaviour in the regions. The opinions of business executives are particularly useful because companies have timely information that is sometimes difficult to distinguish in aggregated data, so their opinion can complement the analysis of activity and inflation. Complementing economic analysis with a regional and sectoral view is particularly useful in periods of high uncertainty or highly atypical such as the current one. For the regional analysis, the territory has been divided into four regions that were defined taking into account the characteristics that, being common to a group of neighboring states, affect their economic performance. These features include:  Geographical location, since economic performance is affected by proximity to different border areas, by the size and concentration of the population, ease of access to maritime trade, etc.  Secondly, the structure of production (I will talk about this later).  Thirdly, the socio-economic conditions, of which we will also see some differences.  And fourthly, the synchronisation of economic cycles. Various studies show that, compared to the rest of the regions, economic activity in the southern region exhibits a lower degree of association with the evolution of national economic activity or that of the United States. These are the four regions into which the national territory is divided, in yellow the north, in green the north center, in red the center and in blue the south: Regional Country Division As can be seen, the boundary is not fulfilled in the case of Baja California Sur (BCS), which is part of the north-central region, while Baja California, the only state with which it borders, is located in the northern region. This is because BCS was considered to have characteristics more akin to the states of the north-central region than to those of the northern border. The northern region is made up of states with a high level of socioeconomic development (strata 5 and 6), while the southern region is made up of the majority of states with a low level of socioeconomic development (strata 1 and 2). The central region concentrates states with medium levels of development (strata 2-4) and the mid-high north (strata 3-6). The productive vocation of the regions can be distinguished according to their specialization. The above graph shows the sectoral structure of regional GDP. Compared to the rest of the regions, the manufacturing sector has a larger share of GDP in the northern region, the agro-industrial sector in the north-centre, services in the centre and mining in the south. For example, the analysis focused on regions and sectors has made it possible to measure the risk due to the increase in the price of nitrogen fertilizers that have been severely affected throughout the pandemic, and particularly with Russia's invasion of Ukraine. To measure the impact that the increase in fertilizer prices would mean for the national economy, the left graph shows the distribution of these products at the national level. The graph shows that the center-north concentrates the highest use of fertilizers (42.2%), followed by the north (25%) and the south (17%). In a second step, the impact of a 10% increase in nitrogen fertilizers on the total production costs of the crops that use them the most (corn, sorghum, wheat and sugarcane) was calculated, taking as a reference the relative importance of these in the total cost of production per hectare. This is shown in the right graph. The largest relative increase in the total cost of production is observed in the south. It is followed by the central regions and the north. Productive specialization, the area planted with crops that use these inputs and regional requirements in the use of nitrogen fertilizers influence these results. As a reference, between February 2020 and April 2022, the international price of urea increased 331.5%. This helps us to measure the magnitude of the increase in the price of some inputs in the agricultural sector in this period. Opinion of Business Executives on Risks to Regional Economic Activity (based on information collected between September 26 and October 20, 2022) The information gathered through interviews also helps to identify risks to regional economic activity. Regarding the downside risks for the following twelve months that were most frequently mentioned in the interview cycle corresponding to the third quarter of last year in all regions, the following stand out:  That public safety indicators deteriorate.  That inflation persists at high levels; and  That the low levels of both public and private investment continue. Additionally, among the downside risks with different importance between regions:  In the north and central north, the United States will experience a recession, which would affect export flows to that country; as well as the possibility of repeated episodes of drought, possibly related to climate change, that affect the performance of its agricultural and industrial sectors.  In the center, the possibility of new waves of COVID-19 contagion and reduced private investment flows; and  In the south, they expressed concern about the possibility of adverse natural phenomena such as hurricanes and earthquakes. Among the factors that could influence growth upwards, in all regions the following stood out:  That public spending, particularly investment in infrastructure works, is higher than expected.  That the levels of public security be strengthened.  That more favorable conditions be observed, both locally and internationally, that encourage greater private investment; and  That there is a faster decline in inflation than anticipated. Factors that could upward influence growth for each region include:  In the north, the possibility of sustaining the creation of sources of formal employment.  In the center, north and south, the possibility that growth in the tourism sector will be greater than anticipated; and  At the centre, that the control of the pandemic supports the recovery of activity more than expected. Another issue that has been closely followed from the regional analysis is the risks associated with climate change. The risk is that extreme weather events could become more frequent and more extreme. Climate change is an additional structural risk to the economic activity of the regions. For example, these graphs show the result of a "Drought Exposure Index" for a group of agricultural products included in the CPI basket. The index captures the proportion of the production of each product that is grown in municipalities that, at each point in time, presented severe, extreme or exceptional drought, and therefore serves as a risk monitoring system. Also, let's take the case of avocado, which is the green line in the graph on the right. In the spring-summer cycle of 2021, more than 90% of the total avocado production in Mexico was in areas with severe drought. We see other similar cases with potatoes, corn, beans, onions, and tomatoes in different cycles of 2021. The relocation of production to Mexico (nearshoring) represents a real opportunity, although with heterogeneous impacts between regions. This topic is a good example of something for which it is difficult to interpret aggregated data. At the current juncture, it is difficult to know whether the changes observed in investment or trade flows are really a response to the desire of firms to change the location of their operation (or their source of suppliers) or are the result of changes in consumption patterns, and it is also difficult to know whether these changes are permanent or not. Therefore, the companies surveyed by the Bank of Mexico were asked if they had observed benefits derived from this phenomenon, being very explicit about what we mean by a process of relocation of production. Companies may have received more foreign direct investment, or they may have had more demand from one of three sources:  Companies established in the United States that previously obtained their inputs from companies in other countries.  Foreign companies that have moved their operation to Mexico, or new foreign companies that have established themselves in the country.  Other companies previously established in Mexico, but which in turn had greater demand from foreign companies. With the data obtained, it was found that 16% of large companies in Mexico have benefited from nearshoring, at least through some of the channels I have already described (black bar in the graph on the left). The impacts have naturally been heterogeneous between regions, reflecting once again the heterogeneity in the productive vocation, with a higher proportion of companies benefiting in the northern region. They have also been different for companies with different characteristics or in different sectors, for example, about a quarter of exporting manufacturing companies or in sectors integrated into global value chains report having seen greater demand or foreign investment due to the relocation of global production. However, this phenomenon has also benefited relevant proportions of companies in the rest of the regions and sectors, reflecting that participation in global chains has positive spillovers. To capitalize on this opportunity and translate into sustained growth in the medium and long term, it will be important to guarantee conditions that encourage investment. When companies were asked about the importance of different factors that make Mexico competitive for the arrival of international companies, the vast majority mentioned the proximity to the United States, the level of salaries and the qualification of the workforce as incentives (green bars): It will be important to guarantee conditions that encourage investment so that the opportunity for relocation global production translates into sustained growth in the long term in the country. In closing, I would like to emphasize that Mexico continues to face a challenging environment for economic activity and inflation. The persistence of inflation has led to tighter monetary stances in the main advanced economies, and together with the economic effects of the war and the uncertainty associated with the evolution of the COVID-19 pandemic, has led to a further deterioration in the global growth outlook and has accentuated the risks for international financial markets. Given this environment, the monetary stance of this Central Institute has been adjusting and, considering the forcefulness of the measures adopted in the reporting period, it is currently in restrictive territory. The priority is to abate inflationary pressures to ensure a macroeconomic environment conducive to sustained growth. In addition, it is important to strengthen domestic sources of growth and foster an environment conducive to generating higher levels of investment. In this sense, progress in controlling the pandemic will continue to be key to achieving a more robust and more certain reactivation of activity, especially in those regions that specialize in services, such as the center, which the pandemic has particularly affected. For its part, greater flexibility in the labour market could allow for a better adjustment of employment in the face of the challenges imposed by the pandemic. Likewise, within the framework of the USMCA and in the context of a relocation of production processes on a global scale, a strengthening of the rule of law and public security would provide greater certainty to companies to facilitate their operation, reduce their costs and encourage investment, not only from the regions that traditionally receive a greater share of such flows, but also from the southern region. The construction of infrastructure projects, particularly those that improve regional connectivity with other markets inside and outside Mexico, as well as those that facilitate access to reliable and efficient energy sources that are less polluting, could also help attract investment in the medium term. As far as the Board of Governors of the Bank of Mexico is concerned, it will continue to determine its monetary stance with the firm commitment to promote an orderly adjustment of relative prices, financial markets and the economy as a whole, which will bring inflation to its 3% target and preserve the anchoring of inflation expectations. This is for the benefit of the Mexican population. Thanks a lot!

Los choques derivados de la pandemia y del conflicto blico siguen incidiendo sobre el panorama inflacionario, lo que constituye un reto para el banco central. Por un lado, en el mbito externo, la inflacin global permanece en niveles altos. En consecuencia, diversos bancos centrales han continuado incrementando sus tasas de referencia. En este contexto, durante la mayor parte de 2022, las tasas de inters tendieron a aumentar y el dlar estadounidense se fortaleci, por lo que las condiciones financieras se apretaron. Title:
"Inauguration of the pilot courses of the Academy of Principles of Responsible Banking (PRB Academy)", Irene Espinosa, Deputy Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

Full text
text: Remarks by Deputy Governor Irene Espinosa Cantellano on the occasion of the INAUGURATION OF THE PILOT COURSES OF THE ACADEMY OF PRINCIPLES OF RESPONSIBLE BANKING (PRB Academy), held on February 27, 2022 (08:30 Hrs.) at the Club de Industriales, Mexico City. I would like to thank the Association of Banks of Mexico (ABM), the United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEPFI) and the German cooperation agency GIZ for their invitation to the inauguration of this pilot course of the Academy of Principles of Responsible Banking (PRB Academy) in Mexico focused on members of the Boards of Directors and CEOs of banks. I welcome the start of this pilot course whose objective is to prepare senior managers of banks for the challenges they face in their businesses and the challenges faced by their clients due to climate change, nature loss, pollution and social problems. I am sure that the course will be useful and will help to define sustainability strategies and goals in their banks and to think about how these strategies and goals should be integrated and become part of the business models of their banks. Mitigating risks and seizing opportunities related to climate change and preserving biodiversity have profound implications for the economy, society, and the financial system. Climate risks and opportunities are two sides of the same coin. Mitigating the physical and transition risks associated with climate change and taking advantage of the development of new, less polluting technologies requires mobilizing huge amounts of resources towards a more climate-friendly economy. environment and society. Taking advantage of these new opportunities and markets will certainly modify the structure of the Mexican economy over time. These changes will strengthen the competitiveness and development possibilities of the Mexican economy, even if they are on a different basis than the historical ones. There is a long way to go since, for example, the effects of climate change and biodiversity are not yet adequately reflected in asset valuations or properly considered in the plans and strategies of banks and companies. In this sense, it is important that you, the banking executives, keep an eye on three global events and trends that will have an impact on Mexico. Fortunately, the ABM, through the Risk Management Symposiums, has already been socializing these events and trends. First of all, I would like to highlight the first two accounting standards on sustainability of the International Sustainability Standards Board that have already been announced will come into force in early 2024. The IFRS SI General Requirements requires companies to provide material information on all significant sustainability risks and opportunities that are necessary for investors to assess the value of the company. In addition, it emphasizes the need to make connections between financial and sustainability information, require that financial information on sustainability be published in a timely manner and that this be reported in the financial statements, or at least in cross-reference to them. IFRS S2 climate disclosure requires organizations to provide material information about climate change risks and opportunities that are significant and necessary for investors to assess the value of the company, including physical climate risks, transition climate risks, and climate change-related opportunities. IFRS S2 incorporates the recommendations of the TCFD. These standards will be applicable from the outset to companies listed on the stock exchange. The Mexican Council of Financial Reporting Standards (CINIF), is responsible for establishing sustainability accounting standards for financial institutions in Mexico, as well as companies that are listed on the stock exchange. Companies shall disclose material information about all significant sustainability-related risks and opportunities to which they are exposed. Secondly, I would like to highlight the work that we have been doing within the Sustainable Finance Committee and at Banco de Mexico to promote the development and application of models for the analysis of climate scenarios. The scenario analysis allows us to understand how the physical risks associated with climate change, as well as the transition risks caused by possible sudden changes in public policy, in the maturation of environmentally friendly technologies and in consumer preferences could affect the economy in the future. Since the middle of last year, we have been working intensively on a model that considers the behavior and interactions between five systems: (i) the economy, (ii) climate, (iii) water, (iv) the energy system, and (v) agriculture and land use. Based on assumptions of socioeconomic trajectories (population, economic activity, technologies and public policies), the model determines changes in production structures in long-term horizons that even reach the year 2100. The analysis of scenarios with these global models is a tool that enriches the strategic planning of banks by informing, with a solid scientific basis, on the risks and opportunities related to climate change in the economy as a whole and in different sectors and technologies. In this regard, I would like to mention that IFRS S2 proposes to require companies to disclose their resilience to different climate scenarios, as well as climate-related opportunities. Banco de Mexico together with the TCFD Mexico Consortium has been working on the design of the first scenario analysis pilot for Mexican financial institutions that I hope will be announced shortly. Thirdly, I would like to mention the growing importance that the development of transition plans for organisations towards sustainability is gaining at a global level. Although there are different definitions of transition plans and reference frameworks, with different objectives, elements and target audiences, predominantly linked to elements of climate disclosure (IFRS S2), investors and creditors increasingly demand from companies the plans, policies and actions they are going to take around sustainability. as well as the robustness and coherence of these plans and policies and the consistency in their implementation. The challenges of climate change and environmental degradation are global. But in emerging economies, financing needs for investments in adaptation and mitigation are enormous due to their vulnerability to climate change and the lower development and resilience of their infrastructure. Capacity building in sustainable finance is a complex and multidimensional issue that needs to be promoted so that financial authorities, financial institutions and companies are in the right position to identify risks and opportunities related to climate change and sustainability. It is essential that the different actors identify and generate relevant information and that they have instruments, tools and models to measure these risks and opportunities. That is why the Sustainable Finance Committee is currently building a Training Hub that, through an editorial line that will be defined by experts, will offer a repository of information that will allow different types of users (financial authorities, financial institutions, non-financial companies and the general public) to access educational materials on relevant topics free of charge. We will surely find synergies with the Academy of Principles of Responsible Banking with this objective of providing training to financial authorities. Thank you very much and I wish you much success.

Adems, enfatiza la necesidad de hacer conexiones entre la informacin financiera y de sostenibilidad, requerir que la informacin financiera sobre sostenibilidad se 2 publique oportunamente y que esta se reporte en los estados financieros, o al menos en referencia cruzada a ellos. El IFRS S2 de divulgacin climtica requiere que las organizaciones proporcionen informacin material sobre los riesgos y las oportunidades sobre cambio climtico que sean significativos y necesarios para que los inversionistas puedan evaluar el valor de la empresa, incluyendo riesgos climticos fsicos, riesgos climticos de transicin, y oportunidades relacionadas con el cambio climtico. El IFRS S2 incorpora las recomendaciones del TCFD. Estos estndares, sern aplicables de inicio a las empresas listadas en bolsa. El Consejo Mexicano de Normas de Informacin Financiera (CINIF), es responsable de establecer las normas contables de sostenibilidad para las instituciones financieras en Mxico, as como las empresas que estn listadas en bolsa. Las empresas debern divulgar informacin material sobre todos los riesgos y las oportunidades significativos relacionados con la sustentabilidad a los que estn expuestas. En segundo lugar, quisiera destacar el trabajo que dentro del Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles y en Banco de Mxico hemos venido realizando para impulsar el desarrollo y la aplicacin de modelos para el anlisis de escenarios climticos. El anlisis de escenarios permite entender cmo los riesgos fsicos asociados con el cambio climtico, as como los riesgos de transicin ocasionados por posibles cambios repentinos en la poltica pblica, en la maduracin de tecnologas amigables con el medio ambiente y en las preferencias de los consumidores podran afectar la economa en el futuro. 3 Desde mediados del ao pasado hemos venido trabajando intensamente en un modelo que considera el comportamiento y las interacciones entre cinco sistemas: (i) la economa, (ii) el clima, (iii) el agua, (iv) el sistema energtico y (v) la agricultura y el uso de suelo. A partir de supuestos de trayectorias socioeconmicas (poblacin, actividad econmica, tecnologas y polticas pblicas), el modelo determina cambios en las estructuras de produccin en horizontes de largo plazo que incluso llegan al ao 2100. El anlisis de escenarios con estos modelos globales es una herramienta que permite enriquecer la planeacin estratgica de los bancos al informar, con una base cientfica slida, sobre los riesgos y las oportunidades relacionados al cambio climtico en la economa en su conjunto y en distintos sectores y tecnologas. Al respecto, quisiera mencionar que la IFRS S2 propone requerir que las empresas divulguen sobre su resiliencia ante diferentes escenarios climticos, adems de oportunidades relacionadas con el clima. Banco de Mxico junto con el Consorcio TCFD Mxico ha venido trabajando en el diseo del primer piloto de anlisis de escenarios para instituciones financieras mexicanas que espero se anuncie en breve. En tercer lugar, quisiera mencionar la creciente importancia que a nivel global est cobrando el desarrollo de planes de transicin de las organizaciones hacia la sostenibilidad. Si bien existen diversas definiciones de planes de transicin y de marcos de referencia, con diferentes objetivos, elementos y pblicos objetivos, predominantemente ligados a elementos de la divulgacin 4 climtica (IFRS S2), los inversionistas y acreedores crecientemente demandan saber de las empresas los planes, las polticas y acciones que van a tomar en torno a la sustentabilidad, as como la robustez y coherencia de dichos planes y las polticas y la consistencia en su implementacin. Los retos del cambio climtico y la degradacin ambiental son globales. Pero en economas emergentes, las necesidades de financiamiento de inversiones en adaptacin y mitigacin son enormes debido a su vulnerabilidad al cambio climtico y el menor desarrollo y resiliencia de su infraestructura. El desarrollo de capacidades en materia de finanzas sostenibles es un tema complejo y multidimensional que se requiere impulsar para que las autoridades financieras, instituciones financieras y las empresas estn en una posicin adecuada para identificar los riesgos y las oportunidades relacionadas con el cambio climtico y la sostenibilidad. Es indispensable que los distintos actores identifiquen y generen la informacin relevante y que cuenten instrumentos, herramientas y modelos para medir estos riesgos y oportunidades. Es por ello que el Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles actualmente est construyendo un Hub de Capacitacin que, a travs de una lnea editorial que ser definida por expertos, ofrecer un repositorio de informacin que permitir a distintos tipos de usuarios (autoridades financieras, instituciones financieras, empresas no financieras y pblico en general) acceder de manera gratuita a materiales educativos sobre los temas de relevancia. 5 Seguramente encontraremos sinergias con la Academia de Principios de Banca Responsable con este objetivo de brindar capacitacin a las autoridades financieras. Muchas gracias y les deseo mucho xito. 6
