text: WORDS OF MTRA. IRENE ESPINOSA ON THE OCCASION OF THE CLOSING OF THE CONFERENCE OF THE COMMITTEE ON SUSTAINABLE FINANCE: "TOWARDS THE IMPLEMENTATION OF CLIMATE SCENARIOS IN MEXICO" Mexico City, October 31, 2023  In the context of climate change, it is often easier to focus the conversation on the risks associated with climate change and the economic and financial losses it can cause than to identify and seize the opportunities that arise as a result of it.  During this conference, both dialogues have been addressed in detail, but recognizing that there is increasing talk about the opportunities that are being generated in the transition to a low-carbon economy and how these opportunities can be used to create financially profitable and sustainably viable projects, both in the real economy and in its financial system.  In this regard, I would like to emphasize two central points of this complex process. First, the opening of new markets for goods and services will also require the development of new skills in the labor market, so the social value of human capital formation is evident and we must promote it.  The training effort also contributes to the process of raising awareness towards a collaborative and organized economy, with the aim of making the transition fair and inclusive, especially for vulnerable communities, which also have a very important role in the conservation and restoration of our country's natural capital.  And second, we must recognize the great efforts that have been made within the Sustainable Finance Committee, through all its working groups, in order to advance the sustainable finance agenda in our country. In particular, I would like to highlight the remarkable progress made towards the implementation of climate scenarios in Mexico, which has been the central axis of this conference that concludes today.  As a result of the interesting panels we have had over these two days, it is clear that the effects and, therefore, the relevance of climate change for the financial system is of the utmost importance. Therefore, the use of climate scenario analysis, as projection tools, is very relevant to prepare for different plausible contexts.  During these two days it has become clear that the design of scenarios involves a long process to select and evaluate the most appropriate models, cooperation with the academic sector and with international agencies and organizations, which account for the complexity that this multidisciplinary task entails and the coordination that must exist between all participants.  Models are complex and have their limitations. However, they are our best approach to the complicated task of incorporating climate change and its effects into economic analysis.  It is interesting to hear how progress has been made in the implementation of these scenario models in an intense work that has been going on for several years and is constantly evolving and improving. The calibration of these models to the socio-economic reality of our country has been a task to which the Committee on Sustainable Finance has dedicated itself and has made important progress with the support of experts. However, it must be remembered that this is an ongoing task.  As we have seen, for this purpose, there are several models and tools related to this type of analysis that can be used in a complementary way, including GCAM, GEMMES and CLIMRISK.  However, it is necessary to have very precise information from different sectors and disciplines to generate analyses robust that are useful and that allow us to truly have simplified representations of possible scenarios, that are useful for investors, decision makers, etc.  In addition, in parallel to the development of scenario analysis, it is very important to work in a coordinated and articulated manner, between the members of the financial sector, the public and private sectors.  Taking this into consideration, BANXICO has taken the relevance of these scenario analyses with the utmost seriousness, so it will continue to work on this issue, in order to identify climate-related risks and opportunities for the Mexican financial sector.  I would also like to take this opportunity to highlight the importance of financial and non-financial institutions themselves internalizing and raising awareness about the integration of these models and exercises into their own management and risk management frameworks. Forums like this let us see that we are moving in the right direction. Listening to participants from the private, public and academic sectors share their experiences in the implementation and integration of environmental risks in their models and activities has undoubtedly been a very productive collaboration.  I must not omit the central role that the government, through its public policies and financial authorities, has to successfully transition to a green economy. There must be harmonious coordination of the objectives in all sectors and at all levels. However, it has become clear from this conference that the public sector will not be able to achieve it alone. The participation and collaboration of all sectors of the economy is essential and, in terms of sustainable finance, the mobilization of sufficient resources to finance the transition is a major challenge that, as a society, we must face.  Finally, I would like to recognize the valuable work carried out by the Sustainable Finance Committee to coordinate the authorities of the Mexican financial system in generating analyses, tools, and capacities around issues related to sustainability. As an example of this, there are the Sustainable Taxonomy of Mexico, the Sustainable Finance Mobilization Strategy, the conference of these two days, and the pilot of scenario analysis in Mexico that was presented to us in the previous panel.  Without further ado, I greatly appreciate the participation of the panelists, as well as the varied audience that, above all, will allow us to work on developing better climate scenarios. Thanks a lot!

Title:
"Climate Emergency and Just Transition, MX23 Sustainable Finance Forum", Irene Espinosa, Deputy Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

Full text
text: MX23 SUSTAINABLE FINANCE FORUM "CLIMATE EMERGENCY AND JUST TRANSITION" Mexican Council for Sustainable Finance Conference: "Just Transition" Irene Espinosa Cantellano Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mexico Interactive Museum of Economics (MIDE) Mexico City, November 15, 2023 (12:35-12:55 hours) Alba Aguilar, Executive Director of the Mexican Council of Sustainable Finance; Dear Speakers and Panelists; Ladies and gentlemen: Good afternoon. It is a great honour for me to participate in the 2023 edition of the Sustainable Finance Forum with the theme "Climate Emergency and Just Transition". The need to act immediately and turn our economies around to transition to a sustainable and net-zero economy is undeniable. But as the United Nations Development Programme has pointed out, we must not only act quickly, but also in a "fair and inclusive" manner. We know that an efficient transition to a sustainable economy will provide great opportunities for countries, their communities and workers to thrive in a new economic paradigm that is climate change-neutral and preserves biodiversity and natural capital. However, an accelerated transition, without considering the socio-economic impacts derived from the transformation of production processes, can seriously affect millions of people, whose main sources of income derive from economic activities that will have to be reduced, transformed, diversified or even disappear. And it is to be expected that the adverse effects will be greater in economies such as Mexico, which must make a great effort to decarbonize and has geographical, socioeconomic and demographic characteristics that imply enormous challenges of adaptation and transition. * * * I would like to begin my speech by commenting on some definitions of "just transition" and the main benefits that can be derived from it, and then address one of the main roles that the financial system can play in this process. Finally, I will take the opportunity to share with you some relevant advances that the Sustainable Finance Committee has made in the greening agenda of the financial system, and that can help to have a fairer transition, and the importance of financial institutions being an example in the sustainable agenda. Regressive effects of climate change To arrive at an appropriate definition of "just transition", I think it is pertinent first of all to remember that the effects of climate change on the economy can be highly regressive in countries such as Mexico, since these impacts harm the most vulnerable population to a greater extent; it affects their sources of income, their homes and their way of life, depriving them of their means of subsistence. Many low-income families carry out their productive activities outdoors and do not have adequate medical care, which makes them especially vulnerable to the effects of climate change, such as droughts, tropical cyclones, floods and rising sea levels. Changes in the environment can even trigger massive migrations of people, who have lost their sources of work, in order to survive. On the other hand, these meteorological phenomena significantly reduce agricultural yields, which necessarily translates into an increase in food prices. Since the poorest households spend a greater proportion of their income on their food needs, they feel the consequences of climate change the most. These social costs can be immense and only reinforce the need to act quickly to curb climate change. However, the transition must not only be swift but also just, inclusive and orderly, as this process can also entail huge social costs, especially in terms of job losses and the obsolescence of skills in the new sustainable economy. Defining "just transition" Although the concept of "just transition" is not new, in recent years it has been used in the environmental context to refer to all social groups being included in the new sustainable economic paradigm. The International Labour Organization defines a just transition as one that creates decent job opportunities in the process of greening the economy to "leave no one behind". For its part, the European Commission goes further, defining a just transition as one that provides and guarantees better decent jobs, greater training opportunities and greater job security for all workers affected, both by climate change and by mitigation policies. Agreeing on a definition of just transition is undoubtedly the first step to advance the work agenda. In my view, a working definition of "just transition" should incorporate both the social costs of physical risks and those of the transition, as proposed by the European Commission. It must also be recognized that a just transition implies a continuous process of shared responsibility, which necessarily involves several actors: governments at all levels, companies and labor organizations. Benefits of a Just Transition Of course, the benefits of a just and inclusive transition derive mainly from mitigating the huge social costs of materializing physical and transition risks, which are most important in emerging and developing economies. But as the United Nations Development Programme points out, there are many ways in which a just transition can help address the effects of climate change and move towards a sustainable economy. Here are the three that seem most important to me: First, if governments are able to show the benefits of transitioning to a low-emission economy, in terms not only of mitigating climate change but also of preserving the competitiveness of their industries, access to financial markets and the creation of new "green jobs", they will be able to gain greater public support for their sustainable investment policies and projects. which in turn will allow us to advance more effectively in the environmental agenda and have much more reach. Second, the greatest progress in the environmental agenda under the just transition approach will promote precisely the creation of "green jobs", necessary for the expansion of the new sustainable paradigm, which will offer competitive remuneration, social security and health benefits to the working population. The new quality jobs should improve the living conditions of communities and attract new displaced workers from other sectors. And third, the above benefits make it possible to unify efforts to fight climate change. It must be remembered that, by definition, a just transition implies a shared responsibility. In this sense, a just transition strategy, integrated into action plans to combat climate change, will help changemakers focus on decarbonization, without forgetting to strive for fair and inclusive results. In other words, incorporating the social dimension will allow them to act more quickly in these urgent tasks. Financial system and just transition So far, we have highlighted the relevance of starting from an appropriate operational definition of "just transition", which considers the social impacts, both of climate change itself and of the policies for its mitigation. We have also emphasized the need to work collaboratively between governments, companies and representatives of the labor sector to take advantage of the immense opportunities offered by the transition to a sustainable economy, and that these are distributed in society, accelerating the emergence of new green jobs and promoting the development of new skills, especially in the most affected population. At this point, it must be recognized that the financial system will play a central role in this process and the authorities and financial institutions, at the global and national levels, must be prepared to do what we have to do. The mobilization of financial resources is vital for a just, orderly, and efficient transition, especially for emerging economies, which must invest gigantic amounts of funds in mitigation and adaptation projects and activities, as well as in the transition, adoption of new sustainable technologies, human capital formation, and creation of procedures and systems to comply with reporting and risk disclosure standards. In particular, disclosure and disclosure by companies will be essential to better value assets in financial markets, in order to better reflect the environmental impacts of their activities, and thus promote greater efficiency in financing and capital allocation towards sustainable and transition activities. In this regard, an illustrative mechanism is the Just Transition Fund created by the European Union in 2021, which supports member states that have identified the territories where they expect the adverse impacts of the transition to climate neutrality to materialize to a greater extent. This Fund supports the diversification and conversion of the above-mentioned territories through the recovery and retraining of workers, investment in small and medium-sized enterprises, the creation of new enterprises, research and development, environmental rehabilitation and clean energy. To fulfill its function, the disclosure and disclosure of information is crucial. Mainstreaming ESG issues Now that we have entered the realm of the financial system and its role in the just transition, I would like to share with you a topic on international capital mobilization that deserves our attention and relates directly to corporate disclosure. Because country-level ESG ratings are highly correlated with per capita income, there is a danger that, in the absence of corporate-level data, investors will close gaps using ESG data from the country, which could limit companies' access to sources of financing. In addition, recent research shows that in their sovereign ESG ratings, credit rating agencies do not fully reflect the level of preparedness of emerging countries to transition to a low-carbon economy or their exposure to stranded assets. In addition, in the case of emerging countries, they are generally not rewarded in their sovereign ESG ratings for having good environmental policies. Particularly, in the case of low- and middle-income countries, the correlation between the environmental pillar rating and the sovereign rating is negative. The better the performance in the environmental pillar, the lower the sovereign credit rating. Thus, the mainstreaming of ESG issues entails the risk of diverting resources to higher-income countries and can accentuate the underrepresentation of emerging and developing countries in global capital markets. Following this line, we must not neglect the multiple aspects of the human being as a social being; from issues of human rights, communication, decent working conditions, equitable remuneration, gender and diversity issues, social justice and transparency, to mention a few. The challenge is precisely to incorporate these elements into the traditional performance measurements of institutions and to define their social impact contributions aimed at improving people's lives. In this context, it is important that the global debate on ESG issues is shaped by the perspectives of emerging countries. In Mexico, we are moving in that direction. The Sustainable Taxonomy of Mexico, published last March, is a pioneer in including the social component within its structure, which will be a reference for investors in addition to supporting the country's sustainable economic transition. It is also worth highlighting the work of the Mexican Council for Financial Reporting Standards (CINIF) which, taking into account the international sustainability standards IFRS SI and S2, published last June, has proposed a roadmap for the implementation of sustainability standards in Mexico applicable to public interest companies and small and medium-sized enterprises. The CINIF currently has a set of 30 indicators for these companies in the three ESG pillars under public consultation, and until the end of November: 16 environmental, 6 social and 8 corporate governance. The fact that public interest entities collect and disseminate these indicators will promote awareness within companies and help them adopt practices in favor of sustainability, which will improve their ESG rating over time. Although these indicators will represent an important advance, in due course it will be necessary to consider complementing them with forward-looking information and data on the transition of organizations towards sustainability. And for this information to be useful to investors, it will need to be available with a similar opportunity as financial information. Progress in the Sustainable Finance Committee Now I would like to share with you two lines of work of the Committee on Sustainable Finance, in which the financial authorities and the main associations of the financial system participate as observers, which can contribute to supporting a just transition. 1.- The analysis of climate scenarios In the risk group, under the coordination of Banco de Mexico, we have been working on the development of new tools and prospective models that allow us to identify the risks and opportunities associated with climate change and its impacts. Historical data does not reflect the risks we are facing and will face with climate change. As an example, with historical data, the probability of a category 3, 4 or 5 hurricane arriving in Acapulco was zero (CENAPRED). The speed with which Otis transformed from a tropical storm to a Category 5 hurricane is unprecedented. That is why the rigorous development of the analysis of future climate scenarios, which is based not so much on historical data but on models of global climate change projected for different plausible futures, 5, 10, 20 and more years, are necessary to identify vulnerabilities, but also development opportunities for the country, including just transition objectives. It is important to clarify that, at the international level, the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors to Green the Financial System (NGFS) and the Financial Stability Board's Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD, FSB) have been insisting on conducting scenario analysis for several years now. Likewise, last June, the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) of the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), of which Mexico is a party, established that scenario analysis should be required of companies to which these global accounting standards apply. The analysis of climate scenarios helps to generate capacities in authorities and companies to analyze the financial and economic risks associated with the climate and environmental crisis and can be used as an input for the development of transition plans and strategies of governments and companies, which do not neglect the social component. Training Hub (RAiCES) As I mentioned earlier, a just transition will require the development of new capacities in the population to take advantage of the opportunities that will arise in the transition to a sustainable economy. That is why the Committee on Sustainable Finance approved the creation of the "Digital Repository for Learning and Collaboration in Sustainable Finance" (RAiCES), which consists of a platform that will provide relevant content on sustainable finance in various formats. RAiCES will be a public good accessible in Spanish free of charge and available 24/7. The platform seeks to contribute to raising awareness of the relevance of sustainable finance and the development of capacities in this area. RAiCES will target diverse audiences: authorities and financial institutions, companies, the general public, young people, and local and indigenous communities. Each of these types of audiences will have navigation guides designed exclusively for them. RAiCES has collaborated with experts to develop a structured and validated guide to incorporate and classify material and create guided tours within its platform for users. In addition, it will respond to the growing interest in reporting and disclosure standards, sustainable and green taxonomies, analysis of environmental and social risks and opportunities, analysis of climate scenarios, and new financial instruments in capital markets for the mobilization of resources towards sustainable activities, among other topics. The good judge for his house begins In conclusion, I would like to emphasize the importance of the financial authorities reflecting the application of the principles whose establishment we seek to promote in the economy and the financial system. In particular, as authorities that issue regulations and carry out supervisory actions on financial institutions, we must "lead by example" on climate change. I would like to acknowledge that, for years, the Bank of Mexico has been implementing concrete measures to promote the care of the environment in different aspects within its scope of operation. However, the need to adopt urgent measures to combat climate change and its effects, as established in the thirteenth UN Sustainable Development Goal, requires leading institutions of the financial system, such as central banks, to create a comprehensive strategy in order to have an institutional framework that allows managing the risks of climate change in their different functions and operations. and in short, medium and long-term horizons. In Mexico, this strategy considers the interaction that the Bank of Mexico carries out with the main financial authorities of the country, mainly within the Financial System Stability Council, through its Sustainable Finance Committee, and reflects the various works carried out in recent years to establish the institutional framework for sustainable finance recently created in our country and which serves as the basis for applying this agenda in our country. This strategy also seeks to offer participants in the financial system a demonstration effect, by implementing best practices through our own operations, as well as ensuring that Banco de Mexico is resilient to risks arising from climate change, for example, in the manufacture and distribution of the national currency. This plan is in line with the fulfilment of our aims and priority objective established in the legal framework that applies to us. It is also the result of careful analysis to enhance the impact of the actions to be carried out. Finally, I would like to emphasize that the concept of just transition is especially relevant in economies like ours, where most of the natural capital is precisely distributed in vulnerable communities, so it is our responsibility as a society to try to establish the right conditions and align the incentives for its conservation and regeneration, without neglecting the living conditions of all its inhabitants. We must be aware that these actions will benefit us all and also allow us to combat entrenched socioeconomic inequalities and trigger economic development to reach its full potential. At Banco de Mexico we are aware of our great social responsibility in the climate agenda towards a regenerative economy, which implies an inclusive, equitable, just and, above all, sustainable transition in the long term. For all these reasons, I want to recognize the Mexican Council for Sustainable Finance and all the participants in this conference for incorporating the "fair" dimension into the sustainable finance agenda in our country. Thanks a lot!
text_original: FORO FINANZAS SOSTENIBLES MX23 "EMERGENCIA CLIMTICA Y TRANSICIN JUSTA" Consejo Mexicano de Finanzas Sostenibles Conferencia: "Transicin Justa" Irene Espinosa Cantellano1 Subgobernadora del Banco de Mxico Museo Interactivo de Economa (MIDE) Ciudad de Mxico a 15 de noviembre de 2023 (12:35-12:55 horas) Alba Aguilar, Directora Ejecutiva del Consejo Mexicano de Finanzas Sostenibles; Estimados conferencistas y panelistas; Seoras y seores: 1 Las opiniones y puntos de vista expresados en este documento son responsabilidad de la autora y no necesariamente representan la posicin institucional del Banco de Mxico o de su Junta de Gobierno. 1 Buenas tardes. Es para m gran honor participar en la edicin 2023 del Foro de Finanzas Sostenibles que lleva por tema "Emergencia Climtica y Transicin Justa". Es innegable la necesidad de actuar inmediatamente y dar un giro en nuestras economas para transitar a una economa sostenible y con cero emisiones netas. Pero como lo ha sealado el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo, no solo debemos actuar con rapidez, sino tambin de una manera "justa e inclusiva". Sabemos que una transicin eficiente hacia una economa sostenible brindar grandes oportunidades para que los pases, sus comunidades y trabajadores prosperen en un nuevo paradigma econmico que sea neutral en cuanto al cambio climtico y preserve la biodiversidad y el capital natural. No obstante, una transicin acelerada, sin considerar los impactos socioeconmicos derivados de la transformacin de los procesos productivos, puede afectar gravemente a millones de personas, cuyas principales fuentes de ingresos derivan de actividades econmicas que debern reducirse, transformarse, diversificarse o incluso desaparecer. Y es de esperar que los efectos adversos sean mayores en economas como la mexicana,2 que debe hacer un gran esfuerzo de descarbonizacin y presenta caractersticas 2 La economa mexicana se ubica en el quinceavo lugar en el mundo en la emisin de dixido de carbono https://www.statista.com/statistics/270499/co2-emissions-in-selected-countries/. 2 geogrficas, socioeconmicas y demogrficas que implican enormes retos de adaptacin y transicin. * * * Quiero iniciar mi intervencin comentando algunas definiciones sobre "transicin justa" y los principales beneficios que de ella se pueden derivar, para luego abordar uno de los principales roles que el sistema financiero puede tener en este proceso. Finalmente, aprovechar para compartirles algunos avances relevantes que ha realizado el Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles en la agenda de enverdecimiento del sistema financiero, y que pueden ayudar a tener una transicin ms justa, y la importancia de que las instituciones financieras sean ejemplo en la agenda sostenible. Efectos regresivos del cambio climtico Para llegar a una definicin apropiada de "transicin justa", creo pertinente en primer lugar recordar que los efectos del cambio climtico sobre la economa pueden ser altamente regresivos en pases como Mxico, ya que dichos impactos perjudican en mayor medida a la poblacin ms vulnerable; afecta sus fuentes de ingreso, sus viviendas y su forma de vida, privndolos de sus medios de subsistencia. Muchas familias de bajos ingresos desempean sus actividades productivas a la intemperie y no cuentan con atencin mdica adecuada, lo que las hace especialmente vulnerables a los efectos del cambio climtico, como son las sequas, los ciclones tropicales, 3 las inundaciones y el aumento en el nivel de mar. Los cambios en el medioambiente incluso pueden detonar migraciones masivas de personas, que han perdido sus fuentes de trabajo, para subsistir. Por otra parte, estos fenmenos meteorolgicos reducen significativamente el rendimiento agrcola, lo que necesariamente se traduce en incremento en los precios de los alimentos. Puesto que los hogares ms pobres destinan una mayor proporcin de sus ingresos a cubrir sus necesidades alimentarias, ellos resienten mayormente las consecuencias del cambio climtico. Estos costos sociales pueden ser inmensos y solo refuerzan la necesidad de actuar con rapidez para frenar el cambio climtico. No obstante, la transicin no solo debe ser rpida sino justa, incluyente y ordenada, ya que dicho proceso tambin puede conllevar enormes costos sociales, especialmente en las prdidas de empleos y la obsolescencia de capacidades en la nueva economa sostenible. Definiendo "transicin justa" Si bien el concepto de "transicin justa" no es nuevo, en los ltimos aos se ha venido usando en el contexto ambiental para referirse a que todos los grupos sociales sean incluidos en el nuevo paradigma econmico sostenible. 4 La Organizacin Mundial del Trabajo define una transicin justa como aquella que crea oportunidades laborales decentes en el proceso de ecologizacin de la economa para "no dejar a nadie atrs". Por su parte, la Comisin Europea va ms all, al definir una transicin justa como aquella que provee y garantiza mejores trabajos decentes, mayores oportunidades de entrenamiento y mayor seguridad laboral para todos los trabajadores afectados, tanto por el cambio climtico como por las polticas de mitigacin. Acordar una definicin de transicin justa es, sin duda, el primer paso para avanzar en la agenda de trabajo. En mi opinin, una definicin funcional de "transicin justa" debe incorporar tanto los costos sociales derivados de riesgos fsicos como los ocasionados por la transicin, tal como lo propone la Comisin Europea. Tambin hay que reconocer que una transicin justa implica un proceso continuo de responsabilidad compartida, el cual necesariamente involucra varios actores: los gobiernos en todos sus niveles, las empresas y las organizaciones laborales. Beneficios de una transicin justa Naturalmente, los beneficios de una transicin justa e incluyente derivan principalmente de mitigar los enormes costos sociales derivados de la materializacin de 5 los riesgos fsicos y de transicin, los cuales son ms importantes en economas emergentes y en desarrollo. Pero como lo seala el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo, son muchas las maneras en que una transicin justa puede ayudar a enfrentar los efectos del cambio climtico y avanzar hacia una economa sostenible.3 A continuacin menciono las tres que me parecen ms importantes: En primer lugar, si los gobiernos son capaces de mostrar los beneficios de transitar a una economa baja en emisiones, en trminos no solo de la mitigacin del cambio climtico sino de la preservacin de la competitividad de sus industrias, del acceso a los mercados financieros y de la creacin de nuevos "empleos verdes", podrn obtener un mayor respaldo del pblico en sus polticas y proyectos de inversin sostenibles, lo que a su vez permitir avanzar con mayor efectividad en la agenda ambiental y tener mucho ms alcance. En segundo lugar, el mayor avance en la agenda ambiental bajo el enfoque de transicin justa promover precisamente la creacin de "empleos verdes", necesarios para la expansin del nuevo paradigma sostenible, que ofrecern remuneraciones competitivas, seguridad social y beneficios para la salud a la poblacin trabajadora. Los nuevos empleos 3 https://climatepromise.undp.org/es/news-and-stories/aue-es-la-transicion-iusta-v-por-aue-es- importante. 6 de calidad debern mejorar las condiciones de vida de las comunidades y atraer nuevos trabajadores desplazados de otros sectores. Y en tercero, los beneficios anteriores permiten unificar esfuerzos para luchar contra el cambio climtico. Hay que recordar que, por definicin, una transicin justa implica una responsabilidad compartida. En este sentido, una estrategia de transicin justa, integrada a los planes de accin en el combate al cambio climtico, ayudar a los promotores del cambio a enfocarse en la descarbonizacin, sin olvidar esforzarse por rendir resultados justos e inclusivos. En otras palabras, incorporar la dimensin social les permitir actuar con mayor celeridad en estas tareas impostergables. Sistema financiero y transicin justa Hasta ahora hemos destacado la relevancia de partir de una definicin operacional apropiada de "transicin justa", que contemple los impactos sociales, tanto del propio cambio climtico como de las polticas para su mitigacin. Tambin hemos enfatizado la necesidad de trabajar de manera colaborativa entre gobiernos, empresas y representantes del sector laboral para aprovechar las inmensas oportunidades que ofrece la transicin a una economa sostenible, y que estas sean distribuidas en la sociedad, agilizando el surgimiento de nuevos empleos verdes y fomentando el desarrollo de nuevas capacidades, especialmente en la poblacin ms afectada. 7 En este punto, hay reconocer que el sistema financiero tendr un rol central en este proceso y las autoridades e instituciones financieras, a nivel global y nacional, debemos estar preparados para hacer lo que nos toca. La movilizacin de recursos financieros resulta vital para una transicin justa, ordenada y eficiente, principalmente para las economas emergentes, que deben invertir gigantescas cantidades de fondos en proyectos y actividades de mitigacin y adaptacin, as como en la transicin, adopcin de nuevas tecnologas sostenibles, formacin de capital humano, y creacin de procedimientos y sistemas para cumplir con los estndares de reporteo y divulgacin de riesgos. En particular, la revelacin y divulgacin de informacin por parte de las empresas sern indispensables para valuar mejor los activos en los mercados financieros, a fin de reflejar mejor los impactos ambientales de sus actividades, y as promover mayor eficiencia en el financiamiento y la asignacin de capital hacia actividades sostenibles y de transicin. Al respecto, un mecanismo ilustrativo es el Fondo de Transicin Justa creado por la Unin Europea en 2021, el cual apoya a los estados miembros que han identificado los territorios donde esperan que se materialicen en mayor medida los impactos adversos por la transicin hacia la neutralidad climtica.4 4 https://commission.europa.eu/strategv-and-policv/priorities-2019-2024/european-green-deal/finance-and-green- deal/just-transition-mechanism/just-transition-funding-sources en. 8 Este Fondo apoya la diversificacin y la reconversin de los territorios mencionados mediante la recuperacin y recapacitacin de trabajadores, la inversin en pequeas y medianas empresas, la creacin de nuevas empresas, la investigacin y desarrollo, la rehabilitacin ambiental y la energa limpia. Para cumplir con su funcin, la revelacin y divulgacin de informacin es crucial. La transversalizacin de los temas ASG Ahora que hemos entrado al mbito del sistema financiero y su papel en la transicin justa, quisiera compartirles un tema sobre la movilizacin de capital internacional que merece nuestra atencin y se relaciona directamente con la revelacin de informacin de las empresas. Debido a que las calificaciones ASG a nivel pas estn altamente correlacionadas con el ingreso per cpita, existe el peligro de que, en ausencia de datos a nivel corporativo, los inversionistas cierren las brechas utilizando datos ASG del pas, lo que pudiera limitar el acceso de las empresas a fuentes de financiamiento. Adicionalmente, investigaciones recientes muestran que en sus calificaciones ASG soberanas, las calificadoras crediticias no reflejan plenamente el nivel de preparacin de 9 los pases emergentes para transitar a una economa baja en carbono o su exposicin a activos varados.5 Adems, en el caso de pases emergentes, generalmente no son recompensados en sus calificaciones ASG soberanas por tener buenas polticas en materia ambiental. Particularmente, para el caso de los pases con ingresos medios y bajos, la correlacin de la calificacin del pilar ambiental y la calificacin soberana es negativa. A mejor desempeo en el pilar ambiental, menor calificacin de crdito soberana. As, la transversalizacin de los temas ASG conlleva el riesgo de desvo de recursos hacia pases con mayores ingresos y puede acentuar la subrepresentacin de pases emergentes y en vas de desarrollo en los mercados de capitales globales. Siguiendo esta lnea, no debemos descuidar los mltiples aspectos del ser humano como ser social; desde temas de derechos humanos, comunicacin, condiciones de trabajo dignas, remuneracin equitativa, cuestiones de gnero y diversidad, justicia social y transparencia, por mencionar algunos. El reto est precisamente en incorporar estos elementos en las mediciones tradicionales de desempeo de las instituciones y definir sus contribuciones de impacto social orientadas a mejorar la vida de las personas. 5 Gratcheva, E, B Gurhy, A Skarnulis, F Stewart and D Wang (2022): Credit worthy: ESG factors and sovereign credit ratings, World Bank. 10 En este contexto es importante que el debate global sobre los temas ASG sea moldeado con las perspectivas de los pases emergentes. En Mxico, estamos avanzando en esa direccin. La Taxonoma Sostenible de Mxico, publicada en marzo pasado, es pionera al incluir el componente social dentro de su estructura, lo cual ser referente para los inversionistas adems de apoyar la transicin econmica sostenible del pas. Tambin cabe destacar el trabajo del Consejo Mexicano de Normas de Informacin Financiera (CINIF) que, tomando en cuenta los estndares de sostenibilidad internacionales IFRS SI y S2, publicados en junio pasado, ha propuesto una hoja de ruta para la implementacin de estndares de sostenibilidad en Mxico aplicables a empresas de inters pblico y pequeas y medianas empresas. El CINIF tiene actualmente en consulta pblica, y hasta finales de este mes de noviembre, un conjunto de 30 indicadores para estas empresas en los tres pilares ASG: 16 ambientales, 6 sociales y 8 de gobierno corporativo. El que las entidades de inters pblico recopilen y divulguen estos indicadores, promover la concientizacin al interior de las empresas y coadyuvar a que adopten prcticas en favor de la sostenibilidad, lo que mejorar su calificacin ASG a lo largo del tiempo. 11 Si bien estos indicadores representarn un avance importante, en su momento habr que considerar complementar estos con informacin prospectiva y datos sobre la transicin de las organizaciones hacia la sostenibilidad. Y para que esta informacin sea til a los inversionistas, deber estar disponible con una oportunidad similar a la de la informacin financiera. Avances en el Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles Ahora quisiera compartirles dos lneas de trabajo del Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles, en el que participamos las autoridades financieras y las principales asociaciones del sistema financiero como observadoras, que pueden contribuir a apoyar una transicin justa. 1.- El Anlisis de escenarios climticos En el grupo de riesgos, bajo la coordinacin de Banco de Mxico, hemos estado trabajando en el desarrollo de nuevas herramientas y modelos prospectivos que nos permitan identificar los riesgos y oportunidades asociados al cambio climtico y sus impactos. Los datos histricos no reflejan los riesgos que estamos enfrentando y que vamos a enfrentar con el cambio climtico. Como ejemplo, con datos histricos, la probabilidad de que arribara un huracn categora 3, 4 o 5 en Acapulco era cero (CENAPRED). La velocidad 12 con la que se transform Otis de tormenta tropical a un huracn categora 5 no tiene precedentes. Es por ello por lo que el desarrollo riguroso del anlisis de escenarios climticos futuros, que se basa no tanto en datos histricos sino en modelos del cambio climtico global proyectados para diferentes futuros plausibles, a 5, 10, 20 y ms aos, son necesarios para identificar vulnerabilidades, pero tambin oportunidades de desarrollo para el pas, incluyendo objetivos de transicin justa. Es importante aclarar que, a nivel internacional, la Red de Bancos Centrales y Supervisores para Enverdecer el Sistema Financiero (NGFS) y el Grupo de Trabajo sobre Divulgacin de Informacin Financiera Relacionada con el Clima del Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera (TCFD, FSB) han estado insistiendo en realizar anlisis de escenarios desde hace varios aos. Asimismo, en junio pasado, el Consejo Internacional de Normas de Sostenibilidad (ISSB) de las Normas Internacionales de Informacin Financiera (IFRS), del cual Mxico es parte, estableci que el anlisis de escenarios debe ser requerido a las empresas a las que aplica estos estndares contables globales. El anlisis de escenarios climticos ayuda a generar capacidades en autoridades y empresas para analizar los riesgos financieros y econmicos asociados a la crisis climtica 13 y ambiental y puede ser utilizado como insumo para el desarrollo de planes y estrategias de transicin de gobiernos y empresas, que no dejen de lado el componente social. Hub de Capacitacin (RACES) Como mencion antes, una transicin justa requerir el desarrollo de nuevas capacidades en la poblacin para aprovechar las oportunidades que surgirn en la transicin hacia una economa sostenible. Es por ello que el Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles aprob la creacin del "Repositorio Digital para el Aprendizaje y Colaboracin en Finanzas Sostenibles" (RACES), el cual consiste en una plataforma que proporcionar contenido pertinente sobre finanzas sostenibles en diversos formatos. RACES ser un bien pblico accesible en espaol de forma gratuita y que estar disponible las 24 horas, los 7 das de la semana. La plataforma busca contribuir a la concientizacin de la relevancia de las finanzas sostenibles y al desarrollo de capacidades en esta materia. RACES tendr como pblico objetivo a diversas audiencias: autoridades e instituciones financieras, empresas, pblico general, jvenes y comunidades locales e indgenas. Cada uno de estos tipos de audiencias tendr guas de navegacin diseadas exclusivamente para ellos. 14 RACES ha colaborado con expertos para desarrollar una gua estructurada y validada para incorporar y clasificar material y crear visitas guiadas dentro de su plataforma para los usuarios. Adems, responder al creciente inters por las normas de reporteo y divulgacin, las taxonomas sostenibles y verdes, el anlisis de riesgos y oportunidades ambientales y sociales, el anlisis de escenarios climticos, y los nuevos instrumentos financieros en los mercados de capitales para la movilizacin de recursos hacia actividades sostenibles, entre otros temas. El buen juez por su casa empieza Para concluir, quisiera enfatizar la importancia de que las autoridades financieras reflejemos la aplicacin de los principios cuya instauracin buscamos promover en la economa y el sistema financiero. En particular, como autoridades que emitimos regulacin y realizamos acciones de supervisin a instituciones financieras, debemos "predicar con el ejemplo" en materia de cambio climtico. Quisiera reconocer que, desde hace aos, el Banco de Mxico ha venido implementado medidas concretas para favorecer el cuidado del medio ambiente en distintos aspectos dentro de su mbito de operacin. 15 Sin embargo, la necesidad de adoptar medidas urgentes para combatir el cambio climtico y sus efectos, como lo establece el treceavo objetivo de desarrollo sostenible de la ONU, exige a instituciones lderes del sistema financiero, como los bancos centrales, crear una estrategia integral con el objeto de contar con un marco institucional que permita administrar los riesgos del cambio climtico en sus distintas funciones y operaciones, y en horizontes de corto, mediano y largo plazo. En Mxico, tal estrategia considera la interaccin que el Banco de Mxico realiza con las principales autoridades financieras del pas, principalmente dentro del Consejo de Estabilidad del Sistema Financiero, a travs de su Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles, y refleja los diversos trabajos realizados durante los ltimos aos para establecer el marco institucional de finanzas sostenibles recientemente creado en nuestro pas y que sirve de base para aplicar en nuestro pas esta agenda. Esta estrategia tambin busca ofrecer a los participantes del sistema financiero un efecto demostracin, al implementar las mejores prcticas a travs de nuestras propias operaciones, as como garantizar que el Banco de Mxico es resiliente a los riesgos derivados del cambio climtico, por ejemplo, en la fabricacin y distribucin de la moneda nacional. 16 Este plan se ajusta al cumplimiento de nuestras finalidades y objetivo prioritario establecidos en el marco jurdico que nos aplica. Asimismo, resulta de un anlisis cuidadoso para potenciar el impacto de las acciones a realizar. Finalmente, quisiera destacar que el concepto de transicin justa cobra especial relevancia en economas como la nuestra, donde la mayor parte del capital natural se encuentra precisamente distribuido en comunidades vulnerables, por lo que es nuestra responsabilidad como sociedad el procurar establecer las condiciones adecuadas y alinear los incentivos para su conservacin y regeneracin, sin descuidar las condiciones de vida de todos sus habitantes. Debemos tomar consciencia de que estas acciones nos beneficiarn a todos y permiten adems combatir las desigualdades socioeconmicas arraigadas y detonar el desarrollo econmico para alcanzar su mximo potencial. En el Banco de Mxico estamos conscientes de nuestra gran responsabilidad social en la agenda climtica hacia una economa regenerativa, que implique una transicin incluyente, equitativa, justa y, sobre todo, sostenible en el largo plazo. Por todo ello, quiero reconocer al Consejo Mexicano de Finanzas Sostenibles y a todos los participantes en esta conferencia por incorporar la dimensin "justa" en la agenda de finanzas sostenibles en nuestro pas. Muchas gracias! 17

Title:
"Closing of the Banxico University Links 2023 sixth edition program", Irene Espinosa, Deputy Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

text: Closing of the "Banxico University Links" 2023-Sixth Edition program Mexico City, December 6, 2023 Good morning everyone! I would like to begin by thanking Jessica Serrano, Director of Financial Education and Cultural Development, for this kind invitation as an exponent of the sixth edition of the "Banxico University Links" program, which, like previous years, culminates successfully today. Congratulations Jessica and her entire team for this great effort, in turning Enlaces Universitarios into a channel for the dissemination of economic and financial knowledge that is essential for the Bank, and which, in addition to its diversity and inclusive approach, has a reach to practically the entire Mexican population. Undoubtedly, the convening power of the program is largely due to the enthusiastic participation of our large university community, but particularly to the willingness and knowledge of the students selected today. Thank you for your great interest in "Enlaces Universitarios Banxico" and for being part of the success of the program. You are key pieces for better and effective communication between society and the Bank of Mexico. * * * More than ever, the issue that concerns us today as a society is to advance the agenda of equality, governance and the environment, in order to guarantee sustainable and inclusive growth for future generations. In our daily lives, we witness the effects of climate change: high temperatures, droughts, floods caused by atypical rainfall, and recently we saw how a tropical storm became a category 5 hurricane in a few hours, which caused human and physical losses that are still difficult to quantify. The loss of natural capital and the degradation of ecosystems have not only significantly impacted our ways of life and productive activities, but also constituted one of the greatest threats to the stability of financial systems, and to the world economy as a whole. In recent years, and despite the heterogeneity between countries, there has been a common awareness among financial authorities of the need to redouble efforts to achieve a greater and better understanding of environmental risks and their transmission channels to the economy and, in particular, to the financial system. Precisely, the field that this discipline closely studies is called "Sustainable Finance". As the mandates of central banks and supervisors are to make the financial system resilient to face risks that threaten its stability, the analysis of risks arising from climate change is part of their area of competence. Therefore, as central banks, we must ensure that we have a framework for assessing these risks that is reliable, homogeneous and timely; this, in order to incorporate them appropriately in the financial and strategic decisions of the industry, and to promote the allocation of resources from the financial system towards sustainable activities and projects, which in addition to economic and financial returns, generate benefits to communities, while mitigating potential damage to ecosystems to move towards a green and low-carbon economy. Physical risks are linked to weather events related to climate change (such as heat waves, floods, wildfires, and cyclones). Given recent developments, these will increase in severity and frequency, in addition to other longer-term progressive climate changes (such as changes in precipitation patterns, extreme climate variability, ocean acidification, sea level rise, and average temperatures). On the other hand, transition risks are generated by the policies issued by authorities to mitigate polluting emissions, by changes in consumption patterns derived from assuming new paradigms, by technological advances that allow exploring new forms of energy generation and production of goods. This can disrupt energy supply chains and generate a series of stranded assets due to obsolescence or limitations in receiving financing. For Mexico, the topic of Sustainable Finance is of special interest, since, due to the geographical characteristics, location, biodiversity and distribution of our population, exposure to climate-related risks and the depletion of natural resources is high. From our trenches, the Bank of Mexico has actively participated in international finance forums and committees Sustainable, thus endorsing its firm commitment to contribute with forceful actions in its field of faculty, to contribute and facilitate that our economy travels on the path of sustainability and in a future with zero net emissions. Thus, Banco de Mexico plays a central role in the coordination of financial authorities at the national and international level in the field of financial stability and sustainable finance, thanks to its role as a founding member of the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors to Green the Financial System (NGFS). Created in 2017, this network is made up of central banks and supervisors, committed to the dissemination of best practices, which contribute to the management of climate risks in the financial sector, as well as promote the mobilization of financing and capital to support the transition to a sustainable economy. Specifically, the Bank of Mexico has actively participated in the construction of climate scenarios and stress exercises to analyze how the risks associated with climate change affect the economy and the financial system, as well as to evaluate the resilience of financial institutions to the materialization of environmental risks. It also promotes the holding of seminars, workshops and conferences in an atmosphere of knowledge exchange and technical assistance on these topics. On the other hand, since 2020, the Bank of Mexico's Financial Stability Report includes a section on environmental risks and analyzes the exposure of financial institutions' credit portfolios to these risks. Also in 2020, the Sustainable Finance Committee was created, as part of the Financial System Stability Council, which brings together different financial authorities in our country, and of which the Bank of Mexico serves as technical secretary. The main objective of this Committee is to support the Financial System Stability Council through the preparation of analyses, evaluations, proposals, and recommendations on sustainable finance in Mexico. Due to the relevance of the issue, in 2021 the Directorate of Environmental and Social Risk Analysis and Policies was created within the structure of this central bank, reflecting the great interest and commitment of the Institution to the transition to a green and inclusive economy. To achieve these objectives, it is essential to create interdisciplinary analytical capacities on issues of risks, biodiversity, geology, among others. Thus, at the initiative of the Bank of Mexico, the Sustainable Finance Committee approved in 2022 the creation of a "Training Hub" with the aim of providing free access to a digital repository, which contains auxiliary material on sustainable finance training topics, aimed at financial authorities, financial institutions, non-financial companies and the general public. in addition to promoting the collaboration of the private, public and academic sectors. Thus, this initiative aims to join the efforts of the Bank of Mexico with the academic and university community with the aim of raising awareness and ensuring that the issue is internalized and actively integrated into the process of training human capital and its capacities from an early stage. The Bank of Mexico is aware of the fundamental role of the link between higher education institutions, financial authorities and professionals to create an agenda of cooperation and dialogue to find the best route towards this goal, through the training of professionals aware of this problem. I have no doubt that those selected today will be our great allies for dissemination and avid users of the Hub. In conclusion, I would like to emphasize the imperative need to address the high levels of pollution, the loss of biodiversity and the impacts of climate change on the world economy, without neglecting everyday socio-economic problems. It is for this reason that we must continue with education and outreach efforts, to raise awareness of climate risks and expose the severity of the situation. I am sure that by working together we will be able to advance this agenda for the benefit of society. Thanks a lot!
text_original: Clausura del programa "Enlaces Universitarios Banxico" 2023-Sexta Edicin Ciudad de Mxico, 6 de diciembre de 2023 Muy buenos das a todas y todos! Quiero empezar por agradecer a Jssica Serrano, Directora de Educacin Financiera y Fomento Cultural, por esta amable invitacin como exponente de la sexta edicin del programa "Enlaces Universitarios Banxico" y que, al igual que los aos anteriores, culmina hoy de forma exitosa. Felicidades Jssica y a todo su equipo por este gran esfuerzo, al convertir a Enlaces Universitarios en un canal de difusin del conocimiento econmico y financiero indispensable para el Banco, y que adems por su enfoque de diversidad e incluyente, tiene un alcance prcticamente a toda la poblacin mexicana. Sin duda, el poder de convocatoria del programa se debe en gran medida a la entusiasta participacin de nuestra gran comunidad universitaria, pero particularmente a la disposicin y el conocimiento de las y los estudiantes seleccionados hoy presentes. i Gracias por su gran inters en "Enlaces Universitarios Banxico" y ser partcipe del xito del programa. Ustedes son piezas clave para una mejor y efectiva comunicacin entre la sociedad y el Banco de Mxico. * * * Ms que nunca, el tema que hoy nos ocupa como sociedad es avanzar en la agenda de igualdad, gobernanza y medio ambiente, a fin de garantizar un crecimiento sostenible e incluyente para las futuras generaciones. En nuestra vida cotidiana, somos testigo de los efectos del cambio climtico: elevadas temperaturas, sequas, inundaciones causadas por lluvias atpicas, y recientemente vimos cmo una tormenta tropical se convirti en unas cuantas horas en un huracn categora 5, que ocasion prdidas humanasy fsicas an difciles de cuantificar. La prdida de capital natural y la degradacin de los ecosistemas no solo han impactado de forma significativa a nuestras formas de vida y actividades productivas, sino constituyentes una de las mayores amenazas para la estabilidad de los sistemas financieros, y para la economa mundial en su conjunto. En los ltimos aos, y no obstante a la heterogeneidad entre pases, existe una consciencia comn entre las autoridades financieras sobre 2 la necesidad de redoblar los esfuerzos para lograr un mayor y mejor entendimiento sobre los riesgos ambientales y sus canales de transmisin hacia la economa y, en particular, hacia el sistema financiero. Precisamente, al campo que estudia de cerca dicha disciplina se le denomina las "Finanzas Sostenibles". Puesto que los mandatos de los bancos centrales y de los supervisores consiste en dotar al sistema financiero de resiliencia para hacer frente a los riesgos que amenacen su estabilidad, el anlisis de los riesgos derivados del cambio climtico forma parte de su rea de competencia. Por ello, como bancos centrales, debemos asegurar el contar con un marco de evaluacin de dichos riesgos que sea confiable, homognea y oportuna; ello, con el fin de incorporarlos de forma adecuada en las decisiones financieras y estratgicas de la industria, y propiciar la asignacin de recursos del sistema financiero hacia actividades y proyectos sustentables, que adems de los rendimientos econmicos y financieros, generen beneficios a las comunidades, al tiempo de mitigar los daos potenciales a los ecosistemas para transitar hacia una economa verde y baja en emisiones de carbono. Los riesgos fsicos, estn vinculados con los fenmenos meteorolgicos relacionados con el cambio climtico (tales como olas 3 de calor, inundaciones, incendios forestales y ciclones). Dada la evolucin reciente, estos aumentarn su severidad y frecuencia, en adicin a otros cambios progresivos del clima a ms largo plazo (tales como cambios en los patrones de precipitacin, extrema variabilidad del clima, acidificacin ocenica, aumento del nivel del mar y de las temperaturas promedio). Por otro lado, los riesgos de transicin se generan por las polticas emitidas por autoridades para mitigar las emisiones contaminantes, por cambios en los patrones de consumo derivados de asumir nuevos paradigmas, por avances tecnolgicos que permiten explorar nuevas formas de generacin de energa y produccin de bienes. Ello puede alterar las cadenas de suministro de energa y generar una serie de activos varados por obsolescencia o por las limitantes para recibir financiamiento. Para Mxico, el tema de las Finanzas Sostenibles resulta de especial inters, ya que, por las caractersticas geogrficas, ubicacin, biodiversidad y distribucin de nuestra poblacin, la exposicin a los riesgos relacionados con el clima y al agotamiento de los recursos naturales es elevada. Desde nuestra trinchera, el Banco de Mxico ha participado activamente en foros y comits internacionales de Finanzas 4 Sostenibles, refrendando as su firme compromiso de contribuir con acciones contundentes en su mbito de facultad, para coadyuvar y facilitar que nuestra economa transite en la senda de sostenibilidad y en un futuro con cero emisiones netas. As, el Banco de Mxico desempea un papel central en la coordinacin de autoridades financieras a nivel nacional e internacional en materia de estabilidad financiera y finanzas sostenibles, gracias a su papel como miembro fundador de la Red de Bancos Centrales y Supervisores para Enverdecer el Sistema Financiero (NGFS por sus siglas en ingls). Creada en 2017, dicha red est conformada por bancos centrales y supervisores, comprometidos con la divulgacin de mejores prcticas, que contribuyan a la gestin de riesgos climatolgicos en el sector financiero, as como promover la movilizacin de financiamiento y capitales para apoyar la transicin hacia una economa sostenible. Especficamente, el Banco de Mxico ha participado activamente en la construccin de escenarios climticos y ejercicios de estrs para analizar cmo los riesgos asociados al cambio climtico repercuten sobre la economa y el sistema financiero, as como para evaluar la 5 resiliencia de las instituciones financieras ante la materializacin de los riegos ambientales. Asimismo, promueve la realizacin de seminarios, talleres y conferencias en un ambiente de intercambio de conocimientos y asistencia tcnica sobre estos temas. Por otro lado, desde 2020, el Reporte de Estabilidad Financiera del Banco de Mxico incluye una seccin de riesgos ambientalesy analiza la exposicin de las carteras de crdito de las instituciones financieras a estos riesgos. Tambin en 2020, se cre el Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles, como parte del Consejo de Estabilidad del Sistema Financiero, que agrupa a distintas autoridades financieras en nuestro pas, y del cual el Banco de Mxico funge como secretario tcnico. Este Comit tiene como principal objetivo apoyar al Consejo de Estabilidad del Sistema Financiero mediante la elaboracin de anlisis, evaluaciones, propuestas y recomendaciones en materia de finanzas sostenibles en Mxico. Debido a la relevancia del tema, en 2021 se cre dentro de la estructura de este banco central la Direccin de Anlisis y Polticas de Riesgos Ambientales y Sociales, reflejando el gran inters y 6 compromiso de la Institucin con la transicin hacia una economa verde e inclusiva. Para lograr estos objetivos, resulta indispensable crear capacidades analticas interdisciplinarias en temas de riesgos, biodiversidad geologa, entre otros. Es as que, a iniciativa del Banco de Mxico, el Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles aporb en 2022 la creacin de un "Hub de Capacitacin" con el objetivo de proveer acceso gratuito a un repositorio digital, el cual contiene material auxiliar en temas de capacitacin en finanzas sostenibles, dirigido a autoridades financieras, instituciones financieras, empresas no financieras y pblico en general, adems de promover la colaboracin del sector privado, pblico y acadmico. As, esta iniciativa pretende sumar los esfuerzos del Banco de Mxico con la comunidad acadmica y universitaria con el objetivo de concientizar y lograr que el tema se internalice e integre activamente en el proceso de formacin del capital humano y de sus capacidades desde una etapa temprana. El Banco de Mxico est consciente del rol fundamental del vnculo entre las instituciones de educacin superior, las autoridades financieras y los profesionales para crear una agenda de cooperacin 7 y dilogo para encontrar la mejor ruta hacia este objetivo, mediante la formacin de profesionistas conscientes de esta problemtica. No tengo duda de que las y los seleccionados hoy sern nuestros grandes aliados para la difusin y vidos usuarios del Hub. Para concluir, quiero enfatizar la necesidad imperativa de atender los elevados niveles de contaminacin, la prdida de biodiversidad y los impactos del cambio climtico en la economa mundial, sin que por ello, desatender los problemas socioeconmicos cotidianos. Es por lo anterior que debemos continuar con los esfuerzos de educacin y divulgacin, para lograr la concientizacin de los riesgos climticos y exponer la severidad de la situacin. Estoy segura de que trabajando en conjunto podremos avanzar en dicha agenda en beneficio de la sociedad. Muchas gracias! 8

Mexico City, March 8, 2022 Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, Constitutional President of the Mexican United States; Dr. Olga Sanchez Cordero, President of the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Senators; Dr. Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, Head of Government of Mexico City; Mtra. Loretta Ortiz Ahlf, Minister of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation; Andrea Chavez Trevino, Federal Deputy; Dr. Nadine Gasman Zylbermann, President of the National Institute of Women; 1 1 2 2 I would like to begin this conversation by noting that, since the beginning of this year, the Board of Governors of the Bank of Mexico, which designs and dictates the monetary policy of our country, has a very relevant characteristic: it is mostly made up of women. Among the twenty largest economies in the world, only the central bank of Australia shares this characteristic of our issuing institute. Mexico is one of the few economies that entrusts the purchasing power of its currency to a collegiate body where women are in the majority. It is worth reflecting then on how the evolution of our society has produced the current configuration of our Governing Board. About how these paths meet. 3 3 Historians agree that around 1953-1954 the extensive period of economic expansion began in our country that was later known as "stabilizing development", a process in which the role of our central bank was decisive, providing stability and confidence to the economy, which raised the level of well-being of millions of Mexicans. Such a period of economic development, based on a vigorous domestic market and sound fiscal and monetary stability, preceded and is contemporary with the social movement that sought to achieve equal rights for women. 4 4 Their demands were adopted by General Lazaro Cardenas, who presented the initiative during his six-year term, and the efforts of the movement ended up materializing on October 17, 1953 with the publication in the Official Gazette of the constitutional reform that granted, after a complicated process, the right to vote to women. It is up to historians to reflect and shed light on the coincidence between the great achievements of the movement for gender equality, crystallized in 1953 in the full voting rights of Mexican women, and the beginning of "stabilizing development", the longest period of economic growth and stability in Mexico's recent history. 5 5 It is very important that an economy recognizes the work of women in all its areas and that we have the right to equal education, employment and opportunities. This is one of the necessary ingredients for us to have a country with economic well-being whose wealth is distributed more equitably. We have come a long way as a society, but we still have a pending task. The most recent data show that, although women represent just over half of the country's population, according to the National Survey of Occupation and Employment, corresponding to the fourth quarter of 2021, only 45 out of every 100 women of working age are exercising some formal employment, contrasting with 76 out of every 100 in the case of the male population.

text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the signing of the Framework Agreement for Coordination and Inter-institutional Public-Private Collaboration on Gender Equality in the Mexican Financial System. Mexico City, March 18, 2022. Dr. Rogelio Ramirez de la O., Secretary of Finance and Credit Public; Maestro Gabriel Yorio, Undersecretary of Finance and Credit Public; Distinguished representatives of financial authorities and institutions; Ladies and gentlemen: I am very honored to participate in the signing of this important agreement and also to speak on behalf of the Bank of Mexico, which is one of the very few central banks in the world in which women constitute a majority on its Governing Board and where concrete progress is being made in terms of labor equality and non-discrimination. Greater participation in the labour force of women, under conditions of equality, is a fundamental right and an ethical imperative. In addition, there are powerful economic reasons to promote it, as there is empirical evidence that greater participation of women in the labor market contributes to improving the efficiency of companies and institutions, as well as to boosting economic growth. For this reason, it is essential to continue promoting the incorporation of women into the different areas of work and to guarantee an equitable environment for their professional development. In recent decades, more and more women have joined the financial sector; however, this increased participation is not yet proportionally reflected in their representation in decision-making positions. For example, very few women have had the opportunity to head a private and public banking institution in Mexico, and their presence in other decision-making positions in these institutions has also been a minority. In this regard, I believe that it is necessary to identify the different factors that prevent many women, with solid academic credentials and work merits, from reaching management positions in the financial field and to establish protocols and mechanisms that, based on best practices and evaluations at the national and international levels, balance the conditions of competition. This implies a comprehensive gender perspective, which includes, to mention just a few: (i) equitable and unbiased criteria in terms of recruitment, remuneration and professional promotion; ii) standards, training and awareness strategies that sanction and eradicate any form of discrimination, harassment or gender violence in the workplace, and iii) more flexible work practices for those who, in addition to their professional activity, face care responsibilities. Hence the relevance and opportunity of this agreement to promote gender equality in the financial sector. This is an extraordinary opportunity for public and private financial institutions to act in coordination and provide a decisive boost to equality between women and men in this strategic sector for the country's development. I am sure that creating a more conducive environment to recognize, promote and take advantage of the capacity and effort of women in the sector will bring advantages both for the institutions in the area, and for the economy in general. For women, it represents greater economic and personal independence and the possibility of fully developing their work skills or their entrepreneurial initiative. For households, women's labor and financial empowerment implies longer-term savings and spending patterns, focused on the benefit of the family. For the economy in general, it means incorporating the great reservoir of initiative, commitment and talent that millions of women can contribute. For this reason, I welcome this joint effort to promote gender equality in the financial sector. This can lead us to satisfy a basic precept of justice and, at the same time, to exploit an enormous potential that increases the competitiveness of the sector's institutions and strengthens the country's growth and the well-being of the entire population. Thanks a lot.

Title:
"Inclusive Banking in the Digital Age and the Challenges of Climate Change, 85th Banking Convention", Victoria Rodrguez, Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)
