text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the Eighty-Fifth Banking Convention, "Inclusive banking in the digital age and the challenges of climate change". Acapulco, Guerrero, March 24, 2022 Dr. Rogelio Ramirez de la O., Secretary of Finance and Credit Public; Lie Daniel Becker Feldman, President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Dr. Olga Sanchez Cordero, President of the Board of Directors of the Chamber of Senators; Deputy Sergio Gutierrez Luna, President of the Chamber of Deputies; Lie. Evelyn Salgado Pineda, Governor of the State of Guerrero; Distinguished members of the presidium, Ladies and gentlemen: It is a pleasure to participate in this Eighty-Fifth National Banking Convention, which has as its central theme "Inclusive banking in the digital age and the challenges of climate change". At the Central Bank, we are convinced that broad and strict transparency and accountability, as well as continuous communication with the various sectors of the economy, contribute to improving the effectiveness of our actions and strengthen our credibility in the eyes of society. For this reason, I am grateful for the invitation of the Association of Banks of Mexico, since this Convention constitutes a privileged space for public dialogue between the main actors in the financial sector and the authorities. This meeting is taking place in the context of a uniquely complex and uncertain geopolitical and economic scenario, which includes the economic effects of the pandemic, the development of a war in Eastern Europe, as well as unusual global inflationary pressures. In this speech I will address the international environment, its effect on prices in Mexico and the actions that the Central Bank has adopted to achieve its priority objective, which is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency. I will also elaborate on the specific themes of this Convention, in particular the opportunity represented by technological advances to achieve a more inclusive financial system and the challenges posed by climate change.  The effects of the international environment The world, and in particular central banks, are immersed in a situation not seen in nearly four decades: inflation figures in most economies are at levels not seen since the 1980s. This is the result of a set of shocks caused both directly by the health emergency, and by the effects of greater demand in the face of stimulus policies to cushion the effect of the pandemic in advanced countries and, more recently, by those caused by the war between Russia and Ukraine. The pandemic has represented an unprecedented challenge for the world economy. Governments in virtually every country were forced to take extraordinary measures to protect public health and mitigate the impact on production and employment. The vaccination strategy has contributed to the mitigation of the pandemic and to the gradual return of economic activity to normal. However, it remains to be seen to what extent the health emergency has caused medium and long-term effects on different sectors of the economy that could encounter some challenges to return to previous normal conditions. In addition, the growth outlook for the world economy in 2022 has been revised in view of the possible implications of the geopolitical conflict, which could also have longer-term implications. Disruptions in several sectors, with semiconductors and transportation being notorious, are generating increases in production costs. This in a context of recovery in global demand and a recomposition of spending on goods, which, given the impossibility of scaling supply at the same pace, have led to an imbalance between global supply and demand for various products. In turn, this imbalance has caused inflation in several economies to be at levels higher than those of their central banks' targets. In this already complex situation, a new geopolitical risk factor materializes, with the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The initial effects of this conflict on financial and commodity markets are an additional shock to that of the pandemic. In particular, given the weight that these countries have in the energy and grain markets, the most immediate effect has been on the prices of these products. This conflict was triggered only recently, so there is high uncertainty at the moment about how its development would affect prices in different markets. Thus, although its impact will depend on the magnitude of the conflict and its duration, it is perceived that it implies upside risks to inflation. Faced with persistent inflationary pressures and the advance of the economic recovery, central banks in most major advanced economies began to modify their monetary stance. Thus, the Federal Reserve of the United States, and the Banks Central banks in Canada and the United Kingdom, among others, increased their benchmark interest rates. Meanwhile, in emerging economies, a large number of central banks continue to adjust their benchmark interest rates upwards. The tightening of monetary and financial conditions at the global level constitutes a risk for national financial markets. However, so far they have shown an orderly behavior, albeit with episodes of volatility. In our country, economic activity has been recovering, after the initial shock of the pandemic, accompanied by a strengthening of the labor market. Thus, the Mexican economy is expected to continue to reactivate, driven by both domestic and external demand. The shocks derived from the pandemic have continued to generate pressures on inflation in our country, which has remained at high levels. In addition, the conflict is expected to imply a more complex environment for domestic inflation. In this context, and given the social and economic costs derived from inflation, which affect the lower-income population to a greater extent, the Bank of Mexico has reaffirmed its commitment to achieve an environment of low and stable inflation. In doing so, it also contributes to maintaining the solid macroeconomic fundamentals required to face such a complex environment. Thus, the Bank of Mexico has been adopting timely actions in order to achieve the convergence of inflation to its target and maintain the anchoring of inflation expectations. In this regard, in today's monetary policy decision, the Governing Board assessed the magnitude and diversity of the shocks that have affected inflation and its determinants, as well as the risks of contaminating medium- and long-term expectations and price formation. It also considered the greatest challenges in the face of the tightening of global monetary and financial conditions, the environment of heightened uncertainty and the greater inflationary pressures associated with the geopolitical conflict. Based on this, and with the presence of all its members, it unanimously decided to increase the target for the Overnight Interbank Interest Rate by 50 basis points to a level of 6.5%. With this, the monetary policy stance is adjusted to the trajectory required for inflation to converge to its 3% target within the forecast horizon, and the commitment of the Bank of Mexico to its constitutional mandate is endorsed.  Importance of a stable and inclusive financial system and the role of the Bank of Mexico In addition to the priority mission of the Bank of Mexico, the Central Institute has the purpose of promoting the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of the payment system. In our country, since the crisis of 1994-1995, a solid regulatory structure was designed that has been continuously strengthened. This, together with the emergency measures implemented at the time and a series of prudent and timely decisions adopted by banking institutions and authorities, such as the postponement of loan payments, the offer of restructurings and the formation of extraordinary reserves, has allowed the financial system to withstand the onslaught of the COVID-19 health contingency. This means that the banking system is in a strong position to drive economic recovery. One of the most important contributions to recovery that the banking system can make is to promote financial inclusion. Multiple benefits of having an inclusive financial system have been documented, both economic and social, such as boosting economic growth, combating poverty and inequality, promoting regional development and promoting gender parity, among others. In light of these benefits, over the past decade, financial authorities in Mexico have made efforts to include them. In particular, Banco de Mexico has actively participated in the National Council for Financial Inclusion and adopted multiple regulatory measures and actions that favor inclusion, among which the following stand out: o Deposit accounts have been established with simplified opening requirements and the association of accounts to a cell phone number has been facilitated. o The regulatory framework was modified to allow young people, from 15 years of age, to open basic bank accounts. o Workers have been authorized to take out loans associated with their payroll account at any institution. o The CoDi digital payment platform was launched, with free access and no cost for its users, which only requires a mobile device with an internet connection and a bank account. o Platforms have been opened that allow the comparison of the cost of credits, with complete and timely information. As a result of these and many other measures taken by the financial authorities, in recent years the system has tended towards greater inclusion. According to information from the National Financial Inclusion Surveys, in 2012, 35.5% of adults had a deposit account in a financial institution; by 2018 this percentage increased to 47.1 percent. Similarly, the percentage of people with formal credit increased in that period from 27.5% to 31.1%, while in the case of retirement savings accounts or Afore, the percentage increased from 19.7% to 39.5%. However, as these figures reflect, there is still ample room for improvement. The development of digital technologies in the Mexican financial system provides a unique opportunity to streamline operations, design new products and expand the coverage of financial services. Recent experience stemming from the pandemic has provided lessons on the benefits of digital payments. Households adjusted their consumption patterns to the lockdown, giving a boost to online commerce and digital payments. In turn, companies accelerated their digitalization processes, both in terms of their operation itself and in some financial aspects. Another opportunity that digital technologies offer to improve inclusion refers to credit services, as they allow the collection and processing of large volumes of information that facilitates aspects such as credit evaluation. Credit is precisely one of the issues in which the banking system can make a significant contribution to economic recovery. Empirical evidence confirms a direct relationship between credit to the non-bank private sector as a percentage of GDP and an economy's long-term growth rate. However, at the international level, Mexico has one of the lowest ratios of credit to GDP, even compared to countries of similar development. The banking system has solvency and liquidity conditions to significantly increase financing volumes. The Bank of Mexico considers that the prudent granting of credit is a key variable to support the effort, talent and initiative of Mexicans and to promote long-term growth. Financial inclusion must also contribute to promoting equality between women and men. To date, a gender gap persists in access to financial services and many women lack such instruments. Greater inclusion of women strengthens the foundations of economic growth. That is why, like those who have spoken before me, I am pleased to reiterate that a few days ago the Framework Agreement for Coordination and Inter-institutional Public-Private Collaboration on Gender Equality in the Mexican Financial System was signed, with the participation of this Central Bank. This agreement seeks to establish conditions of greater equity in the recruitment and promotion processes of women in the financial sector and, at the same time, opens the door for greater financial inclusion of women and a better offer of products and services with a gender approach.  Climate change considerations Climate change is one of the most relevant and systemic challenges we face today and in the years to come: multiple academic exercises show how environmental effects adversely affect a growing number of sectors in the economy. Global warming and environmental degradation are associated with a lower quality of life and well-being, as well as a deterioration of development opportunities in the long term. It is essential for the financial system to properly assess environmental risks and identify sustainable investment opportunities. An inadequate integration of these risks into credit and investment processes can affect the proper functioning of the financial system and affect its stability, as well as the efficient allocation of resources in the economy. The Bank of Mexico has been actively participating in the international sustainable finance agenda. It is a founding member of the Network to Green the Financial System, which brings together more than one hundred central banks and financial supervisors and aims to build capacities in authorities and financial institutions to identify and manage climate risks, as well as mobilize capital towards environmentally friendly activities. The Bank of Mexico is also part of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the Financial Stability Board, which have an ambitious agenda related to climate change and the financial system. In 2020, the Financial Stability Board established the Sustainable Finance Committee, which aims to prepare analyses, and make assessments, proposals, and recommendations on sustainable finance, with the purpose of promoting the proper functioning of the financial system and identifying and mitigating the impact of risks related to this matter. In the near future, policymakers and the financial sector face a number of challenges in sustainable finance. The Bank of Mexico is committed to this agenda. To this end, it has promoted, and will continue to promote, collaboration between authorities and financial institutions.  Closing Ladies and gentlemen: Price stability is an indispensable but not sufficient condition for economic development. In particular, in order to achieve sustained economic growth, it is essential to have a stable, inclusive, and modern financial system that provides services in good conditions of price, quality, and coverage for Mexican families and companies. This system must safely intermediate the savings of the public; to offer suitable services for the various sectors of the population and to generate credit that contributes to improving the productivity of people and companies in our country. In these historical circumstances, it is necessary to recognize that in order to take advantage of growth opportunities, the concurrence of authorities and intermediaries is required. That is why I celebrate this meeting with the bankers' guild of Mexico, since their active participation is essential to build a virtuous circle of greater inclusion, greater solidity and depth of the financial system and greater growth. As far as the Bank of Mexico is concerned, you can be sure of the support and collaboration necessary to advance the common issues that contribute to the development of our country. Without further ado, I wish them every success in the work of this Convention.

Victoria Rodrguez Ceja, gobernadora del Banco de Mxico, durante la Octogsima Quinta Convencin Bancaria, Una banca incluyente en la era digital y los retos del cambio climtico. Acapulco, Guerrero, 24 de marzo de 2022 Doctor Rogelio Ramrez de la O., Secretario de Hacienda y Crdito Pblico; Lie Daniel Becker Feldman, Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Dra. Olga Snchez Cordero, Presidenta de la Mesa Directiva de la Cmara de Senadores; Diputado Sergio Gutirrez Luna, Presidente de la Cmara de Diputados; Lie. Evelyn Salgado Pineda, Gobernadora del Estado de Guerrero; Distinguidos miembros del presidium; Seoras y seores: i Es un gusto participar en esta Octogsima Quinta Convencin Nacional Bancaria, la cual tiene como tema central Una banca incluyente en la era digital y los retos del cambio climtico. En el Banco Central estamos convencidos de que una amplia y estricta transparencia y rendicin de cuentas, as como la comunicacin continua con los diversos sectores de la economa, contribuyen a mejorar la eficacia de nuestras acciones y fortalecen nuestra credibilidad ante la sociedad. Por eso, agradezco la invitacin de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico, pues esta Convencin constituye un espacio privilegiado para el dilogo pblico entre los principales actores del sector financiero y las autoridades. Este encuentro se lleva a cabo en el marco de un escenario geopoltico y econmico singularmente complejo e incierto, que incluye los efectos econmicos de la pandemia, el desarrollo de una guerra en Europa oriental, as como inusitadas presiones inflacionarias globales. En esta intervencin abordar el entorno internacional, su efecto sobre los precios en Mxico y las acciones que ha adoptado el Banco Central para alcanzar su objetivo prioritario que es procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. Elaborar asimismo sobre los temas especficos de esta Convencin, en particular la oportunidad que representan los avances tecnolgicos para alcanzar un sistema financiero ms incluyente y los desafos que implica el cambio climtico. 2 i) Los efectos del entorno internacional El mundo y, en particular los bancos centrales, nos encontramos inmersos en una coyuntura no vista en cerca de cuatro dcadas: las cifras de inflacin de la mayora de las economas se encuentran en niveles no registrados desde la dcada de los ochenta. Esto es resultado de un conjunto de choques provocados tanto directamente por la emergencia sanitaria, como por los efectos de una mayor demanda ante las polticas de estmulo para amortiguar el efecto de la pandemia en los pases avanzados y, ms recientemente, por los causados por el conflicto blico entre Rusia y Ucrania. La pandemia ha representado un reto indito para la economa mundial. Los gobiernos de prcticamente todos los pases se vieron en la necesidad de tomar medidas extraordinarias con el fin de proteger la salud pblica y mitigar el impacto sobre la produccin y el empleo. La estrategia de vacunacin ha contribuido a la atenuacin de la pandemia y a que la actividad econmica regrese gradualmente a la normalidad. Sin embargo, todava est por verse en qu medida la emergencia sanitaria ha provocado afectaciones de mediano y largo plazo en distintos sectores de la economa que pudieran encontrar algunos retos para volver a las condiciones de normalidad previas. Adicionalmente, las perspectivas de crecimiento en 2022 para la economa mundial se han revisado ante las posibles implicaciones del conflicto geopoltico, el cual tambin podra tener implicaciones de mayor plazo. 3 Las disrupciones en varios sectores, siendo casos notorios el de los semiconductores o el de transporte, estn generando incrementos en los costos de produccin. Ello en un contexto de recuperacin de la demanda global y de una recomposicin del gasto hacia mercancas, las cuales, ante la imposibilidad de escalar la oferta al mismo ritmo, han derivado en un desbalance entre la oferta y la demanda mundial de diversos productos. A su vez, este desbalance ha ocasionado que la inflacin en diversas economas se haya ubicado en niveles superiores a los de los objetivos de sus bancos centrales. En esta coyuntura ya de por s compleja, se materializa un nuevo factor de riesgo geopoltico, con el conflicto Rusia-Ucrania. Los efectos iniciales de este conflicto sobre los mercados financieros y de materias primas constituyen un choque adicional al de la pandemia. En particular, dado el peso que estos pases tienen en los mercados de energa y granos, el efecto ms inmediato ha sido sobre los precios de estos productos. Este conflicto se desencaden solo recientemente, de modo que existe alta incertidumbre al momento sobre cmo su desarrollo afectara los precios en distintos mercados. As, si bien su impacto depender de la magnitud del conflicto y de su duracin, se percibe que implique riesgos al alza sobre la inflacin. Ante las persistentes presiones inflacionarias y el avance de la recuperacin econmica, los bancos centrales de la mayora de las principales economas avanzadas comenzaron a modificar su postura monetaria. As, la Reserva Federal de los Estados Unidos, y los Bancos 4 Centrales de Canad, y el Reino Unido, entre otros, incrementaron sus tasas de inters de referencia. Por su parte, en las economas emergentes, un amplio nmero de bancos centrales continan ajustando al alza sus tasas de inters de referencia. El apretamiento de las condiciones monetarias y financieras a nivel global constituye un riesgo para los mercados financieros nacionales. Sin embargo, hasta ahora han mostrado un comportamiento ordenado, si bien con episodios de volatilidad. En nuestro pas, la actividad econmica se ha venido recuperando, luego del choque inicial de la pandemia, acompaado de un fortalecimiento del mercado laboral. De este modo, se anticipa que la economa mexicana contine reactivndose, impulsada tanto por la demanda interna como por la externa. Los choques derivados de la pandemia han continuado generando presiones sobre la inflacin en nuestro pas, la cual se ha mantenido en niveles elevados. Adems, se anticipa que el conflicto implique un entorno ms complejo para la inflacin domstica. En este contexto, y dados los costos sociales y econmicos derivados de la inflacin, que afectan en mayor medida a la poblacin de menores ingresos, el Banco de Mxico ha refrendado su compromiso de lograr un ambiente de inflacin baja y estable. Con ello adems, contribuye a mantener los fundamentos macroeconmicos slidos que se requieren para enfrentar un entorno tan complejo. 5 De este modo, el Banco de Mxico ha venido adoptando acciones oportunas con la finalidad de lograr la convergencia de la inflacin a su meta y mantener el anclaje de las expectativas de inflacin. En este sentido, en la decisin de poltica monetaria del da de hoy, la Junta de Gobierno evalu la magnitud y la diversidad de los choques que han afectado a la inflacin y sus determinantes, as como los riesgos de que se contaminen las expectativas de mediano y largo plazos y la formacin de precios. Consider tambin los mayores retos ante el apretamiento de las condiciones monetarias y financieras globales, el entorno de acentuada incertidumbre y las mayores presiones inflacionarias asociadas al conflicto geopoltico. Con base en ello, y con la presencia de todos sus miembros, decidi por unanimidad incrementar en 50 puntos base el objetivo para la Tasa de Inters Interbancaria a un da a un nivel de 6.5%. Con esto la postura de poltica monetaria se ajusta a la trayectoria que se requiere para que la inflacin converja a su meta de 3% dentro del horizonte de pronstico, y se refrenda el compromiso del Banco de Mxico con su mandato constitucional. ii) Importancia de contar con un sistema financiero estable e incluyente y el papel del Banco de Mxico Adems de la misin prioritaria del Banco de Mxico, el Instituto Central tiene las finalidades de promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y propiciar el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. En nuestro pas, desde la crisis de 1994-1995, se dise una slida estructura regulatoria que se ha venido reforzando continuamente. Lo 6 anterior, aunado a las medidas de emergencia en su momento implementadas y a una serie de decisiones prudentes y oportunas adoptadas por las instituciones bancarias y las autoridades, tales como la posposicin del pago de los crditos, la oferta de reestructuras y la formacin de reservas extraordinarias, ha permitido que el sistema financiero resistiera el embate de la contingencia sanitaria COVID-19. Esto significa que el sistema bancario se encuentra en una posicin slida para impulsar la recuperacin econmica. Una de las contribuciones ms importantes a la recuperacin que puede hacer el sistema bancario es promover la inclusin financiera. Se han documentado mltiples beneficios de contar con un sistema financiero incluyente, tanto econmicos como sociales, tales como impulsar el crecimiento econmico, combatir la pobreza y la desigualdad, fomentar el desarrollo regional e impulsar la paridad de gnero, entre otros. En vista de dichos beneficios, durante la ltima dcada, las autoridades financieras en Mxico han llevado a cabo esfuerzos a favor de la inclusin. En particular, el Banco de Mxico ha participado activamente en el Consejo Nacional de Inclusin Financiera y adoptado mltiples medidas regulatorias y acciones que favorecen la inclusin, entre las que destacan: o Se han establecido cuentas de depsito con requerimientos de apertura simplificados y se ha facilitado la asociacin de cuentas a un nmero de telfono celular. o Se modific el marco regulatorio para permitir a jvenes, a partir de los 15 aos de edad, abrir cuentas bancarias bsicas. 7 o Se ha autorizado que los trabajadores puedan contratar crditos asociados a su cuenta de nmina en cualquier institucin. o Se lanz la plataforma de pagos digitales CoDi, de acceso libre y sin costo para sus usuarios, la cual, slo requiere un dispositivo mvil con conexin a internet y una cuenta bancaria. o Se han abierto plataformas que permiten la comparacin del costo de los crditos, con informacin completa y oportuna. Como resultado de estas y muchas otras medidas adoptadas por las autoridades financieras, en los ltimos aos el sistema ha tendido hacia una mayor inclusin. De acuerdo con la informacin de las Encuestas Nacionales de Inclusin Financiera, en 2012, el 35.5% de los adultos contaban con una cuenta de depsito en una institucin financiera; para 2018 dicho porcentaje aument a 47.1 por ciento. De manera similar, el porcentaje de personas con crdito formal aument en ese periodo de 27.5% a 31.1%, mientras que en el caso de cuentas de ahorro para el retiro o Afore, el porcentaje aument de 19.7% a 39.5%. Sin embargo, como reflejan estas cifras, sigue habiendo un amplio margen para mejorar. El desarrollo de tecnologas digitales en el sistema financiero mexicano, brinda una oportunidad nica para agilizar las operaciones, disear nuevos productos y ampliar la cobertura de los servicios financieros. La experiencia reciente derivada de la pandemia ha proporcionado lecciones sobre los beneficios de los pagos digitales. Los hogares ajustaron sus patrones de consumo al confinamiento, dando un impulso 8 al comercio en lnea y a los pagos digitales. A su vez, las empresas aceleraron sus procesos de digitalizacin, tanto en lo relacionado con su operacin misma como en algunos aspectos financieros. Otra oportunidad que las tecnologas digitales ofrecen para mejorar la inclusin se refiere a los servicios de crdito, pues permiten el acopio y procesamiento de grandes volmenes de informacin que facilita aspectos como la evaluacin crediticia. Precisamente el crdito es uno de los temas en los que el sistema bancario puede hacer una contribucin significativa a la recuperacin econmica. La evidencia emprica confirma una relacin directa entre el crdito al sector privado no bancario como porcentaje del PIB y la tasa de crecimiento de largo plazo de una economa. Sin embargo, a nivel internacional, Mxico presenta una de las razones ms bajas de crdito a PIB, incluso comparado con pases de desarrollo similar. El sistema bancario cuenta con condiciones de solvencia y liquidez para incrementar de manera relevante los volmenes de financiamiento. El Banco de Mxico considera que el otorgamiento prudente del crdito, es una variable clave para apoyar el esfuerzo, talento e iniciativa de los mexicanos y para propiciar el crecimiento de largo plazo. La inclusin financiera debe contribuir tambin a fomentar la equidad entre mujeres y hombres. Hasta la fecha persiste una brecha de gnero en el acceso a los servicios financieros y son muchas las mujeres que carecen de este tipo de instrumentos. Una mayor inclusin de la mujer fortalece las bases del crecimiento econmico. Por eso, al igual que a quienes me precedieron en el uso de la palabra, me complace reiterar 9 que hace unos das se firm el Convenio Marco de Coordinacin y Colaboracin Interinstitucional Pblico-Privado en Materia de Igualdad de Gnero en el Sistema Financiero Mexicano, con la participacin de este Banco Central. Con dicho convenio se busca establecer condiciones de mayor equidad en los procesos de reclutamiento y promocin de las mujeres en el sector financiero y, a la vez, se abre la puerta para una mayor inclusin financiera de la mujer y una mejor oferta de productos y servicios con enfoque de gnero. iii) Consideraciones respecto al cambio climtico El cambio climtico es uno de los retos ms relevantes y sistmicos que enfrentamos hoy y en los aos por venir: mltiples ejercicios acadmicos muestran cmo los efectos ambientales afectan desfavorablemente a un nmero creciente de sectores en la economa. El calentamiento global y la degradacin ambiental se asocian con una menor calidad de vida y bienestar, as como con un deterioro de las oportunidades de desarrollo en el largo plazo. Para el sistema financiero es fundamental valorar adecuadamente los riesgos ambientales e identificar oportunidades de inversin sostenibles. Una inadecuada integracin de estos riesgos en los procesos de crdito e inversin puede incidir sobre el buen funcionamiento del sistema financiero y afectar su estabilidad, as como la asignacin eficiente de recursos en la economa. El Banco de Mxico ha venido participando activamente en la agenda internacional de finanzas sostenibles. Es miembro fundador de la Red 10 para Enverdecer el Sistema Financiero la cual agrupa a ms de cien bancos centrales y supervisores financieros y tiene el objetivo de crear capacidades en autoridades e instituciones financieras para identificar y administrar riesgos climticos as como movilizar capital hacia actividades amigables con el medio ambiente. El Banco de Mxico tambin forma parte del Comit de Supervisin Bancaria de Basilea y del Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera, que tienen una ambiciosa agenda relacionada al cambio climtico y el sistema financiero. En 2020, el Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera estableci el Comit de Finanzas Sostenibles que tiene por objeto elaborar anlisis, y realizar evaluaciones, propuestas y recomendaciones en materia de finanzas sostenibles, con el propsito de fomentar el buen funcionamiento del sistema financiero e identificar y mitigar el impacto de los riesgos relacionados con esta materia. En el futuro prximo las autoridades y el sector financiero enfrentan diversos retos en materia de finanzas sostenibles. El Banco de Mxico est comprometido con esta agenda. Para este efecto, ha impulsado, y continuar impulsando, la colaboracin entre autoridades e instituciones financieras. iv) Cierre Seoras y seores: La estabilidad de precios es una condicin indispensable pero no suficiente para el desarrollo econmico. 11 En particular, para alcanzar un crecimiento econmico sostenido es fundamental contar con un sistema financiero estable, inclusivo, moderno, que provea servicios en buenas condiciones de precio, calidad y cobertura para las familias y empresas mexicanas. Este sistema debe intermediar de manera segura el ahorro del pblico; ofrecer servicios idneos para los diversos sectores de la poblacin y generar crdito que contribuya a mejorar la productividad de personas y empresas en nuestro pas. En estas circunstancias histricas es necesario reconocer que para aprovechar las oportunidades de crecimiento, se requiere la concurrencia de las autoridades y los intermediarios. Por eso, celebro este encuentro con el gremio de los banqueros de Mxico, pues su concurso activo es fundamental para construir un crculo virtuoso de mayor inclusin, mayor solidez y profundidad del sistema financiero y mayor crecimiento. En lo que respecta al Banco de Mxico, pueden estar seguros de contar con el apoyo y la colaboracin necesarios para avanzar los temas comunes que contribuyan con el desarrollo de nuestro pas. Sin ms, les deseo el mayor de los xitos en los trabajos de esta Convencin. 12

Title:
"Appearance before the Senate of the Republic", Victoria Rodrguez, Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

Full text
text: Appearance before the Senate of the Republic, Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico. April 21, 2022 Senator Alejandro Armenia Mier, President of the Finance and Public Credit Committee; Senator Nuvia Mayorga Delgado, Secretary of the Commission; Senator Victor Oswaldo Fuentes Solis, Secretary of the Commission; Distinguished members of the Finance and Public Credit Commission of the Senate of the Republic." I appear before this Committee on Finance and Public Credit of the Senate of the Republic, as provided for in Article 47, section XIII, of the Law of the Bank of Mexico, in order to submit to this body of the Chamber of Senators the report on the fulfillment of the mandate established for this central institution, which includes the exercise by the Bank of Mexico of the powers conferred on it to to comply with the priority objective of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, as well as the purposes of promoting the healthy development of the financial system and fostering the proper functioning of payment systems. Accountability is an indispensable part of exercising central bank autonomy. Society has entrusted us with the procurement of the purchasing power of the national currency, so the transparency of our actions is a daily exercise. This appearance is a very important part of the actions that make up the exercise of the autonomy of our functions and our management. I would like to begin my appearance with some reflections on the current state of global inflationary dynamics and the challenges it presents for the monetary policy of central banks in the world. Subsequently, I would like to report in detail on the behavior of the national economy and the evolution of inflation in our country, to conclude with a timely review of the Mexican financial system, as well as the advances and prospects for the country's payment systems, which is immersed in a profound technological transformation. At the current juncture, the world's central banks, including Mexico's, are facing the most difficult situation in the last four decades. The COVID-19 pandemic implied a supply shock on a global scale, as the health confinement dislocated the normal functioning of the supply and logistics chains of multiple sectors. At the same time, in a broad set of economies, governments and central banks implemented significant fiscal and monetary stimuli in order to support both the liquidity of the financial system and aggregate demand under conditions in which employment suffered a significant reduction. The confluence of factors from both the supply and demand sides to which the pandemic gave rise made for an inflationary dynamic that was already complicated, to which the impact and uncertainty of the conflict in Ukraine has been added. The two countries involved in the conflict represent a high percentage in markets critical to price formation in international markets, especially in the energy, grains, minerals and metals sectors. Thus, the impact that the conflict has had on these markets has been immediate and has complicated the outlook for central banks in their work to control inflation. In this adverse environment, central bank action has rarely been so important. In the face of such complex price dynamics, we must be clear to society and economic actors that our commitment to protecting the purchasing power of the currency is unwavering and that the Bank of Mexico will act in a timely manner so that inflation converges towards the 3% target. Among the costs of inflation, it is worth noting that it reduces the purchasing power of money. Since lower-income families have less access to the financial system, they tend to keep a higher proportion of their income in cash. Consequently, it is these families that are most affected by the inflationary phenomenon, which tends to increase poverty and inequality in income distribution. In addition to the above, high and volatile inflation tends to have a negative impact on the growth and development of countries. This is because, among other factors, it affects the long-term planning of economic agents; it distorts their decisions affecting the efficient allocation of resources in the economy; and it can lead to a process of financial disintermediation. Based on these premises, the Bank of Mexico has been working to comply with its constitutional mandate to ensure price stability by implementing a prudent and timely monetary policy based on the information available. In particular, in view of the aforementioned economic effects, as of June 2021 the Bank of Mexico has been increasing its reference rate from a level of 4.0% to the 6.50% at which it currently stands. International Economic Environment On the international front, the confluence of factors mentioned above has led to a generalized reduction in economic growth estimates by international financial organizations. If we take as a reference those published by the International Monetary Fund in April of this year, the downward reduction in the estimate of global economic growth is 0.8 percentage points compared to the forecasts published in January. Among the main revisions are those of Russia, the euro area, and the United Kingdom, whose growth slowed by 11.3, 1.1, and 1.0 percentage points, respectively. For our country, the reduction in global activity also resulted in a reduction in the estimated growth for 2022. The effects of the Omicron variant of SARS-CoV-2 and the geopolitical conflict explain the revision of growth forecasts. However, vaccination campaigns have contributed to hospitalizations and deaths being only a fraction of those suffered in past peaks. At the global level, inflation figures show the complexity of the current situation. In the United States, the annual pace of consumer inflation as of March 2022 is 8.5 percent, the highest since December 1981, while producer inflation for the same month, at 11.20 percent, is the highest figure in the history of this record, suggesting latent pressures in the cost chain. There are few exceptions, China, Japan, and some Southeast Asian economies, since in general, economies, both developed and emerging, are setting annual inflation figures higher than those recorded in several decades. Inflation in the euro area hit a 7.5 percent pace in March, accelerating from 5.9 percent in February, largely as a result of the energy and grain price shock caused by the conflict in Ukraine. Normalization of monetary stances This inflationary dynamic has caused most central banks, both in developed and emerging economies, to begin to normalize their monetary stance with respect to the ample stimulus granted during the pandemic. However, the standardization process has been heterogeneous between countries. Regarding the monetary normalization process in the United States, which is particularly important for Mexico, due to the intense relationship between the two countries, on March 15 the Federal Reserve decided to increase its Federal Funds rate target by 25 hundredths. Based on this decision, a series of comments by officials of the central institute, as well as the reaction of the markets to indicators of prices, economic activity and employment, allow us to project that interest rates will have successive increases in the remainder of the year, and additionally, that these increases will probably be higher and faster than had been anticipated. which implies an additional challenge for the conduct of Monetary Policy in our country. Evolution of the national economy Although not exempt from episodes of volatility, some of them important, the Mexican peso has so far been able to absorb the various disturbances from abroad with efficiency and solidity, operating from October of last year to date in a range between 19.79 and 21.92 pesos per dollar. In a flexible exchange rate regime, it is precisely the role of the exchange rate to accommodate external shocks and help cushion a greater impact on the real economy. For their part, during the last year, interest rates in Mexico have increased across the board. In particular, short-term bonds have been adjusted upwards mainly due to increases in the Bank of Mexico's reference rate since June last year. In turn, medium- and long-term interest rates have increased in line with the increases observed in interest rates in the United States, associated with the prospect of monetary withdrawal in that country. After contracting 8.2 percent in 2020 as a result of the initial shock of the pandemic, national economic activity showed a growth of 4.8% in 2021, which continued to recover after the initial shock of the pandemic, although it has not yet recovered the levels observed before the health crisis. The growth figure for 2021 reflected that, although the economy showed a reactivation as greater opening of activities and greater mobility of the population were achieved, other factors limited its dynamism, such as bottlenecks in production, shortages of inputs -particularly in the automotive sector-, and episodes of increases in infections. Monthly data on economic activity has shown an upward trajectory since November, supported by both industrial and service sector expansions, while agricultural activities have remained at relatively high levels. However, the environment for growth remains complex. Regarding the Bank of Mexico's growth forecasts, for 2022 a GDP expansion of between 1.6 and 3.2 percent is expected, with a point estimate of 2.4 percent. For 2023, GDP growth is anticipated between 1.9 and 3.9 percent with a point estimate of 2.9 percent. Domestic inflation situation In March 2022, annual headline inflation in our country stood at 7.45 percent. The environment for inflation continues to be complex, as the effects of the shocks associated with the pandemic, which have not been fully resolved, have been compounded by greater pressures on energy and other raw materials derived from the war conflict. Annual core inflation accumulated sixteen consecutive months of increases, reaching 6.78 percent in March. Inside, pressures have been observed in both merchandise and services inflation. Annual non-core inflation has been at high levels, standing at 9.45 percent in March 2022. This has been pressured by high annual variations in the prices of agricultural and energy products, although those of energy have shown a decrease in 2022. The Board of Governors of the Bank of Mexico has evaluated the magnitude and diversity of inflationary shocks, as well as the risk of contaminating longer-term expectations. He also considered the greater challenges associated with the tightening of global monetary and financial conditions and the greater inflationary pressures associated with the geopolitical conflict in Eastern Europe. Faced with this scenario, the Bank of Mexico has taken monetary policy actions in a prudent and timely manner:  From June to November 2021, the Board increased the benchmark rate by 25 basis points at each of its monetary policy meetings;  Subsequently, at the December 2021, February 2022 and March 2022 meetings, the rate of reference by 50 basis points in each of these sessions, highlighting the unanimity in the vote in the most recent decision;  As a result, the reference rate went from a level of 4.0 percent between February and June 2021, to its current level of 6.5 percent. Considering these adjustments, the short-term real ex ante interest rate currently stands at 1.91 percent, within the estimated range for the neutral rate. Given the complex environment that inflation continues to face and the pressures that are anticipated in the face of the persistence of the effects of the pandemic and the shocks initially expected by the geopolitical conflict, inflation forecasts were significantly revised upwards with the March 2022 Monetary Policy announcement. Headline inflation is expected to decline over the course of 2022 and converge to the 3 percent target towards the end of the forecast horizon. For annual core inflation, it is expected to increase still in the first half of 2022, and then decrease and converge to levels close to 3 percent in mid-2023. However, the balance of risks for inflation has deteriorated and remains on the rise. Upside risks include the persistence of core inflation at elevated levels, and additional inflationary pressures resulting from the pandemic and geopolitical conflict. 2.- FINANCIAL SYSTEM In addition to its priority objective of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, the purposes of the Central Institute are to promote the healthy development of the financial system and to promote the proper functioning of payment systems; This implies fostering the conditions so that financial products and services are of quality, accessible and affordable to the entire population at all times and that the operational continuity and resilience of the financial system is guaranteed in their provision. The Mexican banking system is now in a solid position to drive economic recovery, thanks to the regulatory structure that has been strengthened over the last decades and the measures opportunely implemented by financial institutions and authorities to address the health contingency, such as the rescheduling of the payment of loans granted to bank users. the offer of restructuring of these credits and the formation of extraordinary reserves. In general, the main activity of Mexican banks (i.e., the collection and granting of credit) experienced a sustained increase from 2016 to the first half of 2020. This trend was largely modified as a result of the pandemic, which encouraged deposits and reduced the granting of credit. This pattern is not exclusive to Mexico. One of the effects of the health emergency in most economies was the net accumulation of savings; Although the dynamics of this phenomenon have moderated in recent months, the environment of uncertainty caused by the pandemic increased the importance of liquid monetary assets, that is, the demand for cash and bank deposits both on demand and in the term by the private sector. The interruption of the credit trend was differentiated. Of note has been the resistance that, both internationally and in Mexico, housing credit has experienced, which represents about 50 percent of the commercial banking credit portfolio to households in Mexico, and which managed to remain in growth during most of the last two years. contrary to consumer credit, which presented a significant contraction in 2021 and whose dynamism is close to recovering growth. However, in the case of large companies, the demand for credit, depressed in the pandemic, began only a slow recovery in 2021 conditioned by the faltering economic recovery, as well as by granting conditions that continue to be tight compared to the pre-pandemic period. On the other hand, financing for smaller companies has registered a reduction in its dynamism since 2019, The pandemic resulted in a tightening in the conditions of granting, which have not been reversed, while a recovery in the demand for credit from 2021 is notorious. During the pandemic, the Bank of Mexico supported the credit market for companies and households through two liquidity facilities. The first of them was "Financing for individuals and MSMEs by releasing the Monetary Regulation Deposit (DRM) or through term reports", through which the Bank of Mexico provided liquidity to credit institutions so that they could channel it to individuals and MSMEs. The freed resources were associated with withdrawals of Monetary Regulation Deposits from credit institutions, as well as reports with eligible securities, and their cost was equal to the target of the one-day interbank interest rate. The second was the line of "Financing oriented to MSMEs guaranteed with corporate credits", through which financing was granted to credit institutions guaranteed with the credit portfolio to companies in the corporate sector, so that in turn, these institutions channeled credits to MSMEs, at reference rate cost. The facilities concluded on September 30, 2021, with a total of 428,233 individuals and MSMEs benefiting. The above and other precautionary measures and prudence in the granting of credit have helped to ensure that, after a rebound in the most difficult part of the confinement, the NPL ratio of the Mexican financial system is lower than the pre-pandemic level. Other indicators illustrate the strength of the national banking system: solvency and liquidity levels did not deteriorate during the health emergency, and in particular the Liquidity Coverage Ratio is above 100 percent; this is linked, among other things, to the fact that during the pandemic, the Bank of Mexico and the CNBV implemented facilities to maintain adequate liquidity levels, including the flexibility of the Coverage Ratio of Liquidity by the Bank Liquidity Regulation Committee, made up of both authorities. As part of its responsibility to support the healthy development of the national financial system, Banco de Mexico puts the user of financial services at the center of its efforts, focusing on:  Improve transparency and information services available to users by trying to provide them with sufficient elements for good financial decision-making;  Improve efficiency and competition in service delivery to expand the quantity and variety of supply, as well as to lead to lower costs; and  Protect the interests of users by preventing the possibility of their interests being violated, while promoting financial inclusion. How Payment Systems Work The Bank of Mexico has among its purposes to promote the proper functioning of payment systems, for which it has defined a long-term vision that seeks to ensure that the economic and financial decisions made by users are not distorted by the way they make their payments. The objective of this vision is that all Mexicans have access to means to send and receive electronic payments; that these are secure, immediate, at a low cost and are available at any time; that there is transparency in each transaction; and, that in the event of an inconvenience, there are clear responsibilities. The SPEI has become the most important infrastructure of the payment system in the Mexican banking sector and its recent evolution has shown massive adoption, allowing transfers to be made from the internet or mobile application and encompassing multiple payments for both public and private services in an increasing way. At the end of 2021, the operations of this system grew 62 percent compared to 2020. In March of this year, amendments to the SPEI rules were published in order to continue promoting the healthy development of the financial system and protect the interests of the public, expanding the access of more actors to the payment network without reducing the security of the system, and expanding the infrastructure to meet the growing demand for payments and the demand to send and receive money among the population. The CoDi platform, which allows you to request payments through electronic transfers through SPEI using a smartphone or mobile device in an efficient, secure and real-time way, has had a satisfactory acceptance and continues to grow. From its implementation until the end of 2021, CoDi reached 12 million validated accounts, of which 770 thousand made at least one payment and 616 thousand at least one collection, reaching 3.6 million operations for an amount of 2,934.5 million pesos. In 2021 in particular, a total of 2.4 million operations were settled. Although today SPEI and CoDi have the elements to meet the needs of users, within the framework of the implementation of a clearing and settlement infrastructure, the SPEI infrastructure renovation project, SPEI 2.0, arises. The objective is to have a modern payment architecture that can meet future requirements and meet new payment needs in a high availability scheme that allows greater interoperability between payment systems and markets, as a result of the sustained growth in the volume of operations in the Mexican payment market. SPEI 2.0 will allow the incorporation of services, such as settlement services in other currencies, within the same architecture; payment against payment in foreign exchange operations; and delivery versus payment in transactions with securities, always complying with the conditions of being scalable, continuous, secure and parallelizable. In addition, Banco de Mexico has developed the Identity Authentication and Validation System (SAVI), with the aim of making it easier for banking users to prove their identity through efficient processes, allow the secure and regulated exchange of information, have a reliable record at the financial system level, and help reduce the costs necessary to prove identity. The SAVI is made up of three modules: the Database of International Transfers of Funds or in Foreign Currency (BDT), which provides information to financial institutions regarding international transfers and which is already in operation; the Knowledge of Customers Database involved in such operations (BDCC), which will maintain information and documentation files of users in a secure and confidential manner and the Biometric Information Validation Module (MVIB), which will allow the identity of users operating in the financial system to be identified. Regarding the last two modules, they are in advanced stages of technological development and will come into operation as the corresponding regulatory frameworks are updated to guarantee the security and efficiency of the management of these information resources. As part of the long-term payments strategy, the Bank of Mexico has initiated the development of a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), which is part of the long-term payments strategy, with the proposal of an infrastructure for the registration of resources. An CBDC is an electronic record in favor of an end user, which is the responsibility of the central bank in the form of a liability for him and which constitutes an integral part of the monetary base like the coins and banknotes that we know and therefore must fulfill the three main functions: being a means of payment, unit of account and store of value. The MDBC seeks to generate means of payment aimed at financial inclusion, expand the options for making fast, secure, efficient and interoperable payments in the economy, and implement complementary functionalities to the means of payment, such as automation and programmability mechanisms, promoting innovation. We estimate at the Bank of Mexico that this process will take about three years for its definitive operation. Other Tools As part of its transparency strategy, Banco de Mexico has designed a set of tools aimed at empowering users. It is not feasible to have a competitive financial system without participatory users and for this they require having complete, reliable and timely information, presented in a friendly way and through the most accessible channels possible. In this sense, the central bank has developed a series of platforms aimed at providing information on the alternatives available to users:  The Deposit Account Comparator guides the user in their search, facilitating the selection of the ideal account according to their needs and preferences;  The bank credit comparator facilitates the comparison of the cost of credits, helping users to know the available options before choosing, allowing them to filter and sort generic results according to their preferences;  The bank credit offering platform reduces the cost of searching for and comparing credit, as well as the cost of acquiring customers, allowing banks to make offers in a competitive environment and encouraging access to credit. Regarding this platform, in 2022 it will be released for credit cards, and later personal, automotive, and mortgage loans will be included. To promote a competitive financial system that empowers users, it is convenient for customers to have the ability to move between providers. Since November 2015, workers who receive their salaries in bank accounts can carry out the procedure to receive their resources also from the bank where they want to have their account, which facilitates the process and provides the right incentives to the bank that wants to attract the paymasters. To date, there have been four million successful porting requests. A reflection of a healthy financial system is that services are provided in the best conditions of quality and price to users and that they obtain high levels of satisfaction when using them. To this end, the Bank of Mexico monitors the levels of satisfaction of users of financial services through a survey that is nationally representative. Using the results of the survey, it is possible to construct user satisfaction indicators with the quality of existing products and services, which guide us in their calibration and in the generation of new ones. An additional element to generate more competition and better conditions for users is the incorporation of technological innovations that, by ensuring adequate conditions of competition and security, produce tangible social benefits. In this sense, the Law to Regulate Financial Technology Institutions has encouraged the entry of new participants in the financial sector. Banco de Mexico has worked in coordination with the other competent financial authorities in the authorization process of these new participants, always taking care that the diversity of business models and the innovative schemes allowed by these authorities adhere satisfactorily to the regulations and operations accepted by the sector. Since 2019, 139 applications have been received from financial technology institutions, of which 87 correspond to electronic payment fund institutions; 45 to collective financing institutions; and 7 to companies that operate with innovative models. Of these requests, 28 have been withdrawn and, of the remaining 111, 83 have been resolved and 28 are still in process. 3. FINAL CONSIDERATIONS Honorable Senators: The constitutional mandate of the Bank of Mexico establishes as a priority the protection of the purchasing power of the national currency. The current situation presents very complex challenges that have postponed reaching the established inflation target. That is why we consider it a priority that there is a general consensus in our society regarding the importance of the convergence of inflation towards our 3 percent target and that we share the view that the effect of inflation on the income and assets of the population is very costly. In this sense, the efforts of education, dissemination, transparency and accountability of our Issuing Institute are fundamental. But while the achievement of the inflation target faces particularly challenging conditions, where factors of different kinds contribute to the deferral of the convergence of inflation towards our policy objective over time, I would just as clearly want to emphasize the Bank's unequivocal commitment to achieving this convergence. It is also important to mention that additionally, but as an integral part of our mandate, the Bank of Mexico must develop the financial system and the means of payment so that citizens in general, users or not of financial services, have the best conditions for their well-being and quality of life to prosper in a framework of competition. quality and safety. The Bank of Mexico is a provider of public goods, of services within everyone's reach, of infrastructures that seek the common good in a framework of transparency and equal access for members of the national economy. The central bank's vision in this regard is broad and far-reaching, as we are convinced that the affordability of these public goods is a requirement for economic growth and the well-being of families in the long term.
