text: Remarks by Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the 86th Banking Convention Merida, March 16, 2023 Lie. Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, Constitutional President of the United States of Mexico; Lie. Mauricio Vila Dosal, Governor of the State of Yucatan; Dr. Rogelio Ramirez de la O., Secretary of Finance and Public Credit; Gabriel Yorio Gonzalez, Undersecretary of Finance and Public Credit; Dr. Jesus de la Fuente Rodriguez, President of the Banking and Securities Commission; Lie. Daniel Becker Feldman, President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Distinguished members of the Presidium; Ladies and gentlemen: Greeting It is an honor to participate in this Eighty-Sixth Banking Convention, which, on this occasion, enjoys the hospitality of the beautiful city of Merida. I am grateful for the kind invitation of the Association of Banks of Mexico (ABM). Throughout its history, the ABM has collaborated with the authorities to promote the expansion of the banking sector and the development of the country and has opened exceptional spaces for dialogue, such as this Convention. The Convention usually brings together world-class experts around a central theme, which this year is "Challenges and opportunities: inclusion, sustainability and nearshoring". For Banco de Mexico, participating in this meeting is an opportunity to strengthen our communication with the most relevant financial actors, which contributes to improving the understanding and effectiveness of our policies. I will take advantage of my speech to, on the one hand, highlight the validity and relevance of the purposes of the Bank of Mexico in the current global circumstances and, on the other, convey the bank's diagnosis of recent economic developments, as well as elaborate on the inflationary outlook and our monetary policy stance. I would also like to mention some of the main challenges regarding financial and payment systems. The Bank's purposes and the current circumstances The Bank of Mexico's priority objective, established in the Constitution of our country, is to seek to maintain the purchasing power of the national currency. In addition, the law entrusts it with promoting the healthy development of the financial system, as well as promoting the proper functioning of the payment system. These three purposes are closely related, and generate tangible benefits for society as a whole, particularly for the most disadvantaged. Experience clearly shows that persistent inflation above central banks' targets undermines the foundations of economic growth and deteriorates the quality of life of the population. Although inflation affects society as a whole, it hurts lower-income sectors to a greater extent. For this reason, in recent decades a consensus has been reached that price stability is an invaluable collective good and a central foundation of any viable process of sustained growth and equity. Based on this consensus, in many countries, including Mexico, very important progress has been made in the fight against inflation. However, as a result of the pandemic and more recently the war in Ukraine, the world has faced unexpected challenges that have implied an inflationary period of a severity not seen in decades. On the one hand, the pandemic, in addition to the irreparable human losses it entailed, forced the paralysis of many economic activities, as well as other actions of social isolation, which profoundly affected the economy and the daily lives of people around the world. On the other hand, the war between Russia and Ukraine, in addition to its dramatic human and economic cost in the region, has severely impacted the rest of the world, both because of its threats to peace, and because of the importance of these countries in the production of critical inputs for the global economy. Thus, in recent years, a series of phenomena have been concatenated, such as health confinements, the disruption of production chains, the aftermath of war, trade frictions between nations and the granting of abundant fiscal stimuli, mainly in advanced economies. All this has dislocated both supply and demand and has spread inflationary pressures globally. After a period of heterogeneous economic recovery after the pandemic, in the face of inflation levels not seen in decades, central banks, both advanced and emerging economies, have adjusted their benchmark rates upwards and some have announced that they will remain high for an extended period. In this context of tight monetary and financial conditions, coupled with the repercussions of the war in Ukraine, global economic growth moderated during the fourth quarter of 2022 and forecasts for 2023 by the main multilateral organisations point to a slowdown in it. Headline inflation remains high, and while headline inflation declined in several economies, core inflation, which better reflects the inflationary trend, has yet to clearly show a downward turning point. As far as our country is concerned, in the fourth quarter of 2022, the Mexican economy continued to grow, although with less dynamism than in previous quarters. On the price side, in February, annual headline inflation stood at 7.62%; while core inflation stood at 8.29%. The latter component does not yet show a favourable dynamic, as the annual change in the prices of goods has shown a slower decline than expected and that of services has continued to increase. Given this circumstance, in the monetary policy decision of February 9, the forecasts for headline and core inflation were adjusted for the entire horizon and inflation is expected to converge to the target in the fourth quarter of 2024. In this decision, the Governing Board evaluated the magnitude and diversity of inflationary shocks and their determinants, as well as the evolution of medium and long-term expectations and the price formation process. Based on these elements, it determined that, given the dynamics of core inflation, it was necessary to repeat the magnitude of the increase in the reference rate of the previous meeting and decided, unanimously, to increase the target for the Overnight Interbank Interest Rate by 50 basis points to a level of 11%. As stated in the statement, the Governing Board will closely monitor the various factors that affect the expected path for inflation and its expectations. The purpose is to determine a reference rate consistent at all times, both with the orderly and sustained convergence of headline inflation to the 3% target in the period in which monetary policy operates, and with an adequate adjustment of the economy and financial markets. For the next meeting, the Governing Board will consider the monetary stance that has already been reached, as well as the evolution of the data. The monetary policy actions that have been implemented since the beginning of the current upward cycle in June 2021 have contributed to the fact that, despite the severity of the shocks, longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable. Thus, at the Bank of Mexico we act with opportunity and in accordance with our legal mandate: the unwavering objective is to consolidate price stability. Promote the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of the payment system Another function that the law mandates to the Bank of Mexico is to promote the healthy development of the financial system and the proper functioning of the payment system. As you know, financial stability is a fundamental part of this mandate. For this reason, both the Bank of Mexico and the other authorities represented here ensure that it is maintained. The Mexican banking system is well capitalized and with adequate levels of liquidity, in both cases well above the regulatory minimums. The stress tests that we published in the Stability Report confirm this since, even in the face of severe but plausible adverse scenarios, banks remain solvent and with sufficient liquidity. Therefore, in the absence of additional shocks, we do not expect recent developments in the United States banking system or in international markets to have relevant negative effects on Mexican banking. What happened to some banks in that country can be characterized as a typical episode of bank runs, which could have had their origin in three factors. First, inadequate management of interest rate risk. Second, an excessive concentration of exposures in one sector of the economy, especially for one of the banks. Finally, that the proportion of depositors of these banks with balances above the coverage of the deposit insurance was very high. The combination of these factors undermined the confidence of depositors, who went to withdraw their resources for fear of facing losses. As for the events in the international markets, mainly European, they respond to the fact that in an environment of high uncertainty, there was negative news about a global systemically important bank, which generated significant increases in the volatility of several assets and an increase in investors' risk aversion. The financial authorities in charge of said bank announced that as it complies with the capital and liquidity requirements required of this type of institution, if necessary, they will provide liquidity to the entity, and the bank has indicated that it will use this facility. These episodes remind us that depositors' trust is essential for banks to be able to carry out their essential tasks of transforming terms and risks, so it is essential to constantly reinforce it. To this end, it is important to prudently manage risks without underestimating the risk of concentration, to promote an environment of healthy competition, to maintain high standards of customer service and scrupulous, complete and timely compliance with the regulatory framework and its amendments. Also that the authorities must remain alert and act selectively using the tools that may be necessary, as the case may be. A stable, healthy and inclusive financial system allows the public's savings to be channelled towards the most desirable objectives for society. The fact that the majority of the population has access to financial services in the best quality and cost conditions has numerous positive effects, such as leveling opportunities between the different social sectors, reducing backwardness and promoting gender parity. In addition, greater financial inclusion makes the transmission of monetary policy more effective. In this regard, I would like to reiterate that the Bank of Mexico will be attentive at all times to the development of global and local financial markets in order to fulfill its mandate to promote the healthy development of the financial system for the benefit of the population. Banco de Mexico participates in the main global coordination forums to promote financial health and stability and, at the national level, is part of the Financial System Stability Council, in which Mexican authorities interact to monitor possible vulnerabilities and respond to any contingency. Credit institutions operate with high levels of capital and liquidity, which allows them to face adverse scenarios, as I mentioned a few moments ago. In short, the banking system is in a favorable situation to promote economic reactivation. This is manifesting itself in a recovery in credit, even in the current complex circumstances, which denotes confidence going forward. In order for banks to enhance their contribution to development, a process of continuous improvement is necessary that includes, on the one hand, a wider range of financial products and services under the most appropriate conditions of price and quality for homes and businesses and, on the other hand, that consumers have the tools to make an optimal choice of products. as well as a more appropriate planning of all its financial operations. The Bank of Mexico has placed the user of financial services at the center of its actions and has deployed a large number of instruments that rely on technological advances. These instruments seek to generate incentives for intermediaries to compete with better products and services and, also, to train participatory, well-informed users who are aware of their rights. Among the instruments that the Bank has recently developed are:  A catalog of categories that establishes that the commissions associated with a service have the same name, regardless of the financial product to which they are associated or the financial institution that offers them. This makes it easier to compare fee amounts between institutions and products and promotes greater transparency and competition.  For some years now, the Bank of Mexico has been offering a generic comparator of the cost of credit, which contains complete, reliable and timely information provided by intermediaries. From 2019 to date, more than half a million people have consulted this tool, which favors a good decision by customers and, at the same time, encourages institutions to offer better products.  Complementing the generic comparator, Banco de Mexico is enabling an innovative and unique platform at the international level, so that people looking for a loan can, through an application on their smartphones, send an application to several providers and receive personalized offers, according to their need and risk profile. The platform leverages digital technologies to reduce search and acquisition costs incurred by users and providers. This benefits everyone because it generates greater efficiency in the process, empowers consumers and increases the potential customers of institutions. The success of this instrument depends on the active participation of intermediaries, so I call on all banking institutions to join this platform.  Likewise, the Bank of Mexico has created a tool that allows users to compare the costs and characteristics of the different deposit products. This development has been challenging, as the costs incurred by a user of a deposit product depend on their usage profile. In this way, the tool collects information from the user to determine the type of products suitable for that profile. As far as the payment system is concerned, promoting its proper functioning is a goal of the Bank of Mexico. The fact that all Mexicans can carry out their transactions in a secure, efficient and expeditious manner is a factor that supports both the competitiveness of the economy and equity, since for those sectors that lack access to modern means of payment, a transaction is usually insecure and expensive. In this area, digital payment services represent a central aspect so that the sending and receiving of payments can be carried out securely, immediately, at a low cost and with availability for the user at any time. A reflection of these premises can be seen today in the Interbank Electronic Payment System, SPEI, the most important infrastructure of the payment system in the Mexican financial system. Its recent evolution has shown massive adoption, allowing transfers from the internet or mobile application, collection requests via CoDi, and increasingly covering multiple payments for both public and private services. Interoperability is and will continue to be a guiding axis for the SPEI developments, that is why Banco de Mexico, in coordination with the ABM, its affiliated banks and other financial institutions, is developing a functionality so that SPEI participants can develop and offer their customers a transfer service knowing only the beneficiary's telephone number. without the need to provide further information. DiMo may be the name under which banks and financial institutions offer this service, thus having more options to promote and facilitate the use of electronic payments through mobile devices. I invite banks and financial institutions to carry out implementations and the registration of users of the service in order to extend the reach that these services will have. As financial activity evolves and the economic environment changes, there is an increasing need to identify challenges and opportunities and to creatively coordinate on new fronts. Hence the relevance of the thematic axis that was chosen for this convention, "Challenges and opportunities: inclusion, sustainability and nearshoring". I have already elaborated on the importance of financial inclusion. Sustainability, on the other hand, alludes to the urgent need to weigh aspects such as climate change and environmental preservation in economic and financial considerations. This is essential both to limit the high financial risks and social costs involved in climate phenomena, and to promote more sustainable and responsible development for future generations. Advancing in inclusion and sustainability will help us to take advantage of emerging phenomena such as nearshoring, which is the trend, strengthened after the pandemic, to reconfigure supply chains in spaces geographically close to destination markets. Indeed, the severe bottlenecks generated by the pandemic, exacerbated by the war between Russia and Ukraine, as well as other geopolitical tensions, have led to increased interest in supply chain resilience and fluidity and in reconfigurations for that purpose. In this regard, Mexico has an obvious comparative advantage, given its proximity to the largest economy in the world. In addition to its geographical location, it highlights the abundance of free trade agreements and trade agreements, which offer companies based in the country advantages to import inputs from abroad and access to a wide variety of markets. Additionally, Mexico has strong macroeconomic fundamentals compared to other economies, which also makes it attractive as an investment destination. Ladies and gentlemen: In the face of the unexpected events that have transformed the global economy and finance in recent years, cooperation between all economic actors and policymakers is essential. We must anticipate scenarios, identify common goals and take advantage of the opportunities that are looming for the benefit of the country. In particular, the central bank shares the aspiration of intermediaries and society to consolidate price stability and a sound and inclusive financial system. These conditions generate certainty, allow better decision-making for companies and individuals, stimulate talents and social energies, encourage productive investment and favor the creation of better-paid jobs. At the Bank of Mexico we will continue to promote, in accordance with our legal mandate, the stability of the purchasing power of our currency, as well as the healthy development of the financial and payment system. That is the best way to contribute to building, on firm foundations, the possibilities of a more solid, sustainable and equitable growth of the economy, as well as to seek greater well-being for Mexicans. Thanks a lot.

Daniel Becker Feldman, Presidente de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico; Distinguidos miembros del Presidium; Seoras y seores: 2 Salutacin Es un honor participar en esta Octogsima Sexta Convencin Bancaria, la cual, en esta ocasin, goza de la hospitalidad de la bella ciudad de Mrida. Aprovechar mi intervencin para, por un lado, resaltar la vigencia y relevancia de las finalidades del Banco de Mxico en las actuales circunstancias globales y, por el otro, transmitirles el diagnstico del 3 banco sobre la evolucin econmica reciente, as como abundar sobre el panorama inflacionario y nuestra postura de poltica monetaria. Igualmente, quiero mencionar algunos de los principales retos respecto a los sistemas financiero y de pagos. Las finalidades del Banco y la actual circunstancia El Banco de Mxico tiene como objetivo prioritario, establecido en la Constitucin de nuestro pas, procurar mantener el poder adquisitivo de la moneda nacional. Adems, la ley le encomienda promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero, as como propiciar el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. Estas tres finalidades se encuentran estrechamente relacionadas, y generan beneficios tangibles para toda la sociedad, particularmente para los ms desfavorecidos. La experiencia demuestra claramente que una inflacin persistente y por encima de los objetivos de los bancos centrales mina las bases del crecimiento econmico y deteriora la calidad de vida de la poblacin. Si bien la inflacin afecta a toda la sociedad, perjudica en mayor medida a los sectores de menores ingresos. Por eso, en las ltimas dcadas se alcanz el consenso de que la estabilidad de precios es un bien 4 colectivo inapreciable y un cimiento central de cualquier proceso viable de crecimiento sostenido y con equidad. A partir de este consenso, en muchos pases, incluido Mxico, se han logrado avances muy importantes en el combate a la inflacin. Por un lado, la pandemia, adems de las irreparables prdidas humanas que acarre, oblig a la paralizacin de muchas actividades econmicas, as como a otras acciones de aislamiento social, que afectaron profundamente la economa y la vida cotidiana de las personas en todo el mundo. Todo ello, ha dislocado tanto la oferta como la demanda y ha extendido globalmente las presiones inflacionarias. Luego de un periodo de recuperacin econmica heterognea tras la pandemia, ante niveles de inflacin inditos en dcadas, los bancos centrales, tanto de economas avanzadas como emergentes, han ajustado al alza sus tasas de referencia y algunos han anunciado que permanecern elevadas por un periodo prolongado. En este contexto de condiciones monetarias y financieras apretadas, aunado a las repercusiones de la guerra en Ucrania, el crecimiento econmico mundial se moder durante el cuarto trimestre de 2022 y las previsiones para 2023 por parte de los principales organismos multilaterales apuntan a una desaceleracin del mismo. La inflacin global permanece elevada y, si bien la general disminuy en varias economas, en diversos pases la inflacin subyacente, que muestra mejor la tendencia 6 inflacionaria, todava no manifiesta de manera clara un punto de inflexin a la baja. En lo que atae a nuestro pas, en el cuarto trimestre de 2022, la economa mexicana continu creciendo, aunque con menor dinamismo que en los trimestres previos. Por el lado de los precios, en febrero, la inflacin general anual se ubic en 7.62%; mientras que la subyacente se situ en 8.29%. Este ltimo componente todava no muestra una dinmica favorable, pues la variacin anual de los precios de las mercancas ha mostrado un descenso ms lento al previsto y la de los servicios ha continuado aumentando. Ante esta circunstancia, en la decisin de poltica monetaria del 9 de febrero, los pronsticos para las inflaciones general y subyacente se ajustaron para todo el horizonte y se anticipa que la inflacin converja a la meta en el cuarto trimestre de 2024. En dicha decisin, la Junta de Gobierno evalu la magnitud y diversidad de los choques inflacionarios y sus determinantes, as como la evolucin 7 de las expectativas de mediano y largo plazos y el proceso de formacin de precios. A partir de estos elementos, determin que, ante la dinmica de la inflacin subyacente, era necesario repetir la magnitud del incremento en la tasa de referencia de la reunin anterior y decidi, por unanimidad, aumentar en 50 puntos base el objetivo para la Tasa de Inters Interbancaria a un da hasta un nivel de 11%. Como se expres en el comunicado, la Junta de Gobierno vigilar estrechamente los diversos factores que inciden en la trayectoria prevista para la inflacin y en sus expectativas. El propsito es determinar una tasa de referencia congruente en todo momento, tanto con la convergencia ordenada y sostenida de la inflacin general a la meta de 3% en el plazo en el que opera la poltica monetaria, como con un ajuste adecuado de la economa y de los mercados financieros. Para la prxima reunin la Junta de Gobierno considerar la postura monetaria que ya se ha alcanzado, as como la evolucin de los datos. Las acciones de poltica monetaria que se han implementado desde el inicio del actual ciclo alcista en junio de 2021, han contribuido a que, a 8 pesar de la severidad de los choques, las expectativas de inflacin de mayor plazo se hayan mantenido estables. As, en el Banco de Mxico actuamos con oportunidad y en apego a nuestro mandato legal: el objetivo indeclinable consiste en consolidar la estabilidad de precios. Promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos Otra funcin que la ley mandata al Banco de Mxico es promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero y el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. Como ustedes saben, la estabilidad financiera es parte fundamental de este mandato. Por ello, tanto el Banco de Mxico como las otras autoridades aqu representadas velan por mantenerla. El sistema bancario mexicano se encuentra bien capitalizado y con niveles adecuados de liquidez, en ambos casos con holgura sobre los mnimos regulatorios. Las pruebas de estrs que publicamos en el Reporte de Estabilidad as lo confirman ya que, aun ante escenarios adversos 9 severos pero plausibles, los bancos se mantienen solventes y con suficiente liquidez. Por lo tanto, en ausencia de choques adicionales, no esperamos que los acontecimientos recientes en el sistema bancario de los Estados Unidos o en los mercados internacionales tengan efectos negativos relevantes sobre la banca mexicana. Lo que ocurri a algunos bancos de dicho pas se puede caracterizar como un episodio tpico de corridas bancadas, que pudieron haber tenido su origen en tres factores. Primero, un manejo inadecuado del riesgo de tasa de inters. Segundo, una concentracin excesiva de exposiciones en un sector de la economa, especialmente para uno de los bancos. Finalmente, que la proporcin de depositantes de estos bancos con saldos por encima de la cobertura del seguro de depsito era muy elevada. La combinacin de estos factores min la confianza de los depositantes, que acudieron a retirar sus recursos por miedo a enfrentar prdidas. En cuanto a los eventos en los mercados internacionales, principalmente europeos, responden a que en un ambiente de elevada incertidumbre se dieron noticias negativas sobre un banco de importancia sistmica global, lo que gener incrementos importantes en la volatilidad de varios activos y un aumento en la aversin al riesgo de 10 los inversionistas. Las autoridades financieras encargadas de dicho banco anunciaron que como cumple con los requerimientos de capital y liquidez exigibles a este tipo de instituciones, de ser necesario, darn liquidez a la entidad, y el banco ha sealado que usar dicha facilidad. Estos episodios nos recuerdan que la confianza de los depositantes es fundamental para que los bancos puedan realizar sus labores primordiales de transformacin de plazos y de riesgos, por lo que es fundamental reforzarla constantemente. Para ello, es importante un manejo prudente de riesgos sin menospreciar el riesgo de concentracin, fomentar un ambiente de sana competencia, mantener altos estndares de servicio a los clientes y un cumplimiento escrupuloso, completo y puntual del marco regulatorio y de sus modificaciones. Tambin que las autoridades debemos permanecer alerta y actuar utilizando selectivamente las herramientas que pudieran ser necesarias, segn el caso. Un sistema financiero estable, saludable e inclusivo permite encauzar el ahorro del pblico hacia los objetivos ms deseables para la sociedad. El hecho de que la mayora de la poblacin disponga de 11 acceso a servicios financieros en las mejores condiciones de calidad y costo tiene numerosos efectos positivos, tales como nivelar oportunidades entre los distintos sectores sociales, abatir rezagos e impulsar la paridad de gnero. Adems, la mayor inclusin financiera hace ms efectiva la transmisin de la poltica monetaria. En este sentido quisiera reiterar que el Banco de Mxico estar atento en todo momento al desarrollo de los mercados financieros globales y locales con el fin de dar cumplimiento a su mandato de promover el sano desarrollo del sistema financiero en beneficio de la poblacin. El Banco de Mxico participa en los principales foros de coordinacin global para promover la salud y la estabilidad financiera y, en el plano nacional, es parte del Consejo de Estabilidad del Sistema Financiero, en el que las autoridades mexicanas en la materia interactan para vigilar eventuales vulnerabilidades y responder a cualquier contingencia. Las instituciones de crdito operan con elevados niveles de capital y liquidez, que les permite hacer frente a escenarios adversos, como coment hace unos momentos. En resumen, el sistema bancario se encuentra en una situacin propicia para impulsar la reactivacin econmica. Esto se est manifestando en una recuperacin del crdito, 12 incluso en las complejas circunstancias actuales, lo que denota confianza hacia delante. Para que la banca potencie su aportacin al desarrollo es necesario un proceso de mejora continua que comprende, por un lado, una oferta ms amplia de productos y servicios financieros en las condiciones ms adecuadas de precio y calidad para los hogares y negocios y, por otro lado, que los consumidores tengan herramientas para hacer una eleccin ptima de productos, as como una planeacin ms apropiada de todas sus operaciones financieras. El Banco de Mxico ha colocado al usuario de los servicios financieros en el centro de sus acciones y ha desplegado un amplio nmero de instrumentos que descansan en los avances tecnolgicos. Estos instrumentos buscan generar incentivos para que los intermediarios compitan con mejores productos y servicios y, tambin, formar usuarios participativos, bien informados y conscientes de sus derechos. Entre los instrumentos que recientemente ha desarrollado el Banco destacan: 13 i) Un catlogo de categoras que establece que las comisiones asociadas a un servicio tengan el mismo nombre, sin importar el producto financiero al cual estn asociados o la entidad financiera que los ofrezca. Esto facilita la comparacin de los montos de las comisiones entre instituciones y productos y promueve la mayor transparencia y competencia. ii) El Banco de Mxico ofrece desde hace algunos aos un comparador genrico del costo de crditos, que contiene informacin completa, confiable y oportuna, provista por los intermediarios. De 2019 a la fecha, ms de medio milln de personas han consultado esta herramienta, lo que favorece una buena decisin de los clientes y, a la vez, incentiva a las instituciones a ofrecer mejores productos. iii) Complementando el comparador genrico, el Banco de Mxico est habilitando una plataforma, innovadora y nica a nivel internacional, para que las personas que buscan un crdito puedan, a travs de una aplicacin en sus telfonos inteligentes, enviar una solicitud a varios proveedores y recibir ofertas personalizadas, de acuerdo con su necesidad y perfil de riesgo. La plataforma aprovecha las tecnologas digitales 14 para reducir los costos de bsqueda y adquisicin en que incurren usuarios y proveedores. Esto beneficia a todos pues genera mayor eficiencia en el proceso, empodera a los consumidores y aumenta los clientes potenciales de las instituciones. El xito de este instrumento depende de la participacin activa de los intermediarios, por lo que hago un llamado a todas las instituciones bancarias para que se incorporen a dicha plataforma. iv) Igualmente, el Banco de Mxico ha creado una herramienta que permite a los usuarios comparar los costos y las caractersticas de los distintos productos de depsito. Este desarrollo ha sido un reto, dado que los costos en que incurre un usuario de un producto de depsito dependen de su perfil de uso. De esta forma, la herramienta recaba informacin del usuario para determinar el tipo de productos idneos para dicho perfil. En lo que atae al sistema de pagos, propiciar el buen funcionamiento de este es una finalidad del Banco de Mxico. El que todos los mexicanos puedan realizar sus transacciones de manera segura, eficiente y expedita es un factor que apoya tanto la competitividad de la 15 economa como la equidad, pues para aquellos sectores que carecen de acceso a medios de pago modernos, una transaccin suele ser insegura y costosa. En este mbito, los servicios de pago digitales representan un aspecto central para que el envo y la recepcin de pagos pueda realizarse de manera segura, inmediata, a bajo costo y con disponibilidad para el usuario en cualquier momento. Un reflejo de estas premisas se observa hoy en el Sistema de Pagos Electrnicos Interbancarios, SPEI, la infraestructura ms importante del sistema de pagos en el sistema financiero mexicano. Su evolucin reciente ha mostrado una adopcin masiva, permitiendo realizar transferencias desde internet o aplicacin mvil, solicitudes de cobro va CoDi, y abarcando mltiples pagos de servicios tanto pblicos como privados de manera creciente. La interoperabilidad es y seguir siendo un eje rector para los desarrollos del SPEI, es por eso que el Banco de Mxico, en coordinacin con la ABM, sus bancos agremiados y otras entidades financieras, se encuentra desarrollando una funcionalidad para que los participantes del SPEI puedan desarrollar y ofrecer a sus clientes un 16 servicio de envo de transferencias conociendo solo el nmero de telfono del beneficiario, sin que sea necesario proporcionar mayor informacin. DiMo podr ser el nombre con el que bancos e instituciones financieras ofrezcan este servicio, teniendo con ello ms opciones para fomentar y facilitar el uso de pagos electrnicos a travs de dispositivos mviles. Invito a los bancos e instituciones financieras, a que lleven a cabo implementaciones y el registro de usuarios al servicio a fin de extender el alcance que tendrn estos servicios. A medida que la actividad financiera evoluciona y el entorno econmico cambia, se incrementa la necesidad de identificar desafos y oportunidades y de coordinarse creativamente en nuevos frentes. De ah la relevancia del eje temtico que se eligi para esta convencin, Retos y oportunidades: inclusin, sostenibilidad y nearshoring. Ya he abundado sobre la importancia de la inclusin financiera. La sostenibilidad, por su parte, alude a la necesidad impostergable de ponderar aspectos como el cambio climtico y la preservacin del medio 17 ambiente en las consideraciones econmicas y financieras. Ello es imprescindible tanto para limitar los altos riesgos financieros y costos sociales que implican los fenmenos climticos, como para promover un desarrollo ms sostenible y responsable con las generaciones futuras. Avanzar en inclusin y sostenibilidad nos ayudar a aprovechar fenmenos emergentes como el de la relocalizacin o nearshoring, que es la tendencia, fortalecida tras la pandemia, a reconfigurar las cadenas de suministro en los espacios cercanos geogrficamente a los mercados de destino. Title:
"Appearance before the Senate of the Republic"", Victoria Rodrguez, Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

Full text
text: Appearance before the Senate of the Republic of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico. Mexico City, April 25, 2023 Senator Ernesto Perez Astorga, President of the Finance and Public Credit Committee; Senator Nuvia Mayorga Delgado, Secretary of the Commission; Senator Victor Fuentes Solis, Secretary of the Commission; Distinguished members of the Finance and Public Credit Commission of the Senate of the Republic. Introduction I am pleased to appear before this Committee on Finance and Public Credit of the Senate of the Republic, for the purpose of presenting the Report on the fulfillment of the mandates of our central institute, provided for in Article 47, section XIII, of the Law of the Bank of Mexico. For the Bank of Mexico, timely accountability, transparency in the exercise of its functions, as well as the adequate communication of its objectives are essential tools, as they contribute to entrenching trust and consolidating its credibility in society. For this reason, I highly value the opportunity to appear again before this Sovereignty to address the new events that have impacted the global environment and the national economy. Below, I will describe in detail the actions that the Bank has undertaken to achieve its priority objective of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency, as well as the purposes of promoting the healthy development of the financial system, promoting the proper functioning of payment systems and providing the country's economy with national currency. During 2022 and so far in 2023, the national economy has continued to face a complex and uncertain global environment. In particular, for the Bank of Mexico's area of competence, this environment has been characterized mainly by inflationary pressures not seen in decades, whose persistent and widespread nature has affected the prices of a large number of goods and services in the household consumption basket in a set of economies, including Mexico's. Likewise, during this period, there have been events that have tested the Mexican financial system, its resilience and its contribution to stability and economic growth. I am going to refer, first of all, to the issue of price stability, which is the priority mandate of this central institute. Secondly, I will talk about the other purposes of the Bank of Mexico, such as the healthy development of the financial system, the proper functioning of payment systems and providing the country's economy with national currency. SECTION I. INFLATION Priority objective of the Bank of Mexico The priority objective that the Constitution entrusts to the Bank of Mexico is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the Mexican currency. The logic of this mandate is clear, since both economic theory and the historical experience of many countries corroborate that inflation is one of the phenomena that most harm economic growth and generate social inequality. Indeed, the constant and disorderly increase in prices hinders the planning of consumption and productive activities, inhibits investment and savings and decreases the quality of life of the entire population, disproportionately affecting the poorest sectors. For this reason, a consensus has been reached that price stability is a fundamental foundation for any process of sustainable and equitable economic growth. For all of the above, during this period of unprecedented inflationary pressures, at the Bank of Mexico we have used all the tools at our disposal to preserve the achievement of our priority mandate. International economic environment After a long period in which significant progress had been made in price stability in a number of countries, unusual inflationary pressures have arisen in recent years. It should be noted that the origin of the current inflationary pressures lies in events that could hardly have been predicted, such as the COVID-19 pandemic or the war in Ukraine. The pandemic, a health event unrelated to the economic cycle, implied a global challenge that generated a large number of unfortunate human losses, dislocated production processes and supply chains and disrupted the daily lives of millions of people around the world. For its part, the war in Eastern Europe, in addition to its human cost and its challenges to world peace, has had very significant repercussions on the prices of essential inputs in the international economy, such as food and energy, which, in turn, have had a strong impact on global inflation. In particular, after the most severe period of isolation during the pandemic, the reopening of activities in various economies, the shift in consumption patterns towards goods, and stimulus measures, mainly in advanced economies, led to an expansion of aggregate demand at the global level. This led to the fact that in several markets the supply had difficulty adjusting at the same pace as the demand, which exerted upward pressure on prices in a multiplicity of goods and services. The conflagration in Eastern Europe exacerbated these inflationary pressures, due to the uncertainty caused and additional disruptions in supply chains. In this context, the global economy in 2022 moderated its growth towards the fourth quarter and the forecasts for 2023 by the main multilateral organizations point to a slowdown. The current economic environment and, in particular, inflationary pressures have posed a significant monetary policy challenge. Central banks, both emerging and advanced, have had to respond decisively by increasing their benchmark rates to deal with deep inflationary pressures. In early 2022, monetary authorities in most advanced economies began cycles of hikes in their benchmark interest rates. In several cases, this process occurred at a faster pace than anticipated. For their part, the central banks of the main emerging economies, which had already started their upward cycle in 2021, continued to increase their reference rates in 2022. In the second half of 2022, some signs of mitigation of the factors that had been pressuring inflation at the global level began to be observed. Among them, an improvement in the operation of supply chains, in addition to a stabilization and reduction in the international prices of raw materials. This situation allowed headline inflation to begin to decline in various economies, both advanced and emerging, although the core component has had a heterogeneous behavior between countries and, in several cases, it still continues to increase. In this context, most central banks have moderated the pace of hikes, with some signaling that rates will remain elevated for a long time. Evolution of the economy and inflation in Mexico Domestically, during 2022 the Mexican economy presented a growth of 3.1 percent at an annual rate. It highlights that, in the third quarter of last year, national economic activity reached the levels observed prior to the pandemic. In addition, in the last quarter of the previous year and in the first months of 2023, the national economy continued to grow. In addition to the above, during 2022 various labor market indicators reached the levels recorded before the pandemic. Currently, the Bank of Mexico anticipates that GDP growth for 2023 will be between 0.8 and 2.4 percent, with a central estimate of 1.6 percent, while for 2024 the economy is expected to grow between 0.8 and 2.8 percent, with a point forecast of 1.8 percent. Regarding the inflationary outlook, headline inflation at an annual rate showed significant increases during 2022. In particular, it went from a level, already high, of 7.36 percent in December 2021 to one of 8.70 percent in August 2022, to later decrease, closing 2022 at 7.82 percent, while in the first half of April of the current year it stood at 6.24 percent. The moderation in headline inflation has been largely due to the decline in the non-core component, which has been helped by lower pressures on agricultural commodity prices and the reduction in annual changes in the prices of some energy products since the second half of last year. Throughout 2022, the core component, which excludes volatile components such as some agricultural and energy prices, faced pressures, mainly associated with increases in production costs, derived from disruptions in supply chains, as well as higher prices recorded by various inputs. In particular, core inflation was affected by the increase in international commodity prices that affected consumer food prices. This indicator interrupted a 24-month period of consecutive increases in December last year. Thus, core inflation rose from 5.94 percent in December 2021 to 8.51 percent in November 2022, decreasing slightly to 8.35 percent in December. In its most recent reading corresponding to the first half of April 2023, this indicator stands at 7.75 percent. The persistence of this component at high levels is one of the most important obstacles for inflation to consolidate a sustained reduction towards our target of 3 percent over the forecast horizon, so we remain vigilant of its dynamics. Within core inflation, merchandise inflation went from 7.40 percent in December 2021 to 11.28 percent in November 2022, particularly highlighting the pressures that have been observed in the food component. Subsequently, reflecting the mitigation of some of the shocks, merchandise inflation has fallen to 9.73 percent in the first half of April 2023. In contrast, annual services inflation has continued to show an upward trend. It went from 4.30 percent in December 2021 to 5.42 percent in the first half of April 2023. Services have also suffered from higher production costs, while their demand has increased as the pandemic has been tightly controlled. Monetary policy stances Given the complex and uncertain inflationary outlook, in the decisions corresponding to the meetings of February, March and May 2022, the Governing Board decided to adjust the monetary policy rate upwards by 50 basis points to bring it to a level of 7.00 percent. However, in the face of a deterioration in the inflationary outlook and to avoid further damage, increases of a greater magnitude were necessary. Thus, in the decisions of June, August, September and November 2022, the Board of Governors of the Bank of Mexico decided to increase the reference rate by 75 basis points at each meeting. Subsequently, at the December 2022 and February 2023 meetings, the Bank of Mexico increased the benchmark rate by 50 basis points on each occasion. In December 2022, while headline inflation had declined, core inflation had continued to rise, albeit at a slower pace than in previous months. Thus, the Governing Board decided to reduce the pace of increases from 75 to 50 basis points at that meeting. Subsequently, at the February meeting, the outlook was more complex than anticipated, given the persistent dynamics of core inflation. The Governing Board estimated that inflation would decrease more slowly than previously anticipated and that the balance of risks continued to be skewed upwards, so it decided to repeat the magnitude of the increase in the reference rate of 50 basis points of the previous meeting. With this decision, the monetary stance was further strengthened. Thus, in the March 30 decision, the Bank of Mexico found itself in a stronger position to face the challenges of the inflationary environment. Moreover, at this last meeting, the expected trajectories for headline and core inflation were adjusted only marginally with respect to those corresponding to the previous decision. Although there had been an episode of international financial turbulence associated with events in the banking systems of the United States and Europe, this did not affect the inflationary dynamics in Mexico. Thus, considering the evolution of the inflationary outlook in the country and the monetary stance already reached, the Governing Board unanimously decided to increase the reference rate by 25 basis points to a level of 11.25 percent. In order to make its decisions, the Bank of Mexico carries out a very broad and exhaustive analysis of the various economic variables, as well as the nature of inflationary pressures and their influence on price formation. Thus, the decisions adopted support and reinforce the commitment of the Bank of Mexico and its Governing Board to its constitutional mandate. These actions have contributed to the fact that, despite the unprecedented nature and severity of the inflationary shocks that our country has faced, longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable. If it were not for these actions, it is likely that these expectations, a fundamental reference in the price formation process of the entire economy, would have registered significant increases. Such a situation would have led to even higher and more persistent inflation, with a corresponding deterioration in the purchasing power of the national currency and in the well-being of society, especially the most vulnerable sectors. Similarly, the aforementioned actions have contributed to the orderly behavior of the national financial markets, including the foreign exchange market. It is important to note that, in the face of the tightening of monetary conditions at the global level, the dollar has registered a generalized appreciation. This pressure on the currencies of emerging economies makes it even more difficult to control inflation. In the case of the Mexican peso, despite some episodes of volatility, it has exhibited remarkable resilience. The behavior of our currency has been due to the country's solid macroeconomic fundamentals. However, in this regard, I would like to emphasize that the monetary policy of the Bank of Mexico obeys our priority objective of price stability. Consequently, there is no exchange rate target, nor an interest rate differential with respect to that of any other economy. The importance of any variable in our decision-making lies in the degree to which that variable affects the inflationary process. SECTION II FINANCIAL AND PAYMENT SYSTEMS The Bank of Mexico also has the purpose of promoting the healthy development of the financial system and promoting the proper functioning of the payment system, as well as the task of providing the economy with working capital in the necessary quantities. The Law for the Transparency and Regulation of Financial Services or LTOSF, and other regulations issued by the Legislature, have provided tools to this Central Institute to fulfill these purposes. The stability of the financial system For a financial system to be healthy, it must be stable, competitive, efficient, and accessible. When it does not meet any of these conditions, it limits the welfare of users and inhibits the potential contribution of the financial system to economic growth, as well as complicates the transmission of monetary policy. In terms of its stability, the Mexican financial system has shown its resilience in the face of the challenges it faced, first due to the health contingency and, more recently, due to the risk aversion generated by the problems of some banking institutions in the United States and Europe, which, although it has spread to other international financial markets, Its effects have diminished significantly. The Bank of Mexico permanently monitors the stability of the financial system and participates in the main international forums to promote global financial health and stability, while, at the national level, it participates in the Financial System Stability Council, in which the Mexican authorities in this area interact and coordinate to monitor possible vulnerabilities. In addition, the Bank carries out permanent evaluation work on the resilience of the financial system as a whole. In this regard, allow me to reiterate that, according to the monitoring of the financial health of institutions, the Mexican financial system is well capitalized and with ample liquidity reserves, and that, in the absence of additional unfavorable events, no direct effects on the Mexican banking system are expected to jeopardize its solvency. Let me comment on the recent failure of some international banks, as well as the reasons to hope that this situation will not affect banks established in Mexico:  The specifics of Silicon Valley Bank and its own risk management, which underestimated interest rate risk, concentrated its exposures in a group of depositors from the same sector of the economy with a significant stake, many of whom had balances that were well known. on top of the insurance coverage, factors that exposed it to a bank run. The nervousness spread to other North American institutions with similar characteristics, although, so far, these are specific cases associated with the similarity between these banks either by sector to which they serve or by the characteristics of their depositors.  In the case of Credit Suisse, although doubts about its viability can be inscribed in the environment of marked uncertainty, the bank had been reducing its balance sheet for several years after having suffered significant losses in the derivatives markets and with management questioned by the markets. Additionally, one of its main shareholders indicated that he would not invest more in the institution due to several factors on which he would not comment. In both cases, the corresponding financial authorities have acted in a timely manner to prevent contagion.  With respect to these cases, Mexican banks do not present credit exposures or through securities with the affected entities in the US and Europe, which imply losses for their balance sheets. On the other hand, the exposure to interest rate risk of banks and brokerage firms has decreased and is relatively low.  All Mexican banking institutions comfortably meet international standards in terms of regulatory liquidity requirements, unlike the institutions intervened in the United States, whose sector is not subject to these standards. This is a key difference between Mexican and United States banks. Banks in the United States that have assets of less than 250 billion are not subject to the liquidity standards set by the Basel III agreement. In particular, they do not calculate the Liquidity Coverage Ratio and the Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR); nor are they obliged to make a timely calculation of interest rate risk in their bank book, which leads to the securities that in their assets, do not reflect variations in their market value. Finally, they are not considered for the stress tests that the Federal Reserve conducts annually. In contrast, all banks in Mexico must meet the regulatory liquidity requirements and are subject to stress tests by the National Banking and Securities Commission and the analysis of the Bank of Mexico itself, in harmony with the standards established in the Basel III agreement. In fact, the stress tests we published in the most recent Stability Report show that, even in the face of severe adverse scenarios, the Mexican banking system would continue to meet the capital and liquidity requirements required by the current regulatory standards.  As our banks also have comfortable levels of capital, there do not seem to be any fundamental reasons that could stress the liquidity situation of the banking system.  The market prices of the shares of Mexican banks or their financial groups have reflected a limited impact compared to those of other countries, which seems to indicate that the market recognizes a low interconnection with the affected institutions. The solid macro-financial framework that exists in Mexico, based on fiscal discipline, balance in the external accounts, a flexible exchange rate and a robust financial system, are essential to cushion this type of shock. However, the nervousness in the international financial markets could continue and the financial authorities are aware of the importance of being prepared for additional events that may arise and of acting with opportunity and determination to mitigate the impact of such contingencies. On the other hand, although changes in financial conditions could temporarily affect the process of granting credit by Mexican banks, their liquidity and solvency conditions place them in a good position to continue promoting economic recovery, which is already beginning to be observed in various indicators. Among them, the total bank credit portfolio as of December 2022 grew 4.2 percent in real terms compared to the same period of the previous year, reaching a level close to that observed before the pandemic. The greatest growth is manifested in the credit card segment, but it is also seen in other types of credit such as business credit. It is also observed that, despite the increase in reference interest rates, the interest rates on loans faced by consumers, on average, have increased at a slower pace. Greater efficiency, competition and consumer protection in the financial system In terms of competitiveness and efficiency, financial systems often face market failures that impose barriers to achieving competitive and efficient behavior. The Bank of Mexico, making use of the powers conferred on it by law, has adopted measures to seek to eradicate these barriers and achieve a competitive and innovative financial system that better meets the needs of users. I would like to highlight the progress of these measures:  The LTOSF indicates that, in order to make the system more efficient and reduce costs, financial institutions may exempt or reduce the collection of commissions from customers of other entities for the use of their infrastructure, subject to the execution of an agreement authorized by the Bank of Mexico. During 2022, Banco de Mexico authorized a new agreement to share ATM networks and two existing agreements were updated. These agreements allow customers of the financial institutions that subscribe to them not only to access a wider network of ATMs than that provided by their own institution, but also to pay no fees for the use of ATMs of another financial institution participating in the agreement, or for them to be lower. By the end of 2022, 24 agreements had been authorized to share ATM infrastructure, which has benefited millions of customers.  With regard to the payroll account service, the employer usually selects the bank where its workers' accounts are opened. However, since 2015 the LTOSF has given workers the freedom to choose the bank where they want to have their payroll account, which must be transferred to that institution at no cost. To comply with this rule, the Bank of Mexico implemented the mechanics for "payroll portability". In the previous appearance I informed you that 4 million operations had been authorized, to this date, 5.7 million successful payroll portability requests have been accumulated, which favors competition and empowers workers.  The SPEI is the most important payment system in Mexico. In recent years, there has been a steady and growing adoption of SPEI by the population. Thus, in the fourth quarter of the 2022, 55.9 million individuals used it, which is equivalent to 60 percent of the adult population. It highlights that the total amount of transactions made by end users was 184.5 trillion pesos during 2022, which is equivalent to approximately 6.58 times GDP. In 2022, the SPEI continued with the growth that has been characterizing it in recent years. During the past year, there was a growth of 40 percent in the number of operations carried out in the system and 13 percent in real terms in the amount traded in the system.  In order to maintain its service and operating standards in the face of the sustained growth in the number of transfers processed and to preserve its operational continuity, SPEI's transfer processing capacity was expanded as of May 2022. It is important to note that the availability index observed for this service was more than 99.98 percent.  Also within the scope of their competence, Banco de Mexico and other financial authorities have collaborated in the process of authorizing Financial Technology Institutions or FTIs. ITFs represent an opportunity for the growth and development of financial services and expand the range of products and services available to users. To date, 26 collective funding institutions and 45 electronic payment fund institutions have been authorized. On the other hand, in relation to transparency and consumer protection, the Bank of Mexico considers it essential to provide users with the necessary information to make better decisions. By training participatory, well-informed and rights-aware consumers, it is possible to increase competition and generate better services and products. To that end, Banco de Mexico has developed a suite of information services and, in some cases, has been directly involved in the provision of payment services that benefit users. Next, I am going to talk to you about some of these projects.  The LTOSF mandates the Bank of Mexico to manage a registry of commissions in which institutions must report the increases they intend to carry out in credit and payment services. As part of the administration of this registry, the Bank of Mexico established a catalog of fee categories whose purpose is to introduce greater transparency, simplify the information provided to users, and promote competition. This catalog establishes that the commissions associated with the same service or event must have the same name, regardless of the financial product with which they are associated or the financial institution that offers them. The new catalog will make it easier, on the one hand, for users to compare the amounts of commissions charged on products provided by different financial service providers and, on the other hand, for better cost comparison tools to be developed for the benefit of users.  The Bank of Mexico has been offering a generic comparator of the cost of credit products for some years now. This tool, on the one hand, contains complete, reliable and timely information; on the other, it has a design that makes it easier for the customer to choose the credit product they are looking for, as it eliminates biases in the presentation. Consultations can be made using both a computer and a mobile phone. To date, the accumulated queries to the comparator's platform amount to more than half a million since it began operating in January 2019. Each of these visits translates into an informed decision by a user.  Complementing the generic credit product comparator and making use of the best available technology, Banco de Mexico is enabling a platform so that people looking for a loan can, through an application on their smartphones, send a request to several providers and receive personalized offers according to their need and risk profile. The platform leverages digital technologies to reduce the search and acquisition costs that users and suppliers often incur, generating efficiency and giving greater power of choice to customers.  Continuing in the field of transparency, Banco de Mexico has the power to design methodologies so that users can compare the cost of credits, through a single indicator that summarizes all the costs that the potential customer has to incur. This is the so-called Total Annual Cost (CAT) that It includes not only the interest rate of the loan, but also the commissions and costs for insurance, among other factors. A similar indicator has also been designed for savings or investment products, with the so-called Total Annual Profit (GAT). However, there is no similar indicator for transactional deposit products, known as demand deposits because the resources are always available to be withdrawn. This makes it difficult for users to choose these products. To mitigate this problem, Banco de Mexico has developed a tool that allows users to compare the costs and features of transactional deposit products. The development has been challenging, given that the costs incurred by users of deposit products depend on their usage profile and the ways of charging for these products are varied. For this reason, the tool collects information on the way in which customers plan to use the services in order to, through some search filters, determine the products that best suit those usage profiles. The tool is now available to use.  In February 2023, Banco de Mexico made available to SPEI participants the infrastructure that will support the services of DiMo, a payment instruction service that aims to allow transfers to be sent, using only the beneficiary's cell phone number. The storage of the information will be carried out securely and with the express consent of the customer. We hope that in the coming months the banks and other SPEI participants will complete their developments to bring this new service to their customers. Money Issuance In parallel to the promotion of electronic payments, one of the constitutional obligations of the Bank of Mexico is the issuance of banknotes and coins. The Bank of Mexico issues high-quality paper money in the quantities necessary to meet the needs of the national economy. Banknotes issued by the Bank of Mexico have high security standards, are durable and functional and reproduce symbols, landscapes and characters that identify and unify us as Mexicans. At the end of 2022, there were 8,304 million banknotes in circulation, for an amount of 2,624 billion pesos, which represents an increase of 9.8 percent in number of pieces and 9.4 percent in amount, compared to the previous year. As for coins, at the end of 2022, there were 44,730 million pieces in circulation, which is equivalent to an amount of 76 billion pesos; This represents an increase of 5.2 percent in the number of pieces and 9.9 percent in the amount compared to the previous year. It should be noted that in October 2021, the last of the six banknotes that make up the new family of G banknotes was put into circulation, which corresponded to the denomination of 50 pesos. In April 2022, this banknote was recognized as the "Banknote of the Year 2021" by the International Banknote Society due to its harmonious design and printing process. In this way, the Bank of Mexico not only issues money with the strictest criteria of security, quality and durability, but also produces some of the most beautiful banknotes in the world. Ladies and Gentlemen Senators, In addition to a monetary policy focused on price stability, the Mexican economy has solid macroeconomic fundamentals that distinguish it from other economies of comparable development. These include: (i) a well-capitalized banking system and adequate levels of liquidity, (ii) sustainable external accounts, (iii) fiscal discipline, (iv) a flexible exchange rate regime that allows the economy to adjust to shocks, and (v) adequate levels of international reserves. These elements place the national economy in a resilient position in the face of the complex and uncertain economic environment through which all economies are passing. Currently, Mexico is in a better position than in the past to face an external situation characterized by astringent financial conditions, derived from the cycle of monetary tightening at the global level and by challenges to the stability of the international financial system. In this context, the fulfillment of the institutional objectives of the Bank of Mexico contributes significantly to the strength and certainty of our country. Therefore, the Bank of Mexico confirms its commitment to its priority objective of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the national currency and, in a complex scenario, will remain firm in its efforts to consolidate an environment of low and stable inflation. This should have an impact on a more conducive environment for making long-term decisions in terms of investment and production, as well as on the preservation of the purchasing power and assets of the entire population. Similarly, the Bank of Mexico will continue to promote a stable, healthy, and competitive financial system, as well as a more efficient payment system. This should be reflected in better financial services and better support for the initiative and talent of Mexicans, as well as in greater efficiency in carrying out all their economic transactions. In this way, the legal mandates of the Bank of Mexico translate into benefits and greater opportunities for the population. Finally, I thank you once again for the opportunity to submit to this Sovereignty our periodic report of actions. I place myself at your service to elaborate on any aspect of this exhibition. SECCIN I. El Banco de Mxico, ofrece, desde hace algunos aos, un comparador genrico del costo de productos de crdito. Esta herramienta, por un lado, contiene informacin completa, confiable y oportuna; por el otro, tiene un diseo que facilita al 26 cliente la eleccin del producto de crdito buscado, pues elimina sesgos en la presentacin. Las consultas pueden hacerse tanto usando una computadora como un telfono mvil. A la fecha, las consultas acumuladas a la plataforma del comparador ascienden a ms de medio milln desde que comenz a operar en enero de 2019. Cada una de estas visitas se traduce en una decisin informada de un usuario.  Complementando al comparador genrico de productos de crdito y haciendo uso de la mejor tecnologa disponible, el Banco de Mxico est habilitando una plataforma para que las personas en bsqueda de un crdito puedan, mediante una aplicacin en sus telfonos inteligentes, enviar una solicitud a varios proveedores y recibir ofertas personalizadas de acuerdo con su necesidad y perfil de riesgo. La plataforma aprovecha las tecnologas digitales para reducir los costos de bsqueda y adquisicin en los que suelen incurrir usuarios y proveedores, generando eficiencia y dando mayor poder de eleccin a los clientes.  Siguiendo en el mbito de la transparencia, Banco de Mxico tiene facultades para disear metodologas para que los usuarios puedan comparar el costo de los crditos, a travs de un indicador 27 nico que resume todos los costos en los que el cliente potencial tiene que incurrir. Este es el llamado Costo Anual Total (CAT) que incluye no solo la tasa de inters del crdito, sino las comisiones y costos por seguros, entre otros factores. Un indicador similar se ha diseado tambin para productos de ahorro o inversin, con la llamada Ganancia Anual Total (GAT). Sin embargo, no existe un indicador similar para los productos de depsito transaccionales, los conocidos como depsitos a la vista porque los recursos estn siempre disponibles para ser retirados. Esta dificulta la eleccin de estos productos por parte de los usuarios. Para mitigar este problema, el Banco de Mxico ha desarrollado una herramienta que permite a los usuarios comparar los costos y las caractersticas de los productos de depsito transaccionales. El desarrollo ha sido un reto, dado que los costos en que incurren los usuarios de los productos de depsito dependen de su perfil de uso y las formas de cobro por estos productos son variadas. Por esta razn, la herramienta recaba informacin de la forma en que los clientes planean usar los servicios para, a travs de algunos filtros de bsqueda, determinar los productos que mejor se 28 adecan a esos perfiles de uso. La herramienta ya est disponible para ser utilizada.  En febrero de 2023, el Banco de Mxico puso a disposicin de los participantes del SPEI la infraestructura que soportar los servicios de DiMo, un servicio de instruccin de pagos que tiene por objetivo permitir el envo de transferencias, utilizando nicamente el nmero de celular del beneficiario. El almacenamiento de la informacin se realizar de manera segura y con consentimiento expreso del cliente. Esperamos que en los prximos meses los bancos y dems participantes del SPEI culminen sus desarrollos para llevar este nuevo servicio a sus clientes. Emisin de dinero De manera paralela a la promocin de los pagos electrnicos, una de las obligaciones constitucionales del Banco de Mxico es la emisin de billetes y monedas. El Banco de Mxico emite papel moneda de alta calidad en las cantidades necesarias para satisfacer las necesidades de la economa nacional. Los billetes emitidos por el Banco de Mxico tienen altos estndares de seguridad, son durables y funcionales y 29 reproducen smbolos, paisajes y personajes que nos identifican y unifican como mexicanos. Al cierre de 2022 se tenan en circulacin 8,304 millones de billetes, por un monto de 2,624 miles de millones de pesos, lo que representa un incremento de 9.8 por ciento en nmero de piezas y de 9.4 por ciento en monto, respecto del ao anterior. En cuanto a monedas, al cierre de 2022 se tenan en circulacin 44,730 millones de piezas, que equivalen a un monto de 76 mil millones de pesos; esto representa un incremento de 5.2 por ciento en el nmero de piezas y de 9.9 por ciento en el monto respecto del ao anterior. Cabe sealar que en octubre de 2021 se puso en circulacin el ltimo de los seis billetes que integran la nueva familia de billetes G, que correspondi a la denominacin de 50 pesos. En abril de 2022 este billete fue reconocido como el Billete del ao 2021 por la Sociedad Internacional de Billetes de Banco debido a su armonioso diseo y a su proceso de impresin. De este modo, el Banco de Mxico no solo emite dinero con los ms estrictos criterios de seguridad, calidad y durabilidad, sino que elabora algunos de los billetes ms bellos del mundo. 30 Seoras y seores senadores: Adems de una poltica monetaria enfocada en la estabilidad de precios, la economa mexicana cuenta con slidos fundamentos macroeconmicos que la distinguen de otras economas de desarrollo comparable. Actualmente, Mxico se encuentra en mejor posicin que en el pasado para hacer frente a una coyuntura externa caracterizada por condiciones financieras astringentes, derivadas del ciclo de apretamiento monetario a nivel global y por retos a la estabilidad del sistema financiero internacional. 31 En este contexto, el cumplimiento de los objetivos institucionales del Banco de Mxico contribuye de manera significativa a la fortaleza y certidumbre de nuestro pas. Ello debe incidir en un ambiente ms propicio para tomar decisiones de largo plazo en materia de inversin y produccin, as como en una preservacin del poder adquisitivo y el patrimonio de toda la poblacin. De manera similar, el Banco de Mxico seguir promoviendo un sistema financiero estable, sano y competitivo, as como un sistema de pagos ms eficiente. Ello debe reflejarse en mejores servicios financieros y en un mejor respaldo para la iniciativa y talento de los mexicanos, as como en una mayor eficiencia en la realizacin de todas sus transacciones econmicas. 32 De este modo, los mandatos legales del Banco de Mxico se traducen en beneficios y en mayores oportunidades para la poblacin. text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of the BANXICO Challenge Award. Mexico City, May 25, 2023 Good afternoon everyone. It is a source of great joy to participate in this award ceremony of this year's Banxico Challenge Award and to greet its finalists. This is a contest that dates back to 2016 and seeks to motivate higher education students from all over the country to reflect on the current economic situation and monetary policy in Mexico. With the establishment of the Banxico Challenge Award, three purposes have been sought. On the one hand, to help society to properly understand the functions of the Bank of Mexico and to appreciate the concrete benefits of its work in promoting price stability and the proper functioning of the country's financial and payment system. This exercise is very important to strengthen the social consensus around the tasks of the central bank. On the other hand, to strengthen academic ties between the Bank of Mexico and higher education institutions at the undergraduate level. Through this approach, the institution provides information and incentives for students to approach the topics of economics and monetary policy. This greater linkage allows the Bank to stimulate vocations and also detect talents that, in the future, will enrich the cadres of specialists in central banking. Finally, this type of contest contributes to increasing the economic and financial culture of the population, through the participating students, who play an important role in disseminating their family and social environment. The rules of the Award are clear. Students form teams of between three and five members that may be advised by a professor or a graduate student. Once constituted, the teams present a research paper in which, based on an analysis of the economic situation and the determinants of inflation, they develop and support a monetary policy stance, which also weighs financial stability. The contest comprises two stages. In the first, the jury, made up of officials from different areas of the Bank of Mexico, chooses the 10 best research papers, which will be semifinalists. In the second, the research papers that will go on to the final are chosen from among these ten. The finalists verbally present their monetary policy stance to the jury. This stage is particularly interesting, as it requires from the participants not only theoretical knowledge, but also a pragmatic sense and a capacity for exposition and persuasion. The dynamics of the Prize encourage team members to hypothetically assume the role and responsibility of members of the collegiate body that makes monetary policy decisions in a central bank. This challenge is complex and stimulating, as the economic environment has been radically transformed in recent years and monetary policy decisions are facing new determinants and dilemmas. Indeed, both the pandemic we suffered between 2020 and 2021, and the ongoing war in Eastern Europe, were totally unpredictable events. These events affected the economy, trade and global production chains and have generated global inflationary pressures, the magnitude, variety and persistence of which had not been seen in decades. At this juncture, monetary policy decision-makers are facing unprecedented circumstances. When making a determination, it is necessary to analyze a greater number of variables and assess their possible impact. For example, it is important to locate the different sources of inflationary pressures and weigh their possible medium- and long-term effects on price formation. In short, the task of making decisions has become more complex. For the Bank of Mexico, the exercise carried out within the framework of this award is very useful. For example, in his research work he shows a very adequate handling of the usual instruments and tools of analysis, as well as an openness to new approaches. In the case of the finalists, these characteristics of academic rigor are usually added to a remarkable creativity in the exhibition. There is no doubt that all of us who had access to his work learn from him and recognize his merits. For this reason, I greatly appreciate and deeply thank all the students who competed this year for their participation. For this eighth edition of the Banxico Challenge, 199 teams were registered. In total, 923 people participated, including students and advisors. Student participation reached 825 people, distributed in 46% men and 54% women. Teams from more than 20 states were registered. Of the institutions that represent these teams, 71% are public and 29% private. It is already customary for the determination of the juries to be very difficult, both because of the quantity and quality of the analysis works that are received, and because of the solidity and ease with which the finalist teams perform in the last phase of oral presentation. I also take this opportunity to thank the jurors for their neat and hard work. As always, it has been an honor for Banco de Mexico to endorse its relationship with higher education students through this event. I am pleased to announce below the finalist teams that earned mentions, as well as the winning team. Thank you very much and congratulations.
