text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the inauguration of the Seventh Conference on Equality and Non-Discrimination of the Bank of Mexico. Mexico City, July 17, 2023 Distinguished members of the presidium; Ladies and gentlemen, It is an honor to welcome you most cordially to the Seventh Conference on Equality and Non-Discrimination of the Bank of Mexico. Our central bank plays a crucial role in the stability of the economy and is a benchmark for the country's financial institutions. For this reason, for us it is very important to promote and implement labor policies that favor the full development of all people. Consequently, every year a space for reflection and dialogue is opened in our institution to promote and strengthen an egalitarian, fair and non-discriminatory work culture. The elimination of discrimination in any of its forms must be a priority issue on the agenda of both public and public organizations and private, since this phenomenon generates a negative impact on the individuals or sectors of the population it affects. Discrimination limits the possibilities of individual development, harms social cohesion and solidarity and even inhibits a country's growth potential. Indeed, when discrimination is committed, not only is an act unacceptable in modern and democratic societies, but the potential contribution of certain segments to economic and social development is reduced. The Bank of Mexico's main objective is to ensure the stability of the purchasing power of the currency, and as complementary purposes to promote the healthy development of the financial system and to promote the proper functioning of payment systems. This means that our greatest contribution to the country's well-being is to give people certainty of the value of the currency so that they can allocate their resources efficiently. In this regard, we are convinced that greater diversity and inclusion in our institution generate greater identification with an increasingly heterogeneous society and, reciprocally, promote greater social credibility towards the work we do. We are aware that the formation of teams diverse in gender, beliefs, ethnicity, age or training, contributes to facing the complex challenges we face with a better perspective. In this context, in 2018 the Bank of Mexico established the "Committee on Labor Equality and Non-Discrimination" which, with the participation of representatives from all areas, proposes and monitors policies and practices in this area. In addition, the Equality and Non-Discrimination Policy was issued aimed at eradicating any type of discrimination and workplace violence among the Bank's staff, while describing the commitments sought by this Institute to achieve equality of rights and opportunities and stimulate the full development of its employees. In this regard, we have made progress in aspects such as gender balance, managing to increase the representation of women in the bank in recent years. It is true that we still have challenges, so we continue to adopt tools aimed at guaranteeing equal opportunities in the selection and mobility processes of personnel and to continue promoting a greater gender balance at all levels. In addition to the search for gender equality, the Bank of Mexico's policy covers multiple areas. Let me mention just a few of the very diverse actions that we have promoted in recent years: i) adaptations have been made to the Bank's facilities to improve accessibility for people with disabilities; ii) a protocol and a safe and confidential mechanism has been established, with the figure of a counselor, to report possible cases of harassment and violence in the workplace; iii) greater facilities have been provided to personnel with care obligations and; (iv) indications in indigenous languages on the characteristics of banknotes have been included on the external website. All these actions address and prevent different expressions of discrimination and have concrete benefits on the quality of life and empowerment of people. This work in favor of equity and non-discrimination is carried out in accordance with international best practices and is subject to a verification and certification process. In this regard, I would like to highlight the two certifications to which the Bank of Mexico has been subjected in recent years. The first is the International Certification in Gender Equality and the second is the certification in the Mexican Standard on Labor Equality and Non-Discrimination. With regard to the International Certification, it should be noted that in 2021 the Bank reached the second of the three possible levels, the "Move" level, which recognizes the achievement of concrete goals and commitments to improve gender balance throughout the organizational structure, foster an inclusive culture, and promote pay equity. This last point has been reflected as a commitment by the Bank to verify annually that gender is not a determining variable to explain the remuneration of our staff. Regarding the Mexican Standard, this year the Bank achieved the recertification achieved in 2019, by covering 100 points, out of the 100 possible points in the mandatory requirements, and achieving 2 additional non-mandatory measures, which seek access for all people to equal opportunities. The struggle for the promotion of equity and for the eradication of discrimination is ongoing. Forums such as the one that brings us together today are the right opportunity to reflect and continue building an institutional culture of equity and respect. This is the space and the time to commit ourselves to continue working for a society where all people, regardless of their gender, physical characteristics, different abilities or preferences, have equal opportunities and can fully develop their professional potential and human qualities. Thanks a lot.

Ladies and gentlemen: Good afternoon, it is a pleasure to be here with you in the garden of the Casa Azul and to accompany you in such a special activity, such as the cancellation of a postage stamp commemorating the 65th anniversary of the opening of the Frida Kahlo Museum. The quality and intensity of Frida Kahlo's pictorial work, as well as her charismatic personality, made her a memorable presence on the national and international art scene. Thus, when in 1954, with just 47 years old, Frida Kahlo died, she had already left an imperishable mark on the culture of her time. This celebrity has increased posthumously. On the one hand, his pictorial work has generated wide recognition among specialized critics and has reached increasingly larger audiences. On the other hand, her figure, highlighted in several biographies, fiction books and films, has become enormously popular and, today, she is one of the most admired and inspiring women. Indeed, it is impossible not to appreciate the talent and altruism of this artist and social fighter who participated in a leading way in the most relevant political events and aesthetic movements of her time and who, with a strong character and an unwavering will to work, managed to overcome the most varied adversities, from gender prejudices to accidents and diseases. In 1955, just a year after Frida's death, Mexican painter and muralist Diego Rivera set up a trust under the administration of the Bank of Mexico. In this trust, Diego contributed the ownership of this house that belonged to his deceased spouse Frida Kahlo so that the aesthetic legacy of the artist would be preserved there. This is the foundation of the Frida Kahlo Museum, "Casa Azul." Likewise, Rivera transferred another property where he was creating a kind of City of the Arts, along with a collection of 50,000 pre-Hispanic pieces. That is what today makes up the "Anahuacalli Museum". The contributions made by Diego Rivera were intended to preserve for posterity the testimony of the work and activity of Frida and herself, keeping the Museums of both artists open. For more than six decades, the Bank of Mexico, in its capacity as trustee and administrator of this heritage, has had the challenge of creating the ideal conditions to consolidate these two important venues for artistic dissemination. As far as the "Blue House" is concerned, as is known, this space was the place where Frida was born, spent much of her life and died. In addition to being Frida's family home, the "Blue House" was, at the time, a lively intellectual gathering point and a space of refuge for some of the most prominent politicians and artists of the last century. 65 years ago, in 1958, this house opened its doors to the public as a Museum and today it is pleased to be a worldwide reference, with an average of 500,000 visitors a year. The work of the Museum has involved both conserving and classifying the varied heritage it has, as well as designing attractive activities for all types of visitors. Through a first-rate museographic work, the "Blue House" allows you to enter the intimacy of the great artist, evoke her everyday environments, reconstruct fundamental episodes of her life and appreciate her creative habits. Thanks to this, it has been possible to connect with the public and contribute to maintaining interest in one of the greatest symbols of Mexican culture. Today brings together another happy event, which consists of canceling and circulating a postage stamp that commemorates the 65th anniversary of the "Blue House". This beautiful stamp adds to the valuable iconography around Frida Kahlo and continues to fix, in an endearing way, the presence of this artist in contemporary memory. I can only thank you for the invitation to such an emotional event and reiterate the commitment of our central bank to, in its capacity as trustee, continue to safeguard the extraordinary legacy that Frida and Diego wanted to leave to the people of Mexico. Thank you very much and congratulations

Title:
"Comida de la Asociacin de Bancos de Mxico", Victoria Rodrguez, Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

Full text
text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the lunch of the Association of Banks of Mexico. Mexico City, August 23, 2023 Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit; Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen members of the banking and financial community: Introduction I am grateful for the invitation to attend this lunch organized by the Association of Banks of Mexico, whose host on this occasion is Activer. (ABM). This traditional meeting is an opportunity to review the common agenda of the financial sector and strengthen the ties of collaboration between intermediaries and authorities, in a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. This communication is especially important in light of the challenges we face. Allow me to take a few minutes to sketch a brief overview of the international and national economic environment and to describe the main actions of the central bank to achieve its objectives of ensuring the stability of the purchasing power of the Mexican currency, as well as promoting the healthy development and functioning of the financial and payment systems. International environment The growth outlook for the world economy for 2023 by international organisations has been revised upwards in recent months, although they still point to a slowdown compared to the previous year. They highlight challenges to downward growth, such as the complex economic situation in China and the possible effects of the recent tightening on long-term credit conditions. Headline inflation continued to decline in most countries, thanks to lower pressures on energy and food prices. However, it remained at high levels and often above central banks' targets. For its part, core inflation has shown some decrease, but remains at relatively high levels. Against this backdrop, the central banks of the main economies, such as the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, increased their reference rates and signaled a greater dependence on data to determine their forward movements. As for the international financial markets, in recent months there had been less volatility. However, since August, volatility has increased, due to concerns about the United States' fiscal position, and its effects on the balance of supply and demand of assets in longer-term markets. National Economic Outlook In our country, during the second quarter of 2023, economic activity continued to expand at a faster rate than anticipated. This is related to the good performance of domestic spending, in addition to the dynamism of the industrial and services sectors, and the slight recovery of primary activities. According to INEGI's timely estimate, GDP in real terms registered a seasonally adjusted quarterly increase of 0.91% in the second quarter. In addition, in the same period, the labor market continued to show strength. As for inflation, after standing at a level of 8.70% in September 2022, this indicator has been falling to 4.79% in July of this year. Core inflation continued to decline, to stand at 6.64% in July. The disinflation process has been supported by the gradual reduction in core inflation, as well as the notable decline in non-core inflation, which has recently registered uncharacteristically low, even negative, levels. Monetary policy In the face of the complex inflationary environment, which took shape in recent months, the Bank of Mexico has adopted timely and forceful actions to fulfill its institutional mandate to maintain the stability of the purchasing power of the Mexican currency. From June 2021 to March 2023, an increase in the reference rate of 725 basis points was accumulated to reach a level of 11.25%. In particular, the actions implemented since June 2022 made it possible to achieve a monetary policy stance above the upper limit of the neutral range, as required by the severe inflationary outlook. These actions have managed to keep long-term inflation expectations anchored and promote an orderly adjustment of the financial markets. Given the gradual improvement in the inflation outlook and considering the monetary policy stance achieved, the Bank of Mexico reduced the pace of adjustments and, in the last three decisions, has kept the reference rate unchanged. The inflationary outlook is expected to be complicated and uncertain over the entire forecast horizon and therefore it is considered necessary to maintain the benchmark rate at its current level for an extended period. The Governing Board will closely monitor inflationary pressures, as well as all factors that affect the expected path of inflation and its expectations. Thus, the central bank reaffirms its commitment to consolidate an environment of low and stable inflation, which protects the purchasing power of our currency and provides certainty to all economic agents. Financial System I will now refer to some issues that we are jointly promoting to improve the regulation of the financial system, as well as to increase its competition. Improving the regulatory framework of the Mexican banking system in order to align ourselves with best practices and reduce systemic risk is a constant task in which we seek consensus with intermediaries and, therefore, regulatory proposals go through a consultation period to enrich them. In the coming months, you will implement reforms on margins, derivative transaction identifiers and reference rates, among others. It is an enormous effort on their part that will undoubtedly result in the strengthening of an essential public good, financial stability. On the other hand, this month we submitted to public consultation the modifications to the 31 requirements to enter into derivative transactions, which includes the best national practices and will be open until August 30. Likewise, on March 3, the catalog of commission categories came into force. I am grateful for the participation of the ABM in the preparation of this catalogue that improves the transparency of the concepts of commission collection and reduces the number of existing concepts. For this initiative to materialize in favor of users, it is important that all banks adopt the new catalog with the greatest opportunity. The Bank of Mexico has defined a mechanism for the mass migration of fees in order to guide them in this process of transition to the new taxonomy. We are also working on modifications to the regulatory framework of Loans Associated with Payroll in order to establish clear rules regarding the procedures, contracts and information flows that must be observed by the crediting bank, the bank that maintains the payroll account and the worker, in order to facilitate the charges to the payroll account. In addition, a procedure will be established so that the collection of the credit persists in the event that the worker changes his payroll account to another bank. We have completed the project inside the Bank of Mexico and we will shortly present it to the ABM to receive its feedback. With regard to measures to increase competition and efficiency, as you know, the Bank of Mexico developed a digital credit placement platform that allows users to send a credit application to several bidders and receive personalized offers to their needs and risk profile. This platform reduces the search and choice costs incurred by users, as well as the costs of searching for customers and placing loans from banks. For the platform to achieve the expected benefits for users and banks, it is necessary for all institutions to participate. In this regard, I want to recognize the banks that are venturing into the first stage, which consists of offering credit cards, and I invite the rest again to join this relevant initiative. Regarding the "Financial Services Comparator", which, for some years now, has allowed users to compare the cost of credits, recently, there has been a notable increase in its use, which has doubled it. To complement this useful tool, in March 2023 the Bank of Mexico integrated the functionality of comparing the costs and characteristics of the different deposit products. Payment Systems With regard to the payment system, we want to continue promoting the use of secure, fast and low-cost means of payment, adapted to the different needs of the population, as well as improving the operation and security of these systems. In this regard, the implementation of Dimo by banks continues. At the end of last week, there were already seven authorized institutions, of which six are credit institutions. Thus, we are approaching 500,000 customers who can operate transfers. There are four other credit institutions already certified; that could start offering this service in the near future. Likewise, we will continue efforts to extend the adoption of CoDi, as an effective alternative means of payment for the population. Maintaining strict cybersecurity controls is an urgent need of the financial system and adequate compliance with these controls is a priority for the Bank of Mexico. At the beginning of August, the modifications to the SPEI and SPID regulations aimed at strengthening the cybersecurity controls of the participants of these payment systems were put up for consultation. The amendments are intended to: (i) provide greater clarity in the definitions contained to facilitate understanding and compliance with existing obligations; ii) to specify and strengthen existing obligations, and iii) to strengthen the cybersecurity framework of the participants. The regulation contemplates reasonable implementation deadlines for adaptations in processes and technological infrastructure. The public consultation will be open until August 30. Likewise, this year, the work of the SPEI Participants Forum was resumed, which is a space for the members of the system to express their opinions on the development of operational, business and technological issues related to this payment system. This forum contemplates the creation of specialized consultation groups, in order to have better elements when designing and implementing the system's development policy. As you can see, there are many specific projects that involve us and permanent communication between intermediaries and authorities is essential. For this reason, I thank you again for this pleasant opportunity to catch up on the shared challenges and, as always, I reiterate the willingness of the Bank of Mexico to maintain the closest and most positive communication at all levels. This collaboration will allow us to move towards our common aspiration: an environment of price stability, as well as an increasingly solid financial system and payment system, which stimulate the country's sustained growth and the well-being of Mexicans. Thanks a lot.

Este tradicional encuentro constituye una oportunidad para revisar la agenda comn del sector financiero y estrechar los lazos de colaboracin entre intermediarios y autoridades, en un ambiente relajado y amistoso. Esta comunicacin es especialmente importante a la luz de los retos que enfrentamos. Permtanme ocupar unos minutos en esbozar un breve panorama del entorno econmico internacional y nacional y en 2 describir las principales acciones del banco central para alcanzar sus objetivos de procurar la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda mexicana, as como promover el sano desarrollo y funcionamiento de los sistemas financiero y de pagos. Entorno internacional Las perspectivas de crecimiento de la economa mundial para 2023 por parte de organismos internacionales se han revisado al alza en los ltimos meses, aunque an siguen apuntando a una desaceleracin con respecto al ao anterior. Destacan retos para el crecimiento a la baja, como por ejemplo, la compleja situacin econmica en China y los posibles efectos del apretamiento reciente en las condiciones crediticias de largo plazo. La inflacin general continu disminuyendo en la mayora de los pases, gracias a las menores presiones en los precios de los energticos y alimentos. No obstante, se mantuvo en niveles elevados y, a menudo, por encima de los objetivos de los bancos centrales. Por su parte, la inflacin subyacente ha exhibido cierta disminucin, pero contina en niveles relativamente altos. 3 Ante este panorama, los bancos centrales de las principales economas, como la Reserva Federal y el Banco Central Europeo, incrementaron sus tasas de referencia y sealaron una mayor dependencia de datos para determinar sus movimientos hacia delante. En cuanto a os mercados financieros internacionales, en los ltimos meses se haba experimentado menor volatilidad. No obstante, a partir de agosto, la volatilidad ha aumentado, por las preocupaciones sobre la posicin fiscal de Estados Unidos, y sus efectos en el balance de oferta y demanda de activos en los mercados de mayor plazo. Panorama econmico nacional En nuestro pas, durante el segundo trimestre de 2023 la actividad econmica continu expandindose a un ritmo superior al anticipado. Esto se relaciona con el buen comportamiento del gasto interno, adems del dinamismo de los sectores industrial y de servicios, y la ligera recuperacin de las actividades primarias. De acuerdo con la estimacin oportuna del INEGI, el PIB en trminos reales registr en el segundo trimestre un alza trimestral desestacionalizada de 0.91%. 4 Adems, en el mismo periodo, el mercado laboral sigui mostrando fortaleza. En lo que atae a la inflacin, luego de situarse en un nivel de 8.70% en septiembre de 2022, este indicador ha venido descendiendo hasta el 4.79% de julio de este ao. La inflacin subyacente continu reducindose, para situarse en 6.64% en julio. El proceso de desinflacin ha estado apoyado en la reduccin, si bien gradual, de la inflacin subyacente, as como en el notable descenso de la no subyacente, la cual recientemente ha registrado niveles atpicamente bajos, incluso negativos. Poltica monetaria Ante el complejo entorno inflacionario, que se configur en los meses pasados, el Banco de Mxico ha adoptado acciones oportunas y contundentes para cumplir su mandato institucional de mantener la estabilidad del poder adquisitivo de la moneda mexicana. Desde junio de 2021 hasta marzo de 2023, se acumul un incremento en la tasa de referencia de 725 puntos base para llegar a un nivel de 5 11.25%. En particular, las acciones implementadas desde junio de 2022 permitieron alcanzar una postura de poltica monetaria por encima del lmite superior del rango de neutralidad, tal como lo requera el severo panorama inflacionario. Estas acciones han logrado mantener ancladas las expectativas de inflacin de largo plazo y propiciar un ajuste ordenado de los mercados financieros. Ante la mejora gradual de las perspectivas de inflacin y considerando la postura de poltica monetaria alcanzada, el Banco de Mxico redujo el ritmo de ajustes y, en las ltimas tres decisiones, ha mantenido la tasa de referencia sin cambios. Se estima que el panorama inflacionario ser complicado e incierto a lo largo de todo el horizonte de pronstico y, por ello, se considera que ser necesario mantener la tasa de referencia en su nivel actual durante un periodo prolongado. La Junta de Gobierno vigilar estrechamente las presiones inflacionarias, as como todos los factores que inciden en la trayectoria prevista para la inflacin y en sus expectativas. As, el banco central reafirma su compromiso de consolidar un entorno de inflacin 6 baja y estable, que proteja el poder adquisitivo de nuestra moneda y brinde certidumbre a todos los agentes econmicos. Sistema Financiero Ahora me referir a algunos temas que estamos impulsando conjuntamente para mejorar la regulacin del sistema financiero, as como para elevar su competencia. La mejora del marco regulatorio del sistema bancario mexicano con el fin de alinearnos con las mejores prcticas y reducir el riesgo sistmico, es una tarea constante en la que buscamos el consenso con los intermediarios y, por eso, las propuestas regulatorias pasan por un periodo de consulta para enriquecerlas. En los prximos meses ustedes implementaran las reformas sobre mrgenes, identificadores de operaciones derivadas y tasas de referencia, entre otras. Es un esfuerzo enorme de su parte que, sin duda redundar en el fortalecimiento de un bien pblico esencial, la estabilidad financiera. Por otro lado, este mes sometimos a consulta pblica las modificaciones a los 31 requerimientos para celebrar operaciones derivadas, que 7 recoge las mejores prcticas nacionales y estar abierta hasta el 30 de agosto. Igualmente, el pasado 3 de marzo entr en vigor el catlogo de categoras de comisiones. Agradezco la participacin de la ABM en la elaboracin de este catlogo que mejora la transparencia de los conceptos de cobro de comisiones y reduce el nmero de conceptos existentes. Para que esta iniciativa se materialice en favor de los usuarios, es importante que todos los bancos adopten el nuevo catlogo con la mayor oportunidad. El Banco de Mxico ha definido un mecanismo para la migracin masiva de comisiones con el fin de guiarlos en este proceso de transicin a la nueva taxonoma. Estamos trabajando tambin en modificaciones al marco regulatorio de los Crditos Asociados a la Nmina con el fin de establecer reglas claras respecto a los procedimientos, contratos y flujos de informacin que debern observar el banco acreditante, el banco que lleva la cuenta de nmina y el trabajador, con el propsito de facilitar los cargos en la cuenta de nmina. Adems, se establecer un procedimiento para que el cobro del crdito persista en el caso en que el trabajador cambie su 8 cuenta de nmina a otro banco. Hemos finalizado el proyecto en el interior del Banco de Mxico y en breve lo presentaremos a la ABM para recibir su retroalimentacin. En lo que se refiere a medidas para elevar la competencia y eficiencia, como saben, el Banco de Mxico desarroll una plataforma digital de colocacin de crditos que permite que los usuarios enven una solicitud de crdito a varios oferentes y reciban ofertas personalizadas a sus necesidades y perfil de riesgo. Esta plataforma reduce los costos de bsqueda y eleccin en que incurren los usuarios, as como los costos de bsqueda de clientes y colocacin de crditos de los bancos. Para que la plataforma logre los beneficios esperados para usuarios y bancos, es necesario que todas las instituciones participen. Al respecto, quiero reconocer a los bancos que estn incursionando en la primera etapa que consiste en el ofrecimiento de tarjetas de crdito e invito nuevamente al resto para que se unan a esta relevante iniciativa. Respecto al Comparador de servicios financieros, que, desde hace algunos aos, permite a los usuarios comparar el costo de crditos, recientemente, ha habido un notable incremento en su uso, que lo ha 9 duplicado. Para complementar esta til herramienta, en marzo de 2023 el Banco de Mxico integr la funcionalidad de comparar los costos y las caractersticas de los distintos productos de depsito. Sistemas de Pagos En lo que se refiere al sistema de pagos queremos seguir promoviendo la utilizacin de medios de pago seguros, rpidos y de bajo costo, adecuados a las distintas necesidades de la poblacin, as como mejorar el funcionamiento y seguridad de dichos sistemas. Al respecto, la implementacin de Dimo por parte de la banca contina. Al cierre de la semana pasada ya se contaba con siete instituciones habilitadas, de las cuales seis son instituciones de crdito. As, nos acercamos a los 500,000 clientes que pueden operar transferencias. Existen otras cuatro instituciones de crdito ya certificadas; que podran empezar a ofrecer este servicio en fechas prximas. Igualmente, continuaremos los esfuerzos para que se extienda la adopcin de CoDi, como un eficaz medio de pago alternativo para la poblacin. 10 El mantener controles estrictos en materia de ciberseguridad es una necesidad perentoria del sistema financiero y el adecuado cumplimiento de estos controles es una prioridad para el Banco de Mxico. A principios de agosto, se pusieron a consulta las modificaciones a la normativa de SPEI y SPID encaminadas a fortalecer los controles de ciberseguridad de los participantes de estos sistemas de pagos. Las modificaciones tienen por objeto: i) dar mayor claridad en las definiciones contenidas para facilitar el entendimiento y el cumplimiento de las obligaciones vigentes; ii) precisar y fortalecer obligaciones existentes, y iii) reforzar el marco de ciberseguridad de los participantes. La norma contempla plazos de implementacin razonables para las adecuaciones en procesos e infraestructura tecnolgica. La consulta pblica estar abierta hasta el prximo 30 de agosto. Asimismo, este ao, se retomaron los trabajos del Foro de Participantes del SPEI, que constituye un espacio para que los miembros del sistema puedan externar sus opiniones sobre el desarrollo de los temas operativos, de negocio y tecnolgicos relacionados con este sistema de pagos. Este foro contempla la creacin de grupos de consulta 11 especializados, con el fin de contar con mejores elementos al momento de disear e implementar la poltica de desarrollo del sistema. Como pueden ver, los proyectos concretos que nos involucran son mltiples y la comunicacin permanente entre intermediarios y autoridades resulta fundamental. Por eso, agradezco nuevamente esta grata oportunidad de ponernos al da en los retos compartidos y, como siempre, les reitero la disposicin del Banco de Mxico para mantener las ms estrecha y positiva comunicacin a todos los niveles. Esta colaboracin nos permitir avanzar hacia nuestra aspiracin comn: un entorno de estabilidad de precios, as como un sistema financiero y un sistema de pagos cada vez ms slidos, que estimulen el crecimiento sostenido del pas y el bienestar de las y los mexicanos. Muchas gracias.

text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the lunch of the Association of Banks of Mexico. Mexico City, October 25, 2023 Mr. Secretary of Finance and Public Credit; Mr. President of the Association of Banks of Mexico; Ladies and gentlemen members of the banking and financial community: Introduction I am grateful for the invitation to attend this lunch of the Associates Committee of the Association of Banks of Mexico, whose host on this occasion is Fundacion Donde Banco. I am very happy to share this space again with all of you, which allows us a very productive communication, which in light of the challenges we currently face, is of particular importance. That is why I want to take this opportunity to share with you some perspectives on the economy in the global and national context, as well as to make some comments on the financial system in our country. Let me start by saying that, on the external front, during this year, economic activity in the United States has expanded at a faster rate than expected and the labor market has shown strength. Inflation in that country remains elevated, and some analysts expect it to decline toward its target at a slower pace than previously expected. In this context, a further tightening of financial conditions has been observed. Sovereign interest rates, primarily medium and long-term, have increased significantly around the world, and the U.S. dollar has appreciated across the board. In line with this behavior of the international financial markets, in Mexico the interest rates of longer-term government securities have also increased. Likewise, the Mexican peso, like the currencies of most advanced and emerging economies, has depreciated against the U.S. dollar. I would highlight that, despite this recent behavior that is due to global factors, during the year the national currency has been distinguished by its resilience, compared to the currencies of emerging economies. This reflects our country's strong macroeconomic fundamentals relative to other economies. Regarding national economic activity, in the first half of 2023 it showed greater dynamism than expected. This was associated, primarily, with a better-than-expected performance of the U.S. economy, as well as with higher domestic spending. With the information available for the third quarter of this year, it can be seen that the expansion has continued, driven by the progress of the three major sectors of activity. Going forward, we anticipate that the economy will continue to expand, albeit at a slower pace. This is in line with the moderation expected for the US economy, especially in its industrial production. I would like to mention that our forecasts will be updated based on the data we have available at the end of November, when we publish our next Quarterly Report. Regarding inflation, given the effects of the shocks of the pandemic and the conflict in Ukraine, in our country, as in most advanced and emerging economies, it reached levels not seen in decades. In Mexico, headline inflation peaked at 8.70% in August 2022, and has fallen to 4.27% in the first half of October 2023. At the beginning of the disinflationary period, the non-core component explained, primarily, the fall in headline inflation. However, more recently, core inflation has also contributed to the decline in headline inflation, going from 8.51% in November 2022, when it peaked in this episode, to 5.54% in the first half of October 2023. As we have pointed out in our communications, we are in the phase of disinflation. However, some shocks continue to have an impact on prices, especially those of services. Therefore, we anticipate that headline and core inflation would continue to fall, to be around the 3% target by the second half of 2025. As for the conduct of monetary policy, given the severity of the inflationary episode we have faced, it has been necessary to act in a timely and forceful manner. Thus, the Bank of Mexico began an upward cycle in June 2021. Since the meeting in May of this year, considering the monetary stance reached and that we are already in the disinflation phase, we have kept the rate unchanged at 11.25%. As we have pointed out in our latest monetary policy statements, the Governing Board estimates that the inflationary outlook will be complicated and uncertain throughout the forecast horizon, with upside risks. Given this, in order to achieve the orderly and sustained convergence of headline inflation to its 3% target, it considers that it will be necessary to maintain the reference rate at its current level for a prolonged period. I would also highlight the message we have given in our communiques to the effect that the Central Bank reaffirms its commitment to its priority mandate and the need to persevere in its efforts to consolidate an environment of low and stable inflation. Financial system Let me now make a few comments on the national financial system. I would start by saying that in this complex environment our banking system remains solid, profitable and resilient, although the challenges and pending issues that we have talked about on previous occasions remain. A challenge facing the banking system is to meet the growing demand for credit while maintaining prudence in the granting of loans. In recent months we have seen that bank credit to both households and companies continues to expand at positive rates, but it has not yet recovered the level it had before the pandemic as a proportion of GDP. On the other hand, the expected loss and non-performing loans indicators remain at reasonable levels on an aggregate basis. Likewise, commercial banks maintain capital and liquidity levels that comfortably exceed the regulatory minimums, so they do not present a significant restriction from the point of view of the supply of resources. Also, increasing competition in some segments, as well as increasing access and inclusion for both companies and people who are not yet served by the banking sector continues to represent a challenge for the sector. In this regard, the Bank of Mexico has taken a set of actions to promote competition and financial inclusion, with the ultimate goal of improving the well-being of Mexicans. It is worth mentioning that, in the development of these initiatives, the Bank of Mexico has had the collaboration of the ABM. An initiative of the Bank of Mexico is the platform for offering individualized loans that takes advantage of digital channels to connect applicants with credit providers, reducing search costs for applicants and customer acquisition costs for providers. To ensure the success of the platform, a sufficient number of issuers and customers are required to participate. Currently, 6 institutions are collaborating with the Bank in the development of the credit card platform. I reiterate my recognition to these institutions that have joined the first stage of the project, as well as my invitation to the rest of them to participate. Another initiative of the Bank is the adoption of a fee catalogue, which aims to improve transparency in the collection of services that users purchase. To date, 7 months after its introduction, less than 5% of the commissions have adopted the new denominations, so, in order to promote a more dynamic adoption, a draft modification of provisions was recently submitted to public consultation that, on the one hand, will allow institutions to make a massive change of commission denominations without modifying their level; and on the other, it establishes a peremptory deadline for the institutions to modify all the commissions. The public consultation closes on 27 October. With regard to the adoption of the new reference rates, in our case the THE of funding, the issue continues to be a priority. From 1 January next year, the 91-day and 182-day TIIEs will no longer be usable, and from 2025 the use of the 28-day THE will no longer be allowed. Over the past few years, we've worked with all of you to define concrete steps to ease the transition. The Bank of Mexico has already published all the necessary information, including different support elements that facilitate the adoption of this rate. It is important that the sector adopts it and becomes an example, making it easier for its customers to know it and use it for their financial operations. To address the issue of initial margins, I would comment that one of the lessons of the great financial crisis was the need to improve the operation of the OTC derivatives market, increase its transparency and reduce the systemic risks associated with it. To this end, several initiatives were taken internationally, such as the standardization of contracts, the negotiation of contracts through electronic platforms when appropriate and their centralized settlement, as well as the application of higher capital requirements and the obligation to exchange margins for operations not settled centrally. We have worked closely with the ABM and the AMIB to implement these reforms in Mexico, which will surely make the Mexican financial system safer and reduce systemic risk. We have also listened carefully to their views, and we are reflecting in an important way within the Bank on the next steps to take. We will let you know the conclusions once we have them. Regarding the evolution of payment systems, I would like to tell you that we are already seeing a greater offer of Dimo's service by some financial institutions, although others are still working on obtaining the necessary infrastructure for registration. It is important to redouble efforts so that in the coming months entities continue to join this process, allowing more and more users to have access to a service that simplifies the sending of electronic transfers. On the other hand, the public consultation on the draft provisions to amend the SPEI and SPID Rules, issued at the beginning of August, is in a stage of analysis of results. I tell you that, with this reform, the Bank of Mexico seeks to update the elements that the participants of the payment systems must comply with with respect to the computer security requirements currently included in these rules, as well as to align such provisions with the international cybersecurity frameworks in force. Also, reforms to the SPEI rules that regulate indirect participation and processing of remittances are in the implementation phase. These reforms were issued in order for the indirect participation service to be provided in a standardized and accessible way and, in the case of remittances, they establish a new messaging system to provide greater traceability to these operations. For this reason, it is important that financial institutions conclude their certifications to operate messaging related to these services as soon as possible, with a view to the implementation date in March 2024. Conclusion Finally, I would like to emphasize that the disinflation process has continued to advance in our country. I would mention, again, that headline inflation, after having reached its maximum level of 8.70% in August 2022 in this inflationary episode, has fallen to 4.27% in its last reading. Likewise, the core component, which better reflects the trend in inflation, has also fallen. In particular, it has declined from its high of 8.51 in November 2022 to 5.54% in the first half of October. In other words, it has shown a downward trajectory for almost a year. I would highlight that, despite this important progress in reducing inflation, at the Bank of Mexico we are aware that we continue to face challenges. Inflation is still above our target. Likewise, the balance of risks for its expected trajectory remains skewed to the upside. However, I would emphasize that this balance has not deteriorated. Likewise, going forward, we expect headline and core inflation to continue to decline. This is considering our monetary stance and the dissipation of the effects of shocks. Although we still have work to do, I would not like to miss this opportunity to highlight the path we have already traveled. I would also like to take this opportunity to reiterate the willingness of the Bank of Mexico to continue to maintain communication and dialogue at all levels, as it has been until now. Permanent communication between intermediaries and authorities is essential to maintain the soundness of the banking system and implement changes that seek to strengthen its resilience and competitiveness at the international level. This close dialogue and collaboration will allow us to get closer to achieving our common goal: an environment of price stability, as well as an increasingly solid, competitive and inclusive financial system and payment system, which contribute to achieving the country's sustained growth and the well-being of Mexicans. Thanks a lot

Actualmente 6 instituciones estn colaborando con el Banco en el desarrollo de la plataforma de tarjetas de crdito. Reitero mi reconocimiento a estas instituciones que se han sumado a la primera etapa del proyecto, as como mi invitacin a participar al resto de ellas. 7 Otra iniciativa del Banco es la adopcin de un catlogo de comisiones, que tiene por objeto mejorar la transparencia en el cobro de los servicios que los usuarios adquieren. A la fecha, luego de 7 meses de su introduccin, menos del 5% de las comisiones han adoptado las nuevas denominaciones, por lo que, con el fin de promover una adopcin ms dinmica, recientemente se someti a consulta pblica un proyecto de modificacin de disposiciones que por un lado, permitir que las instituciones puedan hacer un cambio masivo de denominaciones de comisiones sin modificar el nivel de las mismas; y por el otro, establece un plazo perentorio para que las instituciones modifiquen la totalidad de las comisiones. La consulta pblica se cierra el 27 de octubre. En lo que se refiere a la adopcin de las nuevas tasas de referencia, en nuestro caso la THE de fondeo, el tema sigue siendo una prioridad. A partir del 1 de enero del prximo ao, ya no podrn utilizarse las TIIEs de 91 y 182 das, y a partir de 2025 no se permitir el uso de la THE a 28 das. Durante los ltimos aos, hemos trabajado con todos ustedes para definir pasos concretos que faciliten la transicin. El Banco de Mxico ha publicado ya toda la informacin necesaria, incluyendo distintos elementos de apoyo que facilitan la adopcin de esta tasa. Es 8 importante que el sector la adopte y se convierta en un ejemplo, facilitando que sus clientes la conozcan y la usen para sus operaciones financieras. Para abordar el tema de mrgenes iniciales comentara que, una de las lecciones de la gran crisis financiera, fue la necesidad de mejorar la operacin del mercado de derivados extraburstiles, incrementar su transparencia y reducir los riesgos de carcter sistmico asociados al mismo. Con este fin se tomaron internacionalmente varias iniciativas como la estandarizacin de los contratos, la negociacin de estos a travs de plataformas electrnicas cuando resultara adecuado y su liquidacin centralizada, as como la aplicacin de mayores requerimientos de capital y la obligatoriedad de intercambiar mrgenes para las operaciones no liquidadas de manera centralizada. Hemos trabajado de manera cercana con la ABM y la AMIB para implementar en Mxico estas reformas, que seguramente propiciarn que el sistema financiero mexicano sea ms seguro y que el riesgo sistmico se reduzca. Tambin hemos escuchado de manera atenta sus puntos de vista, y estamos reflexionando de manera importante al interior del 9 Banco sobre los siguientes pasos a seguir. Les haremos saber las conclusiones una vez que contemos con ellas. En cuanto a la evolucin de los sistemas de pago, me gustara comentarles que ya estamos viendo una mayor oferta del servicio de Dimo por parte de algunas entidades financieras, aunque otras an siguen trabajando en obtener la infraestructura necesaria para el registro. Es importante redoblar esfuerzos para que en los prximos meses se sigan sumando entidades a este proceso, permitiendo que cada vez ms usuarios tengan acceso a un servicio que simplifica el envo de transferencias electrnicas. Por otro lado, la consulta pblica de los proyectos de disposiciones para modificar las Reglas del SPEI y SPID, emitida a principios de agosto, se encuentra en una etapa de anlisis de resultados. Les comento que, con esta reforma, el Banco de Mxico busca que se actualicen los elementos que los participantes de los sistemas de pagos deben cumplir respecto a los requisitos de seguridad informtica actualmente incluidos en estas reglas, as como alinear tales disposiciones a los marcos de ciberseguridad internacionales vigentes. 10 Tambin, las reformas a las reglas del SPEI que norman la participacin indirecta y procesamiento de remesas se encuentran en fase de implementacin. Estas reformas fueron emitidas con el objeto de que el servicio de participacin indirecta se preste de forma estandarizada y accesible y, en el caso de remesas, establecen una nueva mensajera para brindar mayor trazabilidad a estas operaciones. Por ello es importante que las entidades financieras concluyan a la brevedad sus certificaciones para operar la mensajera relacionada con estos servicios, de cara a la fecha de implementacin en marzo de 2024. Conclusin Finalmente, me gustara destacar que el proceso de desinflacin ha seguido avanzando en nuestro pas. Mencionara, nuevamente, que la inflacin general, despus de haber alcanzado en agosto de 2022 su nivel mximo de 8.70% en este episodio inflacionario, ha descendido hasta ubicarse en 4.27% en su ltima lectura. Asimismo, el componente subyacente, que refleja mejor la tendencia de la inflacin, tambin ha descendido. En particular, se ha reducido desde su mximo de 8.51 en noviembre de 2022 hasta ubicarse en 5.54% en la primera quincena de i octubre. Es decir, ha mostrado una trayectoria a la baja durante casi un ao. Destacara que, a pesar de este importante avance en la reduccin de la inflacin, en el Banco de Mxico estamos conscientes de que seguimos enfrentando retos. La inflacin todava se ubica por encima de nuestra meta. Asimismo, el balance de riesgos para su trayectoria prevista se mantiene sesgado al alza. No obstante, enfatizara que dicho balance no se ha deteriorado. Asimismo, hacia delante, esperamos que las inflaciones general y subyacente continen disminuyendo. Ello considerando nuestra postura monetaria y la disipacin de los efectos de los choques. Si bien an tenemos tarea pendiente, no quisiera dejar pasar esta oportunidad para destacar el camino que ya hemos recorrido. Tambin, quiero aprovechar la oportunidad para reiterarles la disposicin del Banco de Mxico para continuar manteniendo la comunicacin y el dilogo a todos los niveles, como ha sido hasta ahora. La comunicacin permanente entre intermediarios y autoridades resulta fundamental para mantener la solidez del sistema bancario e implementar los cambios que buscan fortalecer su resiliencia y su competitividad a nivel internacional. Este dilogo y colaboracin estrechas nos permitir acercarnos ms a la consecucin de nuestra 12 meta comn: un entorno de estabilidad de precios, as como un sistema financiero y un sistema de pagos cada vez ms slidos, competitivos e incluyentes, que coadyuven a alcanzar el crecimiento sostenido del pas y el bienestar de las y los mexicanos. Muchas gracias 13

Title:
"Putting into circulation the commemorative coin of the two hundred years of diplomatic relations between the United Mexican States and the United States of America", Victoria Rodrguez, Governor of Banco de Mxico (available only in Spanish)

text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the launch of the coin commemorating the two hundred years of diplomatic relations between the United States of Mexico and the United States of America. Mexico City, December 6, 2023 Janet Yellen, Secretary of the Treasury of the United States of America; Rogelio Ramirez de la O, Secretary of Finance and Public Credit; Ken Salazar, Ambassador of the United States to Mexico; Roberto Velasco Alvarez, Head of the North American Unit of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, representing Foreign Minister Alicia Barcena Ibarra, Secretary of Foreign Affairs; Gina Andrea Cruz Blackledge, Chair of the Relations Commission North American Foreign Affairs of the Senate of the Republic. Media representatives; Ladies and gentlemen: Good morning to all of you. It is an honour for me to welcome you to the Interactive Museum of Economics, this avant-garde space in terms of the dissemination of economic and financial culture, to which I thank for its hospitality. Since December 2022, and throughout 2023, the two hundred years of diplomatic relations between the governments of the Mexican United States and the United States of America have been commemorated. Now, within the framework of the celebrations that motivate us to gather today to celebrate this significant event, considering that the minting of currency is an exclusive faculty of the Mexican State, it was planned to mint a commemorative coin, with a denomination of twenty pesos, which would represent friendship, sovereignty and cooperation between our countries. It is noteworthy that the Congress of the Union is the one that defines the characteristics of our currencies, and in the case of this one, the initiative was presented in the Senate of the Republic through its Foreign Relations Commission for North America. After its approval in both chambers, on June 16 the "Decree establishing the characteristics of a commemorative coin of the Two Hundred Years of Diplomatic Relations between Mexican United States and the United States of America is established in the Official Gazette of the Federation", and after that the Bank of Mexico requested the mint of Mexico the minting of five million of this piece. During two centuries of diplomatic relations between Mexico and the United States, where over time coincidences and common interests have prevailed and mechanisms for dialogue and cooperation have been established at all levels. Therefore, it can be said that our countries share a productive and promising relationship. I would like to touch briefly on the economic aspect of this deep shared history. Since the end of the nineteenth century, there have been close ties in trade and investment between our countries, which have been strengthened and multiplied over time. The entry into force of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) in 1994 is undoubtedly a decisive event in the economic relationship between Mexico and the United States, since it provided a set of institutional rules to promote and facilitate trade flows, investment, and the development of regional value chains. In doing so, it provided an environment of stability and certainty for greater integration for the benefit of all members of the region. Today, Mexico ranks first as a country of origin for imports from the United States and second as the main destination for U.S. exports. Moreover, in the context of the process of reconfiguration in global value chains, new opportunities are opening up to strengthen the bilateral relationship. Mexico is a natural and extremely convenient destination for the relocation of companies and activities that seek to be closer to the U.S. market. Today, we already see evidence that this so-called nearshoring is occurring and is expected to accelerate in the coming years, increasing the integration of our productive apparatuses, the competitiveness of our economies and the well-being of our societies. The thriving economic interaction and the many aspects of our bilateral relationship are a sign of the ties that unite us. Hence, the opportunity of the commemorative coin, whose presentation brings us together today. Let me describe its most relevant features:  Its denomination is twenty pesos, it has a dodecagonal shape and its diameter is 30 millimeters. The core of the coin is made of silver nickel silver and its perimetric ring is made of bronze-aluminium.  On the obverse it shows, like all Mexican coins, the national coat of arms, which is surrounded by the legend "UNITED MEXICAN STATES".  On its reverse it displays: "On the left the golden eagle representing the Mexican United States and, on the right, the bald eagle representing the United States of America."  It has security elements integrated by the microtext "FRIENDSHIP, SOVEREIGNTY AND COOPERATION", and a latent image, which is a number "200". In the upper outline it refers to the "TWO HUNDRED YEARS OF DIPLOMATIC RELATIONS UNITED MEXICAN STATES - UNITED STATES OF AMERICA". We know that coins and banknotes, apart from functioning as a means of payment, allow us to identify with their themes and motifs, as well as with shared values and aspirations. For this reason, I want to emphasize the central motif of this coin, which is based on the figures of the golden eagle and the bald eagle, which are a fundamental part of the respective national symbologies of our countries. On the one hand, the golden eagle, which represents the firm will for freedom and sovereignty, constitutes a powerful element of identity among Mexicans and, since the dawn of Independence, it was incorporated into various banners and adopted as a national emblem. On the other hand, the bald eagle symbolizes fundamental characteristics, such as courage and freedom. The bald eagle was incorporated into the Great Seal of the United States in 1782 and, since then, it has had a fundamental presence on the banknotes and coins of that country. Due to these historical connotations, as well as its aesthetic value, it is a fact that, as has happened with other pieces, this new twenty-peso coin will not only serve as a means of payment, unit of account and store of value, but will also be treasured by the user public and widely esteemed by the numismatic community. I congratulate the staff of the Mint of Mexico, whose great work and craft is observed in pieces of nationally and internationally recognized quality. Thus, with the introduction of this beautiful currency, which can be exchanged from today, we offer an endearing testimony of these two hundred years of diplomatic relations between our countries and the continuity of a future full of friendship, cooperation and bilateral progress. Thanks a lot

Permtanme describir sus caractersticas ms relevantes:  Su denominacin es de veinte pesos, tiene forma dodecagonal y su dimetro es de 30 milmetros. Por eso, quiero poner nfasis en el motivo central de esta moneda, que se basa en las figuras del guila real y el guila calva, las cuales son parte fundamental de las respectivas simbologas nacionales de nuestros pases. Por un lado, el guila real, que representa la firme voluntad de libertad y soberana, constituye un poderoso elemento de identidad entre los mexicanos y, desde los albores de la Independencia, fue incorporada a diversos estandartes y adoptada como un emblema nacional. Por otro lado, el guila calva, simboliza caractersticas fundamentales, como el valor y la libertad. text: Words of the Lie. Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, governor of the Bank of Mexico, during the presentation of the Banxico Contact Award, 2023. Mexico City, December 7, 2023 Introduction It is a pleasure to participate in the delivery of the Fifteenth Edition of the Banxico Contact Award, this national contest aimed at high school students that has achieved so much roots in the student community of our country. In its 15 years of existence, this contest has been one of the most successful instruments of financial education and academic engagement of the Bank of Mexico. Since its creation in 2009, more than 66 thousand participants from public and private educational institutions from all the States have registered, and more than 8 thousand works or videos have been received. The Prize, which brings us together today, is a mechanism to link the Bank of Mexico with high school students. This is very relevant for us, as they are on the eve of choosing their professional career and deciding how they will integrate into productive life. Therefore, we want you to be able to learn more about the functions and strategies of the Bank of Mexico and evaluate the social and economic importance of its tasks. The interaction that this contest fosters is very enriching. On the one hand, the fact that you reflect on the theme assigned by the Bank allows you to access topics and valuable information and to deploy your academic and intellectual skills, such as organizing an exhibition in a logical, coherent and persuasive way. In turn, the Bank of Mexico can have a first-hand diagnosis of the economic-financial knowledge of students at this level and the opportunity to detect talents and vocations. Theme of the 2023 edition. The theme assigned for this edition was "Sustainability. The role of the financial system in the transition to a sustainable economy". One of the greatest contemporary challenges is to promote the sustainability of the economy and limit the negative effects that certain productive activities can unleash. Climate change, environmental degradation and the loss of biodiversity are factors that have an economic impact, contribute to increasing the incidence of natural phenomena, deteriorate the environment and livelihoods of large segments of the population and can generate episodes of food scarcity or mass migration. For this reason, greater global awareness of the magnitude of these challenges has been created and various initiatives have been discussed to mitigate them, promoting changes in the current paradigms of production, consumption and investment. In this regard, institutions and companies have at their disposal a series of environmental, social and governance criteria, the so-called ESG, which allow investment to be oriented towards activities that have a sustainable approach and a proven social benefit. Let me briefly touch on these so-called ESG considerations. Environmental considerations are criteria aimed at protecting the environment. This involves various actions such as promoting the development and use of processes that contribute to the preservation of biodiversity, among others. Social considerations are actions that seek to promote social cohesion and guarantee human rights, equal opportunities and inclusion. These actions focus on ensuring that an organization's impact on society is positive. Good governance considerations are actions aimed at promoting better management, both in private companies and in governments, to evaluate and manage issues related to aspects such as greater transparency and accountability of organizations, among others. Given that environmental phenomena have a global scope and constitute a source of financial risks, central banks, financial supervisors and participants in the financial system as a whole must be especially attentive to their detection and mitigation. In particular, financial sector institutions should clearly and transparently assess their exposure to climate risks, as well as encourage the adoption of ESG criteria and stimulate socially responsible investment. In this regard, the Bank of Mexico participates in the main multilateral discussion forums on the subject, such as the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for the Greening of the Financial System. In addition, the Bank, together with other authorities, encourages participants in the Mexican financial system to improve their climate risk assessment and encourage the adoption of environmental criteria. Participation process and results As you know, the participation process is transparent. Students form teams of three or four members and a teacher and sign up for a platform. Then, the teams solve an online questionnaire on aspects of general economics, the functions and purposes of the Bank of Mexico and prepare a written work or a video, called "Entrada", in which they analyze the proposed topic and send it online. The 150 teams that obtain the highest score in the questionnaire win the opportunity to have their entries evaluated by the qualifying jury. From these teams, 10 semi-finalists are chosen from each category and, subsequently, the three finalists per category are defined. The Qualifying Jury is made up of members of the various areas of the Bank of Mexico and recognized representatives of institutions in the economic-financial environment. In this edition, the teams had to choose one of the three ESG criteria, environmental, social or good governance, for the development of their work or video and had the possibility of relying on the material that is placed on the contest page. In response to the call, this year 2302 students were enrolled advised by 253 teachers, 55.7% of them women and 43.8% men, with a total of 640 teams. It is worth noting the participation of schools from all the states of the Republic, which fills us with pleasure. As usual, their findings and contributions were very outstanding and the level of quality and competence was very high. It is very encouraging to see the high level of awareness and commitment that you have, as well as the knowledge and valuable proposals that you make to address the central problems of our time. For this reason, I congratulate all the participants and, in particular, the finalists and those who are winners of this stimulating competition. Thank you very much and congratulations.

Dado que los fenmenos ambientales tienen un alcance global y constituyen una fuente de riesgos financieros, los bancos centrales, supervisores financieros y participantes del sistema financiero en su conjunto deben estar especialmente atentos a su deteccin y mitigacin. 4 En particular, las instituciones del sector financiero deben evaluar de manera clara y transparente su exposicin a riesgos climticos, as como fomentar la adopcin de los criterios ASG y estimular la inversin socialmente responsable. Al respecto, el Banco de Mxico participa en los principales foros multilaterales de discusin en la materia, como la Red de Bancos Centrales y Supervisores para el Enverdecimiento del Sistema Financiero. Adems, el Banco, junto con otras autoridades, impulsa que los participantes del sistema financiero mexicano mejoren su evaluacin de riesgo climtico y fomenten la adopcin de criterios ambientales. Proceso de participacin y resultados Como ustedes saben, el proceso de participacin es transparente. Los estudiantes forman equipos de tres o cuatro integrantes y un docente y se inscriben en una plataforma. Luego, los equipos resuelven un cuestionario en lnea sobre aspectos de economa general, de las funciones y finalidades del Banco de Mxico y elaboran un trabajo 5 escrito o un video, denominado Entrada, en el que analizan el tema que se propone y lo envan en lnea. Los 150 equipos que obtienen la mayor calificacin en el cuestionario, ganan la oportunidad de que sus entradas sean evaluadas por el jurado calificador. De estos equipos se eligen 10 semifinalistas de cada categora y, posteriormente, se definen los tres finalistas por categora. El Jurado Calificador est conformado por miembros de las diversas reas del Banco de Mxico y por reconocidos representantes de instituciones del medio econmico-financiero. En esta edicin, los equipos debieron elegir uno de los tres criterios ASG, ambientales, sociales o de buen gobierno, para el desarrollo de su trabajo o video y tenan la posibilidad de apoyarse en el material que se coloca en la pgina del concurso. Respondiendo a la convocatoria, este ao se inscribieron 2302 estudiantes asesorados por 253 docentes, 55.7% de ellos mujeres y 43.8% hombres, con un total de 640 equipos. Es de destacar la 6 participacin de escuelas de todos los estados de la Repblica, lo que nos llena de gusto. Como es costumbre, sus hallazgos y aportaciones fueron muy destacados y el nivel de calidad y competencia fue muy alto. Es muy alentador constatar el elevado nivel de conciencia y compromiso que tienen ustedes, as como el conocimiento y valiosas propuestas que hacen para atender problemticas centrales de nuestro tiempo. Por eso, felicito a todos los participantes y, en particular, a los finalistas y a quienes resulten ganadores de este estimulante concurso. Muchas gracias y enhorabuena. 7

Title: The state of the Mexican economy
Subtitle: Speech by Dr Guillermo Ortiz, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, at the LXVI Banking Convention, Mrida, Yucatn, 4 April 2003.
text: Guillermo Ortiz: The state of the Mexican economy Speech by Dr Guillermo Ortiz, Governor of the Bank of Mexico, at the LXVI Banking Convention, Merida, Yucatan, 4 April 2003. * * * It is an honor to participate, once more, in the National Banking Convention. This meeting takes place in a context of uncertainty about the recovery of the global economy. The recession of the Mexican economy is mainly a consequence of the links we have with the rest of the world. However, the relative performance by the Mexican economy during the recent slowdown is based on two key elements: first, reinforcement of the macroeconomic fundamentals, and second, development of the institutions the country has fostered in recent decades. I will talk about these two crucial factors during my remarks and the challenges we face in order to foster a stronger and more competitive economy allowing for sustained and broad development for all Mexicans. With this purpose in mind, I will stress the hurdles that the current international environment poses for us and the pending tasks we have to accomplish in order to forge a better future for the years to come. External environment The recovery of economic activity in the United States after the 2001 recession has been weak. The slowdown was the consequence of the necessity businesses faced to assimilate investment volumes that had been realized during the nineties, mainly in the areas of technology and telecommunications. The main difference between this recession and others in the past is that this one will end only through the gradual recovery of investment. The vulnerability of the American economy along with corporate scandals, political tensions derived from the Iraq conflict, and the loss of the economys dynamism, have weakened consumer confidence. In sum, we can highlight a series of issues that are contributing to making the recovery of the world economy much more uncertain:  The deepening of the pessimism of economic agents motivated mainly by the Iraq war;  The possibility of new terrorist attacks;  Uncertainty about the oil price level and volatility;  An increase of risk aversion in the international financial markets. And over the medium term:  The current account deficit and the low domestic savings rate of the United States together with the absence of structural reforms in Europe and Japan that would allow for a rebound in their economies and an orderly adjustment of the world economy. Resistance to the world recession The Mexican economy has not been able to isolate itself from the global recession that has materialized in three ways: a lower growth rate, a drop in employment and a virtual standstill of Mexican exports. Notwithstanding the above, the Mexican economys performance in 2001 and 2002 presents some positive aspects. We can highlight the fact that Mexico has experienced a normal recession since 2001, if such a word is allowed. Throughout decades, Mexico knew the dark side of recessions, the one that we used to call crisis. However, the experience that we have had with the recession that started in 2001 and the incipient recovery of 2002 has been quite different:  The public deficit has been close to its target in the last two years;  In 2002, the current account deficit was below 3% of GDP and was financed almost entirely by FDI; 19/2003 1  The exchange rate was relatively stable in 2001 and 2002, and actually, current peso depreciation has not affected the price level because exchange-rate pass-through has been virtually nonexistent;  Inflation has been under control;  The main peso-denominated nominal interest rates have fallen to single-digit levels, and the government and some private enterprises are issuing bonds in pesos at longer terms (up to ten years);  Foreign direct investment reached a record high in 2001 and maintained a high level in 2002. The vulnerability of the Mexican economy to recent external disturbances has been limited because of three factors: a) We have been able to advance in the strengthening of the macroeconomic fundamentals; b) The economic links with the United States have been reinforced, and c) In recent years, Mexico has consolidated its institutions, politically and economically. Institutional improvements Two types of factors have contributed to the strengthening of the Mexican economy. It is important to highlight the economic policies that have been implemented, including the floating exchange-rate regime and the inflation-targeting framework that has been adopted for the conduct of monetary policy. In addition, progress achieved through the consolidation of the institutional framework has reinforced the effects of economic policy. In the wake of the 1995 crisis, the public has developed a growing consciousness about the importance of prudent economic policies, and a consensus has slowly gathered in favor of reaching a lower inflation rate and keeping a lower fiscal deficit. Although a lot of progress has been made on the institutional framework in many areas, I will focus on the elements I believe are the most important:  Fiscal discipline;  Inflation abatement;  Consolidation and capitalization of the financial sector;  Reinforcement of electoral institutions and increased democratic credibility;  Independence of the Supreme Court of Justice;  NAFTA benefits. With the objective of reinforcing the foundation for economic development, the current administration has continued efforts to maintain the health of the public finances. Fiscal prudence is reflected by the fact that public debt presents a sustainable level and a very comfortable maturity profile. Also, the public sector deficit has not increased when the oil price has fallen and the pace of economic activity has slowed. To this end, it is important to mention that the fact that the Mexican Congress is not dominated by a single political party has not weakened fiscal discipline (although public finances have not been modified structurally, an issue I will discuss later). In the fight against inflation, we continue to make progress. After three consecutive years in which the inflation target was met, in 2002 the annual rate was 120 basis points above target. However, this deviation was a consequence of the evolution of the agricultural sub index, whose prices are extremely volatile, and of the goods subject to government-administered prices, which are not determined by the market. This year it is to be expected that the inflation rate will converge to our 3 percent target. We have been able to manage the external shocks we faced in recent years thanks to the floating exchange-rate regime. Likewise, stability has allowed an important increase in our international reserves. No doubt, our reserves have been one of the factors that explain the isolation of the Mexican economy from contamination by the events in Argentina, Brazil and Venezuela. They were also a determining factor during the process by which Mexico was given investment-grade status and hence has obtained better credit conditions in the international capital markets. Given the current level of international assets that Banco de Mexico has, the marginal advantages of accruing them at such a high pace have diminished. That is why the Exchange Commission recently 2 19/2003 agreed on a mechanism that will reduce the rate of accumulation of international reserves. This mechanism is transparent, its operation does not imply a discretional intervention in the market by the authorities, and it is also neutral with respect to the exchange rate. In the last few years, the financial system has seen important advances. Now, the banking system presents sound capitalization ratios, satisfactory results and a better regulatory framework. It is important to mention that the legal framework in which the banking system operates has formed the groundwork for its expansion. Stability will be an important issue that will permit the renewal of credit. To this end, it is quite significant that some banks have already started to renew credit. However, the behavior is not yet widespread and amounts of new credit to date are insufficient to contribute properly to economic development. In the political arena we have witnessed important institutional progress. For example, the creation almost a decade ago of the autonomous Federal Electoral Institute was a great success. Election transparency has contributed in a very important way to the economy through the so-called democratic bonus. No doubt the electoral legitimacy of the public authority is an essential factor for the political stability of the country. With the consolidation of the democratic system, judicial power is more independent from the other powers. The Supreme Court is well respected, and its responsibility has been gradually transmitted to the federal courts to stimulate their improvement. Also, the local courts have been influenced by the Supreme Courts performance, although to a smaller extent. As is known, an efficient judicial system constitutes an element of great value for economic development because, at the end of the day, it guarantees property rights and gives certainty to the decisions of economic agents. Recent studies point out that an adequate legal framework and an efficient law enforcement system are key to the development of nations. Therefore, this is a crucial element in the classification of debtors risk and in the determination of credit costs. The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) has had not only a remarkable impact on Mexicos external trade, but has also been the engine of the institutional change that Mexico has experienced. In this respect, NAFTA has given certainty to trade relations between Mexico and other countries and has opened widespread investment opportunities. NAFTA has also contributed to Mexicos industrial modernization, to fostering innovation and competition and to creating a more predictable legal environment for all economic agents. To a great extent, developed countries are developed because of the strength of their institutions. Economic development calls for clear and predictable rules, and institutions that assure they will be enforced. The challenges: pending reforms It is not foreseeable that in the immediate future the world economy will present a favorable expansion pattern. The principal hurdles are the enormous current account deficit of the United States and an imminent fiscal deficit, to which we have to add the lack of structural reforms in Japan and Europe. It is evident that a situation in which the U.S. economy is absorbing two thirds of the worlds savings is not sustainable. In other words, there should be an adjustment in the world economy in the future that, amongst other things, should imply a dollar depreciation. If such adjustment is not accompanied by a rebound of the European and Japanese economies, it is not foreseeable that it will take place in an accelerated-growth context. Even under the most optimistic scenario it is not possible to expect, in the medium term, global growth comparable to that of the nineties. Hence, the premises on which the development of the Mexican economy has been based in recent years should be modified. It will be necessary to consolidate internal sources of growth. The key to success rests in the capacity of the Mexican economy to become more productive and more competitive in the international arena.
